papers.title: Synthesis-Aware Molecular Generation via Reaction-Driven Global Search
papers.abstract: Synthesizability remains a central challenge in de novo molecular generation. Conventional goal-directed molecular optimization methods, where molecules are generated by optimizing target properties often suffer from low synthetic accessibility. Existing strategies typically address this gap through post hoc filtering or by restricting generation to predefined reaction schemes. The former decouples synthesis from optimization, whereas the latter improves feasibility at the cost of restricting molecular exploration. We present RxnMol, a synthesis-aware molecular optimization framework in which each candidate is encoded as a synthetic-route representation: an ordered sequence of readily available molecular building blocks. A pretrained reaction prediction model converts these building blocks into a product molecule through sequential reaction prediction, while a population-based global optimization algorithm modifies the route representation and evaluates the resulting molecule against the target objective. Thus, molecular optimization operates on synthetic routes rather than solely on final molecular structures. Each selected molecule is obtained from the optimized route representation by RxnMol; therefore, the improved objective values remain directly tied to the corresponding synthetic routes predicted by the model. Across protein target and bioactivity optimization tasks, RxnMol improves Top-1 performance on both generative baselines that optimize molecular structures directly and template-based synthesis-constrained methods in most benchmarks. Together, these results show that de novo molecular design can be formulated as route optimization, where reaction prediction translates route representations into product molecules for objective evaluation.

papers.title: Synthesis of spiro-1,2-dihydropyridine derivatives via cycloisomerization of 3-aza-1,5-enynes catalyzed by gold(I) complex/polyoxometalate hybrids.
papers.abstract: This study reports an optimized method for the synthesis of spiro-1,2-dihydropyridines via the cycloisomerization of 3-aza-1,5-enynes, catalyzed by heterogeneous gold(I)–polyoxometalate (POM) hybrids. By replacing traditional homogeneous catalysts with these hybrid systems, we achieved high yields (up to 82% isolated) and shortened reaction times, while minimizing product degradation. The reaction scope was demonstrated across a broad range of substrates, including aryl, alkyl, and heterocyclic derivatives, as well as variations in ring size and nitrogen substituents using 5 mol% of IPrAuI(MeCN).H5P2W18O64 as catalyst.

papers.title: Stereopure β-Hydroxy Cycloalkane Carboxylic Acids and Their Fluorinated Derivatives as Promising Chemotypes for Drug Discovery: Multigram Synthesis, Physicochemical and Biological Evaluation
papers.abstract: An efficient synthetic approach to all stereoisomers of enantiopure β-hydroxycycloalkane carboxylic acids based on enzymatic resolution of appropriate synthetic equivalents was developed. The developed methodology was used for the preparation of other building blocks relevant to medicinal chemistry, including β-methoxy- and β-fluoro-substituted cycloalkane carboxylic acids. In addition to that, diastereopure gem-difluorinated β-hydroxycycloalkane carboxylic acids were also synthesized. The obtained series of building blocks was subjected to physicochemical characterization, including p K a and Log P measurements. Furthermore, they were used to synthesize serotonin receptor modulators that were evaluated in an animal study using isolated rat cortex nerve terminals and measuring the mitochondrial membrane potential and ROS generation with fluorimetry along with serotonin.

papers.title: Regenerative catalyst system enables efficient and durable electrosynthesis of hydroxylamine from nitric acid
papers.abstract: Direct synthesis of hydroxylamine (NH2OH) via electrochemical nitrate reduction offers a promising alternative for sustainable production of nitrogen-containing chemicals. However, catalyst aging, especially in acidic media, remains a critical challenge due to the irreversible surface reconstruction under cathodic potentials, which limits long-term catalytic activity and product selectivity. Here, we develop a regenerative catalyst strategy for efficient and enduring NH2OH electrosynthesis from nitric acid (HNO3). By introducing a trace amount of Bi3+ in solution, nanostructured metallic Bi is formed in situ to facilitate nitrate electroreduction reaction, delivering a NH2OH Faradaic efficiency of over 90% between -1.0 to -1.5 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode. Inversely, switching the applied voltage to open-circuit potential can fully reset the aged catalyst back into its ionic state. Leveraging this reversible Bi3+/Bi redox cycle, we demonstrate a continuous operation of HNO3-to-NH2OH conversion for 30 days, with a consistent product selectivity of over 90% and current density of ~ 0.4 A cm-2.

papers.title: Ubiquitous Relationships between Autofluorescence Lifetimes and Cure in Polymer Adhesives and Sealants
papers.abstract: Investigating the curing of adhesives and sealants generally requires sample removal or destruction, material modification, or loss of spatial information, leading to challenges in understanding and controlling cure and in preventing material failures. Contrary to prevailing assumptions that autofluorescence is too dim or nonspecific to enable microscopic and macroscopic characterization of these materials, we here discover ubiquitous relationships between degree of cure and autofluorescence lifetimes. These correlations enable a nondestructive, spatially resolved, and real-time cure measurement of unmodified adhesives and sealants. The technique harnesses fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) and spans various mechanisms of curing and compositions, including copolymerizing thermosets, step-growth and chain-growth polymerizations, and solventdriven hardening processes. (e.g., silicones, polyvinyl acetate, cyanoacrylate, acrylic paint, and polyurethanes). Unexpectedly, all examined materials are sufficiently autofluorescent to display these relationships, without modification—and the correlations exist despite the nonspecific autofluorescence signal. Complementary dynamic mechanical analysis and fluorescence anisotropy measurements pinpoint the mechanistic origin of these relationships to the unique microenvironment hardening processes in each material. Insight gained reveals spatially uneven cure, cure at composite joints, and the emergence of microenvironment diversity. Our findings establish FLIM as an effective tool to spectroscopically monitor cure across adhesives, sealants, and paints.

papers.title: Autofluorescence Lifetime and Anisotropy Enable In Situ Polymer Molecular-Weight Measurement
papers.abstract: Traditional methods for polymer molecular-weight determination are poorly suited to insoluble polymers, lack spatial resolution, and are slowed by their incompatibility with in situ measurements. Alternative fluorescence-based approaches are conventionally believed to require incorporation of exogenous fluorophores or covalent polymer labeling. In contrast, here we discover that nonconjugated, exclusively-hydrocarbon polymers (polynorbornene, polydicyclopentadiene, poly(norbornene-co-dicyclopentadiene), and poly(cyclooctene-co-dicyclopentadiene)) derived from ruthenium-catalyzed ring-opening metathesis exhibit unexpectedly strong autofluorescent signals that enable fluorescence lifetime and polarization measurements without added fluorophores or chain modification. Remarkably, the resulting autofluorescence signal is sensitive to changes in molecular weight. Quantitative correlations between fluorescence lifetime and number-average molecular weight (Mn), and between anisotropy-derived effective rotational correlation time and Mn, enabled spectroscopic measurement of molecular weight. After initial calibration of the spectroscopic signals to Mn as measured through a traditional technique, the method was amenable to ongoing precipitation-polymerization reactions with Mn ranging from 20–630 kg/mol. Different polymer systems exhibited optimal measurement through either lifetime- or anisotropy-based analysis. The autofluorescence appears to originate from the aggregation of the polymer chains, while the molecular weight dependence of this signal arises from differential flexibility of the polymer chains. This work establishes a spectroscopic platform for in situ molecular weight determination of insoluble polymers without sample isolation or dissolution, providing new opportunities for accelerated process optimization, reaction monitoring, and high-throughput catalyst discovery.

papers.title: Asymmetric Copper-Catalyzed Propargylic Substitution Reaction of Propargylic Acetates with Ambident Nucleophile 5-Aminopyrazoles
papers.abstract: Absract: An asymmetric copper-catalyzed propargylic substitution reaction of propargylic acetates with ambident 5-aminopyrazoles was developed. Under optimized conditions, the relevant products with a wide range of substrates and good functional tolerance were obtained in 51-99% yields and up to 99:1 er. A gram-scale reaction and synthetic transformations demonstrated the practicality, delivering chiral γ-aryl-substituted propargylic products with high enantioselectivity.

papers.title: Ultrabroadband Plasmonic–MOF Hybrid Photocatalysts for Integrated Solar Fuel Generation via CO2 Reduction and Water Splitting
papers.abstract: The increasing global energy demand and escalating atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration have intensified the search for sustainable technologies capable of simultaneously mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and generating clean fuels. Photocatalytic solar fuel generation has emerged as one of the most promising approaches for converting solar energy into chemical energy through carbon dioxide reduction and water splitting. However, conventional photocatalysts are limited by narrow light absorption ranges, rapid charge carrier recombination, and poor catalytic efficiency under visible and near-infrared irradiation. In this work, ultrabroadband plasmonic–metal–organic framework (MOF) hybrid photocatalysts were rationally engineered to achieve enhanced solar-driven CO2 reduction coupled with hydrogen evolution. A plasmonic Au–Cu nanoparticle system integrated with a UiO-66-NH2 MOF framework was synthesized via a solvothermal-assisted in situ growth strategy to improve charge separation, broaden light harvesting capabilities, and facilitate catalytic active site accessibility. The synthesized hybrid photocatalysts were comprehensively characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), ultraviolet–visible diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (UV–Vis DRS), photoluminescence spectroscopy (PL), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and transient photocurrent response measurements. Structural analysis confirmed the successful integration of plasmonic nanoparticles within the porous MOF architecture while preserving crystallinity and high surface area. Photocatalytic experiments demonstrated a substantial enhancement in CO2 conversion and hydrogen production under simulated solar irradiation. The optimized Au–Cu/UiO-66-NH2 photocatalyst achieved methane and methanol generation rates of 312.4 μmol g-1 h-1 and 184.7 μmol g-1 h-1, respectively, while simultaneously producing hydrogen at a rate of 1286 μmol g-1 h-1. The enhanced performance was attributed to synergistic plasmonic effects, ultrabroadband absorption extending into the near-infrared region, improved charge separation, and efficient interfacial electron transfer between the plasmonic nanoparticles and MOF framework. The present study provides a promising strategy for the development of next-generation multifunctional photocatalysts for integrated solar fuel production and carbon-neutral energy conversion.

papers.title: Advancing Cation–π Interaction Modeling: Development of Novel Force Field Models
papers.abstract: Cation–π interactions, noncovalent attractions between cations and electron-rich π systems, play important roles in biomolecular recognition, protein folding, enzymatic catalysis, and supramolecular assembly. Despite the widespread use of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to study such systems, accurately modeling cation–π interactions remains challenging. The classical Lennard-Jones (12-6) potential is inadequate because it omits charge-induced-dipole effects. The 12-6-4 model addresses this by adding a C4/r4 induction term and has been shown to substantially improve descriptions of cation–π interactions in biological contexts. Here we present a 12-6-4-NBFIX parameterization for cation–aromatic amino acid interactions within the AMBER force field, in which atom-pair-specific C12, C6, and C4 parameters are derived via atoms-in-molecules (AIM) analysis and jointly optimized against high-level energy decomposition analysis (EDA) results from symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT) or sobEDA. Joint optimization of all three parameters yields C4 values with markedly improved transferability across ions of the same oxidation state compared with approaches that optimize C4 alone, and produces individual energy components in better agreement with the SAPT analysis. Despite this improvement, the 12-6-4-NBFIX model exhibits systematic short-range deviations. We therefore introduce the ASPECT (Ab initio Screened Pauli-repulsion, Electrostatics and Classical Tang-Toennies) model, which incorporates three physically motivated enhancements: (1) replacing the r−12 repulsion wall with a Buckingham exponential term supplemented by a small C12 term to prevent potential overturn in the short-range; (2) applying Tang–Toennies damping functions to both the C6/r6 dispersion and C4/r4 induction terms; and (3) considering the charge-penetration effects via atomic- charge screening functions. The ASPECT model achieves excellent agreement with both total interaction energies and all individual EDA components across the full interaction range, representing a significant advance over the 12-6-4-NBFIX approach. The enlarged parameter space does, however, increase the risk of overfitting, and careful validation is recommended prior to production use. Finally, we proposed a strategy for parameterizing force fields governing protein-metal ion interactions. Using the 12-6-4-NBFIX model as an example, our simulations demonstrated the effectiveness of this strategy in capturing protein–ion interactions within CusF, a metallochaperone whose metal site involves cation–π interaction, and its W44M mutant. Notably, the 12-6-4-NBFIX model predicted a more favorable ion binding affinity for the W44M mutant relative to the wild-type, consistent with experimental observations. In sum, in this study we have developed advanced force field models for simulating cation–π interactions in proteins. These models provide physically grounded, transferable descriptions of cation–π interactions and a robust foundation for accurate MD simulations of metal-ion-containing biological and materials systems.

papers.title: Deciphering Electrochemical Generation, Transport, and Reactivity of Hydrogen Species in the Electrochemical Palladium Membrane Reactor
papers.abstract: Electrochemical palladium membrane reactor (ePMR) enables hydrogenation chemistry by mechanically separating but (electro)chemically coupling electrochemical reduction of proton and chemical hydrogenation by transporting hydrogen species through a dense Pd membrane, yet the identity and transport mechanism of the reactive hydrogen species remain underdefined. In this work, we disentangled the roles of hydrogen species including hydrogen atoms and molecules for both electrochemical and chemical compartments using 1-hexyne electrochemical hydrogenation reaction as a model reaction. Tafel analysis with H+/D+ electrolytes, kinetic isotope effects, and quantification of products show that the rate-limiting step and apparent kinetics were strongly affected by the electron transfer kinetics and hydrogen permeation through the Pd membrane. Furthermore, mathematical description of hydrogen atom transport through the Pd membrane was successfully elucidated. Electrochemically deposited Pd, Rh, and PdRh layers with controlled thickness and morphology tuned the reaction pathway of hydrogen atom versus H2-mediation at the chemical compartment, enabling systematic variation of 1-hexyne conversion and n-hexane selectivity. A dominant role of in situ generation and re-dissociation of H*/H2 was verified in the hydrogenation process supported by control experiments including gas-purging experiments. These insights establish design principles of catalyst engineering for ePMR which strategically couple atomic and molecular hydrogen transport for efficient and selective organic hydrogenation.

papers.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Electrolyte Structural Transport Mechanism: Attempt Frequencies and Activation Free Energies
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion transport through an electrolyte, in addition to standard diffusion (vehicular), a second Li+ transport mechanism, called structural diffusion, is important. Very recently the molecular-level process, partial desolvation (a solvent molecule leaving the Li+/solvent cluster), that is responsible for structural diffusion was delineated. Here, we deepen our understanding of structural diffusion. The concentration dependence of Li+ structural diffusion in liquids with three different anions was studied using ultrafast two dimensional infrared experiments. The time dependencies of the fundamental physical fluctuations that underlie partial desolvation were determined. These fluctuations correspond to the attempt frequencies in transition-state theory. Attempt frequencies in the context of molecular transtition state theory have not previously been measured. Knowing the partial desolvation rates and the attempt frequencies enabled the determination of the activation free energies for partial desolvation, which range from ~7 to ~9 kJ/mol. The quantitative results provide the path from molecular-level fluctuations to diffusion constants.

papers.title: Resolution-Robust Mid-IR ATR-FTIR Classification of Mixed Plastic Waste with PVC Screening and Polyethylene Subclassification
papers.abstract: Reliable and chemistry-specific presorting of mixed plastic waste is essential for safe and efficient valorization. In this study, a resolution-robust mid-infrared attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) workflow coupled with simple machine-learning classifiers is presented for poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) screening and subclassification of three polyethylene (PE) grades: low-density polyethylene (LDPE), linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE), and high-density polyethylene (HDPE). A total of 770 ATR-FTIR spectra in the fingerprint region (2500–500 cm⁻¹) were collected from seven plastics: LDPE, LLDPE, HDPE, PP, PS, PET, and PVC, using commercial pellets together with post-consumer PET and discarded PVC gloves. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to compress the high-dimensional, correlated spectral inputs into a low-dimensional score space, reducing multicollinearity and overfitting risk while preserving class-identifiable fingerprint information. The resulting PCA structure showed clear low-dimensional separability among the plastic classes and PE subclasses, supporting the use of simple classifiers rather than heavily parameterized black-box architectures. Support-vector machine (SVM) and shallow deep neural network (DNN) classifiers were trained on the PCA scores, with internal-test and strictly independent external-validation performances evaluated separately. For the baseline dataset (2 cm⁻¹), both classifiers achieved 100% external-validation accuracy. Even after degradation to effective spectral resolutions of 8 and 16 cm⁻¹, SVM and shallow DNN maintained 100% internal-test and external-validation accuracy across PVC screening, PE-grade subclassification, and full seven-class discrimination. These results demonstrate a resolution-robust, PCA-interpretable, and externally validated ATR-FTIR/ML workflow for practical plastic presorting.

papers.title: Differential Coats-Redfern Framework for Conversion-Resolved Temperature-Programmed Kinetics
papers.abstract: Temperature-programmed measurements such as thermogravimetry (TG) are routinely interpreted with Coasts-Redfern (CR) or isoconversional methods. Classical CR provides model-dependent activation energies (Ea) and pre-exponential factors (A) from a single heating ramp but relies on a global straight-line fit of ln[g(α)/T2] versus 1/T, which does not provide a rigorous differential definition of Ea and averages over curvature, obscuring local kinetic information since 1964. In this study, we reformulate CR in a differential framework (d-CR) by recognizing that the rigorous activation energy is given by the local derivative of ln[g(α)/T2] versus 1/T. In the infinitesimal-window limit, the CR relation yields conversion-resolved kinetic triplets {Ea(α), A(α), dα/dt} along a single heating rate for any chosen solid-state model. This converts CR from a single {Ea, A} pair into a dense kinetic field that enables two internal consistency checks unavailable in the classical workflow: (i) point-by-point rate-parity tests between reconstructed and experimental rates and (ii) conversion-variant compensation analysis in the {Ea(α), ln A(α)} plane. We benchmark d-CR against classical CR on non-catalyzed and zeolite-catalyzed thermolysis of pristine low-density polyethylene (LDPE), quantifying the bias introduced by global CR linearization even at high R2 and embedding d-CR into the isoconversional model selection workflow. To test applicability beyond polymers and thermogravimetry under isoconversional-free conditions, we apply d-CR to dehydration of Na2HPO4 and temperature-programmed in-situ FT-IR at a single heating rate. The d-CR framework thus improves a long-standing integral linearization into a conversion-resolved, model-aware kinetic analysis that is directly applicable to existing temperature-programmed datasets beyond thermogravimetry.

papers.title: Promotion of oxygen evolution reaction on Cu-oxide electrode via Ce-Driven Lattice Distortion
papers.abstract: Incorporating Ce, which favors a higher coordination number than Cu, into a CuO x host significantly boosts Oxygen Evolution Reaction (OER) performance, reaching optimal catalytic activity at 40% Ce inclusion. We have, for the first time, imaged the electrode surface optically under OER conditions. The heterogeneous surface has active regions where O 2 bubble formation was observed and were presented alongside MOOH* intermediates, indicating their direct relevance to OER. This study couples in situ Raman spectroscopy with isotope substitution experiments. The in situ Raman findings reveal a clear correlation between a highly oxidized Cu 3+ -type species and OER activity across multiple samples. Vibrational characterization, along with isotopic substitution studies, indicated that such sites are a part of the -Cu-O-Cu- extended network. Theoretical modeling suggests that copper centers are likely to be preferentially oxidized during oxidation of Ce-doped copper oxide, facilitating the formation of highly oxidized Cu 3+ -type species. A significant reduction (~50%) in the apparent activation energy was observed for the Ce-incorporated copper oxide compared with the pristine counterpart.

papers.title: Red-Light Tomographic Volumetric 3D Printing in Seconds for Fabrication of Colorless Structures
papers.abstract: Non-pulsed red light photopolymerization is attractive for volumetric additive manufacturing because longer wavelengths can improve light penetration, lower scattering, and reduce photodamage compared with ultra-violet or blue irradiation. In this work, we utilized methylene blue and triethanolamine as a sacrificial type II photoinitiating system for poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogel printing with a custom-made red-light tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing system. With the optimized formulation, PEGDA hydrogel structures were printed by red light within 30 s. The resulting constructs were colorless, extractable, and contained fully formed internal channels. This work establishes a type II photochemistry system as a promising route for extending tomographic volumetric 3D printing toward lower-energy visible-light irradiation and rapid fabrication of colorless hydrogel constructs.

papers.title: Interplay between helical Δ/Λ chirality and the ligand-based asymmetric centre in cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes: Possibility for selective sensing of d-serine
papers.abstract: Cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes can possess Δ/Λ chirality and incorporate chiral ligands, enabling diverse photochemical applications, including sensing and asymmetric catalysis. Herein, two series of chiral iridium(III) complexes with or without a butyl group in their cyclometalated ligand framework were synthesised and characterised to clarify the role of the ligand framework in modulating the effects of Δ/Λ and ligand chirality on luminescence properties. The complexes were prepared by reacting enantiopure Δ- or Λ-[Ir( n BuBQ) 2 Cl] ( 1 ; n BuBQ = monodeprotonated 2-butyl-benzo[ h ]quinoline) and racemic [Ir(HBQ) 2 (CH 3 CN) 2 ]PF 6 ( 2 ; HBQ = monodeprotonated benzo[ h ]quinoline) with d - or l -serine. Precursor 1 exhibited higher substitutional lability than precursor 2 under comparable conditions because of its coordinatively unsaturated five-coordinate structure. Each precursor yielded four enantiomerically pure stereoisomers—Δ 1 - d , Λ 1 - d , Δ 1 - l , and Λ 1 - l ( 1 -series) and Δ 2 - d , Λ 2 - d , Δ 2 - l , and Λ 2 - l ( 2 -series)—enabling the systematic isolation and comparison of all possible stereoisomers in each series. Molecular structure analysis by single-crystal X-ray crystallography and theoretical calculations suggest intramolecular interactions between the serine ligand and n BuBQ framework in the 1 -series. In dichloromethane, the diastereomeric sets in the 1 -series ( i.e. , Δ 1 - d /Λ 1 - l and Λ 1 - d /Δ 1 - l ) showed much larger differences in emission intensity and radiative rate constant than those in the 2 -series. These results suggest that the butyl group in the ligand framework influences how differences arising from the combination of Δ/Λ chirality and d / l configuration of the coordinated serine ligand are manifested in the luminescence properties of the complexes. This work may provide a useful guideline for the ligand framework design toward selective luminescence sensing of d -serine.

papers.title: Pore-networked membranes based on the in-situ gelation of metal-organic frameworks
papers.abstract: The integration of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as fillers with polymers as matrices, known as mixed-matrix membranes, aims to overcome the low processability of MOFs while maintaining their adsorbent properties for separation applications. However, the aggregation of MOF nanoparticles and their poor compatibility with polymers compromise the membrane stability and performance. Here we report the fabrication of pore-networked membranes (PNMs) by in situ gelating MOF nanoparticles into mesoscale colloidal networks with hierarchical porosities within the polymer matrix. In contrast to most conventional hybrid strategies that rely on the homogeneous dispersion of MOF fillers, PNMs are characterized by an interconnected colloidal MOF network as the continuous porous phase across the whole membrane material. As proof of concept, a series of zirconium-based MOFs was used to fabricate PNMs. We comprehensively studied the effect of MOF ligands on their capability of gelating and forming a continuous MOF phase with homogeneous distribution. Various polymer matrices are screened to tailor membrane fabrication to enhance mechanical stability and improve performance in the uptake of water pollutants. Our PNM strategy provides an alternative pathway to bridge MOF adsorbents and processable polymers for better material performance.

papers.title: Many-Body Screening Drives Nanoscale Core-Level Variation at the Water Interface
papers.abstract: The depth at which the interfacial behavior of liquid water transitions into bulk behavior is critical towards understanding atmospherically relevant processes. Using intrinsic chemical shifts of O 1s core-levels, we demonstrate that the bulk electronic behavior emerges within 6 Å of the vacuum–liquid interface. This rapid onset is in remarkable agreement with observations from non-linear vibrational spectroscopy, yet has a different physical origin. Within the interfacial region, we observe an intrinsic core-level bending of 1.0 eV. Using many-body methods, we show that the level bending is driven by the differences in optical dielectric-screening at the interface compared to the bulk, and not due to differences in the hydrogen-bonding network. On the vaccum-side, the O 1s core-level energies attain the gas-phase values at a distance of 10 Å from the interface.

papers.title: CCSBase2: A Unified Benchmark Dataset and Machine Learning Framework for Robust CCS Prediction
papers.abstract: The identification of unknown analytes remains a persistent challenge in untargeted mass spectrometry-based analyses. Ion mobility–mass spectrometry (IM-MS) has expanded identification capabilities by enabling the use of collision cross section (CCS) as an orthogonal molecular identifier, but experimentally measured CCS values remain sparse relative to the breadth of known chemical space. Machine learning (ML) approaches have emerged as a complementary strategy for CCS prediction. Many existing models, however, suffer from poor generalizability and accuracy across structurally diverse chemical classes. Here, we present CCSBase2, a large, unified CCS database comprising 62,043 measurements assembled by integrating multiple public datasets, along with a classical ML framework for CCS prediction using Morgan Fingerprint Counts. CCSBase2 achieved a mean relative error of 1.69%, median relative error of 1.23%, and root mean squared error of 4.65 on a held-out test set. All models were trained on a consumer-grade M4 Pro CPU, demonstrating that accurate CCS prediction can be achieved with minimal computational resources while maintaining strong performance when generalized to out-of-distribution compounds. The final model is available at https://ccsbase.net/ccsbase2, and the codebase and datasets are freely available at GitHub.

papers.title: Microstructural Control of L-Lactide/ε-Caprolactone Copolymers using Amidinate-Based Aluminium Catalysts
papers.abstract: The development of copolymers derived from L-lactide (L-LA) and ε-caprolactone (CL) represents a sustainable strategy in the design of next-generation biodegradable materials, alternative to conventional non-degradable industrial polymers. In this work, novel dialkyl and alkyl/alkoxide aluminium complexes supported by scorpionate-derived ligands have been prepared. Thus, dialkyl derivatives [AlR 2 (κ 2 -NN’)] (κ 2 -NN’ = pbpamd, R = Me 1 , Et 2 ; tbpamd, R = Et 3 ) were easily obtained by reaction of AlR 3 with the corresponding protio ligand. Complexes 1 and 2 adopt a chelating coordination mode, while complex 3 can display a CH– 3a or NH– 3b tautomer, depending on the experimental conditions. Further exposure of 1 and 3a to dry air afforded two mixed alkyl-alkoxide aluminium dimers [Al(R)(μ-OR)(κ 2 -NN’)] 2 (κ 2 -NN’ = pbpamd, R = Me 4 ; tbpamd, R = Et 5 ) by oxygen insertion on the Al–C bond. 2D DOSY NMR experiments evidenced the different dimerization tendencies of 4 and 5 . X-Ray crystal structure analysis of 2 , 4 and 5 confirmed unambiguously the different ligand arrangements proposed. Interestingly, complexes 1 , 3a , 3b , 4 , and 5 were initially evaluated as initiators for the ring-opening copolymerisation (ROCOP) of L-lactide and ε -caprolactone under different procedures. Among them, alkyl/alkoxide 5 exhibited the highest activity and showed moderate random preference in the poly(L-lactide)- co- poly( ε -caprolactone) copolymers, via a “one-pot/one-step” method. Alternatively, dialkyls 1 – 3 promoted blockier architectures, facilitating preferential L-LA insertion, under these conditions. More importantly, initiators 1 and 5 successfully promoted diblock poly(L-lactide)- b- poly( ε -caprolactone) materials, via a “one-pot/two-step” procedure. Expectedly, copolymers composition directly impacted over material thermal properties. Thus, DSC analysis of mild gradient-type architectures revealed lower T m values than blockier microstructures, whereas diblock compositions exhibited two endotherms in the range of PCL and PLLA homopolymers, respectively. Significant impact of monomer incorporation in the PLA- co -PCL copolymers was also revealed in the TGA profiles; as PLLA block increases, the degradation onset temperature clearly decreases.

papers.title: Carbonyl Derivatization Tunes Triplet-State Aromaticity and Dynamics in Fused-Ring Cyclic Amides
papers.abstract: Singlet fission (SF) and triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC) are photophysical processes which, respectively, result in the division of one high energy singlet state into two lower-energy triplet states, and vice versa. These processes are components of strategies to overcome the efficiency limits of photovoltaic devices, by funneling more energy into silicon solar cells. Molecules featuring a fused π -conjugated ring system interrupted by amide groups have recently attracted interest for singlet fission owing to their greater stability than acene-based chromophores. While aromaticity has been regularly used to design chromophores for both SF and TTA-UC and rationalize results, debate continues about the relevance and application of the concept. Here, we describe the spectroscopic properties of novel derivatives of a 5-6-5 fused-ring chromophore with a central 8 π 1,4-diacyl-1,4-dihydropyrazine ring. Density functional theory calculations suggest that the parent chromophore does not meet the key thermodynamic criterion for SF, i.e. E (S 1 ) ≥ 2 E (T 1 ), but that modifying the carbonyl groups via microwave-assisted thionation and subsequent silver(I)-promoted condensation will substantially modulate the E (T 1 )/ E (S 1 ) ratio. Through photophysical measurements including time-resolved absorption and magneto-photoluminescence, we demonstrate that intersystem crossing followed by triplet-triplet annihilation occurs upon excitation of a dicyanomethylene-substituted derivative. We propose an explanation for these observations in terms of Mandado’s (2 n + 1) aromaticity rule, which provides guidance for future designs of multiexcitonic chromophore systems based on the cyclic amide motif.

papers.title: Direct Synthesis of Super-Hydrophilic Poly(2-oxazoline)s and Tuning Their Thermoresponsive Behavior
papers.abstract: Poly(2-oxazolines) (POx) are emerging as biocompatible alternatives to poly(ethylene glycol), yet the accessible chemical space of hydrophilic POx remains limited. Poly(2methoxymethyl-2-oxazoline) (pMeOMeOx) was previously considered inaccessible via direct cationic ring-opening polymerization (CROP), instead requiring multistep postpolymerization modification routes. Here, we demonstrate that this limitation originates not from incompatibility with CROP, but from β-elimination during synthesis of longer ether-functionalized 2-oxazolines. A shorter methoxymethyl substituent in MeOMeOx avoids this instability. Direct synthesis of pMeOMeOx and its oxazine analogue pMeOMeOzi was achieved via living CROP, enabling access to well-defined homo- and copolymers. The methoxymethyl substituent accelerated propagation approximately threefold relative to 2-methyl-2-oxazoline and 2-methyl-2-oxazine analogues, establishing these monomers among the fastest propagating alkyl-substituted POx/POzi systems reported to date. Salt-induced cloud point measurements further revealed exceptionally high hydration stability of pMeOMeOx, exceeding that of pMeOx, pMeOMeOzi, and poly(vinylpyrrolidone). Thermoresponsive behavior was independently introduced through copolymerization with a thioether-containing monomer or partial thionation, revealing fundamentally different dehydration and phase-separation pathways for thioether- and thioamide-containing polymers. Together, this work establishes direct access to a previously inaccessible class of highly hydrophilic POx and demonstrates how sulfur functionality and its position within the polymer architecture can be used to engineer hydration and thermoresponsive behavior.

papers.title: Decoupling Quantum Capacitance and Interfacial Dielectric Saturation in Wrinkled MXene Supercapacitor Electrodes: A Resource-Efficient Multiscale Computational Framework
papers.abstract: Predicting the exact thermodynamic performance limits of transition metal carbide (MXene) supercapacitor electrodes remains a grand challenge due to the complex multiscale coupling of sub-nanometer ionic packing, electronic quantum capacitance, and dielectric saturation under intense interfacial electric fields. Standard continuum models ignore finite ionic size and electronic structure effects, while fully ab initio quantum mechanical simulations of wrinkled material systems require massive computational superclusters (> 128 GB RAM). In this work, we present a resource-efficient, self-consistentmultiscale computational framework solved in FEniCSx that couples database-mined Density Functional Theory (DFT) and semi-empirical Density Functional Tight-Binding (DFTB+) structures with a Bikerman-Kornyshev Modified Poisson-Boltzmann (MPB) model. Developed specifically to run under a strict memory envelope (< 1.5 GB RAM), our engine incorporates logarithmic boundary layer mesh grading, memory-guarded PETSc Krylov iterative solvers (GMRES with ILU(0) preconditioning), and a three-tier convergence stabilization protocol. Using experimental and computational data for wrinkled Ti3C2O2 electrodes, we demonstrate that structural corrugation wave strains induce a 2.4%–7.4% localized charge density calibration shift (γ) relative to flat surfaces. We evaluate global capacitance limits (Ctotal) and analyze modeldependent uncertainty by benchmarking the classical Booth dielectric model against an exponential saturation formulation. Our results establish a self-consistently calculated upper bound of 62.84 F/g for interfacial capacitance at−1.0V,with ameandielectric sensitivity coefficient of 7.99%, establishing the physical and computational bounds of next-generation energy storage simulations.

papers.title: Hydration-Gated Photoinduced Electron Transfer in O-BODIPY Dyes
papers.abstract: Fluorescent probes based on photoinduced electron transfer (PET) are widely used to image intracellular microenvironments, yet achieving a selective activation of PET by a single environmental parameter remains a challenge. Here we report donor–acceptor dyads based on the O-BODIPY chromophore in which PET is selectively activated by aqueous hydration rather than by generic solvent polarity. Replacing the fluorine groups at boron with triethylene glycol (TEG) chains confers aqueous solubility and modulates the electronic properties of the boron-coordinated core, suppressing PET in polar organic solvents while enabling efficient charge separation specifically in water. This switching arises from hydrogen bonding at the alkoxy oxygens, which strengthens the effective acceptor character of the BODIPY, as confirmed by electrochemical measurements, transient absorption spectroscopy, and DFT calculations. The mechanism is general across dyads incorporating various donors and can be extended to red-emitting chromophores by substitution of the BODIPY scaffold. The lead compound, 5-TEG, displays hydration-dependent fluorescence lifetimes spanning a 6 ns range. In fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) of living cells, tumor spheroids, and intestinal organoids, 5-TEG provides exceptional brightness and spatially resolved lifetime contrast, enabling segmentation of subcellular compartments and reporting on microenvironmental differences. These results establish hydration-gated PET as a tunable photophysical mechanism for designing fluorescence probes with lifetime-encoded readouts in complex biological environments.

papers.title: VALIDITY IS NOT ENOUGH: QUANTIFYING STRUCTURAL COLLAPSE AND INHERITANCE LOSS IN SELFIES-BASED MOLECULAR CROSSOVER
papers.abstract: SELFIES (Self-Referencing Embedded Strings) has emerged as a robust molecular representation that theoretically guarantees chemically valid molecule generation, addressing the invalidity problem commonly observed in SMILES-based molecular optimization. Owing to this validity guarantee, SELFIES has been increasingly adopted in evolutionary molecular design and machine learningbased molecular generation. However, while SELFIES ensures robustness through deterministic grammar-based correction, its impact on evolutionary search dynamics, particularly molecular crossover semantics and structural inheritance, remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we systematically investigate how SELFIES correction affects molecular crossover in genetic algorithms (GAs). Specifically, we analyze (1) post-crossover structural collapse, (2) parent-child structural inheritance, and (3) cumulative multi-generational effects through 10,000 large-scale crossover simulations and multi-generational evolutionary experiments using drug-like molecules sampled from the ZINC20 database. Our results reveal that SELFIES decoding frequently induces structural collapse after crossover, leading to token shortening, molecular weight reduction, and low scaffold retention. Furthermore, parent-child similarity analysis based on Morgan fingerprints demonstrates weakened structural inheritance between parent and offspring molecules. Multi-generational simulations further show progressive reductions in molecular size and scaffold diversity, suggesting cumulative collapse effects across generations. These findings indicate that validity guarantee alone may be insufficient for effective evolutionary molecular search. While SELFIES provides robust chemically valid generation, its correction mechanism may unintentionally alter crossover semantics and constrain structural diversity during evolutionary exploration. This study provides quantitative evidence for reconsidering molecular crossover design in SELFIES-based evolutionary frameworks.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Toxicity of Deep Eutectic Solvents Derived from Betaine, L-Proline and Polyols
papers.abstract: In recent years, DESs are emerging as greener alternatives to conventional organic solvents and ionic liquids in various industrial applications. Due to their ease of preparation, low cost and excellent tunable properties, researchers are exploring the applications of DESs in the textile industry, cosmetics, biomass valorization and biocatalysis. However, the environmental impact and toxicity of DESs have been less studied. Existing studies suggest controversial conclusions. Some studies suggest that DESs are less toxic, while others report higher toxicity. Most of the studies have focused on choline chloride-based DESs. The toxicity of DESs depends on the individual DES components, the cell lines or the species used for the study, making it very difficult to predict their effects. In the present work, we investigated the cytotoxicity and antimicrobial activity of betaine-, L-proline- and polyol-based DESs using multiple cell lines. Our results revealed that the studied DESs are less toxic and their antimicrobial properties depend on the nature of the DES components and their composition ratio. These findings provide valuable insights into the biological safety of non-choline chloride-based DESs and support their potential for sustainable industrial applications.

papers.title: Strain-Induced Anisotropic Transport and Degeneracy Breaking in Monolayer and Bilayer Black Phosphorus: A DFT Based Analysis
papers.abstract: This study illustrates a DFT calculation of the electronic properties of unstrained monolayer and bilayer black phosphorus with 4% uniaxial strain. It uses the PBE functional theory on the GGA level, as well as optimized structure and band structures obtained from SCF calculations. The unstrained monolayer showed a direct bandgap of approximately 0.82 eV while the bilayer showed a reduced bandgap of 0.27 eV due to interlayer coupling. Under tensile strain (4%), the bilayer structure showed clear lifting of band degeneracy near the conduction band minimum, which was not observed for the monolayer. Modulation due to strain was more pronounced in the monolayer with the bandgap increased under tensile strain. Though the bilayer showed weaker tunability with stronger symmetry distortion effects. It is evident from the curvature analysis of the band that higher carrier mobility is preferred by monolayer BP, hence preferably balanced n-MOS and p-MOS active, while the bilayer is preferable for p-MOS operation under tensile strain. The observations confirm that strain and number of layers can be utilized to successfully engineer the black phosphorus's electronic properties towards nano-electronic and straintronic applications.

papers.title: Realizing a 4,3,3-Connected tfe Topology in an Imidazole-Linked Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework
papers.abstract: Reticular chemistry relies on translating molecular geometry into periodic topology, yet many theoretically possible nets remain inaccessible because low-symmetry multinodal connectivity is difficult to crystallize. Here we report TU-433, an imidazole-linked three-dimensional covalent organic framework that realizes the first tfe topology COF and, to our knowledge, the first 4,3,3-connected reticular framework in 2 either COFs or MOFs. Through topological simplification, an 8-connected aldehyde node and a trigonal 3connected amine node evolve into a trinodal network containing one 4-connected and two crystallographically distinct 3-connected vertices. Crystallographic analysis, porosity measurements, spectroscopy, microscopy, electrochemical characterization, and computational modeling establish a noninterpenetrated crystalline framework with permanent microporosity, exceptional aqueous stability, polarized imidazole-rich pore environments, and measurable charge-transport capability derived from its conjugated heteroaromatic backbone. Beyond topological novelty, TU-433 functions as a robust adsorbent for anionic pollutants, delivering the highest reported Acid Orange 7 uptake among known adsorbents, together with efficient capture of Cr(VI) and Mn(VII) oxo-anions, regenerability, and activity in real textile wastewater. Mechanistic studies reveal that proton-responsive imidazole sites, π-rich pore walls, and confinement within the tfe lattice cooperate to drive adsorption. This work expands the accessible topology landscape of COFs and demonstrates how unprecedented connectivity can be coupled to practical waterremediation function.

papers.title: A Strategic Journey from Atomically Precise Metal Nanoclusters to Frameworks: Structural Evolution and Its Impact
papers.abstract: text. Achieving precise control over how discrete nanoscale units organize into extended architectures remains a central challenge in nanocluster chemistry. In this work, we present a ligand-directed strategy that enables the systematic transformation of a single Cu8 nanocluster building block into a series of ordered structures spanning dimer, 1D, 2D, and 3D architectures. The approach relies on differentiating the roles of surface-bound thiolate ligands, where one stabilizes the cluster core and another serves as a coordinatively active site that can 2 be selectively triggered. By tuning the chemical environment, we initiate controlled assembly through protonation of ligands, allowing stepwise growth without altering the intrinsic cluster composition. This design provides a rare opportunity to examine how structural dimensionality alone governs material properties. As the architecture evolves, increased intercluster connectivity modifies electronic configuration, restricts structural flexibility, and alters surface accessibility. These collective effects translate into distinct catalytic responses during electrochemical CO2 conversion, where both activity and product distribution depend sensitively on the degree of organization. In addition, the extended frameworks exhibit enhanced robustness compared to discrete nanoclusters under reaction conditions. Overall, this work establishes a versatile platform for linking nanoscale precision with emergent functionality through controlled structural evolution.

papers.title: Synergistically Enhancing Room-Temperature Phosphorescence, Circularly Polarized Luminescence, and Stimuli Responsiveness through Luminophore-Polymer Interaction Engineering
papers.abstract: Multifunctional room-temperature phosphorescent (RTP) materials hold great promise for diverse applications, but the simultaneous integration of high RTP performance, pronounced chiroptical activity, and stimuli responsiveness in a single system remains challenging. This work presents a luminophore-polymer interaction engineering strategy to develop multifunctional polymer-based RTP materials. Chiral covalently locked binaphthyl organoboron emitters (R/S-BBO and R/S-BBOH) were incorporated into the poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) matrix to construct three systems with progressively strengthened luminophore-polymer interactions: R/S-BBO@PVA with weak non-covalent interactions, R/S-BBOH@PVA featuring enhanced hydrogen bonding, and R/S-BBOH-PVA with dynamic covalent confinement. As the luminophore-polymer interaction increases, local rigidity, network confinement, and triplet-state stability are all reinforced, effectively suppressing non-radiative deactivation. Consequently, the R‑BBOH‑PVA system exhibits outstanding performance, including an ultralong phosphorescence lifetime of 967.51 ms, a phosphorescence quantum yield of 5.73%, and a luminescence dissymmetry factor of 3.9 × 10-3, together with resolvable circularly polarized RTP. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that dynamic borate ester linkages not only rigidify the local microenvironment and stabilize triplet excitons, but also enhance spin-orbit coupling. In addition, the dynamic borate ester network endows the material with reversible ammonia/thermal responsiveness and enables triplet-sensitized Förster resonance energy transfer, leading to multicolor chiral afterglow emission and multidimensional information encryption. This study offers an effective route for precisely tuning luminophore-polymer interactions to realize high-performance, stimuli-responsive.

papers.title: Harnessing Diazo Compounds as Alkoxycarbonyl Methylene Radical Linchpins: Truce–Smiles Rearrangement toward Amido Esters and Isoquinolinedione Scaffolds
papers.abstract: The radical reactivity of acceptor-type diazo compounds is harnessed in the photochemical Truce–Smiles rearrangement of N-aryl-N-arylsulfonyl acrylamides to access β,β′-disubstituted amido esters. Visible-light irradiation promotes single-electron transfer, generating a diazo-derived carbon-centred radical that triggers a cascade of intramolecular aryl migration. The rational design of starting materials and the cascade technique can be extended to yield isoquinolinedione frameworks that display atropisomerism. Mechanistic investigations, including radical-trapping experiments, EPR studies, Stern-Volmer studies, cyclic voltammetry, and crossover experiments, support a radical-mediated mechanism involving intramolecular aryl radical migration via a spiro intermediate. Isotopic labelling studies suggest that water is the proton source for the PCET process. This mild and metal-free photochemical strategy delivers the products in good yields and showcases the untapped potential of diazo chemistry for radical-based transformations beyond traditional carbene pathways. The synthetic utility of this photochemical methodology is explored in the synthesis of an oxindole scaffold, polycarbocycles and a scale-up process.

papers.title: Choosing lower-end strategies in analytical measurement
papers.abstract: Lower-end analytical claims are often treated as formula-selection problems involving signal-to-noise ratios, σ/S calculations, blank-based estimates, regression residuals, intercept dispersion, or empirical lower-range validation. This framing is incomplete because these routes do not describe the same evidentiary object. This article develops a metrological framework for selecting lower-end strategies by distinguishing reagent blanks, method blanks, zero calibrators, and forced mathematical origins, and by separating baseline noise, blank variability, calibration scatter, intercept instability, heteroscedasticity, non-linearity, matrix effects, and full-method variability. The framework links analytical calibration practice with ICH Q2(R2), ICH M10, FDA bioanalytical validation, EPA method detection limit logic, CLSI EP17, ISO 11843, VIM-compatible terminology, Eurachem validation guidance, and GUM uncertainty propagation. It argues that a detection, quantification, reporting, or decision-facing lower-bound claim is fit for purpose only when the evidence source, variance model, calibration structure, uncertainty statement, and intended analytical use are aligned. Worked examples illustrate an intercept-based detection-limit estimate with uncertainty and an iteratively reweighted least-squares treatment of mixed additive/proportional variance. The proposed framework rejects universal low-end recipes and replaces them with an evidence map: baseline-controlled systems may justify signal-to-noise approaches; blank-dominated procedures require blank or method-blank evidence; heteroscedastic and non-linear systems require explicit variance or precision-profile modelling; and decision-facing reporting generally requires empirical full-method validation. The correct lower-end strategy is the one that matches the actual lower-end problem.

papers.title: Hantavirus ANDV Glycoprotein Gc: Comprehensive Analysis and Molecular Docking of 35 FDA-Approved Antiviral Ligands
papers.abstract: Hantavirus ANDV represents a critical hemorrhagic fever pathogen with 35–40% case fatality rates and no FDA-approved antiviral therapy. This comprehensive computational study systematically evaluates all 35 FDA-approved antiviral compounds through molecular docking against ANDV Glycoprotein Gc to identify optimal therapeutic candidates. A three-tiered quantitative evaluation framework—binding affinity (kcal/mol), contact score (critical residue engagement, 0–6), and disruption score (structural perturbation, 1–9)—was applied to predict clinical viability and genetic barriers to resistance. Molecular docking simulations identified Remdesivir as the optimal lead candidate with -9.1 kcal/mol binding affinity, maximum contact score (5/6), and highest disruption index (9/9). Only 10 of 35 compounds (29%) demonstrated adequate binding affinity (< -7.5 kcal/mol) and genetic barrier for clinical development, stratified into Tier 1 monotherapy candidates (5 compounds) and Tier 1A combination therapy agents (5 compounds). Aromatic residue engagement (tryptophan, tyrosine, phenylalanine) emerged as the dominant binding determinant, with complete aromatic triad engagement yielding 2.53 kcal/mol enhanced affinity relative to absent engagement. In silico evidence suggests Remdesivir as the optimal monotherapy candidate warranting immediate biochemical and cell-based evaluation, while computational data support pairing Remdesivir with Indinavir or Nirmatrelvir for complementary contact profiles and extreme genetic barrier to resistance, candidates that merit priority advancement to preclinical and clinical development. This analysis establishes quantitative scientific frameworks for antiviral compound prioritization, resistance prediction mechanisms, and rational design of combination therapy regimens specific to ANDV Glycoprotein Gc targeting, identifying a focused pipeline of 10 compounds for translational evaluation.

papers.title: Mechanistic Origins of D1 Excited-State Formation in Radical-Based Organic Light-Emitting Diodes
papers.abstract: Radical-based organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) emit from a doublet excited state, D1, enabling spin-allowed radiative decay without the singlet-triplet exciton constraints of closed-shell emitters. However, the charge-mediated pathways by which D1 is populated under electrical excitation remain unclear. Here, we evaluate, by means of quantum-chemical calculations and Marcus-type theoretical modelling, how competing charge-mediated pathways populate the emissive D1 state in three TTMbased radical emitters: TTM-1Cz, TTM-3PCz, and TTM-3NCz. We compare anionmediated, cation-mediated, charge-charge annihilation, and excited-charge pathways within a minimal CBP-host model. The calculated energetics and rates indicate that D1 formation is most consistently associated with anion-mediated charge recombination, D0 → D− S0 → D1, while excited-anion pathways may also contribute indirectly through higher-lying D2 or Q1 states followed by internal conversion. In contrast, cation-mediated routes are generally disfavoured and, undesirable relaxation pathways returning charged species to D0 are kinetically suppressed. Overall, this work provides a mechanistic framework for D1 formation in radical OLED emitters and highlights anion-mediated pathways as the most plausible route to emissive doublet-state population.

papers.title: Using Relative Binding Free Energy Calculations for Rank Ordering of Endocrine Disrupting Compounds to the Human Estrogen Receptor Alpha
papers.abstract: Endocrine disrupting compounds (EDCs) pose an increasing burden on both human and environmental health with computational predictions being considered promising new approach methodologies to improve risk assessment. Molecular docking has found widespread use to study the interaction between environmental pollutants and ligand activated receptors such as the estrogen receptor alpha (ERa). More rigorous approaches, such as alchemical relative binding free energy (RBFE) calculations, on the other hand, are rarely applied. Here, we provide an assessment of the applicability domain of molecular docking as a new approach methodology and compare its performance to RBFE calculations. We show that molecular docking can accurately predict binding poses of EDCs to the human ERa when receptor flexibility is considered. However, we also demonstrate a lack of correlation between the docking scores and experimental measures of affinity and transactivation potency over diverse chemical spaces. As an alternative, RBFE calculations using λ dynamics were tested on a congeneric series of bisphenols, showing a higher sensitivity than molecular docking towards small structural changes between EDCs (Kendall 𝜏 docking = 0.491; 𝜏 RBFE = 0.714). Despite higher computational costs associated with RBFE than docking, our results suggest that RBFE has the potential to facilitate in silico risk assessment.

papers.title: Deuteration of Polyethylene Glycols through Pd/CCatalyzed C(sp3)–H Activation
papers.abstract: Polyethylene glycol is a widely utilized polymer with diverse applications in pharmaceutical and biomedical sciences, owing to its outstanding solubility, excellent biocompatibility, and proven ability to enhance pharmacokinetic profiles. Deuterium labeling of PEG provides a powerful tool for probing drug distribution and metabolic behavior, thereby facilitating the development of advanced diagnostic and therapeutic agents. Despite the pervasive use of PEG, direct methods for its deuterium incorporation have been reported only sparingly. Herein, we report an efficient and practical protocol for the direct deuterium labeling of PEG derivatives employing a readily removable heterogeneous catalyst and inexpensive heavy water as the deuterium source. This strategy offers a cost-effective and operationally straightforward approach and is readily applicable to PEG derivatives bearing terminal, easily deprotectable MOM groups. The present methodology is expected to expand the synthetic versatility of PEG functionalization and underscores the potential of direct deuteration strategies in pharmacological and biomedical research.

papers.title: Nanometric porous mixed nickel-copper oxide aerogels for the ammonia oxidation reaction
papers.abstract: Hydrogen is considered a promising carbon-free energy carrier. However, storage and transport are obstacles thatmake its use challenging in reality. One proposed solution is using ammonia as an indirect hydrogen storage medium, from which hydrogen can be obtained through electrochemical processes. The ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR) is crucial for this application with NiCuOOH having great potential as a PGM-free catalyst. In recent years, aerogels have received attention as a class of materials due to their unique properties, including very high surface area and high porosity. For this reason, they have been increasingly studied as catalysts. Here, nanometric mixedmetal nickel-copper oxide aerogels were synthesized with a modified epoxide route preparation and tested as AOR catalysts. The characterization shows that copper integrates into the nickel oxide structure and that crystallinity increases with rising copper content. The investigations show that copper increases AOR activity to 17 mA cm-2 at 1.8 V (vs. RHE) in 0.1 M KOH and 55 mM NH4Cl solution. It is demonstrated that the pore volume (3.83 cm3 g-1) and Ni to Cu ratio (Ni80Cu20) are decisive factors and predetermine the AOR performance. Due to the unique structure of aerogels, they achieve higher current densities than their powder equivalents.

papers.title: Cross Cyclotrimerization of Arynes
papers.abstract: Controlling the formation and assembly of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) remains a central challenge in molecular materials design. Triphenylenes are important PAH scaffolds, yet direct synthesis from arynes typically affords symmetric products because of uncontrolled aryne reactivity. Here we report an order-controlled [2+2+2] cyclotrimerization that unites three distinct arynes through a preorganized diarylnickelacycle intermediate. Experimental observation of this nickelacycle, supported by DFT calculations, reveals polarity inversion governs sequence control. Readily accessible o-borylaryl triflates serve as dual precursors for electrophilic free arynes and nucleophilic aryne–Ni complexes, enabling convergent assembly. The method tolerates electronically diverse and sterically congested substrates, providing access to C2symmetric and fully unsymmetrical triphenylenes. This strategy establishes a general platform for the programmable synthesis of tailored PAHs for nanographene chemistry and organic electronics.

papers.title: A multiscale benchmark reveals physically shift-dependent generalization in polymer thermal-property prediction
papers.abstract: Polymer machine-learning models often represent materials mainly through repeat-unit strings or monomer graphs, yet thermal-transition properties are governed by coupled chemical, chain-scale, topological, morphological and processing variables. This gap is most consequential during extrapolative deployment, where models must transfer across molecular-weight regimes, branching architectures, crosslinked networks, stereoregularity classes or polymer families rather than interpolate among similar samples. Here we introduce PolyOlefinX, a literature-derived multiscale benchmark for extrapolative prediction of polymer thermal-transition properties. The primary benchmark comprises 2,733 curated melting-temperature records and frozen out-of-distribution protocols spanning random, cluster-level, molecular-weight, branching, crosslinking, tacticity and family-level chemistry shifts. We further extend the framework to crystallization temperature and glass-transition temperature using target-specific robust splits. Across melting-temperature tasks, transferable descriptor scale depends strongly on the physical source of distribution shift: multiscale metadata improves several within-domain and topology-related extrapolation regimes, whereas compact repeat-unit chemistry descriptors transfer more robustly across polymer-family boundaries. The crystallization- and glass-transition-temperature extensions reveal that random and cluster-level generalization can remain feasible while PE/PP-to-PS transfer produces large, robust errors, particularly for crystallization temperature. PolyOlefinX therefore provides a reproducible benchmark and stress-test framework for identifying when polymer machine-learning models transfer, when they fail and which scale of materials information is required under a given physical shift.

papers.title: Integrating Coupled-Cluster Theory within AI Workflows for Accurate Molecular Geometries
papers.abstract: We introduce a hybrid data-driven coupled-cluster framework that enables efficient coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD)-level geometry optimizations through direct prediction of wavefunction parameters. In conventional CCSD, each optimization step requires solving the nonlinear t-amplitude equations and the linear Λ-equations, both scaling as O(N6), making geometry optimizations computationally demanding. ΛDDCC replaces these iterative solvers with neural network predictions of the t and λ amplitudes, thereby removing the dominant computational bottleneck. The model utilizes a physically grounded representation of electron correlation, combining excitation-based descriptors with a molecular orbital framework defined through orbital centroids. This design enables accurate recovery of the coupled-cluster wave function parameters, which in turn yields reliable nuclear gradients throughout the optimization process. Across a diverse set of thermally perturbed geometries and out-of-sample molecules, ΛDDCC reproduces CCSD geometries with near-quantitative agreement, while reducing computational cost by over an order of magnitude. These results establish ΛDDCC as an effective and transferable strategy for accelerating high-level electronic structure calculations, providing a practical route toward routine CCSD-quality geometry optimization in

papers.title: Breaking Equivariance in 3D Molecule Generation
papers.abstract: Equivariant neural networks are commonly embedded in current molecule generators, incorporating inductive biases by design. We found that the utility of these networks depends on the architecture employed, with autoregressive models suffering from a collapse to lower dimensional spaces dependent upon the rank of input vectors used, as described by The Fundamental Theorem of Invariant Theory. We show this through practical examples by sampling the models Pocket2Mol, PocketFlow, and Tensor Field Networks. Subsequently, we recommend other representations and architectures to ensure equivariance by design, or to break symmetry through the addition of noise.

papers.title: Quantifying the impact of grain boundaries on surface morphology and activity of surface sites towards CO2 chemisorption
papers.abstract: Grain boundaries (GBs) introduce unique structural and electronic heterogeneity in metals. These planar defects display undercoordinated atoms, distorted lattices and localized charge variations that profoundly influence catalytic processes. To assess the structural diversity of the surfaces exposed due to the presence of GBs, we developed a methodology that assigns a numerical measure of similarity between different surfaces. Using this framework, we selected eight gold GB structures that represent the most diverse geometries with favorable formation energies. To gauge how active each site is towards chemical reactions, we specifically studied the chemisorption of CO2 on a handful of selected sites and compared with the top site of a Au(111) surface. Neutral Au surfaces do not spontaneously chemisorb CO2, so excess surface charge was systematically applied to probe charge dependent activation. The change in energy difference between the physisorbed and chemisorbed states (∆Epc) as a function of surface charge density was taken as a parameter to probe the activity of the various top sites across the selected surfaces. Interestingly, there are low energy surfaces where some sites are more active than the reference top site of a Au(111) plane while others are less reactive. We further discovered a predictive chemical marker, partial atomic charge on the C atom, that correlates strongly with the ordering of ∆Epc under charge neutral conditions to enable rapid screening of active sites.

papers.title: Navigating Large Chemical Spaces using Graph Theory and Integer Programming
papers.abstract: Navigating and analyzing large chemical spaces is necessary to accelerate the design and discovery of new molecules and chemical processes. In this work, we introduce a computational framework that integrates graph theory and integer programming to enable efficient navigation of large chemical spaces. Our framework represents the chemical space as a graph, wherein nodes represent molecules and edges represent degree of similarity or connectivity based on domain-specific information. Using the graph representation, we identify representative molecules by computing the so-called minimum dominating set (MDS) which, in our context, is the minimum set of molecules that is connected to all other molecules. We present a suite of solution strategies for the MDS problem including heuristic and rigorous integer programming (IP) approaches. We show that these approaches allow us to capture physicochemical properties and domain-specific logic and constraints, facilitating the identification of molecules with target properties. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach by navigating the chemical space of per-and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFAS); this comprises approximately 15,000 molecular structures. We compare our framework against against traditional dimensionality reduction and clustering methods, such as t-SNE and K-means clustering.

papers.title: From T′-Type to Channel Like Anion Ordering: Structure, Thermal Stability, and Magnetic Properties of the Ruddlesden-Popper Oxyfluorides Pr2CuO3F2 and Nd2CuO3F2
papers.abstract: In this contribution we report on the oxyfluorides Pr2CuO3F2 and Nd2CuO3F2. Both compounds are obtained from fluorination of the corresponding oxides Ln2CuO4 (Ln = Pr, Nd) with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) as fluorine source. The oxyfluorides show a monoclinic distorted version of the channel like anion ordered structure of La2NiO3F2 while both precursor oxides crystallize in the 2D-layered T′-type structure. By in situ X-ray diffraction optimized synthesis parameters were obtained and a one-step transition from the oxide to the oxyfluoride was identified. The absence of reaction intermediates is assumed to be related to the square planar coordination of Cu in the oxides, which allows for the direct incorporation of fluorine on the empty apical octahedral positions. Both oxyfluorides are metastable with thermal decomposition above 470 °C as found by additional in situ XRD investigations. From magnetic susceptibility measurements an antiferromagnetic transition with an ordering temperature TN~240 K was derived for both compounds. The presence of a magnetic hysteresis at 5K and 2 K was attributed to the contribution of Pr3+, and Nd3+ moments and further investigated by specific heat measurements. The presented results highlight the importance of an appropriate fluorination reagent for the oxyfluoride formation, as well as the strong influence of anionic substitution on the structural and physical properties of such compounds.

papers.title: Photoelectrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia: Materials, Methods, and Metrics
papers.abstract: Ammonia is a crucial chemical feedstock, and its production is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions. Electrochemical approaches offer greener routes to ammonia synthesis, but direct nitrogen fixation remains highly challenging. An alternative strategy is the reduction of nitrate, a pollutant commonly found in wastewater, into ammonia and related products. When coupled with lightabsorbing materials, this process can be driven photoelectrochemically, enabling modular systems that simultaneously recover waste nitrogen and generate valuable chemicals. In this review, we critically assess the thermodynamic framework underpinning nitrate reduction, clarify reported redox potentials and reaction pathways, examine analytical methodologies for nitrogen product quantification, and summarise the emerging materials and device architectures for (photo)electrocatalytic nitrate reduction. Finally, we provide recommendations to improve experimental standardisation and accelerate progress in the field.

papers.title: Benchmarking the Use of Machine Learning with Multiple Nonspecific Pulsed-Current Ion Selective Electrodes for Multi-Ion Quantification
papers.abstract: The development of low-cost sensors for nitrate and phosphate monitoring in waterways is crucial for improving agricultural practices and mitigating environmental and economic impacts. In this work, we investigate detection of these anions under pulsed current using the combined responses from three nonspecific electrodes made from common membrane support polymers: poly-vinyl acetate (PVA), poly-vinyl chloride (PVC), and poly-acrylonitrile (PAN). We measure the potential vs. time responses in solutions containing individual nitrate, phosphate, and chloride ions, and generate a synthetic dataset for ion mixtures from individual ion responses. We apply tree-based and neural-based machine learning (ML) algorithms to assess the feasibility of multi-ion detection using combined responses from multiple nonspecific electrodes. Our results demonstrate proof of concept for more robust and versatile multi-ion sensors without the need for membrane materials development. However, the approach remains constrained by factors such as manufacturing variability and the effort and cost required to generate sufficiently large training datasets. Under the assumptions of our synthetic dataset, we identify that >1,000 measurements are required to achieve a mean absolute percent error of ~10% from the combined response of three nonspecific electrodes for simultaneous detection of nitrate, phosphate, and chloride. This work establishes example datasets for individual ion sensing and mixed ion responses that can be used by the broader electrochemical sensing community, and highlights both the promise of applying pulsed-current sensing with ML for multi-ion monitoring, and the technological gap in high volume data needed to make this vision a reality.

papers.title: High-throughput, Picosecond Laser Interference-Patterned Doping of Thin Films for Spatially Resolved OER Screening
papers.abstract: The development of efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts requires a detailed understanding of how structural and compositional modifications influence the catalytic performance. Here, we present a high-throughput platform to induce structural and chemical modification in Co3O4 thin films by combining direct laser interference patterning (DLIP) with picosecond-pulsed laser defect engineering in liquids (PUDEL) and spatially resolved electrochemical screening via scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM). This approach enables the generation of spatially varying surface modifications within a single experiment, including controlled film restructuring, defect formation, and compositional changes. Localized measurements reveal that the OER activity is maximized at moderate laser fluence, where film restructuring and compositional changes occur, while excessive fluence leads to ablation and reduced performance. Despite detectable Fe incorporation, activity trends are primarily governed by structural changes of the Co3O4 film. This work establishes DLIP-PUDEL combined with SECCM as a platform for rapid structure–activity correlation and accelerated electrocatalyst development.

papers.title: Identifying Critical Operating Constraints for Soluble Lead Redox Flow Battery Stability: A 25-Cycle Analysis of Charge-Discharge Asymmetry
papers.abstract: The soluble lead redox flow battery (SLRFB) offers a low-cost, membrane-free architecture for grid-scale energy storage, but its short cycle life remains a barrier to deployment. Prior work has shown that high charging current density and electrolyte agitation can extend cyclability to several hundred cycles, and in one report, to 2000 cycles. The relative roles of the charge and discharge half-cycles, however, are not known, leaving open the question of which step should be targeted for further improvement. In this work, we decouple the two by independently varying the applied current density during charging and discharging, with and without electrolyte stirring, using the standard PbMS/MSA electrolyte. Over 25 cycles, stable and reproducible operation is found to require a strict dual condition: stirring combined with high current density during both half-cycles. Symmetric highrate operation in unstirred cells holds charge efficiency near 90% for about 10 cycles before drifting; asymmetric high–low combinations degrade rapidly and lose reproducibility, indicating that deposit formation and dissolution are jointly sensitive to reaction rate and electrolyte transport. We also define the potential recovery capacity, WR, a scalar that relates cyclic discharge capacity to the twostep recharging potential profile and tracks the onset of degradation.

papers.title: β-Citronellol as a Sustainable Additive for Mechanochemical Suzuki-Miyaura Cross-Coupling Reactions
papers.abstract: Mechanochemistry has emerged as a more sustainable and facile synthetic platform for solvent-free transition metal-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions. Here, the discovery of β-citronellol as a sustainable additive for liquid assisted grinding is reported. It is found that β-citronellol enables the mechanochemical cross-coupling reactions of various aryl halides and aryl boronic acids in moderate to excellent yields under ambient conditions without phosphine ligands or the application of external heating. Additionally, the reaction is found to proceed with heteroaryl boronic acids on the gram-scale, and it is applicable towards the synthesis of functional organic compounds with extended π-conjugation.

papers.title: Identification of Metal-Organic Frameworks for CO2 Capture from Humid Flue Gas: Integrating Molecular Simulation, Machine Learning, and Experimental Synthesis
papers.abstract: Increasing global CO2 emissions are driving efforts to develop advanced carbon capture materials.
