papers.abstract: Understanding the impact of biomass burning, including wildfires, on air quality requires accurate quantification of associated surface-level pollution, which is often underpredicted due to chemical aging and variable confounding sources. Using methodology that incorporates decades of aerosol spectroscopy and isolates biomass burning across wood combustion types and fire sizes, we find that biomass burning contributes over 40% of organic 5 particulate matter across a majority of 43 measurement sites in the Northeastern U.S. We differentiate substantial contributions from wildfires, prescribed burns, and other anthropogenic activities, while finding that half of smoke originates from minor events that often go undetected. With biomass burning comprising an increasing fraction of pollution, transferable approaches to routinely estimate its impacts are critical to informing science and policy in a changing world.

papers.title: ChemCorr: A Unified Framework for Molecular Property Prediction and Chemical Knowledge Graph Reasoning via Correlation-Aware Pre-training
papers.abstract: The intersection of deep learning and chemistry has opened new avenues for molecular property prediction, reaction outcome forecasting, and chemical knowledge graph reasoning. However, existing approaches treat these tasks in isolation, failing to exploit the synergistic relationships between molecular structure representations, reaction pathway dependencies, and crosslingual chemical knowledge. In this paper, we propose ChemCorr, a unified framework that integrates four synergistic modules: (1) a Correlation-Aware Molecular Pre-training (CAMP) module that explicitly learns structure-property correlations through contrastive pre-training objectives, bridging the gap between molecular graph encodings and property profiles; (2) a Chemical Reaction Pathway Reasoning (CRPR) module that models causal and temporal dependencies in multi-step chemical reactions via temporal attention mechanisms; (3) a Cross-modal Chemical KGQA (CCKQA) module that enables zero-shot cross-lingual question answering over chemical knowledge graphs through language-agnostic entity alignment; and (4) a Fine-grained Molecular Retrieval (FGMR) module that preserves substructural relevance signals through token-level knowledge distillation. Evaluated on four diverse benchmarks, including MoleculeNet for property prediction, USPTO-50k for reaction prediction, ChEBI-KGQA for knowledge graph question answering, and ChemPatent-Retrieval for literature retrieval, ChemCorr achieves state-ofthe-art performance across all tasks. Notably, it improves reaction prediction accuracy by 3.3% and KGQA Hits@1 by 3.8% over the strongest baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of correlation-aware pre-training and the complementary benefits of joint optimization across chemical AI tasks.

papers.title: Practical computational exploration of chemical reaction space: Assessing the chemical stability of active pharmaceutical ingredients under acidic conditions
papers.abstract: Understanding the chemical degradation of active pharmaceutical ingredients is critical for formulation development and regulatory compliance, yet existing computational tools either rely on predefined reaction rules that limit their ability to discover unanticipated pathways, or lack the ability to distinguish energetically accessible products from all formally possible ones. Here we present an automated workflow that requires no predefined reaction rules and explores degradation reaction networks directly from the potential energy surface. The approach combines semiempirical metadynamics for reaction discovery, systematic energy-and count-based filtering, density functional theory refinement, and microkinetic modelling to calculate time-and temperature-dependent product distributions. Applied to the acid-catalysed degradation of BMS-644950, the workflow constructs a reaction network of 1720 species and 2471 elementary steps, reduced by filtering to eight candidate degradation products. From this reduced network, microkinetic simulations correctly identify the two experimentally observed lactone products as the dominant species and propose a tentative structure to a previously uncharacterised 466 Da impurity.(R. Hemingway et al., Organic process research & development 2024, 28, 674–692) The calculations further reveal that several thermodynamically favourable products remain unobserved because activation barriers of 36–40 kcal mol−1 render them kinetically inaccessible on the experimental timescale, a distinction that reaction-rule-based methods cannot make. The complete exploration finishes within three days on a compute cluster, demonstrating that automated, physics-based degradation modelling is now tractable for drug-like molecules at industrially relevant scales and can be extended to other stress conditions.

papers.title: Electrochemical Performance of Electrodeposited Carbon at various Current Densities as Anode Material for Lithium-ion Batteries (LIBs)
papers.abstract: Electrolytic reduction of molten carbonates (Li/K/Na) has been suggested as an effective approach improving the performance of lithium-ion batteries as anode material. However, the generation of specific carbon phases still poses a challenge, and this area needs more exploration. Herein, novel carbonaceous materials were synthesized by using molten carbonates as exciting new method of producing tuned carbons for battery applications. The electrochemical properties as measured using galvanostatic charge-discharge, cycle ability, rate performance, cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy were observed to be greatly enhanced by using the carbonate-derived anode as compared to the commercial graphite. The modified carbon anode material exhibits superior initial discharge capacity of 359 mAh g-1 at 0.1 C with coulombic efficiency of 95.70% and 279 mAh g-1 at 1 C with capacity retention (coulombic efficiency) of 85.8% (100%) after 100 cycles in the potential window of 0.01-2 V (vs Li/Li+). In comparison commercially available graphite exhibit only 350 mAh g-1 at 0.1 C, corresponding to lower first coulombic efficiency of 89.26% and 191 mAh g-1 at 1 C with capacity retention (coulombic efficiency) of 83.8% (94%) after 100 cycles. The great improvement in the de-/lithiation kinetic can be accredited to the enhancement in apparent lithium-ion diffusion coefficient through the electrodeposited carbon material.

papers.title: POT-PISA: Core-Degradable Particles via Aqueous via Radical Ring-Opening Polymerisation-Induced Self-Assembly Using 7-Phenyloxepane-2-Thione
papers.abstract: We report the successful synthesis of novel core-degradable nanoparticles using 7-phenyloxepane-2-thione (POT) via an aqueous radical ring-opening polymerisation-induced self-assembly process. These nanoparticles efficiently degrade in the presence of amines, demonstrating a molar mass reduction of the core by up to 85%.

papers.title: Bi-catalyzed Coupling of C(sp3) with Weakly Coordinating Triflate and Sulfonimide Anions
papers.abstract: In this article we report on the ability of bismuth to catalyze the coupling between C(sp 3 ) centers and weakly coordinating anions such as triflates and sulfonimides. The protocol uses cyclopropanols as nucleophiles, which upon β–C cleavage, forge a Bi III homoenolate. Oxidation of these intermediates with 1-fluoro-2,4,6-trimethylpyridinium triflate (NFTPT) or N-fluorobenzenesulfonimide (NFSI) delivers the C(sp 3 )–OTf or C(sp 3 )–NSI, respectively, in high yields. The protocol is characterized by the high nucleofugality of Bi III in catalysis, which manifests the unique redox behavior of Bi in redox catalysis.

papers.title: Sensitized near-infrared luminescence in sulfur-coordinated lanthanide complexes for machine learning-enhanced thermometry
papers.abstract: Lanthanide (Ln3+) coordination complexes featuring only Ln–S bonds have optical properties uniquely modulated by soft donor atoms. Yet, these complexes and their applications are underexplored, due to the stricter environmental control required for their preparation relative to complexes containing Ln–O bonds. Herein, we show that Ln-S coordination is ideally suited to generate information-rich near-infrared (NIR) photoluminescence, laying the optimal ground for machine learning-driven optical sensing. We prepared three new homoleptic complexes with general formula [K(2.2.2-cryptand)][Ln(L)4] (Ln = Nd3+ (1-Nd), Gd3+ (1-Gd), or Yb3+ (1-Yb); L = 2,6-bis-(4-tert-butylphenyl)phenyldithiocarboxylate). In all complexes, the Ln3+ ion is dodecahedrally coordinated to eight sulfur atoms, which exert a moderate, anisotropic ligand field—as unveiled via magnetic measurements and ab initio calculations. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence and optical absorption measurements allowed identifying the electronic transitions and energy transfer mechanisms underpinning the complexes’ optical properties, which are dominated by ligand sensitization of the Ln3+ emission. Survey of the photoluminescence-vs-temperature (calibration) datasets indicated the amenability of 1-Nd and 1-Yb to luminescence thermometry. Chiefly, the complex spectral variations induced by thermal changes can be comprehensively analyzed via Principal Component Analysis, thus extracting global optical features with readout precision that is one order of magnitude higher than classical, local spectral features. More broadly, this study demonstrates that spectral complexity in molecular systems sets the necessary preconditions for advanced optical sensing supported by machine learning algorithms.

papers.title: Defect-Engineered La2Mo2O9@SnO2 Heterostructure Electrodes for Tunable Hybrid Charge Storage
papers.abstract: The rational design of hybrid electrode materials capable of simultaneously enabling fast charge transfer and enhanced redox activity remains a central challenge in electrochemical energy storage. In this work, defect-engineered La2Mo2O9@SnO2 (LMO@SnO2) heterostructures were developed via a hydrothermal route to achieve tunable hybrid charge storage behaviour. Comprehensive structural and surface analyses confirm the formation of phase-coexisting heterointerfaces accompanied by progressive oxygen vacancy generation, increased Mo5+ content, and enhanced surface area (7.2 to 23 m2 g-1), collectively improving electrolyte accessibility and charge transport pathways. Electrochemical investigations reveal a systematic enhancement in performance with increasing SnO2 incorporation, with the optimized LMO@2M SnO2 electrode delivering a high specific capacitance of ~910 F g-1 at 5 A g-1 along with excellent rate capability. Kinetic analysis demonstrates a clear transition from surface-controlled to diffusion-assisted charge storage, confirming the emergence of a hybrid pseudocapacitive mechanism. The champion LMO@2M SnO2 electrode also maintained a stable coulombic efficiency of approximately 95.15% over 2000 cycles after initial activation, confirming good electrochemical reversibility and structural stability. This behaviour is attributed to the synergistic interplay between oxygen-vacancy-induced electronic modulation, Sn–O–Mo interfacial coupling, and mesoporous architecture. These findings establish defect-engineered LMO–SnO2 heterostructures as an effective platform for tailoring charge storage mechanisms and enhancing electrochemical performance in hybrid energy storage systems.

papers.title: Predicting PROTAC Oral Bioavailability with Physics-Based Foundation Model Finetuning
papers.abstract: PROTACs (Proteolysis Targeting Chimeras) are bifunctional degraders that harness the ubiquitin–proteasome system to eliminate disease-relevant proteins. Their large molecular size and inherent beyond-Rule-of-Five properties pose significant challenges to oral bioavailability, and reliable predictive models for intestinal absorption remain elusive. Here, we present a deep learning framework for PROTAC oral bioavailability prediction based on foundation model finetuning of a graph neural network pretrained on diverse ADME endpoints. A key innovation is physics-based multitask finetuning, in which expert-knowledge descriptors including effective polar surface area (ePSA), chromatographic LogD, and quantum mechanically derived radius of gyration and solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) serve as auxiliary tasks, embedding structural priors into the model without compromising virtual screening speed. Benchmarked against score-based approaches (ETR, BBI, AB-MPS) and classical machine learning baselines across cross-validation, temporal, and project-based splits on a dataset of over 200 in-house mouse pharmacokinetic studies, the finetuned foundation model consistently outperformed all alternatives in interpolation and temporal extrapolation settings. Prospective application in active drug discovery projects demonstrated its utility for prioritizing compounds balancing cellular potency with favorable predicted absorption.

papers.title: Light-Driven Control of Polar Order in Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystals
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric nematic (NF) liquid crystals are polar fluids that combine long-range orientational order with spontaneous macroscopic polarization and exceptionally large dielectric permittivity. While these properties make NF materials attractive for responsive soft devices, incorporating additional functionality remains challenging because polar order is highly sensitive to molecular mismatch. Here we introduce a molecular design strategy that enables optical control of NF materials using azobenzene-based mesogens structurally matched to the archetypal NF compound DIO. Two derivatives are themselves ferroelectric nematogens, demonstrating that photoisomerizable mesogens can intrinsically sustain and modulate NF polar order, with large and reversible light-induced changes in polarization and dielectric permittivity. The same structural matching principle also enables non-NF azobenzenes to co-assemble with DIO at concentrations up to 20 wt% while preserving ferroelectric nematic order. In selected blends, light irradiation shifts the transition between ferroelectric nematic and antiferroelectric smectic order, reversibly switching the material between high- and low-permittivity states. Together, light and temperature provide complementary handles to navigate this phase landscape of competing ferroelectric and antiferroelectric order. These results provide a molecular design strategy for programming collective polar order in ferroelectric nematic fluids using light-responsive mesogens.

papers.title: A Replicate-Aware Biophysical Triage Workflow for De-Risking Protein-Ligand Hypotheses Before Experimental Validation
papers.abstract: Computational protein-ligand studies often treat ligand retention during molecular dynamics as evidence of preserved binding quality. This assumption is risky in drug-repurposing and resistance settings, where a ligand may remain pocket-associated while losing canonical contact fidelity, adopting a weakened pose, or showing replicate-dependent behavior. Here, we present a replicate-aware biophysical triage workflow, referred to in this manuscript as Gen2, for de-risking protein-ligand hypotheses before experimental validation. Gen2 uses predefined quality-control and trajectory-adjudication principles to evaluate whether a protein-ligand hypothesis remains structurally interpretable across replicate molecular dynamics simulations. We applied the workflow to two primary benchmark modules. In SARS-CoV-2 main protease, apo 6Y2E served as the ligand-free baseline, 6W63/X77 as a noncovalent positive-control anchor, and 6Y2E-lopinavir as a weak or nonvalidated comparator. X77 showed replicate-supported active-site retention and was accepted as the positive-control anchor, whereas lopinavir remained active-site associated but failed to preserve robust, replicate-consistent canonical late-pose quality. In BCL2-venetoclax systems, WT 6O0K behaved as a preserved positive anchor, F104L 6O0M showed bounded impairment without ligand escape, and G101V 6O0L showed replicate-asymmetric resistance-linked perturbation of neighboring groove contacts rather than direct G101 contact loss. Across both systems, ligand retention and binding-quality preservation were separable outcomes. The two modules were selected as orthogonal stress tests of the same methodological problem, not as evidence that the workflow is a universal potency or clinical-response predictor. Gen2 is not an affinity predictor, potency predictor, clinical-resistance model, or replacement for biochemical or cellular validation. Its intended role is to classify computational protein-ligand hypotheses as preserved, weakened, asymmetric, nonideal, setup-limited, or unsuitable for prioritized experimental escalation.

papers.title: Simple Preparation of Polysubstituted Tetrahydropyranes: Study of the Stereoselective Intramolecular Proton Transfer to Enol Ethers
papers.abstract: Polysubstituted tetrahydropyrans (THPs) have been prepared from hydroxy-enol ethers using an original, simple one-pot protocol with silicon-based reagents and BF3•Et 2 O. The mechanistic study revealed that, under the optimized reaction conditions, suitably substituted gamma-hydroxy-2,2disubstituted enol ethers undergo diastereoselective, intramolecular proton transfer, allowing for the cyclisation-functionalisation sequence to take place with high levels of diastereocontrol for the two newly formed stereogenic centres. The optimized conditions were applied to a scope of gamma-hydroxy enol ethers giving the expected polysubstituted tetrahydropyrans with good to high yields. A sequential, one-pot version of this reaction using sub-stoichiometric amounts of a combination of two Lewis acids is also described.

papers.title: Recovery and Characterization of Industrial grade d-Limonene from Waste Tire Pyrolysis Oil for Sustainable Coating Applications
papers.abstract: The growing accumulation of end-of-life tires represents a significant environmental challenge due to limited sustainable disposal and recycling pathways. Tire pyrolysis has emerged as a promising thermochemical conversion strategy for transforming waste tires into valuable products, including pyrolysis oil, gas, char, and high-value chemicals such as d-limonene. As a renewable terpene with wide industrial applications in polymers, coatings, solvents, adhesives, fragrances, and printing inks, d-limonene recovery from waste-derived streams offers strong potential for circular economy integration. In this study, high-purity d-limonene was recovered from waste tire pyrolysis oil using a scalable purification route involving fractional distillation followed by solvent-based purification. The effect of pyrolysis temperature on d-limonene yield was systematically evaluated, with optimal recovery observed at moderate temperatures of 450–500 °C, where minimized secondary cracking favored preservation of monoterpenes. The recovered product was characterized using GC–MS, FTIR, and TGA, alongside physicochemical analyses including density, refractive index, boiling point, flash point, appearance, and solubility to assess purity and application suitability. GC–MS analysis confirmed a d-limonene purity of 90–92%, while FTIR spectra verified characteristic terpene functional groups, and thermal analysis indicated acceptable stability for industrial use. The results demonstrate that waste tire pyrolysis can serve as a sustainable and economically viable source of industrial-grade d-limonene. This work demonstrates a simplified scalable purification route combining controlled batch pyrolysis and selective fractionation for producing industrially applicable high-purity d-limonene for polymer coating applications.

papers.title: Operando Electrochemical Fluorescent Microscopy Highlights Local Buffering and Mass Transport Effects in Polymer-Promoted Electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Many environmentally relevant electrocatalytic reactions proceed via proton coupled electron transfer (PCET) mechanisms, which are not only dependent on highly active surface catalysts, but also on favorable local pH conditions. To that end, protic polymer coatings have been reported to promote PCET-reactions. However, they modulate the local reaction environment in numerous ways obscuring meaningful conclusions on the origin of this promotion. To deconvolute the effect of local pH in protic polymer-coatings from other contributions we developed a method for operando determination of in-polymer pH values using electrochemical fluorescence microscopy. Polyethylene imine (PEI) was equipped with a fluorescent pH probe, coated on polycrystalline gold and electrochemical hydrogen evolution was applied as a pH-sensitive model reaction. Temporal changes of the average pH values throughout the whole thickness of the polymer film were quantified by widefield microscopy, while the spatial distribution of pH-profiles within the films were determined by confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). Complementing the experimental results with finite-element modeling identified two polymer induced effects: i) local differences in the mass transport of the proton donors and ii) a pronounced local buffering by the highly concentrated ammonium groups inside the polymer-coating. The latter was corroborated by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV): While the buffering PEI-coating decreased the onset potential of hydrogen evolution, a control polymer (polyvinyl alcohol), which cannot be deprotonated in the aqueous pH-window, did not promote electrocatalysis. These findings highlight the operando pH-modulation by protic polymer coatings and understanding this phenomenon will be crucial for rational design of polymer-coatings for PCET-reactions.

papers.title: Data-Driven Discovery of Structure–Reactivity Relationships in Oxidative Addition at Zerovalent Nickel Centers
papers.abstract: Understanding the factors that control CO2 insertion into Ni–alkyne complexes is essential for improving the regioselectivity of Ni-catalyzed reductive carboxylation reactions. Here, we combine highperformance computing, experimental validation, and interpretable machine learning to identify structurereactivity relationships governing oxidative cyclization of CO2 at zerovalent bipyridine–Ni–alkyne complexes. The MACE machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) was used to generate a large thermochemical dataset of optimized Ni–alkyne reactants and Type I/Type II nickelacycle products, enabling systematic analysis of reaction Gibbs free energies and regioisomer stability across a broad ligandsubstrate space. Experimental IR spectra of representative Ni–alkyne complexes confirmed key structural assignments but also revealed that MACE-optimized geometries underestimate Ni-to-alkyne πbackbonding, leading to systematically blue-shifted alkyne stretching frequencies relative to experiment and DFT. Despite this limitation, MACE-derived relative free energies provided useful thermodynamic descriptors for product regioselectivity when CO2 insertion was experimentally observed. Equivariant graph neural networks predicted reaction free energies directly from reactant geometries with high accuracy, while GNNExplainer localized the dominant structural information to the Ni–alkyne fragment and nearby alkyne substituents. Complementary random-forest models showed that overall CO2-insertion thermodynamics are governed primarily by alkyne sterics, Ni-center accessibility, and product nickelacycle stabilization, whereas regioselectivity is controlled mainly by product-side descriptors associated with the relative stability of the Type I and Type II nickelacycles. These results establish a scalable, experimentally anchored workflow for using MLIP-generated datasets and interpretable machine learning to discover chemically meaningful design rules in organometallic CO2-functionalization chemistry.

papers.title: Computational Framework for Discovering Mixtures of Green Solvents for Liquid-Liquid Separations
papers.abstract: Solvent selection is a critical step in the design of liquid-phase chemical processes that impacts process sustainability and profitability. Solvent selection is challenging because it requires evaluation of multiple behaviors, including phase behavior, solubility, and sustainability. Solvents are also often incorporated as mixtures, substantially increasing the size of the solvent design space and motivating the development of computational methods to minimize experimental screening. In this work, we present a computational framework to address the challenge of selecting solvent mixtures comprised of sustainable, non-toxic solvents for the liquid-phase separation of lignin-derived products, which is particularly challenging due to the similar physicochemical properties of these species. We train a machine-learning model to predict the partition coefficient, log 10 K P , of a solute as a thermodynamic descriptor of preferential partitioning between two immiscible liquid phases formed in a solvent mixture. By representing solvent mixture properties using Hansen solubility parameters and incorporating simple solute descriptors, we show the capability of this model to accurately predict log10KP values for a range of chemically similar lignin-derived solutes obtained from two distinct experimental datasets in the literature. We then combine log 10 K P predictions with the computational evaluation of phase behavior and solvent sustainability to screen solvents for two case studies: replacing halogenated solvent mixtures with green alternatives and identifying solvent mixtures suitable for separating lignin products via centrifugal partition chromatography. The proposed data-driven computational tools can (1) accelerate the discovery of green solvent mixtures and (2) promote sustainable lignin valorization by identifying solvent mixtures for separating lignin-derived products.

papers.title: Ion Transfer at a Paper-Based Liquid-Liquid Interface
papers.abstract: Electrochemical studies of the interface between two immiscible liquids (ITIES) are gaining increasing importance due to the biomimetic nature of ion transfer processes and their broad potential for analytical applications. Despite their numerous advantages, classical ITIES systems exhibit significant limitations, primarily due to the low mechanical stability of the phase boundary and the use of toxic, poorly conducting organic solvents. In response to these challenges, we have developed a compact ITIES system based on a paper, in which the paper serves as a carrier for both liquid phases. The porous structure of cellulose stabilizes the solutions and enables controlled liquid transport. Furthermore, the incorporation of an organogel results in a more stable and miniaturizable phase boundary with well-defined geometry, leading to high repeatability in electrochemical measurements. This platform presents a promising solution for low-cost, single-use analytical systems based on ITIES electrochemistry, making it suitable for point-of-need applications and compatible with portable potentiostats.

papers.title: Condition-aware prediction of copolymer architecture
papers.abstract: The architecture of a copolymer determines how the material behaves. Designing a polymer for a target property, therefore, should begin with designing for a target architecture. Yet no method predicts the architecture a given monomer pair will react to under given conditions. Even though reactivity ratios have been known since Mayo and Lewis to depend on solvent, temperature, and polymerization mechanism, every predictive approach, from the Q–e scheme of Alfrey and Price to recent machine-learning models, takes monomer structure alone as input. Measurements for thousands of monomer pairs exist but are scattered across eight decades of literature, much of it predating machine-readable publishing and surviving only as scanned page images. We address this gap with PolyCARP, a classifier that predicts copolymer architecture from monomer pair and reaction conditions before any synthesis, trained on a database we extracted from the literature. A vision–language-model pipeline parses 1,206 publications, yielding 3,791 copolymerizations annotated with reactivity ratios, solvent, temperature, and polymerization mechanism. This, to our knowledge, is the first dataset at this scale to record reaction conditions per entry. For any monomer pair and set of conditions, PolyCARP returns an architecture class and the nearest experimental analogues in the database. We validate the tool against a literature case study, where it captures solvent-driven architectural transitions, and against three prospective laboratory copolymerizations. The database, model, and code are openly released—enabling the community to extend both data and models, and to make more of polymer chemistry predictable.

papers.title: Influence of Non-Polar Amino Acids on the Phase Transitions of Atmospheric Aerosol Particles
papers.abstract: The fate of aerosol particles in the atmosphere depends in part on their composition, morphology, and phase transitions. Studies of aerosol phase transitions have focused on aerosol particles with organic compounds consisting of C, H, and O atoms, although a substantial fraction of organic compounds contain heteroatoms such as sulfur and nitrogen. In this study, non-polar amino acids were used to study the effect of organonitrogen compounds on the phase transitions of droplets using optical microscopy. The ternary internal mixtures used were composed of ammonium sulfate (AS), a non-polar amino acid, and either 2-methylglutaric acid (2MGA) or 1,2,6-hexanetriol (126HT) (model oxidized organic compounds). The morphology, phase transitions, and spatially resolved chemical composition were characterized using optical and Raman microscopies. A suppression of the separation relative humidity was observed when the concentration of amino acid was more than 50% of the organic compound by weight. For some systems, the amino acid crystallizes, while the oxidized organic compounds and ammonium sulfate undergo liquid-liquid phase separation, yielding a three-phase system. Trends in the efflorescence relative humidity depend on the solubility of the amino acid. These studies are important in understanding the impact of organic-organic interactions as well as organonitrogen compounds on the phase transitions of aerosol particles, which have consequences for heterogeneous chemistry and cloud droplet nucleation in the atmosphere.

papers.title: Very Short Single-Acceptor Hydrogen Bonding in Liquid Chlorosulfonic Acid Enables Long Chain Formation
papers.abstract: Chlorosulfonic acid is a superacid widely used as a sulfonating and chlorosulfonating agent. Here, we have used total neutron and X-ray scattering to understand its intra- and intermolecular structure, and interactions in the liquid phase. The behaviour is dominated by very short hydrogen bonds between the hydroxyl groups and the sulfonyl oxygens (H···Ooxo 1.43 Å and 1.66 Å), comparable in length to intramolecular hydrogen bonds with the resulting coordination number of 0.96 of sulfonyl oxygen around hydrogen below 2 Å. The hydrogen bonding leads to formation of branched head-to-tail chains and the intramolecular structure distorts to give three near-equal S-O bond lengths, consistent with the superacid’s low viscosity and high acidity.

papers.title: An enzymology oriented protein virtual screening software - WhatCat
papers.abstract: To advance the goal of rational protein design, we have developed the software WhatCat, that has the ability to fully automatically run and analyze molecular dynamics and metadynamics trajectories. Catalytic proficiency of enzymes and its origin can be assessed using electric field strength and residue-wise decomposition, both of which are GPU accelerated and use a polarizable forcefield for a higher accuracy. All software functionality is accessible through a command line interface that is suitable for non-expert users, as well as a Python API allowing for scripting. Future work will aim to integrate additional physics-based modelling, bioinformatics and machine learning techniques under the WhatCat umbrella to allow for a wider range of computational workflows for aiding protein design.

papers.title: Metal-Free trifluoromethylation of indolizines through an electron Donor–Acceptor complex
papers.abstract: Indolizine scaffolds have attracted considerable interest owing to their broad potential in medicinal chemistry. In this work, we describe an original strategy for functionalizing the C-3 position of the indolizine core through a light-mediated three-component trifluoroalkylation reaction. This approach eliminates the need for a photocatalyst, enabling reactions to be conducted under milder and more environmentally friendly conditions than conventional trifluoroalkylation methods. Based on mechanistic investigations, we propose that the reaction proceeds via the in situ formation of an electron donor-acceptor (EDA) complex. The successful incorporation of a wide range of substituents at the C-3 position demonstrates the versatility and robustness of the developed protocol, enabling the synthesis of 20 trifluoromethylindolizine derivatives with yields up to 82%. Overall, this methodology simplifies access to C-3 functionalized indolizines and facilitates the exploration of new structures of potential biological interest.

papers.title: 4D printing of multi-state pH-responsive microstructures
papers.abstract: Deep eutectic systems (DESs) are emerging as highly versatile functional materials for 3D printing, particularly in multiphoton 3D laser printing (MPLP), a powerful technique for the fabrication of complex microstructures with high spatial resolution. Here, we present a versatile strategy for the fabrication of multi-state pH-responsive microactuators based on polymerizable DESs using MPLP. By incorporating vinyl phosphonic acid and vinyl imidazole as functional monomers, respectively, we establish two actively responsive DESs that exhibit antagonistic swelling behavior across the pH range while maintaining excellent printability. The printed 3D microstructures show pronounced and reversible pH-responsive actuation with high cycling stability. Combining both materials within single architectures enables multi-state and bidirectional actuation beyond conventional bilayer systems. Complex actuator geometries further demonstrate the versatility of the platform. A hyperelastic theory implemented in a finite element framework can predict the experimentally observed actuation patterns. These results highlight the potential of polymerizable DESs as a new material platform for advanced microscale soft robotic, sensing, and adaptive systems.

papers.title: Modular Synthesis of γ-Chloro Ketones through Carbochlorination of Olefins Mediated by Copper(I) Photoredox Catalysis
papers.abstract: γ-Chloro ketones are multifunctional synthons that serve as versatile linchpins for the rapid assembly of molecular complexity. Despite this strategic value, their broader adoption remains conspicuously limited as a consequence of the intrinsic challenges associated with their preparation. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven, copper-catalyzed carbochlorination of olefins that provides γ-chloro ketones from readily available α-chloro analogues. The resulting products engage as versatile building blocks, enabling direct access to a range of heterocycles, (spiro-)cyclopropanes, and γ-functionalized ketones. A key feature of this transformation is the use of heteroleptic Cu(I) photocatalysts, which combine strong reducing power in the excited state with ligand exchange processes that enable terminal bond formation at the copper center. This duality enables reactivity that is not readily accessed with common organic or iridium-based photocatalysts. Mechanistic studies support the involvement of two active photocatalytic species that together enable the challenging access to α-keto radicals from α-chloro ketones. They further underscore the role of the dmp ligand in stabilizing Cu(II) intermediates, thereby facilitating carbon–chlorine bond formation. This simple and efficient methodology provides expedient access to multifunctional building blocks, set up for downstream diversification.

papers.title: Bioorthogonal tools for ethanolamine lipids and protein conjugates
papers.abstract: Phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) is the second most abundant class of phospholipids in eukaryotic membranes, as well as a precursor for essential post-translational protein modifications, such as PE conjugates of ubiquitin and ATG8/LC3 that play key roles in autophagy, and glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchors of numerous cell surface proteins. Bioorthogonal chemistry has revolutionized how phospholipid biosynthesis, transport, and turnover are studied, with clickable metabolic precursors now available for several phospholipid classes. Yet a probe for labeling PE and PE-derived protein modifications has not yet been developed. Here, we introduce an alkyne-tagged ethanolamine analog (AlkEA) that is incorporated into PE via the Kennedy pathway and can be derivatized by copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) for visualization and affinity enrichment. Confocal microscopy revealed the subcellular distribution of AlkEA-labeled PE in the ER, Golgi, mitochondria, and autophagosomes, while lipidomic analysis demonstrated AlkEA incorporation across diverse PE species. AlkEA labeling also allowed affinity isolation of PE-conjugated LC3 and ubiquitin, as well as that of a prototypical GPI-anchored protein. AlkEA is thus a minimally perturbing tool broadly applicable to dissecting PE metabolism and PE-dependent protein modifications.

papers.title: Hydrogen-bond Network Reorganization in Liquid Water under Vibrational Strong Coupling
papers.abstract: Water mediates chemical transformation, and energy exchanges through a flexible hydrogen-bond network, while how collective responses emerge from local hydrogen-bond structures remains a fundamental question. Here we show that the molecular ensemble of liquid water is collectively reorganized under vibrational ultra-strong coupling (V-USC) in a Fabry–Perot cavity. Distinct infrared spectroscopic responses of the OH-stretching bands associated with network, intermediate and isolated water reveal an unusual retardation of thermal disordering within the hydrogen-bond network. Significant increases in the population fractions of intermediate and isolated water at elevated temperature indicate a non-conventional redistribution of hydrogen-bonded water configurations under V-USC. Precise tuning of the coupling strength leads to selective narrowing of the upper polariton linewidth towards values comparable to the homogeneous limit of water molecules. Correlation analysis on the independent behavior of population redistribution and linewidth narrowing suggests extended intermolecular correlations in V-USC water beyond those of bulk water. The present findings suggest that vacuum-field-mediated collective interactions can reorganize hydrogen-bond networks even under dark conditions, providing novel insight into the equilibrium and dynamical responses of aqueous molecular ensembles.

papers.title: Shining Light on (Co-)Polyaspartates: A Photoresponsive Alignment Medium with Induced Analyte Reorientation
papers.abstract: Alignment media are highly relevant tools in NMR-based structure elucidation of (organic) molecules, as they enable the measurement of anisotropic observables, such as residual dipolar couplings (RDCs). A major goal, especially for increasingly flexible compounds, is to obtain as much structural information as possible from a single anisotropic sample by applying an external stimulus to change the orientation of the analyte. It is shown herein that light can be used for this purpose if helical (co-)polyaspartates, bearing ortho-fluorinated azobenzenes (FAB) in the polymer sidechain, are applied as alignment medium. In this study, we utilize two FAB-based copolymers as lyotropic liquid crystalline (LLC) phases, which exhibit stable anisotropic environments in both photostationary states (PSS-E, PSS-Z) after irradiation with visible light (violet, green). The photoisomerization induces a change of the FAB-sidechain (geometry, dipole moment). This already leads to a change in analyte orientation, which can be further modulated using temperature as a second stimulus. Furthermore, by proper choice of the polymer composition, the photoinduced inversion of the helical sense of the polymer backbone can be exploited, leading to significantly different interactions with a model analyte. This results in different analyte orientations, which we show to be highly reproducible. This first-ever photoinduced reorientation of an analyte within a single anisotropic sample relying on helix inversion thus represents a pivotal step towards the applicability of multialignment approaches.

papers.title: Feature Selection in Multivariate Linear Regression Models for Data-Efficient Reaction Optimization
papers.abstract: We introduce NaviCat ReaFS (reaction feature selection), a framework for testing and supporting multivariate linear regression models for reaction optimization in small, heterogeneous datasets, where overfitting risk is high and additional experiments are costly. ReaFS combines systematic benchmarking of feature selection methods with targeted diagnostics spanning data, feature-subsets, and predictions. We also introduce a composite score that captures complementary aspects of extrapolative performance, namely candidate recovery, predictive accuracy, and ranking quality, enabling direct comparison of models and feature selection strategies across homogeneous catalysis datasets. ReaFS further integrates cross-validation schemes, data and feature diagnostics, and robustness checks for prospective model assessment. Together, these components provide a practical route to more informed, low-data decisions in reaction optimization.

papers.title: IN SITU FORMATION OF ACTIVE METAL COMPLEXES: SERUM ACTIVATION OF PHOTOSENSITISERS FOR PHOTODYNAMIC THERAPY
papers.abstract: Metal complexes are important tools in biomedicine as therapeutic or diagnostic agents. Yet, inside the organism they can get degraded, loosing efficiency and causing unwanted toxicity. Instead, we want to target metal ions from labile metal pools to attempt forming new metal complexes with biological activity in situ. With this we intend to explore new routes to extend the efficiency of metal-based therapeutic agents and reduce possible toxicity linked to degradation under biological environments. Here we demonstrate our approach by using porphyrin ligands that are capable of binding to serum albumin and get activated with the ions carried by the protein. Newly formed metallo-porphyrins are improved photosensitisers (PS) for photodynamic therapy (PDT), and maintain their anticancer properties better than non-metallated PSs under relevant cell growing conditions.

papers.title: Technical note: On the selection of precooling loops for low-temperature continuous flow chemistry.
papers.abstract: Precooling lines are often used in cryogenic flow chemistry but factors affecting their performance are not well characterised. We present a systematic study on the effects of: flow rate, residence time and internal diameter on the cooling performance of a selection of tubing commonly used in flow chemistry systems, using THF as the solvent. Based on our findings, guidelines for minimum residence times for effective precooling are suggested. The scope and limitations of precooling as a temperature management solution are explored in a series of lithiation reactions on aryl bromides in flow. We surmise that while precooling in flow is important, it is not the only factor relevant in stabilising extremely reactive organolithium species in isolation.

papers.title: MXenes: A Roadmap on Synthesis, Processing, and Applications
papers.abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides whose exceptional compositional, structural, and surface-chemical tunability has driven rapid growth across materials science, chemistry, physics, and engineering. This roadmap consolidates the current state of MXene research, spanning synthesis, processing, fundamental properties, computation, electrochemical energy storage, biomedical applications, electronics, optoelectronics, membranes, sensing, tribology, and extreme-environment technologies. By identifying key advances, persistent challenges, and emerging opportunities, the roadmap provides a forward-looking outlook for guiding MXenes from laboratory discovery toward transformative applications.

papers.title: Ring PEG Synthesis via Bimolecular Ring-Closing Reactions: Selective Preparation of Unimeric Rings via Introduction of Excess Sacrificial Linear Chains
papers.abstract: The efficient preparation of highly pure ring polymers by end-to-end ring-closing reactions of linear precursors remains challenging because the formation of unimeric rings competes with undesired intermolecular coupling to form multimeric products. In this study, we compared two strategies for ring poly(ethylene glycol) (R-PEG) synthesis using linear PEG with a molar mass of 2 kg mol⁻¹ (L-PEG2k): conventional intramolecular ring closing with tosyl chloride (TsCl) and bimolecular ring closing using tetraethylene glycol ditosylate (Ts-TEG-Ts) as a low-molar-mass linker. The cyclized products were purified by α -cyclodextrin ( α -CD) inclusion complexation to selectively remove linear species and were characterized by SEC and MALDI-TOF MS. Under equimolar conditions, both intramolecular and bimolecular ring-closing reactions afforded R-PEG in ca. 30% yield, with similar product distributions consisting of ca. 90% unimeric rings and 10% multimeric rings. In contrast, introducing excess L-PEG2k relative to TsCl or Ts-TEG-Ts suppressed multimeric ring formation, and the bimolecular strategy provided a better balance between purified product yield and unimeric-ring enrichment. These results demonstrate that excess L-PEG chains can function as sacrificial linear chains by promoting preferential single-end incorporation of the low-molar-mass linker, while the remaining linear species are removed by α -CD purification. This sacrificial-linear-chain strategy provides a practical route to unimer-enriched R-PEG.

papers.title: Direct Observation and Unambiguous Assignment of 15N–13C Correlations Using SLIC-SABRE Hyperpolarization
papers.abstract: Direct observation of heteronuclear correlations by conventional thermal NMR is often limited by low sensitivity. Signal amplification by reversible exchange with spinlock induced crossing pulses (SLIC-SABRE), a parahydrogen-based hyperpolarization method operating at low field without magnetic shielding, provides a simple and accessible route for enhancing the sensitivity of 13C and 15N nuclei. Here, we show that SLIC-SABRE enables direct observation of 15N–13C spin correlations at natural 13C abundance (1.1%), with resolved 15N–13C J–couplings and measurable 13C-induced isotope shifts of 15N resonances. Combining two-dimensional 15N-detected spectroscopy with complementary one-dimensional 13C-detected experiments enables unambiguous assignment of individual 15N–13C connectivities and access to site-specific coupling information. The approach is demonstrated for 15N-labeled metronidazole and a selenadiazole derivative containing multiple 15N–13C pairs, with heteronuclear 2D correlation spectra acquired within 40 min. These results highlight hyperpolarized 15N–13C correlation spectroscopy as a route to rapid access to heteronuclear connectivities, coupling constants, and local structural information in nitrogen-containing compounds.

papers.title: Zn-ion hybrid capacitor cyclic stability enhancement via Zn-nitride coating
papers.abstract: By depositing zinc nitride on bare Zn, the present study showcases that nitride coating suppresses the insulating oxide/hydroxide layer formation, controls the growth of Zn nucleation and forms a uniform network of Zn nanostructures. Hence, an aqueous zinc-ion hybrid micro-capacitor delivers better charge-storage performance and long lifespan with capacitance retention of 110% after 10000 cycles. Corresponding author email: subrata.ghoshk@rediffmail.com or subrata.ghosh@upes.ac.in (S.G.) and carlo.casari@polimi.it (C.S.C.)

papers.title: Investigating the Effects of Surface Chemistry and Pore Structure in Grafted PEM Fuel Cell Catalyst Layers
papers.abstract: The carbon support surface chemistry strongly influences ionomer interactions, water management, and electrochemical performance in polymer electrolyte fuel cell catalyst layers; however, studies that decouple these effects from Pt particle size remain limited. Here, diazonium grafting is applied to commercial 40 wt% Pt/Vulcan and Pt/Ketjenblack catalysts to introduce five aryl functionalities (–NO 2 ,–NH 2 ,–CF 3 ,–COOH,–SO 3 H) spanning a wide range of polarities and wettabilities without altering Pt dispersion. Ex-situ characterization (x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, N 2 physisorption, contact angle, and dynamic vapor sorption) confirms successful functionalization and shows that grafting on Ketjenblack occurs preferentially at external surfaces, reducing pore accessibility. In 5 cm 2 single-cell tests, nitrogen-containing functionalities reduce cathode proton transport resistance, increasing current density at 0.7 V (1.20 vs 1.01 A cm -2 , I/C=0.6). For hydrophilic and hydrophobic groups, optimal performance depends strongly on the ionomer-to-carbon ratio: hydrophilic functionalities enhance performance at low I/C (0.1) but become detrimental at higher I/C (0.6) due to increased water retention and unfavorable ionomer interactions. These effects are amplified for porous Ketjenblack, where pore blockage offsets gains from surface modification. These findings establish that surface functionalization and support porosity cannot be optimized independently, and suggest that next-generation mesoporous carbon supports could incorporate pore architectures compatible with surface modification.

papers.title: Toward On-the-Fly Prediction of Reaction Energetics for High-Throughput Screening
papers.abstract: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict reaction properties such as barrier heights, reaction energies, rates, or yields, as well as the underlying molecular geometries, including transition state structures. While such predictions have the potential to provide mechanistic insight for high-impact applications such as synthesis planning and reaction optimization, the field remains at an early stage of development. This Perspective discusses and critically assesses the current state-of-the art in (organic) reaction property prediction, highlighting the key limitations related to data availability and quality, molecular and transformation representations, and machine learning architectures used in both predictive and generative models. A special focus is given on current challenges and on possible paths forward toward efficient and accurate machine learning models for on-the-fly prediction of reaction energetics.

papers.title: Experimentally Mapping the Molecular Pathways and Intermolecular Forces that Drive Elasticity in Flexible Crystals
papers.abstract: Elastically flexible molecular crystals are an emerging class of advanced materials, driving innovation in fields ranging from electronics to medicinal applications. At the fundamental level, bulk material elasticity is governed by the nature of the intermolecular forces found in the material, which are not directly probed using structural (crystallographic) measurements. Low-frequency vibrational spectroscopy, on the other hand, directly interrogates these interactions, and is applied here to directly measure strain in the intermolecular coordinate in mechanically-bent crystals of copper (II) acetylacetonate (Cu(acac)2). This represents the first instance of a direct measurement of the modulation of intermolecular forces through bending strain, enabling identification of the particular coordinates involved in bulk elastic phenomena without the need for large-scale instrumentation such as synchrotrons. From such observations, it is possible to derive a thermodynamic picture of the forces that govern elastic crystals, which highlights the delicate interplay between stabilizing and destabilizing interactions within the material that promote the elastic phenomena in these crystals.

papers.title: Elucidating Structural and Activity Differences Between Tautomerases cis-CaaD and Cg10062: Implications For 3-Hydroxypropionic Acid Production from Acetylenecarboxylic Acid
papers.abstract: In efforts to reduce harmful greenhouse gasses such as methane (CH 4 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), we look to acetylenecarboxylic acid (ACA). ACA may be derived from CH 4 and CO 2 and converted into high priority target chemicals, such as 3-hydroxypropionic acid which is being targeted to be produced through biocatalytic methods over petroleum-derived, which are non-renewable, produces environmental pollution, and non-sustainable. Here we evaluate the tautomerase enzyme cis -CaaD and its almost exclusive conversion of ACA to intermediate product malonate semialdehyde (MSA) which can further be enzymatically converted to high priority target chemicals. We also compare cis -CaaD to the previously evaluated tautomerase Cg10062 which has 54% similarity yet in its native form does not afford primarily MSA (15% product formation) but rather follows a decarboxylation pathway to produce acetaldehyde (ACH, 85% product formation). Although cis -CaaD produces predominantly MSA, Cg10062 is more catalytically efficient. Through trapping of intermediates in atomic resolution crystal structures we are able to gain a better understanding of the covalent mechanism of cis - CaaD. Structural evaluation of cis -CaaD and Cg10062 variants gives rationale for different product profiles. By evaluating atomic interaction between active site residues, subtle positional changes of residue 114 in Cg10062 versus cis -CaaD lead to either hydration or hydration and decarboxylation. Additionally, structural evaluations of cis -CaaD and Cg10062 chimeras illustrate the C- terminal's necessity in activity by coordination of Arg70 into the active site. This further understanding of cis- CaaD and Cg10062 will enable better bioconversion of ACA to high value chemicals.

papers.title: Spin-polarized oxygen evolution catalysis enabled by a honeycomb quantum magnet
papers.abstract: The spin state of electrocatalysts has recently emerged as a critical factor governing the kinetics of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we demonstrate that intrinsic spin polarization, enabled by magnetic anisotropy in frustrated quantum magnets, can drive highly efficient OER without external magnetic fields. Using the honeycomb cobaltate series Na2Co2–xNixTeO6 (0 ≤ x ≤ 1.0), we systematically modulate spin interactions via chemical substitution while preserving crystal symmetry. Experimental and theoretical analyses show that the parent compound Na2Co2TeO6, a Kitaev-type frustrated antiferromagnet, exhibits a spin-polarized electronic structure in its ground state, which correlates with markedly superior OER performance. Electrochemical measurements reveal a monotonic decline in catalytic activity per active Co atoms with increasing Ni content, with NCTO exhibiting the lowest overpotential of 290 mV, lowest Tafel slope of 40 mV/dev, and highest turnover frequency per active site. Notably, all compositions display enhanced stability potentially attributed to lattice contraction driven by spin–lattice coupling inherent to frustrated magnets. This study identifies quantum magnets as a promising new class of catalytic materials, opening a paradigm shift in spin-based electrocatalyst design.

papers.title: Investigating Interlayer Charge Transport of 2D Lead Halide Perovskites via Constrained Density Functional Theory
papers.abstract: We investigate interlayer charge transport in two-dimensional (2D) lead halide perovskites (LHPs) using constrained density functional theory (CDFT) to compute diabatic couplings of both interlayer electron and hole transfer. We first examine the dependence of the results on various choices within the CDFT methodology and conclude that an increasing amount of exact Hartree-Fock exchange with a larger surface dimension of the supercell improves the overall quality of the results. We then examine the dependence of the electron and hole diabatic couplings on the nature of the organic linker, the interlayer distance, and the crystal structure of the inorganic lattice. Our results show that the electron coupling is smaller than the hole coupling, and that both couplings are sensitive to the layer configurations. Our work provides fundamental insight into the relationship between 2D LHP structure and interlayer charge transport, which can guide future design principles for 2D LHP-based optoelectronics.

papers.title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
papers.abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accounts for more than a quarter of all plastic produced, owing to its exceptional material properties and scalable production. However, pristine PE lacks critical properties, such as adhesion, that are needed for many additional commercial applications. Selective post-polymerization functionalization of PE can impart properties that are absent in the pristine polymer, but global functionalization in a uniform medium perturbs bulk properties. Here, we demonstrate catalytic functionalization of solid PE at a solid–liquid interface. The resulting materials possess enhanced surface properties while maintaining bulk properties, such as melting temperature or tensile strength. The method selectively converts methylene units to ketones with just 0.001 mol% iron catalyst below 80 °C with inexpensive oxidants. PE functionalized at the solid–liquid interface adheres to glass up to 90-fold more strongly than pristine PE and up to 4-fold more strongly than PE functionalized in a uniform medium at a comparable level. We demonstrate that the surface ketones can be modified to enhance adhesive strength further and that the augmented surface properties persist for longer than they do after other unselective functionalizations. Thus, selective C–H bond functionalization at the solid–liquid interface produces materials inaccessible by bulk functionalization methods or by traditional surface oxidations.

papers.title: Identification of small molecules targeting Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA Gyrase through a fragment-based drug discovery strategy
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis remains a serious threat to public health and is the leading infectious cause of death worldwide. The standard treatment of tuberculosis consists of at least four different antimicrobials. It is associated with side effects and a long treatment duration, which can make adherence difficult and increase the risk of drug resistance. Thus, the continuous search for new tuberculosis treatments is essential. Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the main etiological agent of tuberculosis, does not encode topoisomerase IV; DNA gyrase is the sole type II topoisomerase, presumably assuming all functions of this enzyme group. In recent years, fluoroquinolones, such as moxifloxacin, have been considered a therapeutic option for tuberculosis treatment, despite previously reported resistance. Additionally, given the essential role of DNA gyrase in M. tuberculosis, numerous studies have aimed to identify alternative drugs that target this enzyme. Herein, we have applied a fragment-based drug discovery approach to identify and validate lowaffinity compounds that inhibit M. tuberculosis DNA gyrase, thereby providing a starting point for developing potent inhibitors. To that end, we employed a range of biophysical and biochemical techniques to identify at least five compounds that bind to DNA gyrase and disturb its activity. These compounds affect the early steps of the gyrase catalytic cycle and prevent the formation of DNA breaks, likely by blocking conformational changes required for DNA cleavage. The threedimensional structure of M. tuberculosis DNA gyrase in complex with the most potent compound, solved by cryo-electron microscopy, indicates that it binds near the interface between the GyrA and GyrB subunits of gyrase and causes extensive conformational changes in the TOPRIM domain of the GyrB subunit. This work provides insights into the development of a series of compounds with practical applications in tuberculosis treatment that target DNA gyrase via a novel mechanism of action.

papers.title: Actinide Tris(tetramethylcyclopentadienide) Complexes: Bonding and Electronic Structures Across the Isostructural [An(C5Me4H)3] (An = Th, U, Np, Pu, Am) Series
papers.abstract: Understanding how metal–ligand bonding evolves across the actinide series is central to the rational development of separations, nuclear fuel cycle, and waste management strategies, yet systematic experimental studies remain scarce owing to the difficulty of handling transuranium elements. Here we report the synthesis and isolation of [NpIII(Cptet)3] and [PuIII(Cptet)3] (Cptet = {C5Me4H}), which complete a rare isostructural series of trivalent triscyclopentadienide complexes [MIII(Cptet)3] spanning five early actinides (M = Th, U, Np, Pu, Am). Metal–carbon distances from thorium to americium show remarkably little variation, despite the decrease in metal ionic radius across this series, and unlike previously reported lanthanide analogues with similar metal ionic radii, which rules out steric congestion as the cause. Density functional theory and multi-reference ab initio calculations reveal that the 5𝑓 orbitals stabilise and contract markedly across the series, crossing below the ligand π-dominant manifold by americium. Topological analysis of the electron density exposes a polar covalent metal–ligand interaction that peaks around uranium/neptunium. These factors are tensioned across the series, such that covalency-induced bond length shortening is key for early actinides, while for later examples, the ionic bonding precludes bond length contraction due to electron-electron repulsion between the ligands and the non-bonding metal 5𝑓 electrons. UV-Vis-NIR spectroscopy, supported by CASSCF/RASSCF calculations, tracks the spectroscopic consequences of this electronic reorganization. Together, these results provide a self-consistent experimental and computational benchmark for electronic structure evolution across the first half of the actinide series within a single, structurally invariant ligand platform.

papers.title: An Original Biosynthetic Route to 3-Hydroxypropionic Acid
papers.abstract: The β-hydroxycarboxylic acid functionality of 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP) makes it a versatile building block chemical that can be converted to industrially relevant chemicals such as acrylic acid. Optimization of existing routes commonly utilizing glucose or glycerol as feedstocks is the most commonly targeted area of 3-HP research. In this study, 3-HP biosynthesis is demonstrated using a unique and novel carbon feedstock, acetylenecarboxylic acid (ACA), that can be C1-derived. ACA may be derived from methane and carbon dioxide by methane dehydrodimerization and subsequent monocarboxylation. A novel variant of tautomerase enzyme Cg10062 is used for transformation of ACA to malonate semialdehyde (MSA), a 3-HP precursor. Cg10062 activity is coupled with NADPH-dependent dehydrogenase YdfG to afford successful synthesis of 3-HP with cofactor regeneration. The two-step three-enzyme synthesis was demonstrated using as low as 0.001 equivalents of NADPH relative to ACA. A similar system was also demonstrated using soluble NADH-dependent MmsB.

papers.title: Chlorine-Mediated Low-Temperature Solar-Thermally Catalytic PMMA Degradation into Liquid Fuels
papers.abstract: The accumulation of waste plastics (PMMA, PVC, PET, and polyolefins) severely impedes carbon resource cycling. Converting waste polymers into liquid fuels not only mitigates serious environmental pollution but also facilitates the recycling of these valuable carbon-energy carriers. Current industrial catalytic cracking of polymers typically requires reaction temperatures above 400°C, resulting in high energy consumption, difficulties in controlling reaction pathways and product selectivity, and substantial formation of low-value coke residues. Based on a novel chain-activation and cracking strategy, this study achieves low-temperature catalytic degradation of PMMA into liquid fuels via chlorine-mediated solar-thermal catalysis, using dichlorobenzene to generate chlorine radicals (Cl·). With layered FeOCl catalysts under mild conditions (130-150 ℃) and light irradiation (utilizing photo-generated holes), PMMA was successfully converted into alkanes (C 14 -C 20 ). Under optimized conditions, polymer degradation reached 90 ~ 95%, yielding primarily liquid fuels along with chlorinated polypropylene (Cl-PP, 10-20% by mass), and trace amounts of gaseous products (H 2 , CH 4 , CO, CO 2 ). This approach demonstrates broader applicability to other plastics (PVC and PE/PET blend). It effectively overcomes the limitations of conventional high-temperature processes along with superior selectivity, controllability, and clean energy input, offering a promising solution for sustainable carbon resource utilization.

papers.title: Impact of Halogen Anisotropy on the Membrane Permeability of Halogenated Drugs
papers.abstract: Membrane permeability is central to drug absorption and intracellular target engagement, but the contribution of specific noncovalent interactions to passive permeation remains difficult to quantify. While hydrogen bonds (HBs) are known to strongly influence membrane crossing, the role of halogen bonds (XBs) is still poorly understood, despite the widespread use of halogenation in medicinal chemistry. Here, we systematically investigate how explicit modeling of halogen anisotropy through an extra point (EP), used to emulate the σ-hole, affects the permeability of two activated XB probes and six halogenated drugs. Molecular dynamics and umbrella sampling simulations were combined with the inhomogeneous solubility--diffusion model (ISDM) and a PMF-based permeability ranking. Inclusion of the EP had little effect on chlorinated compounds, a modest effect on bromazepam, and a pronounced effect on amiodarone, indicating that the impact of halogen anisotropy is strongly dependent on the strength of the XB donor and on the molecular environment. ISDM reproduced the experimental Caco-2 permeability trends with high accuracy ( r = 0.99 without EP and r = 0.93 with EP), although amiodarone was underestimated when the EP was included, consistent with an excessive stabilization of iodinated molecules in polar environments when using current force field parameters. Beyond permeability coefficients, we analyzed XB/HB formation probabilities and introduced a spatially resolved decomposition of ligand--membrane interaction energies into electrostatic and van der Waals contributions along the membrane insertion coordinate. This atom/group-resolved analysis shows that XBs can stabilize halogenated compounds at the water--lipid interface, but that excessive electrostatic stabilization may also favor interfacial trapping and reduce effective permeability. Overall, our results show that σ-holes do affect membrane permeability, but mainly for strong XB donors, and that their contribution reflects a delicate balance between membrane recognition, desolvation, and hydrophobic partitioning.

papers.title: Interplay of local and long-range structure underpins electrochemical behaviour in disordered rock salt LiNiO2
papers.abstract: Lithium nickel oxide (LiNiO2, LNO) is a promising Co-free cathode but suffers structural degradation at high and low voltages. Here we report the synthesis of a cation-disordered rock-salt LiNiO2 (DRS-LNO; Li:Ni ≈ 1:1) from mechanochemical treatment of layered LNO. Its electrochemical behaviour arises from the interplay between local and average structure: reverse Monte Carlo modelling of total scattering data reveals pronounced Li–Li and Ni–Ni clustering (Warren–Cowley α (NiLi) = 0.054(4)) and expanded Li–O distances, enabling Li diffusion pathways that allow ~70% of Li to participate in long-range transport. This accounts for the unexpectedly high first-cycle charge capacity of 185(9) mAh g -1 at 10 mA g -1 despite the absence of Li excess. The disordered average structure leads to small isotropic volume changes (~2.1%) over large electrochemical windows, also accessing reversible capacity from low-voltage Ni 3+ /Ni 2+ redox at low voltages. Operando total scattering suggests that reversible Ni migration takes place at high delithiation, forming regions of α-NaFeO2-like local order. On discharge, the reduction from Ni 3+ to Ni 2+ is associated with the reversible formation of a secondary phase whose formation can be partially suppressed at higher current densities, with implications in the cycling stability of DRS-LNO. These results show that mechanochemistry can access unique local structural motifs that tune electrochemical behaviour, expanding the design space for next-generation cathodes.

papers.title: Catalysis by a metastable photoswitchable cage
papers.abstract: A visible-light-responsive ligand together with a non-switchable ligand can be assembled into a mixture of molecular cages with palladium(II) ions. When irradiated with 530 nm light, the system converges to form a single product, a metastable, mixed ligand molecular cage. This cage can be reversibly disassembled using 424 nm light, an example of integrative self-sorting controlled by light. The metastable assembly can catalyze both Michael addition and nitroaldol reactions. Importantly, visible light accesses a metastable catalytic state inaccessible under thermodynamic control. We demonstrate that the active assembled species can be switched on and off at will using visible irradiation. The metastable species is the most catalytically active assembly.

papers.title: Mg2+ Catalyzes Nonenzymatic RNA Primer Extension through a Concerted Outer-Sphere Mechanism
papers.abstract: The nonenzymatic replication of the primordial genetic material was an essential stage in the origin of life. One intensively studied model for this process is the template-directed extension of an RNA primer with imidazolium-bridged dinucleotide substrates. This reaction is catalyzed by divalent metal ions such as Mg 2+ , but the mechanism of catalysis remains poorly understood. We have utilized classical molecular dynamics (MD) together with hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) to investigate the catalytic role of Mg 2+ . We used these approaches to compute the free energy landscape along key reaction coordinates, and to quantify the impact of Mg 2+ coordination at each step of the primer extension reaction. The presence of Mg 2+ in the reaction center significantly lowers the pKa of the nucleophilic 3′-OH group and reduces the probability of O2′ attack. Based on the energetics of potential reaction pathways, our results suggest a preferred mechanism in which Mg 2+ becomes outer sphere coordinated to the oxygen of the 3′-hydroxyl group of the extending primer, followed by concerted proton transfer and nucleophilic attack on the phosphate of the incoming nucleotide. Our results demonstrate the dual structural and electronic roles of Mg 2+ in catalysis and provide insights that may inform the search for metal ion chelators that further enhance nonenzymatic primer extension.

papers.title: Transferable Enzyme-Polymer Stickers for Modular Assembly of Single and Multi-analyte Biosensors
Thermally Driven Skyrmion Oscillators in Ferromagnetic Nanoring with Engineered Damping Asymmetry
papers.abstract: Magnetic spin-based nano oscillators are promising candidates for next-generation microwave signal generation due to their performance and compatibility, but current-driven designs suffer from Joule heating and reduce energy efficiency. To overcome these limitations, we propose a thermally driven skyrmion oscillator that eliminates the need for electrical currents. Our design employs a two-half ferromagnetic nanoring with engineered Gilbert damping asymmetry and a tangential temperature gradient that induces a net gradient among the material parameters resulting periodic or non-periodic and annihilation in skyrmion motion. The periodic condition of skyrmion dynamics is considered as spiking signal-based oscillator with ~8.7 MHz oscillations at 15 K/μm-degree TTG on average circumference of 2𝜋 × 400𝑛𝑚 for constant 𝛼1 = 0.005 and 𝛼2 = 0.001. However, for non-periodic conditions or stochastic skyrmion motion, the device produces irregular, unpredictable spike signal outputs. The proposed device is also analyzed with device disorder effects like roughness and defects. The electrical spiking output is considered with footprint of magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) with nanoring through magnetoresistive (MR) effects. The resulting device leverages waste heat, avoids Joule heating, and provides a robust, thermally tunable platform for future energy-efficient spintronic technologies, including neuromorphic computing, probabilistic hardware, and unconventional signal processing damping. By combining TTG with spatially tailored damping, the thermally induced variations in material parameters generate intrinsic Brownian forces that propel the skyrmion in opposite directions across the two halves of the ring, moving from hot to cold in one segment and from cold to hot in the other. The resulting motion produces either periodic or aperiodic oscillations around the nanoring, governed primarily by the ring’s geometry, the degree of damping asymmetry, and the applied TTG. This mechanism eliminates the need for external electrical currents, dramatically reducing energy consumption. Because it relies on temperature as a naturally available and often abundant resource at the nanoscale, it can even utilize waste heat from the system. These features make the concept especially promising for neuromorphic and probabilistic computing. Overall, the proposed approach enables ultra-low-power, thermally tunable oscillators with potential applications in neuromorphic architecture, random number generation, and unconventional signal processing.

papers.title: Rapid Evaluation of Glassy Carbon Electrode Surface with Machine Vision
papers.abstract: Automation of electrochemical methods is crucial to achieve high-throughput experimentation (HTE) and self-driving laboratories (SDLs) for accelerating chemistry and materials engineering on pressing research challenges. Obtaining reproducible and reliable electrochemical results requires frequent monitoring of the experimental apparatus, particularly the surface condition of the electrodes. Here, a rapid surface evaluation method that combines optical macro imaging with machine learning (ML) is investigated. We demonstrated that the degradation of a glassy-carbon (GC) electrode can be quantified using only an optical image. This approach enables easily automatable, non-intrusive, and rapid monitoring of electrode health without significantly increasing the complexity of the experimental setup, while also providing spatially resolved insights into degradation.

papers.title: Threonine enhances activity of bio-friendly alanine-rich antifreeze protein mimetics
papers.abstract: The growth of large ice crystals is a challenge in diverse fields from biomedicine and foods to transportation and building. Current ice recrystallization inhibitors both in commercial and research use require high concentrations or face toxicity challenges. We developed simple peptide-based polymers that mimic the composition and function of natural antifreeze proteins evolved in extremophile organisms. We found that while alanine plays a dominant role in antifreeze activity, threonine residues enhance potency. Threonine-dependent activity enhancement was observed in ice recrystallization assays where crystal size is measured, and in proof-of-concept cryogenic assays where full function of a sensitive biological enzyme was retained over 8 freeze-thaw cycles using only 10 µg/mL of polymer as an additive. Since these simple polypeptides are based entirely on natural amino acids and are economical to prepare, we envision broad applications in any scenario where ice growth must be limited.

papers.title: From reproducibility to comparability in computational photochemistry: lessons from the PhotoChem Explorer prototype
papers.abstract: We present the PhotoChem Explorer (PCE) prototype, a proof-of-concept web-based platform that represents computational photochemistry studies of gas-phase molecules in a structured and queryable form. Rather than treating excited-state dynamics simulations as isolated results reported in heterogeneous formats and across different sources, PCE organizes studies according to their molecular systems, computational workflows, methodological choices, and associated observables, enabling relationships and trends to be explored systematically across studies. In this way, the prototype illustrates how structured data representations could support improved findability, comparison, reproducibility, and reuse in computational photochemistry. At a fundamental level, it demonstrates how excited-state dynamics studies could become part of a more connected and cumulative body of knowledge, potentially enabling new modes of investigation. The prototype exposes practical challenges that must be addressed to realize this vision, including the development of shared representations, workflow descriptions, and their integration into scientific practice. More broadly, PCE is intended as a practice-driven experimentation platform to stimulate discussion and iterative community development of standards and representations for excited-state dynamics studies.

papers.title: Bridging catalytic and semiconductor properties of reducible oxides with operando EPR-detected microwave conductivity
papers.abstract: Oxygen vacancies strongly influence the chemical and physical behaviour of reducible oxides. This work introduces a new framework for understanding their role by linking the semiconductor characteristics of reducible oxides with their catalytic performance. The study employs an original experimental strategy based on operando microwave (MW) conductivity measurements, supported by ex situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and operando XANES and XRD analyses. Three oxide catalysts (CeO 2 , TbO x , and PrO x ) are examined during NH 3 oxidation, where vacancies are generated through lattice oxygen participation following the Mars-van Krevelen mechanism. The results show that the intrinsic p-type conductivity of mixed-valence oxides like TbO x and PrO x enhances NH3 oxidation, compared to n-type semiconductors, such as CeO 2 .
