NH 3 activation by the more oxidized M4+ states (interpreted as holes in the semiconductor picture) and the facile interconversion between M 3+ and M 4+ states (corresponding to hole transport) are identified as key factors governing catalytic activity. Dynamic product formation, associated with the reduction of M 4+ to M 3+ , is further proposed to be linked to the formation of the M 2 O 3 phase with consequent bandgap increase and electron-hole recombination. Overall, this study offers a simple and unifying perspective on the catalytic behaviour of reducible oxides through their semiconductor properties, opening new pathways for catalyst design and interpretation.

papers.title: How does macromolecular crowding affect protein-Ligand association? A multiscale Brownian dynamics simulation approach
papers.abstract: Macromolecular crowding is known to influence the diffusive, binding, kinetic and equilibrium properties of proteins in a range of environments such as occur inside biological cells or in highly concentrated solutions of protein therapeutics. However a quantitative understanding of the effects of macromolecular crowding on the rates of protein-small molecule binding is lacking. Here, we present an adaptive model to simulate the association of two solutes in a macromolecularly crowded environment using Brownian dynamics and to compute the corresponding bimolecular association rate constant. The adaptive model represents interactions with atomistic detail for short-range crowder–noncrowder interactions, while using a coarse-grained approach for long-range crowder–noncrowder interactions and all crowder–crowder interactions. This multi-scale approach is integrated in the Simulation of Diffusional Association (SDA) software for Brownian dynamics simulation of biomolecular diffusion. We applied this model to compute the rates of association for two contrasting protein-small molecule inhibitor complexes in environments varying in macromolecular crowder type and density, and we used Markov State modeling of the encounter trajectories to analyze the binding pathways. The results reveal competing effects: whereas the presence of the crowders can hinder ligand binding by reducing the translational diffusion rates of the solutes and obstructing the protein binding sites, crowders can also enhance the bimolecular association rate by other mechanisms, including channeling and the caging effect.

papers.title: Sequence Scanning Improves Accuracy for Antibody-Antigen and Molecular Glue Ternary Complex Co-Folding
papers.abstract: Accurately modeling biomolecular interactions is crucial for understanding biological function and can accelerate drug discovery efforts. Deep learning based co-folding methods such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2 can successfully predict many different biomolecular complexes. However, these models show lower success rates in predicting antibodyantigen and molecular glue (MG) ternary complexes, two cases of high relevance to pharmaceutical research. Here, we present sequence scanning, a new workflow we tested on Boltz and Protenix that significantly improves accuracy in these domains using systematic constraints to enhance overall sampling diversity. For both use cases we assess the performance of the method on large, diverse benchmark sets. We find improved accuracy of the sequence scanning workflow in predicting antibody-antigen interface contacts and in pose prediction quality for MGs compared to previously published results. We also discuss remaining challenges and potential improvements to the method.

papers.title: Red Light Photoswitching in Discrete Indigo Self-Assemblies
papers.abstract: Indigo dyes are functionalized with aromatic groups, including metal ion binding heterocycles. The photoswitching properties of the dyes in solution show that changing the aromatic groups connected to the indigo core allows for fine-tuning of photoswitching properties. The combination of a di(pyridyl)-functionalized indigo with palladium(II) ions results in the formation of a [Pd2L4]4+ dimer, a [Pd3L6]6+ trimer or a [Pd6L12]12+, depending on solvent and the palladium salt used. Irradiation of the dimeric assembly with red light disassembled the structure as measured by 1H NMR spectroscopy, which reforms within minutes in the dark. Repeated switching cycles confirm robust switching using red light.

papers.title: Do the Core Parameters Matter? Coarse-grained Simulations of Neutral Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: The aggregation of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) influences their optical properties, including localized surface plasmon resonance, through plasmonic coupling between adjacent particles. For hydrophobic AuNPs embedded in lipid membranes, however, the mechanisms governing aggregation remain poorly understood. Although coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations are well suited to study these processes, commonly used ligand–nanoparticle (NP) models neglect explicit core interactions. Here, we test whether core properties regulate NP aggregation by simulating multiple Martini NP models in a membrane environment. In contrast to the assumption that surface ligands effectively shield the core, we find that interactions with the environment remain sensitive to core parameters even at maximum ligand coverage. Furthermore, core–solvent interactions are consistent with a mechanism that directly drives nanoparticle aggregation. These results suggest that core interactions can contribute to the aggregation of functionalized nanoparticles.

papers.title: Metal-Dependent Regulation of CO2-to-Syngas Electroreduction in Cation-Exchanged SU-102.
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2-to-syngas conversion requires simultaneous control over CO2 reduction and hydrogen evolution within stable electrocatalysts. Here, we show that post-synthetic cation exchange in the robust anionic Zr-based MOF SU-102 enables tunable syngas electrosynthesis while preserving framework crystallinity. Exchange of the charge-balancing DMA+ cations with Zn2+ or Ag species generates distinct catalytic behaviors during CO2 electroreduction. SU-102-Zn exhibits balanced and relatively potential-independent syngas production, whereas SU-102-Ag promotes CO-rich syngas generation with strongly potential-dependent selectivity, reaching a CO Faradaic efficiency of 93% at −1.4 V versus RHE. Structural characterization reveals that Zn remains incorporated as exchanged cationic species, while Ag undergoes partial reduction to form metallic Ag domains stabilized by the MOF scaffold. Density functional theory calculations indicate that Zn2+ and Ag regulate syngas formation through distinct catalytic mechanisms, where Zn2+ sites within the MOF framework promote balanced syngas production, while metallic Ag domains drive potential-dependent CO selectivity. This work demonstrates that post-synthetic cation exchange in stable anionic MOFs provides an effective strategy for regulating syngas composition through modulation of local catalytic environments.

papers.title: Weighted Molecular Views with Global Attention Tokens
papers.abstract: Accurate molecular property prediction strongly depends on the quality of molecular representations used as input to machine learning models. [1] proposed a molecular featurization method based on atomic coordinates that generates weighted views of a molecule. [2] proposedmodifications in [1] to the featurizationmethod for dimensionality reduction, which led to reduced empirical performance. In this work, we propose an alternative approach for dimensionality reduction and computational efficiency. Our proposed modifications increase the representativeness of molecular representations by generating additional molecular views, while reducing the dimensionality of these representations through the introduction of a global node into the architecture. The proposed modifications were evaluated on the QM9 dataset, where they demonstrated improved predictive performance. This work also provides a theoretical perspective to support and explain the proposed modifications.

papers.title: Chemically Intuitive Descriptors for Predicting C–H Borylation Regioselectivity
papers.abstract: We present a robust machine-learning (ML) framework incorporating chemically intuitive descriptors to predict regioselectivity in C–H borylation reactions. Our method integrates electronic parameters (pKa values, CM5 atomic charges, Fukui indices) and steric metrics (buried volume, solvent-accessible surface area) to systematically capture the nuanced interplay between sterics and electronics. Extensive analysis demonstrates that ligand-specific features notably enhance predictive accuracy. Among various ML models tested, tree-based algorithms, particularly LightGBM, achieved good performance (F1-score: 72%), surpassing Graph Neural Network (GNN) approaches but slightly trailing transformer-based models. Notably, we introduce a simple chemically intuitive predictive model using only one steric descriptor (%Vbur) and one electronic descriptor (pKa), which predicts regioselectivity accurately in a significant subset of reactions, highlighting its practical value and interpretability. Validation on pharmaceutical intermediates underscores the efficacy and practical applicability of both the comprehensive and simplified model, positioning our approach as an accessible, interpretable, and powerful tool for regioselectivity predictions in late-stage functionalization.

papers.title: IN SITU FORMATION OF ACTIVE METAL COMPLEXES: SERUM ACTIVATION OF PHOTOSENSITISERS FOR PHOTODYNAMIC THERAPY
papers.abstract: Metal complexes are important tools in biomedicine as therapeutic or diagnostic agents. Yet, inside the organism they can get degraded, loosing efficiency and causing unwanted toxicity. Instead, we want to target metal ions from labile metal pools to attempt forming new metal complexes with biological activity in situ. With this we intend to explore new routes to extend the efficiency of metal-based therapeutic agents and reduce possible toxicity linked to degradation under biological environments. Here we demonstrate our approach by using porphyrin ligands that are capable of binding to serum albumin and get activated with the ions carried by the protein. Newly formed metallo-porphyrins are improved photosensitisers (PS) for photodynamic therapy (PDT), and maintain their anticancer properties better than non-metallated PSs under relevant cell growing conditions.

papers.title: Nonadiabatic Dynamics of Uracil in Aqueous Solution from QM/MM in Periodic Boundary Conditions Combined with Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip TDDFT
papers.abstract: Understanding the excited-state dynamics of nucleobases in aqueous environments is essential for elucidating the mechanisms underlying DNA and RNA photostability. While puckered uracil structures have been theoretically predicted and observed in the gas phase following UV excitation, their behavior in solution remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the ultrafast photodynamics of uracil in water using a newly developed nonadiabatic surface-hopping QM/MM approach combined with MRSF-TDDFT, explicitly accounting for solvent effects and periodic boundary conditions. Our simulations characterize the dominant pathways and timescales of internal conversion, showing that twisted conformations previously predicted in the gas phase also emerge in solution. By comparing gas-phase and solution dynamics, we show how water modulates the population of puckered conformers and influences the radiationless decay pathways. The simulations further suggest that trajectories reaching the conical-intersection region preferentially evolve toward planar or twisted geometries in the ground-state. Twisted conformations become more populated during the nonequilibrium dynamics in solution. These findings provide molecular-level insight into nucleobase photodynamics in the condensed phase and demonstrate the potential of the present framework for simulating excited-state dynamics in complex biological environments.

papers.title: ICE-CAP: Ice Crystal Engineering for Cryogel Architecture Programming. Modulation of Material Properties with Ice-Binding Polymers.
papers.abstract: Macroporous cryogels are formed by polymerising monomers around ice crystal templates, with water as the only waste product making them appealing as tuneable and sustainable scaffolds. Cryogels have found application in diverse areas spanning pollutant removal, vaccine delivery, tissue culture and stationary phases for purification. However, there is an unmet challenge in that the ice crystal templates are intrinsically dynamic and evolve during polymerisation, leading to heterogeneity and complicating reproducibility. Here we overcome this challenge using ice-binding protein-inspired polymers which pre-program the ice crystal template size within cryogels through selective ice crystal surface binding. The ice crystal growth within monomer and ice-binding polymer solutions is first optimized to unlock precision tuning of the resulting pore size. This ice-crystal programming is shown to fine-tune the rheological and mechanical properties of the resulting materials, whilst holding all other parameters constant. The impact of tuneable pore size is demonstrated in model dye removal and release studies. This approach unlocks wider applications of cryogels exploiting biomimetic solutions to tune the crucial ice crystal template.

papers.title: Scalable formal synthesis of (R)-(+)-etomoxir
papers.abstract: Etomoxir is a covalent inhibitor of CPT1, a transmembrane mitochondrial protein that acts as the rate-limiting enzyme for fatty acid oxidation. Given its role in metabolic diseases such as diabetes, regulation of fatty acid biosynthesis and β-oxidation kinetics through CPT1 inhibition are effective treatments for such diseases. Previously reported syntheses of (+)-etomoxir either require early installation of a para-chlorophenolic ether which precludes the potential for late stage aryl substitution, or employ large scale pyrophoric reactions in early synthetic operations which are challenging to scale. We demonstrate the scalability of a new synthetic route to intercept a late-stage allylic alcohol en route to (+)-etomoxir, featuring a catalytic aerobic oxidation and a one-flask tandem aldol condensation- reduction sequence, to install a key allylic methylene. Importantly, the sequence described avoids pyrophoric reagents such as alklylithium bases, and can be used to access etomoxir and its analogs.

papers.title: Excitonic Amplification of Solid-State Red Circularly Polarized Luminescence through Chiral Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: The realization of intense red circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from purely organic systems is impeded by intrinsically low magnetic-to-electric transition dipole moment ratios ( m / μ ), the inverse relationship between luminescence dissymmetry and PL quantum yield (ϕ PL ), and severe nonradiative losses including excimer formation in the solid state. The problem is further compounded by the need to undertake complex enantioselective synthesis and isolation of enantiopure dyes. Here, we address these challenges by achieving a high degree of chiral symmetry breaking in the supramolecular polymerization of an axially chiral, trichromophoric perylene bisimide (PBI 3 ). In a racemic mixture containing multiple chiral PBI 3 rotamers, non-specific interactions with small-molecular chiral additives induce homochirality at the nucleation stage. Resultant homochiral polymers exhibit exceptional chiral memory and the ability to seed chiral growth in subsequent batches of racemic monomers. Non-coplanar geometry of PBI 3 helps to suppress excimer formation in these assemblies, enabling spectrally pure excitonic PL at 650 nm with a high ϕ PL of 36%. Additive-free homochiral assemblies display a red CPL with high dissymmetry factor ( g lum ) of 0.013 and a remarkable CPL brightness ( B CPL ) of 67.6 M -1 cm -1 ) that is also preserved in thin films. TDDFT calculations on PBI 3 monomer reveal that long-range exciton coupling amplifies chiroptical responses by two orders of magnitude, thus establishing supramolecular organization as a powerful strategy for achieving intense, red CPL with high color purity from purely organic materials.

papers.title: Following the Spin-Transition in Iron(II) Complexes by Crystallographic Disorder Modelling
papers.abstract: Spin crossover in iron(II) complexes refers to the switch between a low‑spin M = 1 and a high‑spin M = 5 state, producing pronounced magnetic, optical and structural changes. Single-crystal X‑ray diffraction directly monitors the accompanying crystallographic modifications. Here we show that Hirshfeld Atom Refinement (HAR), which employs ab‑initio electron‑density‑derived atomic form factors, allows quantitative modelling of co‑existing LS and HS isomers as crystallographic disorder. Applying this method to four representative iron(II) SCO complexes — [Fe(phen)2(SCN)2], [Fe(pic)3]Cl2·EtOH, [Fe(PM‑Bia)2(NCS)2] and [Fe(tpa)(SCN)2]2·MeOH — we refined temperature‑dependent site‑occupancy factors that correspond to the HS fraction. High‑resolution data (in‑house and synchrotron) reveal abrupt or gradual changes of the HS and LS- fractions. Reproducibility measurements across different crystals yield uncertainties ≤0.5 %, and the choice of hybrid DFT functional influences the occupancies only marginally. Even a two‑step transition, observable for [Fe(tpa)(SCN)2]2·MeOH, is accurately described using a simple disorder model. Consequently, HAR‑based disorder refinement provides a robust, quantitative crystallographic tool for probing spin‑state superpositions in SCO materials.

papers.title: Grid-free quantum crystallographic refinement using unbiased analytic atomic form factors from density fitting
papers.abstract: Accurate crystal structure determination requires reliable models of how atoms scatter X-rays and electrons. While quantum crystallographic methods such as Hirshfeld atom refinement (HAR) markedly improve upon the widely used Independent Atom Model (IAM) by incorporating ab initio electron densities, their reliance on numerical real-space grids imposes a significant computational bottleneck. Here, we present a density-fitting-based refinement scheme that addresses this limitation by expanding the molecular electron density via the Resolution-of-the-Identity (RI) approach into atom-centred Gaussian contributions. This enables fully analytic evaluation of aspherical X-ray and electron scattering factors, eliminating the need for real-space grids or reference atoms entirely. Benchmark refinements on a diverse set of small-molecule crystals within Olex2/NoSpherA2 demonstrate that the RI-based model reproduces R values, residual electron density, X–H bond lengths, and anisotropic displacement parameters on par with HAR, while offering substantially improved computational efficiency. This is most prominent particularly at high diffraction resolution and for larger asymmetric units.

papers.title: Characterization of epoxy‐modified lipids in the seeds of Kalijiri (Centratherum anthelminticum)
papers.abstract: Epoxy fatty acids can be formed in low quantities during oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids and occur as a complex mixture of isomers. In contrast, some plants such as Kalijiri (Centratherum anthelminticum), which is consumed in traditional Ayurvedic medicine, are known to accumulate high quantities of epoxy fatty acids, including vernolic acid (cis-12,13-epoxy oleic acid). However, to this day the extent of epoxy-modified lipid species, their spatial distribution and possible roles in C. anthelminticum and other plants are unclear. In this study, we analysed the lipids from seeds of C. anthelminticum by GC-MS, UHPLC-IMS-MS/MS and MALDI-MSI for elucidation of molecular composition and spatial distribution. Vernolic acid contributed c. 70% to the total fatty acids and a total of 24 epoxy-modified lipid species from three lipid classes could be annotated by UHPLC-IMS-MS/MS. MALDI-MSI showed different spatial distributions of the major epoxy-modified triacylglycerols within the seed, indicating specific roles of these compounds. Finally, planting experiments showed that vernolic acid was absent in other plant parts or immature seeds but accumulated again during seed maturation. Our work contributes new details to the body of knowledge on this plant species. The data can also be used as reference for analysis of epoxy-lipids in food and other matrices.

papers.title: Photoinduced Trifluoromethyl- and Difluoromethyl-Chalcogenation of α-Diazo Compounds
papers.abstract: The trifluoromethylthio (SCF3) and derived moieties play an important role in drug design and related fields since their unique electronic and lipophilic properties. The trifluoromethylthiolation-based functionalization of diazo compounds provides a concise and efficient access to SCF3 and related functional groups in recent years. However, most of the current methods depend on harsh conditions and metal salts, involving limited reaction type and substrate scope. Herein, we report a novel protocol to construct highly functionalized trifluoromethylthiolated and derived scaffolds via the trifluoromethyl- and difluoromethyl-chalcogenation of α-diazo compounds under mild and green conditions using photochemical strategy, which exhibits broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance. Moreover, the gram-scale synthesis, antibacterial tests and control experiments were carried out to explore the application and mechanism of this transformation.

papers.title: Bioisostere Editing of Bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanes (BCPs) to Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHs) Enabled by [4+1] Reaction of Vinyl BCPs and Carbon Monoxide
papers.abstract: Developing methods to synthesize various bioisosteres mimicking substituted benzene rings is revolutionizing drug discovery. Many bioisosteres such as bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanes (BCPs) and bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHs) have been developed, but methods to synthesize these bioisosteres are limited. We proposed a skeletal editing strategy converting newly designed BCP derivatives, vinyl bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanes (vinyl BCPs) into vinyl bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanones (vinyl BCHones) through Rh-catalyzed [4+1] reaction of vinyl BCPs and carbon monoxide. Vinyl-BCPs and vinyl-BCHones are bioisosteres of di- and tri-substituted benzenes, respectively. The key to the success of this skeletal editing is that the vinyl group in vinyl BCHs can help the C-C cleavage of the four-membered ring in the BCP moiety and then realize carbonyl insertion The mechanism of this [4+1] reaction has also been investigated by DFT calculations.

papers.title: Magnetic anisotropy of tellurium(I) and selenium(I)† in a Li3N host crystal
papers.abstract: Magnetic anisotropy in low-coordinate main-group compounds has recently emerged as a promising route toward realizing single-molecule magnet behavior beyond traditional transition-metal and lanthanide systems. In this work, we investigate the electronic structure and magnetic properties of selenium-and tellurium-doped Li3N crystals using a combination of periodic density functional theory and embedded ionic-crystal QM/MM multireference calculations. Substitution of Li(1) sites by Se(I) and Te(I) generates low-coordinate np3 configurations embedded in a highly symmetric crystalline environment. Periodic calculations reveal substantial differences in spin localization and covalency between the two dopants: Te-doping stabilizes a spin-polarized electronic structure with localized magnetic character, whereas stronger Se 4p–N 2p hybridization leads to increased delocalization and a non-magnetic DFT ground state. Multireference SA-CASSCF/NEVPT2 calculations show that both systems possess magnetically isotropic ground states dominated by a singly occupied σ bonding orbital, while the first excited states exhibit pronounced axial magnetic anisotropy arising from nearly degenerate π∗ x and π∗ y orbitals coupled through spin–orbit interaction. For Te-doped clusters, extremely small transverse g-tensor components (gx,gy ≈ 0.002) and large axial components (gz ≈ 3.9) indicate near-ideal magnetic axiality, slightly stronger than in the Se analogues. The larger spin–orbit coupling of tellurium also produces significantly enhanced spin–orbit splitting relative to selenium. These results demonstrate that heavy main-group elements embedded in suitable low-coordinate environments can support highly anisotropic magnetic states and further support theoretical design principles for main-group single-molecule magnets.

papers.title: Constraint-Aware Machine Learning Framework for Hydrogel Formulation and Reverse Design
papers.abstract: Hydrogel formulation is governed by complex and nonlinear relationships between compositional variables, physicochemical interactions, and experimentally imposed feasibility constraints, making the rational identification of high-performing mixtures a challenging task in practice. In this work, we present a constraint-aware computational framework for the prediction and optimization of hydrogel formulation under ordinal experimental assessment. The proposed approach integrates ordinal neural network models, specifically CORAL and CORN, with treebased ensemble learners, including Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, and XGBoost, within a unified pipeline that combines predictive modeling, feasible-region Monte Carlo sampling, probabilistic mixture inference, and explainable artificial intelligence. Formulations are represented through normalized component fractions subject to bounded ranges, compositional conservation, and hydrogel-specific logical constraints, enabling direct exploration of experimentally meaningful solution spaces. The results show that explicitly accounting for ordinal structure improves predictive reliability, while ensemble methods provide strong robustness and capture nonlinear compositional effects with high accuracy and substantial ordinal agreement. In particular, gradient-boosting-based models achieved the strongest overall performance, whereas ordinal neural models contributed smoother and more consistent probability distributions across adjacent quality categories. SHAP-based interpretability analysis revealed that hydrogel quality is primarily governed by a limited subset of influential variables and that most model behavior is predominantly additive, with only a small number of meaningful interactions. Beyond prediction, the framework enables reverse design by identifying regions of the formulation space associated with a high probability of achieving the target performance category and by providing both compositional ranges and percentage-based candidate formulations suitable for experimental implementation. The entire workflow is deployed as an interactive web-based application, allowing users to train models, define constraints, explore feasible regions, and iteratively improve the system as new experimental data and feedback become available. Together, these results establish a practical and adaptive decision-support framework for hydrogel formulation and provide a generalizable methodology for constrained ordinal optimization in chemical and materials design.

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Accelerated Density Functional Theory
papers.abstract: The predictive power of machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLPs) is fundamentally capped by the accuracy of the underlying electronic structure theory used for training. In this work, we quantify how the choice of exchange–correlation functional propagates into predicted thermodynamic behavior, using silicon as a representative system for high-pressure phase study. We employ a datae!cient framework to generate a comprehensive dataset, which is subsequently relabeled using four functionals of increasing complexity: PBE, PW91, SCAN, and HSE06. Individual ChIMES MLPs were trained to these data and validated against their respective reference theories across structural, mechanical, and dynamical properties. The 0–10 GPa melt line and 300 K solid–solid phase diagram up to 100 GPa was determined for each, as well as the full phase diagram up to 3500 K and 100 GPa for HSE06. We show that GGA-level functionals (PBE and PW91) yield melt temperatures and solid–solid transition pressures disagree significantly with experiment and that of the functionals studied, HSE06 yields the most experimentally-consistent predictions.

papers.title: The influence of the alcohol's acidity on organo-base catalyzed carbamate formation from aliphatic isocyanates
papers.abstract: This study presents findings on Lewis and Brønsted base catalysis in the reaction of aliphatic isocyanates with aliphatic and aromatic alcohols at room temperature and under solvent-free conditions. The electronic properties of the alcohols were examined to determine their impact on reaction rates, using Lewis and Brønsted bases, as well as the Lewis acid dibutyltin dilaureate (DBTL), as a reference. The results for primary aliphatic alcohols showed that none of the organo-bases could compete with DBTL in terms of catalytic activity. However, a strong dependence of the alcohols' acidity on the reaction rate was observed. With organo-base catalysis, more acidic alcohols, particularly phenols, react faster than less acidic ones. The opposite trend was observed with DBTL. Selectivity tests revealed preferential consumption of the more acidic alcohol when base-catalysis was used. DBTL causes aliphatic alcohols to react more readily than phenols. Accordingly, base catalysis offers high activity and selectivity in the carbamate formation from aromatic alcohols and aliphatic isocyanates.

papers.title: Highly-Soluble Iron Carborane Complex as Negolyte for an all Iron Redox Flow Battery
papers.abstract: The redox potential of the iron(III) carborane complex [Fe(C 2 B 9 H 11 ) 2 ] - at E ½ = -0.269 V vs Ag/AgCl at a wide pH range and its high solubility in aqueous media (Cmax = 2 ± 0.2 M) makes it a promising active material for redox flow batteries (RFBs). The single crystal X-ray structure of the oxonium salt, H 3 O[Fe(C 2 B 9 H 11 ) 2 ]·(H 2 O) 4.6 }, shows that the complex anion form stacks comprising four units oriented in a pinwheel pattern and associated by dihydrogen bonds. The stacks are well separated by channels filled with water that weave through the structure. Pairing [Fe(C 2 B 9 H 11 ) 2 ] - as the negolyte with FeSO 4 , an all-soluble iron RFB with a cell potential (E cell ) of 0.75 V was constructed. The [Fe(C 2 B 9 H 11 ) 2 ] - is robust for at least 1200 cycles, providing proof of concept for [Fe(C 2 B 9 H 11 ) 2 ] - as an energy material in all-soluble iron RFBs under both acidic and neutral conditions.

papers.title: Magnetomechanical coupling driven athermal monoclinic to rhombohedral transformation in CrI3 system
papers.abstract: Stacking-dependent magnetism in 2D materials, caused by variations in translational symmetry, has drawn major interest for its potential applications. In bulk CrI3, the monoclinic to rhombohedral transition at 220 K changes the lattice from AA to ABC honeycomb stacking. However, in thin crystals, it is shown that altered octahedral bond angles partially hinder this transition, resulting in the coexistence of an athermal monoclinic phase with the rhombohedral structure for many hours below 218 K. This coexistence results in successive magnetic orderings: a ferromagnetic (FM) state in the stable rhombohedral phase and an antiferromagnetic (AFM) state in the athermal monoclinic phase within a narrow temperature range (61–45 K). Structural separation, rather than electronic phase separation, defines these two magnetic phases. Furthermore, it is rather noteworthy that magnetic field excursions tune the mesoscopic magnetomechanical coupling in the athermal monoclinic phase, driving the transformation from the AFM order to the FM state in the rhombohedral structure owing to a lower energy of the interstructural transition compared with intrastructural spin-flip processes.

papers.title: Chemoenzymatic Access to Stereodefined Phosphorothioate Oligonucleotides by Stereoselective DNA Ligation
papers.abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated that stereopure oligonucleotide phosphorothioates (PS), with defined configuration, provide significant advantages over stereorandom mixtures in therapeutic oligonucleotides improving their efficacy. Current synthesis of long stereopure PS oligonucleotides relies primarily on stepwise chemical approaches using chiral P(III) or P(V) reagents, including auxiliary-based strategies or stereodefined monomers. Although these methods enable precise control over PS configuration, they suffer from low overall yields, impurity accumulation, high labor demands, and limited scalability and sustainability. Herein, we evaluate a chemoenzymatic alternative based on templatedirected DNA ligation of shorter oligonucleotide fragments bearing a prochiral 5′-monophosphorothioate group. A series of ligation reactions was performed using a panel of commercially available DNA ligases to determine the stereochemical outcome of PS formation during ligation. In all cases, ligation proceeded with complete stereoselectivity, affording exclusively the RP configuration at the newly formed PS linkages. Kinetic experiments were additionally conducted to compare the reactivity of standard 5′-phosphate and 5′-phosphorothioate substrates. These results demonstrate that the chemoenzymatic approach using DNA ligation can be exploited to generate fully stereodefined oligonucleotides from modular fragments and suggest the feasibility of engineering ligases with inverted stereochemical preference to access SP-selective ligation. This chemoenzymatic strategy could overcome the current limitations producing stereodefined PS oligonucleotides in higher overall yields and purities.

papers.title: DNA-Directed Patterned Secretome Capture Array for Spatially Resolved Localized Cytokine Mapping
papers.abstract: Precise measurement of localized cytokine secretion remains a significant challenge, particularly in preserving spatial context. Here, we present a DNA-directed patterning platform for spatially-resolved capture and detection of secreted cytokines from individual cells. Glass substrates were functionalized with arrays of oligonucleotides that enable site-specific hybridization of labeled antibody conjugates, generating spatially defined cytokine capture regions. Using interleukin-2 (IL-2) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) as model analytes, we demonstrate multiplexed antibody patterning, verified conjugation efficiency, and established functional cytokine capture with a limit of detection of 1 ng mL-1. Quantitative fluorescence imaging confirmed that the platform supports sensitive and reproducible detection across a defined dynamic range. Integration with single-cell patterning of Jurkat T cells further enabled localized detection of IL-2 secretion following pharmacological activation, with signal confined to individual cell positions, demonstrating the ability to resolve secretion events in situ. Together, these results establish a proof-of-concept for a versatile, scalable platform that combines spatial control with cytokine detection, offering a new approach to interrogating localized cell signaling and functional heterogeneity in immune systems.

papers.title: Kinetic and Thermodynamic Control of Benzo[a]phenoxazin Ligand Binding to Oncogenic c-MYC DNA G-Quadruplex
papers.abstract: G-quadruplex (G4) DNA structures in oncogenic promoter regions play crucial roles in gene regulation and represent promising targets for anticancer therapeutics. Polyaromatic small molecule ligands, including benzo[a]phenoxazin-based derivatives, selectively bind G4 structures through π-π stacking or groove/loop binding, thereby mitigating transcriptional activity. However, the kinetic and thermodynamic parameters governing ligand-G4 interactions, particularly the ligand’s residence time within the G4 complex, have not been sufficiently characterized, although the residence time has been found to be a key parameter of drug efficacy and resistance in proteins. Here, we combine fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) with atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, including well-tempered metadynamics (WT-MetaD), and infrequent metadynamics (iMetaD), to characterize the binding thermodynamics and kinetics of a substituted cationic benzo[a]phenoxazin ligand with parallel G4 DNA formed by a 22-mer c-MYC promoter sequence. Steady-state fluorescence titration shows high binding affinity of the ligand to the parallel c-MYC G4 ( K = (2.9 ∓ 0.3) x 10 7 M -1 ), primarily driven by π-π stacking of benzo[a]phenoxazin aromatic core on the solvent-exposed 5’-terminal G-tetrad, along with stabilizing hydrogen-bond and salt-bridge interactions. FCS measurements reveal rapid reaction-coupled diffusion kinetics, yielding a ligand association rate of ݇ k on = (2.4 ∓ 0.2) x 10 9 M -1 s -1 and a ligand residence time ( τ res ) of ~10 ms in the G4-bound state, showing that ligand dissociation is the rate-limiting step. WT-MetaD simulations, employing contact-pair-based and hydration collective variables, enable reconstruction of a converged free-energy surface that provides binding free energy consistent with the experimental value and reveals multiple π-stacked binding orientations of the ligand on the G-tetrad, separated by barriers of ~30–35 kJ mol -1 . Extensive iMetaD simulations capture highly directional ligand-dissociation pathways through the loop region formed by T7, G8 and G9 of G4-DNA and recover a ligand residence time of ~9 ms, which closely matches the FCS result and directly validate iMetaD-derived kinetics. These findings establish a quantitative benchmark between enhanced-sampling simulations and experimentally measured kinetic and thermodynamic parameters for the interaction of benzo[a]phenoxazin with c-MYC G4 DNA. This work provides a generalizable multiscale framework for elucidating deeper molecular insight into ligand-G4 recognition across energy and time scales, identifying ligand residence time as a critical parameter that may be optimized through rational design of next-generation benzo[a]phenoxazin-based G4-targeted compounds with better efficacy.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn at the authors' request to address a third-party concern regarding the subject matter of the manuscript. The withdrawal does not reflect any issues with the scientific validity, integrity, or originality of the research.

papers.title: Scaffold-Aware QSAR Modelling of Cyclin-Dependent Kinase 2 Inhibition: Multi-Model Benchmarking, Applicability Domain Assessment, and an Open-Source Decision-Support Platform
papers.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) is a validated oncology target whose aberrant activation drives uncontrolled cell-cycle progression in diverse cancers. Despite sustained pharmaceutical interest, the rational prioritisation of CDK2-directed chemical matter remains hindered by the scarcity of publicly accessible, rigorously validated predictive tools that couple potency estimation with interpretable chemical evidence. Here we report the development, validation, and deployment of a quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) model for CDK2 inhibition, constructed from a curated ChEMBL dataset and evaluated under a deliberately stringent scaffold-stratified validation framework. We retrieved 2,716 IC50 bioactivity records for CDK2 (CHEMBL301) from ChEMBL, of which 2,057 unique compounds survived a nine-stage curation pipeline encompassing SMILES sanitisation, salt stripping, InChIKey-based deduplication, pIC50 conversion, and physicochemical outlier removal. The final dataset spans 892 Murcko scaffolds and a pIC50 range of 3.01–9.52 (mean 6.49 ± 1.27). Four regression algorithms Ridge regression, Random Forest, support vector regression with a radial basis function kernel (SVR–RBF), and XGBoost were benchmarked against a scaffold-stratified 80/20 split, ensuring zero scaffold overlap between training (n = 1,645) and test (n = 412) partitions. Following hyperparameter optimisation via randomised search cross-validation, the selected Random Forest model achieved a scaffold-split test R2 of 0.429, RMSE of 0.918 pIC50 units, and Pearson r of 0.673, with five-fold cross-validation returning R2 = 0.678 ± 0.028 and RMSE = 0.715 ± 0.031. Y-randomisation confirmed that predictive signal is genuine and not an artefact of chance correlation. The trained model is deployed as an open-source, publicly accessible Streamlit web application ChemBLitz: CDK2 Pharmacological Diagnostic Suite that integrates pIC50 prediction with applicability domain assessment (Tanimoto-based, three-tier threshold), ensemble uncertainty quantification, PAINS screening, Lipinski/Veber/QED developability profiling, ligand efficiency calculation, and Murcko scaffold context. This "prediction-plus-evidence" paradigm shifts the model from a point predictor to a decision-support service, enabling informed medicinal chemistry judgements at the hit-to-lead stage.

papers.title: QuADMET-Former: Pre-training on Quantum Mechanical Properties Improves ADMET Prediction
papers.abstract: In principle, quantum chemistry allows us to quantify electronic and geometric properties of molecules and their interactions. Thus, incorporating pre-calculated quantum mechanical properties into deep learning models could improve their ability to predict important pharmacological properties of small molecules and potential drugs. However, this opportunity to incorporate better physicochemical inductive bias has been underexploited in the recent wave of AI-driven drug discovery. We show that pre-training Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) models-specifically the TorchMD-NET model-to predict quantum mechanical molecular and atomic properties like dipole moments, HOMO-LUMO gap, and partial charges, we can obtain more accurate models to predict absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicological (ADMET) properties. Moreover, we explore the interplay between quantum chemistry and three-dimensional structure by introducing a novel structure pre-training strategy where the equivariant transformer is pre-trained on three-dimensional molecular fingerprints known as E3FPs. We ran QuADMET-Former, MapLight+GNN and Quantum Informed Pre-training on 23 ADMET benchmarks drawn from Therapeutic Data Commons (TDC), Biogen ADME, and OpenADMET, and found them to outperform both MapLight+GNN, the best-performing single model on the TDC benchmark, and Quantum Informed pre-training, a state-of-the-art method for quantum chemistry-informed ADMET prediction, on very challenging spectral splits. QuADMET-Former performed best on 16 of the 23 datasets (13 out of those 16 were statistically significant). The optimal pre-training target combination varies across tasks, suggesting that quantum mechanical and geometric features capture complementary aspects of molecular behaviour. Our results establish quantum chemistry-grounded pre-training as a practical and impactful strategy for ADMET prediction under strict generalization conditions, and highlight the underexplored interplay between 3D molecular geometry and electronic structure in representation learning for small-molecule drug discovery.

papers.title: The Newton-X Platform for Mixed Quantum–Classical Dynamics
papers.abstract: Mixed quantum–classical dynamics (MQCD) methods are effective models for excited-state processes in quasi-classical molecular systems, in which nuclear motion is described by classical trajectories while electronic populations undergo quantum nonadiabatic transitions. This article presents Newton-X 26, a new generation of the Newton-X platform that consolidates two decades of development into a modular ecosystem for generating spectra and initial conditions, propagating dynamics, and analyzing, postprocessing, and archiving data. Newton-X 26 supports multiple MQCD strategies, including surface hopping, decoherence-corrected Ehrenfest dynamics, and ab initio multiple spawning, and connects to a range of electronic-structure engines through dedicated interfaces. The platform emphasizes efficient execution for large trajectory ensembles, enabling systematic convergence analyses and uncertainty estimation. Complementary tools support automated data curation, machine-learning-assisted workflows, and reproducible FAIR-oriented reporting and sharing. Taken together, Newton-X 26 provides an open-source environment for routine MQCD applications and continued method development across multiple electronic- structure levels.

papers.title: BigMixSolDB: Extraction of a solubility database in solvent mixtures with an uncertainty-quantified large language model-based pipeline
papers.abstract: The rapidly expanding body of chemical literature contains physical data scattered across unstructured text and complex tables in thousands of publications. Translating this information into machine-readable formats is essential for training data-driven chemical models. The lack of uncertainty quantification in computationally extracted datasets makes manual extraction and curation still necessary. We here address this challenge and present an uncertainty-quantified data extraction pipeline. Our fully automated pipeline utilizes large language models (LLMs) to extract complex tabular and textual chemical data directly from scientific PDFs. We systematically assess several modern LLMs and document-to-text conversion frameworks. We benchmark the uncertainty in extracted data by comparison of our computationally extracted databases with large, existing databases on solubility that are manually curated. Our pipeline achieves between 93 and 79% of the literature contained data, with extraction errors being on par with aleatoric limits that exist in the manually curated databases. We showcase the utility of our pipeline by deploying the optimized pipeline to extract data from 2,301 articles to generate BigMixSolDB, a comprehensive database on solubility in complex mixtures. BigMixSolDBcomprises over 299,000 filtered solubility entries spanning single, binary, and ternary solvent systems. Our results demonstrate how integrated LLM-based pipelines can be used for literature data extraction that is comparable with manual curation. We envision that these frameworks can be used for large-scale, accurate extraction of literature data into datasets for machine learning applications.

papers.title: EXPERIMENTAL AND COMPUTATIONAL 11 B NMR COMPARATIVE STUDY OF MOVPE-GROWN RHOMBOHEDRAL AND BULK HEXAGONAL BORON NITRIDE
papers.abstract: Layered boron nitride (BN) is a two-dimensional (2D) insulator that exhibits several polytypes, which differ in the stacking sequence of adjacent atomic planes. The relative shift and rotation of subsequent planes modify the crystal symmetry and thereby determine the crystal's fundamental properties. While most previous NMR-oriented studies have focused on AA'-stacked hexagonal BN (hBN), ABC-stacked rhombohedral BN (rBN) has not yet been investigated. In this study, we present the magic-angle spinning 11 B NMR spectra of rBN and compare them with those of hBN and with DFT calculations. We also measure spin-lattice relaxation of both polytypes. Our findings suggest that both phases exhibit nearly identical NMR parameters, including chemical shifts and quadrupole couplings. However, our rBN and hBN samples differ significantly in relaxation, which may be attributed to different growth methods, resulting in different concentrations of paramagnetic centers. Interestingly, we also observe extremely long spin-lattice relaxation times for terminal groups in hBN, which have rendered them unobservable in many previous studies. Experimental and computational 11 B NMR comparative study of MOVPE-grown rhombohedral and bulk hexagonal boron nitride A PREPRINT

papers.title: Understanding and Reporting PFAS Exposure: Wide-scope Retrospective Suspect Screening of High-resolution Mass Spectrometry Data from Exposomics Studies
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) comprise thousands of persistent and structurally diverse chemicals that contribute to chronic human exposure. Yet, routine biomonitoring targets only a limited set of regulated legacy compounds, underestimating overall exposure. We present a retrospective, wide-scope suspect screening analysis framework to extract PFAS information from archived LC–HRMS exposomics datasets. A curated list of 1,666 PFAS, filtered for reversed-phase LC compatibility and enriched with structural descriptors, predicted retention indices, and MS$ fragments, was used to reprocess two human biomonitoring studies involving firefighter serum pools and population-based plasma samples. Candidate features were prioritized using precursor accuracy, isotopic patterns, and MS2 similarity, followed by spectral quality filtering and retention time-index regression models based on isotopically labeled standards, reinforcing identification confidence. The reanalysis recovered up to 80% of previously reported PFAS while revealing overlooked high-confidence carboxylic, sulfonic, and sulfonamidoacetic acid homologs, and >30 tentative PFAS series, encompassing isomeric clusters (alcohols and ethers) and structurally distinct subclasses (alkylpyrimidine PFAS). The reanalysis framework also revealed shared homolog patterns across exposure contexts. By framing PFAS chemical space and providing a reusable repository of confirmed and tentative structures, this framework reinterprets HRMS biobanked data, improving PFAS pattern assessment.

papers.title: Open- and Closed Shell Roles of Sensitiser and Annihilator in Pseudo-Single Component Mixtures for Upconversion
papers.abstract: Photochemical upconversion by annihilation of two triplet excitons to a higher-energy singlet state enables energy control of photons in optoelectronics and photonics. Upconversion initiated by a closed-shell sensitiser is limited by energy losses from singlet–triplet intersystem crossing. Here we explore open-shell organic radicals as sensitisers and their closed-shell hydrogenated analogues as annihilators in photon upconversion. The sensitiser combines optical transitions from a triphenylmethyl (TTM-1Cz) radical with energy-degenerate triplet states of an anthracene-based component (DPA) in one molecule (TTM-1Cz-DPA). The difference of one hydrogen atom in its closed-shell counterpart (HTTM-1Cz-DPA) switches the spin-optical properties to an annihilator that can mediate efficient upconversion. Red-to-blue photon upconversion by intermolecular energy transfer, from open-shell sensitiser to closed-shell annihilator, is demonstrated in solution with an apparent anti-Stokes shift higher than 0.9 eV and 7% quantum efficiency. We evaluate this mechanism against true ‘single component’ mixtures for upconversion and find that the presence of hydrogenated precursor with radicals is essential for high performance. Understanding the emergent spin-optical properties from paired open-shell and closed-shell systems enables new opportunities for energy management from the same molecular frame.

papers.title: ChiralSPE: Benchmarking Trustworthiness and Symmetry in Atomistic Foundation Models based on OMol25
papers.abstract: Atomistic foundation potentials trained on massive datasets like OMol25 are increasingly used for zero-shot workflows, but their trustworthiness under strict physics constraints remains unclear (Problem). Chirality provides a rigorous stress test: enantiomers (mirror-image molecules) must have identical energies and force fields that are exact mirror transforms, yet existing benchmarks emphasize average MAE or downstream property prediction (e.g., optical rotation) rather than fundamental symmetry compliance. I introduce ChiralSPE, a new benchmark derived from the CMRT corpus that contains verified chiral molecules with energies and forces computed ab initio at the OMol25 level of theory (ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPD), and I perform a zero-shot audit of leading atomistic foundation models (Orb, UMA, MACE) (Method). Despite strong average accuracy, I find that these models frequently violate chiral symmetry constraints, and I further evaluate whether uncertainty quantification mechanisms can reliably flag such symmetry-breaking failures (Results).

papers.title: Reimaging acylation chemistry with nucleophilic indicator organocatalysts that uncover a temperature-dependent mechanistic switch
papers.abstract: Acylation reactions are a cornerstone of synthetic organic chemistry with ester and amide bond couplings as one of the most central and frequently employed reactions in medicinal chemistry. However, the availability of a wide range of specialized activation reagents and catalysts necessitates time-consuming and resource-intensive screenings to perform and optimize certain acylation reactions. To streamline this process, we report a new class of nucleophilic acylation catalysts based on the azopyridine scaffold that combine an enhanced catalytic activity with an intrinsic indicator function. The two catalysts, DMAAP and PPAY, enable the direct optical detection of the catalytically active N-acylpyridinium species through a pronounced, reversible color change. This indicator system revealed that N-acylpyridinium formation is enhanced at low temperatures. Subsequent kinetics analyses uncovered electrophile- and catalyst-dependent behavior which does not correlate with literature models: While pyridine and DMAP show opposing trends with respect to temperature, highly unusual parabolic Eyring plots were obtained for DMAAP and PPAY in combination with benzoyl chloride. Microkinetic simulations and NMR titration studies support a mechanistic rationale involving competing steps concerning the temperature-dependent N-acylpyridinium equilibria and the subsequent acyl transfer to the terminal nucleophile. Overall, our studies showcase that DMAAP and PPAY significantly outperform the predominantly used DMAP in esterification and amidation reactions, with rate accelerations of up to ~50-fold at low temperatures. Their function as indicators allowed to streamline the performance and optimization of acylation reactions by providing a visual confirmation for the formation of the catalytically active intermediate. These findings establish azopyridines as a powerful nucleophilic catalyst class with an exceptionally rare ability to reversibly self-report catalytic states.

papers.title: Chirality Transfer from Peptide Crystals to Achiral BODIPY Dyes Enables Enhanced Circularly Polarized Luminescence
papers.abstract: Diphenylalanine (FF), the core recognition motif of the amyloid-β peptide, is renowned for its versatile self-assembly in aqueous media. In the present work, we report for the first time that a hydrophobic diphenylalanine derivative functionalized with tert-butoxycarbonyl and tert-butyl ester protecting groups self-organizes into elongated crystalline microfibers upon dissolution in hexafluoroisopropanol followed by water dilution. Two structurally distinct BODIPY-functionalized FF derivatives, green-and red-emitting, the latter featuring extended conjugation and terminal hydroxyl groups, were incorporated at 1 mol% during fiber crystallization. The resulting BODIPY-doped microfibers were characterized by single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, chir/optical spectroscopy, confocal microscopy, and two-photon microscopy. Although all BODIPY-functionalized FF derivatives exhibit negligible chiroptical activity in solution, BODIPY-doped microfibers embedded in a 6% poly(vinyl alcohol) hydrogel display strong induced CD and CPL signals. These results demonstrate efficient transfer of chirality from the chiral supramolecular organization of the fibers to the embedded fluorophores. The red-emitting BODIPY derivative exhibited nearly twice as high dissymmetry factor values compared to its green-emitting counterpart, reaching a luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) close to 10−2. This work establishes peptide-based crystalline microfibers as versatile scaffolds for amplifying the chiroptical activity of embedded dyes, offering a modular platform to engineer advanced optically responsive materials with tailored functionality.

papers.title: Urease immobilised membrane incorporated microfluidic devices for potential hemodialysis applications
papers.abstract: *correspondence: syed.mehdi2019@my.ntu.ac.uk ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0009-2207-2447 Abstract: Chronic kidney disease is one of the leading causes of mortality globally. Hemodialysis is a bulky procedure with patient impaired for 3 – 4 hours. A membrane integrated microfluidic device has been used for dialysis with more portability and ease of use for patients. Here we demonstrate an optimised method for cellulose acetate (CA) and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane integration in microfluidic device, in a single step. The microdevice exhibited urea reduction ratio of 12 and 16 for CA and PVDF, respectively. Urease was chemically immobilised on the device for regeneration of dialysate and improve overall efficiency. After immobilisation, the urea reduction ratio increased to 92, with 98% of dialysate regenerated. This study provides a general method of single step, thermal bonding of membrane integrated microdevice and also a multifunctional microfluidic device for potential applications in hemodialysis.

papers.title: Excited-State Dynamics and Charge-Transfer Properties of 2-Aminophenol Schiff Bases: Implications for NLO and DSSC Performance
papers.abstract: Organic π-conjugated systems with efficient intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) have attracted considerable attention due to their promising optoelectronic behavior in nonlinear optical (NLO) materials and dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) applications. Since both share a common physical origin in ICT, the systematic investigation of donor–π–acceptor Schiff base systems offers a coherent framework for dual optoelectronic evaluation. In this context, the present work investigates three 2-aminophenol Schiff bases, namely (E)-2-[(2hydroxyphenyl)iminomethyl]phenol (HL1), (E)-2-[(3-nitrobenzylidene)amino]phenol (HL2), and (E)-2-[(2-chlorobenzylidene)amino]phenol (HL3) to explore their optoelectronic properties for potential NLO and DSSC applications. The compounds were synthesized and characterized using UV-Vis and FTIR. Structural confirmation was supported by excellent agreement between experimental and scaled theoretical FTIR spectra, evidenced by excellent linear correlation coefficients. Geometrical optimization and frequency analysis at the B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) level confirmed all structures as true energy minima, and the resulting HOMO–LUMO energy levels indicated suitable frontier orbital alignments for DSSC sensitization in all three compounds. MEP, DOS, TDM, dipole moment, and exciton binding energy analyses revealed a well-defined D–π–A ICT architecture for HL2 and donor-to-πspacer charge transfer for HL1 and HL3. TD-DFT calculations at both B3LYP and CAM-B3LYP levels in seven solvents confirmed strong light-harvesting efficiency for HL1 and HL3, with HL1 showing the strongest electron injection driving force (ΔGinject = −2.032 eV, CAM-B3LYP) and highest open-circuit voltage (VOC = 2.234 V). The first-order hyperpolarizability of HL2 reached 112 times that of urea in acetonitrile, identifying it as a strong NLO-active candidate. Overall, HL2 is identified as the superior NLO material while HL1 and HL3 emerge as more promising DSSC sensitizer candidates based on their favorable intrinsic photovoltaic descriptors.

papers.title: Controlling a Difficult Radical Sequence Enables Asymmetric β-Lactam Synthesis
papers.abstract: Radical reactions offer powerful opportunities in synthesis, but controlling their stereochemical course remains difficult, especially when productive bond formation must compete with fragmentation and other fast radical pathways. We report a catalyst-controlled radical strategy for the asymmetric synthesis of β-lactams from readily accessible α-diazoacetamides. A rationally designed cobalt metalloradical catalyst supported by an alkyne-bridged chiral amidoporphyrin ligand enables enantioselective 1,4-C–H alkylation through a stepwise mechanism involving 1,4-hydrogen atom abstraction followed by 4- exo-tet radical substitution, a combination of elementary radical steps that is typically disfavored. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions across a broad range of substrates, including complex derivatives of drugs and natural products, to furnish chiral β-lactams in high yields and enantioselectivities. Computational and experimental studies reveal that a confined chiral cavity and cooperative non-covalent interactions direct both radical reactivity and stereocontrol. The resulting chiral β-lactams undergo diverse stereospecific transformations and provide access to the cholesterol-lowering drug (–)-ezetimibe.

papers.title: Reproducibility, Replicability, and Research Quality in Homogeneous Catalysis
papers.abstract: Researchers from all sectors of homogeneous catalysis convened in response to concerns regarding reproducibility in science to analyze the issue and provide recommendations. In addition to an in-person workshop, the group engaged the broader homogeneous catalysis community through a webinar series and virtually during the workshop. Results of the project affirm that homogeneous catalysis is not in a reproducibility crisis, as evidenced by the field’s current and past contributions to society that have led to economic growth and advances in a range of industries from agriculture to consumer goods to human health. However, it is not uncommon for researchers to encounter obstacles related to reproducibility. Ensuring reproducibility remains the responsibility of the community, both in current work and in training future researchers. This report is intended to engage key stakeholders, including disciplinary societies, publishers, employers, research leaders, and researchers, in practices that maximize reproducible homogeneous catalysis and ensure continued innovation and translatable discoveries. Recommendations made herein are also framed to be applicable beyond homogeneous catalysis, empowering the broader chemical if not scientific community.

papers.title: Self-limited clustering of nanoparticles through electrostatic stabilization at the cluster scale
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle aggregation is a crucial phenomenon in biomedical applications and is typically expected when electrostatic stabilization weakens. Yet the mechanisms governing whether aggregation proceeds indefinitely or arrests at finite cluster size remain poorly understood. Here we show that citrate-capped upconverting nanoparticles (UCNPs) undergo self-limited clustering through electrostatic stabilization at the cluster scale rather than uncontrolled aggregation. Their narrow size distributions enable small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) to resolve equilibrium clusters with ~2–10 primary particles, revealing interaction mechanisms that are otherwise obscured in more polydisperse systems. We find that dilution lowers nanoparticle surface charge, likely through partial citrate dissolution, thus initiating aggregation. However, as clusters form, residual primary-particle charges accumulate to restore long-range repulsion, arresting further growth. DLVO calculations predict year-scale cluster stability, confirmed by SAXS after 14 months. In physiological media, protein-free simulated blood promotes extensive aggregation, whereas protein-containing media and fetal bovine serum keep aggregation limited despite similarly high ionic strength, providing a basis for predicting and controlling nanoparticle clustering in biological environments.

papers.title: Bio-inspired deoxynucleoside-containing polymer double networks: tunable thermosets and the influence of base pairing
papers.abstract: Leveraging the multiple hydrogen bonds of nucleobases into bio-inspired synthetic materials is a powerful strategy towards advanced materials. Here, we report a series of polymer double networks derived from the four DNA-nucleosides and study the influence of covalent and non-covalent crosslinking on the thermomechanical properties of the resulting materials. The thiol-ene photopolymerization process is modular, robust, and was shown to be compatible with a range of di- and tri-thiol molecules, as well as with nucleoside-derived diene and triene monomers. The addition of base pairing to form the double network drastically increases the materials strength, with the Young’s modulus increasing 25 times, compared to covalent crosslinking alone. The versatility of the polymerization system can also be exploited to further tune the properties of the resulting hydrolytically degradable thermosets, enabling the enhancement of ultimate tensile strength up to 8.3 MPa and elongation at break up to 390%, swelling up to 150% by mass in THF and thermal stability up to 250°C. The strategy presented here allows to access previously inaccessible regions of the material space for thiol-ene polymer networks.

papers.title: Accessible Automation-Inspired RAFT Copolymerization for Sequence-Controlled Polymer Design
papers.abstract: Sequence control in radical polymerization plays a critical role in defining polymer properties, yet achieving such control typically relies on high-cost automated platforms with limited accessibility. Here, we present a semi-batch reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) copolymerization strategy using a syringe pump as a low-cost and modular alternative to high-end robotic systems. Using the copolymerization of oligo(ethylene glycol) methyl ether acrylate and fluorescein o-acrylate as a model system, we directly benchmark this approach against previously reported Chemspeed-enabled workflows. The results highlight that syringe pump-based semi-batch systems can offer a practical and accessible alternative to fully automated platforms.

papers.title: Controlling defect density in two-dimensional colloidal crystals using low-frequency AC electric fields
papers.abstract: Colloidal crystals are promising platforms for structural color due to their ability to modulate light through periodic structures with lattice spacings comparable to visible wavelengths. In two-dimensional systems that generate color via grating diffraction, the optical response is strongly influenced by the density and distribution of defects. While assembly directed by electric fields provides a versatile route to fabricate such structures, understanding of the kinetics of assembly and its impact on the density of defects remains limited. Here, we establish low-frequency AC electric fields as a rapid and tunable approach for assembling micron-sized particles into two-dimensional colloidal crystals. Using small-angle light scattering (SALS), confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM), and quantitative image analysis, we characterize the structural evolution and kinetics of assembly across a range of frequencies and voltages. Assembly occurs on timescales of a few seconds, substantially faster than many existing field-directed approaches. We find that faster assembly, achieved at lower frequencies or higher voltages, leads to increased defect densities, demonstrating a direct relationship between kinetics and microstructure. Guided by these insights, we implement time-modulated electric fields (duty cycles) to control crystallization dynamics. By selecting on/off times comparable to characteristic assembly and melting times, we enable particle rearrangement and grain coarsening, doubling the average grain size and reducing defect fractions by up to 50% relative to steady fields. The resulting structures exhibit tunable diffraction patterns relevant for applications using reconfigurable structural color. These results highlight the role of kinetics as a key design parameter for field-directed colloidal assembly.

papers.title: Polarizability of Particles with Combined Chemical and Geometrical Anisotropy: The Case of Janus Ellipsoids
papers.abstract: While various factors influence the polarizability of colloidal particles, the concurrent effects of chemical and geometric anisotropy have yet to be quantified. We address this gap by investigating Janus ellipsoids with aspect ratios ranging from 1.5 to 5, which serve as model systems for particles with combined anisotropy. Electrorotation measurements reveal three distinct relaxations due to concentration polarization, induced charge polarization, and the Maxwell–Wagner–O’Konski mechanism. Surface charge, particle aspect ratio, and medium conductivity govern the observed behavior, with conductivity offering the greatest experimental flexibility for tuning polarizability. Crucially, while these mechanisms are traditionally treated as distinct, our results demonstrate that concentration polarization and induced charge polarization can overlap and compete in the low frequency regime. This finding has significant implications for active matter experiments, which are frequently conducted at these frequencies. These insights provide guidance for leveraging polarization mechanisms to control separation, propulsion, and field directed assembly of anisotropic particles.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because it is an incomplete duplicate of another preprint (10.26434/chemrxiv.15004279/v1).

papers.title: Degradation-Aware Plastic Sorting Using Spectroscopy, Barcode Additives, and Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Plastics undergo complex degradation processes that signiQicantly inQluence their recyclability, performance, and value in circular materials systems. However, traditional sorting practices classify plastics solely by polymer type (e.g., polypropylene, PP; poly(ethylene terephthalate), PET), ignoring their degree of degradation (i.e., age, conditions), and resulting in post-consumer recycled (PCR) materials (i.e., downcycling) with reduced material quality. This work presents a predictive, nondestructive framework for determining the age of plastics using vibrational spectroscopy, machine learning, and a forward-looking additive-based strategy. Mild thermal aging experiments on commercial PET (at 50 °C for two weeks) revealed no measurable chemical or structural changes in FTIR spectra and no signiQicant mass loss in thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), demonstrating the insensitivity of conventional methods to early-stage degradation. In contrast, Raman spectroscopy data collected from the literature combined with deep learning enabled robust classiQication of aged versus unaged materials. Two architectures were evaluated, namely Figure2CNN and ResNet1D, achieving mean accuracies of 90.16% ± 4.50% and 89.61% ± 2.27%, respectively, with Figure2CNN achieving higher overall accuracy and ResNet1D exhibiting lower variance across folds. However, per-sample evaluation revealed that ResNet1D exhibited complete majority-class collapse, correctly classifying zero stable samples across all folds, while Figure2CNN demonstrated balanced discrimination across both classes and is therefore the recommended architecture for this task. To promote practical deployment, an interactive inference dashboard was developed that performs real-time preprocessing and classiQication of Raman spectral data. Finally, a forward-looking additive-based "age barcode" approach using triazole-derived UV absorber additives is proposed to enhance sensitivity and interpretability of degradation detection. This integrated framework combines spectroscopy, advanced computation, and chemical design to offer the potential for accurate, scalable aging assessment for improved plastic recycling.

papers.title: A Model Hamiltonian Map for Organic Semiconductor Doping Regimes
papers.abstract: Molecular doping of organic semiconductors (OSCs) depends on coupled energetic and electronic parameters that control integer charge transfer, charge-transfer complex formation, and double doping. Here, we use exact diagonalization of a coarse-grained Pariser–Parr–Pople-style Hamiltonian to map OSC doping regimes across molecularly tunable parameters: the OSC–dopant energy offset, on-site Hubbard repulsions, intermolecular electronic couplings, and inter-site Coulomb interactions. Minimal two-site, three-site, and extended OSCaggregate models show that Hubbard repulsion is essential for stabilizing single-polaron states, suppressing bipolaron formation, and enabling double-doped states with charge delocalized across OSC aggregates. In contrast, strong OSC–dopant electronic coupling promotes partial charge-transfer-complex character, while strong OSC–OSC coupling and weak Coulomb binding favor delocalized integer-charge carriers. These results provide a compact theoretical framework for rationalizing and designing OSC–dopant pairs with targeted charge-transfer character and doping efficiency.

papers.title: Mechanistic Understanding of Proton Transport in Metal–Organic Frameworks via Universal Machine-Learned Potentials
papers.abstract: Proton transport in porous materials is an integral process in science and engineering. Recently, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanoporous materials for proton-exchange membranes (PEMs); however, the fundamental understanding of proton transport in MOFs remains unelucidated. Here, we developed universal machinelearned potentials (uMLPs) to investigate proton transport properties and mechanisms in pertinent MOFs, namely UiO-66 and MOF-808. After validating the prediction accuracy across diverse physical properties, we fine-tuned a uMLP to simulate proton transport in bulk water and MOFs. Importantly, the uMLP accurately reproduced the experimental proton diffusivity in bulk water, which cannot be achieved via conventional potentials. Subsequently, uMLP-driven molecular dynamics (MLP-MD) simulations reveal that proton hopping (Grotthuss mechanism) is governed by hydrogen-bond (H-bond) structure. Our mechanistic analysis reveals previously unelucidated insights into the proton transfer mechanism: MOFs with smaller pores exhibit higher energy barriers for proton transfer and H-bond exchange, thereby inhibiting proton hopping under nanoconfinement. Furthermore, the effects of incorporating linker-functionalization and defects in MOFs were investigated; while linker-functionalization exacerbates nanoconfinement and hinders proton transfer, incorporating defects facilitates proton hopping by lowering energy barriers for proton transfer and H-bond exchange. Finally, analysis of structure-transport relationships evidences that H-bond structure governs proton transport in MOFs. Beyond developing accurate uMLPs for describing complex proton transport across diverse MOFs, we reveal previously unexplored mechanisms of proton transport under nanoconfinement and elucidate key structure−transport relationships that will guide the design of PEMs.

papers.title: Beyond Go/No-Go Decisions: A Regional Selection Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Molecule Screening
papers.abstract: In drug discovery, quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models are widely used to guide Go/No-Go decisions within the Design–Make–Test–Analyze (DMTA) cycle. However, conventional decision heuristics typically rely on a single cutoff, leading to a rigid binary select/discard paradigm. This approach is particularly ill-suited for borderline compounds near the decision boundary, where screening decisions are especially sensitive to prediction uncertainty and premature choices may either discard viable leads or advance likely failures, thereby increasing downstream assay costs. To address this limitation, we propose Regional Selection (RS), an uncertainty-aware three-way decision framework that partitions compounds into Predicted Pass, Predicted Fail, and Predicted Indeterminate regions. By explicitly reserving high-uncertainty compounds for targeted follow-up, RS avoids the pitfalls of premature binary classification. We formalize this framework through Regional Selection Inference (RSI), which casts region assignment as a multiple-hypothesis testing problem. We develop two imple- mentations of RSI: an empirical calibration-based method (RSI-EC), which thresholds uncertainty-normalized scores via empirical calibration, and a conformal selectionbased method (RSI-CS), which constructs conformal p-values for region assignment. RSI-EC is supported by large-sample calibration arguments, whereas RSI-CS provides finite-sample, distribution-free guarantees under exchangeability. Extensive evaluations across 15 high-dimensional QSAR benchmarks show that both RSI procedures reliably control the false discovery rate while maintaining high screening power. In limited-data regimes, RSI-CS yields particularly stable FDR control, whereas RSI-EC can be slightly less conservative; both perform strongly as sample sizes increase. We further study a cost-aware extension that incorporates asymmetric downstream costs through the score construction while keeping the nominal FDR target fixed. This extension introduces a tuning parameter that can reduce realized downstream cost, with dataset-dependent trade-offs against screening power. Overall, RSI offers a mathematically grounded and resource-aware alternative to single-threshold screening, allowing discovery teams to better balance decision confidence with assay budgets.

papers.title: Kornblum-Type Oxidative Ring-Opening Reaction of a Tricyclo[4.3.0.05,7]nonane Derivative for the Synthesis of a CD Ring System of Steroids
papers.abstract: We have developed a facile method for the transformation of a tricyclo[4.3.0.0 5,7 ]nonane derivative to a diastereomeric mixture of suitably oxygenated hydrindan isomers, wherein oxidative ring-opening, intramolecular proton transfer, and deethoxycarbonylation sequentially proceeded in a single operation upon heating with Ni(OTf) 2 in the presence of DABCO in DMSO at 150 °C.

papers.title: Electron-Donor-Acceptor Complex Enabled Electrophilic C(sp2)-C(sp3) Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: The construction of C(sp 2 )-C(sp 3 ) bonds is fundamental to pharmaceutical synthesis, yet metal-free approaches to electrophilic cross-coupling remain underdeveloped. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven, metal-free cross-coupling between heteroaryl nitriles and alkyl bromides enabled by a rationally designed aminosilane, (TMS) 3 SiNHPh. This reagent forms an electron-donor-acceptor (EDA) complex with electron-deficient nitriles via π-π interactions. Photoinduced electron transfer generates a silyl radical that triggers XAT from alkyl bromides, delivering alkyl radicals for subsequent decyanative coupling. The method accommodates a broad range of substrates, providing alkylated heteroarenes in moderate to good yields, and extends to Miniscitype C-H alkylations, underscoring the versatility of this platform. This work demonstrates that strategic EDA donor design can address a long-standing challenge in metal-free electrophilic coupling.

papers.title: Benchmarking Gamma Base: a deterministic composition-only engine for pre-DFT materials screening
papers.abstract: High-throughput materials discovery often begins with large sets of candidate compositions, while density functional theory (DFT), synthesis, and high-fidelity characterization remain expensive enough to require early prioritization.
