We present Gamma Base, a deterministic, composition-only screening engine that ranks inorganic material candidates before DFT using tabulated element-level electronic descriptors. Gamma Base is white-box, CPU-only, target-aware, and does not require crystal structures or fitting to a supervised training set. We benchmarked the engine across 59 Materials Project-derived datasets covering more than 200,000 inorganic compounds and four screening targets: formation energy, energy above hull, higher band gap, and lower band gap. The primary metric is enrichment@25, defined as the number of top-decile target hits found in the top-25 ranked candidates relative to random selection. The strongest global result is observed for formation-energy screening, with mean enrichment of 4.10x across 58 datasets and 593 aggregate top-25 hits. Band gap higher screening achieves 2.07x mean enrichment globally and substantially higher enrichment in chemically coherent families, including sulfides, phosphides, nitrides, selenides, borides, carbides, oxides, halide perovskites, and spinels. Energy-above-hull enrichment is more modest at 1.48x, partly because large tied groups at exactly zero hull energy mask ranking improvements under top-decile metrics; continuous rank correlation shows complementary improvement. Enrichment outputs, dataset inventory, and evaluation scripts will be released to allow independent verification of reported metrics without requiring access to the proprietary scoring engine. These results support Gamma Base as a deterministic pre-DFT prioritization layer, not as a replacement for DFT or a predictor of absolute properties.

papers.title: Lipoic Acid Without the Side Chain: Sublimable Homopolymers and Degradable Copolymers Based on 1,2-Dithiolane
papers.abstract: Depolymerization, the complete degradation of a polymer into its monomers, is of great interest for the development of circular materials. But current depolymerizations require high temperatures, suffer from low monomer recovery, and/or require a separate repolymerization step. Herein, unsubstituted 1,2-dithiolane, which is unstable in pure form, was successfully prepared, stored, and polymerized in solution. Poly(1,2-dithiolane), i.e., poly(trimethylene disulfide), was prepared through radical and cationic ring-opening polymerization procedures in solution, but also, leveraging the monomer instability, upon evaporation of a monomer solution. Poly(1,2-dithiolane) depolymerized efficiently to monomer when heated to 90 °C. Uniquely, the monomer was gaseous at this temperature and spontaneously repolymerized into a solid polymer upon cooling. The resulting polymer could be sublimed repeatedly. The widespread applicability was demonstrated through depositing insoluble hydrophobic waterproof coatings, the thermal removal of such coatings, and the purification of a contaminated polymer through sublimation. Additionally, 1,2-dithiolane was found to undergo radical ring-opening copolymerization with styrene, acrylates, vinyl acetate, and methyl methacrylate introducing cleavable S–S and C–S bonds into the backbone. Key requirements for the development of other sublimable polymers are discussed and anticipated to lead to the development of tailored depolymerizable circular materials.

papers.title: The role of terminal heavy chalcogenide ligands in enabling hydride transfer reactivity of W=E (E = S, Se) models for molybdenum hydroxylases
papers.abstract: Whereas molybdenum-dependent hydroxylases in the xanthine oxidase family catalyze site-selective C–H hydroxylation reactions utilizing terminal molybdenum sulfide (Mo=S) active sites, certain variants such as nicotinate dehydrogenase (NDH) replace the sulfide ligand by a selenide (Mo=Se) to enable activation of less reactive C–H bonds. To probe the origins of this dependence on terminal chalcogenide identity, we prepared and crystallographically characterized a synthetic model complex of the NDH active site, [(bdt)W(O)2Se]2-, a dioxotungsten(VI) selenide complex supported by benzene-1,2-dithiolate (bdt), for comparison to the previously reported [(bdt)W(O)3]2- and [(bdt)W(O)2S]2- analogues. Electronic structure analyses combining experimental UV-Vis spectroscopy and DFT calculations indicate that replacement of terminal oxo ligands by heavier chalcogenides introduces accessible low-energy acceptor orbitals associated with more spatially distributed W=E (E = S, Se) bonding interactions. Treatment of the terminal selenido and sulfido complexes with BH4– led to reduced tungsten products accompanied by liberation of free hydroselenide (HSe–) and hydrosulfide (HS–), respectively, whereas the corresponding trioxo analogue was unreactive under analogous conditions. These findings provide direct experimental support for

papers.title: A Novel Operando Tool for Mechanochemistry: NQR spectroscopy
papers.abstract: In this contribution we present for the first time an operando study of mechanochemical syntheses relying on Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance spectroscopy (NQR). This method represents, to date, the best functional alternative to NMR spectroscopy for the real-time monitoring of ball-milling (BM) syntheses. Two mechanochemical syntheses were followed in operando mode by NQR, namely the formation of a halogen-bonded co-crystal and the preparation of a hybrid perovskite, demonstrating potential applications of this novel technique, as well as its complementarity to more conventional operando methods used in mechanochemistry. Lastly, we show that our BM-NQR set-up can also be used in real-time to follow the temperature evolution directly inside the milling jar.

papers.title: π-Conjugation Mediates Competing J12–J13 Interactions at the Nanometric Scale in Linear Fe(III) Porphyrin Trimers
papers.abstract: The control of spin-spin interactions is a central challenge in designing materials for quantum technologies. A promising avenue for increasing magnetic coupling between spin centers is to connect them via a delocalized π-conjugated system. Here, we synthesized a family of porphyrins (monomer, dimers and trimers) with high-spin Fe III centers and studied their magnetic interactions. The linearly fused Fe(III)Cl porphyrin trimers exhibit nearest neighbor and second neighbor couplings of the same sign and order of magnitude ( J 12 = –24.3 GHz; J 13 = –10.8 GHz) between spin centers at 0.84 nm and 1.7 nm, respectively. These antiferromagnetic interactions lead to frustration, realizing a nontrivial Heisenberg spin system. The persistence of the long-range exchange coupling ( J 13 ) demonstrates that π-mediation is effective despite the spin polarization of the π-system induced by the central iron center. This work establishes a design principle for constructing non-trivial antiferromagnetic Heisenberg spin chains in which metal spin centers interact over several nanometers.

papers.title: Beyond Numerical Hallucination: Context-Alignment Failures in LLM-Assisted Quantum Dot Synthesis Literature Curation
papers.abstract: Reliability work for LLM-assisted materials literature curation has focused on numerical hallucination — fabrication of values absent from source documents. Here we define a recurrent residual failure class, context-alignment failure: cases in which extracted values are source-supported but bound to the wrong sample identity, synthesis stage, measurement state, or source modality. We developed a provenance-preserving four-layer curation workflow with semantic guardrails and human truth-gate review, applied to InP and I–III–VI quantum dot synthesis literature. Analysis of 56 logged curation incidents partitioned residual failures into four families — sample binding, stage-state assignment, source linkage, and pipeline metadata — with three families recurrent in both corpora. Twenty semantic guardrails were evaluated on the retrospective replay set; every logged incident matched at least one guardrail tier, a retrospective taxonomy-completeness result over the observed incident set rather than a prospective claim of error prevention or deterministic per-call replay. No incident in the post-commit residual pool was classified as pure numerical hallucination under the prespecified taxonomy; pre-extraction starter failures intercepted by guardrail G01 are reported separately. The workflow was evaluated on a 247-record method-validation corpus spanning 153 papers; an intra-rater stability check yielded 76.1% exact agreement (Wilson 95% CI 72.2–79.6%) and 83.5% exact+near agreement across 510 field-value pairs. Auditable LLM-assisted materials curation therefore requires provenance-preserving context binding beyond numerical fact-checking. As general-purpose large language models are increasingly used to extract scientific information from materials synthesis literature, context-alignment failure operates as an application-facing reliability ceiling for LLM-assisted curation that is separable from numerical hallucination.

papers.title: A biocompatible workflow for in vivo spin imaging using charge-engineered polyglycerol nanodiamonds
papers.abstract: Surface condition critically influences the biological labeling and performance of nanodiamond (ND) quantum sensors hosting nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spins. Polyglycerol (PG) grafting improves colloidal stability and suppresses nonspecific biomolecular adsorption, but can also reduce intestinal retention, making sufficient ND loading a key challenge for in vivo optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) imaging. Here, we introduce PG-grafted NDs with different terminal groups,–COOH, SO3Na, and NH2, to investigate charge-dependent biocompatibility for whole-intestinal ODMR imaging in Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans). Positively charged PG-NH2 NDs exhibit the highest intestinal retention in C. elegans without detectable toxicity, while maintaining bright fluorescence and stable NV spin signals. Combined with an adaptive masking algorithm to remove halo artifacts resulting from strong fluorescence, this labeling strategy enables reliable two-dimensional in vivo spin-active fluorescence imaging over the entire worm body. These findings identify surface-charge engineering of PG-grafted NDs as a practical strategy for establishing bright and biocompatible workflows for quantum-sensor-based bioimaging.

papers.title: Physiology-Informed Calibration of hERG Cardiotoxicity Predictions via Conformal Prediction
papers.abstract: Drug-induced blockade of the hERG (KCNH2) potassium channel is the leading proximal cause of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes, and is a standard component of preclinical cardiac safety filings International Council for Harmon-isation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use [2005]. Most published hERG classifiers report AUROC alone and emit uncalibrated point probabilities. We pair a chemistry baseline (CatBoost on the MapLight ECFP4 ⊕ Avalon ⊕ RDKit-200d stack Therapeutics Data Commons [2024]) with eight biomarkers derived per compound from O’Hara–Rudy 2011 ventricular simulations O’Hara et al. [2011], and wrap the fusion model in cross-conformal prediction (CV+, LAC method Sadinle et al. [2019], Taquet et al. [2022]). On the TDC hERG benchmark Huang et al. [2021] (523 train / 132 test) we report three honest findings, replicated across five seeds. (1) Fusion does not improve discrimination—5-seed AUROC 0.842 ± 0.007 vs chem-only 0.846 ± 0.008—an outcome we explain analytically: under the current Hill bridge each biomarker is a deterministic monotone transform of the chemistry probability, so monotonerank metrics are invariant. (2) Calibration improves substantially: 15-bin ECE drops from 0.111 ± 0.006 to 0.049 ± 0.007 (56% relative reduction, roughly an order of magnitude larger than either model’s per-seed std). (3) CV+ conformal yields empirically valid coverage (0.902 at α = 0.10, 0.932 at α = 0.05) with average prediction-set size 1.21 at α = 0.10—i.e. roughly 79% of test compounds receive a confident singleton prediction at the 90% nominal coverage level. The test set is small (n = 132); we therefore emphasize seed-averaged effect sizes over single-seed point estimates. The Hill bridge is a deliberately simple two-anchor proxy; a learned IC50 regressor with multi-channel CiPA simulation would unlock AUROC gains this study does not attempt to claim.

papers.title: Formal meta-C−H Acylation of Pyridines through N-Heterocyclic Carbene and Photoredox Dual Catalysis
papers.abstract: Incorporating an acyl group onto a pyridine ring without pre-installed transformable functional groups is particularly attractive in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. While established methods allows for acylation at ortho- or para-positions, selective meta-C−H acylation remains an unsolved problem. Here, we report a mild protocol meta-C−H acylation of pyridines via redox-neutral temporary dearomatization. The sequence involves tandem cycloadditive dearomatization, synergistic N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)/photoredox-catalyzed C−H acylation, and acid-promoted rearomatization. Mechanistical investigations, including experimental studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support a pathway involving the concurrent generation of oxazino-pyridinederived allylic-type radicals and acyl azolium radicals, followed by their radical−radical cross-coupling.

papers.title: A Chiral MOF Coupling Structural Order with Spin-Selective Catalysis for Oxygen Evolution Reaction
papers.abstract: The efficiency of Electrochemical Water Splitting (EWS) can be improved exploiting spin-polarized currents produced by chiral materials through the Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect. During EWS, electron spin polarization (SP) favours the formation of O 2 in its triplet ground state lowering the overpotential required to drive the Oxygen Evolution Reaction (OER). However, most systems studied so far lack of well-defined structural properties. In this work, a family of nickel(II)-based coordination polymers exhibiting low (Ni-L1), intermediate (Ni-L2), and high (Ni-L3) crystallinity were prepared by solvothermal synthesis using 1,4-benzenedicarboxylic acid ligands (H 2 L) functionalized with both achiral (L=A) and chiral (L=C) alkoxy side chains. Ni-L3 are 2D Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) composed by sheets of hexanickel(II) metallacrown subunits. The Ni-C materials show asymmetric SP accompanied by enhanced catalytic activity during OER as compared with their Ni-A counterparts. Moreover, the largest values of SP (~50%) and OER enhancement are observed in the most crystalline samples Ni-C2 and Ni-C3, although these materials and their achiral analogues retain ~40% and ~25% of intact alkoxy groups, respectively. Our work demonstrates that long-range order has a determining role in SP, indicating that chiral MOFs are ideal system to investigate CISS effect through structureproperties correlation studies.

papers.title: Plasma Protein Association with High Drug-Loaded Polymer Micelles: An Atomistic Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Polymeric micelles are widely studied drug delivery platforms whose interactions with plasma proteins influence in vivo performance. However, the combined effects of non-pEG hydrophilic coronas and high drug loading on protein adsorption remain poorly understood. We performed all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the association of three plasma proteins: apolipoprotein E (ApoE), human serum albumin (HSA), and immunoglobulin G (IgG), with curcumin-loaded ABA triblock copolymer micelles. To isolate corona effects, micelles shared an hydrophobic core chemistry and differed only in the hydrophilic A-block: poly(ethylene glycol) (pEG), poly(N,N-dimethylacrylamide) (pDMAA), or poly(sarcosine) (pSAR). Two drug loadings (20% and 60% drug/polymer mass ratio) were examined. Binding was assessed via contact areas, hydrogen bonds, and interaction energies. pEG micelles showed the strongest protein association. pDMAA and pSAR exhibited weaker, surface-limited interactions. These simulations provide molecular-level insight into protein adsorption on drug-loaded polymeric micelles and compare alternative hydrophilic A-blocks to pEG.

papers.title: Multi-element analysis of Bordeaux red wines by tandem ICP-mass spectrometry for objective verification of their protected designation of origin using chemometrics
papers.abstract: For French wine, the label “Appellation d’Origine Contrôlée (AOC)” not only indicates that the grapes used come exclusively from a specific geographical area, but also guarantees a certain quality and terroir notion expected from a wine carrying such AOC label. To counter potential fraud, objective verification of the geographical origin of AOC-labeled wines is of crucial importance. We investigated whether the trace elemental composition of red wines from the Bordeaux wine region determined by tandem ICPmass spectrometry can be used for this purpose. Red wines from five appellations, i.e., the AOCs Pomerol, Saint-Émilion (Grand Cru), Médoc, Graves, and Côtes de Bourg, have been analysed for their trace element composition and the data thus obtained were processed with chemometrics. This provided a robust differentiation between subregions – Garonne (AOC Médoc and AOC Graves), Libournais (AOC Pomerol and AOC Saint-Émilion), and AOC Côtes de Bourg – in Bordeaux, and individual AOC labels.

papers.title: Biomimetic Phosphonate Functionalization of Fisetin Derivatives: An In Silico Approach Toward Targeting the XRCC1 BRCT1 Domain
papers.abstract: Background: XRCC1 is a scaffold protein involved in the Base Excision Repair (BER) pathway and plays a central role in coordinating DNA repair machinery. Elevated XRCC1 expression has been associated with resistance to radiotherapy and DNA-damaging chemotherapeutics in multiple cancers. Because XRCC1 BRCT domains recognize phosphorylated motifs on interacting proteins, targeting these phosphopeptide-recognition interfaces may represent a promising strategy for disrupting DNA repair signaling. Fisetin, a naturally occurring dietary flavonoid, possesses reported anticancer and pro-apoptotic properties; however, its scaffold may benefit from rational structural optimization for improved protein–protein interaction targeting. Methods: In this study, an in silico rational drug design strategy was used to generate phosphonate-functionalized fisetin derivatives. Using RDKit-assisted ligand engineering and SMINA molecular docking, hydroxyl groups at the 3- and 7-positions of fisetin were substituted with phosphonate moieties ) to generate biomimetic phosphopeptide-inspired analogs. Docking simulations were performed against the XRCC1 BRCT1 domain (PDB ID: 2D8M) using blind docking protocols centered on the predicted binding cleft. Results: Wild-type fisetin demonstrated a baseline binding affinity of toward the XRCC1 BRCT1 domain. Both phosphonate-modified derivatives exhibited improved predicted binding affinities, with the 3-phosphonate and 7-phosphonate analogs achieving docking scores of . Structural interaction analysis suggested favorable electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions between the phosphonate groups and positively charged residues within the BRCT1 binding pocket, supporting the proposed biomimetic recognition mechanism. Conclusion: The incorporation of phosphonate functional groups onto the fisetin scaffold modestly improved the predicted binding affinity toward the XRCC1 BRCT1 domain, supporting the feasibility of biomimetic phosphopeptide-inspired flavonoid optimization for targeting DNA repair-associated protein interfaces. These findings identify phosphonate-modified fisetin derivatives as promising computational lead scaffolds for further molecular dynamics, ADMET profiling, and experimental validation studies.

papers.title: Potential-averaged ∆SCF methods: underlying formalism and evaluation of accuracy of excitation energies
papers.abstract: Several new ∆SCF (∆-Self-Consistent-Field) methods to calculate energies of excited electronic states within a density-functional framework are presented. Like ∆SCF methods in general, the new methods have a firm formal basis in the fundamental density theorem and the associated generalizedadiabatic-connection Kohn-Sham (GAC-KS) formalism derived in Phys. Rev. A 59, 3359 (1999). The GAC-KS formalism is elucidated, its meaning as a formal justification of ∆SCF methods is explained, and its relation to the optimized effective potential (OEP) method is discussed. Four ∆SCF approaches employing the OEP method are presented that differ by the treatment of open shells and states that cannot be represented by a single Slater determinant. From these four parent KS-OEP methods, four simplified methods are derived. One is the well-known unrestricted Kohn-Sham (UKS) method commonly used in ∆SCF calculation, the other three new methods replace the OEP step by a simple averaging of exchange-correlation potentials and are named potential-averaged Kohn-Sham (pa-KS) methods. The pa-KS methods, as well as their parent KS-OEP methods, are free of spin contamination, and all yield more accurate singlet and triplet excitation energies than the standard UKS method. Interestingly, the pa-KS methods are slightly more accurate than their parent KS-OEP methods. Because pa-KS methods require minimal implementation effort in existing KS codes while outperforming time-dependent density-functional methods, they are highly promising for practical applications.

papers.title: Accelerated Dissolution of CuFeS2 under Anodic Polarization in Aqueous Solution of Carboxylic Acid
papers.abstract: The slow dissolution of chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) limits the efficiency of hydrometallurgical copper extraction. Here, we investigate the anodic dissolution behavior of CuFeS2 in aqueous electrolytes capable of generating free radicals. Linear sweep voltammetry and electrolysis at a constant potential reveal that acetate- and propionate-based aqueous solutions significantly enhance anodic currents and dissolution rates of CuFeS2. Acetate solutions show the highest efficiency, as confirmed by ICP-OES analysis, while suppressing sulfur-rich passivation. Surface analyses by SEM and EDS indicate substantial morphological evolution during dissolution. The electrolytic solutions that are active for CuFeS2 anodic dissolution are also known as those for Kolbe-type reactions, suggesting radical species being formed under anodic polarization. Furthermore, the dissolution rate exhibits a clear pH dependence, which is consistent with the trend observed in the Kolbe-type reactions. These results demonstrate an important role of free radicals in the wet chemical process of minerals and provide a new strategy for improving hydrometallurgical processes.

papers.title: Chromatograms: A modular infrastructure for scalable chromatographic data handling in R
papers.abstract: Analysis of liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC–MS) data in metabolomics, proteomics and related fields typically involves inspecting, filtering, and quality-assessing chromatographic regions extracted from raw files. In R, xcms provides the key infrastructure for efficient large-scale LC-MS analysis, but for this particular task it is limited due to the way chromatographic data is handled. We present Chromatograms, an open-source R/Bioconductor package and a core component of the R for Mass Spectrometry ecosystem, which introduces a flexible infrastructure for chromatographic data with a pluggable backend system and a lazy evaluation processing queue with native parallelization support. An additional function, chromExtract(), accepts a peak table produced by any external peak-picking software and returns the corresponding chromatograms extracted from the raw files, ready for downstream analysis. Benchmarks on public LC–HRMS data from MetaboLights show that Chromatograms maintains essentially constant instantiation time as the number of extracted chromatograms grows, whereas the legacy xcms implementation scales strongly with target count (a 28-fold increase from 10 to 1000 EICs) and requires substantially more memory; lazy evaluation combined with subset access delivers more than three orders of magnitude speed-up for targeted workflows. As a demonstration, peak tables produced by any upstream tool can be imported, linked to the raw files, and passed directly to MsQuality for automated peak-quality assessment, a workflow that previously required either format conversion between tools or commitment to a single processing ecosystem. Together, these features make Chromatograms a scalable, interoperable foundation for analysis of chromatographic LC–MS data in R.

papers.title: Meniscus-Driven Growth of Cobalt Hydroxide on Graphite: A Binder-Free Electrode Architecture for Alkaline Oxygen Evolution
papers.abstract: Binder-free oxygen evolution electrodes with strong catalyst-support integration are important for practical alkaline water electrolysis. Here, a cobalt hydroxide catalytic layer was grown directly on graphite through a simple open-vessel aqueous deposition route exploiting the evolving air-liquid interface during solvent evaporation. As the solution level recedes, the moving meniscus establishes a localized growth front that confines nucleation along the waterline, producing a spatially defined cobalt hydroxide band without polymer binders, surfactants, or high-pressure processing. Scanning electron microscopy reveals a platelet-dominated nanosheet morphology characteristic of the brucite-type cobalt hydroxide framework, forming a mechanically integrated catalytic layer directly on the conductive graphite substrate. In 1.0 M KOH, the electrode reaches 10 mA cm-2 at an overpotential of 339.9 mV, with an onset potential of 1.459 V versus RHE and a Tafel slope of 75.55 mV dec-1. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy gives a charge-transfer resistance of 78.24 Ω, reflecting a functional electrode-electrolyte interface, and chronopotentiometry at 10 mA cm-2 over 6 h confirms stable short-term operation. These results demonstrate that evaporation-front-mediated deposition is a viable, single-step strategy for fabricating directly integrated binder-free cobalt hydroxide electrodes with effective interfacial charge-transfer characteristics.

papers.title: Acid Strength–Dependent Oligomerization Pathways in Furan Acylation
papers.abstract: The acid-catalyzed acylation of furan with acetic anhydride to 2-acetylfuran (AF) offers a promising route for biomass valorization, yet acid-induced oligomerization limits its practical scalability. Herein, we systematically investigate the effect of acid strength on AF selectivity and oligomer formation using five liquid Brønsted acids spanning a wide Hammett acidity range (H0 ≈ −4.66 to −14.6). The AF yield exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on acid strength, rising from 77.9% to 81.1% for moderately strong acids before dropping sharply to 52.5% under superacidic conditions. Gel-permeation chromatography (GPC) revealed that oligomer molecular weight increases monotonically with acid strength, while the oligomer fraction mirrors the non-monotonic AF yield trend. High-resolution LC–ESI–MS/MS identified diacetylfuran (DAF) as the dominant side product and distinguishes two mechanistically distinct oligomer families: those arising from nucleophilic substitution at the carbonyl group (NSCO) and those from ring substitution (NSRO), the latter emerging prominently only under strongly acidic conditions. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that activation free-energy barriers for AF formation, DAF formation, and oligomerization initiation scale linearly with catalyst deprotonation energy with statistically indistinguishable slopes, indicating that increasing acid strength uniformly accelerates both productive and unproductive pathways. These findings demonstrate that the observed selectivity behavior originates from a coupled interplay of kinetic and thermodynamic factors, and that acid-strength tuning alone is insufficient to suppress oligomerization.

papers.title: Predicting solubility curves in solvent mixtures using thermodynamic cycles and machine learning
papers.abstract: Predicting solubility limits of neutral organic compounds in solvent mixtures is crucial across chemical engineering, pharmaceuticals, environmental science, and biomedical research. Understanding solute interactions with solvent combinations at varying temperatures enables flexible solvent tailoring in drug development. Machine learning has shown great potential for solvent screening, offering alternatives to costly experimental measurements, yet existing approaches remain limited to single-solvent systems. In this work, we extend two previously developed machine learning models, SolProp and FusionCycle, to handle mixed-solvent systems, evaluating them against conventional machine learning models similarly adapted for mixtures. These methodologies are broadly categorized as Thermo-ML, trained on solubility-related properties via thermodynamic cycles, and Direct-ML, trained directly on solubility data. Models are benchmarked on a dataset of approximately 126,831 experimental solubility measurements in binary solvents, with FusionCycle-mix achieving a root-mean-square error below 1 log unit, demonstrating strong predictive performance in complex multi component systems.

papers.title: Revisiting Deep Learning DTA Methods from the Dataset Viewpoint
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a study revisiting deep learning drug-target affinity models, which are otherwise used as benchmark methods in the literature to compare more complex and heavy-weighted architectures. We focus on training and testing these models using pKd values from BindingDB, a dataset that presents binding affinity information of a high variety of ligans and proteins. These activity data need a proper pre-treatment and curation prior to actually using them for production tasks, a factor that is often overlooked in the literature. We show that a combination of a thorough curation of the dataset and a proper hyperparameter tuning of slight modifications of the revisited models (e.g, by using pretrained protein embeddings to describe the proteins) provides beyond state of the art performances at a much lower computational cost, with respect to more demanding deep learning models. We study the distributions of the protein and ligand learned (or eventually, pre-trained) embeddings, to observe how they classify the proteins depending on the (super)families they belong to (for the former), and how they distribute in the embedding space depending on the values of their binding affinities, with respect to a given protein (for the latter). We take advantage of the graph representations of the ligands to further approach explainability at an atom-wise level, by computing the directional derivative of the model with respect to each of the atoms of a ligand. This method, unlike other derivative-based approaches such as Grad-CAM and variants, turns out to be extremely useful for regression tasks of binding affinities, as this provides direct means of assessing which atoms contribute to an increase/decrease of the binding affinity, depending on both the sign of the directional derivative, and on its absolute value-an indication of how steep the function is with respect to each atom.

papers.title: Ruthenium(II) Complexes with Styryl-Derivatized Bipyridine Ligands for Two Photon Absorption and Photodynamic Therapy
papers.abstract: Cancer remains a major global health challenge, and the limitations of conventional therapies continue to motivate more selective treatment strategies. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) relies on the light-triggered generation of reactive oxygen species, making the design of excited-state photosensitizers central to its efficacy. Here, π-extended Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes bearing stilbene-functionalized bipyridine ligands were prepared to examine structure–property–activity relationships for one- and two-photon PDT. Variation of substituent electronics (OMe vs NMe2) and the monodentate ligand (Cl- vs SCN-) influenced singlet oxygen quantum yields (ΦΔ), lipophilicity [Log(Do/w)], excited-state emission, two-photon absorption, and light-dependent cytotoxicity in SK-MEL-28 cells. The NMe2 derivatives generally showed stronger photodynamic performance than the OMe analogs, while SCN substitution increased lipophilicity and modulated photophysical behavior. Two-photon absorption (2PA) studies showed moderate 2PA responses for 1b and 2b in the 700–800 nm region, supporting potential NIR activation. Phototoxicity decreased under hypoxia but remained measurable, consistent with an oxygen-dependent PDT mechanism.

papers.title: Formulation Optimization: Machine Learning and Molecular Dynamics for Accelerated Discovery
papers.abstract: The design of chemical mixtures, or formulations, is a critical yet challenging aspect of materials science due to the combinatorial explosion of possible ingredient and composition variations. Traditional trial-and-error methods are costly, especially when optimizing for multiple target properties concurrently. To accelerate formulation discovery, we developed a multiparameter, hierarchical optimization framework that integrates high-throughput machine learning (ML) predictions with sophisticated search algorithms. We first trained highly accurate ML models to predict properties such as density and heat of vaporization from chemical structure and composition using a large dataset of simulated solvent mixtures. We then rigorously benchmarked various optimization algorithms. For composition optimization, the differential evolution algorithm was identified as the most robust and efficient method, rapidly identifying optimal compositions with minimal ML prediction calls. For ingredient selection, a genetic algorithm (GA) significantly outperformed brute force, random, and Bayesian optimization approaches, finding a much higher proportion of top-performing formulations with the fewest samples. By coupling GA for ingredient selection with differential evolution for composition refinement, the hierarchical workflow successfully maximized a multiparameter optimization score across diverse materials applications, including minimizing solvent viscosity, maximizing drug solubility, and maximizing motor octane number. Representative candidates from the lowest, middle, and highest scoring ranges when minimizing viscosity were subsequently evaluated using classical molecular dynamics simulations, validating the prediction trends made by the data-driven optimization approach. This work highlights a robust, intelligent, and rapid computer-aided workflow for navigating the complex design space of chemical mixtures, minimizing the need for extensive physical experimentation and accelerating the discovery of high-performing, tailored formulations.

papers.title: Activation-Induced Turbostratic Ordering in pDCPD-Derived Hard Carbon Enables Stable Carbonate-Based Sodium-Ion Storage
papers.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries are widely considered a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries, due to the abundance and low cost of their raw materials. However, the development of high-performance and cost-effective electrode materials remains a significant challenge, particularly when competing with lithium iron phosphate systems. Herein, we present a hard carbon material derived from readily available poly(dicyclopentadiene) for use as a negative electrode in SIBs. This study investigates the influence of carbonization temperature and subsequent CO2 activation on the HC’s structure and electrochemical performance. The impact of activation proved to be dependent upon the first stage carbonization temperature, creating greater local ordering for samples carbonized at higher temperatures. The removal of defects and decrease in average graphitic nano-domain length resulted in a turbostratic structure that enhanced rate performance and capacity retention when compared with non-activated samples. The optimized HC exhibits a reversible capacity of 352 mAh/g at 0.1 C and a capacity retention of 88.1% after 500 cycles with a carbonate based electrolyte. This work introduces a cost-effective approach for producing hard carbon materials with distinctive nanostructure and provides valuable insights into achieving long cycle life in sodium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Efficiently computing physical charging free energies at all intermediate states along alchemical pathways
papers.abstract: Many problems in chemistry and biology involve charging free energy calculations for partially or fully charged atoms within solvation free energy calculations. One way is to use standard alchemical free energy methods, but they can be expensive, and they don’t give useful atom-wise or site-specific decompositions. Another way is bottom-up approaches, which compute solvation free energies from atomistic level components and use accurate additivity rules, but they require large precomputed databases. Here, we give a fast way to generate such databases, using a λ-resolved free energy (λFE) strategy. By resolving physical charging free energies at all intermediate λ values from a single alchemical free energy simulation, λFE eliminates the need for separate alchemical charging calculations for atom types that differ only in their charge. We show it is robust across a range of charges, LJ parameters, system sizes, and three water models (TIP3P, TIP4P/EW, and TIP4P/2005). It reduces the computational cost of creating a precomputed database by an order of magnitude.

papers.title: Generalized Turnstile Rotation: Formulation, Visualization, Workflow Implementation, and Application for Modeling Polytopal Rearrangements
Hierarchical chiral self-assembly of nanocylinders composed of sequence-defined mesogenic dimers
papers.abstract: Chiral ensembles can arise through supramolecular curvature that resolves geometric frustrations in the packing of bent, achiral molecular or colloidal building blocks. Here, we leverage orthogonal protection-deprotection click chemistry to create sequence-defined mesogenic heterodimers exhibiting emergent chirality. We compare the hierarchical self-assembly of the synthesized asymmetric, achiral heterodimers, which differ only in the position of a methyl substituent. Both dimers form chiral spherulites composed of nanocylinders. However, the detailed arrangement of nanocylinders depends on the position of the methyl substituent and the crystallization conditions. Despite the chemical similarity, in one dimer, two crystalline forms are optically active. They form conglomerates of dextrorotatory and levorotatory spherulites. The other dimer forms more highly anisotropic spherulites that mask circular birefringence arising from the misorientation of nanocylinders, while mapping of nanocylinder directors reveals a sense at the spherulite surface. We propose that differences in nanocylinder arrangements may arise from changes in nanocylinder curvature and dimensions dictated by the methyl substituent position, inducing chirality. These results demonstrate multiscale hierarchical assembly relevant to dense systems of tubular structures and highlight the role of sequence and molecular design in directing the bottom-up hierarchical self-assembly and chirality of mesogenic systems.

papers.title: Activity Descriptors of Mo2C-based Catalysts for C-OH Bond Activation
papers.abstract: Deriving structure-activity relationships is crucial for designing efficient catalysts. To aid in this quest, data-driven methods such as machine learning (ML) are emerging to unravel the complicated multi-dimensional structure–activity relationships in heterogeneous catalysis. In this work, we incorporate ML tools with accurate density functional theory (DFT) energetics, electronic and geometric features to establish the structure-activity relationships in the context of designing efficient orthorhombic molybdenum carbide (Mo2C)-based catalysts for hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) reaction. Our previous studies show that C-OH activation is the rate-determining step in the HDO reaction over Mo2C (101) surface. In this work, DFT is used to obtain accurate barriers (Ea), reaction energy (∆E) for the C-OH activation in HDO over the most stable and meta-stable facets of Mo2C and transition metal doped Mo2C. Then we constructed the feature database of all structures of Mo2C based catalysts and employed scikit-learn’s ML models to obtain the best primary features correlating with the activity (Ea). The results show that Kernal Ridge Regression (KRR) gives the best ML model for predicting Ea of C-OH bond breaking (on unseen data) with a mean test RMSE of 0.25 eV. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses for all the ML models was combined in a systematic manner to reveal that ∆E, d-band center, and d MC are the most important features governing the activity of Mo2C-based catalysts for C-OH bond activation. Finally, SISSO was used to validate the SHAP results, and to obtain a 2-dimensional generic descriptor which is also physically interpretable to some extent. This SISSO model yielded test RMSE score of 0.14 eV, which is well below the DFT level error margin (±0.20 eV).

papers.title: Aggregation-induced emission luminogens based on restriction of intramolecular vibration
papers.abstract: Over the past two decades, high-performance materials with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics have emerged as indispensable components in modern functional materials science. Among them, AIEgens based on the restriction of intramolecular rotation (RIR) mechanism have been thoroughly studied and developed. AIEgens operating via the restriction of intramolecular vibration (RIV) mechanism have emerged as a promising yet underexplored class; however, they remain constrained by a limited repertoire of molecular scaffolds and poorly defined design principles. This review categorizes reported RIV-type AIEgens into four types based on a geometry-oriented classification of molecular deformation modes: structural inversion driven by aromaticity, bending, twisting, and molecular bond vibration. The representative structures and underlying RIV mechanisms are elaborated in detail, aiming to establish a framework for the rational design and functional expansion of next-generation RIV-type AIEgens, with the ultimate goal of broadening their applications in optoelectronics and biomaterials.

papers.title: Accurate and Precise Trace-Level Cytokine Quantification in Blood: An Internal-Standard-Integrated Digital SERS Immunoassay for Detecting Immune Dysregulation in Major Depressive Disorder
papers.abstract: Accurate and precise quantification of trace-level cytokines in complex biological matrices remains challenging, limiting their use as longitudinal biomarkers in clinical studies. Here, we present a nanotechnology-enabled surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) platform incorporating an internal standard (IS) for digital, attomolar-level multiplex cytokine quantification. This platform enables precise digital trace-level detection of IL-1β, IL-6, IL-12, and TNF-α. Using an orthogonal recombinant protein IS to correct assay- and SERS-related variability, this platform addresses key barriers to reliable trace-protein measurements and broader clinical adoption. Incorporation of the IS reduced the inter-replicate coefficient of variation from ~40 - 60% to 2 - 3%, and improved accuracy to ~95 - 105%, enabling robust cytokine quantification in human plasma. Compared with a widely used clinical electrochemiluminescence (ECL) assay, our internal-standard-integrated chip enables accurate and precise quantification while maintaining multiplex capability, consistently detecting cytokine levels near or below ECL-defined quantification limits. We demonstrate the potential clinical utility of this analytical approach in mood disorders, where aberrant immune activation and low-level inflammation have been implicated, particularly in major depressive disorder (MDD). Spike-in experiments and measurements in plasma samples from individuals with MDD validate the chip’s analytical performance and support its potential for longitudinal monitoring of immune activation in clinical cohorts.

papers.title: Engineering Electronic Asymmetry in Geometrically Symmetric Tri-Indium Molecules for N-O Bond Activation
papers.abstract: Precise asymmetric active sites can promote the activation of inert N-O bonds for catalytic nitrogen oxide reduction (NOxRR), yet their construction and underlying physical activation principles remain elusive. Here, by screening 16 molecular architectures via density functional theory (DFT), we identify a structurally precise homonuclear p-block tri-indium molecule as an exceptional catalyst for NO-to-NH3 conversion. Despite its geometrically symmetric framework, local coordination disparity induces profound electronic asymmetry. We elucidate the fundamental activation principle: a synergistic push-pull effect where an electron-deficient central indium serves as a Lewis acidic docking site, while electron-rich terminal indiums act as an electron reservoir. This multi-site synergy drives a massive 0.71 |e| charge transfer into the NO π* antibonding orbital, elongating the N-O bond to 1.26 Å and enabling a remarkably low thermodynamic limiting barrier of 0.14 eV. Furthermore, the tri-indium cluster effectively suppresses the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) through a strong competitive adsorption advantage of NO over both protons and water. This study establishes coordination-engineered p-block clusters as a highly controllable paradigm for sustainable nitrogen cycling.

papers.title: Beyond Two-Body Correlations: The Many-body, Excess Entropy of Water Across the Entire Phase Diagram
papers.abstract: The excess entropy is a fundamental thermodynamic variable for understanding the properties and anomalous behavior of liquid water. Barring computationally intensive methods, such as thermodynamic integration, rapid and accurate methods for calculating the excess entropy remains elusive. Previous attempts for estimating the excess entropy have relied on solely calculating the 2-body translational entropy, and more rarely, additional calculations of the 2-body orientational entropy. In this work, we demonstrate that the Two-Phase Thermodynamics (2PT) method provides a robust, dynamics-based route to estimating the excess entropy of liquid water across a wide range of thermodynamic conditions (220 < T < 360 K, 0.85 < ρ < 1.3 g/cm3). By analyzing the vibrational density of states obtained from molecular dynamics simulations, 2PT captures contributions beyond the two-body approximation without requiring explicit higher-order correlation functions. We show that while the total two-body entropy appears to reproduces experiments near ambient conditions, we show that this is largely due to fortuitous cancellation of error, and it fails to describe trends across the full phase diagram, particularly in regimes where many-body correlations become significant. In contrast, the 2PT-derived excess entropy more faithfully reproduces the phase-dependent trends observed in reference data. These results highlight limitations of pair-correlation-based entropy estimators and establish 2PT as a computationally efficient alternative for capturing many-body effects in complex liquids, while motivating further extensions beyond its hard-sphere-based partitioning in regimes of strongly non-Markovian dynamics.

papers.title: Ioniza on Poten al of JP-10 Fuel: A First-Principles Study Addressing a 50-Year Gap in Experimental Data
papers.abstract: The ionization potential of exo-tetrahydrodicyclopentadiene (exo-JP-10, C10H16), a strained hydrocarbon central to advanced propulsion, has remained unresolved for decades due to its cage-like structure, the inherent instability of its cation, and the absence of reliable theoretical predictions. The first ionization potential (IP) was reported once at 9.35 ± 0.05 eV in 1973 yet it has resisted consistent theoretical validation. In this study, we present the first quantitative confirmation using density functional theory (DFT) based ΔSCF, Hartree–Fock (HF), and outer valence Green’s function (OVGF) methods. The ΔSCF(DFT) and G4 composite methods well reproduces the experimental IP at 9.31 eV and 9.27 eV, respectively, whereas Koopmans’ Theorem (HF) and standard OVGF systematically overestimate the value. The second-order OVGF method (OVGF(2)) not only yields a first IP for JP-10 that is consistent with the ΔSCF result, but also provides outer-valence IPs extending up to 17.5 eV. Orbital analysis reveals that ionization perturbs α electrons more strongly than β in the valence space (a β electron is removed at ionization), as well as substantial shifts in the carbon 1s core electron energies. These electronic reorganizations are mirrored in the calculated 13C NMR spectrum, where the junction carbons (C1-C4) and C10, C6/C7 undergo pronounced deshielding. This study delivers the first rigorously validated theoretical value for the ionization potential of JP-10, closing a 50-year gap in understanding this high-energy-density hydrocarbon. By establishing ΔSCF as a reliable approach for characterizing unstable cations and leveraging OVGF(2) to compute outer-valence IPs up to 17.5 eV, the present study links core- and valence-level electronic reorganizations to measurable spectroscopic signatures. These insights not only 2 advance JP-10 ionization process but also deepen our understanding of strained hydrocarbon architectures, providing a foundation for the rational design of thermally stable, electronically tunable molecules for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) development and advanced propulsion systems.

papers.title: Beyond Multiscale: A Neural Network-Unified Molecular Model for Asymmetry-Free Dynamics Simulation
papers.abstract: Adaptive multiscale simulations, such as adaptive QM/MM, are indispensable for investigating complex solution dynamics but historically suffer from a fundamental dilemma: the dynamic exchange of identical solvent molecules across different model resolutions introduces a physical asymmetry. This asymmetry forces a prohibitive trade-off between severe structural distortions and the violation of Hamiltonian conservation (continuous energy drift). To definitively resolve this issue, we propose the ”Integrated Molecular Model,” a paradigm-shifting framework that mathematically unifies multiple resolutions into a single, dynamically consistent potential. By employing a neural network that takes only the multiscale weight functions as input descriptors, our model learns to systematically cancel the non-physical transition forces originating from spatial discontinuities. As a proof-of-concept, we validated this unified framework on bulk water, aqueous ionic solutions, and reactive hydronium ions. Our approach not only faithfully restores artifact-free solvation structures but also strictly conserves the Hamiltonian, enabling unprecedentedly stable, long-term simulations under the microcanonical (NVE) ensemble. Consequently, the model successfully eliminates artificial thermostat-induced breathing modes, allowing for the rigorous evaluation of intrinsic dynamical properties such as diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, owing to its physically informed network design, the correction potential introduces less than 2\% additional computational overhead and demonstrates remarkable zero-shot transferability across chemically similar ionic species. By fundamentally eradicating the inherent asymmetry of adaptive multiscale modeling, this highly scalable framework establishes a robust foundation for high-fidelity simulations of complex condensed-phase phenomena, including reactive dynamics at solid-liquid interfaces and ion transport in battery electrolytes.

papers.title: Dynamic Kinetic Resolution of Spirocyclopropyl Allenes in a (4+3)-Cycloaddition Approach Toward Cyclohepta[cd]indolones
papers.abstract: An expedient approach toward the ubiquitous cyclohepta[cd]indolone scaffold employing a RhII/AgI-catalyzed (4+3)cycloaddition between a 1,3-enyne bearing an instrumental propargyl acetate and a diazooxindole is presented herein. The union of 3- and 4-atom components proceeds through a RhII-catalyzed cyclopropanation followed by a AgI-catalyzed 1,3-acetoxy rearrangement to set the stage for a [3,3]-rearrangement that engages the arene of the oxindole component resulting in a streamlined assembly of the core molecular framework. The stereoconvergence of cyclopropane and allene stereoisomers through a dynamic kinetic resolution is instrumental in achieving complete E-selective formation of the exocyclic olefin and high yields of the cycloadducts observed across a diverse array of 1,3-enynes and diazooxindole substrates.

papers.title: Toward Rational Metal-Organic Framework Design for Gallium Adsorption
papers.abstract: Gallium (Ga) is an important element for semiconductor and optoelectronic applications. Yet, production of high-purity Ga and a reliable supply chain remain challenging due to limited primary resources and geopolitical factors, which highlights recovery of Ga from wastewater as an alternative avenue to maintain a viable Ga supply chain. However, Ga recovery remains challenging because it is commonly present at low concentrations and coexists with competing metal ions in complex aqueous systems. Adsorption has emerged as a promising strategy for Ga recovery due to its operational simplicity, technical readiness, adaptness to the existing utilities, and cost-effectiveness. Readily tunable surface chemistry of adsorbents can potentially further improve recovery performance. However, studies on metal-organic framework (MOF)-based Ga adsorbents remain relatively limited, making it difficult to establish clear design principles based only on existing MOF literature. In this mini-review, we summarize representative Ga adsorption studies across different materials, including MOFs, polymer/resin, inorganic oxides, and bio-derived/hybrid materials. By comparing their functional groups, adsorption performances, and mechanisms, we identify several common features governing Ga capture. Across these systems, Ga adsorption is primarily dominated by coordination interactions, especially involving O-donor sites such as hydroxyl, amidoxime, catechol, and hydroxamic acid groups. At the same time, pH-dependent Ga speciation, active-site accessibility, pore structure, and solution complexity strongly affect adsorption performances. These insights suggest that future MOF design should focus on integrating strong O-rich binding sites, accessible pore environments, controlled functional group distribution, and chemical stability under realistic recovery conditions. This review provides a mechanism guided perspective for translating lessons from broader adsorbent systems into the rational design of MOF-based materials for selective Ga capture.

papers.title: Core-Shell Heterojunctions based on Covalent Organic Frameworks: Ultralong-Lived Charge-Separated States and Efficient CO2 Photoreduction
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess structural tunability, high surface area, and extended delocalization of π-electrons but remain limited by challenges in constructing well-defined structure for efficient charge separation. Here, we employed a structural strategy to address this limitation through the construction of core-shell COF heterojunctions via lattice-mismatch-free epitaxial growth between isostructural but electronically distinct donor and acceptor COFs. The resulting core-shell architectures enable efficient spatial separation of photogenerated electrons and holes across well-defined heterointerfaces, while preserving high crystallinity. Nanoscale phase separation is confirmed by HAADF-EDS mapping and XPS analysis. Light-induced electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) measurements reveal significantly enhanced populations of ultralong-lived charge-separated states in the core-shell COFs compared to their single-phase counterparts, indicating suppressed charge recombination and improved charge separation. The resulting heterostructures show efficient two-electron CO 2 photoreduction to CO and HCOOH, coupled with four-electron H 2 O oxidation, thereby requiring no sacrificial agents. The results demonstrate the importance of engineered D/A interfaces in COF photocatalysis.

papers.title: ResistaMet GUI: open-source electrical characterization for Keithley 2400 series sourcemeters
papers.abstract: ResistaMet GUI is a desktop application for electrical characterization using Keithley 2400 series source measure units (SMUs) over a GPIB interface. These instruments are commonly used by electrical engineers, materials scientists, and other physical scientists to characterize electrically active devices and materials. This software is benchwritten and tested with 6 primary measurement modes: two-and four-wire resistance, constant-voltage and constantcurrent biasing for long runs (with in-run event annotations), I-V sweep, collinear 4-point probe per ASTM F84, and van der Pauw per ASTM F76 Method A. Each reading carries an instrument uncertainty propagated from the Keithley datasheet’s per-range accuracy specs, all the way through to derived quantities like sheet resistance and resistivity. An in-package Keithley simulator, calibrated against captured SCPI traces from our bench Keithley 2420 and replayed in CI, allows users to test and practice each mode without an SMU, and keeps documented hardware quirks from regressing.

papers.title: Accelerating the Bioeconomy Through UK–India Partnership: A Roadmap for Sustainable Chemicals Innovation
papers.abstract: This note presents the outcomes of workshops which were organised to examine the settings required to improve collaboration between India and UK in bio-based chemicals and sustainable innovation sectors. Cross-sector input from industry, academia and policy makers in both countries led to the identification of key barriers towards transitioning from fossil derived to bio-based chemical production. Discussion on lignin valorisation and role of specialty and commodity chemicals in this transition were presented as examples. This work draws on workshop evidence to propose a bilateral roadmap for industry partners, researchers and policymakers to accelerate this transition and collaboration. On consolidating the discussions, four main conclusions emerged, including the importance of bilateral investment, introduction of carbon pricing, long term policy certainty, as well as regulatory frameworks and shared use of open access demonstration facilities, modelled on established practices as seen in the pharmaceutical industry by organisations such as CPI and ITRI. These will be essential to scale up bio-chemical production.

papers.title: Asymmetric Radical Sulfinylation via Stereoablative Sulfinyl Radical Generation
papers.abstract: Stereogenic sulfur functional groups constitute an important class of chiral motifs with broad utility in medicinal chemistry, asymmetric synthesis, and catalysis, yet catalytic strategies for their enantioselective construction from simple and abundant precursors remain limited. We report herein a previously unexplored enantioconvergent decarboxylative sulfinylation of carboxylic acids enabled by a merger of acridine photocatalysis and cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric carbon–sulfur bond formation. This catalytic platform leverages stable N-sulfinylphthalimides as sulfinyl group transfer reagents and proceeds through a stereoablative S–N bond cleavage process that generates a sulfinyl radical under mild conditions. The method provides efficient access to chiral sulfoxides with high enantioselectivity. Mechanistic studies revealed that acridinyl radical-mediated PCET activation of the sulfinamide reagent, followed by selective co-balt‑catalyzed sulfinyl radical trapping and coupling of the resulting sulfinylcobalt intermediate with an alkyl radical collectively underpin the observed stereocontrol and efficiency. Together, these findings establish a mechanistically distinct blueprint for asymmetric radical sulfoxide synthesis and open new avenues for catalytic strategies that leverage stereoablative radical processes to access sulfur-centered stereogenic motifs.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Protein-Ligand Binding Mode Prediction with Counterfactual Pocket Perturbation
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of protein–ligand binding modes is crucial for structure-based drug discovery. However, current pose prediction methods are often integrated with binding affinity scoring functions without providing a reliable measure of the confidence or reliability of individual pose predictions. We present a hybrid docking and machine learning workflow for binding mode prediction and evaluate whether counterfactual perturbations of pocket-ligand interaction features can support uncertainty-aware pose prediction. Here, the candidate poses were generated with AutoDock Vina and ranked using a geometry-aware gradient-boosted tree model trained on PLINDER-derived protein-ligand complexes. To estimate uncertainty, we masked hydrogen-bond, hydrophobic, metal, polar, clash, and contact-shell feature groups and measured prediction sensitivity. The chemical counterfactual uncertainty detected the failed top-1 predictions with AUROC 0.895 and average precision 0.878. The selective prediction substantially improved reliability: retaining the lowest-uncertainty 50% of predictions increased top-1 success to 88.79%. These results suggest that uncertainty-aware pose prediction can provide actionable confidence estimates for docking-based binding mode prediction, and that counterfactual pocket perturbation offers a practical route toward interpretable failure detection.

papers.title: Chromatograms: A modular infrastructure for scalable chromatographic data handling in R
papers.abstract: Analysis of liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC–MS) data in metabolomics, proteomics and related fields typically involves inspecting, filtering, and quality-assessing chromatographic regions extracted from raw files. In R, xcms provides the key infrastructure for efficient large-scale LC-MS analysis, but for this particular task it is limited due to the way chromatographic data is handled. We present Chromatograms, an open-source R/Bioconductor package and a core component of the R for Mass Spectrometry ecosystem, which introduces a flexible infrastructure for chromatographic data with a pluggable backend system and a lazy evaluation processing queue with native parallelization support. An additional function, chromExtract(), accepts a peak table produced by any external peak-picking software and returns the corresponding chromatograms extracted from the raw files, ready for downstream analysis. Benchmarks on public LC–HRMS data from MetaboLights show that Chromatograms maintains essentially constant instantiation time as the number of extracted chromatograms grows, whereas the legacy xcms implementation scales strongly with target count (a 28-fold increase from 10 to 1000 EICs) and requires substantially more memory; lazy evaluation combined with subset access delivers more than three orders of magnitude speed-up for targeted workflows. As a demonstration, peak tables produced by any upstream tool can be imported, linked to the raw files, and passed directly to MsQuality for automated peak-quality assessment, a workflow that previously required either format conversion between tools or commitment to a single processing ecosystem. Together, these features make Chromatograms a scalable, interoperable foundation for analysis of chromatographic LC–MS data in R.

papers.title: Accurate Calculation of the Thermal Conductivity of Liquids from Molecular Dynamics Using a Heat Flux Decomposition Based Correction
papers.abstract: Thermal conductivity (λ ) of liquids is a critical property for numerous applications, yet classical all-atom force fields consistently overestimate it in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. This work identifies the overestimation of energies stored and transferred through bonded interactions, particularly high-frequency vibrations, as the primary cause of this inaccuracy. Using heat flux decomposition techniques, we developed a physics-informed algebraic correction model to adjust MD-predicted λ values. The model was trained on simple pure fluids and evaluated for a wide range of molecular liquids, ionic liquids (ILs), and IL/refrigerant mixtures. The correction significantly improves both qualitative and quantitative agreement with experimental data, providing a reliable and computationally efficient method for predicting thermal conductivity of liquids using standard classical all-atom force fields.

papers.title: Synthesis of Verdazyl Radicals for Anchoring to Gold Substrates
papers.abstract: Verdazyl radicals featuring thiomethyl groups at the 1 and 5 positions were synthesized employing modified conventional methodologies. Designed with appropriate anchoring groups for incorporation into molecular junctions, the verdazyl radicals were characterized using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, UV-visible spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry (CV) and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). We observed electrochemically reversible oxidation and reduction of these radicals in solution, and the correlation between gas-phase ionization and electron affinity modulations were considered by DFT calculations.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because it is an unintentional duplicate of 10.26434/chemrxiv.15003962/v2.

papers.title: Vortex-guided chirality selection in an organic single crystal
papers.abstract: Chiral symmetry breaking can produce homochirality from small biases, but how external rotational fields select handedness remains unknown. Here we show that optical vortices control the chirality produced during chiral symmetry breaking in a single crystal. A phenothiazine derivative undergoes a single-crystal-to-single-crystal transition from a racemic compound to a conglomerate with chiral selectivity exceeding 90% under optical vortices irradiation. Using polarization-resolved two-photon fluorescence, second-harmonic generation, Raman microscopy and single-crystal X-ray diffraction, we visualized the accompanying molecular rearrangement and revealed that the boundary between the achiral and chiral phases hosts an in situ racemization layer, mechanically soft and switchable to either chirality. We propose that optical torque couples to this racemization layer, thereby driving collective chirality selection and cooperative amplification as the front propagates. Our results establish rotational motion as a fundamental ingredient in the emergence and amplification of homochirality.

papers.title: Beneficial Reduction of Surface Compositional Complexity in High-Entropy Oxide Oxygen Evolution Reaction Catalysts into a Ternary Phase
papers.abstract: Cost-competitive green hydrogen production via water electrolysis is limited by the scalability and economics of electrolyzers, particularly regarding the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalyst. High-entropy oxides hold significant promise, yet the drivers of activity and stability are debated due to challenges in characterizing the catalytically relevant surface. Addressing this, we present the first surface-specific comprehensive quantification of chemical and coordination evolution in compositionally complex high-entropy Ni/Co/Fe/Mn/Cr (hydr)oxide electrocatalysts using synchrotron-based X-ray spectroscopies assisted by charge transfer multiplet calculations. An electrochemically driven surface transformation to ternary Ni/Co/Fe or Ni/Co/Mn (oxy)hydroxide in alkaline media is revealed to enable long-term efficient OER performance. This beneficial reduction in compositional complexity, and thus entropy, is induced by leaching of Cr, Mn, and Fe, enriching catalytically active octahedrally coordinated nickel and cobalt species, and is accelerated by a short-range-ordered phase (X-ray amorphous) compared to the crystalline counterpart. These findings highlight the importance of characterizing the surface chemical evolution of high-entropy materials and guide the engineering of next-generation compositionally complex transition-metal-based OER catalysts.

papers.title: AI-Driven Decoding and Targeting of Pathological Biomolecular Condensates
Carbocation-Based Proximity Labeling
papers.abstract: Photocatalytic proximity labeling platforms use localized release of reactive species to covalently label proteins near a photocatalyst, facilitating the identification of protein interactions. Singlet oxygen, Michael acceptors, radicals, nitrenes, and carbenes are currently used for labeling, with spatial resolution dictated by reactive intermediate lifetime and signal to noise limited by non-catalyzed reactivity. Here, we report a high-resolution proximity labeling platform based on photocatalytic generation of benzylic carbocations from coumarin precursors. Carbocations combine promiscuous crosslinking with limited diffusion in water (t 1/2 < 3 ns) and low non-catalyzed background labeling, properties that enable demanding applications such as small molecule target identification, binding affinity profiling, and proteinprotein interaction discovery on cell surfaces. We show that coumarin-based reagents can be used for improved identification of labeled proteins while maintaining compatibility with commonly used photocatalysts and light setups, allowing them to be used as drop-in replacements for diazirines in existing workflows.

papers.title: Deep learning-based reconstruction of low-transient GABA-edited magnetic resonance spectra for high-accuracy quantification
papers.abstract: Objective: To enable accurate γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) quantification from low signal averages in MEscher-GArwood Point-Resolved SpectroScopy (MEGA-PRESS), thereby reducing acquisition time and improving clinical applicability. Methods: A spectroscopy-oriented one-dimensional multichannel Vision Transformer was proposed for GABA+ signal reconstruction from low number of signal averages (low-NSA, 10 transients) MEGA-PRESS magnetic resonance spectra (MRS). The model removes the classification token while preserving all spectral tokens and incorporates a dedicated spectral decoder. A dual-source semisynthetic (DSS) dataset generation strategy was designed, where weighted combinations of high-NSA spectra (0.00-5.00 ppm) and their corresponding fitted GABA+ signals (2.79-3.20 ppm) were used to construct input and labels in the training data. Results: Using high-NSA (NSA160) quantification results as the reference, the proposed method reduced the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of the quantification results from 13.32 ± 3.46% (with conventional NSA10) to 3.78 ± 1.46%, with a mean reduction of 9.53% (95% CI: 7.09%–11.97%, p < 0.05). Conclusion: The proposed Transformer-based framework enables accurate reconstruction of GABA+ signals from low-NSA MEGA-PRESS data, preserving both quantitative accuracy and spectral shape. Significance: This approach substantially reduces acquisition times and facilitates faster, more practical in vivo GABA quantification in clinical and research settings.

papers.title: A Noncanonical Mechanism of Substrate Recognition by O-GlcNAc Transferase Revealed by Markov State Models and Transition State Analysis
papers.abstract: O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) modifies thousands of nuclear and cytoplasmic proteins, primarily within intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). However, there is no conserved consensus sequence at the O-GlcNAc modification sites. Traditional models suggest OGT recognizes substrates by the tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) lumen, through conserved asparagine and aspartate ladders, yet some substrates do not depend on canonical TPR-lumen recognition. Here, we use an SMG9-derived peptide to elucidate a noncanonical recognition mechanism for OGT guided by short linear motifs (SLiMs). We performed ~2.1 milliseconds of aggregate all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Using this data, we applied Transition State identification via Dispersion and vAriational principle Regularized neural networks (TS-DAR) together with Markov state models (MSMs). Our analysis reveals an induced-fit-dominant and multi-step recognition mechanism. First, the SMG9 substrate anchors at the intervening-domain (Int-D) SLiM pocket. This interaction promotes substrate engagement at a previously uncharacterized external site at the TPR-glycosyltransferase-domain (TPR-GTD) interface. This intermediate state progressively guides the O-GlcNAcylation segment, that contains unmodified O-GlcNAcylation site T114, toward the catalytic site. Transition-state ensembles further reveal that transient hydrophobic interactions facilitate this stepwise recognition process. To validate these predictions, we performed transition-state mutation simulations and biolayer interferometry (BLI) experimental measurements. Mutation of a key residue at the newly identified TPR-GTD external site (F878A) strongly impaired SMG9 binding, whereas mutations disrupting the canonical TPR asparagine ladder (N434A/N468A) produced minimal effects. Our results establish a noncanonical Int-D-engaged recognition pathway distinct from the canonical TPR-lumen recognition mode and provide a dynamic mechanistic framework for how OGT selectively recognizes flexible IDR-containing substrates.

papers.title: High-Throughput COSMO-RS Screening of Deep Eutectic Solvents for Selective Biomass Valorisation: A Sonneratia alba Case Study
papers.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DES) have emerged as promising green extraction media owing to their tuneable physicochemical properties and low environmental impact. However, the combinatorial space of possible DES formulations renders exhaustive experimental screening prohibitively resource-intensive. In this work, we report a high-throughput computational screening of 168 binary DES systems for the selective extraction of 12 primary and secondary metabolites from Sonneratia alba, a mangrove species of significant ethnopharmacological interest. These 12 evaluated metabolites, including quercetin, lignin, and cellobiose, structurally represent universal components of higher plant matrices, thereby establishing this predictive thermodynamic model as a translatable blueprint for diverse biomass upcycling applications. Thermodynamic descriptors, including infinite-dilution activity coefficients (ln γ∞), solubility capacities (C∞), and absolute selectivities (S∞), were computed across 9 molar ratios and 21 temperatures (0–100°C). Calculations utilized the COSMO-RS model parameterised via quantum chemical geometries (r2SCAN-3c) and surface charge distributions (BP86/def2-TZVP) generated within the ORCA framework, yielding an exhaustive dataset of 31,857 discrete thermodynamic state points. The opencosmorspy implementation facilitated this batch computation, proving that open-source COSMO-RS workflows represent a robust, cost-effective alternative to proprietary software. Screening identified the sodium propionate:1,3-butanediol system (3:1 molar ratio, 60°C) as the thermodynamic apex. It demonstrated a massive quercetin capacity (C∞=2.62×109) while functioning as a highly selective extraction medium, achieving absolute selectivities exceeding 1016 against lipophilic impurities. These findings provide a fundamental, physics-based blueprint for the sustainable, rational design of mangrove-derived nutraceuticals.

papers.title: Water-Soluble Luminescent Trityl Radical for Fluorescence/Magnetic Resonance Dual-Modal Imaging Probe
papers.abstract: Tris(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM) radicals are promising scaffolds for fluorescence imaging (FI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) owing to their long-wavelength emission and intrinsic paramagnetism. Incorporating donor-acceptor (D-A) architectures into TTM radicals has been an established strategy to enhance brightness and photostability of TTM radicals. However, conventional D-A type TTM radicals exhibit strong chargetransfer (CT)-dominated emission that is easily quenched in water due to accelerated non-radiative decay known as the energy-gap law. Here, we report water-soluble TTM radicals (TTM-trisTP3B and TTM-trisTP9B) which exhibit hybridized locally excited and CT character through rational modulation of the donor units and their substitution positions. New radicals exhibited high photostability and deep-red emission with photoluminescence quantum yields of 1.4% (TTM-trisTP3B, 690 nm), and 1.1% (TTM-trisTP9B, 685 nm) in water. Their dual functionality as both fluorescent probes and MRI contrast agents was demonstrated. TTM-trisTP3B was taken up by living cells, localized near the cell nucleus, and showed fluorescence. New radicals also provided a clear longitudinal relaxation time (T1)-weighted MRI contrast. This work represents the first demonstration of trityl radical functioning as practical FI/MRI dual-modal imaging probes, establishing a molecular platform without any surfactants or metals in which fluorophore and electron-spin source are unified.

papers.title: Unlocking Dormant Li⁺ Pathways Drives Fast Ion Transport in Li4Ti5O12 Oxide Spinels
papers.abstract: Li-rich lithium titanate (Li 4+ x Ti 5 O 12 , x > 0) is known for its superior ionic conductivity, yet we show that even stoichiometric Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 (LTO, x = 0), typically characterized by sluggish ion dynamics, can become a fast ion conductor without any change in Li content. Local defects, such as oxygen vacancies, introduced by vacuum treatment, without incorporating additional Li+ ions, activate a previously inaccessible 8 a -16 c -8 a diffusion pathway in non-lithiated LTO, markedly enhancing Li + mobility throughout the bulk. Using a synergistic combination of impedance spectroscopy, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), we elucidate the diffusion processes responsible for this transformation. Lithium-NMR unambiguously shows that the formerly localized Li + hopping process transforms into long-range ion transport upon vacuum treatment, evidencing the activation of extended diffusion pathways. Atomic-scale analysis reveals the structural and dynamic modifications that precondition the material for rapid Li + insertion, rendering zero-strain LTO one of the most promising anode materials for lithium-based batteries employing solid electrolytes. These findings resolve the long-standing conductivity puzzle of stoichiometric spinel LTO ( x = 0) by uncovering a previously unrecognized transport mechanism that may also operate in other spinel-type ion conductors with similar Li + distributions. This insight establishes a new route for controlling ion transport in spinel-based materials, relevant for next-generation energy storage technologies where precise control of ion dynamics is essential.

papers.title: A unifying framework for the calibration and characterization of dissolved organic matter fluorescence sensors
papers.abstract: Fluorescent dissolved organic matter (FDOM) sensors are widely used to monitor quantity and quality of dissolved organic matter (DOM). Yet, sensor calibration and characterization procedures remain inconsistent across platforms and manufacturers, hindering widespread use and interoperability of data collected.
