We make three formal contributions. First, we define the Molecular World Model (MWM) through four axioms (Universal Representation, Comparability, Physical Grounding, Predictive Completeness). Second, we introduce Molecular Acoustic Fingerprinting (MAF) as the first validated perception layer for the MWM: a unified oscillatory encoding in which the full 3D+ molecular state is represented as wave superpositions at 16,000 Hz, natively compatible with pretrained voice AI infrastructure (wav2vec2, Whisper) via a shared Fourier basis. Third, we validate PAF (the protein implementation of MAF) on 5,531 KLIFS kinase structures: all-30-channel accuracy 82.68% (d = 0.2193, 85× baseline); optimal 23-channel subset 85.21%, demonstrating that channel selection outperforms both equal weighting and learned SE attention (80.15%). Zero-shot voice AI transfer (wav2vec2 frozen on human speech) improves molecular discrimination from d = 0.5652 to d = 0.5727. The cubyl cation—whose

papers.title: Network Topology and Linear Viscoelasticity of Vitrimers – A Polymer Physics Perspective
papers.abstract: Covalently cross‑linked polymers that undergo associative exchange, in which bond formation precedes bond cleavage, can simultaneously maintain network connectivity while permitting topological fluctuations. First proposed to explain the thermorheological behavior of industrial polysulfide rubbers, associative cross-link exchange now defines the field of vitrimers – polymer networks that unite the durability of thermosets with the processability of thermoplastics. This Perspective examines how the apparent tension between connectivity constraints and structural rearrangements governs vitrimer physical chemistry. In contrast to existing reviews, the article applies polymer physics frameworks to understand how associative cross-links alter the relationship between network topology and structural relaxations. It begins by outlining the history of associative exchange in polymer networks, from the “cross-link exchange” hypothesis of Tobolsky to modern day vitrimers, and continues by reviewing core concepts in vitrimer chemistry. The central discussion focuses on recent advances in understanding how associative cross‑links modulate the network topology and linear viscoelasticity of polymeric materials. The network topology section relates vitrimer network structure to key observables: gel fraction, rubbery plateau modulus, equilibrium swelling ratio, and glass transition temperature. The linear viscoelasticity section connects the interplay between backbone segmental motions and cross‑link exchange to the fast and slow relaxation regimes observed in rheology measurements. Throughout, results from simulations and experiments are compared with established polymer physics models, with agreements and discrepancies identified. The Perspective also compares the physical behavior of vitrimers to that of dissociative networks, and spotlights open questions for guiding the next phase of vitrimer research.

papers.title: Mapping Internal Damage Fields Induced by Stress Softening in Dissipative Nanocomposite Elastomers
papers.abstract: Stress-softening (the Mullins effect) in nanocomposite elastomers under heterogeneous deformation remains poorly understood because most previous studies focused on simple uniaxial deformation. Here, we propose a methodology to quantify and visualize heterogeneous internal damage. A universal damage function (UDF) based on strain invariants, established from cyclic loading-unloading tests under various uniform deformation modes, enables conversion of strain fields measured by digital image correlation into internal damage maps. The method is applied to two heterogeneous deformation scenarios: (i) notch opening and (ii) stretching with a circular defect. In case (i), teardrop-shaped damage zones are identified, indicating that stress redistribution that contribute to crack-growth resistance. In case (ii), the results reveal a competition between stress concentration and softening-induced stress reduction near the defect edge, which governs fracture initiation. The proposed approach provides profound insights into the fracture and toughening mechanisms of dissipative nanocomposite elastomers.

papers.title: Ultraslow Intramolecular Singlet Fission of a Tetracene Dyad Having a Nonconjugated Linker that Inhibits Triplet-triplet Annihilation
papers.abstract: To accomplish efficient utilization of triplet excitons, generated in intramolecular singlet fission (SF) systems, undesirable triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA) must be suppressed. In the currently described effort, we designed and assessed the intramolecular SF properties of the novel tetracene dyad, Tc–DDD–Tc , in which two 5,12-bis(triisopropylsilylethynyl)tetracene ( Tc ) units are linked by a nonconjugated dibenzobicyclo[3.3.1]nonadienedione ( DDD ) unit. Time-resolved spectroscopic analysis revealed that ultraslow intramolecular SF occurs in Tc–DDD–Tc owing to weak electronic coupling between the two Tc units, whose carbon atoms directly bonded to the DDD unit are separated by 9.5 Å. The kinetic analysis demonstrated that the nonconjugated DDD unit effectively inhibits TTA, and that Tc–DDD–Tc forms a solventdependent long-lived triplet pair ( 3 Tc–DDD– 3 Tc)* state. This phenomenon is potentially applicable to quantum qubits in quantum information sciences and technologies.

papers.title: A Multi-Parameter Quantitative Structure–Property Relationship (QSPR) Model for Boiling Point Prediction of Organic Compounds
papers.abstract: This paper presents a group-wise Quantitative Structure–Property Relationship (QSPR) model for predicting the normal boiling points (NBP) of organic compounds using simple, structurally interpretable molecular descriptors. The model employs up to 14 descriptors per functional group class — including molecular weight (MW), hydrogen-bond donors (HBD), hydrogen-bond acceptors (HBA), ring count, aromaticity, individual halogen counts (F, Cl, Br, I), a non-linear Cl2 term, carboxyl count, nitro count, branching correction, and amide substitution type — all countable by direct inspection of the structural formula. A dataset of 732 compounds across 18 functional group classes was compiled from established chemical reference sources. Key design choices include: a quartic polynomial for straight-chain alkanes spanning MW = 16–563 g/mol (MAE = 3.20°C); a Cl2 descriptor capturing the non-linear saturation of successive chlorine substitution (CCl4 error = 4.0°C); a quadratic aromatic hydrocarbon equation accounting for accelerating π–π stacking with ring fusion (R2 = 0.9866, improving from 0.9531 with a linear equation); and separate primary, secondary, and tertiary amide sub-groups encoding N-substitution effects. The tertiary amide group is modelled by a linear equation (R2 = 0.5371) following rejection of a polynomial form that produced physically unreasonable external predictions. The model achieves overall R2 = 0.9547 and MAE = 11.58°C, representing a 74.5% MAE reduction versus a global MW-only baseline (MAE = 45.44°C). Preliminary external validation on 30 reliable-group unseen compounds yields MAE = 5.35°C, closely matching cross-validation estimates. The aromatic nitro group failure (R2 = 0.143) constitutes direct evidence that co-substituent electronic interactions dominate boiling point variation in that class beyond MW-based frameworks. The model is deployed as a freely accessible interactive web application.

papers.title: Molecular-Topology-Guided Multiple-Resonance Emitters with Sub-10-nm Bandwidths: Ultranarrow High-Efficiency Solution-Processable OLEDs
papers.abstract: Ultranarrow-band emitters are essential for high-colour-purity organic light-emitting diodes, but their discovery remains largely empirical because spectral narrowing is difficult to predict. Progress has been limited by inefficient synthesis-and-testing cycles and the lack of simple design rules linking molecular structure to excited-state relaxation. Here we establish a predictive design framework for ultranarrow multiple-resonance emitters by treating molecular topology as an explicit handle on structural relaxation. High-throughput screening of B,N-doped triangulene fusion modes identifies an alternating fusion pattern that minimizes reorganization energy and yields a ground-state descriptor for spectral narrowing without explicit excited-state calculations. Guided by this framework, we synthesize sky-blue emitters with photoluminescence bandwidths down to 9.1 nm and solution-processed devices with 10.9-nm electroluminescence bandwidths and 38.1% external quantum efficiency.

papers.title: Ring PEG Synthesis via Bimolecular Ring-Closing Reactions: Selective Preparation of Unimeric Rings via Introduction of Excess Sacrificial Linear Chains
papers.abstract: The efficient preparation of highly pure ring polymers by end-to-end ring-closing reactions of linear precursors remains challenging because the formation of unimeric rings competes with undesired intermolecular coupling to form multimeric products. In this study, we compared two strategies for ring poly(ethylene glycol) (R-PEG) synthesis using linear PEG with a molar mass of 2 kg mol⁻¹ (L-PEG2k): conventional intramolecular ring closing with tosyl chloride (TsCl) and bimolecular ring closing using tetraethylene glycol ditosylate (Ts-TEG-Ts) as a low-molar-mass linker. The cyclized products were purified by α -cyclodextrin ( α -CD) inclusion complexation to selectively remove linear species and were characterized by SEC and MALDI-TOF MS. Under equimolar conditions, both intramolecular and bimolecular ring-closing reactions afforded R-PEG in ca. 30% yield, with similar product distributions consisting of ca. 90% unimeric rings and 10% multimeric rings. In contrast, introducing excess L-PEG2k relative to TsCl or Ts-TEG-Ts suppressed multimeric ring formation, and the bimolecular strategy provided a better balance between purified product yield and unimeric-ring enrichment. These results demonstrate that excess L-PEG chains can function as sacrificial linear chains by promoting preferential single-end incorporation of the low-molar-mass linker, while the remaining linear species are removed by α -CD purification. This sacrificial-linear-chain strategy provides a practical route to unimer-enriched R-PEG.

papers.title: Rational Control of Photochromic Colors in Aza-Diarylethenes
papers.abstract: Photochromic molecules capable of reversible structural transformation upon light irradiation have attracted considerable attention for applications in molecular switches, optical memories, and sensing systems. In such applications, controlling the color of the photogenerated isomer is a key challenge. Here we report the systematic control of photochromic colors in aza-diarylethenes through molecular design of nitrogen-containing aryl units. A series of aza-diarylethenes incorporating pyrimidine-based aryl groups were synthesized and their photochromic properties were investigated in solution. Upon UV irradiation, the compounds undergo reversible electrocyclic reactions to generate closed-ring isomers exhibiting distinct visible absorption bands. TD-DFT calculations revealed that the visible absorption originates from two electronic transitions associated with different molecular segments. Extension of π-conjugation through phenyl-substituted pyrimidine units stabilizes the LUMO levels, resulting in a red shift of the absorption bands and enabling systematic color tuning. Furthermore, the perceived colors predicted from the calculated absorption spectra show good agreement with the experimentally observed colors. These results demonstrate that the combination of rational molecular design and computational prediction provides an effective strategy for controlling photochromic colors in aza-diarylethenes. The present work establishes design guidelines for color-tunable photochromic molecules and provides a framework for predictive color design in molecular photoswitches.

papers.title: Large-scale multi-task regression and classification models for sustainability of molecular systems
papers.abstract: New materials and molecules with improved properties are needed to continue advancing society in such fields as energy, space exploration, and electronics. Unfortunately, the typical process of discovery and characterization of new material is time-consuming, which has hindered the co-design of material and product or material and manufacturing. Predictive models using machine learning (ML) capable of forecasting the properties of new materials before they are synthesized have the potential to accelerate this process and enable co-design. However, the introduction of new materials is invariably a multi-objective process and needs to balance performance with sustainability metrics, including economic, environmental, and human health. Most ML efforts to accelerate discovery have focused on performance. This paper aggregates databases of toxicology, global warming potential (GWP), and fundamental physicochemical properties of molecules and uses the combined resource to train multi-task ML models. The models are trained for 617 classification and 30 regression metrics and outperform most current single-property models. Also, a chemical extraction study was performed using per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances to investigate the limits of our model when presented with molecules that are outside of the chemical space contained within our training data. We believe we have demonstrated that the data aggregation and models can accelerate the introduction of new materials in a wide range of applications.

papers.title: Photoexcited-nitroarene/nickel-dual catalysis for scalable and direct C(sp3)-C cross-coupling in flow
papers.abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) offers a sustainable avenue for unlocking the synthetic potential of native C(sp3)-H bonds. However, the highly regioselective construction of C(sp3)-C(sp3) linkages from ubiquitous hydrocarbon feedstocks remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we introduce a metallaphotoredox platform that leverages simple, commercially available nitroarenes as unique HAT photocatalysts, exploiting their highly electrophilic oxygen-centered diradical excited states for selective C(sp3)-H cleavage. Merged with nickel catalysis, this approach enables the direct and efficient construction of C(sp3)-C(sp2) and challenging C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds from unactivated hydrocarbons. The practicality of this protocol is highlighted by rapid reaction kinetics, a broad substrate scope and excellent scalability to achieve 100-mmol synthesis by its implementation in continuous-flow mode. Detailed mechanistic and computational investigations reveal that the triplet nitroarene functions as a potent oxygen-centered diradical, facilitating a regioselective C(sp3)-H abstraction that seamlessly intercepts the nickel catalytic cycle to accomplish the crosscoupling.

papers.title: Impact of Chronic Micro-Particulate Exposure on Enamel Microhardness: an in vitro Simulation Model of Combined Occupational Particulate Deposition and Abrasion
Chirality-induced spin polarization: Some fundamental ingredients
papers.abstract: This paper examines some fundamental ingredients that produce enantiomerspecific spin-polarization in chiral systems, leading to chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS). In particular, it examines parity and time-reversal symmetries of the key quantities, such as linear and angular momenta and spin. Enantiomer-specific spinpolarization emerges because of the symmetry relationship between the two mirror images that results in different transformation properties for axial and polar vectors. It is best described by pseudoscalars. The analysis of the structure of the spin–orbit coupling (SOC) operator shows that the chirality of the system enters the picture via the shapes of molecular orbitals, which are determined by (electrostatic) molecular field. The spin–orbit operator detects the handedness of the orbitals and reports on it by the phase of the individual matrix elements. This explains how a local operator can sense the effect of a distant molecular field. Symmetry of the SOC also explains different electronic population dynamics observed in chiral and non-chiral molecules. Drawing from the field of molecular magnetism, we connect spin-polarization with magnetic anisotropy and show that the latter is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for the former. The anisotropy requires a non-zero expectation value of the angular momentum operator in the spin–orbit-perturbed states and lifting electronic degeneracy within the multiplet. Formal theoretical analysis is supplemented by numerical examples.

papers.title: Computational Identification of Natural Product Modulators Targeting PTPN6 in the Ferroptosis-Immune Axis of Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion: An Integrated Bioinformatic, Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) affects 2-5% of couples of reproductive age, and roughly half of all cases lack a molecular explanation. Recent evidence points to ferroptosis, iron-dependent, lipid-peroxide-driven death of decidual stromal cells and trophoblasts, as a key driver of the pathology, yet no small molecules targeting the pathway have been described. The question is whether PTPN6 (SHP-1), a ferroptosis-linked phosphatase reported as a hub gene in RSA endometrial transcriptomes, could be targeted by natural products. Differentially expressed genes from the publicly available GSE165004 microarray cohort were overlapped with the FerrDb V3 ferroptosis-driver list and ranked by cytoHubba degree centrality, which confirmed PTPN6 as a top-scoring hub and the chosen structural target. The COCONUT 2.0 natural-product collection (~430,000 compounds) was reduced by Lipinski filtering and a DataWarrior Tanimoto similarity search against the co-crystallized reference ligand of PDB 4GS0; the survivors were docked into the catalytic site through Glide HTVS → SP → XP and rescored with Prime MM-GBSA. Seven natural products came through this cascade, two of which bound more favorably than the native reference. Post-docking screening of ADMET and toxicity profiles (ADMETlab 3.0, ProTox 3.0) singled out CNP0242013, a prenylated dihydroxybenzoic acid, as the lead with the cleanest predicted safety profile. Across a 100 ns explicit-solvent Desmond MD trajectory, the CNP0242013-PTPN6 complex stayed anchored at the catalytic P-loop with a backbone Cα RMSD of 1.89 Å to 2.47 Å, and projection of the trajectory onto the first two principal components revealed a single, sharply defined free-energy minimum. CNP0242013 thus offers a starting point for experimental work on SHP-1 inhibition in ferroptosis-driven miscarriage.

papers.title: Assessment of in vitro toxicity of chloronitramide anion (CNAM)
papers.abstract: In 2024, the chloronitramide anion (CNAM) was identified as a degradation product of inorganic chloramines, more than 40 years since its existence was suggested. However, to our knowledge, no studies have evaluated the toxicity of CNAM. In this manuscript, we evaluate CNAM in vitro toxicity using the Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells chronic cytotoxicity assay. CNAM exhibited a LC 50 value of 9.99 x 10 -5 M (99.9 µM; 9.45 mg/L), where LC 50 denotes the concentration causing 50% cell death. These results indicate that CNAM is more toxic than regulated disinfection by-products (DBPs), including trihalomethanes (THMs) and haloacetic acids (HAAs). Toxicity-weighted DBP concentration analyses further demonstrated that CNAM is the major driver in chloraminated drinking water cytotoxicity, accounting on average for 71% of the calculated cytotoxicity index (CTI). In chlorinated tap water, CTI analysis showed that CNAM contributed, on average, 8.0% of the total DBP-associated toxicity. In waters treated with chloramines, toxicity-weighted concentration index values for CNAM exceeded those of all other evaluated DBP classes, including haloacetonitriles (HANs), haloacetamides (HAMs), haloacetaldehydes (HALs), halonitromethanes (HNMs), THMs, HAAs and haloketones (HKs). Additional in vitro testing further suggests that CNAM induces substantial oxidative stress in CHO cells, whereas mitochondrial dysfunction and DNA damage were not significant under the tested conditions.

papers.title: Tailoring Roof-Shaped Nematogens -Alignment and Biaxial Packing in a Nematic LC Phase
papers.abstract: Inspired by a recently postulated nematogen design, two molecules with an inverted substitution pattern of lateral chains were synthesised, for which one realises an optimum biaxial aspect ratio and improved interdigitation of hexyl groups along the minor molecular axis. The impact of the substitution pattern on the packing along the minor director is confirmed by increased order parameters (XRS) and the local packing of defined conformers (solid-state NMR spectroscopy). Molecular dynamics predicts a rather high biaxiality parameter for the nematic phase of the correctly substituted mesogen. Temperature variable polarised optical microscopy studies on homogeneous and homeotropic aligned samples and investigations of the capacitance and resistance provide evidence for a phase transition in the nematic region from a uniaxial nematic N 1 to a new N 2 phase with biaxial order.

papers.title: QUAD: A Composite Risk Framework Integrating Uncertainty, Applicability Domain, and Model Disagreement for Reliable QSAR Predictions
papers.abstract: Quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models are widely used to predict molecular bioactivity; however, conventional global performance metrics provide limited insight into the reliability of individual predictions. To address this limitation, we introduce QUAD, a post-hoc framework that integrates three complementary indicators of prediction risk: ensemble-based model uncertainty, applicability domain (AD) risk, and model disagreement. QUAD enables molecule-level reliability assessment without modification of the underlying predictive model. The framework was evaluated on two Alzheimer's disease-relevant targets, β-site amyloid precursor protein cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1) and glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β), using ECFP4 fingerprints and Random Forest regression with fixed external train-test splits. Baseline models demonstrated consistent generalizability, with test-set performance of R² = 0.638 (RMSE = 0.801, MAE = 0.577) for BACE1 (1,514 molecules) and R² = 0.692 (RMSE = 0.777, MAE = 0.564) for GSK3β (4,093 molecules), supported by cross-validated and external Q² metrics. Ensemble-based uncertainty exhibited a moderate association with absolute prediction error for BACE1 (Pearson r = 0.366) and a stronger relationship for GSK3β (r = 0.443), highlighting dataset-dependent reliability behavior. The composite QUAD reliability score reflected these patterns, showing conservative stratification for BACE1 (r = 0.310) and a clearer monotonic relationship with error for GSK3β (r = 0.439). These findings demonstrate that prediction reliability in QSAR modeling is inherently multifactorial and target-specific. Rather than optimizing a single uncertainty measure, QUAD integrates heterogeneous risk signals into a transparent reliability ranking that supports compound prioritization and risk-aware decision-making. Owing to its model-agnostic design and minimal computational overhead, QUAD can be readily incorporated into existing QSAR workflows, providing a practical framework for molecule-level reliability assessment in computational drug discovery.

papers.title: ChemSpace Copilot: Agentic AI for Interactive Visualization and Exploration of Chemical Space
papers.abstract: Chemography provides a foundational approach to exploring chemical space by compressing high-dimensional representations of chemical structures into 2D maps, enabling clearer interpretation of similarity, diversity, and activity. Such maps power core chemoinformatics tasksstructure-activity relationship analysis, library design, virtual screening, and de novo design. In practice, effective use of chemography relies on manual application of data analysis tools and expert-driven interpretation of the resulting landscapes for hypothesis generation. To automate chemography-guided discovery, we introduce ChemSpace Copilotan agentic AI application that encapsulates standard chemographic workflows based on the non-linear dimensionality reduction technique Generative Topographic Mapping (GTM). ChemSpace Copilot enables researchers to perform chemographic tasks end-to-end through an intuitive, chatbot-style interface. Its modular toolkit integrates chemical data retrieval from ChEMBL, GTM parameter optimization, chemotype analysis and report generation. We further demonstrate the extensibility of the framework by integrating generative deep learning models with the synthesis planning, enabling effective and illustrative end-to-end molecular discovery from design to synthetic feasibility. We demonstrate its utility across three tasks: exploration of ChEMBL's chemical space, chemography-guided compound generation, and synthesis prediction.

papers.title: Simulation of unimolecular fluoromethane dissociation on a quantum computer using the cascaded variational quantum eigensolver algorithm
papers.abstract: Simulating chemical reactions on quantum computers has the potential to offer insight that cannot be gained practically from conventional quantum-chemical approaches on classical computers. This is because quantum computing provides a platform for efficient, high-level electronic structure calculations that approach the full configuration interaction (FCI) limit. Herein, we apply the cascaded variational quantum eigensolver (CVQE) algorithm to simulate the unimolecular dissociation of fluoromethane (CH 3 F) by two pathways: (1) CH 3 F → CH 2 + HF and (2) CH 3 F → CHF + H 2 . We compare the results of CVQE calculations performed on the ibm_torino quantum computer to configuration interaction (CI) benchmarks run on a classical computer. Our results demonstrate that CVQE predicts lower energies than classical configuration interaction with singles, doubles, and triples (CISDT) for all geometries considered, and achieves chemical accuracy relative to FCI in nearly all cases. This suggests that quantum computing with CVQE can provide high-level electronic structure information for chemical reactions and other cases that require the simulation of multiple geometries.

papers.title: Data-Efficient Mapping of Copolymerization Curves and Reactivity Ratios via Gradient Flow Polymerization, Inline ATR-FTIR, and Lasso Regression
A Digitally Controlled Flow–Batch Platform for Reproducible Radical Copolymerization with Reduced Composition Drift
papers.abstract: Free-radical copolymerization is widely used in industry to produce copolymers from diverse monomers, but transferring laboratory syntheses to manufacturing remains challenging because changes in mixing and heat-transfer conditions can alter polymer properties. Here, we report a digitally controlled flow–batch platform that integrates a micromixer, a heated tubular flow reactor, and batch reactors. In this configuration, the micromixer provides rapid and reproducible mixing, the flow stage provides rapid thermal initialization under low-conversion conditions, and the batch stage completes the reaction at high conversion while accommodating additional monomer dosing. Rapid mixing and heating in the flow stage mitigated the early-stage formation of very-high-molecular-weight polymer, while additional monomer dosing designed from initiator-decomposition kinetics suppressed composition drift during the batch stage. Together, these operations reduced the time-dependent variation in copolymer composition and molecular weight under high-conversion conditions. In a demonstration using four parallel batch reactors, the platform produced 1.97 kg of copolymer (dry basis) in an 8 h run. The proposed platform provides a practical process strategy for reproducible radical copolymerization in small-lot manufacturing of advanced polymer materials.

papers.title: Decarbonizing Chemical Feedstocks: Patent-Based Evidence on Rising Utilization of Pyrolysis and Carbon Capture
papers.abstract: The chemicals industry remains structurally dependent on fossil-derived feedstocks, even as efforts to reduce operational emissions continue. This paper provides patent-based evidence on innovation in alternative feedstock pathways, focusing on plastic waste pyrolysis and carbon capture and utilization (CCU). Using priority patent filings from 2018–2024 and publicly available production data,4 we compare growth in waste-derived hydrocarbons and CO2-based chemical conversion with that of conventional fossil-based hydrocarbon production. Our analysis shows that patent filings in waste-derived liquid hydrocarbons have grown more rapidly than filings associated with refining technologies. Carbon capture patents that incorporate digital technologies have also expanded at higher rates than carbon capture patents overall. Despite this acceleration, structural constraints remain significant. Pyrolysis depends on waste collection infrastructure and feedstock consistency, while CCU deployment is closely tied to low-carbon hydrogen availability and electricity costs. Although our research highlights the growing emphasis on upstream carbon substitution, economic and infrastructure conditions will shape the scale of adoption of these technologies.

papers.title: A Smooth and Fully Differentiable Molecular Cavity Based on Discretization via Reference-Onto-Surface Projection
papers.abstract: We present a new molecular cavity for the use in continuum models that consists of two independent components: i.) a smooth van der Waals (SvdW) surface, which is fully differentiable and recovers the properties of a solvent-excluded-surface (SES) while remaining free of geometric singularities, and ii.) a Discretization scheme via Reference-Onto-surface Projection (DROP), a general approach to discretize arbitrary differentiable implicit surfaces that leads to fully consistent analytical derivatives. DROP can be used with any differentiable level set and can thus be generalized beyond molecular cavities, which we demonstrate here for a genus-2 surface. The integration consistency of DROP shows excellent agreement with conventional marching cubes meshing. We validate the SvdW-DROP cavity for applications with the Conductor-like Polarizable Continuum Model (CPCM) and the GOSTSHYP pressure model and compare the cavity with other state-of-the-art cavity construction schemes. Due to the smooth surface with no crevices, a more homogeneous CPCM surface charge distribution and lower outlying charges are obtained, compared with regular vdW cavities. Surface area and polarization energy scans show fully smooth energies and stable gradients, which are further validated using ab initio molecular dynamics simulations and geometry optimizations. Due to its near linear scaling with system size, smooth potential energy surface, fully consistent derivatives, and avoidance of unfavorable kinks and crevices in its surface, the SvdW-DROP cavity outperforms conventional vdW-type cavity construction as well as state-of-the-art SES-type schemes.

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of π-Extended Ruthenium(II) Complexes for Cancer-Targeted Photodynamic Therapy
papers.abstract: Cancer remains a major global health challenge, and the limitations of conventional therapies continue to motivate more selective treatment strategies. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) relies on the light-triggered generation of reactive oxygen species, making the design of excited-state photosensitizers central to its efficacy. Here, π-extended Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes bearing stilbene-functionalized bipyridine ligands were prepared to examine structure–property–activity relationships for one- and two-photon PDT. Variation of substituent electronics (OMe vs NMe2) and the monodentate ligand (Cl- vs SCN-) influenced singlet oxygen quantum yields (ΦΔ), lipophilicity [Log(Do/w)], excited-state emission, two-photon absorption, and light-dependent cytotoxicity in SK-MEL-28 cells. The NMe2 derivatives generally showed stronger photodynamic performance than the OMe analogs, while SCN substitution increased lipophilicity and modulated photophysical behavior. Two-photon absorption (2PA) studies showed moderate 2PA responses for 1b and 2b in the 700–800 nm region, supporting potential NIR activation. Phototoxicity decreased under hypoxia but remained measurable, consistent with an oxygen-dependent PDT mechanism.

papers.title: Computational Hit-Finding for a CNS-Penetrant Multi-Target Panel Against HIV-1 Reservoirs: Prioritization of Six Novel Candidates Across Six Mechanistic Targets
papers.abstract: Background: HIV-1 establishes latent reservoirs in CNS-resident microglia that are inaccessible to current antiretroviral therapy (ART) due to poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration of most antiretrovirals. No approved drug regimen simultaneously addresses latency reversal, transcriptional silencing, viral entry, capsid function, and selective elimination of reactivated cells within the CNS compartment. Methods: We employed a structure-based computational pipeline integrating AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, SMINA-Vinardo orthogonal rescoring, RDKit-derived CNS-MPO scoring, PAMPA-BBB permeability prediction (Di et al. 2003 correlation), ESOL aqueous solubility estimation, PAINS/Brenk structural alert filtering, ligand efficiency metrics, anti-target selectivity profiling (hERG/CYP3A4/BRAF), metabolic soft-spot prediction, conformational strain analysis, and knowledge-based retrosynthetic planning. A total of 85 computational analyses were performed across iterative design-dock-filter cycles. Results: Six candidates were prioritized from >200 enumerated analogs, each targeting a distinct mechanistic node of the HIV-1 lifecycle relevant to CNS reservoirs: (1) MTL-A08v2, a dual BRD4/HDAC2 latency-reversing agent; (2) VIC-CCR52-e_2Pyridyl, a dual CCR5/CCR2 entry inhibitor with anti-neuroinflammatory potential; (3) TAR-CNS-1, an aminoquinazoline-bipyridyl TAR RNA binder designed to silence Tat-mediated proviral transcription (block-and-lock); (4) HDAC-CNS-1, a selective HDAC2 inhibitor for complementary latency reversal via epigenetic derepression; (5) CA-CNS-1, the first reported CNS-permeable HIV-1 capsid inhibitor; and (6) SMAC-CNS-1, a monomeric Smac mimetic for selective elimination of reactivated reservoir cells. All candidates satisfy Lipinski/Veber/Ghose/Egan druglikeness rules, demonstrate favorable hERG selectivity (DDG > 0.86 kcal/mol), pass PAINS/Brenk filters (6/6 PAINS-clean), and maintain ligand efficiency LE >= 0.30. Estimated panel synthesis cost is $530-1220/g at 5-10 g scale. Conclusions: This work demonstrates that computational methods can identify chemically diverse, BBB-permeable hit compounds against multiple HIV-1 targets simultaneously. All six candidates are proposed for experimental validation. No therapeutic claims are made; this is a hit-finding study providing a computational foundation for future medicinal chemistry optimization and biological testing.

papers.title: Unsymmetrical Ligand Backbone Drives Site-Selective Assembly of Heterometallic Complexes
papers.abstract: Heterometallic catalysts harness cooperative interactions between distinct metal centers to enable unique reactivity; however, their development remains limited by inherent synthetic challenges associated with their selective assembly. Here, we report that 2,7-di(pyridin-2-yl)imidazo[1,2-a]pyrimidine (dpip) enables the one-step, site-selective formation of the heterometallic complexes [Ni2Cu2(dpip)2(µ–OH)2(O2CCF3)5(H2O)2][O2CCF3] (NiCu), [Ni2Cu(dpip)(µ–OH)(O2CCF3)5(H2O)] (2NiCu), and [Co2Cu(dpip)(µ–OH)(O2CCF3)5(MeCN)] (2CoCu). Metal redistribution experiments, in which the homometallic complexes [Ni3(dpip)(µ–OH)(O2CCF3)5(MeCN)(H2O)] (3Ni) and [Cu2(dpip)(µ–OH)(O2CCF3)3] (2Cu) were treated with Cu(O2CCF3)2·H2O and Ni(O2CCF3)2·4H2O, afforded the heterometallic complexes NiCu and 2NiCu, consistent with reversible metal exchange and thermodynamically controlled assembly. Comparative experiments using a symmetric 1,8-naphthyridine-based ligand yielded an unselective mixture of complexes, demonstrating that the imidazopyrimidine backbone is critical for directing selective heterometallic assembly. Quantum-chemical calculations were used to construct thermodynamic cycles describing metal exchange reactions and the relative affinity of each metal center for each binding site within dpip. The resulting Gibbs energies (ΔG298) indicated that the heterometallic complexes are thermodynamically more stable than their homometallic counterparts. Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) deletion analyses attributed the site selectivity in the heterometallic complexes to stronger copper(II) interactions at the more electron-donating imidazole-containing binding site. Consistent with this electronic differentiation, synthesis of the monometallic complex [Pd(dpip)(O2CCF3)2] showed selective coordination at the more electron-donating site. Together, these results demonstrate that imidazopyrimidine-based ligands provide a platform for the controlled assembly of heterometallic complexes.

papers.title: Covalent inclusion of calix[4]arenes in Tröger's base polymers of intrinsic microporosity for physical aging mitigation
papers.abstract: Polymeric membrane-based technology offers an energy-efficient solution for post-combustion carbon capture. Owing to their rigid, contorted backbones that endow them with exceptional CO 2 permeability, Polymers of Intrinsic Microporosity (PIMs) are among the most promising candidates, but their application is constrained by physical aging. Here, the covalent inclusion of calix[4]arenes as monomeric units in PIMs based on Tröger's Base (PIM-TBs) is presented as valuable solution for the mitigation of this progressive free-volume collapse, by taking advantage of their intrinsic cavity. For this purpose, upper rim functionalised diamino-tetrapropoxy calix[4]arenes in defined geometrical arrangements ( cone , partial cone , and 1,3-alternate ) are exploited in the preparation of both homo- ( PIM-CXn-TBs ) and co-polymers ( PIM-Trip-CXn-TBs ) with diaminotriptycene units, which are fully characterised in terms of molecular weight distributions, textural parameters and CO 2 /N 2 adsorption properties at room temperature. PIM-Trip-CX3-TB , obtained from the copolymerisation of the 1,3-alternate conformer, and its post-polymerisation dealkylated counterpart ( PIM-Trip-CX3(OH)-TB ) are solution processed in films and tested in permeation and aging experiments. These studies reveal that, whereas the propylated copolymer mirrors the aging behaviour of pristine PIM-Trip-TB , PIM-Trip-CX3(OH)-TB exhibits a reduced early-stage loss of CO 2 permeability, thus evidencing a concomitant effect of the covalent calix[4]arene incorporation and cavity rigidification promoted by intramolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions.

papers.title: Frequent Hitter Prediction Beyond Classification Models
Spacing Over Sequence: Design Considerations for Polystyrene-binding Polypeptides
papers.abstract: Plastic-binding polypeptides have emerging applications in biosensor design, materials functionalization, and nanoplastic capture, and the rational design of new sequences requires the development of structural and sequence-based design principles. Here, we demonstrate a computational workflow combining atomistic molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling to evaluate polypeptide binding to polystyrene, a common commodity plastic. We investigate three candidate sequences previously proposed as polystyrene binders, all enriched in aromatic or cationic residues expected to interact with polystyrene’s aromatic rings. We find that two sequences bind stably through apparent π-stacking and cation-π interactions, while one fails to bind despite similar composition. Our analysis demonstrates that composition alone does not determine successful binding and that amino acid spacing and accessibility to multiple binding configurations are determining factors for stable polystyrene binding.

papers.title: An analytically differentiable submatrix-descriptor neural-network potential for molecular simulations of liquid water
papers.abstract: Machine-learning potentials can accelerate atomistic simulations, but their use in molecular dynamics requires descriptors that are symmetry preserving, differentiable and straightforward to evaluate. We present a compact neural-network potential based on local submatrix descriptors and apply it to liquid water. A sparsified Coulomb or sine matrix is reduced to atom-centred submatrices, which are converted into fixedlength descriptors by deterministic neighbour ranking. A single shared network maps all atomic descriptors to energy contributions, avoiding element-specific subnetworks while retaining chemical identity through the matrix elements. Because the descriptor is differentiable, conservative forces are obtained analytically by the chain rule. For periodic liquid water, five-fold cross-validation gives a lowest mean absolute energy error of 0.0609 eV atom−1 with the sine-matrix descriptor. Analytical forces agree with finite-difference derivatives of the trained model, and conservative-force dynamics preserves the qualitative oxygen–oxygen radial distribution function.

papers.title: Euclidean Embedding of Reaction Networks for Dimensionality Reduction of Chemical Spaces
papers.abstract: Exploring complex chemical reactions is challenging due to the high dimensionality of potential energy surfaces (PESs). Stoichiometry-preserving reaction networks (RNs), constructed using bond-breaking and bond-forming rules, provide a discrete representation of chemical space with an underlying low-dimensional metric structure. Moreover, these RNs resemble regular lattices with a small degree of random edge rewiring. In this work, we show that these RNs coupled with weighted-path metrics can be embedded into low-dimensional Euclidean spaces, producing a significant and chemically informed dimensionality reduction of the PES. Across CHNO RNs spanning diverse stoichiometries and sizes, we compare linear embedding methods, including classical multidimensional scaling (cMDS) and landmark MDS (LMDS), with nonlinear approaches such as metric MDS (mMDS), Isomap, t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE), and kernel principal component analysis (KPCA). Incorporating kinetic heuristics as edge weights does not significantly increase embedding error or the optimal embedding dimensionality relative to constant edge weights. Although mMDS provides the best distance preservation, it scales poorly with network size. To address this limitation, we introduce a distance-preserving encoder that combines LMDS initialization with neural network refinement and achieves mMDS-level accuracy at a computational cost comparable to LMDS. The resulting embeddings exhibit high fidelity (Kendall τ > 0.84, normalized stress σ < 0.09, and R2 > 0.95) and reduce the dimensionality of the reactive chemical space by a factor of 3–10 relative to the underlying PES. The optimal embedding dimension scales as O(log n) with the number of nodes n. Randomization experiments indicate that the observed near-Euclidean structure is specific to RNs and is related to their chemically constrained topologies and symmetric edge weights, in contrast to general sparse graphs. Pathway discovery experiments further demonstrate that shortest-path searches in the embedding space recover chemically feasible pathways consistent with those identified in the original RNs. These results establish low-dimensional Euclidean embeddings of RNs as a compact and searchable representation of chemical reaction spaces.

papers.title: Iron-Catalyzed [1+1+1] Cyclopropanation via Stereoselective Ester Olefination
papers.abstract: Traditional precious metal catalysis benefits from well-characterized inner-sphere elementary steps in which a single complex binds and unites substrates at the metal center. In contrast, base metal catalysts have recently demonstrated competence in cross-coupling transformations via iterative outer-sphere reactions in which product bond formation occurs via serial additions to the ligand, not the metal. Despite the emerging diversity of two-component outer-sphere reactions, comparable multicomponent outer-sphere couplings remain rare. Herein we describe an iron-catalyzed [1+1+1] synthesis of cyclopropanols through iterative outer-sphere reactions between two carbenes and an ester. This reaction initially generates silyl enol ethers stereo-, regio- and chemoselectively via a traceless, directed olefination which can be further exploited to enable transformations unavailable to prior methods.

papers.title: High-Concentration Acid-Base Generation via Decoupled Mediated Electrodialysis
papers.abstract: Electrified generation of acids and bases from saline waste streams is essential for sustainable waste utilization and crucial to building a circular ecosystem. Existing salt splitting technologies, such as electrolytic electrodialysis (EED) and bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) are hindered by proton leakage, high energy consumption and complex multi-stack architecture. Here, we introduce a decoupled mediated electrodialysis (DMED) method for acid-base generation that fundamentally prevents proton leakage and improves energy consumption. By introducing a redox mediator to decouple the acid and base generation process, an unprecedentedly high concentration of H + (8.90 M) and OH - (5.20 M) can be generated. High current efficiencies (> 85%) for both acid and base generation could be achieved even at a current density of 100 mA cm -2 . We further demonstrate DMED in nickel laterite extraction, where acid and base are heavily used for leaching and precipitation. DMED electrochemically regenerates the consumed H 2 SO 4 and NaOH from the residual solution to enable a fully electrified closed-loop extraction process. Such integration greatly reduces chemical consumption and hazardous waste discharge, transforming a traditionally linear operation into a circular one. Beyond mining, this platform offers a scalable and energy-efficient route to electrify acid-base production from diverse saline waste sources, opening new possibilities for sustainable manufacturing and efficient resource recovery

papers.title: A comparative study of ADP and KDP Solution Structure: Interplay of Hydrogen Bonding and Ion Association
papers.abstract: Ammonium dihydrogen phosphate and potassium dihydrogen phosphate are widely used hydrogen-bonded crystals in nonlinear optics and also play important roles in technological and biological contexts. While their solid-state properties have been extensively studied, comparatively less attention has been given to their solution-phase structure, particularly for ammonium dihydrogen phosphate, where molecular-level insights remain limited. Since solution structure is closely linked to nucleation, crystal growth, and transport behaviour, a systematic understanding of these systems is essential. In this work, molecular dynamics simulations are employed to investigate the solution structure and hydrogen-bonding behaviour of aqueous ammonium dihydrogen phosphate and to compare it with potassium dihydrogen phosphate over a range of concentrations using different water models. A slightly modified ammonium model is found to better reproduce hydration structure reported by ab initio simulations. Local structure is characterized using radial distribution functions, coordination numbers, and spatial density distributions, while mobility is analysed through mean-squared displacements. Substitution of potassium by the hydrogen-bond-active ammonium ion leads to significant differences in ion association and hydrogen-bond connectivity. Structure factors are calculated to enable comparison with experimental X-ray scattering data and show reasonable agreement. The analysis further reveals that water structure evolves with concentration, indicating its active role in ion association and clustering rather than acting as a passive background. Overall, the results demonstrate that, despite similar crystal structures, the presence of the hydrogen-bonding ammonium ion leads to distinct solution structures, which are likely to influence nucleation and crystal growth behaviour.

papers.title: Towards direct dynamics simulation of photochemistry without the Born-Oppenheimer approximation
papers.abstract: The simulation of photochemical reactions requires a quantum mechanical treatment of electronic and nuclear dynamics. Most simulation approaches use the Born-Oppenheimer (BO) approximation and calculations of nonadiabatic couplings to evolve a wavefunction on a set of BO electronic states. However, the use of BO states present several challenges such as discontinuous surfaces, singular terms in the Hamiltonian, and double-valued boundary conditions. We present a direct dynamics approach for molecular vibronic dynamics which does not invoke the BO approximation simply by avoiding diagonalization of the electronic part of the Hamiltonian. By employing a diabatic propagation scheme for the orbitals, we ensure that all electronic terms vary smoothly as a function of nuclear coordinates in a basis of configuration state functions (CSFs). We derive equations of motion for mixed quantum-classical dynamics techniques employing averaged potentials, such that the simulated trajectories evolve on linear combinations of CSF surfaces. We test our approach for lithium hydride and ethylene. In contrast with BO electronic surfaces, we find that all CSF surfaces and couplings are smooth and integrable in the vicinity of conical intersections and weak avoided crossings. Comparisons of the dynamics of photoexcited lithium hydride show that Ehrenfest dynamics reproduce changes in electronic state populations, but lead to over-coherence. Our equations of motion for coupled-trajectory dynamics fail to reduce the over-coherence problem due to the reliance of the derivation on the BO approximation. With further work on the selection of orbitals and the mixed quantum-classical equations of motion, our work shows the potential of a pre-BO wavefunction ansatz for practical nonadiabatic dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Direct-to-Biology for Bacterial Ribosome Binders
papers.abstract: Antibiotics are central to our ability to practice modern medicine. Many of our most effective agents in this space target the bacterial ribosome and arise from natural products or their derivatives. A critical design criterion for improving antibiotic behavior is to optimize ribosomal RNA contact. Yet, a historical reliance on top-down approaches for antibiotic identification has limited the discovery of structurally novel and potentially effective interactions with rRNA, because each new derivative must run the gauntlet of entering bacteria, evading efflux pumps, avoiding inactivation, and overcoming ribosome modification. Here, we present a bottom-up approach for antibiotic discovery which allows unpurified small molecules to be rapidly profiled for novel rRNA binding interactions with bacterial ribosomes. Central to this advance was recognizing that inactive states of antibiotic natural products can be accessed via chemical steps or by changes in concentration, thereby abolishing ribosome binding. In this way, any restoration of small molecule activity arises from the establishment of novel binding contacts with the ribosome. This in vitro approach was insensitive to chemical impurities and thus allowed large swathes of chemical space to be explored, ultimately yielding a structurally novel ligand which was preorganized for interaction with key components of the peptidyl transferase center. Iterative application of this ligand prioritization pipeline further improved binding and activity toward Gram-positive strains, yielding a candidate molecule primed for downstream medicinal chemistry optimization. We anticipate that these findings will address the urgent need for antibiotics featuring novel rRNA contacts toward the creation of more effective antibiotic agents.

papers.title: Computationally Assessing the Thermodynamic Stability and Transport Properties of Defective Multivalent Solid Ion Conductors
papers.abstract: Multivalent batteries offer potential advantages over their lithium counterparts, but their development is currently hindered by a scarcity of solid electrolyte and electrode materials with high multivalent ionic conductivity. Multivalent ions often migrate via a vacancy-mediated mechanism, but the intrinsic concentration of vacancies in many materials is too low to support fast ion conduction. The vacancy concentration, and potentially the conductivity, can be increased via aliovalent substitution of ions with those of a different charge. Such strategies have been applied previously to monovalent ion conductors but remain underexplored in the context of their multivalent counterparts. This study leverages density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations to assess the thermodynamic stability and transport properties of multivalent ion conductors containing vacancies and aliovalent substitutions. We consider ten prototypical antiperovskite compounds with the initial formula M 3 AB, where M is Mg or Ca and A and B are pnictogens, and replace pnictogens with either halogens or chalcogens to introduce vacancies. The energy above the convex hull, defect formation energy, and various reaction energies representing possible synthetic pathways are used to assess stability. This analysis reveals substituted Ca 3 PSb, Ca 3 NBi, and Mg 3 NBi as stable compositions. In all compounds, substitutions with smaller ions, such as F and O, are generally found to be more energetically favorable than those with larger ions. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that ion migration events only involve a single ion, in contrast to many monovalent superionic conductors, in which concerted mechanisms are often observed. These findings suggest possible synthetic approaches to improving multivalent ionic conductivity for future experimental efforts.

papers.title: The Application of Isoborneol in the Organic Chemistry Laboratory
papers.abstract: Many universities have been facing major financial constraints due to federal and state funding changes. As a result, selecting reactions that are low-cost to demonstrate fundamental chemical synthesis has become increasingly attractive to chemical educators. Undergraduate organic chemistry courses commonly involve the use of alcohol-bearing compounds to perform oxidation, acylation, or protection reactions. The standard cost of these experiments ranges from $0.38–$2.59. Here, we describe the use of isoborneol, a low-cost alcohol-bearing compound, to recapitulate these standard transformations in a cost-effective manner. Protection of the alcohol can be achieved either through an alkyl group or an acyl group. For alkyl protection, isoborneol was reacted with iodomethane in the presence of sodium hydride. Acylation protection was achieved using acetic anhydride and sodium acetate. Oxidation of the alcohol to a carbonyl was performed using a “green synthesis” approach with common household bleach. Subsequently, reduction of the carbonyl back to an alcohol was achieved using sodium borohydride. All reactions produced distinct products with yields ranging from 25–75%. Importantly, the total cost of these reactions was $6.13. This highlights the utility of a single compound to perform a broad range of alcohol-based reactions for undergraduate classroom laboratories.

papers.title: Nonlinear Imaging of Bacterial Membranes During Adhesion
papers.abstract: Electrostatic interactions between bacteria and abiotic surfaces induce changes that propagate from the cell exterior to perturb the inner membrane and associated cellular processes. Direct optical readouts that disentangle the potentially coupled effects from these interactions remain limited. Here we use simultaneous second-harmonic generation (SHG) and two-photon fluorescence (TPF) microscopy of the styryl dye FM 1-43 to probe how adhesion to substrates of different surface charge alters the inner-membrane environment of Escherichia coli. From negatively charged glass to positively functionalized surfaces, the initial SHG and TPF signals exhibit opposing substrate-dependent trends. The SHG readout is consistent with previously proposed alterations in inner membrane potential due to charge regulation, but also reveals a substrate-dependent spatially heterogeneous response. In contrast, the magnitude and time dependence of the TPF signals cannot be explained by membrane potential alterations, but is instead suggestive of a probe population associated with mechanosensitive channel activation and subsequent adaptation. Together, these results establish concurrent SHG/TPF imaging as an integrated tool for directly capturing how surface electrostatics bridge bacterial adhesion with inner membrane physiology.

papers.title: Synthesis of silylated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons by lithium-mediated mechanochemical Birch reductive silylation
papers.abstract: Silicon-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (Si-PAHs) are important functional π-conjugated molecules, but their synthesis is still largely dependent on the multistep preparation of precursors, such as halogenated PAHs. Herein, we report a lithium-mediated mechanochemical Birch reductive silylation of unfunctionalized PAHs in air at room temperature. Various silylated PAHs (Si-PAHs) and hydrogenated analogs were obtained directly from unfunctionalized PAHs by ball-milling PAHs with bulk Li(0) in a small amount of THF additive, followed by treatment with chlorosilanes, fluorosilanes , or hydrosilanes. This method accommodates a range of PAHs, including chrysene, fluoranthene, and perylene derivatives, and enables access to various substitution patterns that are difficult to achieve using conventional synthetic methods. The resulting Si-PAHs exhibit enhanced solubility and fluorescent quantum yields, along with a characteristic red shift in absorption and emission. Furthermore, the combination of the previously developed Li(0)-mediated mechanochemical cyclodehydrogenation and Birch reductive arylation with the present silylation enabled one-pot access to more complicated functional Si-PAHs.

papers.title: Mechanochemical Birch Reductive Alkylation of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
papers.abstract: Direct alkylation of unfunctionalized polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) is crucial for tuning their solubility, processability, and electronic properties. However, classical Friedel–Crafts alkylation often fails to introduce primary or secondary alkyl groups because of carbocation rearrangement and overalkylation. This study reports lithium(0)-mediated mechanochemical Birch reductive alkylation of PAHs using readily available alkyl fluorides. Vigorous ball milling of Li wire generated highly reactive aromatic anions at room temperature under ambient atmosphere. The process did not require solvents for solubilization, highly reactive but hazardous metals such as sodium(0) and potassium(0), or elevated reaction temperatures under an inert atmosphere. The developed method allows the introduction of diverse primary, secondary, chiral, and functionalized alkyl groups. Furthermore, combining the present method with previously developed mechanochemical cyclodehydrogenation/Birch reductive arylation provides streamlined access to complex functionalized PAHs.

papers.title: Accelerating discovery of phosphorescent blue OLED emitters using chemical foundation models
papers.abstract: In OLED displays, phosphorescent emitter molecules are used for red and green but not for blue pixels. Iridium organometallics are promising phosphorescent emitters, but a molecule satisfying the requirements of color, brightness, and stability has not yet been developed. One strategy to discover an emitter is virtual screening, in which computational predictions are used to prioritize candidates for synthesis. Due to the computational difficulty of screening with first-principles methods such as density functional theory (DFT), empirical machine-learning methods have been used for virtual screening. Recently, machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have provided fast proxies for DFT energies. This suggests that virtual screening could be conducted with ML proxies for DFT calculations rather than empirical ML, but this has not yet been applied to OLEDs. We show on a dataset of experimental values extracted from the literature that for emission wavelength, MLIP-based predictions are not inferior to empirical ML. Using an MLIP, we screened millions of molecules for blue emission. Although blue emission is not sufficient for an emitter, our results suggest that further development of virtual screening could focus on machine learned proxies for DFT prediction pipelines rather than models trained to experimental data.

papers.title: Leveraging latent space models for enzyme discovery and sampling
papers.abstract: The exponential growth in available protein sequence data has broadened enzyme discovery opportunities but simultaneously highlighted a significant gap between sequence and function information. Traditional tools like phylogenetic trees and sequence similarity networks (SSNs) are widely adopted for sampling enzymes for novel transformations. However, their utility suffers from inherent limitations, which are exacerbated for large enzyme families. Phylogenetic trees, while useful for studying evolutionary relationships, become computationally intensive and difficult to visualize for larger protein datasets. SSNs, on the other hand, are sensitive to user-defined thresholds for sequence clustering and easily fail to capture more distant relationships between clusters. Additionally, both tools are alignment based and cannot capture higher-order interactions between residues. In this study, we address these limitations by optimizing a variational autoencoder (VAE)-based latent space model to visualize and explore enzyme sequence-function landscapes. By training our models on simulated datasets and real enzyme families, such as cyclases and flavin-dependent monooxygenases (FDMOs), we demonstrated that the optimized latent space effectively preserves phylogenetic relationships and enables high-resolution clustering for functionally distinct enzymes. The models further outperform traditional SSNs in capturing local and global relationships in a continuous two-dimensional space, enabling the discovery of multiple uncharacterized FDMOs for oxidative dearomatization and decarboxylative hydroxylation that illustrates their application. Our findings show that lowdimensional latent spaces can serve as valuable tools for enzyme discovery, allowing for interpolation and extrapolation to guide novel enzyme sampling for biocatalytic reactions.

papers.title: Particle-Resolved Kinetics of Nesquehonite Nucleation and Growth in a Microfluidic Reactor
papers.abstract: Carbon mineralization offers a pathway for permanent CO 2 sequestration via stable carbonate phases within magnesium-rich solutions derived from serpentine mining residues. The precipitation and growth kinetics were monitored in a microfluidic reactor with temperature control spanning thermodynamically distinct regimes for relatively high CO 2 /Mg nesquehonite (MgCO 3 ·3H 2 O) compared to hydromagnesite (Mg 5 (CO 3 ) 4 (OH) 2 ·4H 2 O). The high surface area polydimethylsiloxane microchannel environment was observed to stabilize nesquehonite formation to 70 °C. An apparent activation energy of 107 ± 12 kJ mol-1 was determined for nesquehonite formation, significantly higher than values reported for bulk systems (~70 kJ mol -1 ). Taken together, this behaviour is consistent with the stabilization of precursor species under the availability of silica-derived interfacial species. Silicon was not measurably incorporated into either of the precipitated phases, consistent with an interfacial stabilizing role over a consumable reactant. These findings provide mechanistic insight into magnesium carbonate formation under microfluidic conditions and point to new approaches to formation of CO 2 -dense precipitates over an expanded temperature range.

papers.title: Sustainable Photothermal Nanomedicine: Green Synthesis and Optimisation of Laser–Activated Plasmonic Nanoparticles for Deep-Tissue Therapy
papers.abstract: Sustainable photothermal nanomedicine has emerged as a promising approach for minimally invasive cancer treatment through the conversion of near–infrared (NIR) light into localised heat using plasmonic nanoparticles. Despite significant advancements in photothermal therapy, clinical translation remains hindered by issues related to synthesis sustainability, biological targeting efficiency, reproducibility, and the lack of integrated optimisation frameworks. This critically analyses plasmonic nanomaterials that exhibit localised surface plasmon resonance (LSPR), focusing particularly on the incorporation of green synthesis approaches and photothermal design principles. Plant-mediated, microbial, and biomoleculeassisted synthesis fabrication strategies are assessed for their potential to lessen environmental impact and enhance biocompatibility compared to traditional chemical synthesis techniques. Essential physicochemical factors, including nanoparticle size, morphology, surface chemistry, and dielectric environment, are examined concerning their influence on photothermal conversion efficiency and NIR absorption behaviour. To address the multifaceted challenges of sustainable photothermal nanomedicine, a Five-Layer Sustainable Photothermal Optimisation Framework is proposed integrating material design, green synthesis limitations, optical tuning, biological compatibility, translational scalability, and laser–tissue interaction parameters. The review further highlights ongoing limitations in reproducibility, standardisation, and long-term translational feasibility within existing plasmonic systems. Collectively, this review provides a system–level conceptual framework intended to facilitate the development of safer, more sustainable, and clinically translatable photothermal nanoplatforms for future cancer therapies.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn at the authors' request to address a third-party concern regarding the subject matter of the manuscript. The withdrawal does not reflect any issues with the scientific validity, integrity, or originality of the research.

papers.title: The Safety and Risks of Propylene Glycol as An Excipient in Pharmaceuticals: A Scoping Review Including Environmental Footprint
papers.abstract: Propylene glycol (PG) is a ubiquitous pharmaceutical excipient utilized for its superior solvent properties in oral, topical, and intravenous medications. Although categorized as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS), its potential for systemic toxicity remains a significant clinical concern. This research investigates the safety profile and associated risks of PG exposure, focusing on the mechanisms of toxicity such as lactic acidosis, hyperosmolality, and central nervous system depression. Special emphasis is placed on vulnerable populations, including neonates and patients with renal or hepatic impairment, who face heightened risks due to immature metabolic pathways. Furthermore, the study explores the unseen risk of cumulative exposure in polypharmacy settings. The review contextualizes PG within the broader landscape of pharmaceutical excipient safety, drawing parallels with other commonly used excipients such as sodium benzoate, benzoic acid, and benzalkonium chloride. By reviewing current regulatory guidelines and evaluating clinical monitoring techniques, this paper provides a comprehensive assessment of PG safety. Ultimately, it suggests formulation alternatives and stricter labeling requirements to mitigate adverse outcomes and enhance patient safety in modern clinical practice.

papers.title: Developing and evaluating an accessible method for testing portable air cleaners
papers.abstract: In this work we present a simplified method to measure the performance of homemade air cleaners to enable community-engaged and citizen science. CADR values measured using the simplified method in a residence with low-cost sensors were ≈ 26% lower than laboratory measurements using research-grade instruments, providing a conservative estimate. We evaluated ten portable air cleaners, including seven homemade (“DIY”) prototypes plus three commercial models for several physical and economic parameters. The most effective prototype at reducing PM2.5 concentrations was a 4-filter Corsi-Rosenthal box. The inclusion of a shroud around the fan outlet increased the CADR by ≈ 11%. A single 4-inch-thick MERV 13 filter attached to a box fan also yielded high CADR values with a slim aspect ratio and low initial cost, which can be a good option for some space-constrained indoor environments or as a window attachment. Additional tests found minimal concerns related to the feasibility of operating a homemade air cleaner in a home setting, including motor temperature and power consumption. Analyzing a collection of 135 DIY and commercially available PAC models shows that the average DIY model costs incur a significantly lower initial cost per CADR unit, at 0.41 ± 0.35 $/cfm compared to 1.5 ± 1.3 $/cfm for commercially available units. This work highlights the practical nature of homemade air cleaners and enables members of the public to evaluate their own models using affordable and readily available tools.

papers.title: Orientation and coupling in sum-frequency generation spectra of interfacial water
papers.abstract: Vibrational sum-frequency generation (SFG) spectroscopy is one of the most direct probes of interfacial water, but the structural meaning of the broad hydrogen-bonded O–H stretch band remains ambiguous because molecular orientation and vibrational coupling are entangled. Here we establish a structure-resolved interpretation of the water–air SFG response by decomposing simulated spectra into instantaneous-layer and orientational motifs. The spectra are obtained from partially adiabatic centroid molecular dynamics trajectories, which include nuclear quantum effects, and evaluated with the surface-specific velocity–velocity correlation function formalism. The decomposition shows that the positive free-O–H response is generated mainly by top-layer molecules with an O–H bond pointing toward the vapour phase, whereas the negative hydrogen-bonded band is dominated by motifs with bonded O–H groups oriented toward the liquid. A central result is that water molecules whose dipoles and O–H bonds are nearly parallel to the interface are locally weak in the intramolecular SFG response but become spectroscopically visible through intermolecular vibrational coupling. The second layer contributes only weakly to the net spectrum because oppositely oriented motifs largely cancel. These findings provide a physically constrained spectra–structure assignment for interfacial water and clarify why fitted SFG bands should not be interpreted as independent static species.

papers.title: Detecting Methylation in MCF7 Cells with a Combination of SCX- and No-Enrichment Methods
papers.abstract: Methylation is an important post-translational modification that impacts cellular processes. Yet, methylation is difficult to detect with proteomics because it is less common compared to other modifications and often localized on low-abundance peptides. Although methylation does not alter physiochemical properties of amino acids, there is a reduced probability of trypsin cleavage after methylated lysine or arginine, leading to increased positive charges on methylated peptides. Strong-cation exchange (SCX) can be used to enrich methylated peptides. However, the number of methylation sites identified with SCX varies across previous studies, likely due to the use of different stationary phases and supports, elution strategies, and combinations of multiple enrichment techniques. Therefore, we hypothesize that commercially available SCX tips with a MS-friendly, ammonium-acetate elution can be used to enrich methylated peptides. Our results show that SCX effectively fractionates peptides by charge, which is associated with number of missed cleavages, and methylated peptides elute in fractions with high concentrations of ammonium acetate. When comparing SCX and no-enrichment methods, complementary methylation sites are identified, differing by sequence motifs. Ultimately, these results suggest that both SCX and no-enrichment methods may be required to effectively profile the methylome of complex biological samples. Data has been deposited into MassIVE (MSV000098142).

papers.title: Fluorine-Induced Elimination Drives Covalent Capture in Isocitrate Lyase
papers.abstract: Fluorinated succinate analogues were evaluated as mechanistic probes of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isocitrate lyase ( Mt ICL). Whereas geminal difluoro and trifluoro derivatives ( 1 and 2 ) exhibited nonproductive inhibition and meso -2,3-difluorosuccinate ( 3 ) displayed slow-onset reversible inhibition ( K i = 28 µM), the monofluorosuccinate enantiomers (( R )- 4 and ( S )- 4 ) produced time-dependent irreversible inactivation. Inactivation by 4 was observable under turnover conditions in the presence of glyoxylate and succinate, consistent with a two-step kinetic mechanism. The S enantiomer inactivated more efficiently than ( R )- 4 , consistent with stereoelectronic alignment required for elimination of HF following abstraction of the pro-S proton. 1 H NMR analysis detected maleate formation from (S)-4, and mass spectrometry revealed a +132 Da adduct consistent with covalent modification of Cys191. Notably, k inact / K I values for 4 exceeded that measured for maleate, indicating that covalent capture occurs from an enzyme-bound intermediate prior to product release. These results support a mechanism in which fluorine substitution redirects the enolate-generating half-reaction of Mt ICL toward elimination and covalent modification. ( S )-2-Fluorosuccinate therefore represents a succinate-analogue mechanism-based inactivator that exploits a catalytic step distinct from previously described isocitrate-analogue inhibitors.

papers.title: PEARL: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Retrieval-Augmented Learning for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction requires representations that capture both the sequential chemistry encoded in SMILES strings and the three-dimensional geometry governing binding and toxicity. No systematic benchmark has directly compared parameter-efficient adaptation of 1D chemical language models (CLMs) against an SE(3)-equivariant 3D model across diverse molecular tasks, or examined whether retrieval-augmented context can bridge the gap between these representation classes. Methods: We introduce PEARL (Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Retrieval-augmented Learning), which (i) benchmarks Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) uniformly across three CLM families-ChemBERTa, MolFormer, and Uni-Mol-on four molecular property datasets, and (ii) introduces a Retrieval-Augmented Feature Enhancement (RAFE) pipeline that enriches predictions with label-free physicochemical neighborhood context from the ZINC-250k knowledge base. Results: Uni-Mol’s SE(3)-equivariant architecture achieves the best BACE inhibitor classification (MCC=0.623), an 8% absolute gain over the best SMILES-based model, confirming that 3D geometry provides an inductive advantage for binding-affinity tasks. On BBBP, RAFE with MolFormer achieves MCC=0.798, matching end-to-end LoRA while providing interpretable chemical-neighborhood context. On the five-class Flavor task, RAFE reaches MCC=0.804, though, statistically indistinguishable from end-to-end LoRA (MCC=0.801). All models achieve 75-97% parameter reduction via LoRA, matching or exceeding published baselines, including GROVER-Large and Mole-BERT. Availability: Code is available at https://github.com/ raghvendra5688/PEARL.

papers.title: Non-target analytical workflow for gas-phase atmospheric chemicals collected on XAD resin and application to passive samplers
papers.abstract: The atmospheric gas phase is underrepresented in non-target screening of environmental organic chemicals, partly due to limited evidence on sorbent suitability. Here, we developed and optimized a workflow for non-target analysis (NTA) of styrene-divinylbenzene copolymeric (XAD) resin-based air samples that involves both gas (GC) and liquid chromatography (LC) high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). More than 60 000 features were detected in passive air samplers (PAS) deployed over 4 to 48 weeks. Of ~34 000 features retained after blank filtration, ~14 000 (41%) showed an increasing signal with deployment time, suggesting that they represent substances with volatility and degradability sufficiently low for accumulation on XAD without substantial re-evaporation or degradation during the prolonged sampling period. Such linear uptake is a prerequisite for comparing PAS-derived signals across deployments and chemical classes. Chemical identification by reference standards (level 1) and spectral library matching (level 2) initially identified/annotated 116 compounds, many of which were bioactive and/or brown carbon species. Combining advanced downstream computational workflows of feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) and in silico prediction (NAP/MetFrag) allowed for the structural annotation (level 3) of >8300 LC-HRMS features, including several compounds of natural and anthropogenic origin which were not previously reported in the atmospheric gas phase. Several long-chain fatty acids showed rapid early increases implausible with atmospheric origins and are likely to originate from microbial growth on the resin. Overall, our results demonstrated that XAD is a sorbent compatible with comprehensive NTA and suitable for time-integrated passive sampling of a diverse range of gas-phase organic chemicals from the atmosphere.

papers.title: Longitudinal Piezojunction Effect in SiC/Si Heterojunction for Ultrasensitive Mechanical Sensors
papers.abstract: Highly sensitive mechanical sensors are essential for advanced sensing applications. However, the piezojunction effect for mechanical sensing, wherein mechanical strain modulates charge-carrier transport across the interface of semiconductor heterojunction, remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate the train-induced quantum mechanical effects in n-3C-SiC/p-Si heterojunction, probing carrier transport along the [110] crystallographic orientation under controlled uniaxial strain. Under a forward bias of 5 V, the heterojunction achieves a longitudinal gauge factor (GF) of 106.2, representing a 112% enhancement over the transverse GF, and an approximately 29-fold improvement compared with previously reported longitudinal GFs in n-3C-SiC thin-film.
