By correlating charge-carrier transport measurements with band-structure considerations, we identify a synergistic interplay of strain‑induced conduction‑band valley shifts in 3C‑SiC, valence‑band splitting in Si, and redistribution of carrier effective-mass tensor components under applied strain. Furthermore, we show that forward bias systematically reduces the heterojunction barrier height and depletion width, enabling bias-tunable carrier injection across the heterointerface. Our findings establish a physical framework connecting crystallographic orientation, energy band structure, and interfacial charge carrier dynamics to macroscopic piezoresistive anisotropy in semiconductor heterojunctions. Beyond the specific 3C-SiC/Si system, these results offer broadly applicable design principles for strain-engineered heterojunction devices with broad applications in wearable electronics, MEMS, and precision robotics.

papers.title: Agentic, autonomous design evolution of machine-learned interatomic potentials
papers.abstract: Autonomous agents can write code, run experiments and propose follow-up trials, but systematic autoresearch requires more than isolated candidate generation. AutoResearch-MLIP tests this boundary in machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), treating development as autonomous evolution of implemented designs rather than one-shot architecture proposal. A skill-programmed harness constrains the process: MLIP-Autoresearch governs trial orchestration, evaluator interfaces and continuation decisions, while MLIP-Evidence converts papers, repositories and code audits into design evidence before executable trials. Starting from a generated near-zero pair-distance MLP seed, the protocol reconstructs a 40-generation lineage of 280 evaluated trials. The lineage explores local interaction, readout, representation, long-range-inspired and periodic-graph design elements while using failures as constraints. Post hoc MD22 and OMat24-derived checks place the final evolved candidate among competitive baselines. The work demonstrates auditable design evolution: hypotheses, code edits, measurements, failures and continuation decisions remain linked throughout autonomous research.

papers.title: Cu(II/I)-Pyridinophane Complexes: O2 Reactivity and 64Cu PET Imaging Studies
papers.abstract: The redox versatility of copper between the Cu(I) and Cu(II) oxidation states is central to its function in a variety of biological processes, including electron transfer, oxygen transport, and redox catalysis by metalloenzymes. Motivated by these biological paradigms, we report the design and development of a new series of chelators based on the 2aza[3,2](2,6)pyridinophane (RN3) ligands (RN3, R = H, Me, 2-methylpyridyl, and 2methylpicolinate). These ligands are designed to replicate key features of metalloenzyme active sites and to modulate the copper coordination environment. The new RN3 ligands have been fully characterized by NMR spectroscopy, high-resolution mass spectrometry, and UV-vis spectrophotometric titrations. The Cu(I) and Cu(II) complexes supported by these ligands were synthesized and characterized structurally and spectroscopically to investigate the effects of ligand denticity, variation in donor atoms, and chelate ring size on coordination geometry, bond 2 parameters, and redox behavior. Special attention is given to the reactivity of Cu(I) complexes towards O2, offering insights into pathways of O2 activation and reduction. The RN3 ligands also demonstrate promising stability and binding affinity for both Cu(II) and Cu(I) ions, underscoring their potential for 64Cu-based positron emission tomography (PET) imaging applications.

papers.title: Water-Soluble POSS Enables Concurrent Coalescence and Crosslinking for Multiscale-Reinforced, VOC-Free Waterborne Coatings
papers.abstract: Waterborne thermoset coatings face a fundamental formulation dilemma, whereby premature crosslinking restricts latex particle deformation and polymer diffusion, thus necessitating the use of VOC-emitting coalescing agents to achieve continuous film formation. Here, this dilemma is resolved using a water-soluble, amine-functionalized polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (NPOSS) to promote cooperative coalescence and interparticle crosslinking in a latex of epoxy-functionalized core–shell microspheres. Dissolved in water, NPOSS can transiently plasticize the latex particles to facilitate coalescence while exhibiting a moderate reaction rate that permits interparticle diffusion prior to extensive crosslinking. Cryo-TEM directly visualizes how this mechanism enables particle coalescence prior to bulk water removal, while ATR-FTIR confirms continued post-drying network densification. This process yields a multiscale reinforcement architecture comprising a molecular-scale covalent network, nanoscale chemical heterogeneity, and micrometer-scale compositional homogeneity. Driven by this multiscale reinforcement, the NPOSS network simultaneously delivers remarkable enhancements in both macroscopic strength and toughness. Transparent coatings prepared without added coalescing agents or co-solvents exhibit 2H hardness, 6.60 N scratch resistance, >89% visible transmittance, and strong chemical resistance, thereby establishing this approach viable for VOC-free waterborne thermoset coatings.

papers.title: Emulsion-assisted electroless synthesis of Fe-Co-Ni-B multicomponent electrocatalyst nanoparticles for hydrogen evolution reaction
papers.abstract: We report an emulsion-assisted electroless synthesis of multicomponent Fe–Co–Ni–B nanoparticles composed of less-noble metals. Using a water-in-oil emulsion, the supply of a borohydride as a reducing agent from the organic phase enables suppression of hydroxide formation in the aqueous phase and promotes the formation of metallic nanoparticles. The thus obtained nanoparticles exhibit an amorphous metal–boride core with a thin oxide/hydroxide shell and homogeneous elemental distribution. Control experiments with a single metallic component reveal that multicomponent reduction facilitates metallic Fe incorporation. The droplet size in the emulsion is found to critically influence reduction behavior, indicating the existence of an optimal nanoscale reaction volume. Electrochemical measurements in alkaline media demonstrate enhanced hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity of Fe–Co–Ni–B compared to single-metal counterparts, highlighting the beneficial effect of multicomponent alloying. This method offers a simple and scalable strategy toward the production of multicomponent alloy nanoparticles with improved catalytic performance.

papers.title: Synthesis and Characterization of a Methoxypolyethylene Glycol-Modified Bortezomib Prodrug
papers.abstract: To address the low water solubility, nonspecific biodistribution, low tumor penetration, and easy inactivation of bortezomib (BTZ) under physiological conditions, we designed and synthesized a novel methoxypolyethylene glycol-modified bortezomib prodrug (mPEG2000-DEA-BTZ). This prodrug employs diethanolamine as a linker and mPEG2000 as the polymer chain, synthesized via a three-step reaction, and its chemical structure was confirmed by 1H NMR. Solubility experiments showed that in PBS buffer at pH 7.4, the solubility of mPEG2000-DEA-BTZ was ≥ 436.0 mg/mL, equivalent to a bortezomib solubility of ≥ 66.7 mg/mL, over 167-fold higher than that of free BTZ (399 μg/mL). In vitro release experiments demonstrated that only ~2% of BTZ was released from the prodrug within 24 h at pH 7.4, indicating excellent physiological stability. In contrast, drug release was markedly accelerated under acidic conditions (pH 6.5 and pH 5.0), with the cumulative release exceeding 90% at pH 5.0 within 4 h and approaching complete release at 24 h. Compared with the previously reported mPEG5000-CA-BTZ prodrug, the lower molecular weight mPEG2000 and diethanolamine linker used in this study significantly improved the drug release rate and completeness. This pH-sensitive prodrug is expected to improve the pharmacokinetic profile of bortezomib and achieve acidic tumor microenvironment-triggered targeted release, demonstrating significant potential for clinical translation.

papers.title: From Top to Bottom: Manufacturing Process-context Aware Resolution of Energy Device Electrodes through a 3D Diffusion Generative Model
papers.abstract: Optimization of electrochemical energy storage and conversion devices often relies on electrode microstructure properties, of which its 3D representation provides the most complete link between manufacturing process and device performance. Deep generative models can address slow experimental throughput and high computational cost of traditional microstructure resolution, yet most literature focuses on Generative Adversarial Networks, known for mode collapse issues. This work applies a generative Diffusion model to synthesize 3D-resolved multiphase microstructures of LIB and Polymer Electrolyte Membrane Fuel Cell electrodes, sourced from experimental imaging and computer-based simulations. Generated volumes are validated against training data based on microstructural descriptors including volume fraction, specific surface area, and tortuosity factor. Regarding the latter, standard cubic sub-volume augmentation for generative model training fails to capture depth-dependent features in thick and heavily processed microstructures, such as calendered electrodes. A depth-aware augmentation pipeline is proposed to incorporate full electrode thickness into training samples, improving through-thickness tortuosity accuracy of generated samples. Furthermore, 3D-resolved multiphysics simulation on the generated microstructures reproduce the performance behavior of their training counterparts with high accuracy. These results establish Diffusion models as a viable framework to generate commercially relevant electrode data, intended for computational optimization and design of next-generation energy devices.

papers.title: Long-term hygrothermal degradation of PLA 2D nanocomposites: Decoupling physical plasticization from irreversible hydrolytic failure
papers.abstract: The long-term environmental resilience of poly(lactic acid) (PLA) remains a critical bottleneck for its application in sustainable infrastructure. This study investigates the hygrothermal degradation of PLA reinforced with 1 wt.% of three distinct 2D nanofillers: organomodified nanoclay (NC), graphene nanoplatelets (GNP), and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). Specimens were exposed to a controlled environment of 40◦C and 75% relative humidity for six months. While moisture uptake remained low (0.3%–0.7%), mechanical and rheological characterisation revealed severe underlying chemical degradation. Impact testing and DSC analysis identified hBN as the most effective stabiliser, preserving 86% of toughness and maintaining a consistent crystallisation profile. In contrast, neat PLA and NC composites experienced a near-total collapse of melt viscosity, signalling significant chain scission. A comparative analysis with previous water immersion data demonstrates that while liquid contact accelerates early plasticization, long-term humidity exposure leads to a more brittle, irreversible failure mode. These findings highlight the critical role of filler chemistry in extending the environmental shelf-life of bio-based polyesters.

papers.title: A Data-Driven Framework for Precision Hydroxyurea Therapy in Pediatric Sickle Cell Anemia Using Microsensor Arrays and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: This manuscript presents a structured data-driven framework for the precise quantification of hydroxyurea in pediatric sickle cell anemia patient samples. By integrating multidimensional patient clinical metadata with temporal alignment of dosing and sampling, along with highly overlapping and masking electrochemical signatures originating from blood samples, we developed a robust approach to mitigate signal noise and artifacts in sensor data, enabling reliable quantification in a small clinical cohort (n = 50). To enhance predictive accuracy, multiple feature-engineering strategies were employed, incorporating diverse representations of electrochemical variability, including averaged repeat signals across samples and electrodes, frequency-domain features, and normalized signal integrals. Benchmarking of multiple machine-learning models using 50 iterations of nested cross-validation, together with preprocessing via nonlinear kernel cosine principal component analysis, showed that Elastic Net performed best for Repeat-2 across samples and electrodes (R2) and R2-50% configurations, resulting mean RMSE values of 69.56 µM (5.29 µg/mL) and 66.53 µM (5.06 µg/mL), respectively. To address the loss of temporal electrochemical variability during preprocessing (from the full 21-electrode dataset to a refined 13-electrode), we further implemented a reservoir computing approach combined with Elastic Net regression, which reduced the RMSE to 62.37 µM (4.74 µg/mL) without evidence of systematic overfitting. A comprehensive optimism-bias assessment indicated that signal-averaging approaches were more stable (mean bias = 1.64 µM for the R2 dataset) than frequency-domain features. In parallel, the classification pipeline for patient stratification achieved an accuracy of 0.82 and an F1-score of 0.79. Building on the reference study by Shukla et al. (Anal. Chem. 2025, 97, 44, 24399-24414), this work emphasizes model robustness, advanced electrochemical feature engineering, and introduces patient demographic information as an additional factor to improve generalization. Overall, these findings establish a validated framework for AI-enabled point-of-care systems for hydroxyurea therapeutic drug monitoring in pediatric sickle cell anemia and provide a foundation for more precise, data-driven clinical decision-making across diverse healthcare settings.

papers.title: The interplay of nanoparticle size and reaction temperature limits the ammonia decomposition kinetics on dual-site Ni catalysts
papers.abstract: The utilization of renewable hydrogen that was transported and stored as green ammonia relies on a highly efficient ammonia decomposition catalyst. Industrial demand for high-purity hydrogen requires operation at high temperature of at least 500 °C due to the endothermicity of the reaction. At these conditions, abundant Ni/MgO catalysts with nanoparticles larger than 5 nm are not limited by the widely studied N-N recombination, but the rate-determining step (RDS) has changed to ammonia dehydrogenation. A combined experimental and theoretical study on size-controlled Ni/MgO catalysts explains this behavior in a dual-site / dual-RDS model by the interplay of a size-induced lack of edge sites that are active in ammonia dehydrogenation, and an increase in the free energy barrier of this step relative to the N-N recombination. Catalyst design thus needs to aim at a stabilization of an optimal Ni nanoparticle size at high reaction temperatures to balance the two possible kinetic limitations by an optimal relative abundance of the edge sites active in ammonia dehydrogenation and the B5 sites for N-N recombination. Such stabilization is demonstrated for co-precipitated and ex-solved Ni/MgO catalysts where the optimal size is determined to be 5-6 nm. Future catalyst development for high-temperature ammonia decomposition should target the promotion of the ammonia dehydrogenation sites on larger particles and /or the modification of smaller particles to facilitate the N-N recombination step.

papers.title: Tracing Dissolved Iridium in Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis Using Operando Hard-X-Ray Fluorescence
papers.abstract: Dissolution of iridium in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer anodes is a critical challenge on the path towards low-cost and durable water electrolysis. While end-of-test analysis of electrolyzers showed that most of the dissolved catalyst redeposits in the membrane and the cathode catalyst layer, this approach offers only limited insight into the dynamics of iridium dissolution, transport, and redeposition mechanisms. By means of 2D-mapping with synchrotron-based operando X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy, we detected dissolved iridium in the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) during electrolysis operation and traced the dynamics of its transport under varied operation conditions with reasonable temporal (20 min per map) and spatial (10 µm) resolution. During electrolysis, we observed an accumulation of dissolved iridium in the cathode catalyst layer. With the toggling flow of dry gas at the cathode, we can distinguish between mobile and redeposited iridium. Though thermodynamically favored, no significant deposition within the cathode was observed after ~1 h of electrolysis. The results obtained are another puzzle piece in the understanding of iridium dissolution in electrolyzers towards its possible mitigation.

papers.title: Redox Buffering and Corrosion in Molten Chloride Salts Dictated by Chlorobasicity
papers.abstract: This study establishes an in-situ synchrotron approach to directly link molten-salt chemistry, redox-buffer speciation, and alloy corrosion in chloride melts. Using a first-of-its-kind corrosion cell coupled to simultaneous X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray fluorescence (XRF), we monitor europium redox-buffer speciation and chromium dissolution during corrosion of Ni-20Cr in molten LiCl-KCl and KCl-MgCl 2 salts. To build a mechanistic framework, we combine UV-Vis optical basicity measurements, in-situ electrochemistry, and molecular dynamics simulations to quantify how salt chlorobasicity reshapes europium solvation and shifts the Eu(III)/Eu(II) apparent potential. Increasing MgCl 2 content drives the apparent potential of the Eu(III)/Eu(II) couple +0.45 V relative to LiCl-KCl and stabilizes Eu(II)-compatible solvation environments. In-situ, time-resolved Eu L3-edge XANES reveals progressive Eu(III) reduction in KCl-MgCl 2 melts, while Eu(III) remains predominantly stable in LiCl-KCl. This behavior is consistent with a chlorobasicity-activated reaction with boron nitride (BN) cell components. In less chlorobasic melts, salt redox chemistry enables BN chlorination, allowing BN to act as a sacrificial reductant and chlorinating agent that promotes Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion, whereas this pathway is not thermodynamically favored in LiCl-KCl. During active corrosion of Ni-20Cr, coupled Eu XANES and Cr XRF measurements show concurrent Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion and Cr dissolution, confirming that Eu(III) is the oxidizing species driving chromium oxidation. Together, these results demonstrate that chlorobasicity is a central control variable for redox-buffer speciation and corrosion thermodynamics, and more broadly that chlorobasicity can enable or suppress reactive pathways with structural materials in high-temperature molten salts.

papers.title: Electrochemical Oxidation-Promoted Sequential Cyclization/Aromatization toward Carbazole Synthesis
papers.abstract: An electrochemical strategy for the synthesis of carbazole frameworks has been developed. Bromidemediated anodic oxidation generates electrophilic [Br+] species, which selectively oxidize the indole core and trigger a subsequent intramolecular endo-cyclization/aromatization sequence, thereby furnishing carbazole derivatives via a bioinspired pathway. Notably, the electrochemical protocol enables controlled, gradual generation of the reactive species, effectively suppressing overoxidation and preventing the formation of inseparable brominated byproducts that are typically observed under conventional chemical conditions. Mechanistic studies, including cyclic voltammetry, support preferential oxidation of the indole moiety and highlight the key role of bromide as a redox mediator. This operationally simple and efficient method provides a valuable approach to carbazole-containing scaffolds and is expected to facilitate the total synthesis of indolosesquiterpene natural products.

papers.title: Expanding Chemical Space Enables Data–Driven Structure–Activity Relationships in Cage Catalysis
papers.abstract: Data-driven approaches are increasingly popular in catalysis, supplementing and even replacing traditional strategies that largely relied on empirical optimization. However, their application in the field of bio-inspired cage catalysis remains largely unexplored, primarily due to the limited chemical space of known catalytically active cages. As a result, mechanistic insights are often obtained using computationally intensive DFT calculations on a handful of structurally similar cages. As chemical systems grow in complexity, this approach becomes impractical. Herein, we report an experimental/computational framework that significantly expediates the exploration of a much wider structural landscape while offering experimental insights. This is made possible by a novel in situ experimental procedure – which circumvents the traditional time-consuming process of prepare, isolate, characterize, and test – coupled with data-driven methods to identify molecular features that govern activity. Using this approach, we experimentally explored 30 unique PdnL2n cages (n = 2–4) shown to mediate a nitro-aldol reaction with activity spanning over four orders of magnitude. Using this dataset, a random forest model trained on molecular descriptors was developed to predict ΔG‡ (MAE of 0.4 kcal mol−1 and R2 = 0.9). Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlighted geometric preorganization and electrostatic interactions within the cage as key determinants of catalytic efficiency. Moreover, DFT calculations on a selection of cages further validated these insights, indicating that meaningful mechanistic understanding can be achieved at significantly reduced computational cost. We anticipate that this integrated screen / data-driven / mechanistic strategy will provide a blueprint workflow for understanding the reactivity of metal-organic cages and encourage the generation of more comprehensive datasets across cage families, ultimately enabling the rational design of improved catalytic architectures.

papers.title: Unlocking Iridium Chemical Space for Antibiotic Discovery through One-Pot Combinatorial Synthesis in a Direct-to-Biology Approach
papers.abstract: Antibacterial resistance continues to drive the need for exploring novel chemical space beyond conventional organic scaffolds. Metal-based compounds have emerged as a promising class of antibiotic candidates, demonstrating high hit rates against priority bacterial pathogens without exhibiting increased toxicity compared to purely organic molecules. Here, we report a one-pot, three-component combinatorial strategy for the synthesis of piano-stool Ir(III) cyclopentadienyl Schiff-base complexes as potential antibacterial agents. Using 15 picolinaldehydes (A–O), 24 amines (1–24), and four Cp/Cp* iridium precursors (Cp1–4), a library of 1440 complexes was generated and screened directly from crude reaction mixtures in a direct-to-biology approach. Biological screening revealed pronounced activity against Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus, particularly for biphenyl-substituted Cp (Cp2) complexes, while no activity was observed against Gram-negative bacteria. A subset of the compounds exhibits potent and selective antibacterial activity with low mammalian cell toxicity. Dose-response validation identified 4 promising hit candidates, of which Ir15 displays low-micromolar activity against a panel of Gram-positive pathogens, limited haemolysis, and moderate cytotoxicity. Initial mechanistic studies indicate that Ir15 acts through a membrane-associated mode of action involving mild membrane depolarisation without large pore formation, alongside changes in nucleoid morphology. Overall, this work establishes Ir(III) Cp Schiff-base complexes as a modular antibacterial platform and identifies Ir15 as a promising lead compound for further optimisation.

papers.title: Superparamagnetic Biomembranes for Dynamic Nanoparticle and Molecular Patterning
papers.abstract: We introduce superparamagnetic biomembranes as a novel, actively tunable hybrid platform. The superparamagnetic biomembranes are supported lipid bilayers (SLBs) with defined lipid composition and site-specific coupling of proteins and superparamagnetic nanoparticles (MNPs). 2 Application of magnetic field gradients induces rapid and fully reversible lateral transport of lipidanchored MNPs with forces in the femtonewton range. Using single magnetic tips as well as multiple magnetic tips and line structures, we achieve parallelized and spatially defined MNP patterning. Transition of the SLB from the liquid-crystalline to the gel phase enables reversible immobilization of the patterned MNP distributions. Local MNP accumulation displaces lipids and membrane-associated proteins, including Neutravidin, mEGFP, and CD19, thereby generating inverse molecular gradients that are recognized by living cells. This biocompatible substrate with dynamically controllable nanoparticle and molecular organization provides a versatile framework for applications in bio- and nanotechnology.

papers.title: Iron-Carbon-Cesium Blended Ammonia Catalyst by Metal-Induced Graphitization
papers.abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a potential hydrogen carrier in a future hydrogen economy and an alternative fuel to petroleum. Due to economic and environmental concerns, worldwide research focuses on developing less energy-intensive methods to produce non-noble metal 2 catalysts for efficient NH 3 synthesis under milder conditions. This work presents an approach to fabricate a carbon (C)-based, cesium (Cs)-promoted iron (Fe) catalyst that exhibits an excellent and stable NH 3 production performance, surpassing the activity of any reported C-based non-noble metal catalysts. We demonstrate that this outstanding performance is related to the unique structural morphology of the catalyst, featuring carbon onions with an Fe core, embedded within an amorphous C-framework, with the Cs promoter enriched on the surface of Fe nanoparticles. It was achieved by metal-induced lowtemperature graphitization of carbon at as low as 600 °C. The robustness and abundant active sites afforded by these morphological features enable more efficient NH 3 synthesis compared to traditional C-based catalysts fabricated by impregnation. This economical and facile strategy for preparing conductive metal-carbon composites extends beyond the general design principles applicable not only to heterogeneous catalysis but also to a broad range of functional materials, opening new avenues for material design.

papers.title: Redox-mediated electrified method for green and low-cost spent lithium-ion battery materials recycling
papers.abstract: After 30 years of commercialization and mass production, a myriad of lithium-ion batteries have been produced. It has generated a massive amount of battery waste after the batteries reach their lifetime. This would be more so with the widespread applications of lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles. For sustainable development, it has never been so pressing to recycle the spent batteries and valorize the useful components. However, the commonly used pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical methods are either energy-intensive or consume large amounts of chemicals. Here, using LiCoO 2 as an example, we report a closed-loop electrified chemical process based on redox-targeting reactions to recover valuable species from spent battery materials using only electricity and water. Complimentary reductive leaching of LiCoO 2 and oxidative leaching of LiFePO 4 were performed with anthraquinone-2,7-disulfonate as a regenerative redox mediator to sequentially break down LiCoO 2 and achieve efficient separation of Co 2+ and Li + in the form of Co(OH) 2 and LiOH. This cost-effective and environmentally friendly method was also extended to the recycling of LiNi x Mn y Co z O 2 with a high recovery rate of Li+ and transition metal species. It is anticipated that the electrified chemical recycling method demonstrated here would provide a credible solution to the valorization of battery waste and contribute to the sustainable development of lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Total Synthesis of Benthol A. Part 2. The Nominal and the Actual Natural Product
papers.abstract: The total synthesis of the dinoflagellate-derived “super carbon chain compound” benthol A rigorously confirmed what the analysis of one of the required building blocks had forecasted, namely that the configuration of the secondary alcohol at C40 had been misassigned by the isolation team as the only one of a total of 35 stereogenic centers decorating the backbone of this polyol/polyether derivative. This conclusion bears implications because the original assignment had been solely based on computational data, which had resulted in a remarkably high score of 99.93% that was ultimately misleading. The multi-convergent blueprint underlying the successful approach accounts for the fact that a longest linear sequence of 32 steps sufficed to reach this intricate marine natural product. The inherent flexibility should also empower future studies aiming at a detailed mapping of the pharmacophore of this compound endowed with significant antiplasmodial activity.

papers.title: Total Synthesis of Benthol A. Part 1. Forecast of a Structure Revision
papers.abstract: Benthol A, a dinoflagellate-derived polyol/polyether marine natural product endowed with potent anti-malaria and appreciable antiviral activity, consists of a 72 C-atom linear backbone featuring 35 stereogenic centers and four stereogenic alkenes. The constitution and stereostructure of this intriguing “super carbon chain compound” had been assigned by the isolation team by a combination of spectroscopic, chemical and computational means. Outlined in this and the accompanying paper is the first total synthesis of this challenging target, which came along with a subtle structure revision. During the synthesis of the required building blocks, a spectral irregularity was noticed in that the 13C NMR chemical shifts as well as some of the 3JH,H coupling constants of the synthetic samples deviated notably from the data reported for the C31 – C41 region of benthol A corresponding to the tetrahydropyran E-ring and its vicinity. A systematic, synthesis-driven approach made it possible to narrow down the likely site of error with a high degree of certainty to a single, incorrectly assigned stereocenter, i. e. the C40 position; interestingly, the configuration of this site had been determined by the isolation team solely by computational means. In chemical terms, our studies showed how the proper choice of a propargylic protecting group allows the regiochemical course of a gold catalyzed spiroketalization reaction to be steered. Moreover, carbonyl homologation by the addition of a highly functionalized but entirely unstabilized diazo derivative generated in situ to an equally highly functionalized aldehyde proved to be a very adequate method for the coupling of elaborate building blocks (Buchner-Curtius-Schlotterbeck reaction).

papers.title: Supervised Source-Task Pretraining for Low-Data Electrochemical Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Electrochemical molecular property data obtained from experiments or high-level quantum chemical calculations are often limited in size, which constrains the direct use of graph neural networks for predicting oxidation potentials and redox-reaction-related energies. Here, we investigate supervised source-task pretraining as a candidate strategy for low-data molecular prediction by using QM9 as the source domain, pretraining a GINE molecular graph encoder on HOMO, LUMO, HOMO-LUMO gap, and u0, and transferring the resulting encoders to OxPot oxidation-potential prediction and RedDB reaction-energy-related prediction. Across random and scaffold splits and multiple downstream labeleddata budgets, pretraining improved performance only under specific conditions: OxPot benefited more consistently from HOMO and LUMO source tasks, whereas RedDB showed a more dispersed transfer pattern in which gap and u0 could also be competitive. Pretraining-scale and pretraining-seed analyses further supported a sample-size-dependent stage hypothesis in which negative transfer is more likely at extreme-low-data budgets, a positive-transfer window can emerge at low-to-mid data budgets, and gains may diminish or become negative again at higher budgets depending on source-task alignment, downstream difficulty, split difficulty, and source-domain scale.

papers.title: Surface-Chemistry-Driven Enhancement of Spin Coherence in Nanodiamonds under Zero Applied Magnetic Field
papers.abstract: Nanodiamonds hosting nitrogen–vacancy (NV) centers are promising quantum sensors for probing biological environments, yet their spin coherence is highly sensitive to surface chemistry. Here, we systematically investigate how bio-relevant surface coatings govern NV spin coherence under zero applied magnetic field. Bare nanodiamonds were compared with noncovalently encapsulated nanogel (NG) and covalently grafted polyglycerol (PG) coatings using Hahn echo and geometric spin echo sequences optimized for rapid biosensing. Relative to the bare-ND Hahn-echo baseline, the combined use of geometric spin echo and surface coating increased T 2 by 86% for PG-coated NDs and 36% for NG-coated NDs; within geometric spin echo alone, PG-coated NDs showed a 42% increase and NG-coated NDs do not show significant change relative to bare NDs., despite comparable reductions in paramagnetic signatures. These results reveal that covalent surface passivation suppresses surface noise more effectively than noncovalent encapsulation, directly linking surface chemistry to the quantum coherence performance. These findings establish a quantitative link between interface design and spin coherence under zero applied magnetic field, providing materials design rules for next-generation nanodiamond-based quantum biosensors.

papers.title: Catalysis by a metastable photoswitchable cage
papers.abstract: A visible-light-responsive ligand together with a non-switchable ligand can be assembled into a mixture of molecular cages with palladium(II) ions. When irradiated with 530 nm light, the system converges to form a single product, a metastable, mixedligand molecular cage. This cage can be reversibly disassembled using 424 nm light, an example of integrative self-sorting controlled by light. The metastable assembly can catalyze both Michael addition and nitroaldol reactions. Importantly, visible light accesses a metastable catalytic state inaccessible under thermodynamic control. We demonstrate that the active assembled species can be switched on and off at will using visible irradiation. The metastable species is the most catalytically active assembly.

papers.title: Undivided Parallel Paired Electrolysed Chemoselective Cathodic Reduction of α-Keto Amides and Anodic Oxidative Esterification of Aldehydes
papers.abstract: A sustainable parallel paired electrolysis (PPE) methodology has been developed to synthesise αhydroxy amides via chemoselective hydride-free cathodic ketone reduction over amide in α-keto amides at a Pt cathode, and the formation of esters via anodic oxidative esterification of aldehydes at a Pt anode in alcohol. In this PPE, any substitution on α-keto amide not only affects the yield of the reduction process, but also influences the oxidation process as well. Similarly, if a substitution on the aldehyde increases the yield of the oxidation product, it also increases the yield of the reduction product due to potential alignment. In this PPE, aldehydes are necessary for the reduction of α-keto amide by suppressing the formation of hemiketal intermediate at the cathode to form the reduced product, while the oxidation process occurs independently in the absence of α-keto amides at the anode. EPR, CV, controlled experiments, and radical-quenching experiments suggest a radical reaction pathway with an alkoxy radical intermediate generated at the anode and a radical anion intermediate at the cathode. The formation of an acyl radical is crucial in this reaction to suppress the formation of the hemiketal intermediate. The deuterium labelled study reveals that the source of hydrogen is alcohols.

papers.title: Neutral Ligands, Distinct Zeta Potentials: Consequences for Hafnium Oxide Nanoparticles Biodistribution
papers.abstract: Nanoparticles (NPs) are extensively explored in biological contexts, and while their core composition determines their specific functionality, surface chemistry governs their interactions with the biological environment. In this work, we used ultrasmall (d < 5 nm) hafnium oxide nanoparticles (HfO2 NPs) as a model system, given their biocompatibility and established use in contrast-enhanced X-ray computed tomography and external-beam radiotherapy. We systematically compared three surface ligands featuring the same high-affinity nitrocatechol anchoring group but different terminal moieties: a short ethylene glycol oligomer, a 2 kDa polyethylene glycol (PEG) polymer, and a short zwitterion. Despite the neutral character of all ligand tails, only the long PEG chains yielded nanoparticles with a neutral zeta-potential. The short ligands all produced nanoparticles with negative zeta-potential, which was found to be an essential component of their colloidal stability. This negative zeta-potential was correlated with enhanced uptake by THP-1 macrophages in vitro and short circulation times in vivo in zebrafish larvae. In contrast, HfO2 NPs stabilized with long (2 kDa) PEG chains largely escaped detection by the phagocyte system. They exhibited prolonged circulation and extravasation in the zebrafish larva model, highlighting their promise for future targeted nanomedicine delivery.

papers.title: Coupled Electron–Ion Transfer Drives Nickel Nanofilm Formation at a Water‑Free Deep-Eutectic-Solvent/Oil Interface
papers.abstract: Nickel nanofilms were prepared at an ethaline/oil interface, which is a water‑free deep‑eutectic‑solvent (DES)/oil (O) interface, where the absence of water enables a unique environment for interfacial redox chemistry. When NiCl42− in ethaline was contacted with decamethylcobaltocene (DMCc) in toluene at the liquid/liquid interface, nickel nanoparticles nucleated and subsequently assembled into two‑dimensional networks that developed into continuous nanofilms floating at the interface. Liquid/liquid electrochemistry and post-reaction UV–Vis spectroscopy measurements revealed that the reduction of NiCl42− proceeds spontaneously through a coupled electron–ion transfer pathway, in which the electron transfer between NiCl42− and DMCc is balanced by the ion transfer of the generated DMCc+ from the O phase to the DES phase. This charge‑compensated, spontaneous ET–IT mechanism demonstrates that water‑free DES/O interfaces can serve as functional soft templates for substrate‑free base metal nanofilm fabrication.

papers.title: FAVES V4: A Production-Deployed Compliance and Liability Screening System for Drug Discovery at 122M-Compound Scale, Aligned to HHS/ONC FAVES and NIST AI 600-1
papers.abstract: FAVES V4 is a compliance and liability screening system for drug discovery, aligned to two complementary federal frameworks: the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services / Office of the National Coordinator FAVES rubric for trustworthy AI in healthcare and life sciences,31 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1),38 which names chemical and biological design tools as a distinct chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) risk class (Section 2.1). The five letters; Fair, Appropriate, Valid, Effective, Safe; are not principles asserted in this paper; they are operational properties demonstrated against published evidence in production, with named action-ID anchors drawn from NIST AI 600-1 throughout Section 4. A single-API screening call returns regulatory status (DEA / FDA / CWC / EPA / EU REACH), structural alerts (1,585 SMARTS across PAINS, Brenk, NIH, ZINC, and 7 ChEMBL sub-catalogs via RDKit FilterCatalog), pharmacokinetic classification (BOILED-Egg), and prior-art disclosure (InChIKey identity resolution against PubChem and a local 122M-compound database), with per-field provenance metadata. The system is deployed in production with both live RDKit computation (~5 ms per molecule) and a precomputed database cache (122,407,635 documents). The five FAVES properties are operationalized through a complete governance bundle: an Intended Use Statement (Appropriate), risk-based component classification mapped to GAMP and CSA (Valid), end-to-end validation protocol with predetermined acceptance criteria (Valid), three-layer audit trail with two non-skippable layers (Safe), and change-control SOP with a worked rollback example (Safe). Validation across five tests against predetermined acceptance criteria; V3 regulatory benchmark, V4 field completeness, BOILED-Egg implementation, prior-art resolution, and external cross-RDKit-version reproducibility; yields 362/362 compounds passing post-fix at the time of submission. The initial 341/342 pre-fix execution identified a single defect; an incorrect cortisol SMILES in the deployed FDA whitelist that omitted the 11β-hydroxyl; which was root-caused, corrected, deployed, and re-validated through the documented change-control SOP. We report both numbers transparently: the defect was surfaced because the validation was honestly scoped to the full 102-compound regulatory benchmark rather than an undersized fixture, and the change-control loop functioning visibly in production is itself a stronger claim than a never-exercised one. To our knowledge, this is the first cheminformatics screening system whose full HHS/ONC-and NIST AI 600-1-aligned governance scaffolding is described in operational detail, with each of the five FAVES properties demonstrated against public evidence. The benchmark dataset, validation reports, and latency measurements are released for reproducibility; the seven NMCP-FAVES governance documents are summarized in Section 4 with NIST action-ID anchors and worked examples, and full operational versions are available from the corresponding author.

papers.title: RETRACTED: Machine Learning-Guided Virtual Screening Identifies Candidate COX-2 Inhibitors: A Computational Prioritization Study
papers.abstract: Retracted by the author because incorrect underlying data was used. A corrected version is available at 10.26434/chemrxiv.15005946/v1.

papers.title: Open-Source Modular Laboratory Robots as Building Blocks for Flexible Assembly of Self-Driving Labs
papers.abstract: Lab automation is a key enabler of algorithmic-driven research in materials science, by increasing the throughput and accelerating experimental workflows researchers can generate the large amounts of experimental datasets required to validate and refine machine learning and artificial intelligence models. Nonetheless, access to automation remains limited to a small subset of the scientific community due to the high cost of commercial systems, limited expertise and lack of flexible automation tools for evolving research workflows. In response, research groups have developed custom automation solutions by retrofitting low-cost motion platforms, such as 3D printers or CNC machines, to perform experimental tasks. However, these platforms have not been originally designed to meet the requirements of materials science and engineering (MSE) experiments, leading to solutions that do not necessarily scale well with common laboratory infrastructure and practices. Here we introduce the Qubot , a flexible and modular robotic platform designed to meet the requirements of MSE experiments that is built from standardized cost-effective components, lowering the financial and technical barriers for adoption. We characterize the Qubot performance using internationally recognised protocols, demonstrating repeatability and precision superior to commonly used motion platforms that are retrofitted for experimental work. Finally, we validate the design through stress testing in representative experimental tasks and demonstrate their flexible modularity by applying them in two fully automated laboratory workflows related to the preparation and characterization of shampoo formulations and polymer electrolytes.

papers.title: Quantifying the Synergistic and Antagonistic Effects of Metal–Organic Complexation on Aerosol Oxidative Potential via Redox Kinetics
papers.abstract: Oxidative potential (OP) is an indicator of the ability of redox-active species in particulate matter (PM) to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) via aqueous redox chemistry in lung lining fluid. Previous studies have reported synergistic and antagonistic OP interaction effects in mixtures of metals and non-redox-active organics. These effects have been attributed to complexation-induced redox potential and kinetic changes; however, their quantitative validity remains unclear. Here, we evaluated this mechanism using a newly developed chemical equilibrium–kinetic DTT assay model for Fe–oxalate systems. Experiments showed weak interaction effects at oxalate-to-Fe ratios of several tens and strong antagonistic effects at ratios of several hundreds. These ratios include atmospheric conditions and the model successfully reproduced the OP interaction effects through redox potential-driven kinetic changes. Although Fe–oxalate complexation enhanced Fe(II)-driven oxidant reduction kinetics, it simultaneously shifted the Fe redox balance toward Fe(III) and decreased Fe(II) concentrations, limiting the synergistic enhancement. Meanwhile, the strong antagonistic effect was explained by an increased fraction of inert Fe(III)–(oxalate)₃. In contrast, the several-fold synergistic effects observed at extremely high oxalate-to-Fe ratios could not be explained solely by redox potential-driven kinetic changes, suggesting additional mechanisms. These findings contribute to understanding non-additive OP effects and PM toxicity.

papers.title: Improving interdisciplinary research: Ontology and database to structure characteristics of Microplastics (MP)
papers.abstract: Microplastics (MP) are a major environmental pollutant with highly variable properties. They present challenges to society that attract researchers from various disciplines. Important re-search questions include the transport and fate in the environment, the ecological impact and ecotoxicological effects, and the changing properties of MP exposed to different environments. For this question interdisciplinary research is needed which requires a common conceptual approach for discussing MP. Such an ontology connected to a database, that allows interdisciplinary researchers to exchange and harmonize knowledge, is presented here. The ontology structures the key characteristics of MP particles, including particle properties, material properties, parameters of particle degradation, eco-coronas, and biofilms. Additionally, the ontology enables comprehensible and reproducible research through the documentation of manufacturing processes, sample preparation and measurement techniques. A connection to other MP research topics, such as toxicity studies and environmental transport vie unique MP identifiers opens the door to synergistic effects to achieve a deeper understanding of the interplay of MP properties and their behavior and effects.

papers.title: Development of a versatile testing apparatus for measuring hollow fiber membrane flux and permeance
papers.abstract: Despite the widespread adoption of hollow fiber membranes for wastewater treatment application, there remains few available methods of reliably determining the flux, permeance and separation ability of individual hollow fiber membranes for both for outside-in and inside-out operation. We present a new apparatus that can measure the flux and permeance of individual or multiple hollow fiber membranes in both the outside-in and inside-out orientations, partnered with a python-based open-source permeance analysis software. Firstly, we demonstrate the reliability of the instrument in two different configurations. We compare the difference between testing 3 individual membranes and 3 sets of 3 membranes with their permeance combined through manifolds, in dead-end mode. Secondly, we use the apparatus to study compaction and fouling of hollow fiber membranes in both outside-in and inside-out orientation in dead-end mode, with behaviour differences observed dependent on membrane orientation. For the studied ultrafiltration (UF) membranes, there was not a significant difference in performance depending on orientation, however for the microfiltration (MF) membranes, severe compaction-induced flux loss was observed for the inside-out orientation, with no significant compaction observed in outside-in orientation. Additionally, the orientation of liquid flow significantly affected the flux and permeance measurements of fouled MF membranes. We related the difference in permeance to the differences in structure, as characterized by SEM and liquid-liquid porometry. Deviation in results between the two orientations demonstrates the importance of being able to test hollow fiber membranes in both outside-in and inside-out orientations. This newly designed apparatus will be used to further investigate fundamental mechanisms that affect hollow fiber membrane permeance.

papers.title: Integrating GC-MS with Computational Toxicology for Pesticide Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: Pesticide risk assessment separates analytical detection from toxicological evaluation, leaving a practical gap: regulatory-compliant residue levels reveal nothing about the biological hazard of detected compounds, and computational toxicology models are rarely validated against real environmental measurements. This study presents an integrated framework combining GC-MS residue quantification with QSAR-based toxicity prediction, using Mordred molecular descriptors and Random Forest and Gradient Boosting classifiers, deployed as an open-source web API for real-time risk assessment. The framework is demonstrated on three composite cassava samples from a smallholder production system, in which seven pesticides spanning organochlorines, organophosphates, and pyrethroids were detected at 0.40% to 2.20% of Maximum Residue Limits. Toxicity prediction returned uniformly non-mutagenic and non-carcinogenic classifications across all compounds, despite established IARC carcinogen classifications for several organochlorines. Concordance with literature classifications was 28.6% for Ames mutagenicity, indicating systematic under-prediction for persistent organochlorines. This reflects toxicity mechanisms including bioaccumulation and endocrine disruption that extend beyond features captured by topological and constitutional molecular descriptors. Integrated risk scoring identified four compounds warranting medium-priority monitoring despite full regulatory compliance, demonstrating that toxicity-weighted assessment differentiates hazard profiles that concentration-based screening cannot. The framework's modular architecture, separating analytical input, descriptor calculation, toxicity prediction, and risk integration, supports extension to additional crops, chemical classes, and toxicological endpoints. All components are openly available.

papers.title: Quantifying the Coherence Wall: FeMoCo Quantum Chemistry from 48 to 108 Qubits on IBM Heron r2
papers.abstract: We quantify the depth-dependent loss of many-body correlation information in FeMoCo-scale quantum chemistry circuits executed on IBM Heron r2. The workflow combines LUCJ circuit execution, Aurora-DD control, sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), DMRG prior construction, and ph-AFQMC refinement across 48-, 56-, 80-, and 108-qubit active-space instances. Rather than treating the 108-qubit energy as a chemical-accuracy claim, we separate statistical precision, systematic phaseless bias, and extractable correlation signal. The 108-qubit CAS(54e,54o) run reaches a ph-AFQMC statistical standard error of ±0.67 mHa, while the single-determinant phaseless bias remains approximately 1,103 mHa relative to DMRG M = 500. Conversely, a classical DMRG multi-determinant ph-AFQMC route reaches chemical accuracy at 48 qubits, with a residual phaseless bias of +1.07 mHa. Four-point spatial-correlation amplitudes decay from 0.226 at 48 qubits to 0.101 at 80 qubits and 0.045 at 108 qubits; fitting the 48-qubit amplitude gives a per-qubit scaling parameter ϵq = 0.0304 that predicts the 80- and 108-qubit amplitudes within 19–26% relative error without additional free parameters. Exhaustive Bayesian and machine-learning signal extraction yields an out-of-fold ceiling of r ≈ 0.03 at 108 qubits under the present Heron r2, shot-count, circuit-depth, and DMRG M = 800 reference conditions. We therefore define the observed coherence wall as a conditional hardware-characterization metric for this benchmark rather than a universal physical constant. The results suggest that residual incoherent noise channels, including TLS-associated loss and relaxation, now dominate over statistical sampling error in this regime.

papers.title: Semiconducting Covalent Organic Frameworks based on Trioxotriangulene Neutral Radicals
papers.abstract: Electrically conductive two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) have emerged as a versatile class of crystalline porous polymers with promising applications in electronics and energy storage. However, high conductivities are typically achieved via post-synthetic doping to generate charge carriers, which can compromise crystallinity, porosity, and structural homogeneity. Persistent neutral radical conductors provide an attractive alternative, as their unpaired electrons can generate free charge carriers without the need for counterions. Nevertheless, the incorporation of highly delocalized p-radicals into COFs remains largely unexplored. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of imine-linked 2D COFs incorporating spin-delocalized trioxotriangulene (TOT) neutral radicals through two complementary synthetic approaches. Direct use of a TOT radical derivative functionalized with free amine groups affords a highly crystalline framework (TOT-COF-H) that exhibits semiconducting behavior (s RT = 1.2 × 10 -4 S cm -1 ), a reduced band gap ( E g = 1.09 eV), and low activation energy (0.24 eV). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for integrating spin-delocalized neutral radical building blocks into COFs, enabling the development of intrinsically conductive, porous, and crystalline organic frameworks without the need for extrinsic doping.

papers.title: Selective Growth of (6,5)- and (9,8)- Enriched Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
papers.abstract: The chirality-controlled growth of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) is important for the application of SWCNTs in high performance semiconductor devices. In this work, the chirality-selective growth of (6,5) and (9,8) SWCNTs was achieved in bulk phase, using cobalt-sulfur catalyst precursor system with MgO as the catalyst support. Under the optimal condition, characterized by UV-visible- near infrared absorption spectrum, SWCNTs of (6,5) and (9,8) accounted for 28% and 30% of the total, respectively. TEM characterizations showed bimodal diameter distribution of the as-grown SWCNTs, which is consistent with the absorption spectrum. Due to the significant difference of tube diameter, SWCNTs of (6,5) and (9,8) could be separated in aqueous two-phase system to obtain (9,8)-enriched SWCNT dispersion. Catalyst preparation condition, reduction temperature, growth temperature and carbon source affected the chirality distribution of the as-grown SWCNTs. We proposed that under the optimal condition, the diameter distribution of Co clusters presented bimodal distribution. In addition, the growth kinetics of (n,n-1)-SWCNTs is favorable against other chiralities. Therefore, the selective growth of SWCNTs of (6,5) and (9,8) may be ascribed to the dual diameter distribution of Co nanoparticles and the higher growth rates of (n,n-1)-SWCNTs. This work shows the possibility to realize the chirality-selective growth of more than one chiralities whose diameters are different significantly.

papers.title: An introduction to modern reaction optimization. How to develop a closed-loop reaction optimization system with Python, Bayesian optimization, continuous-flow chemistry, and in-line analysis.
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of chemical sciences is redefining how reaction optimization is implemented. This article provides a step-by-step guide to closed-loop optimization of organic reactions using Python, Bayesian optimization, continuous-flow chemistry, and in-line spectroscopic analysis. A nucleophilic aromatic substitution case study illustrates how computational tools and experimental chemistry can be integrated for efficient exploration of chemical space and rapid identification of optimal conditions. Key concepts are introduced and fully illustrated in the Supporting Information, with Jupyter Notebooks offering both complete code implementations and partially filled exercises for training. It is assumed that the reader has fundamental knowledge of Python, including conditionals, loops, coding structures as functions, and basic libraries. By bridging coding and practical experimental knowledge, this work highlights Python literacy as a central requirement for the next generation of chemists.

papers.title: Probabilistic Pourbaix diagrams with complexing agents: a case study of an aqueous nickel--ammonia--citrate system
papers.abstract: Pourbaix diagrams are essential tools for guiding aqueous electrochemical experiments, yet they are often limited to pure metals or alloys and the equilibrium lines in the Pourbaix diagrams are considered to be deterministic phase boundaries despite substantial variation in reported thermodynamic parameters. Here, we present a probabilistic Pourbaix diagram framework that incorporates complexing agents and explicitly accounts for the variability in equilibrium constants, demonstrated through a case study on the aqueous nickel–ammonia–citrate electrolyte system. Monte Carlo simulation (𝑁 = 1000 samples) is used to propagate variability in reported equilibrium constants through a multicomponent speciation model. We find that ammonia progressively stabilises dissolved nickel(II) under alkaline conditions by forming Ni(NH3) n 2+ complexes (𝑛 = 1–6), shifting the Ni(OH) 2 precipitation onset from pH 6.63 (ammonia-free) to pH 12.66 at a 20:1 ammonia-to-nickel molar ratio. Citrate achieves a comparable stabilisation effect at lower concentrations, delaying precipitation to pH 9.29 at a citrate-to-nickel molar ratio of only 2.5. For the combined bath (𝐶 Ni = 0.2, 𝐶 Cit = 0.25, 𝐶 NH3 = 0.33 mol L −1 ), the probabilistic treatment reveals substantial uncertainty in the onset of Ni(OH) 2 (s) precipitation: while the deterministic model predicts a sharp onset near pH 8.9, the Monte Carlo ensemble indicates that precipitation may begin as early as pH 6 and may not become certain until around pH 11 due to uncertainity in the underlying thermodynamic data. The resulting probabilistic Pourbaix diagram identifies domains of high thermodynamic confidence from those of genuine ambiguity, providing a foundation for the design and interpretation of nickel electrodeposition from ammonia–citrate baths.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Repurposing of Antivirals Identifies Boceprevir as an anti-Trypanosoma cruzi Agent
papers.abstract: To find treatments for the SARS-CoV-2 infection, several antivirals were repurposed or developed, many of which are inhibitors of proteases involved in the viral infective cycle. Since many human parasites are also dependent on proteases, those inhibitors can provide a starting point for new treatments for neglected diseases. In this work, a machine learning model was used to classify antiviral compounds as potential inhibitors of the Trypanosoma cruzi main protease, cruzain. From the top hits, boceprevir, an antiviral approved for treating chronic hepatitis C, was selected, presenting high micromolar affinity ( pK i = 6.39) against cruzain and a reversible inhibition mechanism. X-ray crystallography of the boceprevir-cruzain complex confirmed covalent adduct formation and binding mode consistent with that of known cruzain inhibitors. On in vitro assays against intracellular amastigotes, boceprevir yielded a p EC 50 = 4.54, a promising baseline for a non-optimized compound that highlights the potential of repurposing antivirals as antiparasitic agents.

papers.title: Identification of Key Amino Acid Residues in the Adenylation Domains of Polymyxin Synthetase Responsible for L-Threonine Adenylation in Paenibacillus polymyxa NBRC3020 Strain.
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT In non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) research, expanding our understanding of the relationship between active-site amino acid residues in adenylation (A) domains, which govern substrate recognition, and their adenylation activity and substrate specificity remains essential, as detailed biochemical characterization is still limited. In this study, we investigated the adenylation activity of two L-threonine (L-Thr)-specific A domains, A2 and A10, derived from the NRPS responsible for polymyxin D biosynthesis in Paenibacillus polymyxa NBRC 3020. To preserve enzymatic functionality, these domains were heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli BAP-1 not as isolated domains but as part of larger enzyme modules containing adjacent functional domains: A2–T2–C2 (module 2) and COM–A10–T10–TE (module 10). Adenylation activity was evaluated indirectly by quantifying pyrophosphate produced as a byproduct of the adenylation reaction. Both modules exhibited the highest activity toward L-Thr while also showing measurable activity toward structurally related amino acids, including L-serine (L-Ser), L-allo-threonine (L-allo-Thr), and Dalanine (D-Ala), indicating relatively broad substrate specificity. Previous studies have classified LThr-activating A domains into two groups: those with strict specificity for L-Thr and those with broader substrate tolerance toward structurally similar amino acids such as L-Ser. Our results indicate that A2 and A10 belong to the latter group. Docking simulations based on AlphaFold3-predicted structures identified three residues within the 10-amino-acid “Stachelhaus code”—Phe, Met, and His—as key determinants involved in recognition of the L-Thr side chain. Alanine substitution of these residues caused marked reductions in adenylation activity, experimentally confirming their essential roles in substrate recognition. To further elucidate the structural basis of substrate selectivity, we compared A domains exhibiting strict L-Thr specificity with those displaying broader substrate

papers.title: RETRACTED: In Silico Humanization and Structural Evaluation of the Fab G42 Anti-Hantavirus Antibody Fragment
papers.abstract: Retracted at the author’s request because the report contains fundamental errors that render the results inaccurate. Computational antibody humanization is commonly used to reduce predicted immunogenicity in non-human monoclonal antibodies while attempting to preserve structural and antigen-binding characteristics. In this study, an *in silico* workflow was applied to the Fab G42 anti-hantavirus antibody fragment obtained from a published Protein Data Bank (PDB) structure. The heavy and light chain sequences were analyzed for predicted MHC-II-associated immunogenic regions using the IEDB MHC-II Binding Prediction Tool. Framework optimization and sequence humanization were subsequently performed using the BioPhi/Sapiens platform. The resulting humanized antibody sequences were structurally modeled using AlphaFold 3 to evaluate predicted folding integrity and heterodimer organization. Finally, protein–protein docking simulations were conducted between the predicted humanized antibody structure and the Puumala virus Gn glycoprotein ectodomain using PatchDock. The generated models demonstrated preservation of the immunoglobulin fold and produced several candidate docking orientations exhibiting geometric compatibility with the viral glycoprotein surface. These findings represent a preliminary computational assessment of a humanized anti-hantavirus antibody framework and provide a basis for future refinement and experimental validation.

papers.title: Microfluidic sample compartmentalization for biomolecular concentration quantification using a nanopore sensor
papers.abstract: Determination of the concentration of a biomolecule in a sample is a fundamental measurement in analytical chemistry and central to many diagnostic applications. Solid-state nanopores (ssNPs) stand out as leading candidates to quantify biomolecules due to their capacity to achieve label-free electrical detection with single molecule resolution. Often, the concentration of a biomolecular sample is estimated in relation to the ssNP capture rate, i.e., the number of molecules translocated by the nanopore per unit time. However, this method poses challenges due to variability in capture rates, which have proven difficult to control experimentally. In this work, we introduce a microtrap, i.e. a microfluidic device with an integrated nanopore sensor, that leverages sample compartmentalization in known pL volumes allowing direct molecule counting and eliminating the need for capture rate calibration. We demonstrate direct quantification of pico- to nanomolar concentrations of double stranded DNA (dsDNA) and green fluorescent protein (GFP) molecules in minutes and without the need for calibration of the nanopore sensor capture rate. Moreover, we demonstrate the ability to preconcentrate the biomolecular sample by real-time tuning of the microtrap volume, which can be used to reduce the measurement time and to lower the detection limit.

papers.title: Large-scale multi-task regression and classification models for sustainability of molecular systems
papers.abstract: New materials and molecules with improved properties are needed to continue advancing society in such fields as energy, space exploration, and electronics. Unfortunately, the typical process of discovery and characterization of new material is time-consuming, which has hindered the co-design of material and product or material and manufacturing. Predictive models using machine learning (ML) capable of forecasting the properties of new materials before they are synthesized have the potential to accelerate this process and enable co-design. However, the introduction of new materials is invariably a multi-objective process and needs to balance performance with sustainability metrics, including economic, environmental, and human health. Most ML efforts to accelerate discovery have focused on performance. This paper aggregates databases of toxicology, global warming potential (GWP), and fundamental physicochemical properties of molecules and uses the combined resource to train multi-task ML models. The models are trained for 617 classification and 30 regression metrics and outperform most current single-property models. Also, a chemical extraction study was performed using per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances to investigate the limits of our model when presented with molecules that are outside of the chemical space contained within our training data. We believe we have demonstrated that the data aggregation and models can accelerate the introduction of new materials in a wide range of applications.

papers.title: Predicting DNA Aptamer-Ligand Binding Affinities with DeltaGzip
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting DNA–ligand binding affinities is critical for the scalable design of DNA aptamer-based sensors, yet the field lacks computational tools in virtual screening that balance computational efficiency with experiment-level accuracy. Here, we adapt DeltaGzip, an affinity prediction protocol combining molecular dynamics simulation with Gzip lossless compression, to DNA aptamer–ligand systems. To this end we refined the calculation of enthalpy, performed representation learning to improve the entropy calculation, and introduced a pre-screening step to filter out non-binding ligands. In the absence of suitable datasets for method validation, we have performed isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements of the binding free energy for a dopamine-binding DNA aptamer binding 22 different molecular ligands with varying affinity. Our experiments show that DeltaGzip’s predictions agree with the ITC measurements, both qualitatively and quantitatively.

papers.title: Continuous flotation unlocks full recovery of silver from end-of-life solar cells
papers.abstract: We have recently demonstrated that froth flotation can be used to selectively recover metallic silver from end-of-life crystalline silicon solar cells using a 1 L flotation cell operated in batch mode, at ambient temperature with AEROFLOAT 242 and AEROPHINE 3418A as collectors. In a single-stage batch flotation test, 97.6% silver recovery was achieved with a 32-fold upgrade, establishing froth flotation as an effective pathway for silver recovery from photovoltaic waste. Ultimately, it is essential to deliver economic scalability to any new technological advancement. Building on that work, the present study examines the transition from batch to continuous flotation operation as a key step toward scalable silver recovery. The work processed approximately 22 kg of solar cell material, corresponding to around 468 kg of rooftop photovoltaic panels, based on the solar cell fraction representing about 4.7% of the original panel mass. Under continuous operating conditions covering a period of around 90 minutes the silver recovery was maintained close to 100%. The gas-liquid residence time was only 1 minute. Under steady-state conditions covering a 42-minute operating window, the average silver upgrade was approximately 83-fold, while the recovery was virtually 100%. The results demonstrate that the flotation separation is robust, rapid and scalable, and is consistent with validation at approximately a Technology Readiness Level of 5.

papers.title: Formulation Optimization: Machine Learning and Molecular Dynamics for Accelerated Discovery
papers.abstract: The design of chemical mixtures, or formulations, is a critical yet challenging aspect of materials science due to the combinatorial explosion of possible ingredient and composition variations. Traditional trial-and-error methods are costly, especially when optimizing for multiple target properties concurrently. To accelerate formulation discovery, we developed a multiparameter, hierarchical optimization framework that integrates high-throughput machine learning (ML) predictions with sophisticated search algorithms. We first trained highly accurate ML models to predict properties such as density and heat of vaporization from chemical structure and composition using a large dataset of simulated solvent mixtures. We then rigorously benchmarked various optimization algorithms. For composition optimization, the differential evolution algorithm was identified as the most robust and efficient method, rapidly identifying optimal compositions with minimal ML prediction calls. For ingredient selection, a genetic algorithm (GA) significantly outperformed brute force, random, and Bayesian optimization approaches, finding a much higher proportion of top-performing formulations with the fewest samples. By coupling GA for ingredient selection with differential evolution for composition refinement, the hierarchical workflow successfully maximized a multiparameter optimization score across diverse materials applications, including minimizing solvent viscosity, maximizing drug solubility, and maximizing motor octane number. Representative candidates from the lowest, middle, and highest scoring ranges when minimizing viscosity were subsequently evaluated using classical molecular dynamics simulations, validating the prediction trends made by the data-driven optimization approach. This work highlights a robust, intelligent, and rapid computer-aided workflow for navigating 1 the complex design space of chemical mixtures, minimizing the need for extensive physical experimentation and accelerating the discovery of high-performing, tailored formulations.

papers.title: StereoPep: Do Molecular Models Understand Stereochemistry? A Benchmark on Synthetic Diastereomeric Peptides
papers.abstract: Existing peptide models saturate natural-sequence proteomics benchmarks, but whether they capture the underlying physicochemical dynamics or merely pattern-match on sequence statistics remains unclear. Public peptide datasets offer no axis along which to test this: non-canonical residues and stereochemical variation are essentially absent. We introduce StereoPep, a benchmark of 48,788 chemically synthesized peptides spanning 11 libraries, produced in the laboratory via high-throughput flow synthesis and characterized experimentally by reversephase liquid chromatography retention time. Unlike model-generated synthetic data, every peptide in StereoPep is a real molecule paired with a chromatographic measurement. The dataset is constructed around matched diastereomeric pairs (sequences identical in primary structure but differing at a single stereocenter), providing a direct test of whether models capture three-dimensional stereochemical information. StereoPep enables progress across multiple fields: it serves as a benchmark for stereochemistry-aware molecular representations and geometric deep learning, supports adapting protein language models to non-canonical residues, and underpins emerging proteomics multiplexing strategies that encode samples through retention-time shifts. Across specialized retention-time models, graph-based architectures, and protein language models, all approaches predict overall retention reasonably well (Pearson r ≈ 0.80) but collapse on diastereomer pair discrimination (AUC ≈ 0.55), revealing that current representations encode atomic composition far better than 3D structure.

papers.title: Tunable multimetallic nanoparticle exsolution from high-entropy spinel oxides
papers.abstract: Metal nanoparticle exsolution from oxides is a powerful route to generate stable metal-oxide interfaces relevant for catalysis, but controlling the process remains challenging. High-entropy oxides (HEOs) serve as compositionally complex and defect-tolerant host lattices that broaden the scope of this process beyond conventional oxides. Here, we use several in situ X-ray and microscopic techniques to track the structural, chemical, and electronic evolution of spinel-type HEOs during thermally induced exsolution under reducing conditions. We show that exsolution proceeds through composition-dependent pathways dictated by the ability of the host lattice to undergo local structural rearrangements. By varying the nominal B-site composition, we control whether exsolution occurs directly from the spinel lattice or through transient rock salt intermediates. These findings establish metal nanoparticle exsolution from high-entropy spinels as a structure- and composition-governed process and identify local rearrangements as the basis for tuning the exsolved phase composition and extent.

papers.title: A Label-Free Si-BioFET with Linearly Assembled Gold Nanoparticles for the Detection of miR-141
papers.abstract: Sensitivity of field-effect transistor biosensors (BioFETs) for nucleic acid detection is often limited by weak electrostatic control and low probe density at the sensing interface. Here, we present a BioFET platform with improved sensitivity based on lightly p-doped Schottky-barrier silicon nanobelt transistors, exhibiting reproducible ambipolar behavior in a back-gated configuration. These devices are encapsulated with an Al2O3/ZrO2 nanolaminate to prevent device performance degradation and facilitate stable biofunctionalization. Dry-state measurements demonstrate selective detection of prostate cancer biomarker, miR-141, after immobilization of complementary capture DNA, achieving detection down to the ~100 pM range, and discrimination against the non-complementary sequence, miR-155. To enhance sensitivity, template-assisted self-assembly of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) is used to form ordered linear structures directly on the sensing region. The supracolloidal assembly of AuNPs at the sensing interface tunes the receptor spacing and orientation and amplifies the influence of target hybridization on transistor response. Compared to planar devices, the hybrid AuNPBioFET exhibits improved signal modulation while preserving the label-free detection mechanism. This approach bridges scalable top-down semiconductor technology and bottomup self-assembled nanostructures, providing an innovative pathway for developing biosensing platforms with high sensitivity and multiplexing capabilities for detecting nucleic acids.

papers.title: Local Acidity as a Corrosiveness Descriptor of Fluorinated Ether Solvents in Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: Electrolyte engineering based on solvent fluorination has proven effective for stabilizing lithium (Li) metal batteries by weakening the Li+-solvent interaction. However, the influence of fluorination on the chemical reactivity of an electrolyte toward Li metal remains poorly understood. Here, the effects of fluorination are systematically investigated by increasing the degree of fluorination (from 2 to 5 substituents) of the terminal carbon atom of the 1-ethoxy-2-methoxyethane (EME) and 1-(2-methoxyethoxy)propane (MEP) backbones (denoted F2EME, F4MEP, and F5MEP). Fluorination-induced corrosion deviates from that suggested by conventionally calculated LUMO-based rationales; instead, it is quantitatively described by the local pKa associated with cleavage of the ether C–O bond. Among the three derivatives, F4MEP is identified as the optimal solvent; it is sufficiently fluorinated to promote the formation of an anion-rich solvation structure for an inorganic-rich, protective Li metal interphase, yet it is not severely corrosive as it is not over-fluorinated. Consequently, an F4MEP-based 20 μm-Li||NCM811 full-cell retains 80% of its capacity over 368 cycles. This study establishes the local pKa as a descriptor for evaluating the solvent corrosiveness and highlights the necessity of optimizing the degree of fluorination for high-performance Li metal battery electrolytes.

papers.title: Enantioselective Hydrogenation of Hydroxyacetone on Intrinsically Chiral Pt(643) Surfaces
papers.abstract: Asymmetric catalysis underpins pharmaceutical synthesis but is dominated by homogeneous molecular catalysts that complicate product separation and recycling. Heterogeneous alternatives, including hybrid systems in which molecular catalysts are immobilised on solid supports, often suffer from diminished activity and poor stability. Here, we use density functional theory and microkinetic modelling to evaluate intrinsically chiral platinum surfaces as a heterogeneous alternative, taking the hydrogenation of hydroxyacetone to 1,2-propanediol (1,2-PD) as a model reaction.
