The reaction follows an EnT-initiated Witkop oxidation, as supported by spectroscopic, electrochemical, photophysical and computational studies. The transformation exhibits broad substrate scope, exceptional functional group tolerance, and excellent scalable practicality. Notably, gram-scale synthesis of diverse bioactive agents and the Phase III clinical drug cetilistat have been achieved. Overall, this work expands the mechanistic landscape of EDA photochemistry and offers a modular, non-covalent strategy for heterocycle skeletal editing, which may open new directions in radical synthesis and drug discovery.

papers.title: Giant Band Gap Renormalization Dictates Current–Voltage Behavior of 2D Semiconductor Electrodes
papers.abstract: 2 electrochemical and solid-state device behavior unknown. Here we show that giant BGR governs the J–V behavior of monolayer (ML) MoS2 electrodes at electrochemical interfaces by reducing the energy-level overlap between semiconductor and molecular acceptor states, suppressing the interfacial electron-transfer rate constant (ket) by an order of magnitude. Using in situ spectroelectrochemistry and many-body theory, we find that Eg changes by >0.2 eV with n over a 400 mV electrochemical potential window. Across independently prepared ML-MoS2 electrodes, variations in n produce a continuum of electrochemical responses ranging from reversible to irreversible behavior. These results establish BGR as a governing parameter in 2D semiconductor electrochemistry, provide a framework for accessing the Marcus inverted regime in (photo)electrocatalytic and voltage-tunable sensing applications,7–10 and suggest that BGR may contribute more broadly to device-to-device variability in 2D electronics, including threshold-voltage variations in field-effect transistors.11–15 2D semiconductors exhibit giant BGR — exceeding 500 meV in ML-MoS24,6 versus 25 meV in bulk AlxGa1-xAs16— owing to strong Coulomb interactions, reduced dielectric screening, and quantum confinement.17,18 The central hypothesis is that the giant magnitude of BGR in 2D semiconductors dictates the electrochemical J-V response in ways previous works have not captured. The salient features of the Marcus-Gerischer framework19–22 for current flow at semiconductor/electrolyte (SC|EL) interfaces are depicted in Figure 1a for a bulk n-type semiconductor in contact with a redox couple in the absence of illumination. At equilibrium, the net current J is zero because the forward electron transfer rate from semiconductor conduction band states to oxidized solution molecules (O) exactly balances the reverse rate from reduced molecules (R) back to the semiconductor (see Supplementary Information eq. S6). Figure 1b illustrates how J varies with the applied potential (Eapp) for an “ideal” bulk SC|EL interface in which the conduction band edge energy (Ecb) remains when in contact with [O]s and [R]s, i.e. the concentrations of oxidized and reduced redox species at the electrode surface, respectively. Applying negative potentials increases the cathodic current (Jcath = qketn[O]s) because the electron concentration n increases exponentially as Eapp, is made more negative, where q is the elementary charge and ket is the intrinsic electron-transfer rate constant between the conduction band and the redox couple (O/R). papers.title: Probing the Electronic Origins of Heterometallic Tuning in Platinum Complexes by 195Pt NMR Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Incorporation of secondary, effectively Lewis acidic metal cations into heterometallic complexes is a useful strategy for tuning chemical properties and reactivity, but addressing the origins of metal-driven tunability and quantitative correlation of metal-focused data with computational modeling have not received the attention they deserve. Here, the synthesis and characterization of a series of diamagnetic complexes containing platinum(II) and secondary cations (K + , Sr 2+ , and Lu 3+ ) are reported, along with nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements of 195 Pt chemical shifts (δ 195 Pt). Similar to related species, the spectroscopic and electrochemical properties of the complexes depend on the Lewis acidity, or charge density, of the secondary cations; the change in δ 195 Pt was found to be particularly well correlated with Lewis acidity and was therefore studied in detail. Computational investigations of the 195 Pt NMR data reveal that the secondary cations induce changes in electron donation to platinum from bridging phenoxide moieties that lead to the experimental chemical shifts. In sum, the results both i) establish a quantitative model for understanding cation-driven tuning in complexes of this type as well as ii) demonstrate the usefulness of 195 Pt NMR as tool for studying Pt-heterometallic compounds.

papers.title: Sub-kJ/mol Precision at Practical Cost for Molecular Solids through Local Coupled Cluster Approaches
papers.abstract: Generation of numerically converged coupled-cluster reference energies of molecular crystals remains highly non-routine. Yet, such data points are critically needed as computational methodologies strive to reach correlated wave-function accuracy in condensed-phase systems. Localized-orbital coupled-cluster approaches applied within the many-body expansion promise a scalable route to these reference results. Here, we report solutions to technical challenge when using this methodology—at long intermolecular distances, the numerical noise due to local approximations can accumulate for some molecular crystals into a large-scale drift of the correlation energy, especially in the nonadditive three-body contributions. Within the local natural orbital (LNO) coupled-cluster method, we suggest well-balanced ways to overcome this issue. At the benchmark level, we propose improved LNO-CCSD(T) settings, which removes the artifacts at long distances and attains the numerical precision of 0.2 kJ/mol (maximum error) in the lattice energy with practical cost orders of magnitude lower than that of canonical CCSD(T). As an even more scalable solution, we propose a multi-level strategy, which utilizes the established routine LNO-CCSD(T) precision tiers (Tight, vTight), but retains the numerical stability of the benchmark level, thanks to the treatment of long-distance three-body systems with the random-phase approximation.

papers.title: Single-Chain Fluorinated Catalysts for Efficient SABRE Pyruvate Hyperpolarization and <100 ppb Iridium in Aqueous Solutions
papers.abstract: Signal Amplification by Reversible Exchange (SABRE) delivers rapid and inexpensive NMR hyperpolarization using iridium-catalyzed transfer from parahydrogen. For biomedical translation, the resulting SABRE-hyperpolarized metabolites must combine high signal enhancement with efficient removal of the toxic iridium catalyst prior to administration. Here we introduce three single-chain fluorinated Ir–NHC catalysts (NHC = IMesF1, SIMesF1, and IPrF1) for the SABRE hyperpolarization of [1-13C]pyruvate. The catalyst Ir-IMesF1 delivers ~4% 13C polarization with 50% parahydrogen in methanol-d4 (~12% extrapolated to 100% parahydrogen), which is comparable to the benchmark Ir-IMes catalyst, and approximately three times higher than delivered by the previously reported perfluorinated Ir-SIMesF2 system under identical conditions. By combining these catalysts with a redissolution (ReD)-SABRE protocol, aqueous extraction, and filtration through fluorinated silica, the residual iridium content is reduced by nearly two orders of magnitude relative to Ir-IMes, and threefold relative to Ir-SIMesF2, thereby yielding improved aqueous solutions containing <100 ppb Ir. These results are used to demonstrate efficient SABRE hyperpolarization, with simultaneous ultra-low residual iridium levels for the real-time monitoring of the in vitro enzymatic conversion of pyruvate to lactate with partial parahydrogen enrichment.

papers.title: Enhancement of Triplet–Triplet Annihilation Upconversion in Organically Modified Clay Colloids
papers.abstract: Controlling the spatial distribution of energy donors and acceptors within constrained microenvironments remains a fundamental challenge in the development of efficient triplet–triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC) and advanced photofunctional materials. Herein, we report the rational modulation of TTA-UC in an R-limonene-swollen organoclay (Sumecton-SAN) system using four iridium(III) complexes as donors: two cationic species, [Ir(ppy) 2 (phen)]PF 6 ( Ir1-PF 6 ) and [Ir(piq) 2 (phen)]PF 6 ( Ir2-PF 6 ), and two neutral analogues, [Ir(ppy) 2 (acac)] ( Ir3 ) and [Ir(piq) 2 (acac)] ( Ir4 ). We initially demonstrate that cationic Ir(III) sensitizers suffer from severe UC quenching in clay colloids due to spatial segregation; specifically, the cationic donors are electrostatically anchored to the polar clay surface via ion exchange, while the hydrophobic 9,10-diphenylanthracene (DPA) acceptors preferentially partition into the R-limonene-rich, hydrophobic interlayer domains. To overcome this microenvironmental mismatch, we employed the neutral Ir(III) complexes Ir3 and Ir4 . In these neutral systems, UC emission was significantly enhanced when the iridium complexes were loaded at a low density (corresponding to 5% of the cation exchange capacity (CEC) of the clay). Conversely, at a higher loading density corresponding to 50% of the CEC, Ir3 exhibited a marked decrease in UC emission, whereas the sterically bulkier Ir4 sustained its enhanced emission compared to the clay-free homogeneous solution. We attribute this difference to the aggregation-induced self-quenching of Ir3 on the clay surface at high concentrations, which was effectively suppressed by the steric hindrance of Ir4 . Furthermore, excited-state lifetime measurements of Ir2-PF 6 and Ir4 in the presence and absence of the clay revealed contrasting behavior: the lifetime of Ir2-PF 6 was shortened (the excited state of Ir2 + was destabilized) in the presence of the clay, whereas that of Ir4 was prolonged (the excited state of Ir4 was stabilized). These results suggest that both the neutral iridium donors and the DPA acceptors co-localize on the organically modified hydrophobic clay surfaces. Consequently, their molecular diffusion is effectively restricted to two dimensions, leading to amplified UC emission compared to that in a homogeneous solution. Based on these findings, we highlight the crucial role of tailoring the hydrophobic microenvironment on 2D clay sheet surfaces to facilitate efficient TTA-UC.

papers.title: First Structural Determination of an Isolable and Planar Tropyl Radical
papers.abstract: Planar hydrocarbon-based tropyl radicals remain elusive because seven-membered open-shell systems readily undergo structural deformation and intermolecular reactions. Herein, we report the design, isolation, and structural characterization of dibenzotropyl radicals bearing anthryl-based π-systems. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations predicted that bianthryl and teranthryl substituents stabilize orthogonally twisted conformations containing a planar dibenzotropyl radical unit while suppressing the formation of reactive folded structures. One-electron reduction of the corresponding dibenzotropyliums afforded persistent neutral radicals for both the bianthryl and teranthryl derivatives, which are stable under ambient conditions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis of the bianthryl-substituted radical revealed a sterically unperturbed planar dibenzotropyl structure, providing the first crystallographic evidence for a planar hydrocarbon-based tropyl radical. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical studies revealed reversible redox interconversion between the cationic and radical states while retaining the planar seven-membered framework. These findings provide insight into redox-active seven-membered π-systems and establish a design strategy for stable open-shell hydrocarbons.

papers.title: Apparent Power as a Unifying Metric for Frontal Polymerization
papers.abstract: The success of chemical transformations is governed by both thermodynamic and kinetic factors. Together, the heat of a reaction and the rate at which that heat is released manifest as power. In self-sustained transformations such as frontal polymerization, the balance between power generated and power transfer governs propagation dynamics. Herein, we demonstrate the use of an experimentally practical apparent power expression to characterize frontal polymerization. Initially, we validated our expression by frontally polymerizing 1,5-cyclooctadiene, dicyclopentadiene, and 5-ethylidene-2-norbornene at various initiator loadings, finding a strong correlation between apparent power and reaction propagation. Specifically, raising a system’s apparent power drove a progressive transition in the observed front regime, from quenched through unstable to uniform. We further demonstrated that modulating apparent power also influences backbone isomerization in 1,5-cyclooctadiene polymers. Additionally, the maximum front temperature and the rate at which it is achieved were found to decrease as the balance between output and input power narrows. To further validate our expression, we used heat sinks to systematically vary the reaction power, supporting the correlation between distinct front regimes with specific values of apparent power. Moreover, geometric normalization extended this framework beyond our experimental systems to literature examples, allowing more meaningful comparisons across variable reactions. This new analytical tool offers a more holistic comparison of monomers and reaction mechanisms that are otherwise different regarding their thermodynamics and kinetics alone. We anticipate that this foundational study will lay the groundwork for the use of apparent power as a more representative metric to characterize self-sustained reactions.

papers.title: Strong Light–Matter Coupling as a Photonic Substituent: Correlation-Enhanced Control of Regioselectivity in Nitrobenzene
papers.abstract: Strong coupling to the vacuum electromagnetic field of optical cavities has been proposed as a route to control ground-state chemical reactivity, enabling “photonic substituent effects.” Recent theoretical work predicted that cavity coupling can invert intrinsic regioselectivity in electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Here, we revisit this prediction using correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics. QED-CCSD calculations reveal substantially enhanced energetic reordering of Wheland intermediates relative to previous approaches, indicating that regioselective control may be achievable under more experimentally feasible cavity-coupling strengths than previously predicted. QED-DMRG analysis shows that this effect arises from cavity-induced reweighting of resonance structures, reinforcing the idea of a photonic substituent effect that is similarly influential on molecular electronic structure as chemical substituents. Complementary ab initio molecular dynamics simulations driven by QED-DFT analytic gradients demonstrate that orientational fluctuations introduce a competing dynamical constraint on selectivity, suggesting conditions where canonical 100% meta selectivity could be modified to give mixtures of ortho and meta or para and meta electrophilic aromatic substitution products.

papers.title: Transfer Learning from Lithium-Ion to Zinc-Ion Batteries: Cross-Chemistry Capacity Prediction with Limited Target Data
papers.abstract: Zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) are emerging as a low-cost, safe alternative to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but their data scarcity makes accurate lifetime prediction challenging. We investigate whether degradation knowledge from data-rich LIB datasets (Severson/MATR: 124 cells; CALCE: 8 cells) can be transferred to improve capacity prediction for ZIBs under limited data regimes (N = 2–40 training cells). We propose a Selective Multi-Task Gaussian Process (Selective MT-GP) that explicitly partitions features by transferability: the exponential decay rate (exp_b) is shared across both chemistries via an inter-task kernel, while the differential capacity variance (∆var(dQ/dV )) — which exhibits a 1000-fold absolute scale gap between chemistries — is treated as a Zn-ion-private feature. Our experiments reveal a crossover near N ≈ 20: below this threshold, Li-ion labels appear to harm Zn-ion predictions (negative transfer), while above it, selective feature transfer outperforms naïve approaches. At N = 2, GP-Direct achieves only 50.5% empirical coverage of its stated 90% credible intervals (NLL = 3.44) — barely above a coin flip. Selective MT-GP raises coverage to 81% (NLL = 1.07, a 3.2× improvement) by anchoring posterior variance to 132 Li-ion cells, preventing hyperparameter collapse onto two data points. For battery management systems that make safety-critical decisions from early cycle data, this calibration gap is consequential: a model reporting 90% credible intervals that achieve only 50% empirical coverage will systematically underestimate risk in the data-scarce regime. Cross-chemistry transfer’s primary contribution in this regime is not point accuracy but honest uncertainty.

papers.title: Non-Native Thiol and Aniline Methylation, Including Enantioselective Dithiol Desymmetrization, by Multi-Component Cobamide-Dependent Methyltransferases Using Unactivated Methyl Donors
papers.abstract: Despite their potential synthetic utility, cobamide-dependent MTases are relatively underutilized for biocatalysis. We developed mixed MtaABC/MtgABC enzyme platforms capable of catalyzing methylation of non-native thiol and aniline substrates using unactivated methyl donors like methanol and glycine betaine. This approach allows highly enantioselective and site-selective methylation of aliphatic thiols with high turnover number (up to 6000), providing the first demonstration of enantioselective non-native catalysis by cobamide dependent enzymes. The MtaAC+MtgB system was subsequently engineered through site-directed mutagenesis, resulting in large enhancements in activity for the desymmetrization of non-native ester-containing prochiral thiols. These findings establish MTase complexes as a promising platform for non-native biocatalysis.

papers.title: Adsorption of Chiral Ir(III) Complexes on Clay Nanosheets: Optical-Purity-Dependent Packing and Amplified Circularly Polarized Luminescence
papers.abstract: Controlling the spatial distribution of photoluminescent molecules within constrained microenvironments remains a fundamental challenge in enhancing their photophysical properties. Herein, we demonstrate that the differential adsorption behaviors of enantiopure and racemic octahedral iridium(III) complexes on clay nanosheets can be exploited to modulate their photophysical and chiroptical properties, particularly circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Two structurally related chiral complexes, [Ir(ppy) 2 (phen)](PF 6 ) ( Ir1-PF 6 ) and [Ir(piq) 2 (phen)](PF 6 ) ( Ir2-PF 6 ), were investigated. Upon adsorption onto colloidal clay, the pseudo- C 3 -symmetric Ir1 + cation exhibited UV–vis, photoluminescence (PL), and electronic circular dichroism (ECD) spectra distinctly different from those in solution, a phenomenon absent for the sterically bulkier Ir2 + complex. This spectral modulation is attributed to a precise size match between the Ir1 + ligands and the hexagonal cavities of the clay surface, leading to conformational locking that effectively suppresses nonradiative decay. Crucially, Ir1 + displayed distinct photophysical properties between its enantiopure and racemic forms, stemming from contrasting, optical-purity-dependent packing modes. While the racemate was proposed to form stable heterochiral pairs irrespective of loading density, the enantiopure complex underwent dense packing and concentration quenching at higher loadings. Furthermore, despite having the same absolute configuration, Ir1 + and Ir2 + exhibited opposite CPL signs in solution—an inversion computationally attributed to ligand-dependent changes in orbital topologies. Upon confinement within the clay matrix, the CPL intensity of enantiopure Ir1 + was significantly amplified, whereas that of Ir2 + decreased. This enhancement of the CPL intensity of Ir1 + upon clay adsorption closely parallels the effects of cryogenic cooling. These findings establish clay nanosheets as powerful structural scaffolds for transforming weakly emissive molecules into highly functional chiral luminescent materials.

papers.title: The Canalised Cleavage of Glucosepane
papers.abstract: We report a strategy for chemical cleavage and de-clamping of glucosepane, the dominant protein–protein advanced glycation end-product (AGE) crosslink in aged human tissue. Glucosepane exceeds other AGE crosslinks in collagen and elastin by ~10–100-fold and accumulates in long-lived matrix, yet prior AGE-breaker attempts have relied on chemistries mismatched to its bicyclic aminal–amidine core. No peer-reviewed chemical cleavage method has been reported since glucosepane’s structural identification and total synthesis. The proposed cleavage sequence activates the lysine-side C–N bond, intercepts the opened/iminium intermediate with an aminooxy (α-effect) nucleophile before closure or re-crosslinking, and completes severance by second-site capture, hydrolysis, or post-capture redox chemistry of the trapped adduct. Lewis-acid activation, mild-acid and general-acid catalysis, and bifunctional preorganization increase neutral entry into the opened/iminium product pathway; targeted N1 oxidation adds redox entry through α-deprotonation followed by second oxidation, Bond-A β-scission, or photochemical priming; and matrix strain and water-activity effects further bias aged collagen toward the same chemistry. Direct β-scission remains the simplest projected redox route to the first Bond-A break in targeted mature-collagen treatment. In the bifunctional format, the activating group and aminooxy trap are held in one scaffold, making trapping effectively intramolecular (10³–10⁵ M effective molarity; ~2 × 10⁴–2 × 10⁶ above 50 mM bulk scavenger). The high-effective-molarity branch model favors second capture and complete severance (≈0.992) over recrosslinking (≈10⁻⁵), and rigid picolyl/aminooxy scaffolds place leading bifunctional opening barriers at ~13.0–13.4 kcal mol⁻¹, corresponding to projected opening rates of ~2.3–4.4 × 10³ s⁻¹. In the kinetic projection, substrate preselection plus accelerated opening and local capture raises the product-selectivity metric 295.5-fold (9.175 × 10⁻⁵ to 0.0271). Selectivity rests on lesion topology, local glucosepane burden, preorganized trap/scavenger capture, and physiological matrix strain; aromatic side reactions are tracked directly in the same product assay. Downstream MMP remodeling then amplifies the tissue response after chemical cleavage. The DFT/PCM descriptor panel places closed glucosepane at 5.68 eV; tryptophan/indole is the closest general side-chain comparator at 5.47–5.55 eV but is essentially absent from mature type I collagen; p-cresol/tyrosine and histidine lie higher at ~5.91 and 6.04 eV. After aminooxy trapping, the glucosepane-derived adduct lies at 2.80 eV, more than 2.6 eV below tryptophan/indole and more than 3.1 eV below the mature-collagen Tyr/p-cresol comparator (~5.91 eV). Constrained closed-state radical-cation scans bound direct redox access: the bare Bond-A surface peaks near 29.7 kcal mol⁻¹ and remains ~22.2 kcal mol⁻¹ uphill at 3.00 Å, with tested Zn geometries still high in energy. The α-deprotonation/second-oxidation branch is supported by a ~14.6 kcal mol⁻¹ transition-state diagnostic and is the strongest positive driver of projected trapped-product formation in sensitivity analysis (ρ = 0.615). Productive redox chemistry is therefore framed as targeted β-scission or iminium-forming entry into the trapped-product pathway, not nonspecific fragmentation. The anti-glucosepane Glu3 DNA aptamer supplies a validated glucosepane-binding handle for localization (K_D = 17.10 ± 0.96 nM; 10–15 kDa; below the ~40 kDa fibril size-exclusion threshold; Li et al., Nanoscale Horizons 2025 [74]), and ocular collagen provides the clearest first redox-access setting because corneal stroma and Bruch’s membrane are collagen-rich, avascular, and light-accessible. These results define a catalyst-trap/redox route for glucosepane crosslink cleavage and a chemically specific framework for addressing accumulated, turnover-resistant molecular lesions with suitable trappable or fragmentation-prone chemistry.

papers.title: An energy-corrected fast post-SCF local-hybrid scheme for highly accurate energy differences of large main-group systems
papers.abstract: Local-hybrid (LH) density functionals admix exact exchange locally in real space and thereby can be powerful tools to ameliorate the usual zero-sum game between reducing self-interaction errors and modeling static correlation. But as with other hybrid functionals the practical use of LHs for large systems is limited by the cost of evaluating exact-exchange quantities self-consistently. Here we introduce an energy-corrected local-hybrid framework, EC(LH)@(m)GGA, in which a computationally expedient semi-local reference density is used for a single post-SCF evaluation with an advanced LH. Using the recent neural-network-based LH25nP LH as a prototype, we show that the EC route based on GGA or meta-GGA orbitals preserves the characteristic accuracy profile of the parent local hybrid and reaches state-of-the-art rung 4 performance on the GMTKN55 test suite (WTMAD-2 around 2.4–2.7 kcal/mol, depending on grid). The top performance of LH25nP for spin-restricted bond dissociation as a strong-correlation measure is retained in this framework. The dominant post-SCF overhead in timing is governed by the EC grid. For the practical grid size 3, the total EC(LH)@(m)GGA cost is only about ∼2–3× that of a GGA single point, typically about an order of magnitude less than a full LH SCF. Overall, EC(LH)@(m)GGA provides a simple post-SCF route to state-of-the-art rung-4 energetics at a cost close to semi-local DFT, applicable to large systems.

papers.title: Zinc halide flux-assisted vitrification of metal-organic frameworks enables chemical diversification and tunable gas sorption
papers.abstract: The vitrification of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) enables melt processing into bulk, shaped and membrane-type porous materials, yet the limited chemical diversity of existing MOF glass formers restricts structural and functional tunability. Here, we demonstrate a general flux-melting strategy in which the inorganic zinc halide glass formers (ZnCl 2 , ZnBr 2 or ZnI 2 ) are co-melted with seven zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs) spanning different imidazolate-type linkers and network topologies, including both established ZIF glass formers and frameworks that do not melt or vitrify on their own. The zinc halides act as compatible co-network formers and reactive fluxes, promoting extensive ligand exchange between halides and imidazolate linkers in the melt. This process generates mixed halide-imidazolate coordination glass networks whose structure, connectivity and porosity can be tuned systematically through composition. One of the resulting mixed coordination glasses displays substantially enhanced thermodynamic sorption selectivity for propylene over propane compared to its parent ZIF glass. These results establish zinc-halide flux melting as a general route to expand the compositional space of MOF glasses and introduce mixed coordination networks as a new design paradigm for functional porous glasses.

papers.title: Synthonpedia -A free reaction database as a tool for retrosynthetic analysis
papers.abstract: Retrosynthetic analysis is a fundamental pillar of organic synthesis, yet its execution is often constrained by human biases and the inherent limitations of current computational tools. While artificial intelligence (AI) has made significant strides in automating synthetic planning, many existing platforms operate as "black boxes" that inherit popularity biases from literature data. Here, we introduce Synthonpedia, a community-driven, open-access platform designed to redefine the retrosynthetic workflow through a human-machine cooperation model. Using “radical synthons” as data format organized in a database structure, Synthonpedia simplifies the algorithmic matching process and liberates chemical intuition from conventional reactivity trends. This streamlined logic results in a minimal computational footprint, enabling a complete retrosynthetitc analysis on consumer-grade hardware. We demonstrate the power of this approach through a proof-of-concept one-layer retrosynthesis of clavulanic acid, uncovering non intuitive disconnections that showcase the platform’s capacity for unbiased reaction space exploration. Synthonpedia stands as a sustainable, transparent infrastructure for the democratization of synthetic knowledge.

papers.title: A Mild and Site-Selective Nucleophilic C−H Functionalization of Pyridines via its Stable N-alkylated Salts
papers.abstract: Direct, site-selective C-H functionalization of pyridines offers an efficient approach to both streamlined synthesis and late-stage modification of bioactive and functional molecules. Existing approaches to direct nucleophilic substitution typically rely on highly reactive nitrogen-activating groups, which limit nucleophile scope and functional group tolerance and often suffer from poor site selectivity. Although milder activating groups address some of these limitations, they generally require additional installation and removal steps. Herein, we report a mild and general strategy employing designed alkyl halide activators that enables one-pot, site-selective functionalization of pyridines with synthetically valuable yet challenging nucleophiles. This strategy allows, for the first time, direct pyridine functionalization with a broad range of phosphites and amines, in addition to methoxide and cyanide. The mild and redox-neutral reaction conditions are particularly well suited for late-stage functionalization (LSF) of pharmaceutically relevant molecules, enabling site-selective modification with both phosphites and amines. The rational design of the alkyl halide activators, together with careful analysis of side-product formation, reveals the delicate balance required for success with electronically diverse nucleophiles and suggests broader applicability of this C-H functionalization strategy.

papers.title: Trends in Computational Metabolomics: A Perspective on Five Years of Software Development, Challenges, and Opportunities (2021–2025)
papers.abstract: Metabolomics software development has accelerated rapidly, yet no recent systematic analysis has quantified how the landscape is evolving across computational methods, geographies, and the research community's technology adoption. There is a strong need within the metabolomics research community to keep pace with the rapid expansion of accessible and free computational tools and resources. Given the lack of existence of such a treatise since 2021 and the surge in advances in ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS), single-cell and spatial metabolomics, and multimodal omics-based discovery, we offer a curated database that aggregates 746 mass spectrometry- and spectroscopy-based tools across 37 categories, from data preprocessing to metabolite annotation. We report four structural shifts that redefine the field's trajectory. First, machine learning (ML) adoption in tools increased by 2.4-fold from 10.9% (2021) to 26.6% (2025). Second, annotation as a category commands the most tools (17%) and the highest ML investment of any of the proposed tool categories. The dominant strategy has shifted from library matching (2021) to spectrum prediction (2024) and, more recently, to de novo structure generation (2025), thereby progressively reducing reliance on accessible experimental spectral reference databases. Third, Python has displaced R as the dominant programming language, with a sharp inflection in 2023 coinciding with the ML surge, while web-server-only tools have sharply declined. Fourth, transformer architectures grew significantly, and in 2025, the first few large language model (LLM)- based and other multimodal metabolomics tools emerged, signaling a transition from task-specific classifiers towards pretrained, transferable representations. Concurrently, adoption of preprints as a publishing venue also rose by 2.5-fold, and, notably, mentions of benchmarking and explainability each increased by 8-18-fold, indicating a growing community-wide need and maturation. This computational metabolomics database is now made available here: https://github.com/enveda/computational-metabolomics-review .

papers.title: Cross-Metathesis of an Iron Carbene with Diazenes
papers.abstract: Olefin metathesis is one of the most versatile reactions in a synthetic chemist’s toolbox. Metathesis of C=X (X = O, N,(=NR)2) substrates has also been developed; however, the simple cross-metathesis of diazenes and olefins remains unrealized, in part due to the lack of mechanistic information about deactivation pathways for traditional olefin cross-metathesis catalysts. Herein, we report the reactions of [{PC(sp2)P}Fe(NCtBu)(N2)] ([PC(sp2)P] = bis(2-di-iso-propylphosphino)methylene) with cyclic diazenes, and the formation of metathesis-related products. These reactions led to the isolation of a diazametallacyclobutane from diazocine that ring opens to afford an in situ iron imido complex, which undergoes an intramolecular C-H amination to afford an iron-indoline. Restricting this side reaction with dibenzodiazepine led to the formation of an iron imide complex, which was stabilized and characterized by a one-electron oxidation.

papers.title: Spin Manipulation Effect in Photodeprotection Reaction Using Triplet Ground-State Cation
papers.abstract: Photolabile protecting groups (PPGs), which temporarily mask functional groups (LGs) and regenerate their activity upon light irradiation of PPG–LGs under reagent-free neutral conditions, have been widely utilized in diverse research fields ranging from organic synthesis to neuroscience. However, under conditions where diffusion of the ion pair consisting of PPG+ and LG– is unfavorable, charge recombination reaction becomes dominant, making efficient photodeprotection difficult. If triplet ground-state cations could be generated, the recombination process would become spin-forbidden, thereby enhancing photodeprotection efficiency. As a proof of concept, we newly designed a PPG capable of generating the triplet ground-state cation, 2-(4-methoxyphenyl)-1Hinden-1-ylium cation (T-PMI+). The generation process and dynamics of T-PMI+ were investigated by ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, while its reactivity was elucidated through chemical trapping experiments by benzyl bromide, molecular oxygen, and ferrocene. This study demonstrates spin manipulation as a new strategy for boosting the efficiency of photo-deprotection reactions. Notably, a remarkably high deprotection selectivity of 92% was achieved.

papers.title: A Hybrid Graph Neural Network and Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Framework for Multi-Drug Concentration Prediction with Explainability and Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: Background. Predicting human pharmacokinetics from molecular structure remains a translational bottleneck in early drug development. Mechanistic physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models offer interpretability but depend on parameter estimates that are rarely accurate for novel compounds. Data-driven machine learning models capture chemical structure effectively but lack physiological grounding. Hybrid approaches that combine the two have shown promise, but their multi-drug generalisation and behaviour under realistic parameter uncertainty have not been characterised systematically. Methods. We present a hybrid framework that couples a message-passing graph neural network (GNN) encoder, pretrained on ESOL and Lipophilicity with additional masked-atom reconstruction over a ChEMBL-derived corpus, with a differentiable one-compartment oral PK simulator. The model predicts patient-specific clearance, volume of distribution, and absorption rate from molecular structure and patient covariates, then integrates these through an explicit Euler ODE solver. Training and evaluation cover six pharmacokinetically diverse drugs (theophylline, warfarin, midazolam, caffeine, acetaminophen, digoxin). Comparators include a population-PBPK baseline with realistic log-normal parameter uncertainty, multilayer perceptron, random forest, XGBoost, and a vanilla GNN. Ablations isolate the contributions of mechanistic structure, transfer learning, and joint training. Ibuprofen serves as a zeroshot external compound. Monte Carlo prediction intervals (N=1000) are calibrated against held-out observations, and KernelSHAP attributions are computed on predicted area under the curve. Results. The hybrid achieves test R2 between 0.78 and 0.93 across six training drugs, with RMSE of 21.5%–29.5% of mean concentration. Against the realistic PBPK baseline, the full hybrid achieves a mean R2 of 0.851 versus 0.341, with paired comparisons significant on per-patient RMSE for five of six drugs. Zeroshot inference on ibuprofen reaches R2 = 0.836 with no fine-tuning. Monte Carlo intervals show pooled 90% coverage of 87.5% with heterogeneous per-drug calibration (caffeine −7.6 percentage points). SHAP attributions identify dose-normalised inputs, body weight, sex, and age as the dominant patient-level drivers, consistent with established pharmacology. Conclusions. Coupling structure-aware molecular encoding with a differentiable mechanistic simulator yields accurate, interpretable PK predictions that generalise across diverse clearance mechanisms and transfer zero-shot to a held-out compound. The hybrid's advantage emerges most strongly on drugs where population PBPK parameters are unreliable. Heterogeneous per-drug calibration and the patientconditional scope of the explainability analysis point toward drug-specific uncertainty modelling and graph-level attribution as natural extensions.

papers.title: Dynamic Hydrogen Bonding Networks Govern CO2 Adsorption in COF-999
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with olenfin-linked backbone and covalently attached amines (e.g. COF-999) have emerged as highly tunable and efficient sorbents for the direct air capture of CO 2 . However, the rational design of next-generation COF materials is hindered by lack of molecular-level understanding of their operating principles, largely due to the intrinsic dynamics of the COF materials. Here, we utilize reactive machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with ab initio fidelity to perform large-scale molecular dynamics simulations integrated with enhanced sampling, allowing for exhaustively mapping the free-energy surfaces of CO 2 chemisorption into COF-999. Our results reveal that under dry conditions, stable chemisorption is restricted to amines within specific cage-like local environments, while the majority of amines remain inactive due to pronounced steric hindrance or the absence of hydrogen bonding environment. In contrast, wet COF-999 expands the population of active amines via a water-induced, loosely packed amine network and more dynamic hydrogen bonding networks, which stabilize both transition states and chemisorbed *CO 2 states. This study provides the first comprehensive molecular-level mechanistic insight into CO 2 chemisorption in COFs, establishing fundamental design principles for next-generation functional materials for carbon capture.

papers.title: Study of the Physical Model of Microbial Fuel Cells in Emergency Lamp as a Lighting Solution in Disaster Evacuation Shelters
papers.abstract: The first studies of microbial fuel cells (MFC) were published more than a decade ago, but the technology didn't catch the attention of scientists until it was discovered that microorganisms could transfer electrons without an external redox medium. Microbial Fuel Cells (MFC) have been used to generate power from various chemicals such as acetate, lactate, and glucose. This study develops the MFC system as an energy source for emergency lighting to provide lighting in evacuation sites that do not have access to electricity. So that it can be a solution to limited lighting in evacuees with limited access to electricity. The purpose of this study was to determine the performance of Microbial Fuel Cells as an energy source for emergency lights, and to analyze the performance improvements made using experimental methods. While the implementation stages are in the form of literature study, collection of tools and materials, design and physical models of emergency lights, fabrication, testing of physical models, parameter measurements, data collection, and analysis of data results. The results showed that the bioelectric potential produced was 27.036 mW/m2, and the smallest was 0.827 mW/m2. Factors that improve the performance of this MFC are MFC operating time, reactor volume, substrate treatment, electrode material, and reactor configuration. The effect of power on light intensity is not too influential if the power source meets the capabilities of the device, with an average intensity generated of 0.822 cd.

papers.title: QuantumPioneer: Scalable generation of quantum chemical data for solution-phase hydrogen transfer reactions
papers.abstract: High-fidelity quantum chemical (QM) datasets that jointly resolve reaction thermochemistry, kinetics, and solvation at scale remain scarce, especially for radical chemistry. We introduce QuantumPioneer, an open-access reaction-centered QM database and workflow for small organic molecules, focused on peroxyl-mediated hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and the corresponding homolytic bond dissociation reactions. QuantumPioneer contains 348,258 species (2–21 heavy atoms), 167,237 validated HAT transition states (TS) with corresponding reaction energies and homolytic bond dissociation energies (BDEs), and over 100 million COSMO-RS solvation free energies (∆Go solv) and enthalpies (∆Ho solv) across 295 solvents. The workflow uses ωB97X-D/def2-SVP geometries, DLPNO-CCSD(T)-F12d/def2-TZVP single-point energies, empirical thermochemical corrections, transition-state theory, and COSMORS BP-TZVPD-FINE solvation in a single high-throughput pipeline. Our benchmarks show reliable accuracy, with mean absolute errors compared to experimental data of 0.82 kcal/mol for gas-phase enthalpies of formation, 1.60 kcal/mol for C–H BDEs, 1.45 kcal/mol for HAT barriers, and 0.57 kcal/mol for ∆Go solv values. We demonstrate two predictive applications. First, we show that a combined BDE and HAT-barrier model identifies experimentally observed oxidative degradation sites in drug-like molecules with a 91% top-5 hit rate and 80% site-level recall. Second, a QM-parameterized Abraham model enables rapid solvation energy estimates at near-COSMO-RS accuracy within its training domain, reproducing ∆Go solv and ∆Ho solv

papers.title: Exploring the Antibacterial Potential of Plant-Derived Bioactive Compounds Against Escherichia coli : A Comprehensive Virtual Screening Study
papers.abstract: The rising prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli has intensified the demand for the development of novel antibacterial agents with enhanced therapeutic efficacy.In the present study, a comprehensive in silico virtual screening pipeline was developed to evaluate the inhibitory potential of flavonoids against E. coli DNA Gyrase B (PDB ID: 1KZN), a critical enzyme involved in bacterial DNA replication and supercoiling. A curated library of 65 flavonoids and flavonoid-derived phytochemicals was retrieved from the PubChem database and prepared using RDKit and Meeko for molecular docking analysis. High-throughput docking was performed using AutoDock Vina, followed by structure–activity relationship (SAR) analysis, Lipinski drug-likeness profiling, and protein–ligand interaction analysis. Among the screened compounds, Naringin demonstrated the strongest binding affinity with a docking score of −10.060 kcal/mol, followed by Hesperidin, Epigallocatechin gallate, Luteolin, and Procyanidin B2. Drug-likeness analysis revealed that although glycosylated flavonoids showed stronger docking scores, Luteolin displayed a more favorable balance between binding affinity and pharmacokinetic properties. Visualization and interaction profiling identified key amino acid residues, including ASN46, VAL71, THR165, and VAL167, involved in stabilizing the Luteolin–DNA Gyrase B complex. Furthermore, SAR analysis suggested that binding affinity was influenced not only by lipophilicity but also by hydrogen bonding and molecular orientation within the active site. Overall, this study highlights flavonoids as promising lead compounds for antibacterial drug discovery and provides a computational framework for future in vitro and in vivo validation studies targeting multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens.

papers.title: Full-Chain Quantitative Model for Catalyst-Reaction Systems: Establishment and Application of Nine Core Equations
papers.abstract: Traditional catalytic research and development rely heavily on the trial-and-error method, which suffers from long research cycles, high experimental costs, ambiguous quantitative correlation between microscopic structures and macroscopic performances, and poor industrial transformation efficiency. This study innovatively integrates artificial intelligence technology with professional catalytic theories to construct a full-chain quantitative model containing nine core equations. Based on standardized measurable physical and chemical parameters, the model covers nine key modules: structural matching, adsorption coverage, reaction kinetics, competitive adsorption, stability under extreme conditions, temperature-pressure regulation, comprehensive performance evaluation, dynamic deactivation and theoretical correlation. A closed-loop research logic of forward performance prediction and reverse system design is established. In terms of research methodology, this work adopts a new collaborative paradigm where human researchers dominate research directions while artificial intelligence serves as an efficient computational tool. Researchers define scientific frameworks and core objectives, and guide general large language models to complete formula derivation, parameter fitting and numerical verification. All derived equations are cross-validated with independent published experimental data to ensure physical rationality and numerical consistency. The model is applicable to single/multi-component reaction systems, atmospheric/high-pressure conditions and conventional/extreme service environments, including CO2 hydrogenation, ammonia synthesis, alkane reforming and other mainstream catalytic fields. Practical verification proves that this model can effectively shorten R&D cycles and reduce experimental investment, providing accurate quantitative tools for rational catalyst design and industrial implementation.

papers.title: Modulation of Membrane Permeability in Oleic Acid Vesicles under an Oxygen-Dependent Enzymatic Reaction System
papers.abstract: Molecular self-assemblies formed by single-chain amphiphiles, including oleic acid, have attracted considerable attention as functional materials capable of controlling the uptake and release of substances in response to pH changes in the surrounding environment. However, oleic acid selfassemblies are sensitive to slight pH changes, often undergoing structural transformation or collapse, making their precise control challenging. In this study, we investigated changes in the membrane structure of oleic acid vesicles in an oxygen-dependent enzymatic reaction system accompanied by a gradual pH decrease. In Tris buffer (pH 8.0) containing alcohol oxidase and methanol, fluorescence changes of a polarity-sensitive probe revealed alterations in the local membrane environment. In addition, the fluorescence intensity of encapsulated hydrophilic molecules gradually decreased over time, suggesting changes in membrane permeability. A slight decrease in pH was observed during the reaction process. These results suggest that gradual changes in the neutralization degree of oleic acid, caused by the generation of formaldehyde and subsequently formic acid through methanol oxidation, altered the vesicular membrane structure, leading to a transient increase in membrane permeability.

papers.title: Dynamics and Energy Relaxation of Formic Acid Dimers Following Inner Valence Ionization
papers.abstract: We study gas-phase dissociation of the formic acid dimer dication as a model for DNA base-pair interactions after inner-valence 56 eV EUV ionization. Employing reaction microscopy, we measure the 3D momenta of electrons and fragment ions in coincidence to reconstruct channel-resolved electron kinetic energies, fragment kinetic energy release, and angular distributions. Two fragmentation pathways occur with similar yields: symmetric (HCOOH+ + HCOOH+) and asymmetric breakup (HCOOH+ + HCOO+ + H). Electronenergy signatures and angular correlations distinguish direct double ionization (DDI) from sequential ionization (SI) with a ratio of 3:2. In SI, low-energy electrons and their nearisotropic angular distributions indicate a competition between intramolecular autoionization (AI) and nonlocal intermolecular Coulombic decay (ICD). Real-time simulations of the electron dynamics support AI/ICD-driven secondary ionization on sub-20 fs timescales. The process depends on whether the initially ionized orbital has carbonyl or hydroxyl oxygen character, with charge and energy transfer occurring between diagonally adjacent oxygen atoms rather than along hydrogen bonds.

papers.title: Reorganizing Periodicity: A New Classification of the Periodic Table of the Elements
papers.abstract: The periodic table of the elements is a fundamental brick in the foundation of chemistry. The current periodic table arranges elements in the increasing order of their atomic numbers and successfully classify them but it is not optimal when it come to display the continuity in the periodic trends of physicochemical the properties. Herein, a new classification system is proposed in which elements are classified according to the nature of their periodicity. This model proposes that s-and p-block elements show primary periodicity, d-block elements display a different secondary periodicity controlled by ns and (n-1)d orbital filling and f-block elements show tertiary periodicity governed by gradual filling of f-orbital. Therefore, d-block elements are placed separately under the s-and p-block elements. This table can also provide a placement for predicted g-block elements. This purpose of this classification is not to replace the conventional periodic table, but to present it as a chemicalperiodicity table. It may exhibit improved periodic trends across periods and can be a handy tool for education, and future discussion of periodic-table extension.

papers.title: Amino Acids in Human Health and Disease: Biochemical Characteristics, Therapeutic Applications, and Pathology of Amino Acid Metabolism
Electrolyte Switching Reveals Electric Double Layer Dynamics and Electrocatalytic Electrolyte Effects
papers.abstract: New insights into the electric double layer (EDL) under strongly driven electrocatalytic (EC) conditions are obtained by measuring its rearrangement kinetics in response to abrupt switching of bulk electrolyte composition (55 ms for complete exchange up to the outer Helmholtz plane (OHP)). The aqueous alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is used as a model EC system, motivated by its opposite alkali metal hydroxide effect: catalyst activity decreases with increasing cation radius on Pt (Li + > Na + > K + > Cs + ) whereas the trend is opposite for Ag. Monitoring the constant potential HER current as the electrolyte composition is switched between two different cations (e.g. Li + and Cs + ) provides an overall kinetic picture as the EDL rearranges to accommodate the new cation. For both Pt and Ag, the transition time is asymmetric; switching from a smaller ionic radius to a larger one is faster than the reverse. Transition times also increase with greater ionic radius difference between the cations and at more negative potentials. The transition time trends are consistent with more weakly hydrated cations having stronger electrostatic ion-electrode interactions. EDL rearrangement kinetics appear unaffected by the simultaneously occurring reactions. In mixed electrolyte experiments, Cs + -dominated kinetics are maintained up to 90% LiOH in LiOH/CsOH electrolytes on Pt, whereas current monotonically increases with increasing CsOH fraction on Ag. While the Stern layer largely dictates Pt cation effects, structure further from the surface impacts kinetics on Ag. Our work emphasizes the spatial extent of electrolyte influence which needs to be captured by theory.

papers.title: Beyond isolated capacity values: A multivariant framework for the evaluation of urea adsorption performance
papers.abstract: Carbon-based materials are widely utilized as promising adsorbents for removing urea from complex urine matrices, thereby mitigating eutrophication and enabling the recovery of a valuable nitrogen source for fertilizers, chemical reagents, pharmaceuticals, and energy storage devices. However, reported urea adsorption capacities of carbon-based materials span orders of magnitude, hindering fair comparison of adsorption performance and limiting their practical implementation. Such discrepancies are often attributed to differences in material structure and properties. Nevertheless, the effects of the experimental parameters used during adsorption tests are important and are rarely systematically examined. Here, we investigate urea adsorption on various carbon-based materials using controlled batch and fixed-bed column experiments. We demonstrate that the equilibrium adsorption capacity (qe) varies strongly with experimental conditions, while the maximum adsorption capacity (qm) is an intrinsic property of an adsorbent; however, it should be reported with caution. Fixed-bed column results further show that batch-derived adsorption capacities are difficult to attain under continuous-flow operation. Accordingly, we propose a more comprehensive evaluation framework that links batch adsorption metrics with their attainability in fixed-bed columns, enabling a more meaningful assessment of urea adsorption performance beyond isolated capacity values.

papers.title: Extreme Ultraviolet Light-Triggered Reaction Cascades in Hybrid Metal Halide Photoresists
papers.abstract: Photolithographic processes employing extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light are critical to fabricating nextgeneration microelectronics; however, improving photoresist sensitivity remains a challenge with organic photoresists due to their low EUV absorption. Hybrid photoresists that pair high EUV-opacity components with those needed for chemical patterning could improve sensitivity, yet we lack context for how resist architectures dictate photoionization efficiency, ensuing reaction rates, and selectivity in reaction products for different chemistries. Here, we tailor the dimensionality and composition of metal halide perovskiteinspired materials to understand and control how EUV exposure impacts total electron yield, speciesspecific rates of off-gassing, dose-dependent changes in film thickness, and patternability using a dry developer. We identify non-classical chemical transformations initiated by low energy electron attachment to electrostatically charged cations in the organic ligands that trigger reaction cascades, whereby a plurality of gaseous species are liberated and dictate resist tone without requiring an exogenous photoacid generator or post-exposure bake. This emerging understanding of EUV light–matter interactions substantially deviates from conventional wisdom and lays the groundwork for high-precision lithography to meet stringent demands of artificial intelligence and quantum computing chip architectures.

papers.title: Catch-and-Release of Molybdate [MoO4] 2– by a Synthetic “Molybdophore” Host.
papers.abstract: Flexible, neutral 2,2′-diindolylmethane-derived ligands L1 and L2 feature two “protic pockets” (comprised of vicinal N–H indole / N–H amide groups) that encapsulate the tetrahedral oxy-di-anion [MoO₄]²⁻ in CD₃CN. Monitoring incremental additions of [ n Bu 4 ] 2 [MoO 4 ] to CD 3 CN solutions of L1 perturb the observed chemical shifts (δ obs ), consistent with the establishment of 2:1 host-guest equilibria (2 L1 + [MoO 4 ] 2– ⇌ L1 + [ L1 •MoO 4 ] 2– ⇌ [2 L1 •MoO 4 ] 2– ; K ₁₁ ≈ 1.6 × 10⁵ M⁻¹ and K ₂₁ ≈ 3 × 10³ M⁻¹). The 1:1 host-guest adduct [ L2 ·MoO₄]²⁻ was characterized as the bis-tetrabutylammonium salt. X-ray structural comparisons suggest that the receptors can adapt their cavity size by increasing θ indole/indole and θ indole/amide (dihedral angles between the two indoloyl planes and the plane defined by an indole and its decorating amide substituent) – increasing spacing between the two “protic pockets” of the host. The addition of acids HBF 4 •Et 2 O or HNTf 2 to solutions of [ L2 ·MoO₄]²⁻ release the guest as a precipitated polyoxomolybdate (“molybdenum blues”). X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy suggests that the ratio of Mo(VI)/Mo(V) changes with the receptor/acid identity. Our work illustrates that flexible polyprotic hosts, if designed appropriately, can recognize metallates like [MoO 4 ] 2– .

papers.title: A scale-invariant spectral spacing law predicts atomic K-edge frequencies of heavy and superheavy elements (Z = 100–150) without relativistic input
papers.abstract: The K-edge frequencies (𝜈 max ) of atoms beyond Xe obey an empirical linear spectral spacing law, Δ𝜈 max = 𝑎 + 𝑏.𝜈 max , with 𝑅 2 = 0.9998 across experimental K-edges for 𝑍 = 55–99. The law is asymptotically scale-invariant, with Δ𝜈 max /𝜈 max → 2.01%, and contains no dependence on atomic number or electronic structure. Applied recursively from a single anchor atom (Cs), it predicts K-edge energies for elements lacking experimental measurements (Po, At, Rn, Fr, Ra, Ac, Pa) with ∼ 0.1% median deviation and reproduces relativistic Dirac–Fock values for 𝑍 = 111–118 to sub-percent accuracy without theoretical input or element-specific parameters. The same asymptotic slope is recovered within 2% from a fit restricted to 𝑍 = 55–82, before relativistic and QED corrections are predicted to become significant. We report empirically anchored K-edge predictions for all elements 𝑍 = 100–150, including 𝜈 max (Og) = (5.292 ± 0.015) × 10 19 s −1 . The success of a single-neighbor recursion at this precision indicates that K-edge frequencies are not independent, but form a sequentially constrained low-dimensional spectral structure.

papers.title: Diphosphaindenyl π-Complexes as a Platform for Hapticity-Controlled Metaloligand Design
papers.abstract: Owing to the indenyl effect, phosphonium-substituted diphosphaindenyl ( PPI Ar ) π-complexes of 3d metal carbonyl fragments provide access to distinct η⁵ and η³ coordination modes, enabling systematic modulation of their metaloligand behavior. Specifically, reaction of [Cr(CO) 3 ( η 5 - PPI tol )] ( 1 ) and [Fe(CO) 3 ( η 3 - PPI Ph )] ( 2 ) with coinage metal salts lead to the formation of the trimetallic complexes [AuCl{Fe(CO) 3 ( η 3 - PPI P h )} 2 ] ( 4 ), [Ag{Fe(CO) 3 ( η 3 - PPI Ph )} 2 ][OTf] ([ 5 ][OTf]) and [Ag{Cr(CO) 3 ( η 5 - PPI tol )} 2 ][BF 4 ] ([ 6 ][BF4]). While the iron-based metaloligands act as σ-donors via phosphorus lone pairs, the chromium complex adopts a distinct η 4 ,μ 2 bridging coordination mode enabling covalent metal-metal interactions. As such, [ 6 ][BF4] represents a rare example of a structurally characterised complex featuring Cr−Ag bonding. Energy decomposition analysis attributes the divergent metaloligand behavior primarily to a balance between non-orbital interaction terms and geometric preparation energies.

papers.title: Tail-to-Tail Olefin Cross-coupling via Photoredox Activation of Alkylboranes
papers.abstract: Olefin cross-coupling (OXC) has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) bonds from simple and abundant feedstocks such as alkenes; however, achieving tail-to-tail regioselectivity remains a longstanding challenge. Herein, we report a modular approach that reliably enables this regiochemical outcome. This strategy leverages in situ Brown hydroboration of unactivated alkenes to generate linear organoboranes, which are directly engaged in a photocatalytic Giese-type addition without intermediate isolation. Detailed mechanistic investigation shows that alkylboranes can be used as radical progenitors via photoredox catalysis in the presence of coordinating solvents. The operational simplicity and broad applicability of this protocol render it a practical platform for the rapid synthesis of sp3-rich molecules from olefins via an unconventional disconnection.

papers.title: End-to-end discovery of MOFs for ambient CH4 adsorption
papers.abstract: We report an end-to-end computational–experimental workflow for the discovery of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), demonstrated by the computational design and synthesis of two novel Zn-based frameworks, UCHI-1 and UCHI-2, exhibiting enhanced methane uptake and selectivity at low pressure under ambient conditions (298 K, 1 bar). The workflow enables the rational selection and experimental realization of metal-organic frameworks combining data mining, machine-learning driven adsorption prediction, and structure generation, with experimental synthesis and validation within a closed-loop discovery pipeline. Analysis of existing and newly generated MOFs reveals the structure–property relationships governing low-pressure methane adsorption, identifying an optimal pore size and shape, framework densities, linker functionalities, and framework topologies that maximize dispersive C–H/π and Van der Waals interactions. Beyond the specific materials identified herein, the results establish this workflow as a scalable and extensible platform for accelerated MOF discovery, with clear routes toward further optimization and automation while demonstrating practical applicability beyond purely theoretical exploration of hypothetical materials.

papers.title: Reliability of generative structure-based drug design models under pocket featurization stress
papers.abstract: Generative models for structure-based drug design (SBDD) are evaluated almost exclusively on molecular output quality—validity, uniqueness, and synthetic accessibility computed from a single fixed featurization of the target binding pocket. This design measures what models can generate but not whether their outputs are reliable under the input variation that drug discovery workflows routinely introduce. Here we introduce a perturbation-based reliability benchmark and apply it to two leading SBDD generative models, DiffSBDD and Pocket2Mol, across 47 diverse protein–ligand complexes from the RCSB Protein Data Bank. Four featurization stresses—atom-order shuffle, sub-Ångström coordinate jitter, and ±1.5 Å crop-radius adjustment—aim to preserve binding-site chemistry while varying how the pocket tensor is constructed from the same structural model. DiffSBDD achieves full generation coverage across all 47 pockets but is flagged brittle on every pocket at threshold τ ≤ 0.10, with brittleness rates of 0.979 and 0.915 at τ = 0.15 and 0.20 respectively. Pocket2Mol generates valid molecules on only 13 of 47 pockets and exhibits brittleness rate 1.0 on those covered cases. Individual failures are substantial: coordinate jitter alone reduces molecule validity for PDB entry 3RFM from 0.85 to 0.50, a collapse attributable to perturbations smaller than typical crystallographic uncertainty. Complementary nearest-residue mutation experiments on 20 pockets reveal a second failure mode: DiffSBDD responds to only 32 of 40 biologically meaningful perturbations, with directionally interpretable responses in 65.6% of responsive cases and inconsistent Vina docking score shifts under tryptophan substitution. Together these results demonstrate a dual reliability failure in current SBDD generative models—fragility to representational noise that should be inconsequential, and inconsistent sensitivity to biological signals that should be decisive. We argue that SBDD benchmarks should routinely report generation coverage, brittleness under featurization stress, and meaningful-perturbation responsiveness alongside conventional quality metrics.

papers.title: Pre-Formulated, Shelf-Stable, Dendritic Cell-Targeting Nanogel mRNA Vaccine Delivery Platform
papers.abstract: Current mRNA-based vaccine platforms are limited by complex fabrication, stringent cold-chain dependence, and off-target in vivo delivery, restricting their global accessibility, and targeting precision. Here we show a modular mRNA delivery platform; our approach integrates inverse microemulsion-derived polymeric nanogels with adsorption-based mRNA loading and the capability for ligand-directed targeting to develop Targeted Reductively-cleavable Acrylate-based Inverse microemulsion Nanogels (TRAINs). By decoupling nanoparticle fabrication from mRNA loading, pre-formed TRAINs can be stockpiled and later combined with newly designed mRNA, enabling a plug-and-play strategy for rapid adaption to emerging pathogens, which is particularly advantageous for pandemic preparedness. This architecture supports efficient mRNA association and robust cellular uptake and translation in HEK293T cells. TRAIN also enable post-synthetic surface functionalization; as a proof of concept, CD206-targeted TRAINs promoted selective delivery to antigen presenting cells (APCs), producing sustained and localized protein expression in BALB/c mice and preferential mRNA delivery to myeloid APCs in heterogeneous human peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Together, these results demonstrate TRAINs as a surface-customizable, adsorption-based mRNA delivery platform with potential for APC-targeted vaccination and rapid, adaptable vaccine deployment.

papers.title: ConPET-Driven Aryl Halide Reduction with a Donor-Acceptor-Donor Anion Radical
papers.abstract: This study investigates the anion radical of a donor-acceptor-donor molecule, namely 4,7-di(thiophen-2-yl)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole (TBT), as a photosensitizer for conPET reactions. Fluorescence lifetime decay and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy on TBT –• revealed a doublet excited state lifetime of 250 ± 6 ps. Cyclic voltammetry and excited-state energy (E 0,0 ) analysis determined the excited state oxidation potential, E(*TBT –• /TBT) = -2.80 V vs. SCE. Rehm-Weller analysis of the excited state (*TBT –• ) quenching kinetics also corroborated the estimated excited state oxidation potential. Model reactions with a series of aryl bromides monitored by 19 F-NMR and HPLC confirmed that TBT –• can act as a strongly reducing photosensitizer for visible light-mediated aryl halide reduction via a conPET mechanism.

papers.title: Chemical Signatures of Descriptor Performance in Band Gap Prediction for Organic Molecules
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models for molecular property prediction depend critically on the representation used to encode molecular structure. For properties such as the band gap (HOMO-LUMO gap), descriptor choice is difficult to anticipate because the target is electronic in origin but remains strongly shaped by molecular composition and structure. Here, we compare four molecular representations for band gap prediction on a large dataset or organic molecules extracted from the CSD: the geometry-based descriptors SOAP and SLATM, the quantum-informed descriptor MODA, and molecular embeddings extracted from the pretrained MACE-OFF model. In addition to global error metrics, we featurize the molecules to associate descriptor errors to interpretable molecular motifs, enabling chemically resolved analyses of shared difficulty, pairwise descriptor advantage, and descriptor-specific outlier tails. In absolute terms, MACE gives the best overall performance, followed by SLATM, MODA, and SOAP, but no descriptor is uniformly optimal: even lower-ranked descriptors are often the best for substantial subsets of molecules. The chemically resolved analysis reveals that descriptor failures are not random, but are associated with specific molecular motifs responsible for creating-or amplifying-a mismatch between the information encoded by a descriptor, and the electronic factors controlling the band gap. A frontier-molecular-orbital variant of MODA, MODAFMO, supports this interpretation by showing that part of the noise introduced by ”spectator” motifs can be anticipated and reduced, thereby improving the coupling between the molecular representation and the target property. Overall, these results show that descriptor performance in band gap prediction is best understood as a chemistry-dependent tradeoff rather than as a single global ranking, and that error analysis can provide chemical insight into what different molecular representations encode.

papers.title: Weighted Views Representation with Multi-Head Coulomb Attention for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: We extend the weighted views molecular featurization framework (d’Avezac, Botts, Mohlenkamp and Zunger, 2011) by enriching with single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information. We use these enriched views within a machine-learning architecture incorporating shared Transformers whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions, weighted aggregation of view outputs, and a final prediction neural network. On the QM7 atomization energy benchmark, our method achieves a test MAE of 3.6 kcal/mol, competitive with leading approaches. On a task of ranking enantiomers by docking scores, where chirality is essential, we attain 72.2% accuracy, surpassing prior methods including ChIRo (72.0%) and SphereNet (68.6%).

papers.title: Sand Micro-Abrasion and Its Contribution to Accelerated Occlusal Wear: An In Vitro and Field-Correlated Study Using Simulated Silicate Particulate Exposure
papers.abstract: Objective: To quantify the contribution of sand micro-abrasion to occlusal wear under simulated desert conditions and correlate in vitro findings with standardized environmental particulate exposure profiles. Methods: Commercial dental enamel analogs (hydroxyapatitebased composite discs) and CAD/CAM resin-based restorative blocks were subjected to cyclic mechanical loading (50 N, 1.2 Hz) in a custom-built abrasion chamber. Three particulate conditions were tested: (i) control (no particles), (ii) fine desert dust (1–10 µm), and (iii) mixed sand particulate (10–200 µm), sourced from standardized ISO silica powders. A controlled aerosolization system simulated airborne particle deposition during mastication cycles. Surface loss (µm), roughness (Ra), and microcrack propagation were assessed via non-contact profilometry and SEM. A field-correlation model was established using published desert particulate density datasets and replicated deposition rates. Results: Mixed particulate exposure resulted in a 4.7-fold increase in volumetric wear compared to control (p < 0.001), while fine dust induced significant surface roughness without proportional bulk loss. SEM revealed characteristic micro-chipping and intergranular fracture patterns. Wear progression followed a non-linear trend with a transition from polishing to erosive regimes at particle sizes >50 µm. Significance: Sand micro-abrasion significantly accelerates occlusal wear under desert-like conditions, with particle size distribution acting as a critical determinant. These findings support a dual-mechanism model combining micro-cutting and fatigue-induced fracture. Also, these findings show that populations exposed to high particulate environments may experience accelerated dental wear independent of dietary factors.

papers.title: In silico identification of praziquantel as a putative vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
papers.abstract: Background: Tolvaptan, a vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R) antagonist, is the only approved disease-modifying therapy for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Its clinical use is limited by an FDA Black Box warning for idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury (DILI), creating an unmet need for V2R antagonists with improved safety profiles. We additionally test whether the screening methodology generalizes by reapplying the entire pipeline to a second, unrelated protein target. Methods: We performed a virtual screen of 3,790 chemically diverse drug-like ChEMBL molecules (max_phase ≥ 2, MW 250–550) against the recently solved tolvaptan-bound V2R structure (PDB 9HAP) using AutoDock Vina (exhaustiveness 8) on a consumer laptop CPU. Candidates passing the tolvaptan score threshold (≤ −8.43 kcal/mol) were filtered through staged drug-likeness, PAINS, and reactive-group filters, then categorized into priority tiers using Tanimoto novelty against known vaptans and ChEMBL clinical-phase metadata. Top candidates were structurally validated by computing receptor-residue contact overlap with the tolvaptan reference pose, cross-validated by independent AI-based blind docking with DiffDock-L, and assessed for predicted hepatotoxicity using admet-AI. Cross-receptor selectivity was characterized by Vina counter-docking against AlphaFold-predicted V1a, V1b, and oxytocin (OTR) receptors using toggle-tryptophan-centered docking boxes. Atom-level binding-mode comparison between praziquantel and tolvaptan was performed by distance-based interaction analysis on the Mode-1 docked poses. To probe methodology generalization, the entire pipeline was reapplied to an unrelated protein target — secreted phospholipase A2 group IIA (sPLA2, PDB 1OXL), an enzyme implicated in snake-venom lethality — with varespladib (a clinically investigated pan-sPLA2 inhibitor) as a reference-anchor compound at every triage step and a five-move triage funnel applied to the 3,724-ligand library: druglikeness; cross-target Vina-bias diagnostic; ADMET; active-site catalytic-residue (His48 + Asp49) contact validation; decoy-distribution check; snake-vs-human selectivity counter-screen against human PLA2G2A (PDB 1KVO); and DiffDock-L rescore. Pipeline reproducibility was independently assessed by docking varespladib twice via independent paths (explicit reference dock and incidental presence in the ChEMBL library). Results: Three Tier-1 candidates were selected for full validation: praziquantel, olaparib, and glimepiride. Praziquantel — an FDA-approved antiparasitic on the WHO Essential Medicines List — emerged as the strongest cross-validated candidate: Vina score −9.75 kcal/mol (vs tolvaptan −8.43), DiffDock-L rank-1 confidence −1.01 (vs tolvaptan −1.35; both moderate confidence), and 75% binding-pocket residue overlap with tolvaptan including engagement of the W6.48 toggle switch. Critically, admet-AI predicted approximately half the DILI risk of tolvaptan (0.466 vs 0.918) along with reduced predicted hERG cardiac liability and lower lipophilicity. Olaparib showed cross-method binding agreement but matched tolvaptan's high predicted DILI; glimepiride was rejected by DiffDock disagreement. No prior literature was identified linking praziquantel to V2R or ADPKD. Counter-screen against V1a, V1b, and oxytocin receptors confirmed praziquantel as V2-preferring (V2R−V1A delta = −4.09 kcal/mol, more selective than tolvaptan's −2.82), with the caveat that the V2R−OTR delta (−2.05 kcal/mol) is the weakest of the three discriminations. Atom-level interaction analysis revealed that praziquantel engages the same critical V2R residues as tolvaptan (Q89, Q93, Q116, W6.48 toggle tryptophan, K113) with three hydrogen bonds versus tolvaptan's two, despite a structurally distinct pyrazinoisoquinoline scaffold (versus tolvaptan's benzazepine), providing a mechanistic rationale for the predicted hepatotoxicity differential. A targeted SAR scan around the praziquantel cyclohexyl substituent generated 37 designed analogs evaluated through the same full pipeline; three analogs beat praziquantel on at least two of four target criteria, most notably a spiro[2.5]octan-6-yl variant with a 64% reduction in predicted DILI (0.169 vs 0.466) and reduced OTR engagement at the cost of a modest decrease in predicted V2R binding strength. Methodology generalization to sPLA2 yielded 3,721 successful dockings (99.92%) over 6.07 hours of wall-clock screening, with varespladib (Vina −9.55 kcal/mol) ranking in the top ~15% of the library — broadly consistent with its established biological role. After the five-move triage funnel, a four-way validated eight-candidate shortlist emerged. The strongest snake-selective candidate is cipargamin, an antimalarial spiroindolone in Phase 2 trials (snake-sPLA2 Vina −10.77 kcal/mol, snake-vs-human selectivity Δ = −2.34 kcal/mol, His48-engaging active-site STRONG verdict, DiffDock-L confidence comparable to or better than varespladib); drospirenone, an approved oral progestin, emerged as an unexpected separate Tier-1 candidate with the best ADMET profile in the panel (predicted DILI 0.08, hERG 0.12). Two methodology disclosures arose from the sPLA2 work: (i) initial human-counter-receptor docking boxes centered on a 216-atom substrate-analogue ligand drifted 24 Å from the catalytic histidine, producing a uniform selectivity artifact caught only because the varespladib reference anchor produced a biologically-implausible result; the fix is to anchor docking boxes on a catalytic-residue side-chain atom (His48 NE2) when the bound inhibitor spans the substrate channel; (ii) DiffDock-L is not absolutely calibrated for small (~125-residue) secreted enzymes, so its sPLA2 confidences must be interpreted relative to a reference compound rather than against the published absolute threshold. Reproducibility-by-duplicate: varespladib's Vina Mode-1 scores agreed to 0.056 kcal/mol across two independent dockings (explicit reference dock and incidental ChEMBL-library presence) — well within Vina's normal run-to-run variance. Conclusions: We report computational evidence that praziquantel is a putative V2R-binding repurposing candidate with predicted hepatotoxicity substantially lower than tolvaptan and a V2-selectivity profile more favorable than the current standard of care; we additionally disclose three computationally-designed praziquantel analogs predicted to further improve on the parent compound's ADMET profile. The screening methodology generalizes to a second unrelated protein target (sPLA2), where it produced a four-way validated eight-candidate shortlist headed by cipargamin and drospirenone as secondary, separately-pursuable repurposing hypotheses for snake-envenomation sPLA2 inhibition; signal quality is target-dependent and two methodology disclosures (catalytic-residue-anchored docking boxes for small enzymes; reference-anchor sanity checks at every triage step) are reported in support of the generalization claim.
