These predictions warrant experimental validation: V2R radioligand binding, functional cAMP suppression assays (including parallel OTR counter-screening), ADPKD cell-line cyst models, and prospective synthesis-and-test of the designed analogs for the V2R arm; sPLA2 inhibition assays and in vivo snakebite-envenomation models for the sPLA2 arm. The full pipeline is reproducible on a consumer CPU/GPU laptop using public open-source tools. We make no clinical claims; in vitro and in vivo validation are required before any therapeutic implications can be assessed.

papers.title: First-principles multi-scale design of gas diffusion electrodes for electrochemical CO2
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction on copper offers a route to valuable fuels and chemicals, but performance depends strongly on electrolyzer design, which is not yet well understood due to the multiscale complexity coupling kinetics and transport. Here, we address this using a first-principles multiscale modeling framework for gas diffusion electrodes. By constructing digital twins of previously reported experimental electrolyzers, the simulations identify two critical cell design parameter groups which control spatial product selectivity: (1) Electrochemical surface area of the catalyst, which governs current densities across the catalyst layer and voltage range; and (2) catalyst support properties, which govern activity near the gas inlet at high currents. Under the latter conditions, high out-flux of gaseous products blocks the incoming CO2 gas, a process strongly influenced by substrate pore size. We also present evidence for product selectivity regions within the catalyst layer, and their sensitive dependence on GDE design. This work extends the scope of first-principles simulations to shed important light into the multi-scale complexity of modern electrolyzers.

papers.title: NIR-II Image-Guided Photothermogenetics with AIE Photothermal Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Neurons, the fundamental computational units of the nervous system, can be modulated by electrical stimulation, chemogenetics, optogenetics, and related approaches. However, each modality imposes practical constraints that can limit broad implementation in neuroscience. Here, we develop photothermogenetic nanoparticles (NPs) based on an aggregation-induced emission luminogen (AIEgen) to modulate neural activity through activation of Transient Receptor Potential Cation Channel Subfamily V Member 1 (TRPV1). Upon 808 nm irradiation, the AIEgen nanoformulation generates localized photothermal heating while emitting near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence, enabling simultaneous actuation and visualization. In an open-field assay, mice receiving stereotaxic delivery of the AIEgen NPs together with TRPV1 overexpression in the motor cortex show increased locomotor activity under NIR-II fluorescence guidance during NIR stimulation. These results establish an image-guided photothermogenetic platform for tether-free neuromodulation in vivo.

papers.title: Intrinsic Functionality-Enabled δ-Selective C(sp3)–H Functionalization of α-Amino Acids via Nitrogen-Centered Radical Relay
papers.abstract: δ-Selective C(sp3)–H functionalization of amino acids remains a longstanding challenge. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven strategy that enables intrinsic functionality-enabled remote selectivity by directly exploiting the native amino group, thereby obviating the need for exogenous directing groups. Photoredox-mediated single-electron oxidation generates N-centered radicals that undergo 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer (1,5-HAT) to form distal carbon radicals, which engage in alkene addition followed by radical–polar crossover to deliver the products. The method exhibits broad scope, high site-selectivity, and compatibility with peptides and complex molecules, providing a general platform for late-stage diversification of amino acids.

papers.title: Pharmacokinetic Studies of Amyloid-targeting Bis(styryl)benzene Agents for Alzheimer’s Disease
papers.abstract: The pharmacokinetics (PK) and biodistribution of radiolabeled amyloid-β (Aβ)targeting probes have been extensively characterized in the context of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), whereas the corresponding non-radiolabeled scaffolds remain largely unexplored in vivo. Herein, we report in vivo PK studies of the widely used amyloid probe Methoxy-X04 (MeX04) in transgenic 5xFAD and wild-type (WT) mice. In plasma, MeX04 shows comparable exposure between 5xFAD and WT mice, indicating no major genotypedependent differences in systemic clearance. In contrast, brain exposure was markedly increased in 5xFAD mice, with higher brain Cmax and AUC parameters and slower washout, consistent with Aβ-dependent sequestration and retention in AD brain tissue. Notably, fluorescence microscopy revealed that the fluorescence intensity of amyloid plaque-bound MeX04 closely mirrored the total brain concentration, and we then employed ex vivo fluorescence intensity quantification to evaluate the PK of a related bis(styryl)benzene compound, LS-4, which is proposed to exhibit increased affinity for soluble Aβ aggregates. We then performed age-dependent ex vivo staining of compoundbound Aβ aggregates in 5xFAD brains, and LS-4 exhibits appreciable amyloid-bound fluorescence intensity in younger 5xFAD mice, consistent with its higher affinity for Aβ oligomers, whereas MeX04 exhibited stronger fluorescent intensity in older mice. Consequently, we propose an efficient approach to track temporal changes in the PK of Aβ-binding compounds by ex vivo evaluation of their amyloid-bound fluorescence intensity, providing a rapid assessment of the general PK trends of newly developed amyloid-binding probes.

papers.title: Open-Source Modular Laboratory Robots as Building Blocks for Flexible
papers.abstract: Lab automation is a key enabler of algorithmic-driven research in materials science, by increasing the throughput and accelerating experimental workflows researchers can generate the large amounts of experimental datasets required to validate and refine machine learning and artificial intelligence models. Nonetheless, access to automation remains limited to a small subset of the scientific community due to the high cost of commercial systems, limited expertise and lack of flexible automation tools for evolving research workflows. In response, research groups have developed custom automation solutions by retrofitting low-cost motion platforms, such as 3D printers or CNC machines, to perform experimental tasks. However, these platforms have not been originally designed to meet the requirements of materials science and engineering (MSE) experiments, leading to solutions that do not necessarily scale well with common laboratory infrastructure and practices. Here we introduce the Qubot , a flexible and modular robotic platform designed to meet the requirements of MSE experiments that is built from standardized cost-effective components, lowering the financial and technical barriers for adoption. We characterize the Qubot performance using internationally recognised protocols, demonstrating repeatability and precision superior to commonly used motion platforms that are retrofitted for experimental work. Finally, we validate the design through stress testing in representative experimental tasks and demonstrate their flexible modularity by applying them in two fully automated laboratory workflows related to the preparation and characterization of shampoo formulations and polymer electrolytes.

papers.title: Design Rules for Externally Triggered Drug Uncaging under Optical and Radiolytic Regimes
papers.abstract: Externally triggered prodrug activation can improve therapeutic index by decoupling systemic distribution from pharmacological activity. This review examines prodrug uncaging strategies enabled by electromagnetic radiation through the lens of activation physics and clinical constraints, spanning UV–visible–near-infrared photochemistry and ionizing radiation. Differences in clinical applicability arise from fundamentally contrasting activation physics and irradiation geometry. While recent reviews have cataloged externally triggered prodrug systems across multiple modalities, we instead organize the field by activation regime and evaluate these systems under clinically realistic constraints. In photochemical activation, direct light-chromophore coupling enables predictable bond cleavage through defined excited-state pathways, but effective application is constrained by tissue optics and beam-sample geometry. X- and γ-rays penetrate deeply into tissues, but their uncaging pathway is indirect via diffusible water radiolysis products, resulting in stochastic rather than deterministic cleavage chemistry. We evaluate these platforms using deliverability, irradiation geometry, dose efficiency under clinically realistic conditions, microenvironment dependence, and functional group compatibility. We conclude with practical design rules and a decision framework that aligns targeted pathology and treatment objectives with the appropriate trigger chemistry, payload selection, and delivery strategy under the governing activation physics.

papers.title: Ultrabroadband Plasmonic–MOF Photocatalysts for Efficient Near-Infrared-Driven CO2 Reduction
papers.abstract: The efficient conversion of carbon dioxide into value-added chemicals using solar energy remains a critical scientific and technological challenge, particularly due to the limited utilization of the near-infrared (NIR) region of the solar spectrum. In this study, we report the design and synthesis of an ultrabroadband plasmonic–metal–organic framework (MOF) hybrid photocatalyst capable of driving the Carbon Dioxide Reduction Reaction under NIR irradiation. Gold nanorods with tuneable longitudinal surface plasmon resonance were successfully integrated into a UiO-66-NH2 framework through an in-situ encapsulation strategy followed by mild thermal treatment to enhance interfacial coupling. The resulting composite exhibits strong and continuous light absorption across the 300–1200 nm range, enabling efficient harvesting of low-energy photons. Under 808 nm irradiation, the optimized catalyst demonstrates a CO production rate of 152.3 μmol g-1 h-1 with a selectivity exceeding 90%. Detailed spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses reveal that plasmon-induced hot carrier generation and efficient interfacial charge transfer play a decisive role in enhancing photocatalytic performance. This work provides a viable pathway for extending photocatalytic activity into the NIR region and contributes to the advancement of solar-to-chemical energy conversion technologies.

papers.title: The Structural and Dynamical Effect of Monolignol Coniferyl Alcohol on Biomembranes: Partitioning without Perturbation
papers.abstract: Monolignols are lignin precursors that must cross the plasma membrane before polymerization in the cell wall, but their interaction with lipid membranes remains poorly defined experimentally. In this work, we used Neutron Membrane Diffraction, Small-Angle Neutron Scattering, Neutron Spin Echo, and Quasi-Elastic Neutron Scattering to examine the structural and dynamical effects of coniferyl alcohol (CA) in a DOPC/DOPE model membrane. Partially deuterated coniferyl alcohol (CA-D5) enabled contrast-sensitive measurements of its distribution within the bilayer. The structural measurements show that CA-D5 partitions broadly through the membrane, with no distinct accumulation at a specific bilayer depth. The bilayer thickness and vesicle morphology remain largely preserved, with only modest thinning observed from the reconstructed scattering length density profiles. Dynamically, CA-D5 softens the membrane at the collective level, as shown by a reduced effective bending modulus from Neutron Spin Echo, but the effect saturates quickly with concentration. At the molecular scale, Quasi-Elastic Neutron Scattering shows that lipid lateral diffusivity is not systematically changed, although the jump distance increases at higher CAD5 concentration. These results indicate that CA is incorporated into lipid bilayers without strong disruption of membrane structure or local lipid mobility. The findings provide a molecular-level picture of monolignol–membrane compatibility and support the physical feasibility of membrane permeation without extensive bilayer reorganization.

papers.title: Orbital-Isotopic Modulation of Stereoelectronic Interactions
papers.abstract: Isotope effects are traditionally interpreted in terms of mass-dependent vibrational motion and zero-point energy differences. Here, we show that isotopic substitution can also modulate stereoelectronic interactions by changing donor–acceptor orbital energy alignment through nuclear quantum effects. Using constrained nuclear–electronic orbital density functional theory combined with natural bond orbital analysis, we identify an orbital-isotopic effect in which H/D substitution changes bonding–antibonding energy gaps at the beyond-Born–Oppenheimer electronic-structure level. Methane reveals the primary local response, whereas ethane and a deuterated dioxane derivative demonstrate its propagation into σ → σ∗ hyperconjugation and n → σ∗ anomeric effects. These results expand isotope effects from a purely vibrational-energy concept to a chemically intuitive electronic-structure descriptor for analyzing stereoelectronic interactions.

papers.title: Post-synthetic Bromination of a Dinuclear Aluminum Helicate and Its Chiroptical Properties
papers.abstract: Dinuclear aluminum-based triple-stranded helicates were functionalized through post-synthetic bromination with N-bromosuccinimide, enabling direct modification of a pre-assembled helical framework. By controlling of the reagent equivalents, mono- and octadecabrominated derivatives were selectively obtained while the helical structure was preserved. Increasing the degree of bromination induced red shifts in both the absorption and emission wavelength, reflecting systematic modulation of the electronic structures. In addition, the complexes exhibit large Stokes shifts, and optical resolution of these complexes yields enantiomers exhibiting mirror-image circular dichroism and circularly polarized luminescence.

papers.title: Ultrasensitive and Rapid Identification of Aromatic Toxins in Water using Multicolored Living Biosensors
papers.abstract: Simultaneous identification of isostructural xenobiotics within complex aqueous mixtures remains a long-standing challenge in environmental monitoring. Using a combination of specialized biosensors, we provide a generic and reliable strategy for direct, ultrasensitive detection of aromatic priority pollutants such as phenolics and BTEX in water samples. Highly specific biosensor modules were integrated with genetically-encoded fluorescent proteins to generate a multi-colored palette of whole-cell biosensors which detect monoaromatics over a broad range (1-105 ppb). Acquisition of spectral profiles from individual sensor cells, each specific for a particular pollutant, enabled the discrimination of signals emanating from single biosensors thereby allowing for concurrent identification of multiple pollutants in mixtures. Our synthetic biology based methodology is robust and easily adaptable to a multitude of biosensor designs – apart from water pollution where several toxic contaminants coexist, the proposed strategy can be extended to monitor human health where rapid recognition of biomarkers is crucial for efficient diagnosis.

papers.title: Alkali-ion pump for scalable exfoliation of high-quality graphene
Optically induced microwave-free dynamic nuclear polarization in liquids using porphyrins and BDPA radical
papers.abstract: Optical dynamic nuclear polarization (oDNP) in liquids offers a promising route to microwave-free nuclear magnetic resonance signal amplification but remains limited to a single dye–radical system (e.g., Rose Bengal–TEMPO), with only modest enhancements and poor photostability. Here we show that porphyrin–BDPA pairs overcome these limitations, yielding enhancement factors up to –7.5 and –25 for bulk 1H spins in room-temperature solution at 0.35 and 0.16 T, respectively. Enhancements at X-band are approximately twofold higher than those observed on previously reported oDNP systems. Importantly, NMR signal amplification is achieved with high photostability, eliminating the need for flow conditions, and using a low-power incoherent light source (<0.9 W). The measured enhancements scale with optical power, indicating that the present performances are not fundamentally limited. This work establishes porphyrins as a versatile platform for optical hyperpolarization and opens new directions for light-driven DNP in liquids.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Principle of Chemical Reaction: Vinyl Free-radical Polymerization
papers.abstract: Free-radical polymerization of vinyl monomers was discussed in the framework of new thermodynamics. Average electron temperatures in the outer atomic layer and bonds were used as criteria to infer reaction probabilities, reaction heat, and possible linking structures between two units. For example, the free radical temperature of AIBN-C* is 0.9754×105 K, while that of BPO-O* is 1.1496×105 K. The electron temperature in CH2=CH2 is 1.0214×105 K. Still, when a benzene ring is present, the temperatures differ, i.e., 0.9838 (attaching benzene) and 1.0249×105 K. Heat flows from the higher to the lower temperature, resulting in a difference in probability that a carbon attacks a free radical or vice versa. Hence, the probability of the structure linking monomeric units is estimated. Four electrons in the single bonds of -CH2-CH2- is 1.0428 ×105 K. Therefore, the polymerization heat of CH2=CH2 is 4× 𝑅∆𝑇 = 106.5 kJ/mol (Ref. 107.5 kJ/mol). For styrene, the heat of each propagation step varies with the linking structures. The probabilities estimated by the heat ratios are: head-tail/tail-head, 86.87%; tail-tail, 11.02%; and head-head, 2.11%. Copolymerization of St/MMA is also analyzed. A thermodynamic equation for the instantaneous composition of St is deduced. In summary, the electron temperature provides a simple, straightforward approach to quantifying the mechanism of all organic reactions.

papers.title: Developing Scotch tape Exfoliation Methods for Two-Dimensional Magnetic Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: The emergence of two-dimensional materials has transformed solid-state chemistry and condensed matter physics, yet intrinsic magnetism remains rare in atomically thin systems. Magnetic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a compelling and chemically versatile platform to address this challenge, combining tuneable magnetic interactions with crystal structures amenable to exfoliation. In this Review, we examine the development of the micro-mechanical “Scotch tape” method for the isolation of two-dimensional magnetic MOFs, benchmarking it against established exfoliation approaches and highlighting its unique ability to yield larger, higher-quality nanosheets. Through key case studies, we assess the current state of the field, identifying critical limitations including poor reproducibility, insufficient methodological reporting, challenges in crystal growth, and difficulties in applying surface-sensitive magnetic characterisation techniques. We further discuss how these barriers may be overcome through community-driven standardisation of exfoliation protocols, advances in crystal engineering, and the integration of computational and data-driven approaches to predict exfoliation behaviour. Finally, we outline emerging opportunities for tailoring magnetic and surface properties in MOF nanosheets, positioning Scotch tape exfoliation as a powerful yet underutilised route toward the rational design and discovery of next-generation two-dimensional magnetic materials.

papers.title: Aqueous Two-Phase Extraction Enables the Chirality and Handedness Sorting of Mechanically Interlocked Derivatives of SWCNTs
papers.abstract: The integration of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) into photonics and electronics requires their precise separation by chirality and handedness, alongside chemical functionalization. Typically, these requirements are addressed sequentially, with functionalization following the tedious sorting of pristine tubes. We demonstrate that aqueous two-phase extraction (ATPE) enables the high-resolution sorting of mechanically interlocked nanotubes (MINTs), resolving chirality and handedness directly from functionalized precursors. We identify a critical functionalization threshold (~25 wt.%) below which ATPE protocols transfer seamlessly from pristine to modified nanotubes with high efficiency. Using pH-driven and trisurfactant methodologies, we isolate chirality-pure (6,5) MINTs and resolve their enantiomers with high enantiomeric purity (~85%), while maintaining their full structural integrity. This work establishes design principles for the post-synthetic sorting of functionalized nanotubes, providing a direct route to chirality-pure materials with tailorable electronic properties for sensing, catalysis, and quantum technologies.

papers.title: Study of friction and adhesion behaviour of PDMS elastomer
papers.abstract: Friction and adhesion between soft elastomers such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and glass are fundamental interfacial phenomena that critically influence performance in numerous scientific and technological applications. The unique combination of PDMS elastomer’s flexibility, transparency, and chemical stability, along with the rigidity and smoothness of glass, enables their pairing in systems where controlled adhesion and friction are required. This combination finds applications in diverse areas such as microfluidics, lab-on-a-chip devices, soft robotics, and wearable sensors. Reliable and tunable interfacial properties are needed to keep microchannels sealed, make diagnostic platforms stable, and ensure proper gripping or motion. In this study, the interfacial friction and adhesion between PDMS elastomers and borosilicate glass were systematically investigated using a tribometer. Two experimental conditions were examined: (i) variation of the PDMS base-tocuring agent mixing ratio, and (ii) adjustment of curing parameters, namely temperature and time. The influence of these factors on the elastic modulus of PDMS elastomer was correlated with the resulting frictional and adhesive responses at the interface. The results reveal that an increased elastic modulus, achieved through higher curing agent ratios and elevated curing conditions, leads to higher friction forces but reduced adhesion. Conversely, a lower elastic modulus, associated with reduced curing agent content and milder curing conditions, yields lower friction forces and enhanced adhesion.

papers.title: 50 MHz WSe2 Photodetectors from Roll-to-Roll Exfoliated Films
papers.abstract: In this study, we investigate the time-resolved photodetection characteristics of multilayer WSe 2 films fabricated via roll-to-roll mechanical exfoliation. By systematically studying the bias and irradiance dependence of the photocurrent dynamics, and by employing spatially resolved photocurrent mapping, we provide insights into the mechanisms governing the device response. We demonstrate a pronounced irradiance dependence of the response times and reveal decay times of 9.8 ns as well as 3 dB electrical bandwidths exceeding 50 MHz, rendering these devices on par with high-quality, manually exfoliated WSe 2 photodetectors. These results establish roll-to-roll exfoliation as a powerful and scalable fabrication technique capable of producing high-speed photodetectors.

papers.title: Using a low-storage contour-integral eigensolver for nonsymmetric matrices with collocation to compute vibrational spectra
papers.abstract: Collocation is advantageous for computing vibrational spectra because it obviates the need for quadrature. However, to use collocation one must solve a non-Hermitian matrix eigenvalue problem. Simple, accurate Lanczos algorithms that require storing only a few vectors can only be used for symmetric matrices. Established eigensolvers for nonsymmetric problems require storing (and orthogonalizing) many vectors. For large matrices they require a lot of memory. We propose a low-storage eigensolver combining the block Sakurai-Sugiura method and the multi-shift quasi-minimal residual (QMR) linear solver. It requires storing only a few vectors. The method has many of the advantages of the well-known Cullum and Willoughby (CW) Lanczos approach for symmetric matrices.

papers.title: Human Body as a Model for Distributed Intelligence in Self-Driving Laboratories
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories are emerging as a transformative paradigm for accelerating scientific discovery through the integration of artificial intelligence, automation, and robotics. However, the intrinsic complexity and unpredictability of experimental environments challenge the feasibility of fully centralized laboratory control architectures. In this perspective, we propose the human body as a conceptual model for the design of distributed-intelligence self-driving laboratories. Inspired by the organization of the nervous system, we distinguish two complementary levels of control: a high-level cognitive layer responsible for reasoning, planning, and scientific decision-making, and a distributed adaptive layer responsible for local operational optimization, sensing, and real-time reaction to environmental changes. We discuss how such an architecture can enable laboratories to dynamically adapt to unpredictable events including precipitation, thermal runaway, viscosity changes, robotic handling failures, or evolving reaction conditions. Concrete implementation examples are presented, including adaptive instrumentation, distributed sensing, automated method selection, Bayesian optimization, multimodal robotic perception, and local orchestration frameworks currently under development at Swiss Cat+ at EPFL. We further propose a two-layer architecture composed of an interpretation and compilation layer coupled to a self-adaptive operational layer capable of autonomous execution and optimization. Finally, we discuss how this distributed-intelligence paradigm could provide the basis for future cloud-distributed laboratory infrastructures combining centralized generative AI systems with locally adaptive laboratory environments. Overall, this perspective argues that distributed adaptive intelligence, rather than purely centralized control, may constitute a critical foundation for the next generation of scalable, resilient, and autonomous scientific laboratories.

papers.title: Benchmark Maturity in MOF Adsorption Machine Learning: When Do Conclusions Become Scientifically Reliable?
papers.abstract: Benchmark tables increasingly determine how metal–organic framework (MOF) machinelearning studies justify descriptor choice, model complexity, and screening readiness, yet the reliability of those conclusions is rarely examined as a function of data volume. Here we recast MOF benchmarking as a maturity problem: when does a benchmark become large enough to support stable scientific conclusions rather than only competitive numerical scores? Using a fixed external test set, nested training subsets, and repeated retraining of 16 lightweight descriptor–model pipelines on a large ARC–MOF-derived tabular adsorption dataset, we quantify external-test error together with ranking reproducibility, pairwise probability of superiority, screening stability, and convergence of feature effects. For the main task, CO2 uptake at 0.15 bar, the best RMSE improves from 0.6347 at n = 500 to 0.4433 at full data. The more important transition is qualitative: a practically stable regime emerges near n ≈ 5 × 103–104, where method ranking, elite-candidate recovery, and feature-effect interpretation become substantially more reproducible even though absolute error continues to improve. Within this benchmark, geometry-plus-topology pipelines define the leading accuracy frontier, while topology-only models remain systematically weaker. These results show that strong benchmark accuracy alone is insufficient for defensible claims about descriptor value, model superiority, or screening readiness.

papers.title: Total Synthesis and Structural Revision of Rhabdobranin Reveals a Cryptic Gram-Negative Antibiotic
papers.abstract: Gram-negative bacteria present a major clinical challenge but also remain an underexplored source of antibacterial natural products. Resistance-guided genome mining of the entomopathogenic symbiont Xenorhabdus identified the rdb biosynthetic gene cluster, which encodes a putative prodrug antibiotic, pre-rhabdobranin. However, the inability to isolate the proposed active metabolite, rhabdobranin, has prevented direct functional evaluation. Here we report a convergent total synthesis of the proposed structure of pre-rhabdobranin B, which revealed a stereochemical misassignment at the N -terminal arginine residue. Synthesis of both rhabdobranin epimers showed that, although they are nearly indistinguishable by standard analytical methods, inversion at this single stereocenter has a pronounced effect on antibacterial activity. Biological evaluation of the revised rhabdobranin structure revealed potent antibacterial activity against Gram-negative pathogens, including WHO critical-priority carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. Biochemical and cellular studies further showed that the GNAT-family acetyltransferase RdbK N -acetylates rhabdobranin and attenuates its activity, establishing a secondary self-resistance mechanism. These findings validate resistance-gene-guided discovery in Gram-negative symbionts as a strategy for uncovering cryptic antibiotics and identify rhabdobranin as a promising scaffold for Gram-negative antibiotic development.

papers.title: Nanoscale Growth Mechanisms of Gypsum: Implications for Environmental Control of Crystal Habits
papers.abstract: Gypsum precipitation is a common process observed in diverse natural settings, offering valuable insights into (paleo)environmental conditions. It also holds significant industrial value, notably in wallboard production. However, its precipitation also poses severe challenges, for example, during water desalination. Despite numerous experimental and computational studies on gypsum since the late 19th century, the growth behavior and crystal habit remain poorly understood. In this work, we studied the nanoscale growth mechanisms controlling the formation of gypsum crystals from supersaturated solutions. We developed a method for obtaining oriented samples of natural idiomorphic gypsum crystals, enabling atomic force microscopy (AFM) imaging and microtopography characterization of all facets. Using this novel approach we (re-)examined the extensively studied {010} form, and, for the first time, the {120}, {-111}, and {011} forms. Remarkably, each form is dominated by a specific growth behavior, including cluster-mediated growth for {010}, stepped face growth for {120}, 2D nucleation and spiral growth for the {-111} form, and rough growth for {011}. These experimental findings differ from theoretical predictions, where all four forms are considered flat faces (F faces). We further demonstrate that the interplay between growth mechanisms of different forms, and the control that external factors exert on these, are the two key factors that dictate the crystal habit. Overall, this study establishes a framework for linking gypsum crystal morphology to the prevailing environmental conditions during growth. This understanding is critical not only for comprehending gypsum deposit formation in the geological record but also for the processing of advanced geomaterials and more effective anti-scaling strategies.

papers.title: “Store-and-Release” Strategy Enables Nickel-Catalyzed Deaminative Migratory Arylation of Aliphatic Amines
papers.abstract: While migratory functionalization reactions provide a powerful means to navigate broader chemical space, their application to aliphatic amines remains particularly elusive. Herein, we describe the nickel-catalyzed migratory arylation of aliphatic amines using Katritzky salts enabled by a “store-and-release” strategy. This strategy leverages dihydropyridines, which are traditionally viewed as chemical dead-ends under reductive cross-coupling conditions, as latent reservoirs to store and release translocated alkyl radicals, thereby decoupling the chain-walking event from the cross-coupling cycle. The developed protocol enables migratory functionalization of Katritzky salts derived from a wide range of primary amines, and a variety of aryl and heteroaryl bromides. The reaction exhibits broad functional group tolerance, accommodating alkenes, polar functionalities, and substrates derived from pharmaceutically relevant compounds. This methodology enables expanded small-molecule library synthesis through regiodivergent deaminative arylations. Preliminary mechanistic studies support the “store-and-release” design principle, rendering it as a platform that can be applied for other migratory functionalization reactions.

papers.title: Docking-Informed and Multi-Objective Generative AI for Ligand Optimization: Comparison with Combinatorial Design.
papers.abstract: The discovery and optimization of small molecules across multiple physicochemical and biological objectives remain a major challenge in drug development. Here, we present a comparative analysis of two complementary generative in silico design strategies using methylbiocin (MBC), an inhibitor of the human CMG helicase, as a case study. The CMG helicase is the primary DNA-replicative helicase and an emerging therapeutic vulnerability in recalcitrant cancers driven by mutant K/H-Ras. In the first approach, we construct a scaffold-focused combinatorial library using commercially available Enamine building blocks to systematically redesign the tail region of MBC. In parallel, we apply generative AI reinforcement learning (RL) within the continuous latent space of a variational autoencoder to perform multi-objective molecular optimization. We evaluate both strategies based on their ability to improve key medicinal chemistry properties, including lipophilicity, synthetic accessibility, molecular weight and size, structural similarity, and predicted docking score. Pareto front analysis reveals distinct optimization behaviors and trade-offs. The RL-based approach more effectively identifies molecules with favorable balances between reduced lipophilicity and improved synthetic accessibility but shows limitations when docking scores are incorporated directly as noisy optimization objectives. In contrast, the combinatorial strategy is more effective at recovering high-affinity candidates while maintaining acceptable physicochemical profiles. Together, these results highlight the complementary strengths of rule-based combinatorial expansion and latent-space RL and provide practical guidance for applying generative AI to multi-objective medicinal chemistry optimization against challenging targets such as the CMG helicase.

papers.title: MetalPicker – a metallomics software tool for the discovery of metal complexes
papers.abstract: Organic ligands found in nature can combine with a variety of metals such as Fe, Ni, Cu, Zn, Pb, Hg and exhibit distinctive isotopologue fingerprints. These fingerprints can be experimentally targeted to detect and identify known and unknown organic metal complexes as well as the associated chelating ligands in diverse sample matrices using liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS). Here, we introduce MetalPicker, a new software program that finds all signal characteristics linked to metal complexes in LC-HRMS data. MetalPicker is a graphical user interface desktop software application which can determine the identity of metal complexes using accurate mass isotopologue data and create extracted ion chromatogram plots in the non-targeted analysis mode. In addition, MetalPicker also allows for the targeted extraction of ion chromatograms which can be further employed for quantitative analysis via peak area integration. The tool’s inputs include an mzML file, the charge of the metal complexes, and the complex’s central metal atom and total number of carbon atoms in the complex. Both targeted and non-targeted modes can be used independently or in conjunction. With its intuitive user interfaces, MetalPicker offers a comprehensive suite of tools for both targeted and non-targeted metallomics studies.

papers.title: Spirofluorene-rigidified indolocarbazole dual-boron multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitters for ultra-narrowband high-efficiency electroluminescence
papers.abstract: Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters are research focuses for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) targeting ultra-highdefinition displays. Expanding the multi-resonance plane through multi-boron structures enables emission color tuning and spectral narrowing, which rigid indolocarbazole moieties could further reinforce. However, excessive expansion of conjugated aromatic planes leads to severe aggregation-caused quenching. Herein, we combined the spirofluorene-based multi-resonance skeleton with indolocarbazoles as the bridging unit to construct a double-boron architecture, aiming to utilize the threedimensional spatial rigidity of spirofluorene while suppressing intermolecular interactions in aggregated states. Three isomeric emitters were thereby obtained, with emission maxima at 524–565 nm. All emitters exhibit full widths at half-maximum below 20 nm, with the narrowest being 17 nm, and these emitters maintain narrow-band emission even at a high doping concentration of 6 wt%, where film spectral broadening is limited to within 3 nm. OLEDs based on these emitters display narrow bandwidths of 22–26 nm, a highest maximum EQE of 36.2%, and low efficiency roll-off, corresponding to a high EQE of up to 30.2% even under ultra-high luminance of 5×104 cd m-2. This work confirms the feasibility of spirofluorene-modified multi-boron largeplane multi-resonance emitters and provides a reliable molecular design strategy for narrowband OLEDs.

papers.title: High-Frequency and -Field Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Studies of Yellow/Orange/Red Pigments based on Fe3+ in Trigonal Bipyramidal Coordination
papers.abstract: The material YInO3 is amenable to doping of its trigonal bipyramidal (TBP) In3+ site by a wide range of metal ions. Among these are Mn3+ (S = 2) and Fe3+ (S = 5/2). The former, YIn1-xMnxO3, was previously the subject of an earlier investigation by high-frequency and -field electron paramagnetic resonance (HFEPR) spectroscopy. HFEPR is here applied to YIn1−xFexO3 (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.3). This material exhibits a strong HFEPR response and spectra that can be readily analyzed using an S = 5/2 spin Hamiltonian with only second order zero-field splitting (zfs) terms: D = −1.095 cm–1, E = 0. The spectral appearance is strongly dependent on both temperature and iron doping level, even for these In-rich samples. The zfs is semi-quantitatively analyzed using a ligand-field theory (LFT) model, which suggests that the small magnitude, negative D value arises from spin-orbit coupling (SOC) of the 6A1′ (in D3h idealized point group symmetry) ground state primarily with the lowest lying 4E″ excited state.

papers.title: FlowPilot: A Multi-Agent AI System for Continuous Flow Chemistry Process Design
papers.abstract: Designing a continuous flow process demands coordinated reasoning across fluid dynamics, heat and mass transfer, materials compatibility, and safety, a multi-domain problem exceeding the reliable scope of a single-shot large language model (LLM). We present FlowPilot, to our knowledge the first multi-agent AI pipeline for sustainable continuous flow process design. LLM agents interpret chemistry and mechanism, while a nine-step deterministic calculator and approximately 2,500 handbook-derived design rules perform all quantitative computation. A seven-agent Council deliberates over candidate designs under bounded domain authority, selecting a final design via a weighted Process Value Score quantifying improvement over batch. Benchmarking across a 4×4 matrix of commercial and local LLM endpoints shows that the council contributes measurable design quality beyond model capability alone. We validate FlowPilot on an isoxazole cycloaddition benchmark and two end-to-end case studies: a photoredox Giese addition with aerobic oxidation and a thermal α-bromination with inline quench.

papers.title: Statistical Convergence and Uncertainty in Electrocatalytic Benchmarking of Ir and Ru Oxygen Evolution Catalysts
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts are often benchmarked using a small number of measurements, with performance differences commonly assessed based on calculated mean activity and standard deviation (SD). However, dispersion metrics alone do not quantify the uncertainty of the estimated mean, and therefore, cannot support statistically robust comparisons between catalyst systems. In this work, we aim to elucidate the convergence of statistical variables with the specific goal of estimating the sample size required to achieve a certain level of significance. We begin by demonstrating a medium-throughput workflow combining parallel hydrothermal synthesis with multi-working-electrode (MWE) screening to generate more than sixty independent measurements of two OER catalysts, i.e., IrOx and RuOx nanoparticles supported on antimony-doped tin oxide (ATO). The resulting datasets reveal markedly different statistical behaviors between the two catalysts. IrOx/ATO exhibits narrow distributions, near-normal profiles, and consistent activity across synthesis batches. In contrast, RuOx/ATO shows broader dispersion, deviations from normality, and statistically significant batch-to-batch differences that are not adequately captured by the calculated SD alone, largely due to the presence of outliers. Using simulated normal-distributed datasets with and without outliers, we evaluate statistical variables as a function of sample size and compare simulations with the experimentally optained data set. The results show that approximately seven measurements are required to obtain a reliable estimation of the underlying activity data. Our findings establish a statistically rigorous framework for electrocatalytic benchmarking and provide practical guidance for sample-size selection and data reporting in acidic OER studies.

papers.title: Group 13 Metals as X-type Ligands for Transition Metals
papers.abstract: The use of group 13 metalloligands (M = Al, Ga, In) in transition metal chemistry has proliferated in the last two decades as advances in their synthesis has democratised access to this class of compounds. These group 13 elements tend to be more electropositive than transition metal counterparts which result in highly polarised bonds, and strong σ-donation character. As a result, a body of work within the literature suggests that metalloligands of group 13 offer unique electronic environments at transition metals that can engender novel or enhanced reactivity at transition-metal sites. In addition to this, group 13 element centres offer a Lewis acidic coordination site for substrates allowing for cooperative and synergic effects to enable challenging bond activation reactions. This article will explore the synthesis, reactivity, and structure of Group 13 X-type metalloligands (Al, Ga, In), defined by the covalent bond classification method pioneered by Green. This article will focus on results described between 2000-2025. The article is structured according to transition metal group and loosely ordered examples of Al, Ga, and In sequentially except in circumstances for which a series is described. Similarly, 3d transition metals are described first, followed by heavier 4d and 5d.

papers.title: Mechanistic New Insights into Photodegradation of Trityl Radicals
papers.abstract: ：In this study, the chlorine-free trityl radicals MesDPM-H (D0) and deuterated MesDPM-D were synthesized and investigated their luminescence and excited-state reactivity. Their excited-state (D1) lifetimes were 3–4 times longer than that of TTM, with photoluminescence quantum yields improved by ~65%. Time-resolved transient absorption measurements revealed that D1 un-dergoes both intramolecular radical cyclization and intermolecular reactions with the ground state D0. Furthermore, the cyclized radical C showed second-order decay and reacted intermolecularly with D0 at concentrations above ~10 mM.

papers.title: DNA Reactor Assay Assisted Study of Affinity Labelling: Aptamer Directed Selective and Diversified Conjugation of Antibody
AI-Assisted Design of Charge Transfer Excitation and Experimental Validation of Aluminum(III) Complexes for Efficient Red-to-Near-Infrared Emission
papers.abstract: The rational design of coordination complexes with precisely controlled excited-state dynamics remains a major challenge in the discovery of functional materials, particularly in multidimensional chemical spaces. In this context, aluminum complexes are particularly attractive because of their earth abundance, low toxicity, and unique ability to form structurally robust, luminescent helicates with versatile photophysical properties. Here, we report an AI-assisted computational–experimental strategy for metal complexes to design aluminum(III) dinuclear helicates exhibiting efficient long-wavelength emission. By integrating density functional theory calculations with asynchronous Bayesian optimization, we systematically modulated ligand electron density, conjugation length, and symmetry to control inter- 2 and intraligand charge–transfer processes. On the basis of the optimized methods, we synthesized five helicates, which displayed deep-red emission with quantum yields of up to 0.96 (λmax = 603 nm) and broadband emission extending into the near-infrared region (λmax = 671 nm), with considerable spectral weight extending to approximately 800 nm, remarkably properties in aluminum complexes. Transient absorption spectroscopy revealed that suppression of interligand charge transfer minimizes nonradiative decay and enables high quantum yields. The large apparent Stokes shifts arise from the combined effects of intraligand charge transfer and pronounced excited-state structural relaxation, which work together to stabilize the emissive state. In addition, the helicates further exhibit circularly polarized luminescence after optical resolution. These findings establish a scalable and generalizable AI-assisted strategy for designing sustainable coordination luminophores beyond purely organic systems.

papers.title: Scalable synthesis of nonthmicin reveals dual activity against Clostridioides difficile
papers.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a severe diarrhoeal disease with substantial mortality, frequent recurrence, and limited treatment options. Here we describe a scalable total synthesis of ecteinamycin, a polyether ionophore with anti-C. difficile activity, and its congener nonthmicin. Key steps include two electrochemical decarboxylative alkenylations, an enzyme-catalyzed anti-Baldwin cyclization, and a redox-economic asymmetric C–C bond formation. This synthesis enabled systematic biological evaluation. Nonthmicin showed potent and selective suppression of C. difficile, protected mammalian cells from toxin B (TcdB)-induced cytopathology, and displayed therapeutic efficacy in a mouse model of CDI. Structure-function studies identified the exo-methylene-bearing tetronic acid motif as important for anti-C. difficile potency. These findings challenge the prevailing view of polyether ionophores as broad-spectrum membrane-active agents and suggest new therapeutic possibilities for CDI.

papers.title: Coverage-Dependent Interfacial Effects Govern Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Nitrite on Silver
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction is a key reaction in sustainable nitrogen cycling and water remediation, yet the mechanistic interpretation of its voltammetric response remains poorly understood. On silver electrodes, cyclic voltammograms often display multiple cathodic features assigned to different reaction steps or adsorbed intermediates, although a consistent mechanistic 2 interpretation remains elusive. Here, we combine cyclic voltammetry analysis with in-situ product detection using scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM) to investigate nitrate-to-nitrite electroreduction on silver. We show that the cathodic response changes from a single peak to two distinct features with increasing nitrate concentration. Analysis of concentration, scan rate, and pH dependencies suggests that these features are consistent with distinct interfacial regimes promoted by an increasing nitrate availability. SECM enables the direct correlation of each voltammetric feature with local nitrite formation, demonstrating that all observed peaks originate from the nitrate-to-nitrite reduction step under different interfacial conditions. These findings show that adsorbate coverage and interfacial environment strongly influence the voltammetric response of nitrate reduction on silver, providing a framework for interpreting complex electrocatalytic behaviour in this system.

papers.title: Stereodivergent Csp3–Csp3 Bond Construction via Lewis base/Iridium Cooperative Catalysis: A Modular Synthesis of Tertiary Fluoride-containing Stereodiads.
papers.abstract: The synthesis of tertiary fluoride-containing stereogenic centers remains a significant challenge. This is challenge is amplified when such units are embedded within vicinal stereocenters arrays, where both absolute and relative stereochemistry must be controlled. Here we disclose a stereodivergent Lewis base–iridium cooperative catalysis method that unites a-fluorinated C1-ammonium enolate and p(allyl)Ir intermediates to construct tertiary fluoride-containing stereodiads. Each catalyst is independently responsible for the configurational outcome of each stereocenter comprising the stereodiad during Csp3–Csp3 bond construction. Noteworthy is the conversion of easily prepared racemic a-fluoro esters to single a-fluoro C1-ammonium enolates via Lewis base catalysis.

papers.title: Mimicking natural ammonification from plasma-activated water using single-atom anchored Ru-NRCOFs as a selective electrocatalyst for Nitrogen reduction
papers.abstract: Sustainable energy storage and conversion technologies are being developed, as green energy technologies and decarbonization continue to advance rapidly. Conventional battery systems are limited in their capacity to self-charge and store energy, while hydrogen, ammonia, or ethanol are more environmentally friendly options. However, safety and economic issues arise from the high flammability and handling costs of hydrogen storage. Ammonia, despite its name, is a carbon-free hydrogen carrier composed of both nitrogen and hydrogen that has high energy density, chemical stability, and ease of liquefaction, making it superior and the most critical fuel in the next generation of listed fuel resources. The Haber-Bosch process that currently adapted for industrial production, is an energy-intensive and contribute 2 % of the global greenhouse gas emissions. Alternatively, green electrochemical ammonia production is a much more robust, eco-friendly and economical. We have used plasma-activated water as a precursor of nitrogen, such as nitrate (NO3-) and nitrite (NO2-), which have higher solubility than N2 and have lower bond dissociation energies. Here we have demonstrated Ruthenium-based covalent organic framework (Ru–NRCOF) catalyst that is efficient and selective for electrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia in alkaline media. We have successfully achieved Faradaic efficiency of 95.5% with ammonia yield rate of 936 mg h-1 mg-1cat at -1.0 V vs. RHE, along with very good operational stability. This work describes the potential of framework-engineered Ru catalysts for sustainable ammonia synthesis, advancing the development of green fuels and renewable energy storage technologies.

papers.title: Implementation of the Gaussian electronic structure program into QCArchive, an open-source ecosystem for large-scale quantum chemistry computations
papers.abstract: We present how to implement any quantum chemistry software packages in the Quantum Chemistry Archive (QCArchive) 1,2 platform in general and in particular, how to do it for Gaussian 3 , a widely used ab initio quantum chemistry software package. QCArchive is an open-source Python-based platform which is an umbrella name to accumulate and serve high-volume quantum chemical calculations for the chemistry community. QCArchive provides an ecosystem to submit many chemistry computations at the same time, and gives tools to control and manage them in a unified environment. The primacy of QCArchive is that it enables users to use many quantum chemistry (QC) programs, including CFOUR, GAMESS(US) 4 , NWChem 5 , Turbomole 6 , Molpro 7 , MOPAC, OpenMM, Psi4 8 , Q-CHEM 9 , RDKit, TorchANI, xTB, and Gaussian which the last case is written and implemented and is explained in this work. By utilizing these QC programs and the environment of QCArchive, it is much easier and efficient to run desired computations in a large scale on atomic/molecular systems in a short time to obtain atomic/molecular properties of interest such as energy, charge, dipole moments, frequency, or any other computational quantities.

papers.title: Efficient and Scalable Expansion of Property Limits via Novelty-Guided Exploration
papers.abstract: Finding diverse and high-quality candidates in vast design spaces remains an important challenge in scientific research, including molecular design and material discovery. A recent line of work treats observed properties as samples from an unknown distribution and selects candidates that promote more uniform coverage of the property space using Stein discrepancy as the metric. However, these methods do not explicitly account for the information gain of newly acquired data, which can limit exploration of novel regions. In addition, they are not designed for efficient batch selection and may suffer performance degradation when applied in batch settings. Moreover, they incur substantial computational cost due to both large per-iteration overhead and increasing cost as the number of observations grows. To address these limitations, we incorporate predictive 1 uncertainty into the objective function and introduce diversity-aware batch selection strategies to promote informative and diverse candidates. In addition, we propose a sampled Stein novelty estimator and efficient tensor calculations that significantly reduce computational overhead. Performance and runtime evaluations on molecular and materials datasets show that our method enables scalable and sample-efficient expansion of property-space coverage.

papers.title: Tetramethylsilane Coordination to Neutral, Heavier Alkaline Earth Metal Complexes
papers.abstract: The extremely bulky xanthene bridged diamido-barium complex, [(EtNONTCHP)Ba(6toluene)] 1-Ba (EtNONTCHP = 4,5-bis{(TCHP)NH}-2,7-diethyl-9,9-dimethyl-xanthene, TCHP = 2,4,6-tricyclohexylphenyl) has been prepared and shown to exist as a weakly associated polymer in the solid-state. While this was shown to be unreactive towards tetramethylsilane (TMS), its lighter analogues [(EtNONTCHP)M(6-toluene)] 1-M (M = Ca and Sr), react with TMS to give the 1:1 complexes [(EtNONTCHP)M(6-toluene)(2-H,H-TMS)] 2-M (M = Ca or Sr), which represent the first examples of TMS complexes of these metals. Crystallographic characterization indicates that the TMS ligands in these species ligate their metal centers in a 2-H,H-mode. The results of

papers.title: High-throughput multireference calculations of magnetic properties of lanthanide complexes
papers.abstract: Molecular magnets based on lanthanides are promising candidates for quantum information technologies. However, progress toward practical applications is limited by the small number of compounds with useful magnetic properties. Computational screening could accelerate discovery, but accurate prediction of lanthanide electronic and magnetic properties requires multireference electronic structure methods, which remain difficult to perform at scale. Additionally, the calculation of magnetic properties with perturbative approaches following the multireference calculations is sensitive to the number of states included in the spin–orbit treatment, defined as model space, which generally must be selected manually. Here, we develop an automated workflow for multireference calculations of monolanthanide complexes based on complete active space wave functions, followed by state-interaction spin–orbit coupling. The protocol iteratively selects the model space using an energy-based criterion while preserving near-degenerate manifolds. Benchmark calculations on lanthanide hexachlorides show that the approach reproduces experimental ligand-field splittings with mean absolute errors of 100-200 cm −1 across the lanthanide series. We further analyze the effect of model-space size on magnetic anisotropy and g-tensors in representative Dy and Er single-ion magnets.

papers.title: Exchange- versus anisotropy-driven magnetism in phenoxido-bridged Ni(II) and Co(II) dimers
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT Two phenoxido-bridged dinuclear Ni(II) and Co(II) complexes, [M2(SAIDPPO)2(NO3)2] (M = Ni, Co), have been synthesized using a new Schiff base phosphine oxide ligand (SAIDPPO–). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed closely related Ni2O2 and Co2O2 cores with distinct magnetostructural features. Magnetic studies showed that the Ni(II) complex (1) exhibits ferromagnetic coupling (J = +9.75 cm-1) associated with a near-orthogonal Ni–O–Ni angle (95.50°) and pronounced easy-axis anisotropy (D = −19.44 cm-1). In contrast, the Co(II) analog (2) displays weak antiferromagnetic coupling (J ≈ −4.32 cm-1) combined with significant easy-axis anisotropy (D = −28.45 cm-1) arising from strong spin-orbit coupling. The comparison of the Ni2O2 and Co2O2 cores highlights how subtle structural variations, particularly the M–O–M angle, govern the balance between exchange interactions and magnetic anisotropy.

papers.title: Crystalline Environment Enhances Intersystem Crossing in Donor-Acceptor Co-Crystals Despite Structural Rigidity
Vapor Phase Infiltration Towards the In Situ Growth of ZIF-8 Within Polymers
papers.abstract: Vapor phase infiltration (VPI) of metal-organic reactants has emerged as a technique for postsynthetically introducing metal oxides into polymers, forming composite hybrid organic-inorganic materials. VPI of organic molecules, though seldom explored, could serve as a means for introducing other materials into polymers, such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), which could be used in the solvent-free synthesis of mixed matrix membranes (MMMs). In this work, we aim to demonstrate successful VPI of ZIF-8 into acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS), as a demonstration of MOF infiltration into polymers. After exposing ABS to zinc oxide VPI and vapor exposure to 2-methylimidazole (2-HmIM), the characteristic peaks for ZIF-8 were observed via XRD. To confirm reactant infiltration, ToF-SIMS depth profiling was used to detect ions corresponding to zinc, 2-HmIM, and their reaction product. To eliminate contributions from ZIF-8 crystals formed on the polymer surface, infiltrated polymers were etched in water to remove surface ZIF-8. XRD measurements show that crystalline ZIF-8 is still present after etching with water suggesting that ZIF-8 crystals are present within the subsurface of the polymer. This work provides a proof-of-concept for MOF infiltration and growth using only vapor-phase methods.

papers.title: Complementary Morphology and Chemical Mapping of Organic Semiconductor Nanoparticles by STXM and Soft X-ray Ptychography
papers.abstract: Resolving the nanoscale morphology of donor-acceptor heterojunction systems remains a challenge for conventional characterization techniques which often lack either chemical sensitivity or sufficient spatial resolution. Here we present the characterization of organic semiconducting nanoparticles by combining scanning transmission X-ray microscopy (STXM) and soft X-ray ptychography (SXP). STXM provides chemically specific composition maps while SXP provides high resolution amplitude and phase images. This approach when applied to P3HT/PC61BM and PTQ10/ITIC-4F nanoparticles, synthesized by different fabrication routes, namely miniemulsion and nanoprecipitation, show radially segregated core-shell morphology and intermixed morphology. These results establish STXM and SXP as complementary techniques for morphological study especially in radiation-sensitive organic semiconductor nanoparticles.

papers.title: Transport-Modulated SECCM Enables Intrinsic HER Kinetics and Structure-Activity Mapping on Pt
papers.abstract: Platinum is the benchmark catalyst for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media, yet its intrinsic activity remains difficult to quantify due to extremely fast kinetics. Conventional methods for measuring the intrinsic kinetics of HER are often limited by mass transport, masking facet-dependent effects. Here, we introduce transport-modulated scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (TM-SECCM), a technique that employs a dual-channel nanopipette with an applied inter-channel bias to induce controlled electromigration and electroosmotic flow. This nanofluidic control increases the mass-transport coefficient to ~30 cm/s, enabling direct determination of exchange current densities (j0) via spatially resolved Koutecký-Levich & Tafel analyses. Local j0 values up to ~1 A/cm2 were measured for HER on Pt, among the highest values reported to date. Correlating the local kinetics with corresponding grain orientations obtained via co-localized electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) reveals facet-dependent HER kinetics, and a positive correlation between activity and the density of the kink and step atoms, underscoring the role of these undercoordinated sites. These results establish a framework for quantifying intrinsic electrocatalytic activity in kinetically fast reacting electrocatalytic systems and the rational design of high-performance electrocatalysts.

papers.title: HiMac: High-Throughput Initialization of Multidentate Adsorption Configurations for Geometry Relaxation and Transition-State Searches
papers.abstract: High-throughput computation is essential for the rational design of heterogeneous catalysts, and the quality of initial adsorption configurations directly determines the efficiency and success rate of subsequent geometry optimization. Existing heuristic methods are constrained by rigid-body approximations, which makes them difficult to handle complex multidentate adsorption, and the low-precision force-field correction schemes they rely on lack generality. To address this issue, this work proposes a general algorithm, High-Throughput Initialization of Multidentate Adsorption Configurations (HiMac). The algorithm reformulates configuration generation as a multi-objective optimization problem. It employs forward kinematics to model molecular flexibility and combines it with a loss function based on parent molecule similarity, thereby unifying site selection with pose adjustment. A statistical learning module is further integrated to prioritize the exploration of chemically favorable sites and reduce computational cost. Experiments show that HiMac generates high quality initial configurations for geometry relaxation and transition-state searches, applies to arbitrary adsorbate-surface systems, and provides a general and efficient method to accelerate the rational design of heterogeneous catalysts.

papers.title: Identification of Boronic Acid-based Amidation Catalysts Using Artificial Intelligence – A ChatGPT-guided Optimization Strategy
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a powerful tool for catalyst optimization in organic synthesis. Yet, applications are often restricted by the need for large datasets, programming expertise, and specialized knowledge in model development. Boronic acidcatalyzed amidation reactions represent an attractive target for AI-guided optimization because of their synthetic relevance, detailed mechanistic understanding, and the need for improved catalysts for amidations. Here, an AI-guided workflow for catalyst optimization in boronic acidcatalyzed amidation reactions was established using the large-language model ChatGPT for code generation and workflow development. A dataset was generated by high-throughput screening of 459 arylboronic acids and combined with DFT-derived steric and electronic descriptors of the catalysts for model training. The model enabled the identification of the unprecedented catalyst FIBA with higher activity than the benchmark catalyst MIBA. In addition, detailed data analysis of the highly active but poorly predicted diboronic acid catalyst DBA led to the identification of a distinct activation mode involving higher-order boronate aggregates that activate and preorganize the amine nucleophile. Thus, improved catalyst performance and new mechanistic insight were obtained through an AI-guided workflow.

papers.title: Information-Geometric Conditioning of Atomistic Datasets for Efficient Learning
papers.abstract: Atomic structures are not merely assemblies of local chemical environments, but collective objects defined by their compositional proportions. Yet this intrinsic character has long been overlooked in favor of the natural Euclidean geometry applied to continuous feature spaces. Because the distribution of these environments is inherently a nonnegative and normalized compositional object, its informational identity is better represented as a point on a statistical manifold. Here, we introduce a new framework, Covering Histogram-based atomic Environments through Sampling on Statistical manifolds (CHESS), which refines datasets by representing each frame as a statistical state using histograms of embeddings of local atomic environments. Maximizing diversity through distance-based sampling on this representation explicitly removes geometrically redundant configurations and yields local tangent subspaces with nearly twofold larger effective rank than random sampling. This more balanced excitation of gradient directions improves conditioning and accelerates the convergence of derivative-sensitive observables governed by local energy gradients.

papers.title: The Effect of Redox Cycling on the Fate of Tetrahedral Iron in Smectites
papers.abstract: Redox reactions involving Fe-bearing clay minerals play a significant role in the cycling of elements such as carbon, and for the mobility of inorganic and organic contaminants in subsurface environments. The layered alumo-silicate structure of clay minerals can accommodate up to 30 wt% Fe in both octahedral and tetrahedral coordination. Tetrahedral Fe is naturally present in Fe-rich clay minerals like nontronite, yet the behavior and fate of tetrahedral Fe during redox reactions remains poorly constrained. Here, we synthesized a series of nontronites with 0 to 27% of the total Fe present as tetrahedral Fe(III) that we subjected to chemical reduction, re-oxidation, and re-reduction with dithionite and hydrogen peroxide, respectively. We used FT-IR and Mössbauer spectroscopies, SEM-EDS, HRTEM and XRD to monitor changes in crystal chemistry and the fate of tetrahedral Fe during the redox manipulation. Reduction of all nontronites resulted in almost all structural Fe becoming reduced (77-100% Fe(II)/Fe total ), including a portion of the initially present tetrahedral Fe, and re-oxidation restored all Fe to its ferric form. The initial 2:1 smectite structure was conserved throughout all redox manipulations, with the typical structural changes during Fe reduction, mainly trioctahedral domain formation and structural OH-group loss, being largely reverted by re-oxidation. However, the initial reduction led to significant loss of tetrahedral Fe from the nontronite structure, and the tetrahedral Fe content in all nontronites converged to the same value of ~0.2 per half formula unit. The concomitant decrease in particle size and number of stacked layers in a significant portion of each nontronite led to the presence of two distinct populations of particles and suggests partial reductive dissolution as a plausible mechanism for tetrahedral Fe release. While some of the Fe was present in the aqueous phase, increased interlayer distances in reduced and re-oxidized nontronites implies that 48-63% of the released Fe became intercalated, presumably in the form of hydroxylated pillars. Overall, highly similar structures, crystal chemistry, and tetrahedral Fe content resulted for all nontronites irrespective of their initial tetrahedral Fe content and remained stable in subsequent redox manipulations, indicating the reversible reduction and re-oxidation of both octahedral and tetrahedral Fe in the initially altered clay mineral structure. Our results provide compelling evidence for why naturally occurring clay minerals contain only low amounts of tetrahedral Fe and that both octahedral and tetrahedral Fe in clay minerals may contribute to electron transfer reactions in natural environments.

papers.title: Non-mean Field Approaches for Surface Catalysis: Analytical Description of Reaction Kinetics with Adsorbate-Adsorbate Interactions
Time-resolved Extreme Ultraviolet Photoelectron Spectroscopy of 4-Bromophenolate Anions in a Liquid Jet
papers.abstract: The dynamics of photo-excited 4-bromophenolate anions in aqueous solution are investigated using femtosecond extreme ultraviolet (XUV) time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (TRPES) in a liquid flat jet. Excitation to the first singlet S 1 (1 1 ππ * ) excited state at 290 nm yields lifetimes of ~160 fs and 1.1 ps that are attributed to the timescale for the transition from the initially excited S 1 state to the optically-dark 1 πσ * state and the subsequent decay of the 1 πσ * state, respectively. Excitation at 240 nm to the second singlet excited state (S 2 , 2 1 ππ * ) reveals an additional ultrafast component assigned to S 2 ®S 1 decay with a lifetime of 60 fs. Subsequent decay components show lifetimes of 130 fs and 1.4 ps, corresponding to the transition from S 1 to the 1 πσ * state and its subsequent decay. These dynamics differ from the phenolate anion, which undergoes S 1 ®S 0 internal conversion and hydrated electron formation within ~20 ps upon S 1 excitation. Instead, photoexcited 4-bromophenolate decays through the 1 πσ * state, which is repulsive along the C-Br bond length and correlates to ·C 6 H 4 O· (biradical fragment) + Brˉ. Quantum chemical calculations suggest that the S 1 - 1 πσ * state crossing involves a small potential energy barrier that promotes a facile non-adiabatic transition. This study highlights the competing dynamics between photo-oxidation and non-adiabatic relaxation within the framework of anions in aqueous solution.

papers.title: Relations between H-C and M-C bond strengths: influence of the organic ligand and the metal
papers.abstract: This review describes the thermodynamics of C–H bond activation in various hydrocarbons, especially (poly)fluorinated benzenes, by transition metal complexes, through experiments and computational studies, with a focus on the latter. Experimental metal-carbon bond dissociation enthalpies (BDEs), determined relative to an internal reference, were used to establish the relationship between H–C and M–C BDEs. In parallel, bond dissociation enthalpies or energies were computed with DFT methods. For a given metal complex and a set of sufficiently similar organic substrates a linear correlation with a characteristic slope R M-C/H-C was obtained. Since far more H-C BDEs are known than M-C BDEs, these correlations provide a powerful predictive tool. Both experimental and computational studies indicate that the slope is always greater than 1 and quantitatively agree on its value when comparison could be made, suggesting a systematic thermodynamic preference for cleaving stronger hydrogen-carbon bonds. The R M-C/H-C value is particularly high for (poly)fluorobenzenes, with the greatest increase in M–C BDE occurring when fluorine atoms are ortho to the M–C bond, as found by experiments. Values of R M-C/H-C almost up to 3 have been reported. The polarity of the M–C bond, greater than that of the H–C bond, is suggested to be the cause of the high value of R M-C/H-C and the associated observed high selectivity in C–H bond activation. Recent experimental studies suggested that Co is more selective than Rh and Ir for C–H bond activation in (poly)fluorobenzenes. A computational study of the thermodynamics of C–H activation in C 6 F n H 6-n (n = 0, 5) by CpM(CO) (M = Co, Rh, Ir) confirms that R M-C/H-C is highest for Co and shows again a relation between R M-C/H-C and the polarity of the M–C bond. Additionally, the R M-C/H-C value is shown to be inversely related to the strength of the M–C bond since the Co–C BDE is the weakest for group 9 transition metals. Further studies are needed to confirm the generality of the finding that 3d transition metal complexes could be more selective in C–H activation than their heavier congeners. Correlations are also found between M–X and H–X (X = O, N) BDEs with slopes varying from 0.9 to 1.4. The ranking of M-X BDEs (M–C < M–N < M–O) is discussed as well as the magnitudes of the correlation slopes that is generally higher for aromatic substituents. Although this review is centred on reactions with thermodynamically controlled product distributions, some reactions are recognised in which kinetically controlled products follow thermodynamics. For all systems, computations appear to provide accurate information and can replace experiments if needed. Prediction of relative bond strengths in many organometallic species from knowledge of bond strengths for cognate organic molecules can be achieved.

papers.title: Breaking Symmetry in Nanoparticle Superlattices via Spontaneous Valency
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle superlattices enable programmable material structure through ligand-mediated interactions, but attractive ligand interactions typically limit assembly to densely packed lattices that maximize nearest neighbor bonding. Intentionally programmed directional bonding and valency are therefore typically assumed to require particle-level anisotropy in shape or surface patterning. Using assemblies of flexible isotropic nanoparticles, we show here that valency need not be encoded by particle geometry, but can instead emerge spontaneously during assembly. When ligand coronas are sufficiently deformable, ligands reorganize to align along interparticle interfaces, generating an effective valency. Using a combination of experiment and simulation, we show that increasing ligand deformability lowers lattice coordination numbers, and are able to establish design principles for assembling isotropic building blocks into lattices with lower coordination, packing density, and symmetry than would be predicted from hard-sphere packing. The work presented here therefore establishes ligand flexibility as a design parameter for programming coordination in nanoparticle assembly.

papers.title: Photoswitchable peptides for light-controlled recognition of G-quadruplex DNA
papers.abstract: Light-responsive ligands enable regulation of biomolecular recognition with spatiotemporal precision. Here, we report two arylazopyrazole-peptide conjugates that reversibly recognize G-quadruplex (G4) DNA in different isomerization states. Both peptide conjugates preferentially bind to DNA G4s over a range of RNA G4s and non-G4 nucleic acid targets. Despite broadly similar DNA G4 affinities in the E -state, divergent photoregulation behaviours are observed upon E → Z photoisomerisation with 365 nm light. The short cationic peptide KTRK undergoes near-binary dissociation in the Z -state, whereas the longer aromatic GKKRGFAF peptide retains binding capacity, although with markedly weaker affinity in the Z -state. Through molecular modelling studies, we show that these distinct binding modulations depend on the native binding capacity of the peptide. When association is driven by photoswitch-G4 interactions, binding can be turned on/off with light; when the peptide can also bind, affinity can be retained upon irradiation. Upon back-isomerisation with 530 nm light, the original binding profiles are restored in both cases, with no observed photofatigue over 10 cycles, establishing photoswitchable peptides as a platform for selective and reversible recognition of G4 structures in DNA.

papers.title: Fine-Tuned Machine Learning Models for the Discovery of Dye Nanoparticles with Enhanced Lung Delivery
papers.abstract: Drug delivery using self-assembling drug-excipient nanoparticles offers a scalable strategy to improve the solubility, bioavailability, and biodistribution of poorly soluble therapeutics. However, progress in the development and translation of these materials has been limited by the lack of safe excipients capable of stabilizing drug-rich nanoparticles that allow for extrahepatic delivery. Here, we present an adaptive machine learning-guided workflow for excipient discovery that prospectively prioritizes candidate dyes and identifies clinically relevant drugs compatible with dye-based nanoparticle formulations. Guided by model predictions, we deployed semiautomated synthesis together with in vitro and in vivo experimental validation to evaluate and characterize the resulting nanoparticles. We identified two FDA-approved dye excipients and rediscovered a third dye as favorable excipients. Fine-tuning our machine learning models enabled us to identify 35 previously unreported nanoparticle formulations utilizing these dyes. Importantly, in proof-of-concept in vivo biodistribution studies, these dye excipients enabled the encapsulation of the anticancer drug sorafenib with distinct extrahepatic biodistribution profiles, including preferential accumulation in the lung. Taken together, this work establishes an adaptive machine learning-driven framework for excipient discovery and demonstrates that small-molecule dye excipients can serve as modular regulators of nanoparticle biodistribution. These findings expand the molecular and computational toolboxes for drug-excipient nanoparticle design and prototype the excipient selection process as a potentially powerful strategy to tune in vivo drug delivery.

papers.title: Apparent Power as a Unifying Metric for Frontal Polymerization
papers.abstract: The success of chemical transformations is governed by both thermodynamic and kinetic factors. Together, the heat of a reaction and the rate at which that heat is released manifest as power. In self-sustained transformations such as frontal polymerization, the balance between power generated and power transfer governs propagation dynamics. Herein, we demonstrate the use of an experimentally practical apparent power expression to characterize frontal polymerization.
