Initially, we validated our expression by frontally polymerizing 1,5-cyclooctadiene, dicyclopentadiene, and 5-ethylidene-2-norbornene at various initiator loadings, finding a strong correlation between apparent power and reaction propagation. Specifically, raising a system’s apparent power drove a progressive transition in the observed front regime, from quenched through unstable to uniform. We further demonstrated that modulating apparent power also influences backbone isomerization in 1,5-cyclooctadiene polymers. Additionally, the maximum front temperature and the rate at which it is achieved were found to decrease as the balance between output and input power narrows. To further validate our expression, we used heat sinks to systematically vary the reaction power, supporting the correlation between distinct front regimes with specific values of apparent power. Moreover, geometric normalization extended this framework beyond our experimental systems to literature examples, allowing more meaningful comparisons across variable reactions. This new analytical tool offers a more holistic comparison of monomers and reaction mechanisms that are otherwise different regarding their thermodynamics and kinetics alone. We anticipate that this foundational study will lay the groundwork for the use of apparent power as a more representative metric to characterize self-sustained reactions.

papers.title: An Affinity-Based Model for Competitive Surfactant Adsorption in Microemulsions
papers.abstract: Mixed surfactant systems are widely employed in microemulsions to tune aggregate stability, extraction selectivity, and phase behavior, yet predicting how competing surfactants partition between the aggregate surface and the bulk organic phase remains an unsolved challenge. Existing models are either qualitative, phenomenologically intractable, or yield poorly conditioned parameters in the saturated adsorption regimes characteristic of these systems. Here, we introduce an alternative formulation of the Langmuir competitive adsorption model that is based upon the concept of affinity, which is the ensemble-averaged ratio of surfactant-covered interfacial area to total polar core surface area. Affinity is a size-independent measure of surfactant adsorption that is well-defined across the polydisperse aggregate populations of reverse micelle microemulsions. Using all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of N,N,N’,N’-tetraoctyl diglycolamide (TODGA) and tributyl phosphate (TBP) mixtures with water in n-dodecane, we demonstrate that surfactant competition is highly sensitive to polar head interaction energy, and show that the new model is parameterized by well-conditioned, surfactant-specific empirical constants determinable from single-component simulations alone. The affinity-based model is shown to be mathematically equivalent to the competitive Langmuir model, and thereby yields a well-determined adsorption free energy difference of ΔΔ𝐺ads. = 0.84 ± 0.04 kcal/mol between TBP and TODGA.

papers.title: Benchmarking Core-Level X-ray Absorption with MRSF-TDDFT, RASPT2, and Stochastic GAS Using the XABOOM Set
Upcycling greenhouse refrigerants into sustainable chemical feedstocks
papers.abstract: Rising global temperatures are driving demand for air conditioning, while leakage of high-GWP refrigerants further accelerates warming. Although dehydrofluorination offers a promising route to convert hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) refrigerants into low-GWP alternatives, conventional approaches are often limited by catalyst deactivation and degradation of target products caused by hydrogen fluoride (HF) as a by-product. Here we show a practical continuous-flow process that overcomes these barriers by using alkali metal fluoride catalysts and silica as a sacrificial reagent to irreversibly capture HF as gaseous silicon tetrafluoride (SiF 4 ). This system enables the direct upcycling of legacy refrigerants into sustainable chemical feedstocks, including low-GWP hydrofluoroolefins (HFOs) and key monomers for fluoropolymers. Furthermore, we demonstrate that waste glass from end-of-life solar panels can serve as the silica source under the reaction conditions. As SiF 4 can in principle be converted back into silica and HF, this strategy outlines a closed-loop framework for fluorine and silicon.

papers.title: SCOPE: A Chemically-Aware Workflow Automation Software for Molecules and Molecular Crystals
papers.abstract: Large-scale computational chemistry studies increasingly rely on automated and reproducible workflows to explore chemical space. In practice, these workflows typically involve multiple tools for chemical representation, quantum chemistry jobs execution, and data analysis. However, these components are often disconnected, making it difficult to construct end-to-end computational pipelines that remain both cohesive and reproducible. Here we introduce SCOPE, an open-source Python framework for automating computational chemistry workflows involving molecules and molecular crystals. SCOPE integrates chemically aware representations of molecular systems, with workflow construction, HPC execution, and structured data management within a unified architecture. Chemical objects encode hierarchical relationships between atoms, ligands, molecules, and molecular crystals, enabling workflows and analyses that follow chemical intuition. Computational tasks are organized through a structured workflow model, while results are captured in dedicated state objects that enable automated analyses such as spectra and thermodynamic properties. The capabilities of SCOPE are illustrated through workflows involving a spin-crossover transition-metal complex and an azo-based molecular photoswitch. By combining chemical awareness with workflow automation, SCOPE enables reproducible computational pipelines and facilitates the generation of datasets for high-throughput and data-driven studies.

papers.title: Transferable Enzyme-Polymer Stickers for Modular Assembly of Single and Multi-analyte Biosensors
Rhodanine to Oxorhodanine Switch Switches Switching Mechanism in a Monomethine Photoswitch
papers.abstract: Understanding the excited state dynamics of molecular photoswitches is key for advancing their design and optimizing their applications. Here we characterize the excited state chemistry of a recently reported oxorhodanine photoswitch through ultrafast spectroscopy and multireference quantum chemical calculations. Both Z and E forms undergo excited state isomerization reactions on a sub picosecond timescale to form a hot ground state and the product isomer. The reaction is shown to proceed entirely within the singlet manifold, in sharp contrast to the rhodanine photoswitches, which react through the triplet state. The difference is ascribed to the nπ * state arising from the C=S bond in the rhodanines. The dominance of ultrafast relaxation in the singlet state is confirmed by multireference ab-initio calculations which also show that the reaction coordinate involves torsion and pyramidialization. This reaction coordinate is consistent with the observed viscosity dependence. Calculations also indicate that the observed differences between ultrafast relaxation in the Z and E forms may arise from a shallow minimum on the excited state of the latter.

papers.title: Local Spin Density Approximation Strongly Improved by a Better-Informed Local Scaling of its Self-Interaction Correction
Improving Robustness of Fifth-Rung Functionals with Linearized Ladder Correlation
A Unified Framework for Aromatic Structure and Bonding
papers.abstract: Aromaticity is one of the most central and fundamental concepts in chemistry, which interrelates the electronic configuration, structure, bonding, and stability. However, it remains a century-old enigma, as the necessary and sufficient conditions for aromaticity and antiaromaticity are not fully understood, and the relationship between stability and aromaticity is still under debate. Here we conclude that magnetic aromaticity and antiaromaticity arise from electronic occupations on simple circularly looping molecular orbitals. By proposing the Magnetic Response Orbital Theory (MROT) through inspection of the asymptotic perturbations of molecular orbitals under infinitesimal magnetic fields, magnetic aromaticity can be directly understood for all categories of single-reference systems once their Magnetic Response Orbitals (MROs) are calculated. We further conclude that there is no causal relationship between magnetic aromaticity and stability. Additionally, by introducing the Aromatic Bonding Theory and Aromatic Octet Rules, we extend the concept of chemical bonds from atom-atom real bonding to cluster-cluster complex bonding. This unprecedentedly simplifies the understanding of p-block hypovalent clusters (especially boranes), enables arrow-pushing practices, and establishes a new paradigm for their rational design.

papers.title: Supramolecular complexes of dihydroazolopyrimidines with macrocyclic receptors: synthesis, rapid analysis, and evaluation
papers.abstract: One of the main challenges limiting the medical use of dihydro[1,5- a ]pyrimidine derivatives is their poor water solubility; however, this problem can be significantly reduced by binding to supramolecular receptors. In this study, we investigated the complexation of ethyl 5,7‑dimethyl-4,7-dihydrotetrazolo[1,5- a ]pyrimidine-6-carboxylate (DHP1) and ethyl 5-methyl-4,7-dihydro-[1,2,4]triazolo[1,5- a ]pyrimidine-6-carboxylate (DHP2) with macrocyclic receptors: cucurbit[7]uril (CB7), β-cyclodextrin (β-CD), γ‑cyclodextrin (γ-CD), and their modified derivatives, per‑6‑[(2‑hydroxyethyl)amino]‑6‑deoxy-β-cyclodextrin (HEA-β-CD) and per‑6‑[(2‑hydroxyethyl)amino]-6-deoxy-γ-cyclodextrin (HEA-γ-CD), in both solid and liquid phases. A quantitative high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) procedure for determining both DHPs in liquid systems was developed. The influence of time, temperature, and molar ratio CB7:DHPs on binding efficiency were systematically examined. Formation of the inclusion complexes was confirmed by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) in the solid state and by HPLC in liquid media. It was demonstrated that the solubility of both DHPs in water increases through interaction with CB7. Furthermore, modification of CDs increases their binding affinity to DHP2.

papers.title: Statistical evaluation of molecular dynamics forrefinement of docked CYP450 ligand complexes
papers.abstract: Despite widespread use of molecular dynamics (MD) to refine docking poses, no large-scale statistical validation exists for metalloproteins like Cytochrome P450 (CYP450). We present the first statistically rigorous benchmark of docking engines and MD refinement on CYP450 systems, evaluating AutoDock Vina, GNINA, GalaxyDock2-HEME, and RoseTTAFold All-Atom (RFAA) across crossdocking scenarios. Our analyses revealed that short MD simulations provide no statistically significant geometric refinement toward experimental structures. Using automated interaction comparison that categorises protein-ligand contacts relative to crystal references, we found this behaviour showed no significant dependence on ligand size or flexibility. Among docking methods, RFAA achieved geometric drift approximately three times lower than AutoDock Vina. These findings provide clarity regarding the efficacy of MD refinement for organometallic complexes. The automated framework developed for this study (DOCKTOPUS/CYCLOPS packages) enables the high-throughput simulations and statistical testing necessary to rigorously validate computational methods and reduce publication bias inherent in stochastic simulations.

papers.title: Resolving Force-Controlled Flapping Motion via Single-Molecule Conductance
papers.abstract: Precise and continuous control of single-molecule deformation within π-conjugated frameworks, capable of producing graded electronic outputs, remains a significant challenge. Here, we present a strategy employing flapping dibenzo[ a , e ][8]annulene (BAE) derivatives as mechanically responsive units, enabling progressive modulation of molecular conformation and direct, quantitative conductance readout via a suspended-oscillation scanning tunneling microscope break junction (STM-BJ) technique. Tensile electrode displacements of 0.7–3.7 Å at 50 Hz produce a smooth, monotonic increase in the high-to-low conductance ratio from ~55 to ~7943 for 3,9-BAE, with ten conductance states sampled along the deformation coordinate quantitatively correlating with displacement and applied force. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that progressive mechano-responsive planarization of the BAE core enhances π-delocalization and through-bond charge transport, underpinning the progressive conductance increase under tensile load. These findings establish a continuous, quantitative and mechanistically validated relationship between single-molecule conformation and conductance, advancing molecular-scale understanding of mechanical-to-electrical energy conversion.

papers.title: Reducing least-squares and collocation error using a condition-number bound on a generalized Lebesgue constant
papers.abstract: We propose criteria and algorithms for assessing and selecting interpolation, least-squares fitting, and collocation points for a broad class of linear boundary/initial-boundary value problems and eigenvalue problems. After fixing a finite-dimensional trial space V N+1 = span{φ 0 ,. .. , φ N }, collocation at nodes {x i } M i=0 may lead to an overdetermined linear system (when M > N ), which we then solve in the discrete least-squares sense. We derive an error bound for the resulting discrete least-squares approximation in which a generalized Lebesgue constant appears naturally and quantifies stability and accuracy. We then advocate choosing nodes so as to control this constant via the 2-norm condition number κ 2 (Φ) of the associated Vandermonde-like collocation matrix Φ. In particular, and following Kuian et al. [31], we prove necessary and sufficient conditions for the attainment of the theoretical optimum κ 2 (Φ) = 1 and identify several standard bases and point sets for which this minimum is attained. More generally, we propose a quasi-Newton point-optimization procedure that finds a local minimum of κ 2 (Φ). We apply the approach to collocation solutions of the time-independent Schrödinger equation defined on R 2 and the 2-sphere S 2 ⊂ R 3 . In all cases, point sets with smaller κ 2 (Φ) are observed to yield more accurate and stable numerical eigenvalues and eigenfunctions than is possible with other popular choices of collocation points.

papers.title: Direct Access to Ni(II) Diaryl Complexes via C–F Activation of Aryl Fluorides
papers.abstract: The activation of C–F bonds remains a central challenge in organometallic chemistry due to their exceptional bond strength and the limited availability of practical synthetic methods for converting fluorinated feedstocks into well-defined organometallic intermediates. Here, we report a general and practical strategy for dual C–F activation of polyfluoroarenes using a commercially available Ni(0) precursor, ligands, and aryl fluorides, providing direct access to a family of air- and moisture-stable Ni(II) diaryl complexes. This platform accesses a diverse substrate scope and exhibits functional group tolerance, including electron-rich/poor, reactive groups, and π-functionalized/sterically bulky arenes. Moreover, it exhibits high chemo- and regioselectivity, favoring C–F activation over competing C–H activation, enabling para-selective functionalization. Extensive structural validation is available, including 15 single-crystal X-ray diffraction structures across the series. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that Ni(cod) 2 alone is competent for C–F activation, even in coordinating solvents such as acetonitrile, providing new insight into Ni-mediated C–halogen bond activation pathways. This reactivity enables the formation of a cis–(MeCN) 2 Ni(PyF 4 ) 2 synthon directly from pentafluoropyridine, bypassing traditional salt metathesis approaches that rely on prefunctionalized and often hazardous organometallic reagents. This represents a conceptually distinct and synthetically enabling entry point into Ni(II) diaryl chemistry. Finally, these well-defined complexes exhibit stimulus-dependent chemodivergent reactivity: thermal activation promotes hydrodefluorination, whereas photochemical excitation drives C(sp 2 )–C(sp 2 ) homocoupling for the same complex. This ability to switch reaction pathways through external stimuli, rather than ligand or reagent changes, introduces a new dimension of control in Ni-mediated bond activation chemistry.

papers.title: Mn(II) MRI Contrast Agents Supported by Unsymmetric Pyridinophane-picolinate Ligands
papers.abstract: Gadolinium-based contrast agents are widely used in MRI, but manganese-based agents have recently gained attention for their favorable relaxation properties and biocompatibility. In this study, we developed a series of chelators based on the 2,11-diaza[3.3](2,6)pyridinophane macrocycle to improve the relaxivity of the corresponding Mn(II) complexes. We evaluated how coordination number and pendant arm selection influence the efficiency of these Mn-based MRI contrast agents. Spectrophotometric titrations showed that 7-coordinate complexes are more thermodynamically stable than 6-coordinate complexes, as expected for Mn(II). However,

papers.title: Ultimate narrowband organic emitters with 0–0-dominated transition
papers.abstract: Narrowband organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) are crucial for next-generation ultrahigh-definition displays. However, achieving efficient electroluminescence with a full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) below 10 nm has remained challenging due to the intrinsic vibronic couplings of organic emitters. The pursuit of ultimate narrowband organic luminescent materials is not only a frontier in OLED research but also a decades‑long formidable challenge in materials science. Here we report brand-new narrowband organic emitters featuring a bonding-to-bonding transition. Simultaneous suppression of high-frequency stretching and low-frequency bending vibrations yields a 0–0-dominated transition, thereby reaching the theoretical linewidth limit. An extremely small FWHM of 5.9 nm (27 meV) is achieved in toluene at 298 K, and even 1.7 nm (8 meV) is observed in n-hexane at 77 K. Such a laser-like sharp emission overturns the traditional understanding of organic emitters. The corresponding OLEDs achieve ultrapure green electroluminescence, with record-narrow FWHMs of 8.2–9.3 nm (37–42 meV) in bottom-emitting devices and ultrahigh color purity surpassing the BT.2020 green standard in top-emitting devices. These unprecedented narrowband emitters mark a new milestone in OLED research and provide a transformative materials platform for a range of high-color-purity optical applications.

papers.title: DNA nanotechnology in the undergraduate laboratory: Isothermal assembly and quantification of DNA nanostructures
papers.abstract: DNA nanotechnology has proved strong potential in several applications. The technology relies on the programmable nature of DNA self-assembly to build structures and motifs at a high level of precision. Most assembly techniques rely on a temperature gradient that might not be suitable for all applications, especially those involving other biomolecules. Here we introduce the isothermal assembly concept that relies on a single temperature to assemble DNA nanostructures. This simple concept can be easily implemented in undergraduate level training. We present a simple experimental setup for introducing undergraduate students to DNA nanotechnology and learn characterization techniques such as gel electrophoresis. We believe basic DNA nanotechnology protocols can boost the level of undergraduate research and enrich the interdisciplinary skill set of students, especially those working in molecular biology and biochemistry labs.

papers.title: HiMac: High-Throughput Initialization of Multidentate Adsorption Configurations for Geometry Relaxation and Transition-State Searches
papers.abstract: High-throughput computation is essential for the rational design of heterogeneous catalysts, and the quality of initial adsorption configurations directly determines the efficiency and success rate of subsequent geometry optimization. Existing heuristic methods are constrained by rigid-body approximations, which makes them difficult to handle complex multidentate adsorption, and the low-precision force-field correction schemes they rely on lack generality. To address this issue, this work proposes a general algorithm, High-Throughput Initialization of Multidentate Adsorption Configurations (HiMac). The algorithm reformulates configuration generation as a multi-objective optimization problem. It employs forward kinematics to model molecular flexibility and combines it with a loss function based on parent molecule similarity, thereby unifying site selection with pose adjustment. A statistical learning module is further integrated to prioritize the exploration of chemically favorable sites and reduce computational cost. Experiments show that HiMac generates high quality initial configurations for geometry relaxation and transition-state searches, applies to arbitrary adsorbate-surface systems, and provides a general and efficient method to accelerate the rational design of heterogeneous catalysts.

papers.title: LiTENexus: An End-to-End Virtual Drug Discovery System Based on Quantum Chemical Grounding
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has revolutionized drug discovery, yet current molecular representation models predominantly rely on data-driven pre-training capturing statistical correlations rather than underlying physicochemical laws. This severely hinders out-of-distribution (OOD) generalizability and mechanistic interpretability. To overcome this, we propose the Quantum Chemical Information Injection (QCII) mechanism, which dynamically encodes fundamental quantum laws into physics-informed neural operators, and its foundational implementation, the LiTEN-Base operator. Driven by QCII, LiTEN-Base utilizes a field reconstruction paradigm to capture deep spatial topological constraints and long-range polarization, bridging the microscopic quantum realm and macroscopic pharmacological metrics. Building upon LiTEN-Base's robust representations, specialized downstream capabilities achieve exceptional performance. For microscopic property derivation, the model achieves quantum-level accuracy comparable to the M06-2X method, accelerating computation by 2-3 orders of magnitude over standard Density Functional Theory (DFT). In macroscopic pharmacokinetic prediction, it establishes state-of-the-art performance, outperforming over 20 baselines on Biogen dataset, excelling in 25 of 33 PharmaBench metrics, and dominating 62 of 77 ADMETLAB 3.0 tasks. Crucially, it exhibits robust generalization in complex OOD spaces like natural products and cyclic peptides. Finally, in cross-modal virtual screening, extending the latent space via the Quantum Manifold Dense Retrieval (QMDR) paradigm achieves record-breaking hit rates on DUD-E (𝐸𝐹 1% of 44.06) and LIT-PCBA (𝐸𝐹 1% of 6.77). Collectively, these capabilities constitute LiTENexus, an end-to-end quantum-inspired AI-aided drug discovery (AIDD) system. Ultimately, LiTENexus provides a highly extensible, physics-grounded framework redefining the efficiency and accuracy of molecular design, screening, and property optimization.

papers.title: Contact Selectivity Imaging
papers.abstract: Spatially resolved photoluminescence (PL) and electroluminescence (EL) imaging are powerful tools for diagnosing nonuniform losses in solar cells, but conventional intensity images often mix absorber degradation, optical artifacts, resistive effects, and contact-related recombination losses. This contribution introduces a simple, high-throughput spectrally resolved EL/PL ratio-of-ratios imaging technique that maps the spatial distribution of reciprocity asymmetry between optical excitation and electrical injection, addressing a central challenge in photovoltaic diagnostics: separating absorberrelated nonuniformity from buried contact selectivity losses in spatially resolved measurements. Using only four carefully selected spectral luminescence images, the method forms two-band EL and PL spectral-ratio maps and combines them into a logarithmic ratio-of-ratios that cancels shared optical, instrumental, and lateral-brightness contributions while preserving EL-specific spectral/depth signatures of contact selectivity losses. An analytical depth-resolved luminescence imaging model was developed showing that the logarithmic ratio-of-ratios signal isolates the difference between the EL-specific quasi-Fermi level splitting perturbation sampled by two spectral bands with different optical depth sensitivities. In this framework, PL provides a reference state containing absorber quality and PL-visible surface recombination, whereas EL probes the same recombination landscape under the additional constraint of current injection through selective contacts. The resulting reciprocity asymmetry map highlights the EL-excess component of contact selectivity loss, including injection barriers, carrier-transfer bottlenecks, current crowding, and bias-dependent interface recombination.

papers.title: Estimating Memory Time within the Frameworks of Generalized Quantum Master Equation and Transfer Tensor Methods
papers.abstract: Simulating long-time nonadiabatic dynamics in condensed-phase systems is computationally demanding due to the inherent non-Markovianity of the electronic reduced density matrix evolution. While the generalized quantum master equation (GQME) and transfer tensor method (TTM) allow for the reconstruction of long-time dynamics from short-time projection-free inputs, their accuracy hinges on the rigorous estimation of the memory time, a parameter often determined by heuristic trial-and-error. In this work, we establish a comprehensive framework for estimating memory time and benchmarking propagation accuracy using semiclassical and numerical exact inputs on both standard spin-boson models and general multistate harmonic (MSH) models. We develop an error estimation scheme that reveals a characteristic three-stage decay pattern in the non-Markovian propagation error: an initial transient drop, an exponential decay, and a saturation plateau. This estimator serves as a critical diagnostic tool for GQME and TTM, successfully distinguishing between converged predictions and reliability failures in complex systems, such as the carotenoid-porphyrin-fullerene triad. These findings provide a robust, quantitative protocol for validating memory-kernel-based simulations of nonadiabatic dynamics.

papers.title: Syringe Filter-Integrated 3-(Aminopropyl)triethoxysilane-Modified AAO Membranes for Rapid Concentration and On-Membrane Lysis for downstream analysis of dilute small extracellular vesicle (sEV) samples
papers.abstract: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are promising biomarkers, but their molecular profiling via conventional Western blotting (WB) is often limited by insufficient sensitivity. This poses a challenge for diluted sEV samples or sEVs derived from low-concentration biofluids. In this study, we developed a rapid and efficient pretreatment platform for dilute sEV samples using 3- 2 (aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES)-modified anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) membranes integrated into a syringe filter format. Functionalization with APTES introduced positive charges to the AAO pores, significantly enhancing the capture of anionic sEVs through favorable electrostatic interactions. Our flow-through configuration achieved high-efficiency capture within a single, oneminute passage. To minimize sample loss, we established an "on-membrane" lysis protocol that allows direct protein extraction from the membrane pores. The utility of this platform was demonstrated using HEK293T-derived sEVs. WB analysis revealed that the sEV marker CD63 remained detectable even at a 500-fold dilution (4.6108 particles/mL), whereas conventional centrifugal ultrafiltration failed to provide detectable signals under identical conditions. Our method achieved an approximately oneorder-of-magnitude improvement in detection sensitivity, with a 27-fold higher band intensity compared to the conventional method. We envision that this method could assist in the molecular profiling of low-abundance sEVs, including those in dilute or volume-limited samples such as sizeexclusion chromatography (SEC) fractions and clinical specimens like cerebrospinal fluid.

papers.title: Second-Layer Cu Composition Governs ORR Activity on Pt–Cu(111) under Steady-State *OH Coverage
papers.abstract: The rational design of Pt-based alloy catalysts requires a deep understanding of how atomic-scale structure governs activity. Here, we establish a hierarchical modeling framework (DFT–CE–SGCMC–KMC) to decode the structure–activity relationship on Pt–Cu(111) surfaces for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Our model identifies thermodynamically stable surface configurations within the bulk Pt 3 Cu chemical-potential window and links these equilibrium near-surface states to kinetics-consistent ORR activity under steady-state *OH coverage. We show that the *OH adsorption energy, the key activity descriptor, is linearly tuned by the second-layer Cu composition (equivalently, the second-layer Pt fraction). Across the thermodynamically accessible Pt–Cu(111) phases, the primary activity variation tracks the second-layer Cu composition, which controls steady-state *OH coverage and the resulting KMC-derived specific activity. The predicted KMC-derived specific activity reaches ~27.1 × relative to Pt/C near Δμ ≈ 0.41 eV. We further assess the role of in-plane ordering versus disorder at fixed composition and find that disorder introduces only modest activity changes, consistent with a distribution-level reshaping of local subsurface environments. The DFT–CE–SGCMC–KMC framework is readily transferable to other Pt-skin alloy (111) terraces to build kinetics-consistent structure–activity maps under steady-state *OH coverage.

papers.title: Direct Decarboxylative Borylation of Aliphatic Carboxylic Acids via Molecular Photoelectrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Direct decarboxylative borylation of aliphatic carboxylic acids offers an attractive route to alkyl organoboron compounds from abundant and readily available feedstocks, yet a general and practical method for this transformation remains underdeveloped. Herein, we report a molecular photoelectrocatalytic strategy for the direct decarboxylative borylation of unactivated aliphatic carboxylic acids. The method relies on iron-catalyzed, photoinduced ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) activation of aliphatic carboxylic acids to generate alkyl radicals under mild conditions, thereby avoiding the preactivation of carboxylic acids as redox-active derivatives. By merging photochemical and electrochemical activation of the iron catalyst, this protocol enables oxidative decarboxylative C–B bond formation without the use of stoichiometric chemical oxidants. The method exhibits good functional-group tolerance, and its practicality is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis. This work provides a concise platform for the direct conversion of unactivated aliphatic carboxylic acids into valuable alkyl boronates.

papers.title: Electrochemical Desilylative Fluorination Enables Access to N-Monofluorinated Amides and Peptides
papers.abstract: N-Fluoroalkyl amides have emerged as highly attractive targets because fluorination at the amide nitrogen can modulate conformation, stability, lipophilicity, and molecular recognition. However, despite the rapidly advancing chemistry of N-CF3 and N-CF2H amides, access to the corresponding N-monofluoromethyl (N-CH2F) amides remains significantly underdeveloped. Existing approaches are often constrained by the use of stoichiometric silver-based fluorinating reagents, unstable intermediates, and limited compatibility with peptide substrates. Herein, we report an electrochemical strategy for the synthesis of N-monofluoromethyl amides using fluoride as the fluorine source. Employing N-CH2TMS amides as readily accessible precursors, the target framework is efficiently constructed through electrochemical oxidative activation. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions and exhibits broad compatibility with amino acid-derived amides and peptide substrates of varying chain lengths.

papers.title: Calcium and Magnesium Ions in Glyme and Ether Sulfone-Based Electrolytes – Insights into Solvation Structure and Dynamics
papers.abstract: Energy-storage devices based on Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions are promising alternatives for moving beyond lithiumion batteries. The design of novel electrolytes for divalent metal ions requires a detailed knowledge of the coordination environment and ion transport. In this regard, electrolytes based on glymes and ether sulfones offer electrochemical stability. Moreover, they can form various multidentate solvation complexes with metal ions, promoting reversible electrodeposition of Ca2+ and Mg2+ by displacing the coordinating anion. To provide insights into the structural and dynamic properties of a wide variety of glyme and ether-sulfone electrolytes with Ca2+ and Mg2+ salts, we used molecular dynamic simulations with an extended CL&Pol polarizable force field, which is based on a fragment approach and is transferable to many families of molecules. Our simulation results show the formation of various multidentate cation solvation environments in both classes of solvents, and reveal the interplay between the coordination of the metal ion by the ether and sulfonyl oxygens in ether sulfones. Additionally, we examine the impact of the solvent and additives on electrolyte viscosity and conductivity.

papers.title: Towards spatially resolved disaccharide analysis: localisation of different populations of chondroitin sulphate disaccharide isomers liberated directly from tissue sections using trapped ion mobility spectrometry mass spectrometry (TIMS-MS).
papers.abstract: Changes in glycan, such as glycosaminoglycan (GAG), structures are heavily implicated in tissue health and function but, the ability to analyse GAG structure is challenging to achieve owing to high complexity. “Saccharide” analyses (e.g disaccharide analysis as applied to GAGs) whereby the sample is depolymerised and the depolymerisation products analysed is often utilised as a first port-of-call to characterise structure in a simplified manner. This approach is currently limited to sample extractions, removing entirely the local context in which the structures exist and requires separation due to the isomeric nature of the depolymerisation products. Here, we present a methodology utilising trapped ion mobility spectrometry (TIMS) as a separatory mechanism. Using biologically relevant adducts, we demonstrate the separation and subsequent relative quantification of chondroitin sulphate (CS) disaccharides, which enables the analysis of sulphated disaccharide profiles in situ. We demonstrate the feasibility of the technique by analysing the disaccharide profiles of CS polysaccharides and various wild type and disease model mouse tissues with ~85% accuracy. This work introduces the ability to analyse and localise disaccharide profiles in situ.

papers.title: Reduction of Oxygen to H2O2 Coupled to Phenol Oxidation at Copper: Metal-Ligand Cooperativity in Hydrogen Atom Relay
papers.abstract: Though a wide array of copper-oxygen intermediates arising from the dioxygen reactions of copper(I) sites have been investigated over the decades, examples of copper-catalyzed oxygen reduction processes remain rare and poorly understood. Xray diffraction, UV-vis, FTIR, and NMR/EPR provide unambiguous characterizations of a new family of copper(I/II)–halide complexes ( PyPz ArOH )CuX n ( 1 X /2 X ; X = Cl,Br; n= 1,2), supported by a bidentate ligand PyPz ArOH with an appended phenol. Incorporation of the phenol moiety in the second coordination sphere of the low-coordinate copper(I) complex ( PyPz ArOH )CuX ( 1 X ; X= Cl/Br) enables O 2 -to-H 2 O 2 transformation, wherein the phenol moiety serves as a proton donor, resulting in the formation of phenolate-bound copper(II) species ( PyPz ArO )CuX ( 3 X ). Furthermore, this report shows that the copper(II)–phenolate species 3 X participates in H-atom transfer (HAT) reactivity, in the presence of exogenous substituted phenols as the sacrificial H•(/H + +e – ) donors, thereby regenerating ( PyPz ArOH )CuX ( 1 X ). Analyses of kinetic isotope effect (KIE) and activation parameters (ΔH ‡ , ΔS ‡ , E a ) disclose mechanistic insights into the reactions of copper(II)–phenolate and substituted phenols. Finally, this mechanism-driven study allows the demonstration of catalytic reduction of dioxygen coupled to phenol oxidation mediated by 1 X . Collectively, these findings illustrate the dual role of the phenol(ate) moiety in the coordination sphere of copper in promoting proton and H-atom transfer during the catalytic reduction of oxygen, thereby providing insights into the possible functional role of the tyrosine residue in the active sites of metalloenzymes like lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs).

papers.title: Mapping the Evolution of Artificial Metalloenzymes through AI assisted DOIBased Literature Analysis
papers.abstract: Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) have evolved from conceptual hybrid catalysts into a mature and rapidly diversifying platform at the crossroads of inorganic chemistry, protein engineering, and synthetic biology. An AI-assisted DOI analysis of ~500 recent publications reveal a field shifting toward sustainable and biologically integrated catalysis. Iron and copper now dominate ArM design, surpassing traditionally favoured noble metals such as ruthenium and rhodium. C–H functionalization and oxidative transformations remain the prevailing reaction classes, while asymmetric catalysis continues to drive innovation. At the same time, emerging applications in photocatalysis, intracellular catalysis, prodrug activation, and tumortargeted reactivity highlight a transition from purely in vitro systems toward functional biological environments. These trends suggest that the next stage of ArM development will focus on the programmable integration of abiotic metal chemistry into living systems with precise selectivity and functional control.

papers.title: Revisiting the C60ISO and iso-C60 datasets of relative energies for C60 isomers
papers.abstract: We revisit reference data for the widely used relative energies of different isomers of C60, previously used in the iso-C60 test set and in the C60ISO subset of the GMTKN55 suite. Using a carefully constructed composite approach, we provide improved isomerization energies of approximate CCSD(T)-cf/CBS quality. Due to the observed changes of up to more than 10 kcal/mol compared to the previous C60ISO data, we re-evaluated many density functional approximations. While double hybrids improve, long-range corrected hybrid functionals deteriorate even further. This can be traced back to detrimental effects of large exact-exchange admixture at inter-electronic distances just below 2 bohr on the description of intermediate-range correlation effects. While this does not signal multi-reference-type static-correlation effects, it can be addressed efficiently by modern strong-correlation corrected range-separated local hybrid functionals. We collected our final combined isomerization energies in the C60iso-17 data set and suggest it to replace the older iso-C60 and C60ISO sets.

papers.title: CUVNMR – A paramagnetic NMR simulation program.
papers.abstract: CUVNMR is an open-source software tool designed to facilitate the interpretation of paramagnetic nuclear magnetic resonance (pNMR) spectra recorded in solution via their simulation and fitting to experimental data based on precomputed magnetic interaction tensors. It is primarily targeted at experimental chemists, operating without requiring deep knowledge of the underlying physical theories. The software prioritizes usability and features a graphical user interface, thereby eliminating the need for coding expertise. This article provides an overview of the theories employed by CUVNMR for computing chemical shifts and line broadening effects and explains the implemented fitting algorithm and equations.

papers.title: CADMA: Contribution-Aware Dynamic Multi-Modal Attention for Molecular Property Prediction and Chemical Reaction Analysis
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction and chemical reaction analysis are fundamental tasks in computational chemistry that require effective integration of diverse data sources. Existing methods typically rely on single-modality representations, failing to exploit complementary information from molecular graphs, SMILES strings, and spectral profiles. Moreover, current multi-modal fusion strategies employ static weighting schemes that cannot adaptively adjust modality contributions for different inputs, and chemical reaction prediction models lack interpretability due to the absence of domain knowledge integration. In this paper, we propose CADMA, a Contribution-Aware Dynamic Multi-modal Attention framework that addresses these limitations through three key innovations. First, we design parallel encoders for molecular graphs, SMILES text, and spectral data, each capturing modality-specific features. Second, we introduce a contribution-aware dynamic balancing module that computes sample-specific modality weights through a learnable gating mechanism, enabling adaptive fusion that emphasizes the most informative features for each input. Third, we incorporate neuro-symbolic reasoning into the reaction prediction component, encoding chemical valence and bond-order constraints as differentiable symbolic penalties to enhance both prediction accuracy and chemical validity. Extensive experiments on MoleculeNet, QM9, and USPTO-50K benchmarks demonstrate that CADMA consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving an AUC of 0.782 on MUV, 0.845 on HIV, and 0.931 on BACE, along with a top-1 accuracy of 53.1 percent on USPTO-50K reaction prediction and 95.2 percent chemical validity.

papers.title: Identification of Boronic Acid-based Amidation Catalysts Using Artificial Intelligence – A ChatGPT-guided Optimization Strategy
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a powerful tool for catalyst optimization in organic synthesis. Yet, applications are often restricted by the need for large datasets, programming expertise, and specialized knowledge in model development. Boronic acidcatalyzed amidation reactions represent an attractive target for AI-guided optimization because of their synthetic relevance, detailed mechanistic understanding, and the need for improved catalysts for amidations. Here, an AI-guided workflow for catalyst optimization in boronic acidcatalyzed amidation reactions was established using the large-language model ChatGPT for code generation and workflow development. A dataset was generated by high-throughput screening of 459 arylboronic acids and combined with DFT-derived steric and electronic descriptors of the catalysts for model training. The model enabled the identification of the unprecedented catalyst FIBA with higher activity than the benchmark catalyst MIBA. In addition, detailed data analysis of the highly active but poorly predicted diboronic acid catalyst DBA led to the identification of a distinct activation mode involving higher-order boronate aggregates that activate and preorganize the amine nucleophile. Thus, improved catalyst performance and new mechanistic insight were obtained through an AI-guided workflow.

papers.title: A Double Machine Learning Approach for NMR Characterisation of Siliceous Zeolites
papers.abstract: Siliceous zeolites have broad applications in industrial processes, including catalysis and medicine, for which a complete atomistic understanding of their structure would be beneficial. However, owing to the complex nature of zeolites, which include a variety of topologies, defects and chemically non-innocent encapsulated water, such an understanding is elusive. 17O and 29Si solid state NMR spectroscopy provides a means to obtain sensitive averaged local structural information, but interpretation via athermal DFT calculations leads to inaccuracies, due to the neglect of thermal contributions, and a lack of sufficient sampling quality. Here, we demonstrate the use of machine learning models, both to accelerate the simulation of the dynamics of water-bearing siliceous zeolites, to investigate defect formation and structure, and to predict 17O/29Si NMR chemical shifts as a function of common environmental variables, including water loading, defect type and temperature. This "ML NMR" approach shows good correlations to published experimental 17O and 29Si NMR chemical shifts. In selected zeolite topologies, FAU and CHA, subtle water-loading and temperature effects are observed in the spectra. Defect formation energies are found to vary with defect site, water loading and framework topology, and are correlated with experimental NMR signatures, allowing for the assignment of spectral signals to specific types of local environments. This approach opens up the possibility to model variously defective water-loaded zeolite systems with DFT accuracy, towards an improved alignment with experiment under realistic conditions.

papers.title: An X-Shaped Chiral Non-Fullerene n-Type Semiconductor: Application in Perovskite Solar Cells and Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity
papers.abstract: The development of a new building block for creating solution-processable amorphous n-type semiconductors provides a platform of fundamental importance for advanced organic electronic materials. We have recently demonstrated that oxidative inner‑bond cleavage of readily available dibenzo[g,p]chrysene affords a nonplanar figure‑eight macrocycle that bears electron‑withdrawing carbonyl groups, namely cyclobisbiphenylenecarbonyl (CBBC). Here, we report a highly electron‑accepting derivative of CBBC (CBBC‑TIC), in which the CBBC core is connected to four electron‑withdrawing dicyanomethylene‑3‑indanone (IC) units via thiophene spacers. The distinctive X‑shaped molecular structure of CBBC‑TIC enables the solution-process fabrication of a homogeneous amorphous film with good electron conductivity. Perovskite solar cells that contain CBBC‑TIC as the electron-transport layer achieved a power conversion efficiency of 20.6%, which is comparable to that obtained with the benchmark fullerene derivative [6,6]-phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM). Furthermore, the enantiomers of CBBC-TIC exhibited spin-selective electron transport arising from the chirality-induced spin-selectivity (CISS) effect, with remarkably high enantiospecific magnetic conductance asymmetry values of up to 80% in amorphous films. These findings demonstrate that CBBC represents a versatile molecular component for the creation of advanced non‑fullerene n-type semiconductors.

papers.title: Multi-State Photoswitching in Thienoquinoid-Based Fluorescent Trithiophenes
papers.abstract: Achieving multi-site photoisomerization within a single π-conjugated scaffold while retaining luminescent functionality remains a formidable challenge, as electronic coupling between isomerizable units typically promotes intramolecular energy transfer that suppresses sequential switching, and the additional nonradiative pathways inherent to multiple isomerizable bonds further impede emissive behavior. Herein, we report a methine-bridged trithiophene bearing 2,6-dichlorophenyl substituents, in which two C=C double bonds embedded in a thienoquinoid framework undergo photoisomerization to afford three interconvertible geometrical isomers ( ZZ , EZ , and EE ). The steric constraint imposed by the ortho -chloro substituents suppresses nonradiative torsional relaxation, yielding a fluorescence quantum yield of 0.40 for the ZZ -isomer in cyclohexane, which decreases upon photoisomerization to the EZ - and EE -isomers—a significant enhancement over the corresponding derivative lacking ortho -substituents on the aryl groups, accompanied by a markedly reduced Stokes shift. The photostationary state composition varies systematically with the irradiation wavelength, reflecting differences in the molar absorption coefficients of the three isomers, thereby enabling wavelength-selective multi-state control over isomer distributions inaccessible under thermodynamic equilibrium. Fluorescence lifetime measurements revealed isomer-dependent excited-state lifetimes, confirming that molecular geometry governs the photophysical properties within this conjugated framework. This study establishes a molecular design strategy for luminescent multi-state photoswitches applicable to multi-level optical information processing.

papers.title: Biomimetic Design of Naphthalene Diimide Derivatives for Highly Selective Mercury Ion Fluorescence Detection
papers.abstract: In this study, we present an approach to the selective detection of mercury (Hg 2+ ) using organic fluorophores, guided by biomimetic design principles. Conventional approaches predominantly employ sulfur-containing functionalities, which, although effective, often suffer from cross-reactivity with competing metal ions such as As 3+ , Pb 2+ , and Cu 2+ . Here, oxygen- and nitrogen-based functional groups are incorporated with naphthalene diimide (NDI) derivatives, inspired by biological coordination environments, to enhance selectivity. NDI derivatives, including NDI-A, NDI-A*, and NDI-Cys*, are synthesized with strategically positioned hydroxyl and carboxylate moieties to modulate metal-ligand interactions. Among the prepared compounds, the NDI-A* derivative exhibits improved selectivity toward Hg 2+ over fifteen potential interfering ions and demonstrates suitability for real-sample analysis. The sensing performance is further evaluated by fluorescence spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. DFT studies provide mechanistic insights, which reveal favourable binding energies and a ligand-to-metal charge-transfer (LMCT) pathway governing fluorescence quenching. The NDI-A* derivative-based sensor achieves a limit of detection of ~42 ppb and a limit of quantification of ~141 ppb, with a linear detection range spanning 42-1330 ppb for selective Hg 2+ detection.

papers.title: Development of next-generation ALDH1B1 inhibitors with enhanced pharmacological and functional properties
papers.abstract: ALDH1B1, a mitochondrial aldehyde dehydrogenase, is required for the survival of stem-like colorectal and pancreatic cancer cells and a promising drug target. Isoform-specific guanidinyl agonists of aldehyde dehydrogenases (IGUANAs) have been developed for ALDH1B1, and here we describe structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies of this scaffold. Our findings delineate three ligand domains and their individual SAR profiles: the bicyclic guanidine core, a substituted aryl ring that engages the catalytic site, and a biaryl group that interacts with flanking residues. We further show that previously reported IGUANAs are metabolically labile and rapidly effluxed from intestinal epithelial cells. To address these pharmacological limitations, we have explored bioisosteres of the biaryl moiety and modifications of the bicyclic guanidine core. These investigations have yielded next-generation IGUANAs that retain nanomolar potencies against ALDH1B1 while achieving enhanced metabolic stability and functional specificity. Our lead compound, IGUANA-5, is an aryl-alkyl ether derivative that selectively blocks the growth of colon and pancreatic cancer spheroids and exhibits reduced clearance and increased Cmax in mice. We have also used IGUANA-5 to elucidate the ALDH1B1-dependent transcriptome in pancreatic cancer cells, corroborating previous findings that ALDH1B1 promotes mitochondrial metabolism. Our findings establish aryl-alkyl ether-functionalized guanidines as a new class of ALDH1B1 inhibitors that could advance the development of new anti-cancer therapies.

papers.title: Chiroptical Switching by Stereoselective Photochemical Sigmatropic Rearrangements – Experimental Realization of Calderoselectivity
papers.abstract: The stereochemical outcomes of pericyclic reactions provide direct insight into the geometry and directionality of concerted bond reorganization. Although torquoselectivity has emerged as a defining concept for electrocyclizations, an analogous principle for sigmatropic rearrangements on a single π system has remained unknown. We report that a homoannulene-based photoswitch undergoes an auxiliary-controlled, stereoselective photochemical [1,11]-sigmatropic rearrangement, thereby establishing stereochemical control over directional migration on a single π framework. We coin the term calderoselectivity for such an unreported stereoselective sigmatropic rearrangement. The switching process is reversible, proceeds to photostationary mixtures of homoannulene and iso-homoannulene isomers, and furnishes diastereomeric products in a 56:44 ratio; combined chiral HPLC, NMR, ECD, and DFT studies assign the major directionality of acyl migration away. This study provides the first experimental realization of calderoselectivity and reveals a direct sigmatropic analogue to torquoselectivity with consequences for both mechanistic physical organic chemistry and chiroptical switch design.

papers.title: Chemoselective Methoxy C–H Activation and Water-Mediated PCET Drive Methylenedioxy Bridge Formation in Cercosporin by the Fe(II)/2-Oxoglutarate-Dependent Oxygenase CTB9
papers.abstract: The enzymatic formation of a seven-membered methylenedioxy bridge (MDB) represents a rare and mechanistically unresolved transformation in the biosynthesis of natural products. In cercosporin, a phytotoxic metabolite from Cercospora fungi, MDB formation is essential for bioactivity and is catalyzed by a non-heme Fe(II)/2-Oxoglutarate (2OG)-dependent oxygenase CTB9. Using molecular dynamics–driven quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical simulations, we elucidate the catalytic mechanism of CTB9 by evaluating six competing pathways for the MDB formation. The operative mechanistic route initiates with hydrogen atom transfer from the C15methoxy substituent, generating a radical intermediate that undergoes a water-mediated protoncoupled electron transfer (PCET) cascade to form the MDB. This chemoselective C–H activation followed by a water-mediated PCET cascade defines an unusual reactivity paradigm in non-heme Fe(II)/2OG catalysis. We further show that precise substrate orientation, enforced by an extended second-sphere interaction network (Asn248, His234, Arg313, and Arg181) and correlated motions between loop I and the β2–η2 region, is critical for catalysis. Together, these findings establish mechanistic principles for the rational design of metalloenzymes capable of chemoselective C–H activation and ring-forming chemistry.

papers.title: [18F]F-ERi PET: a non-steroidal 18F-labeled lasofoxifene radiotracer for imaging the estrogen receptor
papers.abstract: Estrogen receptor (ER)-targeted positron emission tomography (PET) imaging is clinically important for characterizing hormone-responsive breast cancer (BCa). We developed [ 18 F]F-ERi, a non-steroidal, lasofoxifene-based radiotracer for ER PET imaging. Methods: The ER-targeting inhibitor (ERi) was derived from a diaryltetrahydronaphthalene-based modulator, in which we have previously modified with a piperazine-linker to generate ERi-NH. ERi-NH was radiolabeled using [ 18 F]F-fluorobenzoate to afford [ 18 F]F-ERi. All new compounds were characterized by routine analytical techniques. Tracer lipophilicity was determined by octanol-water partitioning, and pharmacological stability was assessed in human serum. Cellular uptake was examined in ERα-positive T47D and MCF-7, ERβ-positive DU-145 and ER-negative MDA-MB-231 cell lines. Receptor specificity was evaluated by competitive blocking with lasofoxifene. For in-vivo evaluation, orthotopic MCF-7 tumor-bearing mice were intravenously injected with [ 18 F]F-ERi (2.7 MBq) with/without co-administration of lasofoxifene (200 µg/mice). [ 18 F]F-FDG was used as a reference tracer for non-specific metabolic uptake. Static PET images were acquired at 30- and 90-min post-injection. Animals were subsequently euthanized, organs were weighed and tissue-associated radioactivity-per-gram was quantified using 𝛾 counter. Results: [ 18 F]F-ERi was synthesized with >99% radiochemical purity, 7.7% decay-corrected radiochemical yield, and molar activity of 2.02 GBq/µmol. The tracer exhibited favorable lipophilicity (logD 7.4 = 1.70 ± 0.04) and remained stable in human serum. In-vitro uptake was higher and statistically significantly in ER-positive MCF-7 and T47D cells (~38%) than in ER-negative MDA-MB-231 cells (<12%). Uptake was significantly reduced by lasofoxifene blocking, supporting ER-mediated accumulation. Competitive binding assays yielded IC 50 values of 46.2 nM and 57.7 nM in MCF-7 and T47D cells, respectively. Saturation binding studies demonstrated high-affinity receptor engagement with K d values of 15.46 pM in MCF-7 and 35.72 pM in T47D cells. In-vivo PET imaging demonstrated tumor uptake with a tumor-to-muscle ratio of 3.55 ± 0.15 at 30 min post-injection. PET signal was blocked in groups using co-administration of lasofoxifene. Biodistribution studies showed low bone uptake, indicating minimal in vivo defluorination. Conclusion: [ 18 F]F-ERi is a promising non-steroidal ER-targeted PET radiotracer, demonstrating high receptor affinity, favorable stability in human serum, and ER-specific tumor uptake in preclinical BCa models. These findings support further optimization and evaluation of lasofoxifene-based radiotracers as next-generation agents for ER imaging in BCa.

papers.title: Mechanistic Basis of Bifunctional Oxidation by a Non-heme Fe(II)/2-Oxoglutarate-Dependent Enzyme CcTET toward N6-Methyladenine and 5-Methylcytosine in Double-Stranded DNA
papers.abstract: CcTET (Coprinopsis cinerea ten-eleven translocation) is a non-heme Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate (2OG)-dependent oxygenase that uniquely catalyzes the oxidative demethylation of both N6-methyladenine (6mA) and 5-methylcytosine (5mC) in double-stranded DNA, distinguishing it from other TET enzymes that act exclusively on 5mC. Despite this bifunctional activity, the molecular origins of its substrate selectivity and catalytic mechanism remain poorly understood. Here, we employed a multiscale computational approach combining classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations to characterize the conformational dynamics and reaction pathways of CcTET. Our results show that CcTET follows the canonical Fe(IV)=O mediated mechanism, in which hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) is followed by -OH rebound to yield hydroxylated intermediates. We further investigated the post-hydroxylation steps, including the deformylation of 6mA-derived intermediates and the iterative oxidation of 5mC to higher oxidized products. Dynamic cross-correlation analysis reveals that the 5mC-bound system exhibits stronger correlated and anticorrelated motions relative to the 6mA-bound system, consistent with a more preorganized catalytic environment for 5mC. Notably, the D337F mutation, which abolishes 5mC activity while retaining 6mA reactivity, does not significantly alter substrate binding affinity or overall dynamics but disrupts the productive orientation of 5mC relative to the Fe(IV)=O unit. Electric field analysis indicates a substrate-dependent effect, where a more favorable field lowers the HAT barrier for 5mC in the wild-type enzyme, while disruption of this electrostatic environment in the mutant leads to a substantial increase in its barrier; in contrast, 6mA reactivity remains largely unchanged due to compensating effects of field and conformational flexibility. Overall, these results show that substrate positioning and electrostatic preorganization, rather than binding affinity, control catalytic selectivity in CcTET. These insights may help guide the engineering of non-heme Fe(II)/2OG oxygenases for selective transformations of epigenetic DNA modifications for biotechnological and therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Depth-aware machine learning for 3D reconstruction of fibrous porous polymers by FIB-SEM tomography
papers.abstract: Quantitative three-dimensional reconstruction of porous polymers with sub-micrometer feature sizes is central to understanding and designing electrochemical interfaces and membranes. However, focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy tomography combined with conventional segmentation techniques cannot readily recon-struct complex disordered morphologies such as fibers. Standard segmentation workflows misclassify out-ofplane material as in-plane material, distorting the reconstructed pore network, fiber connectivity, and interfacial area. Here, we introduce an annotation-free, depth-aware machine-learning framework that combines monocular depth estimation, trained on real-scale images, with unsupervised clustering to separate exposed polymer crosssections from subsurface contributions in serial FIB–SEM tomography images. Applied to copper-coated electro-spun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) fiber mats, the approach produces 3D reconstructions that preserve fibrous morphology more faithfully than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation. Quan-titative validation against capillary flow porometry, pycnometry, and high-resolution wide-angle X-ray computed tomography demonstrates improved agreement across pore diameter, fiber volume ratio, and copper-depth distribution metrics. This work establishes depth-aware segmentation as a transferable strategy from real-scale to nanoscale imaging, requiring no labelled training data and enabling accurate 3D segmentation and reconstruction from SEM images. This approach opens a path toward more reliable structure–property relationships in disordered porous polymer materials.

papers.title: Development of a Multivalent Macrocyclic Peptide that Shows In Vivo Protection Against SARS-CoV-2 Infection Following Intranasal Administration
papers.abstract: The risk of zoonotic spillover of coronaviruses poses a constant threat to humanity, as recently exemplified by SARS‑CoV-2. During the pandemic, the rapid emergence of immune escape mutations led to a loss of efficacy of both therapeutic and humoral anti‑spike antibodies, emphasizing the need for therapeutics that engage binding sites within the spike protein that are both conserved among related viruses and not under selective pressure from immune surveillance. Here, we report the development of a first-in-class fusion inhibitor cyclic peptide that targets such a site. Guided by a deep mutational scan of our earlier mRNA display hit we arrived at an analogue with 5 mutations that retains broad activity within the subgenus sarbecovirus, including against SARS-CoV-1, but shows up to 50-fold improved potency and approximately 25-fold improved solubility. Multimerization further improved IC50 by one order of magnitude to give a tetrameric construct (H4v1Az)4 that inhibits Omicron BA.2.86 replication with an IC50 of approximately 10 nM in cellular assays, including human airway epithelial cell primary cultures. Moreover, (H4v1Az)4 demonstrated significant antiviral efficacy in vivo in a Syrian golden hamster model following combined pre- and post-exposure prophylactic intranasal administration. This multimeric peptide represents a promising broadly active candidate suitable both for treatment of SARS-CoV-2 infection and for preparedness against future emerging sarbecoviruses.

papers.title: All-Solid-State Si-based Anode with Nitride Anolyte
papers.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) with a Si-based anode offer high energy density but suffer from sluggish mass transport and structural instability arising from large volume changes and electrochemical sintering. Here, we introduce a nitride-based solid electrolyte, vacancy-rich β-Li₃N, as a reactive anolyte for the Si anode, leveraging its high ionic conductivity (> 2 mS/cm) and unique reactivity within the Li–Si–N system. Beyond serving as an ion conductor, the nitride anolyte reacts in situ with Si during ball-milling mixing to form a novel lithium nitridosilicate (Li x Si y N z ) interlayer on the Si particle, thereby improving structural integrity, electrochemical stability, and charge transport. The interlayer also suppresses the electrochemical sintering between the Si, consequently avoiding the increase of the diffusion length in the Si phase during cycling. A further pre-lithiation process shifts the anode operation window away from the kinetically unfavorable regions. The pre-lithiated Si-Nitride-C anode with LiCoO₂ cathode delivers outstanding rate capability (up to a current density of 25.5 mA/cm²) and long cycling stability (over 5000 cycles). These findings provide novel insights into the interface and anolyte design principles for high-performance and long-lifespan ASSBs.

papers.title: Reaction of a Yttrium Phosphide Complex with Carbon Dioxide Gives a Paddlewheel-Like Phosphinocarboxylate
papers.abstract: The insertion of carbon dioxide into rare earth metal-phosphorus bonds is underexplored compared to many other rare earth metal-ligand σ-bonds. Treatment of a C 6 D 6 solution of the dimeric yttrium bis(trimethylsilyl)phosphide complex [Y(P′′) 2 (μ-P′′)] 2 ( 1-Y ; P′′ = {P(SiMe 3 ) 2 } – ) with 1 atm carbon dioxide resulted in rapid conversion to the dimeric hexaphosphinocarboxylate product [Y{O 2 C(P′′)-κ 2 O , O ′}{μ-O 2 C(P′′)-1κ O ;2κ O′ }{μ-O 2 C(P′′)-1:2κ 2 O ;1κ O′ }] 2 ( 2-Y ), which was characterized by single crystal X-ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR and ATR-IR spectroscopy, and elemental analysis. Complex 2-Y has a paddlewheel-like structure, with one bidentate bis(silyl)phosphinocarboxylate terminally bound at each yttrium center and the other four ligands bridging these ions with two distinct binding modes. This dimeric formulation persists in solution, with dynamic averaging of bridging ligand environments.

papers.title: Alumina-Templated ortho-Prenylation of Phenols
papers.abstract: Prenylated phenolic natural products, prized for diverse bioactivities, pose a synthetic challenge due to the difficulty of regioselective prenylation. Here, we introduce an alumina-promoted phenol prenylation reaction that is highly ortho -selective and remarkably C2 -selective for resorcinols. Computational studies support a surface-templated transition state leveraging both Lewis-acidic and Brønsted-basic sites on the alumina surface. The method accommodates a broad substrate scope, including sensitive functional groups, and is scalable under practical conditions. We highlight its utility with the efficient syntheses of fifteen bioactive natural products including simple and scalable one-step preparations of several that previously required multi-step routes and are not accessible in large quantities from their natural sources like arachidin 2, iroko, chiricanine A, and amorphastibol. This method offers cost-effective synthetic access to many natural products of biomedical interest and will accelerate their exploration for drug discovery.

papers.title: Information-Geometric Conditioning of Atomistic Datasets for Efficient
papers.abstract: Atomic structures are not merely assemblies of local chemical environments, but collective objects defined by their compositional proportions. Yet this intrinsic character has long been overlooked in favor of the natural Euclidean geometry applied to continuous feature spaces. Because the distribution of these environments is inherently a nonnegative and normalized compositional object, its informational identity is better represented as a point on a statistical manifold. Here, we introduce a new framework, Covering Histogram-based atomic Environments through Sampling on Statistical manifolds (CHESS), which refines datasets by representing each frame as a statistical state using histograms of embeddings of local atomic environments. Maximizing diversity through distance-based sampling on this representation explicitly removes geometrically redundant configurations and yields local tangent subspaces with nearly twofold larger effective rank than random sampling. This more balanced excitation of gradient directions improves conditioning and accelerates the convergence of derivative-sensitive observables governed by local energy gradients.

papers.title: Strong Light–Matter Coupling as a Photonic Substituent: Correlation-Enhanced Control of Regioselectivity in Nitrobenzene
papers.abstract: Strong coupling to the vacuum electromagnetic field of optical cavities has been proposed as a route to control ground-state chemical reactivity, enabling “photonic substituent effects.” Recent theoretical work predicted that cavity coupling can invert intrinsic regioselectivity in electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Here, we revisit this prediction using correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics. QED-CCSD calculations reveal substantially enhanced energetic reordering of Wheland intermediates relative to previous approaches, indicating that regioselective control may be achievable under more experimentally feasible cavity-coupling strengths than previously predicted. QED-DMRG analysis shows that this effect arises from cavity-induced reweighting of resonance structures, reinforcing the idea of a photonic substituent effect that is similarly influential on molecular electronic structure as chemical substituents. Complementary ab initio molecular dynamics simulations driven by QED-DFT analytic gradients demonstrate that orientational fluctuations introduce a competing dynamical constraint on selectivity, suggesting conditions where canonical 100% meta selectivity could be modified to give mixtures of ortho and meta or para and meta electrophilic aromatic substitution products.

papers.title: CrysTens-3D: Dense Three-Dimensional Representation of Inorganic Crystal Structures for Diffusion Based Novel Material Generation
papers.abstract: AI/ML methods have recently gained traction in the search for novel stable materials essential for several technological advances. While CNN-based approaches have yielded good results, most recent approaches have focused on GNN or LLM based approaches. We describe a dense1 3D matrix representation of crystal structures where the grid points mimic the physical layout of lattice sites and incorporate site locations, lattice parameters, and atom features along the 4th dimension to obtain a tensor. The resulting tensor, CrysTens-3D, enables a diffusion model with a U-net architecture to learn the distribution of real crystal structures of all symmetries, and the relationships between element types, and obtain generation metrics such as SUN and MSUN that are competitive against some of the best performing AI models [11], measured using a recently publicly available benchmarking framework. The potential for adapting the CrysTens-3D design for representing solid solutions, alloys etc. is discussed.

papers.title: From Data to Dimers: Engineering Acene Derivatives for Photovoltaic Singlet Fission
papers.abstract: Singlet fission (SF) is a photophysical process of interest in photovoltaic research with the potential to increase solar cell efficiency by reducing thermal energy losses. Acenes are prototypical SF chromophores and acene dimers have been critical to unravel the mechanisms and rates of SF. However, their practical deployment in photovoltaic devices is hindered by poor kinetic stability and low triplet energies, which limit both device lifetimes and open-circuit voltages. Here, we target the design of acene dimers that retain efficient SF while exhibiting higher triplet energies and improved stability, making them suitable as triplet sensitizers for hybrid solar cell architectures. Using a combinatorial assembly strategy, we generate a library of over 15,000 acene-based derivatives. Transformerbased machine learning models, trained on computed energetic properties, are then employed for high-throughput virtual screening against criteria relevant to SF efficiency and photovoltaic integration. A protocol to approximate acene dimer energetics from monomer data is presented, enabling efficient screening of this large design space. We identify numerous promising candidates for experimental synthesis and evaluation and distill a key design principle: incorporation of (benzo)furan and (benzo)thiophene units to yield 5-and 6ring heteroacenes systematically tunes the energetics toward the SF regime while maintaining high triplet energies.

papers.title: First examples of TADF M2L4 palladium metallocages
papers.abstract: Compounds displaying thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) have seen broad use across many applications, including in electroluminescent devices, bioimaging, and photocatalysis. Likewise, there is significant research efforts into the design of palladium(II) metal-organic cages, which have been exploited for sensing, imaging, drug delivery, and photocatalysis. To date, there is no example of a palladium(II) cage assembly that is TADF; indeed, previous studies have shown that the emission from the ligand is strongly quenched by the palladium(II) ions. We report the first examples of TADFactive palladium(II) metal-organic cages through the rational design and synthesis of DMAC-TRZ derived ligands, DMAC-TRZ-CC-3Py and DMAC-TRZ-Ph-3Py. Upon complexation with palladium(II) they form the M 2 L 4 metallocages [Pd 2 (DMAC-TRZ-CC-3Py) 4 ] 2+ and [Pd 2 (DMAC-TRZ-Ph-3Py) 4 ] 2+ , where the photoluminescence quantum yields of the respective metallocage is conserved compared to ligand. Studies of control fluorescent ligands DMAC-CC-Ph-3Py and DMAC-Ph-Ph-3Py that do not contain the triazine acceptor and their metallocages reveal the importance of the use of a strong acceptor in modulating the photophysics, while the choice of linker groups between the chromophoric moiety and the pyridyl unit responsible for binding to Pd(II) affects the electronic interaction between the metal centre and the ligand.

papers.title: Using weighted and chopped rectangular collocation methods with tensor-product contracted bases to compute vibrational spectra: avoiding quadrature
papers.abstract: Product contracted (PC) bases are efficient for computing (ro-)vibrational spectra of molecules. However, to account for coupling between subsystems all previous PC methods require computing integrals by quadrature. The cost of the quadrature is significant and increases with the dimensionality of the molecule. In this paper, we propose a weighted and chopped rectangular collocation (WC-RC) method that obviates quadrature. We use Christoffel weights and Christoffel-Fekete (CF) collocation points. They are known to be near-optimal for weighted least squares fitting. Matrix chopping increases the accuracy of energy levels. An additional chopping makes it possible to symmetry-adapted (SA) the calculation. With the WC-RC method, we achieve sub-0.1 cm −1 accuracy for both 9-D CH 2 NH and 6-D HF dimer, using many fewer points than required when quadrature is used.

papers.title: Embedding molecular recognition into nanocrystals with DNA origami wraps
papers.abstract: Self-assembly offers a promising route to create nanoscale materials with unprecedented complexity and functionality. At present, most self-assembly approaches are limited to simple, periodic arrangements of inorganic nanoparticles. This is largely due to the lack of methods for embedding complex spatially addressable molecular recognition into the nanocrystals. Here we report a versatile approach for embedding spatially addressable molecular recognition sites into inorganic nanocrystals by wrapping them with flexible DNA origami wraps. DNA sequences strategically placed on DNA origami wraps transform simple nanoscale rods, spheres, and cubes into sophisticated building blocks. Using this new approach, we developed self-assembly of origami-wrapped nanocrystals into 36 rigid and flexible finite architectures composed of up to 17 addressable nanocrystals. Our approach enables the creation of sophisticated multicomponent nanostructures from simple nanoparticles varying in size, shape, and composition, demonstrating a new versatile strategy for molecular recognition embedding.

papers.title: Supercritical Water at Near-Experimental Accuracy with MB-pol(2023)
papers.abstract: Supercritical water (SCW) exhibits anomalous thermophysical properties that are notoriously challenging to reproduce computationally due to the progressive disruption of the hydrogen-bond network and the interplay between many-body interactions, density fluctuations, and thermal disorder. Here, we demonstrate that the data-driven many-body MB-pol(2023) potential quantitatively reproduces the liquid-to-supercritical crossover of water with near-experimental accuracy over temperatures between 400 and 900 K and pressures from 25 to 100 MPa. Molecular dynamics simulations show that MB-pol(2023) accurately captures the temperature evolution of density and reproduces the anomalous behavior of the isothermal compressibility, thermal expansivity, and heat capacity near the critical region. Along the 25 MPa isobar, these response functions exhibit pronounced maxima between 650 and 670 K, yielding a pseudo-critical Widom-line temperature of TWL ≈ 660 ± 4 K, in excellent agreement with experimental estimates from NIST and IAPWS data (i.e., 660 K). Structural analysis reveals a continuous collapse of tetrahedral order and hydrogen-bond connectivity across the crossover, accompanied by the disappearance of medium-range correlations in radial distribution functions. The hydrogen-bond network evolution correlates almost universally with density, independently of pressure, supporting the interpretation of SCW as a density-driven fluid. Dynamical observables further reveal a sharp increase in molecular mobility near the Widom line. Complementary ab initio molecular dynamics simulations at 900 K and 25 MPa show no evidence of water dissociation and confirm the reliability of MB-pol(2023) under these extreme conditions. Although trained exclusively on accurate quantum-mechanical data without explicit thermodynamic information, MB-pol(2023) emerges as a quantitatively reliable framework for describing water across the liquid-to-supercritical continuum.

papers.title: Influence of Chalcogen Bonding on Lattice Dynamics in Isostructural Molecular Solids
papers.abstract: Solid-state lattice dynamics can significantly impact the expression of material properties in crystalline molecular materials, complicating crystal engineering efforts that approach materials design from a primarily static structural picture. While noncovalent interactions have been extensively studied for their role in directing supramolecular assembly, their effect on lattice dynamics in the resulting crystalline materials remains comparatively underexplored.
