Here, we investigate the influence of chalcogen bonding (Ch-bonding) interaction strength on the expression of vibrational dynamics in a pair of isostructural molecular solids. Chalcogen donor atom substitution from S to Se in naphthalene bis(1,2,6-chalcogenadiazine) ( Nap2Thn - I and Nap2Sen - I , respectively) enables systematic tuning of Ch-bond strength without modification to the crystal packing structure, producing a pair of materials with an identical set of vibrational normal modes. Low-frequency Raman spectroscopy paired with solid-state density functional theory simulations and local mode analysis reveals that that strengthening Ch-bonding interactions by exchanging S for Se selectively increases the force constants and frequencies of normal and local modes in Nap2Sen - I that directly modulate the intermolecular Ch···N coordinate. However, vibrational modes that are not strongly influenced by Ch-bonding interactions are dominated by mass effects, causing the lighter S-based Nap2Thn - I to exhibit higher frequencies. These trends hold at the Brillouin zone center and boundary, and collectively yield a net reduction in the thermal displacement amplitude of the atoms in Nap2Sen - I . Together, these findings demonstrate that directional noncovalent interactions can be harnessed to tune the expression of solid-state lattice dynamics, providing a foundation for the rational design of crystalline molecular materials with targeted dynamic properties.

papers.title: (CH(NH2)2)5Bi2Br11 : a new centrosymmetric organic-inorganic complex metal halide and the role of A-site cation in the determination of polarity
papers.abstract: Organic-inorganic alkylammonium halides of the A 5 B 2 X 11 form exhibit ferroic behaviour that is strongly dependent on their crystal symmetry, yet the role of the organic A-site and the bioctahedral connectivity governing this behaviour remains poorly understood. Here, a new A 5 B 2 X 11 compound, formamidinium bismuth bromide FA 5 Bi 2 X 11 (FA = CH(NH 2 ) 2 ) has been synthesised using a counter diffusion crystal growth (CDCG) method in silica gel. Structural analysis from single crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that FA 5 Bi 2 Br 11 belongs to the Pnnm orthorhombic space group. The effect of formamidinium as the organic cation and its effect on the structural symmetry within the A 5 B 2 X 11 family is explored. The connectivity of bioctahedral [BiBr 11 ] 5- via equitiorial Br - ions and increased orientational freedom of the formamidinium ion in its cation cavity stabilise centrosymmetry, suppressing polar distortion at room temperature. Electrical measurements confirm the structural predication of suppressed ferroelectricity due to preservation of inversion symmetry. This establishes a structure-property relationship and the role of the A-site cation in crystal symmetry and ferroic behaviour for these complex organic-inorganic halides.

papers.title: Bypassing Fundamental Brightness Limits for Microscopy Contrast Agents Through Tailored Excitonic Interactions
papers.abstract: The brightness of fluorescent emitters used in microscopy is conventionally assumed to be limited by their photoluminescence quantum yield. Here, we demonstrate that this assumption overlooks a more fundamental constraint arising from the quantum statistics of photon arrivals. In laser microscopy, the Poisson distribution of excitation photons leads to stochastic multi-exciton generation, resulting in nonradiative exciton–exciton annihilation and reduced emission efficiency. To mitigate these losses, we introduce Highly Undulated Quantum Dots (HUQDs), engineered to minimize inter-exciton interactions and enhance compatibility with laser excitation dynamics. By suppressing annihilation pathways, HUQDs achieve efficient multiphoton emission and exhibit over a 20-fold increase in brightness compared to conventional dyes and spherical quantum dots. This advancement has the potential to enable high-speed data acquisition with reduced marker density, paving the way for faster, more efficient, and higher-contrast optical microscopy in the future.

papers.title: Strain-Engineered Colloidal Quantum Dots for Nonclassical Light Emission
papers.abstract: Photonic quantum information processing stands to benefit from the realization of scalable, customizable emitters. While colloidally synthesized quantum dots address the challenge of scalability, better control over their properties remains desirable before the customizability challenge is fully addressed. To this end, better structure-property correlations need to be established in colloidal materials for these to be usable interesting for photonic information processing. Here we develop a synthesis of colloidal quantum dots that show reduced surface strain profiles. To show that this can be realized on arbitrarily engineered excitonic level structures, we further introduce additional layers to realize core wavefunction engineering. We specifically employ a recently reported motif that allows us to enhance single photon emission probability even at high laser excitation powers. We show that unlike ordinary QDs that exhibit strain at surfaces, these materials show suppressed luminescence intermittency. We show the potential of these QDs for photonic information by using these as deterministic sources of single photons with high purity in successive excitation pulses without employing spectral filtering or external cavities.

papers.title: Non-Symmetric Stapling of Tyrosine-Containing Peptides Driven by Intramolecular Non-Covalent Interactions
papers.abstract: Non-symmetric stapling of native peptides that crosslinking two distinct residues is a valuable tool for enriching diversity of peptide macrocycles, yet it is less achieved due to the high demand for chemo- and siteselectivity control, as well as the competitive intermolecular peptide crosslinking. Herein, we reported a noncovalent interaction activation strategy for non-symmetric stapling of tyrosine-containing peptides by employing ethenesulfonyl fluoride (ESF) as a bifunctional crosslinker. Once covalently anchored to peptide, the sulfonyl fluoride motif is activated by non-covalent interactions, which triggers an intramolecular SuFEx click reaction with tyrosine to afford peptide macrocycles. This approach efficiently crosslinks diverse residue pairs, including Cys–Tyr, His–Tyr and Pro–Tyr. Notably, the protocol is scalable and can be performed in solid-phase synthesis, providing a robust access to tyrosine-bridged peptide macrocycles with excellent diversity.

papers.title: A Spatial Constraints Model for Ubiquitination Efficiency: Guiding the Rational Design of PROTACs/Molecular Glues via a Lennard-Jones-Inspired Function
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation relies on induced proximity between a protein of interest (POI) and an E3 ligase, yet degradation potency frequently diverges from ternary complex affinity revealing a persistent “affinity paradox”. We note that biological systems operate as exquisite precision machines in which every step, from substrate recruitment to ubiquitin transfer, demands precise molecular alignment. Random encounters between reactants produce only entropic chaos and negligible catalytic output. Thus, ubiquitination efficiency (Eub) is the critical missing determinant of degrader performance. Eub was the product of (i) the spatial occupancy probability of a lysine residue P(x,y) within the catalytic window, and (ii) its intrinsic catalytic geometry efficiency Kub. Because the E2–Ub–E3 catalytic center is structurally rigid, ubiquitin transfer possibility becomes a geometry‑constrained nucleophilic attack rather than a diffusion‑controlled reaction. We formalize the intrinsic catalytic efficiency Kub in ubiquitination center using a Lennard‑Jones‑inspired asymmetric function that captures the sharp steric repulsion at short distances and the gradual loss of productive alignment at longer distances.

papers.title: A Framework for Predictable Degradation and Mechanical Property Loss in 3D-printed Networks
papers.abstract: The clinical translation of resorbable medical devices fabricated using photochemical 3D printing has been limited by a lack of resorbable resins and a framework that is able to predict changes in mechanical properties during network degradation. Measurements of mechanical property loss over time under simulated physiological conditions reveal that the incorporation of silyl ether-based crosslinks affords rapid, generalizable, and highly tunable degradation across three distinct 3D printed copolyester networks. We present a model that relates resin chemistry to network degradation kinetics, decouples diffusion and hydrolysis limited network changes and enables the prediction of mechanical properties during degradation. Collectively, this work outlines a versatile strategy for tuning degradation timelines in 3D printed networks and introduces a predictive framework for the design of next-generation resorbable medical devices.

papers.title: Ultralong Room-Temperature Phosphorescence of meso-Hydroxy-BODIPY in Hydrogen-Bonded Matrices: From Molecular Photophysics to Water-Resistant Luminescent Materials
papers.abstract: Here we report ultralong room-temperature phosphorescence (URTP, τ up to 1.10 s at 20°C) from a BODIPY chromophore, exceeding the previously reported BODIPY phosphorescence lifetime by approximately two orders of magnitude. The central design principle exploits the anomalous hydrogen-bond acceptor propensity of meso-hydroxy-BODIPY (BODIPY-OH), which drives preferential incorporation into hydrogen-bond-rich solid matrices and enforces the conformational rigidity required to suppress non-radiative triplet deactivation. An efficient intersystem crossing cascade (S1 → T2 → T1, ΔE=0.21 eV, SOC=0.52 cm -1 ), validated by singlet oxygen sensitization (Φ ∆ up to 44%) and cryogenic luminescence, populates the emissive triplet state without heavy-atom assistance. URTP is universally activated across a structurally diverse hydroxyl-containing matrix library – PVA, sucrose glass, cyanuric acid, melamine–cyanurate (MCA), and silk fibroin fibers and aerogels. Encapsulation within the water-insoluble MCA supramolecular co-crystal retains intense afterglow (τ=1.29 s at 0°C; τ = 0.60 s at 70°C) even under direct liquid-water contact. The results suggest that the pronounced hydrogen-bond acceptor character of BODIPY-OH is the key determinant of its URTP activation across hydroxyl-rich host matrices, opening a pathway toward heavy-atom-free phosphorescent materials for aqueous and biological environments.

papers.title: Process-Informed MOF–Zeolite Selection for Gasification-Derived Hydrogen Purification: Explainable TSA Simulations Reveal Regime-Specific Adsorbent Advantages
papers.abstract: Hydrogen purification from gasification-derived syngas is not a fixed materials-ranking problem: the feed entering the separator is created by the gasifier, and modest changes in temperature, steam rate and impurity fraction can change which species controls adsorbent inventory and regeneration duty. Here, Aspen HYSYS gasification simulations are coupled with TSA performance calculations and an explainable neural-network surrogate to evaluate 203,010 process–material scenarios. The design space spans gasifier temperatures of 650–850 °C, steam feeds of 50–150 kg h−1, TSA thermal set-points of 313.2–450 K, and three representative adsorbents: HKUST-1, Cu-TDPAT and Zeolite 13X. Zeolite 13X is the most robust global benchmark, reaching about 5.0 mol H2 kg−1 h−1 at 20–100 MJ kg−1 H2. Crucially, however, the maps show that this is not a universal zeolite advantage. Cu-TDPAT enters the 13X productivity envelope under methane-influenced and temperatureflexible operation, and the distributional analysis identifies regimes where the modal MOF productivity can match or exceed that of 13X; HKUST-1 occupies a lower-throughput, lower-energy niche when CO excursions are controlled. SHAP analysis identifies product molar flow, feed H2 fraction, impurity composition and TSA temperature as the dominant levers, while small CO/CH4 shifts can reorder the preferred material. The resulting message is deliberately process-informed: Zeolite 13X provides the reliable industrial baseline, whereas MOFs become compelling when their tunable pore chemistry is matched to a specified impurity hierarchy, regeneration window and bed-inventory constraint.

papers.title: “Peierls-like” distortion and high-coercivity cluster glass in lacunar CsCl-related phase: Co1.5Ni1.5Ga4
papers.abstract: This investigation focuses on the solid-state synthesis and a detailed structural and phase analytical investigation of the Co 𝑥 Ni 3−𝑥 Ga 4 series along a constant Ga compositional line within Co⎼Ni⎼Ga phase space. Combined analysis of single crystal X-ray diffraction and neutron powder diffraction of Co 𝑥 Ni 3−𝑥 Ga 4 , 𝑥 = 1.5 reveals a random distribution of Co and Ni over a single Wyckoff site, which contrasts with previous report suggesting atomic ordering. Phase analyses via X-ray powder diffraction indicates a vacancy order-disorder transition as the Co concentration increases beyond a critical limit. DFT calculation predicted a semi-metallic and nonmagnetic ground state, supported by the absence of magnetic peaks or intensity enhancement at 10 K neutron data compared to 300 K. Interestingly “Peierls-like” distortions are observed within the Ga substructure in the vacancy-ordered phase, whereas such distortions are absent in the vacancy-disordered phase. These distortions result in periodic charge localization and exhibit subtle alterations between room temperature and 180 K. Magnetic measurements further reveal cluster spin-glass behavior with a high coercivity. The non-trivial spin dynamics, coupled with large coercivity, makes this phase a compelling candidate for multifunctional applications.

papers.title: A Möbius cyclo[9]carbon
papers.abstract: Möbius-type conjugated systems have long been predicted but remain experimentally elusive in purely carbon molecules. Here we report the on-surface synthesis and characterization of a Möbius-type cyclo[9]carbon, using STM tip-induced reactions of a designed precursor (C9Cl10) on the NaCl/Au(111) surface. Bond-resolved AFM and DFT simulations confirm a nonplanar cyclic geometry. Interestingly, two distinct electronic configurations of C9 are directly observed, including a nonplanar singlet state and a planar triplet state stabilized by adsorption-site-dependent interactions. Negative ion resonance imaging combined with Dyson orbital analysis further reveals clear helical orbital character in the singlet species, whereas the triplet state exhibits conventional cyclocarbon orbital symmetry. These results establish cyclo[9]carbon as the first experimentally realized Möbius-type cyclocarbon.

papers.title: Asymmetric copper-catalysed retro-allylation of homoallyl alcohols. A new tool for stereoselective methallylation †
papers.abstract: The first stereoselective methallylation via a copper-catalysed retro-allylation of homoallylic alcohols is described. High-throughput experimentation (HTE) enabled the rapid identification of effective chiral phosphine ligands and N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) copper complexes, leading to a general and efficient protocol for the stereoselective methallylation of aldehydes and ketones. The corresponding chiral homoallylic alcohols were obtained in high yields (up to 90%) and with good enantioselectivities (up to 83% ee). Notably, the methodology was further extended to oxime ethers and α,β-unsaturated diesters, underscoring its broad applicability for stereoselective allyl transfer.

papers.title: Polydicyclopentadien-Derived Turbostratic Hard Carbon for Long Cycle Life Sodium-Ion Battery Anodes
papers.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries are widely considered a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries, due to the abundance and low cost of their raw materials. However, the development of high-performance and cost-effective electrode materials remains a significant challenge, particularly when competing with lithium iron phosphate systems. Herein, we present a hard carbon material derived from readily available poly(dicyclopentadiene) for use as a negative electrode in SIBs. This study investigates the influence of carbonization temperature and subsequent CO2 activation on the HC’s structure and electrochemical performance. The impact of activation proved to be dependent upon the first stage carbonization temperature, creating greater local ordering for samples carbonized at higher temperatures. The removal of defects and decrease in average graphitic nano-domain length resulted in a turbostratic structure that enhanced rate performance and capacity retention when compared with non-activated samples. The optimized HC exhibits a reversible capacity of 352 mAh/g at 0.1 C and a capacity retention of 88.1% after 500 cycles with a carbonate based electrolyte. This work introduces a cost-effective approach for producing hard carbon materials with distinctive nanostructure and provides valuable insights into achieving long cycle life in sodium-ion batteries.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Systematic Analysis of Beta-Barrel Cross-Sectional Geometry Across 908 Fluorescent Protein Crystal Structures: Relationships Between Barrel Shape, Chromophore Rigidity, and Photophysical Properties
papers.abstract: The 11-stranded beta-barrel of fluorescent proteins is universally conserved, yet its quantitative geometry has not been systematically characterized. Here, we report a computational analysis of beta-barrel cross-sectional geometry across 908 fluorescent protein crystal structures from the RCSB Protein Data Bank. For each structure, the barrel axis was determined by principal component analysis of backbone Cα coordinates, and a perpendicular cross-sectional slice at the chromophore level was characterized by convex hull analysis. The entire computational pipeline, including CIF parsing, coordinate transformation, geometry quantification, spectral data integration, and statistical analysis, was developed using Claude (Anthropic), a large language model accessed through the agentic coding environment Claude Code. Barrel shape, but not size, correlates with emission wavelength: red-shifted proteins have narrower, more elliptical barrels (ρ = –0.290 for minor axis, p < 10-14). The ratio of chromophore to barrel crystallographic B-factors is the strongest predictor of quantum yield (ρ = –0.493, p < 10-17). Chromophore dihedral angles correlate with both barrel eccentricity and photophysical performance. The principal correlations survive Benjamini–Hochberg correction for multiple testing and partial correlation analysis controlling for crystallographic resolution. These findings suggest that the barrel is not a passive scaffold but participates in modulating chromophore rigidity and photophysical output.

papers.title: From Ruby to Molecular Ruby: Excited State Understanding and Design
papers.abstract: The gemstone ruby, corundum (α-Al 2 O 3 )1 with Al 3+ ions partially subsituted by Cr 3+ ions (Al 2 O 3 :Cr 3+ ) possesses exceptional photophysical proper es with an extremely long-lived (4270 µs) spin-flip phosphorescence at 694 nm with very high photoluminescence quantum yield (90%). The phosphorescent soluble molecular congener [Cr(ddpd) 2 ] 3+ called “Molecular Ruby”, emitting at 738 and 775 nm also shows record values in the field of chromium(III) complexes in photoluminescence lifetime (1122 µs) and quantum yield (13.7%). The comparably lower photophysical parameters stress the huge challenge of designing high-performance photoluminescent molecular systems. This tutorial review discusses general design concepts of Molecular Rubies, which are transferable to other photoactive molecular complexes. An introductory theoretical frame is given, including crystal field, ligand field and molecular orbital theory of transition metal complexes, also highlighting photophysical processes in vertical (absorption and emission) and horizontal (internal conversion, intersystem crossing, inductive resonant energy transfer to high-energy oscillators) transitions. These challenges or disadvantages at first sight also include possibilities or levers to significantly tune specifically the photophysical properties and reactivity, such as emission energy and to enable applications in photocatalysis and sensing.

papers.title: Kinetics Beyond Pose: A Structure-independent Framework for koff Prediction Across Diverse Protein Families
papers.abstract: Predicting the ligand–receptor dissociation rate constant (koff) remains to this day a key challenge in drug discovery, despite its well-established relevance to residence time and in vivo drug efficacy, since it depends on the dynamic interaction between the ligand and the receptor site that cannot be immediately reconstructed from equilibrium conditions alone. In this work, we developed a transformer-based machine-learning framework able to predict the koff value relying solely on the protein amino acid sequence and ligand SMILES string, without requiring explicit 3D protein–ligand complex structures. Evaluated on a chemically and biologically diverse dataset, our model achieved competitive performance in cross-validation and on a held-out test set, while also showing robust behavior on the most represented protein families. Our results indicate that promising koff prediction performance can be obtained with a structure-independent representation, by exploiting pretrained protein and molecular language representations as a scalable strategy for kinetics-aware drug discovery.

papers.title: Arene Hydrogenation under Ambient Conditions Enabled by In Situ Formation of Ru-Pd Alloy Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Arene hydrogenation constitutes a direct and strategically valuable entry to three-dimensional molecular architectures from abundant aromatic feedstocks. Despite its conceptual simplicity, the intrinsic stability of aromatic systems typically necessitates forcing conditions, i.e. elevated hydrogen pressures and temperatures, which in turn demand specialized infrastructure and constrain broader adoption in synthetic endeavors. Here, we report a simple strategy for generating a highly active, heterogeneous catalyst in situ that enables the efficient hydrogenation of benzene and pyridine derivatives under ambient conditions. Central to this approach is the combination of bench-stable Ru(NH 3 ) 5 (OTf) 3 and Pd/C pre-catalysts, which form a catalytically competent and recyclable nanocrystalline Ru-Pd solid solution under the reaction conditions. Comprehensive characterization utilizing microscopic and spectroscopic material analysis techniques is reported, revealing detailed information about the composition of the active catalyst. Further mechanistic investigations and comparative studies with other ruthenium sources underscore the distinctive role of Ru(NH 3 ) 5 (OTf) 3 in the catalyst formation process, demonstrating stepwise reductive decomposition of pentaammineruthenium. Collectively, these findings outline a practical approach to arene hydrogenation under ambient conditions while providing important mechanistic insight into the genesis of in situ -formed heterogeneous hydrogenation catalysts.

papers.title: A Decoupling Strategy for Position-Controlled Access to 1,3-Disubstituted Saturated Frameworks
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional architecture and precise placement of functional groups critically influence the performance of drugs and functional materials, yet positional control on saturated carbocycles remains limited1–3. Framework editing, rather than de novo synthesis, offers an attractive strategy for direct site-selective synthesis of functionalized carbocycles. In particular, functional group translocation—migrating an existing substituent within a molecular framework without altering its core structure—has emerged as a powerful approach to access valuable substitution patterns in saturated systems4. However, its development has largely been confined to 1,2-5–10 and 1,4-migrations11,12. Here, we report a general and conceptually distinct platform for formal transannular 1,3-migration of aroyl groups across saturated carbocycles, enabling precise access to 1,3-disubstituted frameworks. This strategy proceeds via a neutral bicyclic intermediate generated by Norrish–Yang photocyclization, which is then oxidatively cleaved with hydrogenatom trapping. A distinctive feature is the coexistence of oxidant Mn(OAc)3 and a thiol reductant without their mutual quenching, enabling independent downstream reactivity. By decoupling cyclization from the migration event, this approach overcomes kinetic constraints that have historically precluded 1,3-translocation13. Broadly applicable to both radical and ionic pathways, this method enables ring expansion, scaffold hopping, distal editing through iterative translocation, and stereospecific modification of chiral substrates.

papers.title: Distribution of Organic Pollutants in the Alluvial Soils as a Result of the Destruction of the Kahovka Dam (Ukraine)
papers.abstract: In June 2023, the Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant's Dam was destroyed by Russian troops, leaving large areas downstream flooded and an area upstream dried-up. Therefore, the objectives of this screening-level study were (i) to determine the content of organic pollutants in the alluvial soils that have dried-up and soils that are above the old water level, and (ii) to determine the pattern of accumulation of organic pollutants in the dried-up zone. The alluvial soils within the city of Zaporizhzhia were sampled from the superficial, 30 cm, layer in six areas in the dried-up zone, drained after the dam’s breach, and also in six areas in the floodplain above the former water level. The composition of organic pollutants was determined using the method of gas chromatography–mass spectrometry. The distribution of organic pollutants in the soils was analyzed based on the hygrophilicity index that we proposed, which was calculated as a ratio of the amount of compound in the soils of the dried-up zone to its amount in the dried-up zone and in unflooded areas together. We identified 155 organic compounds, 24 of which are hazardous toxicants that contaminate the environment. Those compounds were represented by polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, acid esters, aromatic heterocycles, and other compounds. This ecological pollution jeopardizes the urban landscapes of Zaporizhzhia and other setllemens on the banks of the former Kahovka Reservoir and the health of people in southern Ukraine.

papers.title: MLIP-Enhanced Thermochemistry Predictions across Organic Chemical Space
papers.abstract: This work presents thermoMLIP, a machine-learning-interatomic-potential-based workflow for efficient conformer optimization and thermochemistry prediction across organic chemical space. By combining MLIP-driven geometry optimization with robust thermochemical corrections, thermoMLIP achieves near-DFT accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. We show that MLIP-based conformer searches systematically identify lower-energy structures than conventional approaches, improving thermochemical predictions across diverse datasets. Building on this framework, we develop an uncertainty-aware active learning strategy using evidential graph neural networks to construct a large-scale, uniform thermodynamic dataset. Iterative acquisition driven by epistemic uncertainty improves predictive accuracy and reduces model uncertainty. The resulting surrogate model enables rapid prediction of molecular thermodynamic properties and scalable reactivity screening, for example in reaction-network exploration and high-throughput reaction discovery workflows.

papers.title: Framework for Speciation-Gated Mass Transfer at Liquid-Liquid Interfaces
papers.abstract: The behavior of ionizable surfactants at oil/water interfaces is central to applications from emulsification to liquid-liquid extraction, yet predictive control remains a challenge. Current models often decouple interfacial adsorption from the underlying acid-base chemistry that inevitably will influence surfactant availability. Here, we establish a unified thermodynamic framework demonstrating that interfacial phenomena are controlled by speciation-gated mass transfer. Using a homologous series of linear carboxylic acids (C5-C16), we combine dynamic interfacial tension measurements with kinetic phenotyping and a phase-resolved speciation/partitioning model to show that the flux of surface-active species is gated by the acidbase equilibrium. Two kinetic regimes emerge across the series: long-chain acids relax monotonically toward equilibrium, whereas short-chain acids display pronounced non-monotonic behavior, consistent with initial interfacial activity followed by depletion through organic-toaqueous transfer and dissociation in water. Our framework, which explicitly couples partitioning (logP) and dissociation (pKa) parameters, quantitatively predicts the time-dependent interfacial tension, including non-monotonic behavior driven by mass transfer, and the corresponding pH control of the aqueous phase. The model predicts interfacial-tension dynamics and captures the pH switching gate at which the system switches from oil-favored to water-favored behavior. We validate these predictions across concentrations, pHs, and chain lengths, as well as in weak bases (decylamine). This work transforms the design of responsive liquid-liquid interfaces from empirical trial-and-error to a predictive, thermodynamically guided approach, in which pH and molecular structure (pKa and logP) serve as explicit design levers to control interfacial energy and dynamics. Final version: https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.6c04456

papers.title: Direct analysis in real time triple quadrupole mass spectrometry for illicit drug identification and quantification
papers.abstract: Drug mixture composition and compound identifications provide public health, first responder, and law enforcement communities with critical and actionable data, guiding emergency response and interdiction, informing the public, and targeting overdose prevention. The advent of novel synthetic opioids, nitazenes, and benzodiazepines, along with the spread of strong veterinary tranquilizer adulterants ( e.g., xylazine and medetomidine), have created an ever-changing drug landscape. The Testing, Rapid Analysis, and Narcotic Quality (TRANQ) Research Act of 2023 directs research, method development, measurement science, and standards to address these hurdles. In conjunction with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Rapid Drug Analysis and Research (RaDAR) program, aimed at monitoring the chemical makeup of the drug landscape, we are investigating analytical instrumentation to enable drug screening to move from the laboratory to an agile point-of-need setting. We explored compound identification with a direct analysis in real time triple quadrupole mass spectrometer (DART-TQ-MS) and the NIST/NIJ DART-MS Data Interpretation Tool with Forensics Database. Full scan analysis of single-component standards demonstrated limits of detection generally in the tens to hundreds of picograms with a few in the single nanogram range ( i.e., compounds with extremes in volatility). Single-component, mixtures, and real-world street drug samples were investigated with potential identifications made matching against the high-resolution mass spectral library, using both full scan and product ion scan spectra. The development of a compact TQ-MS system enables the future potential for rapid on-site analysis, supporting public health, law enforcement, and forensic applications. This innovation paves the way for mobile, point-of-need drug testing and identification, enhancing our ability to respond to emerging drug threats.

papers.title: Unified Mechanistic Insights into Hydrogen Evolution and Oxidation from Homogeneous to Heterogeneous Electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Direct comparisons between homogeneous and heterogeneous electrocatalysis using the same molecular system remain rare, despite their importance for catalyst design and device integration. Here, we investigate the heterogenization of the DuBois–Shaw nickel catalyst [Ni(P Cy ₂N Arg ₂) 2 ] 2 ⁺ (NiCyArg), a well-characterized molecular electrocatalyst for reversible H₂/H⁺ interconversion, and assess whether its established homogeneous mechanistic framework can be extended to surface-confined conditions. The catalyst was successfully immobilized onto edge-plane graphite electrodes via noncovalent interactions. Cyclic voltammetry over a range of pH values under Ar and H₂ demonstrates that the heterogenized catalyst retains its reversibility and bidirectional catalytic activity near the thermodynamic H₂/H⁺ potential, with a pronounced bias toward hydrogen oxidation. Pourbaix analysis reveals redox potentials and p K ₐ values of key intermediates that closely match those obtained under homogeneous conditions, indicating minimal perturbation of the thermodynamic landscape upon immobilization. Kinetic analysis using a simplified ECrECr model shows that the same chemical step remains rate-limiting in both regimes, while internal proton transfer processes are modestly slowed upon surface confinement. Overall, this work provides a quantitative bridge between homogeneous and heterogeneous systems and demonstrates that solution phase mechanistic models can in some conditions be applied to surface immobilised systems.

papers.title: An Open Data Approach for Comparing CO2 Capture Materials
papers.abstract: Recent advances in CO2 capture research have produced a wide range of sorbent materials with diverse properties and sorption parameters, making direct comparison increasingly challenging. In this minireview, we assess representative CO2 capture materials reported between 2020 and 2025 and show that material class alone is no longer a reliable indicator of performance, as different sorbents increasingly overlap in their operational parameter space. Instead, performance must be evaluated using process-relevant, standardized descriptors that reflect realistic operating conditions. To address this need, we suggest an open data approach that compiles comparable and consistently reported metrics for CO2 sorbents, including capacity, enthalpy, kinetics, stability, and indicative cost. By considering the full capture profile of a material rather than a single sorption parameter, this approach enables transparent, multidimensional comparison and supports application-oriented material selection beyond static benchmarking.

papers.title: Can simple exchange heuristics guide us in predicting magnetic properties of solids?
papers.abstract: The Kanamori-Goodenough-Anderson rules are a textbook heuristic for predicting magnetism. They connect bond angles to magnetic ordering in some transition-metal compounds. Such domain knowledge is highly important for building predictive machine learning models in scenarios with scarce data. Yet, there has been no statistical, large-scale evaluation of the heuristic. Here, we evaluate this heuristic relying on both bond angles and orbital occupancy on an experimental database of magnetic structures. We observe that the heuristic is satisfied for 79% of larger bond angles (>110°) but not for bond angles around 90°, and we discuss the exceptions. We then demonstrate that integrating this heuristic into machine learning models for predicting magnetic ordering improves predictive quality. Notably, these magnetism models can also predict whether non-collinear magnetic ordering might occur. Furthermore, the heuristic provides a useful benchmark for evaluating theoretical methods that calculate magnetic properties. We showcase this here for a well-known DFT+ U dataset.

papers.title: Benzo(b)thiophene-Based Compounds with Negative Dielectric Anisotropy for Microwave Applications
papers.abstract: This study explores the synthesis, mesomorphic properties, and optical behavior of functionalized benzo[b]thiophene derivatives with varying alkyl and alkoxy chain lengths. Special emphasis was placed on compounds exhibiting negative dielectric anisotropy and their potential applications in microwave technologies. The compounds were structurally characterized, and their phase transitions were analyzed using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and polarizing optical microscopy (POM). The spectral properties were investigated through UV-Vis absorption and emission fluorescence spectroscopy, showing significant bathochromic shifts and hyperchromic effects in selected compounds. In addition to the mesomorphic and optical characterization, birefringence and dielectric permittivity measurements were conducted to further evaluate the anisotropic behavior of these compounds. These measurements provided insights into the dielectric response and optical anisotropy, which are key for understanding the compounds’ potential in liquid crystal displays and microwave applications.

papers.title: In-Silico Screening and Molecular Dynamics Evaluation of Spirulina Platensis-Derived Compounds as Potential Antiviral Agents Against Dengue Virus NS2b/NS3 Protease
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a global health concern, with no clinically approved antiviral treatment available to date. The NS2b/NS3 serine protease is an essential viral enzyme responsible for polyprotein processing and represents a promising therapeutic target. This computational study employed molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to identify potential antiviral compounds from Spirulina platensis. A total of 19 bioactive compounds isolated from Spirulina platensis were screened against the dengue virus NS2b/NS3 protease (PDB ID: 2FOM) using PyRx virtual screening with AutoDock Vina. The seven compounds with the highest binding affinities were subjected to 100 nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations using the AMBER14 force field at physiological conditions (pH 7.4, 298 K). ADMET analysis and toxicity profiling were performed to evaluate drug-likeness and safety parameters. Tannin (−8.9 kcal/mol) and Rutin (−7.8 kcal/mol) exhibited the strongest binding affinities and remained stable throughout the simulation. RMSD analysis confirmed complex stability (<3.3 Å for six of seven compounds), while hydrogen bonding patterns revealed sustained interactions between ligands and protein residues. ADMET screening identified gallic acid, oleic acid, alpha-terpineol, and beta-sitosterol as possessing favorable oral bioavailability characteristics. Notably, tannin demonstrated minimal toxicity across major organ systems. Our findings suggest that tannin and rutin from Spirulina platensis are promising lead compounds warranting further experimental validation for dengue antiviral drug development. This study demonstrates the potential of marine-derived natural products in accelerating the discovery of new therapeutic agents against viral infections.

papers.title: The Effect of Redox Cycling on the Fate ofTetrahedral Iron in Smectites
Decarboxylative-Derived 2-Aminoallyl Cations in Copper-Catalyzed Spirocyclization of Naphthols and Indoles
papers.abstract: The dearomatization reactions of indoles or naphthols with 2-aminoallyl cations generated from ethynyl methylene carbamates (EMCCs) for the concise synthesis of spirocyclic compounds represent a significant challenge. This difficulty stems from the substantial energy barrier associated with the initial disruption of aromaticity. Nonetheless, a diverse array of spirocyclic compounds can be prepared in moderate to good yields (69-92%) under mild reaction conditions. This synthetic protocol exhibits notable advantages, including a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group tolerance, and simple operational procedures. Furthermore, scale-up experiments and late-stage functionalization studies have further underscored the practical synthetic value of this methodology. Finally, in terms of the reaction mechanism, besides the cyclization reaction, it also involves the 1,5-hydrogen shift, which constructs an unexpected cyclized compound structure and enhances the interest of the research.

papers.title: From Literature Mining to Reaction Prediction and Mechanistic Investigation: An AI-Agent Framework for Microdroplet Chemistry
papers.abstract: In the past decade, microdroplet chemistry has developed rapidly and the remarkable acceleration of chemical reactions within microdroplets has attracted extensive attention. However, despite the growing number of experimental studies, the field remains highly fragmented, posing significant challenges for systematically summarizing and predicting reaction acceleration phenomena. To address this issue, a unified microdroplet chemistry framework is proposed by integrating literature standardization, machine learning–based knowledge construction and multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) guidance. A large language model (LLM)-assisted pipeline was employed for data extraction, resulting in a structured dataset comprising 861 curated records. Unsupervised clustering analysis reveals that microdroplet-accelerated reactions are mainly distributed across organic transformations, redox chemistry, atmospheric/environmental processes and biochemical reactions. Mechanistic analysis further organizes acceleration effects into a multilevel framework, including interfacial electric fields, partial solvation and extreme pH, among others. Based on this foundation, a multi-agent collaborative system consisting of router, prediction, experimental and theoretical agents was developed. The system enables acceleration probability prediction, experimental condition recommendation, interfacial model construction, automated generation of computational input files and strategy design for theoretical simulations. Through application to representative reaction, the proposed agent system is demonstrated to effectively provide information on reaction acceleration and offer useful guidance for further investigation. Overall, the proposed framework provides a systematic and predictive platform for unexplored microdroplet reactions, offering integrated support for experimental design and theoretical investigation in microdroplet chemistry.

papers.title: Non-mean Field Approaches for Surface Catalysis: Analytical Description of Reaction Kinetics with Adsorbate-Adsorbate Interactions
Mechanistic Analysis of Albumin–Ruthenium Conjugates Reveals Redox-Sensitive, SPARC-Associated Extracellular Prodrug Uncaging
papers.abstract: Selective delivery of cytotoxic agents remains limited by systemic toxicity. Here, we show how tumor-microenvironment-relevant redox conditions and SPARC association influence the activity of an albumin-ruthenium conjugate (ARC) artificial metalloenzyme for biorthogonal prodrug uncaging. ARC efficiently uncages alloc-protected substrates at low micromolar concentrations with minimal intrinsic toxicity. Mechanistic studies reveal pronounced redox sensitivity: catalytic activity is rapidly lost under ambient oxygen but preserved under oxygen-limited and antioxidant conditions, identifying reactive oxygen species as the dominant deactivation pathway. This establishes redox sensitivity as a potential selectivity filter favoring hypoxic tumor environments. We further examine how extracellular protein interactions shape ARC function. The matricellular protein SPARC has been implicated in extracellular retention of albumin within the tumor microenvironment, and SPARC-associated ARC remains catalytically active in both biochemical and cell-based systems. Fluorescence and quenching experiments are consistent with ARC activity in extracellular/pericellular spaces, enabling uncaging without cellular internalization. Together, these results define how redox conditions and albumin-SPARC interactions jointly regulate artificial metalloenzyme activity in biological contexts, providing a mechanistic framework for extracellular biorthogonal drug activation. Graphical Abstract: Generated in Biorender (https://BioRender.com).

papers.title: Parallel Pathway Mechanism Describing Crystal Nucleation in Glass-Forming Liquids
papers.abstract: This work introduces a general parallel pathway mechanism (PPM) for crystal nucleation, combining traditional three-dimensional (3D) classical nucleation theory (CNT) with a twodimensional (2D) nucleation framework. This approach offers enhanced flexibility in describing diverse nucleation kinetics observed across various systems, addressing limitations of existing models like the Turnbull-Fisher (T-F) equation. Unlike the T-F equation, which predicts maximal nucleation near the glass transition temperature (Tg), the PPM relates a maximum nucleation rate that can occur over a wide temperature range, from Tg to near the melting point (Tm). That is because the peak nucleation rate can be precisely tuned by adjusting the relative activation energies of the two parallel routes. At higher temperatures, the 2D mechanism dominates, forming nuclei that rapidly convert to 3D clusters. Conversely, the traditional 3D mechanism, leading directly to spherical crystallites, is favored at lower temperatures. The PPM provides a more robust description of experimental data, particularly for systems exhibiting "U-shaped" activation energy profiles, thereby resolving the challenge with modeling the apparent "CNT breakdown" region often observed at temperatures below where the maximum nucleation rate occurs. While this region has been characterized by incomplete glass relaxation due to dramatically slowing system dynamics, the PPM provides a mechanistic explanation for the difference in nucleation kinetics observed on either side of the maximum.

papers.title: Potassium-rich KVPO4F as anode for potassium batteries
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) energy storage materials belonging to KTiOPO4 (KTP) structural compounds have attracted the attention of researchers. We report the novel one-step hydrothermal synthesis and the comparison of electrochemical performance of Potassium vanadium fluoride phosphate (KVPO4F) with potassium-rich counterpart (K1.1VPO4F). Our investigation revealed that introducing more potassium-ion into the pristine KVPO4F has a tremendous impact in boosting the capacity of the material. Meanwhile, K1.1 VPO4F delivered > 150 mAh g-1 @ 26.6 mA g-1 (C/5 rate) in the potential range of 0.001-3 V whereas KVPO4F presented ~70 mAh g-1 under the identical experimental condition. In addition, K1.1VPO4F demonstrated> 100 mAh g-1 at the 400th cycle while charging-discharging repeatedly at 130 mA g-1 (1C rate). Our investigation may pave the route in the development of potassium-ion battery technology.

papers.title: On the relationship between pore size and capacitance in nanoporous carbon electrodes
papers.abstract: Supercapacitors are energy storage devices characterized by fast charging capabilities. The discovery of enhanced capacitance in nanoporous carbons radically challenged the understanding of their charging mechanism, sparkling the development of in situ characterization methods and computational modeling techniques. However, the microscopic origin of this effect remains debated: The importance of pore size on the capacitance put forward in the seminal study was recently questioned in a work focusing on the carbon disorder. Here we close this debate by reconciling these apparently conflicting perspectives. We demonstrate that, at fixed disorder, capacitance does indeed increase with decreasing pore size. Our conclusions are enabled by molecular dynamics simulations methodological advances, that overcome long-standing limitations and yield quantitative agreement with electrochemical measurements. By bridging the gap between earlier observations and recent interpretations, our study provides a unified framework for understanding capacitance in nanoporous materials and offers guidelines for the design of nextgeneration supercapacitors.

papers.title: 2‑CF2H(D)-Imidazolium Salts: A Reagent Platform for Bis(deuterio)difluoromethylation of Alkenes
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: The difluoromethyl group (–CF2H) has emerged as a privileged motif in modern drug design due to its ability to modulate lipophilicity and metabolic stability. Its deuterated analogue, the (deuterio)difluoromethyl group (–CF2D), offers further potential for enhancing metabolic stability and enabling distinct intermolecular interactions. Molecules bearing vicinal difluoromethyl or (deuterio)difluoromethyl groups can serve as potential bioisosteres of pharmacologically important vicinal diols and amino alcohols. Consequently, the direct and simultaneous installation of two difluoromethyl and (deuterio)difluoromethyl groups across alkenes represents an important synthetic target. To address current limitations, we herein introduced 2-CF2H(D)-benzimidazolium salts as a robust, user‑friendly reagent platform for both bis(difluoromethylation) and bis[(deuterio)difluoromethylation] of a broad range of alkenes, including aryl-substituted and less reactive alkyl derivatives. The synthetic utility of this method is demonstrated through late-stage functionalization and gram-scale synthesis of complex molecules. Preliminary mechanistic studies revealed their distinct behavior in copper and photoredox catalysis. As such, this work establishes these reagents as a versatile platform for the simultaneous formation of C–CF2H and C–CF2D bonds, representing a significant advance in the synthesis of valuable fluorinated and deuterated compounds.

papers.title: Determination of the Enantiomeric Makeup of Ketamine in Street Drug Samples
papers.abstract: Ketamine is an anesthetic drug used recreationally for its psychoactive effects. Recently, the use of ketamine has increased. Ketamine is a chiral compound with two enantiomers, S-ketamine (esketamine) and R-ketamine (arketamine). Though the S- enantiomer is more potent, pharmaceutical ketamine is most often racemic. Asymmetric synthesis or optical resolution can be performed to increase the percentage of S-ketamine in samples, thereby increasing the potency. To investigate the form of ketamine present in the illicit drug supply, chiral liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) was used to analyze 139 drug paraphernalia residue or drug product samples submitted from August 2025 to February 2026. All samples analyzed were found to contain racemic ketamine.

papers.title: A Quantum Mechanical Study on the Degradation of Venturia inaequalis induced by Bacterial Metabolites
papers.abstract: In this treatise, innovative solutions for the bio-control of Venturia inaequalis are investigated through the synergistic action of selected bacterial and fungal species. This work proposes an appropriate microscopic-scale mathematical modeling to analyze the degradation mechanisms of the different matrices within the pathogen’s cell wall. Through the formulation of the model, a specific interaction cluster (2 O − 2 H − 2 C ) responsible for the selective destruction of chitin is identified, the dynamics of which are described by means of a rigorous extension of the mathematical formalism. The application of quantum field theory allows for a comprehensive dissection of the diverse types of molecular interactions, leading to the analytical visualization of chemical bond cleavage modes. Finally, the renormalization process of the model requires the integration of a Yukawa term, introduced to stabilize the interaction field and ensure the theoretical consistency of the proposed bio-control system.

papers.title: Mapping Site-Specific Water Uptake and Transport in Covalent Organic Frameworks through Molecular Dynamics and Operando Vibrational Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Water transport in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is often described in terms of pore size or hydrophilicity, yet the atomistic origins of uptake and mobility remain poorly resolved. Here, we resolve site-specific water adsorption and transport pathways by integrating molecular dynamics simulations with humidity-controlled operando FT-IR spectroscopy. Using two structurally related COFs, TUS-46 and TUS-44, we show that water infiltration is governed by a chemically heterogeneous energy landscape in which oxygen-containing functionalities act as dynamic interaction nodes. TUS-46 exhibits rapid pore filling driven by cooperative hydrogen-bond network formation, whereas the same interactions restrict long-range diffusion, revealing a fundamental decoupling between affinity and mobility. Vibrational signatures, including coupled C=O red shifts and C–C blue shifts, directly confirm site-specific hydration and reversible framework–water interactions. This combined approach establishes a mechanistic framework in which uptake, redistribution, and transport emerge from the interplay of local chemistry and dynamics, offering new design principles for COFs in water-related technologies.

papers.title: Identification and Characterization of Surfactant Binding Sites on the SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein and its Variants by Microseconds-Long Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: While airborne coronavirus virions penetrate respiratory airways, lung surfactants (LS) adsorb on spike proteins and may hinder their binding to cell receptors. In this work, we utilize microsecond-long unbiased and adaptive sampling molecular dynamics simulations performed on the Anton 2 supercomputer to elucidate the molecular mechanisms and dynamic nature of adsorption of lung surfactant lipids and cholesterol to the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and its Delta and Omicron variants. From unbiased simulations of spontaneous multi-surfactant binding, we show that surfactants tend to destabilize the protein and induce enhanced structural fluctuations that can influence the receptor-binding interface. We identify four surfactant binding sites (SBS) that are conserved across the variants, one of which corresponds to the experimentally identified fatty acid binding site (FABS). We analyze the energetics of multi-surfactant binding and show that FABS is the strongest binding site on the RBD, consistent with our previous coarse-grained simulations. Using adaptive sampling with the tempered binding approach, we demonstrate unbinding and rebinding of surfactants from selected binding sites, elucidating the structural dynamics and the binding enthalpy profiles. Identification and quantitative characterization of the binding sites affinity and stability provide a better understanding of the specifics of the lung surfactant–spike protein interactions and may inform the design of surfactant therapies for prevention and mitigation of coronavirus infections.

papers.title: Trends in Fentanyl Adulteration from Rapid Drug Analysis and Research (RaDAR) Drug Checking Samples, January 2024 to January 2026
papers.abstract: In recent years, the United States fentanyl market has experienced a significant increase in adulteration. Street fentanyl samples now often contain local anesthetics, industrial chemicals, veterinary sedatives and other drugs, making tracking more difficult and necessary. While traditional data sources, such as forensic data, often do not report non-controlled adulterants, a growing field of laboratory-based drug checking for public health programs is focused on providing nearcomplete chemical insights into street drug samples. In this work, fentanyl adulteration trends from the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s (NIST) Rapid Drug Analysis and Research (RaDAR) program are examined. Summarizing data from samples collected between January 2024 and January 2026, the detection of α2-agonists, industrial chemicals, local anesthetics, fentanyl analogs, and other drugs in the fentanyl supply is discussed. In addition to qualitative prevalence data, information on the quantitative makeup of these compounds in the fentanyl samples is provided. Data were analyzed for samples collected from the East and West regions of the United States, highlighting key geographical and temporal differences in the street supply.

papers.title: Topology-Informed Design Rules for Deconstructable Thermoset Copolymer Networks
papers.abstract: Existing models of thermoset deconstruction facilitated by incorporating cleavable comonomers rely on a mean-field reverse gel point paradigm, which predicts network dissolution once cleavable bonds reach a critical stoichiometric threshold, but does not account for where those bonds reside within the network architecture. Using reactive coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations coupled with graph-theoretic analysis, we extend this stoichiometric picture to show that deconstructability is governed by the curing-imprinted network topology rather than stoichiometry alone. This topological organization is hierarchical: at the local scale, the elastic effectiveness of crosslink junctions determines which crosslinks constitute the load-bearing scaffold; at the mesoscale, the crosslinking rate kinetically templates that scaffold into topologically modular communities—densely crosslinked clusters connected by sparse bridging strands that sustain network connectivity. Using betweenness centrality to identify nodes that disproportionately lie on inter-community shortest paths, we demonstrate that effective deconstruction of the network into macromolecular fragments requires cleavable comonomers to intercept these high-centrality bridging strands. We further find that under uniform, disassortative comonomer incorporation, this topological requirement provides a mechanistic basis for extending the reverse gel point to incorporate network topology. We also show that modularity imposes a fundamental limit on fragment uniformity that persists even when the centrality requirement is met. Finally, we demonstrate that chain stiffness provides a nearly independent lever to suppress mechanically redundant crosslinks and raise the glass transition temperature without significantly altering the deconstruction outcome. Together, these findings reframe the thermoset design space around network topology and provide actionable guidelines for engineering thermoset copolymers with predictable deconstructability and targeted thermomechanical performance.

papers.title: Chemical Characteristics Driving Formability in Li-Excess Disordered Rocksalt Cathodes
papers.abstract: Li-excess disordered rocksalts are promising next-generation Li-ion battery cathode materials that feature a flexible, site-disordered cation sublattice. Understanding how different cations and their respective ratios can be adjusted is crucial to the further development of these materials. Here, we systematically conceive of a large set of potential disordered rocksalt formulations in which the redox-inactive charge compensator site has been substituted with a wide array of cations. From the phase purity of target formulations, we derive how the features of substituent charge compensator species impact the formability of disordered rocksalts. We find that cation size, cation tendencies to be in a distorted octahedron, and formation enthalpy of competing impurity phases are the primary drivers of amenability to form a locally disordered, single phase product. A subset of rocksalt formulations is also tested as Li-ion battery cathodes.

papers.title: Phase-Engineered 1T/2H-WS2 Heterostructures in Hybrid Carbon Networks for High-Rate and Durable Sodium-Ion Storage
papers.abstract: Metallic 1T transition-metal dichalcogenides are promising for sodium-ion storage because of their higher electrical conductivity and faster ion transport than semiconducting 2H counterparts, yet stabilizing the 1T phase remains challenging. Here, we report phase-engineered WS2/hybrid-carbon nanocomposites prepared by lithium-assisted exfoliation and freeze-drying, delivering high-performance sodium-ion battery (SIB) anode. Integration of reduced graphene oxide and multiwalled carbon nanotubes (rGO and MWCNTs) induces partial phase conversion (2H→1T) in WS2 and yields a stabilized 1T/2H mixed-phase architecture within a conductive carbon network. Structural and spectroscopic analyses support the coexistence of 1T & 2H domains and reveal strong interfacial coupling with the carbon-scaffold, thereby enhancing electrical conductivity, suppressing nanosheet restacking, and improving structural stability. As a result, the 1T/2H-WS2@rGO/MWCNTs composite delivers a reversible capacity of ~500 mAh g-1 at 25 mA g-1, excellent rate capability up to 5 A g-1, and long-term cycling stability over 1000 cycles with negligible capacity decay, ~99.2% capacity retention, together with strong full-cell performance when paired with NaFePO4. First-principles calculations further reveal stronger Na-adsorption and a wider thermodynamically stable sodiation window for 1T-WS2 than for 2H-WS2. These results highlight the combination of phase-engineering and conductive carbon-scaffolding as an effective strategy for developing fast and durable WS2-based anodes for SIBs.

papers.title: Universal Performance Improvements in CuSCN-based Electronic and Photonic Devices Enabled by CuBr2 Doping
papers.abstract: Copper(I) thiocyanate (CuSCN) has become one of the standard hole-transporting layers for an ever-expanding range of device applications. However, solution-processed CuSCN films suffer from hole-trapping SCN − vacancies (V SCN ) and limited p-type conductivity. Herein, we show that doping CuSCN with copper(II) bromide (CuBr 2 ) can deliver dual functions of defect healing and p-doping, greatly improving the hole-transport properties. Applied as a p-channel in thin-film transistors, the field-effect hole mobility is increased by 8-fold up to 0.08 cm 2 V -1 s -1 while crucially keeping a low off-current, unlike previous p-doping attempts. Further, CuBr 2 -doped CuSCN exploited as a hole-transport layer (HTL) in organic solar cells improves charge collection and reduces trap-assisted recombination, pushing power conversion efficiency from ~16% up to 18.3%. Remarkably, the same HTL yields outstanding performance for single-component near-infrared (NIR) organic photodetectors, an emerging simple device structure based solely on organic acceptor as the photoabsorber. CuBr 2 doping effectively suppresses the dark current and improves all device metrics, achieving a specific detectivity of ~10 12 Jones at 840 nm and a cut-off frequency up to 0.56 MHz. The universal improvements of device performance highlight the synergistic benefits of combined defect healing and p-doping effects, enabled by CuBr 2 doping.

papers.title: Synergistic and Dye-Sensitized Contributions in the Visible-Light Photodegradation of Dyes over a Nickel Oxide/Carbon Dot@ZIF-8 Heterogeneous Composite
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis and performance of a ternary nickel oxide nanoparticle/carbon dot@zeolitic imidazole metal-organic framework (NiO/CDs@ZIF-8) photocatalyst for the visible-light driven degradation of organic dyes in water. Methylene blue was used as a model dye owing to its widespread use as a benchmark in photocatalytic studies. Structural and spectroscopic characterization confirms the formation of a heterogeneous composite in which carbon dots are encapsulated within the ZIF-8 framework and NiO nanoparticles are dispersed on the external surface. Systematic variation in CDs and NiO loadings was also investigated to optimize the material’s performance. Under visible-light irradiation, the optimized composite exhibits enhanced activity in degrading methylene blue compared with its individual components and binary counterparts. A synergistic mechanism is proposed in which carbon dots act as the primary sensitizer, NiO promotes charge separation, and ZIF-8 provides a scaffold that concentrates reactants at reactive interfaces. Importantly, our work shows that dye-sensitized photochemical processes can contribute to overall degradation, highlighting the need for a more realistic, holistic perspective when assessing photocatalytic activity in organic dye systems.

papers.title: Quantum crystallography: X-ray orbitals are Kohn-Sham orbitals
papers.abstract: It is suggested that, in restrictive ideal circumstance, the interacting electronic energy of a system can be obtained directly from experimentally accessible X-ray orbitals through inverse Kohn-Sham equation functional integration. The argument rests on the identity, within a unitary transformation, between experimentally fitted X-ray orbitals and theoretically calculated Kohn-Sham orbitals, both of which – in ideal circumstances - yield the same electron density. Using X-ray orbitals, one may evaluate both the Kohn-Sham kinetic energy and the interacting potential energy by functional integration of the exact Kohn-Sham potential, taken directly from the Kohn-Sham equations, expressed in atomic units (a.u.), 𝑣𝑠(𝐫) = 𝜇 + 1 2 ∇2𝜑𝜇(𝐫) 𝜑𝜇(𝐫)

papers.title: Practical Considerations for Operando 7Li NMR in Coin and Pouch Cells
papers.abstract: Operando nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unique insight into chemical changes in batteries during use, but has largely been limited to custom plastic cells. Unfortunately, the metal casings that house commercial batteries distort and shield radiofrequency (RF) fields required for excitation and detection in NMR. Here, we use operando 7 Li NMR spectroscopy to study metal-encased batteries in both coin and pouch cell formats without modifying the cell or casing. We benchmark NMR spectra obtained from stainless steel coin cells and aluminium-laminate pouch cells to plastic coin cells and show that casing composition, auxillary hardware, and sample placement strongly influence observed shift, signal intensity, and lineshape due to bulk magnetic susceptibility effects and RF attenuation upon interacting with cell parts. These effects are most severe in stainless steel coin cells (and in particular 316 grade stainless steel), but can be mitigated through the use of Al spacers and springs, while retaining the stainless steel caps. In light of these considerations, we leverage operando 7 Li NMR to track lithium

papers.title: Machine-learning–enabled virtual screening delivers scaffold-diverse, experimentally validated, c-MET inhibitors
papers.abstract: c-MET (c-mesenchymal-epithelial transition factor) is dysregulated across multiple cancers yet reports of prospectively validated ATP-competitive inhibitor chemotypes remain limited. We sought to discover new c-MET inhibitors by coupling scaffold-aware machine learning with explicit-solvent structure-based triage and targeted assays. A curated activity set yielded a tuned support vector machine that enriched ~5 million molecules. Docking and pose filtering produced 114 candidates; 36 were analyzed using 200 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, from which six were advanced to experimental validation, including two candidates that inhibited c-MET with IC50 values of 1.2 and 18 μM and demonstrated cellular activity consistent with MET dependence (gastric > NSCLC > HeLa). MD revealed stable class-I poses that pack the ligand at the hinge (Tyr1159/Met1160), traverse the Val1092/Met1211 hydrophobic groove, and engage the activation-loop edge (Tyr1230 with auxiliary Asp1222/Arg1208 contacts). Variant docking suggested tolerance to the common mutations D1228N/H/V and D1231Y with moderate sensitivity to Y1230C/H. This work delivers validated and structurally innovative class-I c-MET chemotypes demonstrating that a multi-stage workflow integrating machine learning, docking, and physics-based scoring for ultra-large libraries can accelerate hit identification. The same strategy is directly applicable to other receptor tyrosine kinases that share flanking, hinge-anchoring, hydrophobic sub pockets, and to protein ligand discovery more broadly.

papers.title: Heteroatom Homolytic Substitution (het-SH2): A General Platform for Dialkyl Ether Synthesis
papers.abstract: The modular and selective synthesis of dialkyl ethers, particularly sterically congested variants, remains a longstanding challenge in drug discovery and medicinal chemistry. Hindered alkyl ethers are especially desirable given their prevalence in bioactive natural products and favorable physicochemical properties. Classically, dialkyl ether synthesis relies on nucleophilic substitution strategies; however, SN2 reactions are fundamentally limited by steric congestion at the transition state, while SN1 pathways proceed through promiscuous carbocation intermediates prone to elimination, rearrangement, and loss of stereogenic information. Herein, we report a radical-based paradigm for general dialkyl ether synthesis enabled by an underutilized heteroatom homolytic substitution (het-SH2) mechanism. This mechanistic paradigm overcomes the intrinsic limitations of classical polar substitution chemistry by leveraging carbon-centered radicals generated under mild conditions that are insensitive to steric congestion in the bond-forming transition state. Utilizing a titanium-based catalytic platform in combination with visible-light photoredox catalysis, we demonstrate the efficient coupling of carboxylic acid-derived redox-active esters with alcohols across a broad range of substitution patterns, including 3°–2°, 3°–1°, 2°–2°, and 2°–1° architectures. This strategy grants access to dialkyl ether chemical space largely inaccessible through conventional approaches, including sterically demanding BCP ether bioisosteres, and enables late-stage diversification of complex pharmaceutical scaffolds. Given the generality of the underlying het-SH2 mechanism, this platform is expected to serve as a broadly applicable blueprint for radical-mediated heteroatom bond formation.

papers.title: thermosetMC: Simulation and Fragment-Based Inference of Crosslink Density and Kinetics in Deconstructable Copolymer Thermosets
papers.abstract: Permanent crosslinks can endow thermoset polymers with thermomechanical stability but also render them difficult to recycle. Cleavable comonomer additives can enable selective deconstruction, yet the effective inter-chain crosslink densities of chain-growth thermoset networks remain poorly understood and cannot be inferred from bulk observables alone. Herein, we introduce thermosetMC, a graph-based kinetic Monte Carlo framework for chain-growth thermoset network formation and deconstruction, demonstrated here for ROMP copolymerization of dicyclopentadiene (DCPD) with cleavable comonomers (e.g., silyl-ether iPrSi8), cyclopentene crosslinking, and selective cleavage to generate deconstruction fragment ensembles. Matching experimental dissolution behavior calibrates a low effective inter-chain crosslink density. Our studies reveal a sharp deconstruction percolation boundary dictated by the balance between cleavable unit fraction and effective inter-chain connectivity, with an empirical trend x/f ≈ 4c0/f that holds across cleavable comonomer loadings and crosslink densities. This scaling provides a practical design rule to target deconstructability in deconstructable thermoset networks. Parameter sweeps across reactivity ratios, crosslink kinetics, and reversible propagation identify kinetic regimes for high deconstructability. Finally, fitting thermosetMC to experimental residual-mass data and fragment molecular weight distributions by Bayesian optimization yields an effective kinetic parameter set that reproduces the main experimental trends.

papers.title: Architecture-Specific Failure Modes in hERG QSAR Predictions for Iboga Alkaloids: A Within-Family Empirical Test of the Binding-vs-Blockade Limitation
papers.abstract: The Comprehensive in vitro Proarrhythmia Assay (CiPA) initiative [Sager et al., 2014, Colatsky et al., 2016] and subsequent computational electrophysiology literature [Gomis-Tena et al., 2020, Li et al., 2017] have established that static-descriptor QSAR for hERG blockade has fundamental limitations when binding affinity dissociates from functional blockade. We test this limitation empirically on the iboga alkaloid compound class, a single natural-product family that contains both binding-blockade-correlated regimes (natural compounds) and binding-blockade-decoupled regimes (rationally designed analogs) within one structural scaffold, providing a clean within-family test bed. Three architecturally divergent hERG QSAR tools (Pred-hERG 5.0 [Sanches et al., 2024], LightGBM on ECFP4 fingerprints; ADMET-AI 2.0.1 [Swanson et al., 2024], Chemprop graph neural network; admetSAR 2.0 [Yang et al., 2019], SVM on hand-crafted descriptors) were evaluated on canonical isomeric SMILES for eight iboga alkaloid compounds sourced from PubChem with explicit chain-of-custody documentation. Two of three architectures (GNN, SVM) classify the rationally designed safer-scaffold analog 18-methoxycoronaridine as a hERG Blocker, in disagreement with experimental data (Alper et al. 2016: IC50 >50 µM; Koenig et al. 2013: IC50 14.9 µM, both Non-blocker at the 10 µM threshold). The fingerprint-based Pred-hERG correctly classifies 18-MC as Non-blocker on canonical SMILES, demonstrating architecture-specific sensitivity to side-chain perturbations that the other two architectures do not exhibit. In the opposite direction, Pred-hERG misclassifies noribogaine (the active pharmaceutical ingredient of DMX-1001 from DemeRx IB; FDA IND accepted 2026-04-23, Phase II alcohol use disorder) at the consensus level as Non-blocker, despite multi-source-confirmed experimental IC50 of 2.86–3 µM (Alper et al. 2016; Koenig et al. 2017 iPSC). The Pred-hERG sub-model breakdown reveals that the binary classifier correctly calls noribogaine a Blocker (69.7% confidence) but the deployed service’s consensus rule, combining binary with multiclass and regression sub-models, outputs Non-blocker as the user-facing verdict. The false-negative is a property of the consensus rule rather than any single sub-model. Similarly, Pred-hERG misclassifies natural (-)-voacangine as Nonblocker at 94.6% confidence on canonical SMILES, despite experimental IC50 of 2.25 µM (Alper et al. 2016, single-source patch-clamp characterization). The two-camp pattern (GNN + SVM false-positives on designed analogs; LightGBM/ECFP4 false-negatives on natural potent blockers) reflects how each architectural approach encodes the scaffold-versus-side-chain distinction; both failure directions trace to the kinetic state-dependence that prior CiPA-aligned literature has established theoretically. Independent ECFP4 Tanimoto analysis against Pred-hERG 5.0’s actual published training set (7,307 compounds, 3,918 unique Murcko scaffolds; Sanches et al. 2024 Supporting Information 2) returns maximum similarities of 0.244–0.403 for the eight iboga compounds, with zero scaffold overlap; despite this, Pred-hERG’s reported applicability domain assessment labels seven of eight iboga compounds tested as “Inside AD” across binary, multiclass, and regression sub-models, flagging only oxa-noribogaine (the one compound with a benzofuran-replaced indole) as “Outside AD.” Pred-hERG’s published methodology references the Tropsha-Golbraikh AD framework without specifying the operational similarity metric, threshold, or formula. Predictions for the two iboga alkaloids without published patch-clamp hERG measurements (coronaridine, oxa-noribogaine) are pre-registered on OSF (https://osf.io/uwvx4/, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/UWVX4, 2026-05-12) with falsification dispositions and SHA-256 hash anchors prior to any future experimental electrophysiology validation. Under the April 2026 Executive Order accelerating FDA review of psychedelic compounds, the demonstrated false-negative pattern on DMX-1001’s active ingredient implies that Pred-hERG-style fingerprint triage cannot substitute for experimental electrophysiology on this compound class; the discovery-pipeline false-positive pattern from GNN/SVM tools similarly cannot be relied upon for prioritizing rationally designed safer-scaffold candidates. The contribution to the CiPA-aligned literature is a clean empirical demonstration on a clinically active compound class, with the architecture-specific asymmetric failure pattern as a previously-undescribed elaboration.

papers.title: Nanoliter scale contact drop printing of polymer coatings for waveguide enhanced Raman sensors
papers.abstract: Waveguide-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (WERS) is an emerging chemical sensor platform in which Raman spectra are collected from molecules interacting with the evanescent field near the surface of a photonic chip waveguide. A spiral waveguide geometry enhances Raman signal by providing a relatively long waveguide path length on a small chip surface area. It has been demonstrated that the WERS signal can be further increased by orders of magnitude when the spiral waveguide is coated by a thin film of polymer acting as a sorbent to locally increase the concentration of the target analyte. While printing methods are widely available for water soluble materials such as biomolecules, these have limited performance when applied to polymer sorbents. The desire to expand WERS to multiplex sensors on a single chip has led to the need to develop printing methods to selectively coat discrete waveguide spirals with a distinct polymer. Here, we report on the development of a contact drop printing method in which a nanoliter scale pendant droplet of polymer solution is transferred to the chip surface. A novel printing nozzle has been developed to pin the contact line of the droplet and thus prevent rising meniscus on the outside of the nozzle. A computer controlled XYZ positioning system is then used to place the droplet at the center of the spiral waveguide. Upon solvent evaporation, a circular spot of polymer coating remains. Coatings are demonstrated having desired thickness and uniformity for use in WERS. This new printing technique offers a rapid and low cost process for printing patterns of polymer films without direct contact of the nozzle to the printing surface. The method also does not suffer from limitations in solution viscosity and surface tension imposed by ink-jet printing.

papers.title: Design Rules for Tuning Charge-Transfer Emission in Donor-Acceptor Nanohoops
papers.abstract: Donor-acceptor (D-A) nanohoops provide a unique platform for tuning emission in curved π-systems through modulation of the frontier molecular orbitals as well as through charge-transfer (CT) interactions. Herein, we report a modular, building-block synthetic strategy enabling a systematic structure-property study of D-A nanohoops incorporating the electron acceptor benzothiadiazole (BT) and the electron donor thiophene (thio). Independent variations of ring size, D-A connectivity, and donor incorporation afford predictable tuning of the fluorescent emission across the visible spectrum, large relative Stokes shifts, and pronounced solvatofluorochromism. Combined experimental and computational analysis establishes design rules for fluorescent emission, demonstrating that increased acceptor strain, through-bond D-A interactions, and increased content of electron-modulating units leads to bathochromic shifts in emission, enabling access to highly red-shifted emission as exemplified by compound 7.
