StrainViz calculations reveal that five-membered donor units redistribute strain across the nanohoop scaffold, influencing molecular geometry, while the observed photophysical trends are primarily governed by D-A charge-transfer interactions. Together, these findings position D-A nanohoops as a predictive platform for engineering curved π-systems with a range of different photophysical properties.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of Electron Localization-Delocalization Matrices
papers.abstract: The electron Localization-Delocalization Matrix (LDM) of a molecule, condenses valuable information pertaining to its electron density distribution and its electron pair density distribution. Recent efforts have set out to relate the LDM to graph theory, showing that one can correlate the localization and delocalization indices with several experimental quantities including, pKa values and UV-vis maxima. In the present work, we aim to predict the LDMs of the more than 30k molecules reported in the AIMEL dataset. We explored the prediction of LDMs by training a series of neural networks using different vectorization schemes of the Coulomb matrices. Our model training experiments show that one can properly predict the LDMs of small organic molecules through their CMs, setting the basis for more accurate models.

papers.title: Remote Asymmetric amination of Naphthalene-Blocked Alkynes with amines
papers.abstract: Absract： In this study, we rationally designed and successfully established a versatile copper-catalyzed divergent reaction system by employing alkynyl naphthalates as key substrates. This tunable catalytic strategy exhibits distinct and controllable reaction pathways depending on the type of amine reagents: primary amines undergo a formal [4+1] annulation process to efficiently construct a variety of polycyclic pyrrole derivatives, while secondary amines selectively participate in an enantioselective ε-position substitution reaction, providing chiral alkynyl naphthylamines with high enantiopurity. The present protocol proceeds under mild reaction conditions, featuring a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Notably, gram-scale synthesis and diverse downstream derivatizations of the target products have been successfully achieved, which strongly validate the practicality and synthetic utility of this methodology. We anticipate that this efficient and divergent catalytic approach will serve as a powerful tool for the rapid assembly of structurally diverse polycyclic pyrrole frameworks and the asymmetric synthesis of valuable chiral alkynyl naphthylamines, thus offering a valuable platform for copper-catalyzed divergent synthesis with important implications for organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry.

papers.title: Enantioselective Rhodium-Catalyzed Allylic Addition of Pyrazoles to Terminal 1,3-Enynes
papers.abstract: Round and round – From 1,3-Enynes to Allenes and beyond. Enynes and pyrazoles are prevalent structural motifs in both natural products and pharmaceuticals. Consequently, methods for the selective functionalization of enynes, as well as the enantioselective incorporation of pyrazoles, are of significant interest. Allylation reactions are very important for target-oriented synthesis since the allyl group provides a versatile platform for all kinds of further transformation. Herein, we report the development of a rhodium-catalyzed allylic addition of pyrazoles to terminal 1,3-enynes, enabled by a rhodium/(R)-Xyl-BINAP catalytic system. The transformation proceeds through a 2-fold catalytic process involving an allene intermediate and delivers the 1,4-diamination products in high yields (up to 94%), with exclusive (Z)-diastereoselectivity and high enantiomeric ratios (up to 99:1 er), and broad functional group tolerance. The present method demonstrates the extension of our group’s established rhodium-catalyzed allylic addition of (pro)nucleophiles to allenes and alkynes towards a twofold allylic functionalization of 1,3-enynes.

papers.title: Visualizing a Li-depleted amorphous cathode–electrolyte interphase in sulfide solid-state batteries using in situ cryogenic electron microscopy
papers.abstract: Electrochemical degradation at the cathode/solid-electrolyte interface critically limits the performance of sulfide-based solid-state batteries; however, its nanoscale origin remains unclear. Here, we directly visualize the structural and chemical evolutions of the LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 /Li 6 PS 5 Cl interface during charging using in situ scanning transmission electron microscopy combined with electron energy-loss spectroscopy and energy-filtered nanobeam electron diffraction. A potential-controlled sample-preparation protocol is developed to preserve the native interphase structure during sample preparation, and low-dose-rate cryogenic electron microscopy suppresses electron-beam-induced damage. At the uncoated interface, charging induced the formation of a ~50-nm-thick Li-depleted cathode–electrolyte interphase. In regions within ~20 nm of the interface, the Li concentration decreased to below x = 4 in Li x PS 5 Cl, leading to complete amorphization of the solid electrolyte. Machine-learning-potential molecular dynamics simulations reveal that Li depletion destabilizes the argyrodite Li 6 PS 5 Cl framework and increases the Li-ion migration barrier, thereby identifying the origin of interfacial resistance. Conversely, LiNbO y -coated interfaces exhibited neither pronounced Li depletion nor significant amorphization, even with coating thicknesses as small as 5 nm, thereby elucidating the buffering mechanism of LiNbO y at the cathode/sulfide-solid-electrolyte interface. These results establish Li-depletion-induced structural disorder as a fundamental transport-limiting mechanism at cathode interfaces employing sulfide solid electrolytes, providing a framework for interface engineering.

papers.title: Structured disassembly dictates the lifetime of physical gels in open environments
papers.abstract: The reversible bonds that give physical gels their viscoelasticity and self-healing also drive their dissolution in fluid environments, where most applications operate. This dissolution has been described phenomenologically, system by system, leaving gel functional lifetimes unpredictable from molecular design. We show dissolution is not passive but a structured disassembly, spatially partitioned into bulk swelling and surface erosion, and temporally sequenced with erosion driven by prior swelling. An analytical framework grounded in bond-exchange kinetics and polymer diffusion yields closed-form expressions for both modes. Real-time imaging of DNA-crosslinked gels, with crosslink kinetics tunable more than three orders of magnitude, validates these expressions using only independently measured molecular parameters. Physical gel lifetimes thus become predictable, and ultimately designable.

papers.title: The 18 electron rule and metal-metal bonding
papers.abstract: Understanding the bonding between main group elements involves the use of the qualitative rules of valence and Lewis' octet rule, supplemented by theoretical calculations. For transition metal complexes the now applicable 18 electron rule is complicated by the variable nature of metal valences. As such determining metal-metal bonding can be significantly more problematic regardless of the sophistication of the computational results. This work shows how a novel electron counting protocol combined with both molecular orbital and topological analyses of the electron density can be used to analyze metal-metal interactions in dimolybdenum complexes.

papers.title: An X-Shaped Chiral Non-Fullerene n-Type Semiconductor: Application in Perovskite Solar Cells and Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity
papers.abstract: The development of a new building block for creating solution-processable amorphous n-type semiconductors provides a platform of fundamental importance for advanced organic electronic materials. We have recently demonstrated that oxidative inner‑bond cleavage of readily available dibenzo[g,p]chrysene affords a nonplanar figure‑eight macrocycle that bears electron‑withdrawing carbonyl groups, namely cyclobisbiphenylenecarbonyl (CBBC). Here, we report a highly electron‑accepting derivative of CBBC (CBBC‑TIC), in which the CBBC core is connected to four electron‑withdrawing dicyanomethylene‑3‑indanone (IC) units via thiophene spacers. The distinctive X‑shaped molecular structure of CBBC‑TIC enables the solution-process fabrication of a homogeneous amorphous film with good electron conductivity. Perovskite solar cells that contain CBBC‑TIC as the electron-transport layer achieved a power conversion efficiency of 20.6%, which is comparable to that obtained with the benchmark fullerene derivative [6,6]-phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM). Furthermore, the enantiomers of CBBC-TIC exhibited spin-selective electron transport arising from the chirality-induced spin-selectivity (CISS) effect, with remarkably high enantiospecific magnetic conductance asymmetry values of up to 80% in amorphous films. These findings demonstrate that CBBC represents a versatile molecular component for the creation of advanced non‑fullerene n-type semiconductors.

papers.title: On the Role of Symmetry Breaking Triplet State Conformations in the Phosphorescence of Some Dinuclear Pt(II) complexes
papers.abstract: Dinuclear design of Pt(II) and Ir(III) complexes have been shown to afford significant enhancement of phosphorescence rate, compared to the mononuclear analogues, due to the twice the number of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) paths of the emitting triplet states to singlet states. However, the dinuclear complex Pt 2 Cl 2 , coordinated to a bridging ligand of bis-N^C^N coordinating motif with an alkoxy group at the para-position to each coordinated carbon atom and ancillary coordinated chlorides, has been reported an outlier as its phosphorescence rate is comparable to that of its mononuclear analogue PtCl . Besides that, Pt 2 Cl 2 was assigned Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence (TADF) properties, unusual for Pt(II) complexes with fast decaying triplet state. To understand the photophysical behavior of Pt 2 Cl 2 and its analogues better, we conducted room temperature and cryogenic spectroscopic investigations as well as a computational study of Pt 2 Cl 2 , its mononuclear analogue PtCl , and dinuclear analogue with iodides, Pt 2 I 2 . Our investigations found that the decrease of emission decay time of Pt 2 Cl 2 and Pt 2 I 2 with temperature is by a large extend due to the enhancement of non-radiative decay rate, rather than activation of TADF. Spectroscopic data in line with computational studies of Pt 2 Cl 2 show that in the T 1 state one of the alkoxy groups rotates to conjugate its lone pair with the bridging ligand which breaks the electronic symmetry and shifts the triplet state localization onto one coordination site thus resulting in phosphorescence rate similar to that of the mononuclear PtCl . The direction and extend of this symmetry breaking rotation differentiates structural conformers as well as their properties. Due to the increase of state’s dipole moment in the symmetry-broken structure, the increase of medium polarity is understood to enhance the localization of the T 1 state on one coordination center which agrees with the accompanying decrease of phosphorescence rate. The T 1 state conformers of Pt 2 I 2 have over twice faster phosphorescence than those of Pt 2 Cl 2 and remain less distinct electronically from each other, which is understood as due to the much stronger electronic effect of iodides, compared to chlorides. Computational analysis showed that the previous report on T 1 state character of Pt 2 I 2 as having σ→π* type transition symmetry is erroneous, likely due to the self-interaction error of the DFT method, and the true character is of π→π* type transition symmetry. Our work shows that enhancement of phosphorescence rate in dinuclear structures is assailable by symmetry breaking geometry reorganization in the emitting triplet state which must be accounted for. The previously presented argumentation for TADF properties is found to be an artefact of flawed analysis not accounting for enhancement of non-radiative decay rate with temperature increase.

papers.title: The topographic origin of chemomechanical failure in high-nickel cathodes revealed by operando dark-field X-ray microscopy
papers.abstract: Mechanical degradation in high-nickel cathodes, driven by anisotropic volume changes, remains a primary bottleneck for the lifetime of high-energy density batteries. Yet, the nanoscale origins of strain and defect initiation within individual primary particles remain unclear. Here, in the first application of operando dark-field X-ray microscopy (DFXM) to a battery system, we directly observe a dislocation wall nucleating from a pre-existing topographical flaw on the surface of a single NMC 811 primary particle. We show that failure is not stochastic, but deterministically driven by surface topography; the flaw creates a local stress concentration of ∼100 MPa, exceeding the material’s yield strength, while the bulk particle remains elastic. This observation establishes a direct physical link between primary particle surface morphology and the onset of irreversible plasticity. These findings prescribe a clear design rule: beyond bulk chemical stability, engineering particles with pristine, defect-free surfaces is essential for mitigating strain localisation and extending battery lifetime.

papers.title: Democratizing LYTACs—A Modular Click Chemistry Platform for the Rapid Assembly of Lysosome-Targeting Chimeras
papers.abstract: Lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) are emerging therapeutics that mediate extracellular targeted protein degradation. Through simultaneous engagement of a target protein of interest and a lysosomal trafficking receptor, these bifunctional molecules can facilitate the degradation of both secreted and cell-surface proteins. The original LYTACs were designed to engage the cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor (CI-M6PR) via complex glycopolymer or glycopolypeptide ligands conjugated to target-specific antibodies. However, the complexity of these ligands has limited the broader adoption of LYTACs as research tools. Here we describe a simple, rapid, and modular click chemistry platform for the generation of CI-M6PR-binding LYTACs. The approach utilizes only commercially available reagents and standard laboratory equipment and allows for the conversion of virtually any antibody into a LYTAC. This method for “democratizing” LYTAC generation should facilitate the widespread adoption of these tools for biological discovery.

papers.title: Radical-Assisted Enhanced Intersystem Crossing Enables Efficient Triplet Photochemical Reactions: Application to a BODIPY Photocage
papers.abstract: Photoreaction efficiency via the triplet state is often reduced by rapid singlet decay channels that outcompete spin-forbidden intersystem crossing (ISC). Here we demonstrate that covalently attaching a stable radical to a chromophore induces radical-assisted enhanced intersystem crossing (RAE-ISC), leading to efficient triplet photochemical reactions. Using a TEMPO-substituted BODIPY photocage as a model system, we show that RAE-ISC increases the photoreaction quantum yield by an order of magnitude. Transient absorption spectroscopy and computational calculations confirm that the increased triplet yield, enabled by RAE-ISC, is the key factor underlying the enhanced photochemical efficiency. These results provide proof of concept that RAE-ISC is a new and promising strategy for the future design of chromophores that promote triplet-state photochemical reactivity.

papers.title: Mimicking Extradiol Dioxygenase Reactivity on Iridium
Time-Resolved Raman Spectroscopy of Nitrate Electroreduction Reveals Dynamic Interfacial Adsorbate Reorganization
papers.abstract: Nitrate electroreduction offers a pathway for coupling wastewater remediation with sustainable ammonia production, yet its mechanistic details under operating conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we directly resolve the dynamic evolution of nitrate-derived intermediates at electrified interfaces, addressing a key limitation in understanding dynamic reaction pathways. We employ time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TR-SERS) to monitor the interfacial behavior of NO 3 – and NO 2 – during nitrate reduction on roughened silver electrodes. Potential-dependent vibrational shifts reveal systematic changes in adsorption modes under increasingly cathodic potentials. These spectral features are consistent with a transition from outer-sphere nitrate to more strongly bound configurations preceding nitrite formation. Density functional theory calculations support the vibrational assignments and provide insight into preferred binding motifs across the applied potential range. By directly tracking the temporal evolution of nitrate-derived species, this approach elucidates the sequence of adsorption and transformation steps on Ag. The combined experimental and computational analysis advances molecular-level understanding of nitrate electroreduction and provides a framework for probing dynamic reaction intermediates in nitrogen conversion electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Structure-Based Design of Hybrid Molecules Exhibiting Dual SGLT2 and AT1 Inhibition for Cardiorenal Protection: A Computational and Medicinal Chemistry Strategy
papers.abstract: Heart failure and chronic kidney disease frequently coexist in metabolic syndromes, leading to complex polypharmacy and increased risk of adverse drug interactions. Developing single hybrid molecules with dual-target activity offers a strategy to reduce this burden. This study reports the structure‑based design of hybrid compounds capable of simultaneously modulating the angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptor and the sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) to achieve integrated cardiorenal protection. By combining pharmacophoric elements of telmisartan and empagliflozin, a virtual library of 2,017 bioisosteric derivatives was generated through scaffold hopping and screened via molecular docking against AT1 (PDB: 4ZUD) and SGLT2 (PDB: 7VSI), followed by ADMET‑guided prioritization. Structure–activity analysis highlighted the spatial relationship between the imidazole-derived core and the glycoside moiety as essential for dual affinity, yielding 20 candidates with favorable docking scores (SGLT2: −10.9 to −13.3 kcal/mol; AT1: −10.1 to −11.9 kcal/mol). Molecule 03 showed the strongest dual interactions, engaging Arg167 and Trp84 on AT1 and Asn75, Phe98, and Phe453 on SGLT2, with predicted high intestinal absorption, prolonged exposure, and low cardiotoxic or hepatotoxic risk. These results support AT1/SGLT2 hybridization as a promising approach for next‑generation cardiorenal therapeutics.

papers.title: On the Synthesis and Bioactivity of B-seco Taxanes
papers.abstract: The position and orientation of various substituents on paclitaxel (1a) are recognized to be crucial for its interaction with its beta-tubulin target, as well as for phenotypes such as microtubule stabilization, antitumor activity and peripheral neurotoxicity. Among the four rings on the taxane skeleton, rings A, C and D have been extensively explored, whereas B has been scarcely probed possibly due to the difficult manipulation of its eight-membered ring chemistry. In this work, B-seco paclitaxel (16) has been synthesized and biologically evaluated, demonstrating the importance of an intact eight-membered B ring. Besides, further attempts to re-cyclize the B-seco taxane through olefin metathesis and a base-promoted aldol reaction failed to furnish an expanded B ring, and instead, resulted in the unexpected formation of a dimer (36) of the B-seco baccatin.

papers.title: Revealing the Molecular Origin of Green Fluorescence in meta-Phenylenediamine Derived Carbon Dots
papers.abstract: Understanding and controlling long-wavelength emission in carbon dots (CDs) remains a key challenge that limits their rational design for optoelectronic and energy conversion applications. In this study, we elucidate the mechanism of green emission in CDs derived from metaphenylenediamine (mPDA). Through sequential synthesis, purification, and spectroscopic analysis, we isolate and assign the emissive species to amidated 2,7-diaminophenazine derivatives, demonstrating that molecular fluorophores, rather than graphitic domains, dictate the green emission. Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations further support this assignment, showing excellent agreement with the experimental absorption and emission energies. Further thermal and optical studies support a dual core-shell architecture for those CDs, in which the sp2-rich carbon core enhances structural robustness and photostability, while surface-anchored fluorophores govern the green photoluminescence. To illustrate the practical implications of this structural-optical interplay, integration of greenemitting CDs into TiO2 photoanodes is shown to enhance photocurrent generation and light harvesting efficiency in photoelectrochemical water splitting. This molecular-level understanding establishes a rational design framework for engineering carbon nanomaterials with tailored photophysical and optoelectronic properties.

papers.title: AMOEBA polarizable atomic multipole forcefield parameters for flavins
papers.abstract: Computation of redox potential of cofactors in biological systems requires an accurate description of the interaction between the redox cofactors and the biomolecular environment and an extensive conformational sampling. Seeking to achieve a quantitative leap in redox potential evaluation for flavoproteins, we report here the calibration of sets of parameters to describe flavin molecules in various redox states in the framework of AMOEBA, a multipolar and polarizable forcefield. We calibrate both the isoalloxazine ring in the five biologically relevant redox states and the polyol chain needed to describe riboflavin or flavin adenine dinucleotide molecules. We propose a delineated, step-by-step protocol to accurately account for the physical effects at play. We provide evidence that these parameters produce stable conformations in agreement with quantum chemistry (DFT) calculations. The newly derived AMOEBA forcefield allows to compute interaction energies of lumiflavin with water molecules and aminoacids in very good agreement with quantum chemistry calculations, with a net improvement with respect to a monopolar non-polarizable forcefield. Finally, as a first application, we compute redox free energy of half reactions for two redox couples of lumiflavin in water. The values obtained are once again in better agreement with DFT values than those obtained with a standard classical forcefield.

papers.title: Towards cellular resolution of tryptic peptides in tissue sections by MALDI MS Imaging: A focus on enzyme application
papers.abstract: Bottom-up proteomics coupled with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI imaging) is the preferred method for untargeted localization and identification of proteins in tissue. However, there are no MALDI imaging workflows that offer a combination of high lateral resolution, accurate mass detection, efficient tryptic digestion, and reproducibility. In this study, we developed a MALDI imaging workflow which enables reproducible imaging of tryptic peptides in mammalian tissue sections with high-resolution in mass and space. For the first time, tryptic peptides could be imaged in tissue sections at 10 µm pixel size with high mass resolution (R > 100000 FWHM), mass accuracy (RMSE < 3 ppm) and without discernable delocalization. We achieved this by systematic optimization of trypsin spray parameters including the number of sprays, enzyme volume, density and flow rate and a custom-built digestion chamber specifically designed for high-resolution measurements. MALDI imaging at 10 µm pixel size showed that multiple (10) sprays followed by short incubations and balanced on-tissue moisture are crucial to avoid delocalization and obtaining highly resolved peptide images with sufficient high ion intensities. As a result, up to 283 proteins could be identified using our optimized method based on additional LC-MS/MS data and strict identification criteria. Through increased peptide intensity, we could perform on-tissue MALDI-MS/MS of 16 tryptic peptides and confirm their amino acid sequence. Our results provide insights into the complex on-tissue digestion dynamics associated with MS imaging. Although aimed for high spatial resolution, many findings can be transferred to other MALDI imaging workflows to make it suitable for different spatial proteomics applications.

papers.title: Iron-Binding Hydrogel Sensors for Multi-Well Plate Analysis
papers.abstract: Sensory hydrogels for multi-well plate analysis represent an attractive method of analyte quantification, yet limited examples for metal detection exist to date. In this study we present an iron(III)-sensory hydrogel assay for multiwell plate analysis using deferasirox (DFS). We functionalized DFS to enable its polymerization into networks. The methacrylated DFS derivative (DFSMA) was structurally characterized by NMR spectroscopy. Its binding to iron(III) was retained in solution, when incorporated into a polymer and hydrogel, as assessed by NMR and UVVis spectroscopy. A hydrogel formulation was studied that allowed for a facile production of sensory hydrogels in 96-well plates. Various iron(III) levels were tested, calibration curves for absorbance and fluorescence were crafted, allowing for the quantification of unknown iron(III) levels. Additionally, the selectivity of this hydrogel assay was tested against a variety of (transition) metals, demonstrating its selective nature towards iron(III).

papers.title: Impact of the Physico-Chemical Properties of Surface-Initiated Polymer Brushes on siRNA Binding and Transfection Efficiency
papers.abstract: Rational design of polycationic gene delivery vectors requires understanding how polymer chemistry governs RNA complexation, cellular uptake, and intracellular release kinetics. Using a library of tertiary and quaternary amine-bearing polymer brushes, we reveal how hydrophobicity, pKa, rigidity, and quaternisation modulate siRNA delivery and gene silencing. We demonstrate that RNA binding capacity correlates directly with pH-responsiveness; low pKa chemistries undergo premature deprotonation at physiological pH, limiting transfection efficiency. Chain rigidity was found to significantly affect RNA binding through steric/repulsion effects, in comparison to flexible poly(alkyl) methacrylates, yet some rigid brushes still achieved effective transfection, surprisingly. To isolate the role of structural features from pH-dependent behaviour, we systematically quaternised all chemistries. Quaternisation fundamentally altered binding mechanisms, eliminating pH sensitivity while improving colloidal stability and reducing cytotoxicity. The relationship between hydrophobicity and toxicity proved to be complex: ethyl side chains dramatically increased toxicity relative to methyl groups, yet more hydrophobic isopropyl chains did not, with quaternisation completely reversing ethyl toxicity. In quaternised systems, hydrophobicity modulates competitive desorption, with quaternised methyl-substituted brushes exhibiting slower release than their ethyl-substituted counterparts, while rigid imidazole chemistries provide exceptional desorption resistance. Most remarkably, we demonstrate that the binding capacity of RNA within brushes does not always correlate with cellular internalisation, competitive desorption and transfection efficiency. For instance, rigid imidazole brushes achieved robust gene silencing despite binding substantially less RNA than poly(alkylamine methacrylate) brushes. These structural parameters enable independent control over both the magnitude and temporal dynamics of knockdown, revealing complex non-linear relationships that can be rationally tuned. These findings expand the delivery vector design space beyond conventional approaches, enabling the rational engineering of next-generation polymeric carriers for controlled RNA delivery kinetics.

papers.title: Fluorinated Ionizable Lipids Potentiate Nano-PROTAC-Mediated Protein Degradation by Enhancing Cytosolic Delivery
papers.abstract: Nanoscale proteolysis-targeting chimeras (nano-PROTACs) have emerged as modular platforms for targeted protein degradation, but their activity is often limited by endo-lysosomal sequestration, limiting access to the cytosol for proteasomal degradation. Here, we report fluorinated ionizable lipids as tunable chemical components that potentiate liposome-based nano-PROTAC (LipoTAC)mediated degradation by enhancing cytosolic delivery. We constructed a library of fluorinated ionizable lipids and evaluated their degradation activity using leucine-rich α-2 glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) as a model target. Library screening revealed a structure-dependent activity trend, with fluorinated analogs generally outperforming their nonfluorinated counterparts, and degradation potency varying with the fluorination pattern. The optimized lipid i16αCF3-based LipoTAC achieved an LRG1 degradation DC50 of 3.4 μM and outperformed matched nonfluorinated analogs and the clinically validated ionizable lipid SM102. This architecture retained its potency across distinct targets and targeting ligands, enabling degradation of the cytosolic protein focal adhesion kinase (FAK) with a DC50 of 0.12 μM and of the membrane-associated protein programmed deathligand 1 (PD-L1) with a DC50 of 10 nM. Mechanistic studies showed that i16αCF3-based LipoTAC reshaped the protein corona, engaged both clathrin- and caveolae-mediated uptake, and promoted endosomal escape, thereby improving cytosolic delivery. In 4T1 breast tumor models, i16αCF3-LipoTAC targeting LRG1 prolonged circulation, increased tumor accumulation, and enhanced antitumor efficacy. Co-delivery of doxorubicin further improved therapeutic efficacy while reducing systemic toxicity. These findings establish fluorinated ionizable lipid architecture as a tunable molecular design strategy to enhance nano-PROTAC delivery and protein degradation efficiency.

papers.title: The Shadow of the Barrier—Two Conformal Fossils from the Cohesive Fraction in GERT
papers.abstract: The intrinsic scatter of the Radial Acceleration Relation (RAR), σint ≈ 0.057 dex, is one of the tightest empirical correlations in extragalactic astronomy and has resisted derivation from first principles. This paper derives that number from the same thermodynamic structure that physical chemistry uses to describe systems near a phase boundary, identifying σint as a thermodynamic resolution floor rather than a statistical dispersion. In the Gibbs Energy Redistribution Theory (GERT), gobs/gbar = 1/φ, where φ(x) = fM/(fM + fL) is the cohesive fraction. The cohesive fraction is bounded by the forbidden barrier φ = 1/2 at which the cohesive and entropic forces would balance (∆G = 0, work ceases)—a barrier structurally identical to the supersaturation limit at which a chemical system spontaneously crystallises. The maximum approach to the barrier is φmax = 0.4418 at the recombination epoch. Converting the residual barrier distance 0.5 − φmax = 0.0582 to dex via the Jacobian 1/(φmax ln 10) yields σRAR = 0.0572 dex, in 0.4% agreement with observation, with zero free parameters. Together with the Milgrom acceleration scale a0 (predicted to 0.57% in the preceding paper), the GERT programme now derives two independent galactic observables from a single thermodynamic function calibrated only against cosmological data. The intrinsic scatter is the shadow of the barrier—the imprint of φ < 1/2 on the phenomenology of galactic dynamics.

papers.title: Molecular Insights into Nanoplastic Incorporation in Lipid Bilayers: Theory, Simulation and Experiment
papers.abstract: We use molecular dynamics simulations, free energy calculations, the theory of random walks in confined spaces and atomic force microscopy indention experiments to explore the interaction of polymer with lipid bilayers. As simplified theoretical model systems, we use bilayers in contact with oligostyrenes (5 and 10 monomers) or oligoethylenes (2, 4 and 8 monomers) in an aqueous environment. Molecular dynamics simulations attest the localization of oligomers within the lipid bilayer, and free energy computations suggest a notably small activation barrier for the process of small polymer chain incorporation. For a rigid lipid bilayer, an entropic barrier limits the import of a polymer chain with a radius of gyration comparable to the diameter of the layer's hydrophobic core, which amounts to roughly three nanometers. Based on these results and the experiments, we suggest anchoring to lipid bilayers by chains protruding from nanoparticles as the initial stage of import into cells, multi-cellular organisms and tissues.

papers.title: Understanding the insertion/folding mechanism of penetratin forspecific lipid compositions
Redox Properties of Structural Fe in Clay Minerals: 5. The Role of Fe in the Tetrahedral Sheet of Synthetic Smectites
papers.abstract: Iron-bearing smectite clay minerals are important redox-active phases in soils and sediments. Yet, the influence of iron substitution in the tetrahedral sheet ( Tet Fe) of smectites on their redox properties remains poorly understood.Here, we investigated the repeated reduction and re-oxidation of synthetic smectites, known as synthetic nontronites (SyN), with constant content of Fe in the octhedral sheet, Oct Fe, but variable initial content of Tet Fe. The redox properties of redox-cycled smecites were characterized using mediated electrochemical reduction and oxidation. Fe 2+ /Fe Total ratios determined over a wide range of reduction potentials were assessed for thermodynamic and kinetic descriptors for interfacial electron transfer and the ensuing charge re-distribution and cation migration in the mineral structure. Standard reduction potentials and diffusion coefficients for charge redistribution were insensitive to Tet Fe content, indicating that thermodynamics and bulk charge transport are predominantly governed by the Fe–O–Fe networks in the octahedral sheet. Conversely, Tet Fe accelerated the rate constant of smectite redox reactions by approximately an order of magnitude. Comparison of these thermodynamic and kinetic descriptors between synthetic nontronites and natural reference smectites showed that parameter-values converge within a narrow range across iron-rich dioctahedral smectites. This general finding underscores the dominant role of the Oct Fe networks in controlling smectite redox reactivity in subsurface environments whereas Tet Fe primarily accelerates interfacial electron transfer kinetics to/from Oct Fe.

papers.title: Bulk Spillover across Heterogeneous Interfaces: A Compelling Emerging Paradigm in Materials Science and Catalysis Science
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of in-situ characterization techniques and theoretical calculation methods, researchers have recently discovered that active species can cross the metal/support interface, enter the bulk lattice of the support (3~5 atomic layers and deeper regions) for transport and reaction, a phenomenon defined as “bulk spillover”. This review systematically summarizes the basic concepts, structural characteristics, and scientific significance of bulk spillover, and focuses on elaborating the core mechanisms of bulk oxygen spillover and bulk hydrogen spillover with typical system cases. The paper innovatively proposes a new classification of strong metal-support interaction (SMSI): traditional “surface coating SMSI (SC-SMSI)” and novel “interface migration SMSI (IM-SMSI)”, where the latter emphasizes that active species migrate from the bulk of the support to the interior of the metal to form oxides, alloys, or single-atom doped structures. Furthermore, this review emphasizes the “interface-controlled bulk oxygen transport (iBOT)” and metal-support-interface synergetic mechanism, and prospects future directions such as dynamic trajectory visualization, exploration of bidirectional spillover, and electrocatalytic applications. The discovery of bulk spillover subverts the traditional cognition that “catalytic reactions only occur on the surface”, provides a new pathway for breaking through the “triangular constraint” of catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability, and is expected to promote the bulk spillover practical applications in heterogeneous catalysis.

papers.title: Host-guest chemistry of tetrahedral MII4L6 (M = Fe, Zn) cages equipped with walls featuring antiaromatic pentalene motifs
papers.abstract: Antiaromatic compounds are often difficult to work with due to their relative instability in comparison with aromatic analogues. As a consequence, their application in functional materials remains in its infancy. Here, we report the synthesis of porous M II 4 L 6 (M = Fe, Zn) coordination cages equipped with dibenzo[ a , e ]pentalene panels involving the antiaromatic motif of pentalene stabilized by benzannulation. Both cages encapsulate fullerenes, undergoing pronounced structural reconfiguration upon C 60 inclusion, and displaying broader affinity for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. The cages selectively bind anthraquinone over its reduced form and interact with steroids such as testosterone and cholesterol. Remarkably, the chemical shifts of the guests are affected by the Clar sextets rather than the pentalene motif. These assemblies represent only the second reported example of a supramolecular cage with a cavity fully enclosed by antiaromatic walls, offering new insights into the effects of (anti)aromaticity in confined spaces and demonstrating that appropriately modified antiaromatic units do not inevitably induce paramagnetic deshielding of encapsulated guests.

papers.title: Dataset Merging Strategy for Efficient Construction of a Machine-Learning Force Field: A case of CeO2 Surfaces with an Oxygen Vacancy
papers.abstract: The accuracy and transferability of machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) critically depend on the quality of the training database. Here, we propose a dataset merging strategy for efficiently constructing a transferable MLFF for pristine and oxygen-defective CeO 2 surfaces. The proposed strategy is based on three key elements: (1) initiating on-the-fly training from small, less stable slab models to accelerate early-stage convergence by sampling diverse high-energy configurations; (2) sampling diverse local structures by gradually increasing the MD temperature while avoiding excessively rapid atomic motions and unphysically short contacts; and (3) merging independently generated datasets from slab models with different thicknesses and defect conditions to improve transferability. The resulting MLFF is validated on larger slab models containing 144 atoms and applied to structural optimization of pristine and oxygen-defective surfaces as well as lattice oxygen diffusion pathways on defective surfaces. The predicted pathways and energy barriers are in good agreement with density functional theory (DFT) results, particularly for pathways involving relatively large structural and energetic changes. Furthermore, the MLFF maintains consistent performance for extended CeO 2 (111) surface models containing up to 5183 atoms, approaching to experimentally relevant length scale. These results highlight that systematic dataset merging across model sizes and configurations provides a practical route to constructing transferable MLFFs for complex oxide surfaces.

papers.title: Scaffold-Aware QSAR Modelling of Cyclin-Dependent Kinase 2 Inhibition: Multi-Model Benchmarking, Applicability Domain Assessment, and an Open-Source Decision-Support Platform
papers.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) is a validated oncology target whose aberrant activation drives uncontrolled cell-cycle progression in diverse cancers. Despite sustained pharmaceutical interest, the rational prioritisation of CDK2-directed chemical matter remains hindered by the scarcity of publicly accessible, rigorously validated predictive tools that couple potency estimation with interpretable chemical evidence. Here we report the development, validation, and deployment of a quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) model for CDK2 inhibition, constructed from a curated ChEMBL dataset and evaluated under a deliberately stringent scaffold-stratified validation framework. We retrieved 2,716 IC50 bioactivity records for CDK2 (CHEMBL301) from ChEMBL, of which 2,057 unique compounds survived a nine-stage curation pipeline encompassing SMILES sanitisation, salt stripping, InChIKey-based deduplication, pIC50 conversion, and physicochemical outlier removal. The final dataset spans 892 Murcko scaffolds and a pIC50 range of 3.01–9.52 (mean 6.49 ± 1.27). Four regression algorithms Ridge regression, Random Forest, support vector regression with a radial basis function kernel (SVR–RBF), and XGBoost were benchmarked against a scaffold-stratified 80/20 split, ensuring zero scaffold overlap between training (n = 1,645) and test (n = 412) partitions. Following hyperparameter optimisation via randomised search cross-validation, the selected Random Forest model achieved a scaffold-split test R2 of 0.429, RMSE of 0.918 pIC50 units, and Pearson r of 0.673, with five-fold cross-validation returning R2 = 0.678 ± 0.028 and RMSE = 0.715 ± 0.031. Y-randomisation confirmed that predictive signal is genuine and not an artefact of chance correlation. The trained model is deployed as an open-source, publicly accessible Streamlit web application ChemBLitz: CDK2 Pharmacological Diagnostic Suite that integrates pIC50 prediction with applicability domain assessment (Tanimoto-based, three-tier threshold), ensemble uncertainty quantification, PAINS screening, Lipinski/Veber/QED developability profiling, ligand efficiency calculation, and Murcko scaffold context. This "prediction-plus-evidence" paradigm shifts the model from a point predictor to a decision-support service, enabling informed medicinal chemistry judgements at the hit-to-lead stage.

papers.title: Computational analysis of miR‑26a seed architecture and BDNF 3′UTR thermodynamics across mammals
papers.abstract: Background: Brain‑derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is a key regulator of neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, and neuropsychiatric disease, and is post‑transcriptionally controlled by microRNAs (miRNAs). A PLOS ONE study demonstrated that human BDNF 3′UTR expression is repressed by miR‑26a and miR‑26b in an allele‑specific manner at a polymorphic site defined by rs11030100 and rs11030099, but this site appears poorly conserved across mammals. Objective: To develop a reproducible in‑silico pipeline that (i) compares BDNF 3′UTR architecture across mammals, (ii) maps miR‑26a seed‑like sites, and (iii) profiles miR‑26a–BDNF duplex thermodynamics in human and non‑human species, extending the experimental findings on the human polymorphic site. Methods: We implemented a Google Colab pipeline using Biopython, ViennaRNA, and public sequence/variant databases. RefSeq BDNF mRNA records were retrieved for human, mouse, rat, macaque, and dog via NCBI Entrez; coding sequences (CDS) and 3′UTRs were parsed from GenBank features. We defined miR‑26a‑5p seed motifs (6‑mer, 7mer‑m8, 7mer‑A1, 8‑mer) and scanned BDNF 3′UTRs for reverse‑complement matches. For each seed‑containing window, and for a human 80‑nt window around the first seed hit, we computed miR‑26a–BDNF duplex free energy (ΔG) using ViennaRNA’s duplexfold API. We then aligned the human window to each species’ 3′UTR to identify orthologous segments and computed ΔG on those segments. Variant consequences and GWAS evidence for rs11030100/rs11030099 were queried via Ensembl and the GWAS Catalog. Results: The RefSeq BDNF 3′UTR selected for human (NM_001143816.2) was 2928 nt, comparable in length to the mouse (NM_001316310.1; 2891 nt) and rat (NM_001270638.1; 2899 nt) 3′UTRs, whereas the particular macaque (XM_015114599.3; 316 nt) and dog (NM_001002975.1; 380 nt) records retrieved for this analysis contained markedly shorter 3′UTRs. A simple 6‑mer seed scan (reverse complement of UCAAGU) identified two seed‑like matches in human BDNF (positions 1620 and 1780), one in mouse (1298), and one in rat (1287), but none in the macaque or dog transcripts. Refinement to canonical 7–8‑mer seed classes showed one 7mer‑A1 match in human (position 1780) and one 7mer‑m8 match each in mouse and rat, again with no hits in the short macaque or dog 3′UTRs. ViennaRNA calculations around seed‑containing windows yielded mean ΔG values of approximately −12.2 kcal/mol for the two human windows, −18.7 kcal/mol for the mouse window, and −21.3 kcal/mol for the rat window, indicating thermodynamically favorable duplex formation in all three species. An 80‑nt human window around the first seed position (1620) showed ΔG = −12.2 kcal/mol; because ancestral and “variant” sequences were identical in the current template analysis, ΔΔG was 0 by construction. Local alignment of this human window against each species’ 3′UTR identified orthologous 80‑nt segments with strong sequence similarity and stable predicted duplexes in mouse (ΔG = −22.2 kcal/mol; alignment score 75) and rat (ΔG = −21.3 kcal/mol; score 77), and more moderate ΔG in macaque (−9.9 kcal/mol; score 35) and dog (−12.5 kcal/mol; score 35). Ensembl annotated both rs11030100 and rs11030099 as BDNF 3′UTR variants, and the GWAS Catalog returned no associations for either SNP, consistent with their functional importance in luciferase assays but limited population‑level evidence from current GWAS datasets. Conclusions: This reproducible in‑silico pipeline confirms that multiple miR‑26a seed‑like motifs and thermodynamically favorable miR‑26a–BDNF 3′UTR interactions are present in human, mouse, and rat BDNF transcripts, while highlighting transcript‑selection–dependent differences in apparent 3′UTR length and motif content in macaque and dog. Our results extend the experimentally validated human miR‑26a/b site by placing it in a broader comparative sequence and thermodynamic context, but they do not support a simple model in which strong miR‑26a–BDNF binding is uniquely primate‑specific. Instead, they emphasize that sequence context, alternative 3′UTR isoforms, and species‑specific expression patterns must all be considered when interpreting miRNA‑mediated BDNF regulation and its translational relevance.

papers.title: 63Cu NMR Study of Cu2MTtCh4 (M = Zn, Cd; Tt = Si, Ge, Sn; Ch = S, Se): A Tale of One or Two Sites
papers.abstract: Quaternary chalcogenides Cu 2 MTtCh 4 ( M = Zn, Cd; Tt = Si, Ge, Sn; Ch = S, Se) with diamond-like structures, derived from the cubic sphalerite and hexagonal wurtzite prototypes, have been extensively studied for their optoelectronic properties. The site distributions of the metal cations, which are often unclear, can be probed by 63 Cu solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. NMR parameters were extracted through a combination of multifield magic-angle spinning (MAS) and non-spinning experiments to establish structural trends within these compounds. Substitution of S with Se led to lower frequencies for the 63 Cu isotropic chemical shift. In contrast, substitution with heavier tetrels (Si to Ge to Sn) led to higher frequency chemical shifts, which correlate with narrower band gaps. Ambiguities in structural models were resolved by arguments about local symmetry of Cu sites, as examined by their quadrupole coupling parameters. The experimental results were compared with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, performed using r 2 SCAN and PBE functionals. The predicted electric field gradient (EFG) parameters were accurate, though the calculated magnetic shieldings exhibited limitations in these narrow-gap semiconductors. This work provides an analytical 63 Cu NMR spectroscopy method that can rapidly aid in assessing local structures in these diamond-like compounds and related chalcogenides.

papers.title: HEALER (Hit Expansion to Advanced Leads using Enumerated Reactions): A new Method and Computational Tool for Hit to Lead Optimization
papers.abstract: Rapid generation of synthetically feasible analogs of hit compounds is central to hit-to-lead campaigns in medicinal chemistry. Here we present HEALER, an open-source reaction-based enumerator that constructs analogs of a molecule of interest (such as hit compounds resulting from high throughput screening campaigns) by (i) retrosynthetic fragmentation of a query hit molecule; (ii) fragment-to-building-block matching using a weighted Tversky similarity metric; and (iii) forward recombination via curated SMARTS reaction templates. HEALER outputs analog proposals along with synthetic routes (including reactants and reaction identifiers) and computed “drug likeness” properties typically assessed in medicinal chemistry projects for compound triage. Across diverse benchmark sets (Enamine diverse compounds, ChEMBL lead-like bioactives, and a set of “unsynthesizable” molecules), HEALER showed high analog generation success rates and maintained robust performance on out-of-distribution chemotypes, while imposing minimal synthetic burden. Analogs generated with HEALER typically preserved or improved drug-likeness of the hits, often matching or exceeding the performance of synthesis-aware machine learning generators. To facilitate user experience, we implemented HEALER as a CPU-friendly web application, offering a practical bridge from in silico design to make-ready hit optimization chemistry. Code is available at https://github.com/eneskelestemur/healer.

papers.title: Deep-sea water preserves depth-dependent water molecular network signatures after recovery
papers.abstract: While deep sea water (DSW) is increasingly utilized for its potential health and industrial benefits, understanding of its functionality has centered on mineral composition, leaving the contribution of the water molecular matrix unexplored. This study characterizes depth-dependent structural variations in DSW (600-1500m) using aquaphotomics. Near-infrared spectroscopy coupled with multivariate analysis was applied to examine how water molecular organization reflects the deep-ocean environment. Beyond mineral content, we have discovered that DSW exhibits distinct depth-dependent structural transitions within its hydrogen-bonding network. Strongly hydrogen-bonded water decreases with depth, giving way to smaller clusters such as dimers and hydroxide monohydrates, rather than free water, likely reflecting the unique physicochemical conditions of the deep ocean. Shifts in key absorbance bands suggest deeper DSW represents an environment favoring biomolecular hydration and stabilization. Furthermore, partial least squares (PLS) regression analysis of spectra measured under laboratory conditions successfully predicted the original depth, salinity and in situ temperature of the samples (R 2 = 09514, 0.9419, 0.8221 respectively). These findings demonstrate that DSW retains structural signatures of its original environment. This study establishes an aquaphotomics-based framework for characterizing DSW and highlights the potential of water-structural signatures as new indicators for evaluating its functional properties in healthcare and industrial applications.

papers.title: Explainable Machine Learning for Low-Emission Methane Tri-Reforming: Carbon Formation, Hydrogen Production, and Operating-Window Optimization
papers.abstract: Tri-reforming of methane (TRM) is a promising route for producing hydrogen-rich syngas while partially utilizing CO2, but its deployment is limited by trade-offs among methane conversion, syngas composition, reactor duty, and carbon deposition. In this study, a Gibbsequilibrium model in Aspen Plus was used to generate a database of 46,464 operating points spanning temperature, pressure, and inlet H2O/CH4, CO2/CH4, and O2/CH4 ratios. Decision tree, random forest, XGBoost, and artificial neural network models were trained and compared, followed by SHAP and permutation-importance analysis and multi-objective genetic-algorithm optimization. The neural network showed the best predictive performance. Explainability analysis identified temperature as the dominant factor governing carbon formation, followed by steam, carbon dioxide, and oxygen feed ratios. Optimization revealed multiple distinct operating windows, confirming that no single universal optimum exists and demonstrating a rapid, interpretable framework for low-emission TRM screening and design.

papers.title: Deciphering Chemical Environments in Conformational Datasets Using an IQA Band-matching Protocol
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce BMIQA, a band matching (BM) protocol that harnesses the physical information encoded in topological atomic energies to identify equivalent chemical environments across conformational datasets. By analysing distributions of atomic energies obtained through the Interacting Quantum Atoms (IQA) formalism, BMIQA autonomously discovers chemically equivalent environments, without human intervention and without recourse to any structure-based representation, marking a shift toward a fully physics-driven atom-typing strategy. We validate our approach on datasets comprising seven capped amino acids, three oligopeptides, monomeric water, and water pentamers. Strikingly, capped aliphatic and aromatic amino acids without side-chain heteroatoms are made of only seven atomic environments: three carbon types, two hydrogen types, one oxygen type, and one nitrogen type. This compact and minimal representation persists in homopeptides, and the number of atom types increases only slightly in heteropeptides, remaining far smaller than the total atom count. B M I Q Acaptures subtle physical equivalences. In cysteine, it reveals that the SH and CH substructures correspond to equivalent hydrogen environments, consistent with the similar electronegativities of carbon and sulphur. While isolated water exhibits two local environments, water pentamers display four, including two oxygen and two hydrogen types arising from variable hydrogen bonding. We further show that the energetic fingerprints that characterise atomic environments depend strongly on the level of theory and that Gaussian process regression models trained on IQA energies reproduce the same environments when deployed in molecular dynamics simulations. By providing the means to build an unbiased atom typing scheme, BMIQA constitutes a robust, autonomous, and physically grounded framework for next-generation atom-typed machine learning force fields.

papers.title: Photocatalytic RNA Depyrimidination
papers.abstract: Abasic (AP) sites in RNA are increasingly recognized as functionally significant species in cellular physiology and disease. However, existing approaches to introduce these modifications rely primarily on enzymatic pathways or stochastic damage processes and lack generality and external control, rendering programmable nucleobase deletion in RNA largely inaccessible. Here, we report a catalytic method for selective depyrimidination under exceptionally mild conditions, enabling residue-selective generation of artificial AP sites directly from unmodified RNA mono- and oligonucleotides. By overcoming the intrinsic stability of pyrimidine N-glycosidic bonds, this approach enables chemoselective formation of reactive loci within RNA without prefunctionalization or sequence constraints. This transformation converts nucleobase deletion from an observed outcome into a programmable chemical process, positioning AP sites as chemically addressable features for the structural and functional manipulation of RNA.

papers.title: Photo-CIDNP-Enhanced 19F NMR for Rapid Protein Conformation and Ligand Binding Analysis
papers.abstract: 19 F NMR spectroscopy is a powerful probe of protein conformation and dynamics but is intrinsically limited by low sensitivity common to other NMR techniques. Here, we integrate photochemically induced dynamic nuclear polarization (Photo-CIDNP) with genetically encoded 19 F labels to enhance sensitivity by up to 220-fold, enabling the detection of 100 nM protein within 6.5 minutes. This approach employs commercially available, cost-effective 19 F-labeled amino acid analogues and is broadly applicable to proteins ranging from 6.6 to 54.2 kDa. It allows rapid analysis of conformational changes and ligand binding. Notably, ligand interactions with dissociation constants in the low-micromolar range (sub‑5 μM), which are challenging to detect using conventional 19 F NMR, can be readily characterized. The combination of Photo-CIDNP-induced sensitivity enhancement with the environmental responsiveness of 19 F NMR establishes a practical platform for protein structural and interaction studies.

papers.title: Suzuki-Miyaura Cross-Coupling Using Ketones
papers.abstract: The Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling is among the most frequently used methods to forge new C–C bonds. Organohalides are recognized as the classical electrophilic coupling partner in these reactions. However, given the abundance of oxygen in common feedstock molecules, researchers have sought new and improved methods to harness C–O bonds as alternatives to halides. Today, methods exist to directly cross-couple functional groups such as alcohols, carboxylic acids, and phenols. However, methods to directly engage ketones in cross-coupling reactions are lacking. Herein, we present how ketones can be utilized in the Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction to form valuable alkenyl arenes. The reaction makes use of a Ni/bipyridine catalyst in the presence of pivalic anhydride and KOtBu. Mechanistic studies suggest that the reaction proceeds by a rapid in situ activation of the ketone to form an alkenyl pivalate intermediate, which acts as a pseudohalide in a Ni-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura coupling. The compatibility of the base, activating agent, and low-valent metal catalyst is shown to be central to the reaction’s success.

papers.title: Acid-Catalysed Chain Scission and Tensile Collapse in Cellulose Networks
papers.abstract: Cellulose degradation is traditionally measured by the reduction of its degree of polymerisation (DP). During acid hydrolysis, this decay reaches a plateau known as levelling-off degree of polymerisation (LODP), where the chain scission significantly slows. However, we identify a ‘LODP paradox’: mechanical failure often continues to accelerate even after this chemical stability is reached. To investigate this decoupling, Whatman and rag papers were exposed to hydrogen chloride acid vapour and monitored via spectroscopy, microscopy, and mechanical testing. Crucially, while DP stabilised at the LOPD limit, macroscopic tensile strength continued to decline sharply, marking a critical DP threshold for structural collapse. Zero-span testing and microscopy reveal that this failure is driven by the disintegration of the connections between fibres rather than the shortening of the molecules themselves. These results show that paper does not fall apart just because the molecules get shorter, but because the connections between the fibres break down.

papers.title: Machine learning interatomic potential enhanced thermochemistry predictions across organic compound space
papers.abstract: This work presents thermoMLIP, a machine-learning-interatomic-potential-based workflow for efficient conformer optimization and thermochemistry prediction across organic molecules. By combining MLIP-driven geometry optimization with robust thermochemical corrections, thermoMLIP achieves near-DFT accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. We show that MLIP-based conformer searches systematically identify lower-energy structures than conventional approaches, improving thermochemical predictions across diverse datasets. Building on this framework, we develop an uncertainty-aware active learning strategy using evidential graph neural networks to construct a large-scale, uniform thermodynamic dataset. Iterative acquisition driven by epistemic uncertainty improves predictive accuracy and reduces model uncertainty.

papers.title: Operando Cryogenic Processing Effects on Residual Stress and Magnetism of Martensitic Stainless Steel for Energy Sector
papers.abstract: Martensitic stainless steels (MSS) are widely used in the energy sector due to their high hardenability, corrosion resistance, and favourable mechanical properties. Their performance in extreme environments—such as fusion reactors, offshore systems, and hydrogen infrastructure—depends strongly on the interplay between microstructure, residual stresses, and resulting properties, including magnetic behaviour and mechanical strength. In fusion applications, neutron irradiation and high magnetic fields can significantly alter MSS microstructure, potentially compromising material stability and leading to component failure. To enhance microstructural stability under such conditions, advanced processing methods are required. Cryogenic processing (CP), which involves exposing materials to temperatures below 77 K, has shown promise in improving properties like hardness and corrosion resistance through microstructural refinement. However, the underlying mechanisms governing these improvements, particularly in MSS for energy applications, remain insufficiently understood. Existing studies indicate that CP can influence magnetic properties and residual stresses, but comprehensive operando investigations, especially under strong magnetic fields, are lacking. This study investigates the effects of CP on MSS EN X17CrNi16-2 under different treatment conditions, including conventional heat treatment, CP, and CP combined with magnetic field exposure up to 5 T. The work examines micro-residual stresses (ex-situ and in-situ), magnetic behaviour using advanced microscopy techniques, and mechanical properties via microhardness testing. Additionally, it provides novel insights into the time-dependent mechanisms of CP through advanced neutron measurements, contributing to a deeper understanding of structure–property relationships in MSS for future energy applications.

papers.title: A new perspective on electrochemistry at the ITIES - combining µITIES and confocal microscopy using a gelled organic phase in a glass membrane
papers.abstract: Ion transfer voltammetry using arrays of micro-interfaces between two immiscible electrolyte solutions (µITIES) has emerged as a promising tool for analysis of environmental samples. Here we show that using a gelled organic phase, we can combine µITIES electrochemistry with ex situ techniques, such as confocal fluorescence microscopy. By investigating the transfer of the ionized fluorophore fluorescein, we can use fluorescence confocal microscopy to evaluate the distribution of ions in the organic phase after transfer. We show that the concentration of the fluorophore close to the ITIES after transfer using a constant applied potential is substantially higher than in the aqueous phase, even after a short transfer period. This demonstrates that the use of a high-viscosity organic phase is very promising for analysis and also allows for the combination of ITIES electrochemistry with an array of ex situ measurement techniques.

papers.title: Mechanisms of N2 Production from N-doped Graphenes under Temperature-Programmed Desorption Analysis: A Computational Study
papers.abstract: Temperature-programmed desorption experiments have shown the release of N 2 originating from graphitic N atoms in nitrogen-doped graphenes. However, the microscopic mechanism of this desorption remains unclear. In this study, quantum chemical calculations based on density functional theory were employed to explore reaction pathways for the formation and desorption of N 2 . The calculations revealed that N atoms can migrate within the graphene lattice via repeated Stone–Wales type rearrangement involving the exchange of C–N bonds, resulting in association of two N atoms leading to desorption as an N 2 molecule. Natural bond orbital analysis reveals that this process is facilitated by the relative weakness of bonds involving nitrogen in the graphene lattice. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations for the overall reaction kinetics further supported this picture.

papers.title: Main Group Metals in Redox Catalysis
papers.abstract: Main group metal redox catalysis is no longer a curiosity; it is a credible challenger to transition-metal chemistry. Heavy p-block elements, once dismissed as redox-inert or limited to Lewis acid reactivity, now can execute the core elementary steps of catalysis, including coordination, oxidative addition, reductive elimination, transmetalation, and single-electron transfer events. This review surveys recent advances across groups 13–15, focusing on aluminium, germanium, tin, antimony, and bismuth, the elements that have begun to deliver genuine metal-centred redox catalytic performance. Reactivity is unlocked not by formal oxidation state alone, but by careful ligand design and through ambiphilicity, weak bonding, element–ligand cooperation, and access to open-shell manifolds. The field is advancing fast, but unevenly. Group 13 is just getting started, whereas Ge, Sn, Sb, and especially Bi already operate across both twoelectron and radical regimes. Beyond summarising progress, this review defines the design rules, exposes mechanistic gaps, and highlights opportunities that are likely to decide what comes next. Heavy p-block elements are no longer just substitutes to transition metals. They are competitors, and increasingly, they are setting the terms for sustainable catalysis.

papers.title: An Iterative Evaluation Framework for Non-Canonical Amino Acid Peptide Drug Discovery: Sign-Direction Reproducible Multi-Layer Verification
papers.abstract: Non-canonical amino acid (ncAA) substitutions are central to peptide-drug development, yet quantitative in silico ranking of ncAA variants remains constrained by force-field junction parameters at the canonical / non-canonical boundary, charge-derivation provenance, and the limited reproducibility of MM-PBSA / MM-GBSA scoring at small mutational scales. Khoury et al. (2014) reported a comprehensive same-system MM-GBSA / experimental correlation of R² = 0.388 over 147 ncAAs, defining a defensible field ceiling that newer methods only partially close. We present UPDD (Universal Peptide Drug Discovery), a five-stage iterative pipeline whose differentiating contribution is its Stage-4 evaluation framework for ncAA-modified peptide complexes (ncAA parameterisation → restrained MD → QM/MM single-point → MM-PBSA scoring), integrated with established generation tools (RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + AlphaFold2). We position UPDD at Capability Level 1: a decision-support tool for ncAA variant ranking, not a quantitative experimental predictor. Three methodological contributions are documented: (1) a σ_btwn / σ_w ensemble-quality decomposition with a single-metric Convergence Index (CI = σ_btwn / |⟨⟨ΔG⟩⟩|) carrying a dual interpretation (binding-mode classifier and automated quality-control auditor); (2) a branched ΔΔG architecture with bit-identical wild-type control (intervention isolation verified at floating-point precision); and (3) a multi-layer verification protocol empirically validated by four sequential audit layers — closed-shell charge bias, periodic-boundary serialisation, intra-residue bond integrity for HETATM ncAAs, and source-versus-test consistency. Across six ncAA peptide-target families (1EBP / 1YCR / 2QKH / 2QKI / 3IOL / 7TL8), the framework demonstrates sign-direction reproducibility on a validated subset, six-of-six Definition-3 readiness, and three biophysical detachment events distinguished from periodic-image artefacts. We acknowledge the Khoury R² = 0.388 ceiling, position the next charge-methodology axis (Khoury full RESP) as the planned v0.8 work, and decline universal quantitative-match claims. An iterative active-learning loop with wet-lab K_d feedback is operationally specified, and closed-loop calibration remains the v0.8 / v1.0 milestone.

papers.title: Leveraging Conformational Control of Neratinib’s C–N Axes to Enhance HER4 selectivity in Ovarian Cancer
papers.abstract: Diarylamines are among the most privileged scaffolds in drug discovery, with a myriad of examples in the clinic including the multi-kinase inhibitor neratinib which possesses indications towards HER2 overexpressed breast cancers. Diarylamines possess a complex conformational profile due to the two contiguous rotatable axes stemming from the diarylamine’s nitrogen. An analysis of co-crystal structures of diarylamines bound to proteins in the protein data bank (PDB) revealed that many kinases interact with diarylamines in vastly different small-molecule conformations, leading us to hypothesize that controlling the conformation about one or both axes of a diarylamine can lead to improved target selectivity. Herein we describe work where we lock the conformation of the quinoline-nitrogen axis of neratinib into a planar ‘trans’ conformation via the incorporation of a fluorine atom peri to the axis that serves as an intramolecular hydrogen bonding handle. This conformationally restricted analog possessed markedly improved kinase selectivity towards HER family kinases, particularly HER4, an emerging target for the treatment of some drug-resistant ovarian cancers. This selectivity held in cellular models of HER4 driven cancers. Overall, this work demonstrates that conformational control about the axes of diarylamines can represent a useful way to rapidly build in kinase selectivity into known lead compounds.

papers.title: SENTINEL: A Comprehensive AI-Enhanced Hyperspectral Sorting System and Testbed for Sensing and Machine Learning Applications
papers.abstract: The convergence of Industry 4.0 technologies and circular economy principles is transforming how we address the problem of resource scarcity and waste management. In this work, we introduce SENTINEL (Sensor ENsemble for Testing and INtelligent Evaluation Laboratory), an intelligent testbed system developed by Idaho National Laboratory in collaboration with UHV Technologies, Inc., which is designed to bridge the two problems. SENTINEL exemplifies the application of advanced automation, connectivity, and artificial intelligence to the critical challenge of material identification, quantification, and sorting within complex waste streams. By integrating hyperspectral imaging, computer vision, machine learning, and network architecture, the system achieves real-time, high-throughput characterization and precise sorting of diverse materials like plastics, textiles, biomass, and other waste materials. Operating at INL’s Biomass Feedstock National User Facility, SENTINEL is a testbed for algorithm development, model validation, and deployment of AI-guided characterization at industrial scales. In this work, we explain the instrument design and show three applications where high throughput pixelwise characterization can transform upstream processing and analysis. Beyond its technical innovations, the SENTINEL can address a critical bottleneck in circular economy adoption by enabling cost-effective material characterization, thereby enhancing supply chain resilience, and reducing dependence on foreign resources. SENTINEL demonstrates how Industry 4.0 capabilities can catalyze large-scale circular economy implementation, redefining waste as a valuable economic resource.

papers.title: Mapping Metabolomics Approaches in Natural Product Research for Antihyperglycemic Therapy: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: The global prevalence of diabetes mellitus continues to rise, underscoring the need for more effective therapy. Natural products (NPs) are potential sources of multi-target antihyperglycemic candidates. This scoping review was conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines to systematically evaluate recent trends in metabolomics-based NP drug discovery for antihyperglycemic bioactivity. Among the 122 eligible studies, publication output increased over time, with major contributions from Global South countries, including Malaysia, Egypt, and Indonesia. The studies covered 212 NP species from 73 families, mainly Fabaceae and Asteraceae, with phenolics and flavonoids as the most reported phytochemical groups. Untargeted metabolomics was the dominant approach (72.95%), with LC-MS/MS being the most used analytical platform (34.8%). Computational tools such as GNPS molecular networking and SIRIUS-assisted annotation were increasingly applied. However, most studies relied on in vitro enzyme assays (87.39%), particularly α-glucosidase and α-amylase inhibition, and many provided Level C evidence of bioactivity, indicating limited pharmacological validation. Metabolite annotations were mostly putative, commonly at MSI Level 2. This review highlights the need for stronger metabolite annotation, more physiologically relevant bioassays, including cell-based and in vivo models, and multi-omics approaches to better link chemical profiles with mechanisms of antihyperglycemic action.

papers.title: The topographic origin of chemomechanical failure in high-nickel cathodes revealed by operando dark-field X-ray microscopy
papers.abstract: Mechanical degradation in high-nickel cathodes, driven by anisotropic volume changes, remains a primary bottleneck for the lifetime of high-energy density batteries. Yet, the nanoscale origins of strain and defect initiation within individual primary particles remain unclear. Here, in the first application of operando dark-field X-ray microscopy (DFXM) to a battery system, we directly observe a dislocation wall nucleating from a pre-existing topographical flaw on the surface of a single NMC 811 primary particle. We show that failure is not stochastic, but deterministically driven by surface topography; the flaw creates a local stress concentration of ∼100 MPa, exceeding the material’s yield strength, while the bulk particle remains elastic. This observation establishes a direct physical link between primary particle surface morphology and the onset of irreversible plasticity. These findings prescribe a clear design rule: beyond bulk chemical stability, engineering particles with pristine, defect-free surfaces is essential for mitigating strain localisation and extending battery lifetime.

papers.title: Interfacial kinematics organize degradation across lithium-battery chemistries
papers.abstract: Why do graphite, silicon-composite, lithium-metal and anode-free batteries fail so differently even though all are ultimately constrained by the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI)? Here we show that the key ordering variable is not nominal anode chemistry, but the kinematics of the surface on which the SEI forms. Starting from the Doyle–Fuller–Newman porous-electrode equations, we recast four representative negative-electrode chemistries within a common interphase-centred framework and derive chemistry-specific closures for active area, side-reaction current, porosity change, damage, dead-lithium isolation and cyclable-lithium inventory. Literature-informed calculations under normalized NMC-based conditions reveal a monotonic rise in interphase loss and interface regeneration from graphite to silicon composites, lithium metal and anode-free cells, accompanied by a transition from gradual fade to convex chemomechanical decay, delayed failure knees and severe first-cycle losses. A new kinematic phase diagram, built from the unified diagnostics, places the four chemistries in distinct quadrants with monotonic trajectories. Independent post-hoc analyses of the same data, reported in companion Letters, reveal a parabolic-growth universality across three chemistries and a saddle-node bifurcation that places anode-free cells essentially on a critical point. The framework explains why classical fixed-surface DFN models are often adequate for graphite, must be phase- and stress-resolved for silicon composites, and become incomplete for lithium-metal and anode-free systems unless moving-front, nucleation and inventory-loss physics are added explicitly. This hierarchy provides a practical roadmap for building chemistry-specific DFN/PyBaMM models across next-generation battery platforms.

papers.title: Solution-Processing of Metal-Organochalcogenides (MOCs) and Application in Thin-Film Transistors
papers.abstract: Metal-organochalcogenides (MOCs) have recently emerged as highly promising candidates for optoelectronic applications; however, their integration into devices has been severely limited by the lack of solution-processable routes, as most MOCs are insoluble in conventional solvents. Herein, we report a strategy that employs coordinating diamine solvents to solubilize and process four metal–thiophenolate complexes as a model group of MOCs, enabling the fabrication of high-quality thin films. A high solubility of 150-200 mg mL -1 (>600 mM) can be achieved with 1,3-diaminopropane (DAP). Using copper thiophenolate (CuSPh) as a model system, we elucidate the role of DAP acting as a liquid co-ligand for the dissolution and validate the restoration of the MOC structure upon solvent removal. DAP-based solutions allow for the fabrication of smooth, compact, and uniform films with thickness between 30-40 nm. Notably, solution-processed films of CuSPh with the underlying one-dimensional (1D) structure are demonstrated as a semiconducting p-channel in field-effect transistors, achieving a hole mobility of 5×10 -3 cm 2 V -1 s -1 which is comparable to single-crystalline nanorods of CuSPh. Our ‘ liquid ligand processing ’ concept provides a route for fabricating MOC films using standard solution-based methods and crucially unlocks the applications of MOCs in thin-film devices.

papers.title: Early Detection and Recovery of SCF Convergence Failures in Automated Quantum Chemistry Workflows via Time-Series Learning
papers.abstract: Self-consistent field (SCF) convergence failures represent a major bottleneck in high-throughput quantum chemistry, particularly in open-shell systems. To address this challenge, we introduce an autonomous pipeline that treats the electronic structure descriptors from early spin-unrestricted SCF iterations as a time series. Using statistical descriptors extracted from only ten iterations, a lightweight gradient-boosted classifier accurately predicts convergence failures. The model achieves 94.8% accuracy on 55,000 test molecules after being trained on only 10,000 examples. Coupling this early-warning predictor with a -level-shifting restart heuristic derived from Bayesian Optimization of the level-shifting parameters enables automated recovery of SCF convergence. Across six diverse SCF test sets, our pipeline successfully rescued 57.5% of inherently difficult-to-converge molecules while maintaining a 94.1% convergence rate for easy cases, resulting in a reduction of 460,000 iterations across the 1200 calculations. Overall, this framework provides a highly transferable, data-efficient, and autonomous solution for large-scale electronic structure calculations.

papers.title: A Modular Strategy for the Gram-Scale Synthesis of Tetraarylammonium Salts
