Symmetric VSEPR Geometries from Energy Minimization on a Sphere
papers.abstract: The basic VSEPR molecular geometries are derived by treating electron domains as identical repelling charges constrained to a sphere. In order to minimize the total Coulombic repulsion under the constraint, Lagrange multipliers and the Gram matrix are used to show that the minimum-energy configurations for N = 2, 3, 4 are linear, trigonal planar, and tetrahedral.

papers.title: GRAND BANQUET: A NEXT-GENERATION FRAMEWORK FOR CLASSIFICATION ANALYSIS ON OMICS DATA MATRIX
papers.abstract: The advancement of high-throughput analytical instrumentation has placed analytical science into the "Fourth Paradigm" of data-intensive discovery. In this new era, the limitation of scientific insight is not merely data acquisition but the objective, reproducible interpretation of high-dimensional data matrices. Conventional chemometric workflows remain fundamentally reliant on "try-and-trust" methodologies. These expert-assisted paradigms require analysts to manually select preprocessing filters, feature selection methods, and classification models based on intuition or limited resources. Such subjectivity introduces analyst bias, raising concerns about reproducibility when applied to biological or chemical signals. Inspired by the concept “there is no one silver bullet”, a next-generation chemometrics framework, named Grand Banquet (GB) , is designed to standardise the analytical pipeline in this paper. GB replaces manual selection with a near-exhaustive approach, evaluating 990 pipelines (combinations of 15 preprocessing, 6 feature selection, and 11 classification methods) using various performance indices. Beyond this automatic pipeline, Qwen series Large Language Models (LLMs) have been integrated to generate natural-language narratives of these results, bridging the gap between complex computational outputs and human interpretation. GB offers a near-standard baseline (“Glass-box”) for data analysis and a practical step toward method governance and reproducibility. The operation of GB has been tested on four public datasets from the Chemometrics Group at Copenhagen University. GB generates near-exhaustive pipelines for each dataset, with validation accuracies ranging from 40% to 100%, highlighting its ability to systematically explore the data matrix rather than providing only best-performing results. To pay tribute to experts in this field and to promote the standardisation of data analysis practices, related executable files and manuals has been published on GitHub under the Apache License 2.0 licence (GitHub: https://github.com/Wyplayground/Grand-Banquet_Chemometrics-tool).

papers.title: Insights to orientation dependence of molecular conduction modeled by high-level quantum embedding
papers.abstract: This work investigates how molecular orientation and electrode–molecule interactions influence conductance variations in single-molecule junctions using recently introduced methods that utilize quantum embedding within the NEGF framework. By generating conductance histograms from transmission functions for two experimentally studied systems, we assess the ability of several embedding schemes and conventional DFT approaches to reproduce experimentally observed distributions. The results show that while the wavefunction-in-DFT, SOS-ADC(2)-in-PBE method provides the most balanced description of both mean conductance and histogram width, no method fully captures the behavior of the more rigid dithienophosphole system, likely due to limitations of the underlying structural sampling. These findings highlight the importance of realistic configurational sampling and demonstrate that conductance histograms offer a sensitive benchmark for evaluating theoretical transport methodologies.

papers.title: Evidence for significant multi-Li+ clustering in common lithium-ion battery electrolytes
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion battery (LIB) electrolytes have been empirically optimized to maximize battery lifetime and charge rate, but a detailed understanding of how their atomic-scale structure controls their electrochemical behaviors remains lacking. Here, we combine machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations, nuclear magnetic resonance measurements, electrochemical data, and quantum-chemical calculations to reveal previously unstudied multi-Li+ complexes without anions that are uniquely facile for reduction. This surprising insight explains the success of empirically-chosen ethylene carbonate (EC) containing solvent mixtures and provides a foundation for the rational design of improved electrolytes. Furthermore, our machine learning force field (MLFF) based LIB electrolyte simulations accurately reproduce a wide range of condensed phase experiments, despite being parameterized only to quantum chemical gas phase cluster calculations, and hence provide a compelling demonstration that MLFF models developed from first principles can robustly represent a complex chemical system to atomic resolution.

papers.title: MSOne: A deep learning-enabled software suite for end-to-end analysis of high-resolution LC-MS metabolomics data
papers.abstract: High-resolution LC–MS metabolomics requires transforming noise-dominated raw data into quantitative feature tables and, ultimately, biologically meaningful insights. In practice, this process is fragmented across multiple tools and involves extensive parameter tuning and manual curation. MSOne is a web-based, vendor-agnostic platform that integrates end-to-end analysis, from raw data interrogation to statistical interpretation, within a unified environment. MSOne introduces data-driven, deep learning–based methods for signal extraction and feature quantification, formulating peak detection as a supervised learning problem in both spectral and chromatographic domains. A data-driven noise estimation strategy replaces fixed intensity thresholds, improving sensitivity to low-intensity signals. Feature correspondence across samples is established using robust retention-time alignment and graph-based grouping, while correlation-driven feature tagging assigns isotopes, adducts, and in-source fragments. Metabolite annotation (MSI level 2) combines spectral denoising with composite scoring of MS/MS spectra against reference libraries. Beyond preprocessing, MSOne integrates statistical analysis and machine learning–based interpretation through MetaStat, linking analytical quality with statistical significance to improve reliability of downstream biological interpretation. Interactive visualization across all stages enables transparent curation and rapid iteration from initial results to publication-quality outputs. The use of pre-trained models in inference mode, together with a reduced parameter space, supports reproducible analysis. MSOne improves true-feature recovery, quantitative accuracy, and reproducibility on benchmark datasets while reducing reliance on manual intervention. Scalability is demonstrated through MetaMine, where over 100 public datasets, including studies with hundreds of samples, have been reprocessed using MSOne. Beyond serving as a repository, MetaMine enables data reuse with direct interrogation of intermediate and final results.

papers.title: From Sequence to Redox-Responsive Assembly: Coarse-Grained Simulation, Network Analysis, and Interpretable Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Here we screen 28,557 single-cysteine di-, tri-, and tetrapeptide sequences by paired coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of the monomeric and disulfide-linked dimeric states. We introduce dEdge, a network metric that quantifies redox-induced changes in intermolecular contacts directly and is less confounded by side-chain bulk than the SASA-derived aggregation propensity score. Both the dEdge distribution and the unit-normalized Network Hamiltonian Model parameter-distance distribution are bimodal across the library, identifying a population of sequences with large redox-driven structural shifts as candidates for active self-assembly. An interpretable Transformer encoder predicts dEdge from sequence alone (MAE 0.146). A single-substitution mutation analysis, Integrated-Gradients attribution on the trained model, and an unsupervised principal component analysis of the encoder’s representation converge on a compositional rule for dimer-favoring assembly: acidic or polar residues at the N-terminus together with small polar residues (G, A, Q, N) at internal positions, with aromatic residues acting as suppressors at any position The simulation dataset, NHM parameter library, and trained model together form a sequence-to-assembly resource for future redox-responsive peptide design and screening.

papers.title: Metal–Polymer Soft Framework Ion Gels: Linking Coordination Chemistry to Macroscopic Elasticity
papers.abstract: Linking molecular interactions to the macroscopic mechanical properties of soft materials remains a major challenge in soft-matter science. Here, we develop metal–polymer soft framework (MPF) ion gels, in which metal–ligand coordination complexes function as network-forming interchain bridges within a structurally homogeneous polymer network. Terpyridine-terminated TetraPEG prepolymers were cross-linked with divalent metal ions in an ionic liquid to form uniform coordination-bonded gel networks. The elastic modulus ( G ′) increased in the order Mg 2+ < Zn 2+ < Co 2+ < Ni 2+ , and this trend was quantitatively reproduced by modeling the equilibrium distribution of bis-terpyridine complexes, M(tpy) 2 2+ , acting as network-forming interchain bridges in the polymer network. By integrating coordination thermodynamics with classical rubber elasticity, we established a quantitative framework that determines the stepwise equilibrium constants ( K 1 and K 2 ) for mono- and bis-terpyridine complex formation and accurately predicts the non-monotonic dependence of G ′ on metal-ion concentration. Furthermore, the stress relaxation time ( τ ) was found to increase with increasing coordination bond strength, indicating that the dynamic mechanical response is correlated with the strength of metal–ligand interactions. These results establish a quantitative framework linking coordination thermodynamics with macroscopic gel elasticity and further suggest that coordination interactions also play an important role in controlling the dynamic mechanical response, providing a basis for tuning the properties of coordination-bonded soft materials.

papers.title: Toward Low-Energy Direct-Air Capture by Reversible Proton-Intercalation Mediated Alkalization
papers.abstract: Mitigation strategies to avoid climate change impacts rely on direct air capture (DAC) of CO 2 . We demonstrate absorption of CO 2 at 400 ppm, and its desorption, by using solid proton-intercalation electrodes to swing the pH of an alkaline electrolyte. 1.76±0.16 GJ tonne -1 of electrical energy is used when enriching CO 2 two-fold, extrapolating to 25.3±0.16 GJ tonne -1 to include water condensation and compression energy. Twenty-fold enrichment requires 5.81±2.42 GJ tonne -1 of electrical energy, extrapolating to 7.81±2.42 GJ tonne -1 . Here, symmetric potassium-stabilized alpha-phase manganese dioxide electrodes are used to (de)intercalate protons from two separate electrolyte streams, thereby swinging dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) solubility in an asynchronous cycle wherein electrochemical steps occur in sequence with CO 2 transfer steps. Mixing among aqueous streams is shown by theory to reduce CO 2 transfer, where the retention of DIC concentration during alkalizing/dealkalizing steps is affected by mixing more so than alkali-ion concentration swing. Energy use further reduces by pre-mixing post-absorption and post-desorption electrolytes. Theory predicts that alkali-ion concentration swing increases with increasing electrode specific capacity and decreasing mixing volume, motivating the co-design of active materials and their electrode microstructures to enhance efficiency, productivity, and enrichment. The present DAC cycle may also be implemented using other electrochemical architectures.

papers.title: DPχ: A Charge-Based Machine-Learning Potential Validated on the Pt(111)-Water Electrochemical Interface
Singlet fission tinkertoys based on N-heterocyclic carbenes: the role of stereoisomerism
papers.abstract: Context This theoretical study reports excited states molecular design of potential singlet fission materials based on homo- and heterodimers of N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) and their “locked” analogues. We found that the electronic properties of the investigated compounds can be finely adjusted by an interplay of the following factors: diradical character, topology, type of substituents, extension of the π-conjugation, excited state aromaticity, length of the latch in the “locked” analogues, conformation, and even stereoisomerism. With focus on the stereochemical aspects, this work provides new insights into the molecular design principles in diradicaloid organic materials with attractive electronic and excited state properties. Based on the comprehensive analysis, nine compounds were identified as promising candidates for efficient singlet fission. Methods Due to the large molecular size of the compounds and the importance of both static and dynamic correlation effects, the theoretical study is performed using simplified quantum chemistry (sQC) methods as screening tools, demonstrating their good performance in singlet fission aspect. Excited-state properties and singlet fission propensity of the NHC dimers were evaluated using spin-flip simplified time-dependent density functional theory (SF-sTD-DFT) and unrestricted simplified TDA (UsTDA) calculations. Vertical excitation energies and diradical characters were determined to assess the energetic conditions for singlet fission and to rationalize the effect of topology, substitution, and stereochemistry. The paper is dedicated to the late Prof. Masayoshi Nakano, whose seminal studies on diradicaloids opened a new chapter in the molecular design of modern materials.

papers.title: Synthesis of alkynyl derivatives via copper-catalyzed reactions of terminal alkynyl esters
papers.abstract: a.School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering/State Key Laboratory Incubation Base for Green Processing of Chemical Engineering, Shihezi University, Shihezi, Xinjiang 832003, China. E-mail: lishiwu@shzu.edu.cn. Absract: An asymmetric copper-catalyzed propargylic substitution reaction of propargylic acetates with ambident 5-aminopyrazoles was developed. Under optimized conditions, the relevant products with a wide range of substrates and good functional tolerance were obtained in 51-99% yields and up to 99:1 er. A gram-scale reaction and synthetic transformations demonstrated the practicality, delivering chiral γ-aryl-substituted propargylic products with high enantioselectivity. Furthermore, we investigated remote alkynes and successfully achieved the substitution reactions of alkynyl thiophene esters with 5-aminopyrazole and alkynyl naphthalene esters with aromatic amine, and sodium benzenesulfinate. This work further expands the scope of alkyne chemistry and provides an effective strategy for the development of alkyne chemistry.

papers.title: Coordination-driven Assembly of the Linear Trinuclear Lanthanum Complex Bearing Double Helix Structure
papers.abstract: Linear multinuclear lanthanide complexes are of considerable interest as luminescent, magnetic, and catalytic materials. Herein, we report the assembly of the trinuclear lanthanum complex featuring a double-helical structure. This unusual architecture was formed simply by mixing 2,6-diacetylpyridine with a lanthanum precursor, through multiple aldol reactions and complexation. Optical measurements combined with theoretical calculations revealed that the complex exhibits characteristic absorption and emission properties originating from ligand-to-ligand charge transfer (LLCT) processes.

papers.title: Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones
papers.abstract: Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological and human health studies. Coarse-grain molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. Here, we expand the capabilities of the widely used Martini 3 CG framework by parameterizing and validating a set of 20 steroid hormone models — including both endogenous and synthetic molecules — to enable their study across diverse targets, systems, and fields of interest. Hormone parameterization followed Martini 3 guidelines, while leveraging the similarities with the parent cholesterol molecule, for which a Martini 3 model is available. Notably, we were able to base our parameterization on the hundreds of experimental structures in the protein data bank that contain steroid hormones, instead of relying on atomistic simulations as is typical with Martini. The parameterized models match to within 5% target molecular volumes, and recover the overall hydrophobicity trend of the hormones, although higher hydrophobicities tended to be overestimated. In free simulations of protein-hormone systems the experimentally known binding poses could be recovered for 89% of the cases, indicating a successful parameterization also from a functional standpoint. Since several Martini 3 protein models were tested, we also incidentally show that the flexibility profile of the OLIVES model is the best suited for this type of protein–ligand recognition. We expect that the availability of our fully validated Martini 3 CG steroid hormone models will contribute to new studies, collaborations, and applications across different scientific fields.

papers.title: Stable and Active AuCu and AuPd Electrocatalysts for Platinum-Free Oxygen Reduction Reaction: Design Principles from Ligand-Strain Coupling and Gold Surface Segregation
papers.abstract: Surface-subsurface partitioning of alloying elements affects stability, strain, and adsorption energetics in heterogeneous catalysis, yet remains difficult to control. Here, we use first-principles calculations and atomistic modeling to show that Au M binary alloys ( M = Cu, Pd) provide a model platform for understanding this coupling at the atomic scale. We investigate Au xsurf M 100−xsurf surface alloys supported on fcc(111) substrates Au xsub M 100−xsub , spanning pure metals, monolayers, mixed alloys, and segregated surface-subsurface configurations. We find that alloy stability is governed by a coupled mechanism in which Au segregates to the surface, lowers the surface energy, and generates a self-compressive surface strain that stabilizes the alloy and tunes the adsorption of reaction intermediates. A net compressive surface strain indicates greater stability and a lower likelihood of strong intermediate binding, thereby enhancing activity, particularly in monolayer alloys. However, net compression does not imply a uniformly compressed surface. Instead, we constructed strain maps that show that tensile and compressive regions coexist across the alloyed surfaces. As a result, averaged strain descriptors mask heterogeneous local strain fields and can fail to predict adsorption energetics at bridge, atop, and hollow sites. Using the oxygen reduction reaction as an electrocatalytic model, we show that reliable predictions require site-specific descriptors that capture both short- and long-range effects. Consequently, the net local ligand-strain coupling is the best descriptor of the adsorption energy of intermediates that bind at those sites. Ordered surface alloys, notably the Au 33 Cu 67 /Cu(111) surface alloy and the dilute Au 14 Pd 86 /Pd(111) single-atom alloy, are predicted to be promising, combining near-optimal ORR adsorption energetics with greater structural stability than the corresponding pure-metal surfaces. These results establish a multiscale framework linking Au segregation, surface stability, and catalytic response in strain-engineered alloy catalysts.

papers.title: Efficiently computing charging free energies along alchemical pathways
papers.abstract: Some problems of computational chemistry and biology require computing the solvation free energies of atoms that have partial or full electrostatic charges on them. Doing this by alchemical free energy (AFE) methods can be computationally expensive. Here, we show that an order-of-magnitude speedup is possible when handling multiple atom types by parsing the LJ from the electrostatic components. We introduce the λ-resolved free energy strategy (λFE) for charging an atom up to charge q, for each λ value along the alchemical pathway, from a single alchemical simulation. It eliminates the need for separate alchemical simulations for every atom. λFE strategy is robust across different charges, LJ parameters, system sizes, and for three different water models tested (TIP3P, TIP4P/EW, and TIP4P/2005).

papers.title: On the Role of Symmetry Breaking Triplet State Conformations in the Phosphorescence of Some Dinuclear Pt(II) complexes
papers.abstract: Dinuclear design of Pt(II) and Ir(III) complexes have been shown to afford significant enhancement of phosphorescence rate, compared to the mononuclear analogues, due to the twice the number of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) paths of the emitting triplet states to singlet states. However, the dinuclear complex Pt 2 Cl 2 , coordinated to a bridging ligand of bis-N^C^N coordinating motif with an alkoxy group at the para-position to each coordinated carbon atom and ancillary coordinated chlorides, has been reported an outlier as its phosphorescence rate is comparable to that of its mononuclear analogue PtCl . Besides that, Pt 2 Cl 2 was assigned Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence (TADF) properties, unusual for Pt(II) complexes with fast decaying triplet state. To understand the photophysical behavior of Pt 2 Cl 2 and its analogues better, we conducted room temperature and cryogenic spectroscopic investigations as well as a computational study of Pt 2 Cl 2 , its mononuclear analogue PtCl , and dinuclear analogue with iodides, Pt 2 I 2 . Our investigations found that the decrease of emission decay time of Pt 2 Cl 2 and Pt 2 I 2 with temperature is by a large extend due to the enhancement of non-radiative decay rate, rather than activation of TADF. Spectroscopic data in line with computational studies of Pt 2 Cl 2 show that in the T 1 state one of the alkoxy groups rotates to conjugate its lone pair with the bridging ligand which breaks the electronic symmetry and shifts the triplet state localization onto one coordination site thus resulting in phosphorescence rate similar to that of the mononuclear PtCl . The direction and extend of this symmetry breaking rotation differentiates structural conformers as well as their properties. Due to the increase of state’s dipole moment in the symmetry-broken structure, the increase of medium polarity is understood to enhance the localization of the T 1 state on one coordination center which agrees with the accompanying decrease of phosphorescence rate. The T 1 state conformers of Pt 2 I 2 have over twice faster phosphorescence than those of Pt 2 Cl 2 and remain less distinct electronically from each other, which is understood as due to the much stronger electronic effect of iodides, compared to chlorides. Computational analysis showed that the previous report on T 1 state character of Pt 2 I 2 as having σ→π* type transition symmetry is erroneous, likely due to the self-interaction error of the DFT method, and the true character is of π→π* type transition symmetry. Our work shows that enhancement of phosphorescence rate in dinuclear structures is assailable by symmetry breaking geometry reorganization in the emitting triplet state which must be accounted for. The previously presented argumentation for TADF properties is found to be an artefact of flawed analysis not accounting for enhancement of non-radiative decay rate with temperature increase.

papers.title: Comment on “Charge Instability in Quadrupolar Chromophors: Symmetry Breaking and Solvatochromism” by F. Terenciani et al. (JACS 2006, 128, 15742)
papers.abstract: We comment on the article by F. Terenciani et al., “Charge Instability in Quadrupolar Chromophors: Symmetry Breaking and Solvatochromism” (JACS 2006, 128, 15742). This article proposes a theoretical model for symmetry breaking and electron transfer in symmetric donor-acceptor-donor molecules, and reports experimental results to support the proposed model. However, our analysis demonstrates that their model is inconsistent with their experimental results.

papers.title: Xylose-based diols are safe bisphenol analogues that induce degradability in epoxy resins
papers.abstract: Due to its combination of performance and cost, bisphenol-A remains a dominant component in epoxy resins, despite its classification as an endocrine disruptor and its role in producing materials highly resistant to degradation1,2. Here, we show that diols derived from acetalized xyloses, despite their distinct structure, can closely mimic bisphenol’s reactivity, rigidity and connectivity in epoxies, while offering comparable formulation properties, enabling them to act as drop-in replacements for BPA. Xylose-based diols are easily synthesized by carbohydrate functionalization and hydrogenation under mild conditions, achieving yields of 85% from xylose. Techno-economic analysis shows that the process’s high atom economy and simplicity can lead to pricing competitive with bisphenol-A. Despite being constructed on a xylose core that appears to eliminate toxicity signals, the diol-derived diglycidyl ether exhibited almost identical curing kinetics and comparable thermomechanical properties to conventional systems. Carbon fiber composites and adhesives based on the resin matched the performance of bisphenol analogues while allowing the recycling of the carbon fiber or adherends, and up to 80% of xylose simply by using sulfuric acid. Our findings reveal how abundant sugars can be turned into circular bisphenol replacements without relying on aromatic functionalities, which are difficult to source sustainably and can induce toxicity.

papers.title: Space Power Station with Uncontrolled Fusion
papers.abstract: Nuclear fusion offers the highest energy output per unit mass, making it attractive as an energy resource, in particular for space missions where payload mass is severely constrained. The central challenge to utilize fusion power on Earth lies in simultaneously achieving sufficiently high fuel temperature and density while maintaining confinement long enough for a meaningful fraction of the fuel to undergo fusion. Here we propose a conceptual design for a space-based fusion reactor driven by pulsed, uncontrolled fusion events. We analyze the destructive effects of such reactions on the reactor structure and show that at a scale of 100 m, the reactor proposal can withstand these effects. The estimated net electrical power output is

papers.title: Direct Light Storage with Controlled Dark Release in a Bipyridine-based Covalent Triazine Framework
papers.abstract: Utilizing bifunctional materials capable of simultaneous light harvesting and charge storage presents a compelling direct light-to-charge (electron/hole) storage strategy to circumvent the intermittency of solar energy, thereby enabling reliable power supply under dark conditions. Most of the bifunctional materials reported focus on metal oxides and metal-organic compounds. In contrast, only a few fully organic, metal-free systems exhibiting such bifunctionality have been reported, despite their inherent advantages of rich structural diversity and facile structural tunability, which enable systematic structure–property–function investigations. Here, we report a two-dimensional (2D) 2,2’-bipyridine (bpy) based crystalline covalent triazine framework (CTF), CTF-Bpy, that reversibly stores photogenerated electrons via one-electron reduction of the bpy units. Mechanistic studies suggest that the reduction of the bpy units in CTF-Bpy proceeds via a proton-couped electron transfer (PCET) process, yielding bpyH • as the predominant reduction product within the framework. Photoanodes based on CTF-Bpy show a stable photopotential of –0.92 V vs Ag/AgCl (–0.72 V vs NHE), which is so far the most negative photopotential realized in metal-free bifunctional materials. Under oxygen-free conditions, photogenerated electrons remain stable and can be controllably released on-demand in the dark, either by electrical discharge (for aqueous solar battery applications) or to reduce O 2 to H 2 O 2 . Moreover, this work also establishes CTF-Bpy as the first photochargeable covalent organic framework (COF) and CTF with trapped electrons sufficiently reducing to drive H 2 evolution in the dark, highlighting the promise of using COFs/CTFs for dark photocatalysis. The systematic investigation of the light-induced charge storage properties of CTF-Bpy with a set of spectroscopic and spectro-electrochemical techniques provides a framework for studying optoionic materials and to guide their rational design for tailored dark photocatalysis.

papers.title: From Measurements to Properties: Quantitative Inversion and Validation of Circular Dichroism and Circular Differential Scattering in Nonfluorescent Systems
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT Chirality governs the asymmetric interaction of matter with circularly polarized light. Circular dichroism (CD) and circular differential scattering (CDS) are widely used to probe optical chirality. However, the physical interpretation of CD and CDS observables remained ambiguous. Here, we develop and experimentally validate a unified theoretical framework demonstrating that both signals are governed by coupled differential and total absorption and scattering, stray light, and detection geometry. Guided by this framework, we establish a measurement strategy that integrates concurrent dual-channel CD–CDS acquisition with UV–vis extinction analysis and integrating-sphere-assisted resonance synchronous spectroscopy. This approach enables closedform inversion and validation of differential absorption and scattering together with total absorption and scattering extinction, yielding intrinsic extinction-, absorption-, and scatteringderived g-factor spectra under experimentally verifiable conditions. We demonstrate that robust CDS signals can arise in the absence of intrinsic scattering chirality, establishing CDS as a transport-mediated observable rather than a direct measure of differential scattering. Beer–Lambert scaling provides a necessary validation criterion for CD prior to conversion into ellipticity or g-factor; in contrast, CDS cannot be validated by Beer–Lambert scaling in systems exhibiting intrinsic scattering chirality and requires inversion-based determination of differential scattering. By transforming CD and CDS from geometry-assigned observables into experimentally invertible measures of intrinsic chiral optical constants, this work establishes objective validation criteria for quantitative characterization of molecular, plasmonic, and nanostructured chiral systems. Reported chiroptical g-factors should therefore be interpreted within a rigorously validated inversion paradigm.

papers.title: Nanoscale, Sub-Organellar Mapping of Lysophosphatidic Acid by Photoaffinity Labeling Reveals a Preference for ER Sheets
papers.abstract: Lysophospholipids occupy an unusual niche in membrane biology, as they are low-abundance, non-bilayer-forming lipids that can act both as soluble extracellular agonists of G protein-coupled receptors and as transient constituents of cellular membranes. Although their roles as extracellular signaling agents are well characterized, their intracellular distributions, interactomes, and functions have remained poorly defined. Here, focusing on lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), a prototypical lysophospholipid, we have developed and applied a bifunctional LPA analog to systematically interrogate the subcellular localizations and membrane protein interactomes of LPA. By integrating chemoproteomic target identification with superresolution imaging, we uncovered a previously unappreciated sub-organellar partitioning of LPA, with a preference for endoplasmic reticulum sheet domains relative to tubules. Detailed structure–function analysis of one prominent hit, CKAP4, established its single transmembrane helix as the principal determinant of LPA engagement, illustrating how this photoaffinity labeling approach can report on the nanoscale heterogeneity of the ER membrane. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive view of the LPA interactome and sub-organellar landscape, and points to unanticipated roles for this lysolipid in cell physiology.

papers.title: High-throughput tools for spatially resolved assessment of heterogeneous degradation
papers.abstract: Large-format Li-ion battery cells tend to exhibit spatial heterogeneity in terms of material degradation, which in extreme cases can contribute to the initiation and propagation of severe degradation mechanisms such as Li plating. Studying large cells poses a challenge in terms of sample statistics and effort required for an analysis which covers a large fraction of the electrode surface area. This necessitates high-throughput, quantitative techniques capable of increased surface coverage and in a time-efficient manner. In this study we present a novel method we refer to as “OLSA” (Open-circuit potential based Local State of health Assessment), that maps the local state of health (SoH) within the cell by measurement of local electrode potential combined with a fitting procedure to estimate states of charge and subsequently offsets in lithium inventory, which enables an estimation of SoH. The technique is validated and then demonstrated by mapping aged electrodes from large format prismatic cell. The results show heterogeneous distribution of local SoH and increased LLI in areas of Li plating. We also present image analysis as a complementary method for conveniently evaluating and quantifying visible degradation on the negative electrode with 100% surface coverage. In this work, we show that the regions of lithium plating coincide with lower local SoH and higher LLI. We find that although image analysis provides limited predictive capacity to predict SoH, it is a convenient and powerful tool to assist in understanding the root causes of heterogeneous degradation.

papers.title: Exciton Management in Charge-Transfer TADF OLEDs
papers.abstract: Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitters enable efficient harvesting of triplet excitons in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), yet their performance is often limited by long-lived triplet populations that promote bimolecular annihilation and efficiency roll-off at high brightness. Here, we introduce a exciton management (EM) that targets triplet accumulation independently of conventional Δ E ST minimization by mixing two TADF emitters with complementary, i.e., fast and slow reverse intersystem crossing (rISC) dynamics. Blending enables composition-dependent modification of the exciton dynamics within a coupled excited-state manifold. Time-resolved spectroscopy reveals that the mixed systems exhibit accelerated delayed fluorescence and enhanced effective rISC rates relative to the pure emitters, while simultaneously maintaining high photoluminescence efficiency. Optical excitation power-dependent measurements demonstrate suppressed annihilation signatures, consistent with reduced steady-state triplet densities under high excitation conditions. OLED devices based on mixed-emitter layers establish an intermediate operating regime, combining high low-luminance external quantum efficiencies of up to 30.8% with retained efficiencies of approximately 10-11% at 1000 cd m -2 . These results establish control over the exciton dynamics as a valuable design principle for TADF systems, providing an alternative to conventional strategies based solely on minimizing singlet-triplet energy gaps. More broadly, the approach offers a general framework for exciton management in multi-emitter OLED architectures and highlights the importance of excited-state kinetics for achieving efficient organic optoelectronic devices under high-brightness operation.

papers.title: Intermolecular carbon-carbon bond formation by a chorismate-converting enzyme
papers.abstract: Chorismate is an important precursor to many primary and secondary metabolites. Enzymes that can transform chorismate are therefore useful biocatalysts for constructing bioactive molecules, yet the scope of known chorismate biochemistry is limited. Here, we identify TunB, an enzyme that catalyzes an intermolecular carbon-carbon bond formation with chorismate in the absence of any cofactors. TunB is involved in the biosynthesis of tundrenone, a natural product produced by a methane-oxidizing bacterium and was not predicted to use chorismate as a substrate based on amino acid sequence homology. The discovery of the function of TunB therefore reveals an unexpected chorismate-converting enzyme that may enable the construction of additional scaffolds based on this important metabolite.

papers.title: Engaging Native Carboxylic Acids via Solvent-gated Proton-Relay for Photo(electro)chemical Decarboxylative Functionalization
papers.abstract: Among different ways of generating a radical species, decarboxylation of unactivated, readily available carboxylic acids is an effective, mild, high atom economy protocol. Multiple photocatalytic applications exploiting this manifold have emerged recently, where the radical could be harnessed to forge new C−C bonds. Herein, photoelectrochemistry is leveraged to demonstrate the application of this approach to a net oxidative process. After optimization of the reaction conditions, the reaction scope is assessed, involving the reaction of aliphatic carboxylic acids with nitrogen-containing heteroarenes. Multi-millimolar scale-up experiments are performed, and green metrics evaluated. An in-depth combined spectroscopic and computational study revealed the key role of the protic solvent in activating the excited dibenzo-fused heterocyclic ketone catalyst. Transient absorption spectroscopy, radical trapping, and EPR experiments elucidated the interplay of proton and electron transfer processes that activate native carboxylic acids in a novel solvent-mediated excited state proton transfer mechanism.

papers.title: CatGo: Bridging CLI Coding Agents with Interactive Structure and Workflow Management for Computational Chemistry
papers.abstract: Computational chemistry workflows are increasingly constrained not by individual calculations, but by the manual effort required to assemble, parameterize, execute, and monitor complex multi-step pipelines across heterogeneous electronic-structure engines and computing environments. Existing workflow frameworks alleviate aspects of provenance tracking and job management, yet they remain code-centric and require substantial scripting expertise, limiting accessibility and slowing scientific iteration. Here, we present CatGo, an AI-native computational chemistry platform designed for direct operation by large-language-model (LLM) coding agents through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface. In CatGo, researchers specify scientific objectives in natural language, while CLI-based agents autonomously construct, validate, execute, and monitor directed acyclic graph (DAG) workflows spanning structure generation, catalysis model preparation, electronic-structure calculations, molecular dynamics analysis, and post-processing. CatGo combines a bidirectionally synchronized visual workflow editor with an agent-operable backend, enabling seamless interaction between human users and autonomous agents within a shared workflow state. The platform integrates a catalysisoriented 3D structure environment, adsorption-site generation, heterogeneous workflow orchestration, and unified task abstractions across multiple computational engines including VASP, CP2K, ORCA, LAMMPS, and machine-learning interatomic potential frameworks. To improve agent efficiency and scalability, CatGo introduces compact graph-state serialization and batch workflow mutation operations, substantially reducing LLM tool-calling overhead during large workflow construction. We demonstrate the framework through an end-to-end oxygen reduction reaction workflow on Pt(111), where a single natural-language instruction automatically generates an executable multi-node computational pipeline spanning slab generation, adsorbate placement, geometry optimization, vibrational analysis, and free-energy assembly. Beyond workflow automation, CatGo establishes a unified agentdriven infrastructure for computational chemistry that bridges interactive visualization, autonomous workflow generation, heterogeneous compute resources, and reproducible scientific execution.

papers.title: Hydrophobic Amino Acids Control Nanocrystallinity and Mechanical Properties in Silk Mimetic Hydrogels
papers.abstract: Synthetic hydrogels often lack the exceptional properties of natural materials like spider silk, which derives its mechanics from a hierarchical architecture of β-sheet nanocrystals embedded within an amorphous matrix. Translating this design into synthetic hydrogels has been limited by the poor solubility of highly aggregating, hydrophobic peptide sequences. Here, we report a pseudoproline-based strategy for accessing aggregation-prone peptide-polymer conjugates and assembling them into silk-mimetic hydrogels. Temporary pseudoproline residues suppress intermolecular association during synthesis and conjugation to poly(ethylene glycol), and subsequent acid-mediated deprotection restores canonical residues and enables β-sheet assembly. By systematically varying amino acid identity, peptide length, and polymer architecture, we establish that both crystallinity and mechanical stiffness are more highly correlated with amino acid hydrophobicity than β-sheet propensity. Hydrogels incorporating highly hydrophobic isoleucine sequences exhibited a 15-fold increase in storage modulus compared to those utilizing the alanine sequences traditionally found in native spider silk, 313 kPa versus 20 kPa, respectively. They are up to 80-fold stiffer than equivalent purely covalent PEG networks. X-ray scattering confirms that hydrophobic sequences produce substantially higher crystallinity, with crystalline content also correlating more strongly with hydrophobicity than β-sheet propensity. Polymer topology further modulates mechanics, and linear block copolymers were up to 4.5-fold stiffer than equivalent star-PEG conjugates. Stiffer hydrogels also exhibit disproportionately higher energy dissipation, suggestive of interfacial friction at crystallite boundaries. These results establish molecular design rules for engineering hydrated silk-mimetic hydrogels and show that pseudoproline chemistry enables access to highly hydrophobic β-sheet-forming sequences that would otherwise be synthetically inaccessible.

papers.title: Vibrational Spectra of Anionic Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons in the CH Stretching Region: Anthracene, Pyrene, Perylene, and Fluoranthene
papers.abstract: The CH stretching region of the infrared spectra of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon radical anions (2700-3100 cm-1) is characterized by complicated band patterns that defy straightforward assignments from harmonic calculations. We compare experimental infrared photodissociation spectra of Argon tagged anthracene, pyrene, perylene, and fluoranthene anions with spectra computed using different methods in the framework of vibrational perturbation theory, starting from electronic structure calculations based on density functional theory. We trace the complex behavior in the CH stretching region to Fermi interactions between levels with one vibrational quantum of CH stretching excitation and vibrational states with overall two quanta in lower frequency modes characterized by CH wagging, CC stretching, and CCC bending motions. The resulting vibrational states are strongly mixed in the basis of the harmonic normal modes. Taking all 2:1 Fermi resonances in the relevant frequency range into account typically results in the best agreement between theory and experiment.

papers.title: How do Ionic Liquids Affect the Electronic Properties of Metal Oxide Supported Single Atom Catalysts? A Multiscale Computational Approach
papers.abstract: Ionic liquids (ILs) have attracted increasing attention for modifying single-site Ir(CO) 2 complexes supported on metal oxides due to their electron-donor/acceptor capabilities and their ability to tune the local catalytic environment. Previous computational studies mainly focused on specific ion–catalyst interactions using simplified IL representations or implicit solvation models. In this work, explicit IL-coated Ir(CO) 2 /SiO 2 and Ir(CO) 2 /MgO systems were investigated using a hybrid QM/QM′ ONIOM(PBE0-D3BJ/def2-SVP:PM6) approach with CM5 charge embedding to capture both the effects of support and the long-range electrostatic interactions by the IL layer. The results indicate a non-uniform IL arrangement, where anions mainly interact with the oxide surface and cations remain closer to the CO ligands. MgO support mainly controls the electronic structure through its electron-donating character, while SiO2 support is affected more by IL-induced charge redistribution. CM5 charge embedding improved agreement with experiment for ν (CO) frequencies and captured the IL-dependent trend [BMIM][Ac] > [BMIM][BF4] > [CPMIM][DCA], while [CPMIM][DCA] shows a weak, modedependent response. The limited changes in Ir–C and C–O distances indicate that the IL effect is mainly electronic and electrostatic rather than structural. These findings highlight the importance of explicit IL modeling and charge embedding for describing SCILL-type supported Ir catalysts.

papers.title: How to Critically Analyze Literature on Autonomous Experimentation
papers.abstract: Autonomous experimentation systems, also known as self-driving labs, help researchers fail smarter, learn faster, and spend less resources in their studies. These efficiencies arise from coupling novel artificial intelligence with automated lab tools. The system can then perform experiment design, execution, and analysis in a closed-loop, rapidly homing-in on the users’ goals. As the field of autonomous experimentation grows in popularity, it is important to know how to critically analyze reports of success. Missing information from a report can lead to incorrect reviews and incorrect understanding of a work. We discuss some common questions that a reader or reviewer can ask to better understand the work’s novelty, utility, implementation, and success measures.

papers.title: Leveraging Atropisomerism to Obtain a Mutant-Selective c-KIT Inhibitor in Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors
papers.abstract: Atropisomerism is a stereochemical phenomenon that is becoming increasingly prevalent in the modern drug discovery endeavor. A significant portion of small molecule drugs, including the FDA-approved multi-kinase inhibitor ripretinib, exist as unstable atropisomers, however bind their desired target in a single set of potentially atropisomeric conformations. Herein we describe studies where we synthesize atropisomerically stable analogs of ripretinib and observe divergent selectivity patterns among the atropisomers, with one atropisomer demonstrating selectivity for an oncogenic c-KIT mutant and the other atropisomer displaying intriguing selectivity towards LYN kinase. We then studied the c-KIT-active atropisomer in cellular models of mutant-c-KIT-driven Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), observing low nanomolar activities in line with those of ripretinib. The fact that these analogs had notably improved selectivity while maintaining potent activity in cellular models of GIST suggest they may be leads towards more selective multi-kinase therapeutics for GIST with fewer adverse events.

papers.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Slaked Lime Utilizing a Diaphragm Flow Cell
papers.abstract: Slaked lime (Ca(OH) 2 ) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH) 2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of (CaCO 3 ) to make CaO, followed by an exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO 3 into Ca(OH) 2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO 2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH) 2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid-base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO 3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH) 2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of > 99% pure Ca(OH) 2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm -2 .

papers.title: Robust, transferrable, and automatable techniques for systematic in silico polymerization
papers.abstract: We describe a series of well-defined and computationally-inexpensive procedures for molecular structure translation which require few inputs beyond specification of monomer chemistry, polymer sequence and system size information, and which lend themselves readily to automation via flow-based workflows to create initial descriptions of polymer systems for further simulation. To do this, we lay out a broad, graph-theoretic treatment of polymeric systems which places chemical, geometric, and topological information about a molecular system at the fore and avoids specificity to particular chemical compositions or MD software. Through this formalism, we describe solutions to several common problems encountered when translating chemical specification to polymer structure in rigorous and mathematically-precise terms that avoid ambiguity and admit proofs of the methods’ correctness. Beyond theoretical descriptions, we also supply algorithmic solution methods and provide verbal or pseudocode descriptions which naturally indicate their implementation in software, as well as comments on their domains of validity. Specifically, we describe an algorithm for tracing bond and particle information through a reaction, an algorithm for complete enumeration of chemical structures matching a template called DISCERNMENT, and an algorithm to identify unphysical ring-piercing conformations called PINPRICS.

papers.title: Contrasting pH-Dependency in Knoevenagel Condensation of Meldrum’s Acid Influenced by Substrate Concentration in Micellar Aqueous Solutions
papers.abstract: The effect of pH on Knoevenagel condensation in CTAB micellar aqueous solutions was investigated, revealing distinct reactivity under surfactant-rich and substrate-rich conditions. Under substrate-rich conditions, high pH (basic conditions) afforded the reaction product in high yield. However, when the substrate concentration relative to the surfactant was sufficiently low, the reaction was severely suppressed under the basic conditions and instead proceeded under acidic conditions. These findings highlight the critical role of substrate concentration and offer new insights for biomimetic and aqueous-phase synthetic strategies.

papers.title: SESMic: A versatile reagent for the synthesis of masked sulfinate heterocycles
Octet Completion of Surface H2O Molecules as a Proposed Charge-Driven Trigger for Evaporation and Phase Transition
papers.abstract: Evaporating water is known to carry a net negative charge 1, yet the microscopic trigger that initiates the detachment of individual H2O molecules from the liquid interface remains debated. While prior studies have addressed charge separation via ion diffusion at the phase front 1 or external-field-induced polarization 2, these approaches treat charge as a consequence of — or an external input to — the phase transition, rather than as its trigger. Here, we propose that contact electrification at the air–water interface supplies charge to the hydrogen atoms of interfacial H2O molecules, completing the molecular octet and generating electrostatic repulsion sufficient to expel the molecule into the gas phase. To test this hypothesis, we conducted four experiments: (i) container opening geometry, (ii) a modified gold-leaf electroscope, (iii) closed-circuit bottle configurations, and (iv) applied low voltage (0.10–0.20 V). The gold-leaf electroscope experiment confirmed net charge transfer during phase transition; the closed-circuit copper wire experiment showed that charge dissipation from interfacial H2O suppressed evaporation by ~22%; and the low-voltage experiment showed that evaporation progressively increased (+0.067% → +0.317%) with stepwise voltage increase (0.10 → 0.20 V). These results indicate that the supply and migration of charge at the hydrogen atoms of interfacial H2O molecules is a factor influencing evaporation, with implications for evaporation-driven energy harvesting.

papers.title: A Diversity-Oriented Chemoenzymatic Platform for the Synthesis of Indolactam Natural Products and Analogues Thereof
papers.abstract: Isolated from Streptomyces and other bacterial genera, the indolactams comprise a large family of indole alkaloids bearing a characteristic nine-membered macrolactam core. Early investigations revealed that several family members (e.g., indolactam V, lyngbyatoxin A, and teleocidin B) are potent modulators of protein kinases C (PKCs), a class of ubiquitous serine/threonine kinases that play critical roles in signaling cascades and myriad biological processes. Herein, we describe the development of a modular chemoenzymatic platform for the synthesis of indolactam natural products and derivatives thereof. By leveraging enzymes from teleocidin biosynthesis alongside traditional chemical transformations, we provide rapid and streamlined synthetic access to over twenty functionalized indolactams, lyngbyatoxins, and teleocidins. In particular, we demonstrate the synthetic utility of P450 TleB and prenyltransferase TleC for indole C–H amination and prenylation, respectively, to quickly construct and derivatize indolactam skeletons. Further use of methyltransferase- or Bronsted acid-mediated cyclization generates more complex family members, including teleocidin B-4 and several unnatural analogues thereof.

papers.title: Unusual Skeletal Editing of Oxadiazinones with Aryne Intermediates
papers.abstract: An unusual skeletal editing method involving a 6-to-8 ring expansion of oxadiazinones with aryne intermediates is disclosed. The construction of a new skeleton from oxadiazinones was confirmed by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystallographic analysis. The reaction pathway was switched from the well-studied Diels–Alder reaction followed by the denitrogenation to the ring expansion by using tetrabutylammonium difluorotriphenylsilicate as the activator.

papers.title: Sulfur-Induced Lattice Disordering in Halide Electrolytes Enables Superionic Sodium Ion Conduction
papers.abstract: Amorphous solid electrolytes provide a promising route to overcome the ion-transport limitations of crystalline halide frameworks, yet achieving superionic Na+ conduction remains challenging. Herein, we report a mixed-anion amorphous Na-ion solid-state electrolyte, TaCl5-0.5Na2S (NTSC), synthesized via high-energy ball milling, which exhibits an ultrahigh room-temperature ionic conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm and a low activation energy of 0.276 eV. Structural analyses reveal a highly disordered framework composed of Ta-centered bi-polyhedral interconnected via corner-sharing sulfur atoms [Ta2Cl10S], evidenced by comprehensive characterizations, forming a flexible, disordered amorphous network. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations identify continuous Na+ diffusion pathways with low migration barriers. Complementary topological analyses further indicate that sulfur incorporation leads to local lattice distortions, shortens Na-Na hopping distances, and enhances framework flexibility, collectively enabling fast, multidimensional Na+ transport. When applied in all-solid-state sodium-ion batteries, NTSC enables high reversible capacity (111.95 mAh/g with a Coulombic efficiency of 92.6 % at 0.1 C) and excellent cycling stability (76.9 % initial capacity retention after 200 cycles at 0.2 C) at room temperature. This work establishes mixed-anion amorphization as an effective design strategy for high-performance Na-ion solid electrolytes.

papers.title: Evaluating PBE-D3/M06 for Copper-Catalyzed Carbon Chemistry: From Kinetic Barrier Accuracy to Mechanistic Insights
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of activation barriers is essential for reliable mechanistic modeling of coppercatalyzed carbon conversion reactions, yet remains challenging for conventional density functional theory. Here, we evaluate a hybrid PBE-D3/M06 approach for reaction kinetics on low-index Cu(100), Cu(110), and Cu(111) surfaces. Benchmarking against experimental barriers for seven representative elementary reactions shows that PBE-D3/M06 achieves near-chemical accuracy, with a mean absolute error and root mean square error of 0.06 eV, substantially outperforming PBE and RPBE. The method also reproduces embedded CASPT2 trends for C–C coupling on Cu(111), correctly identifying COH*–CHO* coupling as both kinetically and thermodynamically preferred. Applied to CO2 hydrogenation to methanol on Cu(111), PBE-D3/M06 indicates that the formate-mediated pathway is favored, with HCOOH* hydrogenation as the rate-determining step. These results establish PBE-D3/M06 as an accurate and efficient framework for modeling a broad range of elementary steps in copper-catalyzed carbon chemistry.

papers.title: DNP Enhanced Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy Meets Microplastic – Sample Preparation for Optimal Sensitivity Enhancement
papers.abstract: Pollution with microplastic particles is a major environmental challenge of our time. However, little is known about the ecological hazards degraded polymer particles pose. To answer this, a qualification and quantification of the functional groups created by photooxidation of the polymer is necessary. A versatile tool to study this is the bulk method NMR spectroscopy. However, the low sensitivity of this technique makes it difficult to identify and correctly quantify defects in small concentrations. The sensitivity of NMR spectroscopy can be improved via dynamic nuclear polarisation which uses persistent radicals added to the sample. In this work, we investigate four methods to apply these radicals to weathered microplastic samples and discuss the benefits and drawbacks of each method. Our findings show that dissolving the microplastic particles in a solution of AsymPol in trichloroethylene and evaporating the solvent, to create a film yields the best sample for DNP enhanced NMR spectroscopy, as no disturbing solvent peaks remain in the spectrum and the measurement time can by decreased by a factor 35 compared to conventional solid state NMR spectroscopy. With this enhanced sensitivity we were able to measure and identify all defects of a microplastic sample weathered for 3200 h in less than a minute. Furthermore, for the first time, defects are observed in a microplastic sample weathered for only 400 h. This application of DNP enhanced NMR spectroscopy will allow for rapid screening of weathered microplastic particles enabling defect quantification at low concentrations.

papers.title: Non-exhaustive microextraction as a step towards more sustainable chemical analysis in the field and the clinic
papers.abstract: Advances in Green Analytical Chemistry have resulted in the emergence of miniaturized, integrated, and sustainable analytical workflows that deliver high performance with minimal environmental impact. However, conventional sample preparation remains a critical bottleneck, as it typically relies on exhaustive extraction approaches, in which targeted analytes are fully or close to fully removed from the sample material through laborious, solvent-intensive, and time-consuming procedures. In contrast to exhaustive extraction, many familiar analytical measurements are inherently non-exhaustive yet quantitative, such as pH detector or glucose indicator strips, which interrogate a system without depleting the analyte. Sharing the same principle, non-exhaustive partitioning enrichment—exemplified by solid-phase microextraction (SPME) approach—provides an effective alternative to multicomponent determinations by integrating sampling, extraction, cleanup, and enrichment within a single step. A wide variety of sorbent materials can be used be used to coat different objects – this combination can be optimized for the analyte’s environmental matrix or the chosen downstream detection method. SPME can be coupled with techniques like GC-MS and LC-MS for comprehensive chemical characterization or directly interfaced with advanced detection systems such as mass spectrometry and sensors. High analytical efficiency with minimal solvent consumption is further facilitated by their capacity to be integrated into automated workflows. Together, these developments outline a conceptual framework for the next generation of sustainable sample preparation methodologies, underscoring the transition of analytical chemistry toward unified, adaptive, and environmentally responsible workflows.

papers.title: Building a Physically-Interpretable Compressed Chemical Space via Grid-Based Optimization
papers.abstract: In recent years, deep generative models have been increasingly adopted for molecular optimization and design. In many such models, molecules are encoded into latent spaces that provide compact representations of their features. However, these latent spaces remain di!cult to interpret in physical terms, and it is unclear how much structural and molecular information is retained under compression. This limitation becomes especially important when molecular behavior depends on specific three-dimensional arrangements embedded in an environmental context. Here, we introduce COMPRESS (Compression Of Molecular Physical fields into Reduced Spatial Sites), an optimization framework that represents a small molecule using a fixed number of physically parameterized spatial sites. Each site is defined by three spatial coordinates and three interaction parameters, yielding a fixed-size representation that remains directly interpretable in physical terms. To preserve molecular information, COMPRESS representations are optimized to reproduce the density, electrostatic, and van der Waals fields of the corresponding all-atom molecule on discretized three-dimensional grids. We systematically evaluate how molecular information is retained as the number of sites, K, is reduced. Our analysis covers benzene, 20 chemically diverse chemical scaffolds, benzene dimers, protein-ligand complexes, and 10,000 molecules chosen from the GEOM-Drugs dataset. Across systems, field agreement deteriorates slowly at high resolution and then undergoes a rapid, pronounced transition at lower resolution. We further find that K = 25 conformers captured about 97 % of the molecules from GEOM-Drugs under a loss threshold of 0.05, which we use as an indicator of fidelity. These results show that COMPRESS can provide a fixed-size, physically interpretable molecular representation, enabling compression to be evaluated directly using molecular interaction fields and resulting physical quantities.

papers.title: Chemical Bond Analysis in Biomolecular Systems Using Intrinsic Atomic and Bond Orbitals (IAOs and IBOs) with PySCF
papers.abstract: We describe a simple, interactive protocol for analyzing chemical bonds in molecules using localized orbitals, that can be easily reproduced with minimal setup. We utilize Intrinsic Atomic Orbitals (IAOs) and Intrinsic Bond Orbital (IBOs), which are implemented in PySCF, a free Python-based software for quantum chemistry calculations. The described analysis is applied to a methylated DNA case study. We show how the presented methodology can be used in a Jupyter notebook environment, where the numerical outputs and produced orbitals can be instantly displayed.

papers.title: PDBMINER: RANK AGGREGATION-BASED SELECTION OF QUALIFIED PROTEIN DATA BANK STRUCTURES
papers.abstract: The selection of appropriate Protein Data Bank (PDB) structures is essential for structure-based computational studies such as molecular docking, virtual screening, and molecular dynamics simulations. The quality of the selected structure significantly impacts the reliability and reproducibility of computational outcomes. Researchers typically focus on a limited set of criteria, particularly resolution, for structure selection. However, structural quality encompasses multiple parameters, including crystallographic resolution, R-free, R-observed, R-work, data completeness, mutation status, and structural age. This complexity implies that a PDB entry may excel in one aspect but be inadequate in another, making PDB selection a multi-criteria decision problem. To address this challenge, we developed PDBminer, an automated pipeline designed to systematically identify and prioritize high-quality PDB structures associated with a given UniProt accession. The method retrieves all related PDB entries from the UniProt REST API, extracts structural and experimental quality metrics directly from PDB files, and applies configurable quality filters. Multiple structural criteria—including resolution, R-free, R-observed, R-work, crystallographic completeness, B-factor statistics, mutation presence, and structural age—are integrated using a rank aggregation framework to produce a unified ranking of candidate structures. Additionally, an optional redundancy filtering step removes highly overlapping entries based on UniProt residue coverage, ensuring that only representative structures are retained. Widely studied proteins such as p53 (UniProt: P04637) and the SARS-CoV-2 replicase polyprotein (UniProt: P0DTD1) contain 286 and 2422 associated PDB structures, respectively. Even when only several structural metrics—such as resolution, completeness, R-free, R-observed, R-work, mutation status, and sequence coverage—are considered, manually collecting and comparing these data across thousands of entries can require days of effort. Moreover, identifying optimal structures requires solving a multi-criteria optimization problem involving seven structural quality features, which may take weeks of manual analysis and still fail to guarantee a systematic and unbiased selection. In contrast, PDBminer automatically evaluates all available structures and produces a ranked list of candidate PDB entries within minutes. The final output is a ranked dataset exported as a structured report containing structural metrics, ligand information, and quality indicators for each candidate PDB entry. By combining automated data retrieval, multi-criteria evaluation, and rank aggregation, PDBminer provides a robust and reproducible strategy for selecting optimal PDB structures for structural bioinformatics and computational drug discovery studies. The framework enables systematic prioritization of reliable protein models and serves as a decision-support tool for structure-based computational research.

papers.title: Data-Efficient and Fast Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics through Integrated Active Learning and Knowledge Distillation
papers.abstract: We develop data-efficient machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for fast molecular dynamics simulations combining DeePMD and MACE models within an active learning and knowledge distillation framework. Using liquid water as a case study, we first independently train DeePMD and MACE models from scratch through active learning. We find that MACE requires around 3.5 times less training data than DeepMD, but its inference speed is 10 times lower. We also show that starting from a pretrained foundation model based on the MACE architecture further reduces the training data by a factor of 7, resulting in a fine-tuned foundation model with a 25 times data reduction compared to DeePMD. To overcome the limitation associated with the lower inference speed of MACE potentials, we next develop a knowledge distillation scheme to train a DeePMD potential from the fine-tuned foundation model through an inexpensive active learning workflow. The distilled model is generated with ∼10 times less computer time than the DeePMD model trained from scratch, while showing the same fast inference speed. Comparison with ab initio calculations shows that all the models reach the same level of accuracy in reproducing structural, vibrational, and diffusive properties of liquid water. Our approach enables practical, data-efficient training of customized MLIPs with high speed and accuracy.

papers.title: Scale-Up of Mechanochemical Amidation in Agitator Bead Mills: From Laboratory to Commercial Scale
papers.abstract: Bead mills are widely used in industry for particle size reduction across diverse applications; however, their use as reactors for mechanochemical synthesis has largely remained limited to laboratory studies, with no prior demonstration at manufacturing-relevant scale. Here, we report the direct scale-up of a mechanochemical amidation using standard agitator bead mills. Starting from a laboratory protocol, the process was translated via a pilot unit to an industrial mill, achieving a 22-fold increase in scale (up to 15 kg per batch) without altering core reaction parameters. Ethyl acetate was used in small quantities as a liquid-assisted grinding additive, while equimolar reagent conditions were maintained throughout, eliminating the need for excess reagents and enabling straightforward product isolation without organic solvents, thereby minimizing waste generation. Both semicontinuous and continuous single-pass operation modes delivered high conversion and selectivity within short residence times. At the largest scale, product formation rates reached 65 kg/h. The close consistency between equipment across scales enabled a straightforward transfer, demonstrating that bead milling provides a viable and scalable platform for sustainable mechanochemical manufacturing.

papers.title: Toxicological Implications of Ozone Treatments on Textiles Dyed with Reactive Dyes
papers.abstract: The increasing adoption of ozone treatments on textiles dyed with reactive dyes raises questions regarding the chemical stability of finished products and the adequacy of current compliance frameworks. This technical note adopts a hypothesis-driven approach to identify knowledge gaps in ozone-induced chemical transformations of reactive dyes. Unlike denim, where ozone degrades a single molecule (indigo), reactive dyes are complex structures applied as mixtures, undergoing incompletely characterized oxidative transformations. This work synthesizes theoretical considerations and bibliographic evidence to propose a structured agenda of analytical investigations and controlled experiments necessary to characterize potential risks and inform regulatory frameworks. The study examines primary oxidative degradation mechanisms affecting azo chromophores and metal-complex dyes under gasfiber treatment conditions, with attention to potential neo-formation of chemical species not anticipated in original Safety Data Sheets (SDS). Limitations of REACH and OEKO-TEX® schemes are discussed in relation to post-dyeing processes involving in situ chemical transformations, highlighting a regulatory "grey area." This work does not claim the existence of established risks but emphasizes the need for targeted analytical investigations and regulatory re-evaluation consistent with the evolution of textile finishing technologies.

papers.title: Harnessing Entropy for Switchable Radical Cyclization Cascades
papers.abstract: Radical cyclizations are highly selective and useful transformations in complex molecule synthesis. However, the regioselectivity of radical cyclizations is often determined by substrate structure, and in most cases, selective for 5-exo cyclization products over the 6-endo regioisomer. Herein, we address this challenge using a reaction-condition engineering approach to afford selective access to both the 5-exo and 6-endo radical cyclization products of the same substrate. The approach utilizes temperature to control the kinetic favorability of the 5-exo radical intermediate to engage in either carbon–carbon bond formation through Giese addition to deliver 5-exo functionalized products, or a one-carbon ring expansion to deliver the 6-endo functionalized product. We display this switchable cyclization approach on heteroaryl radical intermediates generated from single electron reductions of heteroaryl halides and on aryl radical intermediates generated via halogen atom transfer. Additionally, density functional theory supports that the kinetically favorable pathway is determined by reaction temperature.

papers.title: Redox-Driven Crystallization, Expansion, and Amorphization of Rutile IrO2 Nanoparticles under PEMWE Operation
papers.abstract: The development of advanced iridium oxide (IrO x ≤ 2) electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains limited by insufficiently defined structure-property relationships. Here, using operando X-ray diffraction and in-house synthesized unsupported mesoporous IrO x nanoparticles with controlled crystallinity, size, and oxidation state, alongside a commercial benchmark material, we show reversible IrO 2 lattice structure and Ir oxidation state changes across cell voltages ranging from 0.05 V to 2.00 V. At low potentials (E < 0.25 V), the IrO 2 surface partially amorphizes, linked to formation of a poorly conductive iridium oxyhydroxide (IrO (1-δ) (OH) (1+δ) ) phase. Under OER conditions, the IrO 2 lattice contracts and Ir-O bond distances shorten. Density functional theory calculations support these reversible structural and chemical transformations and explain their mechanistic origin, while on-line inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry measurements directly correlate these changes with Ir dissolution dynamics. Extending to practical conditions, a proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) operated for 500 h at 2 V shows that an initially amorphous IrO x catalyst crystallizes, ultimately degrading to performance and Tafel slopes comparable to those of rutile IrO 2 . These findings highlight the redox-driven structural flexibility of IrO x materials and link IrO 2 structure, chemistry, OER activity, and Ir dissolution during start–stop operation in PEMWEs.

papers.title: Ultrafast Upcycling of Photovoltaic Silicon Waste into β-Silicon Carbide by Flash Joule Heating
papers.abstract: The rapidly increasing accumulation of end-of-life photovoltaic (PV) modules presents both a major environmental challenge and an opportunity for sustainable resource recovery. Herein, we report an ultrafast Flash Joule Heating (FJH) strategy for directly converting photovoltaic-derived silicon into crystalline silicon carbide (SiC) within milliseconds. Recovered silicon from discarded solar cells was mixed with conductive carbon black and subjected to high-voltage electrical discharge, enabling rapid solid-state Si–C reactions under extreme nonequilibrium thermal conditions. Structural characterization confirmed the successful formation of β-SiC, while the applied voltage strongly influenced phase evolution, crystallinity, and defect generation. Among the investigated conditions, the 140 V sample exhibited the optimal balance between reaction completion and structural ordering, yielding the highest β-SiC fraction and the most favorable crystalline characteristics. In contrast, insufficient conversion was observed at lower voltage, whereas excessive flashing induced structural disorder and peak broadening due to severe thermal shock. Raman analysis further revealed the evolution of SiC vibrational modes accompanied by defect-related carbon features originating from rapid quenching during the flash process. Numerical simulations using MATLAB and COMSOL demonstrated highly localized ultrafast heating and transient thermal distributions during discharge. This work establishes a scalable and energy-efficient route for transforming photovoltaic waste into high-value ceramic materials and highlights the potential of Flash Joule Heating for sustainable waste-to-material conversion technologies.

papers.title: Mechanisms of N2 Production from N-doped Graphenes under Temperature-Programmed Desorption Analysis: A Computational Study
papers.abstract: Temperature-programmed desorption experiments have shown the release of N 2 originating from graphitic N atoms in nitrogen-doped graphenes. However, the microscopic mechanism of this desorption remains unclear. In this study, quantum chemical calculations based on density functional theory were employed to explore reaction pathways for the formation and desorption of N 2 . The calculations revealed that N atoms can migrate within the graphene lattice via repeated Stone–Wales type rearrangement involving the exchange of C–N bonds, resulting in association of two N atoms leading to desorption as an N 2 molecule. Natural bond orbital analysis reveals that this process is facilitated by the relative weakness of bonds involving nitrogen in the graphene lattice. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations for the overall reaction kinetics further supported this picture.

papers.title: Ion adsorption at polymer membranes: Surface polarity controls interfacial structuring in LiCl solutions
papers.abstract: Membrane distillation–crystallization (MD-MCr) has emerged as a promising route for recovering valuable salts and water from brine and wastewater streams; however, its industrial implementation depends critically on membrane robustness, scalability, and material chemistry, which together govern process selectivity and durability. Here, we employ constant chemical potential molecular dynamics (CμMD) simulations to probe the interfacial behaviour of LiCl solutions in contact with polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and polypropylene (PP) membranes across a range of concentrations. Concentration profiles reveal pronounced ion structuring near both polymer surfaces. PVDF exhibits gradual ion accumulation with increasing concentration, whereas PP displays distinct adsorption peaks only at higher salinity. Despite the absence of preferential ion adsorption and the resulting near-neutral interfacial charge distribution, adsorption isotherms and free-energy profiles reveal stronger affinity and greater interfacial heterogeneity for PVDF, arising from its polar fluorine groups. The deeper adsorption free-energy minima observed for PVDF indicate stronger ion–polymer interactions, consistent with the experimentally observed tendency of fluoropolymers to undergo wetting and structural modification upon prolonged exposure to lithium salts. These simulations, therefore, capture the earliest molecular-scale processes preceding membrane degradation.
