By linking polymer polarity, ion adsorption, and interfacial structuring, this work provides a molecular framework for understanding and tailoring ion–polymer interactions in membranes designed for lithium recovery and high-salinity separations.

papers.title: Protein charge transfer far from equilibrium: electron-electron interactions and application to the respiratory complex I
papers.abstract: We discuss electron transfer chains for from equilibrium, as typical for protein-mediated charge transfer across lipid bilayers. In our scenario, self-trapped electrons undergo hopping transport in a strongly polarizable dielectric environment. They are treated within a recently proposed variant of Marcus’ theory of charge transfer far from equilibrium (Castellano et al., PCCP 25, 30887 (2023)). We now consider intersite electron-electron interactions in a mean-field approach, more than one electron per site and topologies away from a linear one. These elements of theory are essential to describe charge transfer in the water-soluble part of the respiratory complex I. For this protein, we identify a crucial electron transfer step that either directly induces conformational changes or provides a coupling to electron-driven proton transfer.

papers.title: Salts of monovalent metal cations (Li-Cs, Ag) with partially fluorinated alkoxyaluminates: [Al{OCH(CF3)2}4]− and [Al{OC(CH3)(CF3)2}4]−.
papers.abstract: While fully fluorinated alkoxyaluminates like [Al{OC(CF 3 ) 3 } 4 ] − have enabled multiple groundbreaking discoveries in the chemistry of highly reactive or unstable cations, their partially fluorinated congeners, particularly [Al{OCH(CF 3 ) 2 } 4 ] − have proven more suitable for some applications, like electrochemistry or ionic salts. Despite the fact, the simplest and most basic salts (i.e. Li-Cs and Ag) of these partially fluorinated alkoxyaluminates have not yet been synthesized and or thoroughly characterized. To fill the gap, this work presents a thorough study of basic M(I) salts of [Al{OCH(CF 3 ) 2 } 4 ] − and [Al{OC(CH 3 )(CF 3 ) 2 } 4 ] − for M = Li-Cs and Ag, including synthetic protocols, crystal structure determination, assessment of thermal stability and solubility in various organic solvents together with spectral characterization (IR, NMR). The obtained results show the vast variability of properties like crystal structure, solubility and thermal stability induced by seemingly minor changes in the structure of alkoxyaluminate anions. Additionally, structures of selected solvates with acetonitrile and products of partial hydrolysis of [Al{OCH(CF 3 ) 2 } 4 ] − are discussed.

papers.title: Polyoxoniobate capped polyoxopalladates
papers.abstract: Polyoxometalates (POMs) derived from early transition metals exhibit remarkable structural diversity and tunable electronic properties. However, polyoxoniobates (PONbs) remain comparatively underexplored, particularly in hybrid systems with late transition metals. Herein, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of a giant hybrid polyoxopalladate–polyoxoniobate cluster, [Pd 19 O 8 (Nb 6 O 19 ) 8 ] 42- (Pd 19 Nb 48 ), obtained under mildly basic hydrothermal conditions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a cube-shaped Pd–Nb oxo framework encapsulating a central Pd 13 polyoxopalladate core. The Pd13 unit retains its characteristic geometry but is uniquely capped by eight Lindqvist-type [Nb 6 O 19 ] 8- clusters, replacing conventional tetrahedral oxanion capping groups. The resulting architecture represents a high nuclearity hybrid motif that integrates features of both polyoxopalladates and polyoxoniobates. Solution studies using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) support the persistence of large cluster fragments, although polydispersity is indicated. This work expands the structural landscape of POM chemistry by demonstrating the compatibility of Pd-based polyoxometalates with highly charged niobate building units, offering new opportunities for integrating basicity with catalytic redox activity.

papers.title: Influence of additives on long-term degradation and microplastic formation of polyethylene
papers.abstract: There are limited studies showing how additive contents used for packaging plastics affect polymer degradation and microplastic formation. Hence, we used accelerated abiotic weathering for studying the mechanisms leading to the degradation of additivated, semi-crystalline low-density polyethylene (LDPE). For this purpose, LDPE plates with different, realistic concentrations of additives (antioxidants and UV stabilizers) were weathered in an accelerated weathering chamber and analyzed using SEM, DSC, high temperature GPC and solid-state 13C CP MAS NMR spectroscopy. Our results reveal that non-UV-stabilized LDPE degrades rapidly, showing extensive microcracking, molecular weight reduction, and formation of polar polymer defects within 600 hours. The addition of hindered amine light stabilizers (HALS) significantly delays these effects, yet their performance varies depending on the specific formulation. While Tinuvin 622 protects the polymer for about 2500 hours before sudden degradation and cracking occurs, Tinuvin 783 effectively prevents severe chain scission and large crack formation over the sampled 4000 hours of exposure. However, even with Tinuvin 783, fine surface microcracks still develop and cause the detachment of small microplastic particles. Ultimately, the most important finding is that even small amounts of additives have strong effects dictating not only the degradation kinetics but also the shape and chemical composition of the secondary microplastic particles formed by fragmentation.

papers.title: A Host-Guest Strategy to Achieve Selective and Robust CO2-to-CO Electrocatalysis in Aqueous Media.
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous materials incorporating molecular catalysts hold strong promise for efficient electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction to value-added products. While activity and selectivity are traditionally tuned through ligand design, increasing attention is being paid to the secondcoordination sphere, which modulates reactivity beyond the metal center. Inspired by enzymatic systems, this outer-sphere environment enhances catalysis through spatial confinement and noncovalent interactions. Here, we report a host-guest strategy to control CO 2 reduction using the [bpyMn(CO) 3 MeCN] + catalyst encapsulated in an anionic cage. When immobilized on electrode surface, the assembly achieves selective CO production. Mechanistic studies indicate that the cage promotes proton-coupled CO 2 binding while preventing catalyst deactivation. This demonstrates that supramolecular second-sphere engineering is a powerful strategy for enhancing electrocatalytic performance and provide a basis for future developments in molecular electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Extending the Python RESP Framework for Extra Point Charge Fitting
papers.abstract: The Restrained Electrostatic Potential (RESP) method is widely used to derive electrostatic parameters for Newtonian-based models. However, conventional nuclei centered charge models can struggle to reproduce anisotropic features such as halogen σ-holes and electron lone-pair regions. Herein, an extension is presented of the Psi4compatible Python resp implementation of Alenaizan et al. that enables partial atomic charge fitting to user-defined extra point sites represented as massless dummy particles. This refactoring introduces an INI-based configuration layer, a revised driver.py that propagates extra point sites through grid/ESP handling, and an updated espfit.py engine that continues to support multi-conformer fitting. Also introduced into the code are functions for computing RMSE and RRMSE metrics. The resulting workflow is transparent, reproducible, and enables the development of both nuclei-centered and off-centered electrostatic models for molecular mechanics-based simulations.

papers.title: Click-polymerized polyenamine membranes for efficient lithium extraction
Regiocontrolled Minisci Alkylations Guided by Phosphonium Ions
papers.abstract: Significant improvements in the regioselectivity of Minisci alkylations have been enabled by adopting N-heteroaryl phosphonium salts as substrates for this textbook transformation. Minisci chemistry has been a workhorse synthetic protocol in industry and academia for decades since it generates more-complex N-heteroaryls such as pyridines by C–H alkylation of the latter species with abundant precursors like carboxylic acids. Its wide scope, robustness, and operational simplicity are also major advantages, but its regioselectivity is often poor and general solutions have been slow to emerge. This strategy draws on reliable regioselective methods to install phosphonium groups onto N-heteroarenes. We have demonstrated herein that C2-alkylation of easily accessible C4-PPh 3 +-containing pyridines and quinolines (and C4-alkylation of C2-PPh 3 +-containing quinolines) regiospecifically generates a range of alkylation patterns that have previously proven challenging for Minisci chemistry to access selectively – especially when using more-abundant alkyl sources. Moreover, the preliminary application of this strategy to further N-heteroarenes shows that sites less- or unreactive with alkyl radicals can be exclusively engaged by using the phosphonium group to block the preferred Minisci reaction site. Finally, after the alkylation, mild hydrolysis can tracelessly remove the PPh 3 + handle, or a suite of established substitutions can be used to enable regiospecific C–H/C–H difunctionalizations across the PPh 3 + installation/Minisci/PPh 3 + substitution sequence.

papers.title: Standard reporting of the uncertainty in reaction yield applied to a CO2 transfer reaction
papers.abstract: In the organic literature, reaction yields are typically reported as single values with no estimate of uncertainty that would enable others to judge the reproducibility of reported procedures. Herein, we demonstrate a simple, standardised approach for reporting reaction yield as its mean value, accompanied by a confidence interval calculated from repeat experiments. We use CO 2 transfer carboxylation to show that variability plots and confidence intervals provide interpretable measures of yield reproducibility and are useful tools to identify outliers and prompt scrutiny of scale-up behaviour or sources of experimental variability. We make recommendations for best practice in reporting the variability of experimental outcomes and introduce a secure browser-based tool, the Physical Sciences Data Infrastructure (PSDI) Variability Plot Generator, to facilitate transparent reporting of process reproducibility.

papers.title: Interpretable Metal-Chemistry and Minimal-Context Descriptors for MOF Water and Activation Stability: A Reproducible Benchmark of Descriptor Sufficiency, Split Sensitivity, and Screening Utility
papers.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely studied for gas storage, separations, catalysis, sensing, and electrochemical conversion, but these functions matter only if the framework survives activation and remains stable in water or humid environments. Yet MOF stability prediction still sits awkwardly between empirical chemical intuition and machine-learning models built from descriptors that are often difficult to interpret or reproduce. Here, we present a chemistry-led benchmark that tests how far stability prediction can be advanced using transparent descriptors, including metal identity, mixed-metal character, open-metal-site information, coarse topology, porosity, and compact thermophysical terms. Using two cleaned CoRE MOF-derived benchmark tables, the activation-stability resource (ASR, 1372 entries) and the framework-survival resource (FSR, 1192 entries), we model continuous solvent and water stability, include thermal stability as a supplementary regression task, and assess threshold-based screening at 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8. Random Forest models with the most complete descriptor regime perform best overall, with water stability consistently more predictable than solvent-removal stability. However, random splits are markedly more optimistic than grouped splits by metal family and topology, exposing a substantial interpolation–extrapolation gap. Overall, the results show that simple, chemically interpretable descriptors contain meaningful stability signal, but credible extrapolative claims require chemically aware validation.

papers.title: Leveling up upconverting nanoparticles with machine learning
papers.abstract: Upconverting nanoparticles (UCNPs) transform low-energy light into higher-energy photons, enabling applications in subwavelength and subsurface imaging, nanoscale sensing, therapeutics, optogenetics, printing, and optical computing. However, the widespread adoption of UCNPs is hindered by their low brightness and limited spectral tunability. Predicting the ideal nanoparticle architectures to overcome these limitations is challenging, because UCNP photophysics are governed by highly nonlinear, complex energy transfer networks that span the excited states of lanthanide dopants. Due to the large number of possible combinations of dopants, concentrations, host matrices, heterostructures, and reaction conditions, optimizing the compositional and synthetic parameters of UCNPs using conventional trial-and-error approaches is intractable. This Account explores how researchers can overcome these challenges and enhance the properties of UCNPs using artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). We first review how the early foundations of AI-guided discovery were established with automated experimental workflows and physical modeling. Using robotic synthesis platforms and differential rate equation models, researchers have successfully navigated high-dimensional compositional spaces to reveal optical phenomena such as energy-looping and photon avalanching in nanoparticles. Building on these data-driven approaches, ML was integrated into UCNP research initially for processing raw characterization data, such as automating the analysis of TEM images and time-resolved luminescence curves. AI approaches were extended to interpret signals in applications that utilize UCNPs, such as classifying the cytotoxicity of drugs based on upconversion luminescence microscopy data. Most significantly, ML is driving the design of new UCNP compositions and structures, including our recent development of closed-loop active learning of UCNP core-shell heterostructures. By coupling Bayesian optimization with kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations, we achieved 110-fold enhancement in UCNP emission over just 40 iterations. To bypass the steep computational cost of simulating UCNP heterostructures with up to 9 shells, we leveraged differentiable deep learning surrogate models based on heterogeneous graph neural networks to perform inverse design. Notably, these hetero-GNNs were able to extrapolate far outside of the model’s training data and predict UCNP heterostructure compositions with 6.5-fold more intense emission than the brightest UCNP in the training set. In the future, we predict that AI/ML approaches will become integral to UCNP research. UCNP experiments may soon be accelerated by autonomous self-driving laboratories in which robotic synthesis, in-line characterization, and ML agents operate in a closed feedback loop to intelligently investigate underexplored chemical spaces. Large language models (LLMs) could parse literature to develop overarching hypotheses and detailed recipes for these autonomous workflows, with generative models suggesting novel structures to test. Together with human creativity and critical analysis, these AI tools will accelerate the discovery of advanced upconverting nanomaterials, aiding fundamental understanding of their mechanisms, and inspiring a broader array of photonic applications.

papers.title: Absolute Binding Free Energy Calculations between the SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease and 130 Drug Leads using Implicit Ligand Theory
papers.abstract: Absolute binding free energy (ΔG) calculations can rank structurally diverse compounds, which could be useful for early-stage drug discovery. Unfortunately, for flexible systems, it can be challenging to sample the receptor conformations necessary to obtain converged ΔG calculations. Here, we address this challenge by leveraging extensive molecular dynamics simulations of apo SARS-CoV-2 main protease (MPro) that were conducted on the Folding@Home distributed computing system. A Markov State Model (MSM) was built to compute the equilibrium probability of each snapshot. Representative snapshots were selected from clusters defined based on occupancy fingerprints of the catalytic site. The binding potential of mean force (BPMF), the binding free energy between a ligand and rigid receptor configuration, was computed between the representative snapshots and 130 drug leads from the COVID Moonshot, an open-source drug discovery project. ΔGs were computed using an exponential average of BPMFs based on implicit ligand theory (ILT). ΔG calculations recapitulated experimental values with a Pearson R of 0.55 and mean-adjusted root mean square error of 1.6 kcal/mol. Accuracy and computational costs were found to be intermediate between docking and previous free energy calculations with a fully flexible receptor. Moreover, in 88% of systems, the calculated ΔG of the native binding pose (RMSD from crystallographic < 3 Å) was within 1 kT of the top-ranked pose.

papers.title: Anti-Kasha emission in DCM-IFC: Computational evaluation of the Type III separated wavefunction hypothesis
papers.abstract: Kasha's rule, which states that the emitting electronic level of a given multiplicity is the lowest excited level of that multiplicity, is central to the understanding of photochemistry, and the exception due to a large (S1-S2) energy gap, exemplified by azulene, is well understood. Over the last few years, examples of large flexible molecules with modest (S1-S2) energy gaps have been reported to show anti-Kasha (AK) emission, and have been rationalised on the basis of highly spatially separated wavefunctions of the two states. Recently, a fluorophore, having such characteristics, was constructed from dicyanomethylene-4H-pyran (DCM) and integrated fluorescein-chromene (IFC), where a spirolactane open/closed switch was shown to regulate AK behaviour. The open form of the molecule illustrated dual emission which was interpreted as emission from both S1 and S2 states. Here, we investigate theoretically both the FC region and the interpolated pathways towards S2/S1-intersection region using implicit solvation. We calculate excited state energies and oscillator strengths employing both time-dependent density functional theory (with a range of functionals) and high-level wavefunction theories, characterising that the S1 state is the brighter of the valence excited states, dominated by locally excited character, whereas the S2 state is of charge-transfer character and is darker in comparison. Our ab-initio calculations indicate that the spectral absorption profiles for the two states overlap, and that there are barrierless internal conversion pathways from the FC region on the S2 surface towards the S2/S1-intersection region, which is consistent with efficient and rapid S2 population decay in this molecule making AK emission less likely. Moreover, energy difference between S1 and S2 states at each of the S1 and S2 excited state minima is unlikely to favour thermal equilibration of population at timescales relevant to emission. Taken together, the present calculations suggest that the experimentally observed anomalous emission requires an alternative interpretation.

papers.title: Where do we go from here? Current state of drug-target binding kinetics and a roadmap to their establishment in drug discovery campaigns
papers.abstract: Due to the observation that kinetic rates can be better correlated with in vivo drug efficacy than simple affinities, significant efforts have been made to develop experimental and computational methods to predict drug-target residence times over the last years. Here, we summarize the discussions and reflections from an international CECAM workshop which took place in March 2025 with participants from both academia and industry, including experimentalists as well as computational scientists, and was dedicated to computational methods for protein-ligand binding kinetics prediction. As currently standing challenges, we identify the need for standardized benchmark data sets, the need to move from simple to more complex and biomedically relevant targets and the question how academia and industry can work together to move the field of drug-target binding kinetics forward. We also discuss what level of accuracy can be expected from computational methods, and highlight that the field would benefit from blind challenges to enable a fair comparison of different computational methods to predict kinetic rates.

papers.title: Bridging Bioassay-Guided Isolation and Metabolomics: Toward Hybrid Strategies in Natural Product Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Natural product (NP) remains an important source of drug discovery, providing approximately 32% of newly introduced small molecule drugs between 1981 to 2019. Their unique chemical complexity presents an abundance of active novel chemical entities, but it also raises challenges in its identification and isolation. Two primary methods dominate these fields: the traditional bioassay-guided isolation (BGI) and the more recent metabolomics-based discovery approaches. Despite extensive use of both methods, a systematic framework that integrates their complementary strengths remain insufficiently developed. To address this gap, this review proposes an integrative framework that links metabolomics-based compound prioritization with subsequent BGI validation. This review critically evaluates findings from peer-reviewed studies published between 1958 to 2024 to compare the principles, technical capabilities, strengths limitations, and bridges their integrative applications in NP drug discovery. Our analysis shows that metabolomics excels in early-stage exploration by providing broad chemical coverage, high sensitivity, and efficient prioritization of active novel compounds, while BGI remains essential for definitive isolation, mechanistic evaluation, and biological activity confirmation. By framing metabolomics as a decision-support stage rather than a replacement for BGI workflows, this review emphasizes integrative discovery that improves efficiency, reduce rediscovery, and preserve chemical rigor. Such hybrid strategies could reduce the research timeline for the discovery of NP-based new chemical entity with improved precision and reproducibility.

papers.title: Amino Acid Alkyl Ester Ferulates as Potential Neuroprotective and Anti-Aging Agents
papers.abstract: Ferulic acid (FA) is a compound characterized by strong antioxidant properties – it neutralizes free radicals and inhibits the formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). These properties make it useful in preventing diseases caused by oxidative stress, such as Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the use of ferulic acid is significantly limited by its low water solubility and poor absorption from the digestive system. This paper presents the synthesis and identification of new ferulic acid derivatives with ethyl, isopropyl, and propyl esters of L-tyrosine and L-phenylalanine. Analytical methods such as NMR, FTIR, DSC, and TG were used to identify and determine the physicochemical properties. The solubility of the obtained derivatives in water and in a PBS buffer solution (pH 7.4) was determined and compared with the solubility of the parent acid. The antioxidant activity was determined using the DPPH, ABTS, and ORAC tests. The inhibitory activity of salts and hydrochlorides of amino acid esters against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) from Electrophorus electricus was also investigated. Molecular docking was then performed to predict the interaction of the tested compounds with the active center of ACHE. All derivatives showed better solubility in water and buffer solution than ferulic acid. The derivative with tyrosine ethyl ester [TyrOEt][FA] showed the highest solubility. Additionally, the obtained derivatives demonstrated antioxidant properties comparable to or greater than those of ferulic acid. In the ORAC assay, derivatives with tyrosine alkyl esters exhibited nearly twofold higher activity than the parent acid. The analyzed compounds also showed greater inhibitory activity against AChE than ferulic acid itself, with the phenylalanine isopropyl ester salt, [PheOiPr][FA], displaying the strongest inhibitory effect. These findings suggest that these derivatives may find application in preventing oxidative stressrelated skin damage as well as in preventing and delaying the progression of Alzheimer’s disease.

papers.title: Polyanionic calix[4]arenes and their 2,2’-bithiazolyl derivatives demonstrating Potent Anti-Human Coronavirus HCoV-229E Activity In Vitro.
papers.abstract: In this study, we report the biological evaluation of six conical calix[4]arene macrocycles as potential antiviral agents against human coronavirus HCoV-229E. They carry at the upper rim four anionic groups (sulfonate, acetate, or methylene phosphonate) and, in three cases, two 2,2’bithiazole units in alternate positions at the lower rim. Guided by the hypothesis that pre-organized negative charges could interfere with positively charged viral proteins involved in host cell entry — such as the spike (S) protein — we assessed their antiviral activity. The three anionic calixarenes without bithiazole arms exhibited modest activity (EC50 of approximately 76 µM for sulfonate, 118 µM for acetate, and 18 µM for phosphonate). In contrast, their bithiazolyl analogues showed greatly enhanced efficacy, with EC50 values of 1.0 µM, 24 µM, and 1.5 µM, respectively. Importantly, all compounds demonstrated low to very low cytotoxicity on human lung fibroblast MRC-5 cells, confirming their favorable safety profile. These findings highlight the strong potential of functionalized calix[4]arenes as a new class of antiviral agents, not only against coronaviruses but possibly a broader range of enveloped viruses.

papers.title: Amphipathic helical peptide-functionalized gold nanoparticles for colorimetric sensing via modulation of salt-induced aggregation upon binding to highly-curved membranes
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a novel colorimetric sensing platform for biological nanovesicles based on amphipathic helical peptide (AHpep)-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). Unlike conventional sensing strategies that typically rely on target-induced aggregation, this approach utilizes the modulation of salt-induced aggregation through target-mediated stabilization. The AHpep units selectively bind to the lipid packing defects of highly curved membranes via a hydrophobic insertion mechanism. This binding provides a physical barrier that enhances the colloidal stability of the AuNPs against salt-induced aggregation, thereby suppressing plasmonic coupling and maintaining the characteristic dispersed red state of the nanoparticles. We show that this stabilization effect is intrinsically curvature-selective; small liposomes (110 nm in diameter) yield significantly more effective stabilization than larger liposomes (700 nm), as confirmed by both UV-vis spectroscopy and dark-field microscopy (DFM). Furthermore, the system enables the selective colorimetric discrimination of enveloped viruses, such as human coronavirus 229E (HCoV), from non-enveloped adeno-associated virus-2 (AAV). While establishing a proof of concept for the sensitive detection of enveloped viruses (limit of detection = 4.9 x 10 7 particles/mL for HCoV), this study provides a straightforward yet powerful strategy for expanding the scope of AuNP-based colorimetric analytical assays for biological nanovesicles.

papers.title: Harnessing triplets via donor rigidification in vacuum-deposited organic photovoltaics
papers.abstract: The power conversion efficiency of organic photovoltaics (OPVs) is fundamentally constrained by substantial non-radiative loss, predominantly from triplet excitons that reside at the lowest excited-state levels. To address this, we designed a conformationally rigidified donor 25 R-D. Using transient absorption spectroscopy, we experimentally verified that triplets can be dissociated back into charge-transfer states and recycled into free carriers, thereby converting a dominant loss pathway into a productive resource. In vacuum-deposited OPVs, this tripletharnessing mechanism enables a fill factor of 75.67%, breaking the long-standing ~68% ceiling for this platform, and a record power conversion efficiency of 11.12%. Our work thus offers a 30 framework for linking molecular structure to device performance through the control of chargecarrier dynamics, establishing donor rigidification as a practical design strategy toward highperformance OPVs.

papers.title: Comparing outdoor and accelerated weathering of polystyrene, polyethylene and polypropylene – towards predicting the fate of environmental microplastics
papers.abstract: Accelerated weathering becomes increasingly popular in microplastic research to produce defined, environmentally relevant reference particles and determine their degradation kinetics. However, to predict the persistence of environmental microplastics, models must be developed that correlate real-life with accelerated weathering. Therefore, we conducted long-term accelerated and outdoor weathering studies using amorphous polystyrene (PS), semi-crystalline low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and polypropylene (PP) particles. In all cases, the particles weather according to the same principles. Photooxidation induces chain scissions, crosslinks and polar, oxygen-containing functional groups. At the same time, the particles degrade following a three-stage model where surface abrasion is followed by fragmentation. While the mechanical stress was similar and kept constant for all experiments, temperature and irradiance varied for the outdoor setting. By introducing a time-dependent acceleration factor composed of the Schwarzschild and Arrhenius laws, we could derive a model with the materialspecific activation energy (EA) and Schwarzschild coefficient p as only free parameters. EA and p determine how strongly the timescales between outdoor and accelerated weathering divide, rendering the model’s predictive power polymer-type dependent. The model uses publicly available weather data and thus predicts seasonal and regional variations of the outdoor degradation rates with higher accuracy compared to common models using an average temperature or a constant acceleration factor. Synopsis: The characteristics of commodity plastics like PS, PE and PP weathered in natural environments can be predicted by parameterizing the irradiance and temperature from accelerated weathering studies.

papers.title: Main Group Metals in Redox Catalysis
papers.abstract: Main group metal redox catalysis is no longer a curiosity; it is a credible challenger to transition-metal chemistry. Heavy p-block elements, once dismissed as redox-inert or limited to Lewis acid reactivity, now can execute the core elementary steps of catalysis, including coordination, oxidative addition, reductive elimination, transmetalation, and single-electron transfer events. This review surveys recent advances across groups 13–15, focusing on aluminium, germanium, tin, antimony, and bismuth, the elements that have begun to deliver genuine metal-centred redox catalytic performance. Reactivity is unlocked not by formal oxidation state alone, but by careful ligand design and through ambiphilicity, weak bonding, element–ligand cooperation, and access to open-shell manifolds. The field is advancing fast, but unevenly. Group 13 is just getting started, whereas Ge, Sn, Sb, and especially Bi already operate across both twoelectron and radical regimes. Beyond summarising progress, this review defines the design rules, exposes mechanistic gaps, and highlights opportunities that are likely to decide what comes next. Heavy p-block elements are no longer just substitutes to transition metals. They are competitors, and increasingly, they are setting the terms for sustainable catalysis.

papers.title: Iterative Non-Canonical Amino Acid Peptide Drug Discovery via Sign-Direction Reproducible Evaluation: A Multi-Layer Verification Framework
papers.abstract: Non-canonical amino acid (ncAA) substitutions are central to peptide-drug development, yet quantitative in silico ranking of ncAA variants remains constrained by force-field junction parameters at the canonical / non-canonical boundary, charge-derivation provenance, and the limited reproducibility of MM-PBSA / MM-GBSA scoring at small mutational scales. Khoury et al. (2014) reported a comprehensive same-system MM-GBSA / experimental correlation of R² = 0.388 over 147 ncAAs, defining a defensible field ceiling that newer methods only partially close. We present UPDD (Universal Peptide Drug Discovery), a five-stage iterative pipeline whose differentiating contribution is its Stage-4 evaluation framework for ncAA-modified peptide complexes (ncAA parameterisation → restrained MD → QM/MM single-point → MM-PBSA scoring), integrated with established generation tools (RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + AlphaFold2). We position UPDD at Capability Level 1: a decision-support tool for ncAA variant ranking, not a quantitative experimental predictor. Three methodological contributions are documented: (1) a σ_btwn / σ_w ensemble-quality decomposition with a single-metric Convergence Index (CI = σ_btwn / |⟨⟨ΔG⟩⟩|) carrying a dual interpretation (binding-mode classifier and automated quality-control auditor); (2) a branched ΔΔG architecture with bit-identical wild-type control (intervention isolation verified at floating-point precision); and (3) a multi-layer verification protocol empirically validated by four sequential audit layers — closed-shell charge bias, periodic-boundary serialisation, intra-residue bond integrity for HETATM ncAAs, and source-versus-test consistency. Across six ncAA peptide-target families (1EBP / 1YCR / 2QKH / 2QKI / 3IOL / 7TL8), the framework demonstrates sign-direction reproducibility on a validated subset, six-of-six Definition-3 readiness, and three biophysical detachment events distinguished from periodic-image artefacts. We acknowledge the Khoury R² = 0.388 ceiling, position the next charge-methodology axis (Khoury full RESP) as the planned v0.8 work, and decline universal quantitative-match claims. An iterative active-learning loop with wet-lab K_d feedback is operationally specified, and closed-loop calibration remains the v0.8 / v1.0 milestone.

papers.title: SIMPLE AND COMPARABLE COMPUTATION OF INCREMENTAL CAPACITY CURVES
papers.abstract: Incremental capacity (IC) analysis is a widely used non-destructive method to characterise the state of Li-ion batteries. However, there is no standard approach to compute IC curves robustly and reproducibly. Most implementations rely on numerical differentation, which amplifies measurement noise and thus requires extensive noise filtering. The smoothing method and associated parameters are selected by trial-and-error, producing inconsistent ad hoc IC curves hindering reliable comparison across studies. We promote voltage histograms as a simple alternative for computing IC curves and introduce voltage reconstruction as an objective criterion to assess their quality. Histogram-based ICs use the intuitive bin size as the only parameter, are robust to voltage noise, require little or no filtering, handle non-monotonic voltage features, and apply to the open-circuit voltage profiles of a variety of active materials. Voltage histograms also reconstruct the voltage curve accurately, enabling quantification of individual IC contributions. We discuss the limitations of the method and associated mitigation strategies. Together, histogram-based implementation and voltage reconstruction offer a reproducible framework for computing IC curves comparable across battery materials, samples, and studies.

papers.title: Smart Polymeric Nanocarriers in Targeted Drug Delivery: From Design to Clinical Translation
papers.abstract: Stimuli-responsive polymeric nanocarriers (SRPNs) are an advanced form of drug delivery systems that have been designed for targeted drug delivery and controlled release of drugs. Unlike conventional drug delivery systems, which are based on passive targeting, SRPNs are triggered by specific internal or external stimuli, such as pH, temperature, enzymes, light, ultrasound, or magnetic fields, to release the drug at the desired location. Stimuliresponsive release of drugs has the potential to offer improved therapeutic efficacy with reduced adverse effects and overall toxicity. This review focuses on polymeric nanocarriers, within the larger context of stimuli-responsive drug delivery systems, including polymeric nanoparticles, micelles, dendrimers, hydrogels, liposomes, and their hybrids. It covers the mechanisms of targeted delivery and stimuli responsiveness, as well as methods of fabrication and evaluation. The role of key physicochemical parameters, including particle size, surface charge, and polymeric composition, in nanocarrier performance is also reviewed. The review covers the present challenges in the translation of SRPNs into practical clinical applications, including issues of toxicity, storage stability, scalability, and regulatory issues. Recent developments in AI-assisted design and personalized medicine, which may improve nanocarrier design and specificity are also discussed. The purpose of this review is to offer a concise synthesis of the importance of stimuli-responsive polymeric nanocarriers in targeted drug delivery.

papers.title: Stability-Aware Multi-Objective Discovery of Metal-Organic Frameworks for Direct Air Capture
papers.abstract: The direct air capture (DAC) of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere requires sorbents that combine strong adsorption at dilute CO2 conditions with resistance to competitive H2O adsorption and robust structural stability. In this work, we present a stability-aware, multiobjective computational framework that integrates machine learning (ML) and evolutionary algorithm (NSGA-III) optimization to identify optimal candidate metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for DAC that exhibit the best trade-offs in stability and performance. We use NSGA-III to explore a large chemical space of over 180 million MOFs that we create by combining experimentally derived building blocks with systematic metal substitution and linker functionalization to maintain synthetic realism. In our workflow, we optimize seven objectives simultaneously: five stability metrics, i.e., thermal, activation, water, acid, and mechanical stability, and two performance metrics, i.e., CO2 uptake and CO2/H2O selectivity. Explicit multicomponent simulations reveal design principles distinct from those obtained under singlecomponent or binary mixture (CO2/N2) conditions. We show that motifs previously found to be favorable, such as open metal sites, metal–oxygen-metal bridges, or uncoordinated nitrogen atoms, do not exhibit advantages under humid conditions. Instead, we identify coordination saturated metal centers and dispersion-dominated environments, including parallel aromatic ring motifs, to enhance CO2 uptake. This work establishes a generalizable framework for stability-aware MOF discovery for DAC under realistic operating conditions, with natural extensions to other challenges, such as point source capture.

papers.title: MetalMiner: A Chemically Informed Workflow for Data-Driven Mining of Metal Coordination Environments from Cambridge Structural Database
papers.abstract: Crystallographic databases contain a vast body of experimentally grounded information on metal coordination chemistry, yet converting these records into analysis-ready datasets remains challenging. In most cases, the chemically meaningful object is not the deposited crystal structure as a whole, but the local metal-centered coordination environment. Large-scale analysis are further complicated by incomplete or inconsistent bonding information, omitted hydrogen atoms, ambiguous oxidation states, structural disorder, and polymeric connectivity. Here, we present MetalMiner, a chemically informed workflow for end-to-end mining of metal coordination environments from the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD). MetalMiner treats the metal site as the fundamental unit of analysis and integrates local cluster extraction, primary-sphere disorder handling, ligand reconstruction and charge assignment, oxidation-state determination, and export of structured, site-resolved outputs for downstream analysis. We demonstrate its broader utility through four connected use cases. First, we construct a curated lanthanide-actinide dataset and use it to map the multiscale organization of Ln3+ coordination space, revealing coordination archetypes, coordination grammar, and underexplored regimes. Second, we use the same dataset to evaluate how effectively Ln3+ ions reproduce the primary coordination environments of trivalent actinides, providing a structure-aware basis for surrogate selection across the f-block. Third, we show that MetalMiner enables scalable generation of computation-ready inputs for first-principles electronic-structure calculations directly from crystallographic records. Fourth, we demonstrate that MetalMiner can produce structured, LLM-ready chemical descriptors from licensed crystallographic data. Together, these results establish MetalMiner as a general framework for converting crystallographic records into curated, chemically interpretable, and machine-actionable datasets for data-driven coordination chemistry.

papers.title: Designed to Guide, Destined to Pollute: The Overlooked Microplastic Source in Agricultural Mulch Films
papers.abstract: Mulching is a common agricultural practice that improves crop quality and yield. However, it also contributes to soil contamination with microplastics, raising environmental concerns. To develop sustainable agricultural policies, quantifying microplastic pollution in soils caused by mulching is essential. Despite their design for perennial use and widespread application, woven polypropylene films have not yet been investigated as a potential microplastic source. Here, we examined microplastic contamination in an agricultural field mulched for twelve years with a black woven polypropylene film with green marking lines. About 4000±1700 polypropylene particles per kilogram of dry soil were detected, with mulch film fragments making up ~60% of the total microplastic load. Although the green marking lines only constitute 2.5 wt% of the applied mulch film, they account for the majority (62%) of these fragments. We show that the significantly faster degradation of the marking lines is caused by enhanced photooxidation due to covalent grafting of the green dye using maleic anhydride and a lack of efficient UV protection. In contrast, the black woven fabric is protected against photooxidation by the addition of carbon black, causing less microplastic contamination (38%). In the pristine films, the environmentally problematic plasticizer DEHP (~0.1 mol%) was identified. However, after twelve years in the field, the DEHP content fell below the detection limit, indicating leaching. Our work highlights the marking lines as a major source of microplastic pollution in the investigated field, which can be easily avoided by alternative film design. Our results further urge a critical reassessment of problematic additives in mulch films.

papers.title: Structure-guided discovery of 1H-pyrazolo[3,4-c]pyridin-3-amines as a novel class of hematopoietic progenitor kinase 1 (HPK1) inhibitors
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic progenitor kinase 1 (HPK1) is an intracellular negative regulator of immune responses, particularly in T cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Compelling genetic evidence indicates that HPK1 impairs multiple stages of antitumor immunity largely via its kinase activity, thereby positioning it as a promising target for cancer immunotherapy. Starting from two 3-aminopyrazole hits identified through in-house screening, we initiated a structure-guided medicinal chemistry campaign. Through multi-stage optimization to enhance potency by engaging the Asp101 residue and to improve kinase selectivity via molecular hybridization, we developed a novel series of 1 H -pyrazolo[3,4- c ]pyridin-3-amine derivatives, from which D5 emerged as a key representative. Compound D5 exhibited potent HPK1 inhibitory activity (IC 50 = 26.3 nM), and inhibited SLP76 phosphorylation and promoted IL-2 secretion in cell-based assays. Importantly, D5 showed favorable selectivity across diversity and immune-focused kinase panels, representing a marked improvement over its earlier analogue C4 . Furthermore, D5 significantly suppressed tumor growth in the CT26 syngeneic mouse model without causing observable body weight loss. Overall, this work provides both a promising lead and a novel chemical scaffold, offering valuable insights and a concrete starting point for HPK1-targeted drug discovery.

papers.title: Organic Full-Stokes Photodetectors Distinguishing Arbitrary Polarization States of Light
papers.abstract: Organic photodetectors have emerged as a promising technology for nextgeneration optoelectronic devices owing to their unique advantages including mechanical flexibility, solution processability, and tunable spectral response. Perceiving the polarization state of light, such as linearly and circularly polarized light information beyond intensity and wavelength, is essential for advanced optoelectronics; however, full-Stokes organic photodetectors that can distinguish arbitrary polarization states of light have not been reported to date. Here, we construct aligned chiral polymer assemblies that integrate chirality and anisotropy simultaneously to achieve the first full-Stokes organic photodetector. The chiral helicene dopants induce pronounced chiroptical activity in polyfluorene-based polymers, while solution shearing yields longrange anisotropy. Photodiodes based on these films demonstrate excellent device performance in detecting both linearly and circularly polarized light, and importantly, full-Stokes photodetection has been demonstrated with minimal measurement errors. This work opens a new space in the field of organic photodetectors toward high-dimensional light perception technology.

papers.title: Leveraging Conformational Control of Neratinib’s C–N Axes to Enhance HER4 selectivity in Ovarian Cancer
papers.abstract: Diarylamines are among the most privileged scaffolds in drug discovery, with a myriad of examples in the clinic including the multi-kinase inhibitor neratinib which possesses indications towards HER2 overexpressed breast cancers. Diarylamines possess a complex conformational profile due to the two contiguous rotatable axes stemming from the diarylamine’s nitrogen. An analysis of co-crystal structures of diarylamines bound to proteins in the protein data bank (PDB) revealed that many kinases interact with diarylamines in vastly different small-molecule conformations, leading us to hypothesize that controlling the conformation about one or both axes of a diarylamine can lead to improved target selectivity. Herein we describe work where we lock the conformation of the quinoline-nitrogen axis of neratinib into a planar ‘trans’ conformation via the incorporation of a fluorine atom peri to the axis that serves as an intramolecular hydrogen bonding handle. This conformationally restricted analog possessed markedly improved kinase selectivity towards HER family kinases, particularly HER4, an emerging target for the treatment of some drug-resistant ovarian cancers. This selectivity held in cellular models of HER4 driven cancers. Overall, this work demonstrates that conformational control about the axes of diarylamines can represent a useful way to rapidly build in kinase selectivity into known lead compounds.

papers.title: EIS-GPT: Transformer-based generation of equivalent circuit for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is widely used to probe electrochemical systems, with impedance spectra commonly interpreted through regression to equivalent circuit models (ECMs). However, ECM identification remains challenging due to structural non-uniqueness and the reliance on expert-driven model selection. Here, we present EIS-GPT, a transformer-based generative framework for ECM prediction that represents circuits as directed acyclic graphs and constructs candidate topologies autoregressively from impedance data. Reinforcement-learning-based fine-tuning is adapted to guide topology generation through reward functions that favor accurate spectral description while accounting for physical plausibility and model complexity. The framework produces candidate circuits that provide competitive spectral explanations while avoiding overfitting. By formulating ECM discovery as structure-aware generative optimization rather than categorical selection, EIS-GPT provides a scalable and transparent strategy for automated impedance model discovery across diverse electrochemical systems.

papers.title: Spatial optimization of multi-scale biorefinery deployment for a diversified bioeconomy in the United States
papers.abstract: Strategic siting of biorefineries is critical for a diversified U.S. bioeconomy, yet industry, policy, and research often focus on either large-scale biofuel plants or smaller-scale specialty bioproduct facilities, with limited coordination across scales. We address this gap by modeling the spatial distribution of biorefineries spanning a 28x difference in processing capacity for purpose-grown crops (using miscanthus as an example). We developed an open-source, spatially explicit framework to integrate techno-economic analysis with logistics and refinery cost surrogate models to evaluate multi-scale deployment across the rainfed U.S. Increasing feedstock density fivefold (2% to 10% of suitable land) reduces transport distances by ~30 to 67% and land requirements by ~15 to 25%, yet decreases minimum selling prices by <10%. This limited economic sensitivity to feedstock availability suggests dense planting is not required for competitive deployment, particularly for smaller-scale facilities. Representing collection areas as irregular rather than circular expands the feasible design space by enabling denser deployment under low-density scenarios. While large-scale refineries anchor regional supply chains, smaller facilities retain substantial spatial flexibility, even when large refineries are already established. These findings highlight the importance of spatial representation and multi-scale coordination in enabling robust, regionally tailored biomanufacturing networks to advance renewable carbon integration without extensive land conversion.

papers.title: SENTINEL: A Comprehensive AI-Enhanced Hyperspectral Sorting System and Testbed for Sensing and Machine Learning Applications
papers.abstract: The convergence of Industry 4.0 technologies and circular economy principles is transforming how we address the problem of resource scarcity and waste management. In this work, we introduce SENTINEL (Sensor ENsemble for Testing and INtelligent Evaluation Laboratory), an intelligent testbed system developed by Idaho National Laboratory in collaboration with UHV Technologies, Inc., which is designed to bridge the two problems. SENTINEL exemplifies the application of advanced automation, connectivity, and artificial intelligence to the critical challenge of material identification, quantification, and sorting within complex waste streams. By integrating hyperspectral imaging, computer vision, machine learning, and network architecture, the system achieves real-time, high-throughput characterization and precise sorting of diverse materials like plastics, textiles, biomass, and other waste materials. Operating at INL’s Biomass Feedstock National User Facility, SENTINEL is a testbed for algorithm development, model validation, and deployment of AI-guided characterization at industrial scales. In this work, we explain the instrument design and show three applications where high throughput pixelwise characterization can transform upstream processing and analysis. Beyond its technical innovations, the SENTINEL can address a critical bottleneck in circular economy adoption by enabling cost-effective material characterization, thereby enhancing supply chain resilience, and reducing dependence on foreign resources. SENTINEL demonstrates how Industry 4.0 capabilities can catalyze large-scale circular economy implementation, redefining waste as a valuable economic resource.

papers.title: An open format for recording sample metadata alongside NMR experiments
papers.abstract: Information about sample composition is essential for the interpretation and reproducibility of NMR experiments, yet at the point of acquisition it is typically recorded informally or not at all. Here we present a lightweight format and associated set of tools to record structured sample metadata alongside NMR experiment data. The format uses a versioned schema covering sample components, buffer composition, NMR tube or rotor properties, personnel, and laboratory references. Metadata are stored as JSON files within experiment data directories, timestamped by creation and ejection events, and experiments are associated with samples implicitly and automatically through their acquisition timestamps. No server or database is required, so metadata are as secure as the associated experimental data. Two applications are provided: a sample manager integrated into Bruker TopSpin, which captures metadata at the point of injection, ejection, or sample exchange, and a browser-based application for viewing and editing metadata outside the spectrometer. The format is supported by the NMR data management platform NOMAD, the Julia library NMRTools.jl, and the titration analysis software NMR TITAN. We describe the correspondence between the schema and the NMR-STAR ontology used by the Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank, and discuss how structured metadata captured at the bench can facilitate subsequent data deposition and compliance with FAIR data principles. The schema and all software are released under the MIT licence, and community input is invited before a stable 1.0 release.

papers.title: Tuning Fluorescence and Singlet Oxygen Generation in Heavy-Atom-Free BODIPYs through Charge-Transfer State Modulation
papers.abstract: Heavy-atom-free photosensitizers are increasingly recognized as versatile alternatives to traditional heavy-atom systems, which often exhibit shortened triplet lifetimes, poor photostability, and limited biocompatibility. Donor-acceptor architectures, particularly compact BODIPY dyads with orthogonal subunits, efficiently promote intramolecular charge-transfer states that facilitate intersystem crossing (ISC) without relying on heavy atoms. In this study, we demonstrate that ISC and excited-state deactivation pathways in compact heavy-atom-free BODIPY dyads can be systematically modulated beyond simple meso-donor variation through the combined effects of core alkylation, boron-centered electron-withdrawing substitution, and solvent polarity. This study integrates the structural design and synthesis of a small family of BODIPY dyads with selected substitution patterns, photophysical characterization in solvents of varying polarity, transient absorption spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry for redox profiling, and DFT/TD-DFT calculations to explore the electronic structure and excited-state properties of these BODIPY derivatives. Our findings indicate that careful meso-donor selection, coupled with systematic core alkylation and boron electron-withdrawing substitution, produces heavy-atomfree BODIPY photosensitizers with tunable photophysical and electrochemical properties, exhibiting solvent- and substitution-dependent behaviors, ranging from high fluorescence with negligible ISC, to dominant ISC with minimal fluorescence, or a balanced contribution of both functions. These results provide a mechanistic framework for engineering heavy-atom-free BODIPY photosensitizers with tunable fluorescence and reactive oxygen generation, opening new opportunities for the development of tailored molecular platforms for bioimaging, photodynamic therapy, and related photonic applications.

papers.title: Nanoscale Three-Dimensional Force Mapping Scanning Electrochemical Microscopy of Graphene decorated with Platinum Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: We present a methodology to image the electrochemical activity at solid-liquid interfaces with nanometer resolution in three dimensions by integrating force volume mapping with scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM). The imaging is performed using an atomic force microscopy (AFM)-SECM cantilever probe, with a nanoscale conducting tip. By monitoring the tip current simultaneously with the cantilever deflection during the recording of AFM force spectra, we collect approach curves well-calibrated with the tip-sample separation. Thus, we obtain a current-volume data cube containing complete approach curves as a function of lateral position, in addition to force-volume data common in 3D-AFM. We incorporate a self-referencing procedure by normalizing the tip current with its surface-free steady-state value at every pixel. The normalized data cube can be interrogated in several ways to map the three-dimensional redox activity at the interface. SECM images can be reconstructed at arbitrary tip-sample separation, unambiguously correlated with the nanoscale topography. Moreover, we can directly visualize the evolution of surface electrochemical activity by mapping the SECM current as a function of tip-sample separation in 3D. We show that very subtle differences in the redox behavior between graphene and Pt nanoparticles for an outer-sphere probe can be clearly distinguished using the presented 3D-AFM-SECM technique.

papers.title: Nickel(I) in an All-Ferric NiFeS Cluster
papers.abstract: Anaerobic carbon monoxide dehydrogenase (CODH) enzymes interconvert CO 2 and CO under mild conditions and with near perfect selectivity. The CODH active site, termed the C-cluster, is a [NiFe 3 S 4 ]-Fe u cluster that can reside in several different oxidation states. Despite decades of research, the electronic structure of the C-cluster remains unresolved and the metal oxidation states are ambiguous. In this study, we interrogate a series of synthetic clusters with [NiFe 3 S 4 ] 3+/2+/1+ cores in multiple oxidation states as models of the C-cluster cubane core. Each cluster is characterized using crystallography, spectroscopy, magnetism, and computations. The most oxidized cluster, [NiFe 3 S 4 ] 3+ , is best described as having Ni 2+ and three Fe 3+ sites. Remarkably, Xray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) data show that reduction to the [NiFe 3 S 4 ] 2+ state results in reduction of nickel to Ni 1+ , even though nearby Fe 3+ sites are present. The fully oxidized Fe 3 +3 subsite can be reduced only after nickel has reached the Ni 1+ state. These results demonstrate that Ni 1+ is a readily accessible oxidation state in FeS clusters topologically relevant to the CODH Ccluster.

papers.title: Correlation of Metal Ion Coordination with Mechanical Properties and Ionic Conductivity in Homogeneous PEG-Based Network Solid Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Understanding the relationship between metal ion coordination within polymer networks and macroscopic properties is a key factor in designing polymer electrolytes. In this study, homogeneous tetra/linear-PEG solid electrolytes were prepared by combining tetrafunctional and linear poly(ethylene glycol)s (tetra-PEG and linear-PEG, respectively), and used as a model system to systematically investigate the effects of polymer network mesh size and metal ion species (Li+, Na+, and Mg2+) on solid electrolyte properties, particularly mechanical properties and ionic conductivity. The resulting tetra/linear-PEG-based electrolytes exhibited significant dependence of both mechanical properties and ionic conductivity on the mesh size. The dependence on metal ion species revealed that the Young’s modulus increased in the order Li < Na < Mg, whereas the molar ionic conductivity decreased in the order Li >> Mg > Na. Raman spectroscopy showed that the coordination states of bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)amide (TFSA) anions strongly depend on the metal ion species: free TFSA and contact ion pairs (CIPs) coexist in the Li system, whereas CIPs and ionic aggregates (AGGs) dominate in the Na and Mg systems. Highenergy X-ray total scattering combined with molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that PEG and TFSA anions (both coordinated via O atoms) competitively coordinate to the metal ions, and that Mg2+ exhibits a relative preference for coordination with PEG over TFSA among the examined ions. This preferential Mg2+–PEG interaction suggests the formation of transient interchain bridging points, which account for the high mechanical strength observed in the Mg system. The Li salt-containing tetra/linear-PEG electrolyte with optimized mesh size exhibited reversible Li deposition/dissolution behavior, indicating its applicability as a solid electrolyte for battery systems.

papers.title: Synthesis and Magnetism of Silver Chromium Selenide Spinels
papers.abstract: Chalcogenide spinels exhibit electronic and magnetic properties that are tunable through lattice occupancy and composition. We report the first synthesis of spinel-phase Ag2Cr2Se4 and AgCr2Se4 and demonstrate an oxidation-induced ferro-to-ferrimagnetic transition associated with Ag+ site occupancy. The Ag spinels are synthesized through air-free cation exchange of CuCr2Se4 nanocrystals driven by excess AgNO3 to yield the ferromagnetic Ag2Cr2Se4 (a = 10.840(3) Å, TC = 151 K, 2 K saturation = 3.1 μB/Cr) with Ag+ occupying both Td 8a and Oh 16c sites. Upon air exposure, Ag2Cr2Se4 converts to ferrimagnetic AgCr2Se4 (a = 10.610(3) Å, TC > 400 K, 2 K saturation = 2.2 μB/Cr) through a loss of Oh-Ag+ alongside the formation of Ag2Se. We attribute the ferro-to-ferrimagnetic transition to the generation of holes in Ag–Se bands, which couple antiferromagnetically to Cr3+. This Ag–Cr–Se spinel system provides an excellent framework for further exploration of magnetic coupling as a function of oxidation and structure.

papers.title: You Only Measure Once: Unified Battery Diagnostics
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of battery technologies demands fast, scalable and information-rich diagnostic methods, yet existing approaches remain fragmented and time-intensive. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) or, more recently, voltage response (VR) in the time domain provide detailed insight into internal electrochemical processes, while chargedischarge cycling yields ground-truth capacity, but these techniques are typically performed separately, limiting their applicability in high-throughput and real-world cases. Here, a unified diagnostic framework is introduced that integrates capacity and impedance information within a single and time-efficient measurement. By embedding multi-frequency perturbations into DC-biased charge and discharge processes and tuning the capacity-to-impedance (CI) ratio, both energy-storage behaviour and electrochemical dynamics are simultaneously encoded in a single VR. Importantly, the diagnostic signal can be fully embedded within standard charging protocols, enabling concurrent energy transfer and state evaluation, thereby achieving a zeroenergy-wasting diagnostic paradigm in which the perturbation energy is not lost but directly contributes to cell charging. This also enables seamless transition between impedance- and capacity-dominated regimes, providing a continuous and information-dense diagnostic space. Systematic analysis across voltage regimes reveals strong voltage dependence of diagnostic sensitivity and ranking consistency, reflecting evolving interfacial kinetics and transport processes. The proposed capacity–impedance coupled excitation improves ranking robustness compared with impedance-based metrics, achieving strong agreement with capacity-based ground truth from full charging/discharging while reducing measurement time by orders of magnitude (1/10,000). The CI framework unifies electrochemical cycling and impedance response within a single physical domain, providing a scalable, non-invasive route for state-ofhealth (SoH) assessment. Overall, this work establishes a generalisable paradigm for highthroughput battery diagnostics across manufacturing, operation and second-life applications.

papers.title: Lewis-acid Mediated Conversion of Dihalogenatedketones to Mono-halogenated Alcohols: a Direct Source to α-halogenated Naphthols
papers.abstract: Despite the considerable synthetic potential of halogenated naphthols; arising from the combined reactivity of the naphthol core and the electronic and steric effects imparted by halogen substitution; this compound class remains largely under investigated. We report herein an operationally simple and economical approach to ortho-halogenated naphthols employing inexpensive starting material; propanedithiol as a terminal reductant with yields reaching up to 78 %. Furthermore, the protocol exhibits broad functional group compatibility, maintaining consistently high yields across a diverse array of substrates.

papers.title: A Subtype-specific Probe for Estrogen Receptor Alpha (ERα) Reveals Imaging of PROTAC-induced Degradation
papers.abstract: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancers depend on estrogen receptor (ER) signaling for growth, yet the chemistry to directly visualize ERα dynamics under pharmacological perturbation remains limited. Proteolysis targeting chimera (PROTAC) offers an alternative approach by promoting degradation of ERα rather than inhibiting alone. Here, we present the design and chemical development of a nonsteroidal ERα-targeted probe, ERi-FL, enabling real-time visualization of ERα-specific dynamics in live cells, tissues, and animal models. ERi-FL derived from a diaryltetrahydronaphthalene scaffold, exhibits high-affinity for ERα (IC 50 = 3-5 nM) and bright imaging contrast with pronounced selectivity over ERbeta (ERβ). Based on relative binding affinity (RBA) to estradiol, ERi-FL exhibits greater than 14-fold selectivity for ERα over ERβ, and greater than 11-fold relative to lasofoxifene. At nanomolar concentrations, ERi-FL permits imaging of ERα under hormone- and estrogen-regulated conditions, allowing insights into ER signaling in biological systems. Applied in the context of PROTAC-induced therapy, ERi-FL revealed ERα degradation in MCF-7 via imaging, with signal intensities tightly correlated to ERα levels. We demonstrate that ERi-FL provides a chemically defined platform for interrogating ERα pharmacology directly. We show it to measure target occupancy, assess subtype selectivity, and evaluate other therapeutic strategies, including imaging the efficacy of targeted protein degraders, such as PROTACs in ER+ cancers.

papers.title: Performance-Based Evolution of Near-Infrared Serotonin Nanosensors from DNA-Wrapped Carbon Nanotube Libraries
papers.abstract: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5HT) is an important neurotransmitter involved in the regulation of mood, appetite, and sleep, and its dysregulation has been associated with disorders such as depression and Parkinson’s disease. Selective molecular tools that can distinguish 5HT from neurochemicals, are essential for advancing both neurochemistry and disease-related research. However, conventional analytical methods are labor-intensive and sometimes suffer from poor discrimination among closely related neurotransmitters. In this study, we developed near-infrared fluorescence 5HT nanosensor based on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA)-wrapped single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) using a performance-based systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment of carbon nanotube (pSELEC) strategy. Unlike conventional affinity-focused selection, this approach prioritized fluorescence modulation as the screening output and combined high-throughput microarray printing, automated fluorescence imaging to evaluate more than 10 6 ssDNA-SWCNT configurations. After characterizing the enriched DNA 2 candidates, Seq6 was selected as finalist scaffold and underwent post-selection engineering such as covalent modification with quencher dye and co-wrapping with dummy DNA. A methylene blue-conjugated Seq6 produced an “turn-off” fluorescence response to 5HT together with an opposite-direction response to dopamine, providing improved discrimination between the two analytes. These results demonstrate that pSELEC is a useful strategy for developing sensitive and selective near-Infrared nanosensors for real-time neurotransmitter sensing.

papers.title: Quantifying the Synergistic and Antagonistic Effects of Metal–Organic Complexation on Aerosol Oxidative Potential via Redox Kinetics
papers.abstract: Oxidative potential (OP) is an indicator of the ability of redox-active species (e.g., transition metals) in aerosols to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) and induce oxidative stress. Previous studies have reported synergistic and antagonistic effects on OP in mixtures of metals and non-redox-active organics. These effects have been attributed to changes in redox potential associated with complexation; however, the quantitative validity of this hypothesis remains unclear. In this study, we evaluated this mechanism using a chemical equilibrium–kinetic model of DTT assay (CEK-DTT model) for Fe–oxalate systems. Complexation-induced changes in redox potential and rate constants were derived from Marcus theory and incorporated into the model. Experiments showed no clear synergistic or antagonistic effects at oxalate-to-Fe ratios up to several tens, whereas increasing the ratio led from strong antagonistic to strong synergistic effects. The model partially reproduced these trends, revealing that the former arises from enhanced Fe(II) reduction rate constants offset by an equilibrium shift toward Fe(III), whereas the latter arises from an increased fraction of inert Fe(III)–(oxalate)3 suppressing DTT oxidation. However, the strong synergistic effect was not reproduced, suggesting missing mechanisms in the model. These findings contribute to the understanding of non-additive OP effects and aerosol toxicity.

papers.title: Surface Chemistry Control of Synthetic Hectorite using Mg/Li Tuning for Targeted Biomedical Applications
papers.abstract: Synthetic hectorite nanoclays, such as Laponite®, are widely explored as model anisotropic colloids and injectable biomaterials due to their high specific surface area, charge anisotropy and ability to form physically cross-linked gels in aqueous environments. Despite this interest, the role of nanoclay surface chemistry in governing application-specific properties such as gelation and protein adsorption remains largely unexplored. In this study, we systematically analyse how modulation of the Mg/Li ratio influences electrokinetic behaviour and gelation performance under physiologically relevant conditions, with a view to optimising clay-based materials for biomedical applications. Synthetic hectorite analogues (RENOVITE®) were engineered via Mg/Li ratio control during hydrothermal synthesis to tune permanent layer charge while preserving structural fidelity. Composition was validated by ICP-OES, while structural and morphological fidelity was confirmed by XRD, ATR-FTIR and SAXS. Electrokinetic measurements revealed a monotonic decrease in permanent basal charge with increasing Mg/Li ratio, accompanied by a systematic shift in agglomeration onset at higher pH. Rheometric characterisation in physiological solutions revealed a clear compositional optimum with an intermediate Mg/Li ratio, yielding maximal storage modulus, while both lower and higher Mg/Li formulations formed weaker networks. This optimum arises from a balance between sufficient platelet delamination (enabled by basal charge) and effective edge-mediated connectivity, positioning the system near a percolation threshold under physiological conditions. In summary, this work establishes a direct link between Mg/Li-mediated surface chemistry, electrokinetics, and diffusion-driven gel mechanics, providing a framework for rationale design of nanoclay biomaterials with tunable performance in biomedical applications.

papers.title: Best of Both: Bipyridine-Crowns for the Active Template CuAAC and Crown Ether Mediated Synthesis of Interlocked Molecules
papers.abstract: Active template Cu-mediated alkyne-azide cycloaddition reactions and crown ether-mediated amine functionalisation approaches to interlocked molecules stand out for their efficiency, simplicity and substrate scope. Here we introduce the bipyridine-crown ether macrocycles, readily available rings that efficiently mediate both powerful methodologies. Furthermore, the bipyridine-crown ether platform is readily modified to allow controlled mechanical disassembly of the interlocked products, and the same modifications give rise to diastereostereoselective mechanical bond formation.

papers.title: Lattice Free Energies of Molecular Crystals Using Normalizing Flow
papers.abstract: Accurate free-energy calculations are essential for predicting thermodynamic stability in complex molecular materials, such as the polymorphic crystal landscapes of pharmaceutical molecules. Classical methods such as the Einstein crystal method (ECM) provide benchmark accuracy but are computationally prohibitive in larger crystal landscapes generated by Crystal Structure Prediction. Here, we develop a scalable framework for the anharmonic free-energy ranking of molecular crystals, based on targeted free-energy perturbation. In particular, we utilise the targeted Bennett acceptance ratio (tBAR) method, where the targeting step employs a bijective map learned via a normalising flow. The maps are trained to analytically transform supercell configurations between the crystal Boltzmann ensembles of interest and an analytical reference state. Exact likelihoods, in turn, enable reliable lattice free-energy estimates directly from physical molecular dynamics data, without alchemical sampling. The method handles supercells with up to 3 x 10 3 degrees of freedom and permits multi-state training with a single model. Validation across succinic acid, Veliparib, and Mivebresib demonstrates excellent agreement with ECM at significantly lower cost. By combining statistical mechanics and machine-learning expressivity, this approach advances anharmonic free energies towards automation and high-throughput applications in molecular and materials design.

papers.title: Artificially intelligent modeling of macromolecular assemblies
papers.abstract: The study of macromolecular assembly formation is one of the most challenging tasks in computational modeling, as it requires extensive exploration of conformational and configurational space, especially when driven by conformational transitions or folding instabilities, which are typically associated with high energy barriers. While this type of study has traditionally been addressed in silico by using techniques that reduce the computational cost of simulations, such as coarse-grained models, artificial intelligence (AI) has recently entered the field at multiple levels, aiding in parameter optimization or trajectory analysis, and even replacing potentials or force calculations. Recently developed algorithms such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold enable the direct prediction of final structures with high efficiency and confidence, an achievement that earned them the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In this work, we review and analyze the different AI-based strategies used to model proteins structure and dynamics and simulate macromolecular assemblies, comparing them with traditional methods, to highlight their respective advantages and limitations. By placing these approaches along an ideal continuum in which accuracy increases as interpretability decreases, we show that hybrid solutions and combinations of methods can be devised to maximize their strengths. Finally, we perspectively outline practical strategies for implementing such integrated approaches in a coherent manner, preserving accuracy and feasibility while maintaining insight into aggregation pathways, intermediate structures, and the molecular mechanisms underlying the phenomenon.

papers.title: Demonstration of an automated bioreactor for controlled acid dosing to enhance marine algae productivity
papers.abstract: Microalgae are an important feedstock in aquaculture with significant economic potential in generating a diversity of bioproducts. To facilitate expansion of microalgal cultivation, a continuous automated bioreactor that uses waste acid to increase carbon bioavailability in seawater for enhanced biomass production was designed and tested with Tetraselmis suecica UTEX2286 . Carbon bioavailability was inferred from culture pH and bioreactor headspace CO 2 concentration measurements and controlled via acidification and seawater dilution. Operating over a period of several days, the culture exhibited greater biomass productivity at a pH setpoint of 7-7.5. Outside of this range, algal activity slowed, accompanied by greater CO 2 released to the headspace and lower pH during incubation. Increasing the carbon introduced to the bioreactor by increasing the dilution factor did not significantly increase the algal productivity. Importantly, acidification led to statistically significant gains in biomass productivity. Preliminary cost analysis showed while seawater is inexpensive, the acid cost drives the overall cost of the designed bioreactor system. Thus, the designed bioreactor and control scheme supports algal cultivation but requires low-cost acid to be economical, which may be achieved by strategically integrating microalgae cultivation with other coastal industries.

papers.title: The first example of Ti(O-iPr)4-EtMgBr-catalyzed 2-zincoethylzincation of N,N-disubstituted 2-alkenylamines
papers.abstract: For the first time, it was demonstrated that the use of the Ti(O-iPr)4-EtMgBr catalytic system in the reaction of N,Ndisubstituted 2-alkenylamines with Et2Zn ensures 2-zincoethylzincation of the double bond. It was established that the Ti(O-iPr)4-EtMgBr-catalyzed reaction of N,N-disubstituted 2-alkenylamines with Et2Zn is accompanied by the regio- and chemoselective formation of tertiary amines in high yields (80-88%). The results of deuterolysis of the reaction mixture indicate the formation of 2-zincoethylzincation products of tertiary 2-alkenylamines.

papers.title: Rescaled electrolyte charge density provides a unifying descriptor of electrocatalytic CO2 reduction in ionic liquid electrolytes.
papers.abstract: Electric field-driven ion accumulation dictates the local environment for electrochemical reactions, often governing the rates and selectivity of electrocatalytic processes.
