Recent studies demonstrate that high salt concentrations can unlock new mechanisms to modulate reactivity, yet the influence of ion-ion correlations on electric double layer formation remains open to discussion. Here, we study ionic liquid-mediated electrochemical CO 2 reduction using 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate (EMIm BF 4 ) dissolved in acetonitrile, dimethyl sulfoxide, and propylene carbonate at concentrations ranging from dilute to neat ionic liquid. By bridging experiments with molecular dynamics simulations, we reveal alignment between electrocatalytic activity and bulk rescaled charge density, or the concentration of charges not neutralized in ion clusters. We also show ion aggregation behavior predicts interfacial screening lengths in quantitative agreement with surface forces measurements. Overall, we reveal that collective ion assembly plays a crucial role in electrocatalysis, opening frontiers in modulating reactivity beyond the active site reminiscent of secondary environment control in enzymatic catalysis.

papers.title: Polyoxoniobate capped polyoxopalladates
papers.abstract: Polyoxometalates (POMs) derived from early transition metals exhibit remarkable structural diversity and tunable electronic properties. However, polyoxoniobates (PONbs) remain comparatively underexplored, particularly in hybrid systems with late transition metals. Herein, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of a giant hybrid polyoxopalladate–polyoxoniobate cluster, [Pd 19 O 8 (Nb 6 O 19 ) 8 ] 42- (Pd 19 Nb 48 ), obtained under mildly basic hydrothermal conditions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a cube-shaped Pd–Nb oxo framework encapsulating a central Pd 13 polyoxopalladate core. The Pd13 unit retains its characteristic geometry but is uniquely capped by eight Lindqvist-type [Nb 6 O 19 ] 8- clusters, replacing conventional tetrahedral oxanion capping groups. The resulting architecture represents a high nuclearity hybrid motif that integrates features of both polyoxopalladates and polyoxoniobates. Solution studies using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) support the persistence of large cluster fragments, although polydispersity is indicated. This work expands the structural landscape of POM chemistry by demonstrating the compatibility of Pd-based polyoxometalates with highly charged niobate building units, offering new opportunities for integrating basicity with catalytic redox activity.

papers.title: Alignment-Free Spectral Approach For Comparing Molecular Surface Properties and Properties For Use in Cheminformatics
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel alignment-free method for characterizing molecular surfaces and their properties with broad applications in cheminformatics. We present a spectral approach that quantifies the shape of a surface and its associated property, such as ethe electrostatic potential, by converting them into characteristic spectra This method is grounded in shape analysis and the Laplace-Beltrami operator that continuously changing as the surface/property changes, capturing both topological changes due to post-bond rupture into radicals and functional group identification of small organic molecules. We demonstrate its effectiveness in organic compound classification and in assessing protein-surface similarity between thermophilic and mesophilic proteins. Our approach is concise, interpretable, and capable of distinguishing molecular shapes and functional groups. This method offers significant potential for advancing data-driven models in material sciences and drug discovery.

papers.title: Catalyst-Free Electrocatalytic Semi-Hydrogenation of Terminal Alkynes via a Solvent-Driven Interphase on Copper
papers.abstract: Selective semi-hydrogenation of alkynes is fundamental to chemical manufacturing but typically relies on metal catalysts, pressurized hydrogen, or additive-intensive electrochemical systems. Here we report a catalyst-free and additive-free electrosynthetic strategy for the highly selective semi-hydrogenation of terminal alkynes under ambient conditions. Using a Mg anode and Cu cathode in Nmethylformamide (NMF), the system achieves >99% conversion and >99% selectivity across a broad substrate scope and is scalable to gram-scale continuous flow. Mechanistic studies indicate that electrolysis induces the spontaneous formation of a solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI)-like layer on the Cu cathode, generating a confined interfacial environment that regulates proton-coupled electron transfer and suppresses over-reduction. These results demonstrate that interfacial design can replace conventional catalysis, providing a minimalist platform for selective electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Kinetics-Based Framework for Predicting Site- and Facial-Selectivity in Ketone Reductions
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting the site and facial selectivity of chemical reactions remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. While reaction outcomes are traditionally evaluated by yield, yields are influenced by side reactions and experimental conditions and do not reliably reflect intrinsic reaction rates. Here, we focus on competition experiments, in which two substrates are reacted simultaneously to directly compare relative reaction rates, and establish a unified kinetic framework for the reduction of ketones with sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in methanol. Reactivity is quantified as activation free energy differences (ΔΔG‡). Highprecision kinetic data obtained for 76 structurally diverse ketone reaction faces show clear correlations with substituent electronic effects and molecular structural strain, demonstrating that reactivity is governed by a cooperative interplay of electronic and structural factors. Furthermore, by leveraging these experimentally derived and reliable kinetic data, transition-state calculations enable a consistent mechanistic interpretation of the contributions of electronic interactions and structural effects. In addition, data-driven analysis based on three-dimensional electronic descriptors, including electron density, electrostatic potential, and LUMO wavefunction, accurately reproduces the observed reactivity trends (r2LOOCV = 0.84) while providing interpretable insights into their origins. Importantly, we demonstrate that the kinetic descriptors derived from simple monoketones can be extended to quantitatively predict site- and face-selectivity in more complex diketones. Overall, this study presents a new strategy for generalizing reactivity from simple to complex molecular systems by integrating yield-independent kinetic metrics with experiment, theory, and data-driven analysis. This approach provides a practical foundation for understanding and controlling site- and stereoselectivity in reactions that have been difficult to predict using conventional methods.

papers.title: Extending Atom-Atom Polarizabilities to Frequency-Dependent Coupled Cluster and MCSCF Response
papers.abstract: The methodology for calculating distributed atom-atom polarizabilities within the Minimal Basis Iterative Stockholder partitioning framework is extended to coupled cluster (CC2, CCSD, CC3) and multi-configurational self-consistent field (MCSCF) wave functions, as well as to frequency-dependent perturbations. The bond capacity, defined as the rank-0 atom-atom polarizability, is benchmarked on small molecules at equilibrium geometries, where various DFT functionals show good agreement with the CC3 reference. The same conclusion holds when probing geometry dependence through a change in the bond angle or dihedral angle, but a significant deviation is observed between the methods for reaction pathways like SN2. The MCSCF implementation is used to study the values across bond breaking, where the rank-0 contribution to the molecular dipole polarizability is found to dominate for various systems. Non-nuclear sites for describing out-of-plane polarizability at the charge-only level are also explored but found ineffective with ab initio derived parameters. Dynamic bond capacities at real and imaginary frequencies are presented and display method dependence consistent with the static values.

papers.title: Optimization of Mirror Reflectivity and Optical Loss in AlGaN/BGaN Blue Edge Emitting Laser Diodes
papers.abstract: This work presents a comprehensive numerical investigation into the optimization of mirror reflectivity and internal optical loss in AlGaN/BGaN blue edge emitting laser diodes (EELDs) emitting at approximately 427 nm using the LASTIP simulation software. A ridge waveguide device [cavity length L = 500 µm, ridge width 1.5 µm] with a three quantum well BGaN active region assumed to be grown over a 2 µm AlN substrate was parametrically delve in across eleven combinations of internal background loss [αi = 10 – 50 cm-1] and facet mirror reflectivity [R = 10 – 90%]. The transverse optical intensity profile was found to be strictly invariant across the entire range yielding a fixed optical confinement factor Γ = 0.16996 and a mode FWHM of 0.376 µm with an asymmetry ratio of 0.41. Exploiting this invariance the threshold material gain was computed analytically for all assumed range revealing a U shaped minimum of gth = 255.1 cm-1 at αi = 26 cm-1, R = 42%. Spatial analyses of the modal absorption and local gain profiles confirmed that this optimum corresponds to the most favourable gain loss contrast across the three QWs. Power current characterisation yielded a minimum threshold current of Ith = 89 mA and a slope efficiency of ηslope = 1.24 W/A at the optimal configuration with wall plug efficiency reaching 37.4% at R = 10% nearly 19 times higher than the R = 90% case. Voltage current analysis confirmed electrical invariance across all the assumed range with a common turn on voltage of 3.8 V and series resistance of approximately 0.182 Ω. These results establish αi = 26 cm-1, R = 42% as the optimal cavity design point providing a quantitative software for practical AlGaN/BGaN blue EELD engineering.

papers.title: Definition of structural ‘crossover’ between two organic conjugated molecules: a practical tool for high-throughput virtual screening of organic (second-order nonlinear optical) chromophores
papers.abstract: In scientific practice, the realization of better materials (chromophores) often starts with relatively good substrates, which means “standing on the shoulders of giants". Organic second-order nonlinear optical (NLO) chromophores have gained great attention in recent decades. This work was mainly designed to explore the effect of structural ‘crossover’ between molecules on tuning the systems’ second-order NLO responses. To this aim, a practical combinationmethod (structural ‘crossover’) was proposed to generate offsprings from two organic conjugated parent molecules. A compound library (size=3924) was generated by applying the proposed ‘crossover’ methods to 6 parent molecules. Several optimal NLO chromophores have been sieved out theoretically via high-throughput virtual screening routine, andmost of them can be easily identified as direct derivatives of the parent molecule DPTCF. In short, the systems have been successfully driven to give better trade-off between NLO response and optical transparency due to the structural disturbance introduced by ‘crossover’.

papers.title: In cellulo observation of newly synthesized nucleotide by spectral tracing of glutamine-derived nitrogen metabolism (QN-STIM) in cancer cells
papers.abstract: De-novo nucleotide biosynthesis is directly linked to glutamine-derived nitrogen metabolism in mammalian cells. It is a fundamental process tightly tied to cellular growth, proliferation, and metabolic reprogramming, particularly in cancer cells. Direct detection and imaging of glutaminederived nitrogen metabolism at the single-cell resolution remains a challenge. The conventional liquid chromatography mass spectrometry-based approach for detecting de novo synthesized nucleotide studies is mostly performed on metabolites extracted from a group of cells, which makes it inherently destructive. Herein, we introduce a novel vibrational spectroscopy-based single-cell metabolic detection and imaging framework, “glutamine (Q)-derived nitrogen spectral tracing and imaging (QN-STIM)”. Using this strategy, we detected and mapped nitrogen flow from glutamine to de novo-synthesized nascent nucleotides at the single-cell level. First, a proof-ofconcept analysis was conducted in human embryonic kidney HEK293T cells and demonstrated the feasibility of this approach in cancer cells, namely human lung carcinoma A549, human glioblastoma U87 MG, and mouse hepatoma Hepa1-6. QN-STIM technique holds immense potential to be an adjunct tool to advance our understanding of nucleotide dynamics during differentiation, stress adaptation, and immune activation, and to evaluate responses to metabolic drugs in cellulo.

papers.title: Mapping Metabolomics Approaches in Natural Product Research for Antihyperglycemic Therapy: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: The global prevalence of diabetes mellitus continues to rise, underscoring the need for more effective therapy. Natural products (NPs) are potential sources of multi-target antihyperglycemic candidates. This scoping review was conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines to systematically evaluate recent trends in metabolomics-based NP drug discovery for antihyperglycemic bioactivity. Among the 122 eligible studies, publication output increased over time, with major contributions from Global South countries, including Malaysia, Egypt, and Indonesia. The studies covered 212 NP species from 73 families, mainly Fabaceae and Asteraceae, with phenolics and flavonoids as the most reported phytochemical groups. Untargeted metabolomics was the dominant approach (72.95%), with LC-MS/MS being the most used analytical platform (34.8%). Computational tools such as GNPS molecular networking and SIRIUS-assisted annotation were increasingly applied. However, most studies relied on in vitro enzyme assays (87.39%), particularly α-glucosidase and α-amylase inhibition, and many provided Level C evidence of bioactivity, indicating limited pharmacological validation. Metabolite annotations were mostly putative, commonly at MSI Level 2. This review highlights the need for stronger metabolite annotation, more physiologically relevant bioassays, including cell-based and in vivo models, and multi-omics approaches to better link chemical profiles with mechanisms of antihyperglycemic action.

papers.title: The topographic origin of chemomechanical failure in high-nickel cathodes revealed by operando dark-field X-ray microscopy
papers.abstract: Mechanical degradation in high-nickel cathodes, driven by anisotropic volume changes, remains a primary bottleneck for the lifetime of high-energy density batteries. Yet, the nanoscale origins of strain and defect initiation within individual primary particles remain unclear. Here, in the first application of operando dark-field X-ray microscopy (DFXM) to a battery system, we directly observe a dislocation wall nucleating from a pre-existing topographical flaw on the surface of a single NMC 811 primary particle. We show that failure is not stochastic, but deterministically driven by surface topography; the flaw creates a local stress concentration of ∼100 MPa, exceeding the material’s yield strength, while the bulk particle remains elastic. This observation establishes a direct physical link between primary particle surface morphology and the onset of irreversible plasticity. These findings prescribe a clear design rule: beyond bulk chemical stability, engineering particles with pristine, defect-free surfaces is essential for mitigating strain localisation and extending battery lifetime.

papers.title: Mobilization and plant uptake of antibiotics in Mexican soils during transition from irrigation with untreated to treated wastewater
papers.abstract: Treatment of wastewater before its reuse for irrigation is increasingly implemented to reduce health and environmental risks. We hypothesized that the transition from irrigation with untreated wastewater (UWW) to irrigation with treated wastewater (TWW) mobilizes previously accumulated antibiotics in soils, thereby increasing their plant uptake and leaching. Soil columns of Vertisols, Phaeozems and Leptosols with a long history of irrigation with UWW were planted with cilantro and irrigated with either UWW or TWW (both unspiked or spiked with antibiotics and quaternary alkylammonium compounds). While irrigation with TWW reduced the uptake of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole by cilantro plants, the leaching of clindamycin and sulfamethoxazole was higher compared to irrigation with UWW. Irrigation with TWW resulted in a stronger net mobilization of sulfamethoxazole from Vertisols and Phaeozems, and of ciprofloxacin from Vertisols and Leptosols. Antibiotics spiked to irrigation water were largely retained or transformed in soils. Antibiotic concentrations in soils were highest along preferential water flow paths and not affected by water treatment. Implementation of wastewater treatment in long-established irrigation systems using untreated wastewater reduces the risk that antibiotics enter the food chain, but increases the risk of groundwater contamination by leached antibiotics at least transiently.

papers.title: Chemically Programmed Interfacial Polarization Enables Scalable Electrodeless Electrosynthesis of Free-Standing Conducting Polymer Thin Films
papers.abstract: Electrosynthesis traditionally requires solid electrodes and a power source, yet a soft interface itself can encode the required driving force. Here, Electrodeless Interfacial Electrosynthesis (ELIE) exploits the intrinsic polarization of immiscible liquid|liquid interfaces to drive oxidative polymerization of conducting polymer thin films without applied power. ELIE reframes electrosynthesis as a chemically polarized interfacial process, producing high‑quality free-standing films using only simple glassware and solution preparation. Salts dissolved in the organic phase comprising hydrophilic cations and hydrophobic anions function as chemical polarizers, generating a tuneable interfacial Galvani potential that mediates electron transfer between aqueous Ce 4+ and organic monomers, producing conducting films of PEDOT, PProDOT, and PProDOT‑Et 2 . Polarizer identity programs the interfacial potential, directing oligomer growth and nanoscale film morphology. ELIE‑grown films exhibit reversible p‑doping, conductivities up to ~20 S cm –1 , and low hysteresis, without post‑treatments. As an initial regenerative‑medicine demonstration, the films exhibit high retinal cell viability, surpassing that of PEDOT:PSS.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Room-Temperature Phosphorescence in a 1,4-Diiodotetrafluorobenzene–Phenanthrene Cocrystal
papers.abstract: Room-temperature phosphorescent (RTP) organic materials are attracting increasing interest for applications in optoelectronics, sensing, photomedicine, bioimaging, and OLED technologies. Metal-free organic emitters are particularly appealing due to their low toxicity, tunable photophysics, and reduced cost compared with organometallic systems. Recent work by Abe et al. (Adv. Mater. 2024, 36, 2211160) demonstrated that cocrystals composed of 1,4-diiodotetrafluorobenzene (DITFB) and phenanthrene (Phen) exhibit efficient RTP, yet the microscopic mechanisms enabling this behaviour remain unclear. Here, we investigate the radiative and non-radiative excited-state processes in the Phen–DITFB system using an embedded multiscale approach to elucidate the factors governing RTP in organic cocrystals. Our results show that cocrystallisation profoundly reshapes the excited-state landscape relative to the isolated molecules. Aggregation increases the density of triplet states near the lowest singlet excited state (S1), creating multiple energetically accessible ISC channels (T4–T10). Spinorbit couplings are simultaneously enhanced through both intermolecular and, in specific cases, intramolecular charge-transfer contributions. The resulting triplet manifold displays a diversity of electronic characters: several states are localised on the DITFB units, enabling intermolecular charge-transfer-assisted S1 → Tn transitions, while T9 shows intramolecular electron reorganisation on Phen that further strengthens the SOC. This interplay between localisation, CT character, and orbital composition produces highly efficient ISC pathways, as confirmed by the computed rate constants. Collectively, these findings provide a detailed mechanistic picture of RTP in the Phen–DITFB cocrystal.

papers.title: Achiral Monomer Regioisomerism Drives Stereomutation in Complementary Supramolecular Coassemblies
papers.abstract: A persistent challenge in constructing multicomponent coassemblies lies in the strong propensity of dissimilar monomers to self-sort, often intensified by stereochemical bias imposed by the absolute chirality of the monomer. We show that complementary hydrogen-bonding interactions between naphthalene diimide (NDI) and perylene bisimide (PBI) derivatives overcome this limitation, enabling the formation of well-defined homochiral coassemblies. Most importantly, we reveal that regioisomerism in the achiral co-monomer plays a decisive role in governing the overall chirality of the coassembly. Subtle differences in the positional arrangement of pyridyl motif modulate the relative orientation of the interacting monomers, thereby altering the balance between competing chiral states. As a result, chirality transfer from the chiral component can be dramatically tuned, leading to outcomes ranging from efficient chiral amplification to complete inversion of supramolecular handedness. These findings establish regioisomerism as a powerful and underexplored design parameter for programming supramolecular chirality and provide new insights into the rational design of functional chiral materials.

papers.title: Machine Learning Potentials for Electrified Interfaces
papers.abstract: Accurate atomistic modelling of electrochemical interfaces requires accounting for applied electrode potential and performing molecular dynamics at constant potential. The computational cost of grandcanonical density functional theory restricts simulations to small system sizes and short timescales. Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have been proven useful for long time and large length scale simulations, but their generalisation to and applicability at electrified interfaces have yet to be demonstrated. In this perspective, we review emerging approaches for developing MLIPs for systems under applied potential, organising them into two categories: (i) linear response methods that learn response properties (electronegativities, Born charges, polarisabilities) and compute energies through physics-based expansions, and (ii) direct learning methods that take the applied electrochemical potential as input variable and learn the potential-dependent energy surface end-to-end. We identify key challenges including training data scarcity, lack of standardisation, and architectural limitations in current MLIPs. To address these issues, we propose flexible templates for incorporating global electrochemical information into MLIP architectures, and data-efficient strategies such as transfer learning and multi-head architectures that leverage abundant existing zero-potential data. We conclude by calling for community initiatives to establish shared datasets and reporting standards for electrified interfaces.

papers.title: Doping-Induced Internal Electric-Field Modulation in g-C3N4/GaSe Heterojunction: Switching Photocatalytic Water Splitting Reaction from Type-II to Z-Scheme Mechanism
papers.abstract: State of the art Z-scheme photocatalysts are more advantageous compared to type-II heterojunctions as they retain high redox capability alongside effective charge transfer. Consequently, the design of efficient Z-scheme photocatalysts for solar-driven water splitting requires careful optimization of favorable band edges, light absorption, charge separation, and preservation of strong redox potentials simultaneously. In this work, we employed first-principles density functional theoretical calculations to study B,F-codoped g-C3N4/GaSe heterojunction as a high performance direct Z-scheme photocatalyst for water splitting reaction. g-C3N4/GaSe is reported as a type II heterojunction with limited visible light adsorption which switched to direct Z-scheme mechanism and showed significant enhancement of visible-light absorption (588 nm) upon doping with B and F atoms. Doping altered the direction of inherent electric field with an improved charge transfer of 0.12 |e| from GaSe to B,F-g-C3N4 unit confirmed the Z-scheme mechanism decisively. Furthermore, band edge analysis reveals that the valence band maxima of the heterojunction is more than +1.23 V (vs. NHE) and conduction band minima is more negative than 0 V (vs. NHE). Therefore, photogenerated electrons in GaSe facilitates hydrogen evolution reaction and holes in B,F-g-C3N4 driving oxygen evolution reaction, evincing the potential application of B,F-codoped g-C3N4/GaSe for water splitting reaction. Furthermore, a solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 14.80% demonstrates quite good photolytic performance of B, F g-C3N4/GaSe heterojunction. This study reveals the role of non-metal doped g-C3N4 as the parent scaffold in heterojunction engineering and thereby modeling high performance Z-scheme photocatalysts for sustainable hydrogen production. (emphasise the doping effect and heterojunction effect seperately)

papers.title: Vibrational spectroscopy in the study of reaction mechanism
papers.abstract: The detailed investigation of reaction mechanisms is nowadays a requirement in nearly all fields of chemistry. Molecular spectroscopy can provide key pieces of information on the reaction scheme. Among all available techniques, vibrational spectroscopy ones ( notably mid- IR absorption, Near-IR absorption, non-resonant Raman scattering, Resonance Raman scattering) represent possibly the most appropriate approaches to get valuable insight on reaction mechanism. In this account/perspective, following the research I have developed so far in different fields (ranging from photochemistry/photobiology to surface chemistry), I will describe the most appropriate vibrational spectroscopy techniques needed to get specific pieces of information. Emphasis will be put on the interplay between the different vibrational spectroscopies and on the synergy with advanced data analysis techniques, quantum chemistry calculations, and other experimental approaches.

papers.title: MOF-808 Mediated Chloride Flux Across Model Membrane Systems
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates the use of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as a new platform for mediating anion transport in bio-mimetic cell models. We employed a lucigenin fluorescence assay to monitor chloride flux in giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs) immobilized to zirconium-based framework, MOF-808. MOF-808, showed chloride transport enabled by its large pores and strong Zr - chloride affinity. In contrast, HKUST-1 despite its high porosity, showed limited chloride transport, underscoring the importance of metal node and pore topology in modulating anion flux. Collapsed MOF-808 showed no ion transport, indicating that the MOF pore integrity is essential. These findings inform us of the role of both metal interactions and pore architecture in facilitating anion transport across phospholipid membranes, providing insights for designing tailored MOFs channels with tunable ion transport features for chloride flux-associated disorders.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Crystallographic Copilots: Context-Aware Augmentation and a Path to Agentic Crystallography
Reduction of Biochemical Oxygen Demand in Wastewater Effluents Using UV LED Photolysis and Advanced Oxidation Processes
papers.abstract: Removal of organic loading in wastewater effluent is a priority for treatment facilities to ensure discharge water adheres to local regulations and is safe for the environment. This study investigated the removal of bulk organic matter (as measured by biochemical and carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand, BOD5 and cBOD5, respectively) from municipal wastewater effluent using 275-280 nm UV LED irradiation under bench-scale and full-scale conditions. Bench-scale removal was evaluated using both collimated beam and flow through UV LED reactors (275 nm) at fluences between 250 - 5000 mJ cm-2 with and without chemical oxidant addition (chlorine) for primary and secondary effluent matrices. Treatment efficacy for the secondary effluent source was also investigated using a full-scale flow-through 280 nm UV LED reactor at a fluence of approximately 148 mJ cm-2 and a flow of 545 m3 day-1. This work determined that UV C LED irradiation can reduce effluent BOD in municipal wastewater matrices (by up to 52%) at both the bench- and full-scale. Mechanistically, the fluorescence profile of UV-exposed samples exhibited a shift in the humic index suggesting that lower weight, protein-like organic compounds were the primary target of the UV C process. This work demonstrates that UV C LED technologies can be a useful tool for water utilities that require additional BOD removal.

papers.title: QuADMET-Former: Pre-training on Quantum Mechanical Properties Improves ADMET Prediction
papers.abstract: In principle, quantum chemistry allows us to quantify electronic and geometric properties of molecules and their interactions. Thus, incorporating pre-calculated quantum mechanical properties into deep learning models could improve their ability to predict important pharmacological properties of small molecules and potential drugs. However, this opportunity to incorporate better physicochemical inductive bias has been underexploited in the recent wave of AI-driven drug discovery. We show that pre-training Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) models-specifically the TorchMD-NET model-to predict quantum mechanical molecular and atomic properties like dipole moments, HOMO-LUMO gap, and partial charges, we can obtain more accurate models to predict absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicological (ADMET) properties. Moreover, we explore the interplay between quantum chemistry and three-dimensional structure by introducing a novel structure pre-training strategy where the equivariant transformer is pre-trained on three-dimensional molecular fingerprints known as E3FPs. We ran QuADMET-Former, MapLight+GNN and Quantum Informed Pre-training on 23 ADMET benchmarks drawn from Therapeutic Data Commons (TDC), Biogen ADME, and OpenADMET, and found them to outperform both MapLight+GNN, the best-performing single model on the TDC benchmark, and Quantum Informed pre-training, a state-of-the-art method for quantum chemistry-informed ADMET prediction, on very challenging spectral splits. QuADMET-Former performed best on 16 of the 23 datasets (13 out of those 16 were statistically significant). The optimal pre-training target combination varies across tasks, suggesting that quantum mechanical and geometric features capture complementary aspects of molecular behaviour. Our results establish quantum chemistry-grounded pre-training as a practical and impactful strategy for ADMET prediction under strict generalization conditions, and highlight the underexplored interplay between 3D molecular geometry and electronic structure in representation learning for small-molecule drug discovery.

papers.title: Molecular Simulations Assisted by an Artificial Intelligence Agent (ArIA)
papers.abstract: Computational chemistry enables the investigation of molecular and materials properties through simulations. Among available methods, density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) are widely applied because they provide practical error margins at affordable computational cost. Despite their broad utility, their effective application requires extensive training in both theoretical chemistry and basic programming, creating a significant entrance barrier for non-specialists. In this work, we develop an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) based on open-source large language models (LLMs) that can be readily deployed on a state-of-the-art personal computers (PCs). This agentic AI is capable of interpreting user instructions, performing simulations with the ORCA program suite, and generating both interactive visualizations and summary reports. Additionally, users can interrogate the simulation results through text queries, making computational chemistry more accessible. We release our agentic AI fully open-source, which will create a collaborative development ecosystem to build upon for future improvements.

papers.title: Review of Machine Learning in Surfactant Science: QSPR Modelling and Generative Approaches
papers.abstract: This paper reviews recent advances in the application of machine learning (ML) methods to quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) modelling and molecular generation in surfactant science. As the variety of surfactant species and annual production volumes continue to grow, their proper characterization becomes increasingly important. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in chemistry represent a promising set of tools for addressing such tasks, in which ML plays a key role. The scope of the paper encompasses QSPR studies of two categories of surfactant properties: intrinsic properties, among which critical micelle concentration and surface tension are considered separately, and practically relevant industrial properties. Modeling approaches for each property type are compared, and their respective advantages, disadvantages, and challenges are discussed. Generative approaches represent the next stage of ML modelling, and this rapidly evolving field is reviewed. De novo generation of molecular structures and surfactant-based formulations is covered, with the relevant approaches described and compared. Finally, the current state of the field and future prospects of ML and AI applications in surfactant science and industry are outlined. Overall, this paper provides a structured evaluation of ML and AI applications across a range of tasks and demonstrates the broad scope of their utility in surfactant studies.

papers.title: Intramolecular control of click-to-release chemistry unlocks fast and quantitative bioorthogonal bond cleavage in living systems
papers.abstract: Bioorthogonal click-to-release reactions are powerful tools for investigating biological dynamics and advancing therapeutic strategies. However, the multi-step mechanisms underlying these reactions prove challenging to control. For tetrazine-triggered cleavage of trans -cyclooctene conjugates, the first bioorthogonal reaction to reach clinical evaluation, slow and erratic tautomerization of the initial post-click intermediate remains a central limitation. Approaches that anchor directing functionalities to tetrazines accelerate this key step but impose trade-offs in tetrazine reactivity and stability. Here, we shift the tautomerization driving force from the tetrazine to the trans -cyclooctene (TCO), introducing iTCO as a click-cleavable linker that encodes intra­molecular control of the post-click mechanism and thereby enables efficient and reliable click-to-release, independent of tetrazine structure, reactivity, and click orientation. Across biological systems of increasing complexity, from in vitro to in vivo , iTCO achieves fast and quantitative bond cleavage with highly reactive tetrazines at low micromolar concentrations within seconds to minutes. Intramolecular control thus resolves a long-standing limitation of click-to-release chemistry, establishing a new performance regime that delivers the speed and reliability required for bioorthogonal bond cleavage in living systems.

papers.title: Tuning Nanostructure of Flame-made Palladium deposited on Cerium Oxide: Unveiling Pd Loading–Activity Relationships in Suzuki–Miyaura Cross-Coupling
Driving Breakthrough Therapies: Why PFAS Motifs Matter in Drug Design
papers.abstract: Concerns regarding long-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) involving PFOS, PFOA, PFNA, etc., have translated into (initiatives for) broad-based legislation that are not appropriately legislating PFAS on a speciated basis, but have instead defined PFAS as class sweeping in fundamental chemistry building blocks for shorter chain carbon-fluorine bonds that are essential to medicinal products. This paper explores the implications for medicinal chemistry and small molecule drug discovery, with emphasis on fluorinated motifs such as –CF2– and –CF3 that are routinely used in active pharmaceutical ingredients to advance the creation of innovative therapeutics. Survey data from medicinal chemists across multiple pharmaceutical organizations indicate that fluorinated substituents are routinely employed to modulate target engagement, selectivity, permeability, metabolic stability, and systemic exposure in drug candidates, especially in therapeutic areas characterized by stringent molecular optimization requirements. Representative examples from recently approved therapies and drugs listed on the World Health Organization Model List of Essential Medicines illustrate how the use of these motifs have facilitated the successful translation of challenging targets into clinically effective drugs. In addition, we discuss the scientific and translational implications raised by applying the proposed uniform PFAS classifications to future pharmaceuticals and highlight the importance of context‑specific evaluation to support regulatory frameworks, but without constraining future drug discovery efforts to address unmet medical needs.

papers.title: Magneto-Optical Spectroscopy Across Three Oxidation States of a Europium Terpyridine Complex
papers.abstract: The multiconfigurational nature of lanthanide ions yields notoriously complex electronic structures, and europium is a useful exemplar of this complexity. Engineering of future europium-based molecules and materials—well known for their luminescence in the +3 oxidation state and magnetism in the +2 oxidation state—rests on a precise understanding of their structure–property relationships. Magneto-optical spectroscopies are well suited to probe these relationships, and we demonstrate their utility here through the characterization of a series of homoleptic europium terpyridine complexes in +3, +2, and formally 0 oxidation states. Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) analysis of the f–f transitions of the Eu(III) complex revealed an effective D 3h local symmetry in solution, higher than suggested by the solid-state structure, through the splitting pattern of its 7 F 0 → 5 D 2 transition. The Eu(II) complex, by contrast, exhibited broad MCD features spanning the visible region arising from 4f 7 → 4f 6 ⊗ ψ 1 transitions (ψ = 5d or Lπ*). We show theoretically and experimentally that when individual components of this progression are unresolved, MCD and magnetic linear dichroism (MLD) spectra display characteristic “pseudo- A 1 ” and “pseudo- A 2 ” lineshapes, respectively. Variable-temperature variable-field measurements of both techniques reveal a near-zero Eu(II) zero-field splitting and confirm the first observation of G 0 MLD intensity for an f-block molecular complex. The formally Eu(0) complex was serendipitously isolated and its properties are consistent with a redox non-innocent [Eu II (mtpy)(mtpy •– ) 2 ] formulation. Together, these results establish MCD and MLD spectroscopies as information-rich tools for probing f-block electronic structure across multiple oxidation states and transition types.

papers.title: A Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Mechanistic Prediction of Hepatotoxicity
papers.abstract: Workflow of proposed hepatotoxicity prediction model Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) continues to be one of the main reasons for late-stage drug attrition, post-marketing withdrawals, and acute liver failure are caused by the DILI phenomenon which is characterized by being multifactorial and idiosyncratic. The availability of in silico hepatotoxicity prediction models has primarily relied on either two-dimensional descriptors or graph topology, thus failing to represent the interplay of molecular geometry, physicochemical determinants, and biologically mediated toxicity pathways in the predictions. This study describes a mechanistically informed multimodal deep-learning framework that combines threedimensional molecular geometry, physicochemical profiling, structural alerts, and biologically derived risk signals for the robust prediction of hepatotoxicity. The proposed structure uses a geometry-aware SchNet encoder that directly learns the spatial and electronic interactions from the atomic coordinates, which is further enhanced by the biophysicochemical expert network that incorporates RDKit descriptors, MACCS fingerprints, and validated biological oracles that capture key hepatotoxicity-relevant mechanisms, such as transporter inhibition and metabolic liability. The heterogeneous representations are combined by a late-integration technique, which enables the retention of domain-specific signals prior to categorization. The model was trained and evaluated using a carefully curated hepatotoxicity dataset prepared from DILIrank 2.0 and TOXRIC. The multimodal framework surpassed traditional machine learning models and classic graph neural networks by its performance on an independent test set attaining an AUC-ROC of 0.80, accuracy of 82.8%, and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.665. In addition, the model showed high sensitivity (92.1%) for hepatotoxic compounds and lost little predictive power under scaffold-split evaluation, implying partial generalization beyond the known chemical series. The interpretation analyses verified the model's compliance with established toxicology and showed the contributions derived from known reactive substructures, physicochemical risk factors, and biologically contextualized signals.

papers.title: New insights on PFAS inputs to the Great Lakes based on sediments from Lakes Superior and Huron
papers.abstract: This study presents the first comprehensive survey of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in sediments from Great Lakes Superior and Huron since 2010. Six cores and surface sediments were collected from Superior and Huron in 2021 and 2022, respectively. Superior surface sediments contained primarily perfluorocarboxylic acids (PFCAs), reflecting atmospheric deposition as Superior’s primary PFAS input. Frequent detections of perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctane sulfonamide (PFOSA) across both lakes suggest atmospheric input of PFOSA as an important contributor of PFOS to sediments. PFAS in Superior were strongly correlated with sediment organic matter (SOM), indicating strong influence of sediment transport and partitioning processes on spatial distributions, while correlations were weaker for Huron. Average surface sediment concentrations were comparable between Superior and Huron except for PFOS, which was >2x more concentrated in Huron sediments, suggesting possible influence of legacy aqueous film-forming foams (AFFF) to PFAS contamination in Huron. Huron spatial patterns were consistent with AFFF contamination originating from southern Georgian Bay spreading to the Huron main body. Temporal profiles for Superior showed gradually increasing PFAS fluxes from the 1960s through 2020. In contrast, PFAS fluxes in Huron near the Main Channel began to rapidly increase in 2007, suggesting that AFFF contamination may have been spreading within the Huron main body for nearly two decades. These results warrant continued efforts to reduce PFAS inputs to the Great Lakes.

papers.title: Sorbates from 1,1-dialkylsubstituted alkenes and 3-haloacrylic esters via Pd(II)-isohypsic catalysis: focus on terpenes.
papers.abstract: Limonene and other 1,1-dialkylsubstituted alkenes undergo a regioselective Pd(II)-catalyzed C–H/C–X coupling with (E) and (Z)-3-bromoacrylates affording 4,4-disubstituted sorbate derivatives as mixtures of geometrical isomers (16 examples). This coupling, previously unreported for the synthesis of 1,3-dienes, follows a mechanism distinct from the well-known Mizoroki-Heck, and works where the Mizoroki-Heck fails. DFT computations allowed to propose a plausible mechanism for this transformation.

papers.title: Chemically Fueled Active Transport Cascades in Large Unilamellar Vesicles
papers.abstract: Biology routinely transduces energy stored in chemical bonds to create transmembrane gradients, which are themselves a crucial on-demand energy store to drive life’s vital processes. We report a strategy for the chemically fueled active transport of molecular cargo in large unilamellar vesicles. We outline the features required for driving active transport across phospholipid bilayers. Through a series of experiments in both hybrid lipid–liquid supported bilayers and biomimetic vesicles, we demonstrate the transmembrane transport of our diacid cargo, and quantify key performance indicators of our system. The active transport mechanism gives rise to the spontaneous generation of transmembrane pH gradients of up to ~0.4 pH units, comparable to the gradient required to drive ATP-synthase. We harness this gradient as an energy source to drive a secondary active transport process through symport/antiport mechanisms. These chemically fueled active transport cascades demonstrate the successive transduction of free energy from chemical bonds to transmembrane proton gradients to transmembrane Na + or Cl − gradients. Our work establishes the first example of chemically fueled active transport in unilamellar vesicles and demonstrates how transmembrane gradients can both absorb energy, and transfer it, as part of a greater systems-level life-like compartmentalized nanotechnology.

papers.title: Experimental Investigation of Gas Crossover and Degradation Induced by Pinholes in PEM Electrolyzers
papers.abstract: Pinholes in the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) of proton exchange membrane electrolyzer cells (PEMECs), often caused by mechanical stress, chemical degradation, or manufacturing flaws, can compromise gas tightness, threatening operational safety, gas purity, and long-term durability. However, only limited data are available on how pinholes in MEAs affect the operational stability of PEMECs. In this study, artificial pinholes ranging from 4 µm to 113 µm were introduced into Nafion™ N115‑based MEAs using focused ion beam milling. Their effect on hydrogen crossover and cell voltage was evaluated before and after an accelerated stress test (AST). Post‑AST measurements provided insight into how pinholes and their size can influence degradation processes. Complementary analyses, including scanning electron microscopy, scanning electrochemical microscopy, ion chromatography, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry and X‑ray computer tomography were employed for in- depth characterization of the MEA samples. The results show that smaller pinholes (≤ 8 µm) have little to no effect on operation and degradation under certain conditions, whereas larger ones accelerate MEA degradation and significantly increase hydrogen crossover.

papers.title: A ∆-Learning Approach to Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Intermolecular Interactions
papers.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) trained by directly learning the total interatomic interaction energies can suffer from limited transferability, unphysical behavior beyond a finite cutoff, and large errors for out-of-distribution geometries such as transition states and uncommon conformers. We evaluate ∆-learning (Delta-learning) as a remedy by training an ANI-style high-dimensional neural network potential as a correction to predict PBE0/aug-cc-pVTZ energies from a third-order tight-binding density functional theory (DFTB3) baseline model. We name this method ANIDFTB-∆ and compare it to an otherwise identical conventional HDNNP (ANIPBE0-Direct) trained to predict directly the PBE0/aug-cc-pVTZ energy. On a held-out test set from the modified ANI-1x training set, ∆-learning reduces the mean absolute error from 2.01 to 0.82 kcal/mol. On selected GMTKN55 benchmarks, the ∆ model systematically improves relative energies for conformers and tautomers and avoids catastrophic outliers on challenging structures. For proton-transfer transition states, neither ANIDFTB-∆ nor ANIDFTB-direct are quantitatively accurate, but the ∆ approach yields substantially smaller errors (MAE 1.53 vs 39.20 kcal/mol) by inheriting the DFTB3’s more reasonable transition-state physics. For intermolecular interactions, ∆-learning offers a qualitative advantage: the direct model predicts zero interaction beyond the 5.2 Å cutoff, whereas the ∆ model retains the long-range electrostatics present in DFTB3. On the DES370K dataset of intermolecular interaction energies, this reduces the interaction-energy MAE from 0.76 to 0.48 kcal/mol overall and from 0.098 to 0.019 kcal/mol on a long-range subset where all inter-monomer distances exceed the cutoff, highlighting improved transferability for noncovalent interactions.

papers.title: A Simple Biorefinery Approach for the Full Valorization of Mango Seeds and Peels into Bioplastics
papers.abstract: Mango industrial processing generates large amounts of byproducts, including peels and finisher pulp (PeP), seed tegument (SeT), and kernel (SeK). These fractions have distinct compositions and remain largely underutilized commercially. Research in this area often relies on complex processing routes that fail to exploit the full potential of these byproducts. In this work, we propose a simple strategy for the comprehensive valorization of all mango byproducts (MBPs) into bioplastics. For this, MBPs were subjected to mild hydrothermal pretreatment (HTP) or dilute alkaline pretreatment (DALP) with sodium hydroxide, subjected to mild hydrothermal pretreatment (HTP) or dilute alkaline pretreatment (DALP) with sodium hydroxide, which selectively partitioned amorphous components and induced distinct structural responses according to the biomass fraction. While HTP better preserved solubilized carbohydrates, DALP promoted more intensive pectin saponification and hemicellulose solubilization. Bioplastic films were then prepared using pretreated PeP, SeK, or a mixture of all byproducts (PePSe). The incorporation of only 10% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) yielded films with tensile strength of up to 11 MPa. The SeK-based films exhibited the lowest water vapor permeability (2.3 g mm kPa-1 h-1 m-2), and all CMC-containing films displayed hydrophobic surfaces (water contact angle > 90°). All bioplastics provided near-total UVA and UVB shielding (> 98%), while the PeP-based films overall exhibited the highest transparency (> 43%). Although the antioxidant activity of the bioplastics decreased compared to that of the corresponding raw MBPs, the PeP-DALP-CMC film retained at least 50% of it. The simplicity and effectiveness of this approach make it promise and potentially scalable to manufacturing sustainable packaging materials, thereby promoting waste valorization and circularity.

papers.title: Excited-state orbital angular momentum enables all-optical molecular spin coherence
papers.abstract: Paramagnetic molecules are promising quantum sensors with dimensions and environmental compatibility inaccessible to solid-state defects. Realizing this promise, however, requires optical methods for initializing and reading out coherent spin dynamics. Ultrafast pump–probe polarization spectroscopy provides such a route, but previous demonstrations have relied on high-symmetry complexes in which ground-state orbital angular momentum enables spin–photon coupling. Here we demonstrate the first ultrafast spin coherence measurements on non-octahedral molecules and show that excited-state orbital angular momentum can instead provide the optical interface in axial tungsten(V)-oxo complexes. Circularly polarized excitation generates room-temperature spin coherence that persists for several nanoseconds, enabling time-domain optical detection of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra, including g value anisotropy in a polymer matrix, and solution-phase DC magnetic field detection down to 5 mT. This work establishes a route to ultrafast, all-optical spin spectroscopy and quantum sensing in lower-symmetry, chemically tunable coordination complexes.

papers.title: Total Synthesis of the Diterpene Alkaloid Thelepogine Through Enyne Hydroamination
papers.abstract: The total synthesis of the atypical diterpene alkaloid thelepogine is reported. Our pathway features the asymmetric construction of a carbotricyclic intermediate that undergoes a 2,3-Wittig–Still rearrangement of a tetrasubstituted allylic alcohol, installing two adjacent quaternary stereocenters. The α-tertiary amine of thelepogine was delineated from a quaternary carbon through a Beckmann-type rearrangement, while the unusual pyrrolizidine moiety was assembled through a copper(I)-catalyzed (4+1) cycloaddition of an amino enyne, amounting to a twofold hydroamination. Our synthesis enabled the full spectroscopic characterization of thelepogine, which had previously been characterized only by single-crystal X-ray diffraction of a derivative, and opens the door to comprehensive biological evaluation.

papers.title: BWs-ADC: The algebraic diagrammatic construction for the polarisation propagator using a size-consistent Brillouin-Wigner partitioning up to third order in perturbation theory
papers.abstract: We present the algebraic diagrammatic construction for the polarisation propagator (PP-ADC) formulated with a twoparameter, size-consistent Brillouin–Wigner partitioning (BWs) up to third order in perturbation theory (BWs-ADC). The resulting method is size-consistent, size-extensive, and regular, and extends the applicability of ADC to systems with degenerate electronic ground states. We demonstrate that the secular matrices of BWs-ADC(2) and BWs-ADC(3) are structurally equivalent to their Møller–Plesset (MP-ADC) counterparts, and determine optimal regularisation parameters by analysing the dissociation of H 2 in a minimal basis. These parameters are subsequently refined using a benchmark set of 122 single excitations comprising both valence and Rydberg states. BWs-ADC(2) favours strong regularisation in the occupied space, whereas virtual-space regularisation is found to significantly increase excitation energy errors. In contrast, BWs-ADC(3) generally benefits from slight de-regularisation. Both methods achieve a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.15 eV, representing a substantial improvement over the corresponding MP-ADC approaches; for BWs-ADC(3), this error is dominated by a small number of outliers, whereas BWs-ADC(2) exhibits more uniform accuracy. A second benchmark demonstrates that parameter-optimised BWs-ADC methods also yield significantly improved oscillator strengths and excited-state dipole moments. Overall, BWs-ADC provides improved accuracy for single-reference systems while simultaneously extending the applicability of ADC to few-reference regimes, including bond dissociation processes, diradical species, and selected transition metal complexes.

papers.title: Li-Ion Transfer at the LLZO–Polycaprolactone Interface: Role of Polymer Chemistry in Interfacial Transport
papers.abstract: Hybrid polymer–ceramic electrolytes are promising candidates for solid-state lithium batteries, yet ion transport across polymerceramic interfaces often limits performance. Here, atomistic molecular-dynamics simulations are used to investigate Li-ion exchange at the Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO)–poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) interface and to compare directly with LLZO–poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) at comparable lithium loading. The LLZO–PCL interface exhibits pronounced interfacial structuring, including strong adsorption of carbonyl oxygen atoms at the ceramic surface and a well-defined first Li+ layer. Li-ion transfer across the interface is quantified from transition statistics and analyzed using free-energy profiles along the surface-normal coordinate. At 700 K, LLZO–PCL shows a substantially higher exchange rate than LLZO—PEO (factor 32), primarily due to a significantly lower free-energy barrier for polymer–ceramic transfer, consistent with weaker Li+ coordination in PCL. An overdamped Kramers analysis together with the intra-well autocorrelation function confirms strongly damped local dynamics and suggests differences in effective friction between the minimum and the barrier region. Overall, the results demonstrate that polymer chemistry controls interfacial Li-ion transfer mainly via the barrier height, identifying polymer coordination strength as a key design parameter for reducing interfacial resistance in hybrid solid electrolytes.

papers.title: Influence of exchange–correlation functional on machine-learnt interatomic potentials accuracy: a systematic study in borosilicate glasses
papers.abstract: Machine-learnt interatomic potential (MLIP) has emerged as a strategy to accelerate molecular simulations, offering the promise of quantum chemical accuracy at a cost close to that of classical force fields. They are commonly trained on reference data obtained at the DFT level, which is itself a sufficiently affordable method to generate thousands of configurations and associated energies and atomic forces. However, this approach suffers from an elephant in the room, which is rarely addressed: the choice of exchange–correlation functional. Although it is understood to have a crucial impact on the accuracy of the description of interactions and therefore on the results of the molecular simulations, it has not been systematically evaluated in the past. To go beyond simple benchmarks on selected configurations, we set out to understand the influence of exchange–correlation (XC) functional on the training of MLIPs, and more importantly on the physical properties of the resulting condensed matter systems. As a complex chemical system to test this, we selected borosilicate glasses of a wide variety of compositions. We produced reference data sets of borosilicate glasses with nine different chemical compositions, with five different XC functionals at the GGA, meta-GGA and hybrid levels. We then trained MLIPs for all of them, produced glasses by melt-quenching, and compared their physical and structural properties with available experimental data. We show that there are significant differences between the different functionals. While the influence on bulk properties such as glass densities is minor, fine structural properties are more sensitive to the choice of functional, in particular when it comes to the coordination of boron atoms. Our results show how MLIPs can help us better understand the strengths and weaknesses of DFT functionals, where investigation through direct ab initio molecular dynamics was too expensive in the past. It also highlights that MLIPs depend on the ground truth on which they are trained, a fact often overlooked in practice, and this influence may be drastic on specific physical properties.

papers.title: Resolving the Structures of AlM2O4+ (M = Fe, Co) through Multireference Methods
papers.abstract: Multicenter transition metal clusters often exhibit a dense manifold of low-lying electronic states arising from the interplay of ligand-field splitting and spin coupling. Together with structural and valence isomerism, these factors make vibrational spectral assignments challenging. The infrared photodissociation (IRPD) spectra of AlM 2 O 4 + (M = Fe, Co) have resisted interpretation because the predicted spectra are sensitive to the isomer and its electronic state. Here we settle the assignment by employing multireference methods in a localized active space framework to identify the low-energy structures and their ground-state electronic configurations, followed by vibrational analysis using Kohn--Sham density functional theory. We show that the experimental IRPD spectra arise from the coexistence of two structural isomers, each in a low-spin ground state. Vibrational spectra calculated for the identified ground states reproduce the experimental IRPD features, whereas those of alternative states do not. This assignment is consistent with reported experimental observations, namely the IRPD spectra, the ion mobility distributions, and the absence of methane reactivity. Analysis of the electronic structure reveals that ligand-field effects dominate over spin coupling in shaping both energetics and vibrational spectra of these clusters. These results show the power of multireference methods capable of treating large active spaces, which are often required for binuclear complexes.

papers.title: Natural and biobased anti-melanosis strategies for penaeid shrimp: critically evaluating the link between enzymatic mechanisms and product-level preservation performance
papers.abstract: Melanosis is a major postharvest quality defect in penaeid shrimp, substantially shortening product shelf life. To prevent black spot formation, the shrimp industry relies mainly on sulphites and 4-hexylresorcinol, two chemical benchmarks not aligned with clean-label and organic production goals. This scoping review critically evaluates natural and biobased interventions reported for shrimp melanosis control, with the explicit aim of assessing how consistently enzyme-level inhibition evidence translates to product-level preservation outcomes, a link that, as the available literature reveals, remains largely unresolved for most candidates. Literature and patent evidence published from 1950 to April 2026 were examined by separating enzyme-level evidence, such as inhibition of shrimp polyphenol oxidase/phenoloxidase (PPO/PO) activity, from product-level evidence, such as visible melanosis suppression during chilled or iced storage. Among the reviewed interventions, many act through overlapping mechanisms, including (partial) PPO/PO suppression, quinone interception, antioxidant effects, metal interactions, and microbial control. Overall, the available studies suggest that shrimp melanosis is rarely controlled by PPO/PO inhibition alone; in practice, delivery, redox effects, matrix interactions, and broader quality preservation often contribute substantially to the final outcome. Finally, we propose an author-defined Target Candidate Profile (TCP) and Target Product Profile (TPP) that integrate mechanism, cold-chain efficacy, safety, sensory compatibility, residue burden, environmental profile, and industrial feasibility to support more rigorous prioritization of future biobased anti-melanosis candidates.

papers.title: Comment on “The discovery and investigation of a crystalline solid solution of an active pharmaceutical ingredient”
papers.abstract: Patel et al. reported the first crystalline solid solution (CSS) formation of an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) using benzocaine as a model, and fitted the solubility data of benzocaine Form I and Form II in water and ethanol with the modified Apelblat and Van’t Hoff models to determine the phase transition temperature (). However, inconsistencies were identified in the thermodynamic model fitting results of benzocaine solubility data presented in their work. Substitution of the reported modified Apelblat model parameters into the equation yielded solubility values with significant systematic deviations from the experimental data, even showing order-of-magnitude discrepancies in multiple systems. In this commentary, re-fitting of the experimental solubility data with the modified Apelblat model is conducted to obtain refitted and accurate parameters, and further analysis of the origin of the systematic fitting deviation in the original study is provided. A simple correction method for the original model parameters is also proposed to improve the reliability and reproducibility of the research results related to benzocaine’s thermodynamic behavior.

papers.title: Pathogen Elimination in Dried Red Blood Cell Preparations via Riboflavin-Ultraviolet Treatment and Supercritical CO2: A Literature-Supported Conceptual Framework with Two-Stage Point-of-Care Donor Screening
papers.abstract: Current blood donor screening requires pathogen-specific immunoassays (ELISA) or rapid diagnostic tests (RDT) for each target disease, incurring per-donor costs of USD 7-10 and turnaround times of 20 minutes to 4 hours. This paper proposes a paradigm shift from pathogen detection to pathogen elimination, integrated within the supercritical CO2 (scCO2) drying pipeline described in the companion publication. Using published log-reduction data from peer-reviewed literature, we demonstrate that riboflavin (80 microM) + ultraviolet illumination (6.24 J/cm2) achieves ≥4 log reduction against all five pathogens mandatorily screened in Thai blood banks: HIV-1/2 (5.40 log), HCV (4.43 log), HBV (4.27 log), Treponema pallidum/Syphilis (>6.00 log), and Plasmodium/Malaria (3.89 log), with scCO2 providing additive antimicrobial activity of 4.2-5.5 log against enveloped pathogens and bacteria. The combined system is projected to meet regulatory 4-log reduction standards for all mandatory Thai screening targets. Post-elimination quality control via optical spectroscopy (UV-Vis, NIR) through the blood collection tube replaces pathogen-specific testing with functional RBC verification — reducing per-donor screening cost from THB 280 to approximately THB 23, and turnaround from 2-4 hours to under 10 minutes. A complementary two-stage point-of-care biosensor architecture is proposed for settings where elimination-based processing is not available. Limitations including non-enveloped virus resistance (Parvovirus B19: 1.5 log) and prion non-inactivation are explicitly acknowledged. This document constitutes a public prior art disclosure under CC BY 4.0.

papers.title: Pyridine-Mediated and Autocatalytic Reaction Pathways in Porphyrin COF Formation – A Quantum Chemical Thermodynamic Study
papers.abstract: The atomic-level mechanism of porphyrin-ed covalent organic framework (COF) assembly remains largely unresolved despite COFs having been synthesized under gas, solid-vapor, and solution-phase conditions. This study employed quantum chemical calculations to unravel the detailed ring-closure dimerization of TAPP-derived porphyrin COFs, comparing gas-phase and pyridine-mediated solution-phase pathways. In the absence of external bases or catalysts, dimerization in the gas phase is shown to be endergonic and hindered by a significant thermodynamic and kinetic barrier. Upon introduction of pyridine as both solvent and base, the reaction pathway is significantly modified: intermediates become stabilized, key proton elimination steps are facilitated, and the overall reaction becomes exergonic. Four principal intermediates are identified, with one intermediate emerging as a structurally and electronically favorable branching point. While one intermediate is kinetically accessible, its low stability leads to rapid bond cleavage, redirecting the pathway via the branching point mentioned above. Electronic structure analysis revealed that pyridine not only modulates frontier orbital energies but also supports an autocatalytic regime, with that favorable intermediate serving as an electronic mediator enabling catalyst-free COF assembly. These findings provide mechanistic clarity for the roles of solvation, acid–base chemistry, and quantum orbital alignment in COF synthesis, offering actionable guidelines for selecting pyridine-like basic solvents to modulate reaction feasibility, tuning porphyrin linker electronics to stabilize key autocatalysis-facilitating intermediates, and adjusting temperature and concentration to promote the necessary electronic reorganization, thereby favoring autocatalytic, catalyst-free COF growth and enhancing COF performance in advanced materials applications.

papers.title: Ambient-Temperature Red Blood Cell Preservation via Supercritical CO2 Desiccation with Food-Grade Bacteriostatic Agents and Perfluorocarbon Oxygen Supplement: A Conceptual Framework for
papers.abstract: Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in resource-limited and geographically remote settings is critically constrained by cold-chain dependency (1–6°C), short shelf life (42 days), and high total cost of ownership under tropical ambient conditions. No existing approved product combines ambient-temperature stability, volume reduction, bacteriostatic protection, and augmented oxygen delivery in a single dried RBC preparation. Here we describe a conceptual multi-component preservation system comprising: (i) intracellular trehalose loading via electroporation as a vitrification agent; (ii) supercritical CO2 (scCO2) desiccation at 31–40°C as a novel, surface-tension-free drying modality; (iii) food-grade bacteriostatic agents — epsilon-polylysine, rosemary extract (rosmarinic acid), citric acid, and ascorbic acid — providing triple-layer microbial control without cold chain; and (iv) Perfluorononane:beta-cyclodextrin (PFN:beta-CD) inclusion complex as the rehydration medium, supplementing oxygen-carrying capacity by approximately 20–30% relative to baseline. Computational simulation predicts ambient shelf life of 730 days at up to 45°C — suitable for Thai tropical conditions year-round. Unit volume is reduced 13-fold (450ml to 35ml) and weight 5-fold (510g to 95g), enabling 5–6x greater transport density per vehicle without refrigeration. Total cost of ownership for rural Thai hospitals is estimated at THB 1,655 per unit versus THB 4,905 for current refrigerated RBC including cold-chain costs — a 66% reduction. This document constitutes a public prior art disclosure under CC BY 4.0.

papers.title: Self-Healing and Tacky Silver Nanowire/Polyborosiloxane Composite Electrodes for Robust Wearable Sensors
papers.abstract: A self-adhesive and self-healing hydration sensor comprising silver nanowire (AgNW)/polyborosiloxane (PBS) composite has been developed for robust monitoring of skin hydration levels. The sensor exploits the supramolecular properties of PBS, arising from reversible Si-O-B dynamic covalent bonding, which confer intrinsic mechanical and electrical self-healing capabilities. The PBS substrate exhibits a low Young's modulus (~240 kPa) matching human skin and exceptional stretchability (~600%), facilitating conformal contact without requiring auxiliary adhesive layers. Mechanical tensile testing demonstrated complete recovery of both Young's modulus and yield strength within three hours following damage, while the AgNW/PBS electrode restored 77% electrical conductivity after 24 hours of ambient healing. Notably, PBS maintains superior adhesion under wet conditions compared to commercial electrocardiography (ECG) patches, rendering the sensor particularly robust for perspiration-intensive applications. On-skin electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) validated accurate detection of skin hydration variations, with exercise monitoring demonstrating the sensor's capability to track dynamic hydration changes during physical activity. These findings establish design principles for conformable, self-healing wearable sensors suitable for continuous health monitoring applications.

papers.title: Oral Perfluorocarbon-Based Oxygen Carrier: A Conceptual Framework for a Perfluorononane–β-Cyclodextrin Inclusion Complex as a Blood-Group-Independent Systemic Oxygen Supplement
papers.abstract: Current allogeneic blood transfusion is constrained by ABO/Rh compatibility requirements, donor dependency, cold-chain logistics, and limited erythrocyte shelf life. Perfluorocarbon (PFC) compounds dissolve molecular oxygen efficiently and are immunologically inert, yet existing PFC preparations require intravenous administration, limiting pre-hospital and resource-constrained deployment. Here we describe a conceptual oral formulation comprising Perfluorononane (PFN, C 9 F 20 ) encapsulated within a β-Cyclodextrin (β-CD) inclusion complex, co-formulated with thermostable Carbonic Anhydrase from Sulphurihydrogenibium yellowstonense (SspCA) to facilitate CO 2 hydration. In-silico ADME profiling (RDKit v2026.3) identifies PFN as the optimal candidate among screened PFCs: MW 488 Da, 20 fluorine atoms, zero bromine, and predicted effective LogP of 3.28 following β-CD complexation within the range permitting gastrointestinal lymphatic absorption. β-CD solubilises PFN for transit through the gastric environment, releasing PFN in the proximal small intestine via competitive displacement by endogenous bile salts; β-CD is subsequently excreted intact in faeces. SspCA (k cat = 9.35 × 105 s−1; t 1/2 = 53 days at 25 °C) manages CO 2 accumulation without dependence on erythrocyte carbonic anhydrase. The formulation is shelf-stable at ambient temperature, requires no crossmatch, and is proposed for pre-operative oxygen reserve loading, pre-exposure supplementation in resource-limited settings, and as an adjunct organ preservation perfusate. This document constitutes a public prior art disclosure; no experimental in vivo data has been generated. Validation via in vitro dissolution, Caco-2 permeability, and animal pharmacokinetic studies is required.

papers.title: Cyclodextrin-Based Adsorbents for Water and Wastewater Treatment: Material Design, Adsorption Mechanisms, and Practical Limitations
papers.abstract: Water pollution from dyes, pharmaceuticals, endocrine-disrupting compounds, and heavy metals remains a persistent environmental challenge because many contaminants are not sufficiently removed by conventional treatment processes, especially at low concentrations. In this context, cyclodextrins have attracted considerable interest for water remediation owing to their ability to form inclusion complexes with organic molecules and to participate in additional interactions such as hydrogen bonding, electrostatic attraction, and metal coordination. Since native cyclodextrins are water-soluble, practical applications in water treatment rely mainly on their conversion into water-insoluble materials, including cross-linked polymers, nanocomposites, magnetic adsorbents, supported systems, and cyclodextrin-derived metalorganic frameworks. This review summarizes recent progress in the use of native and modified cyclodextrin-based materials as adsorbents for the removal of both organic and inorganic pollutants from water and wastewater. Particular attention is given to the relationship between material design and adsorption performance, the main classes of cyclodextrin-derived adsorbents, and the mechanisms governing pollutant uptake. In addition to adsorption efficiency, the review discusses regeneration, biodegradability, toxicity, and the practical limitations that currently restrict the broader application of these materials. Overall, cyclodextrin-derived adsorbents are promising platforms for water purification because they combine molecular recognition with tunable material properties. At the same time, their future development requires more critical evaluation under realistic water-treatment conditions, including complex pollutant mixtures, competing ions, long-term stability, safe cross-linking strategies, and scale-up to industrially relevant systems.

papers.title: σ-Hole Engineering Enables Selective Supramolecular Isomer Formation in Sb(III) Hosts
papers.abstract: Pnictogen bonding (PnB) has emerged as a directional and tunable noncovalent interaction, yet the presence of multiple σ-holes on trivalent pnictogen centers introduces an unresolved question: can individual σ-holes be selectively addressed for binding, and do their relative reactivities remain unchanged upon sequential binding? This work demonstrates that nonsymmetric Sb(III) catecholate hosts exhibit intrinsic selectivity among σ-holes that is strongly dependent on the identity of the directly bonded substituents. Structural studies with polydentate guests reveal distinct and reproducible supramolecular isomers with chloro-substituted hosts favoring a mixed σO/σCl pnictogen bonding motif while phenylsubstituted hosts favor σO/σO. Density functional theory calculations reproduce these preferences but show that the electrostatic potential maxima of the isolated host fail to predict the observed selectivity. Instead, initial binding at the site with the highest electrostatic potential leads to a redistribution of electron density that reshapes the remaining σ-hole landscape, leading, in the case of the chloro-substituted hosts, to an inversion in the relative strengths of the remaining σ-holes, consistent with asymmetric negative cooperativity. These findings establish that σ-hole reactivity in pnictogen bonding systems is not static, but evolves in response to guest binding, providing a framework for the design of selectively addressable and potentially adaptive supramolecular hosts.

papers.title: Phantoms for Nanoscale Characterization of Laser-Pigment Interactions Challenge the Fragmentation Paradigm in Tattoo Removal
papers.abstract: The global rise in tattooing practices and laser-based removal has highlighted the need for a deeper mechanistic understanding of pigment clearance. To date, tattoo removal performed using Nd:YAG picosecond lasers has been predominantly interpreted as a photothermal fragmentation process, based largely on macroscopic and histological observations. However, nanoscale characterization of pigment transformations remains limited. The study introduces a minimal and versatile platform for the nanometric investigation of laser–pigment interactions, enabling systematic analysis under controlled conditions. Two widely used tattoo pigments were selected as model systems: carbon black (CB), clinically recognized as highly responsive to laser treatment, and titanium dioxide (TiO2), known for its resistance to removal. Pristine and laser-irradiated samples were characterized using transmission electron microscopy (TEM, HR-TEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Contrary to the prevailing fragmentation paradigm, CB laser exposure induces aggregate coalescence, accompanied by expansion and partial graphitization of the primary structural units. In contrast, TiO2 exhibits negligible morphological or structural modifications upon irradiation, confirming its poor laser responsiveness. These findings challenge the conventional photothermolysis-based interpretation of tattoo removal and underscore the importance of nanoscale analyses to elucidate underlying mechanisms and its health effect.

papers.title: Layer-by-layer assembly of CPO-27-Ni as a surface mounted metal-organic framework
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks mounted on surfaces (SURMOFs) are important in various devices, and their preparation is in demand. To this end, we report the first layer-by-layer deposition of CPO-27-Ni on gold and alumina coated dies. An ethanol:water mixture, and base (DABCO) added to the linker solution, were key to successful assembly. Controlled growth up to 40 cycles was demonstrated for CPO-27-Ni@Au. When grown on a structured Au surface, CPO-27-Ni@Au showed surface enhanced Raman effects. Angular crystals up to a few hundred nm were prepared at 50 °C, and smoother films were prepared at 30 °C than at 50 °C.
