The results show that protocols reported for bulk CPO-27-Ni synthesis are not necessarily suitable for SURMOF assembly. The layer-by-layer deposition sequences were enabled using a modified, low-cost 3D printer.

papers.title: Light-Driven Bioconjugation of Organometallic Compounds via Aryl Azide Photochemistry
papers.abstract: Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) represent a clinically established modality for targeted cancer therapy. Many bioconjugation strategies have been developed to create ADCs, utilizing biocompatible chemical reactions for specific antibody modification, maintaining their biological functions. A systematic gap persists in the availability of bioconjugation reactions specifically tailored to enable the covalent attachment of organometallic payloads, thereby constraining the translation of this class of promising drug candidates into the ADC drug-delivery paradigm. Here, we report a general photochemical platform for the generation of photoactivatable organometallic bioconjugates, enabling the mild and straightforward covalent attachment of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)–stabilised complexes of various metals (Ru, Cu, Au and Pd) to proteins and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). By harnessing aryl azide photochemistry, we achieved chemospecific lysine side chain modifications in aqueous conditions while preserving antibody bioactivity. Preliminary tests with human serum albumin (HSA) gave tunable drug-to-protein ratios (DPR), high photoconjugation yields and extended stability under physiologically relevant conditions. Applying these methods to trastuzumab produced antibody–organometallic conjugates with controlled metal loading, minimal aggregation, and preserved antigen-binding activity. In vitro biological evaluations revealed that protein conjugation can enhance the cytotoxicity of the parent complexes, with low micromolar IC50 values for gastric and ovarian cancer cell lines.

papers.title: De Novo Design of Enantioselective Artificial Metalloenzyme Photocatalysts Containing Metal Polypyridine Cofactors
papers.abstract: The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins. In this study, we show that generative protein design can be harnessed to create de novo scaffolds that selectively accommodate one enantiomer of a metal polypyridine photocatalyst as a cofactor. The resulting ArMs enable efficient, enantioselective photocatalysis, highlighting a broadly applicable route for programming stereocontrol into metalloenzyme catalysts. High total turnover numbers are achieved, the ArMs can be recycled by simply extracting reaction products and reusing the aqueous ArM solution for subsequent reactions, and even commercially available racemic cofactor can be used for ArM formation. Transient Absorption characterization revealed that improvements to catalysis result from the increased quantum yield and excited state lifetime of the cofactor upon binding and substrate binding proximal to the cofactor within the ArM active site, which controls reaction stereoselectivity and the mechanism of energy transfer involved in photocatalysis. The simplicity of this approach could help transition ArM research out of a small group of specialist labs to any capable of expressing synthetic genes and working with commercially available metal complexes.

papers.title: How 3-O-Glucosylation Modulates Resveratrol Radical Scavenging: A QM-ORSA Study of Polydatin/Piceid, a Stilbenoid Glucoside
papers.abstract: The antioxidant properties of polydatin/piceid (3-O-β-D-glucopyranosyl-resveratrol), a stilbenoid polyphenol widely found in Vitaceae, Liliaceae, and Leguminosae plants and used in traditional medicine, have been investigated against the •OOH radical by means of a density functional theory-based QM-ORSA protocol. Hydrogen Atom Transfer, Single Electron Transfer, and Radical Adduct Formation mechanisms were considered in both aqueous solution at physiological pH and in a lipid-like environment. Conformational analysis confirms that the trans isomer is preferred over the cis form by 4.9 kcal⋅mol-1, and species distribution calculations show that the neutral form dominates at pH 7.4 (98.6%). The results show that 3-O-glucosylation attenuates the aqueous •OOH-scavenging rate relative to trans-resveratrol, mainly by removing one phenolic H-donor from the aglycone framework, but it preserves a competitive HAT route through the remaining C4” hydroxyl. The comparison is therefore medium-dependent: polydatin reacts faster than Trolox in the modeled lipid-like phase, whereas in water its apparent rate constant remains below trans-resveratrol and Trolox under the same protocol.

papers.title: From Atoms to Swarms: The Categorical Spine of Multiscale Materials Modeling and Autonomous Discovery
papers.abstract: Many biological materials and material systems-silk, collagen, bone, spider webs and many others-achieve strength, toughness, adaptability, or resilience by organizing weak interactions and limited molecular alphabets hierarchically. In these systems, function often lives in the organization rather than in the components. Working with such materials computationally cannot mean computing at a single scale. It must mean moving information between scales without destroying what matters. Here we review research that has focused on attempts to identify, formalize, and now operationalize the invariants that survive those handoffs across scales, systems and modalities. The difficulty is structural: the invariants rarely coincide with the most visible features. A spider web is not robust because each silk fiber is intrinsically strong, and bone is not tough because mineral platelets are themselves tough; the function emerges from how nonlinear response, hierarchy, and topology compose. Identifying the compositional invariant-and not any single ingredient-is the modeling problem. This Account traces an arc that begins with reactive molecular dynamics of dynamic fracture, the hierarchical mechanics of collagen and silk, and the mechanism-level coupling between molecules, fibrils, and spider webs. It then moves into machine-learning surrogates, generative inverse design, materiomusic, neurosymbolic reasoning, and finally agentic discovery and plannerless scientific swarms. All these can be read as structure-preserving maps between typed objects, and category theory provides a disciplined vocabulary for stating what each map preserves and what it does not. This is a vocabulary, not a source of theorems, and that distinction matters. Its value is operational as it forces us to declare which types survive a coarse-graining step, which symmetries a learned surrogate respects, and where each diagram fails to commute. In a field where modern AI methods readily produce fluent answers without grounding, that discipline is not optional but must be a disciplined component. The claim put forth here is that the durable product of materials discovery is shifting from isolated artifacts to generative algorithms. A protein, composite microstructure, alloy, field predictor, graph, or piece of materiomusic remains a useful output, but the more transferable result is the loop that produced it: an alphabet of primitives, a grammar of composition, a neural generator, symbolic constraints, a verifier, provenance, and an update rule. When such a system can also revise its own grammar and verifier under physical constraints, the discovery loop becomes self-referential. The deepest claim is therefore that future materials discovery will not be organized primarily around one protein, one composite, one alloy, one melody, or one graph, but around self-revising generative algorithms that can compose, test, falsify, and update scientific worlds while remaining tied to physical evidence. The arc of this paper - from physics-grounded simulation through surrogates, generative design, neurosymbolic reasoning, and swarms - is then best read as a single object viewed at progressively higher levels of self-reference.

papers.title: Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks, Molecular Fingerprints, and Their Fusion for Toxicity Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of molecular toxicity is essential for drug discovery and chemical safety assessment. While molecular fingerprints have long been the dominant representation in quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, graph neural networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as powerful alternatives that learn task-specific features directly from molecular graphs. However, a systematic comparison between graph-based representations, traditional fingerprints, and their combination for toxicity prediction remains limited. In this study, we benchmark multiple GNN architectures and fingerprint-based models across diverse toxicity endpoints, including binary classification and regression tasks. In addition, we investigate hybrid fusion strategies that integrate graph embeddings with fingerprint descriptors. Results show that graph and fingerprint representations provide complementary information, while hybrid models exhibit improved performance on several endpoints, though results are inconsistent across all tasks. Our findings provide practical guidance for representation selection in toxicity modeling and establish a reproducible benchmark framework for future research.

papers.title: Accelerated Screening of Cellulose Additives
papers.abstract: Regenerated cellulose films are promising renewable alternatives to conventional plastics that can be further engineered by controlling plasticization. The quantitative effects of different additives are however poorly understood, making it difficult to choose which compounds to use to engineer a given film property. Here, we address this problem by developing an accelerated screening procedure to model the molecular features of cellulose additives and to predict their efficacy for film modification. Our approach builds on projecting relevant molecular features onto a lower-dimensional latent space to capture systematic feature correlations. This projection provides a key advantage by spanning the chemical variation in the candidates in just a few dimensions to select representative subsets for experiments. The latent dimensions are orthogonal, which makes them promising predictors of additive efficacy for film modification. We demonstrate how testing less than a third of the identified candidates enabled us to model key film properties based on the resulting latent space coordinates. Computational experiments showed that leveraging physics-based insights from molecular dynamics reduced cross-validation errors and enabled predicting film strength with a mean absolute percentage error of 28% based on previously unseen molecules. These results are an important milestone towards understanding the effects of additives on cellulose properties and to harness physics-informed surrogates and high-performance computing for biopolymer modification. Our approach can be fitted to optimize discrete chemical modifications across a wide range of material design problems.

papers.title: Principles and practical measurement and control strategies for achieving ultrahigh CO2 capture rates in amine post-combustion capture plants
papers.abstract: Amine post-combustion capture (PCC) plants must maximise CO2 capture rates to support net-zero targets. This study presents a practical control strategy for achieving up to ~100% added CO2 capture (i.e. the exit CO2 is equivalent to the CO2 in the combustion air), with moderate energy inputs of 3.55-3.65 GJ/tCO2 comparable to 95% capture operation. The method, which efficiently minimises desorber lean loading while closely regulating lean solvent flow to the absorber, is illustrated using process modelling and validated by data from a 75-hour continuous period of ~100% capture in pilot testing at 30 tCO2/day scale. Implementation required only minimal operator training and standard plant instrumentation alongside a flue gas analyser suitable for the resulting ~ 500 ppmv exit CO2 levels. The control approach appears highly transferrable to all commercial amine capture facilities. This paper provides actionable insights for plant design, particularly key instrumentation provisions, and supports permitting guidelines for regulators.

papers.title: Redefining Product Selectivity: A new catalytic approach for the N-formylation of N,N-dimethylaniline derivatives using bio-inspired manganese catalysts
papers.abstract: N-formylated amines represent an important class of synthetic building blocks for several bioactive and complex molecules. Reported herein is an efficient catalytic route using an electron-rich linear tetradentate aminopyridine manganese (II) complex to synthesize N-formylated amines. Our system, composed of Mn(dMMbpbp)/H₂O₂/2-ethylhexanoic acid in acetonitrile, preferentially delivers N-formylation over N-demethylation of N,N-dimethylanilines, in contrast to the typical selectivity reported for tridentate and pentadentate iron and manganese complexes. Kinetic studies indicate that the reaction proceeds through a stepwise pathway, in which the N-demethylation product forms earlier during catalysis than the N-formylation product. We propose that the observed N-formylation selectivity arises from a combination of the use of an electron-rich manganese complex and electronic substrate effects. Overall, our catalytic system accomplishes the highest yield of N-formylated product for electron-rich substrates with a distinct product selectivity so far reported for bio-mimetic C–H oxidation reactions.

papers.title: An Iridium Catalyst Switches the Regioselectivity of Michael Addition Reactions
papers.abstract: The Michael reaction is a cornerstone transformation in organic synthesis. Its regioselectivity is governed by electronic control, and this enforces C–C bond formation exclusively at the βposition of electron-poor alkenes. Here, we report an iridium-catalyzed approach that instead enables unprecedented α-selective “anti-Michael” C(sp3)–H additions to acrylates and other conjugate acceptors. Our strategy is predicated on the use of directing groups to promote the formation of chelated Ir-(aza)-enolates, which engage conjugate acceptors in an inner-sphere carbometallation event. In this process, steric factors override conventional electronic preferences, leading to α-selective C–C bond formations. The method accommodates a broad range of pronucleophiles, including α-amino amides, α-hydroxy ketones, 2-aza-aryl alcohols, and even classical Michael-type 1,3-dicarbonyls, often delivering products with high levels of regio-, diastereo-, and enantiocontrol. Synthetic utility is demonstrated through cascade anti-Michael–lactamization reactions and concise syntheses of complex α-amino acids. Collectively, our studies establish a general and mechanistically enabling solution for achieving α-selective C(sp3)–H additions to conjugate acceptors. This opens new opportunities for regioselective alkene functionalization beyond the classical Michael paradigm.

papers.title: Environmental Impact of Synthetic Cell Technology: Review of Life-Cycle Assessment Data for Feedstocks and Production Methods
papers.abstract: Bottom-up synthetic cells are frequently framed as enabling technologies for a future green bioeconomy, yet their environmental impacts remain poorly quantified. Here, we review and synthesize available life-cycle assessment (LCA) data for the feedstocks, production routes, and assembly methods commonly used in synthetic-cell research, focusing on cradle-to-gate system boundaries. We consider lipids from plant and algal sources, amphiphilic diblock copolymers, recombinant proteins, crude and PURE cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) systems, and key assembly approaches including bulk emulsification and microfluidics. We argue that many of the identified components may also play a role in future generations of synthetic cells that undergo primitive autonomous growth and cell cycles. The data illustrate how design choices in compartment composition, encapsulated biochemistry, and assembly efficiency can shift impacts by orders of magnitude. Early integration of LCA-informed design, such as favoring lower purity where functionally acceptable, using shared feedstocks, reducing material excess, and employing alternative autotrophic or solvent-free production routes, will be decisive for achieving environmentally viable synthetic-cell technologies.

papers.title: Stress-modulated ionic transport limits composite cathode kinetics in solid-state batteries
papers.abstract: High-energy all-solid-state batteries require thick composite cathodes, yet these architectures exhibit heterogeneous reaction distributions that limit performance. Here, we show that chemo-mechanical transport switching governs the spatiotemporal lithiation behaviour in such electrodes. By combining operando depth-resolved diffraction with microstructureresolved and multi-scale simulations, we link utilisation gradients to the dominant transport pathway and demonstrate that the reversal of reaction fronts between charge and discharge arises from dynamically evolving transport limitations. This switching originates from the coupled reconfiguration of electronic and ionic transport networks during cycling. Particle breathing and interfacial delamination disrupt electronic percolation, while stress-field interactions within the solid electrolyte introduce a mechanics-dependent limitation on ionic transport. This stress-limited ionic conduction, governed by the activation volume and elastic properties of the electrolyte, can reduce effective conductivity by orders of magnitude as cathode interparticle spacing decreases and stress fields begin to overlap at high activematerial loadings. Our findings establish a direct link between chemo-mechanical evolution and transport control in solid-state cathodes, and highlight the need for solid electrolytes with low pressure sensitivity and sufficient mechanical compliance to enable high-energy all-solid-state battery architectures.

papers.title: Reproducible electrochemical synthesis, purification, and functionalization of carbon quantum dots for Cu2+ sensing
papers.abstract: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are fluorescent nanomaterials with broad applications in sensing and imaging. A representative procedure yielding functional CQDs for Cu²⁺ detection has been previously reported (Zhu et al., 2022). Here, we describe an experimental workflow to validate this method and examine conditions that may affect reproducibility, including electrochemical synthesis, chromatographic purification, and surface functionalization. The procedure highlights the influence of electrochemical reaction time and post-synthesis processing on CQD surface states, dispersion, and fluorescence properties. Ligand functionalization enables selective fluorescence quenching upon Cu²⁺ binding. Consistent execution of the procedure is required to obtain reproducible results. This workflow provides a practical approach for preparing CQDs with reliable fluorescence response for Cu²⁺ sensing.

papers.title: Restricting Chain Mobility in Semicrystalline Polyethylene and Polypropylene via Dynamic Covalent Cross-links: Major Effects on Elevated-Temperature Creep, Heat Distortion Temperature, and Wear Resistance
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that dynamic covalent cross-links restrict chain mobility and suppress molecular relaxation in semicrystalline polyethylene (PE) and isostatic polypropylene (PP) covalent adaptable networks (CANs) produced by one-step, radical-based reactive processing. This is evidenced by increased resistance of the amorphous domains to solvent swelling and diminished temperature-dependent interfacial relaxation. These molecular-level constraints have major effects on elevated-temperature creep resistance, heat distortion temperature (HDT), and wear performance. Creep behavior was evaluated under relatively high loads across a range of temperatures. At lower temperatures, CAN formation reduces creep resistance due to decreased crystallinity. In contrast, substantial improvements are observed at temperatures approaching but below the melt transition. At 110 °C for PE and 140 °C for PP, creep strain in CANs is reduced by 88% and 61%, respectively, relative to the precursor polymers. Furthermore, dynamic covalent cross-links increase the service temperature of CANs, with HDT improvements of 16 °C in PE CANs and 11 °C in PP CANs. In wear testing, PE CANs exhibit markedly improved resistance, with wear volume reduced by over one-third compared to neat PE. In contrast, PP CANs show decreased wear resistance, with increased wear volume attributed to 2 low-molecular-weight polymer generated via β-scission during radical-based reactive processing. Overall, we show that dynamic covalent cross-linking can sustainably enhance key engineering properties of semicrystalline polyolefins under targeted service conditions.

papers.title: Flash Joule Heating Driven Engineering of Vanadium Oxide Graphene Hybrid Structures for High Performance Zinc Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries are attractive for safe and low-cost energy storage, but their cathode performance is often limited by sluggish Zn2+ transport, poor electronic conductivity and irreversible structural distortion. Here, we demonstrate a voltage-regulated flash Joule heating strategy that converts commercial V2O5 into kinetically favorable mixed-phase vanadium oxide cathodes within seconds. During the ultrafast electrical pulse, carbon black simultaneously acts as a Joule-heating medium, conductive scaffold and reductive agent, enabling rapid oxygen extraction and voltage-dependent reconstruction of the V2O5 lattice. By tuning the discharge voltage, the reduction degree and phase composition can be precisely modulated: insufficient voltage preserves poorly activated V2O5, whereas excessive voltage causes over-reduction and structural degradation. The optimized FV2O5-140 cathode achieves a balanced V2O5/V2O3 heterophase structure, where mixed-valence vanadium sites, defect-rich local environments and an interconnected porous carbon network synergistically accelerate charge transfer, enhance electrolyte penetration and shorten Zn2+ diffusion pathways. Consequently, FV2O5-140 delivers a reversible capacity of 404 mAh g-1 at 0.2 A g-1, retains 263 mAh g-1 at 5 A g-1, and maintains 172 mAh g-1 after 1000 cycles at 5 A g-1. Electrochemical kinetic analysis reveals dominant pseudocapacitive Zn2+ storage, with capacitive contributions increasing from 79% to 89% as the scan rate increases from 0.2 to 1.0 mV s-1, together with Zn2+ diffusion coefficients of 10-10–10-12 cm2 s-1. Ex situ XRD, SEM/EDS and EIS further confirm reversible Zn2+ insertion/extraction, preserved electrode morphology and reduced charge-transfer resistance after activation. This work establishes flash-voltage-controlled phase reconstruction as an effective route to couple structural regulation with electrochemical kinetics, providing a scalable strategy for upgrading low-cost commercial oxides into high-performance multivalent-ion battery cathodes.

papers.title: DFT-based grand canonical study of the stability of crystalline battery materials under operating conditions
papers.abstract: High-throughput computational studies can significantly aid in the identification of crystalline battery materials with improved properties. Here we present a density functional theory-based numerical study addressing the stability of crystalline materials for chloride ion batteries under operating conditions using a grand canonical approach. Cl ion batteries have emerged at the science stage as a potential energy storage technology promising enhanced energy density based on safe and environmentally benign chemistries. Although significant progress has been achieved in this field recently, the discovery of potential materials is only in its infancy. In the present work, we computationally address the materials class of chloride perovskites for the development of new chloride ion battery materials. 18782 intercalation configurations for each of a total of 205 different compounds are evaluated employing a state-of-the-art machine learning interatomic potential and periodic density functional theory calculations. For the analysis, a particular focus is put on the comprehensive investigation with grand canonical diagrams. As this method inclusively covers the thermodynamic relations between the pristine compounds, its intercalation configurations, and potential conversion products under varying electrochemical conditions, we believe this approach is of great aid in the theoretical description and identification of potential materials. Our investigation resulted in the proposal of 23 solid electrolyte materials for further investigation. Six compounds exhibit reversible Cl intercalation/deintercalation, i.e. they are in principle suitable as cathode materials, however, the reversible cycling should only be possible in a rather narrow potential window.

papers.title: Flash Joule Heating Driven Engineering of Vanadium Oxide Graphene Hybrid Structures for High Performance Zinc Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries are attractive for safe and low-cost energy storage, but their cathode performance is often limited by sluggish Zn2+ transport, poor electronic conductivity and irreversible structural distortion. Here, we demonstrate a voltage-regulated flash Joule heating strategy that converts commercial V2O5 into kinetically favorable mixed-phase vanadium oxide cathodes within seconds. The optimized FV2O5-140 cathode achieves a balanced V2O5/V2O3 heterophase structure, where mixed-valence vanadium sites, defect-rich local environments and an interconnected porous carbon network synergistically accelerate charge transfer, enhance electrolyte penetration and shorten Zn2+ diffusion pathways. papers.title: High-Tg Polythioesters from Isomerization Ring-Opening Polymerization of a Renewable Oxanorbornane-Fused Thionolactone
papers.abstract: Polythioesters are gaining increasing interest due to their attractive material properties and improved end-oflife options. However, the lower ring strain of thiolactones compared to lactones limits the accessibility of polythioesters through conventional ring-opening polymerization (ROP). Thionolactone isomerization ROP (IROP) has emerged as a promising alternative, providing an additional thermodynamic driving force through (C=S)–O to (C=O)–S isomerization, enabling polymer synthesis from more readily available monomers. Nevertheless, reported polythioesters typically exhibit low glasstransition temperatures (Tg), and the impact of sulfur substitution on the polymerization characteristics and the material properties remains poorly understood. Here, we report a biobased tricyclic thionolactone (TCTn) that readily undergoes selective IROP to yield high molecular weight P(TCT) (ca. 100 kg mol-1). P(TCT) exhibits one of the highest Tg values reported to date for polythioesters (167 °C), exceeding that of the analogous polyester (130 °C). P(TCT) can be efficiently depolymerized to the (unstrained) tricyclic thiolactone (TCT) via ring closure through backbiting depolymerization. Unexpectedly, depolymerization of P(TCT) under basic conditions through hydrolysis is ten times slower than the polyester analogue. Methanolysis takes place at rates comparable to the polyester, and it is shown that methanolysis rates depend especially on polymer end-groups and the backbiting mechanisms, rather than intrinsic differences between activation barriers, which is supported by DFT calculations. Overall, we provide insights into the rational design of sustainable, high-performance sulfur-containing polymers and into the intricacies of O→S substitution and expand the space of high-Tg norbornane-fused polymers.

papers.title: Photo-Physics of Halogenated-benzylidene-hydrazineyl-4-trifluoromethylthiazole combined Experimental and Computational study
papers.abstract: This study investigates the photophysical properties of halogenated benzylidene hydrazineyl–4-trifluoromethyl thiazole derivatives using combined experimental and computational methods. Structures were confirmed by NMR, IR, and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). Variation of halogen substituents (Cl, Br, I) enabled evaluation of substituent effects on electronic structure and excited-state behavior. Absorption and fluorescence measurements in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) revealed efficient intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), driven by the electron-withdrawing trifluoromethyl group and conjugated hydrazone bridge. The 4bromo-2-hydroxy substituted derivative (3b) additionally shows features consistent with excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT). Computational analysis supported these findings by elucidating frontier orbitals and charge distribution. Notably, despite the presence of heavy atoms and calculated spin-orbit coupled states, no significant population transfer to the triplet manifold was observed neither experimentally nor in simulations. These results demonstrate that how halogenation and electron-withdrawing substitution are effective strategies for tuning the excited-state dynamics of thiazole-based chromophores.

papers.title: ChemAgent: A Multi-Agent Attention Framework with Linear Distilled Encoding for Molecular Property Prediction and Chemical Reaction Optimization
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction and chemical reaction optimization are critical for accelerating drug discovery and materials design, yet existing approaches face significant challenges in capturing long-range dependencies, dynamically adapting to molecular characteristics, integrating multi-modal chemical data, and modeling temporal variations in chemical processes. We propose ChemAgent, a unified multi-agent attention framework that addresses these limitations through four synergistic innovations. First, a Linear Attention Molecular Encoder (LAME) employs distilled attention with rotary position encoding restoration to capture long-range chemical bond dependencies with linear computational complexity. Second, a Multi-Agent Collaboration Module comprising three specialized agents for structure, semantics, and property prediction is coordinated by a dynamic selector that adaptively weights agent contributions based on input molecular characteristics. Third, a Time-Adaptive Weighting strategy combines content-based attention with exponential temporal decay to handle time-varying chemical process data. Fourth, a Hierarchical Ensemble Module fuses multi-granularity molecular representations at the atom, substructure, and molecule levels through cross-level attention. Comprehensive experiments on MoleculeNet benchmarks demonstrate that ChemAgent achieves state-of-the-art AUC scores of 0.819 on HIV, 0.867 on ESOL, 0.918 on BBBP, and 0.831 on Tox21 for molecular property prediction. On the Open Reaction Database, ChemAgent attains an R-squared of 0.867 with an RMSE of 9.15 for chemical reaction yield prediction. Extensive ablation studies confirm that each proposed component contributes meaningfully to the overall performance, and human evaluation demonstrates superior interpretability of the model predictions.

papers.title: Competing Substrate and Free-Surface Effects on Ion Transport in Ultrathin Polymer Electrolyte Films
papers.abstract: Ceramic nanoparticles incorporated into solid polymer electrolytes have been reported to both enhance and suppress ionic conductivity, but the mechanistic origins of these effects remain unclear due to difficulties in isolating interfacial phenomena in disordered bulk systems. Here, we characterize ion transport in ultrathin films of polyethylene oxide–lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide on silica and employ analytical modeling to elucidate how interfaces control thickness-dependent behavior. Ionic conductivity is mostly suppressed with decreasing film thickness at all salt concentrations and temperatures, and the extent of this suppression varies with concentration alone. A modified Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann model incorporating both substrate and free-interface effects on polymer dynamics best captures the observed behavior, outperforming simpler models based on non-conducting layers, ion aggregation, or substrate-only interface effects. This demonstrates how both inorganic surfaces and free interfaces substantially influence polymer mobility and conductivity, suggesting that strategies to optimize composite polymer electrolytes should address the coupled behavior of interfacial polymer dynamics.

papers.title: Strain-Driven Rh(I)-Catalyzed Assembly of 3-Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2-one Scaffolds
papers.abstract: The 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2one moiety represents a scaffold of therapeutic interest found in pharmaceutical and agrochemical agents and serves as a valuable precursor to the 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane framework via lactam reduction. The latter motif is also featured in a range of therapeutics, including antiviral and antidepressant agents, as well as treatments for rare genetic disorders. Herein, we report a rhodium(I)-catalyzed rearrangement of bicyclo[1.1.0]butane (BCB) amides for the synthesis of 3azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2-one derivatives. This transformation exploits the ring strain of the BCB core, enabling bridgehead C–C bond cleavage followed by cycloisomerization. A series of 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2-one derivatives bearing N-aryl, N-benzyl, and N-alkyl substituents were synthesized. The synthetic utility of these derivatives is demonstrated through further functionalization, including reduction to the corresponding 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane scaffold. A plausible mechanistic pathway for the rhodium(I)-catalyzed cycloisomerization of the BCB amide is proposed, involving the formation of a rhodium carbenoid intermediate.

papers.title: Condenophilicity of Supramolecular Polymers Governs Organelle Formation in Fueled Synthetic Cells
papers.abstract: Synthetic cells are compartments designed to mimic the functions and characteristics of living cells. By constructing synthetic cells from abiotic, basic components (bottom-up), it is possible to investigate the minimal requirements for life and gain insights into fundamental principles of biology. Among the available platforms, complex coacervates are particularly attractive, due to their potential to encapsulate a wide range of biomolecules and other cargo, enabling genotype-phenotype mapping. By coupling coacervate formation to a fueled chemical reaction cycle, the synthetic cells become fuel-dependent, growing in the presence of fuel and decaying in its absence, resembling biological cells. However, constructing organelles for these transient synthetic cells, such as membranes and cytoskeletons, has remained an unresolved challenge. Here, we show that supramolecular (co-)polymers can act as organelles for the synthetic cells, depending on their condenophilicity (their affinity for the droplet phase). By using two distinct supramolecular building blocks, the condenophilicity can be modulated. Supramolecular copolymers where only some of the monomers bind to the complex coacervate result in the formation of a membrane structure around the droplet. However, as condenophilicity increases, the polymers partition strongly into the coacervates, leading to the formation of a cytoskeleton. Moreover, we found that these organelles influence the synthetic cell properties, such as morphology and their lifespan. Our results demonstrate that orthogonally assembled structures can serve as organelles for active complex coacervate-based synthetic cells, broadening the existing arsenal of tools to bestow these rudimentary synthetic cells with more life-like properties.

papers.title: A high-throughput experimentation platform for hydroxide electrodeposition and electrochemical evaluation of electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: We report a high-throughput screening system for hydroxide electrocatalysts that integrates hydroxide electrodeposition-based synthesis and electrochemical evaluation. The system combines standardization of the synthesis-and-evaluation workflow through electrodeposition, miniaturization using screen-printed electrodes and a 96-well microplate format, and parallelization through a home-built 32-channel potentiostat system. Reproducibility tests showed good agreement among channels under identical conditions and further demonstrated that condition-dependent performance differences could be stably captured even when different electrodeposition potentials and deposition times were independently assigned to different channels. As a demonstration, 96 conditions defined by the Ni/Fe ratio, supporting electrolyte fraction, electrodeposition potential, and deposition time were screened for Ni–Fe hydroxide electrocatalysts toward the oxygen evolution reaction. Heat-map and decision-tree analyses revealed that the Ni/Fe ratio is the primary factor governing OER overpotential in the Ni–Fe hydroxide system studied here, whereas process factors further differentiate performance within a given compositional region. These results show that, although composition-centered highthroughput screening is effective, incorporation of process conditions is also important for identifying high-performance conditions. The present system provides a practical platform for high-throughput electrocatalyst discovery in a coupled space of composition and process conditions.

papers.title: When Counterions Fall into Place: Alkali Effects on f-Element Phosphomolybdate Crystallization and Speciation
papers.abstract: Effects controlling the speciation and crystallization of f-elements with polyoxomolybdate (POMo) ligands have been scarcely studied compared to the analogous tungstate POMs. Here we investigate polyoxomolybdate complexes with trivalent lanthanides (Ln 3+ ), in solution and solid-state, shedding lights on the complex interplay between the f-elements, POM ligand, and counterions. Alkali counterions play a decisive role in shaping the structure and behavior of POM complexes, including the lanthanide-POMo complexes reported here. A family of Ln(PMo 11 O 39 ) 2 11- compounds with charge-balancing K + and Cs + were synthesized across the lanthanide series, and 16 total structures were characterized by SCXRD, FTIR, and SEM-EDX. Combined solid-state and solution-phase studies enabled direct comparison of structural trends and countercation-dependent solution-state speciation. While potassium analogues exhibit consistent parallel arrangement of POM units in the crystalline lattice, cesium derivatives adopt distinct packing modes, including both parallel and perpendicular orientations. These structural differences are reflected in variations in lattice organization and inter-cluster interactions, highlighting the role of larger alkali cations in directing long-range assembly. Moreover, solution-state 31 P Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) reveal that the countercation (Li + , Na + , K + , Rb + and Cs + studied) directly impacts assembly and thermodynamic equilibria among PMo 11 O 39 7- , Ln(PMo 11 O 39 ) 4- and Ln(PMo 11 O 39 ) 2 11- , prior to crystallization.

papers.title: Thrombin-responsive minimal peptide coacervates for thrombolytic delivery
papers.abstract: Peptide coacervates formed through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) are emerging as promising delivery vehicles because they combine structural simplicity with dynamic cargo sequestration and release. However, integrating biologically relevant triggers into minimal peptide coacervates remains challenging. Here we report thrombin-responsive peptide coacervates based on a short sticker-spacer-sticker design, in which the thrombin-cleavable motif LVPR↓GS is encoded directly into the phase-separating sequence. These peptides form coacervate microdroplets that efficiently sequester protein cargo and rapidly disassemble upon thrombin-mediated cleavage, thereby enabling controlled release of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA). Sequence optimization further reveals that terminal incorporation of an RGD motif enhances LLPS propensity, increases coacervate dynamics and improves partitioning of both tPA and thrombin, resulting in more efficient clot-associated thrombolytic delivery. Finally, incorporation of Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles converts these coacervates into magnetically steerable microrobotic carriers that retain thrombin responsiveness while gaining enhanced stability and directional control. Together, these results establish a minimal peptide coacervate platform for enzyme-activated and magnetically guided thrombolytic delivery, and provide a strategy for engineering functional therapeutic protocells from short designer peptides.

papers.title: A Calibration-Free Quantitative Analysis of Immiscible Binary Polymer Blends: The Crystallinity-Set Filtering (CSF) Method Applied to DSC Data
papers.abstract: The transition toward a circular economy has intensified the need for efficient recycling of polymeric waste. However, quantifying cross-contamination in post-consumer recyclates (PCR) remains challenging for calibration-based approaches due to the variability and limited availability of pristine reference materials. In this study, a novel calibration-free mathematical approach, here termed crystallinity-set filtering (CSF), is proposed for the quantitative analysis of fully immiscible bicomponent semicrystalline polymer blends. This method was applied on differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) data and exploits physically meaningful boundary conditions associated with polymer crystallinity ranges. The CSF approach was validated using high-density polyethylene/polypropylene (HDPE/PP) blends covering the full composition range. The method was directly compared with the conventional calibration-based least squares method (LSM) applied to melting enthalpy data. The results demonstrate that the CSF method outperforms the LSM approach, achieving a minimum mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.70% and R 2 values up to 0.9957, compared to an MAE of 2.61% and an R 2 of 0.9932 obtained with LSM. The proposed method exhibits performance metrics comparable to those reported in the literature for established quantitative techniques. The analysis further shows that CSF accuracy improves as the assumed crystallinity intervals are narrowed, highlighting the importance of realistic constraints derived from literature data or prior experimental knowledge. The reduced accuracy observed near equimolar compositions was attributed to both the widening of the feasible crystallinity set and increased peak overlap in the DSC melting region. Overall, the CSF method represents a robust calibration-free alternative for the quantitative analysis of semicrystalline polymer blends. The log file and the Python code developed in this study are available on GitHub. We believe this approach is particularly promising for assessing thermoplastic polymer cross-contamination in PCR materials where calibration-based strategies are limited, and establishes a new analytical framework that broadens the scope of quantitative polymer blend analysis.

papers.title: Advances in microfluidic devices for hemodialysis: Current Trends and Future Perspective
papers.abstract: End stage kidney disease and patients of chronic kidney disease are one of the most common health conditions across the globe. Dialysis is the only treatment prescribed for the patients waiting for kidney transplant. Current dialysis technologies are bulkier compared to wearable devices and cause mobility issues for patients during long dialysis sessions. Microfluidic based sensors and hemodialyzers have been devised as potential replacement for conventional dialysis setup. This review article summarises the recent trends in microfluidic devices and how these can contribute to a total dialysis solution. First, introduction provides the overview of conventional dialysis with the context to the significance of the development of the technologies in the perspective of human health. Microfluidic sensors developed for detection of biomarkers in saliva, urine and blood for the detection of CKD and AKI. Microfluidic devices for dialysis utilising membranes, hydrogels, sorbent materials. Overview and current trends in wearable devices for hemodialysis. Lastly, Future trends in microfluidic device technologies for hemodialysis in achieving total integrated microfluidic based system for monitoring and separation of metabolites. The challenges and opportunities for the improvement in current technologies.

papers.title: Reversing the 3d6 Relaxation Paradigm: Ultrafast Quintet Decay and Triplet Trapping in the Strong-Field [Co(terpy)2]3+ Complex
papers.abstract: The deactivation mechanism of photoexcited [Co(terpy) 2 ] 3+ (terpy = 2,2':6',2''-terpyridine) in acetonitrile is investigated using transient absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. Ultrafast measurements reveal the formation of a quintet metal-centred ( 5 MC) state, which decays with a time constant of 170 fs via 5 MC → 3 MC intersystem crossing (ISC). Subsequent vibrational cooling occurs on a 5.7 ps timescale, followed by a long-lived 3 MC excited state with a lifetime of 3.4 ns. In contrast to Fe(II) polypyridines, where early-time relaxation proceeds via 3 MC states despite similar accessibility of the quintet manifold in the Franck–Condon (FC) region, [Co(terpy) 2 ] 3+ exhibits direct population of the 5 MC state, thereby reversing the early-time relaxation pathway. Furthermore, the persistence of a nanosecond-lived 3 MC state is unexpected given the strong spin–orbit coupling of Co(III), which would typically enable efficient triplet–singlet relaxation on the picosecond timescale, as observed in Fe(II) analogues. Instead, relaxation is governed by a dynamical bottleneck arising from unfavorable 3 MC → ground-state energetics. These results demonstrate that ultrafast population pathways in 3d 6 complexes are not dictated solely by ligand-field strength or spin–orbit coupling, but by nonequilibrium dynamical factors that can invert established relaxation pathways.

papers.title: Conformational landscapes resolved by ion mobility mass spectrometry reveal mechanisms of polyubiquitin-controlled phase separation
papers.abstract: Polyubiquitin chains regulate phase separation of the ubiquitin-binding shuttle protein ubiquilin-2 (UBQLN2) in a manner that depends on the position of the isopeptide linkage and the length of the polyubiquitin chain. However, conformational heterogeneity of the non-covalent complexes formed between these proteins has rendered the molecular mechanisms underlying this regulation elusive. Here, we have used ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS) to disentangle conformational features of the non-covalent complexes formed by UBQLN2 with different polyubiquitin chains. We demonstrate that the length of the polyubiquitin chain binding to UBQLN2 has a large effect on the conformational distribution of the complex, with increasing chain lengths (up to four ubiquitin subunits) allowing access to more extended conformations of the complex, and shorter chains promoting compaction. This provides the first evidence for differential mechanisms of phase separation regulation by ubiquitin chains of different lengths. We also compare polyubiquitin chains linked by lysine residue (K)48 and by K63, both alone and in complex with UBQLN2. By understanding how K48- and K63-linked tetraubiquitin chains behave in the gas phase, which differs to solution, we propose distinct molecular mechanisms for their regulation of UBQLN2 phase separation. This work, enabled by the unique ability of IM-MS to resolve conformational features of highly heterogeneous biomolecular systems, represents a conceptual breakthrough in understanding polyubiquitin-controlled phase separation mechanisms.

papers.title: Iridium-Catalyzed Regio- and Enantioselective Hydroamination of Allenes furnishing α-Tertiary Chiral Allylic Amines
papers.abstract: We disclose a highly regio- and enantioselective Ir(I)-catalyzed hydroamination of 1,1-disubstituted allenes, providing a broadly applicable access to α-tertiary chiral allylic amines, structural motifs that are mostly inaccessible through other enantioselective strategies. The method employs an a-aminopyridine as nucleophile, and displays a broad substrate scope, accommodating both aryl- and alkyl-substituted allenes. Removal of the pyridine group enables access to primary allylic amines bearing α-tetrasubstituted stereocenters. Notably, addition of i-PrOH after completion of the hydroamination enables an in situ transfer hydrogenation of the generated alkene to deliver the corresponding a-tertiary saturated amines with equally high selectivities. The use of trisubstituted allenes in the hydroamination protocol is also feasible, affording in this case a-secondary allylic amines with high selectivities. Finally, experimental and computational mechanistic studies allow to propose a hydrometalation/C–N bond-forming sequence as the preferred reaction pathway, with the C-N reductive elimination step identified as enantio- and TOF-determining.

papers.title: Cumulative Spectroscopic Detection for Taylor Dispersion Analysis of Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Taylor Dispersion Analysis (TDA) provides a robust approach for determining the hydrodynamic diameter of molecular objects and nanoparticles (NPs), measuring diffusion of the analyte in laminar flow through a long capillary. TDA measurements are usually performed on capillary electrophoresis equipment with in-line absorbance detection. Here, we introduce a simple, yet versatile cumulative spectroscopic detection (CSD) technique for TDA, that precisely samples the radially averaged analyte concentration flowing out of the TDA capillary. CSD can be employed in different optical spectroscopic configurations, such as absorbance, fluorescence or resonant light scattering. A theoretical model of the measurement was formulated that combines Taylor's original expression with an extended injection and then accounts for the accumulation of the analyte in the detection cell. The model was validated by comparing the hydrodynamic radii of various nanoparticle samples measured by TDA-CSD to those obtained by dynamic differential microscopy and dynamic light scattering. Beyond TDA, CSD may be useful for accurate sampling of analyte peaks in other flow-based analysis techniques, such as liquid chromatography.

papers.title: Performance-Based Evolution of Near-Infrared Serotonin Nanosensors from DNA-Wrapped Carbon Nanotube Libraries
papers.abstract: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5HT) is an important neurotransmitter involved in the regulation of mood, appetite, and sleep, and its dysregulation has been associated with disorders such as depression and Parkinson’s disease. Selective molecular tools that can distinguish 5HT from neurochemicals, are essential for advancing both neurochemistry and disease-related research. However, conventional analytical methods are labor-intensive and sometimes suffer from poor discrimination among closely related neurotransmitters. In this study, we developed near-infrared fluorescence 5HT nanosensor based on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA)-wrapped single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) using a performance-based systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment of carbon nanotube (pSELEC) strategy. Unlike conventional affinity-focused selection, this approach prioritized fluorescence modulation as the screening output and combined high-throughput microarray printing, automated fluorescence imaging to evaluate more than 10 6 ssDNA-SWCNT configurations. After characterizing the enriched DNA 2 candidates, Seq6 was selected as finalist scaffold and underwent post-selection engineering such as covalent modification with quencher dye and co-wrapping with dummy DNA. A methylene blue-conjugated Seq6 produced an “turn-off” fluorescence response to 5HT together with an opposite-direction response to dopamine, providing improved discrimination between the two analytes. These results demonstrate that pSELEC is a useful strategy for developing sensitive and selective near-Infrared nanosensors for real-time neurotransmitter sensing.

papers.title: Bottlebrush architecture suppresses crystallization to enable soft, stretchable solid-state polymer electrolyte for lithium-metal batteries
papers.abstract: High-performance solid-state electrolytes are essential for safe, high-energy-density lithium batteries, yet achieving high ionic conductivity and mechanical resilience at room temperature remains challenging. Polyethylene glycol (PEG)–based electrolytes show promise but crystallize below ~42 °C, which suppresses segmental dynamics and ion transport. Here we show that bottlebrush architecture suppresses crystallization in high-molecular-weight PEG, enabling solvent-free polymer electrolytes that combine high conductivity, softness, and stretchability. Bottlebrush polymer electrolytes exhibit smooth temperature-dependent conductivity and achieve room-temperature conductivities more than two orders of magnitude higher than linear PEG systems. The Li+ transport number increases by nearly 20% relative to that of linear PEG–salt electrolytes. Covalently crosslinked bottlebrush networks retain ionic mobility while providing exceptional mechanical robustness, including stable conductivity under compression, extensibility up to 500% strain, and negligible hysteresis over hundreds of mechanical loading-unloading cycles. The bottlebrush PEG electrolyte supports stable lithium-metal battery operation, delivering high Coulombic efficiency (>99.5%) in LiǁNMC811 cells and long-term (>800 hours), lowoverpotential (100 mV) lithium plating–stripping in symmetric LiǁLi cells. These results establish bottlebrush PEG as a versatile platform for deformable, high-performance, and stable solid polymer electrolytes.

papers.title: Organic lithium battery operates efficiently up to 150 °C
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) underpin much of modern technology. However, the performance of traditional cathodes, such as nickel/cobalt oxides or lithium iron phosphate, rapidly fades or even leads to catastrophic failure as the operating temperature rises above 60-65 °C. Here, we report that LIB cells made from TAQ, a recently discovered small-molecule organic cathode, exhibit 15 stable cycling, maintain rapid charge-discharge rates, and deliver higher energy density than traditional inorganic cathodes while operating continuously at temperatures up to 150 °C. We demonstrate that this unusual behavior is enabled by a unique combination of resonance-assisted hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions that lead to chemical stability, facile charge transfer, and fast Li+ transport across a wide temperature range.

papers.title: Molecular Knowledge Representations in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Molecules are quantum-mechanical objects whose complete and exact description is computationally intractable. Even if tractable, the uncertainty of the composition of a material or a mixture forces us to have incomplete representations of the system. The central challenge in modern chemical research is therefore not simply encoding molecular structure, but doing so in ways that are simultaneously useful to machines and interpretable by humans. In this review, we organize the landscape of representations of molecules and their related knowledge through the lens of topology. We distinguish among discrete representations, which can be decomposed into enumerable symbolic units; continuous representations, typically expressed as real-valued vectors that enable gradient-based optimization; and hybrid representations, which combine elements of both paradigms. Beyond molecular structure itself, we extend this perspective to the representation of chemical knowledge: rule-based expert systems that encode chemical understanding as explicit symbolic rules; neural networks that compress knowledge into real-valued parameters; and LLM-based agents that bridge the two by operating over discrete text while orchestrating continuous computational tools. For each family, we examine how knowledge is encoded and transformed, and how the resulting systems facilitate human insight. We argue that LLM-based agents represent a qualitative shift, enabling systems that can reason over chemical language, generate and execute code, and coordinate domain-specific tools. Understanding the strengths and limitations of different representations of our molecular knowledge is essential for building the next generation of interpretable, generalizable, and actionable molecular intelligence.

papers.title: Environment-Tolerant Blinking Fluorophores for Correlative Nanoscopy
papers.abstract: Conventional fluorophores display strongly environment-dependent fluorescence properties, which limits their performance under the oxidizing, high-density and complex interfacial conditions characteristic of advanced imaging experiments. We show that rylene dyes can function as environment-tolerant blinking fluorophores whose intermittency arises from reversible photoinduced charge transfer between the chromophore and ubiquitous environmental acceptors such as oxygen, rather than from specialized buffer chemistries. We then demonstrate that the apparent fluorescence loss under OsO 4 staining arises mainly from static quenching and inner‑filter effects, not from irreversible chemical degradation, and we account for this by a unified model combining distance‑dependent photoinduced electron transfer/FRET with absorption by reduced osmium species. This mechanistic picture explains why rylene emitters remain functional after standard OsO 4 staining and epoxy resin embedding, and yields design rules for fluorophores that retain blinking in such extreme environments. Leveraging this understanding, we label these dyes to biomolecular targets and demonstrate the first dual-color super‑resolution correlative light and electron microscopy on the same section. By integrating mechanistic insight with performance in a stringent application, this work establishes a rational framework for designing next-generation probes for advanced correlative nanoscopy.

papers.title: Membrane Permeability Assay for Cyclic Peptides across a Broad Chemical Space Using DNA-Encoded Libraries
papers.abstract: To establish design principles for membrane-permeable cyclic peptides and thereby enable drug discovery targeting intracellular proteins, it is essential to develop technologies capable of generating large-scale structure–permeability datasets across broad chemical space. However, conventional mass spectrometry-based sequence identification methods for cyclic peptides suffer from low identification rates due to the complexity of fragment analysis and have difficulty distinguishing stereoisomers. These limitations have posed a significant barrier to acquiring large-scale membrane permeability data across broad chemical space. In this study, we addressed these challenges by employing DNA-encoded library (DEL) technology, thereby establishing a platform for evaluating the membrane permeability of cyclic peptides across broad chemical space. We constructed a hexamer cyclic peptide library with a theoretical diversity of 10,240 members and evaluated the membrane permeability of approximately 100 peptides using the parallel artificial membrane permeability assay (PAMPA). Whereas a conventional MS/MS-based method yielded a sequence assignment rate of less than 10% and low data acquisition efficiency, our approach achieved a high sequence assignment rate of approximately 90% and a data acquisition efficiency of approximately 80%. Furthermore, the accuracy of sequence assignment reached 100% in the validated set, enabling the acquisition of highly reliable data compared with conventional approaches. These results demonstrate that our method provides a powerful and high-throughput platform for reliably evaluating the membrane permeability of cyclic peptide libraries across broad chemical space.

papers.title: Iodinated Heptamethine Cyanines for Antimicrobial Photodynamic Therapy: Structure–Activity Relationships, Photostability, and Mechanistic Insights
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (APDT) is a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics due to its broad-spectrum efficacy and low resistance propensity; however, efficient near-infrared (NIR) photosensitizers remain limited. Here, a series of sulfonated and non-sulfonated heptamethine cyanine dyes bearing two, four, or six iodine substituents was synthesized to elucidate structure–activity relationships governing photophysical properties, photostability, and antimicrobial efficacy. Iodine substitution markedly boosts singlet oxygen generation via enhanced spin–orbit coupling, while excessive iodination compromises photostability. Tetraiodinated dyes achieve an optimal balance enabling efficient photoinactivation of S. aureus (≥ 3 log10 reduction at 10 µM, 10–100 J/cm2), whereas higher doses were required for E. coli. Most dyes show low cytotoxicity toward HaCaT keratinocytes and no detectable mutagenicity. Computational studies link iodine incorporation with both accelerated intersystem crossing and access to dissociative excited states responsible for C–I bond cleavage. These findings complement the design principles for NIRactivated cyanine photosensitizers for APDT.

papers.title: Influence of additives on long-term degradation and microplastic formation of polyethylene
papers.abstract: There are limited studies showing how additive contents used for packaging plastics affect polymer degradation and microplastic formation. Hence, we used accelerated abiotic weathering for studying the mechanisms leading to the degradation of additivated, semi-crystalline low-density polyethylene (LDPE). For this purpose, LDPE plates with different, realistic concentrations of additives (antioxidants and UV stabilizers) were weathered in an accelerated weathering chamber and analyzed using SEM, DSC, high temperature GPC and solid-state 13C CP MAS NMR spectroscopy. Our results reveal that non-UV-stabilized LDPE degrades rapidly, showing extensive microcracking, molecular weight reduction, and formation of polar polymer defects within 600 hours. The addition of hindered amine light stabilizers (HALS) significantly delays these effects, yet their performance varies depending on the specific formulation. While Tinuvin 622 protects the polymer for about 2500 hours before sudden degradation and cracking occurs, Tinuvin 783 effectively prevents severe chain scission and large crack formation over the sampled 4000 hours of exposure. However, even with Tinuvin 783, fine surface microcracks still develop and cause the detachment of small microplastic particles. Ultimately, the most important finding is that even small amounts of additives have strong effects dictating not only the degradation kinetics but also the shape and chemical composition of the secondary microplastic particles formed by fragmentation.

papers.title: Boron Cluster Oriented Superhydrophobic Surfaces
papers.abstract: Hydrophobic coatings are critical for applications spanning anti-fouling and selfcleaning technologies. Conventional fluorinated materials rely on complex fabrication methods and often lack mechanical robustness and scalability. Here, we report a new class of solution-processable fluorinated coatings based on atomically precise closo-dodecaborate clusters densely functionalized with fluorinated carbon chains. Our approach to fabricating these boron oriented superhydrophobic surfaces (BOSS) coatings is based on flexible chemical design, allowing for tailored functionalization and easy scalability. This molecular design enables unprecedented chain packing density, yielding coating with surface free energy around 13 mJ/m2 and excellent water repellency. The coatings exhibit thermally triggered, controllable degradation, along with electrochemical activity, fire retardancy, and mechanical durability when applied to common substrates, providing a viable alternative to conventional fluoropolymer systems. Our findings establish three-dimensional boron cluster as effective scaffold for high-density functional group incorporation, enabling the design of robust, next-generation advanced coatings.

papers.title: Mechanism Reduction and Validation of Ammonia/Hydrogen/Air Combustion Leveraging First-Principles-Derived Kinetics
papers.abstract: This work presents a reduced mechanism for NH3/H2/air combustion derived directly from a high-fidelity, firstprinciples-based parent model [1] without empirical modification of kinetic or thermochemical parameters. Starting from a 53-species detailed mechanism, an iterative reduction strategy was used to obtain a 23-species reduced mechanism while preserving the parent chemistry. The reduced mechanism was assessed against a broad validation suite including ignition delay times, laminar burning velocities, jet-stirred reactor species profiles, plug flow reactor species evolution, extinction strain rates, and turbulent computational fluid dynamics (CFD) fidelity tests. Across the canonical validation configurations, the reduced mechanism’s results closely matched those of the detailed parent mechanism, indicating that the dominant ignition, flame-propagation, intermediate-species, and NOxformation pathways are preserved. Relative to representative reduced mechanisms in the literature, the present mechanism provided consistently balanced performance over pure NH3 and NH3/H2 conditions, while avoiding the empirical retuning commonly used in compact ammonia-fuel chemistry. In a CFD simulation of a turbulent partially premixed NH3/H2/N2-air jet flame, the reduced mechanism reproduced the detailed-mechanism predictions of temperature, NH, and NO with negligible visible loss of fidelity while reducing computational cost by approximately a factor of five. The resulting mechanism provides a physically grounded, CFD-practical chemistry model for predictive simulations of ammonia/hydrogen combustion across wide ranges of conditions.

papers.title: Plant-Wide Modeling and Techno-Economic Analysis of Concentrated Acid Hydrolysis for Platform Sugar Production from Lignocellulosic Biomass
papers.abstract: Platform C5 and C6 sugars derived from lignocellulosic biomass are key intermediates for a wide range of bio-based chemicals and fuels. This study presents an integrated framework combining reaction kinetic modeling, parameter estimation, plant-wide process simulation, and technoeconomic analysis for producing C5 and C6 sugars from biomass via concentrated acid hydrolysis (CAH). A species-resolved kinetic model for mixed-acid catalyzed hydrolysis is developed, with parameters estimated using dynamic optimization based on transient experimental data. A scalable commercial scale reactor configuration is also developed and integrated into a plant-wide process model that includes CAH of holocellulose, sugar separation, acid catalyst recovery through highboiling solvent extraction, and acid reconcentration for recycle. A comprehensive techno-economic analysis is conducted to evaluate economic performance of alternative process configurations using the levelized cost of sugar production (LCSP) as the primary metric, and identify economically favorable conditions for sugar production. Results show that acid recovery is the dominant factor influencing process economics, significantly reducing chemical consumption and production cost, while additional heat integration further decreases the overall production expenditures. The proposed integrated configuration provides a minimum LCSP of $197.3/MT, thereby establishing CAH with acid recovery and heat integration as a promising route for sustainable production of platform chemicals and biomass valorization.

papers.title: Weathering of microplastic creates nanometre-sized surface-near cavities – A 129Xe NMR spectroscopic study
papers.abstract: Microplastic particles (MP) undergo structural transformations during weathering that directly influence their ability to adsorb and transport contaminants. Conventional surface-analytical techniques such as atomic force microscopy, scanning electron microscopy and gas adsorption provide useful information on external morphology and total surface area but are inherently limited when absolute surface areas are small and structural changes are dominated by small cavity sizes. While microscopy primarily reveales larger surface defects, smaller cavities remain unresolved and cannot explain the modest surface increase observed by physisorption measurements. To access these environments, hyperpolarized 129 Xe NMR spectroscopy is established as a sensitive, benefiting from a signal enhancement of up to five orders of magnitude non-destructive tool to probe surface-near cavities, enabling resolution of cavities smaller than 50 nm. Reference materials with well-defined pore sizes were used to calibrate xenon chemical shifts based on the Terskikh model, providing a framework for size-dependent interpretation. Application of this approach to artificially weathered polystyrene particles reveals the formation of surface near micro and meso porosities to small to detect with AFM or SEM, that contribute largely to total surface area. These results demonstrate that weathering generates confined adsorption environments inaccessible to classical techniques and highlight the relevance of microporosity as preferential sites for the adsorption and retention of potentially toxic inorganic and organic compounds, thereby contributing to the role of microplastics as vectors for their transport in environmental systems.

papers.title: Novel method for the synthesis of polyimines
papers.abstract: Polyimines are promising and sustainable materials. Their high thermal stability, self-healing ability, simple recycling and opportunity to build conjugated polymers based on imine bonds attracted significant attention to these materials in recent years. Here, we propose a novel approach to polyimines starting from nitrobenzaldehydes. The approach allows to synthesize AB-type polymers, which gains a powerful tool in the design of polyimines.

papers.title: ACE inhibitor metabolites as muscarinic receptor antagonists: a candidate pharmacological mechanism for the epidemiological reduction of colorectal cancer risk?
papers.abstract: Background and Purpose: Long-term ACE inhibitor use is associated with a ~25% reduction in colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence, but no pharmacological mechanism has been established. We investigated whether the active diacid metabolites of ACE inhibitors possess previously unreported muscarinic receptor activity that could link drug exposure to CRC risk reduction. Experimental Approach: Systematic analysis of the EvE Bio quantitative pharmacological profiling dataset (1,397 FDA-approved compounds, 208 targets, FRET-based β-arrestin 2 recruitment assays) identified muscarinic activity for ACE inhibitor metabolites where pure antagonism was confirmed by dual-mode (antagonist/agonist) assay. Molecular docking against M4 (PDB: 5DSG, chain A)[8] and M2 (PDB: 3UON)[9] crystal structures was performed, with interaction fingerprint analysis for additional ACE inhibitor metabolites. Key Results:Benazeprilat is the highest-affinity M4 antagonist among 134 quantified compounds in the dataset (pXC50 = 10.70, apparent IC50 ≈ 20 pM), exceeding all approved M4 antagonists, and a potent M2 antagonist (pXC50 = 9.20). Quinaprilat is a selective M2 antagonist (pXC50 = 8.70, apparent IC50 ≈ 2 nM). Both activities are absent from all major pharmacological databases. Pure M4 antagonism is confirmed (agonist mode: 2% maximal activity). All seven ACE inhibitor class compounds are inactive at M3. Docking confirms orthosteric accommodation via a non-classical anionic pharmacophore that does not engage the conserved Asp105 salt bridge. Conclusions and Implications:Metabolites of widely used ACE inhibitors are potent M4 and M2 antagonists, with a non-classical pharmacophore. Free benazeprilat at therapeutic trough concentrations predicts >95% M4 receptor occupancy, consistent with robust tonic antagonism at a Gi/o-coupled receptor without M1/M3-mediated anticholinergic cross reactive toxicity. These findings provide a candidate pharmacological mechanism for the epidemiological CRC risk reduction.

papers.title: Core/Shell HgCdTe/HgCdSe Quantum Dots for Wavefunction Engineering with Infrared Band Gaps
papers.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are a class of nanomaterials with tunable electronic structure that enables precise control of light-matter interactions for diverse optoelectronic applications. Mercury cadmium chalcogenides are an emerging QD composition for infrared photonic applications, and their heterostructures are expected to diversify functionality. Here, we introduce core/shell HgCdTe/HgCdSe QDs with bandgap energies in the infrared and charge carrier wavefunctions tunable by domain dimensions and the radial distribution of mercury and cadmium. As prepared via mercury cation exchange of core/shell CdTe/CdSe QDs, mercury can be selectively concentrated in either the core or shell, and can fully deplete cadmium to generate HgTe/HgSe QDs. Different alloying regimes shift band offsets between type-I and type-II alignments, in which electrons and holes are colocalized or separated, respectively. Broad bandgap tunability across the infrared spectra with long-term stability in air addresses problems of the constituent QD homostructures of HgTe and HgCdTe with low chemical stability and HgSe and HgCdSe with n-type doping. The photophysical features and oscillator strengths are reported as key figures of merit and compared with quantum mechanical simulations. An optical metrology method based on ultraviolet E 1 critical point features is also developed for determining cation distributions, which is otherwise difficult in small core/shell QDs. These high-quality infrared QDs with controlled charge carrier wavefunctions and overlap may be beneficial for engineering photoluminescence efficiency and optoelectronic device performance in the infrared spectrum.

papers.title: Late-Stage Synthesis of Photoaffinity Labeling Probes
papers.abstract: Photoaffinity labeling is an integral technique in drug development for identifying the biological targets of drug-like molecules. An essential step in this process is the design and synthesis of photocrosslinking probe molecules that contain the key biologically active warhead of the parent molecule, a photo-activatable functional group, and a biorthogonal handle. These components collectively allow for the covalent linkage of the drug to its target and subsequent isolation of the drug-protein conjugate. Current strategies to synthesize probes from their parent molecules rely on previously installed functional groups or a redesigned synthesis. Here, we report the late-stage synthesis of photoaffinity labeling probes using photochemical Minisci chemistry, where we can convert a variety of medicinally relevant aromatic N-heterocycles to their corresponding photocrosslinking probes in a single step. Furthermore, employing our method, we synthesized photoaffinity labeling probe analogs of pioglitazone, a known peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonist. We performed photocrosslinking and pull-down experiments to validate the target of pioglitazone, showcasing the utility of this method.

papers.title: Closing the gap on a $0 budget: ensembling public molecular foundation models for HIV bioactivity prediction
papers.abstract: On the MoleculeNet HIV scaffold-split benchmark, my fine-tuned MolFormer-XL component achieves a per-fold test ROC-AUC of 0.806 ± 0.018 (5-fold mean ± std), statistically tied with Uni-Mol’s 3D-conformer-pretrained result of 0.808 ± 0.003 (Zhou et al., 2023). Combining MolFormer-XL with a from-scratch GATv2-based graph neural network through an out-of-fold logistic stacker yields an out-of-fold ensemble ROC-AUC of 0.865 (95% bootstrap CI [0.850, 0.879], n = 24,391), with a paired-bootstrap p = 0.0015 vs. MolFormer-alone, confirming a small but statistically real ensemble gain. The full pipeline is reproducible end-to-end on freetier Google Colab and consumer Apple Silicon at zero dollars of downstream compute cost, while Uni-Mol’s pretraining required ~160 V100-GPU-hours (≈ $500–$2K of cloud compute) on a 19M-molecule, 209M-conformer corpus. My contribution is methodological: I show that for binary molecular property prediction, principled ensembling of publicly-available pretrained checkpoints, combined with honest scaffold-based evaluation and threshold calibration, matches the SOTA 3D-pretrained model on HIV at zero downstream compute cost—without 3D conformers, without bespoke pretraining, and without GPU-cluster access. Keywords: molecular property prediction, graph neural networks, MolFormer, ensemble learning, scaffold splits, low-resource ML, MoleculeNet HIV.

papers.title: Drugging the KRAS-G12V Lipid Vulnerability: Prenyl-Coumarins As Lead Scaffolds Against ELOVL6
papers.abstract: Background:Elongation of very long-chain fatty acids protein 6 (ELOVL6) is the rate-limiting C16→C18 fatty-acid elongase in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and a recently identified metabolic vulnerability in KRAS-G12V-driven cancers. Despite 132 ChEMBL bioactivities across the elongase family, no ELOVL6-directed inhibitor has reached the clinic, and structure-based design has been hampered by the absence of an experimental human ELOVL6 structure. Approach:We performed a three-stage AutoDock Vina virtual screen against an AlphaFold2 model of human ELOVL6 (UniProt Q9H5J4; AFDB entry AF-Q9H5J4-F1; whole-model pLDDT 92.3, active-site pLDDT 97.0). Stage 1 docked a 1,538-compound library combining FooDB (n = 900), curated ChEMBL ELOVL6 (n = 106) and SCD1 (n = 93) bioactives, FASN/ACC1 landmark inhibitors (n = 7), and four positive controls. Stage 2 expanded the most promising scaffolds by COCONUT natural-product similarity search (n = 152, Tanimoto ≥ 0.35). Stage 3 expanded by PubChem 3D similarity search (n = 213). Internal validation rested on (i) prospective enrichment of ELOVL6 ChEMBL actives (ROC AUC 0.854, EF 1% = 4.8×, EF 5% = 4.5×, BEDROC α=20: 0.44), (ii) pocket-specificity against unrelated FASN/ACC1 landmarks, (iii) per-compound cross-docking of the 13 highest-ranked hits against SCD1 (the closest paralogue), and (iv) an empirically-derived ±1.4 kcal/mol noise floor for cross-compound score comparisons. Results:Three Apiaceae-family prenyl-coumarins: Khelmarin D (−10.38 kcal/mol), Conferone (−10.31 kcal/mol), and Farnesiferol A (−10.30 kcal/mol), emerged as the strongest non-frequent-hitter chemotype. FASN/ACC1 reference inhibitors scored 3.5 kcal/mol weaker than ELOVL6 actives, confirming pocket specificity. The hero pose was robust to a 3.2× exhaustiveness increase (Δ = −0.03 kcal/mol).
