Naturalproduct expansion via COCONUT recovered the best-scoring compound of the entire campaign (analogue #1, −11.24 kcal/mol, Tanimoto 0.557 to Khelmarin D). All 13 top hits were novel against ChEMBL exactmatch of ELOVL6 and SCD1 active sets. Per-compound cross-docking against SCD1 showed unanimous (13/13) ELOVL6 preference with a median ΔΔG of +5.46 kcal/mol, well outside the ±1.4 kcal/mol noise floor. Limitations. The work is computational. Vina scores are not equilibrium binding affinities. The receptor is an AlphaFold2 model lacking the lipid-bilayer environment, and the positive-control pose-recovery RMSD gate was waived in the absence of a co-crystal structure. Spirostanol-class top-rankers are computationally over-scored and explicitly de-prioritised to supplementary data. Conclusion: The Apiaceae prenyl-coumarin chemotype is prioritised as a candidate starting point for ELOVL6 inhibitor development, with explicit cellular fatty-acid elongation and SCD1 cross-reactivity follow-up named.

papers.title: Scaffold-Aware Evaluation Reveals Substantial Performance Inflation in EGFR pIC50 Benchmarks: A Reproducible Analysis on ChEMBL v33
papers.abstract: Background. Quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modelling underpins computational drug discovery. Published benchmarks on ChEMBL data routinely report R2 = 0.70–0.86 for pIC50 prediction, but the validity of these figures under chemically realistic evaluation conditions—where models must generalize to novel scaffolds—has not been systematically quantified. Methods. We curated 10,113 EGFR (CHEMBL203) inhibitors from ChEMBL v33 with deduplication, validity filtering, and Bemis–Murcko scaffold splitting (80/10/10). Three gradient boosting models (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) were evaluated under a four-level Leakage Ladder: (L1) random K-Fold; (L2) multiseed out-of-fold (3 seeds × 5 folds); (L3) scaffold split single model; (L4) nine-predictor ensemble on scaffold test set. Performance was assessed using R2, RMSE, MAE, Concordance Index (CI), and Enrichment Factor at top 5% (EF@5%). Results. Standard K-Fold evaluation yields mean R2 = 0.679, while scaffold-honest evaluation on identical models yields R2 = 0.352—a +93% relative inflation attributable entirely to evaluation methodology (15 independent runs, σ < 0.002). Multi-seed OOF retains substantial inflation (R2 ≈ 0.70). However, the scaffold-honest ensemble achieves CI = 0.728 and EF@5% = 7.78×, exceeding the practical utility threshold (CI > 0.7) and demonstrating that ranking capability transfers across scaffold classes substantially better than absolute regression performance. Conclusions. Standard QSAR benchmarks systematically overestimate model performance on novel chemical space. We recommend that scaffold-aware evaluation and ranking-based metrics (CI, EF) become standard reporting practice. All data, splits, and code are publicly released to facilitate community adoption.

papers.title: Accurate density functional theory forces for charged noncovalent complexes
papers.abstract: Force accuracy is essential for training machine-learned force fields based on density functional theory (DFT) data and for reliably modeling noncovalent interactions (NCIs). Despite this importance and the sensitivity of forces to the underlying density functional approximation, a gap remains in benchmarking DFT force accuracy for NCIs. Here, we assess the force performance of dispersion-enhanced DFT against CCSD(T) references for representative charged NCI dimers. While conventional dispersion-enhanced DFAs exhibit substantial force errors for charged systems, the recently proposed integratively designed (r2SCAN+MBD)@HF systematically reduces these errors [Science Advances 2026, 12, eadz8521]. The improvements in force accuracy of (r2SCAN+MBD)@HF over other DFT approaches are most pronounced for strongly charged dimers, extend to vibrational frequencies, and propagate to improved vibrational spectra from machine-learned force field–based molecular dynamics simulations. Overall, this work establishes (r2SCAN+MBD)@HF as a robust reference level for training machine-learned force fields on both forces and energies in complex ionic environments.

papers.title: SitepKa: Site-Specific Acid and Base pKa Prediction Across Multiple Industrial Solvents
papers.abstract: The propensity of a molecule to donate or accept a proton fundamentally governs its reactivity, solubility, and biological activity across diverse chemical environments; however, accurately predicting the site and extent of protonation or deprotonation at scale remains an unresolved challenge. Existing deep-learning models are largely either limited to predicting pKa values only in aqueous media or unable to resolve site-specific pKa variations. Here we introduce SitepKa, a graph neural network that predicts sitespecific pKa values across water and 34 industrial organic solvents. The model identifies ionisable atoms, classifies each as acidic or basic, and produces site-level estimates through a dual-graph cross-attention architecture that explicitly models solute–solvent interactions, supplemented by Kamlet–Taft solvent descriptors. Trained on 33,269 experimental measurements from ten public sources, SitepKa achieves competitive accuracy on aqueous blind-challenge benchmarks (MAE 1.49–2.30 on SAMPL6–8) and transfers effectively to non-aqueous solvents including DMF and pyridine (MAE 0.87–0.99), a regime where deep-learning tools are largely absent. The model generalises to structurally complex macrolides and glycopeptides well outside its training size range without retraining, and correctly withholds prediction for non-ionisable atoms. These results establish that site-level, multi-solvent pKa prediction is achievable within a single workflow, with broad applicability across chemical and materials sciences, including pharmaceutical design, reaction development, and electrolyte engineering.

papers.title: Spatially Defined Patterning of Diverse Polymers on Triangular DNA Origami
papers.abstract: Biological systems derive structural precision and functional robustness from the spatial organization of distinct molecular interactions within defined nanoscale architectures. Translating this level of control to synthetic systems remains challenging, particularly when structurally diverse polymers must be positioned with defined location and loading. Here, we report a DNA-origami-based platform for the site-selective patterning of polymers bearing different interaction motifs through DNA conjugation and subsequent hybridization to triangular DNA origami (TDO). Using this approach, hydrophilic, hydrophobic, and cationic polymer–DNA conjugates were synthesized by click chemistry and purified by anion exchange chromatography, enabling the preparation of DNA–polymer hybrids across a broader range of polymer properties. On the basis of this TDO–polymer hybrid platform, we established an atomic force microscopybased statistical workflow to assess polymer incorporation on origami templates. Comparative analysis across the polymer series indicates that hybridization efficiency is strongly influenced by the interplay of polymer solubility and steric demand after surface confinement on the origami scaffold. These results establish TDO-directed polymer patterning as a versatile platform for studying and engineering DNApolymer hybrid nanostructures with controlled nanoscale organization.

papers.title: Design and Synthesis of Metabolically stable Tricyclic-SpiroLactams inhibitors of Mycobacterium tuberculosis type-II NADH dehydrogenase: Structure–Activity and Structure–Property Relationship Studies
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), is a critical global health challenge, as treatment efficacy is increasingly undermined by a high incidence of drug-resistant cases. Consequently, it is critical that novel antibiotics against Mtb are developed. Tricyclic spirolactam (TriSLa)-based inhibitors of mycobacterial type II NADH dehydrogenases (Ndh and NdhA) are a promising and novel class of anti-mycobacterial antibiotics that are efficacious in a zebrafish larvae model of M. marinum infection. However, the relatively low metabolic stability of the original TriSLa inhibitors prevented their evaluation in a murine model of Mtb infection. Here we report an extensive structure−activity relationship (SAR) and structure-property relationship (SPR) study of the TriSLa scaffold, leading to the discovery BDM91465 (compound 45), a potent and metabolically stable analog. The cryo-EM structure of BDM91465 bound to Ndh reveals the precise binding pocket of TriSLas and is consistent with the SAR. The tricyclic spirolactam core binds within the menaquinone pocket, with the distal aromatic rings embedded in the protein-micelle interface. Pharmacokinetic studies conducted on BDM91465 confirmed its bioavailability and low clearance, which together equated to extensive exposure above the antibioitic MIC. In vivo efficacy studies of BDM91465 found it to attenuate the growth of Mtb in mice, in line with results generated by the genetic inactivation of Ndh-2. Together this work provides a first example of the in vivo efficacy of an Ndh-2 inhibitor in a murine model of Mtb infection, confiming the proteins in vivo vulnerability and drugability and paving the way for the development of new anti-TB regimens.

papers.title: Humidity-enhanced chemoresistive sensor performance in a p-type spinel metal oxide
papers.abstract: Humidity strongly reduces the sensitivity of most chemoresistive-type gas sensor, restricting their applicability in environmental monitoring, health diagnostics and robotic olfaction. Intense research efforts have tried to enhance humidity resistance by, for instance, reducing the adsorption of hydroxyl species on chemoresistors through surface functionalization, compositional or structural optimization, and heterojunction formation. Here, we demonstrate that humidity-related hydroxyl species can also increase sensing performance by improving molecular reception and catalytic oxidation of analytes. On the example of p-type spinel ZnMn2O4, we observed a ~60% increase in response to parts-per-billion level acetone concentration under humidity compared to dry conditions. By integrating X-ray absorption spectroscopy, in situ IR spectroscopy, and isotopically labeled chemisorption analysis, we demonstrate that surface-adsorbed hydroxyl groups play an active role in analyte oxidation. Notably, oxidation product formation rates were up to an order of magnitude higher under humid conditions compared to dry conditions. These findings advocate a more differentiated discussion of the role of humidity in chemoresistive gas sensors, as surface engineering may not only aim to mitigate its effects but can leverage it to overcome present frontiers in sensitivity and detection limit.

papers.title: Triflation as a General Strategy to Convert Electron-Rich Phenolic Macrocycles into CH-bonding Anion Receptors and Transporters
papers.abstract: CH-bonding anion receptors are a class of supramolecular hosts that combine high chemical robustness, reduced propensity for deprotonation, and distinctive selectivity patterns, making them attractive for transmembrane transport and medicinal applications. Their broader use is, however, limited by the scarcity of scaffolds capable of forming strong CH···anion interactions. Here, we present a general and operationally simple “supramolecular umpolung” strategy that converts π-electron-rich oligophenolic macrocycles into CH-bonding anion receptors and transporters via esterification of their OH groups. Resorcinarenes and pyrogallolarenes were transformed into acetyl (–OAc), triflate (–OTf), and pentafluorobenzenesulfonate (–OPFB) esters. The –OTf and –OPFB derivatives show high anion binding affinities across diverse media, while –OTf derivatives act as excellent anion transporters in lipid bilayers, outperforming benchmark tetranitroresorcinarene 1b. The most active transporter, pyrogallolarene 5b, combines high chloride affinity (Ka ≥ 107 M-1 in THF), outstanding Cl-/NO3- antiport activity (EC50,270s = 0.0017 mol%), and negligible protonophoric activity. Electrostatic surface potential and molecular lipophilicity potential analyses show that highly positive ESP at the CH-binding site and a uniformly lipophilic external surface are crucial for effectiveness. Overall, per-triflated oligophenolic macrocycles give CH-bonding receptors approaching the performance of the best NH-based systems while maintaining excellent Cl- > OH- selectivity, thus overcoming a key limitation of conventional hydrogen-bonding anionophores.

papers.title: Chemical Space Blind Spots: How Chromatographic Selectivity Dictates Chemical Measurability and Coverage of LC-HRMS comprehensive analysis
papers.abstract: Liquid chromatography high-resolution mass spectrometry enables broad chemical detection by comprehensive accurate mass to charge ratio measurement of the components in complex samples; yet analytical design constrains chemical space measurability. A meta-analysis of 236 methods and over 75,000 measured compounds reveals strong convergence toward reversed-phase separations, limiting the coverage of sample chemical diversity. This “measurability trap” narrows the observable chemical space and can lead to the underrepresentation of many environmentally and biologically relevant compounds.

papers.title: Berry-curvature-driven switchable enantioselective electrocatalysis on an achiral topological antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: Enantioselective catalysis is conventionally governed by structural chirality in real space, yet whether electronic asymmetry in momentum space alone can bias enantioselectivity remains unknown. Here we show that Berry curvature in a centrosymmetric antiferromagnet can directly control enantioselective electrocatalysis. Using the kagome metal Mn 3 Ge as a model system, we demonstrate that the electrochemical reduction of ( R )- and ( S )-10-camphorsulfonic acid (CSA) exhibits enantioselectivity that follows the Berry-curvature state, quantified via the anomalous Hall response. The enantiomer excess reverses with the sign of Berry curvature and scales with its magnitude, establishing a quantitative link between electronic topology and chemical selectivity. Notably, both the anomalous Hall signal and the enantioselective response persist after removal of the external magnetic field, indicating that the selectivity is encoded in the Berry-curvature state. Continuous tuning of enantioselectivity is achieved by rotating the magnetic field, enabling dynamic control of the underlying electronic asymmetry. These findings establish Berry curvature as a field-programmable electronic symmetry-breaking mechanism and introduce momentum-space topology as a new design principle for asymmetric catalysis.

papers.title: A Crystalline N-Heterocyclic Carbene Radical Anion
papers.abstract: Free N-heterocyclic Carbene (NHC) radical ions have remained short-lived, mostly elusive, intermediates so far. We probed the square schemes for proton-coupled electron transfers of representative redox-active free NHC. We found that NHC radical anions NHC •– and/or the conjugated acid NHC•H • could be persistent. In the case of a benzoquinone-based NHC, both radical forms were isolated as stable crystalline compounds, characterized, including with single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies, and were engaged in the straighKorward divergent syntheses of NHC-based radicals.

papers.title: A unified experimental-simulation dataset and surrogate models for surfactant property prediction
papers.abstract: Surfactants are structurally diverse molecules whose interfacial properties are central to a wide range of industrial and scientific applications, yet their systematic evaluation remains challenging due to the cost of both wet-lab experiments and molecular simulations. In this work, we construct an extended surfactant dataset, SurfPro-MD, by combining curated experimental data from the SurfPro database with four additional molecular dynamics-derived properties, including diffusion coefficients, viscosity, and interfacial surface tension. The resulting dataset provides a unified description of 1436 surfactant systems across nine physicochemical target properties spanning both experimental and simulation-based measurements. Based on this dataset, we develop a suite of machine learning surrogate models that predict surfactant properties directly from SMILES representations using RDKit-derived molecular descriptors and gradient-boosted regression models. To obtain robust estimates of predictive performance, we employ a cluster-based data splitting strategy combined with multiple independent train/validation/test partitions, enabling assessment of model generalisation across chemically distinct compounds. The resulting models exhibit property-dependent performance, with strong predictive and ranking capability for several simulation-derived and experimental targets, while more complex interfacial properties show lower regression accuracy but still retain meaningful rank correlations. A descriptor-recurrence analysis identifies a small set of molecular features—spanning electronic surface-area distribution, functional-group composition, and global polarisability—that contribute consistently across multiple target properties, with all three appearing among the most important features for diffusion-related models, suggesting partially shared structural determinants of surfactant transport behaviour. Overall, this work provides a systematically evaluated set of predictive models, the augmented SurfPro-MD dataset, and a feature-level analysis of structure–property relationships, offering a practical resource for researchers in academia and industry seeking to screen and compare candidate surfactants without the need for additional experiments or molecular simulations. All data, simulation workflows, and trained models are made publicly available to ensure reproducibility and facilitate further development.

papers.title: Strain-Driven Rh(I)-Catalyzed Assembly of 3-Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2-one Scaffolds
papers.abstract: The 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2one moiety represents a scaffold of therapeutic interest found in pharmaceutical and agrochemical agents and serves as a valuable precursor to the 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane framework via lactam reduction. The latter motif is also featured in a range of therapeutics, including antiviral and antidepressant agents, as well as treatments for rare genetic disorders. Herein, we report a rhodium(I)-catalyzed rearrangement of bicyclo[1.1.0]butane (BCB) amides for the synthesis of 3azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2-one derivatives. This transformation exploits the ring strain of the BCB core, enabling bridgehead C–C bond cleavage followed by cycloisomerization. A series of 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2-one derivatives bearing N-aryl, N-benzyl, and N-alkyl substituents were synthesized. The synthetic utility of these derivatives is demonstrated through further functionalization, including reduction to the corresponding 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane scaffold. A plausible mechanistic pathway for the rhodium(I)-catalyzed cycloisomerization of the BCB amide is proposed, involving the formation of a rhodium carbenoid intermediate.

papers.title: MOF-808 Mediated Chloride Flux Across Model Membrane Systems
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates the use of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as a new platform for mediating anion transport in bio-mimetic cell models. We employed a lucigenin fluorescence assay to monitor chloride flux in giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs) immobilized to zirconium-based framework, MOF-808. MOF-808, showed chloride transport enabled by its large pores and strong Zr - chloride affinity. In contrast, HKUST-1 despite its high porosity, showed limited chloride transport, underscoring the importance of metal node and pore topology in modulating anion flux. Collapsed MOF-808 showed no ion transport, indicating that the MOF pore integrity is essential. These findings inform us of the role of both metal interactions and pore architecture in facilitating anion transport across phospholipid membranes, providing insights for designing tailored MOFs channels with tunable ion transport features for chloride flux-associated disorders.

papers.title: HYDROFOBIC MODIFICATIONS OF CARBONIC ANHYDRASE DISTINCTIVELY IMPROVE PERFORMANCE IN BIOCATALYTIC CARBON CAPTURE
papers.abstract: The enzyme carbonic anhydrase (CA) can accelerate gas-liquid mass transfer of CO2, and extensive research is exploring how to leverage this in industrial carbon capture. At the molecular level, CA promotes capture by catalyzing the conversion of CO2 to bicarbonate near the gas-liquid interface. This mechanism implies that only a minor fraction of the enzyme at the interface actively contributes to capture, and as a result, efficient capture requires high enzyme dosages. Here, we designed and synthesized CA variants with hydrophobic modifications that render them interfacially active. The variants showed dramatic improvements in performance, and in some cases, the specific activity for carbon capture increased by more than two orders of magnitude relative to the unmodified, wild-type enzyme. Conversely, the thermostability and intrinsic enzyme activity in the aqueous bulk were only marginally affected by the modifications. These results implied that the enhanced efficacy of the modified enzymes reflected a general surface-partitioning mechanism. This interpretation provided fundamental insights into the interfacial enzyme process and highlighted a novel, broad avenue for designing catalysts for CO2 capture. Thus, this mechanism suggested that a range of hydrophobic modifications could enhance the activity of any catalyst (enzyme or non-enzyme) during carbon capture in aqueous sorbents.

papers.title: Symmetric versus asymmetric electron transfer in symmetric molecules
papers.abstract: Photoinduced electron transfer (ET) in symmetric donor-acceptor-donor (D-A-D) or (A-D-A) molecules attracts attention due to applications in advanced materials. It is normally assumed that ET occurs asymmetrically, from one donor to acceptor, thus breaking molecular symmetry and resulting in a dipole moment in the excited state. However, the symmetry can be preserved with symmetric ET from both donors leading to a nondipolar state with a high quadrupole moment. Here we report on the symmetric ET in a D-A-D probe, 5,5'-di(9H-carbazol-9-yl)-2,2'-bipyridine. This probe is negligibly solvatochromic in absorption, but highly solvatochromic in emission, and shows a strong decay of the emission oscillator strength in solvents of increasing polarity. We develop a 3-excited-state model that catches the experimental observations quantitatively, much better than the previously proposed 2-state model. Both the symmetric and asymmetric ET are analyzed; the conclusion is in favor of the symmetric ET as it fits well the experimental data, while the asymmetric ET cannot.

papers.title: High-Efficiency Quantum Defect Engineering in Carbon Nanotubes via Oxygen-Free Photochemistry
papers.abstract: Single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) offer potential for a wide range of applications from optoelectronic devices to biomedical diagnostics. One reason are their tunable optical properties, which can be further tailored by introducing a small number of quantum defects. However, the chemical conditions to obtain an optimal number and specific type of quantum defect is difficult to control. Here, we demonstrate that oxygen-free conditions are crucial to control the spectral features. To this end, we analyze the photochemical reaction of (6,5)-SWCNTs with different alkyl and aryl halides, as well as alkenyl/alkynyl compounds under UV irradiation. Removal of oxygen or addition of sulfites shifts the quantum defect related E11* emission peak from ~ 1130 nm to ~ 1100 nm, which suggests that different types of quantum defects are formed. For aryl halides, these conditions increase the E11*/E11 ratio up to 90 %, while reducing the required reactant concentration by ~ 90 %, with reaction times < 10 minutes. For the less reactive alkyl halides, ~ 80-fold smaller reactant concentrations achieve the same E11*/E11 ratios compared to oxygen containing conditions. This procedure allows us to investigate the combined effect of quantum defects and DNA functionalization of SWCNTs on the detection of small molecules. It underlines that efficient incorporation of quantum defects opens a new chemical dimension for SWCNT chemistry and photophysics.

papers.title: Real-Space Imaging of Valence-Electron Bonding Dynamics with Ultrafast Hard X-Ray Scattering
papers.abstract: Chemical reactivity is governed by the time-dependent redistribution of valence electron density, yet ultrafast diffractive imaging probes are typically dominated by scattering from the atoms and/or core electrons and therefore primarily report nuclear motion. Building on recent hard x-ray time-resolved scattering measurements of photoexcited deuterated ammonia, we extend ultrafast x-ray scattering off the evolving valence electron density into a real-space framework by retrieving the time-dependent electron pair density (PD). Using scattering difference signals, we reconstruct transient real-space ∆PDs that directly recover (i) the prompt redistribution of valence electron density following excitation into a diffuse Rydberg orbital, (ii) the subsequent localization of the electron density on the fragments following N–D bond fission, and (iii) distinct electronic-structure fingerprints of ballistic dissociation channels. These ∆PDs provide an intuitive, chemically interpretable measure of bond breaking and rearrangement by tracking the emergence, displacement, and loss of electron density between atomic centers while retaining femtosecond time resolution. Comparison with ab initio simulations guides the interpretation of the recovered ∆PDs and supports the inferred pathway assignments.

papers.title: Z-Scheme Co3O4@N-Doped Carbon/g-C3N4 Heterostructure Derived from ZIF-67 for Efficient Visible-Light Photocatalytic Degradation of Azo Dyes
papers.abstract: The rational design of efficient visible-light-driven photocatalysts for the degradation of persistent azo dyes remains a significant challenge in environmental remediation. Herein, we report a Z-scheme heterostructured photocatalyst constructed from ZIF-67-derived Co3O4@N-doped carbon (Co3O4@NC) integrated with graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4). The composite was synthesized via controlled pyrolysis followed by thermal assembly, yielding a well-defined core–shell Co3O4@NC architecture uniformly anchored on layered g-C3N4 nanosheets. Comprehensive characterization revealed enhanced visible-light absorption with a reduced band gap of 2.45 eV and significantly suppressed charge carrier recombination. The heterostructure exhibited outstanding photocatalytic performance, achieving 98.6% degradation of methyl orange within 60 min under visible-light irradiation (λ ≥ 420 nm). Kinetic analysis followed a pseudo-first-order model with a rate constant of 0.0653 min-1, representing a 3.5-fold improvement over pristine g-C3N4. Mechanistic investigations confirmed a direct Z-scheme charge transfer pathway, where electrons from Co3O4 recombine with holes from g-C3N4, preserving strong redox potentials. Reactive species trapping experiments identified superoxide (•O2-) and hydroxyl radicals (•OH) as the dominant oxidative species. The photocatalyst demonstrated excellent durability, maintaining over 94% activity after five cycles. This work highlights a scalable strategy for engineering MOF-derived Z-scheme photocatalysts with enhanced charge separation and redox capability for efficient wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Aryl-Radical-Avoiding Decarbonylative Deuteration of Aromatic Carboxylic Acids with D2O via Photoredox–Cobalt Co-Catalysis
papers.abstract: Decarboxylative deuteration of readily available aromatic carboxylic acids offers a valuable route to synthesize deuterium-labeled arenes. However, the mainstream aryl-radical pathways are often restrained by the slow generation of aryl radicals and uncontrollable side reactions, making synthesis of deuterated arenes with high activity, chemoselectivity, and functional tolerance markedly challenging. Herein, we report a photoredox/cobalt co-catalyzed aryl-radical-avoiding strategy, enabling the decarbonylative deuteration of aromatic carboxylic acids to deuterated arenes with up to 93% yield and 98% deuterium incorporation using D2O as deuterium source. Multiple characterizations validate that the pathways of arene addition/cyclization, and hydrogen or halogen atom transfer associated with aryl carboxyl radicals and aryl radicals can be suppressed. Furthermore, the wide substrate scope, broad functional-group compatibility, and facile applications to the late-stage deuteration of structurally complex pharmaceuticals and natural product derivatives demonstrate the potential utility.

papers.title: Minimal Structural Modification Tunes Aminopeptidase Selectivity in Hyperpolarized MRI Probes
papers.abstract: Insulin-regulated aminopeptidase (IRAP) is an important biomarker for various diseases, including cancer. However, its selective detection remains challenging due to competing activity from closely related enzymes such as aminopeptidase N (APN). Dynamic nuclear polarization-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DNP-MRI) enables noninvasive detection of enzymatic activity in vivo and represents a powerful platform for metabolic imaging. Although a previously reported IRAP-responsive DNP-MRI probe, Leu-[1- 13 C]Gly- d 2 -NMe 2 , allows detection of metabolic activity in vivo, its susceptibility to APN-mediated cleavage limits its selectivity for IRAP. Here, we report the development of a hyperpolarized molecular probe, Ala( t Bu)-[1- 13 C]Gly- d 2 -NMe 2 , through minimal structural modification of the previous probe. Replacement of the N-terminal leucine residue with a bulky Ala( t Bu) moiety markedly suppressed APN-mediated cleavage, reducing the catalytic efficiency toward APN by approximately 130-fold, while maintaining comparable catalytic efficiency toward IRAP. Furthermore, in vivo DNP-MRI experiments demonstrated successful metabolic imaging of Ala( t Bu)-[1- 13 C]Gly- d 2 -NMe 2 in MCF-7 tumor-bearing mice.

papers.title: Wearable electrofluidic biosensing system for real-time quantitation and adaptive stratification of fluctuating trace sweat antibodies
papers.abstract: However, sweat antibody detection remains particularly challenging because antibody concentrations are substantially lower than those of common sweat markers such as cortisol and glucose. By integrating ultra-sensitive interfacial capacitive sensing with ultra-fast AC electrothermal target enrichment, we develop detachable monolithic biosensors for sweat antibodies, which are based on antigen probe functionalized flexible electrode arrays. A wearable biosensing system, incorporating a pressure-regulated PDMS sweat-collection patch and a wristwatch-style microcapacitance detector, is further constructed to enable real-time quantitation of ultra-trace antibodies in sweat. SARS-CoV-2 N protein antibody and Hepatitis B surface antibody in sweat are tested with a limit of 10-6 ng/mL, a linear range of 10-5~10-1 ng/mL, and a responding time of 30 s. In response to the fluctuations of sweat biomarker levels, adaptive stratification algorithms are implemented by leveraging the sensor’s high dynamic range through machine learning. Validated on 25 volunteers with a stratification balanced accuracy exceeding 0.74, this system provides a versatile wearable platform capable of quantifying and stratifying a broader range of highly fluctuating, low-abundance sweat biomarkers.

papers.title: Acid-catalyzed rearrangement reaction for single-molecule junction formation
papers.abstract: Single-molecule junction formation is not possible for hydrazobenzenes due to the absence of anchoring groups to contact with the Au electrodes. In stark contrast, with the addition of acid, the junction formation is immediate and robust, monitored in real-time via the emergence of the 1.3×10 -3 G 0 conductance peak by the scanning tunneling microscope-based break junction method. We propose that this single-molecule junction is benzidine attaching to Au electrodes through NH 2 →Au dative interactions, which is a rearrangement reaction product of hydrazobenzene, confirmed by measurements of ex situ synthesized benzidine. Critically, we show that in forming the metal-molecule-metal junctions under an applied voltage in a nonpolar solvent, the reaction products become deprotonated, which otherwise requires addition of base. We confirm this hypothesis by showing that for synthesized -NH 3 + terminated compounds, -NH 3 + was converted into -NH 2 upon the junction formation. These results underscore a new acid-catalyzed method for single-molecule device formation.

papers.title: Site-selective Halogenation of Aromatic C-H Bonds via Electrocatalytic Flavin Adenine Dinucleotide Cofactor Regeneration
papers.abstract: Flavin-dependent halogenases (FDHs) catalyze site-selective C-H halogenation of electron-rich aromatic compounds but rely on multienzyme cofactor-recycling systems for a continuous supply of reduced flavin (FADH2). Here, we report an overpotential-driven, mediator-assisted bioelectrocatalytic strategy that eliminates the need for multienzyme cofactor-recycling systems or enzymes immobilized on electrode surfaces. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the FAD/FADH2 redox couple (-0.42 V vs Ag/AgCl, 3.5 M KCl) undergoes proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and participates in the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). While conventional multienzyme cofactor-recycling systems rely on catalase and glutathione to mitigate ORR-derived reactive oxygen species (ROS), bulk electrolysis (-0.7 V) experiments reveal that L-ascorbic acid more effectively suppresses substrate and product ROS-induced degradation. Under these conditions, the yield of 7-bromotryptophan increased from 20% to 46% after 24 h of electrolysis. Increasing the cathodic potential to -1.1 V improved the yield to 64%, likely due to the onset of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which generates surface-adsorbed hydrogen (Hads) through a Volmer-type step that promotes PCET between the electrode and FAD, thereby accelerating FADH2 formation and catalytic turnover. This mechanism becomes more evident upon introducing thermodynamically favorable redox mediators, namely 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone (HNQ) and methyl viologen (MV2+). Because HNQ operates via PCET chemistry, the HNQ/FAD pair, on average, achieved quantitative halogenation faster (within 10 h of electrolysis) than the MV2+/FAD pair (within 12 h of electrolysis), with the HNQ/FAD pair producing up to 8.8 mg of 7-bromotryptophan in a scale-up reactor. Extension to the RebH 4-V variant enables halogenation of larger substrates, establishing a scalable electrochemical platform for FDH catalysis.

papers.title: Metabolite-Gen: Joint Prediction of Sites of Metabolism, Reaction Class, and Metabolite Structures Using Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Predicting the metabolic fate of drug candidates remains a central challenge in pharmaceutical research, with direct implications for efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetic optimisation. We present Metabolite-Gen, a unified graph neural network framework that simultaneously predicts sites of metabolism (SOM) and cytochrome P450–mediated reaction class from molecular graph representations, then applies these predictions to generate structurally feasible metabolite structures. Metabolite-Gen employs a four-layer, four-head GATv2 graph attention encoder with dedicated SOM and reaction classification heads, augmented by DropEdge regularisation, multiclass focal loss for minority reaction classes, and a diversity-aware listwise reranker. Evaluated by 5-fold scaffold-stratified cross-validation on 578 parent–metabolite pairs spanning 12 CYPmediated reaction classes from the MetXBioDB database, Metabolite-Gen achieved mean validation SOM atom-ranking top-1/top-3/top-5 accuracies of 46.1%, 75.3%, and 86.3% (MRR = 0.61), reaction class top-1/top-3/top-5 accuracies of 53.8%, 69.7%, and 72.9% (weighted F1 = 0.52), and end-to-end metabolite structure top-1/top-3/top-5 accuracies of 52.4%, 68.4%, and 71.3% (MRR = 0.60). On the held-out test set (n = 144 molecules), Metabolite-Gen attained SOM top-1/top-3/top-5 of 55.6%, 77.1%, and 84.7% (MRR = 0.66), reaction class top-1/top-3/top-5 of 51.4%, 82.6%, and 91.7% (weighted F1 = 0.51), and metabolite structure top-1/top-3/top-5 of 46.5%, 64.6%, and 69.4% (MRR = 0.56). Critically, Metabolite-Gen integrates atom-level interpretability through explainable AI, enabling practitioners to visualise predicted metabolic soft spots and rationally guide structural modification to reduce metabolic liability — a capability with direct utility in lead optimisation, reactive metabolite risk assessment, and regulatory toxicology. By delivering ranked, structurally explicit metabolite hypotheses from molecular graph representations alone, without requiring experimental biotransformation data or manually curated reaction rules, Metabolite-Gen provides an end-to-end, interpretable pipeline that supports earlystage drug discovery, predictive toxicology, and regulatory risk assessment.

papers.title: Condenophilicity of Supramolecular Polymers Governs Organelle Formation in Fueled Synthetic Cells
papers.abstract: Synthetic cells are compartments designed to mimic the functions and characteristics of living cells. By constructing synthetic cells from abiotic, basic components (bottom-up), it is possible to investigate the minimal requirements for life and gain insights into fundamental principles of biology. Among the available platforms, complex coacervates are particularly attractive, due to their potential to encapsulate a wide range of biomolecules and other cargo, enabling genotype-phenotype mapping. By coupling coacervate formation to a fueled chemical reaction cycle, the synthetic cells become fuel-dependent, growing in the presence of fuel and decaying in its absence, resembling biological cells. However, constructing organelles for these transient synthetic cells, such as membranes and cytoskeletons, has remained an unresolved challenge. Here, we show that supramolecular (co-)polymers can act as organelles for the synthetic cells, depending on their condenophilicity (their affinity for the droplet phase). By using two distinct supramolecular building blocks, the condenophilicity can be modulated. Supramolecular copolymers where only some of the monomers bind to the complex coacervate result in the formation of a membrane structure around the droplet. However, as condenophilicity increases, the polymers partition strongly into the coacervates, leading to the formation of a cytoskeleton. Moreover, we found that these organelles influence the synthetic cell properties, such as morphology and their lifespan. Our results demonstrate that orthogonally assembled structures can serve as organelles for active complex coacervate-based synthetic cells, broadening the existing arsenal of tools to bestow these rudimentary synthetic cells with more life-like properties.

papers.title: Cation Identity, Phase State, and Density as Key Determinants of Radiative Forcing in Atmospheric Sulfate Systems
papers.abstract: Sulfate aerosols strongly influence climate through aerosol–radiation and aerosolcloud interactions and are widely considered for climate mitigation strategies. Despite this relevance, sulfate aerosols are commonly represented using simplified assumptions based on the binary H 2 SO 4 –H 2 O system and a composition-independent refractive index. Here, we show that cation identity, phase state, and density can substantially alter the optical properties of sulfate aerosols and the extent to which their evolution is governed by diffusion-limited mass transport. We combine bulk measurements of density, water activity, and refractive index with single-particle optical trapping and electrodynamic balance experiments to quantify droplet size, radial growth factors, and wavelength-dependent refractive indices. This approach is applied to seven inorganic sulfates (Li 2 SO 4 , Na 2 SO 4 , K 2 SO 4 , (NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 , MgSO 4 , Al 2 (SO 4 ) 3 , and MnSO 4 ) and two short-chain organosulfates. We further introduce a bulk–droplet equivalency framework that retrieves the droplet thermodynamic state (e.g., composition and water activity, including metastable and supersaturated regimes) directly from levitated-droplet measurements. Multivalent sulfates, specifically MgSO 4 , MnSO 4 , and Al 2 (SO 4 ) 3 , exhibit pronounced inflection points and hysteresis consistent with transitions to highly viscous, gel-like phases below RH ≈ 35–40%. In this low-RH regime, these systems display humidity-buffered behavior, in which density, refractive index, and growth factor vary minimally with short-range humidity fluctuations, strongly suppressing water transport and heterogeneous reactivity. Elevated refractive indices at 589 nm, reaching ∼ 1.48 for MgSO 4 and Al 2 (SO 4 ) 3 and ∼ 1.52 for MnSO 4 , yield enhanced shortwave radiative forcing efficiencies relative to conventional sulfate, as shown using Mie scattering and one-dimensional radiative transfer calculations (libRadtran/DISORT) for lognormal size distributions. These results highlight the importance of cation-specific phase behavior and optical properties for accurately representing sulfate aerosols in climate, atmospheric chemistry models, and geoengineering proposals.

papers.title: MIL 125(Ti) Derived TiO2/Graphene Quantum Dot Hybrid for Enhanced Visible Light Photocatalytic Mineralization of Textile Azo Dyes via Plasmonic Assisted Electron Transport
papers.abstract: The development of efficient visible light responsive photocatalysts for the mineralization of persistent azo dyes in textile effluents remains a critical environmental challenge. In this study, a hybrid nanocomposite consisting of MIL,125(Ti), derived TiO2 coupled with graphene quantum dots (GQDs) was synthesized via a controlled solvothermal calcination route and evaluated for photocatalytic degradation of Reactive Black 5 under visible light irradiation (λ = 420–700 nm, intensity = 100 mW cm-2). The MIL 125(Ti) precursor was synthesized at 150 °C for 24 h and subsequently calcined at 450 °C for 3 h in air to obtain anatase phase of TiO2 with a crystallite size of 18.6 nm. GQDs with an average diameter of 4.2 nm were incorporated at a loading of 3.0 wt% through ultrasonic assisted self assembly. The resulting composite exhibited a bandgap reduction from 3.21 eV for pure TiO2 to 2.64 eV, enabling efficient visible light absorption. Photocatalytic studies revealed a degradation efficiency of 97.8% within 120 min and total organic carbon (TOC) removal of 91.3% after 180 min. The enhanced performance was attributed to plasmonic assisted electron transport and efficient charge separation facilitated by GQDs. The reaction followed pseudo first order kinetics with a rate constant of 0.031 min-1. Radical scavenging experiments confirmed the dominant role of hydroxyl (•OH) and superoxide (O2•-) radicals. The hybrid catalyst demonstrated excellent stability with a degradation efficiency retention of 94.6% after five cycles.

papers.title: Unpacking SiO2 Precursor Effects on Aluminothermic Reduction in Molten NaCl-KCl Mixture to Yield Porous Silicon
papers.abstract: Developing lower-energy routes to silicon-based materials is important for improving the sustainability of chemical processes. Porous silicon (p-Si) is a nontoxic material with applications in CO 2 reduction, photocatalytic water splitting, lithium-ion batteries, and on-demand hydrogen generation, yet conventional silicon production relies on energy-intensive carbothermal reduction of SiO 2 at >1500 °C. Aluminothermic reduction offers a lower-temperature alternative, but many reported methods rely on volatile AlCl 3 salt. Recently, we reported a molten-salt-assisted aluminothermic reduction of fumed SiO 2 using a NaCl-KCl mixture that produces p-Si within 2 h that can yield large quantities of hydrogen on-demand. Here, we evaluate the generality of this approach by applying it to additional SiO 2 precursors (−325 mesh and Stöber silica) and investigate the factors governing reduction efficiency. We find that the extent of reduction is strongly dependent on precursor surface area, with high-surface-area fumed SiO 2 undergoing the most complete conversion and Stöber precursor the least. Electron microscopy reveals substantial molten-salt-induced restructuring of SiO 2 , indicating that precursor morphology and surface area play key roles in controlling reduction kinetics. These results establish structure–reactivity relationships for molten-salt aluminothermic reduction and provide guidance for designing more efficient and scalable routes to porous silicon.

papers.title: Drug repurposing identifies Saquinavir as a dual inhibitor of Hepsin and Matriptase: A pharmacophore-based virtual screening, docking, and MD simulation study
papers.abstract: Matriptase and hepsin activities are upregulated in many cancer cells. They continuously provide activating ligands for a dysregulated receptor tyrosine kinase, MET, that promotes tumour invasion, metastasis, and survival. Therefore, a therapy that targets these two proteins for inhibition is a good approach to counter associated cancer. In this study, we developed a pharmacophore model from an inhibitor of matriptase and hepsin and validated it by confirming if it can identify a set of inhibitors from non-inhibitors. Using the valid model, we screened a library of Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drugs to identify the potential inhibitors of matriptase and hepsin. The screening well matches Saquinavir (drug 431) and its isomers drug 120, drug 273, and drug 275 from the zinc database as the potential inhibitors of matriptase and hepsin. To further ascertain the hit drugs’ inhibitory role, studies including molecular docking, Prime MM-GBSA (Molecular Mechanics-Generalised Born Surface Area), and molecular dynamic simulations were used to understand their binding affinity, atomistic interactions, and stability in the proteins. The saquinavir recorded a better binding affinity (docking score) for hepsin and matriptase compared to the reference ligand and co-ligand and was stable with the protein in molecular dynamic simulations. This result gives a new perception into Hepsin and/or Matriptase as a target of saquinavir, contributing to its anticancer properties, and also gives a new look into the design of Hepsin and Matriptase inhibitors.

papers.title: Incorporating Neural Network in the AMOEBA Polarizable Force Field for Ligand Field Effects of Cu2+ Ion
papers.abstract: Characterizing the solvation of open-shell transition metal ions remains a challenge for classical force fields due to ligand field electronic effects. Here, we present AMOEBA+NN, a machine-learning-augmented polarizable potential, to investigate Cu2+ solvation in NH3 and H2O and mixed environments. The model, trained on quantum-mechanical (QM) association energies, accurately reproduces the Cu2+ energy landscape across diverse coordination geometries. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrate that AMOEBA+NN successfully captures the electronically driven Jahn-Teller (JT) distortion. Evidence from radial distribution functions (RDFs) and geometry optimizations reveals characteristic axial elongation, which is absent in conventional classical descriptions. Kinetic analysis shows a highly dynamic Cu2+-NH3 environment with a rapid ligand exchange (residence time of 66.52 ps), contrasting with the H2O system where binding is two to three orders of magnitude more stable. Furthermore, the calculated hydration free energy of -477.59 ± 0.50 kcal/mol shows excellent agreement with experimental data (within 1.31 kcal/mol). This work provides a unified, computationally efficient framework for describing the structural, dynamic, and thermodynamic observables of transition metal coordination.

papers.title: The mechanism of visible-light photochemical rearrangements of conjugated amide enolates
papers.abstract: Deprotonation of conjugated amides forms coloured solutions of lithium enolates (trienolates) that absorb light in the visible range of the electromagnetic spectrum. Irradiation of these extended enolates at a suitable wavelength induces a family of skeletal rearrangements, including bond migrations and ring expansions, that proceed through a biradical intermediate. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal that excitation of the extended enolate chromophore promotes homolysis of the C–N bond of the amide via an intersection seam between the S 1 and S 0 potential energy surfaces. The resulting singlet biradical undergoes rapid recombination to generate rearranged amide products, with regioselectivity governed by the molecular framework. Acyclic trienolates undergo competing [1,3]-, [1,5]-, and [1,7]-migrations, but incorporation of a ring constrains radical recombination resulting in regioselective re-cyclisations. Lack of stereospecificity during the rearrangements, and cyclopropylbenzyl ring openings, coupled with a lack of cross-reactivity in TEMPO trapping and a crossover experiment, indicate the formation of short-lived, solvent-caged radical pairs rather than freely diffusing radicals. These findings establish a general mechanistic rationalisation of visible-light-driven rearrangements of amide enolates, and suggest that ring topology can be used to control the outcome of the biradical recombinations.

papers.title: Structure–Property Relationships in Thermoresponsive Fluorescent Polymers: Roles of Size, Composition, and Architecture
papers.abstract: Thermoresponsive fluorescent polymers (TFPs) provide a versatile platform for optical temperature sensing by coupling phase transitions with changes in fluorescence. Here, we report TFPs based on poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) and poly(ethylene glycol methacrylate) (PEGMA), incorporating fluorescein acrylate (FluA) as a model fluorophore via reversible additionfragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) copolymerization. Linear and hyperbranched architectures were synthesized, with different compositions to exhibit cloud point temperatures (Tcp) within a physiologically relevant temperature window. Fluorescence behavior was investigated as a function of temperature, concentration, and pH. Distinct responses were observed across the Tcp, governed by the interplay between polymer collapse, microenvironmental confinement, and chromophorechromophore interactions. PNIPAM and PEGMA systems containing low fluorescein loading exhibited fluorescence enhancement near the Tcp, followed by quenching at higher temperatures, whereas higher loading systems showed predominantly decreased fluorescence intensity upon heating due to increased chromophore-chromophore interactions. Fluorescence intensity was strongly concentration-dependent, highlighting the role of aggregation, and pH studies revealed changes in both fluorescence intensity and emission maxima, with temperature-responsive fluorescence being most prominent at pH 7 and moderately retained at pH 9. Rheological measurements further demonstrated changes in complex viscosity across the Tcp, linking macroscopic behavior to structural transitions. Hyperbranched polymers exhibited distinct fluorescence and rheological responses compared to linear analogues, underscoring the influence of topology. These results establish structure-property relationships that enable tunable fluorescence responses, providing design guidelines for polymer-based optical thermometers.

papers.title: The Cosmic Equation of State and the Cosmological Constant Problem in GERT
papers.abstract: In physical chemistry, the equation of state of a closed thermodynamic system is the bridge between measurable variables (density, pressure, temperature) and derived state functions (enthalpy, free energy). The previous paper of this series derived the Cauldron equation, the equation of motion of the cosmic substrate treated as a closed thermodynamic system. The present paper integrates the Cauldron equation to obtain the cosmic equation of state H(x) = Hem exp[I(x)/β] explicitly, and develops three consequences. First, the cosmic equation of state is a state function in the strict mathematical sense, admitting direct comparison with the chemistry equations of state (ideal gas, van der Waals). Second, the cosmological constant discrepancy (∼ 10122) dissolves not as a numerical anomaly but as a category mistake: General Relativity sums vacuum modes (a geometric quantity) while observations constrain the remaining thermodynamic fuel (a state-function quantity); the two are not directly comparable without an equation of state to mediate. Third, the Lorentz factor √ 1− v2/c2 is recovered as the chemicalkinetic limit of the internal Work rate, with v = c the threshold at which the available energy fraction for internal process vanishes. General Relativity is the theory of rulers; the Gibbs Energy Redistribution Theory (GERT) is the theory that includes the thermometer.

papers.title: Rigor & Reproducibility in Electrocatalysis: Integrating Theory and Experiment
papers.abstract: Electrocatalysis is central to electrified energy conversion technologies, including the production of fuels and chemicals from renewable electricity. In recent years, atomistic modeling based on density functional theory (DFT) has become an indispensable tool for catalysis researchers because it can provide a molecular-level perspective into catalytic reactivity that is otherwise inaccessible to experimental measurements. Computational electrocatalysis model inputs are intended to capture fundamental understanding of the complex interfacial environment of the catalytic active site, but rely on practical approximations that can affect the reliability of insights gained from DFT. This Perspective outlines a framework for rigorous and reproducible integration of theory and experiment in heterogeneous electrocatalysis research. We discuss state-of-the-art computational methods and sources of error in model development and interpretation. We describe opportunities for validation of theoretical models and experimental interpretations as it pertains to the structure of active sites, reaction energetics, and microkinetic modeling. We provide examples to help computational researchers develop models that move beyond obtaining qualitative agreement with reactivity trends, and toward the development of rigorous mechanistic insights that can be leveraged to predict promising new catalysts or operating conditions. Rigor and reproducibility are enhanced when theory and experiment have multiple nodes of connection, which enhances the longevity and robustness of conclusions and insights about electrocatalytic reactivity.

papers.title: Probing the Molecular Mechanisms of Ion Transport in High-Conductivity Lithium-Ion Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Fluorinated nitrile and acetone solvents have been recently shown to enable lithiumion electrolytes with ionic conductivities of up to 45ms cm−1, more than four times higher than current commercial formulations. To understand the physical origins of this enhanced performance, we employ molecular dynamics simulations to target the ion transport mechanisms. Non-polarizable classical force fields can be tuned to successfully predict the ionic conductivity by down-scaling the electrostatic interactions. However, the structure of the ion solvation shells and consequent transport mechanisms are inconsistent with experimental observations. Important missing interactions are added explicitly via polarisable force fields and implicitly via machine learning force fields, trained on extensive ab initio simulations. Both frameworks fail at recovering the experimental observables for the more complex fluorinated electrolyte, whereas they succeed at predicting the solvation structures in acetone. Our results underscore the importance of accurate force field choice when interpreting the molecular-scale mechanisms of ion transport, particularly for electrolytes with complex chemistries. The simulation framework developed here provides a valuable tool for virtually screening and rationally designing high-performance electrolyte molecules.

papers.title: DNA-encoded origami morphing
papers.abstract: From biological entities to manmade constructions, shape is an essential structural and functional feature 1 . At the nanoscale, this involves key structure-function relationships, ranging from conformation-dependent protein activity 2–4 to morphology-driven properties of synthetic nanomaterials 5,6 . Finding ways to dynamically reshape nanoscale architectures under constant physiological conditions thus emerges as a powerful goal to create smart biocompatible adaptive materials. While DNA origami offers unparalleled precision and robustness for constructing virtually any desired static nanoscale morphology 7,8 , imparting adaptive morphological shift remains a formidable challenge. Current methods are mainly limited to local deformations 9–11 rather than radical transformation, and often involve complex mechanical designs 12–17 or specific stimulus-responsive modules 17–19 . Here, we introduce an exceptionally versatile, modification-free strategy for isothermal, physiologically compatible DNA origami morphing driven by programmable staple-strand competition. We achieve fast, high-yield transformations across diverse 2D and 3D morphologies, including multiple-shape pathways and back-and-forth switches. We further demonstrate modularity through the orthogonal and parallel reconfiguration of independent subdomains within a single DNA scaffold. Moreover, selective shape transformation is achieved from a pool of structures containing DNA origami protected by specific ligation. Strikingly, we leverage this structural plasticity to dynamically reconfigure scaffold-anchored proteins into controllable patterns at 37 °C. This is used to modulate biochemical function, as demonstrated here with the regulation of a glucose oxidase/horseradish peroxidase cascade reaction. Overall, this work establishes a reliable and generic framework for nanoscale programmable morphing and user-defined functional regulation in physiologically compatible conditions.

papers.title: Electronic Communication in Di- and Tri- Nuclear Ruthenium Acetylide Complexes
papers.abstract: The electronic properties of a suite of di- and tri-nuclear ruthenium bis(acetylide)-based complexes incorporating phenylene and naphthylene bridges have been explored experimentally and computationally. The complexes, [{trans-Ru(dmpe) 2 (C≡C t Bu)} 2 (μ-C≡C(2,6-C 10 H 6 )C≡C)], [{trans-Ru(dmpe) 2 (C≡C t Bu)} 2 (μ-C≡C(2,7-C 10 H 6 )C≡C)], and [{trans-Ru(dmpe) 2 (C≡C t Bu)} 3 (μ-(C≡C) 3 (1,3,5-C 6 H 3 )] were formed via the metathesis of terminal organic bisacetylenes with the methylruthenium complex, [trans-Ru(dmpe) 2 (CH 3 )(C≡C t Bu)], in the presence of methanol and under mild conditions. Spectroelectrochemical analyses of these species showed that the linearly π-conjugated 2,6-naphthylene bridge enabled better electronic communication between redox-active ruthenium-acetylide sites than the cross-conjugated 2,7-naphthylene bridge.

papers.title: Towards Scalable and Efficient Machine-Learning Force Fields: The MatPL package and Its Advancements on Neuroevolution Potentials
papers.abstract: The development of accurate and efficient machine-learning interatomic potentials is a transformative technology in computational materials science and molecular dynamics simulations. Here, we introduce the Materials Potential Library (MatPL) , a comprehensive software framework integrating multiple machine-learning potential architectures, with a particular emphasis on advancing the neuroevolution potential (NEP) framework. MatPL incorporates gradient-based optimizers to improve training stability and accuracy. A key innovation is its highly optimized, GPU-native interface for LAMMPS, seamlessly integrated with LAMMPS’s robust Message Passing Interface (MPI) infrastructure. This design transcends the limitations of single-node GPU execution, enabling efficient cross-node scalability without compromising the computational efficiency intrinsic to NEP. MatPL is a high-performance and versatile platform for next-generation atomistic modeling, balancing between high accuracy, training efficiency, and large-scale simulation capability.

papers.title: Two-step bubble printing for continuous nanoparticle assembly through a structured flow field
Suppression of DNA coffee-ring by compacting agents via adsorption at water/substrate and water/air interfaces
papers.abstract: The drying of sessile drops of DNA solutions commonly leads to inhomogeneous deposition caused by the so-called coffee-ring effect, which hampers uniform surface immobilization in biosensing and microarray applications. Here, we investigate how DNA-compacting agents influence DNA patterns formed on negatively and positively charged solid substrates upon drop drying. Using poly-L-lysine and spermine as model compacting agents, we demonstrate that the suppression of the coffee-ring effect can arise from two distinct phenomena depending on the compacting agent concentration regime. At low concentrations, that is, at the threshold for DNA compaction, compacting agents mainly induce electrostatic adsorption of DNA at the water/substrate interface. Conversely, at higher concentrations, DNA compacts and aggregates, leading to trapping of aggregates at the water/air interface during evaporation and preventing their transport and accumulation at the drop contact line. These findings constitute a new way to suppress the coffee-ring effect through DNA neutralization and compaction, and establish adsorption at interfaces as a general strategy for achieving homogeneous DNA coatings.

papers.title: Base-Catalyzed Hydroarsination at Ambient Temperature: Synthesis in Green Solvent
papers.abstract: A practical, transition-metal-free hydroarsination protocol using commercially available, air-stable catalytic NaOH in DMSO is described. Hydroarsination has been sorely underdeveloped , and these conditions enable regioselective anti-Markovnikov addition of diphenylarsine to vinylarenes, Michael acceptors, and alkynes at ambient temperature, affording previously unknown tertiary arsines in good to quantitative yields. Deuterium labeling studies support a nucleophilic mechanism initiated by arsine deprotonation. Because NaOH is not fully soluble in DMSO under conditions screened, the insoluble component provides water management during the reaction as well as additional base to (re)activate arsine, which explains the high activity relative to reported catalysts. This simple methodology expands access to previously inaccessible substrates and therefore structurally diverse tertiary arsines with a substantial improvement in activity and scope over prior catalysts while reducing cost, simplifying purification, and improving green aspects of the reaction.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn to comply with journal policy.

papers.title: Naphthyl substituted Carbodiphosphoranes: Synthesis, Reactivity towards CuCl and Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Properties
papers.abstract: Herein we present the two-step synthesis of two new 2‑naphthyl substituted Carbodiphosphoranes (CDPs). In the first step either two equivalents of P(Naph)Ph 2 (Naph = 2-naphthyl-) and CH 2 Br 2 or P(Naph)Ph 2 and [Ph 3 P(CH 2 Br)]Br are reacted whereby the symmetrical bis phosphonium salt 1a and the unsymmetric salt 1b are obtained. Subsequently, the CDPs 2a and 2b where prepared by deprotonation with two equivalents of potassium hexamethyldisilazanide. After isolation, the coordination chemistry of 2a and 2b towards CuCl is explored where, depending on educt stoichiometry, mononuclear ( 3a , 3b ) and dinuclear compounds ( 4a , 4b ) are obtained. All prepared compounds were characterised by NMR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry and elemental analysis, and for 1a / b , 2a , 3b , and 4a / b single crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction studies could be obtained. Furthermore, the photophysical properties of the free 2-naphthyl substituted CDPs 2a / b and their corresponding Cu I complexes 3a / b and 4a / b have been investigated by steady-state and time-resolved luminescence studies at room temperature and at 77 K in various aggregation states, and further insight is provided by DFT/TD-DFT calculations. While 2a/b display features of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), 3a/b and 4a/b exhibit a much more complex excited state behaviour due to the interplay of metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) and napthyl ligand centered (LC) states, resulting in multiple simultaneous luminescence phenomena involving TADF, 1 LC and 3 LC emission.

papers.title: The Gated Quantum Resonator: A Bayesian Circuit–Hamiltonian Framework for Catalysis, Enzymology, Materials Science and UPE.
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) and hybrid quantum–classical (QM/MM) methods provide powerful tools for simulating chemical and biological systems, yet their application to long-timescale, strongly coupled processes remains limited by non-integrability, chaotic sensitivity, and extreme time-scale separation. These limitations motivate complementary formalisms that emphasize structure, constraint, and evidence integration over brute-force trajectory resolution. Here we introduce the Gated Quantum Resonator (GQR) framework, a Bayesian circuit–Hamiltonian formalism in which reactive coordinates are modeled as coupled vibronic–electronic resonators with gateable interactions. Linearization around operating points maps the effective Hamiltonian onto electrical network analogues, enabling transparent parameterization and rapid Bayesian updating from spectroscopic and mechanistic evidence. The framework provides a unified language for describing non-Arrhenius kinetics, tunnelling assisted by constrained vibronic coherence, and mode-selective transport in open quantum systems. Without resolving full many-body trajectories, GQR identifies protected dynamical subspaces in which coherent evolution can persist under environmental coupling. This formulation is applicable across enzymatic catalysis, heterogeneous and electrocatalytic systems, and radiative phenomena, offering a tractable complement to conventional simulation approaches for hypothesis generation, model reduction, and mechanistic discrimination. ### Post-publication Supporting Developments (2026)

papers.title: ChemMambaFlow: Graph-Enhanced Mamba with Latent Flow Matching for Molecular Property Prediction and Conformation Generation
papers.abstract: We propose ChemMambaFlow, a unified framework that integrates a graphenhanced Mamba encoder with latent flow matching for chemical molecular property prediction and conformation generation. The Graph-Enhanced Mamba Encoder combines graph attention mechanisms with selective state space modeling to capture both local and long-range atomic dependencies. The Latent Flow Matching Conformation Generator efficiently produces 3D molecular structures from SMILES representations through learned probability paths in latent space. A Contribution-Aware Multi-Modal Fusion Module dynamically balances molecular graph and spectroscopic features based on their estimated task contributions. Experiments on MoleculeNet, QM9, and ChemSpectra datasets demonstrate that ChemMambaFlow consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving 88.1% AUROC on HIV, 0.423 RMSE on ESOL, and 0.0176 MAE on QM9, while generating chemically plausible conformations rated 4.43/5 by expert evaluation.

papers.title: Shape- and peptide–water interaction-dependent membrane permeability of cyclic hexapeptides revealed by enhanced-sampling simulations
papers.abstract: Membrane permeability of cyclic peptides is essential for intracellular protein–protein interaction inhibition; however, its underlying determinants remain insufficiently understood. We analyzed six cyclic hexapeptides that share the same amino acid sequence (Leu–Leu–Leu–Leu–Pro–Tyr), residue number, N-methylation degree, and calculated hydrophobicity (MlogP), but differ only in stereochemistry (D or L configurations) and exhibit up to an 80-fold difference in Caco-2 permeability. Two-dimensional replica exchange molecular dynamics simulations were performed in explicit water–phospholipid (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine) bilayer systems, while ensemble-averaged shape-related and interaction-based descriptors were derived from the trajectories. Correlation analyses revealed that peptides with higher membrane permeability preferentially adopted elongated conformations oriented perpendicular to the membrane plane, particularly in the polar membrane regions, and exhibited pronounced interactions with water molecules. These findings are expected to deepen our understanding of the structural and dynamic factors governing cyclic peptide membrane permeability.

papers.title: Boundary-Operator Formulation for Finite-Thickness Chemical Interfaces and Catalytic Boundaries
papers.abstract: Chemical interfaces often determine the effective structure and rate of reaction systems. Classical sharp boundary conditions compress finite thickness, adsorption coverage, electricdouble-layer charge, proton-exchange-membrane selectivity, reaction-zone motion, singular geometry, and interfacial dissipation into a few empirical coefficients. This paper develops a boundary-operator formulation for mathematical chemistry in which a chemical boundary is treated as an explicit state-dependent object rather than as a subsidiary condition imposed on bulk equations. The basic object is a triple boundary object consisting of geometric support, state variables, and energetic role. A finite-thickness boundary may contain sequentially arranged diffusion, electric-double-layer, catalytic, proton-exchange-membrane, and product-desorption sublayers. The sharp boundary is recovered as the mathematical limit δ → 0, whereas δ > 0 describes the physically resolved interfacial region. Under Sobolev-trace, weak-measure, and entropy-production assumptions, the paper formulates trace, jump, conservation, reaction, mass-transfer, double-layer, membrane, variational, and impedance operators. Smooth regions, singular sets, and thick layers are unified by a regular-singular-thick weak balance. Classical Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, surface-reaction, membrane-transport, Butler-Volmer, and Stefan-type relations are recovered as limiting cases. The main computable result is a multilayer-resistance correction of observable Langmuir rates with an explicit local error estimate.

papers.title: Bioinformatics-Guided Discovery of a Thermostable and Highly Promiscuous RiPP Cyclodehydratase
papers.abstract: Ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) often contain backbone-embedded oxazoline/thiazoline heterocycles that are installed by enzymes known as cyclodehydratases. These enzymes are of great interest as biocatalysts for biotechnology applications, as embedded oxazoline/thiazoline heterocycles can induce non-subtle structural and functional changes that alter bioactivity both directly and indirectly. However, the toolkit of existing cyclodehydratases with robust activity, stability, and well-defined sequence specificity is extremely limited. Herein, we apply a genome mining approach to discover two novel cyclodehydratases: TcuD (from Thermomonospora curvata) and TteD (from Thermocatellispora tengchongensis) with improved thermostability; TcuD also displays exceptional substrate scope. Specifically, TcuD showed remarkable tolerance to mutations, insertions, and deletions to its substrate precursor peptide, TcuA, and it could easily modify a diverse set of substrates whose sequences were derived from α-helical regions of structurally characterized proteins. This work expands the repertoire of cyclodehydratases available for biotechnology applications.

papers.title: Sequence Dependence of Folding and Self-Assembly of Glycine-X Repeat Peptides on Graphite
Enhancing Human Plasma Lipidome Characterization in COVID-19 Patients by Combining Nanoflow Liquid Chromatography with Ultraviolet Photodissociation Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: Microbore liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) is a commonly used technique for lipidomic analysis of clinical samples due to its robust and high throughput nature. However, achieving sufficient sensitivity for comprehensive structural characterization of volume-limited clinical samples, such as serum, plasma, or cerebrospinal fluid, remains challenging. In addition, although structural characterization by tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) offers the potential for identification and differentiation of isomers and isobars not achieved by screening lipid masses alone, MS/MS methods may offer reduced sensitivity for low abundance lipids and may falter when key structural features, such as localization of double bonds in glycerophospholipids (GPLs), rely on detection of low abundance fragment ions. Determining this level of structural detail is especially important for clinical lipidomics given that dysregulation of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA)-containing GPLs has been observed in plasma from patients with viral infections, including COVID-19. Herein, we demonstrate the high sensitivity afforded by nanoflow LC-MS in combination with the structural details provided by ultraviolet photodissociation for the characterization of the plasma lipidome from participants with COVID-19 and healthy controls. Compared to conventional microbore LC-MS, nanoflow LCMS achieved a 2400-fold improvement in mass sensitivity and two-fold improvement in chromatographic resolution. Moreover, the approach confirmed dysregulation of PUFA-containing GPLs in COVID-19 samples and enabled expanded structural characterization through double bond localization at the molecular species level.

papers.title: Benzo[b]phosphole fluorophores for ratio-based live cell pH imaging
papers.abstract: Precise measurement of lysosomal pH is essential for understanding its role in health and disease, yet most existing chemical-genetic probes for acidic organelles are limited to intensity-based readouts. We introduce BPOEt-1HTL, a benzo[b]phosphole-derived, HaloTag-targetable pH indicator that delivers quantitative, ratiometric pH imaging. In human embryonic kidney cells, BPOEt-1HTL reports nuclear pH and detects drug-induced increases in lysosomal pH following treatment with Bafilomycin A1, an inhibitor of the vacuolar H+-ATPase. The probe supports both excitation and emission ratio-imaging under one- or two-photon excitation, making it compatible with a wide range of microscope systems. This versatile platform expands the toolkit for mapping pH in acidic organelles, offering new opportunities to investigate lysosomal function in disease-relevant contexts.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Crystallographic Copilots: Indexing and Phase Identification
Synthesis and identification of Sertraline N-nitroso impurity
papers.abstract: N-nitroso impurities in sertraline form through the nitrosation of the sertraline amine in the presence of nitrites or nitrosating agents, especially under acidic conditions or during storage and manufacturing. These impurities develop within the drug product when trace nitrites, excipients, moisture, heat, or prolonged storage facilitate the reaction. The impurity was synthesized by reacting sertraline free base with tert-butyl nitrite under carefully controlled low-temperature conditions. Characterization employed analytical techniques such as HPLC, mass spectrometry, FT-IR, and 1H NMR spectroscopy. FT-IR analysis revealed distinctive vibrations of the nitroso functional group, while 1H NMR confirmed substituted aromatic rings and a nitroso-substituted aliphatic amine structure. This study details the synthetic route and characterization of the sertraline N-nitroso impurity, highlighting critical factors influencing its formation and underscoring the need for stringent manufacturing controls to prevent nitroso contamination.

papers.title: A high-throughput experimentation platform for hydroxide electrodeposition and electrochemical evaluation of electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: We report a high-throughput screening system for hydroxide electrocatalysts that integrates hydroxide electrodeposition-based synthesis and electrochemical evaluation. The system combines standardization of the synthesis-and-evaluation workflow through electrodeposition, miniaturization using screen-printed electrodes and a 96-well microplate format, and parallelization through a home-built 32-channel potentiostat system. Reproducibility tests showed good agreement among channels under identical conditions and further demonstrated that condition-dependent performance differences could be stably captured even when different electrodeposition potentials and deposition times were independently assigned to different channels. As a demonstration, 96 conditions defined by the Ni/Fe ratio, supporting electrolyte fraction, electrodeposition potential, and deposition time were screened for Ni–Fe hydroxide electrocatalysts toward the oxygen evolution reaction. Heat-map and decision-tree analyses revealed that the Ni/Fe ratio is the primary factor governing OER overpotential in the Ni–Fe hydroxide system studied here, whereas process factors further differentiate performance within a given compositional region. These results show that, although composition-centered highthroughput screening is effective, incorporation of process conditions is also important for identifying high-performance conditions. The present system provides a practical platform for high-throughput electrocatalyst discovery in a coupled space of composition and process conditions.

papers.title: Mild and Selective Hydrogenolysis of Aromatic Oxygenates Over a Pt/WO3–ZrO2 Catalyst in a Biphasic System
papers.abstract: The selective hydrogenolysis of lignin-derived aromatic oxygenates to arenes under mild conditions remains a significant challenge due to competing over-hydrogenation of the aromatic ring. Here, we report a Pt/WO3–ZrO2 catalyst that enables mild and selective hydrogenolysis of a broad range of aromatic oxygenates in a water/decane biphasic system (90 °C, 1 atm, 0.1 atm of H2). The biphasic environment efficiently suppresses over-hydrogenation by continuously extracting the arene products into the organic phase, thereby suppressing hydrogenation of the aromatic ring. Kinetic analysis shows that C(sp2)–OMe cleavage precedes C(sp2)–OH cleavage in the hydrogenolysis of 4-ethylguaiacol, while mechanistic studies reveal that the multifunctional nature (acid and redox properties) of the WO3–ZrO2 support enable the selective hydrogenolysis under exceptionally mild conditions. The catalyst exhibits broad substrate scope, high selectivity for aromatic products, and good reusability, providing an efficient platform for producing aromatic hydrocarbons from lignin-derived oxygenates.
