papers.title: Divergent Synthesis of Möbius and Hückel N-Heterocycloarenes from a Common Macrocyclic Backbone
papers.abstract: We report the divergent synthesis of a Möbius N-heterocycloarene (1) and a Hückel Nheterocycloarene (2) from a common macrocyclic precursor. The topology is governed by the annulation reaction: the Scholl reaction yields the Möbius topology, while InCl3-mediated alkyne annulation gives the Hückel topology. In acyclic models, both reactions favor C4/C5 over C2/C7 bond formation, but this regioselectivity reverses in the constrained macrocycle. The Scholl reaction forms three bonds at C2, one at C7, and two at C5—one inducing the 180° twist for the Möbius topology and the other accompanied by a skeletal rearrangement, whereas alkyne annulation exclusively forms C2/C7 bonds to afford the Hückel topology. Crystal structure analysis and computational studies show uneven contortion in 1 and localized aromatic ring currents in both 1 and 2. Compound 2 adopts a saddle-shaped geometry with high conformational flexibility and binds tetrafluoroborate via C–H···F hydrogen bonds in solution.

papers.title: [3]Cyclo-2,9-peropyrenylene: Longitudinally Curved Peropyrene Nanohoops
papers.abstract: The synthesis of curved polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) remains a significant challenge, owing to the intrinsic rigidity of their multi-annulated π-frameworks. Herein, we report the synthesis of curved peropyrene-based nanohoops, representing the first example of cyclic, longitudinally curved peropyrene architectures. These nanohoops were constructed through a gold-mediated synthetic strategy combined with a dynamic reorganization process. This approach enables the incorporation of 2,9-peropyrene units into cyclic π-conjugated frameworks. The resulting nanohoops exhibit unique photophysical behavior arising from the interplay between cyclic π-conjugation of nanohoops and curved peropyrene units.

papers.title: Determination of Ultrafiltration/Diafiltration Process Leachables Clearance Using a Novel Untargeted Liquid Chromatography-High-Resolution Mass Spectrometry Method with In-Silico Quantification
papers.abstract: Untargeted analysis using liquid chromatography high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) provides a comprehensive approach to determine process equipment-related leachables (PERLs) in biomanufacturing processes. A shortcoming of current analytical methods is their inability to provide quantitative information, due to limited availability of reference standards, constituting an important obstacle in understanding the fate of PERLs and their human exposure levels if present in the final drug product. This study presents a semiquantitative workflow based on ionization efficiency (LogIE) measurement of PERLs analyzed by LC-HRMS. A partial least squares (PLS) model based on physicochemical parameters of 31 compounds was built and validated to predict LogIE of unknown compounds and to facilitate their quantitation. The semi-quantitative analysis was internally validated by calculation and comparison of residuals at 5 concentration levels within the linear dynamic range. The workflow was applied and tested to investigate leachable clearance during ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF) processes. Three monoclonal antibodies were spiked with leachables generated from polymeric materials under selected conditions to simulate realistic leachables concentrations. Determined leachable concentrations across UF/DF allowed calculation of clearance percentages (> 90%) and sieving coefficients (S). S values were compared with experimental values from previous studies, determining an average error of 2.7%, indicating acceptable performance of the semiquantitative approach. Results from this wider study under realistic leachable concentrations confirmed Log P as the dominant property in explaining clearance. Lowest clearance is anticipated for compounds with Log P > 7 (highly hydrophobic) while the highest clearance is expected for compounds with Log P < 5 (highly and moderately polar).

papers.title: Chitosan Microgels Enable RNase-Resistant and Gut-Targeted Delivery of dsRNA in Colorado Potato Beetle
papers.abstract: There is evidence that use of agrochemicals contributes to environmental pollution. Spray-induced gene silencing using double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) represents a versatile and target-specific alternative. However, RNA is rapidly degraded in the environment due to the ubiquitous presence of natural ribonucleases (RNases). Here, we formulated dsRNA-Ledprona, the active ingredient in the commercial insecticide Calantha targeting Colorado potato beetle (Leptinotarsa decemlineata), with physically crosslinked chitosan microgels (> 100 µm). Due to the microgels’ pH- and salt-responsiveness, the release of dsRNA can be triggered under conditions, which simulate the beetles’ gut environment. Under greenhouse conditions, the formulation is competitive towards naked dsRNA (100 % mortality). Remarkably, the active treatment with RNase A did not inhibit the efficiency of the formulation (100 % mortality) while naked dsRNA was deactivated (0 % mortality). Moreover, the microgels are degradable by the soil microbiome. This work provides new insights for the design of functional microgel-based RNase-protected and biodegradable dsRNA-formulations.

papers.title: High-Throughput Structure Determination Using Serial Electron Diffraction
papers.abstract: Atomic-scale structure determination is essential for product confirmation in chemical synthesis and for understanding material properties in chemistry, materials science, and pharmaceutical research. However, traditional techniques such as X-ray crystallography and conventional Microcrystal Electron Diffraction (MicroED) are often limited by requirements for large crystals, cryogenic conditions, or complex goniometry, making them less suitable for beam-sensitive or agglomerated nanocrystalline samples. To address these challenges, we employ serial electron diffraction (SerialED) to determine the structures of ten chemically and structurally diverse compounds at room temperature. The analyzed samples include metal-organic frameworks, pharmaceutical compounds, a perovskite, and various organic and metalorganic complexes. Our method enables high-throughput diffraction data collection using commercially available instruments and low-dose exposures, circumventing the need for cryogenic preservation. Sub-angstrom resolution was achieved for all ten structures. Notably, the workflow from sample preparation to structure solution can be completed within an hour time frame using only micrograms of materials. These results demonstrate the versatility and practicality of SerialED as a routine tool for high resolution structure determination of nanocrystals at room temperature, overcoming key limitations of existing methods.

papers.title: Red-Emitting Polyene-Substituted 3-Hydroxyflavones: Interplay of Extended π-Conjugation and Electron Withdrawing Aldehyde Moiety
papers.abstract: 3-Hydroxyflavones (3HFs) are highly sensitive fluorescent probes whose dual emission properties are governed by the Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer (ESIPT) mechanism. Tuning their photophysical properties through extended π-conjugation and electron-withdrawing substituents is important for developing advanced ratiometric sensors. In this study, we designed and characterized a series of novel 3HF derivatives featuring polyenic aldehyde moieties conjugated to the C4' position of the B-ring. The photophysical behavior and photo-induced acid-base properties of these dyes were investigated using UV-vis absorption and fluorescence spectroscopy, complemented by TD-DFT calculations. Experimental results show that extending the polyene chain induces a progressive bathochromic shift. TD-DFT reveals strong intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) connected with a reduced HOMO-LUMO energy gap. Crucially, excited-state IR calculations and Non-Covalent Interaction (NCI) analyses prove that increasing the polyene chain length systematically weakens the intramolecular hydrogen bond (IHB). Consequently, potential energy curve (PEC) scans reveal a proportional increase in the ESIPT activation barrier, providing a fundamental basis for the highly solvent-dependent dual fluorescence profiles detected experimentally. Ultimately, these findings show the potential of utilizing polyene-extended 3HFs as highly environment-sensitive, red-emitting ratiometric probes for a variety of biomedical applications.

papers.title: Tuning the electronic properties of defect-rich MoS2
papers.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), including molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ), have emerged as a promising candidate for novel semiconducting devices. However, in many cases structural defects significantly affect the electronic properties of the material. We study interfaces between defect-rich MoS 2 and perfluorinated cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPcF 16 ) using angle resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES) and surface sensitive core level spectroscopy (SXPS, XAS) utilizing synchrotron radiation. Defects were introduced in synthetic MoS 2 bulk crystals by gentle argon and neon sputtering. Although the band structure is still visible after sputtering, especially SXPS reveals structural and electronic disturbances of the topmost MoS 2 layer. We show how the Fermi energy in such defect-rich MoS 2 can be tuned by the subsequent deposition of CoPcF 16 , possibly due to complex charge rearrangements.

papers.title: AutoNanoShape: Automated Nanocrystal Shape Prediction with Active-Learned Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: A fundamental understanding of nanocrystal morphology is essential for predicting and controlling materials behavior in experimentally unexplored growth environments. Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer a promising route to accelerate morphology prediction by enabling efficient sampling of large configurational space at approaching firstprinciples accuracy, but their practical use to reactive nanocrystal materials remains limited due to uncertain transferability and poorly defined training-data requirements. To address these challenges, we present the AutoNanoShape framework, which combines stepwise global and local sampling with iterative first-principles refinement to develop data-efficient MLIPs for oxide surface and nanocrystal morphology prediction. AutoNanoShape achieves surface free energy accuracies with an MAE of ∼0.1 J/m2, enabling prediction of nanocrystal morphologies for the mineral oxide systems studied here across growth environments ranging from ambient to extreme conditions. We further find that training on surfaces with higher adsorbate coverages transfers more effectively to surfaces with lower adsorbate coverages than the reverse. AutoNanoShape reduces the number of first-principles calculations by∼90% compared to brute-force sampling. The resulting workflow also provides practical guidance for dataset construction, including approximate training-set sizes for both de novo model development and fine-tuning, offering a general strategy for efficient MLIP development in reactive nanocrystal systems.

papers.title: (Hetero)adamantane synthesis: A triple alkylation reaction
papers.abstract: (Hetero)adamantanes containing tetrel bridgeheads are important structures in surface and chemical sciences. Syntheses of diamondoid structures generally occur in a linear fashion, often using harsh conditions. These limitations make it difficult to access diverse (hetero)adamantane-based molecules with interchangeable functional groups for broad applications. The discovery of an expedient and convergent methodology for the synthesis of diamondoid scaffolds is described. The convenient synthetic route proceeding via a triple alkylation reaction represents a breakthrough in accessing the adamantane molecular class. Applications of this transformation to diamondoid tripods containing tetrel bridgeheads (C- and Ge-) were explored.

papers.title: Quantifying the Synergistic and Antagonistic Effects of Metal–Organic Complexation on Aerosol Oxidative Potential via Redox Kinetics
papers.abstract: Oxidative potential (OP) is an indicator of the ability of redox-active species (e.g., transition metals) in aerosols to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) and induce oxidative stress. Previous studies have reported synergistic and antagonistic effects on OP in mixtures of metals and non-redox-active organics. These effects have been attributed to changes in redox potential associated with complexation; however, the quantitative validity of this hypothesis remains unclear. In this study, we evaluated this mechanism using a chemical equilibrium–kinetic model of DTT assay (CEK-DTT model) for Fe–oxalate systems. Complexation-induced changes in redox potential and rate constants were derived from Marcus theory and incorporated into the model. Experiments showed no clear synergistic or antagonistic effects at oxalate-to-Fe ratios up to several tens, whereas increasing the ratio led from strong antagonistic to strong synergistic effects. The model partially reproduced these trends, revealing that the former arises from enhanced Fe(II) reduction rate constants offset by an equilibrium shift toward Fe(III), whereas the latter arises from an increased fraction of inert Fe(III)–(oxalate)3 suppressing DTT oxidation. However, the strong synergistic effect was not reproduced, suggesting missing mechanisms in the model. These findings contribute to the understanding of non-additive OP effects and aerosol toxicity.

papers.title: Towards halogen bonding MOFs: networking with a polyiodinated and perfluorinated terphenyl ligand and divalent zinc
papers.abstract: While halogen bonding has been employed for the construction of organic frameworks, no metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with additional halogen bonding functionality are known to date. Here, we present a suitable ligand for such systems, which combines a polyiodinated and -fluorinated terphenyl core with two carboxyl groups for metal coordination. Depending on the crystallization conditions, the ligand assembles with bivalent zinc cations into three distinct crystalline systems, either: (i) a metal-containing hydrogen-bonded organic framework; (ii) a MOF; or (iii) one-dimensional metal-organic chains with intermolecular halogen bonding and hydrogen bonding between adjacent chains. The 1D chains (iii) are obtained when using carbon disulfide as the crystallization medium, underscoring the potential of uncommon solvents in the design of structurally diverse crystalline materials formed from different supramolecular interactions. This study showcases the role of noncovalent interactions and halogen chemistry in directing crystal packing and highlights the challenges associated with the preparation of porous halogen bonding MOFs.

papers.title: Overcoming Axial‑Chirality Bottleneck in Automated Intermediate Generation for Machine‑Learning Applications
papers.abstract: Machine‑learning (ML) models for predicting chemical reactivity and enantioselectivity increasingly depend on large molecular datasets, yet commonly employed representations remain enantiomer‑blind and fail to resolve stereochemically distinct intermediates. This limitation is particularly severe for transition‑metal catalysis involving axially chiral ligands, where subtle three‑dimensional structural differences control enantioselectivity but are systematically lost in graph‑based and SMILES‑derived encodings. Here, we present an automated pipeline that constructs stereochemically faithful three-dimensional intermediates bearing axially chiral ligands directly from standard two-dimensional inputs. SMARTS-based scaffold recognition combined with dihedral-controlled chirality enforcement generates well-defined axial configurations across diverse ligand families, including bipyridine, biimidazole, BINOL, and spiro frameworks. Reaction-specific geometric templates then assemble these into chemically informed intermediates, yielding a workflow that is straightforwardly extensible across catalytic systems. As a proof of concept, this workflow was applied to generate a dataset of 135 chiral Cu(I)-carbene complexes spanning diverse axially chiral ligand families — from single-axis biphenyl and bipyridine systems to the stereochemically demanding dual-axis biimidazole and spiro frameworks. The complexes were optimized using the GFN2-xTB semiempirical method, and manual inspection of all geometries confirmed that the enforced axial configurations were fully preserved throughout. The optimized structures were subsequently benchmarked against DFT references to assess structural fidelity. Chirality‑defining dihedral angles, ligand bite angles, and steric descriptors show near‑quantitative agreement with DFT, while observed electronic discrepancies reflect known semiempirical limitations rather than structural errors. Requiring less than 0.1% of the computational cost of ab initio workflows, this approach enables scalable generation of chirality‑complete three‑dimensional intermediates and supports their storage using CXSMILES. By resolving a critical stereochemical bottleneck, this work lays the foundation for geometry‑enhanced ML models capable of distinguishing enantiomeric/diastereomeric catalytic intermediates and learning structure–enantioselectivity relationships with chemical fidelity.

papers.title: Targeting the SARS-CoV-2 Non-Structural Proteome: A Blueprint for Next-Generation Small-Molecule Coronavirus Antivirals
papers.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 non-structural proteome remains the most clinically validated and strategically important landscape for direct-acting small-molecule antiviral drug discovery. The success of inhibitors targeting the main protease (Mpro, Nsp5) and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp, Nsp12) has firmly established viral replication enzymes as tractable, druggable, and therapeutically relevant targets, while setting clear benchmarks for translational antiviral development. Building on this foundation, a second wave of non-structural protein (Nsp) targets has emerged with increasing translational promise, including the papain-like protease (PLpro), the bi-functional Nsp14 proofreading and capping machinery, Nsp16 2′-O-methyltransferase, Nsp13 helicase, and Nsp15 endoribonuclease. In parallel, additional components such as Nsp1 and the Mac1 domain of Nsp3 continue to expand the antiviral design space, although they remain at earlier stages of chemical validation. In this review, we comprehensively assess SARS-CoV-2 non-structural proteins through a medicinal chemistry and translational lens, with an emphasis on structural tractability, mechanism of action, quality of chemical matter, cellular and in vivo antiviral evidence, evolutionary conservation, resistance liabilities, and developability. Particular attention is given to the features that distinguish tool compounds from genuinely actionable leads and to the opportunities for rational combination regimens that extend beyond first-generation protease- and polymerase-centred therapy. Collectively, the non-structural proteome offers the strongest foundation for next-generation and potentially broader-spectrum coronavirus antivirals with improved resilience to viral evolution.

papers.title: Circular Stereo Algorithm and Fingerprint for Chiral Resonance Invariant Molecular Representation
papers.abstract: Algorithmic molecular fingerprints remain attractive for high-throughput chemoinformatics because they are fast, discrete, and easy to integrate into screening, similarity search, and machine-learning workflows. However, widely used circular fingerprints such as ECFP rely on conventional molecular graph representations that capture stereochemistry incompletely and may distinguish chemically equivalent resonance forms through localized atom charges and bond-order-dependent encodings. Here, we introduce the Circular Stereo Algorithm (CSA) and the derived Circular Stereo Fingerprint (CSFP), a stereochemically informed, resonance-invariant extension of circular graph refinement built on the StereoMolGraph representation.[Papusha and Leonhard, J. Chem. Inf. Model, 2026, 66, 7, 3830] In this framework, stereochemistry is encoded through local stereodescriptors grounded in group theory, allowing atom-centered and bond-centered stereochemical information to be incorporated directly while avoiding artificial distinctions between resonance structures. We show that CSA yields locally consistent atom invariants for stereoisomers, preserves equivalence across resonance forms, and discriminates challenging stereochemical cases, including delocalized radicals and metal complexes. Compared with ECFP on stereoisomer datasets, CSFP produces less over-discriminating atom identifiers and a more reliable mapping between subgraphs and fingerprints. Evaluation on 1.4 million ChEMBL small molecules shows a low color-refinement-hash collision rate of 0.1%, with remaining ambiguities resolvable by exact StereoMol-Graph isomorphism. We showcase how its mathematical properties make it suitable for substructure search on large-scale datasets.

papers.title: Linking faradaic efficiency for oxygen evolution to water oxidation reaction order on hematite photoanodes
papers.abstract: Water oxidation on metal-oxide (photo)anodes is typically assumed to yield molecular oxygen. Here, we combine operando mass-spectroscopy oxygen detection with spectroelectrochemical rate-law analyses to directly link oxygen evolution selectivity to surface holes density on hematite photoanodes. At low current and hole densities, where first-order kinetics dominate, only a small fraction of the extracted charge produces molecular oxygen, indicating that isolated single-hole water oxidation is unable to drive oxygen evolution. As the surface-hole population increases, the Faradaic efficiency for oxygen evolution rises sharply and approaches a plateau coinciding with the emergence of cooperative third-order kinetics. Quantitative data analysis indicates that oxygen evolution exclusively follows the multihole pathway. Equivalent kinetic and Faradaic efficiency behaviour is also observed for purely electrochemical water oxidation on the same hematite samples, demonstrating that cooperative multihole chemistry is the intrinsic mechanism governing the oxygen evolution reaction on hematite and likely represents a general feature of metal-oxide catalysts.

papers.title: Modeling of CO2/CH4 Mixture Adsorption in Flexible Mg-MOF-74 via Machine-Learned Potentials
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), particularly Mg-MOF-74 with open metal sites, offer a promising platform for the selective adsorption of CO2 over CH4. However, accurately modeling multicomponent gas adsorption in flexible frameworks remains challenging. In this work, we developed a fragment-based machine-learned potential (MLP) trained on high-level density functional theory data (PBE-D4/def2-TZVP) to describe all intramolecular and intermolecular interactions between the components of CO2/CH4 mixture and Mg-MOF-74. By integrating this MLP with a combined molecular dynamic-grand canonical Monte Carlo (MD-GCMC) hybrid scheme, we captured both framework flexibility and adsorption thermodynamics, enabling simulations of competitive adsorption and diffusion in multicomponent systems. Our results demonstrate that fragment-based MLPs can accurately represent binary gas mixtures in MOFs and reveal the critical role of framework flexibility in governing adsorption and transport behavior.

papers.title: Involving Value Chain actors in Safe and Sustainable by Design: Application of a Scoping approach to develop PFAS-free Durable Water Repellent coating for textiles
papers.abstract: The revised Safe and Sustainable by Design framework defines Scoping as an entry point, but a process based methodology to implement Scoping is missing. We develop an SSbD Scoping methodology that involves value chain actors and experts applied to early development of PFAS-free Durable Water repellent textile coating. The PFAS free DWR coating offers potential environmental and human health benefits by eliminating persistent PFAS compounds, reducing occupational exposure, and opening pathways for improved end-of-life management. We present a structured approach to identifying the SSbD aspects of chemical and material innovations in their early stages. It facilitates the identification of safety, sustainability and functional considerations before detailed assessment, using a combination of stakeholder engagement, lifecycle thinking and iterative analysis. Through our approach we explicitly address challenges of trust and team building, time and resource efficiency, defining product application in early innovation, and protecting intellectual property and confidential business information.

papers.title: Augmented Reality for Exploring Reaction Networks and Potential Energy Surfaces in Chemical Education
papers.abstract: Chemistry students are required to understand abstract and structurally complex concepts such as high-dimensional potential energy surfaces (PESs) and densely connected chemical reaction networks (CRNs). In teaching, these systems are usually reduced to textbook figures or screen-based visualizations, which necessarily simplify their spatial and topological structure. This can hinder students’ ability to recognize transition states as saddle points and make it difficult to maintain an overview of complex network connectivity. We designed and implemented an augmented reality (AR) teaching unit in a Master-level chemistry course in which PESs and CRNs are treated as shared, navigable three-dimensional learning objects. The unit extends existing computational coursework through two guided activities, namely exploring model PES as room-scale energy landscapes and navigating a literature-based pentane oxidation mechanism to identify branching pathways and temperature-dependent radical formation routes. An exploratory classroom evaluation (N = 9) combined learningrelated self-assessment with established measures of usability (inspired by the system usability scale SUS), perceived workload (NASA-TLX), and simulator comfort (SSQ items). Students reported the strongest perceived benefits for CRN-related outcomes, particularly understanding connectivity and collaborative discussion supported by a shared spatial reference. Reported gains for PES interpretation were positive but more moderate. Usability ratings indicated that the system could be learned quickly, while workload and eye strain highlighted practical constraints for session duration and onboarding. These results suggest that collaborative AR can complement conventional computational instruction by supporting structural and system-level sense-making for complex reactivity representations, especially when learning relies on discussion and shared interpretation.

papers.title: Ab Initio Unit Cell Determination from Randomly Oriented Electron Diffraction Patterns
papers.abstract: Electron crystallography enables the structural characterization of nanocrystals insufficient for X-ray diffraction; however, ab initio unit cell determination from single diffraction snapshots remains a significant challenge due to the lack of three-dimensional information encoded in planar Ewald sphere slices. While crystal rotation methods can recover this information, they are often unsuitable for beam-sensitive materials, necessitating the use of serial electron diffraction (SerialED) to distribute radiation dose across randomly oriented crystals. Here, we present a robust computational approach and open-source software suite for deriving unit cell parameters from randomly oriented electron diffraction patterns without prior symmetry knowledge. The workflow extracts geometric "facets"—defined by the shortest reciprocal lattice vectors—from individual patterns and utilizes a hybrid global optimization strategy to minimize the geometric discre=pancy between experimental data and a theoretical 3D lattice. The algorithm was rigorously validated against a diverse set of materials spanning cubic, rhombohedral, tetragonal, orthorhombic, and monoclinic systems, ranging from metal-organic frameworks and inorganic compounds to organic pharmaceuticals and biological macromolecules, successfully recovering the correct lattice metrics in all cases. We demonstrate that the method is highly efficient, capable of solving unit cells from as few as 1–6 patterns when symmetry is constrained, or 8–12 patterns for fully unconstrained triclinic searches. This tool streamlines the initial stages of the SerialED pipeline, facilitating the structural analysis of novel, beam-sensitive nanocrystalline materials.

papers.title: One Blob to Rule Them All: A Universal Dual-Topology Nonequilibrium Framework for Relative and Absolute Binding Free Energies via a Lennard-Jones Blob Reference
papers.abstract: Single-topology free energy perturbation (FEP) methods, while accurate for congeneric series, require chemical similarity between ligands, bespoke perturbation networks, and offer no direct route to absolute binding free energies (ABFEs). Here we introduce DT-NE-Alchemy, a dual-topology nonequilibrium (NE) framework that eliminates these constraints through a universal Lennard-Jones (LJ) blob reference state. The LJ blob—a minimal, rigid molecule (as small as a single LJ particle) designed to fit the binding pocket—serves as a common anchor for alchemical transformations. Relative binding free energies between any two ligands are obtained by two-edge transformations L i → blob → L j , yielding all n(n− 1)/2 pairwise values from only n blob-based calculations. Crucially, ABFEs follow directly as ∆Gblob +∆G blob →L i , converting the long-sought ”holy grail” of computational drug design into a practical reality. Applied to 16 MCL-1 ligands spanning indole, benzothiophene, and benzofuran scaffolds, the method achieves Pearson correlations up to 0.88, Kendall τ up to 0.80, and mean unsigned errors of 1.2-1.5 kcal/mol for 120 relative pairs. The methodology delivers credible, tunable confidence intervals directly from BAR analysis-controllable via switching time τ and trajectory count N, without costly replicate simulations. All computational tasks are embarrassingly parallel, perfectly aligned with leadership-class HPC systems. DT-NE-Alchemy is program-agnostic, automatable, and poised to replace FEP+ as the workhorse for scalable, physically grounded binding free energy calculations in AI-driven drug discovery.

papers.title: Organocatalyzed Transesterification of Acrylates: Mechanistic Investigation to its Limitations
papers.abstract: Motivated by in-situ transesterification by the 1,2-diols (glycol, 1,2-propanediol and glycerol) used as H-bond donors in our previous work, we intended to study the process. Literature search revealed the lack of report of such amine catalyzed transesterification protocols. Additionally, ester motifs have been known for their synthetic application in the polymer industry. By tuning these motifs, we might be able to achieve an array of such prototypes for industrial application. Herein, we attempted to design an array of acrylate derivatives using transesterification of methyl acrylate with various alcohols catalysed by amine organocatalyst. This work focuses on the transesterification of acrylate, with both monools and diols as nucleophiles.

papers.title: PSA-GUI: a Windows-based Graphical User Interface for the Projected Superposition Approximation Collision Cross Section Calculation
papers.abstract: The structural analysis of biological molecules from ion mobility/mass spectrometry (IM/MS) experiments requires the comparison of measured collision cross sections with theoretical models. The key step for this purpose is the calculation of collision cross section for the theoretical models. Multiple methodologies have been established, including the Projected Superposition Approximation (PSA) method. In this study, we introduce a Windows-based Graphical User Interface, called PSA-GUI, for PSA calculation leveraging the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) feature of the Windows Operating System that makes it convenient for users to utilize PSA, offering enhanced accessibility and a broader range of options comparing to current implementations of PSA calculation.

papers.title: Identifying Cryptic Binding Sites with Mixed Solvent MD Simulation and SiteMap
papers.abstract: A comprehensive study was conducted to address the challenge of identifying cryptic binding sites in proteins, which are crucial for structure-based drug discovery but are often not apparent in apo protein structures. We developed and validated a novel "induce and identify" workflow that integrates mixed solvent molecular dynamics (MxMD) simulations with SiteMap. This approach leverages MxMD sampling of protein conformations to expose hidden pockets, which are then effectively identified and ranked by SiteMap. Using a challenging dataset of 65 cryptic binding sites, the developed workflow identified the cryptic binding site within the top 5 predictions in 78.5% of cases. We believe the proposed MxMD + SiteMap workflow offers a robust and valuable tool for early-phase drug discovery, enabling the exploration of a broader range of druggable targets by effectively inducing and identifying cryptic binding sites.

papers.title: Multi-task scheduling of self-driving laboratories under scientific constraints
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) integrate automation, robotics, and artificial intelligence to autonomously execute scientific experiments. As SDLs evolve toward concurrent multi-task execution and support for heterogeneous experiments, experimental scheduling becomes a critical decision-making layer, determining the temporal order and execution timing of operations under strict scientific constraints, including operation precedence, station allocation, batch processing, experimental parameters, and critically, time synchronization between consecutive operations. For example, in inorganic synthesis, temporal deviations during nucleation can fundamentally alter material properties. While SDLs offer a promising route toward accelerated discovery, the absence of explicit scheduling for concurrent experiments leads to resource conflicts and uncontrolled interruptions. These deviations undermine the reproducibility and data quality essential for artificial intelligence modeling. Here, we present a multi-task scheduling algorithm that jointly accounts for scientific constraints. We integrated this algorithm into an SDL using a closed-loop communication architecture that enables tight coordination between scheduling and robotic experiment execution. The algorithm was validated through the concurrent multi-task synthesis of gold nanoparticles and metal-organic frameworks, distinct chemical reactions governed by nucleation and growth kinetics. By synchronizing robotic operations with experimental stations as well as chemical workflow, the algorithm preserves chemical fidelity and ensures consistent material quality across concurrent multi-task executions, unattainable with a conventional scheduling algorithm that does not adequately account for scientific constraints. This paradigm establishes a practical scheduling framework for concurrent multitasking in SDLs, ensuring the experimental consistency required to generate the high-fidelity datasets foundational to autonomous, AI-driven scientific discovery.

papers.title: Why We Must Break the World
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is entering materials science and manufacturing at a moment when retrieval is often mistaken for discovery. We argue that models trained to optimize plausibility within a closed theoretical system are structurally biased toward interpolation and away from the anomalies from which scientific revolutions arise. In materials and manufacturing, this limitation becomes acute because the design space is combinatorial, multiscale, and physically constrained. What is needed is not another assistant for summarizing what is already known, but systems that can assemble compositional world models, invert the forward problem, falsify their own principles, and test those principles against simulation and fabrication. Drawing on recent work in graph-native reasoning, inverse protein design, multi-agent scientific discovery, and AI-integrated manufacturing, we outline an architecture for discovery built on three coupled capabilities: world-model construction, adversarial falsification, and physical grounding. We make this architecture operational through a minimum-description-length gate: a proposed world-model break is accepted only when the revised model encodes the accumulated evidence in fewer bits than the model it replaces. We illustrate the loop with a residue-level protein-mechanics case study in which a Breaker-Builder agent system revises a symbolic graph model of crystallographic B-factor data through accepted, rejected, and retracted hypotheses. The central claim is that materials innovation will accelerate when AI moves beyond retrieval and surrogate prediction toward systems that can generate, challenge, and physically realize new hypotheses. In that sense, discovery requires breaking the current world model in order to build the next one.

papers.title: Achieving a Scalable Machine Learning Workflow for Crystal Structure Discovery with Experimental Validations
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) has become a central component of data-driven materials discovery, yet its practical impact remains heavily dependent on how these predictions are translated into experimentally-realizable outcomes. In this review, we examine ML-guided crystal structure discovery through the lens of recommendation as well as unconstrained generation, to emphasize interpretable workflows embedding chemical intuition, physical constraints, and experimental validation. Surveying standalone ML, hybrid ML-DFT, and machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) approaches, we highlight how constrained design spaces, data preprocessing, and validation strategies shape novel discovery success. Drawing on our own experimentally-validated case studies, ranging from supervised and unsupervised learning, as well as recommendation-type explorations, we outline the shift towards interpretable and explainable ML models guiding synthetic decisions and thus revealing trends otherwise previously confirming established trends while uncovering new ones. Collectively, we highlight the results of interpretable ML being more effective when deployed within experimental workflows to bridge learning and chemistry, to enable a reliable discovery pathway of solid state materials.

papers.title: Photochemistry of the Energy-Storing Isomer of a Norbornadiene-Based Molecular Switch: Ring Opening, Rehybridized Intramolecular Charge Transfer, and Isomerization into a Carbene Photoproduct
papers.abstract: Photoswitches based on the norbornadiene-quadricyclane (NBD-QC) isomer pair capture solar energy by undergoing the NBD→QC photoisomerization reaction. The energy-storing QC isomer contains two highly strained three-membered rings, which implies that it may be susceptible to photodegradation through exposure to the ultraviolet (UV) component of sunlight. In the present study, we use nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the UV-induced photochemistry of the QC isomer of a representative NBD-QC photoswitch with a push-pull substitution motif. A pattern recognition algorithm is employed to analyze and systematize the simulation results. We find that the predominant outcome of UV absorption, observed in 75 out of the 100 simulated trajectories, is the opening of the four-membered ring which belongs to the QC moiety, although in about half of the trajectories which follow this relaxation pathway, the ring promptly closes again. However, in a small fraction of trajectories, the QC moiety instead breaks up, leading to the formation of a carbene photoproduct. We hypothesize that that the breakup of the QC moiety is the first step in a reaction pathway which leads to the decomposition of the photoswitch.

papers.title: Coupling Nanoscale Viscoelastic Measurements and Infrared Heating of Polymers with AFM-IR
papers.abstract: In heterogeneous polymer systems, the viscoelastic response of polymers around interfaces or with nanostructured morphology may deviate from bulk values. However, current measurement techniques tend to mask these local variations, which are crucial for understanding and developing these materials. Coupling the high spatial resolution of atomic force microscopy (AFM) with dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) offers an avenue to circumvent this limitation. We previously demonstrated the advantages of using a focused infrared (IR) laser on an AFM-IR system to locally heat a sample during nanomechanical measurements, with heating modulated by varying the IR repetition rate. [1] Herein, we present a brief demonstration of coupling nDMA with our previously demonstrated chemistry-selective IR heating. We first measured the storage and loss modulus of poly(propylene glycol) (PPG)-4,4′-methylenebis(phenyl urea) (MPU) at varying IR repetition rates, demonstrating a viscoelastic modulus response with typical heating characteristics upon crossing the glass transition temperature. We further demonstrated stress relaxation of an enaminelinked vitrimer possessing significant bond dynamicity at elevated temperatures. Overall, this method is in the preliminary stages of development, and this working paper aims to serve as a basis for feedback and discussion.

papers.title: Circularly Polarised Luminescence (CPL) as a Contingency Assay for ‘Mirror Life’ Bio-Hazards
GEMDAT: A Python Toolkit for Site-Resolved Diffusion Analysis in Solid-State Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations have become essential for understanding diffusion mechanisms in solid-state materials such as ionic conductors, fuel cells, and gas sensors, yet most existing studies and software tools extract only standard metrics, leaving much of the information contained in the trajectories unused. Here we introduce GEMDAT, a user-friendly Python toolkit for site-resolved diffusion analysis of MD simulations of solid-state materials ( https://github.com/GEMDAT-repos/GEMDAT ). Beyond mean squared displacements, radial distribution functions, and Arrhenius-based activation energies, GEMDAT provides jump rates, attempt frequencies, site-specific activation energies, rotational diffusion, and percolation. Our tool provides access to vibrational amplitudes, site geometries, and site occupancies — quantities that are also directly comparable to experimental diffraction data. Migration sites can be defined manually or identified automatically from the trajectory. A built-in caching approach, together with rapid visualization capabilities, makes the workflow fast and interactive. We demonstrate GEMDAT on a series of case studies involving crystalline Li- and Na-ion conductors, plastic crystals, amorphous structures, and surface configurations, showing how the code extracts atomic-level structural features and connects them to macroscopic transport properties, thereby guiding the optimization and development of solid-state materials.

papers.title: Redox Regulated Non–Volatility Switching in Single Nanopipette Memory–Diodes
papers.abstract: Nanofluidic memory devices featuring brain-mimicking functions could mitigate von Neumann architecture limitations, but long-term memory and controllable volatility-nonvolatility state-switching which is foundational for higher-order complexity functions remain challenging to establish. By integrating redox polymer PEDOT:PSS into single nanopipette diodes with memristor properties, hysteretic ion transport is regulated by coupled electron transfers which switch nanotip conductivity by hundred folds. Electrochemical oxidation and reduction of PEDOT lock in different nanotip conductivity states, accompanied by periodic bursting and chaotic switching behaviors. Reversible volatile and nonvolatile rectified memory effects are controlled by low electric potential: redox-regulated conductivity state changes in long-term; and pulse train or potential sweeping stimulated short-term memory effects. Integrating gate controls in three-terminal transistors into two-terminal memristor-diodes constitutes a generalizable design principle for advancing iontronics and neuromorphic computing capabilities.

papers.title: Computing Nucleation Rates from Confined Equilibria: The Critical Cluster Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: Nucleation is a fundamental step in the formation of new materials, with rates governing phase transition pathways and outcomes that influence material properties across chemistry, physics and biology. Nevertheless, extracting nucleation rates remains challenging: experiments are limited by the microscopic length scales involved, while molecular simulations are hindered by the rare-event nature of nucleation and the large system sizes required to sample low-supersaturation regimes typical of experiments and industrial processing. Here, we introduce a thermodynamic framework that demonstrates the fundamental equivalence between stable clusters in small, closed systems and critical clusters in open systems. The current work has employed this relation to determine the driving forces and rates for nucleation across an extensive range of supersaturations S, including homogeneous nucleation of argon liquids from vapours (Sargon ∈ [2, 20]) and the more complex nucleation of crystals from multi-component solutions containing ions and water (SNaCl ∈ [1.5, 4]). This has been achieved using a small number of brute-force, finite-size simulations where cluster size statistics and monomer exchange dynamics in the steady-state map directly onto critical clusters in macroscopic systems. By combining this Critical Cluster Equivalence Principle with the computational approach developed here, the current investigation has obtained nucleation rates in excellent agreement with experiments and enhanced sampling simulations. This approach provides a unified and generalizable tool for predicting nucleation rates with minimal computational effort, enabling routine application across a wide range of material systems.

papers.title: ∆-Machine Learning for LC-DFT-level Excitation Energies of Bacteriochlorophyll Molecules in a LH2 Complex
papers.abstract: Bacteriochlorophyll (BChl) molecules are the key pigments in the light-harvesting complex 2 (LH2) of purple bacteria, driving solar energy conversion. During this process, fluctuations in excitation energies of the pigments at ultrafast timescales, modulated by the surrounding protein environment, govern the excitation dynamics within the complex. Because of the relatively large size of these molecules with 85 atoms and their complex electronic structure, these energy fluctuations have so far been estimated using semi-empirical methods or low-level time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT). In this work, we introduce a ∆-machine learning protocol to predict excitation energies at the computationally demanding long-range-corrected (LC) TD-DFT level within a quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) framework, using a semi-empirical tight-binding analogue (TD-LC-DFTB) as a low-cost reference. Excitation energies for 7.2 million BChl geometries from trajectories of the LH2 complex of Rs. molischianum have been determined at the TD-LC-DFT level, both with and without taking the protein environment into account. Unexpectedly, environmental descriptors did not improve performance, so the final model relies solely on molecular descriptors. The resulting LC-DFT and machine-learned excitation energy fluctuations yield reorganization energies closer to experiment than those based on LC-DFTB. The transferability across BChl binding pockets within the protein is, however, limited.

papers.title: Second-order kinetic analysis reveals origins of bifunctional enhancement on alloy electro-oxidation catalysts
papers.abstract: Multi-component electrocatalysts provide wide possibilities to tune reactivity, though the fundamental origins of modification, such as electronic perturbation or bifunctionality, are often ambiguous. Here we demonstrate methods to elucidate operative mechanisms on such materials with microkinetic analysis based on generalized degrees of rate control and second-order kinetic observables. CO electro-oxidation kinetics are analyzed on a series of carbon-supported Ag x Pd 100-x alloys to determine apparent CO and OH – reaction orders, and apparent transfer coefficients (inverse Tafel slopes). Each of these kinetic observables (derivatives of rate) varies across operating conditions, providing a rich dataset with second-order dependencies. The analysis reveals that OH – interacts with Ag sites through only partial charge transfer before coupling to Pd-bound CO. Maximum-likelihood fitting of binding energies, corroborated by grand-canonical density functional theory, also supports electronic effects favoring CO-OH coupling. The observation of non-integer charge transfer steps underscores a broader need for rigorous kinetic characterization beyond Tafel slope analysis.

papers.title: Sub-Percent Rotational Constants for Quasi-Linear Molecules from Topology-Based Vibrational Dynamics
papers.abstract: Predicting the A rotational constant of quasi-linear molecules is a long-standing challenge in molecular spectroscopy, as it requires accurate treatment of large-amplitude bending motions that invalidate standard perturbative approaches. We present a topology-based vibrational dynamics method that achieves sub-1% accuracy on A for all four known CHNO/CHNS quasi-linear species (HNCO, HOCN, HCNO, HNCS), requiring only input nuclear coordinates and bond connectivity—no ab initio potential energy surface calculations are performed. The method combines a Hückelderived molecular Hamiltonian with discrete variable representation (DVR) to solve the one-and two-dimensional bending Schrödinger equation directly, complemented by a physics-based out-of-plane gating criterion that selectively applies zero-point vibrational corrections. The entire vibrational dynamics computation runs in <20 ms on a single CPU core. Sensitivity analysis shows that the method retains sub-5% accuracy even with ±2% perturbation of input bond lengths. We report blind predictions of rotational constants and transition frequencies for three as-yet-undetected isomers—HONC, HCNS, and HSNC—to guide laboratory and astronomical searches.

papers.title: Click-Electrochemical Conjugation of Complex Carbohydrates to Protein and Cell Surfaces
papers.abstract: Carbohydrates play essential roles in biology and medicine, yet their direct conjugation to proteins and cell surfaces remains technically challenging. Here we report a broadly applicable electrochemical strategy for the rapid and chemoselective grafting of native and synthetic complex carbohydrates onto proteins and living cells. A bifunctional N-methylluminol (NML) linker bearing a terminal oxyamine was designed to couple unprotected complex carbohydrates at their reducing end. The resulting glycan–NML conjugates undergo electrobioconjugation with solvent-exposed tyrosine residues of the model protein α-chymotrypsinogen A through selective electrooxidation of the NML anchor at ~+800 mV vs. Ag/AgCl. This operationally simple approach proceeds in aqueous buffer under mild conditions and preserves the structural integrity of both protein and glycan partners. Using a model protein, we demonstrate efficient installation of a chemically diverse panel of glycans, including biologically relevant sialylated and tumor-associated epitopes, with retention of lectin-binding specificity. Extending this chemistry to proteins in cell membranes, we achieve high-density, covalent display of millions of carbohydrate ligands per cell within minutes, without compromising viability. Notably, the method enables direct engineering of immune cell surfaces with sialylated ligands that selectively engage SIGLEC-2, a clinically relevant receptor on B lymphocytes and lymphomas. By providing the first electrochemical route to protein and cell-surface pseudo-glycosylation, this work establishes a versatile platform for probing glycan function and for the development of carbohydrate-based therapeutics in immunology, oncology, and vaccination.

papers.title: Targeting SARS-CoV-2 Structural and Accessory Proteins: Emerging Opportunities for Small-Molecule Coronavirus Antivirals
papers.abstract: Although antiviral development against SARS-CoV-2 has been dominated by replication-directed strategies, structural and accessory proteins offer a complementary and increasingly important opportunity for smallmolecule intervention. These proteins control key processes outside the core replication machinery, including viral entry, membrane remodelling, virion assembly, egress, and host immune modulation, thereby expanding the mechanistic scope of antiviral design. However, many of these targets are membrane-associated, oligomeric, conformationally dynamic, or function through protein–protein interactions, creating distinct challenges in target validation, assay design, and chemical optimisation. In this review, we comprehensively and critically evaluate the structural and accessory proteomes of SARS-CoV-2, with a strict focus on small-molecule tractability and translational relevance. We highlight the most credible direct-acting opportunities, focusing on the membrane (M), envelope (E), and nucleocapsid (N) structural proteins, together with the accessory protein ORF3a, for which emerging chemical matter strengthens confidence in druggability. In contrast, Spike (S) and several host-interface accessory proteins, including ORF6, ORF8, ORF9b, and ORF10, are best viewed as more selective or earlier-stage opportunities that require stronger on-target chemical validation. Emphasis is placed on structural accessibility, mechanism-based assay systems, evidence quality, cellular and in vivo activity, and developability constraints relevant to exposure at the infection site. Rather than replacing replication-directed antivirals, these non-canonical targets are best considered adjunctive or complementary components of future combination strategies designed to broaden antiviral coverage, enhance robustness, and improve pandemic preparedness.

papers.title: A General Route to Robust Sequence-Defined Molecular Cavities
papers.abstract: Supramolecular cavities and assemblies have displayed unique catalytic and binding properties, yet the general, controlled positioning of distinct functional groups in synthetic molecular hosts, as achieved in protein binding pockets and active sites, has remained an unsolved challenge due to the high orders of symmetry inherent to classical self-assembly methods employed for such systems. Here, we report a synthetic strategy in which sequence-defined dendrimers, assembled through iterative multi-component reactions, are converted into molecular cages utilizing ring-closing olefin metathesis. We validate this approach by synthesizing a molecular cage featuring nine endohedral and 18 exohedral functional groups, in which one endohedral position is selectively differentiated, thereby providing access to sequence-defined molecular cavities. Overall, our approach offers a general route to robust, unimolecular cages of unprecedented functional complexity in which up to four of the nine endohedral and eight of the 18 exohedral functional group positions can, in principle, be independently controlled.

papers.title: DragonBall: a suite for vibrational spectroscopy with classical trajectories
papers.abstract: One of the most fascinating and key aspects in simulating vibrational spectra is accounting for the anharmonicity of the vibrational motions. The quasi-classical trajectory (QCT) method allows for the computation of fully anharmonic vibrational spectra, using a single trajectory initialized with quantized energy. Unfortunately, the everyday use of QCT requires constant juggling between the different input and output formats of the various quantum chemistry software and the use of different computational and visualization tools among these steps. In this paper, we showcase Dragonball, a modular Python suite that guides the user in each step of the QCT simulation, from guess geometry to final spectrum.

papers.title: A Host-Guest Strategy to Achieve Selective and Robust CO2-to-CO Electrocatalysis in Aqueous Media.
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous materials incorporating molecular catalysts hold strong promise for efficient electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction to value-added products. While activity and selectivity are traditionally tuned through ligand design, increasing attention is being paid to the secondcoordination sphere, which modulates reactivity beyond the metal center. Inspired by enzymatic systems, this outer-sphere environment enhances catalysis through spatial confinement and noncovalent interactions. Here, we report a host-guest strategy to control CO 2 reduction using the [bpyMn(CO) 3 MeCN] + catalyst encapsulated in an anionic cage. When immobilized on electrode surface, the assembly achieves selective CO production. Mechanistic studies indicate that the cage promotes proton-coupled CO 2 binding while preventing catalyst deactivation. This demonstrates that supramolecular second-sphere engineering is a powerful strategy for enhancing electrocatalytic performance and provide a basis for future developments in molecular electrocatalysts.

papers.title: FTO Preferentially Targets Dimethylated Adenosine in Ribosomal RNA
papers.abstract: The fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) is an Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate–dependent dioxygenase. It catalyzes oxidative demethylation of nucleic acid modifications, with reported substrates primarily in mRNA and tRNA. Here, we identified N6,N6-dimethyladenosine (m66A) as a highly efficient substrate of FTO and demonstrated that rRNA is a target of FTO-mediated demethylation. In FTO-deficient cells, m66A levels increased by 68%, compared to 33% for m6A (N6-methyladenosine). Biochemical assays showed that m66A is processed more efficiently than m6A, with catalytic efficiency enhanced by up to 88-fold. Kinetic analysis revealed an intrinsic asymmetry in the demethylation pathway, in which the initial conversion of m66A to m6A is much faster than subsequent demethylation to A, resulting in a biphasic reaction profile. This stepwise behavior suggests that m6A in certain RNA species may arise as an intermediate during the enzymatic turnover of m66A. Comprehensive computational analyses demonstrated that m66A is more effectively oriented and aligned within the FTO active site, improving catalytic geometry and lowering the activation barrier. Together, these findings established rRNA as an FTO target and identified m66A as a novel dimethyl substrate class, linking RNA demethylation to translational regulation.

papers.title: Carbenylative Buchwald-Hartwig Coupling of Aryl Halides, N-Tosylhydrazones, and Anilines
papers.abstract: A Pd/Cu cocatalyzed synthesis of N-benzhydryl amines from aryl halides (electrophiles), N-tosylhydrazones (carbene equivalents), and anilines (nucleophiles) has been developed. The reaction operates under mild conditions and exhibits broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. The synthetic utility of this approach is highlighted by the concise preparation of various drug molecules and their analogues, as well as its integration into downstream derivatizations. The essential role of Cu complexes is unusual for Pd-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling reactions, which usually do not require a cocatalyst for ligand exchange. We propose that this dual catalysis strategy is necessary to control the timing of Pd amido complex formation.

papers.title: A TREN-Based Tripodal Tris(germylene) as a Tridentate Ligand for Mononuclear Copper(I) Complexes
papers.abstract: This study introduces a novel tripodal tris(germylene) 2, stabilized by TREN-tris(aminotroponimine) 1. Compound 2 was synthesized by treating the in situ-generated tri(lithium) salt of compound 1 with GeCl2·(1,4-dioxane). Interestingly, in its reactivity with various carboxylate salts, compound 2 exhibited divergent behavior. The reaction of 2 with sodium acetate and sodium pivalate yielded tris(germylene carboxylates), 3 and 4, respectively. However, 2’s reaction with sodium formate resulted in the unprecedented cationic µ3-oxo-bridged trigermanium derivative 5. It can be considered a hitherto unknown digermylene oxide-stabilized germylene cation, revealing that TREN-based tris(germylenes) can function as tripodal ligands. This aspect is realized in the mononuclear Cu(I) complexes 6 and 7 isolated in the reactions of tris(germylenes) 3 and 4 with CuI, where all three germylenes were coordinated simultaneously with one copper atom, confirming that TREN-based tris(germylene) can indeed function as tripodal ligands. Furthermore, the utility of these copper complexes, 6 and 7, as catalysts in the azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reactions is also demonstrated.

papers.title: Silver-Modulated Copper Dynamics Under Pulsed Tandem Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
papers.abstract: Pulsed electrolysis and Cu-Ag tandem catalysis are both promising strategies for electrochemical CO 2 reduction, yet their interplay remains unclear. Here, we show that pulsed operation does not preserve the as-prepared Cu-Ag catalyst and instead generates a dynamic bimetallic working state in situ. During prolonged electrolysis, the catalyst evolves toward a favorable selectivity profile with significantly increased CO formation, persistent ethylene production, and suppressed hydrogen, methane, and formate pathways. Correlative SEM/EDS, XPS, ToF-SIMS, and ICP-MS show that this behavior arises from Ag-modulated Cu dissolution and redeposition under pulsed conditions. The resulting catalyst develops near-surface Ag enrichment, a topmost catalytically relevant layer containing both Cu and Ag, persistent Cu loss to the electrolyte, and subsurface cavities. Comparison with pure Cu under identical pulsed conditions further shows that Ag redirects the restructuring pathway of Cu toward a distinct Ag-rich yet still Cu-active catalytic state. Under pulsed CO 2 reduction, Ag therefore acts as a tandem component for CO formation and as a regulator of catalyst evolution.

papers.title: Practical, long-life and lean Lithium Metal Batteries: The Critical Role of Li Inventory
papers.abstract: Practical lithium-metal batteries (LMBs) require minimized loss of lithium inventory (LLI) and mitigation of interfacial instability, with these hurdles amplified in lean-Li and anode-free architectures. Although thin Li foils (≤ 20 µm) for battery applications are now becoming commercially available, the optimum Li reservoir for LMBs remains unresolved. Here we examine the interplay between lithium foil thickness (evaluating 0, 5, 10, 20 & 300 µm) and electrolyte chemistry, demonstrating that they jointly govern capacity loss due to LLI. Cryo-milling, imaging and compositional analysis via time-of-flight secondary-ion-mass-spectroscopy reveal that LP57 electrolyte induces porous Li deposits and heterogeneous LiF distributions linked to high LLI (thus favouring thicker Li foil), whereas a dual-salt electrolyte produces dense, uniform Li plating with significantly reduced LLI, enabling high volumetric energy densities associated with thin foils. Thin Li foils in the range 10 - 20 µm provide extremely high volumetric energy density (> 1,100 Wh L-1, stack-level), while maintaining reasonable capacity retention (> 67 % after 100 cycles). Pouch-cell validation under high stack pressure confirms that the interfacial stability of the dual-salt system is preserved in practical formats. These findings provide quantitative links between Li inventory, SEI chemistry, and energy-density optimisation for manufacturable Li-metal and anode-free batteries.

papers.title: Integrating GC–MS and LC–MS through correlation molecular networking to map fermentation chemistry
papers.abstract: Foods are some of the most chemically complex systems, thus presenting a fundamental analytical challenge: their molecular composition is vast, chemically diverse, and continuously evolving. This analytical challenge is especially relevant in fermented foods, where microbial and enzymatic activity drive profound chemical transformation. Mass spectrometry-based metabolomics is among the most powerful tools for characterizing such systems, but multiple platforms are required to comprehensively capture the chemical landscape; in particular, GC-MS is required for detection of volatile and semi-volatile compounds central to flavor and aroma, while LC–MS captures the broader pool of polar and non-volatile molecules. Integrating these complementary views into a unified, interpretable framework remains challenging, particularly when the goal is to connect volatile products with non-volatile precursors across fermentation time. Here, we demonstrate how cross-platform data fusion using correlation molecular networking, combined with large language model-assisted pattern interpretation, can bridge this gap and reveal complex molecular relationships that neither platform could capture alone. As a model system, we explored kimchi as a fermented food enriched in ingredients with a high content of bioactive metabolites. We tracked daily metabolic changes over a seven-day fermentation period by parallel GC–MS and LC–MS/MS profiling. The resulting cross-platform correlation network recovered distinct ingredient-of-origin modules centered on well-annotated GC-MS volatiles, including garlicderived organosulfur compounds, chili and ginger terpenes, and Brassica-associated isothiocyanates, with groupings of largely unannotated LC-MS features organized around these hubs. Positive and negative cross-platform correlations encoded fermentation stage dynamics and identified candidate precursor–product relationships, including the conversion of phenolic acid precursors to volatile phenols and the progressive rearrangement of sulfur-containing compounds. LLM-assisted interpretation was used as a hypothesis-generation aid to capture topological patterns, which were then manually evaluated against chemical annotation, edge-sign distributions, and primary literature. Together, these results establish cross-platform correlation networking as a general strategy for decoding chemically complex, time-evolving food systems, and position AI-assisted network analysis as a scalable tool for hypothesis generation in untargeted metabolomics.

papers.title: Electrostatic gap fields enable inverse design of peptides controlling biomolecular condensates
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates formed by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) organize many intracellular processes, yet there exist still open questions regarding the control on protein condensation. Here we introduce the electrostatic gap field (Δφ), a principle connecting electrostatic landscapes to phase behavior. Analogous to the energy gap stabilizing the native state in protein folding theory, Δφ quantifies the difference in electrostatic potential within the dilute and the condensed phases and defines a bias toward condensation. Using around 5 ms of molecular dynamics simulations of seven intrinsically disordered region (IDR)-containing proteins across diverse interaction environments, we show that independent of the force field and model construction, condensate formation consistently correlates with the emergence of a characteristic Δφ field. Guided by this principle, we design peptides that reproduce the gap field required to stabilize the condensed phase. Opposite-charge analogues perturb the target field. Machine-learning analysis confirms that Δφ encodes a statistically robust signal of condensation. These results establish electrostatic gap fields as a physically interpretable framework for describing, predicting, and engineering the behavior of biomolecular condensates.

papers.title: Machine learning approach to estimate computational cost and distribute resources for a diverse variety of quantum chemical calculations
papers.abstract: This work presents an artificial neural network (ANN) model, Jaguar Timer, which estimates the wall-clock time of quantum chemical calculations–specifically density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) calculations. The ANN model is trained and tested on data generated with the quantum chemical package Jaguar, but the same concept should be applicable to data that originates from any quantum chemical engine. We show that the model is able to predict accurate DFT and TDDFT wall-clock times with over 97% of testing case having an error below 4 times the observed runtime (and 77% having an error below the factor of 2). Jaguar Timer is designed to support a diverse collection of Jaguar job types and input setting choices and is applicable to a very wide range of wall-clock lengths ranging from seconds to days. The model supports all atom types, basis sets, and the vast majority of exchange-correlation functionals available in Jaguar. Additionally, a wide selection of other input settings are supported, including pseudospectral (i.e. semi-numerical) and analytic integrals, spin-restricted and spin-unrestricted determinants, vacuum and implicit solvent simulations, single point energies and geometry optimizations, vibrational frequency calculations, and TDDFT single point or TDDFT geometry optimizations. Jaguar Timer is also capable of estimating wall-clock times of jobs executed in batched mode and jobs that employ multiple CPU cores. The wide scope of the model is its core benefit and significantly broadens the supported job and input types that have been studied in similar works. The model’s generality enables users of Jaguar to predict the length of a given set of jobs within a vast collection of common and advanced application domains. Such predictions empower users to carefully optimize their Jaguar jobs and workflows to reduce overall runtimes. In particular, we show that the Jaguar Timer estimates can be incorporated into a greedy computational resource assignment algorithm to reduce runtimes automatically within a workflow or within job batching.

papers.title: Virus-integrated biogeochemical models for habitability studies of Enceladus, Europa and Titan
papers.abstract: Biogeochemical models have become critical for answering questions about the habitability of ocean worlds, especially that of early Earth. However, when extended to icy moons, experimental biogeochemical models become especially challenging. Due to less constrained physicochemical parameters extrapolated from former flybys, the most comprehensive approaches could combine experimental and computational models of proposed ocean conditions with microbes present. This perspective makes the case for needing 2 to also include viral pathogens in microbial models as a mechanism for maintaining biogeochemical cycling. Viral shunt, or the release and recycling of organic / inorganic matter in aquatic ocean systems via the viral lysis of prokaryotes, has proven to be a critical source of carbon/sulfur/iron cycling throughout Earth’s in our own oceans. Nonetheless, viral shunt remains understudied in the realm of other ocean world astrobiology and habitability studies. The current knowledge of physicochemical conditions on three example ocean worlds (Enceladus, Europa, and Titan) is briefly summarized to contextualize examples of Earth-based integrated archaeal viruses (Pyrobaculum Filamentous Virus, Sulfolobus Turreted Icosahedral Virus, and Methanosarcina Spherical Virus) that may be suitable for habitability studies for virus-integrated biogeochemical ocean world models.

papers.title: Spectroscopic Probes of the MOF Nanoparticle Interphase Region
papers.abstract: Interfacial interactions dictate the performance of materials ranging from membranes and nanopore technologies to battery electrodes and heterogeneous catalysts. Metal-organic framework (MOF) interfaces pose especially difficult analytical challenges due to the chemical complexity of the external surfaces and interior pore spaces. Herein, we present several spectroscopic strategies for probing both interior and exterior microenvironments of MOF particles using common analytical techniques. Mixed-phase NMR experiments reveal peak broadening of 1H, 7Li, 19F, and 31P nuclear resonances originating from confined LiPF6 in electrolyte-soaked MOF particles. Variable-environment UV-vis spectroscopy reveals undercoordinated surface cobalt sites amenable to small-molecule coordination chemistry that can be monitored in situ by vibrational spectroscopy. For quantitative analysis of the Lewis acidity and polarity of these complex surfaces, we demonstrate the utility of fluorescent probe molecules developed for biological systems. Taken together, these insights portray a distinct chemical environment at the external surfaces of MOF particles that resemble the interphase region of intercalation battery electrodes. More broadly, these techniques provide a complementary suite of interface-specific analytical tools for investigating chemically complex microenvironments.

papers.title: Metal-Free Hydrogen Atom Transfer for Direct Thiolation of Hydridic α- C(sp3)−H Bonds
papers.abstract: C–S bonds play a critical role in organic, material, and bioactive molecules, yet methods involving hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) for their preparation remain underdeveloped. We report a rapid and mild method for α-C(sp3)−S bond formation from thiosulfonates using a simple, inexpensive, and modular diaryl ketone catalyst. The diaryl ketone displays a unique triplet excited state that allows it to behave as both the system photocatalyst and HAT agent, obviating the need for a metal cocatalyst. Reaction efficiency enables high yielding product formation with broad functional group generality in as little as 30 minutes under ambient conditions.

papers.title: In Silico Biophysical Screening of Surface Ligands for Enhanced Nanoparticle Mucopermeation
papers.abstract: The mucus layer — a physiologically relevant hydrogel found in the human gut, respiratory and genital tracts, and on ocular surfaces — forms a formidable, highly evolved barrier, with mucin proteins creating its hygroscopic mesh. This barrier restricts the passage of nanomedicines, which tend to adhere to it and undergo recycling. Hydrophilic ligands such as polyethylene glycol, when grafted onto nanoparticles, are known to enhance mucopermeation, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To investigate this, 79 ligands were virtually selected from the ChEMBL and DrugBank databases based on their similarity to triethylene glycol — an analogue of polyethylene glycol — and on Lipinski–Veber oral bioavailability parameters. The ligands were ranked by similarity score (SS), proposed here as a structural bioinformatic parameter for automated ligand‑candidate prioritisation. A final set of 15 ligands was selected — five ligands per tercile. The top tercile, which included triethylene glycol, had the highest SS values. These 15 ligands were docked with the equilibrated MUC5AC protein structure using two different docking programs. For each ligand, the average docking or binding score (depending on the program used) and the average atomic contact energy (mean of the top five atomic contact energies) were calculated. The SS values showed strong correlation with the average atomic contact energies and moderate correlation with both the average docking and binding scores, and with the six Lipinski–Veber parameters. Overall, the SS values and the average atomic contact energy emerged as useful indicators, highlighting their potential value for efficient and accurate surface‑ligand screening in future nanomedical applications.

papers.title: Mask for Individual Sampling of Tidal and Ruminal Gas Contaminated Breath in Dairy Cows
papers.abstract: Standardized breath sampling in dairy cows is essential for health monitoring and emission control. Yet, controlled measurements of and discrimination between tidal and ruminal gas contaminated breath are challenging. Here, we introduce a sampler designed to collect exhaled breath reproducibly from dairy cows. The system integrates pressure regulators and valves to enable normal breathing patterns. Combined real-time monitoring of CH 4 and CO 2 concentrations facilitates distinction and separate collection of tidal versus ruminal gas contaminated breath into sampling bags. A comprehensive system-level validation is performed, including sampler inertness testing toward various volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Also sample stability over 14 days is exemplarily assessed with Supel™-Inert Multi-Layer Foil bags across different concentration ranges. The sampling mask is validated on 31 dairy cows (total 1187 samples) using proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometry to quantify physiologically relevant VOCs, including acetone, ethanol, isoprene, acetic acid, propionic acid and butyric acid. Overall, this sampler provides a robust, extendable solution for livestock breath sampling and characterization.

papers.title: Computational Mapping of Productive POI–E3 Ligase Conformations to Guide De Novo Degrader Design: Application to WEE1 and PKMYT1 PROTACs
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy, yet rational degrader design remains challenged by the dynamic nature of protein of interest (POI)-E3 ligase interactions. While X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM provide valuable structural snapshots, they are insufficient for capturing the conformational heterogeneity underpinning efficient ubiquitination and degradation. Here, we present a unified computational workflow to systematically generate and evaluate POI-E3 ligase conformational states for CRBN- and VHL-mediated proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs). The workflow integrates warhead connectivity analysis, conformational clustering, ubiquitination accessibility assessment and molecular dynamics simulations to identify productive POI-E3 ligase geometries. Analysis of experimental structures revealed that PROTAC linkers do not exceed 15 Å, providing a practical attachment-atom distance based filter for docking-derived models. Furthermore, POI-E3 ligase conformations differing by more than 7.5 Å Cα RMSD exhibited distinct ubiquitination profiles, offering quantitative guidance for defining structurally and functionally divergent states. Experimental ternary complexes consistently positioned one or more solvent-exposed POI lysine residues within 50 Å of the E2 catalytic Cys111, establishing a mechanistically grounded criterion for ubiquitination competence. Validation against 34 experimentally determined PROTAC ternary complexes achieved a 97% recovery rate and identified multiple ubiquitination competent conformations beyond experimental snapshots. The workflow was subsequently applied to model productive WEE1-CRBN and PKMYT1-CRBN conformations, for which no experimental structures are available.
