PROTAC induced-fit docking demonstrated that active PROTACs selectively engage productive POI-E3 ligase geometries with linker-compatible attachment atom distances. Overall, this study provides a quantitative, structure-based framework for guiding the rational design of ubiquitination-based degraders.

papers.title: Improving interdisciplinary research: Ontology and database to structure characteristics of Microplastics (MP)
papers.abstract: Microplastics (MP) are a major environmental pollutant with highly variable properties. They present challenges to society that attract researchers from various disciplines. Important re-search questions include the transport and fate in the environment, the ecological impact and ecotoxicological effects, and the changing properties of MP exposed to different environments. For this question interdisciplinary research is needed which requires a common conceptual approach for discussing MP. Such an ontology connected to a database, that allows interdisciplinary researchers to exchange and harmonize knowledge, is presented here. The ontology structures the key characteristics of MP particles, including particle properties, material properties, parameters of particle degradation, eco-coronas, and biofilms. Additionally, the ontology enables comprehensible and reproducible research through the documentation of manufacturing processes, sample preparation and measurement techniques. A connection to other MP research topics, such as toxicity studies and environmental transport vie unique MP identifiers opens the door to synergistic effects to achieve a deeper understanding of the interplay of MP properties and their behavior and effects.

papers.title: LigandHub: Web-Based Ligand Preparation and Docking Output Recovery Platform
Positron Emission Tomography Reveals the Impact of Polymer Structure of PEG Alternatives on Accelerated Blood Clearance of Liposomes
papers.abstract: Poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) lipids are essential components for lipid-based nanocarriers for drug and gene delivery, providing colloidal stabilization and prolonged circulation upon first administration. However, repeated administrations of PEGylated nanocarriers can trigger accelerated blood clearance (ABC), mediated by anti-PEG antibodies (APAs). To address concerns regarding APA-mediated responses, randomized PEG (rPEG) has recently been introduced. rPEG is a polyether structurally similar to PEG and designed to evade established APAs binding mechanisms. Here, we investigate the in vivo pharmacokinetics of first and second administration of gallium-68-labeled polymer lipid (PL)-liposomes using quantitative, dynamic positron emission tomography (PET) imaging over 90 min, and ex vivo biodistribution. We evaluated a PL library, comprising PEG, rPEG, poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline), poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline), poly(2-methyl-2-oxazine), poly(sarcosine) and poly(N,N-dimethylacrylamide). After the first administration, polymer structure strongly influenced liposome blood pool retention at 90 min. Upon second administration 7 days later, rPEG liposomes, in contrast to all other PL formulations, showed no significant change in pharmacokinetic behavior and retained the highest blood pool activity at 90 min. Consistently, only rPEG showed no increase in protein-associated activity in the plasma protein binding assay, indicating that formation of anti-rPEG antibodies under the conditions of this study is unlikely. Notably, rPEG pharmacokinetics also remained unchanged when mice were pretreated with PEG liposomes. This, together with no quantifiable interactions of APAs with rPEG in the plasma protein binding assay, supports low cross-reactivity between rPEG and APAs in vivo. Overall, our results indicate that the random copolymer design of rPEG offers a promising strategy for preserving pharmacokinetics under repeated-dosing conditions.

papers.title: When Counterions Fall into Place: Alkali Effects on f-Element Phosphomolybdate Crystallization and Speciation
papers.abstract: Effects controlling the speciation and crystallization of f-elements with polyoxomolybdate (POMo) ligands have been scarcely studied compared to the analogous tungstate POMs. Here we investigate polyoxomolybdate complexes with trivalent lanthanides (Ln 3+ ), in solution and solid-state, shedding lights on the complex interplay between the f-elements, POM ligand, and counterions. Alkali counterions play a decisive role in shaping the structure and behavior of POM complexes, including the lanthanide-POMo complexes reported here. A family of Ln(PMo 11 O 39 ) 2 11- compounds with charge-balancing K + and Cs + were synthesized across the lanthanide series, and 16 total structures were characterized by SCXRD, FTIR, and SEM-EDX. Combined solid-state and solution-phase studies enabled direct comparison of structural trends and countercation-dependent solution-state speciation. While potassium analogues exhibit consistent parallel arrangement of POM units in the crystalline lattice, cesium derivatives adopt distinct packing modes, including both parallel and perpendicular orientations. These structural differences are reflected in variations in lattice organization and inter-cluster interactions, highlighting the role of larger alkali cations in directing long-range assembly. Moreover, solution-state 31 P Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) reveal that the countercation (Li + , Na + , K + , Rb + and Cs + studied) directly impacts assembly and thermodynamic equilibria among PMo 11 O 39 7- , Ln(PMo 11 O 39 ) 4- and Ln(PMo 11 O 39 ) 2 11- , prior to crystallization.

papers.title: Incorporating Neural Network in the AMOEBA Polarizable Force Field for Ligand Field Effects of Cu2+ Ion
papers.abstract: Characterizing the solvation of open-shell transition metal ions remains a challenge for classical force fields due to ligand field electronic effects. Here, we present AMOEBA+NN, a machine-learning-augmented polarizable potential, to investigate Cu2+ solvation in NH3 and H2O and mixed environments. The model, trained on quantum-mechanical (QM) association energies, accurately reproduces the Cu2+ energy landscape across diverse coordination geometries. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrate that AMOEBA+NN successfully captures the electronically driven Jahn-Teller (JT) distortion. Evidence from radial distribution functions (RDFs) and geometry optimizations reveals characteristic axial elongation, which is absent in conventional classical descriptions. Kinetic analysis shows a highly dynamic Cu2+-NH3 environment with a rapid ligand exchange (residence time of 66.52 ps), contrasting with the H2O system where binding is two to three orders of magnitude more stable. Furthermore, the calculated hydration free energy of -477.59 ± 0.50 kcal/mol shows excellent agreement with experimental data (within 1.31 kcal/mol). This work provides a unified, computationally efficient framework for describing the structural, dynamic, and thermodynamic observables of transition metal coordination.

papers.title: Precomputed Grid Potential (PGP) Method: Exact Acceleration of Particle Mesh Ewald for
Modeling Water Transport in Prototype Thermal Energy Storage Materials: Potassium Carbonate and Potassium Carbonate Sesquihydrate
papers.abstract: K2CO3 is a promising thermochemical energy storage material due to its ability to absorb and release heat through reversible hydration reactions. Nevertheless, the implementation of K2CO3 and other salts that undergo hydration reactions is constrained by their slow reaction kinetics. Experimentally, these sluggish kinetics are reflected in the existence of a metastable zone near the hydration/dehydration equilibrium line. However, the atomistic mechanisms that limit reaction rates are incompletely understood. Here, first-principles calculations are employed to investigate the thermodynamics and kinetics of hydration and dehydration in bulk K2CO3 and its hydrate, K2CO3 · 1.5 H2O. The energetics and site preferences for water insertion into K2CO3 at the early stages of hydration are predicted, as are the formation energies for water vacancies at the outset of K2CO3 · 1.5 H2O dehydration. In the hydrate, the energetics for water desorption are consistent with experimental observations of a two-step dehydration process. Several water diffusion pathways are explored in the bulk for both the anhydrous and hydrated phases. The calculated free-energy migration barriers reveal that in anhydrous K2CO3 diffusion occurs preferentially along [120] and [120] directions, parallel to the carbonate planes. In the hydrate, vacancymediated water migration is also anisotropic, with the lowest barriers observed for migration within water planes in the [001] direction. The calculated diffusion coefficients suggest that water diffusion in the hydrate is slightly faster than in the salt. In sum, this study provides insights into the atomic scale energetics and mechanisms underlying hydration reactions for thermal energy storage.

papers.title: A Study of Factors Influencing the Selectivity and Batch Reaction Kinetics of Raney(r) Nickel Catalyzed Nitrile Hydrogenation
papers.abstract: In this work, an extensive study was carried out to quantify the effects of various reaction conditions on the rate and selectivity of liquid-phase butyronitrile hydrogenation. In this reaction, butylamine is the desired product, and dibutylamine is produced as an unwanted by-product. Liquid-phase catalytic butyronitrile hydrogenation reactions were carried out in batch reactors at hydrogen pressures from 1–15 atm and at temperatures from 20–75 °C. Methanol was used as a solvent. The stirring speed was set sufficiently high to avoid mass transfer limitations. Experiments were performed using several Raney(r) nickel catalysts: an unpromoted catalyst, Fe promoted catalysts, Cr promoted catalysts, and a Fe and Cr doubly-promoted catalyst. Fe and/or Cr promotion increases the reaction rate while having little impact on the selectivity to primary amine. The effects of adding NaOH, NaCl, and butylamine to the reaction mixture were measured separately. Water was also sometimes added to the reaction mixture (e.g., 50 mL methanol plus 10 mL water for the 1 atm batch reactions). An effective activation energy of 45 kJ/mol was computed for the unpromoted catalyst. Consistent with prior reports, NaOH addition improved the selectivity to butylamine by suppressing the condensation pathway. It was observed that adding NaCl to the reaction mixture improved the selectivity to primary amine. Adsorption experiments showed that butylamine adsorbed on two different site groups. One site group was blocked by added [OH] - , and the other site group was blocked by adsorbed carbon monoxide (CO). We propose and discuss some specific kinetic models as potential explanations for the observed reactivity and selectivity trends.

papers.title: Ru-Doped Single-Atom Alloys for Ammonia Decomposition via First-Principles Simulations
papers.abstract: Ammonia decomposition is an attractive route for on-demand hydrogen production from carbonfree chemicals. However, the rational design of efficient catalysts remains challenging due to intrinsic trade-offs in surface reactivity: catalysts that effectively activate N-H bonds often bind reaction intermediates too strongly, leading to surface poisoning and sluggish product desorption. Ruthenium (Ru) is among the most active metals for this reaction, yet its strong nitrogen adsorption and scarcity limit its practical utilization. Here, we employed first-principles calculations to design single-atom alloys (SAAs), in which isolated Ru atoms are dispersed within 3d-5d transition-metal hosts to maximize the atom efficiency of Ru while potentially improving catalytic reactivity. We first evaluated the thermodynamic stability of various Ru-doped SAAs against dopant aggregation and subsurface segregation. We then systematically investigated the reaction energetics of ammonia decomposition, focusing on the trade-off between ammonia dehydrogenation and the associative desorption of N2 and H2. Thermodynamic screening identified Ru/Fe, Ru/Co, and Ru/Ni SAAs as promising candidates with favorable energetics for associative desorption. Notably, further kinetic analysis revealed that Ru/Fe SAA is highly active for ammonia decomposition, exhibiting reduced barriers for both dehydrogenation and associative desorption compared with pure Ru. In addition, we identified the adsorption energy of atomic nitrogen as an effective descriptor correlating well with catalytic reactivity across the SAAs. This work provides fundamental insights into overcoming catalytic limitations through atomic doping strategies, while demonstrating how SAAs maximize the atomic efficiency of scarce noble metals and guiding the design of more efficient catalysts for ammonia decomposition.

papers.title: The mechanism of visible-light photochemical rearrangements of conjugated amide enolates
papers.abstract: Deprotonation of conjugated amides forms coloured solutions of lithium enolates (trienolates) that absorb light in the visible range of the electromagnetic spectrum. Irradiation of these extended enolates at a suitable wavelength induces a family of skeletal rearrangements, including bond migrations and ring expansions, that proceed through a biradical intermediate. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal that excitation of the extended enolate chromophore promotes homolysis of the C–N bond of the amide via an intersection seam between the S1 and S0 potential energy surfaces. The resulting singlet biradical undergoes rapid recombination to generate rearranged amide products, with regioselectivity governed by the molecular framework. Acyclic trienolates undergo competing [1,3]-, [1,5]-, and [1,7]-migrations, but incorporation of a ring constrains radical recombination resulting in regioselective re-cyclisations. Lack of stereospecificity during the rearrangements, and cyclopropylbenzyl ring openings, coupled with with a lack of cross-reactivity in TEMPO trapping and a crossover experiment, indicate the formation of short-lived, solvent-caged radical pairs rather than freely diffusing radicals. These findings establish a general mechanistic rationalisation of visible-light-driven rearrangements of amide enolates, and suggest that ring topology can be used to control the outcome of the biradical recombinations.

papers.title: PCET-Promoted Photocatalytic Two-Carbon Homologation of Cyclic Alcohols via Wittig Olefination
papers.abstract: A unified strategy to access substituted cycloalkenes through two-carbon homologation of the cycloalkanols is described. A visible-light-driven proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process mediated by an organic dye photocatalyst is sequentially coupled with intramolecular Wittig olefination, affording valuable cycloalkenes from previously unexplored ketone derivatives across a broad substrate scope with excellent yields. The post-synthetic diversification of the products serves as a synthetic handle for the downstream manipulations, thus offering opportunities to build up many complex molecular architectures. Combined experimental studies support a sequential mechanism involving radical ring fragmentation-addition followed by ionic Wittig olefination, affording the desired cycloalkene derivatives.

papers.title: Structure–Property Relationships in Thermoresponsive Fluorescent Polymers: Roles of Size, Composition, and Architecture
papers.abstract: Thermoresponsive fluorescent polymers (TFPs) provide a versatile platform for optical temperature sensing by coupling phase transitions with changes in fluorescence. Here, we report TFPs based on poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) and poly(ethylene glycol methacrylate) (PEGMA), incorporating fluorescein acrylate (FluA) as a model fluorophore via reversible additionfragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) copolymerization. Linear and hyperbranched architectures were synthesized, with different compositions to exhibit cloud point temperatures (Tcp) within a physiologically relevant temperature window. Fluorescence behavior was investigated as a function of temperature, concentration, and pH. Distinct responses were observed across the Tcp, governed by the interplay between polymer collapse, microenvironmental confinement, and chromophorechromophore interactions. PNIPAM and PEGMA systems containing low fluorescein loading exhibited fluorescence enhancement near the Tcp, followed by quenching at higher temperatures, whereas higher loading systems showed predominantly decreased fluorescence intensity upon heating due to increased chromophore-chromophore interactions. Fluorescence intensity was strongly concentration-dependent, highlighting the role of aggregation, and pH studies revealed changes in both fluorescence intensity and emission maxima, with temperature-responsive fluorescence being most prominent at pH 7 and moderately retained at pH 9. Rheological measurements further demonstrated changes in complex viscosity across the Tcp, linking macroscopic behavior to structural transitions. Hyperbranched polymers exhibited distinct fluorescence and rheological responses compared to linear analogues, underscoring the influence of topology. These results establish structure-property relationships that enable tunable fluorescence responses, providing design guidelines for polymer-based optical thermometers.

papers.title: Biophysical Modeling of Stability in Biogenic Silver Nanoparticles Derived from Corn Silk and Onion Extracts: A DLVO-Based Analysis
papers.abstract: Green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) is an alternative to chemical reduction, and a greener method, but one that still lacks the ability to control colloidal stability with precision. The phytochemical matrices of corn silk and onion extracts were used to synthesize AgNPs in this study. The wet-lab characterization through Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) indicated a very well dispersed hydrodynamic diameter of 76.52 nm and a polydispersity index of 0.239, which made the botanical metabolites very well dispersed initially. Nevertheless, electrophoretic light scattering revealed near-zero zeta potential (0.1 + 0.7 mV) which is a sign of extreme thermodynamic instability and quick agglomeration. Computational classical Derjaguin-Landau-Verwey-Overbeek (DLVO) theory was used to explain the biophysical mechanisms that cause this colloidal failure. The interparticle energy landscape was modeled using Python and found the full collapse of the electrostatic double-layer repulsive barrier. Interaction profile proved to be completely dominated by attractive Van der Waals forces (VTotal < 0) providing no thermodynamic obstacle to aggregation. This work offers a powerful, quantitative scheme of the assessment of capping agent failure, which explains the need of the electrostatic modulation in the biogenic production of sub-100 nm metal nanoparticles.

papers.title: Conformational Landscape of 2-Aminopurine-Substituted RNA Oligonucleotides from Machine-Learning-Driven Enhanced Sampling
papers.abstract: Fluorescent base analogs, such as 2-aminopurine (2AP), are frequently used to investigate nucleic acid conformational dynamics, particularly base-stacking interactions, through fluorescence spectroscopy. Although 2AP substitution can induce structural perturbations, properly accounting for these effects enables its use as a probe of complex RNA dynamics. Here, we apply explainable machine-learning-derived surrogate-model collective variables to perform enhanced-sampling simulations that comprehensively explore the free-energy landscapes of both 2AP-substituted and unsubstituted RNA dinucleotides and trinucleotides. Our results show that while 2AP substitution does not significantly alter stacking propensity, it substantially modulates the free energy landscape, leading to a redistribution of populations among stacking modes. The fraction of stacked 2AP conformations closely correlates with experimentally observed "dark state" populations, supporting the hypothesis that base stacking quenches 2AP fluorescence and promotes dark state formation. This work and follow-up studies in larger, physiologically relevant RNA systems will establish the ability to correlate observed emissive or dark states of 2-AP with specific structures within the free-energy landscape.

papers.title: Defect Topology Governs Lithiation Pathways in Graphite Anodes
papers.abstract: The electrochemical behaviour of graphite anodes is strongly affected by structural disorder, yet graphite crystallinity is often described using averaged descriptors that do not resolve the underlying defect landscape. Here, we investigate a series of industrially relevant graphite samples combining high‑resolution synchrotron X‑ray diffraction with FAULTS‑based analysis of planar defects and operando measurements. We show that graphites with similar average crystallographic signatures span distinct defect‑topology regimes defined by different combinations of stacking faults, rhombohedral (3R) intergrowths and turbostratic interlayers. Operando diffraction reveals that lithium insertion does not initiate within an ideal 2H host, but proceeds preferentially through stacking‑faulted and 3R‑related environments, which provide structurally accessible insertion pathways. In contrast, turbostratic interlayers do not participate in early lithium insertion and correlate with reduced reversible capacity. These results demonstrate that graphite behaviour is governed by defect topology rather than by a single degree of disorder and highlight the need for defect‑resolved structural descriptors to rationalize lithium intercalation mechanisms in graphite.

papers.title: Second-Generation N,N´-Disubstituted Aliphatic Diamines: Discovery of Potent Hits for Multi-Species Leishmaniasis Treatment.
papers.abstract: Kinetoplastid diseases remain a major global health challenge, highlighting the need for new antiparasitic chemotypes. N,N′-disubstituted aliphatic diamines have emerged as a promising scaffold against trypanosomatid parasites. Building on our previous studies, we expanded the structure–activity relationship (SAR) of this chemotype through the synthesis of forty-two analogues obtained by one-pot reductive amination of aliphatic diamine linkers with structurally diverse aromatic and heteroaromatic aldehydes. The compounds were first evaluated against the extracellular stages of Trypanosoma cruzi, Trypanosoma brucei, and Leishmania donovani. Several derivatives displayed pIC50 values above 6.0 and selectivity index above 10. Based on these results, nine hits were further evaluated against the promastigote and amastigote stages of L. amazonensis, L. braziliensis, and L. infantum, responsible for cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis. Among them, compounds 12a, 12m, and 8e showed potent activity against intracellular amastigotes with selectivity indices above 10, highlighting this scaffold as a promising starting point for antileishmanial drug discovery.

papers.title: Operation-Induced BiVO4 Surface Reconstruction Modulates Photoelectrochemical Glycerol Photooxidation Stability and Activity
papers.abstract: Operation-induced surface reconstruction of photoelectrodes is poorly understood and underexplored as a path to control photoelectrochemical stability. Here, we show how adaptive junctions form in association with the surface reconstruction of bismuth vanadate during glycerol oxidation and how these surfaces have electrolyte-dependent kinetics and effects on durability. Preferential vanadium dissolution in both acidic and alkaline media forms a bismuth-rich layer, for which opposing catalytic roles with respect to pH are found. In situ measurements through a dual-working-electrode platform quantify the changes in photovoltage and charge-transfer resistance derived from adaptive junction formation during glycerol oxidation, while also enabling quantitative separation of the driving forces for charge separation and interfacial catalysis. The reconstructed surface in acidic media improves hole transfer kinetics, functions as a glycerol oxidation catalyst, and imparts photostability. Surface reconstruction in alkaline media exhibits the opposite behavior, impeding hole injection. The resulting instability is mitigated through in situ surface activation by adding trace Ni 2+ ions to the electrolyte without cocatalyst predeposition. This study thus shows the significance of surface reconstruction for the design of durable photoelectrodes for applications using anodic organic electro-oxidation.

papers.title: Extending the Python RESP Framework for Extra Point Charge Fitting
papers.abstract: The Restrained Electrostatic Potential (RESP) method is widely used to derive electrostatic parameters for Newtonian-based models. However, conventional nucleicentered charge models can struggle to reproduce anisotropic features such as halogen σ-holes and electron lone-pair regions. Herein, an extension is presented of the Psi4compatible Python resp implementation of Alenaizan et al. that enables partial atomic charge fitting to user-defined extra point sites represented as massless dummy particles. This refactoring introduces an INI-based configuration layer, a revised driver.py that propagates extra point sites through grid/ESP handling, and an updated espfit.py engine that continues to support multi-conformer fitting. Also introduced into the code are functions for computing RMSE and RRMSE metrics. The resulting workflow is transparent, reproducible, and enables the development of both nuclei-centered and off-centered electrostatic models for molecular mechanics-based simulations.

papers.title: Solvent-Modulated Reactivity of a d1 Manganate–Pyridine System: Epoxide Formation, U-Shaped Substituent Effects, and Evidence for an Optimal Electronic Window
papers.abstract: The reaction between high-valent manganate (MnO42-, d1) and pyridine was investigated using density functional theory (DFT). Geometries were optimized at the B3LYP-D3/def2-SVP level, followed by single-point energy refinements at the B3LYP-D3/def2-SVPD level. A U-shaped relationship was identified between the HOMO–LUMO gap of the system and the Hammett constant (σp) of substituents on the pyridine ring. The unsubstituted pyridine system exhibits the narrowest gap (0.81 eV in gas phase), accompanied by the formation of an epoxide intermediate at the pyridine ring. Both electron-withdrawing (e.g., –CN, –NO2) and electron-donating (e.g., –NH2) substituents widen the gap, reducing reactivity. In aqueous solution (CPCM model), the parent pyridine system further evolves, with the HOMO–LUMO gap decreasing to 0.70 eV, both frontier orbital energies becoming negative, and the pyridine ring observed to lose planarity. Coupled with the formation of a solvent-separated ion pair, these structural and electronic changes suggest the pyridine ring may have undergone further oxidation under aqueous conditions. The –CN substituted system exhibits similar stabilization in water (gap 1.55 eV, all-negative orbital energies), while preserving the relative gap ordering observed in the gas phase. Electron-withdrawing substituents are found to increase the HOMO–LUMO gap, enhance intermediate stability, and reduce reactivity, while electron-donating substituents have the opposite effect. This work identifies an optimal electronic window for the reaction, providing a quantitative framework for controlling the formation and stability of reactive intermediates in high-valent metal–oxo chemistry through substituent and solvent modulation.

papers.title: N-Aminopyridinium Ylides as Triplet Nitrene Precursors for the Photocatalytic Imination of Sulfoxides and Sulfides: Application to Peptide Modification at Methionine Residues
papers.abstract: Sulfoximines and sulfilimines are increasingly recognized as valuable functional groups in medicinal and synthetic chemistry. Photochemical imination via nitrene transfer provides straightforward access to these sulfur-based motifs from readily available sulfoxides and sulfides, without requiring elevated temperatures or Lewis acidic transition metals. However, this approach remains underutilized owing to the inherent challenges in controlling the chemoselectivity of highly electrophilic singlet free nitrenes. Herein, we report a broadly applicable imination of sulfoxides and sulfides via energy transfer (EnT) photocatalysis, featuring the strategic use of triplet nitrenes. Specifically, the absence of a low-lying empty orbital suppresses the indiscriminate reactivity inherent to singlet nitrenes toward nucleophilic functional groups. Concurrently, their electrophilic diradical nature enables the imination of intrinsically oxidizable sulfur-based functional groups via a single electron transfer (SET)-based mechanism. The potential of our strategy was unlocked by using N-aminopyridinium ylides as triplet nitrene precursors designed via a computation-guided approach based on the Marcus theory. These ylides underwent EnT more efficiently than conventional azides and enabled the facile generation of N-sulfonyl triplet nitrenes, even when using a mild photocatalyst. We also demonstrated the practical utility of our method through the late-stage functionalization of peptides at methionine residues, facilitating their structural diversification and conjugation.

papers.title: The Microstructures of Promoted Raney(r) Nickel Alloys and Catalysts
papers.abstract: This study measured various effects of iron and chromium promotion on the microstructures of Raney(r) nickel alloys and catalysts. The following alloys and catalysts were studied: (i) unpromoted, (ii) multiple levels of Fe promotion, (iii) multiple levels of Cr promotion, and (iv) doubly-promoted with Fe and Cr. Microstructures and phase compositions of some initial alloys were characterized using backscattered scanning electron microscopy (SEM), electron microprobe, optical microscopy, and x-ray diffraction. Backscattered SEM and electron microprobe analysis showed the microstructure is composed of several phases: Al 3 Ni 2 , Al 3 Ni, promoter-rich phase(s) (which are absent in the unpromoted alloy), and a eutectic phase. The Fe and Cr promoters concentrate in the promoter-rich phases in these alloys. Based on XRD pattern and the phase diagram, we have assigned ‘Fe promoter phase 1’, present in some Raney nickel alloys promoted with ≥ 2 wt.% Fe, as the decagonite (Al 71 Ni 24 Fe 5 ) quasicrystal. This was a major finding, because decagonite was previously thought to be rare. Also, ‘Fe promoter phase 2’, present in all of the Fe-only promoted alloys, Al 9 Ni (2-y) Fe y (where y was 0.37 to 0.77) crystalline phase has been proposed, based on the findings of this study. A phi phase of composition Al 77.5 Cr 12 Ni 10.5 has been proposed for ‘Cr promoter phase’ (present in Cr-only promoted alloys) in this study. A ‘Cr, Fe promoter phase’ of approximate composition Al 75.5 Ni 13-14 Cr 6-7 Fe 4 was present in the Cr, Fe doubly-promoted alloys. The alloys were crushed into a powder and leached in aqueous sodium hydroxide solution. After leaching, the catalysts were washed and subsequently characterized. Nitrogen adsorption at 77 K was performed to extract the total surface area and pore size distribution of each catalyst. Carbon monoxide and hydrogen gas adsorption were performed to measure each catalyst’s metallic surface area. For some catalysts, bulk elemental composition was quantified using atomic absorption spectroscopy, and the surface compositions and oxidation states were studied using x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). XPS results showed that Cr is oxidized to Cr(+III) during the leaching procedure to form a compound (likely chromium hydroxide) that increases the total surface area (while having negligible effect on the metallic surface area) and also leads to smaller pore diameters.

papers.title: Prediction of Helical Twisting Power Using Machine Learning and Its Correlation with Molecular Structures
papers.abstract: Helical twisting power (HTP) of chiral dopants determines the pitch of chiral nematic liquid crystals and is therefore a key parameter for controlling their optical properties. However, predicting HTP directly from molecular structure remains challenging because chirality transfer from molecular dopants to macroscopic helical organization depends on stereochemistry, molecular conformation, and host–dopant interactions. Here, we developed a machine-learning framework to predict HTP values from molecular descriptors derived from experimentally reported chiral dopants. For dopants with stereogenic centres, the Gaussian process regression model achieved reliable predictive performance (R2 = 0.72, MAE = 8.9 μm-1), whereas substantially lower accuracy was obtained for axially chiral dopants. This indicates that the structural descriptors used in this study capture key information relevant to chirality transfer in stereogeniccentre-based dopants, while additional conformational factors, such as dihedral-angle distributions, are required for axially chiral systems. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) -based feature analysis revealed that HTP is influenced by a combination of molecular rigidity, aromaticity, heteroatom content, host compatibility, and molecular shape anisotropy. These results demonstrate that machine learning can extract implicit structure–property relationships underlying chiral induction in liquid crystals and provide a data-driven framework for the rational design of chiral dopants.

papers.title: Shear viscosity of liquid Sb and Bi from pseudopotential theory: Validation, limitations, and the temperature-insensitive soft-tail contribution
papers.abstract: The temperature-dependent shear viscosity η(T ) of liquid Sb and Bi is computed from each melting point to 500K above it using the Bretonnet–Silbert pseudopotential, five local-field corrections, and the Rice–Allnatt transport theory. The viscosity is decomposed into kinetic (η k ), hard-core (η h2 ), and soft-tail (η s ) contributions. It is shown that ηs constitutes 54–59% of the total viscosity, is nearly temperature- independent, causing |dη/dT | to be systematically too small: for both elements, η is underestimated near the melting point (−16% for Sb, −32% for Bi) and overestimated at high temperatures (+31% for Sb at 1300K, +13% for Bi at 1095K), with a crossover near 1050K (Sb) and 850K (Bi). This insensitivity is traced partly to the use of the hard-sphere pair-distribution function g HS (r): replacing it with the modified hypernetted-chain g MHNC increases η s by 7–21%, yet the experimental temperature gradient is still not recovered, pointing to a deeper limitation inherent in the Rice–Allnatt decomposition itself. The choice of local-field correction changes η by only ~3%, and the pseudopotential parameters shift the absolute value by factors of 2–3 but do not improve the temperature gradient. Comparison with ab initio molecular-dynamics viscosities confirms that the pseudopotential approach underestimates the absolute viscosity of Bi; the available ab initio data also suggest a weaker temperature dependence than experiment.

papers.title: Robotic Workflow for Autonomous Glass Discovery
papers.abstract: Today's glass development must meet increasingly complex property profiles within an ever-shorter time-to-market. However, the disruptive progress required in glass development to overcome this challenge is hampered by manual workflows, empirical trial-and-error approaches, and a lack of process documentation. Moreover, computer-aided glass formulation tools such as databases or property prediction tools currently suffer from insufficient database consistency, variable data fidelity, and a significant lack of property and process data. To this end, a cross-laboratory infrastructure has been established that combines computer-aided glass formulation and robot-assisted glass synthesis. This infrastructure provides a steadily expandable web-based glass data space, machine learning-driven data mining and property modeling tools, as well as a robotic glass melting system equipped with inline sensors and semi-autonomous intervention tools for process optimization and system protection. An underlying backbone ontology defines the machine-readable glass terminology and semantic relations. Logging and codifying even subconscious process expertise and human intervention, this robot-assisted infrastructure guarantees exact reproducibility and builds up an ever-growing expert knowledge system over time. This article aims to illustrate the significant progress made with this approach while also highlighting ongoing needs on the way to autonomous glass development.

papers.title: Simple hybrid predictive model for point-of-care pharmaceutical tablet disintegration
papers.abstract: Predicting point-of-care performance of pharmaceutical tablets remains a fundamental challenge due to the lack of mechanistically grounded, longitudinal models. A hybrid model that accurately predicts longterm disintegration times solely from at-line porosity measurements (f at−line ) is established. Validated against a unique five-year real-time stability dataset (R 2 > 0.92), the model captures the complex interplay of formulation and geometry across the commercial operating range (f at−line ∈ [0.1, 0.3]). The model parameters are demonstrated to function as quantitative physicochemical stability indicators This framework is agnostic to characterisation hardware and provides a robust, non-destructive alternative to traditional pharmacopoeial testing. By mechanistically linking initial structure to long-term efficacy, this approach facilitates Quality by Design and real-time release testing, ensuring that quality standards are preserved from manufacture to patient administration.

papers.title: Clickable Turn-On Nanoparticles for Target-Specific Intracellular Activation
papers.abstract: Precise visualization of nanoparticles (NPs) at the subcellular level is crucial for targeted drug delivery. However, NPs functionalized with permanently fluorescent probes are challenging to detect when only a small fraction reaches the target compartment, as weak fluorescence signals are obscured by intense fluorescence from NPs accumulated in off-target subcellular compartments. Here, we introduce ‘turn on’ NPs that activate fluorescence via an inverse electron demand Diels–Alder (iEDDA) reaction only at their intracellular target. NPs were functionalized with coumarin-102-tetrazine (C102-Tet) turn-on fluorescence upon reaction with trans-cyclooctene (TCO), which was immobilized to microtubules via anchors of various geometry and spatial accessibility. We generated polymer NPs composed of poly(lactide-co-glycolide) (PLGA) and poly(ethylene glycol)-poly(lactic acid) (PEG–PLA), systematically varying PEG chain length (2k vs 5k) and C102-Tet surface density. Direct stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (dSTORM) resolved individual NPs of ~80 nm and confirmed that C102-Tet presented on the NP surface remains reactive. Quantitatively, 15–45% of C102-Tet groups participated in the iEDDA reaction, depending on PEG chain length and surface density. To overcome insufficient endosomal escape, NPs were directly delivered into the cytosol to demonstrate the fluorogenic NP concept that becomes activated only upon bio-orthogonal reaction at the intracellular target. Confocal microscopy and super-resolution SIM2 imaging revealed NP fluorescence aligned along microtubules and support target-specific iEDDA activation on the surface of NPs. This strategy enables high-contrast tracking of nanocarriers at defined intracellular targets.

papers.title: Chemistry of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: Environmental Behaviors Governed by Metal–Chalcogen Bonding
papers.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), including MoS 2 , MoSe 2 , MoTe 2 , and WS 2 , have emerged as a versatile class of two-dimensional (2D) materials for environmental applications, spanning pollutant capture, water purification, air remediation, chemical sensing, and catalytic conversion. Their high surface-to-volume ratios and tunable electronic properties enable their use as adsorbents for heavy metals and greenhouse gases, sensing platforms capable of ppb–ppt detection of toxic species such as NO 2 , SO 2 , and NH 3 , and catalytic materials for green energy technologies, including the photocatalytic and electrocatalytic conversion of CO 2 into value-added products. However, practical implementation remains limited by challenges in controlling sheet morphology and defect populations, which critically influence reactivity, selectivity, and long-term stability. Here, we present a bonding-centric perspective that links the environmental behavior of TMDs to the chemistry of the metal–chalcogen bond. We show that systematic variations in bond strength, polarity, and charge redistribution across the MoX 2 (X = S, Se, Te) series govern interactions at environmental surfaces and interfaces, including pristine basal planes, defect-engineered systems, and intercalated multilayer structures. These differences dictate adsorption strength, charge transfer, and catalytic pathways for environmentally relevant species. By unifying these effects within a single mechanistic framework, this perspective establishes design principles for tailoring TMD-based materials with enhanced selectivity, stability, and efficiency. In doing so, it outlines a pathway toward next-generation environmental technologies for climate action and sustainable resource management.

papers.title: Simplified Time-Dependent Density-Functional Theory for Noble Metal Nanoclusters: Progress Toward the Tamm–Dancoff Approximation
papers.abstract: We investigate the optical and plasmonic properties of noble metal nanoclusters containing a few hundred atoms using the simplified TDDFT framework. Compared with full sTDDFT, we find that the Tamm–Dancoff approximation underestimates plasmonband intensities and systematically blue-shifts resonance energies, although it preserves the overall spectral shape in the 2–5 eV range while offering lower computational cost. Building on our previous work [J. Phys. Chem. C 2023, 127, 7718], we further confirm that global and range-separated hybrid functionals are required for an accurate description of plasmon resonances. Benchmarking against polTDDFT shows that sTDDFT offers an efficient and reliable alternative, whereas polTDDFT remains the reference method for describing collective excitations in large noble metal nanoclusters.

papers.title: Solvent coordination-driven amplification of circularly polarized luminescence in a helical Zn(II) complex
papers.abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from helical molecules has attracted considerable attention for next-generation optoelectronic devices. In this study, we synthesized a helical Zn(II) complex that exhibits CPL amplification upon solvent coordination to the metal centre. A chiral Schiff-base ligand was prepared from commercially available optically pure 1,2-diphenylethylenediamine and was induced to form a helical three-dimensional framework by coordination with zinc ions. In non-coordinating solvents, such as toluene, the complex undergoes rapid helical inversion between the (M,M) and (P,P) forms, resulting in decreased emission and CPL intensity. In contrast, coordination of solvent molecules such as tetrahydrofuran to the zinc centre effectively suppresses this helical inversion, leading to an enhanced CPL response with a glum value of up to 4.0 × 10−3. These findings indicate that metallohelicenes are promising candidates for use as controllable CPL materials.

papers.title: Efficient and regenerable ion-exchange resin beads for PFAS capture and circular management
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants that pose global environmental and health risks, yet their efficient removal and safe management remain challenging. Here we report a series of regenerable ion-exchange resin beads, which can be directly implemented in continuous cartridge systems for the effective removal of PFAS from landfill leachate, including challenging short-chain analogues. The well-defined spherical morphology of the beads plays a critical role in minimizing swelling-induced pressure buildup under fixed-bed operation, enabling sustained, long-term PFAS capture under continuous flow conditions. The beads achieve > 97% removal efficiency across all tested PFAS, good sorption and desorption regeneration ability, while rapid small-scale column tests demonstrate a >10,000-fold increase in breakthrough bed volumes compared with the commercial resin PFA694E. The concentrated PFAS eluate generated during regeneration is subsequently employed as an electrolyte additive for aqueous zinc batteries, where the C-F bonds from PFAS can be destructed and converted into a ZnF2-rich interphase. As a result, both symmetric and full cells exhibit enhanced cycling stability and improved capacity retention compared with the control batteries. This capture-concentrate-utilize pathway reframes PFAS from persistent contaminants to functional resources, providing a strategy for circular PFAS management and sustainable water treatment.

papers.title: Multimodal Descriptor Integration and Two-tier Sequential Stacking for Structure-based Prediction of Compound Autofluorescence in the EUOS25 Challenge
papers.abstract: The EUOS25 challenge formalized the prediction of compound autofluorescence, a major source of false positives in fluorescence-based high-throughput screening, from molecular structure alone. We describe the winning fluorescence solution, which combined a multimodal descriptor strategy with a two-tier stacked modeling framework. Approximately 2,300 features—spanning multi-Hamiltonian semiempirical (MOPAC) quantities, xTB-derived thermodynamic summaries, extended cheminformatics surfaces, and GNN-derived auxiliary embeddings—were integrated into a single wide training matrix. Out-of-fold predictions, generated by Tier 1 base learners (XGBoost and an XGBoost random-forest-style variant) under 4 × 4 nested cross-validation (CV), were consumed by Tier 2 together with the original descriptors. The Tier 2 learners then sequentially predicted four binary endpoints (T340 → F340/450 → T450 → F480). Because the final models incorporated the leaderboard set, generalization is reported using nested CV and blind-test AUC only. The blind-set AUCs were 0.869 (T340), 0.894 (F340/450), 0.676 (T450), and 0.707 (F480), yielding fluorescence and transmittance property means of 0.801 and 0.773, respectively. These results demonstrate that systematic multimodal descriptor integration, explicit feature-matrix feeding rules for stacked learning, and target-aware sequential propagation can produce robust structure-only spectral-liability models without relying on a graph neural network as the sole predictive core.

papers.title: An Integrated Workflow Comprising AI, Physics and Experiment: Discovery of Nanomolar-Potent Inhibitors
papers.abstract: The drug discovery process remains very slow and unreliable, requiring about 10 years and $2-3 billion for a single new drug at a success rate of around 5%. To address this, we have recently created a complex and highly heterogeneous workflow called IMPECCABLE which is designed to transform much of the drug discovery process into a far more reliable in silico environment. It runs on Frontier, the world’s first exascale machine and has recently been implemented on the second such machine, Aurora. A variety of in silico discovery methods exist, including physics-based and artificial intelligence (AI) approaches. Despite their limitations, these methods are complementary, and we combine them here within IMPECCABLE, an integrated framework which efficiently and reliably explores the vast chemical space of small molecule binders. IMPECCABLE involves screening, generating and evaluating candidate compounds. The environment is comprised of several interlocking and interacting stages. In the first of these, an exceptionally fast machine learning model acts as a docking surrogate for rapidly screening billions of compounds and provides a ranked series of binding poses for the best ones. In a generative multi-objective active learning loop, the accurate binding free energies from physics-based free energy methods, including ESMACS and TIES, guide REINVENT to predict compounds not only with higher binding affinities, but which are also synthesizable while ensuring diversity and novelty. The full iterative workflow spans both hit identification and hit-to-lead optimization and includes medicinal chemists in the process. Applying IMPECCABLE to two disease-related protein targets, WDR91 and TNKS2, we demonstrate its capability to iteratively produce experimentally makeable potent binders. The potential hits discovered were further optimized and chiral purified via an iterative REINVENT-TIES cycle. We identified a potent hit for WDR91, which was synthesised in five steps, exhibiting nanomolar binding affinity with a KD value of 352 ± 32 nM.

papers.title: Temperature Dependence of the Hydrated Electron’s g-Factor and Persistence of a Cavity-Localized Electron at Elevated Temperature
papers.abstract: The structure of the aqueous electron, e − (aq), has been the focus of intense scrutiny from both theory and experiment. The temperature dependence of its g -factor, measured via electron paramagnetic resonance and significantly shifted from the free-electron value, has been suggested to be inconsistent with the conventional picture of an electron localized in a cavity. Here, we use ab initio molecular dynamics simulations and quantum chemistry calculations to compute the ensemble-averaged, isotropic g -factor for e − (aq) over the entire liquid-phase temperature range. A temperature-dependent shift is obtained, in reasonable agreement with experiment, without any qualitative change in either the localized structure of e − (aq) or its average coordination number. Far from being inconsistent with the measurements, persistence of the cavity structure actually supports the rather mild temperature dependence of the g -factor because the amount of spin density hosted in oxygen orbitals, which is quantified by our calculations, is found to change very little with temperature. These results support a cavity structure for e − (aq) over the entire liquid range at atmospheric pressure. The simulations are broadly consistent with spectroscopic measurements demonstrating that the molar extinction coefficient is insensitive to temperature and that there are no abrupt temperature-induced changes in the absorption spectrum, even into the supercooled and supercritical water regimes. This analysis further entrenches the cavity-centric picture of e − (aq).

papers.title: Stabilizing Polymer Dielectrics at Interfaces for High-density Energy Storage
papers.abstract: Polymer-based dielectric film capacitors are essential for high-power energy storage in applications such as electric vehicles, wearable electronics, and biomedical implants. 1-7 However, conventional polymer dielectrics are fundamentally limited by low energy density. 8,9 In this work, we demonstrate a strategy to enhance energy density in ultrathin polymer films (~15–100 nm) by exploiting surface interactions that stabilize the polymer under high electric fields. This enhancement arises from a van der Waals (vdW) pinning effect, in which interfacial forces constrain polymer chain motion and improve structural stability. Additionally, nonequilibrium chain conformations at the polymer–substrate interface is shown to further strengthen vdW pinning by increasing surface adsorption. By crosslinking or surface grafting, these pinning effects become thermally robust. The ultrathin linear dielectric nanocapacitors show low leakage current, achieving energy densities up to ~78 J/cm³ with over 90% efficiency. These findings establish substrate–polymer interactions, rather than chemical composition alone, as a powerful design paradigm for engineering high-performance polymer dielectrics, enabling energy storage capabilities beyond conventional limits and opening new pathways for next-generation electronic devices.

papers.title: Solvent Polarity as a Diagnostic for Vibronic/Vibrational Coherences Distinction in an Efficient TADF-TTA Switchable Emitter
papers.abstract: Distinguishing vibrational and vibronic coherences using pump-probe spectroscopy alone remains a fundamental challenge, typically requiring multidimensional techniques or temperature-dependent studies. No robust pump-probe-only strategy exists for thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitters, where temperature methods fail due to conformational changes and suppressed CT repopulation. Here, we introduce a novel polarity-dependent criterion using 35-fs pump-probe spectroscopy in 1,8-naphthalimide D-A emitters (A1-A3, with anthracene, pyrene, and carbazole substituents, respectively, at various positions). In non-polar n-hexane, resonant locally excited-charge transfer (LE-CT) vibronic coherences persist with 105 cm -1 beats across both LE-CT bands; while the polar DCM stabilizes CT, which widens the LE-CT gap (968 to 4274 cm -1 ), and quenches vibronic coherences. Thus, quenching vibronic but not vibrational (35 cm -1 ) oscillations. This is the first pump-probe only distinction of vibronic coupling in a TADF emitter (A1). This is also the first report showing a Dynamic TADF (non-polar)/TTA (polar) switching in a single deep blue emitter: A1 shows TADF in hexane (222% emission gain due to triplet contribution) and converts to TTA in DCM (179% gain), demonstrating the polarity robust superiority of TADF-TTA switchable emitters over TADF-only. A2 yields pure blue TTA (CIE 0.15, 0.06; QY 0.44/0.69 degassed). We anticipate this study to enable versatile, high-efficiency D-A optical materials and help distinguish vibrational and vibronic coherences in D-A and TADF systems.

papers.title: Coupled Cluster Free Energies for Atmospheric Molecular Clusters: Benchmark and Matching Experimental Free Energies
papers.abstract: The initial formation of secondary aerosols, a large cause of uncertainty in modern radiative forcing modeling, can be simulated using quantum chemical methods. When based on quantum chemistry, the simulations have an exponential dependence on the free energy, requiring a high-accuracy description. In this study, we have computed harmonic frequencies and quasi-harmonic free energies for a set of 11 monomers and 27 dimers relevant for atmospheric molecular clusters at the DF-CCSD(F12b)(T*)/cc-pVDZ-F12 level of theory. The set is used to benchmark the M06-2X, PW91, ωB97X-D3BJ functions with the Jensen, Karlsruhe, and Pople style basis sets. The composite methods B97-3c, r2SCAN-3c, and ωB97X- 3c are also tested. We find ωB97X-D3BJ/ma-def2-SVP to be an optimal choice as it has low errors (mean absolute error of 0.13 kcal/mol) and few outliers in the thermal contribution. For calculations on larger clusters, B97-3c stands out. Using the ωB97X-D3BJ/ma-def2-SVP and B97-3c level of theories, we compute anharmonic frequencies using the VPT2 method and determine an anharmonic scaling factor of 0.961 and 0.953 for ωB97X-D3BJ/ma-def2-SVP and B97-3c frequencies, respectively. The scaling factor together with incorporating multi-conformer entropy effects and a high-level single-point correction at the Normal LNO-CCSD(T)/CBS(aug- 3,aug-4) are used to compare to experimental determined free energies of the 11 hydrogen-bonded systems. We find that we obtain sub 1 kcal/mol errors when incorporating the scaling factor, the multi-conformer entropy effects, and the single point correction.

papers.title: Rapid and Selective Metal-Free O2 Reduction to H2O2 Using a Molecular CpN3 Electrocatalyst
papers.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a commodity chemical used broadly in the industrial sector that heavily relies on the 80+ year old anthraquinone process, requiring significant energy input in combination with precious metal catalyzed hydrogenation. We describe a metal-free molecular cyclopentadiene-iminium ([Cp N3 H] 2+ ) electrocatalyst for producing H 2 O 2 under ambient conditions with high Faradaic efficiency (up to 95%) and turnover frequency (TOF up to 10 4 s -1 ), surpassing some of the most active transition-metal based molecular catalyst systems. The amine-rich radical cation intermediate ([Cp N3 H] +• ) transfers a potent hydrogen atom (H•) to O 2 through an unusual radical-rebound mechanism to form a key hydroperoxyl intermediate ([Cp N3 OOH] +• ), with cutting-edge computational (DFT) and experimental mechanistic analyses in excellent agreement. This work demonstrates an innovative and sustainable molecular approach to furnish a valuable commodity chemical through an electrically driven process without the need for transition metals.

papers.title: Vibronic Coherences Rationalize Dual Emission in 1,8-Naphthalimide Derivatives, and Realizing their Efficient Triplet Harvesting Capability
Armstrong's Range Exponent Electron Configuration Model (AREECM)
papers.abstract: Traditional electron-configuration notation (e.g., 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6) represents multi-electron systems using integer orbital occupations that reflect dominant configurations but do not explicitly encode the multi-configurational nature of correlated electronic states. In wavefunction-based electronic structure theory, the electronic state is expressed as a linear combination of configurations, each assigning integer electron occupations to orbitals and contributing with a finite coefficient. Standard notation typically reflects only the dominant configuration, while the underlying distribution of contributing configurations remains implicit. This work introduces Armstrong’s Range Exponent Electron Configuration Model (AREECM), a representational framework that replaces fixed integer occupations with bounded intervals derived from the configuration interaction expansion of the electronic wavefunction. For each subshell, AREECM determines minimum and maximum occupation numbers nMin​ and nMax, over a selected configuration support set defined by a cumulative weight threshold. These are normalized by the total electron count Z, yielding fractional bounds PMin=nMinZ, PMax=nMaxZ expressed in the form nl^Z*[PMin, PMax]v where the suffix v encodes the support-selection criterion. AREECM provides a compact representation of configurational variability within standard electronic structure descriptions without modifying underlying quantum mechanical formalism. It encodes the range of subshell occupations implied by the wavefunction while remaining compatible with conventional electron-configuration notation.

papers.title: The Cosmic Equation of State in GERT—Closed-System Thermodynamics, the Resolution of the Cosmological Constant Problem, and the Recovery of Relativistic Time as a
papers.abstract: In physical chemistry, the equation of state of a closed thermodynamic system is the bridge between measurable variables (density, pressure, temperature) and derived state functions (enthalpy, free energy). The previous paper of this series derived the Cauldron equation, the equation of motion of the cosmic substrate treated as a closed thermodynamic system. The present paper integrates the Cauldron equation to obtain the cosmic equation of state H(x) = Hem exp[I(x)/β] explicitly, and develops three consequences. First, the cosmic equation of state is a state function in the strict mathematical sense, admitting direct comparison with the chemistry equations of state (ideal gas, van der Waals). Second, the cosmological constant discrepancy (∼ 10122) dissolves not as a numerical anomaly but as a category mistake: General Relativity sums vacuum modes (a geometric quantity) while observations constrain the remaining thermodynamic fuel (a state-function quantity); the two are not directly comparable without an equation of state to mediate. Third, the Lorentz factor √ 1− v2/c2 is recovered as the chemicalkinetic limit of the internal Work rate, with v = c the threshold at which the available energy fraction for internal process vanishes. General Relativity is the theory of rulers; the Gibbs Energy Redistribution Theory (GERT) is the theory that includes the thermometer.

papers.title: Self-Consistent Incorporation of Generalized Born Model into RCI-LC-DFTB for Photoinduced Charge-Separated States
papers.abstract: The self-consistent incorporation of Generalized Born (GB) model into the restrictionbased configuration interaction long-range corrected density functional tight binding (RCI-LC-DFTB) framework enables a state-specific description of solvent polarization effects in photoinduced charge-separated (CS) states. In this scheme, the GB model contribution is constructed from the charge distribution of a selected target state and incorporated into the configuration interaction Hamiltonian through an effective oneelectron operator, preserving the chemically intuitive interpretation of charge-localized diabatic configurations. We apply the method to two triphenylamine–naphthalene diimide (MTA–MNDI) donor–acceptor dyads connected by twisted phenylene–ethynylene bridges of different lengths. Our calculations demonstrate that solvent polarization significantly stabilizes the CS configuration, altering the energetic ordering between locally excited and CS states to thermodynamically drive charge separation. This approach offers a computationally ecient and chemically transparent framework for describing state-specific solvation and photophysical kinetics in large donor–acceptor assemblies.

papers.title: Beyond the Enthalpy-Entropy Compensation: The Mathematical Inevitability of Apparent Kinetic Compensation Effect in Complex Electrochemical Reactions
papers.abstract: The kinetic compensation effect (KCE), i.e., a linear correlation between potential-dependent activation energy () and logarithm of pre-exponential factor (), is frequently observed when analyzing electrochemical reaction kinetics via the classical Arrhenius analysis. However, the physical origin of KCE remains fiercely debated, with interpretations ranging from intrinsic enthalpy-entropy trade-offs to experimental/artificial artifacts. This work addresses the core controversies surrounding KCE by integrating theoretical insights from elementary charge transfer reactions and kinetic analysis of complex reaction networks. Firstly, we clarify that for elementary electrochemical reactions, intrinsic activation energy and intrinsic pre-exponential factor are temperature dependent but free of intrinsic KCE, while KCE emerges inevitably from classical Arrhenius fitting, even for minor temperature-induced changes in . After that, we prove that for complex reactions (including either parallel or sequential pathways or both), KCE can be a pure mathematical artifact of forcing multi-step kinetics into a single-step Arrhenius framework. From the point of view of electrons, all electron-transfer elementary steps in complex electrocatalysis which occur consecutively are equivalent of their occurrence in parallel at different active sites, since the measurement of current density is the sum of every ET steps. This inevitably leads to the appearance of the apparent KCE. Our study indicates one should be careful when directly associating the potential dependent and derived by classical Arrhenius treatment to microscopic mechanisms. Instead of the conventional Arrhenius analysis, we suggest one would better carry out detailed microkinetic simulation in order to derive the intrinsic kinetic parameters of such complicated reactions.

papers.title: SKYNET: An Interpretable Hybrid Network For Protein Structural Class Prediction
Transfer Learning from Lithium-Ion to Zinc-Ion Batteries: Cross-Chemistry Capacity Prediction with Limited Target Data
papers.abstract: Published Zn-ion cathode data are limited relative to Li-ion datasets, which constrains model training for grid-storage applications. We examine whether adding 150 simulated Li-ion cathode records improves prediction of initial discharge capacity in a 75-entry Zn-ion set, using a 7-variable cross-chemistry schema covering operating window, rate proxy, and coarse structure tags. RF, GBR, and MLP models were compared across five training setups, from Zn-only fitting to transfer-based variants including instance weighting and neural fine-tuning. The benefit is largest at low target-data fractions: at 20% Zn data, weighted GBR raised R2 from −0.555 to −0.209; at 80%, from 0.266 to 0.361. Using all Zn records, the Zn-only RF (R2 = 0.473 ± 0.172, MAE = 47.2 mAh g−1) was best. MLP models were unstable at this sample size (R2 = −1.228 with transfer). Permutation analysis ranked current density highest (0.582), then average voltage (0.389) and crystal-structure encoding (0.350). Li-derived examples mainly damp variance in small Zn fits; once Zn labels are adequate, mechanistic mismatch limits further gains.

papers.title: Dielectric Mie-Resonant Metasurface Integrated ATR Chip for Spectrally Tuneable Surface-Enhanced Infrared Spectroscopy in Aqueous Media
papers.abstract: Label-free molecular fingerprinting of proteins in aqueous media requires overcoming three core challenges: water's strong mid-IR absorption, the limited sensitivity of conventional ATR crystals for trace analytes, and the high fabrication cost of plasmonic SEIRA substrates. Here we introduce the µ-SEIRA chip, a monolithic all-silicon platform combining micro-attenuated total reflection (µ-ATR) with dielectric Mie-resonant metasurfaces for on-chip surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA) spectroscopy. Arrays of silicon micropillars provide spectrally tuneable field enhancement through dielectric Mie resonances, achieving a peak enhancement factor of 6.3 relative to a flat silicon µ-ATR reference and a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.57 mM for aqueous sodium acetate, each obtained from chip geometries independently optimised for maximum enhancement and detection sensitivity respectively. The pillar resonance can be tuned to overlap preferentially with targeted vibrational bands; in BSA measurements, this produced preferential amplification of the Amide II band (~1550 cm-1) over Amide I (~1650 cm-1), resolving BSA signals at 1.5 µM in aqueous solution. Fabricated entirely from silicon using CMOS-compatible processes, the chip is low-cost and disposable, eliminating the cross-contamination and throughput constraints of reusable ATR crystals. This platform provides a scalable, quantitative route to infrared molecular fingerprinting of proteins and other biomolecules directly in aqueous media.

papers.title: Tau2: a program for the simulation of magnetic relaxation
papers.abstract: Tau2 is a Python reimplementation and development of our code Tau, which calculates magnetic relaxation rates via the one-phonon (Orbach and direct) and two-phonon Raman-I mechanisms. It is substantially faster than Tau, by a factor of up to 12000 times for Raman-I rates, and is more numerically accurate due to careful design of the integration grid. The most important optimisation is that Raman rates are calculated via the calculation of a temperature-independent “Raman spectral density”, which avoids recalculation of the expensive sum over phonon pairs for each temperature. Tau2 takes advantage of just-in-time compilation with Numba to minimise the overheads of the interpreted Python language. The improved algorithm drastically reduces the cost of calculating magnetic relaxation rates, making the computational cost of routine rate calculations trivial, and allows for simulation of far larger spin systems which would not previously have been feasible.

papers.title: Generation and atmospheric evolution of light-absorbing carbonaceous aerosol from thermal degradation of plastic
papers.abstract: Open burning of plastic waste is a significant source of carbonaceous aerosol, including nanoplastics, in the atmosphere. As these particles are carried downwind, they undergo atmospheric aging through irradiation and oxidation, with potential impacts on their optical properties and, in turn, interactions with sunlight. Here, we report measurements of the initial and dynamic light absorption of carbonaceous aerosol from the thermal degradation of plastic, i.e., polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG). Four colors (red, yellow, blue, and colorless) of PETG were selected for thermal degradation in a tube furnace across a wide range of temperatures. The generation of nanoparticles was confirmed using a scanning mobility particle sizer. Carbonaceous aerosol was collected on filters for characterization and aging experiments. Characterization included infrared and visible spectroscopy for composition and absorption, respectively, and colorimetry. Depending on the combustion conditions, the aerosol ranged from organic to elemental (i.e., black) carbon. The organic aerosol included polymer and non-polymer species, distinguished using infrared spectroscopy. Selected light-absorbing organic aerosol samples from red and yellow PETG underwent irradiation in a solar simulator and oxidation in a flow tube with ozone at 50 ppb. The organic aerosol lost absorption more through irradiation than ozone oxidation, i.e., 1 d of irradiation led to a significant, 50% decrease for samples from both red and yellow PETG. Together, the results demonstrate that the initial absorption of carbonaceous aerosol from open burning of plastics varies significantly and that the absorption of light-absorbing organic aerosol at moderate temperatures is highly dynamic upon atmospheric aging.

papers.title: Solid-electrolyte interphase enables catalyst-free electrocatalytic semi-hydrogenation of terminal alkynes in an undivided cell
Union of the in situ Generated ortho-Quinone Methides (o-QMs) with Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABB) towards the Synthesis of Functionalized Azetidines
papers.abstract: We herein disclose the reaction of in situ generated ortho-quinone methides (o-QMs) with Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABB). The reaction proceeded through an orthogonal Lewis acid activation of the precursor compounds to o-QMs in presence of ABB and serves as the key for the current development. The 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP) plays an important role as solvent in the reaction. Importantly, similar reaction of p-QMs with ABB could be promoted only in HFIP. This study highlights a new strategy for the formation of functionalized azetidines..

papers.title: Facile Gram-Scale Solution Phase Synthesis of a Universal Cathepsin B Cleavable Antibody-Drug Conjugate Linker
papers.abstract: Antibody drug conjugates (ADCs) are a key therapy in the cancer treatment arsenal. Critical to the success of the ADC is the release of the drug cargo at the desired site and, thus, enzymatically or chemically responsive linkers, connecting the drug to the antibody, play a central role. Linkers containing the peptide sequence Glu-Val-Cit are particularly important as cleavage of this peptide occurs by both murine and human cathepsin B enzymes. Additional linker design considerations include components for free drug release via the self-immolative moiety para-aminobenzyl alcohol (PABOH), copper-free click conjugation to an azide functionalized antibody using dibenzocyclooctyne (DBCO), and aqueous solubility via a polyethylene glycol space (PEG). To facilitate wide-spread use and translation, we describe the 9-step gram scale synthesis of the linker DBCO-PEG4-Glu-Val-Cit-PABOH conjugated to monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE). Using only liquid-phase synthesis protocols and precipitation-based intermediate isolations gives the drug-linker conjugate in 36% yield and this method is an improvement over prior methods (yield <1%). Finally, we prepare the corresponding MMAE-linked ADC and validate its potency in human breast cancer cell lines.

papers.title: Polyethylene-block-Polyacrylate Block Copolymer Electrolytes with High Room-Temperature Ionic Conductivity
papers.abstract: Conventional block copolymer (BCP) based polymer electrolytes take advantage of the mechanical strength provided by a high glass transition temperature (Tg) block, and the ion-conducting properties of a low Tg block. However, the presence of a glassy phase often limits conductivity by suppressing segmental mobility. In this work, we develop polyethylene-block-poly(meth)acrylate block copolymers doped with ionic liquid 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (EMIM-TFSI) and achieve a significantly high ionic conductivity of ~1 mS/cm at room temperature. The high conductivity is attributed to the low Tg of both blocks which leads to enhanced chain dynamics and efficient ion transport, coupled with a sharp interface between PE and PMMA blocks and crystallinity of the PE block. At the same time, our mechanical measurements show that these materials retain elastic solid-like behavior, providing the mechanical stability required for solid electrolyte applications. We also studied the effects of nanoscale morphology on ionic transport for a better understanding of the high ionic conductivity of these systems. Our study indicates that nanoscale interfacial structure and segmental chain motion jointly contribute to the elevated ionic conductivity of these materials. Overall, these polyethylene-blockpoly(meth)acrylate electrolytes represent a promising route toward mechanically robust, thermally stable, and highly conductive solid-state electrolytes.

papers.title: Peptide heterogeneity enables and stabilises peptide/nucleic acid coacervates
papers.abstract: Prebiotic environments were likely dominated by chemically heterogeneous mixtures of short peptides and oligonucleotides, yet the consequences of this diversity for the emergence of primitive compartments remain poorly understood. Here, we show that peptide length, sequence, and compositional complexity critically shape coacervation with short nucleic acids under prebiotically relevant conditions. Longer peptides form more stable coacervates, but mixed systems often outperform their pure components, revealing that heterogeneity can strengthen rather than destabilise phase separation. Sequence-specific effects further tune assembly: arginine-rich peptides outcompete lysine analogues, C-terminal glycine weakens stability, and even negatively charged residues can promote coacervation when multivalency and hydrogen bonding are preserved. Most strikingly, a chemically diverse tripeptide library readily coacervates with a range of DNA and RNA oligonucleotides, while retaining robust biomolecular partitioning and enhanced tolerance to Mg 2+ stress. Together, these findings indicate that prebiotic chemical imperfection does not hinder protocell formation, but instead provides a powerful route to functional primitive coacervates.

papers.title: New Implementation of Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory and Application to Molecules with Variable Diradical Character and Conical Intersections
papers.abstract: Mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT) improves upon the original spin-flip TDDFT (SF-TDDFT) approach by expanding the configurational space of the response states via a mixed-reference reduced density matrix, specifically, an equal mixture of the density matrices from the MS = +1 and MS = −1 components of the lowest triplet state. MRSF-TDDFT improves the description of the spin-flip target states and the respective energy differences and eliminates the problem of spin-contamination that often spoils the description of higher-lying states in SF-TDDFT. This article presents the theoretical framework and details of a new implementation of MRSF-TDDFT in the Q-Chem software package. The implementation includes calculations of energies and properties, including transition dipole moments, oscillator strengths, spin–orbit couplings, and density-matrix based analyses of the MRSF states and transitions. The capabilities of the theory are illustrated by applications to diradicals and a reduced retinal model, the penta-2,4-dieniminium cation, used to evaluate the performance of electronic structure methods in describing conical intersections.

papers.title: Giant barocaloric effect from spin crossover in a green nitroprusside framework†
papers.abstract: The interest in spin crossover for solid-state cooling is growing. We investigate the spin crossover transitions of [Fe(pyridine)2Fe(CN)5NO] and [Fe(pyrazine)Fe(CN)5NO] by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, high-pressure X-ray diffraction, magnetometry, and high-pressure calorimetry. The dehydrated form of the latter compound shows a reversible cooling effect (∆Tad,rev) of ∼15K at 1.2 kbar. This is high in the context of other reported spin-crossover barocalorics, and competitive within the field at large. The excellent performance results from a large barocaloric coefficient (dT1/2/dp = 35K kbar−1). In addition, the one-pot synthesis is simple and free from toxic solvents.

papers.title: Intrachain Interactions Accelerate Access to a Modifiable Fluoro-Polyester Library With End-of Life Fluoride Recyclability
papers.abstract: The growing polymer chain is typically viewed as a passive product of catalysis, yet here we show that its microstructure can actively govern catalytic rate. In the ring-opening copolymerisation (ROCOP) of fluorinated epoxides with cyclic anhydrides, rate acceleration occurs most clearly when both monomers are aromatic and only one is fluorinated. Density functional theory and mechanistic experiments rule out interactions with the catalyst as the origin of this effect, instead implicating intrachain π–π stacking between the fluorinated carboxylate chain end and aromatic units of the growing polyester as the dominant transition-state-stabilising interaction. With each turnover, the polymer chain constructs a structured non-covalent environment around the active centre, a role conceptually analogous to the binding cavity of an enzyme. This principle is accompanied by a broad fluorinated polyester library with tunable glass transition temperatures spanning below −14 °C to 144 °C, straightforward post-polymerisation modification via para-fluoro thiol-click chemistry, and quantitative fluorine recovery as sodium fluoride upon degradation. These findings reframe chain microstructure as an underexploited handle for controlling reactivity in chain-growth polymerisation.

papers.title: Zwitterionic Polysiloxanes with Extreme Dielectric Permittivity
papers.abstract: The design and synthesis of high permittivity polymers face a key challenge; namely, strong polarization requires concentrated dipoles that give rise to high thermal transition temperatures. The inverse relationship between permittivity and mobility limits the dielectric constant of all dipolar materials. Consequently, for pure polymers, the largest known dielectric constants are roughly 100 for vinylidene fluoride copolymers at the Curie temperature and 35 for room-temperature polymer melts. Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of a zwitterionic polysiloxane with a static dielectric constant of 420 at room temperature, the largest value achieved to date.
