This specific polysiloxane contains pendent zwitterionic dipoles with long, flexible spacers that simultaneously amplify dipole moment and dilute strong coulombic interactions, yielding a glass transition temperature Tg of-14 °C. This novel high-κ dielectric polymer overcomes the permittivity-mobility limitation thereby challenging the existing paradigm for dipolar polymer dielectrics.

papers.title: Assessing the accuracy of Bayesian-optimized CGMD in predicting polymer miscibility
papers.abstract: Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) presents a computationally efficient alternative to all-atom (AA) simulations for modeling polymer systems, yet the accuracy of its predictions for emergent thermodynamic properties remains a critical challenge. This study builds upon our previous work, which introduced a Bayesian optimization framework for refining Martini3 force field topologies, to validate the transferability of these optimized models to multi-component systems. We demonstrate that CG force fields, optimized solely against single-chain properties (density and radius of gyration), can qualitatively estimate the complex phase behavior of polymer blends. Bayesian-optimized topologies for polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), polystyrene (PS), poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA), and polyethylene (PE) were evaluated through direct simulation of binary blend morphologies. The framework successfully predicted macroscopic phase separation in the immiscible PS-PMMA system and complete miscibility in the PVDF-PMMA system, with resulting density profiles showing excellent qualitative agreement with experimental observations. Flory-Huggins interaction parameters (χ) estimated from Hildebrand solubility parameters (𝛿) correctly rank relative miscibilities and align qualitatively with literature trends, though quantitative values are systematically overestimated due to limitations of the regular solution approximation. Our results show that optimizing for fundamental properties such as density and radius of gyration (achieving <10% error) implicitly captures the necessary thermodynamic contributions to predict complex, multi-component phase behaviors. This work establishes Bayesian-optimized CGMD as a robust and predictive tool for polymer blend thermodynamics, effectively bridging the gap between computational efficiency and predictive fidelity in materials discovery.

papers.title: Droplet microfluidic hydrogen/deuterium exchange for investigating protein dynamics with millisecond precision
papers.abstract: Hydrogen/deuterium exchange (HDX) methods for studying protein dynamics would benefit from millisecond-scale incubations to probe intrinsically disordered proteins, highly dynamic regions and conformation changes. Here we investigate droplet microfluidics for rapid mixing to trigger D 2 O labelling, uniform incubations and rapid droplet merging for acid quenching in advance of mass spectrometry. A surfactant-free merging approach combining expansion elements for synchronised droplet collision proved robust. The high diffusive flux of D 2 O and protons enable microsecond mixing to trigger and arrest D 2 O labelling, respectively, affording the possibility of single millisecond incubations. Droplet HDX processors were used to measure the fast uptake characteristics of a model peptide. Forward exchange measurements demonstrate D 2 O labelling to be the rate-limiting step, in essence defining 10 milliseconds as the minimum practical incubation time for proteins in typical physiological conditions. With the ability to access millisecond time scales the fast dynamics of calmodulin, a model of calcium-triggered allostery with rapid conformational switching, was investigated. At 10 milliseconds, we could observe significant deuterium uptake within the well-defined EF-hand motifs (Ca 2+ binding sites). These findings demonstrate millisecond HDX enabled by droplet microfluidics allows areas of heightened plasticity to be detected within a stably folded protein.

papers.title: An Alkali Amide Approach to Triphosphabenzenes
papers.abstract: A new approach to triphosphabenzenes using simple and commercially available organolithium reagents is presented. LiNMe 2 catalyzes the cyclotrimerization of triphenylmethylphosphaalkyne ( 1 ) to yield 2,4,6-tris(triphenylmethyl)-Dewar-1,3,5-triphosphabenzene ( 2 ). The reaction is solvent dependent where noncoordinating solvents allow the reaction to proceed catalytically. In contrast THF traps the cyclic λ 4 -triphosphabenzene anion 3 , intercepting the addition of LiNMe 2 during the cyclotrimerization of 1 . In the absence of the stabilizing effect of THF, LiNMe 2 is eliminated from 3 and the symmetric 1,3,5-triphosphabenzene 2’ forms. Expanding to other Group 1 amides, KN(SiMe 3 ) 2 mediates the cyclotrimerization of 1 via a C( sp 3 )–H deprotonation of weakly acidic benzyl derivatives, allowing the synthesis and characterization of functionalized λ 4 -triphosphabenzene anions and λ 5 -triphosphabenzenes ( 6a to 6e ).

papers.title: Dual Active Forms of Milstein’s Catalyst for Ester Hydrogenation
papers.abstract: In this article, we report that Milstein’s ruthenium-pincer catalyst for ester hydrogenation, previously shown to convert to a highly active form through release of ethane, is also moderately active in its original form prior to ethane release, provided an alcohol co-catalyst is present. We describe a detailed experimental and computational study of the mechanism of ester hydrogenation catalyzed by the original form of Milstein’s catalyst. We demonstrate through kinetic studies that the esterhydrogenation reaction is first-order in ester and ruthenium catalyst, zero-order in hydrogen, and exhibits a saturation dependence on the concentration of the product alcohol. By studying catalyst speciation spectroscopically, we establish that an equilibrium between two potential resting states, a dihydride complex and a hydridoalkoxide complex, is shifted nearly completely toward the dihydride under catalytically relevant conditions. We report a thorough computational analysis of the mechanism using density functional theory, which is fully consistent with the observed kinetics and catalyst resting speciation. In the minimum-energy pathway, ester reduction proceeds through dechelation of the pincer ligand’s diethylamino group, and the CH 2 linkers of the pincer ligand are not involved in catalytic turnover.

papers.title: Title: Going NUTS on SAXS: Quantifying Nanoparticle Interactions from Small Angle X-ray Scattering Data using No-U-Turn Sampling
papers.abstract: Small angle x-ray scattering (SAXS) is a powerful technique for probing nanoscale structure and interactions in colloidal systems. Interparticle interactions are typically inferred through model-based fitting of experimental SAXS profiles, but this inverse problem is inherently ill-posed, as multiple parameter combinations can yield equally good fits. Bayesian methods provide a natural framework to address this challenge, enabling systematic exploration of the parameter space to obtain sets of plausible solutions rather than a single-best fit solution provided by existing fitting methods. In this work, we employ a machine learning-accelerated No-U-Turn Sampling (NUTS) workflow to analyse experimentally obtained SAXS profiles of gold nanoparticles with varying sizes, ligand chemistries, solvent conditions, and temperatures to systematically investigate how these factors affect colloidal interactions and stability. This approach allows for quantification of DLVO interaction parameters while providing a framework which could be extended to study more complex, non-DLVO interactions within colloidal systems.

papers.title: Rigor & Reproducibility in Electrocatalysis: Integrating Theory and Experiment
papers.abstract: Electrocatalysis is central to electrified energy conversion technologies, including the production of fuels and chemicals from renewable electricity. In recent years, atomistic modeling based on density functional theory (DFT) has become an indispensable tool for catalysis researchers because it can provide a molecular-level perspective into catalytic reactivity that is otherwise inaccessible to experimental measurements. Computational electrocatalysis model inputs are intended to capture fundamental understanding of the complex interfacial environment of the catalytic active site, but rely on practical approximations that can affect the reliability of insights gained from DFT. This Perspective outlines a framework for rigorous and reproducible integration of theory and experiment in heterogeneous electrocatalysis research. We discuss state-of-the-art computational methods and sources of error in model development and interpretation. We describe opportunities for validation of theoretical models and experimental interpretations as it pertains to the structure of active sites, reaction energetics, and microkinetic modeling. We provide examples to help computational researchers develop models that move beyond obtaining qualitative agreement with reactivity trends, and toward the development of rigorous mechanistic insights that can be leveraged to predict promising new catalysts or operating conditions. Rigor and reproducibility are enhanced when theory and experiment have multiple nodes of connection, which enhances the longevity and robustness of conclusions and insights about electrocatalytic reactivity.

papers.title: Computer-Guided In-situ Screening of Poly(acetylene)s for Gene Delivery
papers.abstract: We report a new methodology for the discovery of polymer-based gene vectors that enables the simultaneous optimization of polymer composition and polyplex formulation, while bypassing the need to prepare, isolate, and characterise new candidates using conventional polymer synthesis. At the core of this approach is the combination of computer-aided experimental design, in situ screening of polymer composition and polyplex formulation, and machine learning, which allows us to treat polymer synthesis and formulation as a single optimizable problem. Central to this methodology is a new reactive and water-soluble poly(acetylene), poly(N-(propargyl)-2-(aminooxy)-acetamide), which can be functionalized in aqueous conditions with readily available aldehydes. This provides candidate polymers under biologically compatible conditions, which are then directly complexed with nucleic acids and evaluated within the same workflow. Iterative modelling then correlates inputs readily controlled by the operator—such as reagent concentrations and ratios—with the key performance metric, transfection efficiency, guiding subsequent rounds of candidate generation. In doing so, we move beyond post hoc correlations of physicochemical properties to establish an iterative, data-driven methodology for materials discovery. Ultimately, this methodology has unlocked the potential of poly(acetylene)s, a polymer family not previously explored in this context, to move beyond compositional mimicry and capture the dynamic helicity that underpins nucleic acid complexation and delivery in natural systems.

papers.title: Mechanistic Pluralism in a Pd(II)-Catalyzed Aminopalladation Probed by Helium Nanodroplet Ion Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: We employed mass spectrometry and infrared ion spectroscopy of mass-selected ions in ultracold helium nanodroplets to identify and structurally characterize transient species probed during the intramolecular aminopalladation step of a palladium(II) chloride-catalyzed reaction of O-allyl tosylcarbamate. We also evaluated the effect of quaternary ammonium salt addition on the reaction mechanism. By recording mass spectra of reaction mixtures under different conditions, we identified signals with m/z ratios and isotope patterns consistent with previously proposed intermediates for both syn- and anti-aminopalladation pathways were identified. Addition of tetramethylammonium (TMA) acetate reduced the intensity of the antiaminopalladation (anti-AP) exclusive intermediate. The isolated anti-AP intermediate, characterized by helium nanodroplet spectroscopy, was consistent with previously proposed structures, while the other intermediate of interest corresponded to two isomeric intermediates: one exclusive to the syn-AP step and another present in both proposed reaction pathways. Reaction monitoring under conditions similar to those used in synthesis revealed the evolution of the isomer mixture over time, which was interpreted as the consumption of the syn-AP exclusive intermediate and the formation of the intermediate common to both pathways. These results provide experimental evidence that both syn- and anti-aminopalladation pathways are feasible and could contribute to the reaction outcome.

papers.title: α-Alkylated α-Amino Acids Reduce the Aggregation of Unfolded Peptides
papers.abstract: Aberrant aggregation complicates the development of bioactive peptides. Here, we generate new α-ethylated variants of proteinogenic amino acids and demonstrate that they prevent peptide aggregation through a mechanism distinct from their α-methylated counterparts. Whereas α-methylated residues prevent aggregation by favoring helix formation, α-ethylated residues prevent aggregation without promoting secondary structure.

papers.title: Piecewise Stereoselective Assembly of Multi-Substituted Alkenes
papers.abstract: Multi-substituted alkenes are valuable structural motifs that also serve as key intermediates in complexity-building transformations; however, their stereoselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Vinyl bromides are appealing coupling handles for alkene synthesis, though their application would be greatly enhanced if they could be coupled directly with alkyl radicals derived from feedstock alcohols. Herein, we report a nickel metallaphotoredox-enabled deoxygenative cross-coupling of vinyl bromides with alcohols, providing a direct, modular approach to multi-substituted alkenes. This transformation exhibits broad substrate scope across both alcohol and vinyl bromide partners, delivering over 30 multi-substituted alkenes. Moreover, we developed a complementary stereoselective bromovinylation from readily synthesized gem -dibromoolefins to address the limited availability of stereodefined vinyl bromides. In the presence of a phthalimide additive, selective monofunctionalization enables access to over 40 stereodefined vinyl bromides, providing a general and stereoselective pathway to these otherwise difficult-to-access intermediates. Direct access to vinyl bromides enables piecewise stereoselective assembly of multi-substituted alkenes through sequential alcohol coupling or stereoretentive Suzuki-Miyaura reactions. These strategies are illustrated via iterative cross-coupling sequences and the total synthesis of (+)-sponalisolide B.

papers.title: Structural Hotspot Conditioning for Diffusion-Based Molecular Design
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based generative models have emerged as powerful tools for structure-based molecular design, yet their effectiveness depends critically on how prior information about protein–ligand interactions is incorporated into the generative process. In this work, we propose and systematically investigate structural hotspot conditioning as a mechanism to inject interaction-relevant chemical knowledge into pocketconditioned diffusion models. We evaluate three complementary strategies developed for defining atomlevel reference points: docking score–based atom selection, structure-based pharmacophore localization, and data-driven prediction of hydrogen-bonding sites. Using MolSnapper as a unified diffusion-based generative model, we benchmark these strategies on a standardized CrossDocked2020 test set, evaluating docking-derived affinity estimates, physicochemical quality, structural plausibility, and chemical diversity. Compared to established baselines, our explicit hotspot-based conditioning systematically alters generative behavior, enabling controllable trade-offs between affinity, chemical feasibility, and diversity. An iterative case study on the shallow allosteric pocket of Ube2T further illustrates how alternating hotspot strategies supports effective exploration and prioritization of ligand candidates for challenging targets. Overall, this work establishes structural hotspot conditioning as a flexible and tunable design variable for guiding diffusion-based molecular generation toward chemically meaningful solutions.

papers.title: PNA-Guided Modular Self-Assembly of Antibody-Oligonucleotide Constructs Enables Targeted Oligonucleotide Delivery
papers.abstract: Antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates (AOCs) hold strong potential for targeted nucleic acid delivery, but developments are limited by labor-intensive covalent chemistries and structural heterogeneity. Here, we introduce a modular, non-covalent AOC platform based on affinity-driven construct assembly between a recombinant antibody containing anti-tag domains and a synthetic peptide–peptide nucleic acid (pTagPNA) hybrid. This approach enables rapid, purification-free conjugation of antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) with defined antibodyoligonucleotide ratios. Using an ASO targeting MALAT1, a long non-coding RNA implicated in cancer progression, we demonstrate successful receptor-mediated uptake and ~50% knockdown of MALAT1 expression after 24 hours in B cells. The platform maintains antibody functionality, avoids immunogenic tags, and is compatible with different loading ratios and pTag variants. By eliminating the need for covalent conjugation and instead making use of noncovalent self-assembly chemistries, which leads to increased construct homogeneity, this work establishes a new versatile delivery strategy for oligonucleotide therapeutics, with broad applicability in oncology, immunology, and genetic diseases.

papers.title: On the role of the host-guest interaction in the spin conversion of Multi-Resonant TADF systems: a vibronic picture
papers.abstract: Multi-Resonant Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence (MR-TADF) systems are valuable solutions to enhance the performance of light-emitting devices thanks to their narrow emission and small ΔE ST . While TADF is often absent in solutions, it is frequently activated upon introducing the MR emitter in a host matrix. This solid-state enhancement turned out to be sensitive to the host’s chemical nature. Experimental measurements on the MR emitter, DABNA-1, suggested that the TADF behavior is active in mCBP but suppressed in DPEPO. This difference was attributed to the mediation of a higher-lying exciplex state in the spin conversion, thermally accessible in mCBP while not in DPEPO. In this work, we employed high-level wavefunction based methods (SCS-CC2) to model the electronic structure, the conformational and environmental effects and the spin conversion kinetics of mCBP:DABNA-1 and DPEPO:DABNA-1 dimers. Our calculations revealed that, in both host environments, the exciplex state remains nearly 1 eV above S 1 and T 1 , ruling out its direct mediation even when accounting for conformational and environmental effects. By including the Herzberg-Teller and the Spin-Vibronic Coupling mechanisms into Fermi’s Golden Rule, the ISC and RISC rates resulted to be of the same order of magnitude (10 6 s -1 and 10 3 s -1 , respectively) in both mCBP:DABNA-1 and DPEPO:DABNA-1. The identical spin conversion picture predicted in both hosts challenges the current understanding of the host-guest interaction in MR-TADF systems. Further experimental and theoretical studies are necessary to unambiguously rationalize the spin conversion dynamics, also including secondary non-radiative processes.

papers.title: Tipping the Scales: A Mechanical Analogy for Band Filling in Metals
papers.abstract: Band theory offers a useful framework for understanding the physical properties of metals, yet students in introductory chemistry courses consistently find the concepts of band filling and bonding versus antibonding states challenging. In particular, the connection between electron occupancy of a broad s-d band and trends in metallic bond strength across Groups 1–12 is frequently misunderstood. To address this difficulty, we describe an inexpensive, interactive classroom demonstration that uses a mechanical seesaw analogy to model band filling and its consequences for metallic bonding. Golf balls placed at fixed positions along the seesaw represent electrons occupying bonding and antibonding regions of a single composite band, while the force measured at one end of the seesaw corresponds to net bond strength. As the seesaw is progressively loaded, the measured force follows an inverted U-shaped trend that mirrors experimental melting point trends for transition metals. Student feedback collected immediately after the demonstration indicates improved conceptual understanding of bonding versus antibonding and a clearer connection between band filling and metallic bond strength. This demonstration provides a tangible, low-cost approach for reinforcing band theory concepts at the introductory level.

papers.title: Tissue-Stratified Functional Interpretation of Frontotemporal Dementia Risk Loci using AlphaGenome and GTEx Molecular QTL Integration
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is a major cause of early-onset dementia. In sporadic FTD, non-coding risk variants are likely to act through tissue-specific regulatory mechanisms, making GWAS loci difficult to interpret mechanistically. METHODS: We analyzed sporadic FTD GWAS summary statistics (4,685 cases; 15,308 controls), harmonized variants to GRCh38, defined LD-based loci, scored candidates with AlphaGenome, and integrated GENCODE, ENCODE cCREs, GTEx brain and blood/immune eQTL/sQTL evidence, SuSiE PIP summaries, and GTEx gene expression. RESULTS: Among 66,726 candidate variants, overlapping loci collapsed into three genome-wide significant signals. In each signal, the top integrated functional candidate differed from the lead GWAS SNP. Tissue-stratified evidence supported one brain-dominant 17q21.31 signal, one mixed 17q21.31 signal, and one blood/immune-dominant chromosome 19 signal. DISCUSSION: This framework generates tissue-aware, testable variant-gene hypotheses from sFTD GWAS loci and provides a practical foundation for experimental follow-up and future colocalization analyses.

papers.title: Thrombin-responsive minimal peptide coacervates for thrombolytic delivery
papers.abstract: Peptide coacervates formed through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) are emerging as promising delivery vehicles because they combine structural simplicity with dynamic cargo sequestration and release. However, integrating biologically relevant triggers into minimal peptide coacervates remains challenging. Here we report thrombin-responsive peptide coacervates based on a short sticker-spacer-sticker design, in which the thrombin-cleavable motif LVPR↓GS is encoded directly into the phase-separating sequence. These peptides form coacervate microdroplets that efficiently sequester protein cargo and rapidly disassemble upon thrombin-mediated cleavage, thereby enabling controlled release of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA). Sequence optimization further reveals that terminal incorporation of an RGD motif enhances LLPS propensity, increases coacervate dynamics and improves partitioning of both tPA and thrombin, resulting in more efficient clot-associated thrombolytic delivery. Finally, incorporation of Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles converts these coacervates into magnetically steerable microrobotic carriers that retain thrombin responsiveness while gaining enhanced stability and directional control. Together, these results establish a minimal peptide coacervate platform for enzyme-activated and magnetically guided thrombolytic delivery, and provide a strategy for engineering functional therapeutic protocells from short designer peptides.

papers.title: PyRosettaCluster: a Python framework for scalable and reproducible bio-macromolecular modeling and design
papers.abstract: The Rosetta software suite offers a set of powerful tools for bio-macromolecular modeling and design capable of high-resolution protein structure refinement and generation of de novo designed proteins with sub-angstrom atomic accuracy. Leveraging these tools at scale requires both immense computational resources and domain expertise, without which may lead to results that are not scientifically reproducible by independent investigators, in part due to challenges in communicating all of the necessary runtime configurations and system requirements. To address these reproducibility challenges for large-scale simulation, we developed PyRosettaCluster , a versatile Python-based framework integrated into PyRosetta software to automatically capture the simulation data required to accurately reproduce a decoy and directly encode it into every output decoy file. PyRosettaCluster abstracts away complicated task execution orchestration details for distributed workflows, effectively parallelizing modular, user-defined PyRosetta protocols parameterized by user-defined tasks using the lightweight Dask library. PyRosettaCluster supports integration of emerging third-party software applications into PyRosetta protocols, enabling inference of modern graphics processing unit (GPU)-accelerated artificial intelligence (AI) models for bio-macromolecular modeling and design tasks, provided they preserve deterministic runtime behavior for reproducibility purposes. Integration with the Dask-Jobqueue library enables job scheduling on high-performance computing (HPC) or elastic cloud compute infrastructure with arbitrary compute resources. Overall, this multipurpose tool provides a basis for scalable and reproducible bio-macromolecular modeling and design workflows in PyRosetta software. PyRosettaCluster was merged into the Rosetta software suite codebase in September 2020, and its source code has been publicly accessible since March 2024.

papers.title: Sequence-Transferrable Machine Learning Prediction of Flavin-Dependent Photoenzyme Spectral Properties
papers.abstract: Predicting the optical properties of proteins is critical for the understanding and design of photoactive proteins. Red-shifting flavin-dependent photoenzymes’ spectra beyond the usual blue range has become an attractive goal for potential industrial use of photoenzymes for chemical synthesis. However, making such predictions using quantum chemical methods can be computationally intractable, especially if the correct description of the photoexcitation requires multireference methods. We present a sequence-transferrable machine learning framework, LIGand-based PROtein-agnostic SPECTral prediciton (LIG-PROSPECT), to predict the absorption spectra of flavin-dependent photoenzyme variants in the presence of specific substrates. We make use of structural descriptors of cofactor-substrate ensembles as a proxy to represent the 3D conformational features of protein sequences to enable the classification of cyan-light and red-light absorbing peaks for different conformations and the prediction of spectral features of the proteins using linear regression, offering resource-efficient alternatives to multireference quantum mechanical calculations for screening protein sequences for desired photophysical properties.

papers.title: Optimized Octahedral Geometry and Hidden Rigidity of a mer-Tridentate N-Heterocyclic Carbene Ligand Enhance Luminescence of an Fe(III) Complex
papers.abstract: Fe(III) N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) complexes are emerging photoactive first-row transition metal complexes. While optimizing ligand bite angles is a widely employed strategy to extend photoactive excited states, the lack of tridentate NHC ligands prevents exploration of better coordination geometries in the first-row transition metal complexes. Here, we demonstrate that a newly designed methylene-bridged mer-tridentate NHC ligand provides an improved coordination bite angle. Continuous Shape Measure (CShM) analysis reveals that the Fe(III) complex exhibits a significantly improved octahedral geometry (0.35) compared to existing phenylene-bridged mer-tridentate ligands (3.15). This optimized geometry results in a prolonged 2LMCT lifetime (τ = 670 ps), which is longer compared to the Fe(III) complexes with reported bidentate or mer-tridentate ligands. The complex retains a better octahedral geometry even in the distorted quartet metal-centered (4MC) state, indicating enhanced structural rigidity of the coordination environment. The methylene-bridges seem inherently flexible; however, we revealed that the geometric constraints of the mer-tridentate arrangement and methylene moieties provide counterintuitive hidden structural rigidity. This work establishes the new mer-tridentate NHC ligand scaffold as a promising ligand platform for developing photoactive first-row transition metal complexes.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn to comply with journal policy.

papers.title: Hybrid Adsorption-Liquefaction Process for Post-combustion CO2 Capture
papers.abstract: The potential of a hybrid process combining two separation processes: pressure-vacuum swing adsorption (PVSA) and cryogenic CO 2 purification/liquefaction is explored using a system-level integrated techno-economic optimization framework. Detailed process models of the PVSA and the liquefaction units developed in gProms were used to train Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based surrogates. These surrogates were integrated with a detailed costing framework to perform techno-economic optimization of both standalone PVSA and hybrid processes. A wide range of flue gas CO 2 compositions ranging from 3.5-30 mol % are studied. Unconstrained cost optimizations of a standalone PVSA process for feed CO 2 compositions ≤13 mol% showed that at low-purity levels (≤60 mol%) and high recovery levels (≥90%), the cost of CO 2 avoided reduced by more than half compared to when the standalone-PVSA process produces both high purity (≥95 mol%) and high recovery (≥90%). Parametric analysis of a cryogenic CO 2 purification process showed that a high level of purification (purity ≥ 98 mol%) is achievable with only two flash stages, with reasonable recoveries. The hybrid process was found to be cost-competitive with a conventional monoethanolamine (MEA) absorption process for flue gas CO 2 compositions ≥7.5 mol% under the constraints of ≥95 mol% purity and ≥90% overall recovery. The key advantages of the hybrid are the avoidance of deep vacuums, the reduction in plant footprint, and the ability to meet product oxygen specifications.

papers.title: Electrotunable Kapitza Resistance at Electrode-Water Interfaces: The Importance of Electrode Metallicity
papers.abstract: The electrolyte-water-metal interface plays a vital role in electrochemical processes within nanocapacitors and in thermal management in nanoscale devices. Understanding the microscopic origins of thermal transport at these nanomaterial-fluid interfaces is crucial for advancing technologies in areas such as electrochemical energy storage and thermoplasmonics. Here, we use constant potential molecular dynamics simulations with fully dynamic electrodes to create steady heat fluxes in confined solutions that can respond to changes in the interfacial electrostatic environment at constant voltages. Our findings reveal that the Kapitza Resistance (KR) can be adjusted by applying voltage, altering ionic strength through the addition of salt, and, importantly, varying the metallicity of the electrodes. We show that the KR decreases with increasing electrode polarization, and salt concentrations above one molal further improve this voltage response, particularly with high effective metallicity (highly polarizable) electrodes. We attribute this response to a synergistic effect induced by the presence of the ions next to the electrodes, and the reorientation of a nanometer-thick layer of water that solvates the electrodes. We present in our work a large scale, non-equilibrium analysis that provides predictions of conditions necessary to tune the KR by considering experimentally relevant factors, including electrode metallicity, capacitance, and bias voltage.

papers.title: Probing the free rotary oscillations around a single ruthenium atom in anorganometallic complex
papers.abstract: A variety of rotary molecular motors powered by light, chemical energy or tunnelling electrons have been synthesized and their operation in solution, in gels or on surfaces has been demonstrated. However, the single-molecule mechanics of such machines remain scarcely studied and very little data regarding their quantified performances have been disclosed. Here, we report on the synthesis of a series of molecules incorporating a five-arm rotor subunit and the direct quantitative measurement of the work generated by its rotation around the central ruthenium atom. We have used single-molecule force spectroscopy (SMFS) to detect the autonomous oscillations. We demonstrate that a mechanical load does not prevent rotation and show that the chemical nature of the arms influences the energy barrier, causing differences in the work that the motor can generate. Our results illustrate that SMFS, which is now widely used to probe processes at the scale of a few tens of nanometers in biomacromolecules, can detect motions around a single atom in a tiny synthetic molecule.

papers.title: Probing the Molecular Mechanisms of Ion Transport in High-Conductivity Lithium-Ion Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Fluorinated nitrile and acetone solvents have been recently shown to enable lithiumion electrolytes with ionic conductivities of up to 45ms cm−1, more than four times higher than current commercial formulations. To understand the physical origins of this enhanced performance, we employ molecular dynamics simulations to target the ion transport mechanisms. Non-polarizable classical force fields can be tuned to successfully predict the ionic conductivity by down-scaling the electrostatic interactions. However, the structure of the ion solvation shells and consequent transport mechanisms are inconsistent with experimental observations. Important missing interactions are added explicitly via polarisable force fields and implicitly via machine learning force fields, trained on extensive ab initio simulations. Both frameworks fail at recovering the experimental observables for the more complex fluorinated electrolyte, whereas they succeed at predicting the solvation structures in acetone. Our results underscore the importance of accurate force field choice when interpreting the molecular-scale mechanisms of ion transport, particularly for electrolytes with complex chemistries. The simulation framework developed here provides a valuable tool for virtually screening and rationally designing high-performance electrolyte molecules.

papers.title: A novel selenium-substituted meso-phenyl BODIPY with potential theranostic applications: viscosity sensing and singlet-oxygen photosensitization
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a novel strategy for the development of theranostic compounds based on selenium-containing meso-phenyl BODIPYs. The synthesized compound exhibited a high fluorescence quantum yield and sensitivity to changes in the viscosity of the medium. In addition, it displayed singlet-oxygen photosensitizing capability. The compound shows a balanced combination of these two properties —viscosity sensing and photosensitization—, standing out compared with most meso-phenyl BODIPYs, which are not efficient photosensitizers, and iodinated meso-phenyl BODIPYs, which are typically weakly emissive. The simultaneous integration of these two functions remains challenging because fluorescence emission and singlet-oxygen generation are typically competing photophysical pathways. For this reason, the selenium-containing mesophenyl BODIPY reported here is proposed as a lead structure for the development of a broader family of theranostic compounds.

papers.title: Narrowband sky-blue emission from acceptor-extended MR-
papers.abstract: Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) dendrimers are promising solution-processable emitters for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), combining the well-defined structures of small molecules with the processability of macromolecular systems. Here we report the design, synthesis, and optoelectronic characterization of novel multiresonant TADF (MR-TADF) dendrimers TCzBN-BMes and TCzBN-DBMes, in which a 3,6-substituted carbazole or its dendrons are further functionalized with electron-accepting dimesitylborane groups. This dendron engineering strategy attenuates the dendron donor strength, preserving narrowband sky-blue emission compared to TCzBN-tCz with all-carbazole dendrimers. In dilute toluene TCzBN-BMes and TCzBN-DBMes exhibit λPL of 477 and 474 nm, with full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 25 and 21 nm and photoluminescence quantum yields (ΦPL) of 79 and 76%, respectively. In doped films ΦPL increases to 92 and 88% while maintaining narrowband profiles (FWHM = 26 and 23 nm). Solution-processed OLEDs based on TCzBN-BMes and TCzBN-DBMes achieve maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEmax) of 12.6 and 10.9% with CIE coordinates of (0.12, 0.22) and (0.12, 0.20), respectively. Incorporation into hyperfluorescent devices reduces efficiency roll-off, with TCzBN-BMes reaching an enhanced EQEmax of 14.5% at CIE (0.16, 0.30) when supported by sensitisation. These results demonstrate that dendron functionalization 2 with electron-accepting units offers an approach to developing narrowband blue emission in MR-TADF dendrimers, while preserving high device performance.

papers.title: Multi-objective Optimization of Synthetically Accessible Homogeneous Catalysts Reveals Tradeoffs for Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
papers.abstract: The selective conversion of methane to methanol remains a major challenge in catalysis, and no earth-abundant homogeneous catalyst has been demonstrated to carry out this transformation with high turnover. To explore previously synthesized complexes that might be amenable for this transformation, we start from macrocyclic ligands from experimental structures in the Cambridge Structural Database. After expanding this set of ligands with Hammett-tuning functionalization, we construct a design space of 21.9 million Mn and Fe catalysts. We employ active learning using neural network surrogate models with quantified uncertainty to efficiently identify catalysts with optimal methane-to-methanol turnover. We do this by jointly optimizing density functional theory (DFT)-computed hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and methyl radical rebound energetics. Square planar tetraaza-based macrocycles in combination with low-spin Fe(II) or Mn(II) emerge as a privileged class of transition metal complexes within the Pareto-optimal set, with Mn(II) catalysts exhibiting balanced energetic tradeoffs of the two steps. In contrast, porphyrin catalysts exhibit favorable HAT but unfavorable rebound, and seesaw catalysts, which are not widely employed, are indeed the least favorable in our set. Full reaction coordinate analysis of representative Pareto-optimal catalysts reveals that HAT and rebound thermodynamics no longer govern turnover, which is instead determined by the stability of the metal-oxo intermediate and the rebound kinetic barrier. Nonetheless, the resulting energetic spans for these catalysts remain competitive with known earth-abundant, methane-to-methanol catalysts, underscoring the effectiveness of active learning for discovering previously unexplored, synthetically accessible catalysts and unraveling catalyst design principles for methane-to-methanol reactivity.

papers.title: Stable isotopes and green analytical chemistry: state of the art and perspectives
papers.abstract: Stable isotope analysis has become an essential source of information in fields ranging from authentication and environmental sciences to metabolism and health. Its development has been driven primarily by analytical performance, from bulk isotope ratio measurements to compound specific isotope analysis (CSIA) and position specific isotope analysis (PSIA). However, the environmental cost of these workflows has rarely been considered explicitly. This review examines stable isotope analysis through the lens of Green Analytical Chemistry (GAC), White Analytical Chemistry (WAC) and Green Sample Preparation (GSP) metrics. We discuss the main isotope platforms, including isotope ratio mass spectrometry (IRMS)-based bulk and compound-specific methods, quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), gas chromatography-pyrolysis-gas chromatography-combustion-IRMS (GC-pyrolysis-GC-c-IRMS), Orbitrap-IRMS and laser absorption spectroscopy. Particular attention is paid to sample preparation, derivatization, carrier-gas consumption, high-temperature conversion, toxic reagents, acquisition time and instrumental energy demand. The comparison of representative CSIA and PSIA workflows shows that greenness is highly method and analyte dependent, and that improved environmental performance must be weighed against metrological requirements. Future progress will depend on derivatization-free strategies, miniaturized and automated workflows, lower gas and solvent consumption, gas recycling and the broader development of laser-based alternatives.

papers.title: Nickel/photoredox dual-catalyzed ortho-C-H suphenylation and selenylation of primary aryl amines: efficient synthesis of dibenzothiazepines and their new dibenzoselenazepine bioisosteres
Molecular Mechanisms of Deposit Control Additive Inhibition by Biofuels
papers.abstract: Blending biofuels into gasoline can have several environmental and performance benefits. However, high ethanol concentrations are known to reduce the effectiveness of deposit control additives (DCAs) that operate by adsorption onto deposit surfaces. The fundamental physicochemical difference between fossil fuels and biofuels is that the former are mostly non-polar hydrocarbons, while the latter are predominantly oxygen-containing polar species. Here, we use molecular modelling to reveal how the presence of ethanol molecules affects the binding strength of three DCAs with markedly different chemistries to carbonaceous deposits from surrogate fuel blends. For a zwitterionic DCA, ethanol forms a structured solvation shell around the charged head-group, which reduces its adsorption free energy on the model deposits by around 75%. Both the adsorption free energy energy and local ethanol density at the ionic DCA headgroups saturate at low (5% volume) ethanol concentration. For a Mannich base DCA, no solvation shell forms around the DCA, even at high concentrations (85% volume). Ethanol molecules interact with the non-ionic head-group at rates that are indistinguishable from the bulk self-network, and thus the adsorption free energy is insensitive to ethanol concentration. Polyisobutylene succinimide DCAs are an intermediate case between the Mannich base and zwitterionic DCAs, the adsorption free energy decreases only at high ethanol concentrations. Our simulation results agree qualitatively with engine test results and explain why DCAs designed for ethanol-free gasoline are not efficient in alcohol-containing formulations. These findings provide molecular-level insights to guide the rational design of DCAs for ethanol-containing fuels, which will continue to be important in the mobility landscape to enable a smoother transition towards net-zero.

papers.title: Magnetic spin-crossover molecular sensor for acetates
papers.abstract: The development of functional molecular sensors based on spin-crossover metal complexes remains a challenging topic. Here, we present our approach for such chemosensors. We introduce boronic acid groups as receptors into the well-known family of spin-crossover bis(pyrazol-1-yl)pyridine iron(II) complexes. Using this ligand system, the receptor site can be introduced at different positions, and the ligand field can be fine-tuned through the use of additional substituents. This strategy enabled us to develop the very first spin-crossover molecular sensor that responds to common acetate anions. The chemosensor exhibits both colorimetric and magnetic responses, is robust, and operates at room temperature in solution.

papers.title: Environmentally-Acquired Microplastics in Edible Tissues of Broiler and Free-Range Local Chickens (Gallus gallus domesticus) in Nigeria: ATR-FTIR and SEM Characterization Comparing Alkaline (KOH) and Fenton Oxidative Digestion Mercy O. Boyi1*Adetutu O. Aliyu2 Saidu Garba2 Abdulafeez O. Akorede
papers.abstract: Microplastic (MP) contamination of commercially consumed poultry tissues represents an emerging but poorly characterized food safety risk, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa where plastic waste management infrastructure is severely inadequate. This study provides evidence of environmentally-acquired MPs in the liver, heart, and breast muscle of broiler and free-range local chickens (Gallus gallus domesticus) sourced from Chikun Local Government Area, Kaduna State, Nigeria. Ten chickens, five intensively farmed broilers and five free-range local birds were processed using two independent digestion protocols: alkaline (10% w/v KOH) and Fenton oxidative (H2O2/Fe2+), each applied to separate sample sub-sets across three tissues (liver, heart, breast muscle). Isolated particles were characterized by Attenuated Total Reflectance Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM). ATR-FTIR identified five polymer types: polyethylene (PE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polystyrene (PS), polypropylene (PP), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC). Broiler tissues showed consistently greater MP loading and polymer diversity, with PET and PE dominant reflecting intensive farm plastic infrastructure (feed bags, PET troughs, packaging). Free-range local chicken tissues were characterized predominantly by PS, PP, and PVC, consistent with open-environment. A tissue-specific accumulation hierarchy was demonstrated: liver > heart > breast muscle, corresponding to portal-vascular translocation. Fenton oxidative digestion systematically outperformed KOH, uniquely detecting PET. SEM analysis of 19 MP-positive filter samples revealed five morphological categories: films/sheets (47%), angular fragments (37%), granules/pellets (16%), fibres (11%), and spheres. These findings reveal that commercially consumed Nigerian poultry can serve as a dietary vector for human MP exposure and support Fenton oxidative digestion as the recommended protocol for edible tissue MP analysis.

papers.title: Ligand-controlled Selectivity of a Rh/Fe3O4(001) Single-atom Model Catalyst
papers.abstract: The properties of single-atom catalysts are governed by their local environment, motivating efforts to control catalytic performance by tailoring their coordination sphere. In this context, we address the critical role of single ligands bound to individual catalytic centers in controlling their selectivity. Using temperature-programmed desorption and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we demonstrate that Rh model single-atom catalysts on Fe3O4(001) activate the low-temperature oxidation of ethanol to acetaldehyde. However, the subsequent decomposition of acetaldehyde to methane and carbon monoxide can further occur. The formed carbon monoxide remains strongly bound to the Rh center, while the ligand regulates the Rh sites, ultimately catalyzing the selective oxidation of ethanol to acetaldehyde. This behavior can be reproduced by exposing the model system to carbon monoxide, which highlights that single-atom catalysts are truly dynamic in their response to the reaction conditions. Their performance may be impacted by the co-adsorption of ligands that strongly coordinate to the functional catalytic centers. These selectivity-regulating ligands may be formed from intermediates or products, be present as impurities, or intentionally added. Our surface science approach allows us to vary the coordination sphere one ligand at a time, introducing the precision characteristic of coordination chemistry into heterogeneous catalysis.

papers.title: Exceptional homochirality and spin absorption via meniscus-driven chiral symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: Introducing chirality into material systems typically relies on incorporating stereocenters during synthesis or the use of chiral additives. Alternatively, physical chiral induction offers unique advantages to chemical approaches in their ability to modulate homochirality and helical sense without changing the chemical structure. Here, a remarkably straightforward approach to inducing molecular-scale chiral symmetry breaking by manipulating the macroscopic symmetry of the meniscus during evaporative assembly is reported. This meniscus-driven approach led to orders of magnitude boost of circular dichroism (CD) dissymmetric absorption while yielding complete homochirality over centimeter scale across multiple class of intrinsically achiral semiconducting polymers. Fluid dynamic simulations show that sufficiently tilting the meniscus leads to a vorticity gradient that twists the polymer nanofibers into consistent helical sense across the meniscus, a mechanism fully supported by multi-scale morphological characterizations. Such exceptional homochirality yields a three-fold increase in spin-mixing conductance across the polymer/ferromagnet interface compared to the heterochiral counterpart. Attributed to chirality-enhanced spin-orbit coupling comparable to that of conventional heavy metals, our findings pave the way for solution-processable chiral spintronics operable at ambient conditions.

papers.title: Chemically Tunable Spin Frustrated Triangles as New Candidates for Molecular Spin Qubits
papers.abstract: Molecular spin triangles have been theoretically predicted to exhibit spin electric coupling (SEC) holding significant promising in quantum information technology. The possibility of nanoscale manipulation of spin states by the application of electric field offers several advantages over the standard magnetic field-based control of spin states. Experimentally, the antiferromagnetically coupled spins systems arranged in a triangular cluster (M3) where M = Cu2+, Co2+, Fe3+ have been explored to reveal spin electric coupling by utilizing voltage pulses for modulating the phase accumulation within spin-echo sequences in pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) experiments. Despite the rapid experimental progress in this field in last one decade, the role of spin anisotropy, antisymmetric exchange interactions and structural distortions in driving the strength of magnetoelectric coupling effects remains underexplored. Here we report an isostructural series of molecular spin triangles based on triaminoguanidine ligand scaffold with metal centres as Cu2+ (S = 1/2, complex 1), Co2+ (S = 3/2, complex 2), and Mn2+ (S = 5/2, complex 3) ions laying groundwork for chemically tunable magnetoelectric spin qubits. Herein, for the first time, we report the antiferromagnetically coupled Mn3 triangle by incorporating the triaminoguanidine ligand motif. DFT calculations reveal distinct magnetic exchange coupling strengths among the Mn3, Co3, and Cu3 spin triangles. Continuous-wave (cw) EPR spectroscopy reveals a paramagnetic ground state for all M3 triangle studied for the antiferromagnetically coupled clusters with half integer spin on each metal ion. Pulsed EPR measurements establish microsecond phase memory times (T2 ~ 0.8–2.3 μs) and long spin-lattice relaxation times for all three complexes at cryogenic temperatures, confirming the quantum coherence prerequisites for spin-electric coupling (SEC) detection. This series spanning S = 1/2, 3/2, and 5/2 within a single structural scaffold provides a chemically controlled platform for systematically disentangling the microscopic contributions to spin electric coupling across the 3d transition metal series.

papers.title: Chiral excited-state dynamics drive circularly polarized luminescence in a europium complex
papers.abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from chiral molecules and materials underpins emerging applications in display technology, optical sensing, and quantum information science. However, achieving a high degree of circular polarization is an open challenge, partly because the chirality of electronic excited states remains difficult to resolve directly during their evolution. Here, ultrafast circular dichroism spectroscopy maps the complete electronic and chiral structural evolution of a prototypical CPL emitter, CsEu((+,-)-hfbc)4 (hfbc = 3-heptafluorobutyryl camphorate). Its exceptional degree of circular polarization results from the electronic coupling of the Eu(III)-centered luminescent transitions to the chiral environment of the helically arranged sensitizing ligands. Combined with transient absorption measurements and electronic structure calculations, we unravel the intra-molecular energy transfer to the metal-ion, and extract the chiral spectroscopic signature of all involved excited states through their ligand-centered circular dichroism. We find that excitation of the luminescent Eu(III)-ion increases the helical twist of the ligand sphere by 3.0±1.4◦ toward an ideal square-antiprismatic geometry, where the CPL performance is most favorable. More generally, the results show that our approach may resolve previously inaccessible chiral excited-state dynamics in emerging chiral optical materials.

papers.title: Microplastics as vectors and reservoirs of pharmaceuticals and drugs of abuse: mechanisms, occurrence and analytical challenges
papers.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly investigated as particulate phases capable of interacting with emerging organic contaminants in aquatic environments. This review critically evaluates the analytical and mechanistic foundations for considering MPs as potential reservoirs and vectors of pharmaceuticals and drugs of abuse. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of physicochemical speciation, including pH-dependent lipophilicity (logD), ionization equilibria, and the evolution of polymer surfaces, in governing contaminant-particle interactions. Experimental evidence indicates that sorption onto MPs cannot be described solely by hydrophobic partitioning (logKow), but involves coupled mechanisms, including electrostatic interactions, surface oxidation induced by aging, and biofilm-mediated processes. While a growing body of literature addresses pharmaceutical sorption, quantitative data on drugs of abuse and new psychoactive substances remain largely lacking, limiting predictive modeling capabilities. A critical gap is represented by the scarcity of pH-dependent plastic-water partition coefficients (Kpw) for ionizable compounds. From an analytical perspective, the integration of microplastic sampling with LC-HRMS-based workflows introduces significant methodological challenges. Sampling artifacts, extraction-induced redistribution, matrix effects in electrospray ionization, adduct formation, in-source fragmentation, and variability in identification confidence levels in non-target analysis directly affect data interpretation. The lack of harmonized QA/QC protocols further limits comparability across studies. The transition toward a dynamic and quantitative framework requires the integration of controlled sorption experiments with HRMS, standardized reporting, and models that account for chemical speciation. Such integration is essential to achieve robust exposure assessments in anthropogenically impacted aquatic systems.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for pKA Shift Prediction: Establishing a Common Baseline for Molecular Modeling Accuracy
authors: Nico F. A. van der Vegt
papers.abstract: The charge of peptides and proteins, determined by the effective pKA of their residues, is one of the key factors determining their function. Molecular interactions modulate the effective pKAs, shifting them relative to the bare pKA of isolated functional groups. Computational costs of predicting the effective pKAs range from CPU days for all-atom simulations to fractions of a second for the most simplified approaches. Herein, we examined to what extent the higher computational cost is balanced by higher accuracy. As a model system, we used short peptide sequences systematically combining acidic and basic residues, previously studied experimentally and by all-atom simulations. We supplemented the existing results with our own all-atom simulations, a coarse-grained approach, and two fast approximate approaches: FPTS and pepKalc. Our hypothesis that the predictions from all-atom approaches are more accurate than the approximate ones was confirmed only partly. The pKA shifts from most approaches agreed qualitatively but differed quantitatively. Two out of the four all-atom approaches matched the experiments significantly better than the others, while the remaining two were comparable or worse than the approximate ones. Our key finding is that all-atom simulations can be more accurate; however, their accuracy depends not only on the chosen force field, but also on other technical details that are often overlooked. Furthermore, comparing pKA shifts predicted by various simulations requires accounting for different pKA inputs. We show how to shift them to a common reference, enabling for the first time a rigorous and unified comparison across diverse pKA prediction methodologies.

papers.title: FlowerS[4]arene: Synthesis and cooperative solvent encapsulation by hierarchical self-assembly
papers.abstract: A scalable reaction pathway with convenient purification afforded FlowerS[4]arenes. The macrocycle selectively undergoes chiral self-sorting into guest-bound discrete assemblies based solely on weak interactions. The cooperative binding within the assembly overcomes the limitation of conventional guest binding by individual hosts.

papers.title: “Synergistic MgO–CaO Assisted Reduced ZnO Vulcanization of Reclaim Rubber: Comparative Analysis of Cure Kinetics, Crosslink Density, and Mechanical Properties”
papers.abstract: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is an essential activator in sulfur vulcanization; however, excessive zinc release during rubber processing and disposal contributes to aquatic toxicity1˒2. The present work investigates a reduced-ZnO vulcanization strategy for reclaim rubber through synergistic activation using MgO and CaO in an MBT–DPG accelerated sulfur curing system3˒4. Compounds were cured at 140 °C, and cure characteristics were evaluated using rheometer parameters (minimum torque, ML; maximum torque, MH; scorch time, ts2; and optimum cure time, tc90) followed by mechanical characterization5. In this art of work, reduced-ZnO vulcanization strategy for reclaim rubber is investigated using a synergistic MgO–CaO activation system within an MBT–DPG accelerated sulfur cure framework23,24. Cure behavior is evaluated at 140 °C through rheological parameters and mechanical performance is assessed through tensile testing. This work aims to (i) determine the extent to which ZnO can be reduced without critical performance loss, (ii) analyze the compensating role of MgO–CaO synergy in maintaining cure kinetics and torque development, and (iii) establish a direct correlation between crosslink density indicators and mechanical integrity25,26,27. This study proposes a practical and environmentally responsive approach to sustainable vulcanization of reclaim rubber while preserving essential performance characteristics28,29. It seems from results that the conventional 5 phr (parts per hundred rubber) ZnO formulation exhibited the highest torque development (MH = 67.6 dN·m) and tensile strength (82.13 MPa), indicating high crosslink density but relatively lower elongation at break (298%), Page 2 of 35 reflecting increased network rigidity6˒7. Partial substitution with 3 phr ZnO / 1.5 phr MgO / 0.5 phr CaO system resulted in moderated torque (MH ≈ 55.7 dN·m) and controlled cure kinetics (tc90 ≈ 3.57 min), while maintaining substantial tensile strength (67.16 MPa; ~82% strength retention) and significantly improved elongation (391%). This formulation demonstrated the highest toughness index, confirming a more balanced crosslink network8˒9. Further reduction to 2 phr ZnO led to decreased torque and extended cure time, suggesting insufficient activation and reduced crosslink efficiency10. The results establish that MgO–CaO synergistic activation effectively compensates for ZnO reduction in reclaim rubber systems, preserving cure behavior and mechanical integrity while lowering zinc content4. The study provides a practical pathway toward environmentally responsible vulcanization without critical performance compromise.

papers.title: Epistatic Modulation of Sec/Cys Catalysis in GPX6 Revealed by EVB Free-Energy Landscapes
papers.abstract: Glutathione peroxidase 6 (GPX6) provides a natural system for asking how catalytic chemistry is reshaped by evolutionary sequence background. Primate GPX6 retains catalytic selenocysteine, whereas rodents have independently replaced it with cysteine, but the energetic consequences of this Sec/Cys exchange within each homologous scaffold remain unclear. Here, empirical valence bond simulations were used to quantify the proton-transfer step that generates the reactive selenolate or thiolate in human and mouse GPX6. Introducing selenocysteine into mouse GPX6 lowers the activation barrier by 2.84 kcal/mol, whereas replacing selenocysteine with cysteine in human GPX6 raises it by 1.43 kcal/mol, showing that the selenium advantage is amplified or damped by the surrounding protein scaffold. Greedy pathway free energy calculations with the empirical valence bond method across 20 proximal substitutions reveal multiple feasible routes between homologs and a recurring energetic pattern in which the effect of each substitution depends on the catalytic background in which it is introduced. Projection onto the GPX6 phylogeny indicates that rodent Cys-GPX6 is best understood as a compensatory catalytic regime rather than a simple loss of selenium chemistry.

papers.title: Spiro-Induced Strain as a Design Principle for Long-Lived Singlet Diradicals with π-Single Bond Character
papers.abstract: Singlet 1,3-diradicals with π single-bond character exhibit unique electronic structures and attractive photophysical and redox properties; however, their practical utilization is severely limited by rapid σ-bond formation and competing rearrangement pathways. Here, we demonstrate that spiro-induced strain provides a design principle for controlling competing reaction pathways in singlet diradicals. Quantum chemical calculations using CASSCF and broken-symmetry DFT methods reveal that this strain destabilizes both σ-bonded products and the corresponding transition states, thereby suppressing σ-bond formation. This effect is 2 most pronounced for SP1, which achieves an optimal balance between strain and structural flexibility, resulting in the highest activation barrier and the longest predicted lifetime among the systems examined. In addition, intramolecular alkoxy migration is suppressed in smaller spiro frameworks, further contributing to kinetic persistence. These findings establish spiroinduced strain as an effective strategy for realizing long-lived singlet diradicals with π singlebond character.

papers.title: Investigating configuration entropy in ceramic super-ionic conductors
papers.abstract: Fast Li + ion diffusion in ceramic solid electrolytes is often explained by timedependent ion-correlation effects such as concerted motion and the paddle-wheel effect, but many commonly used modeling approaches exclude some or all configuration entropy, which can lead to misleading results and conclusions. In this work, we separate the effects of ion distribution, ion−ion interactions, and framework dynamics using transition-state-theory-based models and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. We show that simplified barrier-based models that neglect the full distributional space of the ions lead to overestimated diffusion, while excluding the full configuration entropy of ion−ion interactions results in a failure to accurately describe the energy landscape. However, an averaged ensemble distribution that includes configuration entropy, but lacks time resolution, is sufficient to accurately reproduce the flat energy landscapes identified in fast ionic conductors such as Li 10 GeP 2 S 12 , Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 , and Li 7 La 3 Zr 2 O 12 . Framework dynamics further enhance diffusion in most structures by broadening low-energy regions and lowering effective barriers, increasing the diffusion on average by ∼0.5 orders of magnitude, with especially large effects in Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 and Li 3 PS 4 , while LiNbO 3 shows the opposite behavior due to stronger Li−O interactions. Overall, our results show that configuration entropy plays a central role in Li + ion transport and should be clearly separated from true time-dependent correlation effects when interpreting diffusion mechanisms.

papers.title: Impact of Carrier Concentration, Framework Potential and Structural Variations on Li-Diffusivity in Li1+xAlxTi2–xPO4
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the diffusion in the prominent ceramic solid state electrolyte Lithium Aluminum Titanium Phosphate (LATP) Li1+xAlxTi2–xPO4 in the entire range of substitution concentrations 0 ≤ x ≤ 2. Employing different computational tools, namely sampling the potential energy surface of the Li+-ions and performing molecular dynamics simulations, allows to separate the different mechanisms which lead to a change in the Li+-ion diffusion upon changing the Al substitution concentration. Using a finetuned machine learning potential allows to study larger simulation cells and run longer MD simulations. This leads to converged, stable, diffusion coefficients and illustrates the spread in diffusion coefficients at constant substitution concentrations. The concentration of Li+-ions is identified to have the strongest contribution to an increased diffusion, while local and cell rearrangements lead to a decreased diffusion at higher levels of Al substitution.

papers.title: Mesoionic Carbene-Metal Amide TADF Emitters: An Approach Towards Near-Unity Quantum Yield and Enhanced Non-Linear Optical (NLO) Properties
papers.abstract: Carbene-metal-amide (CMA) complexes have emerged as an efficient class of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitters for optoelectronic applications. Although N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-based CMAs are widely researched, their mesoionic NHC (mNHC) counterparts are underexplored despite providing unique electronic structures and enhanced σ-donor properties. In this work, we present a series of mNHC coinage metal amide complexes (Cu, Ag, Au) (5-10) with imidazolylidene-derived ligands, representing the first systematic investigation of their photophysical behaviour. These complexes exhibit dual locally excited (LE) and charge-transfer (CT) emissions, where the latter is highly oxygen-sensitive and contains long-lived microsecond components, establishing TADF as the emission channel. The emission maxima are also strongly influenced by both donor substituents (carbazole versus tert-butyl carbazole) and metal identity, falling between 575 and 618 nm in solution and remaining unchanged in solid-state and PMMA matrices. Quantum yields for photoluminescence as high as 0.97 in deaerated toluene, 0.91 in PMMA, and delayed lifetimes on the order of tens of microseconds highlight effective triplet harvesting. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) and time-resolved PL studies demonstrate low singlet-triplet energy splitting (ΔEST ≈ 0.14 eV) and high radiative decay rate constants [kr (S1) ≈ 1.8 × 107 s-1], which make these complexes efficient emitters. Moreover, donor-substituted (5-10) complexes exhibit excellent mechanochromic luminescence (MCL) properties, and their incorporation in UV-excited converted LED prototypes proves their stability and usability in device applications. Expanding the horizon of possibilities, we report that these complexes act as an efficient nonlinear optical material, showing second- and third-harmonic generation responses. The centrosymmetric nature of complex 2-7 shows χ(3) values between 0.38 × 10−18 m2 V−2 to 0.85 × 10−18 m2 V−2, and a laser-induced damage threshold (LIDT) of 17.51 to 27.86 GWcm−2. However, the non-centrosymmetric nature of complex 8-10 further makes them efficient SHG materials, with a χ(2) value between 0.07-0.08 pmV−1 at 1180 nm and LIDT value between 47-35 GW cm−2. These results make imidazolylidene mNHC-metal amides a new family of earth-abundant, high-efficiency TADF emitters with strong applications toward next-generation OLEDs, and opening new avenues for exploring main-group organometallic compounds in next-generation polarisation-sensitive photonic devices.

papers.title: Development of cell-mimetic sponge droplets stable to coalescence
papers.abstract: The advent of synthetic cells has allowed the precise reconstruction of cellular functionalities by offering well-defined systems for compartmentalization of biomolecules and biochemical reactions. Coacervates are liquid-liquid phase separated microdroplets that have emerged as an attractive synthetic cell model owing to their robustness of formation and molecularly crowded nature. Sponge droplets are coacervates composed of a bicontinuous network of surfactant bilayers interspersed by aqueous channels, and are engineerable in a facile manner. However, a significant limitation to the use of these sponge droplets as synthetic cell mimics, is their inherent tendency to coalesce, a process wherein smaller droplets rapidly fuse in solution to form a single separate phase, and therefore the identities of the individual microcontainers is lost. Here, we describe for the first time, a strategy for developing sponge droplets that are stable to coalescence. Programming the surface of sponge droplets with a peripheral protein layer endows them with a resistance to fusion. Our data shows that despite the peripheral protein layer; these stable sponge droplets retain their sponge-like nanostructure and ability to sequester molecules in a programmable fashion. Remarkably, perturbing the protein layer eliminates their stability, and the droplets become susceptible to coalescence, over again. Our results delineate a novel approach for the construction of fusion-resistant sponge droplets using an interfacial protein coating, which allows robust generation of distinct cell-mimetic microcompartments that combine the utilities of lipid membrane-based self-assembled systems and coacervate droplets.

papers.title: Cubic-Equivariant k-Space Convolution and a Differentiable Bond-Valence Field for Ionic-Conductivity Prediction in Solid-State Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Predicting the room-temperature ionic conductivity 𝜎 of solid-state lithium-ion electrolytes from crystal structure remains a bottleneck for materials discovery. I introduce two architectural primitives. k-SEC is a neural encoder whose feature maps live in reciprocal space throughout the network and whose cubic-group equivariance is enforced by construction via cubic-harmonic directional filters and a cross-shell gated attention modulated only by k-magnitudes. DBVF (Differentiable Bond-Valence Field) embeds Brown’s bond-valence sum into the network as a learnable module—the first treatment of Brown’s tabulated parameters as trainable parameters of a neural network. On the OBELiX benchmark (281 labelled solid electrolytes, 5-fold cross-validation × 5 seeds) the joint model attains MAE 1.047 [95 % CI 0.925–1.183] standalone and 0.980 in a stacked ensemble with a gradient-boosted-tree baseline; Spearman 𝜌 = 0.78 with 70 % top-10 precision. An unsupervised screen of 18,574 Li-containing Materials Project crystals identifies all four known fast-Li-ion conductor families in its top-15. A control experiment shows the DBVF gain is realised only through end-to-end training; a learning-curve experiment shows a 45 % gap reduction to the tabular baseline as training samples grow from 90 to 135 per fold, before plateauing at OBELiX scale.

papers.title: 2,6- and 2,7-Diazatriptycene-Based Boron Complexes: Synthesis, Optical Properties, and Crystal Structures
papers.abstract: Boron-bridged 2,6- and 2,7-diazatriptycene complexes were synthesized as fluorescent three-dimensional π-systems. Single-crystal X-ray analysis revealed distinct packing modes: the chiral 2,6-isomer formed loosely packed trimeric clusters with large solvent-accessible voids, whereas the 2,7-isomer adopted a denser herringbone-like packing structure. Both complexes exhibited blue fluorescence in solution with higher photoluminescence quantum yields than ppy-BMe2. TD-DFT calculations indicated that boron coordination suppresses the dark n–π* character of diazatriptycenes and converts the S1 state into an allowed π–π* transition. These findings establish boron coordination as an effective approach for developing photofunctional azatriptycene-based three-dimensional π-systems.

papers.title: Interfacial Chemistry tunes Performance in a Polysulfone-based MUF-16 Mixed Matrix Membrane for Pre-Combustion CO2-Capture.
papers.abstract: Mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) are a promising technology for gas separation of different gas mixtures such as H2/CO2; however, their performance is often limited by poor interfacial compatibility between polymer and filler. One effective strategy to overcome this challenge is covalent polymer-filler attachment, which compatibilizes the interface, promotes defect-free membrane formation, and therefore enhances the gas separation properties. However, many existing approaches require MOF pre-treatment or additional synthetic steps, compromising MOF stability, complicating processing and limiting scalability. Herein, we report on a rational polymer design strategy that enables covalent bonding to the MOF directly during membrane fabrication. A chloromethyl-functionalized polysulfone (PSUCH2Cl) is used to form covalent linkages with MUF-16 through a nucleophilic substitution reaction. Successful bonding is directly confirmed by fluorescence, demonstrating that the reaction proceeds in situ during membrane formation without the need for post-modification or filler pre-treatment. This simple, straightforward and efficient approach improved polymer-filler compatibility as observed from SEM micrographs. As a result, the optimized membrane, PSUCH2Cl-MUF-16/DMF (15 wt.%), shows a higher H2/CO2 separation factor of 98 in comparation with the non-optimized PSU-MUF-16/DMF MMM (15 wt.%) with a separation factor of 47.5.

papers.title: Reactive Orbital Energy Theory Analysis of Woodward-Hoffmann Rule Violations in Electrocyclic Reactions
papers.abstract: Using reactive orbital energy theory (ROET), we investigated from the perspective of electron motion why pericyclic pathways that violate the Woodward-Hoffmann (WH) rules can occur. For eight representative WH-violating pericyclic reactions, we comparatively analyzed the WH-allowed and WH-forbidden pathways in terms of the electrostatic forces exerted on the nuclei by the occupied reactive orbitals (OROs) identified by ROET as driving the reaction. The reactions were classified into three types: (1) those in which no HOMO-LUMO crossing appears along the WH-forbidden pathway and the ORO is localized in the early stage of the reaction; (2) those in which a HOMO-LUMO crossing occurs before the transition state (TS) along the WHforbidden pathway and thus does not generate a large electrostatic force opposing the reaction direction at the TS; and (3) special cases in which additional factors, such as HOMO-LUMO crossings in both pathways or steric constraints, play decisive roles. These results show that WH-rule violations arise from the absence or modification of key features of WH-consistent reactions, namely ORO stabilization in the allowed pathway and a HOMO-LUMO crossing at or shortly after the TS in the forbidden pathway. Overall, ROET provides a unified perspective on pericyclic reactions through orbitalenergy variations.

papers.title: Why the Woodward-Hoffmann Rules Work: A Reactive Orbital Energy Theory Analysis of Pericyclic Reactions
papers.abstract: Reactive orbital energy theory (ROET), an orbital-energy-based electronic-structure framework, elucidates the electron motions that drive pericyclic reactions and helps clarify the orbital-energy basis of WH-type stereoselectivity. For WH-allowed electrocyclic reactions, symmetry-conserving pathways are favored because the occupied reactive orbital (ORO) is strongly stabilized in the vicinity of the transition state, thereby lowering the barrier. This stabilization is correlated with symmetry-allowed occupied-occupied crossings between nearby occupied orbitals of different symmetry, which preserve the character of the ORO and facilitate the dominant occupied-virtual response. By contrast, in WH-forbidden pathways, a HOMO-LUMO crossing near the transition state is associated with an electrostatic force opposite to the reaction direction, thereby increasing the barrier. For cycloadditions, the ene reaction, and sigmatropic rearrangements, ROET reveals that cycloadditions are driven by electron transfer from diene π orbitals, that the propylene-ethylene ene reaction is driven by back-donation from ethylene to the migrating hydrogen, and that sigmatropic rearrangements are driven by electron motion along the main-chain π system of conjugated double bonds. A unifying feature is that, when viewed in terms of the ORO rather than the HOMO, the pericyclic step proceeds through constructive orbital overlap within the ORO. ROET thus provides an energetically grounded perspective that clarifies the origin of WH-type stereoselectivity in the electrocyclic reactions examined here and offers a common interpretive framework for the other pericyclic classes analyzed in this study.

papers.title: Host–Guest-Induced Remote Charge Amplification in Ruthenium Complexes Enables Entropy Engineering of Redox Reactions
papers.abstract: Controlling redox thermodynamics without perturbing the primary metal coordination of redox-active complexes remains a major challenge in molecular design. Here we propose a chemical strategy based on the secondary coordination sphere (SCS) engineering, in which host–guest encapsulation and release of metal ion at spatially remote crown-ether sites enables tuning of the net charge in those complexes. A crown-ether-functionalized tris(bipyridyl) ruthenium complex (Ru-crown15) selectively binds two Li+ ions in a stepwise manner, effectively increasing the net charge of the complex through host–guest interaction. Temperature-dependent electrochemical measurements reveal that the redox entropy increases with the number of binding Li+ ions, which is in good agreement with a Born-type solvation model. This long-range modulation of thermodynamic parameters highlights the SCS engineering as a versatile approach for molecular-level entropy control in redox systems and offers a route to tune the thermogalvanic responses.

papers.title: Palladium-triggered Bioorthogonal Phenylalanine Decaging
Feasibility of Grass-to-Gas on Dairy Farms: A Probabilistic Techno-Economic Comparison of Renewable Natural Gas and Electricity Production
