papers.abstract: Farm-scale anaerobic digestion (AD) of dairy manure has been economically constrained due to limited financial returns and high investment risks. Co-digestion with lignocellulosic biomass, particularly grasses, has been proposed to enhance methane production while providing additional ecosystem services. Through techno-economic and uncertainty analysis, this study evaluates co-digestion of dairy manure with corn stover, switchgrass, and winter rye in a 1,000-cow dairy farm system. Two biomass sourcing strategies (i.e., on-farm and purchased) and two energy conversion pathways, electricity generation via combined heat and power and renewable natural gas (RNG) production via biogas upgrading, were assessed. Co-digestion consistently lowered the minimum selling price (MSP) of electricity and RNG relative to manure-only AD, but electricity generation remained economically infeasible (net present value < 0) across all scenarios. In contrast, RNG production offered a viable path towards improved performance, with positive net preset values for purchased corn stover and winter rye in 22% and 45% of simulations, respectively, achieving an MSP competitive with market 1 conditions. Winter rye showed the strongest overall performance and was the only feedstock to approach conditional feasibility under current policy and market conditions. Nevertheless, economic viability remained highly sensitive to policy incentives, indicating persistent investment risk. These results demonstrate that co-digestion can enhance the economic performance of manure-based AD, but viability depends critically on feedstock selection, biogas end-use pathway, and policy stability.

papers.title: Computational Characterization of Solute Permeability in ELP Membranes for Synthetic Cells
papers.abstract: Elastin-like polypeptides (ELP) are versatile biopolymers for constructing synthetic cell membranes. Applications in biosynthesis, molecular secretion, and payload delivery require an understanding of solute transport across ELP membranes. In this work, we integrate coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations with the inhomogeneous solubility-diffusion (ISD) model to investigate passive permeation of small solutes across ELP membranes of varying sequence composition and stability. We observe that mechanically robust ELP bilayers remain highly permeable to small solutes but exhibit an unexpected non-monotonic dependence on solute hydrophobicity. By backmapping the coarse-grained bead solutes to all-atom resolution, we identify specific molecular motifs that may promote or suppress solute transport through the ELP membrane. Across different ELP systems, we find that water permeability is only weakly dependent upon membrane stability but strongly dependent upon the ELP hydrophilic guest residues. Compositional analyses suggest that side chain flexibility and hydrophilicity of the guest residues in the hydrophilic block modulate interfacial solvation and regulate water permeation. Our results provide a broad computational characterization of ELP membrane permeability and present a predictive tool to tune the sequence of ELP-based vesicles for engineered passive transport of molecular cargoes.

papers.title: Riding toward Selectivity: Optimization of Covalent 7-Azaindole-Based BMX Kinase Inhibitors
papers.abstract: The Tyrosine Kinase Expressed in Hepatocellular Carcinoma (TEC) family comprises five nonreceptor tyrosine kinases – BTK, ITK, BMX, TXK, and TEC – which play key roles in immunological signal transduction. Although BTK and ITK have been extensively studied, selective inhibitor development for TEC, TXK, and BMX remains scarce. In a recent study, we identified a new class of covalent BMX inhibitors with a 7-azaindole core. These compounds exhibit potent inhibitory activity and robust cellular target engagement but had limited selectivity across TEC family members, especially BTK, which is the closest relative of BMX. Here, we describe the next generation of BMX inhibitors that incorporate diverse N-acylamino substituents at the azaindole 5-position or variations in the linker and warhead region. These modifications were designed to exploit subtle structural differences between BMX and BTK in the pocket behind the gatekeeper residue as well as in the front pocket. Our compounds display excellent BMX potency in the sub-nanomolar range along with improved selectivity against BTK and other TEC family kinases. We identified compound 11i as a new BMX lead compound with strong cellular target engagement, good in vitro metabolic stability, a favourable kinome profile, and fast covalent inactivation kinetics. These properties position compound 11i among the best BMX chemical probes currently available.

papers.title: Long-horizon forecasting of electrolysis stability from early-stage operating data through temporal learning
papers.abstract: Electrochemical devices such as electrolyzers are central to a sustainable, electrified future, and the ability to predict device-level stability from early-stage operation can substantially accelerate technology development. Data-driven stability forecasting offers a promising route toward this goal but remains challenged by the complexity of open, dynamic electrochemical systems and the limited availability of high-quality training data. Here, we develop ElectroTS, a data-driven electrolysis prognostic framework that integrates data-adaptive rectification with temporal sequence modeling to enable robust prediction of lifetime, degradation rates, and uncertainty in electrolytic systems. We first construct well-structured stability datasets for anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) and CO 2 solid oxide electrolyzer cells (SOEC), explicitly designed for long-horizon forecasting. Using only early-stage operating data, ElectroTS enables forecasting over operating durations exceeding tenfold the input window and beyond 1,000 hours, providing actionable guidance for rapid screening of materials and operating conditions. Moreover, few-shot transfer learning enables efficient cross-platform generalization, as demonstrated across low-temperature aqueous and high-temperature solid-state electrolysis systems. This work establishes a generalizable, long-horizon forecasting framework for data-driven stability prediction across electrochemical energy technologies.

papers.title: Reductive Deoxygenation of Aromatic Aldehydes and Ketones with Boron Triiodide
papers.abstract: Deoxygenation of carbonyls is an area of value in synthetic transformations because it allows for traceless utilization of carbonyl chemistry, a mainstay in synthetic manipulations. Since oxygenation patterns are common in biological settings, deoxygenation can also be used to valorize biologically-derived feedstocks such as lignin. Herein, we describe the use of potassium borohydride and iodine, two common and benchtop stable reagents, to generate boron triiodide in situ, which performs full deoxygenation of aryl aldehydes and ketones. For aldehydes, benzyl iodide products are formed, whereas for ketones the methine is produced. Byproducts upon workup are low toxicity boric acid and iodide salts, making the process practical and appealing for a wide range of applications.

papers.title: Accurate Molecular Nonlinear Properties On A Semiempirical Budget Using The TDDFT-ris Model
papers.abstract: Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TDDFT) is a workhorse computational tool for predicting nonlinear optical properties from first principles. However, its computational cost often limits its practicality for large molecules. We evaluate nonlinear response properties using our recently developed semiempirical model, TDDFT-ris (ris), and its extension, TDDFT-risp (risp), which use minimal auxiliary basis to approximate electron-repulsion integrals. Against full TDDFT with def2-SVPD calculations, ris and risp accurately reproduce (hyper)polarizabilities for a small fraction of the computational cost. For example, ris has a mean relative error of 8% when computing mean polarizabilities, which is reduced to 2% by risp. Furthermore, the strong physical justification for the risp method allows us to cure systematic failures in monopole-based semiempirical models (like ris) when computing nonlinear properties of planar molecules. Thus, ris and risp are powerful and inexpensive tools for predicting nonlinear optical properties either qualitatively or nearly quantitatively.

papers.title: Exploring the Electronic and Structural Modulation in a Novel Bimetallic NiFe Metal Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: A novel mixed-ligand bimetallic NiFe-MOF was synthesized using 4,4′-bipyrimidine and D-camphorate linkers, forming a 3D framework. Compared to monometallic analogues, Fe incorporation significantly enhances porosity and surface area, yielding a highly porous structure, while reducing the bandgap to 2.6 eV. The material shows improved visible-light absorption, enabling tunable photoactive properties.

papers.title: Harnessing Hidden van der Waals Interactions Between Alkyl Chains and Oxide Surfaces for Discrimination of Butylamine Isomers
papers.abstract: Discriminating structural isomers on oxide surfaces remains fundamentally challenging due to the dominance of strong specific interactions between the surface and molecular functional groups. Here, we demonstrate gas-phase discrimination of butylamine isomers by tuning surface Lewis acidity to weaken acid–base interactions, enabling van der Waals (vdW)-governed desorption dynamics. Using ZnO nanowires as a representative oxide surface, we observed distinct desorption behaviors among butylamine isomers; density functional theory calculations revealed that differences in vdW interactions between the butyl chains and the surface underpin this discrimination. To amplify these vdW-derived differences, ZnO surfaces were modified with MgO, which has lower Lewis acidity than ZnO, to attenuate acid–base interactions between surface metal-cation sites and NH 2 groups. This attenuation was evidenced by a shift in the N–H asymmetric stretching band of adsorbed n -butylamine to higher wavenumbers in infrared spectra. The MgO-modified surfaces exhibited enhanced and reproducible differentiation of n -, sec -, and tert -butylamine based on desorption kinetics. Conversely, modification with strongly acidic WO 3 suppressed these vdW-driven differences. Collectively, these results establish a general strategy for molecular discrimination on oxide surfaces by tuning the balance between specific surface interactions and vdW interactions.

papers.title: K5Ir: Reduced Iridium Stabilized in a High-Pressure Semimetal
papers.abstract: Alkali binary compounds offer a way to expand our understanding of the periodic table. Specifically, the redox inert nature of alkali cations, even within some intermetallic compounds, enables one to access exotic oxidation states. Iridium presents a test case, as it is the transition metal best positioned to form a trianion, which would be the most highly charged transition metal anion reported. Pressure, known to modulate both reactivity and electronic structure to stabilize exotic phases, is a promising path to this species. Others predicted that reduction of Ir with alkali metals at high pressure may yield phases containing the Ir 3− ion. We tested these predictions by reacting a K-rich mixture of K and Ir at 19.5(6) GPa and 493 K. This reaction yields K 5 Ir, which adopts the rare but simple BaSn 5 crystal structure. Hybrid functional electronic structure calculations, net atomic charge analysis, and Ir L 3 -edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal K 5 Ir is a semimetal with a carrier density ~10 20 cm −3 which features strongly reduced Ir and both oxidized and neutral K on different sites. The (negative) net atomic charge of Ir in K 5 Ir exceeds those of Pt 2− in Cs 2 Pt and Ir(III-) in putative Na 3 [Ir(CO) 3 ], suggesting an extreme for the distribution of charge in the vicinity of a transition metal. First-principles crystal structure prediction indicates that several other K−Ir compounds await discovery.

papers.title: The Tsetlin Machine: A “Third Way” in QSAR Modelling
Machine learning the quantum topology of chemical bonds
papers.abstract: The chemical bonding can be characterized within quantum chemical topology (QCT), which provides a real-space description via the topological analysis of the electron density and the electron localization function (ELF). While QCT has traditionally been applied on a molecule-by-molecule basis, recent advances in machine learning (ML) and the availability of large quantum chemical datasets now enable bonding analysis at scale. Here, we integrate ELF-based topological descriptors with ML to establish a data-driven framework for mapping chemical bonding across the QM9 dataset. Wavefunctions computed at the B3LYP/6-31G(2df,p) level were used to extract ELF basin populations, which were paired with geometric and bonding descriptors to construct a bond-level dataset. Statistical analysis revealed relationships between ELF populations, bond lengths, and local chemical environments. Regression models were trained to predict ELF electron populations directly from molecular geometry. The best performance was obtained when local environmental descriptors were included, reducing the prediction error by a factor of two relative to models using only bond type and bond length. These results demonstrate real-space bonding parameters, such as bond electron populations, can be predicted from simple structural features, enabling scalable and interpretable exploration of chemical bonding across large chemical spaces.

papers.title: In Situ SAXS Investigation of Hydrated Membrane Nanostructure in Polymer Electrolyte Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Understanding the hydration state of polymer electrolyte membranes (PEMs) in operating fuel cells is essential for enhancing performance and ensuring long-term durability. Here, we present an in situ small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) approach that enables direct observation of PEM hydration within membrane electrode assemblies. A dedicated in situ SAXS cell was developed to suppress scattering from catalyst layers and isolate membrane-specific signals. In situ measurements revealed that break-in procedures enhanced the structural ordering of the nanophase-separated water domains in the hydrated PEM without altering the water-domain spacing. Systematic measurements further showed that water-domain spacing increased at lower cell temperatures and higher current densities, providing direct structural evidence of hydration dynamics in PEMs. These findings demonstrate that in situ SAXS is a powerful tool for probing membrane nanostructures under realistic fuel cell conditions.

papers.title: AI-driven simulation of stochastic electrochemiluminescence
papers.abstract: Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) is a vital analytical technique widely used in immunosensing and emerging applica-tions in biological imaging. Traditional ECL simulations rely on finite element methods, which provide valuable insights into reaction dynamics and spatial distribution of species. However, such methods are limited in mesoscopic environ-ments where stochastic effects become significant. Here, I present a novel approach using ChatGPTo1 to generate a Py-thon-based stochastic simulation for ECL reactions in a nanofluidic channel, incorporating diffusion, electrochemical and chemical reactions, and photon emission. The simulation successfully replicates results from finite element models while offering additional insights into time-dependent behaviors and enabling noise analysis for simulated luminescence traces. The iterative development of this simulation using ChatGPT was rapid, requiring minimal coding expertise while leveraging the model’s "reasoning" capabilities to implement physical principles, verify calculations, and optimize per-formance. This work demonstrates that large language models (LLMs) can serve as effective co-intelligence tools, facili-tating the development of complex simulations in electrochemistry. AI-driven tools/LLMs have a promising role in ad-vancing electrochemistry research, though careful validation remains essential to ensure scientific accuracy.

papers.title: Cation-Assisted Structure Effect in Cobalt Porphyrin-Based Catalysts for Selective CO2 Electroreduction over HER
papers.abstract: Local electrostatic fields and confinement play an important role in catalysis. Two cobalt electrocatalysts, a planar cobalt tetraphenylporphyrin (Co-TPP) and a cobalt porphyrin cage (Co-Cage), are used in the mechanistic model studies of CO 2 RR and HER. The enzyme-inspired synthesized Co-Cage provides a 3D confined space for the reaction active site. While variation in structure was observed to affect selectivity of the electrochemical reduction of CO 2 and hydrogen evolution, adding cations affords improvement in lowering overpotential and in increasing current density which reflects reaction rate in CO 2 electroreduction to CO. Density functional theory (DFT)-based molecular dynamics (MD) simulations involving explicit solvent molecules were performed to elucidate water-mediated proton transfers in these two competitive reactions, disclosing how the special micro-environment of the cage catalyst affects the reaction outcome. Furthermore, the cation effect associated with the host/guest chemistry has been shown to play a key role in the substrate activation of CO 2 RR in cooperation with static DFT calculations. This study reveals quantitatively the role of cations, solvent molecules, and confinement in key non-redox steps of electrochemical CO 2 conversion and the competing HER pathway. It shows that variations in hydrogen-bond networks shape free-energy profiles and highlights the need for explicit solvent to realistically model reaction pathways, rationalizing catalyst activity and selectivity.

papers.title: NEVPT2 Multiple Spawning Molecular Dynamics Simulations for Uracil
papers.abstract: The quasidegenerate n-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (QD-NEVPT2) for complete active space reference wavefunctions has been implemented in the OpenMolcas package. The implementation utilizes the efficient formulation of Kollmar et al. for the electronic energy, which is extended here to the calculation of analytic derivatives. To demonstrate its utility, the method is applied to classical and non-adiabatic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of uracil. The non-adiabatic MD simulations describe the ultrafast deactivation from the ππ∗ to the nπ∗ state, demonstrating the applicability of the method to photochemical processes. Furthermore, a machine learning-based analysis of the trajectory data extracts key geometrical parameters that are associated with the magnitude of the time-derivative coupling.

papers.title: Tetrazine-based bioorthogonal reactions to image hypoxia in cancer cells
papers.abstract: Suboptimal oxygen supply in solid tumors controls a variety of cancer hallmarks and impairs responsiveness to anticancer treatments. Yet, tools to visualize hypoxia in cancer are still limited. Here we present an application of the tetrazine-dienophile inverse-electron demand Diels Alder (IEDDA) reaction for hypoxia visualization. In this approach, trans-cyclooctene-clickable 2-nitroimidazoles work in combination with tetrazine-functionalized probes for live imaging of differential levels of hypoxia in two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) models. We used tetrazine-based fluorescent probes to determine oxygen levels in cell monolayers, spheroids and patient-derived organoids, and applied a “click-to-release” approach to dissect the diffusion of the released probe in the surrounding peripheral regions, allowing to quantify the by-stander effect. Given the compatibility of the tetrazine-dienophile click reaction with living organisms, the combination of clickable 2-nitroimidazoles with tetrazine-based reporters opens a new avenue for in vivo hypoxia imaging.

papers.title: Synthesis and Preliminary Fire Retardancy Screening of a Mg–Al Layered Double Hydroxide Colloidal Gel Coating on Cellulosic and Wood Substrates
papers.abstract: Fire safety of cellulosic and wood-based materials is a persistent concern in construction, packaging, and interior applications. Halogenated flame retardants, while effective, release toxic acid gases upon combustion. This preliminary communication reports a simplified co‑precipitation synthesis of a magnesium–aluminium layered double hydroxide (Mg–Al LDH) colloidal gel using only standard laboratory stirring and heating equipment. The gel was applied as a single dip coating to standard paper, glossy paperboard (~350 GSM), and birch wood (~2 mm). X‑ray diffraction of the dried solid confirmed formation of a semi‑crystalline Mg–Al LDH phase, with characteristic non‑basal reflections at 32.82° and 61.67° 2θ (Cu‑Kα) and no detectable halogen‑containing impurities. Qualitative candle‑flame exposure tests (≥60 s) showed that all uncoated controls ignited within 2–15 s, whereas LDH‑coated samples exhibited no ignition, localised charring, and immediate self‑extinguishment. The observed fire retardancy is consistent with the known dual mechanism of endothermic gas release and inorganic char formation. This work provides an initial screening of a scalable, halogen‑free coating; quantitative fire testing (LOI, cone calorimetry) is planned to fully characterise the system.

papers.title: Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity in Chiral Solids
papers.abstract: Chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a striking phenomenon in which electron transport through chiral systems generates highly spin-polarized currents, even at room temperature and in the absence of magnetic field or strong atomic spin–orbit coupling. While CISS has been intensively studied in molecular systems, its microscopic origin remains controversial, partly due to experimental limitations inherent to nanoscale molecules. In this review, the author focuses on CISS in chiral solids and introduces a classification into two categories based on time-reversal symmetry (𝒯): CISS(I), a 𝒯–even response associated with collinear current-induced spin polarization, and CISS(II), a 𝒯–broken response involving antiparallel spin-pair formation under non-equilibrium conditions. The author further proposes an operational definition based on transport measurements, allowing direct comparison with experiments, including magnetoconductance studies in molecular systems. Recent experiments on chiral metals and superconductors are discussed in this framework, highlighting enhanced spin polarization, nonlocal spin transport, and symmetry conversion between structural and magnetic chirality. These results suggest that chiral solids provide a platform to bridge molecular and condensed-matter perspectives and to explore non-equilibrium spin–chirality coupling.

papers.title: Split-functional p-type dopants for organic semiconductors
papers.abstract: Organic semiconductors (OSCs) are extensively used in next-generation optoelectronic devices. Efficient and stable electronic doping broadens their applications. Traditional doping methods, especially metal salts, often face challenges such as low doping efficiency, ion migration, instability under ambient conditions, limited compatibility with hole-transport layers, and reliance on additives or complex processing. Here, metal-free modular split-functional dopant systems are developed. By separating charge-transfer and thermal-stability functions, this design enables independent tuning of charge-transfer ability, solubility, compatibility during film formation, and stability of the doped films. This strategy enables rapid, additive-free p-type doping under ambient conditions across various OSCs with higher efficiency than metal-salt-based doping. OSC films doped with split-functional systems exhibit uniform doping and reduced ion migration under applied electric fields, unlike traditionally doped films. The functionality introduced by the dopants enhance the thermal stability of the doped films, which remain stable for >1000 hours under continuous thermal stress at 100 °C. These dopant systems are compatible with a wide range of hole-transport materials without requiring additional additives. The synthetic simplicity, versatility, ambient processibility and scalability of this approach make split-functional dopants a promising platform for creating highly stable hole-transport layers in perovskite solar cells, enabling the development of efficient, stable devices.

papers.title: 𝝅-𝝅 stacked dimer junctions formed with silver electrodes
papers.abstract: The catalytic properties of metal electrodes offer unique prospects for the construction of single-molecule devices, yet compared to the most used gold electrodes, silver, as electrodes in the formation of single-molecule junctions, remains underexplored. Herein, we report a series of amine-terminated poly(para-phenylene)s that exhibit a low conductance peak with the conductance around one order of magnitude lower than the conductance of their corresponding single-molecule junctions when silver electrodes are used and a high bias voltage is applied. We further find that if silver electrodes are replaced by gold electrodes, a low conductance with much larger junction elongation length is seen, and if a bias voltage lower than 700 mV is applied, we do not see the low conductance peak. This low conductance decays exponentially with the increase of the number of phenyl rings in the molecular backbone, and its decay constant is similar to that of single-molecule junctions formed with either silver or gold electrodes. Through measurements of additional molecular structures and density functional theory calculations, we suggest that the low conductance is from the 𝝅-𝝅 stacked dimer junctions formed with the silver electrodes. This work showcases the potential of silver electrodes in creating novel metal-molecule-metal junctions.

papers.title: Complementary Moisture Retention of Ergothioneine and Hyaluronic Acid in Aqueous Formulations: Evidence from Gravimetric Desiccation and Polymer Substrate Assays
papers.abstract: Ergothioneine (EGT) is a naturally occurring imidazolethione amino acid derivative with a structurally rich polar framework encompassing a thione group, a zwitterionic betaine moiety, and multiple hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors. These physicochemical features suggest potential humectant activity that has not previously been characterized. Sodium hyaluronate (HA), the benchmark humectant in aqueous formulation chemistry, retains moisture primarily through osmotic and electrostatic mechanisms. We hypothesized that EGT may complement HA's moisture-retaining properties through a structurally orthogonal hydrogen-bonding mechanism. Here, we report two complementary experimental assessments: (1) a gravimetric desiccation assay in which formulations were weighed over 2 and 5 days in a controlled desiccating environment, and (2) a polymer substrate assay in which hydrophilic polymer disks equilibrated with each formulation were monitored for residual moisture over 17 hours. The combined EGT (0.5% w/v) and HA (0.1% w/v) formulation (EGT-0.5) maintained 47.85% moisture in solution after 5 days, numerically exceeding both the EGT-free buffered control (45.74%) and the buffer-free reference (40.12%). On the polymer substrate, EGT-0.5 consistently outperformed the EGT-free control at all timepoints, with the moisture retention advantage increasing from +1.35% at 1 hour to +2.63% at 17 hours. These results, supported by a dose-response experiment confirming 0.5% w/v as the apparent optimal EGT concentration and by an EGT-alone control demonstrating complementary action with HA, provide experimental evidence that EGT enhances moisture retention in HA-based aqueous systems.

papers.title: A Universal Shear-Bond Descriptor and Machine-Learning Potentials Enable Large-Scale Discovery of Negative Thermal Expansion Materials
papers.abstract: Negative thermal expansion (NTE) materials are crucial for mitigating thermal stresses and designing dimensionally stable components in advanced technologies, yet compounds exhibiting this anomalous behavior remain intrinsically rare. The discovery of novel NTE crystals has traditionally relied on serendipitous empirical observation and physical intuition, severely hindered by the absence of universal design principles. Here, by integrating more than a century of accumulated thermal-expansion data with state-of-the-art machine learning, we identify explainable, macroscopic mechanical descriptors for thermal expansion, that is the shear modulus (G) and the bonding modulus (Ẽ). These descriptors enable the construction of a universal thermal-expansion landscape based on the shear-bond ratio (G/Ẽ), supporting robust classification between positive and negative thermal expansion materials across diverse structural and chemical spaces. Guided by these universal descriptors and powered by high-throughput, finite-temperature simulations using universal machine-learning interatomic potentials, we theoretically predict 6,697 NTE crystals exhibiting wide operating temperature windows. Validating this theory-driven paradigm, the experimental synthesis and characterization of 11 previously unreported compounds directly confirm the robust predictive power and transferability of our framework. These results bridge macroscopic mechanics with microscopic lattice dynamics, transforming the discovery of NTE materials into a systematic, scalable, and data-driven science.

papers.title: Union of the in situ Generated ortho-Quinone Methides (o-QMs) with Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABB) towards the Synthesis of Functionalized Azetidines
papers.abstract: We herein disclose the reaction of in situ generated ortho-quinone methides (o-QMs) with Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABB). The reaction proceeded through an orthogonal Lewis acid activation of the precursor compounds to o-QMs in presence of ABB and serves as the key for the current development. The 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP) plays an important role as solvent in the reaction. Importantly, similar reaction of p-QMs with ABB could be promoted only in HFIP. This study highlights a new strategy for the formation of functionalized azetidines..

papers.title: Accessibility-controlled sequestration of mixed PFAS in coal fly ash–cement systems via coupled adsorption and stabilization
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) removal via adsorption generates PFAS-laden residuals that require safe long-term management. This study proposes a coupled adsorption–solidification strategy in which thermochemically modified coal fly ash (CFA) serves as both a PFAS adsorbent and a supplementary cementitious material for immobilization in concrete. Both singular and mixed PFAS (PFBA, PFHxA, PFOA, PFDA, and PFDoDA; C4–C12) were adsorbed from deionized water and landfill leachate, followed by incorporation of PFAS-loaded CFA into concrete (10–40% cement replacement). Semi-dynamic leaching tests (EPA Method 1315) were conducted over 63 days to evaluate release kinetics and underlying mechanisms. Adsorption followed Langmuir behavior, with capacities increasing with PFAS chain length. Leaching profiles exhibited a single-peaked release profile with a maximum at approximately Day 7, followed by monotonic decline. Effective diffusion coefficients ranged from 10-13 to 10-13 cm2⸱s-1. All systems exhibited leachability indices (LI) > 8, indicating low PFAS mobility and effective immobilization. Compared to deionized water, landfill leachate significantly suppressed PFAS release, is likely associated with dissolved organic matter and cation-mediated interactions that reduce PFAS availability and transport. This work demonstrates a practical and scalable pathway for managing PFAS-laden residuals while valorizing coal fly ash, providing a sustainable solution for PFAS containment in cementitious systems.

papers.title: Unraveling mechanistic pathways and selectivity patterns in visible light-driven aliphatic C-H functionalization with carbon nitride photocatalyst
papers.abstract: Visible light-driven heterogeneous photocatalysis based on carbon nitride materials has recently emerged as a sustainable platform for aliphatic C–H functionalization, although key mechanistic aspects and selectivity factors remain poorly understood. Herein, we report a combined experimental and computational investigation, wherein mesoporous graphitic carbon nitride (mpg-CN) has been exploited in Giese-type C–H functionalization reactions of diverse aliphatic substrates. Under mild and additive-free conditions, mpg-CN enabled the redox-neutral formation of C( sp 3 )–C( sp 3 ) bond with electron-poor olefins, displaying a reactivity profile strongly dependent on substrate structure. Mechanistic studies, supported by density functional theory calculations, reveal that C–H bond cleavage proceeds via a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathway. A clear correlation between bond dissociation free energies and functionalization yield has been identified, establishing a thermodynamic threshold for reactivity. Furthermore, adsorption of substrates within the catalyst surface grooves emerges as a key factor dictating both reactivity and site selectivity, when applicable. In particular, steric constraints and substrate-surface interactions govern accessibility to reactive sites, leading to distinctive selectivity patterns compared to homogeneous photocatalysts, notably the decatungstate anion. These findings highlight the unique role of heterogeneous environments in modulating reactivity and provide fundamental insights for the rational design of selective carbon nitride-based photocatalytic transformations.

papers.title: 𝑆𝑒𝑛𝐼2: A Defect-Engineered Flowable Liquid Semiconductor
papers.abstract: Liquid semiconductors have long been regarded as a scientific curiosity, with no practical realization despite decades of speculation. Here we report the discovery of a selenium iodide liquid semiconductor, 𝑆𝑒 𝑛 𝐼 2 (𝑛~69), that overcomes the fundamental limitations of structural disorder and defect states which have historically precluded semiconducting behavior in the liquid phase. Unlike elemental selenium, which suffers from chain-end defect states, 𝑆𝑒 𝑛 𝐼 2 is shown to be defect free due to passivation. Further, its solutions in iodine remain liquid at moderate temperatures (330 K) while preserving an optically accessible bandgap. The material exhibits robust semiconducting properties during flow, including fixed resistivity, persistent photoconductivity, and electrochemical tunability. Our results establish liquid semiconductors as a viable materials class, bridging a half-century-old gap between theoretical possibility and functional device implementation. #Equal Contributors

papers.title: General EPR pattern from molecular hydrino produced in various reactors
papers.abstract: Hydrino, H(1/p), is any small form of atomic hydrogen with state energy E n = -13.598/n 2 eV, in which n = 1/p, and p is a limited integer 1 < p ≤ 137. Electron transition to a hydrino state is non-radiative and requires a quantized amount of energy, 2mE1 (m is integer) to be transferred to a catalyst. Furthermore, hydrino can dimerize to molecular hydrino, H 2 (1/p), by loss of its bond energy, e.g., to a reaction wall. In contrast to molecular hydrogen, molecular hydrino is paramagnetic with S = 1/2. We have previously reported a uniquely sharp multi-line EPR spectrum for gaseous molecular hydrino included in spheres of gallium oxide hydroxide, H 2 (1/4)@Ga(O)OH, which was produced in a plasma discharge reactor with gallium as an electrode and nascent water as the catalyst. Contrarily, EPR spectra of a very different nature are exhibited by H 2 (1/4) produced in multiple reactors of different type. Broad-line powder patterns are observed extending from 0 to some 8000 Gauss in dual-mode X-band. Unusual temperature dependence includes anti-Curie behaviour and a magnetic phase transition around 107 K. Frequency-dependent resonance conditions are identified in L-, S-, X-, and Q-band. The broad EPR is analyzed in terms of a temperature-dependent dimer-of-dimers to dimer equilibrium of molecular hydrino interstitially included in the microcrystals of powder hosts. The room-temperature EPR provides a simple fingerprint identification tool to monitor the production of molecular hydrino in stable catchers.

papers.title: Categorical Compound Database: Oscillation-Counted Molecular Identification Through Ternary Phase Space Addressing
papers.abstract: Molecular database search in traditional cheminformatics requires O(N × d) pairwise fingerprint comparisons per query, where N is the number of database compounds and d is the fingerprint dimensionality. For PubChem-scale databases (N ≈ 108, d = 1024), this amounts to ∼ 1011 operations per query. We demonstrate that this computational burden arises from an unnatural representation: molecules are encoded as arbitrary bit vectors in an extrinsic descriptor space, forcing similarity to be computed rather than read. We develop an alternative founded on a single axiom—the Bounded Phase Space Law—from which we derive that every stable molecule is a bounded oscillatory system whose identity is fully characterised by three independent entropy coordinates: knowledge entropy Sk (spectral energy distribu-tion), temporal entropy St (timescale span), and evolution entropy Se (harmonic network density). These three coordinates define a compact metric space S = [0, 1]3 in which molecules are intrinsi-cally addressed. The three-dimensionality of this space makes base-3 the natural encoding: each ternary digit (trit) refines one coordinate dimension, and an interleaved ternary string provides a hierarchical address that is simultaneously a position and a path. We construct a ternary trie—the categorical compound database—in which search is O(k) trie traversal for k-trit resolution, inde-pendent of database size N . Fuzzy search reduces to prefix truncation: shorter prefixes yield coarser resolution and more matches, with each trit cor-responding to one oscillation-counting observation. We validate on 39 compounds from the NIST Computational Chemistry Comparison and Benchmark Database spanning diatomics through polyatomics. All 39 compounds are uniquely resolved at trit depth 12. Five of six chemically defined families (halomethanes, hydrogen halides, homonuclear diatomics, linear triatomics, bent triatomics) show intra-group ternary cohesion exceeding inter-group similarity (cohesion ratios 1.09–4.38), with chemical groupings emerging at depth 3 without any chemical knowledge being encoded. At depth 12, the ternary trie achieves a 3,328× speedup over brute-force fingerprint search (N = 39, d = 1024); at PubChem scale (N = 108), the projected speedup exceeds 109. The fundamental insight is that molecular search is not computation but phase space addressing: each trit is one oscillation-counting observation, and the address is the search.

papers.title: Isomer-Engineered Aggregation-Induced Emission Pro-Photosensitizers for Precise Bladder Cancer Phototheranostics
papers.abstract: The rational design of efficient phototheranostic agents relies on elucidating the influence of molecular structural features on pro-photosensitizer (pro-PS) activation and the photophysical characteristics associated with the aggregation of activated products. Herein, we developed a set of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) positional isomers (denoted p -TBP, m -TBP, o -TBP) and their phosphorylated pro-PSs (TBPP isomers). Among the TBP isomers, the para -substituted one showed superior fluorescence emission and reactive oxygen species generation capability. Meanwhile, its corresponding pro-PS, p -TBPP, could be efficiently activated via dephosphorylation mediated by tumor-overexpressed alkaline phosphatase (ALP), thereby achieving a dual enhancement of both fluorescence intensity and photodynamic activity. As a proof of concept, p -TBPP allows accurate delineation of ex vivo human bladder tumor tissues and orthotopic bladder lesions, as well as selective ablation of bladder cancer cells with negligible damage to normal tissues. This positional isomer engineering strategy provides valuable guidance for the structural design of pro-PSs, facilitating sensitive tumor visualization and effective therapy in vivo . †These authors contributed equally to this work.

papers.title: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Parameters of Ultracold Metal Monohalides and Monohydrides: A Relativistic DFT Study
papers.abstract: In this work, we present four-component relativistic density functional theory (DFT) calculations of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) parameters, specifically hyperfine coupling constants (HFCCs; A-tensors) and electronic g-tensors, for a series of diatomic molecules (CaF, SrF, BaF, HgF, SrCl, BaCl, HgCl, SrH, and HgH). These systems are promising candidates for laser cooling and for precision measurements aimed at probing physics beyond the Standard Model. We systematically investigate the influence of basis sets, exchange-correlation functionals, and molecular geometries on the accurate prediction of these EPR parameters.The comparison of computed results with available experimental data and previously reported theoretical studies indicates good agreement between the DFT results and the literature. Overall, this study evaluates the reliability of relativistic DFT methodologies for predicting EPR parameters in diatomic systems and highlights their potential as useful tools for future investigations of more complex heavy-element-containing ultracold molecules relevant to high-precision spectroscopy.

papers.title: Accelerating Proton Affinity Prediction with Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Accurate gas-phase proton affinities (PAs) are essential for designing proton carriers in anhydrous fuel cells, rationalizing acid-base chemistry, and guiding high-throughput molecular screening, yet the expense of high-level quantum-chemical calculations limits their routine application to large libraries. We develop a multi-fidelity ∆-learning framework that learns the systematic correction between fast PM7 semi-empirical calculations and high-fidelity references (specifically, experimental gas-phase PAs from the NIST WebBook and B3LYP/def2-TZVP DFT values) using only PM7 electronic properties and cheminformatics descriptors, without requiring DFT-derived features. On a 1,155-molecule benchmark derived from the NIST WebBook, an ExtraTrees model reduces the PM7 mean absolute error (MAE) from 8.21 to 2.87 kcal/mol (65% reduction), matching the accuracy ceiling set by B3LYP/def2-TZVP against experiment (3.74 kcal/mol), despite using no DFT-derived features. We extend ∆-learning to the more challenging task of site-specific PA prediction on a 251-molecule, 821-site k-means dataset constructed for chemical diversity, reducing the PM7 baseline from 17.96 to 6.85 kcal/mol (62% reduction). Functional group analysis and SHAP interpretation reveal two distinct PM7 failure regimes: systematic underestimation for aromatic nitrogen heterocycles, ethers, and amides due to inadequate treatment of electronic delocalization upon protonation, and systematic overestimation for nitriles and strained ring systems. These patterns provide practical guidelines for model deployment. We demonstrate the framework’s utility in a seven-stage agentic screening pipeline for anhydrous proton carrier discovery. The pipeline combines FAISS similarity search, PM7 + ∆-ML prediction with ensemble uncertainty quantification, large language model-assisted chemical reasoning (Claude Opus 4.6), and multi-objective Pareto optimization to reduce 821,435 pre-filtered ZINC molecules to 30 DFT-validated candidates. Of these, 29 (97%) fall within the target proton-affinity window (210-235 kcal/mol); post-hoc substructure verification confirms that 27 of these satisfy the structural requirements for Grotthuss-type proton transport, with a prospective MAE of 5.59 kcal/mol. Five priority leads are identified, including commercially available 3-amino-1 H -pyrazole and (3-(thiophen-2-yl)-1 H -pyrazol-5-yl)methanol, with DFT-validated proton affinities in the range 226-231 kcal/mol, above the experimental PA of imidazole (225.3 kcal/mol), the benchmark anhydrous proton carrier, and favorable synthetic accessibility scores.

papers.title: Generation of Tailorable Multi-Property Molecules via Multimodal Spectral Fusion Evolution
papers.abstract: Molecular generation stands at the forefront of intelligent molecular design, promising transformative advances in the discovery of molecules meeting druglikeness or catalysis requirements. However, existing generative models typically focus on optimizing a single target property at a time, hindered by the intrinsic difficulty of simultaneously encoding and evolving multiple structural features. Herein, we developed MUltimodal Spectral fusion Evolution (MUSE)—a spectroscopy-guided generative framework that unifies multimodal spectroscopic descriptors as a universal chemical language for multi-property molecular creation. A Spectra-to-Molecules (S2M) model, as one of MUSE's core modules, achieved high success rate in molecular structure generation by training on a self-built density functional theory (DFT) levelmultimodal spectral database. Leveraging the continuously variable nature of spectral descriptors, MUSE achieved synergistic integration of structural, vibrational, and electronic information by combining complementary spectroscopic modalities. Through evolutionary algorithms that constrain the generation direction of multiproperty molecules, the framework enables an up to 700-fold increase in the enrichment of rare quadruple-property candidates. This work provides a scalable pathway for multiobjective discovery in chemistry and materials science.

papers.title: How to Balance a Bifunctional Catalyst: Effect of MoOx Loading on Pd‑MoOx/Al2O3 for Glucose Hydrogenolysis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT: Biomass-derived glucose is a versatile feedstock for producing value added chemicals such as propylene glycol and ethylene glycol, offering a sustainable alternative to fossil-based feedstocks. While previous studies have primarily focused on ethylene glycol, the present work emphasizes the formation of propylene glycol. Commonly, tungsten-containing catalysts are used for this reaction. Since molybdenum is expected to exhibit similar properties, molybdenum-based catalysts were employed. Accordingly, a series of 1Pd-yMoOx/Al2O3 catalysts with different MoOx loadings (1.5, 3, 5, 7 and 10 wt%) were prepared via incipient wetness impregnation of γ-Al2O3. The catalysts were analyzed with XRD, ICP-OES, N2 physisorption, TGA, CO pulse chemisorption, TPR and STEM-EDX. Catalytic tests in glucose hydrogenolysis were carried out using a trickle-bed reactor. This study highlights that the catalyst’s activity for the various reactions, such as isomerization, hydrogenation and retro-aldol condensation, must be precisely controlled in this complex reaction network. Increasing MoOx content decreases the hydrogenation activity while enhancing retro-aldol cleavage, which favors the formation of the desired product, propylene glycol. This behavior is attributed to larger palladium particles at higher MoOx loadings, demonstrating that smaller particles are not always beneficial for the selective formation of target products.

papers.title: Click-polymerized polyenamine membranes for efficient lithium extraction
A Bioorthogonal Reaction Network Programs Selective Death in an Ensemble of Assorted Protocells
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separated coacervates offer a reliable protocell platform for understanding fundamentals of cellular processes, disease progression, and bottom-up synthesis of minimal cells. Synthetic protocells replicate key non-equilibrium features of living systems through fuel-dependent compartmentalization, growth, adaptation, and destruction. However, a significant challenge remains in achieving programmed and irreversible control over their fates in a complex ensemble of protocells, akin to programmed cell death in natural cells known as apoptosis. Here, we introduce a fuel-driven coacervate that undergoes selective apoptosis by an orthogonal chemical signal. The signal receiving protocells are transiently created by activating a bivalent aldehyde-containing terephthalaldehyde monomer using bisulfite to generate a negatively charged α-hydroxy sulfonate, which undergoes phase separation with poly(hexamethylene biguanide) polymer through salt-bridge interactions. The resulting liquid-core membraneless protocell exhibits tunable lifetime, regulated by formaldehyde that regenerates the neutral aldehyde and concomitantly disassembles. When organized into communicating protocell populations, enzymatic formaldehyde production in one compartment selectively induces the programmed dissolution of target protocells, exhibiting autocrine and paracrine signaling behavior. Remarkably, the orthogonal formaldehyde signaling network enables fractional killing of target protocells in an ensemble of heterogenous protocell community, while preserving the phenotypes and native functional activities of non-targeted population. Together, this work establishes the utility of aldehyde-bisulfite chemistry in adaptable coacervates through charge reversal and competitive binding, showcasing a general strategy for constructing programmable, nonequilibrium cell-like systems. Beyond advancing the design of synthetic life-like materials, the approach holds great potential in designing bioorthogonal strategies for drug delivery, sensing, and therapeutics.

papers.title: Dynamic Stereoisomerism in Spirocyclic Kratom Alkaloids: Mechanistic Insights into Retro-Mannich Isomerization
papers.abstract: The ongoing opioid crisis highlights the need for safer analgesics with reduced addiction potential and respiratory depression risks. Alkaloids from Mitragyna speciosa (kratom), such as mitragynine and its potent metabolite mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (MPS), can guide the development of nextgeneration opioid analgesics. Previous studies have shown that MPS exists as a (dynamical) mixture of isomers under physiological conditions. In order to understand the isomerization procedure of MPS and an analogous alkaloid (rhynchophylline), we have performed high-level quantum chemical calculations. The computed Gibbs free energy profiles reproduce experimental stability trends and reveal that isomerization proceeds via ring-opened intermediates through retro-Mannich and Mannich reactions. Our results confirm that these alkaloids exist as dynamic ensembles under physiological conditions, providing molecular insight for designing safer opioid therapeutics.

papers.title: DNA-encoded origami morphing
papers.abstract: From biological entities to manmade constructions, shape is an essential structural and functional feature1. At the nanoscale, this involves key structure-function relationships, ranging from conformationdependent protein activity 2–4 to morphology-driven properties of synthetic nanomaterials5,6. Finding ways to dynamically reshape nanoscale architectures under constant physiological conditions thus emerges as a powerful goal to create smart biocompatible adaptive materials. While DNA origami offers unparalleled precision and robustness for constructing virtually any desired static nanoscale morphology7,8, imparting adaptive morphological shift remains a formidable challenge. Current methods are mainly limited to local deformations9–11 rather than radical transformation, and often involve complex mechanical designs12–17 or specific stimulus-responsive modules17–19. Here, we introduce an exceptionally versatile, modification-free strategy for isothermal, physiologically compatible DNA origami morphing driven by programmable staple-strand competition. We achieve fast, high-yield transformations across diverse 2D and 3D morphologies, including multiple-shape pathways and back-and-forth switches. We further demonstrate modularity through the orthogonal and parallel reconfiguration of independent subdomains within a single DNA scaffold. Strikingly, we leverage this structural plasticity to dynamically reconfigure scaffoldanchored proteins into controllable patterns at 37 °C. This is used to modulate biochemical function, as demonstrated here with the regulation of a glucose oxidase/horseradish peroxidase cascade reaction. Overall, this work establishes a reliable and generic framework for nanoscale programmable morphing and user-defined functional regulation in physiologically compatible conditions.

papers.title: Cyclam(OH)4 as an adaptable co-former for co-crystals with organic proton donors
papers.abstract: While (macro)cyclic amines are widely used as co-formers in the design of supramolecular hydrogen-bonded crystalline networks, organic hydroxylamines remain almost unexplored in this context. Here, co-crystallization of the tetra-N-hydroxylated cyclam with several organic hydrogen-bond donors (pharmaceutically relevant carboxylic acids, hydroquinone) was investigated for the first time. The results demonstrate co-former-dependent control over crystal packing, proton transfer, supramolecular organization, macrocyclic conformation, and tautomerization leading to either “closed” H-bonded subunits or novel three-dimensional self-catenated H-bonded networks. In specific cases, the dynamic nature of crystal formation gives rise to conformational polymorphs. Remarkably, a very rare tautomerization of the hydroxylamine unit to the N-oxide form was observed in the co-crystal of cyclam(OH)4 with hydroquinone. Comparison of the observed H-bonding parameters and patterns with those of the known co-crystals of unsubstituted cyclam highlights the pronounced advantage of the hydroxylated scaffold in engineering supramolecular hydrogen-bonded motifs.

papers.title: Leveraging Ace-SABRE and PETALUTE to Detect and Image Hyperpolarized [1-13C]pyruvate Metabolism in Yeast
Fabrication of High Endurance Separators for Next Generation Lithium-Ion Batteries Through Molecular Design of Sepiolite Clays
papers.abstract: The growing use of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) in grid-scale storage, nuclear power plants, consumer electronics, electric vehicles, and aerospace has raised serious safety concerns, particularly due to their inferior thermal stability. One viable solution is to develop new separators with high temperature stability. Here, an eco-friendly, sustainable, low-cost, heat-resistant, and flame-retardant sepiolite-zwitterion (betaine) clay membrane has been fabricated without the use of polymers. While traditional polymer and glass microfiber separators fail above 120 °C and 750 °C, respectively, this sepiolite-clay-based alternative remains structurally robust even at 860 °C. Also, it exhibits excellent flexibility, wettability, ionic conductivity, electrolyte uptake (300%), and a high Li-ion transference number (tLi-ion = 73). The structural micropores of sepiolite fibers, inter-fiber micropores, and mesopores provide a less tortuous pathway for ion transport. This helps to maintain a uniform lithium-ion concentration gradient at the lithium metal surface. The Li//Li cell using this clay-based separator thus exhibits stable lithium plating/stripping even after 2000 hours. Additionally, the corresponding NMC811//Li and NMC811//Graphite cells exhibit exceptional cycling stability, large capacity, and exceptional rate performance. Furthermore, early tests indicate that the sepiolite-betaine separator with a commercial liquid electrolyte enables the LIB to operate safely at 155 °C. This scalable, aqueous-solvent-based, biocompatible phyllosilicate separator offers an intriguing approach toward high-safety LIBs.

papers.title: Bromine monoxide radical dominates dimethylsulfide oxidation before the springtime onset of Arctic ice melt
papers.abstract: To understand the atmospheric fate of dimethylsulfide (DMS) during the Arctic spring-to-summer transition and the onset of ice melt, we measured volatile methylated sulfur (VMS) species, including DMS and DMS-derived oxidation products, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and dimethyl sulfone (DMSO 2 ), in the Fram Strait during May and June of 2023. Elevated DMSO contributions to VMS, depleted O 3 , high surface albedo, and air temperatures < 0 ◦ C in air masses influenced by snow-covered sea-ice regions demonstrate that BrO • -initiated oxidation dominated DMS loss prior to the onset of sea-ice melt. GEOS-Chem simulations demonstrate that BrO • is an important oxidant for DMS, but modeled BrO • concentrations from sea salt debromination alone are too low to replicate observed O 3 , DMSO, and DMSO 2 , highlighting the importance of bromine activation in sunlit saline snow. BrO • -initiated oxidation reduces the DMS lifetime, and oxidizes DMS through methanesulfinic acid (MSIA) more quickly in the gas phase and in higher yields compared to • OH-initiated oxidation alone. Once melt onset begins and snowpack-driven halogen activation shuts off, • OH oxidation will dominate Arctic DMS oxidation. Our observations highlight the seasonal variability of halogen oxidation impacting sulfur species in the Arctic marine region, which are likely to change as sea ice extent decreases and the melt season in the Arctic lengthens.

papers.title: Inclusion complexes of cannabinoids with cyclodextrins: Theoretical methods to evaluate and discuss drug repurposing
papers.abstract: Neurological diseases, such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s, are significant problems today due to the growing number of elderly people. As the world population ages, a higher number of people with neurological disorders is expected. The literature has shown that natural products may be used as a possible treatment for this class of diseases. Cannabinoid-based drugs are currently used in the treatment of numerous neurological diseases, making them interesting targets for drug repurposing. Additionally, the human body cannabinoid receptor system makes the cannabinoid class attractive for drug repurposing. One strategy is to encapsulate these molecules in macrocycles to enhance their solubility and improve oral administration, drug delivery, and controlled liberation, enabling their use against other diseases. The main goal of the present study is to evaluate the formation of inclusion complexes of cannabicyclol (CBL) and cannabidiol (CBD) with β-cyclodextrin and γ-cyclodextrin, using multiscale methods (ONIOM) and molecular dynamics simulations (MD). Different ONIOM schemes were tested to investigate the methodological effects on thermodynamic and structural parameters, providing a robust dataset for future methodological choices. Thermochemical properties were calculated and compared to available experimental data, and noncovalent interaction calculations conducted to verify the contribution of hydrogen bonds and van der Waals interactions to the complex stability. All proposed complexes are stable due to hydrophobic host-guest interactions, with a portion of the guest remaining outside the cavity and interacting with solvent molecules. The LoP calculations showed improved water solubility after complex formation, which is desirable for drugs intended for oral administration. The calculated properties were used to discuss drug repurposing and the impact of the inclusion complex formation in on drug development.

papers.title: Initial velocities of hydrated ions under an electropotential field, their molar masses, and total hydration numbers
papers.abstract: The inner hydration shell, where water is electrostricted, has always been the main area of study. But it appears that the bulk water, which is affected by the ion electric field, is not given the same degree of attention. This largely theoretical study aims to develop equation-based models that can be used to calculate the initial velocities of ions when an electrical potential gradient is applied, as well as the total number of water molecules pulled to the ions and their molar masses (including the mass of the electrostricted water). Theoretical and computational approaches were employed to analyze literature-based data. The initial velocity was approximately 3.8 exp. (–8) m/s for cobalt ions and 26 exp. (–8) m/s for oxonium ions. The equivalent total hydration number ranged from 4 for oxonium ions to 60 for cobalt ions. Initial velocities ranged from 1.65 exp. (–8) m/s for epinephrine to 2.88 exp. (–8) m/s for glycinate, and the corresponding total hydration number ranged from 38 for glycinate to 64 for epinephrine. The molar masses of the hydrated ions ranged from 765 g/mol for glycinate to 1,333 g/mol for epinephrine and from 85.81 g/mol for oxonium ions to 1,137.8 g/mol for cobalt ions. The trajectory and biological function of biomolecules can be impacted by their hydrated mass. The lowest and highest velocities are associated with the lowest and highest total hydration numbers. Future research could focus on determining the electrophoretic mobilities of all physiologically active biomolecules at physiological pH and body temperature.

papers.title: Molecular Insights Shaping the Design of Metal-Organic Framework-based Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Understanding the molecular determinants of Li + transport in quasi-solid-state electrolytes (QSSEs) is critical for the design of next-generation energy storage materials. Here, we investigate Li + conduction in an isoreticular series of anionic metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), Li 3 [(Cu 4 Cl) 3 L 8 ] (L 3− = linker), to disentangle the effects of pore size and linker functionality on ion conductivity. Contrary to expectation based on previous studies, despite their structural differences, the MOFs show pore size-independent Li + conductivity, whereas the linker functional groups can impose an effect. Using 7 Li magic-angle-spinning solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance, we identify the major Li + conducting species residing in the open pore channels, which, upon the addition of propylene carbonate, display liquid-like transport with low activation energies. The similar local environments and liquid-like dynamics of these species give rise to conductivities on the order of 10 −5 S/cm across the isoreticular series, though the interactions between tetrazolate nitrogens in linkers and Li + restrict ion mobility, leading to a modest decrease in conductivity. This study provides molecular-level insights into Li + transport in anionic MOF-based electrolytes and thus establishes the design principles for developing efficient QSSEs.

papers.title: A CALIBRATION-FREE QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF IMMISCIBLE BINARY POLYMER BLENDS: THE CRISTALLINITY-SET FILTERING (CSF) METHOD APPLIED TO DSC DATA
papers.abstract: The transition toward a circular economy has intensified the need for efficient recycling of polymeric waste. However, quantifying cross-contamination in post-consumer recyclates (PCR) remains challenging for calibration-based approaches due to the variability and limited availability of pristine reference materials. In this study, a novel calibration-free mathematical approach, here termed crystallinity-set filtering (CSF), is proposed for the quantitative analysis of fully immiscible bicomponent semicrystalline polymer blends. This method was applied on differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) data and exploits physically meaningful boundary conditions associated with polymer crystallinity ranges. The CSF approach was validated using high-density polyethylene/polypropylene (HDPE/PP) blends covering the full composition range. The method was directly compared with the conventional calibration-based least squares method (LSM) applied to melting enthalpy data. The results demonstrate that the CSF method outperforms the LSM approach, achieving a minimum mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.70% and R2 values up to 0.9957, compared to an MAE of 2.61% and an R2 of 0.9932 obtained with LSM. The proposed method exhibits performance metrics comparable to those reported in the literature for established quantitative techniques. The analysis further shows that CSF accuracy improves as the assumed crystallinity intervals are narrowed, highlighting the importance of realistic constraints derived from literature data or prior experimental knowledge. The reduced accuracy observed near equimolar compositions was attributed to both the widening of the feasible crystallinity set and increased peak overlap in the DSC melting region. Overall, the CSF method represents a robust calibration-free alternative for the quantitative analysis of semicrystalline polymer blends. The log file and the Python code developed in this study are available on GitHub. We believe this approach is particularly promising for assessing thermoplastic polymer cross-contamination in PCR materials where calibration-based strategies are limited, and establishes a new analytical framework that broadens the scope of quantitative polymer blend analysis.

papers.title: Soft Sensors Enable Real-Time Ion Concentration Measurements
papers.abstract: Analytical techniques such as Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-OES) are widely used to measure ion concentrations, but are time-consuming, laborintensive, and costly. The required sample collection, preparation, and offline, energyintensive analysis render ICP-OES inadequate for real-time monitoring in membrane processes. Conductivity sensors provide rapid, in situ measurements of the electrical conductivity of ionic solutions, offering an attractive alternative for real-time tracking of ionic species during membrane processes; however, converting conductivity measurements into ion concentrations in multicomponent systems remains a significant challenge. This work addresses this limitation by developing soft sensors that estimate ion concentrations in real time using conductivity data from inexpensive sensors and mathematical models that map conductivity measurements to ion concentrations. Specifically, the Shedlovsky and mean spherical approximation (MSA) models are deployed, and their conductivity predictions are validated using experimental data representative of electronic waste and lithium-ion battery leachate. By capturing key physical phenomena in ion transport in the presence of the electric field generated by the conductivity sensor, such as electrophoretic and relaxation effects, these models accurately predict the conductivity of single, binary, and ternary salt feed solutions. Furthermore, Shedlovsky and MSA-based soft sensors are applied to estimate real-time ion concentrations in the permeate solution of a membrane-based separation, and the estimates are validated against ICP-OES analysis, demonstrating good agreement (within 5%). Overall, this study demonstrates that the development of scientifically rigorous and generalizable soft sensors is essential for enabling rapid, reliable, and efficient measurement of ion concentrations in complex ionic environments.

papers.title: Multiexciton Modulation via a Redox-Active Bridge in Singlet Fission Chromophores
papers.abstract: Emerging paradigms in multiexciton photochemistry are shifting the focus beyond traditional single- exciton approaches, advancing toward complex photoinduced multi-electron photoredox chemistry. These processes offer significant potential for overcoming current limitations in solar energy conversion, artificial photosynthesis, and next generation photocatalysis. However, conventional spectroscopic methods struggle to unambiguously identify when specific double redox events occur. Here, we introduce an approach to detect excited transients of intramolecular singlet fission (iSF) chromophores under electrochemical bias to change their redox states. Upon reduction, the iSF dynamics are modulated by constructive and destructive quantum interference effects (CQI and DQI, respectively). Transient 2 absorption spectroelectrochemistry (TA-SEC) was employed to track the excited state dynamics across different oxidation states of an electroactive anthraquinone (AQ) bridge linking two pentacene chromophores. We found the bridge's redox state strongly impacts iSF dynamics: the neutral AQ bridge induces a DQI effect, yielding predominantly slow iSF. Double reduction restores aromaticity, activating CQI and dramatically enhancing iSF (accelerating from 66 ps to 2 ps), whereas the singly reduced intermediate completely blocks the iSF path. This unconventional molecular design of a redox-switchable bridge in an iSF chromophore proves that modulated multiexciton dynamics can serve as a powerful, unambiguous probe for redox-active singlet fission systems.

papers.title: Advancing automated microplastic detection: validation of a method using particle detection software and µ-Raman spectroscopy for 20 – 53 µm particles
papers.abstract: Research on microplastics is developing rapidly, but methods for quantifying the smallest particles (1-100 µm) remain limited. Automated spectroscopic methods using µ-FTIR and µ-Raman spectroscopy have been developed, but these methods are often time-consuming, require expensive filters, or show poor recovery of smaller particles. To address these problems, and as part of a larger effort to develop a cost-effective method for the rapid quantification of microplastic particles, we developed and validated a method for quantifying 20 – 53 µm microplastic fragments using µ-Raman spectroscopy on polycarbonate filters. Our method is fast, reliable, and does not require expensive consumables. We validated a method for polyethylene, polystyrene, and polyethylene terephthalate fragments with good precision for one sample run multiple times (~3 – 7% coefficient of variation) and independent samples of the same mass (~18 – 35%, depending on polymer). Recovery, tested across a larger size range of particles (up to 106 µm), ranged from 69 – 77% across polymers. KOH treatment (10 or 20%) reduced the recovery of our small polyethylene terephthalate particles. Our method proves promising, and we will continue its development and validation across a greater diversity of polymers, sizes and shapes, as well as with weathered particles extracted from environmental matrices.

papers.title: New Implementation of Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory and Application to Molecules with Variable Diradical Character and Conical Intersections
papers.abstract: Mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSFTDDFT) improves upon the original spin-flip TDDFT (SF-TDDFT) approach by expanding the configurational space of the response states via a mixed-reference reduced density matrix, specifically, an equal mixture of the density matrices from the MS = +1 and MS = −1 components of the lowest triplet state. MRSF-TDDFT improves the description of the spin-flip target states and the respective energy differences and eliminates the problem of spin-contamination that often spoils the description of higher-lying states in SF-TDDFT. This article presents the theoretical framework and details of a new implementation of MRSF-TDDFT in the Q-Chem software package. The implementation includes calculations of energies and properties, including transition dipole moments, oscillator strengths, spin–orbit couplings, and density-matrix based analyses of the MRSF states and transitions. The capabilities of the theory are illustrated by applications to diradicals and a reduced retinal model, the penta-2,4-dieniminium cation, used to evaluate the performance of electronic structure methods in describing conical intersections.

papers.title: Entanglement-Dominated Thermosets Enable High Performance with High-Fidelity Regeneration
papers.abstract: Thermoset plastics underpin structural materials, electronics, and transportation, yet their permanent covalent networks make recycling difficult.1–5 Existing recycling strategies for high‑Tg engineering applications that incorporate exchangeable6–15 or cleavable bonds16–20 often compromise stiffness, creep resistance, or thermal stability, and typically treat covalent junctions as the primary load-bearing elements.21,22 Rather than considering recycling as the recovery of degraded networks, here we construct thermosets in which high mechanical performance arises predominantly from dense chain entanglements, while only a sparse fraction of trigger-cleavable junctions preserves network connectivity. Long, rigid, entangled polyolefin backbones generated by frontal polymerization form high-Tg, glassy polymers with high stiffness, high toughness, and excellent creep suppression, yet fully deconstruct to soluble, linear oligomers. Programming oligomer length and end-group chemistry enables their reuse as re-entangling building blocks that regenerate thermosets with generation-invariant thermomechanical properties, including in high-temperature fiber reinforced composite matrices and additively manufactured structures. By demonstrating that load-bearing in high‑Tg engineering thermosets can be delivered primarily by entangled strands while sparse cleavable junctions preserve connectivity, this strategy maintains network topology across generations and establishes an entanglement-dominated design principle for regenerable, high-performance networks based on entanglement-dominated architectures.

papers.title: The Quantum-Volume and Bragg-Williams Equations of State
papers.abstract: The quantum-volume (qv) and Bragg-Williams equations of state, as derived from a lattice gas model, are exploited. The qv equation of state includes a temperaturedependent excluded volume related to the thermal wavelength included in the translational contribution to the molecular partition function, but apart from this contribution intermolecular interactions are not included. The qv equation of state has the correct limiting behaviour both in the limit of an ideal gas and in the packing-density limit. It also includes a non-classical contribution to the internal energy and thereby a manyparticle contribution to the kinetic energy, and it supports the view that it is both the position as well as the momentum of a system of particles that are distributed over the volume to maximize the multiplicity of the system. The qv equation of state is extended with intermolecular interactions through the Bragg-Williams mean-field approach, including also a hard-core contribution. For a one-component lattice gas, analytical expressions are presented for the pressure and the critical point as well as for the internal energy, the isochoric heat capacity, and the chemical potential, and results are presented for some simple systems. Given its relative simplicity, essentially on a textbook level, the model shows promising results, in particular for the temperature dependence of the isochoric heat capacity that shows a maximum close to the critical temperature. The presented model is supposed to serve as a foundation for further model extensions as well as for the development of interpretable analytical models in molecular thermodynamics for more complex systems and processes.

papers.title: 1 An Integrated Workflow Comprising AI, Physics and Experiment: Discovery of Nanomolar-Potent Inhibitors
papers.abstract: The drug discovery process remains very slow and unreliable, requiring about 10 years and $2-3 billion for a single new drug at a success rate of around 5%. To address this, we have recently created a complex and highly heterogeneous workflow called IMPECCABLE which is designed to transform much of the drug discovery process into a far more reliable in silico environment. It runs on Frontier, the world’s first exascale machine and has recently been implemented on the second such machine, Aurora. A variety of in silico discovery methods exist, including physics-based and artificial intelligence (AI) approaches. Despite their limitations, these methods are complementary, and we combine them here within IMPECCABLE, an integrated framework which efficiently and reliably explores the vast chemical space of small molecule binders. IMPECCABLE involves screening, generating and evaluating candidate compounds. The environment is comprised of several interlocking and interacting stages. In the first of these, an exceptionally fast machine learning model acts as a docking surrogate for rapidly screening billions of compounds and provides a ranked series of binding poses for the best ones. In a generative multi-objective active learning loop, the accurate binding free energies from physics-based free energy methods, including ESMACS and TIES, guide REINVENT to predict compounds not only with higher binding affinities, but which are also synthesizable while ensuring diversity and novelty. The full iterative workflow spans both hit identification and hit-to-lead optimization and includes medicinal chemists in the process. Applying IMPECCABLE to two disease-related protein targets, WDR91 and TNKS2, we demonstrate its capability to iteratively produce experimentally makeable potent binders. The potential hits discovered were further optimized and chiral purified via an iterative REINVENT-TIES cycle. We identified a potent hit for WDR91, which was synthesised in five steps, exhibiting nanomolar binding affinity with a KD value of 352 ± 32 nM.

papers.title: Development of a versatile testing apparatus for measuring hollow fiber membrane flux and permeance
papers.abstract: Despite the widespread adoption of hollow fiber membranes for wastewater treatment application, there remains few available methods of reliably determining the flux, permeance and separation ability of individual hollow fiber membranes for both for outside-in and inside-out operation. We present a new apparatus that can measure the flux and permeance of individual or multiple hollow fiber membranes in both the outside-in and inside-out orientations, partnered with a python-based open-source permeance analysis software. Firstly, we demonstrate the reliability of the instrument in two different configurations. We compare the difference between testing 3 individual membranes and 3 sets of 3 membranes with their permeance combined through manifolds, in dead-end mode. Secondly, we use the apparatus to study compaction and fouling of hollow fiber membranes in both outside-in and inside-out orientation in dead-end mode, with behaviour differences observed dependent on membrane orientation. For the studied ultrafiltration (UF) membranes, there was not a significant difference in performance depending on orientation, however for the microfiltration (MF) membranes, severe compaction-induced flux loss was observed for the inside-out orientation, with no significant compaction observed in outside-in orientation. Additionally, the orientation of liquid flow significantly affected the flux and permeance measurements of fouled MF membranes. We related the difference in permeance to the differences in structure, as characterized by SEM and liquid-liquid porometry. Deviation in results between the two orientations demonstrates the importance of being able to test hollow fiber membranes in both outside-in and inside-out orientations. This newly designed apparatus will be used to further investigate fundamental mechanisms that affect hollow fiber membrane permeance.
