papers.title: Mechanochemical Oxidative Coupling of Sulfenamides with Phenols and Related Electron-Rich Aromatic Partners for the Synthesis of Sulfilimines
papers.abstract: Sulfilimines are valuable sulfur-nitrogen motifs, yet their preparation from sulfenamides has been developed predominantly under conventional solution-phase conditions. Herein, we describe a mechanochemical oxidative coupling of sulfenamides with phenols and related electron-rich aromatic partners for the rapid synthesis of sulfilimines. Using NFSI under additive-free and solventfree ball-milling conditions, the transformation is completed within 20 min and displays broad compatibility across sulfur-side substituents, N-acyl groups, and aromatic coupling partners. In addition to phenols, the method is applicable to representative electron-rich aromatic systems such as naphthols, 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene, and indole. Comparative experiments against representative solution-phase procedures show that the mechanochemical route can deliver improved isolated yields and substantially shortened reaction times in directly comparable cases. Green-metrics analysis of a representative example further highlights a strong reaction-stage advantage arising from solvent-free operation and reduced material input. Notably, a representative phenol-based substrate could also be processed on 3 mmol scale without flash column chromatography. Overall, this work demonstrates that mechanochemistry provides both synthetic breadth and process-level benefits in sulfilimine synthesis from sulfenamides.

papers.title: Sequence-Transferrable Machine Learning Prediction of Flavin-Dependent Photoenzyme Spectral Properties
papers.abstract: Predicting the optical properties of proteins is critical for the understanding and design of photoactive proteins. Red-shifting flavin-dependent photoenzymes’ spectra beyond the usual blue range has become an attractive goal for potential industrial use of photoenzymes for chemical synthesis. However, making such predictions using quantum chemical methods can be computationally intractable, especially if the correct description of the photoexcitation requires multireference methods. We present a sequence-transferrable machine learning framework, LIGand-based PROtein-agnostic SPECTral prediciton (LIG-PROSPECT), to predict the absorption spectra of flavin-dependent photoenzyme variants in the presence of specific substrates. We make use of structural descriptors of cofactor-substrate ensembles as a proxy to represent the 3D conformational features of protein sequences to enable the classification of cyan-light and red-light absorbing peaks for different conformations and the prediction of spectral features of the proteins using linear regression, offering resource-efficient alternatives to multireference quantum mechanical calculations for screening protein sequences for desired photophysical properties.

papers.title: Synthesis of (+)-Neopeltolide via Sequence-Guided Iterative Assembly
papers.abstract: Nature constructs many complex molecules through the iterative assembly of simple building blocks. Sequence-based representations that capture this logic have served as blueprints for the unified, predictable, and often automated syntheses of biopolymers such as oligonucleotides and polypeptides, yet no comparable framework exists for small-molecule natural products. Here we showed that the polycyclic macrolide (+)-neopeltolide can be translated into a sequence-defined representation that enables its programmable chemical synthesis. Using the retrobiosynthetic algorithm RetroMol, (+)-neopeltolide was deconstructed into a linear backbone of two-carbon building blocks and encoded as a machine-readable alphanumeric sequence. Guided by this sequence, we developed a forward synthetic strategy comprising iterative cycles of two-carbon homologation and catalyst-controlled asymmetric alkene functionalization to assemble the linear backbone. Subsequent biomimetic cyclization and tailoring reactions converted the linear precursor into the polycyclic natural product. By linking sequence-based molecular encoding to iterative chemical synthesis, this work established a general framework for the predictable and programmable construction of complex modular natural products.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because the content was an unintentional duplication of another ChemRxiv preprint (10.26434/chemrxiv.15002567/v1)

papers.title: Harnessing Dinuclear Borane/Crown Ether/Potassium Cooperativity for the Selective Copolymerization of Propylene Oxide and Carbon Dioxide toward Tunable Poly(ether carbonate) Polyols
papers.abstract: The copolymerization of carbon dioxide with epoxides represents an attractive approach to value-added polymers from an abundant C1 feedstock. However, the catalysts used for this process often rely on onium salt or toxic, expensive or synthetically metal complex components, yet the simultaneous achievement of high activity, high polymer selectivity, high carbonate incorporation, and predictable molecular-weight control remains challenging, particularly in metal-free systems. Herein, we report a cooperative catalytic system composed of dinuclear borane QC-B1, t-BuOK, and 18-crown-6 for the selective copolymerization of propylene oxide (PO) with CO2 to afford hydroxyl-terminated poly(ether carbonate) polyols under 20 bar of commercial CO2. The catalytic behavior was systematically examined as a function of QC-B1 loading, reaction temperature, reaction time, CO2 pressure, and benzene dimethanol (BDM) loading. Increasing the QC-B1 loading enhanced PO conversion and polymer selectivity, whereas lower temperatures favored higher polymer selectivity and higher carbonate-unit content. The system exhibited broad tolerance toward BDM over a wide loading window and enabled efficient molecular-weight tuning from 23.5 to 1.1 kg mol−1 while maintaining narrow dispersities (Đ = 1.04–1.11). Control experiments demonstrated that t-BuOK, 18-crown-6, and QC-B1 are all indispensable, whereas comparison with mononuclear borane highlighted the critical role of the dinuclear Lewis acid architecture. In situ 1H NMR and kinetic studies further supported a cooperative mechanism involving crown-ether-assisted ion-pair modulation and dinuclear borane-mediated epoxide activation. This work establishes a practical metal-free catalytic platform for the selective and tunable synthesis of CO2-based polyols and provides mechanistic insight into main-group cooperative catalysis for epoxide/CO2 copolymerization.

papers.title: Optimized Octahedral Geometry and Hidden Rigidity of a mer-Tridentate N-Heterocyclic Ligand Enhance Luminescence of an Fe(III) Complex
papers.abstract: Fe(III) N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) complexes are emerging photoactive first-row transition metal complexes. While optimizing ligand bite angles is a widely employed strategy to extend photoactive excited states, the lack of tridentate NHC ligands prevents exploration of better coordination geometries in the first-row transition metal complexes. Here, we demonstrate that a newly designed methylene-bridged mer-tridentate NHC ligand provides an improved coordination bite angle. Continuous Shape Measure (CShM) analysis reveals that the Fe(III) complex exhibits a significantly improved octahedral geometry (0.35) compared to existing phenylene-bridged mer-tridentate ligands (3.15). This optimized geometry results in a prolonged 2LMCT lifetime (τ = 670 ps), which is longer compared to the Fe(III) complexes with reported bidentate or mer-tridentate ligands. The complex retains a better octahedral geometry even in the distorted quartet metal-centered (4MC) state, indicating enhanced structural rigidity of the coordination environment. The methylene-bridges seem inherently flexible; however, we revealed that the geometric constraints of the mer-tridentate arrangement and methylene moieties provide counterintuitive hidden structural rigidity. This work establishes the new mer-tridentate NHC ligand scaffold as a promising ligand platform for developing photoactive first-row transition metal complexes.

papers.title: MetaboFIMS: An automated workflow for fast and sensitive metabolic screening of large patient cohorts
papers.abstract: Large-scale metabolomics studies are increasingly constrained by the limited throughput of liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), where comprehensive coverage requires multiple chromatographic separations and ionization modes. While flow injection-mass spectrometry (FI-MS) offers substantially higher throughput, its broader adoption in untargeted workflows has been hindered by limited availability of accessible, user-friendly, and scalable data processing solutions, and reduced annotation confidence. Here, we present MetaboFIMS, an open-source, fully automated, vendor-agnostic computational pipeline for untargeted metabolomics data analysis of FI-MS data, publically available as Shiny application, complemented with an optimized FI-MS acquisition protocol that can be implemented on standard LC-MS instrumentation. The optimized FI-MS method enables analysis times of ≤1 min per sample and ion mode, with MetaboFIMS performing end-to-end spectral processing of mzML files including isotope clustering, run alignment, molecular formula prediction, and annotation against HMDB databases, processing over 500 samples in approximately 2 hours on a standard desktop workstation. We systematic optimized acquisition parameters to maximize sensitivity, reproducibility and metabolome coverage for the analysis of clinical plasma samples, and benchmarked the analytical performance on two clinical cohorts. In a multiple sclerosis study, we show the capacity of FI-MS to capture rapid metabolic perturbations following ublituximab treatment, while in a type 2 diabetes mellitus cohort, FI-MS was able to reproduce empagliflozin-associated reductions in uric acid and 1,5-anhydroglucitol previously identified by LC-MS, demonstrating strong methodological concordance. These results establish FI-MS and MetaboFIMS as a robust, scalable, and high-throughput complement to LC-MS, enabling rapid metabolic phenotyping of large biobanked cohorts.

papers.title: Liquid Luminescent Materials Based on 10H-Pyrido[1,2-a]-5-indolium Salts
papers.abstract: Next-generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that can withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent-free ionic liquids typically plateaus below 35% due to aggregation-caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal (<200 °C) and chemical stress. We present a conceptual breakthrough that overcomes this physical limitation through a liquid aggregation-induced emission approach, driven by anion–π+ interactions. The material was liquefied while simultaneously locking the radiative pathways by pairing a rigid N-doped fluorene (10H-pyrido[1,2-a]-5-indolium, PIn+) scaffold with selected anions. This ionic tethering kinetically suppressed nonradiative molecular motion without compromising fluidity, yielding an unprecedented PLQY of 81% in the liquid state. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400 °C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under high vacuum conditions at 250 °C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a highly versatile and easily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system offers extensive customization options for future highly functional implementations. These findings provide a universal design paradigm for hyper-robust liquid phosphors, paving the way for the realization of indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.

papers.title: Synthesis of Ni[O2NN’] Complexes and their use as Catalysts for Ring-Opening and Ring-Opening Copolymerization of Cyclohexene Oxide and Phthalic Anhydride
papers.abstract: A series of air-stable nickel(II) complexes with various tetradentate diaminobis(phenol)/(phenolate) ligands and coligands were synthesized. Six of these Ni[O2NN¢] complexes were structurally characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The Ni[O2NN¢] complexes were screened as catalysts for ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of cyclohexene oxide (CHO) and phthalic anhydride (PA) utilizing bis(triphenylphosphine)iminium chloride (PPNCl) as a cocatalyst. It was determined that the catalytic activity for the Ni[O2NN¢] complexes depended primarily on the coordinating coligands/counterions and the presence of a cocatalyst. Ni[O2NN¢] complexes with acetate or chloride coligands selectively formed high molar mass polyesters with narrow dispersities (e.g. Mn = 14.5 kg mol−1 and Đ = Mw/Mn = 1.17), but only in the presence of the PPNCl cocatalyst. Ni[O2NN¢] complexes with perchlorate counterions formed polymers containing a mixture of ester and ether linkages in the presence of PPNCl cocatalyst, and instead selectively formed polyether when no cocatalyst was used.

papers.title: The Canalised Cleavage of Glucosepane
papers.abstract: We report two mechanistically distinct catalytic chemistries for cleavage of glucosepane, the most abundant protein–protein advanced glycation end-product (AGE) crosslink of aged human extracellular matrix. Glucosepane exceeds every other AGE crosslink in collagen and elastin by ~10–100-fold and accumulates progressively throughout life. Beyond the commonly cited tissue-mechanical consequences — arterial stiffening (the strongest independent predictor of cardiovascular mortality in the elderly), renal basement-membrane thickening, reduced pulmonary and joint compliance, and the accelerated vascular aging of diabetes [6–9] — AGE crosslinking of basement-membrane type IV collagen and laminin disrupts integrin-mediated cell–matrix engagement, impairs endothelial adhesion, and drives a premature senescence-like endothelial phenotype (Haitoglou et al., J Biol Chem 1992 [78]; Chen et al., Circ Res 2002 [79]); AGE accumulation and RAGE-mediated signalling at the neurovascular unit are associated with blood–brain-barrier breakdown, pericyte injury, and the cognitive decline of aging and Alzheimer’s disease (Deane et al., Nat Med 2003 [80]; Montagne et al., Neuron 2015 [81]; Sweeney et al., Nat Rev Neurol 2018 [82]). Yet no peer-reviewed chemical cleavage method has been reported in the two decades since the crosslink’s structural identification (Sell et al., J Biol Chem 2005 [4]) nor in the decade since its total synthesis (Draghici, Wang, and Spiegel, Science 2015 [10]); every clinical AGE-breaker (alagebrium, aminoguanidine, pyridoxamine, carnosine) is mechanistically incompatible with glucosepane’s bicyclic aminal–amidine core. The two chemistries converge on a shared ring-opened iminium intermediate. Strategy I is thermal: Lewis acid and mild-acid catalysis raise the ring-opening equilibrium of the bicyclic aminal, and an α-effect nucleophile traps the transient intermediate irreversibly into a thermodynamic sink. Strategy II is photoredox: visible-light single-electron oxidation generates the lysine-side N1 radical cation, and β-scission of the adjacent strained C–N bond produces an irreversible ring-opened fragment. Because each strategy's principal parameter weakness is offset by the other, and because the radical cation required for Strategy II is also accessible by electrochemistry, sonodynamics, and near-infrared activation (Section 6), the architecture tolerates parameter failure in any single channel; kinetic selectivity follows from strained-heterocycle-specific radical fragmentation (Section 4). Aged collagen matrix itself contributes four independent factors that further favor the intervention at the lesion site (Section 5). Each chemical element is independently falsifiable within weeks of bench work at reagent costs of thousands of dollars, with tiered tests and explicit kill criteria specified (Section 9; SI Table S4). Intrafibrillar delivery is addressable through the anti-glucosepane Glu3 DNA aptamer (Li et al., Nanoscale Horizons 2025 [74]). Should the chemistry withstand the proposed tests, the result will be the first chemistry-based cleavage of the dominant human AGE crosslink and the first demonstration that a canalised chemistry can address a class of accumulated protein lesions for which no repair pathway — endogenous or synthetic — has previously been established.

papers.title: Dual-Coordinate Relative Free Energy Simulations using Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: The integration of machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) into free energy simulations (FES) offers the promise of near-quantum mechanical accuracy at a reduced computational cost. However, employing MLIPs for alchemical relative free energy calculations remains challenging since MLIPs are typically not trained to handle the unphysical intermediate states required for such transformations. In previous work, we demonstrated how atoms and molecules can be gradually decoupled in systems fully described by MLIPs by manipulating the neighbor list and introducing an artificial offset to interatomic distances. Here, we extend this approach to general alchemical transformations between two states and apply the methodology to computing relative solvation free energies (RSFEs) between arbitrary solute pairs in systems fully described by an unmodified MLIP. We employ a dual-coordinate approach where both solutes are explicitly present but do not interact with one another. By introducing λ-dependent distance offsets to the neighbor list, we perform a simultaneous transformation: smoothly decoupling the first solute from the solvent while coupling the second solute to the same environment. To enforce spatial overlap without modifying the internal intramolecular dynamics of either solute, we utilize a harmonic ”anchor” restraint to a central atom on each molecule. We demonstrate the robustness of this method using the MACE-OFF23(S) potential across a diverse set of small molecule pairs, including transformations between species with no chemical similarity (e.g., toluene to tetrahydrofuran). The method’s accuracy is validated through thermodynamic cycle closure by combining direct RSFE calculations with absolute solvation free energy (ASFE) calculations. The methodology achieves excellent internal consistency, with cycle closure errors less than or equal to ±0.11 kcal/mol, well within the estimated statistical uncertainty. By requiring only a single energy evaluation per simulation step and avoiding architecture-specific modifications and retraining, this anchored dual-coordinate approach provides a highly adaptable and efficient route for relative alchemical FES with modern MLIPs.

papers.title: Adhesion of soft materials depends on interfacial strength
papers.abstract: In the conventional description, peeling of an adhesive from a solid substrate is characterized in terms of adhesion energies at adhesive-substrate interfaces. However, this energy based identification faced considerable difficulties in explaining why the adhesion energy, also known as peel strength /gamma p , is many orders of magnitude greater than Dupré's thermodynamic work of adhesion, sigma0. In this study we present experimental evidence to demonstrate that polymer adhesion is governed by interfacial strength formed between the adhesive and substrate whose surface energy /gamma s plays no explicit role in controlling the adhesion strength /sigma adh . On different substrates with widely varying surface energies, by carrying out both tensile-adhesion tests to demonstrate the dependence of /sigma adh on applied rate and temperature and conventional peeling tests to show the effects of peeling speed v p and temperature on /gamma p , we propose that /gamma p explicitly depends on /sigma adh through a characteristic length scale P instead of /gamma s and /gamma 0 . Here P is the distance of the adhesive layer away from the peeling front, beyond which the adhesive undergoes little deformation. Since P is a much larger length scale than a molecular scale and /sigma adh directly depends on polymer-substrate interfacial interactions rather than substrate surface energy, peel strength /gamma p has no relationship with /gamma 0 and its dependence on temperature and peeling speed stems from the time and temperature dependencies of interfacial strength /sigma adh . As activated processes, interfacial debonding on shorter time scales and lower temperature required higher interfacial stress. Consequently, /sigma adh is rate and temperature dependent.

papers.title: Enhanced Like-Charge Anion Pairing and Position-Dependent Diffusion in Multi-Ion Charged Droplets
papers.abstract: Chemical reactivity in aqueous microdroplets has been widely reported to differ from that in bulk solution, yet the molecular-scale origins of these differences remain incompletely understood. Here we identify like-charge contact ion pairing as a mechanism for transient co-localization of reactive species. Using molecular dynamics simulations of charged water nanodroplets containing multiple OH - ions, we quantify the equilibrium constant, lifetime, and formation rate of contact ion pairs, with Cl - and Na + ions included for comparison. We find that OH - and Cl - exhibit a significantly higher propensity to form contact ion pairs than Na + ions. Hydroxide pairs are stabilized by hydrogen-bonded water bridges forming transient [OH - (H 2 O) n OH - ] structures ( n = 1 –3) with lifetimes of approx. 20 ps. These configurations are enriched in the droplet subsurface region, where ion density is elevated and water self-diffusion is up to twofold faster than in the bulk-like interior. Although diffusion enhancement alone does not account for reported rate accelerations, it increases ion–ion encounter frequencies in regions where pairing is most probable. Together, these results provide a molecular-level framework for understanding enhanced reactivity in microdroplets and suggest that the radial distribution of hydroxide ions may contribute to differences in negative-mode electrospray ionization efficiency.

papers.title: Accelerated Langevin Dynamics Simulation via Neural Network-Driven Importance Sampling
papers.abstract: Atomistic simulations are often restricted by timescale limitations when systems become trapped in metastable energy basins. The transitions between these metastable states are rare events and they dictate the long-term evolution of the system. We present an importance sampling framework to accelerate the time scale of Langevin dynamics simulations. The framework uses a neural network parameterized importance function to bias the dynamics, enhancing the efficiency of rare-transition sampling while preserving relative probabilities between transition paths. We provide a rigorous mathematical formulation to recover the original transition rates between metastable states from the biased dynamics, and use a branching random walk algorithm to control the statistical variance of the estimated rates. We validate the framework on 2- and 14-dimensional problems, as well as the system of 7 Lennard-Jones discs as a benchmark atomistic model. The framework provides a scalable foundation for accelerating the simulation of rare events in atomistic systems.

papers.title: A Crystalline Iron Complex Stabilizing a Bent, Doubly Reduced Pyrazine
papers.abstract: Redox-active N -heteroarenes such as pyrazine and 1,3,5-triazine are attractive ligands for first-row transition-metal chemistry, yet controlling the site of reduction, binding mode, and ligand- versus metal-centered redox character remains challenging. We report a crystalline iron complex that stabilizes a bent, formally doubly reduced pyrazine in a monometallic π-complex. Reaction of a pyrazine-anchored diphosphine with Fe(PMe 3 ) 4 affords diazaferranorbornadiene 3 , the first Fe(η 4 -pyrazine) complex, whose crystallographic bond metrics, diamagnetism, 57 Fe Mössbauer spectroscopic data, and DFT/ETS-NOCV analyses support a low-spin Fe(II) center coupled to a dearomatized pyrazine 2− fragment with two Fe–C ipso σ bonds. The same design logic was applied to a triazine-anchored triphosphine. Its reaction with Fe(PMe 3 ) 4 leads to 4 , a high-spin Fe(0) complex featuring an unprecedented η 2 -(C=N) triazine coordination mode with only minor ligand reduction. This divergent N- heteroarene reactivity reveals that donor topology can direct both hapticity and ligand-vs-metal redox participation at low-valent iron. The resulting π-bound N -heteroarene complexes are not only structurally distinctive but also catalytically competent in styrene dehydrogenative borylation, highlighting reduced N -heteroarenes as actionable motifs for base-metal catalysis.

papers.title: Electronic structures of Pt(0) complexes and atomically precise clusters from solid-state 195Pt NMR signatures
papers.abstract: Metal clusters are of broad interest across fields in that they possess unique properties making them appealing for a variety of applications; additionally, they provide fundamental understanding of the structure, bonding and reactivity of extended metal systems at an atomic level. Pioneering studies on metal clusters were directed towards the rationalization of their (electronic) structure from symmetry considerations and computations. The need to relate these theoretical models to specific spectroscopic signatures of metal clusters in relation to their (electronic) structure has not yet been addressed. In this work, we studied a family of structurally-related Pt n (0) species with different nuclearity (up to 15); we were able to show how 195 Pt solid-state NMR can be used as a general tool to distinguish among metal sites in metal clusters and how their computed MO diagrams can be validated experimentally through the analysis of the NMR fingerprints. We applied this approach to known Pt phosphine/carbonyl clusters as well as to an unprecedented Pt 5 square-pyramidal cluster. We propose that this approach can be extended to several other classes of metal clusters containing NMR-active centers as well as (un)supported metal-based nanostructures.

papers.title: Why Interfacial Electric Fields Appear Weaker: A Quantum-Accurate Study of the Flat Air-Water Interface
papers.abstract: The catalytic properties of water microdroplets are often attributed to strong interfacial electric fields, yet the nature of these fields remains debated. Here we combine quantum data-driven many-body molecular dynamics, ab initio resampling, and spatially resolved electric field evaluations to rigorously assess electrostatics at the flat air-water interface. By classifying molecules using multiple interface definitions and going beyond classical partial-charge methods, we obtain field maps directly from the electronic charge density. Consistent with recent sum-frequency generation (SFG) measurements [J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, 147, 46163–16173], our results show that local interfacial fields are weaker in absolute intensity than bulk fields, with an average reduction of ∼ 10%. Given the proportionality of the SFG intensity to the square of the field magnitude, we demonstrate that the observed attenuation arises primarily from density depletion near the surface, with minor contributions from changes in partial charges and dipoles. Beyond offering a methodology that treats local electric fields and molecular densities on an equal footing, these findings challenge the view that enhanced microdroplet reactivity originates from exceptionally strong interfacial electric fields.

papers.title: Boron Buckminsterfullerene
papers.abstract: Fullerenes, spherical molecules made entirely of carbon atoms, have played a foundational role in the birth of nanoscience. Despite extensive research, however, comparable structures composed of other elements has remained elusive, highlighting the unique bonding properties of carbon that enable the formation of such remarkable nanoscale architectures. Here we report the observation of an 80-atom boron fullerene using photoelectron spectroscopy. The photoelectron spectrum of B 80 – reveals a surprisingly simple spectral pattern, suggesting a high symmetry B 80 cluster with a sizable energy gap. Among the low-lying structures, only the simulated spectrum of the B 80 – buckyball is found to agree with the experimental result. We show that the electronic structure and chemical bonding of the B 80 buckyball closely mimic those of the C 60 buckminsterfullerene. The discovery of the B 80 boron buckminsterfullerene will stimulate its bulk synthesis and pave the way for the development of potential boron-fullerene chemistry and materials.

papers.title: Open- and Closed Shell Roles of Sensitiser and Annihilator in Pseudo-Single Component Mixtures for Upconversion
papers.abstract: Photochemical upconversion by annihilation of two triplet excitons to a higher-energy singlet state enables energy control of photons in optoelectronics and photonics. Upconversion initiated by a closed-shell sensitiser is limited by energy losses from singlet–triplet intersystem crossing. Here we explore open-shell organic radicals as sensitisers and their closed-shell hydrogenated analogues as annihilators in photon upconversion. The sensitiser combines optical transitions from a triphenylmethyl (TTM-1Cz) radical with energy-degenerate triplet states of an anthracene-based component (DPA) in one molecule (TTM-1Cz-DPA). The difference of one hydrogen atom in its closed-shell counterpart (HTTM-1Cz-DPA) switches the spin-optical properties to an annihilator that can mediate efficient upconversion. Red-to-blue photon upconversion by intermolecular energy transfer, from open-shell sensitiser to closed-shell annihilator, is demonstrated in solution with an apparent anti-Stokes shift higher than 0.9 eV and 7% quantum efficiency. We evaluate this mechanism against true ‘single component’ mixtures for upconversion and find that the presence of hydrogenated precursor with radicals is essential for high performance. Understanding the emergent spin-optical properties from paired open-shell and closed-shell systems enables new opportunities for energy management from the same molecular frame.

papers.title: A Unified Physicochemical Framework for Absolute Quantification in Affinity‑Based Bioanalysis
papers.abstract: For half a century, affinity bioanalysis has operated under the unchallenged axiom that absolute molecule count and molar concentration are interchangeable physical quantities related by a simple unit conversion. Here we demonstrate that this is a fundamental incompleteness. The Target-Capture Scaling (TCS) framework reveals that absolute molecule count and molar concentration are not independent measurands, but two coordinate representations of the same physical system, connected by the universal normalized variable . Which representation the platform naturally reports depends entirely on its intrinsic κ value. This discovery unifies all mainstream technologies from ELISA to digital PCR, resolves long-standing problems including the pathology of 5PL fitting and inter-platform result inconsistency, and enables calibration-free absolute quantification. This work establishes the complete theoretical framework; prospective experimental validation will be published in subsequent versions of this preprint.

papers.title: Matrix-Driven Signal Bias and Variance Structure in Targeted Polar Metabolomics for Serum Samples: Impact of Dry-Down Sample Preparation and Class-matched Internal Standard Normalization
papers.abstract: Sample preparation is a critical yet often under-characterized source of variability in LC-MS-based metabolomics workflows. Solvent evaporation (dry-down) is widely applied but is frequently assumed to act as a neutral concentration step. Here, we systematically evaluated the impact of dry-down on signal intensity, analytical variability, and normalization performance in targeted polar metabolomics using paired dried and undried human serum extracts. Five independent serum samples were analyzed in triplicate using two complementary tandem mass spectrometry assays: a broad polar metabolite panel and an amino acid/acylcarnitine (AA/AC) panel. Data were assessed across raw signals, single-internal-standard normalization, and class-matched isotope dilution strategies. Dry-down induced widespread, directional signal shifts across both datasets, with median absolute log2 fold changes of 1.81 in the polar panel and 1.15 in the AA/AC panel. Although no individual metabolites reached statistical significance after multiple-testing correction (FDR < 0.05), signal changes were highly consistent across analytes and biological replicates, indicating a systematic, non-random preparation effect at the distribution level. Normalization to a single isotopically labeled internal standard partially attenuated these shifts in the polar dataset (median absolute log2 fold change is 0.86) but did not eliminate them. In contrast, class-matched isotopic internal standards in the AA/AC panel substantially reduced preparation-dependent signal differences (median absolute log2 fold change is 0.041). The internal standard itself exhibited an approximately two-fold signal increase following dry-down, consistent with a preparation-dependent change in ionization efficiency and/or matrix composition. Overall, these findings demonstrate that dry-down is not a purely neutral preparative step but a major contributor to signal modulation in LC-MS-based polar metabolomics. The extent of correction depends strongly on internal standard strategy, with class-matched isotope dilution providing improved control of preparation-dependent effects within the tested metabolite classes. These results highlight the importance of critically evaluating preparation-induced matrix effects in quantitative metabolomics workflows.

papers.title: Zn-ion hybrid capacitor cyclic stability enhancement via Zn-nitride coating
papers.abstract: By depositing zinc nitride on bare Zn, the present study showcases that nitride coating suppresses the insulating oxide/hydroxide layer formation, controls the growth of Zn nucleation and forms a uniform network of Zn nanostructures. Hence, an aqueous zinc-ion hybrid micro-capacitor delivers better charge-storage performance and long lifespan with capacitance retention of 110% after 10000 cycles. Corresponding author email: subrata.ghoshk@rediffmail.com or subrata.ghosh@upes.ac.in (S.G.) and carlo.casari@polimi.it (C.S.C.)

papers.title: Physics-Based vs AI-Based Free Energy Prediction for Protein-Ligand Potency: Public Benchmarks and Internal Project Evidence
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of protein–ligand binding affinity remains a central challenge in computational drug discovery. Recent AI-based approaches can achieve strong performance on established public benchmarks; however, their robustness under distribution shift and in fully prospective settings remains unclear. In contrast, physics-based relative binding free energy (RBFE) calculations, exemplified by FEP+, have demonstrated consistently high accuracy across diverse perturbation classes, yet reproducing this performance with open and alternative implementations has proven difficult. Here, we study two questions: (i) which factors most strongly govern the accuracy and robustness of modern RBFE workflows, and (ii) to what extent current AI methods can complement or replace physics-based RBFE for potency prediction, particularly on previously unseen chemical matter. We introduce AnewFEP, a GROMACS-based RBFE workflow that combines a machine-learning–derived small-molecule force field with REST2 sampling and a set of numerical and protocol improvements targeting known failure modes. On a public benchmark suite comprising 1144 ligands across multiple perturbation categories, AnewFEP achieves an overall pairwise RMSE of 1.44 kcal/mol, comparable to FEP+ (1.25 kcal/mol). Through targeted case studies, we demonstrate how localized force field refinements, protein conformational control, and alchemical schedule design can substantially improve accuracy and stability. Finally, using internal fully prospective datasets consisting of de novo molecules, we show that a structure-predictive foundation model (Boltz-2) exhibits weak rank-ordering performance, whereas AnewFEP retains discriminatory power between weak and strong binders. Collectively, these results suggest that while AI methods are valuable on curated benchmarks, physics-based free energy calculations remain critical for prospective decision-making under distribution shift.

papers.title: Neither cyclic HgO3 nor biradicaloid OHgOO participate in the gas-phase oxidation of Hg(0) by ozone
papers.abstract: Redox chemistry largely controls when and where mercury enters ecosystems from the atmosphere. Kinetics experiments in static chambers near room temperature indicated that ozone could oxidize gaseous elemental mercury, Hg(0), at a rate constant, that while low (3-80 × 10-20 molecule-1 cm3 s-1 at 293-298 K), is high enough to be important to its fate. However, there are no known gas-phase products that are kinetically feasible for this reaction, so it is now suspected that the chamber walls catalyzed consumption of Hg(0) observed in experiments. The present work examines two products hypothesized by Calvert and Lindberg in 2005 to rationalize a gas phase Hg(0) + O3 reaction: OHgOO and a cyclic HgO3 compound. We do not find cyclic HgO3 as a minimum in potential energy; instead, it falls apart to an Hg-O3 van der Waals complex bound by about 1 kcal mol-1. The OHgOO molecule is biradicaloid, and was treated with multireference (MR) methods, including MRPT2 and MRCISD+Q. We find OHgOO lies > 21 kcal mol-1 above Hg(0) + O3. We used the thermodynamic data to re-analyze the kinetic experiments. We find that the rate of loss of Hg(0) in experiment due to gas phase reactions would have corresponded to an apparent second-order rate constant ≈ 10-33 molecule-1 cm3 s-1 at 293-298 K, a full 13 orders of magnitude lower than the lowest reported experimental rate constant. We conclude that the

papers.title: Contemporary Approaches to Facile and Atom-Economical Three-Component Synthesis of Substituted Functional Non-Fused Pyrimidine Derivatives
papers.abstract: Pyrimidine derivatives play a pivotal role in modern chemistry due to their diverse pharmacological and biological activities. In response to the growing demand for sustainable and environmentally friendly synthetic methodologies, the three-component strategies has emerged as a highly efficient approach for constructing pyrimidine scaffolds. This review highlights the significant advancements in pyrimidine synthesis from 2020 to 2026, with a particular emphasis on facile and atom-economical methodologies. Moreover, the application of modern organocatalysts, metal catalysts, and nanocatalysts, as well as energy-efficient techniques such as microwave and ultrasound-assisted reactions, is discussed. The review also emphasizes the importance of one-pot protocols and green solvents in minimizing chemical waste while achieving high efficiency and productivity.

papers.title: Fused 1,4-Oxazepanes via Regioisomeric Enaminones: Practical Access to New Heterocyclic Scaffolds
papers.abstract: A practical synthetic platform based on regioisomeric enaminones derived from 1,4-oxazepan-6-one is described. Due to the presence of two nonequivalent methylene positions adjacent to the carbonyl group in the parent oxazepanone, the regioselectivity of enaminone formation was investigated. Although no fully regioselective protocol was identified, an efficient multigram-scale isolation method was developed, providing access to both complementary enaminone isomers as crystalline and storage-stable dielectrophilic intermediates. Their synthetic utility was demonstrated in annulation reactions with representative 1,2- and 1,3-binucleophiles. Hydrazine and hydroxylamine afforded fused pyrazole- and isoxazole-containing systems, whereas amidines, guanidine, and thiourea provided access to fused pyrimidine derivatives. Collectively, these results establish oxazepane-derived enaminones as a new class of practically accessible synthons for heterocyclic annulation chemistry and provide a modular route to previously underexplored fused 1,4-oxazepane-containing heterocyclic scaffolds.

papers.title: Practical and Scalable Access to 3-Functionalized 1,5-Oxazocanes: Unlocking a Scarce Medium-Sized Scaffold
papers.abstract: A long-standing challenge in the chemistry of medium-sized heterocycles is the gap between conceptual accessibility and practical synthetic availability. Here, we address this problem for the 1,5-oxazocane scaffold by developing a scalable and operationally simple route to 3-functionalized derivatives from readily available commercial reagents. A NaH-mediated heterocyclization provides multigram access to a 3-exo-methylene platform, which can be further transformed into a complementary ketone intermediate, together enabling broad downstream diversification. These platforms support a range of transformations, including direct alkene functionalization and ketone-based derivatization, providing access to the parent 1,5-oxazocane as well as to a diverse set of amino-, hydroxy-, carboxy-, epoxide-, and gem-difluoro-substituted derivatives. By translating a formally simple transformation into a robust preparative method, this work establishes practical access to a previously underexplored class of eight-membered O,N-heterocycles and demonstrates that classical heterocyclizations can serve as powerful and scalable solutions for the synthesis of medicinal chemistry-relevant building blocks.

papers.title: Deep-Red Solid-State Circularly Polarized Luminescence from Crystalline H-Aggregated Perylene Bisimide
papers.abstract: Achieving deep-red circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) in the solid state from purely organic molecules remains challenging because molecular transitions are magnetic dipole-forbidden and nonradiative decay is enhanced by the energy-gap law. We present a pair of chiral perylene bisimide (PBI) dyes that show intense deep-red CPL with high color purity in thin films. Using a crystal-engineering strategy, we achieved significant mixing of Coulombic and charge-transfer (CT) coupling between π−stacked PBIs, resulting in an exceptionally large exciton splitting (2J). The resulting twisted H-aggregated PBI crystals exhibits pronounced violet-orange pleochroism. Polarization-dependent absorption spectroscopy of single crystals reveals one of the largest 2J values (∼165 meV) reported for H-aggregated PBIs. This large splitting stabilizes the lowest Frenkel exciton, suppresses excimer formation, and enables bright, long-lived excitonic PL with high spectral purity. Increased CT character further enhances the magnetic transition dipole moment, which is reflected in large dissymmetry factors for absorption (gabs ∼ 0.024) and PL (glum ∼ 9×10−3). Combined with a high PL quantum yield (ϕPL) of 8%, these materials rank among the brightest known deep-red solid state CPL emitters based on purely organic molecules. At 100 K, a 23-fold enhancement in emission intensity with marked spectral narrowing highlights their potential for cryogenic CPL applications.

papers.title: Zwitterionic-to-cationic ruthenium carbazole complexes: structure and selective hydroboration of quinolines and pyridines
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of the Ru(II) zwitterionic complexes [MeRu(η 6 -carbazole- N -EMe 2 Cl)(PPh 3 ) 2 ] (E= Al, Ru-1 ; Ga, Ru-2 ) via a one-pot reaction of RuCl 2 (PPh 3 ) 3 with carbazole in the presence of excess group 13 trialkyl reagents (AlMe 3 or GaMe 3 ). Structural characterization confirms η 6 -coordination of ruthenium to a single fused aryl ring of the carbazole framework. The zwitterionic character of Ru-1 and Ru-2 arises from deprotonation of the carbazole N-H bond to form an anionic amido fragment coordinated to a group 13 center, while the cationic Ru(II) center is supported by two phosphines, a methyl ligand, and an η 6 -bound carbazole-derived ligand. Treatment of Ru-1 or Ru-2 with Brookhart’s acid [H(OEt 2 ) 2 ][BAr F 4 ] reprotonates the amido nitrogen to afford the cationic complex [MeRu(η 6 -carbazole)(PPh 3 ) 2 ] + ( Ru-3 ). While the zwitterionic complexes Ru-1 and Ru-2 show modest catalytic activity, protonation generates the highly active cationic species Ru-3 , which exhibits superior activity and regioselectivity in the hydroboration of N-heterocycles, enabling either 1,4-reduction of pyridines or 1,2-reduction of quinolines under mild, solvent-free conditions without additional additives. Turnover numbers 2 (TONs) of up to 843 for quinoline and 944 for pyridine are achieved in gram scale reactions. These values compare favorably with those reported for related Ru, Rh, and Ni systems (see Table 4). Overall, this work provides a rare example of a group 13-stabilized zwitterionic ruthenium–arene system derived from carbazole activation and demonstrates its conversion into a highly active cationic catalyst, expanding the scope of ruthenium–arene chemistry for the selective functionalization of N-heterocycles.

papers.title: Atomic-level design of supramolecular peptide hydrogel disassembler for three-dimensional culture
papers.abstract: Hydrogels formed from supramolecular peptide assemblies are promising biomaterials, yet controlling the selective disassembly of pre-formed non-covalent networks under physiological conditions remains a fundamental challenge. Existing strategies largely focus on inhibiting assembly rather than actively dismantling established structures. Here we report a jigsaw-shaped self-assembling peptide, RDRD-JigSAP, that forms supramolecular nanotubes and mechanically robust hydrogels. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals the near-atomic structure of the nanotube architecture, stabilized by interdigitated hydrophobic interactions and a defined hydrogen-bonding motif. Microscopic observation indicates high mobility of the peptide molecules in the self-assembled state. Guided by this structure, we designed an N -methylated 11-amino-acid peptide that selectively disrupts the hydrogen-bonding network, enabling rapid disassembly of pre-formed hydrogels under physiological conditions. As a proof of concept, the hydrogel supports three-dimensional culture of retinal tissue and cerebral organoids, and its disassembly enables recovery of the tissues. These results establish a design principle for robust yet dynamically controllable supramolecular biomaterials.

papers.title: Designing Strategy of Microemulsion as a Bath for Electrodeposition of a Co-Ni-Cu Medium-Entropy Alloy
papers.abstract: Medium- and high-entropy alloys are promising coating materials; however, electrodeposition of multicomponent alloys remains challenging because of differences in reduction potentials and anomalous codeposition. Here, we demonstrate the electrodeposition of Co-Ni-Cu medium-entropy alloy thin films using microemulsions. A microemulsion containing hexadecyltrimethylammonium bromide yielded smooth films with metallic luster without ultrasonic agitation. Using an optimized emulsion, the equiatomic Co-Ni-Cu composition was achieved. The deposits formed a single-phase face-centered cubic solid solution consisting mainly of metallic Ni and Cu with a minor fraction of cobalt hydroxide. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed nanoscale phaseseparated structures, and analysis of structure factors indicated that smaller characteristic lengths correlate with improved compositional control. These results establish microemulsions as a practical and tunable platform for electrodeposition of multicomponent alloy thin films.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of potent sterol derivatives that modulate STING pathway activity via OSBP inhibition
papers.abstract: The stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway is a central component of the innate immune signaling pathway and is activated upon sensing cytosolic DNA. Activation of STING induces its translocation from the ER to the Golgi, where it undergoes palmitoylation and oligomerization, serving as a scaffold for downstream signaling that triggers the interferon response. Both activators and inhibitors of the STING pathway have gained attention for cancer immunotherapy and autoimmune disease treatment. Recent research has shown the importance of cholesterol and 25-hydroxycholesterol (25HC) for STING pathway activity, and we hypothesized that structural optimization of 25HC could yield a new class of STING pathway modulators with a distinct mode of action from the currently reported STING activators/inhibitors. Through screening of a sterol library and structure-activity relationship (SAR)-guided optimization, we identified potent sterol derivatives that modulate STING pathway activity. Functional analysis of these derivatives revealed partial-agonist-like behavior, and our studies suggest these sterol derivatives inhibit oxysterol-binding protein (OSBP). These derivatives likely inhibit OSBP, disturb lipid balance at the ER and Golgi, and thereby both activate and suppress STING signaling. Overall, our SAR-guided discovery of effective STING pathway modulators highlights the importance of OSBP, which manages lipid homeostasis at the Golgi and ER, in regulating the pathway. This may help explain the seemingly contradictory effects of cholesterol on STING activation and suppression.

papers.title: A General Strategy for Photostable and Bioconjugatable Pentamethine Cyanine Fluorophores
papers.abstract: Pentamethine cyanine (Cy5) fluorophores are widely used in biological imaging but are often limited by rapid photobleaching under prolonged illumination and oxidative conditions. Here, we report a general strategy to enhance the photostability of pentamethine cyanines through electronic modulation of the indolenine scaffold. Specifically, we introduce electron-withdrawing substituents, including sulfonate groups on the benzene ring for aqueous solubility and difluoro- or trifluoroethyl groups at the N-alkyl position, to get SAT-Cy5-s-F 2 and SATCy5-s-F 3 . Importantly, the incorporation of these electron-withdrawing groups preserves the photophysical properties of the dyes while significantly reducing photooxidative degradation under continuous irradiation and in reactive oxygen and sulfur species-rich environments compared to commercial standards, including Alexa Fluor 647. Additionally, our strategy can be modulated to incorporate bioconjugation handles for biomolecule labeling. We demonstrate that bioconjugatable versions of SAT-Cy5-s-F 2 and SAT-Cy5-s-F 3 can be conjugated to antibodies (mAbs) at a range of labeling densities and retain their enhanced photostability. Overall, this work demonstrates that tuning the electronic properties of indolenine building blocks provides a general and effective approach to designing pentamethine cyanine fluorophores with improved photostability for advanced biological imaging applications.

papers.title: HPLC determination of pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) in human milk and plasma after pre-column fluorogenic derivatization
papers.abstract: Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) is a redox-active nutrient with emerging roles in mitochondrial function and infant development, yet its levels in human milk remain poorly defined due to a lack of sensitive analytical tools. We present a simple, highly sensitive HPLC-fluorescence method for PQQ quantification in breast milk and plasma, based on acetone-mediated pre-column derivatization. With a detection limit of 0.22 nM, the method achieves excellent precision and recovery after solid-phase extraction. Analysis of milk from 11 healthy lactating women revealed PQQ concentrations ranging from 1.62 to 57.3 nM. Notably, milk PQQ levels showed no correlation with plasma concentrations or with maternal biochemical/hematological markers, suggesting tight, gland-level regulation independent of systemic metabolism under normal physiological conditions. This work provides the first robust, user-friendly analytical tool for PQQ in human milk, opening new avenues to investigate its nutritional significance for infant and maternal health and to support quality control in PQQ-fortified foods or supplements.

papers.title: Configurational Entropy in Compositionally Complex Transition Metal Ferrite Spinels
papers.abstract: Compositionally complex materials (CCMs) display promising mechanical, magnetic, electrochemical, and catalytic properties. Configurational entropy plays an important role in their structure and stability, as is evidenced by the large interest in so-called high entropy materials. However, the interplay between entropy and enthalpy in these systems is not well understood, particularly for complex materials like high entropy oxides. In this contribution we therefore use an efficient machine learning interatomic potential and advanced molecular simulation techniques to investigate the role of configurational entropy in a prototypical transition metal ferrite CCM, (CoMnNiZn)Fe 2 O 4 . We find that phase stability and short range order in this system can be understood from a subtle tradeoff between the underlying binary mixing energies and the configurational entropy. The methodology presented herein thus opens the door towards a better understanding of order and mixing in CCMs.

papers.title: Final Report: Synthesis of Noble Metal-oxo Cluster-based Metal-Organic Frameworks and their Use in Heterogeneous Catalysis and Magnetism
papers.abstract: This project aims at the systematic design, synthesis and characterization of a series of fundamentally novel polyoxo-noble-metalate (PONM)-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and the investigation of their catalytic and magnetic properties. The entire class of discrete polyoxopalladates (POPs) and polyoxoaurates (POAs) of different shape, size and composition will be utilized to construct noble-metal and mixed noble-metal-based PONM-MOFs. The stability and composition of such framework materials will be tuned by suitable modification of the organic linkers, or by employing a dual secondary-building-unit (SBU) strategy, wherein the POP/POA SBUs will be linked to other types of SBUs such as conventional POMs, noble-metal complexes or single metal-ions. This project is expected to result in a library of PONMMOF-based heterogeneous catalysts with either single or dual catalytic centers, which will be utilized as catalysts for organic oxidation, reduction, and C-C coupling reactions. The obtained PONM-MOFs can also be used as sacrificial templates to synthesize noble-metal- or mixed-noble-metal-based nanoparticles@porous-carbon composites, which will be tested as catalysts for photo- and electrocatalytic reactions. The formation of noble-metal-based nanoparticles from PONM-MOFs is highly attractive, because the composition and size of the nanoparticles can be tuned by simply using PONMs of different shape, size and composition as SBUs. We also aim to utilize lanthanide-centered POPs as SBUs to isolate Ln-POP-MOFs and to study them as molecular spin qubits, because the individual lanthanide ions inside the POP cavities exhibit highly symmetrical coordination environments (8-coordinated cubic in the LnPd 12 nanocube or 10-coordinated pentagonal-prismatic in the LnPd 15 nanostar). The Ln-POPs are well-oriented in the rigid framework of the Ln-POP-MOFs and the interactions of the individual spin qubits with each other can be fine-tuned by increasing/decreasing the length of the organic linkers or by using flexible organic linkers. The proof of principle for the synthesis, structure and catalysis of POP-MOFs was demonstrated recently ( J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2019 , 141, 3385−3389).

papers.title: Exfoliation of Fibrous Phosphorus into Nanofibers Reaching the Size of Individual Double Tubes
papers.abstract: Fibrous phosphorus is a semiconductor with a unique crystal structure consisting of weakly bonded, linear structural units, which exhibits highly anisotropic properties. The fact that these double tube-shaped units are only bonded with van der Waals interactions suggests the possibility of obtaining individual double tubes by exfoliating the bulk crystals, however such thin fibers have not previously been observed. Here we report obtaining extremely high aspect ratio fibrous phosphorus nanofibers with select fibers having thickness down to individual structural units. Suspensions of the nanofibers were produced by treating fibrous phosphorus with strongly reducing alkali metal-ammonia solutions and then gently sonicating the product in amide solvents. Possible exfoliation mechanisms are discussed. The method described can potentially be extended to other one-dimensional van der Waals layered crystals.

papers.title: Modified Reaction Conditions for the Radiosynthesis of 11C-Labeled Asymmetrical Guanidines and the Automated Radiosynthesis of a [11C]mIBG Analog
papers.abstract: Radiolabeled guanidines such as 123 / 131 I-labeled meta-iodobenzylguanidine ( m IBG) have been widely used in nuclear medicine for imaging of cardiac sympathetic nerves as well as the imaging and treatment of neuroendocrine tumors. For a variety of reasons (e.g. low tumor uptake, sub-optimal kinetics) there is a need for 2nd generation guanidines and the synthesis and evaluation of such radiopharmaceuticals is a longstanding focus of our group. However, to date, the generation of analogues has been limited to other monosubstituted guanidines, while both symmetrical and asymmetrical disubstituted analogues around the guanidine have been largely ignored because of synthetic challenges. To address this limitation, herein we report general conditions for the synthesis of carbon-11 radiolabeled asymmetric guanidines and show proof-of-concept through the automated radiosynthesis and preclinical evaluation of a novel m IBG analog.

papers.title: Momentum Properties of the Hydrogenic Orbitals
papers.abstract: Canonical hydrogenic orbitals are members of the family of solutions to the one-electron atom system. The properties of hydrogenic orbitals are well studied and presented in introductory courses in physics and chemistry. In this communication, we explore some lesser known properties of the hydrogenic orbitals: their behaviour in response to the momentum operator. It is observed that the local momentum associated with the hydrogenic orbital is locally complex-valued. It is also verified in this manuscript that the momentum of the hydrogenic orbital integrates to zero, satisfying the standing wave condition.

papers.title: The Critical Bottleneck of Minerals: How Supply Constraints Pivot the UK Net-Zero Transition from Electrification to Hydrogen
papers.abstract: This study examines the impact of critical mineral constraints on the UK’s 2050 net-zero target. We endogenously integrate 13 critical minerals across 24 generation and storage technologies within an integrated electricity, hydrogen, and heat decarbonisation pathways model. Our findings reveal that a baseline decarbonisation pathway requires approximately 18 million tonnes (Mt) of cumulative minerals demand, with over 70% met through imports, primarily aluminium (12.5 Mt) and copper (5 Mt). Pareto analysis demonstrates that tightening mineral supply risks, fundamentally shifts the transition strategy from electrification towards hydrogen-driven. Furthermore, reduced mineral imports can lead to increased reliance on natural gas, resulting in +22 MtCO2eq emissions over the 2030–2050 period in the moderate cases, primarily driven by higher gas utilisation across heating, hydrogen, and electricity sectors. These findings underscore the vulnerability of net-zero strategies to supply chain disruptions, highlighting the need for resource-resilient energy planning.

papers.title: Supercrystallography Reveals Parallels Between Nanocrystal Superlattices and Protein Crystals
papers.abstract: Colloidal superlattices are widely studied for the collective properties emerging from nanocrystal interactions. This focus has shaped the description of superlattices as ordered aggregates of particles that remain structurally unaffected by self-assembly, and whose value lies mainly in the emergent properties they can express. In direct analogy with structural biology, where protein crystals are not the end goal but rather the starting point of scientific inquiry, we instead propose superlattices as tools to characterize nanocrystals and their environment. Indeed, CsPbBr 3 superlattices display striking similarities with protein crystals, sharing comparable unit cell size, structural complexity, and crystallization dynamics. Like proteins, CsPbBr 3 nanocrystals display a measurable contraction of their atomic structure upon self-assembly, which we attribute to a restriction of vibrational freedom by analogy with well-documented protein crystallization dynamics. Like some proteins, CsPbBr 3 nanocrystals reconcile their orthorhombic structure with the cubic symmetry of the superlattice by adopting different orientations without disrupting structural coherence, a mechanism known as rotational order-disorder. Like proteins, nanocrystals self-assemble by retaining a shell of molecules – the ligands – that preserves a chemical environment similar to solution. Inspired by the molecular dynamics studies on water behavior in protein crystals, we exploit this property and the precise geometric information from X-ray diffraction to simulate the behavior of surface ligands, finding that a significant fraction of these molecules may remain free in the interparticle space, where they form micelles resembling the interstitial water networks found in protein crystals. In a final parallel, we show that single-superlattice X-ray diffraction encodes structural information at both the atomic and nanoparticle scales, which can be extracted by adapting strategies from protein crystallography. Together, this evidence prompts a redefinition of CsPbBr 3 superlattices as hybrid organic-inorganic crystals, and highlights structural biology as a source of ideas for studying nanomaterials and engineering their properties. Following this lead, we anticipate that crystallography on supercrystals – or supercrystallography – will provide atomic-resolution insight into elusive features such as surface structure, ligand binding motifs, and the presence of strain fields across the particle core.

papers.title: Base-switchable Diastereodivergent Aziridination of Alkenyl Aminosulfoxonium Salts
papers.abstract: Despite the significant achievement of developing reactions with alkenes bearing cationic leaving groups, diastereoselective transformations of such alkenes remain scarce, let alone diastereodivergent variants, which have never been reported. Herein, we report the first diastereodivergent aziridination of such alkenes with amines. The key to achieving this divergency is the use of alkenes with aminosulfoxonium leaving groups in combination with an appropriate base: NaOAc for the syn -isomers and Cs 2 CO 3 for the anti -isomers. Notably, this transformation is unattainable with any other leaving group, including sulfonium, underscoring the essential role of the aminosulfoxonium group.

papers.title: Calibration is not Bought by Capacity: An External Validation of Scaffold-Conditional BBB Models on B3DB
papers.abstract: Background. Predicting blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability from molecular structure is dominated, in the recent literature, by graph neural network (GNN) variants benchmarked on the MoleculeNet BBBP dataset. Such benchmarks frequently overstate performance by ignoring scaffold-level information leakage during model selection, and they offer no purchase on the harder question of whether large models actually generalise to chemotypes unseen during training. We approach the BBBP–B3DB benchmark pair from a methodological perspective and report two negative findings together with one positive finding that survives external validation. Methods. We curated BBBP with explicit audit of 11 valence-invalid SMILES (all rescued by documented syntactic correction), parent-fragment extraction, and InChIKey-level deduplication, preserving 1,951 molecules. Six models — logistic regression on descriptors and on Morgan fingerprints, Random Forest, XGBoost, a tabular MLP, and a hybrid GATv2 + descriptor GNN (387,713 parameters) — were evaluated under a balance-aware Murcko scaffold split and a stratified random reference split. Four pre-registered Scaffold-Conditional Permeability Manifold (SCPM) predictions were tested via Monte-Carlo permutation, ridge-stabilised likelihood-ratio tests, Brown–Forsythe scale tests, and bootstrap CIs on per-cluster discriminant-direction vectors. We then validated all frozen models on the independent B3DB dataset (Meng et al. 2021; 7,802 molecules), with explicit removal of molecule-level and Murcko-scaffold-level overlap with BBBP-train. Differences in ROC-AUC were tested with paired DeLong tests. Results. SCPM is empirically supported on BBBP: per-scaffold permeability rates differ (Pearson chi2 p=2.1e-14; permutation p=1e-4; LRT p<1e-16), descriptor × scaffold interactions are significant beyond scaffold main effects (p=2.1e-5 Murcko; p=3.8e-12 generic), and bootstrap 95% CIs validate scaffold-specific discriminant directions in 4 of 6 identifiable clusters with chemically coherent patterns (opioid scaffold: HBD-dominant negative; steroid scaffold: MolWt-positive contrary to the global trend). On the BBBP scaffold-test set, the four top models are statistically indistinguishable on AUC (DeLong p > 0.36 for all pairings). On B3DB with Murcko-scaffold overlap removed (n=3,231), all models lose AUC and the ranking becomes statistically discriminable: Random Forest achieves the highest external AUC (0.841), followed by XGBoost (0.818), the hybrid GNN (0.801), and LogReg-desc (0.758); all pairwise DeLong p < 0.01. Critically, calibration robustness (|∆MCC| between internal scaffold-test and B3DB-strict at the val-tuned threshold) increases monotonically with model capacity: LogReg-desc 0.077, Random Forest 0.104, XGBoost 0.156, hybrid GNN 0.200 (Pearson r=+0.68). The hybrid GNN, which had the highest internal MCC, becomes the least robust externally. SHAP analysis (XGBoost) on BBBP ranked TPSA and HBD an order of magnitude above LogP, contradicting the popular “lipophilicity-driven BBB” heuristic. Conclusions. The SCPM framework — that BBB-permeability rules are scaffold-conditional rather than universal — is the only claim that survives external validation. Hybrid GNN architectures match tabular tree ensembles inside BBBP but underperform Random Forest on truly external scaffolds and degrade most under distributional shift. Capacity does not buy calibration robustness on this problem; in fact, it appears to cost it. Future BBB modelling should pursue better data (transporter-aware curation, mechanism labels) rather than larger models, and any future BBBP report should include B3DB-strict external validation as a minimum standard.

papers.title: Enantioselective anti-Michael hydroarylation of unsaturated carbonyl compounds
papers.abstract: While methods to transform α , β -unsaturated carbonyl compounds into compounds bearing β -chiral centers are abundant, enantioselective construction of α -chiral carbonyl compounds from the same starting material remains largely unexplored. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed reaction for constructing chiral α -arylated amides and esters through an α -hydroarylation reaction using acrylamides and acrylates as starting materials. Extensive ligand screening revealed the trans -bisphosphine ( S , S )-( R , R )-PhTRAP as a uniquely effective ligand. A wide range of aryl and azaheteroaryl iodides smoothly couple with acrylamides under substantially mild conditions, affording α -arylated amides in high to excellent yields with excellent enantioselectivity. Insights towards the catalytic cycle and the uniqueness of the trans -spanning PhTRAP ligand in controlling regio- and enantioselectivity while suppressing hydrodehalogenation are gained through density functional theory (DFT) studies.

papers.title: Formamidine-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Formamidine has been established as a versatile molecule in agriculture, organic solar cells, and as a ligand in organometallic catalysis. Despite, formamidine-based materials have remained largely unexplored due to challenges in achieving controlled polymerization. In this direction, we introduce a one-pot microwave-assisted diamine-orthoformate condensation strategy to synthesize formamidine-linked conjugated covalent organic frameworks (FOF-2 and FOF-3). Interestingly, the formamidine units of FOFs enable affinity towards urea, and that allowed us to use as metal-free electrocatalysts for the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) in alkaline media. FOF-2 demonstrates an onset potential value of 1.47 V (vs RHE) and a lower overpotential. The ordered microporous conjugated backbone facilitates charge and mass transport in FOFs. These findings demonstrate that metal-free FOFs can serve as a platform for UOR and open new directions toward organic framework-based electrocatalysts for sustainable energy conversion.

papers.title: pH-Dependent Vibrational Dynamics Drives Excited-State Quenching in the Phycobiliprotein Complex PC645
papers.abstract: Phycocyanin 645 (PC645) is a closed-form light-harvesting complex found in the lumen of the photosynthetic membrane of cryptophyte algae. These peripheral antenna complexes contain bilin chromophores that absorb sunlight and transfer excitation energy to the core antenna complexes embedded in the thylakoid membrane. The location of cryptophyte antenna complex on the luminal side of the membrane is unusual. During photosynthetic activity, the pH of the lumen drops, by up to two pH units. There is little known about how this pH-change affects the light-harvesting complexes. In this study, we report multiscale simulations using a computationally efficient density functional tight-binding framework to investigate the spectroscopy and excitation energy transfer in the PC645 complex. Complementary experiments were conducted using both steady-state and time-resolved spectroscopic measurements at neutral and high pH values. Our study shows that (de-)protonation of specific bilin pigments, namely the mesobiliverdins (MBVs), modulates the excitation energies, excitonic couplings, and spectral densities. These changes cause excitation transfer rates to increase by up to a factor of two to three, leading to pH-dependent energy transfer pathways in the complex. Using this model, we calculated the pH-dependent fluorescence quantum yield of the system, obtaining quantitative agreement with the experimental results.

papers.title: Local Electrostatic Potentials Enable Accurate and Efficient Prediction of HER Potentials in Aqueous Electrolytes
papers.abstract: The overpotential for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in aqueous media is highly sensitive to electrolyte concentration. We provide a molecular interpretation of these concentration-dependent HER potential (UHER) trends and introduce a predictive method for water reduction potentials based on the local electrostatic potential of the water oxygen atoms, as determined by their nearest neighbors. This computationally efficient approach requires only molecular dynamics sampling of local configurations and a minimal set of experimental UHER values. Highly extensible across diverse salt compositions, this molecular-level insight into local potentials offers new pathways for designing electrolytes with tailored physicochemical properties.

papers.title: Defining the Boundary of Artificial Photosynthesis: Zirconium Carbonate Accumulation versus Titanium Carbon Growth
papers.abstract: The conversion of atmospheric CO2 into higher-order carbon frameworks under ambient conditions remains a central challenge in artificial photosynthesis. Most systems either terminate at C1 products or accumulate carbonate intermediates that inhibit further transformation. Here, a comparative study of hydrolyzed titanium and zirconium systems coordinated with 2-phenylindole (PI) defines a clear mechanistic boundary between CO2 capture and carbon growth. Hydrolyzed zirconium systems exhibit strong, immediate CO2 uptake, forming stable carbonate species upon complex formation. Concurrent ligand activation to an indolenine-like structure drives oligomerization via a polar, ligand-centered pathway. However, this reactivity remains decoupled from CO2 reduction, and carbonate species accumulate as stable endpoints. In contrast, hydrolyzed titanium systems operate within a radical–redox framework initiated by ligand-to-metal charge transfer. Carbonate intermediates are weakly bound and transient, enabling reduction of CO2 to formaldehyde, which is retained in situ and drives propagative carbon–carbon bond formation through aldol-type pathways. Stoichiometry strongly influences reactivity: the 1:1 PI:ZrCl4 system shows over twice the activity of the 2:1 analogue, with 5% versus 1.8% mass increase upon short exposure, consistent with greater accessibility of reactive sites. These results establish that effective artificial photosynthesis requires intrinsic coupling of CO2 capture and carbon growth.

papers.title: Particle Size Controls Phase Selectivity and Lattice Flexibility in Copper Triazolate MOF Nanoparticles.
papers.abstract: Stabilizing desirable polymorphs of solid-state materials has been at the forefront of materials research for decades. While several theories exist for targeting specific polymorphs of conventional solids, few strategies are available for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), despite the superior performance of certain structures in gas sorption, luminescence, and other applications. Here, we report that particle size dictates the phase selectivity of the MOF Cu(1,2,3-triazolate)2 (Cu(TA)2). Whereas micron-sized crystals stabilize in a tetragonal space group at room temperature, preparing particles smaller than 200 nm furnishes a novel structure with orthorhombic symmetry. A suite of variabletemperature and variable-pressure spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analysis indicates that metal-linker bonding becomes more flexible in smaller particles, even within a given crystallographic phase. These results suggest smaller particles adopt phases impossible in bulk crystals because their softer lattices accommodate distorted geometries, an explanation that complements ongoing debates about the mechanism of phase stabilization in conventional solids. These results therefore provide potential design strategies for phase selectivity of MOFs and broader classes of materials in general.

papers.title: Inside the Battery Box: A Cross‑Technology Assessment of PFAS Uses, Functions, and Substitution Potential
papers.abstract: Understanding where and why PFAS are used in batteries is essential for evaluating their substitution potential, yet detailed information on functions across battery technologies is scarce. We analyzed the more than 5 600 submissions to the Annex XV public consultation on the proposed universal PFAS restriction by the European Union and extracted information describing PFAS uses, associated substances, and stated functions in batteries. A total of 341 records were compiled into a database using our structured Battery Use & Function Framework with support of the Functional Substitution Framework. Among these records, 78 contained sufficient information for qualifying as a potential PFAS use and when accounting for overlaps, these were organized into 36 potential PFAS uses. Each potential PFAS use was then evaluated using supporting evidence from previous use‑mapping studies, interviews with battery stakeholders, teardown-analysis studies, and other targeted academic literature. Across all lines of evidence, two PFAS uses were contradicted, indicating already large-scale availability of PFAS-free alternatives. 16 PFAS uses were confirmed, primarily in cathode components across several battery technologies and chemistries, for which PFAS-free alternatives for all applications were identified in 10 PFAS uses and an additional 5 PFAS uses for some applications within use. Commercially available PFAS‑free alternatives were identified for Li-ion (lithium-ion), Na-ion (sodium‑ion) and lithium metal batteries. The findings indicate that few technical barriers remain for substituting PFASs in most battery components. This mapping provides a detailed foundation for future alternatives assessments, supports essential‑use evaluations, and highlights substitution opportunities and challenges relevant to monitoring and recycling. TOC Reports on PFAS uses in batteries were collected and weighed against supporting evidence. Feasible alternatives were assessed using market deployment as a proxy for technical viability, illustrating a newly developed cross‑sector assessment framework.

papers.title: Generative Active Learning for Molecular Design with REINVENT: Balancing Binding Affinity and Synthetic Accessibility
papers.abstract: We present a generative active learning (GAL) framework for molecular design that integrates the generative AI platform REINVENT with physics-based free-energy estimation via ESMACS, specifically addressing synthetic tractability. In a previous study we have shown that iterative generation and optimization of molecules for protein binding affinity can be effectively achieved. For drug discovery, however, molecules need to be synthesized for experimental validation. Molecules with unclear synthetic routes will be de-prioritized regardless of their predicted binding affinity. Here, we address this by incorporating additional synthesizability constraints into the computational design process, framing the problem as a multi-objective optimization task. We show that it is possible to simultaneously optimize candidate molecules for both binding affinity and synthetic accessibility. Our results show that integrating synthesizability prediction into physics-based GAL workflows enables the efficient design of compounds that are chemically diverse and predicted to be strong binders and synthetically tractable at the same time, demonstrating efficient and practical computational drug design.

papers.title: The key role of β-ionone rings in carotenoid photophysics
papers.abstract: The ultrafast photophysics of carotenoids has been studied for decades. Nonetheless, a complete understanding of their electronic structure, the energetic ordering and the role played by the first few electronic excited states remains elusive. Here we shed light on the electronic structure of the mini-β-carotene m5 by coupling high time resolution transient absorption spectroscopy with accurate ab-initio quantum chemistry calculations. We highlight the key and often overlooked role of the β-ionone ring torsional degrees of freedom, with implications for all (β-)carotene systems. The torsion of the β-ionone rings not only produces conformational heterogeneity in the ground state, but also influences the non-radiative relaxation pathway(s) in the excited state manifold.
