Explicitly accounting for such reaction coordinate allows us to decipher the ultrafast dynamics of the system and provides a consistent interpretation of its transient absorption spectra. Moving beyond traditional models focused solely on the polyene backbone, we eventually introduce a unified and predictive framework based on the role of this torsional coordinate in tuning carotenoid photophysics, within which both polyenes and carotenes naturally fit.

papers.title: 1 Directed evolution of a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase for improved perillyl alcohol biosynthesis via a tailored genetically encoded biosensor
papers.abstract: Perillyl alcohol is a naturally occurring terpene with promising anticancer properties. However, like other oxidized terpenes, its limited biosynthetic availability hinders its development as a therapeutic lead. Cytochrome P450 monooxygenase CYP153A6 catalyzes the key hydroxylation of limonene to yield perillyl alcohol in Escherichia coli, yet the enzyme is the ratelimiting step in this pathway and has not previously been improved by directed evolution. Here, we report the development of a genetically encoded biosensor based on the cymene repressor CymR from Pseudomonas putida F1, engineered to selectively detect perillyl alcohol over its non-hydroxylated precursor limonene, and its application to the directed evolution of CYP153A6. A single substitution (S77L) in the CymR effector-binding pocket dramatically increased biosensor sensitivity and dynamic range toward perillyl alcohol while maintaining discrimination against limonene. The tailored CymR-S77L biosensor was coupled to a CYP153A6 random mutant library to enable high-throughput fluorescence-based screening of variants. Ultimately, seven CYP153A6 variants with improved perillyl alcohol titers were identified. Deconvolution of beneficial mutations revealed that a single substitution, A287T, located near the predicted CYP153A6:ferredoxin reductase interface, was sufficient to increase perillyl alcohol productivity 4.2-fold relative to wild-type without compromising regio- or chemoselectivity. These results demonstrate that biosensor-guided directed evolution is an effective and selective strategy for engineering P450-dependent terpene hydroxylation pathways and establish a generalizable platform for developing monoterpene-responsive biosensors and applying them to the directed evolution of terpene-modifying enzymes.

papers.title: Iso 9-HODE and iso 13-HODE: Novel markers of oil refining
papers.abstract: Worldwide, more than 90% of vegetable oils are refined prior to consumption. Here, novel oxylipins iso 13-HODE (13-hydroxy-8 E ,10 Z -octadecadienoic acid) and iso 9-HODE (9-hydroxy-11 Z ,13 E -octadecadienoic acid) formed during the refining of vegetable oils are identified. The iso HODEs are formed during deodorization through heat-induced reaction by a thermally induced [1,5]-sigmatropic rearrangement of Z,E 13-HODE and E,Z 9-HODE. As demonstrated for 9 different batches of oil, industrial refining of sunflower oil increases the concentration of iso 13-HODE from 65 to 150 nmol/g (rapeseed oil from 5 to 26 nmol/g) upon deodorization, while iso 9-HODE increased from 14 to 65 nmol/g (rapeseed oil 2 to 11 nmol/g). Due to the degradation of the precursor the ratio of iso 13-HODE to Z,E 13-HODE and iso 9-HODE to E,Z 9-HODE is the more sensitive parameter increasing by 10-fold to up to 100-fold during deodorization. Notably, a significant increase of this parameter already occurred when oils are heated to 100 °C. Therefore we suggest iso 9-HODE and iso 13-HODE as new complementary authenticity markers for distinguishing heated from native oils, which warrant further investigation.

papers.title: 1 Capture-SELEX Derived Low Nanomolar Affinity Aptamers for Doxorubicin and Inhibition of Cell Uptake
papers.abstract: Anthracycline chemotherapeutics such as doxorubicin and daunorubicin remain indispensable in cancer treatment but are limited by narrow therapeutic windows, underscoring the need for reliable strategies for real-time drug monitoring and mitigation. Aptamers are attractive for continuous monitoring and therapeutic modulation due to their reversible binding, stability, and low cost; however, the strong nonspecific DNA intercalation of anthracyclines has historically complicated aptamer selection and validation. Here, we used capture-SELEX to obtain DNA aptamers for doxorubicin, yielding three distinct sequence families with well-defined secondary structures and low-nanomolar binding affinities. Using intrinsic fluorescence quenching, isothermal titration calorimetry, and NMR spectroscopy, we rigorously distinguish specific aptamer binding from nonspecific intercalation and demonstrate rapid, Mg2+-independent binding. The lead aptamers bind both doxorubicin and daunorubicin with nanomolar affinity and outperform previously reported immobilization-selected aptamers in affinity and structural clarity. Importantly, these aptamers significantly inhibit cellular uptake of doxorubicin in HeLa cells, highlighting their potential as functional antidotes in addition to sensing elements. We further compare these sequences with the previously reported doxorubicin aptamer and demonstrate improved affinity and structural clarity. This work provides a robust molecular platform for anthracycline monitoring, nanobiosensor development, and therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Interbase FRET Between Cytosine Analogues Reports Holliday Junction Topology, Dynamics, and Stability
papers.abstract: The Holliday junction (HJ) is a four-stranded DNA intermediate, central to homologous recombination and genome maintenance. Here, we demonstrate that the cytosine base analogues tC (1,3-diaza-2-oxophenothiazine; donor) and tCnitro (7-nitro-1,3-diaza-2oxophenothiazine; acceptor) constitute a minimally perturbing Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) pair for probing HJ topology and dynamics in solution. Among four donoracceptor HJ configurations designed, two yielded robust and reproducible FRET efficiencies suitable for high-throughput analysis. These constructs were then used to report open- and stacked-X conformational HJ transitions induced by Mg2+ ions and HJ-binding peptides.

papers.title: Binding Affinity Determines the Success of Endogenous CuII–NTA Spin Labelling for In-Cell EPR Distance Measurements
papers.abstract: In-cell electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy requires robust spin-labelling strategies compatible with cellular conditions. Cu II -NTA coordination to genetically engineered double-histidine (dHis) motifs has shown promise for endogenous labelling in E. coli . Here, we evaluated the effect of varying Cu II -NTA affinity on the success of these experiments. Relaxation induced dipolar modulation enhancement (RIDME)-based titrations revealed dissociation constants ( K d ) in the 10 -6 and 10 -8 range for two different β-sheet i and i+2 dHis sites. In-cell EPR spectra demonstrated that the persistence of the Cu II EPR signal correlates with these binding affinities. The success of in-cell pulsed electron-electron double resonance (PELDOR) involving both β-sheet sites and a high-affinity α-helical site depended on the site; the higher-affinity site yielded analyzable results, the lower-affinity site did not. These results highlight the critical importance of low K d binding sites for reliable in-cell distance measurements with endogenous Cu II -NTA labelling and the substantial sensitivity gain offered by RIDME experiments.

papers.title: Efficient templated synthesis of pillar[6]arenes by in situ generated Lewis adducts
papers.abstract: Pillar[6]arenes exhibit highly valuable host–guest properties owing to their larger cavity relative to the widely studied pillar[5]arenes, yet their broader utilization has been impeded by longstanding challenges in selective and reproducible synthesis. Here, we report a general and efficient templated macrocyclization strategy based on the in situ formation of the Lewis adduct DABCO·2BF3. The remarkable structural complementarity between this hexagonal template and the pillar[6]arene cavity, reinforced by strong CH–π interactions, drives highly selective formation of pillar[6]arenes under BF3·Et2O catalysis in common chlorinated solvents. Under optimized conditions, dodecaethoxy-pillar[6]arene P[6]OEt is obtained in up to 77% yield on gram scale, and the protocol can be readily scaled to multigram quantities without chromatography purification. The method is applicable to a range of monomers bearing saturated alkyl chains and provides straightforward access to the key precursor P[6]OH via dealkylation. Beyond its practical advantages, this work constitutes the first example of macrocyclization templated by a Lewis adduct. By overcoming critical limitations in selectivity, reproducibility, and scalability, this strategy offers an efficient solution for pillar[6]arene synthesis, opening new avenues for application developments.

papers.title: Role of molecular structure and stoichiometry in cocrystals involving halogen bonds to π-systems: an experimental and theoretical study
papers.abstract: Halogen bonding (XB) to aromatic π-systems (C−I···π XBs) is a versatile interaction that remains poorly understood and underexploited in materials design. This work provides a systematic experimental and theoretical study of the robustness and role of C−I···π halogen bonding in the formation of cocrystals. By using indene as a model π-based XB acceptor, this work outlines how introducing a heteroatom (O, N, S) into the arene structure influences the structures and compositions of resulting cocrystals. Systematic mechanochemical screening and single crystal X-ray structure analysis show that in all herein explored cases cocrystal formation leads to the appearance of C−I⋯π type XBs, even in the presence of potentially competing oxygen- or sulfur-atom single-site XB acceptors. Moreover, despite the diversity of herein explored acceptors, cocrystallization was found to lead to the formation of only a small set of three distinct types of halogenbonded architectures, herein termed the (1) one-dimensional chain, (2) ladder, and (3) sandwich herringbone, each involving C−I···π XBs. Combining both gas-phase and periodic density-functional theory calculations enabled a detailed analysis of how the stability of XBs to π-systems is affected by modification of the acceptor, and a possible thermodynamic rationale for the observed accessibility of structural types depending on acceptor choice. The observation that a given halogen bond acceptor can lead to several different types of halogen-bonded solid-state architectures, determined by the ratio of halogen bond donor and acceptor molecules in the cocrystal presents stoichiometry as an important and versatile element of design when developing solid-state materials involving C−I···π XBs.

papers.title: Can machine learning predict solvation effects on energies and geometries of highly charged molecules?
papers.abstract: Recent machine-learning models have shown that implicit solvation based on continuum solvation models can be learned efficiently with graph neural networks. However, previous studies have focused almost exclusively on neutral or only weakly charged molecules, leaving the strongly charged regime essentially unexplored. Here, we systematically investigate which model architectures and architectural components are required to predict solvation energies and corresponding forces for molecules with total charges ranging from −5 to +5. Using reference data generated from the conductor-like screening model for realistic solvation (COSMO-RS) for water, acetonitrile, and cyclohexane, we show that an explicit and robust treatment of molecular charge is essential for reliable performance across charge states. At the same time, highly charged systems prove easier to learn than neutral and singly charged ones, whose solvation energies depend more strongly on subtle structural effects.

papers.title: Understanding the Role of the Local Structure Optimization in Cu-Sbased Single-Atom Catalysts for Oxygen Electroreduction
Non-Native Thiol and Aniline Methylation, Including Enantioselective Dithiol Desymmetrization, by Multi-Component Cobamide-Dependent Methyltransferases Using Unactivated Methyl Donors
papers.abstract: Despite their potential synthetic utility, cobamide-dependent MTases are relatively underutilized for biocatalysis. We developed mixed MtaABC/MtgABC enzyme platforms capable of catalyzing methylation of non-native thiol and aniline substrates using unactivated methyl donors like methanol and glycine betaine. This approach allows highly enantioselective and site-selective methylation of aliphatic thiols with high turnover number (up to 6000), providing the first demonstration of enantioselective non-native catalysis by cobamide dependent enzymes. The MtaAC+MtgB system was subsequently engineered through site-directed mutagenesis, resulting in large enhancements in activity for the desymmetrization of non-native ester-containing prochiral thiols. These findings establish MTase complexes as a promising platform for non-native biocatalysis.

papers.title: Study of Repetition in a Chan-Evans-Lam Reaction Dataset using Bayesian Optimisation
papers.abstract: In organic synthesis, the Chan–Evans–Lam (CEL) reaction is a widely used coupling methodology for enabling carbon–heteroatom bond formation. The process incorporates mild reaction conditions, good scope, and is complementary to other (C-N bond forming) efforts. However, CEL processes are notoriously variable, making reproducibility problematic and the identification of optimal/robust conditions a persistent challenge. In recent years, data-driven and machine learning approaches have gained prominence as efficient tools for rapidly identifying optimal and consistent reaction conditions. Generating sufficient data for machinelearning model training typically requires high-throughput experimentation (HTE). Traditionally, in a HTE campaign involving the optimisation of a chemical reaction and the establishment of a substrate scope, each set of identical experimental conditions is run in triplicate. The ‘statistical need’ for the replication of, apparently identical, conditions has not been substantially investigated. Given the timedependent nature of these campaigns in industry, and the broader issues of reproducibility in synthesis, there is significant worth in the assessment of the value of repetition. Here, we present an offline simulation framework to investigate replication-aware Bayesian Optimisation of chemical reactions. Our approach employs a heteroscedastic Gaussian Process surrogate model, which has been trained on replicate-level observations, where each individual measurement serves as a separate training point with per-condition noise estimates derived from available replicates. We examine how a limited experimental budget can best be distributed between exploring new reaction conditions and repeating previously tested ones. As an offline benchmark, we use an open-source CEL HTE dataset (≈ 3, 600 unique conditions in triplicate), with two objectives: 1) yield of the desired product and 2) selectivity of the desired product relative to a side-product. Our results show that, for both objectives, no replication strategy provides a statistically significant improvement over pure exploration within the available budget. Pure exploration consistently ranks among the strongest strategies, while aggressive replication (mandatory triplication) is clearly detrimental. These findings challenge the default assumption that replication is necessary when optimising under noisy HTE conditions, with broad significance for HTE and traditional one-experiment-at-a-time campaigns in the pharmaceutical and chemical industries.

papers.title: Experimental Validation of Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Lithium-Ion Dynamics in Solid Electrolytes via 7Li NMR
papers.abstract: A significant step toward electrification is the adoption of more sustainable energy storage technologies such as batteries. Safer alternatives to conventional solution-state lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are solid-state batteries, which employ solid-state electrolytes (SSEs). These SSEs can exhibit lithium conductivities comparable to those of liquid electrolytes but are often discovered through experimental trial and error. Computational pipelines powered by universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) offer a cheaper and scalable route to screen large datasets of candidate SSEs. This recent class of models enables rapid materials exploration compared to traditional quantum chemistry methods and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). In this work, we assess the current capabilities of uMLIPs for solid-state lithium battery applications by systematically benchmarking their predictions against experimental solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) diffusion data and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. We considered twelve different Li-based compounds, five ordered electrolytes, three disordered electrolytes, and four cathodes. This study includes eighteen different uMLIPs categorized into four main families, CHGNet, M3GNet, MACE, and ORB. Our results demonstrate that model performance is strongly dependent on both the underlying architecture and the chemical system under investigation. MACE- and ORB-based models consistently achieve higher accuracy across structural, energetic, and diffusion-related properties. However, the reliability of lithium diffusion predictions remains system-dependent, highlighting current limitations in the transferability of uMLIPs for complex materials. These findings provide a critical assessment of the readiness of uMLIPs for integration into computational pipelines aimed at accelerating the discovery of next-generation solid-state battery materials.

papers.title: Zinc Redox Catalysis in the Photochemical Borylation of Fluorocarbons
papers.abstract: Zinc compounds are ubiquitous in synthesis and materials. They find applications as reagents, catalysts, porous materials and as metalloenzymes — all of which rely on the properties of redox stable and electrophilic zinc(II) centres. In this paper we report the first clear example of redox catalysis involving reversible changes between zinc(I) and zinc(II) oxidation states. Under photochemical conditions a zinc(I) compound was shown to react with fluoroarenes. Turnover was achieved through addition of a diborane reagent, resulting in a catalytic borylation of the C(sp2)–F bonds of fluoroarenes. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a key role of a zinc(II) boryl intermediate in the reductive step from zinc(II) to zinc(I). These findings were further exploited in a small array of photocatalytic approaches to the borylation and reductive coupling of C(sp3)–F, C(sp2)–O and C(sp3)–O bonds.

papers.title: Stereoselective Palladium-Catalyzed C(sp3)-H arylation of furanose carboxamides.
papers.abstract: We report the first stereoselective palladium-catalyzed C(sp3)–H arylation of furanose carboxamides at the C3 position, achieving 2,3-cis selectivity without pre-functionalization. Optimized conditions provide diverse arylated furanosides in yields up to 61%, and we established efficient protocols for removing the directing group and deprotecting benzyl groups. DFT calculations rationalize the stereochemical outcome, and this method enables access to suzetrigine analogs, expanding the synthetic toolkit for carbohydrate-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Identify Cryptic Binding Site with Mixed Solvent MD Simulation and SiteMap
papers.abstract: A comprehensive study was conducted to address the challenge of identifying cryptic binding sites in proteins, which are crucial for structure-based drug discovery but are often not apparent in apo protein structures. We developed and validated a novel "induce and identify" workflow that integrates mixed solvent molecular dynamics (MxMD) simulations with SiteMap. This approach leverages MxMD sampling of protein conformations to expose hidden pockets, which are then effectively identified and ranked by SiteMap. Using a challenging dataset of 65 cryptic binding sites, the developed workflow identified the cryptic binding site within the top 5 predictions in 78.5% of cases. We believe the proposed MxMD + SiteMap workflow offers a robust and valuable tool for early-phase drug discovery, enabling the exploration of a broader range of druggable targets by effectively inducing and identifying cryptic binding sites.

papers.title: Subcritical Hydrothermal Synthesis in a Water-Alcohol Co-solvent of Size-Controlled High-Entropy Spinel Oxide Nanoparticles as Oxygen Evolution Electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their unique electronic structure caused by the interactions of the multiple constituent metal elements. The particle size of the catalysts is one of important determining parameters of the catalysts’ OER activity. However, synthesizing size-controlled single-phase HEO nanoparticles (NPs) remain challenging issue. Herein, we report an alcohol-assisted subcritical hydrothermal synthesis strategy to synthesize spinel-based HEO NPs with average diameter of approx. 10 nm composed of five first transition metal elements. Mixing methanol to water as solvent reduces the bulk dielectric constant, decreasing precursor solubility and increasing the degree of supersaturation. This change of the property of the solvent induces simultaneous burst nucleation and suppresses Ostwald ripening, thereby preventing particle coarsening. The crystallite size was systematically tuned from 13.3 nm down to 7.5 nm while maintaining their compositions. The OER activity of the catalysts synthesized by different alcohol content was enhanced significantly by reducing the particle size, which causes an increase of the specific surface area of the catalysts. This work establishes a promising route for designing crystalized HEO NPs with high catalytic activity.

papers.title: Second-Order Jahn–Teller Distortions Induce Glass-like Thermal Conductivity in Sodium Halide Ionic Conductors
papers.abstract: Thermal transport in crystalline solids is typically governed by well-defined phonon propagation, yet an increasing number of ordered materials exhibit anomalous glass-like thermal conductivity whose microscopic origin remains unclear. Here, we show that second-order Jahn–Teller (SOJT) distortions provide a direct electronic structure mechanism for glass-like thermal transport in crystalline ionic conductors. By systematically investigating a series of sodium halides of chemical formula Na x MCl 6 (M=Ta, Nb, Y, Zr, Sb, In), we reveal a pronounced crossover from crystal-like to glasslike thermal conductivity that correlates with the degree of distortion of MCl 6 octahedra. Strong SOJT distortions in some d 0 systems (Ta, Nb) induce large anharmonicity and suppress particle-like phonon transport, leading to glass-like behavior, whereas symmetric environments in d 10 systems (In, Sb) preserve crystalline transport. We identify a bond distortion index as a simple and robust structural descriptor that quantitatively correlates with thermal conductivity across the series. By linking electronic structure, local geometry, and vibrational transport, this work establishes a chemically grounded framework to understand and predict thermal conductivity in complex ionic solids, and provides new design principles for thermally insulating crystalline materials.

papers.title: Regiocontrolled Minisci Alkylations Guided by Phosphonium Ions
papers.abstract: Significant improvements in the regioselectivity of Minisci alkylations have been enabled by adopting N-heteroaryl phosphonium salts as substrates for this textbook transformation. Minisci chemistry has been a workhorse synthetic protocol in industry and academia for decades since it generates more-complex N-heteroaryls such as pyridines by C–H alkylation of the latter species with abundant precursors like carboxylic acids. Its wide scope, robustness, and operational simplicity are also major advantages, but its regioselectivity is often poor and general solutions have been slow to emerge. This strategy draws on reliable regioselective methods to install phosphonium groups onto N-heteroarenes. We have demonstrated herein that C2-alkylation of easily accessible C4-PPh 3 +-containing pyridines and quinolines (and C4-alkylation of C2-PPh 3 +-containing quinolines) regiospecifically generates a range of alkylation patterns that have previously proven challenging for Minisci chemistry to access selectively – especially when using more-abundant alkyl sources. Moreover, the preliminary application of this strategy to further N-heteroarenes shows that sites less- or unreactive with alkyl radicals can be exclusively engaged by using the phosphonium group to block the preferred Minisci reaction site. Finally, after the alkylation, mild hydrolysis can tracelessly remove the PPh 3 + handle, or a suite of established substitutions can be used to enable regiospecific C–H/C–H difunctionalizations across the PPh 3 + installation/Minisci/PPh 3 + substitution sequence.

papers.title: CASCADE and MERIT — frameworks for extracting the directivity and causal architecture of structural covariation in molecular dynamics trajectories
papers.abstract: Biomolecular simulations record how multiple structural variables covary, but existing analytical methods quantify the strength of that covariation without resolving which variable drives which. Here we present CASCADE (Causal Architecture from Structural Covariance Analysis with Directed Edges) and MERIT (Molecular Event-Related Investigation of Transitions), two frameworks that extract the direction of causal influence from molecular dynamics trajectories. CASCADE uses Bayesian network inference with bootstrap stability assessment and a hierarchical mode that removes dominant environmental effects to reveal the internal causal architecture among structural variables. MERIT provides independent temporal validation through Granger causality, transfer entropy, and convergent cross mapping; the pattern of agreement across these three mathematically independent methods classifies the dynamical nature of each causal relationship, distinguishing linear from nonlinear causality in a way inaccessible to any single method. We validate both frameworks on synthetic benchmarks with known causal structure and apply them to membrane protein simulations, where lipid composition, membrane order, and protein conformation covary as a non-separable system that represents the most stringent test case for causal direction extraction. The frameworks reveal that membrane composition reverses the direction of structural influence between transmembrane and juxtamembrane domains of receptor tyrosine kinase dimers through a nonlinear mechanism, a directional property invisible to existing analytical approaches and reproduced across receptor families sharing less than 20% sequence identity.

papers.title: A gradient boosting-based machine learning model for the prediction of hardness of thermoplastic polymers
papers.abstract: Modern experimental techniques can measure the hardness of thin films and structural features on the nanometre scales. These techniques can be applied to many types of material, but as the hardness of the material decreases, more specialized and precise equipment is needed. For polymers, this analysis can be relatively expensive and time consuming, so here we demonstrate a gradient boosting based machine learning model that can provide a fast and reliable prediction of hardness of thermoplastic polymers. This model is based on the XGBoost algorithm and shows reasonably good performance with an R 2 value of 0.65 – 0.88. The features used in this study include experimental (mechanical and thermal properties) and molecular descriptors obtained using RDKit. The model is robust, with reasonable performance obtained when key experimental features are removed and/or when the selection of polymers is reduced. This suggests that this approach will be useful in “bottom-up” strategies for polymeric materials development.

papers.title: A Thiophilic Metal-Mediated Cysteine S-Detritylation Strategy: Enhancing Orthogonality in Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis
papers.abstract: The selective manipulation of cysteine residues in solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), beyond disulfide bridge formation, remains challenging, and an efficient approach for the removal of the widely used trityl (Trt) protecting group under solid-phase conditions is still lacking. To address this issue, herein, a thiophilic transition metal-mediated strategy for the selective S -detritylation of cysteine on resin was developed by modifying a threecomponent catalytic system originally conceived for solution synthesis. The systematic screening of copper, zinc, and silver salts led to the identification of Ag(CF 3 CO 2 ) and AgNO 3 as the most effective promoters of Trt removal. Reaction conditions were optimized to afford reproducible and efficient deprotection, and mechanistic insights were obtained through control experiments. The protocol proved compatible with common protecting groups and environmentally benign solvent systems. Finally, in situ thiol release enabled direct on-resin S -alkylation with a range of aliphatic substituents, including those bearing aromatic moieties, demonstrating the synthetic utility of the method at a new level of orthogonality for late-stage functionalization of cysteine containing resin-bound peptides.

papers.title: Design and synthesis of environmentally improved fluoroquinolones
papers.abstract: A significant challenge associated with antibiotics, and active pharmaceutical ingredients in general, is their intentional design for high stability, which promotes environmental persistence and contributes to the development of antibiotic resistance. Ciprofloxacin, a widely used fluoroquinolone, exemplifies this issue. Using the benign by design (BbD) approach, ciprofloxacin was redesigned into a (bio)degradable fluoroquinolone molecule, termed Cip-hemi. In this design, ciprofloxacin was modified by replacing the persistent cyclopropyl group at the N1 position with a tetrahydrofuran moiety, thereby creating a degradable linker. Herein, we report the development of an efficient and robust synthetic platform to access the Ciphemi scaffold, along with the preparation of a series of novel derivatives. These molecules are developed with a dual-purpose design: to restore high-level antibacterial action while ensuring rapid degradation in the aquatic environment. The optimized synthetic strategy minimizes the use of hazardous solvents and largely avoids labor-intensive purification by flash chromatography, providing a streamlined approach for the preparation of environmentally improved fluoroquinolones.

papers.title: Recent advances in distonic radical cation chemistry: Focus on α-ammonio radicals
papers.abstract: Distonic radical cations are underexplored class of reactive species in which the radical and cationic centers are spatially separated within the same molecule. Among them, the α-ammonio radical exhibits unique reactivity inaccessible to conventional neutral radicals. This short review summarizes the generation methods and characteristic reactivity patterns of α-ammonio radicals, tracing their historical development and highlighting recent advances. Selected state-of-the-art examples demonstrate that these distonic radical cations are promising next-generation intermediates offering access to transformations beyond the reach of classical radical chemistry.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Framework for Descriptor-Empowered Exploring High-Activity Co-Based Quaternary Molten Alloys Catalysts for Methane Pyrolysis
papers.abstract: Methane (CH 4 ) pyrolysis via molten media offers an attractive route to CO 2 ‑free hydrogen production with high‑value carbon as a co‑product. However, the rational design of multicomponent molten catalysts remains challenging due to the dynamic and disordered nature of active sites in the molten state. Here, we present a closed-loop framework that integrates potential catalyst exploration by descriptor data mining, CH 4 pyrolysis testing, and activity mechanism analysis to identify the high-activity catalysts for CH 4 pyrolysis. Using this approach, Bi 70 Ni 18 Cu 6 Co 6 is identified as a promising catalyst for the first time, with experimental validation demonstrating it can achieve 40.3% CH 4 conversion at a moderate 1000 °C with a relative low activation energy (197.3 kJ·mol -1 ), outperforming the same experimental conditions Bi 73 Ni 27 (33.3%) and Bi 76 Ni 18 Cu 6 (37.4%) molten medias. The enhancement stems from a synergistic multi‑solute effect that the co‑dissolution of Ni, Cu, and Co in the low‑surface‑tension Bi solvent increases the density of exposed active sites and promotes direct interaction with CH 4 molecules. In particular, the introducing Co downshift the LUMO energy level of CH 4 molecular orbital (~1.3 eV), facilitating charge antibonding occupation, weakening C–H bonds, thereby accelerating the CH 4 dissociation. These findings provide deep insights of Co-based multi-elementary molten catalysts and chart a clear path toward the rational design of high-performance multicomponent molten catalysts for CH 4 pyrolysis.

papers.title: Interpretable Metal-Chemistry and Minimal-Context Descriptors for MOF Water and Activation Stability: A Reproducible Benchmark of Descriptor Sufficiency, Split Sensitivity, and Screening Utility
papers.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely studied for gas storage, separations, catalysis, sensing, and electrochemical conversion, but these functions matter only if the framework survives activation and remains stable in water or humid environments. Yet MOF stability prediction still sits awkwardly between empirical chemical intuition and machine-learning models built from descriptors that are often difficult to interpret or reproduce. Here, we present a chemistry-led benchmark that tests how far stability prediction can be advanced using transparent descriptors, including metal identity, mixed-metal character, open-metal-site information, coarse topology, porosity, and compact thermophysical terms. Using two cleaned CoRE MOF-derived benchmark tables, the activation-stability resource (ASR, 1372 entries) and the framework-survival resource (FSR, 1192 entries), we model continuous solvent and water stability, include thermal stability as a supplementary regression task, and assess threshold-based screening at 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8. Random Forest models with the most complete descriptor regime perform best overall, with water stability consistently more predictable than solvent-removal stability. However, random splits are markedly more optimistic than grouped splits by metal family and topology, exposing a substantial interpolation–extrapolation gap. Overall, the results show that simple, chemically interpretable descriptors contain meaningful stability signal, but credible extrapolative claims require chemically aware validation.

papers.title: Modulating the reactivity of amine-based electrolytes for stable rechargeable magnesium batteries
papers.abstract: Despite their complementary advantages to lithium- and sodium-ion batteries, rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) still suffer from multiple limitations that impede their practical operation. Amine-based electrolytes have recently emerged as a promising approach to overcome the long-standing challenge of sluggish Mg 2+ ion transport at the metal interface; however, their high reactivity triggers continuous side reactions that undermine long-term stability. After screening a range of methoxyethylamine bidentate derivatives, we identify herein aminoacetaldehyde dimethyl acetal (ADMA)—functionalized with a methoxy substituent—as a single electrolyte solvent that achieves an optimal balance between interfacial ionic transport and (electro)chemical stability. These optimal properties are enabled by ADMA’s concerted modulation of electron donicity and steric hindrance. Consequently, the ADMA-based electrolyte delivers stable cycling for Mg||SS half-cells—even under an operating protocol incorporating intermittent rest periods—as well as for full-cells paired with Mo6S8 and tellurium cathodes. This study highlights that high-performance RMBs can be realized through the sophisticated molecular engineering of electrolyte solvents.

papers.title: Mining Organometallic Reaction Pathways from Supplementary Information at Scale
papers.abstract: Chemical reaction databases have become core scientific infrastructure. Most prominent reaction datasets focus on organic reactions, or only include reactants and products rather than full reaction pathways, leaving organometallic chemistry particularly underserved despite its centrality to catalysis. This gap limits the development of machine learning models for organometallic reactions and their applications in mechanism discovery, selectivity prediction, and catalyst design. This work introduces an open, reaction-centric resource derived from 163194 published articles with supplementary information files across 50+ journals from seven publishers through 2025 using the GoldDIGR (Gold-Data Integration for Generalized Reactions) workflow. Reported organometallic reactions are aggregated and reaction properties are extracted or recalculated, including reactant, product, and transition-state geometries, intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC) traces, reaction classes, and ligand/metal descriptors (coordination, valence-electron counts, bond orders). Bond–electron matrices enable electron-flow analyses along reaction coordinates, and these analyses are visualized as Sankey diagrams connecting local electron rearrangements to class-level patterns. The resulting corpus spans canonical classes, including oxidative addition, reductive elimination, migratory insertion, β-atom elimination, C–H activation, and transmetalation. This literature-wide view enables quantitative mechanistic analyses at scale. As a demonstration of the meta-analyses enabled by this broad-based data generation, we study the relationship between bond-breaking/forming events and transition states to investigate concerted versus sequential scenarios across organometallic chemistry. Class-specific timing asymmetries emerge, with reductive elimination and β-atom elimination events skewed pre-transition-state, oxidative addition and migratory insertion skewed toward post-transition-state, and transmetallation showing the broadest dispersion. By releasing both tooling and data, this work provides a foundation for mechanistic benchmarking and data-driven catalyst design.

papers.title: Vibronic contributions to hyperfine-mediated spin kinetics
papers.abstract: The hyperfine interaction is a cornerstone of spin-dependent processes, yet the kinetic modelling of this mechanism remains limited by the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, obscuring the observation of spin evolution that underpin many photophysical systems. Here, we introduce a unified theoretical framework that rigorously incorporates vibronic contributions through a phase-consistent Herzberg-Teller expansion of the hyperfine Hamiltonian. Application to the FMNH•-Cys• radical pair shows that second-order vibronic coupling enhances hyperfine-mediated electronic transitions between spin states by up to 10 8 − 10 9 -fold. The S◦ →T◦ rate increases from ~5− 40 s −1 (Franck-Condon) to ~2 × 10 8 − 1 × 10 9 s −1 (Herzberg-Teller), while the T◦ →S◦ rate increases from ~4 × 10 2 − 1 × 10 3 s −1 to ~1 × 10 10 − 5 × 10 10 s −1 . This observed nanosecond timescale correlates well with the microsecond lifetime photoadduct formation central to its function. Comparison to spin-orbit coupling (SOC) places these rates within the broader landscape of spin-mixing mechanisms, indicating that the hyperfine interaction operates on chemically relevant timescales. Despite the larger magnitude, SOC-mediated transitions are incoherent; the hyperfine interaction in contrast preserves coherence and is therefore crucial to spin evolution models. This work underscores the importance of incorporating a vibronic description in hyperfine-driven dynamics and provides a generalised methodology that captures essential non-Condon effects even at the single-structure level; thus serving as a complementary tool for systems where full ensemble sampling is impractical or not yet integrated into standard workflows.

papers.title: Metal-based conducive nano-inks: A review of synthesis and characterisation techniques
papers.abstract: In the recent decade, metal-based conductive nano-inks comprising of nanometer-sized metallic particles of high electrical conductivity (mainly Ag and Cu) suspended in a polymer have revolutionized the field of printed electronics. The present review aims to provide an overview of the current state of research in synthesis and characterization techniques for metallic nano-inks and associated challenges. Moreover, the end of the review will discuss future perspectives in this field (from industrial and academic viewpoints).

papers.title: A moving laminated porous frontier governs lithium inventory and lifetime in anode-free lithium-metal batteries
papers.abstract: Anode-free lithium-metal batteries (AF-LMBs) offer the highest practical energy-density ceiling among near-term rechargeable battery architectures, yet their lifetime is set by an interface that cannot be manufactured in advance: the Cu-side boundary is created during charging and dismantled during discharge. Here we show, using a coupled electrochemical–chemical–mesoscale framework, that AFLMB lifetime is governed not by the thickness of a single solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) but by the evolution of a moving laminated porous frontier. We retain the positive-electrode Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) formalism for separator and cathode transport and replace the Cu boundary with a fourteen-state closure that resolves pre-SEI conditioning, incubation, partitioning between buried and top-surface lithium, porous-frontier area amplification, voiding, pressure feedback, dead-lithium accumulation and cyclable inventory. A hybrid Cahn–Hilliard field, Cellular-Potts domain map and reactive kinetic-Monte-Carlo renderer then translate hidden-state trajectories into evolving cross-sections. The resulting picture is geometric as well as chemical: protocols that keep lithium buried beneath a compact frontier retain usable inventory well beyond protocols with similar Coulombic efficiency but earlier switching to topsurface growth. We finally translate this mechanism into an additive-aware fitness score that favours anion-derived, laminated interphases over solvent-derived porous ones, thereby linking electrolyte chemistry, formation history and lifetime in a single screening framework.

papers.title: From Equilibrium Geometry to Coarse-Grained Dynamics: A Rotation-Matrix Patchy-Particle Model Applied to FtsZ Polymerization
papers.abstract: We introduce a differentiable patchy-particle potential for molecular dynamics in which the orientationdependent interaction is governed by the Frobenius inner product of rotation matrices. The potential compares the instantaneous relative orientation of two particles with an arbitrary target rotation Rtgt, encoding all three rotational degrees of freedom in a single smooth switch function. Combined with a complementary distance-dependent switch, the model yields closed-form forces and torques. The target matrix, Rtgt, can be parameterized directly from any known equilibrium configuration without decomposing the geometry into separate angular and torsional components. We demonstrate the framework by simulating FtsZ polymerization with a three-patch coarse-grained model. The simulations reproduce the morphological diversity observed experimentally, in both bulk and membrane-associated conditions: straight filaments, rings, toroids, helical bundles, and laterally aggregated sheets.

papers.title: Deactivation Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (deactNODE)–learning deactivation kinetics from integral data
papers.abstract: Catalyst deactivation critically affects long-term reactor performance. Thus, the development and parameterization of accurate models to predict the effect of operation conditions is crucial for reactor design. Current models are limited by power-law frameworks or lack in flexibility to be used in reactor models. In this work, a rate-based deactivation model is proposed, in which an artificial neural network learns the intrinsic activity gradient as a function of the catalyst state and operating conditions. The model is trained on activity–time data using an integral strategy based on the neural ordinary differential equation method, enabling direct use of experimentally accessible quantities. Using simulated deactivation experiments, systematic hyper-parameter study is conducted to identify suitable network architectures and the NODE training strategy is demonstrated. The model accurately predicts temperature-dependent deactivation data and shows robust interpolation to unseen conditions, even with small data sets. Application to long-term CO methanation experiments over a Ni-based catalyst demonstrates excellent agreement with experimental activity profiles, capturing regime changes and complex temperature effects. The proposed framework provides an accurate and flexible alternative to classical deactivation models which is ready to use in reactor modeling.

papers.title: Interplay of Oxygen Disorder and Superionic Conductivity in La2Mo2O9
papers.abstract: Superionic oxide-ion conductors underpin solid-oxide electrochemical devices, yet the structural origins of abrupt ionic-conductivity transitions remain poorly understood. La 2 Mo 2 O 9 (LAMOX) exhibits a two-orders-of-magnitude increase in ionic conductivity around 580 °C, but its atomic-scale structure, conduction mechanism, and pathways remain elusive, hampering rational design that builds on its remarkable properties. Here, we uncover the structural origin and specific oxygen environments involved in the exchange responsible for the superionic transition in this material, and establish a structural model that provides unprecedented insight into the structural disorder of its oxygen sublattice. This understanding, combined with mapping the O 2- energy landscape, reveals a concerted merry-go-round-type migration mechanism, in which cooperative oxygen motion is driven by repulsive interactions towards stationary oxygen sites and facilitated by an interstitial site that bridges Mo–O polyhedra into a continuous conduction pathway. Our findings redefine the role of oxygen disorder in oxide superionic conductors and delineate design principles for engineering high oxide ion conductivity beyond vacancy-mediated transport.

papers.title: Photoexcited state of a visible-light responsive Fe(II) π-extended isocyanide complex coupled with blue photoluminescence
papers.abstract: Seeking molecular design principles for Fe(II) complexes with long-lived triplet excited states remains important and challenging. Although isocyanide ligands are promising, as their strong ligand-field can suppress deactivation via low-lying metal-centered (MC) states, Fe(II) complexes with reported aryl isocyanides exhibit negligible visible light absorption, and no phosphorescence has been observed so far. Here, we investigated a visible-light absorbing and emitting Fe(II) isocyanide complex bearing quinoline-based isocyanide ligands, in which extended π-conjugation and heteroatoms stabilize the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO). This low-π* orbital enables the formation of a metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) absorption band in the visible region up to 450 nm. Notably, the complex exhibits room-temperature photoluminescence in THF, with an emission maximum at 472 nm and a lifetime of 12 ns. In the time-resolved infrared spectroscopy, the bleach signal of the Fe(II) complex displays kinetics correlating with the photoluminescence from the picosecond to nanosecond range, providing clear evidence for the photoluminescence originating from the Fe(II) complex. Based on spectroscopic results and quantum chemical calculations, the observed emission is assigned to phosphorescence from the triplet ligand-centered ( 3 LC) state. The 3LC state achieves a nanosecond lifetime even with the presence of lower-lying 3 MC states. This work demonstrates that Fe(II) isocyanide complexes can access the excited states with higher-energy and longer-lifetimes than expected values from the previously reported 3 MLCT excited states in Fe(II) complexes.

papers.title: Neutral Amphiphiles Boost Transfection Efficiency and Reduce Inflammation in Polymer Micelle-Mediated mRNA Delivery
papers.abstract: Polymer-based delivery vehicles are a promising non-viral alternative for nucleic acid therapeutics; however, current formulations often have low transfection efficiency or if effective, have high toxicity. Herein, we investigate the use of blended polymeric micelles, an ordered assembly of amphiphilic block copolymers in solution, for the delivery of mRNA. Three cationic amphiphiles consisting of a primary amine (C1), dimethyl amine (C2), or diethyleneimine (C3) were synthesized. Neutral amphiphiles containing morpholino (M), hydroxy (H), dihydroxy (DH), brush PEG (PB), or two linear PEGs (P5K, P10K) were also created. Seventy-five micelles were formed by blending each cationic and neutral amphiphile at 5 compositions. In the absence of serum, C2 micelles with PEG incorporations above 10% had the highest transfection efficiency, however, C3 formulations were more optimal, having more moderate transfection efficiencies and improved viability. In the presence of serum, C3 formulations with 5 and 10% neutral group incorporations were the most effective, maintaining cell viabilities on par with untreated controls and transfection efficiencies superior to purely cationic micelles. Higher neutral loadings of 20 and 40% reduced transfection efficiency. IL-1β release from macrophages during transfection was also measured as an indicator for potential inflammatory responses. Neutral group loadings of 10% with C1 and C2 significantly reduced cytokine release. In contrast, 10% neutral loadings for C3 micelles slightly increased cytokine release; however, these levels were still below those measured for C2 formulations, indicative of improved biocompatibility of C3 relative to C2. One notable exception was 10% M in C3 micelles, which produced levels on par with Nigericin, a known microbial toxin known to include inflammasome activation. Neutral loadings of 40% reduced cytokine release across the formulation space, indicative of improved biocompatibility. Overall, this work demonstrates that changes in formulation chemistry can produce polymeric systems of improved transfection efficiency, without a coinciding increase in toxicity and immunogenicity, to yield more desirable vehicles for nucleic acid delivery.

papers.title: Cobalt-doped Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles as Selective Absorbers for Neutral Color Semitransparent Photovoltaics
Log-scale calibration of serial dilutions for mass-spectrometry-based metabolomics
Reduction of Biochemical Oxygen Demand in Wastewater Effluents Using UV LED Photolysis and Advanced Oxidation Processes
papers.abstract: Removal of organic loading in wastewater effluent is a priority for treatment facilities to ensure discharge water adheres to local regulations and is safe for the environment. This study investigated the removal of bulk organic matter (as measured by biochemical and carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand, BOD5 and cBOD5, respectively) from municipal wastewater effluent using 275-280 nm UV LED irradiation under bench-scale and full-scale conditions. Bench-scale removal was evaluated using both collimated beam and flow through UV LED reactors (275 nm) at fluences between 250 - 5000 mJ cm-2 with and without chemical oxidant addition (chlorine) for primary and secondary effluent matrices. Treatment efficacy for the secondary effluent source was also investigated using a full-scale flow-through 280 nm UV LED reactor at a fluence of approximately 148 mJ cm-2 and a flow of 545 m3 day-1. This work determined that UV C LED irradiation can reduce effluent BOD in municipal wastewater matrices (by up to 52%) at both the bench- and full-scale. Mechanistically, the fluorescence profile of UV-exposed samples exhibited a shift in the humic index suggesting that lower weight, protein-like organic compounds were the primary target of the UV C process. This work demonstrates that UV C LED technologies can be a useful tool for water utilities that require additional BOD removal.

papers.title: Selective Acceleration of Nickel Reduction Enables a One-Pot, Two-Step Deaminative Arylation of Primary Amines with Aryl Chlorides
papers.abstract: Despite the commercial abundance of aryl chlorides and amines, the general, catalytic cross-electrophile coupling of aryl chlorides and N-alkylpyridinium salts remains unknown. The central challenge is a mismatch in reactivity: pyridiniums are too reactive compared to electron-rich aryl bromides and aryl chlorides. Herein we report on how iodide salts selectively accelerate nickel reduction, enabling a twostep, one-pot procedure for the deaminative arylation of primary amines with aryl chlorides via pyridinium intermediates. The scope of the chemistry is broad (23 examples, 70 ± 16% average coupling yield) and these conditions avoid the need for tuned pyridinium salts, slow addition protocols, or stoichiometric nickel.

papers.title: Optimized Octahedral Geometry and Hidden Rigidity of a New Tridentate N-Heterocyclic Carbene Ligand Scaffold Enhances Luminescence of an Fe(III) Complex
papers.abstract: Fe(III) N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) complexes are emerging photoactive first-row transition metal complexes. While optimizing ligand bite angles is a widely employed strategy to extend photoactive excited states, the lack of tridentate NHC ligands prevents exploration of better coordination geometries in the first-row transition metal complexes. Here, we demonstrate that a newly designed methylene-bridged mer-tridentate NHC ligand provides an improved coordination bite angle. Continuous Shape Measure (CShM) analysis reveals that the Fe(III) complex exhibits a significantly improved octahedral geometry (0.35) compared to existing phenylene-bridged mer-tridentate ligands (3.15). This optimized geometry results in a prolonged 2LMCT lifetime (τ = 670 ps), which is longer compared to the Fe(III) complexes with reported bidentate or mer-tridentate ligands. The complex retains a better octahedral geometry even in the distorted quartet metal-centered (4MC) state, indicating enhanced structural rigidity of the coordination environment. The methylene-bridges seem inherently flexible; however, we revealed that the geometric constraints of the mer-tridentate arrangement and methylene moieties provide counterintuitive hidden structural rigidity. This work establishes the new mer-tridentate NHC ligand scaffold as a promising ligand platform for developing photoactive first-row transition metal complexes.

papers.title: RepairMet Explorer: An Explainable Decision-Support Platform Linking DNA Repair, Replication Stress, and Metabolic Vulnerability in Oncology
papers.abstract: Precision oncology increasingly relies on multi-omic and pathway-level data, yet researchers often face a practical gap between biological complexity and actionable experimental prioritization. RepairMet Explorer was designed as a concept software platform that integrates DNA repair status, replication stress signaling, and metabolic adaptation into one interpretable decision layer. The workflow converts a compact set of biologically meaningful inputs, including homologous recombination deficiency, fork instability, glycolytic reliance, glutamine dependence, oxidative stress, and lactate handling, into composite state variables that summarize repair defect, replication burden, glycolytic acid load, mitochondrial plasticity, and redox fragility. These states are then compared with curated vulnerability signatures representing synthetic lethality and adaptive dependency hypotheses, including POLQ/PARP, ATR/WEE1/CHK1, LDHA/lactate export, glutamine anaplerosis, SLC7A11/GPX4-mediated redox buffering, and oxidative phosphorylation stress. A second layer applies evidence weighting so that pathway evidence, functional assays, omics confidence, and expert review can modulate final prioritization without obscuring the underlying biology. The platform returns ranked hypotheses, top contributing variables, cohort summaries, and report-ready outputs intended to support experimental design rather than clinical diagnosis. This manuscript describes the conceptual basis, mathematical framework, software architecture, and illustrative outputs of RepairMet Explorer, and argues that explainable multi-axis prioritization can help move oncology research from fragmented interpretation toward more structured and testable decision-making.

papers.title: Direct Synthesis of 2D Non-layered Metal Mononitrides and Monocarbides via Solid Iodination
papers.abstract: The Stoichiometric transition metal mononitrides and monocarbides (MMX) are advanced ceramics owing to their metallic conductivity, chemical inertness and plasmonics properties. Sculpting these materials with atomically thin thickness to construct two-dimensional (2D) non-layered structure to preserve their merits while could unlock unique optoelectronic properties driven by quantum confinement. However, their isolation is restricted by the robust isotropic bonding of bulk counterparts. Here, we report a solid iodination "over-etching" strategy enabling the topological conversion of MAX phases into pristine 2D MMX (MMXenes). Iodine vapor aggressively extracts both A-site and partial M-site elements of MAX, driving a crystallographic metamorphosis from hexagonal precursors to face-centered cubic (FCC) MMX lattices. Strikingly, these thermodynamically unstable skeletons defy the expected collapse to maintain a 2D morphology with irreducible skeletal limit thicknessof ~0.74 nm, forming atomically thin MMXenes of TiN, TiC, TaC, NbC, VC, ZrC, and their surfaces remain paradoxically devoid of halogen terminations. The resulting "naked" MMXenes exhibit high electrical conductivity as well as exceptional environmental robustness (stable >360 days in water) and thermal stability (673 K in air). Furthermore, this highly efficient process can be readily scaled up to the hundredgram level with a yield of 95%. This work expands the horizon of top-down synthesis, offering a platform for exploring the properties of 2D non-layered ceramics.

papers.title: Ring-Opening Polymerization of Lactide and Ring-Opening Copolymerization of Cyclohexene Oxide and Phthalic Anhydride by Multinuclear Zinc, Magnesium and Potassium Complexes
papers.abstract: The synthesis and structural characterization of multinuclear complexes containing aminobis(phenolate) ligands with zinc and magnesium centres are reported. Trimetallic zinc complex Zn 2 (Zn(OAc) 2 ) [L] 2 ( 1 ) (where [L] = dimethylaminoethylamino-N,N-bis(2-methylene-4-methyl-6methoxyphenolate)) was reacted with magnesium acetate in methanol to form a heterometallic complex, Zn 2 (Mg(OAc) 2 ) [L] 2 with different levels of occupancy at the central metal site depending on the reaction conditions used. Addition of methanolic solutions of Mg(OAc) 2 at –78 °C and warming to room temperature gave a complex with 74% of the central zinc positions replaced with magnesium ( 2 ). Heating the methanolic solution to reflux resulted in a higher displacement of the central zinc positions, giving 94% occupancy of the central metal site by magnesium ( 3 ). A multimetallic complex containing three Zn(II) centres and four K(I) centres, two L ligands, and six acetate co-ligands, {[LZn(OAc)] 2 Zn(KOAc) 4 } ( 4 ), was also synthesized and characterized. Complexes 1 and 3 catalyze the ring-opening polymerization (ROP) of rac -lactide ( rac -LA), giving polyesters with and without the presence of benzyl alcohol (BnOH) as a cocatalyst. Complexes 1 and 3 also catalyze ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of cyclohexene oxide (CHO) and phthalic anhydride (PA), giving moderate molar mass polymers with narrow dispersities.

papers.title: Distribution and Function of Pyrimidine Nucleoside 2'-Hydroxylases across the Tree of Life
papers.abstract: Pyrimidine nucleoside metabolism is classically divided into phosphorolytic and hydrolytic routes mediated by nucleoside phosphorylases and nucleoside hydrolases (NSHs), respectively. While these pathways are well characterised in many organisms, the metabolic fate of 2'-deoxynucleosides, particularly thymidine, remains incompletely understood across non-metazoan lineages. Here, we show that pyrimidine nucleoside 2'-hydroxylase (PDN2'Hs), previously assumed to be fungal-specific, are in fact widely distributed across fungi, plants, and selected bacterial and SAR lineages. Using large-scale sequence-mining, phylogenetic analysis, structural comparison, and biochemical validation, we identify two major evolutionary clades of PDN2'H homologues with conserved catalytic features. A representative panel of enzymes from phylogenetically diverse organisms was biochemically characterised and found to catalyse the conversion of thymidine to 5methyluridine, demonstrating conserved 2'-hydroxylation activity beyond fungi. Collectively, these results establish PDN2'H as a broadly conserved α-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase family that links DNA-derived nucleosides and ribonucleoside catabolic pathways. We propose that PDN2'H functions as a previously unrecognised metabolic gatekeeper that enables the entry of 2'-deoxynucleoside into canonical nucleoside hydrolase-dependent degradation networks. This mechanism provides a unified framework for thymidine turnover across diverse taxa and resolves a long-standing gap in pyrimidine nucleoside metabolism.

papers.title: Extended active learning-guided design of multi-component electrolytes with opposing co-solvent properties
papers.abstract: Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload. Specifically, co-solvent candidates are clustered by molecular properties; co-solvents are then selected, and their pairwise combinations undergo rigorous formulation optimization. Our data-driven approach discovered a non-intuitive electrolyte composition: combining co-solvents with fundamentally opposing properties. This unique formulation, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network while reconstructing the solvation structure, enables Zn||NH4V4O10 full-cells to retain 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. This study unveils the possibility of using active learning to discover unconventional electrolyte formulations that would otherwise be infeasible to identify through human insights.

papers.title: A Scalable One-Pot Strategy for Porphyrin Metal–Organic Frameworks via In situ Linker Synthesis
papers.abstract: Porphyrin metal–organic frameworks (pMOFs) are highly versatile materials for catalysis, energy, and environmental applications, yet their widespread use is limited by the cost and multistep synthesis of porphyrin linkers. Here, we report a one-pot synthetic strategy that integrates porphyrin formation and MOF crystallization, enabling the direct assembly of zirconium-based pMOFs from simple molecular precursors. This approach eliminates the need for linker isolation and purification, significantly reducing synthetic complexity and resource consumption. The method is demonstrated for the benchmark framework PCN-224 and its zinc metalloporphyrin analogue, yielding crystalline, porous materials at multigram scale. Notably, the resulting materials exhibit enhanced mesoporosity, which improves mass transport and enables superior adsorption of large organic dyes, despite lower BET surface areas compared to conventionally synthesized analogues. Importantly, we further demonstrate the generality of this approach by synthesizing USTC-9(Fe), a framework with distinct metal nodes and porphyrin linker geometry. This work establishes a versatile platform for coupling complex linker synthesis with framework assembly, offering a sustainable and scalable route to functional pMOFs and broadening the scope of in situ linker formation in reticular chemistry.

papers.title: Deciphering Twisted Prismatic Structural Evolution in Atomically Precise Copper Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: The stability of the copper nanocluster has always been a concern owing to its low half-cell reduction potential. It is well documented that anion templates are known to tune the structure and impart stability to the nanocluster. Here, using a simple reduction strategy, we have obtained a dihalide-templated copper nanocluster for the first time. The copper cluster, namely, [Cu23(3-Cl)2(SPh-CF3)18(PPh3)6(CF3COO)3], features a unique double triangular prismatic structure. The structure contained a basic unit with the formula of Cu9(3-Cl)2 forming an inner triangular prism, which is further wrapped by a second triangular prism with the formula Cu12(SPh-CF3)18(PPh3)6(CF3COO)3, forming a unique twisted triangular double prismatic geometry. Further, we have proposed a plausible growth mechanism that helps us decipher the evolution of the cluster, and here we observed a peculiar “twisted concentric growth” of the two prisms, which occurs due to the radial dimerization of the Cu11 base prism to form the dimeric Cu23 cluster. The unique growth pattern and structure influence the electronic states of the cluster, as evidenced by experimental and theoretical studies, thereby imparting the material with good photoresponse properties. The new insights into this novel dihalogen templated twisted double prismatic copper cluster may pave the way to understanding the unique structural growth and developing photonic materials.

papers.title: Synergistic Multi-Heteroatom Doping in Three-Dimensional-Porous Iron Single-Atom Catalysts for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction Reaction
papers.abstract: The scarcity of platinum and the sluggish kinetics of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remain central barriers to the scalability of electrochemical energy conversion. Here, we present a rational design for three-dimensional (3D) porous iron single-atom catalysts (SACs) embedded in a multi-heteroatom-doped carbon framework. These electrocatalysts overcome the traditional trade-off between activity-stability. We synthesized atomically dispersed Fe sites in N -doped (Fe 1 - N -C), N,S -doped (Fe 1 - N,S -C), and B,N -doped (Fe 1 - B,N -C) carbons using a sodium chloride-templated freeze-drying/pyrolysis route. Multi-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals that boron incorporation modulates the electronic structure of the Fe-N active sites, and strengthens iron-ligand covalency in the B,N-system. For alkaline ORR, Fe1-B,N-C shows an onset potential of 0.92 V vs. RHE, a kinetic current density of 16.62 mA cm-2, and a metal-normalized mass activity of 11518 A g-1 Fe at 0.7 V, which exceeds that of 10% Pt/C and state-of-the-art Fe- N -C benchmarks. The material also demonstrates a low Tafel slope of 88 mV dec-1, ≈ 100% current retention over 10 h, and methanol tolerance. SCN - poisoning experiments confirm that the Fe-site dominates and the B-site participates in this catalytic reactivity.

papers.title: Practical Quantum CIM Empowerment via All-Domestic-Core Agentic Large Model
papers.abstract: Quantum computing devices are recognized as powerful tools for solving NP-complete problems. How-ever, the intricacy of their modeling presents notable barriers for non-specialists, while the tedious iteration of constraint weights and modeling methodologies also consumes substantial effort on the part of experts. To address these challenges, this study integrates a femtosecond laser-pumped Coherent Ising Machine (CIM) with an LLM-driven agentic system by leveraging the LangGraph and LangChain frameworks. Com-prehensive investigations demonstrate that large language models (LLMs) can effectively perform such tasks in modeling as QUBO/Ising model calibration, constraint weight decision iteration and rapid validation of literature-reported schemes. Notably, all these tasks can be fully implemented based on domestic large models, combined with domestically developed CIM hardware, we truly achieve the practical empowerment of quantum CIM that fully relies on all-domestic agentic large models and hardware. This work successfully realizes robust technological integration, laying a solid foundation for subsequent research. Nevertheless, it also identifies the persisting challenges in the two cutting-edge fields of large models and quantum computing at the current stage. Encouragingly, we unexpectedly discover a promising new paradigm where accumulated knowledge from agent-assisted quantum computing iterations reciprocally enhances the agent’s own problem-solving capability, thereby addressing these challenges.

papers.title: Radical para-Selective C-X (X=C, N, S) Functionalisation of Nitrobenzene
papers.abstract: Achieving selective C-H activation and bond formation in aromatic molecules remains a central task in organic chemistry. Conventional strategies rely on metal-catalysts, pre-functionalized reagents or harsh conditions, increasing synthetic complexity and waste. Radical-based approaches offer a compelling alternative thanks to their unique reactivity patterns, enabling transformations under comparatively mild conditions. Here, by leveraging a single electron transfer (SET) process between Lewis pairs, we report a general radical-based mechanism that affords the one-pot regioselective C-X (X=C, N, and S) functionalisation of bare nitrobenzene 1. Detailed NMR, EPR and XRD spectroscopies coupled to DFT studies show that after SET, the resulting pair of radicals engage in a cross-coupling reaction, which after hydride abstraction, leads to the formation of para-functionalised product under mild conditions. These findings demonstrate that SET to 1 is far more accessible than previously appreciated, with a wide variety of carbanions, amides, alkoxides, organophosphides, and thiolates as compatible partners, positioning the broader class of nitroaromatics as versatile platforms for harnessing radical-pair reactivity in synthesis and expand the scope of metal-free functionalisation strategies. More broadly, they highlight that nitro groups cannot always be regarded as innocent functionalities in the presence of anionic species, with important implications for reaction design and mechanistic interpretation.

papers.title: QuADMET-Former: Pre-training on Quantum Mechanical Properties Improves ADMET Prediction
papers.abstract: In principle, quantum chemistry allows us to quantify electronic and geometric properties of molecules and their interactions. Thus, incorporating pre-calculated quantum mechanical properties into deep learning models could improve their ability to predict important pharmacological properties of small molecules and potential drugs. However, this opportunity to incorporate better physicochemical inductive bias has been underexploited in the recent wave of AI-driven drug discovery. We show that pre-training Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) models-specifically the TorchMD-NET model-to predict quantum mechanical molecular and atomic properties like dipole moments, HOMO-LUMO gap, and partial charges, we can obtain more accurate models to predict absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicological (ADMET) properties. Moreover, we explore the interplay between quantum chemistry and three-dimensional structure by introducing a novel structure pre-training strategy where the equivariant transformer is pre-trained on three-dimensional molecular fingerprints known as E3FPs. We ran QuADMET-Former, MapLight+GNN and Quantum Informed Pre-training on 23 ADMET benchmarks drawn from Therapeutic Data Commons (TDC), Biogen ADME, and OpenADMET, and found them to outperform both MapLight+GNN, the best-performing single model on the TDC benchmark, and Quantum Informed pre-training, a state-of-the-art method for quantum chemistry-informed ADMET prediction, on very challenging spectral splits. QuADMET-Former performed best on 16 of the 23 datasets (13 out of those 16 were statistically significant). The optimal pre-training target combination varies across tasks, suggesting that quantum mechanical and geometric features capture complementary aspects of molecular behaviour. Our results establish quantum chemistry-grounded pre-training as a practical and impactful strategy for ADMET prediction under strict generalization conditions, and highlight the underexplored interplay between 3D molecular geometry and electronic structure in representation learning for small-molecule drug discovery.

papers.title: Ion Mobility and Tandem Ion Mobility Spectrometry for Top-Down Proteomics
papers.abstract: The comprehensive characterization of human proteoforms remains a central bottleneck in elucidating molecular mechanisms underlying human disease. Top-Down Proteomics offers direct access to proteoforms but remains technically challenging, in large due to the difficulty of reliably interpreting fragment ions within highly complex tandem-mass spectra. Ion Mobility Spectrometry (IMS), when integrated with tandem mass spectrometry, has emerged as a powerful approach to enhance both analytical clarity and structural depth in top-down workflows. IMS contributes in three complementary ways: (i) as an additional gas-phase separation dimension, IMS reduces spectral congestion by separating precursor ions prior to fragmentation and by dispersing fragment ions in mobility–mass space after fragmentation; (ii) in multidimensional configurations, IMS directly correlates precursor ions with their corresponding fragment ions, enabling structurally informed fragment assignment; and (iii) through the measurement of collision cross sections, IMS provides access to conformational information for both precursor and fragment ions. By directly linking sequence, modification state, and conformation at the intact proteoform level, IMS-integrated top-down proteomics offers the potential to move beyond identification to interrogate sequence–structure–function relationships of proteoforms.

papers.title: Macropore-Induced Modulation of Response Kinetics and Glucose Response in 3D-Printed Polyampholytic Hydrogels
papers.abstract: A method is presented for 3D stereolithographic printing of polyampholytic glucose-sensitive hydrogels (GSHs), with and without macropores. Polyampholytic GSHs that employ phenylboronic acid to reversibly bind glucose shrink in response to increases in environmental glucose concentration, and shrink in response to increases in the environmental osmolarity value. Values of GSH response magnitude, GSH response time, and GSH elastic shear modulus are presented for nonporous 3D-printed GSHs and macroporous 3D-printed GSHs, with comparison made to results for nonporous polyacrylamide hydrogels synthesized using a conventional bulk polymerization technique. The elastic modulus values of nonporous GSHs that are 3D-printed are substantially smaller than those of nonporous hydrogels which are not 3D-printed. As expected, the introduction of macropores reduces the response time of 3Dprinted GSHs. Unexpectedly, the introduction of macropores also increases the glucose response magnitude of 3D-printed GSHs.

papers.title: A Stimuli-Responsive Hydrogel Containing Immobilized Fluorescent Cd(II)-Binding DNA Aptamers That is Reusable Even in the Presence of DNA-Degrading Nucleases
papers.abstract: Numerous researchers have reported that single strand DNA aptamers dissolved in aqueous solutions can be used to detect target analytes at very low concentrations. Typically a change in fluorescence occurs when the aptamer binds the target analyte due to a change in aptamer conformation. However, for many practical applications, for example wastewater analysis, the wastewater sample contains DNA nucleases that rapidly degrade dissolved DNA aptamers. To address this problem, we immobilize DNA aptamers designed to bind cadmium (II) within a polyacrylamide-based hydrogel. Cadmium is a highly toxic contaminant that is potentially present in nuclear wastewater. We demonstrate that hydrogel immobilization of the aptamer greatly increases its resistance to nuclease degradation, presumably due to diffusion limitations placed upon nucleases by the hydrogel network. In addition, we show that the stimuliresponsive hydrogel can be reused multiple times to determine cadmium concentrations. Unfortunately, acrydite modification of the original aptamer, which is necessary for hydrogel immobilization of the aptamer, reduces the binding affinity between the aptamer and Cd.

papers.title: Vertical Ionization Energies of Boron Chelates: A DFT and Electron Propagator Theory Benchmark
papers.abstract: A comprehensive comparative study of vertical ionization energies (VIEs), vertical electron affinities (VEAs), and Kohn–Sham gaps between the highest occupied (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied (LUMO) molecular orbitals for 41 medium-sized (up to 50 atoms) boron chelate complexes and their precursors is reported. The study combines electron propagator theory (EPT), density functional theory (DFT), and ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS). The EPT-based approaches included the outer-valence Green’s function (OVGF), partial third-order propagator P3, and approximately renormalized partial third-order P3+ methods, while the DFT calculations employed the ωB97X, CAM-B3LYP, M06-2X, and BHandHLYP functionals. Among the EPT methods, the P3/aug-cc-pVDZ combination yields the most accurate VIEs, with a mean deviation (MD) of 0.03 ± 0.20 eV. VIEs were further benchmarked across various geometry optimization methods, basis sets, and DFT functionals, including ωB97M-D4 and ωB97M-V. This analysis establishes that, within the DFT framework, the ωB97M-V functional incorporating the VV10 nonlocal correlation provides the closest agreement with experiment. For βdiketones and their thio-and imino-analogues, this method, combined with r2SCAN-3c geometries and the saug-ANO-pVTZ or def2-QZVPPD basis sets, achieves an accuracy (MD = 0.11 ± 0.18 eV) comparable to that of EPT methods. Across the series of studied compounds, the selected DFT method yields semi-quantitative agreement between theoretical and experimental VIEs (MD = 0.31± 0.25 eV).
