Furthermore, the r2SCAN-3c/ωB97M-V/def2-QZVPPD protocol is identified as optimal for calculating VEAs (MD = 0.18± 0.22 eV) and HOMO–LUMO gaps (MD = 0.11± 0.33 eV) of the studied complexes.

papers.title: MetaboFIMS: An automated workflow for fast and sensitive metabolic screening of large
papers.abstract: Large-scale metabolomics studies are increasingly constrained by the limited throughput of liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), where comprehensive coverage requires multiple chromatographic separations and ionization modes. While flow injection-mass spectrometry (FI-MS) offers substantially higher throughput, its broader adoption in untargeted workflows has been hindered by limited availability of accessible, user-friendly, and scalable data processing solutions, and reduced annotation confidence. Here, we present MetaboFIMS, an open-source, fully automated, vendor-agnostic computational pipeline for untargeted metabolomics data analysis of FI-MS data, publically available as Shiny application, complemented with an optimized FI-MS acquisition protocol that can be implemented on standard LC-MS instrumentation. The optimized FI-MS method enables analysis times of ≤1 min per sample and ion mode, with MetaboFIMS performing end-to-end spectral processing of mzML files including isotope clustering, run alignment, molecular formula prediction, and annotation against HMDB databases, processing over 500 samples in approximately 2 hours on a standard desktop workstation. We systematic optimized acquisition parameters to maximize sensitivity, reproducibility and metabolome coverage for the analysis of clinical plasma samples, and benchmarked the analytical performance on two clinical cohorts. In a multiple sclerosis study, we show the capacity of FI-MS to capture rapid metabolic perturbations following ublituximab treatment, while in a type 2 diabetes mellitus cohort, FI-MS was able to reproduce empagliflozin-associated reductions in uric acid and 1,5-anhydroglucitol previously identified by LC-MS, demonstrating strong methodological concordance. These results establish FI-MS and MetaboFIMS as a robust, scalable, and high-throughput complement to LC-MS, enabling rapid metabolic phenotyping of large biobanked cohorts.

papers.title: Straightforward and Modular Maleimide Synthesis from Ynamides
papers.abstract: Maleimides are privileged scaffolds with broad applications in chemical biology, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their modular synthesis - particularly in non-symmetrical, polysubstituted forms - remains challenging. Herein, we report a general and efficient strategy for their synthesis from readily accessible ynamides and α-ketoesters via in situ generated lithiated ketenimines, engaging in a cascade sequence involving formal anionic (2+2) cycloaddition, cycloreversion, and cyclocondensation. This method enables rapid access to a wide range of densely functionalized maleimides with excellent functional group tolerance, under conditions allowing either retention or removal of the N-protecting group. The resulting scaffolds can be readily diversified, notably through a “nitrogen switch” strategy to access distinct heterocycles. The power of this approach is demonstrated in the concise syntheses of denigrin A and aqabamycin A, as well as the first unified and divergent synthesis of antrodins A-C, highlighting its potential as a versatile platform for the rapid construction of functional maleimide architectures.

papers.title: Speciation of silanol groups on commercial precipitated silicas via IR spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The surface chemistry of amorphous silica is governed by the concentration, speciation, and accessibility of silanol groups, yet quantitative comparison between closely related silica samples remains challenging due to surface heterogeneity and overlapping spectroscopic signatures. In this study, infrared spectroscopy is combined with H-D isotopic exchange and size-selective molecular probes to speciate isolated, internal, and associated silanol populations across a series of silica samples with similar composition but differing surface characteristics. A dilution effect in surface silanol density with increasing specific surface area was observed, and notable batch-to-batch variability further highlights the sensitivity of silanol speciation to subtle differences in material preparation. Nominally similar silicas can exhibit pronounced differences in silanol distribution and accessibility, including measurable batch-to-batch variability that is not reflected by BET surface area or total hydroxyl content. Internal and associated silanols represent a substantial fraction of the total hydroxyl population and display variable accessibility to probe molecules. These findings suggest that global surface descriptors alone are insufficient for describing silica surface chemistry and that explicit consideration of silanol speciation and accessibility is required for reliable interpretation of spectroscopic and chemical measurements.

papers.title: Unravelling solvent-independent excited state proton transfer dynamics in sterically substituted photoactive systems
papers.abstract: Excited state proton transfer (ESPT) plays a central role in the function of many photoactive molecules; however, it can be strongly influenced by environment polarity. Here, we investigate the excited state photodynamics of two structurally complex triazine- and benzotriazole-based molecules that bear sterically bulky substituents around the proton transfer unit: bis-ethylhexyloxyphenol methoxyphenyl triazine (BEMT) and methylene bis-benzotriazolyl tetramethylbutylphenol (MBBT). Using femtosecond transient electronic absorption spectroscopy in solvents of contrasting polarity and hydrogen-bonding character, supported by mixed reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory calculations, we show that ultrafast relaxation in both systems is governed by a largely solvent insensitive intramolecular ESPT. We demonstrate that the solvent-independent behavior primarily arises from intrinsic, electronic, properties of BEMT and MBBT rather than steric substitution. While bulky substituents are not a requisite for efficient intramolecular ESPT, they offer enhanced solvent-invariant ESPT dynamics. This highlights potential design elements for next-generation photoactive systems for tuning excited-state behavior.

papers.title: ChemMamba: Multi-Modal Diffusion Pre-Training with Parameter-Efficient Adapters for Molecular Property Prediction and Generation
papers.abstract: Molecular representation learning is essential for computational chemistry, yet existing methods struggle with multi-modal inputs and costly fine-tuning. We propose ChemMamba, a unified framework integrating multi-modal diffusion pre-training with parameter-efficient chemical adapters. Our approach features a cross-modal encoder that aligns SMILES strings, 2D graphs, and 3D conformations via a diffusion-based objective, capturing complementary structural and geometric features. To address the high cost of model adaptation, we introduce Chem-Adapters, which enable multi-task transfer learning with only 1.6M trainable parameters, a 53× reduction compared to full fine-tuning. Furthermore, a linear-attention diffusion generator is incorporated to reduce the computational complexity of molecular generation from quadratic to linear. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets (MUV, Tox21, SIDER, and ClinTox) demonstrate that ChemMamba achieves state-of-the-art results in property prediction, specifically reaching an AUROC of 0.841 on MUV and 0.908 on ClinTox. In molecular generation tasks on ZINC250K, Chem-Mamba achieves a validity score of 0.952 and a Fréchet ChemNet Distance (FCD) of 8.47, significantly outperforming existing diffusion-based baselines. These results highlight the efficiency and robustness of ChemMamba for both discriminative and generative tasks in drug discovery.

papers.title: Flavin Hydroperoxide and Semiquinone: Structures and Biomimetic Activity
papers.abstract: Flavins are unique natural redox cofactors that can switch between an oxidized, a radical half-reduced, and a fully reduced state. In nature, the interplay between these redox states is orchestrated by the surrounding flavoenzymes and unlocks a myriad of unique chemical transformations. One of the most archetypical flavin properties is the activation of molecular oxygen from air by the reduced cofactor, which proceeds via the half reduced semiquinone radical and leads to a flavin hydroperoxide, the key species in flavin-mediated oxygenations. While central to many natural and biomimetic catalytic processes, both flavin semiquinone and hydroperoxide are transient reactive species and, therefore, have so far evaded structural characterization at the molecular level, including single-crystal diffraction. We close this gap and disclose solid-state structures of both isolated key intermediates, linking their reactivity to enzymatic transformations. The biomimetic oxygenation of tetrahydrocarbazoles, which constitute the core structure of many biologically active natural products, was achieved in high yields using a flavin hydroperoxide. Orthogonal activation of the same substrates was achieved by embedding the flavin semiquinone in a catalytic cycle. A total of seven distinct product classes were accessed, all resembling structures occurring in natural products. Our findings clearly link the reactivity of isolated flavin species to well-studied flavoenzymes. We expect these results to promote the application of flavin catalysts as oxygenation agents at both laboratory and industrial scales.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Workflows to Compute Large-Scale Sets of Absolute Binding Free Energies Aiding Drug Candidate and Binding Pose Selection
papers.abstract: Large-scale Virtual Screening (VS) campaigns of compound libraries can significantly speed up candidate selection in the early stages of drug discovery. The most promising drug candidates are identified by Scoring Functions (SFs), which enable VS campaigns to rank candidate compounds according to their estimated binding affinities. These SFs are typically trained on experimental data reflecting binding affinities (e.g. Dissociation Constant (Kd) values), commonly used as proxies for protein-ligand binding free energies. Because experimental reference data are often unavailable or collected using inconsistent techniques and/or procedures between laboratories, we developed two computational workflows that generate configurational ensembles of soluble protein-ligand complexes with Molecular Dynamics (MD) and compute the Absolute Binding Free Energies (ABFEs) of the sampled ligand binding poses with implicitsolvent calculations. The resulting consistent large-scale datasets of ABFEs address two complementary aspects of virtual screening: quantitative binding affinity estimation and binding pose assessment. Our Binding Affinity Prediction (BAP) workflow estimated protein-ligand binding affinities for 4000+ complexes from the PDBbind 2020 dataset. Our Pose Selector (PS) workflow computed non-converged ABFEs from short Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations estimating the stability of 800,000+ related binding poses.

papers.title: Leveraging General Molecular Fragments to Expand the Design Space of Metal-Organic Polyhedra
papers.abstract: The discovery of functional reticular materials is dependent on optimising the organic building unit to achieve precise chemical and structural properties. However, experimentally characterised chemical building units (CBUs) are only a small fraction of the possible design space, and as such, computer-aided design based on datasets of known reticular materials have fundamental limitations in chemical diversity. Here, we present a general workflow for extracting, analysing, and recombining molecular fragments from large, chemically diverse datasets to systematically expand the accessible organic CBU design space. Using the ChEMBL36 database as a case study, we generate a library of 12,387 unique fragments through filtering, fragmentation, and ontology-driven classification. These fragments are recombined to enumerate a dataset of 44.8 million CBUs. To demonstrate integrating the workflow into designing functional reticular materials, we combine the library with a genetic algorithm and optimise for metal-organic polyhedra (MOPs) estimated as stable, non-toxic drug carriers. The concepts and relationships between the molecular fragments, CBUs, templates, and MOPs are captured and connected through a knowledge graph and ontology integrated in The World Avatar.

papers.title: Nanostructured DNA Barcode Decoding with Solid-State Nanopores: impact of bit spacing and bit shape
papers.abstract: In recent years nanopores have emerged as a powerful tool for the detection of biomolecules at the single-molecule level. Yet simultaneous detection of many different molecules remains a challenge. Toward this goal, nanostructured DNA barcodes is a promising strategy for enabling the multiplexed detection of biomarkers. The general principle is based on DNA nanostructures assembled along the contour of a linear DNA carrier creating a binary sequence. Different molecule of interests are assigned a unique barcode. Here we address two key challenges in the design of nanostructured DNA barcodes when decoded using pores fabricated on thin SiN membranes (10-20 nm thick) and measured with state-of-the-art MHz range bandwidth amplifiers. First, to maximize digital data density and multiplexing, we studied the minimal spacing required between nanostructured bits for clear signal resolution, testing this with compact DNA triangles attached to a carrier molecule. Second, to ensure the unique identification of different bits in the current trace, we explored distinctively sized and shaped DNA nanostructures — specifically DNA stars and helix bundles — designed to generate distinguishable current signatures. Results reveal that for voltage driven translocation, bits positioned at least 160 bp apart and with rigid shapes with fixed orientations optimize the decoding efficiency.

papers.title: Rhodium(I)-hydride mediated ethylene hydrogenation: mechanistic insights and characterization of Rh(I)-ethylene complexes
papers.abstract: The Wilkinson’s catalyst derived Rh I -monohydride complex (PPh 3 ) 3 Rh I H has an outstandingly high reactivity in the hydrogenation of alkenes and alkynes. The study of this reaction with ethylene in the presence of the hydrochloride salt of Barton’s base allowed us to unravel the underlying mechanism. In combination with DFT calculations, we could show that instead of a Wilkinson-like octahedral intermediate, the insertion step of ethylene into the Rh-H bond occurs in a square planar RhI complex. Furthermore, we obtained the single-crystal structure of the novel Rh complex (PPh 3 ) 2 Rh I (C 2 H 4 )Cl, and propose the formation of a cyclometallated Rh I species based on 31 P NMR experiments and 31 P NMR chemical shift calculations.

papers.title: Dynamic correlation suppresses antiferromagnetism in heavily doped Fe-pnictide superconductor LaFeAsO1−xFx
papers.abstract: LaFeAsO is a prototypical iron pnictide that exhibits stripe antiferromagnetism in its parent form and evolves into an unconventional superconductor upon fluorine doping, with transition temperatures reaching ∼41 K. The microscopic origin of the suppression of antiferromagnetism with doping, however, remains under debate, with chemical pressure effects often invoked as the primary mechanism. Here, we revisit this problem using a combination of density functional theory (DFT), DFT+U, hybrid functional approaches, and ab initio dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT). Taking LaFeAsO1−xFx at x = 0.5 as a representative heavily doped case, we demonstrate that chemical pressure alone is insufficient to fully suppress the antiferromagnetic state within static mean-field descriptions. In contrast, DFT+DMFT calculations reveal a collapse of long-range antiferromagnetic order at ∼58 K, just above the superconducting transition temperature, while the undoped compound retains robust magnetic order. This suppression is accompanied by a pronounced sharpening of the quasiparticle peak and a reduction in incoherent scattering, indicative of enhanced electronic coherence upon doping. Our results highlight the essential role of dynamical correlation effects, beyond one-electron and static mean-field approximations, in driving the suppression of magnetism in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO.

papers.title: Extracting kinetic information on the hydrogen evolution on Pt by combining time-resolved microcalorimetry and finite-element modelling.
papers.abstract: For fast and reversible electrocatalytic reactions, like the hydrogen evolution on Pt in acidic media and in the presence of molecular H 2 , it is very challenging to obtain reliable kinetic information from the charge-potential relationship alone. To overcome this issue, we measure the time-resolved heat flux during hydrogen evolution on polycrystalline Pt as complementary information to chronopotentiometric measurements. The interpretation of the data is based on a comparison with a finite element simulation comprising a microkinetic model coupled to mass transport. Using this approach, we estimate the exchange current density to be around 10 – 15 mA cm -2 , for both, the Tafel or the Heyrovský reaction being the rate limiting step. We also find that the coverage of the active hydrogen intermediate is low around the equilibrium potential, even in hydrogen saturated solution.

papers.title: Theoretical calculation of structural, electronic, magnetic, and thermoelectric properties of KMO2 (M = Sm3+, Tb3+ and Dy3+) oxides by the ab initio method.
papers.abstract: Structural, electronic, optical, thermoelectric and magnetic characteristics of potassium-based rare earth oxides are discussed in this paper. Density-functional theory (DFT) based on a full-potential linear augmented plane wave plus local orbital (FP-LAPW + lo) system within Wien2k software; for the exchange-correlation energy (PBE + GGA) approximation was carried out. Crystal structures of these materials have a hexagonal form with a space group (166_R-3m). Therefore, volume-optimized graph results depicted that studied compounds are more energetically stable in ferromagnetic states than in anti-ferromagnetic and non-magnetic states. Moreover, spin polarize band structure and Density of States (DOS) of studied materials shows metallic and semiconductor nature for corresponding spin channels. However, studied materials have half metallic nature with 100% spin polarization at EF. Total and partial magnetic moments of KMO2 and individual atoms existed due to lanthanide ions due to unpaired 4f electronic states that are present at Fermi level EF. Finally, the energy difference between anti-ferromagnetism and ferromagnetism energy versus volume optimization curve gives the value of Curie temperature TC and noticed that room temperature ferromagnetism is possible.

papers.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence for High-Precision Nanomedicine in Ocular Drug Delivery
papers.abstract: Ocular drug delivery persists one of the most challenging limitations in nano-medicine, prohibited by the eye's distinct anatomical barriers and intricate physiological micro-environment. Stimuli-responsive nanobots — nano-scale frameworks capable of autonomously monitoring medication discharge in accordance with endogenous stimulus (pH, enzymes, reactive oxygen species) or exogenous factors (light, magnetic fields, temperature) — constitute a desirable paradigm for reliable ophthalmology. Recent developments at the nexus of stimuli-responsive nano systems for ocular medication administration and AI/ML-guided computational design are extensively investigated in this study. Surveying the present landscape of machine learning models — containing quantitative structure–activity relationships (QSAR), artificial neural algorithms, and deep learning frameworks — employed in nanocarriers synthesis, and analyzing effective fluid dynamics and pharmacokinetic modelling strategies relevant to intraocular medication administration. Identifying the persistent disparity among computational predictions and experimental validation as a central constraint, assessing the underlying causes: data heterogeneity, insufficient standardized ocular-specific datasets, restrained model readability, and the biological intricacy of nano–bio interactions in vivo. Subsequently, recommending a direction for concluding this computational–experimental divide through federated learning frameworks, reasonable AI, digital twin technologies, and integrated elevated efficiency monitoring pipelines, project an alternative to clinically translatable, intelligent ocular nano-therapeutics.

papers.title: The Cauldron Equation—Pre-Relativistic Dynamics, Matter Nucleation, and the Milgrom Scale in GERT
papers.abstract: Background: The preceding papers in this Gibbs Energy Redistribution Theory (GERT) series have established a complete thermodynamic framework for cosmic evolution across all observable scales, from the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) to 191 galactic rotation curves. The four-layer stratigraphy of reality has been formalised and the Cauldron equation identified as the central open problem. The present paper derives that equation. Methods: Using the frozen Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) functions fM (x) and fL(x), together with the monotonic enthalpy condition dH/dτ ≤ 0 and the requirement that the Outward Force creates volume, we derive the minimal Layer 2 (L2) dynamical system for the pre-relativistic Cauldron in the variables (H,x), where H is the normalized enthalpy and x = log10 ρ is the thermodynamic density. The equation contains a normalization convention β (shown to be a gauge choice, not a physical parameter) and a boundary condition HQV (Quasi-Vacuum floor). All key observables are independent of both. Results: Thirteen results emerge from this minimal system, all independent of β and HQV: (1) The Cauldron equation dH/dτ = −(fL − fM )(H −HQV), dx/dτ = −β(1− φ)(fL − fM )(H −HQV)/H reproduces the recombination epoch as the natural turning point of the thermodynamic trajectory—the maximum of the cohesive fraction φ = fM/(fM + fL) falls at x = −17.38, within 0.04 dex of the empirically calibrated recombination peak, without being told where recombination is. (2) The Milgrom acceleration a0 is predicted as a0 = aGERT × φstart/φend = 1.2068 × 10−10 m/s2, agreeing with the observed value to within 0.57%—a parameter-free prediction independent of β. (3) The thermodynamic tension fL − fM is quasi-preserved (3.7%) across the conformal boundary between eons, identifying it as the candidate conformal invariant. (4) The Cauldron consumed 98.2% of the primordial enthalpy before the metric crystallized, leaving 1.8% for the entire Relativistic Window. Structure formation costs 64× more than maintenance—the thermodynamic signature of crystallization. (5) Classical Nucleation Theory (CNT), translated into GERT variables, shows that the nucleation barrier ∆G∗ ∝ (fL − fM )3/f2 M is minimized at x = −17.37 and the nucleation rate J ∝ fM · exp(−(fL − fM )3/f3 M ) peaks at the same density. The fM Gaussian peak is identified as the nucleation resonance—the thermodynamic window in which matter crystallizes from the proto-geometric soup. (6) The nucleation window density (ρ ≈ 4× 10−18 kg/m3) exists in cosmic plasmas but cannot be isolated from the global H ≈ HQV; conversely, laboratory quasi-isolation cannot reach the density. This double bind means that, by everything we know today, the Cauldron’s supersaturation is not reproducible—neither locally nor remotely. The prediction remains: any residual proto-geometric signal should be maximized at this density, but the signal is suppressed by ϵ = HQV/HM ≪ 1. Conclusions: The Universe is a thermodynamic substance passing through the four classical phases of matter: plasma crystallizes into solid (fM peak, recombination), solid melts into liquid (L2 peak, entropic trigger), liquid vaporizes into gas (fL logistic, observed acceleration), and gas expands into vacuum (gas term, intensification). Each transition is governed by the same Gibbs free energy framework that governs phase transitions in a laboratory beaker. The “dark energy problem” is the liquid-to-gas transition. The enthalpic quota H is a global thermodynamic property: supersaturation is not a local condition, and the crystallization window cannot be reopened within our eon. The preceding papers identified the events; this paper explains the mechanism.

papers.title: Recent advances in distonic radical cation chemistry: Focus on α-ammonio radicals
papers.abstract: Distonic radical cations are underexplored class of reactive species in which the radical and cationic centers are spatially separated within the same molecule. Among them, the α-ammonio radical exhibits unique reactivity inaccessible to conventional neutral radicals. This short review summarizes the generation methods and characteristic reactivity patterns of α-ammonio radicals, tracing their historical development and highlighting recent advances. Selected state-of-the-art examples demonstrate that these distonic radical cations are promising next-generation intermediates offering access to transformations beyond the reach of classical radical chemistry.

papers.title: Liquid Luminescent Materials Based on 10H-Pyrido[1,2-a]-5-indolium Salts
papers.abstract: Next-generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that can withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent-free ionic liquids typically plateaus below 35% due to aggregation-caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal (<200 °C) and chemical stress. We present a conceptual breakthrough that overcomes this physical limitation through a liquid aggregation-induced emission approach, driven by anion–π+ interactions. The material was liquefied while simultaneously locking the radiative pathways by pairing a rigid N-doped fluorene (10H-pyrido[1,2-a]-5-indolium, PIn+) scaffold with selected anions. This ionic tethering kinetically suppressed nonradiative molecular motion without compromising fluidity, yielding an unprecedented PLQY of 81% in the liquid state. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400 °C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under high vacuum conditions at 250 °C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a highly versatile and easily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system offers extensive customization options for future highly functional implementations. These findings provide a universal design paradigm for hyper-robust liquid phosphors, paving the way for the realization of indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.

papers.title: VirtualLab_CC: An LLM-Augmented Virtual Laboratory for Automated Computational Chemistry Research
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have opened new avenues for automating scientific research workflows. Systems like the AI Scientist [1] demonstrate fully autonomous endto-end research pipelines for machine learning, but their applicability to domains requiring expensive high-performance computing (HPC) resources, specialized quantum chemistry software, and rigorous thermochemical accuracy remains unexplored. Here we present VirtualLab_CC, a hybrid LLM-augmented virtual laboratory for computational chemistry that integrates Claude (Anthropic) as an orchestration layer with a multi-agent architecture, gated lifecycle management, and bidirectional HPC cluster synchronization. Unlike fully autonomous systems, VirtualLab_CC enforces human-in-the-loop quality gates at every critical decision point while automating routine operations: conformer searches, input generation, job submission and monitoring, output parsing, failure diagnosis, and manuscript preparation. The system manages 21 specialized skills spanning literature review, cluster operations, result extraction, novelty verification, AI-assisted peer review, and citation validation. We demonstrate VirtualLab_CC on a prototype case study of 1,3-dipolar cycloadditions between stabilized Criegee intermediates and biogenic terpene dipolarophiles, involving 17 molecular species, 34 conformers, and over 100 SLURM jobs across multiple calculation stages. The system successfully identified and autocorrected cluster failures, detected a methodological anomaly (a suspiciously low dioxirane barrier requiring IRC verification), and coordinated multi-method validation across three DFT functionals. VirtualLab_CC bridges the gap between fully autonomous AI research and the rigorous quality control demands of computational chemistry, providing a practical framework for LLM-augmented scientific workflows in resource-constrained HPC environments.

papers.title: Computer-Aided Entrainer Design for Extractive Distillation Using Infinitely Sharp Splits
papers.abstract: Extractive distillation represents a viable method for separating close-boiling mixtures and azeotropes, provided that a suitable entrainer can be identified. Relying solely on classical ranking metrics such as selectivity (S∞) and capacity (C∞) at infinite dilution, has been questioned in recent years. In this work, we present an integrated product-process design framework for the identification and ranking of heavy entrainer candidates for the separation of minimum boiling azeotropes. The framework combines computer-aided molecular design (CAMD) with the infinitely sharp split (ISS) shortcut method, enabling rapid computation of key process parameters including the minimum entrainer-to-distillate ratio ((E/D)min) and the corresponding minimum reflux ratio (Rmin). The CAMD-ISS procedure employs group contribution methods for pure component and mixture property prediction, coupled with structural connectivity, thermodynamic, and process constraints to systematically generate and screen entrainer candidates. To validate the predictive capability of the ISS-based ranking, rigorous process simulation and optimization were carried out in Aspen Plus using Differential Evolution, minimizing the total annual cost (TAC) for the top-ranked candidate and two benchmark entrainers. The methodology is demonstrated on the well-studied acetone/methanol separation, where DMSO was confirmed to be a better entrainer than ethylene glycol, consistent with literature findings. Furthermore, the framework identifies 18 promising entrainers that satisfy all imposed constraints. The top candidate, propanedial, exhibits an (E/D)min of 0.33 compared to 0.61 for DMSO, and achieves the lowest TAC (5.30 M$/year) versus ethylene glycol (5.35 M$/year) and DMSO (5.72 M$/year) upon rigorous optimization, despite requiring a larger regeneration column. The results demonstrate that ISS-based metrics, while not capturing regeneration difficulty directly, are sufficient to identify entrainers with favourable overall process economics, and offer more reliable indicators of actual process performance than infinite dilution properties alone.

papers.title: Q-planner: a harness system for quantum chemistry agents
papers.abstract: LLM-based agents for computational chemistry commonly place the model inside an accumulating execution loop, causing context growth proportional to workflow length, unpredictable token costs, and degraded plan reliability at scale. We present a chemistry computation harness that confines LLM invocations to three semantically bounded stages—compound identification, planning, and reporting—while delegating all tool dispatch, parallel scheduling, arithmetic derivation, and artifact routing to a deterministic LangGraph executor that consumes zero LLM tokens during execution; a library of domain skill modules injects specialist quantum chemistry protocols into the planner context at planning time without enlarging the execution context. Across five representative quantum chemistry workflows, average token consumption ranged from 9,100 to 22,300 tokens with zero execution-stage tokens in every case—more than 95% fewer than loop-based multi-agent systems—and a full-scheme plan representation sustained 100% correctness across all 30 high-throughput runs from N = 10 to 100 compounds, dispatching up to 200 concurrent tool nodes from a single planning call. These results demonstrate that robust, cost-predictable quantum chemistry automation is achievable through harness design rather than through larger context windows or more capable base models.

papers.title: Catalyst and Catalysis Co-exploration in Methane Utilization
papers.abstract: Conventional catalyst development is typically confined to reaction-centric approaches, in which catalyst performance is evaluated under fixed feed compositions targeting a single desired product. Such strategies overlook the complexity of multicomponent reaction environments, where multiple competing pathways can emerge. Here, we present a high-throughput approach that enables the simultaneous exploration of catalyst composition and reaction conditions, using methane conversion as a representative system. Methane transformation was systematically investigated over a library of 200 catalysts across a broad CH 4 –O 2 –CO 2 feed compositional space, without imposing predefined reaction targets or stoichiometric constraints. Product formation was monitored using unbiased full mass-scan analysis, allowing hydrocarbons, syngas components, and minor products to emerge directly from the data. Moving beyond conventional benchmarks, optimal performance frequently arises at feed compositions that deviate significantly from the stoichiometric ratios of established methane reactions. Expanding the accessible reaction space not only enhances attainable yields but also reveals high-performing catalysts that would remain unrecognized under fixed-condition evaluation. The results further demonstrate that catalytic performance arises from coupled catalyst–condition interactions, rather than intrinsic material properties assessed at a single feed condition.

papers.title: From Photon Spiral Motion to Superheavy Elements: A Unified Analytical Atomic-Molecular Energy Theory Based on Quantum Phase Vortices and Relativistic Corrections
papers.abstract: Within the constructive theoretical framework, this work establishes the Ether-Vortex Atomic and Molecular Model (EVAM), a fully analytical energy scheme covering the entire periodic table with atomic numbers from to . Three foundational constructive physical pictures, namely photon spiral propagation, etheric structural medium, and electron quantum phase vortex, are introduced with methodological status analogous to imaginary numbers in mathematics. They do not claim ontological physical reality, but merely serve as instrumental structures for unifying theoretical formalism, simplifying analytical derivation, and sustaining self-consistent and stable computation. EVAM adopts exponential wave packets to characterize electronic spatial distributions, realizing strictly analytical integration of all Coulomb interactions while completely eliminating basis sets, numerical integration, and self-consistent field iterations. The computational complexity is reduced to . A constructive relativistic wave packet width formula is constructed to achieve automatic wave packet saturation, which fundamentally eliminates computational divergence for heavy and superheavy elements, enabling uniform, stable, and high-precision descriptions across light, heavy, and superheavy nuclides. Resting on only 10 globally fixed parameters, EVAM achieves chemical accuracy for light atoms and small molecules. For heavy elements, deviations from Dirac–Fock reference data remain below , while superheavy element results are provided exclusively for theoretical benchmarking. All calculations are completed within milliseconds to seconds on a conventional single personal computer. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations attain approximately 115-fold speedup relative to parallel DFT-AIMD computations. Within the constructive paradigm, the model uniformly interprets electron correlation, chemical bonding, and relativistic effects. It can be employed as an independent computational tool for material simulation, catalytic mechanism research, and theoretical investigations of superheavy elements.

papers.title: Complex Network Theory-Driven Rational Design of Ionic Liquid-Based Solid Electrolytes: A New Paradigm
papers.abstract: The development of traditional solid electrolytes has long been constrained by empirical “trial-and-error” approaches. The introduction of complex network theory provides a systematic analytical framework and rational design paradigm for this field. This perspective aims to systematically elaborate on the application of this paradigm in the design and optimization of ionic liquid (IL)-based solid electrolytes. First, we clarify the core concept of abstracting electrolyte systems as dynamic networks (where nodes represent structural units and edges represent transport pathways or interactions) and explore its unique advantages in establishing quantitative “structure-property” relationships. Subsequently, we provide a detailed review of the practical applications of this methodology, mainly including: (1) graph theory-based network topological characterization (such as tortuosity, percolation threshold/critical concentration); (2) network connectivity design based on percolation theory; (3) ion transport mechanism analysis based on network dynamics (such as random walk models, cooperative “paddle-wheel effect”); and (4) performance correlation and prediction based on multiscale network models. On this basis, we systematically summarize IL-functionalization design strategies inspired by network concepts, covering node engineering (covalent grafting, physical doping, interfacial modification), edge property regulation (reducing energy barriers, constructing fast ion channels, dynamic reconstruction), and modular multiscale network integration. Particularly, we deeply explore the frontier direction of integrating complex network theory with machine learning, such as automated network feature extraction, topological inverse optimization, and performance evolution prediction, opening new pathways for high-throughput design and performance prediction of electrolytes. Finally, based on the “network topology blueprint,” we propose a closed-loop design paradigm for IL-based solid electrolytes and prospect the future development of deep integration among network science, materials informatics, and artificial intelligence, aiming to provide systematic methodological guidance for promoting the rational design of high-performance, high-safety solid-state batteries.

papers.title: Nondipole Effects in Atto-second Electronic Dynamics for high intensity LASER driven atoms: figure-of-eight motion of the induced dipole
papers.abstract: Nondipole effects on atto-second electronic dynamics of atoms are examined in this work. An analysis of the induced dipole moment using a nondipole Hamiltonian formalism for laser intensities ranging from 10 11 to 10 15 Wcm −2 for wavelengths of 800 nm (Near Infrared region) and 3504 nm (Mid-Infrared region) is presented for Hydrogen and Helium atom. In the case of Helium, a full configuration interaction wavefunction has been used as an ansatz for the nonperturbative driven dynamics of the two-electron problem. For both Hydrogen and Helium, the induced dipole moment beyond the electric-dipole approximation, describes a figure-eight motion in three-dimensional (3D) space in comparison with a linear motion using dipole approximation. In the long-wavelength regime, the Helium atom exhibits aperiodic chaotic behaviour and an asymmetric figure-eight motion.

papers.title: NNP/CG-MM: Embedding of All-Atom Neural Network Potentials into a Coarse-Grained Molecular Mechanics Environment
papers.abstract: Neural network potentials (NNPs), or neural network-based force fields, are gaining widespread attention for their ability to model complex chemical, materials, and biophysical systems. In NNPs, the total energy of the system can be decomposed into atom-centered components, where the energies and forces are described using a deep neural network. However, despite the flexibility and accuracy of NNPs, they are typically more computationally intensive than classical molecular dynamics. There have been recent advances in embedding NNPs into a molecular mechanics (MM)-based environment to maximize efficiency while retaining the accuracy of NNPs. In this work, we propose a method called NNP/CG-MM, in which an all-atom NN force field is systematically embedded into a coarse-grained molecular mechanics environment (CG-MM). Coarse-graining (CG) involves constructing a simplified representation of a larger fine-grained (FG) system with the goal of significantly accelerating computations while maintaining the accuracy of the FG system when projected onto the CG variable distributions. The NNP-CG coupling terms are constructed using the multiscale CG force-matching (MS-CG) method. The scheme is tested on liquids and in capturing features of the hydrophobic effect, where three-body correlations in the CG solvent can play an important role.

papers.title: Mechanism-Based Drug-Excipient Compatibility Prediction from Molecular Structure
papers.abstract: Drug-excipient incompatibility remains a leading cause of pharmaceutical formulation failure, yet computational prediction tools are limited to lookup tables of documented interactions that fail on novel drugs. I present a mechanism-based approach that detects reactive functional groups directly from SMILES strings (13 patterns via SMARTS matching), classifies excipients by reactive properties (4 classes: reducing sugars, peroxide-containing, alkaline, metal-containing), and predicts degradation mechanisms (11 pathways including three Maillard reaction variants, ester hydrolysis, and thiol oxidation). Applied to 100 drugs not in the system's knowledge base, the method generated 92 predictions; of 38 validated against published literature, 37 were supported and 0 were disconfirmed. An adversarial test set of 17 deliberately challenging cases (prodrugs, sterically shielded groups, electronically deactivated amides, soft electrophiles) produced 17/17 correct classifications. The approach is implemented in OpenMix, an open-source Python framework (pip install openmix) that evaluates formulations from multiple computational perspectives and classifies where they agree or disagree.

papers.title: Multi-task scheduling for chemical processes in self-driving laboratories under scientific constraints
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) integrate process automation, robotics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to accelerate chemical discovery. As SDLs evolve toward concurrent multi-task execution, experimental scheduling becomes a critical decision-making layer, determining the ordering and timing of operations under strict scientific constraints, including operation precedence, station allocation, batch processing, experimental parameters, and critically, time synchronization between consecutive operations. For example, in inorganic synthesis, temporal deviations during nucleation can fundamentally alter material properties. The absence of scheduling for concurrent chemical processes leads to resource conflicts and uncontrolled interruptions, undermining the reproducibility and data quality essential for AI modeling. Here, we present a multi-task scheduling algorithm that jointly accounts for scientific constraints and is integrated into an SDL via a closed-loop architecture that enables tight coordination between scheduling and experimental process execution. Validated through the concurrent multi-task synthesis of gold nanoparticles and metal-organic frameworks, the algorithm preserves chemical fidelity and ensures consistent material quality across concurrent multi-task executions, unattainable with a conventional scheduling algorithm that does not adequately account for scientific constraints. This paradigm establishes a practical scheduling framework for concurrent multitasking in SDLs, ensuring the experimental consistency required to generate the high-fidelity datasets foundational to autonomous, AI-driven scientific discovery.

papers.title: CS-SelectFold: Chemical-shift-guided selection of protein excited-state conformations from a generative protein structure model
papers.abstract: Low-populated protein excited states can play decisive roles in function, ligand recognition, and misfolding, but their structural characterization remains difficult because these conformations are transient and sparsely populated. Here we present CS-SelectFold, a training-free framework that combines generative conformational sampling with NMR chemical-shift-guided post hoc selection to recover low-populated protein conformations. CS-SelectFold uses SimpleFold to sample diverse candidate structures from sequence, applies structural pre-screening to enrich models that escape the dominant ground-state basin, predicts chemical shifts with UCBShift 2.0, and ranks candidates by agreement with experimentally determined excited-state chemical shifts.We benchmarked CS-SelectFold on two proteins with experimentally characterized low-populated states. For the T4 lysozyme L99A cavity mutant, a canonical excited-state system, the method recovered the defining excited-state-like local rearrangement around the engineered cavity, including inward placement of Phe114, consistent with the NMR/CS-Rosetta-derived excited-state model. A two-reference hotspot dRMSD analysis further showed that chemical-shift-based ranking enriched conformations that moved away from the ground-state basin and toward the experimentally defined excited-state basin. For the A39V/N53P/V55L Fyn SH3 domain, which populates an aggregation-prone hidden folding intermediate, CS-SelectFold recovered the key topological signature of the experimentally characterized intermediate: loss of the C-terminal β-strand present in the native state, as confirmed by both three-dimensional structural comparison and secondary-structure analysis.These results establish CS-SelectFold as a practical framework for excited-state structure recovery and suggest that the same sample-and-select principle may extend to broader low-populated hidden conformations, including folding intermediates.

papers.title: Lessons Learned on Obtaining Reliable Conductivity Estimates from Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: The calculation of reliable ionic conductivities from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations is not a straightforward task, especially for strongly correlated systems, such as ionic liquids or highly concentrated electrolytes, where the Nernst–Einstein approach tends to fail. In this manuscript, we present the newly implemented conduct module for TRAVIS. It allows the calculation of the ionic conductivity using the Einstein–Helfand and Green–Kubo approaches, which explicitly include ionic correlations in their formalism. We provide a broad overview of accessible transport properties and compare methods and best practices for obtaining statistically reliable estimates of ionic conductivity and other physicochemical properties derived from electrolyte MD simulations, including transport numbers and the inverse Haven ratio. To validate our implementation and demonstrate the conduct module’s capabilities, we simulated the ionic liquid 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium dicyanamide ([EMIm][DCA]) as well as the ether-based electrolyte lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in ethylene glycol dimethyl ether (LiFSI/DME).

papers.title: Thickness-Dependent Transport Control in Polymer Conformal Coatings for Electrochemical Corrosion Suppression
papers.abstract: Thickness-dependent corrosion suppression in polymer conformal coatings is governed by transport limited reaction rather than geometric barrier effects alone. This study establishes a processing-structure-property correlation for a UV-cured solvent-free acrylate–urethane and a moisturecured solvent-borne modified acrylate applied on Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold plated copper (ENIG–Cu) under biased chloride exposure. Integrated electrochemical, dissolution, and microstructural analyses reveal a strong linear increase in polarization resistance with critical thickness and R2 > 0.9, indicating diffusion-length-controlled enhancement of transport resistance. The densely crosslinked UV-cured network achieves effective suppression at lower thickness, whereas the solvent-borne system requires greater thickness due to higher microstructural heterogeneity. Interfacial elemental mapping confirms that corrosion initiation in thin films originates from chloride-assisted activation at the buried interface, while thicker coatings suppress ion accumulation and exhibit stable dielectric behaviour. These results provide quantitative guidance for thickness optimization in polymerbased corrosion protection systems.

papers.title: Improving Activity and Stability of Candida boidinii Formate Dehydrogenase Through Rational Active Site Engineering
papers.abstract: Formate dehydrogenases represent a highly attractive tool for nicotinamide cofactor regeneration to drive biocatalytic reductions and oxygenations by NADH-dependent oxidoreductases with formate as cheap, atom-economic, terminal reductant. However, despite the clear benefits over other recycling systems, native FDHs remain rather unpopular, mainly due to their intrinsic, low specific activity. While the active site architecture is generally highly conserved across many FDHs from very diverse origins, smaller patterns of dissonance in the active site's vicinity can serve as hotspots for the rational design of more effective variants. In this study, we have created a series of Candida boidinii FDH variants incorporating non-consensus amino acids found in Saccharomyces cerevisiae FDH. A double mutant (C23S/F285D) was identified that exhibits a significantly higher specific activity, an overall more desirable pH and temperature profile, and an improved stability profile.

papers.title: Magnesium Alloy Biomaterials: Innovative Engineering Solutions for Future Biodegradable Implant Materials
papers.abstract: Magnesium (Mg) alloys are promising candidates for temporary orthopaedic and cardiovascular implants due to their biocompatibility, mechanical compatibility with bone, and complete biodegradability in the human body. Although extensive research has focused on alloying and conventional heat treatments to tailor their performance, the application of deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) remains largely unexplored. DCT, which involves exposure to cryogenic temperatures, has been shown to enhance hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion behaviour in various steels and alloys. However, its use in biomedical systems is still at an early stage. In this study, the influence of DCT on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and corrosion behaviour of Mg-Gd alloys with different Gd contents was systematically investigated. Three compositions Mg-2Gd, Mg-5Gd, and Mg-10Gd were examined under conventionally extruded (CHT) and DCT (−196 °C) for 8 h, 24 h and 48 h states. Microstructural and phase characterization was performed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD) and atom probe tomography (APT). Additionally, XRD-based micro-residual stresses were analysed to observe changes in the stress state of the material in response to specific treatment procedure. Next, corrosion behaviour was evaluated by potentiodynamic polarization, while Raman shift spectroscopy was used to analyse surface oxides and passivation layer formation. Mechanical response was assessed via Vickers microhardness testing. The results demonstrate a clear compositiondependent response to DCT. A significant increase in hardness was observed for Mg-5Gd, whereas Mg-2Gd and Mg-10Gd exhibited reduced hardness following treatment. Changes in corrosion behaviour were also observed for all three alloys after DCT, suggesting that cryogenic processing alters the electrochemical response of the materials, likely through modifications of the microstructure. However, the mechanisms governing these corrosion changes remain not yet fully understood and warrant further investigation. These findings highlight the potential of DCT as a supplementary processing route for tailoring the performance of biodegradable Mg-Gd alloys for biomedical applications.

papers.title: Enzyme-Polymer stickers for assembling single and multi-analyte biosensors
Mid-infrared photochemical reaction in confined space driven by resonant vibrational excitation
Mechanistic Insight into Phonon-Driven Bistable Terahertz Functionality via Coupled Symmetry Breaking and Spin Transition in a Hofmann-Type Material
papers.abstract: The light-matter interaction at terahertz (THz) frequencies is poised to advance the frontiers of information processing and its scope can be expanded through integration of switchable materials. In this context, spin-crossover (SCO) materials can enable intriguing functionalities arising from diverse switching pathways, yet remains underexplored. This research gap restricts our understanding of how structural and magnetic changes in SCO systems interplay with low-energy optical stimulus. Herein, we report a novel Hofmann-type framework, [Fe(mpi)₂Pt(CN)₄] where mpi = 4-methoxyphenyl isonicotinate, exhibiting hysteretic spin crossover (~20 K) coupled with crystallographic symmetry breaking. THz dynamics of the framework revealed a pronounced response with a distinct phonon ~0.8 THz with its amplitude tracing the magnetic profile. The dielectric function of the complex exhibits bistability arising from the phonon mode strongly correlated with the structural transition (triclinic P1 ̅ → monoclinic C2/m). The ultralow frequency phonon originates from swaying vibration of the cyanometallic lattice and its peak position remains unaltered upon spin state evolution. Furthermore, leveraging bistable dielectric response of the material, its potential as a digital switch has been demonstrated. This work advances the mechanistic understanding of phonon-driven interplay between symmetry breaking, spin transition, and low-energy radiation in a bistable SCO system.

papers.title: Nested TMAPs to Visualize Billions of Molecules
papers.abstract: Here we present a visualization and clustering framework enabling the exploration of billion-sized chemical datasets, exemplified with the REAL database of 9.6 billion make-on-demand molecules. We represent molecules as 42-dimensional MQN (molecular quantum numbers) fingerprints describing molecular structures with counts for different atom-and bond-types, polar groups and topological features, and cluster the dataset by applying Product Quantization (PQ) and PQkmeans. We retrieve the molecule closest to the cluster centroid as a representative for each cluster and compute a tree-map (TMAP) displaying these representatives organized by MQN-similarity. Each cluster representative in this primary TMAP is linked to a nested secondary TMAP displaying the corresponding cluster content organized by ECFP4 substructure fingerprint similarity. This nested TMAP approach can be computed on a single workstation and gives direct access to the entire dataset down to single molecular structures in two clicks. A nested TMAP for the REAL database is accessible at https://chelombus.gdb.tools/databases/real-database.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of Novel High-Affinity Inhibitors of Naegleria fowleri CYP51
papers.abstract: Naegleria fowleri is the causative agent of primary amoebic meningoencephalitis (PAM), a disease with a mortality rate exceeding 97%. Current therapeutic options are limited and often exhibit high toxicity. This study focuses on Sterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51), a critical enzyme for ergosterol biosynthesis, as a therapeutic target. Using in silico molecular docking, I identified a novel candidate, designated as NOV-24 , with a predicted binding affinity of -10.2 kcal/mol . Pharmacokinetic profiling via SwissADME predicted favorable properties for CNS-directed treatment, including high Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) permeation and high Gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. Key physicochemical parameters included a topological polar surface area (TPSA) of 67.27 Å² and a consensus LogP of 2.81 . In addition, a Synthetic Accessibility score of 4.79 indicated moderate synthetic complexity. Overall, NOV-24 represents a promising theoretical lead for the development of CNS-active anti- Naegleria agents.

papers.title: Overcoming the protonolysis of [n.1.1]propellanes (n = 1 or 3) in a four-component reaction
papers.abstract: Exposure of [n.1.1]propellanes (n = 1 or 3) to acidic nucleophiles typically gives decomposition products due to the instability of bicyclo[n.1.1]alkyl carbocations. This instability makes the synthesis of functionalized bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes from protic nucleophiles and [n.1.1]propellanes particularly challenging. In stark contrast, we now report how the structural integrity of the bicyclo[n.1.1]alkyl motif is maintained in the products of a four-component reaction between [n.1.1]propellanes (n = 1 or 3), N-iodosuccinimide, nine cyclic ethers and multiple classes of protic nucleophiles that span a wide range of pKa values. Crucially, this reaction gives one-step access to 4-hydroxy thalidomide derivatives that enabled us to demonstrate in a whole cell assay that a n-butoxy-bicyclo[1.1.1]pentyl linker is tolerated by the cereblon-E3 ligase complex, which is an important target of proteolysis-targeting chimeras. Experimental rate law and theoretical calculations with a model nucleophile suggest that the four-component reaction relies on the attack by THF of a halogen bond complex formed between N-iodosuccinimide and the propellane, which is assisted by hydrogen bonding of the protic nucleophiles to the succinimide component.

papers.title: Predicting Reactivity and Enantioselectivity from Small Experimental Datasets: A Case Study in Asymmetric Magnesium Catalysis
papers.abstract: Predicting enantioselectivity across broad substrate spaces remains a central challenge in asymmetric catalysis and is typically addressed through extensive experimental screening. Here, we demonstrate that meaningful predictions can emerge from small, carefully curated datasets. Using chalcone epoxidation and thia–Michael addition as magnesium-catalyzed benchmark reactions, we developed a machine-learning framework trained on internally consistent experimental data. Systematic evaluation shows that reactivity classification is robust even for highly homogeneous datasets, whereas predictive regression requires broader distributions of enantioselectivity. Experimental validation confirms that the models capture selectivity trends across previously untested substrates. These results establish that small, high-quality datasets can support practical prediction in asymmetric catalysis, providing a foundation for AI-assisted reaction design and substrate prioritization.

papers.title: Natural Seawater Electrolyte Enables CO2 Reduction Selectivity Transition from C1 to C2 Alcohol on Metal Phosphate Catalysts and Suppression of Cathode Scaling with Buffering Action
papers.abstract: Carbon dioxide electroreduction (CO 2 ER) provides a promising approach to produce renewable fuels, however achieving selective formation of higher value C 1+ products is still a challenge. In this work, we demonstrate that untreated natural seawater enables a shift in CO 2 ER selectivity from methanol (C 1 ) in conventional synthetic electrolyte to ethanol (C 2 ), on transition metal phosphate electrocatalysts. MnPO 4 ·H 2 O, Co 3 (PO 4 ) 2 and Co 3 (PO 4 ) 2 ·8H 2 O catalysts exhibit electrolyte dependent reactivity, with NaHCO 3 favouring C 1 product (CH 3 OH) generation, while seawater electrolyte favours C-C coupling leading to C 2 product (C 2 H 5 OH) generation. Using the literature reported computational insights, it is proposed that seawater’s intrinsic metal ions promote the C-C coupling by creating a local hydrophobic environment at the electrode interface. In-situ Raman spectroscopy and kinetic analyses for HER supports the formation of a local hydrophobic environment at the electrode interface. Additionally, the cathode electrode scaling challenge in this seawater electrolyte is overcome by buffering with NaH 2 PO 4 , which suppresses precipitation and enhances current density. Interestingly, change in seawater electrolyte’s pH from alkaline to acidic, by buffering action, does not change the C 2 product selectivity. Furthermore, the catalysts stability tests were also carried out. This work demonstrates electrolyte driven selectivity control and establishes abundant natural seawater as a scalable, ion rich medium for advancing CO 2 conversion to C 2 renewable fuels.

papers.title: Democratizing Reaction Kinetics through Machine Vision and Learning
papers.abstract: We present a new methodology for measuring reaction rate constants by monitoring pH changes via indicator dyes, achieving precision comparable to traditional NMR techniques, called PRISM ( P arallelized R eaction-rates via I ndicator S pectrometry using M achine-vision). The experimental design, enabled by a serial dilution, allowed for measuring twelve rate constants concurrently, spanning more than four orders of magnitude using 96-well plates, with 1,162 total rate constants collected. Moreover, the instrumentation is 3D-printed, with the remaining components comprising readily available and affordable hardware, promoting the democratized use of this technique to generate uniform data sets. Validation with 19 F-NMR confirmed PRISM’s reliability. Computational investigations reveal a concerted asynchronous S N 2 mechanism, with base-catalyzed pathways exhibiting the lowest energy barriers. To complement the PRISM rate dataset, we developed a classification model that achieves high accuracy for out-of-distribution reactants in determining rate measurability, and a chemically rich graph neural network regression model for predicting quantitative reaction rates. This approach provides a framework that offers a resource-efficient strategy for studying reaction kinetics, which can potentially be applied to any pH-dependent reaction class.

papers.title: Continuous photo-flow synthesis of heterohelicenes
papers.abstract: Heterohelicenes continue to attract interest for their potential applications as organic chiral materials. To keep up with the demand for novel heterohelicene structures, expedient and scaleable synthetic procedures are required. We report a ‘Mallory’ photocyclisation methodology in continuous flow for the synthesis of thia-, oxa- and azahelicenes. This procedure has been sucessfully scaled-up to 9.8 mmol and can be applied to an iterative modular synthesis.

papers.title: Nanostructured Palladium Electrodes for Reliable Confined Electrochemistry: impact on Electrochemical Liquid-Phase TEM
papers.abstract: This work presents a novel technological solution based on molecular-template-assisted electrodeposition of nanostructured metallic palladium thin films on both the reference and counter-electrode of a MEMS-based EC-LPTEM cell. Nanostructuring dramatically increases the electroactive area, reducing RE potential oscillation and CE polarization, thus suppressing gas evolution. When galvanostatically loaded with hydrogen, nanostructured Pd forms a stable PdHα+β phase, functioning as a true on-chip reversible hydrogen electrode with excellent potential stability over extended timescales. While challenges such as Pd redeposition on the on-chip working electrode remains in particular circumstances, this method represents a major step toward accurate operando electrochemical studies and scalable on-chip reference electrode design for advanced microscale devices, enabling stable, reproducible electrochemistry and significantly improving the reliability of EC-LPTEM measurements.

papers.title: Field-Aware and Charge-Informed Machine Learning for Predicting Molecular Responses and Vibrational Spectra
papers.abstract: External electric fields play a crucial role in chemistry, materials, and biology. However, accurately capturing external field effects remains a challenge for machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). By revealing the limitations of conventional architectures in predicting field-dependent response properties, we introduce a physics-informed field-aware equivariant neural network framework that predicts response properties to external electric fields. External electric fields are incorporated through an equivariant embedding layer that concatenates field representations with atomic features, preserving rotational equivariance. The model leverages an energy derivative approach to predict response properties in a single unified architecture. Furthermore, we embed a variational charge equilibration scheme into the model to capture long-range electrostatic interactions. The close agreement between charged-based and energy derivative-based electric dipoles indicates that the model learns the correct underlying physics. The unified framework performs robustly for the prediction of response properties and simulation of IR and Raman spectra across molecular and periodic systems under different external field strengths. By incorporating physical principles into the model, we establish a general and transferable framework for modeling molecular response under external electric fields, providing a robust routine for response properties prediction in external electric fields.

papers.title: Attenuation Calculator: a tool for pre-experiment X-ray energy selection
papers.abstract: Choosing an appropriate X-ray energy before data acquisition is one of the most frequently underestimated decisions in laboratory X-ray computed tomography (XCT). An unsuitable energy degrades transmission, contrast, or both, and the cost is paid in segmentation, quantification, and rescans. Attenuation Calculator (v1.0.0) is an open-source graphical tool that estimates sample transmission and phase linear attenuation coefficients for user-defined multi-phase materials, assuming a monochromatic beam. Although real laboratory sources are polychromatic, an effective beam energy obtained from spectrum simulators such as SpekPy, SpekCalc or Spektr allows a meaningful first-pass assessment of scan feasibility. This note describes the tool and demonstrates its use in two practical cases: (i) selecting the scan energy for a pyrite-bearing mudstone to balance penetration and phase discrimination, and (ii) evaluating copper beam-filter thickness for a 21700 NMC 811 / graphite–silicon cylindrical cell, where excessive filtration is shown to erode cathode-to-anode contrast. The examples are intended to illustrate the kinds of pre-experiment questions the Attenuation Calculator is designed to answer.

papers.title: Environmental Trajectories and the Instability of Nanoparticle Identity: Challenges in
Revisiting the Hydrogen Oxidation Reaction on Gold: The Role of Trace Impurities
papers.abstract: Gold exhibits negligible electrocatalytic activity toward the hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR). Yet, several reports have attributed measurable HOR activity to nanostructured gold and subnanometer Au clusters, suggesting the existence of a critical size regime for catalytic activation. In this study, we systematically examine hydrogen oxidation on gold across multiple length scales using atomically size-selected Au𝑛 clusters (𝑛 = 5, 13, 25, 55), sputter-deposited Au films of defined thickness, and polycrystalline Au wire electrodes. Across all rigorously cleaned systems, no intrinsic HOR activity is observed, independent of size, thickness, and surface structure. In contrast, hydrogen oxidation currents emerge only in the presence of trace foreign metal species. For sputtered films and Au wire electrodes, the activity evolves dynamically, being induced by electrochemical cycling, suppressed by oxidative cleaning, and restored through surface restructuring, directly linking reactivity to surface-segregated impurities. Quantitative analysis shows that already partsper-million levels of such species are sufficient to provoke measurable currents, despite their absence in conventional surface characterization. The results demonstrate that hydrogen oxidation originates from heteroatomic surface ensembles, where trace metal atoms provide hydrogen adsorption sites and adjacent Au facilitates charge transfer, giving rise to emergent bifunctionality. These findings establish that hydrogen oxidation is not an intrinsic property of Au, but an impurity-driven phenomenon, once more highlighting the critical importance of impurity control in electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Microplastics-Induced Binding and Structural Changes in the Milk Proteins: α -Lactalbumin and β -Lactoglobulin
papers.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution poses a global threat to ecosystems, human health, and biodiversity conservation. Among the most common contaminants in both terrestrial and aquatic environments are Polyvinyl Chloride Microplastics (PVC-MPs), Polyethylene Microplastics (PE-MPs), and Polystyrene Microplastics (PS-MPs). The two main whey proteins in milk are α -lactalbumin (α-LA), and β -lactoglobulin (β-LG). They are important to food science, nutrition, and overall health. Because PVC-MPs, PE-MPs, and PS-MPs are highly accessible to animals, they breakdown slowly in the atmosphere, accumulate in the bloodstream of mammals, and can be transferred to breast milk, causing serious health problems. Multispectroscopic investigations were used in this work to evaluate the interaction between the developing pollutants PVC-MPs, PE-MPs, and PS-MPs and α-LA and β-LG under physiologically simulated conditions. According to multispectroscopic investigations, α-LA adsorbed onto MPs in the following order: PE>PS>PVC (KA= 7.74, 5.54, and 5.50 ˟ 106 M-1 respectively) and for β-LG, PS>PVC>PE (KA= 9.21, 6.33, and 3.72˟ 106 M-1 respectively). Once PVC-MPs, PE-MPs, and PS-MPs reach the breastmilk, their small size may allow them to adsorb and bind with α-LA and β-LG, probably changing their physiological function and structure. These findings also imply that PE-MPs and PS-MPs, respectively, stimulate amyloid fibrils in α-LA and β-LG. Furthermore, the results demonstrated that PVC-MPs, PE-MPs, and PS-MPs dramatically changed the secondary structure and microenvironment of α-LA and β-LG, which reduced the α-helix and the interaction is static, exothermic, and electrostatic in nature. In addition to offering vital information about the intermolecular interactions, this work elucidates the potential effects of MPs in milk.

papers.title: Surface Chemistry Control of Synthetic Hectorite using Mg/Li Tuning for Targeted Biomedical Applications
papers.abstract: Synthetic hectorite nanoclays, such as Laponite®, are widely explored as model anisotropic colloids and injectable biomaterials due to their high specific surface area, charge anisotropy and ability to form physically cross-linked gels in aqueous environments. Despite this interest, the role of nanoclay surface chemistry in governing application-specific properties such as gelation and protein adsorption remains largely unexplored. In this study, we systematically analyse how modulation of the Mg/Li ratio influences electrokinetic behaviour and gelation performance under physiologically relevant conditions, with a view to optimising clay-based materials for biomedical applications. Synthetic hectorite analogues (RENOVITE®) were engineered via Mg/Li ratio control during hydrothermal synthesis to tune permanent layer charge while preserving structural fidelity. Composition was validated by ICP-OES, while structural and morphological fidelity was confirmed by XRD, ATR-FTIR and SAXS. Electrokinetic measurements revealed a monotonic decrease in permanent basal charge with increasing Mg/Li ratio, accompanied by a systematic shift in agglomeration onset at higher pH. Rheometric characterisation in physiological solutions revealed a clear compositional optimum with an intermediate Mg/Li ratio, yielding maximal storage modulus, while both lower and higher Mg/Li formulations formed weaker networks. This optimum arises from a balance between sufficient platelet delamination (enabled by basal charge) and effective edge-mediated connectivity, positioning the system near a percolation threshold under physiological conditions. In summary, this work establishes a direct link between Mg/Li-mediated surface chemistry, electrokinetics, and diffusion-driven gel mechanics, providing a framework for rationale design of nanoclay biomaterials with tunable performance in biomedical applications.

papers.title: Effect of Initial Temperature on Pore Collapse Hot Spots in TATB High Explosive
papers.abstract: The shock initiation threshold of insensitive high explosives (IHEs) based on TATB (1,3,5-triamino-2,4,6-trinitrobenzene) is known to exhibit a complicated dependence on initial temperature, but the underlying mechanism is not well understood because of multiple plausible ways in which the temperature might impact hot spot formation processes that govern initiation. To this end, we perform all-atom shock simulations of pore collapse in a TATB crystal with a pre-defined void and analyze resulting hot spot structures for different initial temperatures, both colder and hotter than the ambient level. We represent hot spots as 2D images (i.e., distribution fields) of important energetic and structural parameters, including temperature, temperature rise, intramolecular strain energy, and molecular rotational disorder. To decipher if the initial temperature has any significant effect on hot spot structure beyond normal stochastic variations, we apply a recently developed principal-component-based image distinguishability analysis test. We find that for fixed shock strength and orientation relative to the crystal, the spatial localization of thermal and nonthermal energy in hot spots formed in initially hot and cold TATB crystals is statistically indistinguishable from the room-temperature baseline in most cases. However, the simulations also provide tentative evidence that the shear band ignition mode in TATB may depend on initial temperature through modulation of the density of the band network. These results are expected to help guide treatments of variable initial temperature in macroscale IHE detonation models that are based on the hot spot concept.

papers.title: Synthesis of Ni[O2NN¢] Complexes and their use as Catalysts for Ring-Opening and Ring-Opening Copolymerization of Cyclohexene Oxide and Phthalic Anhydride
papers.abstract: A series of air-stable nickel(II) complexes with various tetradentate diaminobis(phenol)/(phenolate) ligands and coligands were synthesized. Six of these Ni[O2NN¢] complexes were structurally characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The Ni[O2NN¢] complexes were screened as catalysts for ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of cyclohexene oxide (CHO) and phthalic anhydride (PA) utilizing bis(triphenylphosphine)iminium chloride (PPNCl) as a cocatalyst. It was determined that the catalytic activity for the Ni[O2NN¢] complexes depended primarily on the coordinating coligands/counterions and the presence of a cocatalyst. Ni[O2NN¢] complexes with acetate or chloride coligands selectively formed high molar mass polyesters with narrow dispersities (e.g. Mn = 14.5 kg mol−1 and Đ = Mw/Mn = 1.17), but only in the presence of the PPNCl cocatalyst. Ni[O2NN¢] complexes with perchlorate counterions formed polymers containing a mixture of ester and ether linkages in the presence of PPNCl cocatalyst, and instead selectively formed polyether when no cocatalyst was used.

papers.title: TorchFF: A High-Performance GPU-accelerated Differentiable Force Field Library
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) and the development of next-generation force fields (FFs) increasingly rely on automatic differentiation (AD) for efficient simulated property prediction and parameter optimization. However, standard FFs and machine learning (ML) frameworks often suffer from significant performance bottlenecks—such as kernel launch overhead and memory bandwidth limitations—when executing the many-atom, small-kernel operations characteristic of MD sim-ulations. Here, we present TorchFF, a high-performance, differentiable library that extends PyTorch with a suite of customized CUDA operators specifically engineered for molecular modeling. By implementing performance-critical routines—including bonded interactions, multipolar electrostatics, Particle Mesh Ewald (PME), and neighbor list searches—as backend-optimized primitives, TorchFF bridges the gap between the flexible Python ecosystem and the execution speed of compiled MD engines.

papers.title: SOMO–HOMO Inversion in a Radical Cation Derived from a Phenyl-Substituted Highly-Strained Cage Diketone Identified Using g-Tensor Analysis
papers.abstract: SOMO–HOMO inversion (SHI), a phenomenon in which a singly occupied molecular orbital (SOMO) of a radical species has a lower energy than a highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO), is expected to have novel functional consequences. The single strategy developed thus far for creating SHI radicals involves introducing a strong electron-donating group into a stable radical. This restriction limits studies of the properties of SHI radicals. Here, we report that one-electron oxidation of the highly-strained cage diketone C-1 leads to formation of the unprecedented SHI radical cation C-1 •+ , which consists of a spin-localized s framework surrounded by multiple phenyl groups. The SHI phenomenon in C-1 •+ stems from electronic features of the HOMO and HOMO–1 of C-1 , which demonstrates for the first time in a real system that SHI radicals can be designed from their closed-shell precursors. Moreover, results arising from a combination of time-resolved (TR) ESR spectroscopy and theoretical calculations reveal that the g ZZ value of C-1 •+ is smaller than that of a free electron. Based on Pryce’s equation, this finding shows that C-1 •+ is an SHI radical cation. This g -tensor analysis is a novel method for direct determination of SHI in even short-lived radicals.

papers.title: Impact of DNA Sequence and Structure on Polyelectrolyte Complex Micelle Morphology
papers.abstract: Polyelectrolyte complex micelles (PCMs) are promising nucleic acid nanocarriers, however, nucleic acids are usually treated as generic polyanions, leaving the impact of nucleotide sequence and partially hybridized structures unclear. Here we systematically tune DNA stiffness in PCMs using (i) single-stranded sequences with varied purine content and (ii) hybridization structure in the form of hairpins, single-tailed duplexes, and double-tailed duplexes.
