Small-angle X-ray scattering, electron microscopy, and dynamic light scattering reveal a strong bending penalty imposed by increasing DNA stiffness that drives a transition from spherical to less-curved cylindrical or worm-like PCMs with ordered cores. Increasing purine content produces gradual morphological changes, whereas hybridized constructs show sharper transitions. We further link the availability of base-stacking sites to cylindrical PCM length and find that longer block copolymers lower the DNA-stiffness threshold for cylinder formation consistent with larger PCMs. The results establish design rules connecting DNA sequence, structure, and polymer length to PCM morphology.

papers.title: Charge and Spin Aware Graph Neural Network with Spin-polarized Charge Equilibration Method
papers.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer a computationally efficient and accurate approach for simulating complex chemical systems at the atomistic level. However, their predictive capabilities require further refinement to address broader chemical phenomena. This study introduces a charge-and spin-aware ability to equivariant graph neural network MLIPs that has the ability to predict energies, forces, and atomic charges and atomic spin moments in chemical systems. A novel spin-dependent charge equilibration (QEq) method is proposed, extending the MLIP’s applicability to spin-polarized systems. The spin-polarized QEq-enabled MACE models were benchmarked against density functional theory reference datasets, achieving superior predictive accuracy. Notably, the model accurately reproduces polaron distributions on the TiO2 (110) surface, demonstrating its robustness in capturing spin-related properties. This advancement significantly improves the versatility and precision of MLIPs, enabling more reliable atomistic simulations in chemistry and materials science.

papers.title: The Untapped Potential of Dietary Compounds Against KRAS G12V: Virtual Screening Identifies Novel Drug Scaffolds for an Undrugged Oncology Target
papers.abstract: KRAS is the most frequently mutated oncogene in human cancer, driving approximately 25% of all solid tumours and the majority of pancreatic, colorectal, and non-small cell lung cancers. The Switch-II Pocket (SII-P), a cryptic GDP-state allosteric site, has transformed KRAS from an undruggable target into a clinically validated one through the FDA-approved covalent G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib, noncovalent G12D-selective agents, and the pan-RAS molecular glue daraxonrasib. This progress, however, remains unevenly distributed across KRAS variants. No approved therapy exists for KRAS G12V — the second most prevalent oncogenic substitution and a dominant driver in colorectal carcinoma, which precludes covalent pharmacology and confers reduced affinity to existing SII-P scaffolds. Dietary natural products represent a structurally diverse chemical space with varying degrees of human safety precedent that has never been systematically evaluated against the KRAS G12V SII-P. We screened 4,289 drug-like compounds from the FooDB dietary library against KRAS G12V (PDB: 8AZZ) and wild-type KRAS (PDB: 4OBE) using AutoDock Vina 1.2.5, applying a dual-filter for strong predicted G12V affinity (≤ −9.5 kcal/mol) and selectivity matching the clinical-stage reference BI-2865 (ΔΔG ≤ −2.36 kcal/mol). Systematic artefact triage of the top 50 candidates yielded 13 curated leads: 3 method-validation controls and 10 novel leads spanning nine scaffold classes, each profiled across six CRC-relevant KRAS variants and nine Ras-superfamily GTPases. The screen recovers graveoline, a compound experimentally confirmed as a direct KRAS binder by the NCI RAS Initiative, as a method-validation control, and identifies ten novel scaffold classes with no prior KRAS-binding evidence. Erinacine E, a cyathane diterpenoid from Hericium erinaceus , is proposed as the primary experimental candidate on the basis of predicted binding affinity, the strongest food-use safety record among novel leads, consistent KRAS selectivity over all nine Ras-superfamily GTPases, and an essentially isolated position in drug-like chemical space. Gerberinol, a symmetric bicoumarin, emerges as a complementary pan-KRAS lead, outperforming BI-2865 simultaneously against G12V, G12D, and G12C.

papers.title: Strain-Accelerated β-Thiolactone Native Chemical Ligation with Kinetic Proofreading Enables Rapid and Selective Hydrogelation for Biofabrication
papers.abstract: Native chemical ligation (NCL) offers a route to form amide-linked hydrogels under mild aqueous conditions, yet its implementation in biomaterials has been constrained by slow kinetics, free-thiol byproducts, and inhibition in chemically complex environments. Here, we demonstrate that deliberate electrophile design through incorporation of a strain encoded βthiolactone enables rapid and selective NCL-mediated hydrogel formation with a “kinetic proofreading” mechanism. A penicillamine-derived β-thiolactone cross-linker synthesized directly on four-arm polyethylene glycol (PEG, 10 kDa) exhibits fast gelation (tgel ≈ 108 s) in complete cell culture media while maintaining orthogonality to embedded human dermal fibroblasts. Relative to a conventional alkyl thioester and a γ-thiolactone analogue, the strained β-thiolactone displays accelerated gelation and enhanced tolerance to competing endogenous thiols. Mechanistically, geminal dimethyl substitution promotes rapid β-thiolactone recyclization, suppressing unproductive thiol exchange while productive NCL proceeds through an irreversible S-to-N acyl shift. This kinetic control enables direct peptide incorporation during gelation, hydrogel microfiber fabrication, and long-term three-dimensional cell encapsulation. These findings establish electrophile strain and recyclization kinetics as design parameters for engineering selective and mechanically functional covalent biomaterials.

papers.title: Bridging Surface Dynamics and Phase Transitions in CsPbI3 Perovskite With Machine-Learning Force Fields and Dispersion Interactions
papers.abstract: In the rapidly evolving field of machine learning (ML) for atomistic simulations of materials and molecules, achieving transferability across different systems remains a key challenge. In this contribution, we demonstrate a case of transfer learning in which an ML model trained exclusively on surface slab data of the cubic (α) phase of CsPbI 3 perovskite can reproduce the key features of the dynamic behavior for different phases of the bulk material. Using an equivariant message-passing network (MACE) architecture, we construct an efficient ML force-field trained on the dataset obtained from the ab initio molecular dynamics simulations of a CsPbI 3 slab. The resulting model yields stable and reliable trajectories for both slab and bulk, reproducing the experimentally observed phase transitions of CsPbI 3 . We demonstrate that pairwise dispersion methods (TS/D3) mispredict the correct phase of CsPbI 3 bulk at ambient conditions, while more advanced approaches (MBD-NL/rVV10) recover both the experimentally observed phase sequence with increasing temperature (orthorhombic–tetragonal–cubic) and the corresponding phase-transition temperatures. The main source of this discrepancy is the crucial dependence of Cs forces on the level of description of van der Waals (vdW) dispersion. Overall, our results demonstrate that surface–slab datasets augmented with an accurate treatment of vdW dispersion provide a robust foundation for constructing transferable machine-learning force fields that consistently describe both surface and bulk behavior across multiple length scales.

papers.title: Quaternary Structure Governs Ultrafast Energy Transfer in Red Fluorescent Proteins
papers.abstract: Red fluorescent proteins (RFPs) are widely used as genetically encoded reporters and biosensors, yet their photophysics is often interpreted within a framework that treats the chromophore as an isolated fluorophore in solution. Such descriptions overlook interactions among chromophores and with the surrounding protein matrix, which can play a decisive role in ultrafast excited-state dynamics. Here, we investigate these dynamics in a homologous series of RFPs, mCherry, tdTomato, and DsRed2, spanning monomeric to tetrameric quaternary structures, using femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy and anisotropy measurements. We find that oligomerization promotes interchromophore energy transfer between subunits, giving rise to rapid depolarization dynamics absent in monomeric systems. In the tetramer DsRed2, we further resolve an ultrafast energy transfer pathway between spectrally distinct chromophore forms, directly revealing coupling between chemically heterogeneous states within a single protein assembly. These results demonstrate that ultrafast excited-state dynamics in RFPs are governed by collective effects arising from quaternary structure and chromophore heterogeneity, highlighting the limitations of isolated chromophore models and establishing a multichromophoric framework for interpreting fluorescent protein photophysics.

papers.title: Optimized Sodium-Enhanced MALDI-2 Enables Multimodal Imaging of Triacylglycerols
papers.abstract: Triacylglycerols (TAGs) are essential neutral lipids with critical roles in cellular function and disease. However, spatial characterization of these chemical species remains difficult because neutral molecules often exhibit low ionization efficiency with common mass spectrometry-based imaging strategies, such as matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization imaging mass spectrometry (MALDI IMS). Here, we assess how ammonium formate (AmF) or sodium carbonate buffer solution (CBS) tissue washes, combined with varying primary laser power, affect TAG sensitivity with and without MALDI-2 postionization. We found that Na + doping using Na + CBS washes combined with MALDI-2 at 31% total laser power was optimal for both signal intensity and molecular coverage. Additionally, Na + CBS-washed tissues enabled MALDI-2 to be performed using lower laser powers, making this method compatible with sequential microscopy experiments as part of multimodal workflows. Applying this strategy to diseased brain tissue enabled spatial mapping of TAGs linked to Alzheimer’s pathology. This approach balances sensitivity and tissue preservation, providing a robust platform for multimodal spatial lipidomic studies across diverse tissues and disease contexts.

papers.title: Mixed Computational/Experimental Screening for Aqueous Organic Redox Flow Battery Negolytes
papers.abstract: A library of 45 million drug-like compounds was constructed and screened using a combined computational and experimental approach to identify three scaffold structures previously unreported as organic redox flow battery (ORFB) negolytes. Candidate scaffolds were identified through computational screening of reduction potentials, triaged via literature search, and characterized electrochemically. Three scaffolds—pyrido[1,2-a]pyrimidine, saccharin, and thiopyran—showed measurable redox activity. Initial cyclic voltammetry of synthesized derivatives revealed the key challenges for each that must be addressed for development into viable aqueous ORFB negolytes.

papers.title: Effect of Solvent Processing on Transport and Cycling Properties of All-Solid-State Battery Composite Cathodes
papers.abstract: The performance of sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries is commonly evaluated in press cells, and the accompanying positive composite electrodes are typically prepared via dry mixing. Changing the setup to pouch cells would be favorable in terms of reproducibility and industrial relevance but requires the preparation of positive electrodes via solvent-based processes and tape casting. However, the effect of solvents on the interfaces and performance of positive electrode composites is still understudied. Thus, we investigate the effect of o-xylene solvent treatment on the microstructure, effective transport and cycling properties of a positive composite electrode based on Li6PS5Cl and a Nirich electroactive material. We show that xylene slightly reduces the effective ionic conductivity and stronger influences the electronic conductivity of the composite electrodes. Ex-situ spectroscopy characterization indicates possible interfacial layers on top of the NMC particles as the main factors after the xylene treatment which lead to the observed deterioration in cycling behavior.

papers.title: Unactivated Photoredox C–H Amination with Diazirines: Access to Acyldiaziridines.
papers.abstract: A metal-free, photoinduced amination of unactivated C–H bonds from abundant, simple alkanes with diazirines is reported. The transformation provides diversifiable diaziridine products (39 examples) in up to 95% yield. The conditions are suitable for four different classes of C–H bonds, including aldehydes, which results in the formation of previously unavailable acyldiaziridines. This class of molecules is shown to be a versatile precursor that is easily converted to amides, hydrazides, acyl hydrazones, and heterocycles.

papers.title: Unlocking the Potential of Diphosphinoboranes: A Modular Route to Tunable Ambiphilic Ligands
papers.abstract: A new synthetic approach to accessing a wide range of diphosphinoborane ligands and their coordination behaviour to low-valent nickel centres is described. The synthetic route negates the use of ArBCl2, which are challenging to access, and utilizes readily available aryl boronic esters as the boron source. The steric and electronic properties of these diphosphinoboranes (RDPBAr) ligands were elucidated through a combined experimental and computational study focused on Ni(0) complexes. Analysis of the steric properties reveal these ligands all exhibit large bite angles, percentage buried volumes and G-factors. The electronic analysis indicates that the effect of changing the aryl group on the borane, significantly impacts the degree of σ-back donation, with electron deficient groups strengthening this interaction. The structural impact of these ligands leads to the formation of a rare mono-carbonyl Ni(0) complex.

papers.title: The Canalised Cleavage of Glucosepane
papers.abstract: We report two mechanistically distinct catalytic chemistries for cleavage of glucosepane, the most abundant protein–protein advanced glycation end-product (AGE) crosslink of aged human extracellular matrix. Glucosepane exceeds every other AGE crosslink in collagen and elastin by ~10–100-fold and accumulates progressively throughout life. Beyond the commonly cited tissue-mechanical consequences — arterial stiffening (the strongest independent predictor of cardiovascular mortality in the elderly), renal basement-membrane thickening, reduced pulmonary and joint compliance, and the accelerated vascular aging of diabetes [6–9] — AGE crosslinking of basement-membrane type IV collagen and laminin disrupts integrin-mediated cell–matrix engagement, impairs endothelial adhesion, and drives a premature senescence-like endothelial phenotype (Haitoglou et al., J Biol Chem 1992 [78]; Chen et al., Circ Res 2002 [79]); AGE accumulation and RAGE-mediated signalling at the neurovascular unit are associated with blood–brain-barrier breakdown, pericyte injury, and the cognitive decline of aging and Alzheimer’s disease (Deane et al., Nat Med 2003 [80]; Montagne et al., Neuron 2015 [81]; Sweeney et al., Nat Rev Neurol 2018 [82]). Yet no peer-reviewed chemical cleavage method has been reported in the two decades since the crosslink’s structural identification (Sell et al., J Biol Chem 2005 [4]) nor in the decade since its total synthesis (Draghici, Wang, and Spiegel, Science 2015 [10]); every clinical AGE-breaker (alagebrium, aminoguanidine, pyridoxamine, carnosine) is mechanistically incompatible with glucosepane’s bicyclic aminal–amidine core. The two chemistries converge on a shared ring-opened iminium intermediate. Strategy I is thermal: Lewis acid and mild-acid catalysis raise the ring-opening equilibrium of the bicyclic aminal, and an α-effect nucleophile traps the transient intermediate irreversibly into a thermodynamic sink. Strategy II is photoredox: visible-light single-electron oxidation generates the lysine-side N1 radical cation, and β-scission of the adjacent strained C–N bond produces an irreversible ring-opened fragment. Because each strategy's principal parameter weakness is offset by the other, and because the radical cation required for Strategy II is also accessible by electrochemistry, sonodynamics, and near-infrared activation (Section 6), the architecture tolerates parameter failure in any single channel; kinetic selectivity follows from strained-heterocycle-specific radical fragmentation (Section 4). Aged collagen matrix itself contributes four independent factors that further favor the intervention at the lesion site (Section 5). Each chemical element is independently falsifiable within weeks of bench work at reagent costs of thousands of dollars, with tiered tests and explicit kill criteria specified (Section 9; SI Table S4). Intrafibrillar delivery is addressable through the anti-glucosepane Glu3 DNA aptamer (Li et al., Nanoscale Horizons 2025 [74]). Should the chemistry withstand the proposed tests, the result will be the first chemistry-based cleavage of the dominant human AGE crosslink and the first demonstration that a canalised chemistry can address a class of accumulated protein lesions for which no repair pathway — endogenous or synthetic — has previously been established.

papers.title: pH-Inverted Histidine-Rich Nanochelants for Trapping Furin-Processed Polycationic Nanotoxins: A Quantum-Classical Platform for Dual Heavy-Metal Detoxification and Broad-Spectrum Countermeasures
papers.abstract: Furin cleaves polybasic sites in endosomes and the secretory pathway, releasing linear (>3 net positive charges) and concentric (metal-coordinating) nanotoxins that drive metabolic disease, cytokine storms, neurodegeneration, autoimmunity, cancer immune evasion, and infection. We introduce 5H-EAF, an erythritol-capped linear penta-histidine nanochelant (MW ≈ 868 Da) that activates to +4–5 net charge at endosomal pH 5.5–6.5, trapping these species via electrostatic clamping and coordination, then deprotonates and releases harmlessly at neutral pH. DFT (B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVP, explicit solvation) yields Pb²⁺ ΔG = –11 to –16 kcal/mol (low pH) → –3 to –6 kcal/mol (neutral); SARS-CoV-2 PRRAR⁺ motif clamping ΔG ≈ –8 to –13 kcal/mol; and anthrax PA63 pore blockade analogous to validated cationic blockers (Kd nM–µM, planar-bilayer literature) supported by all-atom MD simulations (MM-PBSA ΔG = −28.7 kcal/mol at pH 5.5). The platform speaks furin’s native pH/Ca²⁺/charge language without global inhibition. It unifies GLP-1 optimization, cytokine control, α-syn/amyloid management, Pb neuroprotection, and biodefense against furin-dependent pathogens (anthrax, Ebola, H5N1, SARS-CoV-2, Dengue).

papers.title: Enhanced electronic coupling in tetraaryl molecular junctions with osmium(IV) centers
papers.abstract: Structural motifs based on tetraphenylmethane are widely used in molecular electronic circuits, self-assembled monolayers, and porous frameworks, but their performance in conductive systems is often limited by redox-inactive, sp 3 -hybridized central atoms that interrupt π-conjugation. Here, we show that replacing the group 14 central atom with a tetravalent transition metal provides a design strategy to enhance electronic coupling and enable bias-dependent control of charge transport. We demonstrate this by measuring the single-molecule conductance of oligoaryl wires incorporating tetrahedral osmium(IV), silicon, or carbon centers using scanning tunneling microscope-based break junction measurements. In non-polar solvents, junctions comprising osmium(IV) complexes exhibit a significantly reduced conductance decay with length compared to their organic analogues. In polar media, their conductance can be electrochemically modulated to values up to 80× higher than those of a silane analogue. Combined electrochemical and spectroscopic studies, supported by first-principles calculations, indicate that osmium(IV) wires exhibit more delocalized frontier orbitals and smaller HOMO-LUMO gaps, leading to well-coupled HOMO-derived transmission resonances near the electrode Fermi level. Together, these results establish transition metal tetraaryl complexes as promising building blocks for molecular circuits and extended materials.

papers.title: From Photon Spiral Motion to Superheavy Elements: A Unified Analytical Atomic-Molecular Energy Theory Based on Quantum Phase Vortices and Relativistic Corrections
papers.abstract: Within the constructive theoretical framework, this work establishes the Ether-Vortex Atomic and Molecular Model (EVAM), a fully analytical energy scheme covering the entire periodic table with atomic numbers from to . Three foundational constructive physical pictures, namely photon spiral propagation, etheric structural medium, and electron quantum phase vortex, are introduced with methodological status analogous to imaginary numbers in mathematics. They do not claim ontological physical reality, but merely serve as instrumental structures for unifying theoretical formalism, simplifying analytical derivation, and sustaining self-consistent and stable computation. EVAM adopts exponential wave packets to characterize electronic spatial distributions, realizing strictly analytical integration of all Coulomb interactions while completely eliminating basis sets, numerical integration, and self-consistent field iterations. The computational complexity is reduced to . A constructive relativistic wave packet width formula is constructed to achieve automatic wave packet saturation, which fundamentally eliminates computational divergence for heavy and superheavy elements, enabling uniform, stable, and high-precision descriptions across light, heavy, and superheavy nuclides. Resting on only 10 globally fixed parameters, EVAM achieves chemical accuracy for light atoms and small molecules. For heavy elements, deviations from Dirac–Fock reference data remain below , while superheavy element results are provided exclusively for theoretical benchmarking. All calculations are completed within milliseconds to seconds on a conventional single personal computer. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations attain approximately 115-fold speedup relative to parallel DFT-AIMD computations. Within the constructive paradigm, the model uniformly interprets electron correlation, chemical bonding, and relativistic effects. It can be employed as an independent computational tool for material simulation, catalytic mechanism research, and theoretical investigations of superheavy elements.

papers.title: Organic Chemistry in Practice: Student Learning from Wittig and Epoxidation Experiments in a CURE Framework
papers.abstract: Course-based Undergraduate Research Experiences (CUREs) in undergraduate teaching laboratories are a growing tool for establishing science retention, confidence, and tolerance for obstacles. However, very few examples demonstrating these results have been reported in primarily undergraduate institutions (PUIs), subject to related limitations of scale and instructor support. This article describes the design and implementation of a CURE for second-semester organic chemistry students, consisting of a multi-week sequence including a Wittig reaction with cinnamaldehyde and subsequent epoxidation of asymmetric diene Wittig products. Students collaborated to collect reaction condition data and were tasked with a presentation at the conclusion of the project, fostering communication and collaboration skills. Students were also asked to provide both quantitative and qualitative feedback. Assessment data indicate gains in student confidence, frustration tolerance, identification of experimental challenges, and presentation skills. This work provides a model for future work adapting the outcomes and goals of a CURE to primarily undergraduate institutions.

papers.title: D33E mutation reshapes active and inactive conformations of KRAS
papers.abstract: GTP-bound KRAS cycles between inactive and active conformations through coordinated rearrangements of Switch I and Switch II, yet the structural and kinetic consequences of many clinically observed mutations remain unresolved. The rare D33E substitution lies within the electrostatic network of Switch I and, despite being chemically conservative, exhibits tumorigenesis. Here, we use extensive atomistic simulations and Markov state models (MSMs) of GTP-bound KRAS to characterize how D33E reshapes its conformational landscape and kinetics, including its propensity to sample conformations associated with CRAF binding. Free energy projections along established distance-based reaction coordinates d 1 and d 2 (distances from C a atoms of residues 60 and 35 to γ phosphate) reveal that D33E stabilises switch GTP engaged conformations. Structural mapping of experimentally derived RAS structures onto the simulated landscape identifies two clusters: an inactive cluster and an active, effector binding competent cluster. MSM analysis reveals that D33E substantially enriches the fully switch engaged S1 ensemble, primarily through a sevenfold reduction in exit rates rather than accelerated entry. The negatively charged E37 side chain adopts a new conformation in low d 2 states, not observed in the wildtype, correlating with movements in E62 towards the GTP nucleotide, promoting the S 1 state. S 1 overlaps with experimentally observed effector-bound and GAP-bound complexes in the structural mapping. Within this binding-competent ensemble, D33E rigidifies both switch regions locally and reduces the frequency at which Q61 adopts the catalytic approach geometry required for GAP-stimulated hydrolysis. Together, these observations are consistent with the biochemical profile of D33E, in which enhanced effector binding coincides with substantially reduced GAP stimulated catalysis. This suggests ensemble level population redistribution as a potential contributing mechanism to the oncogenic signaling of D33E. These results shed new light on understanding how mutations modulate KRAS activity.

papers.title: Effect of Solvent Environment and Surface Oxidation on Asphaltene Adsorption at Graphene Oxide Interfaces
papers.abstract: Asphaltene deposition remains a persistent challenge in crude oil recovery, yet the molecular mechanisms governing its adsorption at solid interfaces are not fully understood. In this work, graphene oxide (GO) is used as a model heterogeneous surface to investigate the effects of surface oxidation and solvent environment on asphaltene adsorption using enhanced sampling simulations. A solvent-dependent reversal in adsorption preference is observed: adsorption is favored on more reduced GO surfaces in toluene, but on more oxidized GO surfaces in heptane. This behavior arises from a shift in dominant interaction mechanisms. In toluene, adsorption is governed by π–π interactions with graphitic regions, whereas in heptane, adsorption occurs primarily at oxygen-containing functional groups. Notably, partial exposure of the aromatic core to graphitic domains in oxidized GO enables a mixed adsorption configuration that enhances stabilization. These findings demonstrate that asphaltene adsorption is controlled by a solvent-dependent balance between competing interactions and surface heterogeneity, providing molecular-level insight into interfacial processes relevant to asphaltene deposition.

papers.title: Interpreting and Visualizing VSA Descriptors through VSA Explainer
papers.abstract: Van der Waals Surface Area (VSA) descriptors are physicochemical descriptors frequently used in machine learning (ML)-driven molecular property prediction and quantitative structure–activity relationships (QSAR), yet their binned, aggregated nature makes them difficult to interpret at the atom level. No existing tools decompose VSA descriptor values into atomic contributions for visual interpretation. Here, we present VSA Explainer, an open-source Python tool that enables the interpretation of all five RDKit VSA descriptor families (SlogP VSA, SMR VSA, PEOE VSA, EState VSA, and VSA EState) by highlighting peratom contributions within molecular structures. We demonstrate VSA Explainer on a blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability model as a case study, showing how atomic-level VSA decomposition reveals structure-permeability relationships that aggregate descriptors such as the topological polar surface area (TPSA) cannot capture. For example, beta blockers metoprolol and oxprenolol have identical TPSA yet differ four-fold in brain-to-plasma ratio, and VSA decomposition using VSA Explainer localizes the difference to the allyl ether substituent. VSA Explainer bridges the gap between the predictive power of VSA descriptors and chemical interpretability, enabling medicinal chemists to connect model-identified features to actionable structural insights.

papers.title: Phosphonium Ions as Activating Groups for the Selective Alkylation of Pyridines and Polyazines
papers.abstract: The Minisci reaction is a broadly applicable method for coupling carbon-bearing groups to pyridines, but suffers from poor regio- and site-selectivity, particularly in complex structures. Here, we show that C4-phosphonium salts serve as activating groups in Minisci alkylation processes. In this way, radicals add selectively to pyridines, bearing phosphonium salts over those that don’t in polypyridine structures. Furthermore, the phosphonium salt serves as a blocking group, ensuring regioselective alkylation at the 2-position. The C–P bond is easily cleavable in a simple workup procedure or can be used as a versatile functional handle to construct 2,4-disubstituted pyridines. We also show that site-selective switching reactions are possible by controlling the site of C–P bond formation in drug-like structures.

papers.title: Programmable Chirality Transfer: Seeding-Directed Co-assembly of Functional Molecules with Amyloid Frameworks
papers.abstract: We report a highly effective and universal strategy for linking small achiral functional molecules with amyloid fibrils, enabling efficient transfer of chirality from the chiral amyloid network to supramolecularly co-assembled entities. This seeding-and-co-assembly approach, based on incorporating functional molecules (e.g., dyes) during ongoing seed-directed amyloid formation, facilitates their templating by the amyloid framework while constraining fibril morphological diversity through suppression of secondary nucleation. Chirality transfer is evidenced by pronounced induced electronic circular dichroism (IECD) and vibrational circular dichroism (IVCD), with anisotropy factors (g) reaching up to 1.3*10-2 (gECD) and 1.5*10-3 (gVCD). The induced chirality arises either from supramolecular ordering of flexible molecules on the fibril surface or from incorporation of more rigid pigment molecules into the amyloid framework. Importantly, this process is tunable: dye concentration and solvent type act as programmable parameters that modulate hierarchical organization and chiroptical properties of the resulting assemblies. Overall, this strategy establishes amyloid fibrils as versatile chiral scaffolds for the rational design of hybrid nanomaterials exhibiting strong circular dichroism and/or circularly polarized luminescence.

papers.title: Interplay of Bridge Topology and Conformation in Phenylene-bridged Trityl Biradicals
papers.abstract: Tuning the exchange coupling constant J in multi-spin systems is a valuable tool in the rational design of molecular systems for applications in molecular magnetism, quantum information science, and dynamic nuclear polarization. The phenylene group is an archetypal bridge to couple spins and tune the sign and magnitude of J via topology and substitution. However, there are various examples where meta -phenylene bridges give against the topological rule rise to antiferromagnetic instead of the expected ferromagnetic coupling. Motivated by this, we synthesized an m -phenylene-bridged trityl biradical ( m -ben-(TAM) 2 •• ) and explored its magnetic coupling in comparison to the p -phenylene- and p -xylene-bridged analogues. Using Vibrating Sample Magnetometry (VSM), an unexpected weak antiferromagnetic coupling of -4 GHz is found for m -ben-(TAM) 2 •• in the powder, whereas it increases to -169 GHz in solution based on EPR data. This finding can be rationalized by a large structural change between powder and solution, as investigated by density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. We speculate that these geometric changes lead to changes in the σ-, π-, and through-space contributions to the electronic spin-spin coupling. These results highlight that the design of ferromagnetic molecular magnets cannot only be based on the topological rule.

papers.title: Synthesis of Polyesters from CO2 and Non-Conjugated Terminal Alkynes and Alkyl Halides
papers.abstract: Previous work has shown success in copolymerizing CO2 with aryl-conjugated diynes and dihalides in the presence of silver catalysts, resulting in polyesters with moderate molecular weights. We hypothesized that AB-type monomers, containing both non-conjugated terminal alkynes and alkyl bromides, would allow for a broader scope of monomers to be polymerized, derived from commercial propargyl bromide and bio-derived phenols. Polymerizing propargyl bromide under 14 atm of CO2 in the presence of Cs2CO3 and catalytic AgI and NHC ligand resulted in an intractable powder. As such, we sought to probe this reaction via a series of small-molecule studies. Most surprisingly, these studies revealed that the bromide functional group was susceptible to a competitive SN2 reaction with Cs2CO3, which we believe partially explains the inability of previous systems to reach high molecular weights. Following these preliminary studies, we polymerized a series of nonconjugated diyne monomer with alkyl dibromides, resulting in polymers with moderate Mn values and narrow dispersities. Finally, we synthesized AB-type monomers from bioderived phenols including vanillin and 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde. Polymerization of monomers with benzyl bromides resulted in poorly-soluble molecules due to the competitive carbonate formation. However, the longer alkyl chain a phloretic acidderived monomer allowed for successful polymerization, with a comparable molecular weight to the successful AA/BB-type polymerizations. The modularity of this system will allow us to target new polyesters with desired physical and thermal properties while allowing for further postpolymerizations using the internal alkyne moieties.

papers.title: Iridium(III) Complexes in Visible-Light Energy Transfer Catalysis: Synthetic Applications and Reaction Mechanisms
papers.abstract: Iridium(III) complexes have emerged as powerful and versatile photocatalysts for visible-light-mediated energy transfer (EnT) catalysis. Their uniquely tunable photophysical properties, such as triplet energy, excited-state lifetime, and steric environment play crucial role in controlling reactivity, selectivity, and substrate activation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of Ir-based photocatalysis operating via triplet-triplet energy transfer (TT-EnT), enabling transformations that are inaccessible through conventional thermal or photoredox pathways. We summarize the advances in organic synthesis enabled by Ir(III) photosensitizers in three sections based on the mechanism: (i) transformations proceeding via pure EnT pathways; (ii) processes involving the interplay between EnT and single electron transfer (SET); and (iii) EnT-enabled dual metal catalysis. These strategies enable controlled access to reactive excited states, providing a versatile platform for divergent and selective synthesis of complex molecular frameworks, including cyclic scaffolds commonly found in natural products and bioactive molecules. The detailed reaction mechanisms, including photoinduced intermediates and their role in governing reactivity and selectivity, as well as synthetic potential are the main focus in this review.

papers.title: Ultra-High-Density Double-Stranded DNA Loading on Gold Nanoparticles for Robust Triggering of DNA Circuits
papers.abstract: DNA-functionalised gold nanoparticles (DNA-AuNPs) enable molecular sensing, structural assembly and nanooptics by combining the superior optical characteristics of gold nanoparticles with the programmability of DNA. While conjugation of gold nanoparticles with single-stranded DNA (ssDNA-AuNPs) at high density has been established, conjugation of gold nanoparticles with double-stranded DNA (dsDNA-AuNPs) remained difficult because complementary-strand hybridisation is strongly hindered on crowded nanoparticle surfaces. This limits applications that require duplex DNA, including cargo loading, controlled strand release, and coupling to downstream DNA circuits. Here, we show that this accessibility bottleneck can be overcome by thermally annealing complementary strands onto densely grafted ssDNA-AuNPs, yielding dsDNA surface densities of up to 0.25 dsDNA nm-2, about 6fold higher than previously reported post-hybridisation values. Using 24–54 nm AuNPs and four representative DNA architectures, we systematically resolve how sequence design and nanoparticle size govern ssDNA loading, dsDNA formation, colloidal stability, triggered release, and downstream activation of a catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) circuit. Spacercontaining, unstructured sequences provided the best balance between dense surface coverage and functional accessibility. Released complementary strands remained active at the tens-ofnanomolar level and successfully triggered CHA. Our work establishes sequence- and sizeresolved design rules for engineering dense yet functional dsDNA coronas on AuNPs for responsive nanomaterials, controlled nucleic-acid release, and nanoparticle-coupled molecular computation.

papers.title: VERA: A Visual Node-Based Workflow Platform for Integrated Computational Chemistry and Bioinformatics
papers.abstract: VERA (Virtual Execution and Reaction Architecture) is an open-source, extensible, desktopnative visual workflow platform engineered for computational chemistry, molecular modeling, and bioinformatics research. VERA addresses the persistent and well-documented challenge of integrating heterogeneous scientific tools, including molecular docking engines (AutoDock Vina CPU/GPU), molecular dynamics simulators (GROMACS), cheminformatics libraries (RDKit, OpenBabel), machine learning frameworks (scikit-learn), and publication-quality visualization engines, into a unified, reproducible computational environment accessible to researchers without programming expertise. Built on a directed acyclic graph (DAG) execution paradigm using Python 3.13 and PySide6 (Qt6), VERA provides 106 specialized processing nodes organized across 13 functional categories, covering the complete in silico drug discovery pipeline from molecular input and preparation through structure-based virtual screening, molecular dynamics simulation, statistical analysis, machine learning, and publication-quality visualization. The platform implements a formally defined type-safe port system with 9 canonical data types and automatic compatibility checking, a thread-safe asynchronous workflow execution engine with real-time per-node progress monitoring and subprocess lifecycle management, atomic workflow serialization to a JSON-based format (.vsw), and a plugin architecture enabling community-driven extension of the node library. The theoretical foundations, system architecture, and implementation of key subsystems including the topological execution scheduler, the type inference engine, and the concurrency model are detailed, alongside representative workflows for virtual screening and molecular dynamics analysis with quantitative performance characterization, situating VERA's design decisions within the broader context of reproducible computational science. VERA is freely available under the MIT License at https://github.com/Arifmaulanaazis/Vera.

papers.title: Synergistic Roles of Hydroxyl Groups and Coordinating Ligands in Governing Metal-Specific Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction in Covalent Organic Framework
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction is often framed in terms of metal identity, yet the decisive factor governing reactivity remains the local coordination environment in which that metal is embedded. Here, we demonstrate that a covalent organic framework (COF) can be engineered to encode a hydroxyl–ligand cooperative microenvironment that actively dictates metal-specific catalytic behavior. Using a bipyridine-functionalized, hydroxyl-bearing COF (TU-42) as a platform, we show that postsynthetic incorporation of Fe and Ni produces two fundamentally distinct single-site architectures: a relatively open, electronically adaptive Fe–N/O manifold and a coordination-saturated Ni–N/O/Cl environment. Through a combined electrochemical–spectroscopic–theoretical analysis, we reveal that framework hydroxyl groups do not merely tune the electronic structure, but establish directional hydrogen-bonding interactions with coordinated ligands, dynamically modulating the ligand field and redox accessibility of the active site. This cooperative effect lowers the barrier for nitrate activation, biases reaction topology toward energetically favorable pathways, and enhances the coupling between electron flux and ammonia formation. In contrast, the more rigid and saturated Ni coordination sphere imposes an energetic penalty for substrate access and restricts mechanistic flexibility. This work establishes a design principle in which secondary-sphere interactions embedded within a reticular scaffold govern reaction pathways, offering a route to control electrocatalysis beyond conventional metal-centered strategies.

papers.title: AI Unlocks Superior Catalytic Self-Assembly in Peptides
papers.abstract: Mimicking enzyme efficiency with minimalist peptide scaffolds is a central goal in synthetic biology, yet design is constrained by the huge sequence space and the scarcity of high-quality functional data. Here, we report SAPIENS, a closed-loop framework enabling the de novo design of catalytic self-assembly peptides. Its accuracy stems from a large-scale literature-mined dataset that incorporates robust negative examples to rigorously define self-assembly boundaries. By transferring latent structural rules from relatively abundant assembly data to specific functional predictions, SAPIENS identifies novel sequences that differ from the canonical alternating hydrophobic/hydrophilic pattern. We show that these peptides feature mismatched motifs that reconcile the trade-off between the structural order required for assembly and the local flexibility essential for catalysis. Experimental validation confirms their superior hydrolytic activity across diverse ester substrates and promiscuous oxidative capabilities. This work resolves small-sample challenges and establishes a generalizable strategy for programming functional self-assembling peptides beyond current design limits.

papers.title: Identifying Ice-Philic Protein Patches to Inform the Ice Binding Sites of Antifreeze Proteins
papers.abstract: Antifreeze proteins (AFPs) inhibit ice growth and recrystallization by binding to ice crystals via specific regions on their surface, known as ice-binding sites (IBS). Although the IBS of certain AFPs display regularly-spaced threonine residues that are matched well with the molecular spacings in ice crystals, the IBS of other AFPs lack such structural signatures, making it challenging to identify them. To address this challenge, we introduce a computational framework that systematically promotes ice formation in the AFP hydration shell. We find that ice-philic AFP regions, which form ice in their vicinity most readily, exhibit strong correspondence with the experimentallydetermined IBS. Importantly, such correspondence is observed across a diverse set of AFPs, including those with and without a regular array of threonines. We hope that our framework will expedite the identification of ice-binding sites of newly discovered or designed AFPs.

papers.title: A Miniature Peptide-based Ratiometric, Cell Permeable Sensor Images PI(3,5)P2 Lipid Pools in Organelle Membranes of Living Cells
papers.abstract: Phosphatidylinositol 3,5-bisphosphate [PI(3,5)P2] is a low-abundance phosphoinositide, constituting ~0.05–0.1 mol % of total cellular phosphoinositides, yet plays crucial roles in innate immunity, endolysosomal trafficking, autophagy, and ion channel regulation. Owing to its transient occurrence, fast metabolic turnover, and presence in membranes of acidic intracellular compartments, selective and rapid visualization of PI(3,5)P2 pools in living cells has remained a challenge. Here, we report DAN–TRPML1-PEP , a cell-permeable, peptide-based, ratiometric fluorescent sensor for PI(3,5)P2. The sensor comprises of a 20-amino acid polybasic segment from the N-terminal domain of TRPML1 channel, a native PI(3,5)P2-binding protein. The peptide has been conjugated to a polarity-sensitive dye, 6-dimethylamino-2-acetylnaphthalene (DAN), to afford the sensor. DAN–TRPML1-PEP exhibits a selective ratiometric fluorescence response upon PI(3,5)P2 binding. Importantly, the sensor not only selectively detects PI(3,5)P2 over other physiologically relevant phospholipids but can also distinguish PI(3,5)P2 from closely related phosphoinositides, including PI(3)P and PI(5)P. DAN–TRPML1-PEP rapidly and directly enters living cells and selectively images PI(3,5)P2 within late endosomes, lysosomes, autophagosomes, and endocytic vesicles. The sensor could also be applied for wash-free live-cell imaging of PI(3,5)P2. Hence, DAN–TRPML1-PEP successfully reveals PI(3,5)P2 localization in living cells bringing in a much-required chemical tool for interrogating this key signaling lipid.

papers.title: In Situ Generated Palladium Nanoparticles Catalyzed Intermolecular Reductive Heck Coupling via Transfer Hydrogenation
papers.abstract: The palladium-catalyzed reductive Heck coupling reaction, a well-known transformation, has been used to synthesize numerous challenging compounds, primarily via intramolecular reactions. Counterchallenges, a large catalyst loading, and a tailored ligand were required for the transformation. In the intermediate step following the migratory insertion of Pd into the alkene, hydride transfer is a key step in the reaction, which must occur faster than the β−hydride elimination step to obtain the reductive Heck coupling product, thereby avoiding the Heck-coupled product. Herein, we report in situ-generated palladium nanoparticle (Pd Np)-catalyzed intermolecular reductive Heck coupling, in which isopropanol was used as the hydride source. Under the optimized reaction conditions, styrene ( 1a ) and 1-bromo-4-fluorobenzene ( 2a ) reacted to produce the reductive Heck coupling product 1-fluoro-4-phenethylbenzene (3a) in 98% isolated yield with 0.50 mol% Pd loading. The Pd loading was further decreased to 0.01 mol% for the large-scale reaction. UV-vis studies indicated that Pd nanoparticles formed under the reaction conditions. The nanoparticle nature was further characterized by HRTEM, which revealed that the Pd nanoparticle generated under these conditions had an average diameter of 2–3 nm. The substrate scope of the reaction showed that electron-donating groups gave higher yields than electron-withdrawing groups. The reaction was effective with an unactivated alkene such as 1-octene; however, it yielded a mixture of linear and branched arylated products. The reaction carried out with (CD 3 ) 2 CDOD showed that deuterium was incorporated into the product at the α– and β–positions of the alkene, suggesting 1,2–migration or chain walking of the Pd species. In summary, in situ-generated Pd NPs can catalyze the reductive Heck coupling to give an important class of arylated compounds under ligand-free conditions.

papers.title: A Noble-Gas-Centered Coordinate for Within-Period Ionization Energy Trends and Subshell Anomalies
papers.abstract: We introduce a single dimensionless landscape function Jchem(ρ) = cosh(ρ lnφ)−1, with φ = (1+ √ 5)/2, on the noble-gas-centred coordinate ρ = d/Lp ∈ [0, 1), and show that it organizes the four central atomic observables, first ionization energy IE1, electron affinity EA, Mulliken electronegativity χM , and Pearson chemical hardness η, on a single coordinate axis of the periodic table. Two closed-form landscape steps deliver the four observables: the outward step ∆J+ chem assigned to IE1, and the landscape gap ∆J− chem = Jchem(1)− Jchem(d/Lp) shared by EA and η, with χM following from Mulliken’s identity. Three quantitative results establish the empirical content of the framework. (i) The within-period IE1 envelope reproduces the full noble-gas-to-alkali ordering across periods 2–6: of 34 elements compiled across periods 2–4, 26 lie on the predicted monotone descent, and the 8 deviations sit exactly on the textbook anomaly sites {p3, d5, f7, s2, d10}, recovering inorganic-chemistry shell structure as a single-axis coordinate effect. (ii) Two derived ratio identities, IE1(Gp)/IE1(Gp+1) = φ1/4 for heavy noble-gas pairs and IE1(halogen)/IE1(alkali) = φ2 within a period, agree with NIST data to MAD ≈ 1% and ≈ 5%, respectively, on the benchmark subsets. (iii) The shared-kernel form ∆J− chem provides a one-parameter fit to empirical EA across periods 4–6 (MAE 0.3–0.4 eV), to Pearson hardness η across periods 2–4 (MAE ∼ 1 eV on noble-gas-period-maximum values up to 10.8 eV), and to Mulliken χM across a 15-atom four-class EA/η = C (p) EA/C (p) η is confirmed quantitatively on the period-4 NIST data: the empirical nine-atom mean EA/η = 0.180 matches the predicted constant 0.182 to better than 1%. The framework thus assembles four independent periodic-table observables under a single golden-ratio cosh coordinate, giving a compact analytical reference against which relativistic and shell-anomaly corrections can be quantified.

papers.title: A multifunctional ruthenium(II) polypyridyl complex inhibits amyloid-β aggregation and restores neuronal function in Alzheimer’s disease models
papers.abstract: Progressive accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) assemblies is a defining pathological feature of Alzheimer’s disease, yet chemically defined strategies that both report on and modulate early aggregation remain limited. Here, we develop a series of ruthenium(II) polypyridyl complexes comprising two 2-phenylimidazo[4,5- f ][1,10]phenanthroline (PIP) ligands and a variable diimine ligand. A π-extended dppz derivative (complex 4 ) most effectively suppresses Aβ 1-42 fibrillogenesis, attenuates acetylcholinesterase (AChE) peripheral anionic site (PAS)-facilitated aggregation, and exhibits amyloid-responsive luminescence. Docking, molecular dynamics and enzyme kinetics support engagement of aggregation-prone regions of Aβ and a PAS-proximal surface of AChE. In neuronal models, complex 4 acts as a phosphorescent probe for Aβ, while conferring neuroprotection. In a zebrafish model, it distributes within brain tissue, reduces Aβ deposition, and improves locomotor and cognitive performance. These findings establish a ruthenium coordination scaffold that integrates amyloid recognition, aggregation modulation and luminescent reporting within a single molecular platform, and establishes the potential of metal-based amyloid modulators in treating early-stage Alzheimer’s disease.

papers.title: Lessons Learned from Multi-Year Operation of a Cloud-Hosted Commercial Robot Driven by Domain-Specific Language Models
papers.abstract: The concept of self-driving chemical laboratories builds on top of two technologies: robust artificial intelligence models that translate synthesis designs into executable instructions, potentially incorporating instrument feedback, and robotic workstations capable of executing those procedures seamlessly and without human intervention. Here we present RoboRXN, a cloud-native framework that unifies transformer-based retrosynthesis and chemical action extraction or prediction models with a commercially available synthesis robot and in-line high-resolution LC–MS. Across more than 3000 actions autonomously executed, we analyzed in details 33 reactions distributed among 10 single-step reactions and 9 multi-step campaigns. Eightythree percent of single-steps and all two-step routes succeeded without parameter adjustment; a branched four-step synthesis completed after one on-deck modification. Regardless of the overall success, we systematically encountered three recurring bottlenecks: hardware rigidity, execution-level data gaps, and slow physical feedback, which are seldom reported in the literature, despite being common to many commercial platform design. We delineate how each failure surfaced, quantify its impact on yield or throughput, and outline engineering and data-centric remedies. By publishing both the successes and the blind spots, we hope to redirect community effort from one-off demonstrations toward robust, transparent, and widely adoptable AI-driven laboratories.

papers.title: From Screening to Mechanism-Informed Analysis: A Standardized High-Throughput Electrochemistry Platform for Redox Species Discovery
papers.abstract: Systematic evaluation of redox-active molecules is central to the discovery of next-generation energy-storage chemistries, yet conventional electrochemical workflows remain limited by low throughput and poor cross-condition standardization. Here we present HT-EChem, a high- throughput electrochemical platform that integrates cyclic voltammetry (CV) with a 96 well plate format to enable rapid, reproducible measurements across large sample sets and controlled condition sweeps. HT-EChem operates at microliter-scale sample volumes, substantially reducing reagent consumption and enabling screening when material availability is limited. Using iron-aminopolycarboxylate complexes and representative organic redox molecules as model systems, the platform resolves pH-dependent shifts in redox potentials and changes in reversibility, enabling rapid construction of potential-pH maps and stability-pH profiles. High-density measurements distinguish ligand-dependent electrochemical behavior: Fe-PDTA exhibits dual reduction features consistent with an electrochemical-chemical (EC) sequence involving structural reorganization, whereas Fe-EDTA and Fe-DTPA show a single dominant reduction peak under comparable conditions. By combining automated sample handling with structured data processing, HT-EChem provides a scalable route to generate comparable electrochemical datasets for redox-material screening, mechanism-informed interpretation, and downstream computational analysis.

papers.title: The RNA-First Fallacy: Conflating Evolutionary Ancestry with Prebiotic Primacy
papers.abstract: The RNA World hypothesis remains the most widely accepted framework in origins-of-life research, anchored in compelling biochemical evidence for RNA's deep evolutionary ancestry. However, this viewpoint routinely extends beyond that and is frequently conflated with claims that RNA served as life's primal substrate. This essay argues that the RNA-First paradigm, in its pursuit of this claim, systematically projects biological biases onto a chaotic and combinatorially vast abiotic landscape. It relies on privileged, highly complex molecular constructs whose spontaneous emergence in such combinatorial settings is overwhelmingly implausible. Critically, the experimental evidence accumulated in support of RNA-First has largely demonstrated compatibility of RNA with prebiotic conditions, but not its probability, necessity, or chemical precedence over the numerous alternatives that abiotic chemistry affords. The eventual emergence of RNA chemistry demands a preceding protobiological stage, characterized by chemically diverse, collectively autocatalytic molecular networks. Embracing this broader protobiological framework, and confronting the true combinatorial complexity of abiotic chemistry, is essential for a rigorous and unbiased account of life's origin.

papers.title: Self-Healing Silicon Photoanodes Enabled by Carbonate-Mediated Cu−Fe Schottky Interlayers
papers.abstract: Electrolyte anions strongly influence catalyst durability, yet molecular-level evidence for anion-driven self-healing at buried semiconductor interfaces remains limited. Here, we design a Schottky-type Cu−Fe interlayer on Si that directs hole transport and enables anion-dependent interfacial regeneration. Cu seeding promotes Fe−OOH growth, while Cu(III) motifs, are atomically dispersed and stabilized by carbonate at the Si/Cu−Fe−OOH interface. In-situ spectroscopy further identifies these interfacial motifs as key sites for rapid proton-coupled oxygen evolution. Inner-sphere coordination between Cu(III) and carbonate stabilizes and continuously renews these transient high-valent centers, thereby promoting O−O bond formation. The regenerated photoanodes deliver OER photocurrent densities up to 24 mA cm−2 at 1.8 V vs. RHE under AM 1.5G illumination and operate stably for over 75 h with a stoichiometric H2/O2 ratio of 2:1. This work demonstrates an electrolyte-coded strategy in which anion coordination chemistry drives dynamic regeneration, providing a general framework for designing durable, self-healing oxygen-evolving photoelectrodes.

papers.title: A New Reactive Force Field for NOx-Water Interactions: Development, Evaluation, and Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Peroxynitrite
papers.abstract: Reactive nitrogen species (RNS) are key contributors to plasma-liquid processes and play a critical role in the chemistry of plasma-activated water. Despite their importance, their molecular-level behavior in aqueous environments is still not well understood, largely due to the absence of reliable reactive force fields. In this study, a new ReaxFF parameter set, ReaxFFCHONx-2026, is developed and systematically assessed for modeling nitrogen- and oxygen-containing reactive species in both gas-phase and aqueous conditions relevant to plasma systems. The parameter set is optimized using density functional theory (DFT) reference data for representative NOx reaction pathways and integrated with an existing aqueous/biomolecular ReaxFF framework to enable reactive molecular dynamics simulations in water. Its performance is validated through a range of structural, thermodynamic, and dynamic properties, including radial distribution functions, potential energy profiles, and diffusion coefficients. The results demonstrate strong agreement with DFT calculations and previously reported data, particularly in describing N-O bond breaking and solvation behavior. As a case study, the interaction of peroxynitrite (ONOO⁻) with water is investigated using reactive molecular dynamics, where atomic charges are dynamically determined via the ReaxFF charge equilibration method. The simulations show protonation leading to ONOOH formation, pronounced site-specific solvation around oxygen atoms, and preferential cleavage of the peroxide O-O bond. Analysis of diffusion further indicates that the predicted transport properties of RNS are consistent with available data, supporting the reliability of the developed force field. Overall, ReaxFFCHONx-2026 offers a robust framework for large-scale atomistic simulations of plasma-activated water and reactive nitrogen chemistry.

papers.title: What Is the Real Catalyst in M/NHC Systems? From Molecular Complexes to Cocktail-Type Catalysis
papers.abstract: Complexes of transition metals with N-heterocyclic carbine (NHC) ligands are often introduced and optimized as well-defined molecular precatalysts. However, the collected mechanistic evidence shows that M/NHC systems do not operate in a single universal manner. Depending on the metal, substrate, base, temperature, and ligand environment, the same precatalyst may function in a classical molecular mode with a preserved M–NHC bond, or it may evolve into an NHCdisconnected catalytic manifold composed of ionic metal species, clusters, and nanoparticles. The key mechanistic turning point is cleavage of the M–NHC framework, which can be initiated by NHC reductive elimination such as R–NHC, H–NHC, O–NHC, or N–NHC coupling, as well as by solvolysis or direct transformation. In this mini-review, the development of the mechanistic basis of M/NHC catalysis is outlined: from early evidence for facile lability of the M–NHC framework and the discovery of a new cocktail-type operating mode for Pd/NHC systems to the formulation of dual stabilization and fast/slow release scenarios. A complete classification of the operating states of M/NHC catalytic systems and a kinetic framework describing how these states are reached in practice are described. Taken together, these studies show that NHC ligands can stabilize both molecular active species and dynamic ensembles of metal particles of varying nuclearity, and that the balance between these possibilities is controlled predominantly by reaction conditions rather than by the static structural formula of the M/NHC precatalyst.

papers.title: Autonomous chemically fueled transient self-assembly of cyclic peptide nanotubes
papers.abstract: Cyclic peptide nanotubes (CPNs) are robust supramolecular architectures with highly modular properties, yet their exceptional stability hinders their use in dissipative, out-of-equilibrium systems. Here, we report an autonomous, chemically fueled reaction cycle that transiently converts linear peptides into cyclic analogs, which subsequently self-assemble into CPNs on timescales of hours to days. Cyclization is driven by a Meldrum’s acid derivative, while decyclization is triggered by 1,4-dithiothreitol (DTT) that is gradually released from a pre-fuel, enabling temporal control over nanotube formation and disassembly. By comparing short and longer peptide sequences, we uncover distinct kinetic regimes and map the reaction network governing the formation of multiple intermediates and products. This approach establishes a general strategy to access transient cyclic peptide nanotubes and expands the scope of peptidebased materials toward autonomous, non-equilibrium systems.

papers.title: Regio- and stereoselective carbotrifluoromethylation of alkynes through syn-carboboration.
papers.abstract: An efficient Cu-catalyzed protocol for the carbotrifluoromethylation of alkynes has been developed using Ruppert-Prakash reagent as the CF 3 source. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions to deliver a broad range of β-trifluoromethylated alkenes with excellent regio- and stereoselectivities. The selectivity was achieved via a merge of Cu-catalyzed carboboration with subsequent trifluoromethylation of the resulting vinyl-borate.

papers.title: Cyclic peptides in modern drug discovery: trends and therapeutic directions
papers.abstract: Peptide therapeutics have emerged as an important drug modality, driven by their high target specificity, favorable safety profiles, and expanding chemical design space. Within this landscape, cyclic peptides occupy a unique position between small molecules and large biologics, offering enhanced conformational rigidity, proteolytic stability, and improved target engagement. In this report, we analyze trends in cyclic peptide research using data extracted from the CAS Content Collection over the past two decades. Our analysis reveals a sustained increase in both academic publications and patents related to cyclic peptides, reflecting growing interest across discovery and development stages. Notably, the oral route of administration is gaining increased attention, suggesting progress toward overcoming long-standing bioavailability challenges associated with peptide-based therapeutics. Beyond delivery considerations, we examine how peptide types, cyclization types, and specific chemical modifications co-occur with routes of administration, therapeutic indications, and potential molecular targets. Together, these data-driven insights provide a comprehensive overview of the evolving cyclic peptide landscape and highlight emerging design principles that are shaping the future development of cyclic peptide therapeutics.

papers.title: Quantifying CO2 adsorption motifs in functionalized mesoporous silica using solid-state NMR
papers.abstract: The rapid rise in atmospheric CO2 concentration necessitates the development of efficient carbon capture technologies to achieve carbon neutrality. The CO2 adsorption-based separation using porous materials, especially silica offers a cost effective and reusable solution. In this study, we investigated the immobilization of polyethyleneimine onto mesoporous silica, which is well known for its CO2 adsorption. A systematic series of samples with PEI loadings of 20, 30, 40, 50, and 60 wt % was synthesized and analyzed. Solid-state NMR spectroscopy is a unique tool to probe the non-covalent interactions between the silica surface and imine groups, both during the CO2 adsorption and in the presence of moisture. The solid-state NMR results reveal significant peak shifts and line broadening at 40 wt % loading, indicating the onset of PEI agglomeration. The complementary computational calculations support these experimental observations indicating the formation of carbamic acid species characterized by a resonance at 164 ppm. These insights into the molecular level interactions provide a platform for designing the high-performance amine functionalized adsorbents for carbon capture applications.

papers.title: General Concept for Long Linear Flexible Chain Conformation in Respect to the Structure and Properties of Thermoplastic Polymers
papers.abstract: The present concept suggests a chain-folded conformation for all high-molecular-weight thermoplastic polymers with long, linear and flexible chains. It is assumed that, at a certain stage of synthesis, chain-folded segmental aggregates appear with hexagonal prismatic shapes, which are aligned parallel and ordered into nanoscale areas. These prisms are resistant formations and act as kinetic units and building blocks at all structural changes during relaxation and phase transitions. When crystallization is possible, this is the final stage of the ordering process; chain folding is the reason but not the result of crystallization. This hypothesis provides a new general framework for interpreting the structure and phase-relaxation processes in polymers. It is supported by existing experimental evidences and our previous research findings. Without contradicting generally accepted conformational theories, this concept answers important and still open questions in the field of polymer physics.

papers.title: Density-Corrected Density Functional Theory for Solids
papers.abstract: Density-corrected density functional theory (DC-DFT) considers whether self-consistent densities yield optimal energetics in Kohn-Sham calculations. With considerable success in molecular calculations, we here apply DC-DFT to solid-state calculations with Hartree-Fock (HF) densities. We resolve a known anomaly: that dispersion corrections can worsen results as one climbs Jacob’s ladder. This is illustrated for simple covalent solids, such as Si. The relative energetics of phases of ice are also much improved with HF densities, as is CO absorption on NaCl, while graphite interlayer binding is insensitive to its density.

papers.title: Hydroamination of Cyclooctynes With Primary Hydroxylamines : A new Reaction In The Click Toolbox
papers.abstract: Herein, we report a rapid and efficient conjugation of primary hydroxylamines with cyclooctynes. A range of R–NHOH substrates, including amino acid- and sugar-derived hydroxylamines, react readily with BCN to afford the corresponding adducts in good yields. Evaluation of various cyclooctynes revealed significant differences in reactivity, with DBCO-acid exhibiting the highest rate (k2 > 23 M-1 s-1).

papers.title: Closed-Loop Framework for Descriptor-Empowered Exploring High-Activity Co-Based Quaternary Molten Alloys Catalysts for Methane Pyrolysis
papers.abstract: Methane (CH 4 ) pyrolysis via molten media offers an attractive route to CO 2 ‑free hydrogen production with high‑value carbon as a co‑product. However, the rational design of multicomponent molten catalysts remains challenging due to the dynamic and disordered nature of active sites in the molten state. Here, we present a closed-loop framework that integrates potential catalyst exploration by descriptor data mining, CH 4 pyrolysis testing, and activity mechanism analysis to identify the high-activity catalysts for CH 4 pyrolysis. Using this approach, Bi 70 Ni 18 Cu 6 Co 6 is identified as a promising catalyst for the first time, with experimental validation demonstrating it can achieve 40.3% CH 4 conversion at a moderate 1000 °C with a relative low activation energy (197.3 kJ·mol -1 ), outperforming the same experimental conditions Bi 73 Ni 27 (33.3%) and Bi 76 Ni 18 Cu 6 (37.4%) molten medias. The enhancement stems from a synergistic multi‑solute effect that the co‑dissolution of Ni, Cu, and Co in the low‑surface‑tension Bi solvent increases the density of exposed active sites and promotes direct interaction with CH 4 molecules. In particular, the introducing Co downshift the LUMO energy level of CH 4 molecular orbital (~1.3 eV), facilitating charge antibonding occupation, weakening C–H bonds, thereby accelerating the CH 4 dissociation. These findings provide deep insights of Co-based multi-elementary molten catalysts and chart a clear path toward the rational design of high-performance multicomponent molten catalysts for CH 4 pyrolysis.

papers.title: Rational Design of μ-Opioid Receptor–Preferring Scaffolds with Integrated Calcium Channel Interaction: Analogue-Based Lead Identification Reveals a Shared Pharmacophore Constraint
papers.abstract: This study presents a computational, analogue-driven investigation aimed at identifying and refining a candidate scaffold with preferential μ-opioid receptor (MOR) interaction characteristics and potential secondary compatibility with voltage-gated calcium channelassociated binding regions. Rather than focusing on a single optimised compound, the work adopts an exploratory approach in which an initial scaffold, selected on the basis of predicted physicochemical suitability, was systematically modified and evaluated across an analogue series of approximately 30 structures. Docking was performed against both active-state (5C1M) and inactive-state (9MQ1) MOR conformations, in addition to κ-(4DJH) and δ-opioid (4N6H) receptors and the α2δ-1 calcium channel subunit (8IF3), allowing assessment of receptor-state preference and cross-target interaction behaviour. The parent scaffold demonstrated reproducible orthosteric MOR binding alongside consistent engagement of a defined polar interaction region within 8IF3. However, iterative analogue modification revealed that structural changes improving MOR active-state compatibility frequently disrupted the spatial arrangement required to maintain the calciumchannel-associated interaction motif. This behaviour was consistent across the series and defines a clear tradeoff between MORcompatible binding geometry and preservation of secondary interaction features, indicating the presence of a multi-objective optimisation constraint within this scaffold class. In parallel, reversible acetylation was explored as a strategy to modulate predicted CNS accessibility, acting at the level of delivery rather than core pharmacophore modification. Overall, the study identifies a tractable scaffold framework and characterises its interaction limits, positioning it as a candidate for further refinement. The findings are intended to support lead identification and prioritisation rather than establish functional activity, providing a structured basis for subsequent experimental evaluation.

papers.title: Design and Characterization of a Ligstroside-Derived Photoaffinity Probe
papers.abstract: Ligstroside (LIG) is a phenolic secoiridoid glycoside naturally occurring in olives and structurally related to the widely studied olive constituent oleuropein. Although LIG has been reported to exhibit diverse biological activities, it has received comparatively limited attention, and the molecular targets underlying its bioactivity remain largely unknown, thereby limiting exploration of its pharmacological potential. To facilitate target identification and mechanistic investigation, we designed and synthesized a LIG-derived photoaffinity probe (PAL-LIG) through minimal modification of the LIG scaffold. The probe incorporates a photoactivatable diazirine group that enables UVinduced covalent crosslinking with proximal proteins together with an alkyne handle that allows subsequent bioorthogonal conjugation via copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC). Following photo-crosslinking, probe-labeled proteins can be conjugated with azide-functionalized reporter tags, including biotin for streptavidinbased enrichment and pulldown or TAMRA for fluorescence detection and cellular imaging. Using this strategy, PAL-LIG enables enrichment of potential LIG-binding proteins as well as fluorescence-based visualization of probe labeling in cells. Importantly, PAL-LIG retains biological activity comparable to LIG, as demonstrated by its similar ability to promote ATP production in mouse C2C12 myoblasts, indicating that installation of the photoaffinity and alkyne handles minimally perturbs the intrinsic bioactivity of LIG. Collectively, PAL-LIG provides a chemical tool for investigating the direct protein targets and molecular mechanisms of LIG.

papers.title: A Master Key for Accessible Solid Electrolyte Design
papers.abstract: The solid electrolyte design currently relies on heuristic approaches, lacking a unified framework to correlate atomistic lattice features with the accessible bulk ion transport properties. Nor could the rich literature be interpreted consistently to provide a definitive perspective on new solidelectrolyte engineering by design, with refined composition and lattice information. To address these needs and challenges, here we found a master key (Fig. S1), opening a door for accessible solid electrolyte design by encoding the composition-structure-property relationship validated by Li 10 GeP 2 S 12 (LGPS) and Li 4 GeS 4 (thio-LISICON) solid electrolytes with a new concept called “intrinsic lattice formation strain” (ILFS) (Fig. 1), which originates from the chemical bond formation and lattice relaxation from perfect symmetry of the unit cell. The master key uses Gibbs free energy terms expressed in ILFS to describe the ion transport properties of solid electrolytes that follow the Arrhenius law, correlating the experimental composition-structure-property trends across the open-literature sulfide solid electrolyte database with R 2 > 0.90 for LGPS and > 0.86 for thio-LISICON, respectively. The master key thus offers an intelligent pathway to guide new solid electrolyte design and discovery.

papers.title: A Light-Driven Constitutional Pump
papers.abstract: Achieving high degrees of non-equilibrium in dynamic covalent chemistry remains a major challenge for the synthesis of energy-dissipative matter with life-like behaviors based on reversible covalent bond reorganization. At the molecular level, the central difficulty lies in maximizing the kinetic asymmetry introduced by energy‑driven auxiliary pathways over thermally equilibrating dynamic covalent reactions, whose microscopic reversibility and rapid equilibration intrinsically limit its amplification. Here we report a light-driven constitutional pump that addresses this limitation by embedding a unidirectional, kinetically dominant pathway onto a reversible dynamic covalent metathesis reaction, enabling the system to reach high degrees of non-equilibrium under continuous irradiation. This pumping mechanism is encoded at the molecular design level through conjugative coupling between a diarylethene photoswitch and a polar olefin moiety, which simultaneously enables photonic gating to suppress reverse pathways and generates a high-energy photoisomer intermediate that imposes a strong kinetic preference. As a result, the reaction network is efficiently driven toward a non-equilibrium steady state (NESS), exhibiting pronounced constitutional selection while remaining fully reversible upon removal of the light input. Integration of this pump into polymer networks enables spatiotemporal control over crosslink density, giving rise to photo-adaptive synthetic materials that display non-equilibrium mechanical modulation.

papers.title: A Recent Overview onto Photo/Electro-Catalytic Materials Degradation Mechanistic Insights of Perfluorinated and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS): By-products Determination and AI/ML Implications
papers.abstract: Around 10000 compounds of Poly-and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) exposure is ill-affecting the environmental resources with direct healthcare expenditures around USD 100 billion. This review details electrochemical and photo-catalytic activities of metal centres and carbon-composites towards PFASs degradation. The technical observations and illustrations in the current work are majorly referenced from recent literature published in the last five years (2020 – 2025). The iron and titanium species have shown better remediation abilities which reported with majority of publications. Iron systems (Fe oxides, ZVI) have shown better parameters for electrochemical activities (electrooxidation/reduction) whereas titanium sub oxides (TSO) and bismuth sheets are better related to the photoelectrochemical activity. Other 3d-metal systems like Co, Ni, and boron doped diamond (BDD), carbon structures (activated carbon, carbon sphere and aerogel) are also detailed with PFOA and PFOS treatment. In understanding the degradation mechanism, the radical species activity has densely dominated the process with the support of radical oxygen/sulphur species and charge transfers. Radical species activity, dissolved oxygen influence, and direct electron transfer (DET) mechanism are provided in understanding the heterogeneous catalytic reactions and redox materials chemistry. Decarboxylation, and hydro-defluorination (HDF) mechanisms are explained with a set of findings based on catalyst and chain length of compound (Long/Short-chain). Determination of degradation byproducts and intermediates utilizing different state-of-the-art spectroscopy tools (LC-MS, GC-MS) are detailed in supporting the issue related to the secondary contamination in various remediation sites. Implications of AI/ML towards efficient handling of the various PFASs degradation (or) treatment technologies are discussed briefly.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Chemical Secretions and Their Ecological Role of the Millipede Brachycybe
papers.abstract: Brachycybe is a genus of the millipede subterclass Colobognatha, a group which exhibits rare social characteristics, including species aggregations and male brood care. Although it has been hypothesized that alkaloid-based defensive secretions may also serve as pheromones, no studies have focused on these traits.
