Here, we evaluated the chemical secretions of six species, two of which were previously unstudied, and conducted Y-tube pheromone assays. Chemical investigations led to the structure elucidation of three new metabolites, each containing a carboxylic acid. Y-tube pheromone assays revealed that Brachycybe producta is significantly attracted to conspecifics (p = 0.0428), and is deterred by a different species of alkaloid-producing millipede (p = 0.0161). The former assay was repeated using a mixture of the crude (p = 0.0428) and purified (p = 0.0433) chemical defense secretion from B. producta. This study provides the first evidence that colobognath millipede’s chemical secretions serve both a defensive and as pheromone role.

papers.title: Crown Ether–Structured Secondary Coordination Spheres Enable Methane Formation in Cobalt Porphyrin CO2 Electroreduction
papers.abstract: Secondary coordination sphere engineering provides a powerful strategy to control molecular electrocatalysis beyond primary-sphere electronic effects. Here, we report A 2 B 2 -type cobalt porphyrins bearing electron-donating (–NH 2 ) or electron-withdrawing (–NO 2 ) substituents with and without covalently tethered monoaza-crown ether (CE) motifs. Electrochemical studies in homogeneous and heterogeneous media, combined with cation variation, contact-angle analysis, online GC product quantification, 13 C-labeling experiments, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, were performed to disentangle electronic and secondary-sphere contributions. In aqueous heterogeneous CO 2 electroreduction, CE functionalization induces anodic shifts in onset potential for both substituent series, consistent with electrostatic stabilization of reduced cobalt states by chelated alkali cations. However, only the –NH 2 derivatives exhibit pronounced changes in wettability, catalytic current, and product distribution. In these systems, CO selectivity decreases in favor of enhanced H 2 evolution, while CH 4 formation increases six-fold relative to the non-functionalized analogue under ambient pressure and near-neutral pH. DFT reveals that CE-cation assemblies preferentially adopt syn conformations, stabilized by cation–π interactions, generating a sterically asymmetric “caged” axial site. This architecture reduces the effective rate of CO 2 association yet kinetically inhibits CO dissociation, enabling further reduction of trapped intermediates to CH 4 . These findings establish cation-organized crown ether confinement as a mechanistic design principle for accessing multielectron CO 2 reduction pathways.

papers.title: Molecular Simulations Assisted by an Artificial Intelligence Agent (ArIA)
papers.abstract: Computational chemistry enables the investigation of molecular and materials properties through simulations. Among available methods, density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) are widely applied because they provide practical error margins at affordable computational cost. Despite their broad utility, their effective application requires extensive training in both theoretical chemistry and basic programming, creating a significant entrance barrier for non-specialists. In this work, we develop an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) based on open-source large language models (LLMs) that can be readily deployed on a state-of-the-art personal computers (PCs). This agentic AI is capable of interpreting user instructions, performing simulations with the ORCA program suite, and generating both interactive visualizations and summary reports. Additionally, users can interrogate the simulation results through text queries, making computational chemistry more accessible. We release our agentic AI fully open-source, which will create a collaborative development ecosystem to build upon for future improvements.

papers.title: Hysteresis of Origin in Aqueous Lithium Orotate: Evidence for a Long-Lived Ionic Cluster
papers.abstract: Lithium orotate appears to exert biological effects distinct from those of other lithium salts, raising the question of how lithium and orotate might travel together from gut to target tissue. Standard ion-pair theory predicts only weak contact pairs that live for picoseconds in dilute aqueous solution, insufficient to account for transport as a functional unit. We propose that lithium orotate supports a qualitatively different class of chemical entity, which we call a Partially Ionised Nano-Cluster (PINC): a stable non-aggregating cluster of ions, carrying net charge, existing only in the fully-hydrated state and possessing a defined molecular-scale geometry. The full set of defining attributes is developed in Section 2.1. We propose [LiOr2]as one candidate realisation for lithium orotate, and test a specific - prediction that follows from the concept: that solutions prepared from crystalline material should contain more PINCs than compositionally identical solutions prepared from free ions — a hysteresis of origin. We report that paired wet and rehydrated cells at three concentrations (0.82–1.00 mM) in a 1:1 CsOr + LiCl working solution, show a reproducible +6.0 to +6.6% elevation in rehydrated cells. The signal survives a 25 → 40 → 25 °C thermal cycle: wet cells rise while rehydrated cells hold flat. Five of six pre-registered predictions are confirmed.

papers.title: Intramolecular Hydride Transfer Racemization Coupled with Enzymatic Kinetic Resolution Enables Asymmetric Syntheses of Caged Compounds
papers.abstract: Caged molecules represent an exciting structural class with numerous potential applications, yet reports of their asymmetric synthesis are scarce. In this work, we report a method for the asymmetric synthesis of a variety of caged hydroxyketones/ketoesters, featuring the synergistic effect of a lipase-catalyzed kinetic resolution (KR) combined with the unique ability of the caged hydroxyketone starting materials to undergo racemization via intramolecular hydride transfer, a chemical process which although previously reported had, until the current study, yet to be utilized for this class of compounds in a synthetic context. We find that the lipase from C. Rugosa is able to effect the kinetic resolution of a variety of caged hydroxyketones with high levels of enantioselectivity, including nearly symmetric compounds. We demonstrate that with multiple cycles of recovered starting material racemization, yields surpassing the traditional KR threshold of 50% are achievable without compromising the enantioselectivity.

papers.title: Exploring the Practical Limits of Natural Abundance 13C Kinetic Isotope Effect Measurements
papers.abstract: The use of quantitative 13 C KIE methodology at natural abundance developed by Daniel Singleton, commonly known as the ‘Singleton Method’, to determine kinetic isotope effects (KIEs) provides a powerful tool to probe the fine details of reaction mechanisms. Modern advances in NMR technology have led to improved sensitivity of 13 C NMR spectroscopy, enabling the measurement of more precise 13 C NMR integrations used to determine isotopic enhancement in natural abundance methodology. Herein, we present a systematic experimental examination of the precision limits of both inter- and intramolecular natural abundance 13 C KIE measurements using modern NMR instrumentation. Employing the Baeyer–Villiger oxidation of cyclohexanone as a model system, we measured intermolecular 13 C KIEs across fractional conversions ranging from 15% to 80%. Nonlinear weighted fitting and a 95% prediction interval are provided as guidance in determining the accuracy of measurements across the range of fractional conversions. Statistical analysis shows that relatively accurate measurements can be obtained at lower fractional conversions provided careful attention is given to signal-to-noise, calibration of fractional conversion, and replication of measurements. The requirement of calibrating fractional conversion measurements is emphasized and, in this case, accounted for a difference of nearly 0.4% in the measured 13 C KIE. No significant difference in measured KIEs was found between 400 and 600 MHz instruments. Intramolecular 13 C KIEs measured across 20%–99% conversion yielded a consistent KIE (range 1.044-1.048), confirming independence from fractional conversion. These results establish quantitative benchmarks for precision and accuracy of natural abundance 13 C KIE measurements and expand the practical range of conditions under which reliable mechanistic data can be obtained.

papers.title: n- and p-type CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals via Electrochemical Doping
papers.abstract: Electronic doping underpins many semiconductor applications, but it has remained elusive for lead halide perovskite nanocrystals because their high density and low formation energy of defects easily compensate introduced dopants. Here we use electrochemical doping as a strategy to avoid doping compensation. Electrochemical injection of electrons or holes into the nanocrystal is compensated by surface-adsorbed electrolyte counterions, therefore not compromising crystal structure. We accomplished ambipolar (n- and p-type) doped CsPbBr3 nanocrystals with charge carrier concentrations up to the heavy doping regime (4.8x10 17 cm −3 , corresponding to 0.25 charges per nanocrystal). We show that electrochemical doping is reversible and stable at these high free carrier concentrations. The high extent of doping and stability is enabled by the use of lecithin, a zwitterionic ligand that strongly binds to the surface of the CsPbBr 3 nanocrystals while still allowing ion and electron transfer. Lecithin stabilizes the surface atoms by shifting the potentials for Pb2+ reduction and Br- oxidation outside of the bandgap. The inferred surface-chemistry design rules for stable electrochemical doping can also serve as a guideline for developing CsPbBr 3 nanocrystals stable under high free-carrier concentrations in optoelectronic devices, such as light-emitting diodes or electronically triggered quantum light sources.

papers.title: Determining the Ambimodality of Transition State Structures by the Exploration of Dimensionality-Reduced Potential Energy Surfaces
papers.abstract: Ambimodal reaction pathways are characterized by a post transition state bifurcation (PTSB) on the potential energy surface (PES), which could therefore lead to multiple products from a single and common transition state, without intermediate formation or additional activation barrier. Ambimodality has been widely found in pericyclic reactions and functional group migrations, among other reactions. Currently, it is primarily characterized using ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to explore the PES. However, this approach is computationally expensive and may introduce errors, since downhill trajectories can surpass small energy barriers, leading to spurious identification of ambimodality. Here, a dimensionality-reduced optimization (DRO) strategy based on performing sequential geometric optimizations within a tailored lower-dimensional PES is proposed to determine the ambimodal character of transition states via efficient PES exploration. In the DRO protocol, the dimensionality of the PES is systematically reduced by hindering access to the product identified from the previous intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC) calculation. Subsequently, alternative downhill pathways are explored. Only when an alternative non-IRC product can be reached downhill in a barrierless manner can the transition state be characterized as ambimodal within the DRO protocol. This approach has been validated against different cycloaddition reactions and represents a significant advancement in the study of ambimodal reactions, providing a static, computationally inexpensive, and effective method for characterizing complex reaction pathways directly from transition state structures.

papers.title: Revealing the Structural Origin of Spin–Orbit Coupling with SOPEL
papers.abstract: Spin–orbit coupling is a key ingredient for many photochemical processes, yet it is commonly reported as an opaque scalar quantity with limited chemical interpretability. Here, we introduce the concept of SOPEL (Spin–Orbit Population ELement), an atom-resolved decomposition of spin–orbit coupling matrix elements (SOCMEs) that reveals their structural origin in molecules. We further present practical selection rules for nonzero couplings in the language of real atomic orbitals, providing an intuitive link between local orbital character and the spin–orbit coupling. Together, the concept converts the SOCMEs from a black-box electronic-structure output into a chemically interpretable quantity. By localizing the structural origin of spin–orbit coupling, SOPEL provides a practical framework not only for interpreting spin-forbidden processes in terms of structure and motion, but also for chemically guided molecular design. Applications to iodine-substituted BODIPY, formaldehyde, benzophenone, and triarylamine–terephthalonitrile show that the approach (i) identifies the atoms and fragments that generate spin–orbit coupling, (ii) characterizes spin–vibronic mechanisms, (iii) captures redistribution of the coupling origin across molecular frameworks, and (iv) explains why heavy-atom participation alone does not guarantee strong coupling.

papers.title: Fire at the boundary: airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm
papers.abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke, yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate approximately 5 million residents experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 ng m −3 , over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

papers.title: Extending AIMNet2 to Macrocyclic Peptides Through Data-Efficient Continual Training
papers.abstract: Macrocyclic peptides are among the most promising therapeutic modalities, yet no general-purpose machine learned interatomic potential (MLIP) has been validated for their conformational analysis. We show that AIMNet2 matches the accuracy of MACE-OFF23(S) on the MPCONF196 macrocyclic benchmark, despite macrocycles being entirely absent from its training data, at three-to sixfold lower computational cost. To close the remaining accuracy gap, we introduce a continual training protocol that integrates fewer than 25,000 domain-specific conformers (<0.1% of the training corpus) while preserving accuracy on non-macrocyclic molecules, reducing macrocyclic conformational energy RMSE by 25–27%. Applied to cyclosporine A as an independent test case, the continually trained model reproduces DFT conformational energies with sub-kcal mol −1 accuracy (RMSE 0.78 kcal mol −1 ) and correct rank ordering of all metastable conformers, outperforming all other tested MLIPs and semi-empirical methods. This continual training strategy, together with expanded non-covalent interaction coverage, has been adopted in the AIMNet2 (2025) release, which unifies small-molecule, macrocyclic, and intermolecular interaction treatment in a single production potential.

papers.title: Adaptive Photocatalytic Regimes Enabled by CO2 •− and Two-Photon Excitation Synergy: Cyclization-Carboxylation of Aryl Halides with CO2
papers.abstract: Selective activation of aryl halides across a broad reactivity spectrum remains a central challenge in photoredox catalysis, particularly due to the kinetic barriers associated with C-Cl bond reduction. Herein, we report a unified photocatalytic platform that enables substrate-dependent access to distinct reductive regimes through the synergistic integration of formate-derived CO 2 •- and consecutive two-photon excitation pathways. Under the developed conditions, aryl bromides and chlorides, despite exhibiting similarly demanding reduction potentials, display markedly different reactivity - governed by kinetic factors specific to the substrate and catalytic system. CO 2 •- mediates rapid and thermodynamically matched reduction of aryl bromides, whereas more recalcitrant aryl chlorides are activated via a super-reducing excited photocatalyst radical anion generated through a two-photon photoredox pathway, consistent with a ConPET-type mechanism or solvated electron involvement. Notably, formate serves a dual role as both the precursor to CO 2 •- and the electron donor enabling ConPET or solvated-electron generation, obviating the need for conventional super-stoichiometric sacrificial amines. This adaptive system enables efficient cyclization-carboxylation of (2-halophenoxy)allenes with CO 2 under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies, including kinetic analysis, competition experiments, isotopic labelling, spectroscopic study, and DFT calculations, support a dual-regime mechanism governed by substrate-dependent activation barriers. This work establishes a framework for kinetically gated control of reductive strength in photoredox catalysis by harnessing CO 2 •- as a reductant.

papers.title: Embedded Amide in π-Conjugation as a Tunable Double-Bond Motif for Controlling Optical Properties
papers.abstract: Replacing C=C bonds in aromatic molecules with heteroatom-containing double bond motifs ( e.g. C=N, B–N, C=P) is effective for their electronic modulation. However, structurally modifying these motifs is difficult, making the tunability of their electronic properties challenging. To overcome this limitation, we propose using the amide C–N bond as a tunable double-bond unit. We synthesized a series of amide-embedded pyrenes ( AmPy s) incorporating cis -amide bonds within the π-framework. The degree of C–N double-bond character of the amide was modulated through covalent modifications ( O - and N -methylation), non-covalent interactions (hydrogen bonding), and protonation. Spectroscopic studies revealed that as the C–N bond lengthens, T 1 state energies increase while S 1 state energies remain relatively constant, narrowing the S 1 –T 1 energy gap (∆ E ST ). Computational analysis clarified that short C–N bonds promote localized π-conjugation within two fused K-region rings containing C–N bonds, acting as an electronic insulator that spatially separates unpaired electrons to lower the T 1 state energies. Conversely, long C–N bonds weaken such π-conjugation, leading to more delocalized spin densities, raising the T 1 state energies. This work establishes the amide as a versatile double-bond unit where the C–N bond length serves as a design parameter for tuning electronic properties.

papers.title: Recent Developments in Primary Copper Supply in the United States
papers.abstract: Demand for copper is expected to increase in the United States as energy infrastructure expands to accommodate data centers, new electricity generation, and electric vehicles. While scaling-up recycling of copper is important for meeting domestic demand, a number of active and emerging copper producers have announced new activities for expanding primary copper production. Generalized market and facility-level models representing mine energy and materials flows have been developed, but the potential future portfolio of mining supply is diverse and requires further characterization to support planning for supply chains and technology deployment. Herein, we present a dataset of mine projects, providing estimates of copper productivity by technology pathway. We review diesel, electricity, water, and tailing waste generation factors reported in literature and used in life-cycle assessment databases, highlighting incontinences and gaps where values may not represent primary production of copper in the United States, now and in the future. Using data reported between 2021 and 2026, we find 0.9 and 1.6 million tonnes/year of cathode-grade copper production from active and proposed mine projects, respectively. By gathering data from technical reports, we were able to reproduce domestic production reported most recently by the US Geological Survey. We find 21% of new Cu production is explicitly from leaching processes that avoid sending concentrate to offshore smelters. Our findings suggest limits to domestic smelter capacity could be a bottleneck for new projects generating conventional sulphide ore copper concentrate. Partnerships between mines and providers of key resources such as water, fuel, and electricity could have far reaching effects as copper mining expands beyond the Southwest where it holds an established industrial presence.

papers.title: Achieving efficient organic room temperature phosphorescence through acceptor dendronization
papers.abstract: Organic room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials hold significant promise for applications in optoelectronics, information security, and bioimaging. Recently, significant progress has been made in RTP materials and vacuum deposited organic light-emitting diode (OLED) devices. However, the performance of solution-processed OLEDs is seriously lagging be-hind, due to the lack of RTP molecular strategies that balance exciton stability and solution processability at the single-molecule scale. In this work, we propose an acceptor dendronization strategy for designing RTP materials, successfully achieving highly efficient and stable RTP emissions. This strategy can simultaneously enhance the various processes involved in RTP emission at the single-molecule level: increase the intersystem crossing channels, enhance the spin-orbit coupling con-stants between T1 and S0, and suppress molecular motion. Consequently, it promotes intersystem crossing and triplet radia-tive transition while inhibiting non-radiative transition, thereby efficiently enhancing RTP emission. A proof-of-concept ac-ceptor-dendronized dendrimer exhibits long phosphorescence lifetimes in the milliseconds range in ambient solution and near 100% photoluminescent quantum yields in the doped films. This is the first reported RTP dendrimer to date. An OLED fabricated using this dendrimer in a sky-blue emission achieves an external quantum efficiency of 25.1%, which represent the state-of-the-art efficiency based on solution-processed RTP-OLEDs to date. Our findings offer definitive guidelines for the molecular engineering of RTP materials and pave the way for innovative RTP systems in diverse optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Integration of Liquid Handling Robotics, Turbidimetry, and Machine Learning Towards Inverse Design of LCST Polymer Formulations
papers.abstract: Precise tuning of physical properties such as lower critical solution temperature (LCST) behaviour in polymer formulations is essential for stimuli-responsive materials design, but is typically limited by low-throughput cloud point ( T cp ) determination. To address this, we developed a high-throughput experimentation platform that integrates automated liquid handling, parallel turbidimetry measurements, and machine learning (ML) under a unified Python framework. Using an OT-2 liquid handling robot interfaced with a SPECTROstar Nano plate reader, we enabled automated design of experiments-based sampling of highdimensional formulations, which are prepared robotically and analysed via high-throughput turbidimetry to determine polymer cloud points ( T cp ) for P(NIPAM-co-DMAEMA) copolymers. Overcoming single-variable resolution in traditional methods, our approach enables the simultaneous T cp mapping across polymer, NaCl, and NaOH concentrations, achieving an average measurement throughput of 8 minutes per sample. This workflow generates high-fidelity datasets comprising hundreds of formulation- T cp relationships within days. Supervised ML models trained on these data achieved high predictive accuracy ( R 2 up to 0.96; MSE as low as 0.023 ◦ C 2 ), with SHAP analyses elucidating feature contributions. T cp distribution analysis identified polymer concentration as a dominant driver of T cp variance, particularly in hydrophilic regimes. Using ML, inverse design of formulations was demonstrated, predicting compositions that achieve target transition temperatures with less than 1% error. This work marks a significant shift from closed-loop optimisations of chemical features of polymers to a ML-driven framework for the targeted design of physical properties directly.

papers.title: A Flux-Based Bioaccumulation Model for Growing Organisms: Integrating Countercurrent Gill Exchange into Dynamic Energy Budget Theory
papers.abstract: Bioaccumulation factors in fish vary systematically with body size, food availability, and chemical hydrophobicity, yet widely used fugacity-based models rely on sizeindependent empirical rate constants and cannot explain these patterns mechanistically. Here we present a flux-based model that resolves this limitation by integrating Erickson–McKim (EM) countercurrent gill exchange theory into the Dynamic Energy Budget (DEB) framework. The key methodological advance is requiring simultaneous consistency among four independent flux descriptions at the gill: the advective mass balance, Fick’s diffusion law, the one-compartment DEB model, and the EM countercurrent exact solution. This consistency requirement uniquely determines the effective exposure concentration as a weighted combination of the gill outflow and body concentrations, where the weighting factor is derived from the exponential concentration profile within the gill rather than postulated. The resulting series-resistance structure places the countercurrent correction exclusively on the diffusion resistance, structurally guaranteeing three properties: the maximum bioconcentration factor equals the thermodynamic partition coefficient, gill assimilation efficiency is bounded below unity, and the elimination rate constant scales inversely with body length. The same framework applies to the dietary pathway under the plug-flow reactor assumption, providing a unified treatment of both uptake routes. Systematic comparison with fugacity-based models across six diagnostic indicators demonstrates that the present model captures size-, food condition-, and hydrophobicity-dependent bioaccumulation patterns inaccessible to conventional approaches. Preliminary validation using mercury bioaccumulation data in blackhead seabream ( Acanthopagrus schlegeli )—where Hg(II) and methylmercury exhibit contrasting kinetics within the same species—confirms the predicted size dependence of depuration rates and field biomonitoring concentrations.

papers.title: Engineering Low-Gap Organic Semiconductors via Gold and Copper Peri-Metalation: Insights into Electronic and Spin Regimes from DFT with Interpretable SciML
papers.abstract: Organic semiconductors are constrained by rigid carbon-based frameworks, limiting the tunability of their electronic and spin properties. Here, we show through electronicstructure modeling that peri-metalation of polyacenes with coinage metals, specifically copper and gold, enables targeted engineering of both bandgap and spin regimes, thereby unlocking electronic behaviors not accessible in conventional organic systems. Integration of density functional theory with machine learning allows systematic exploration of the influence of metal identity and arrangement on bandgap narrowing and modulation of the singlet–triplet gap across the polyacene series. Copper incorporation leads to significant bandgap closure through HOMO destabilization and collapses singlet–triplet gaps to values as low as 0.05 eV, resulting in spin-active, optically dark excitons. In contrast, gold peri-metalation preserves structural integrity and moderates electronic reorganization through relativistic orbital stabilization, while the lowest singlet and triplet excitations remain optically dark. Complementary machine-learning analysis using ExtraTrees regressor models, trained on physically interpretable descriptors, capture non-additive, sequence-dependent structure–property relationships with high accuracy (R2 ≈ 0.99) and robust performance under stringent validation, and remain predictive under chemically meaningful extrapolation. Collectively, these findings establish peri-metalated polyacenes as a highly tunable class of hybrid organic–metal semiconductors and provide a computational–chemical framework for rational access to low-bandgap, spin-sensitive electronic regimes beyond traditional organic electronics.

papers.title: Conformational Dependence of Dipole Moments in Zinc Dialkyldithiophosphates: Unexpected Dominance of Alkyl Chain Configurations
papers.abstract: Molecular dipole moments are required for empirical correlations used to estimate thermophysical properties of zinc dialkyldithiophosphates (ZDDPs), an important class of anti-wear additives. We calculated dipole moments for three ZDDPs and their precursor dialkyldithiophosphates using density functional theory and explicitly accounted for their dependence on molecular conformation. We unexpectedly found that dipole ∗Corresponding author. Email: karlj@pitt.edu moments are highly sensitive to conformational degrees of freedom. The dipole moments for each of these six molecules range from almost zero to almost 5 D across different conformers. Surprisingly, this variation appears to be dominated by the conformations of the alkyl chains rather than the polar inorganic core. Despite this wide range, the arithmetic mean and Boltzmann weighted average dipole moments fall within a narrow range of 2.2–2.4 D for all six molecules examined. This consistency arises because the dipole moment shows no correlation with the conformational energy. The robust average value significantly simplifies property estimation by eliminating the need for conformation-specific dipole calculations. We recommend that thermophysical property correlations use a constant dipole moment of 2.3 D for ZDDPs and their precursors. We predict that experimental measurements will yield values close to this average, since they inherently sample an ensemble of conformations.

papers.title: A Synthetic Molybdenum Complex that Mimics All Four Molybdopterin Enzyme Families and Enables Catalytic C–H Oxidation
papers.abstract: Molybdopterin enzymes catalyze a remarkably diverse array of redox transformations, ranging from oxyanion reduction to C–H hydroxylation, through MoVI/MoIV cycling at active sites with conserved dithiolate-coordinated structures. Synthetic models of these active sites have historically struggled to replicate this chemical versatility in part due to comproportionation to inactive MoV dimers, and catalytic turnover remains elusive. Here we report that a [N2S2]2–-supported MoIV=O complex abstracts oxygen atoms from substrates representative of three molybdopterin enzyme families: DMSO, trimethylamine N-oxide, perchlorate, nitrate, and selenate (DMSO reductases); methionine sulfoxide (sulfite oxidases); and benzamidoxime and N-hydroxyphthalimide (mARCs). In the cases of ClO4– and NO3–, efficient oxygen atom transfer (OAT) requires Lewis acid activation by B(C6F5)3. The corresponding MoVI(O)2 redox partner oxidizes formate via hydride abstraction, extending the functional analogy to formate dehydrogenases. The same complex has previously been shown to promote C–H hydroxylation by hydride abstraction akin to the XO family, thus demonstrating

papers.title: Interfacial kinematics organize degradation across lithium-battery chemistries
papers.abstract: Why do graphite, silicon-composite, lithium-metal and anode-free batteries fail so differently even though all are ultimately constrained by the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI)? Here we show that the key ordering variable is not nominal anode chemistry, but the kinematics of the surface on which the SEI forms. Starting from the Doyle–Fuller–Newman porous-electrode equations, we recast four representative negative-electrode chemistries within a common interphase-centred framework and derive chemistry-specific closures for active area, side-reaction current, porosity change, damage, dead-lithium isolation and cyclable-lithium inventory. Literature-informed calculations under normalized NMC-based conditions reveal a monotonic rise in interphase loss and interface regeneration from graphite to silicon composites, lithium metal and anode-free cells, accompanied by a transition from gradual fade to convex chemomechanical decay, delayed failure knees and severe first-cycle losses. The framework explains why classical fixed-surface DFN models are often adequate for graphite, must be phase- and stress-resolved for silicon composites, and become incomplete for lithiummetal and anode-free systems unless moving-front, nucleation and inventory-loss physics are added explicitly. This hierarchy provides a practical roadmap for building chemistry-specific DFN/PyBaMM models across next-generation battery platforms.

papers.title: Activation of Hydroxylated Organic Cathodes Enables High-Rate Sodium Batteries
papers.abstract: Organic cathodes are poised to lower transition metal burdens for producing sodium-ion and sodium metal batteries, yet most struggle to achieve premium performance due to low ionic and electronic conductivity. Maintaining a high concentration of mobile sodium ions in redox-active solids for fast ion transport at all states of charge remains a challenge, as does ensuring a high spin density to facilitate long-range electron transport. Here, we show that sodiation of hydroxylated organic cathode materials reconfigures molecular packing to simultaneously enhance electron and ion transport, yielding new phases whose electronic conductivity (10–3 S cm–1) surpass their progenitors by five orders of magnitude while also shortening the characteristic diffusion time for Na+ ions by 50%. Although sodiation can be performed ex situ, we find it more effective to carry it out in situ during formation, where progressive activation of redox sites coincides with a dramatic improvement in rate capability, enabling cells with specific capacity of 290 mAh g–1 at a discharge current density of 1500 mA g–1 and a remarkably low fade rate of only 0.021% per cycle over 1380 cycles. Sodiation emerges as a promising strategy to activate cathode material architectures toward high-power TWh-scalable energy storage systems.

papers.title: Chlor-alkali electrolysis for battery grade lithium hydroxide production and its potential to replace conventional chemical lithium refining
papers.abstract: The demand for lithium ion batteries (LIB) is expected to reach about 3.1 million tonnes by 2035, driven primarily by rapid growth in electric vehicles and other energy storage applications. A key precursor in manufacturing cathode material in these LIBs is lithium hydroxide (LiOH). Current LiOH production routes involve a wide number of pre-processing and chemical treatment steps starting from various Li sources (spodumene, brine and battery leachate). These chemical routes for LiOH production invoke challenges associated not only with high chemical consumption and excessive waste generation, but also due to its significant energy demand and substantial CO 2 emissions. Electrochemical routes such as chlor-alkali electrolysis, bipolar membrane electrodialysis and electro-electrodialysis serve as sustainable alternatives in reducing the number of chemical steps involved, thereby lowering chemical waste generation such as sodium sulphate. In this perspective, we provide a case for adopting chloralkali electrolysis route for LiOH production by comparing energy consumption, chemical waste generation and CO 2 footprint with the chemical routes. We also propose coupling flash joule heating technology to chlor-alkali electrolysis as a circular pathway to produce LiOH from spodumene, reducing net energy consumption and chemical waste generation significantly. Further, we posit that unless electricity grid is fully decarbonized, electrochemical routes fail to provide a massive benefit over chemical routes in reaching net zero carbon footprint. This underscores the critical role of grid decarbonization in unlocking the full environmental benefits of electrochemical routes for lithium refining.

papers.title: Molecule–Metal Nanostructure Interactions in Plasmonic Chemistry
papers.abstract: Plasmonic chemistry converts metal nanostructures into photocatalysts via three interconnected channels at the molecule–metal interface: enhanced near fields, non-equilibrium charge carriers, and localized heat. This review focuses on this interfacial perspective. We show how adsorbates and ligands do more than just stick to nanoparticles – they reduce plasmon lifetimes, change work functions, modify the density of states, and impact the energy and charge flow during various physical processes. Ultrafast thermalization under pulsed excitation and steady state conditions under continuous illumination open up different pathways for chemical reactions. Although the plasmonic metal is crucial, surface-bound molecules actively participate by scavenging charge carriers, affecting selectivity and stability, and even undergoing chemical transformations. These aspects are crucial for controlling product distributions and enabling novel chemical pathways by exploiting excited-state pathways inaccessible through thermal energy. Together with the nanoscale properties of plasmonic nanostructures, chemical reactions can be confined to nanoscale hot spots shaped by geometry and polarization. These insights inform the development of practical design principles for antenna–reactor hybrids and novel plasmonic materials in which absorption, carrier localization, and interfacial alignment are precisely engineered. Finally, we identify key open questions and the need for operando interfacial techniques to transform these insights into practical tools for selective, solar-driven synthesis.

papers.title: Time-resolved Extreme Ultraviolet Photoelectron Spectroscopy of 4-Bromophenolate Anions in a Liquid Jet
papers.abstract: femtosecond extreme ultraviolet (XUV) time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (TRPES) in a liquid flat jet. Excitation to the first singlet S 1 (1 1 ππ * ) excited state at 290 nm yields lifetimes of ~160 fs and 1.1 ps that are attributed to the timescale for the transition from the initially excited S 1 state to the optically-dark 1 πσ * state and the subsequent decay of the 1 πσ * state, respectively. Excitation at 240 nm to the second singlet excited state (S 2 , 2 1 ππ * ) reveals an additional ultrafast component assigned to decay from the S 2 to the S 1 state with a lifetime of 60 fs. Subsequent decay components show lifetimes of 130 fs and 1.4 ps, corresponding to the transition from S 1 to the 1 πσ * state and its subsequent decay. In contrast to phenolate anions, which result in hydrated electron formation within ~20 ps upon S1 excitation, 4-bromophenolate undergoes rapid decay through the 1 πσ * state, which is repulsive along the C-Br bond length and correlates to C 6 H 4 O + Brˉ. Quantum chemical calculations suggest that the S 1 - 1 πσ * state crossing possesses a small potential energy barrier that promotes a facile non-adiabatic transition. By comparison with phenolate photo-oxidation dynamics, this study highlights the

papers.title: Complex Network Theory-Driven Rational Design of Ionic Liquid-Based Solid Electrolytes: A New Paradigm
papers.abstract: The development of traditional solid electrolytes has long been constrained by empirical “trial-and-error” approaches. The introduction of complex network theory provides a systematic analytical framework and rational design paradigm for this field. This perspective aims to systematically elaborate on the application of this paradigm in the design and optimization of ionic liquid (IL)-based solid electrolytes. First, we clarify the core concept of abstracting electrolyte systems as dynamic networks (where nodes represent structural units and edges represent transport pathways or interactions) and explore its unique advantages in establishing quantitative “structure-property” relationships. Subsequently, we provide a detailed review of the practical applications of this methodology, mainly including: (1) graph theory-based network topological characterization (such as tortuosity, percolation threshold/critical concentration); (2) network connectivity design based on percolation theory; (3) ion transport mechanism analysis based on network dynamics (such as random walk models, cooperative “paddle-wheel effect”); and (4) performance correlation and prediction based on multiscale network models. On this basis, we systematically summarize IL-functionalization design strategies inspired by network concepts, covering node engineering (covalent grafting, physical doping, interfacial modification), edge property regulation (reducing energy barriers, constructing fast ion channels, dynamic reconstruction), and modular multiscale network integration. Particularly, we deeply explore the frontier direction of integrating complex network theory with machine learning, such as automated network feature extraction, topological inverse optimization, and performance evolution prediction, opening new pathways for high-throughput design and performance prediction of electrolytes. Finally, based on the “network topology blueprint,” we propose a closed-loop design paradigm for IL-based solid electrolytes and prospect the future development of deep integration among network science, materials informatics, and artificial intelligence, aiming to provide systematic methodological guidance for promoting the rational design of high-performance, high-safety solid-state batteries.

papers.title: Enhancing Chemistry Education with Forensic Science: Smartphone Analysis of the Luminol Reaction
papers.abstract: This study examines the use of a smartphone ambient light sensor to monitor the chemiluminescent reaction of luminol (5-amino-2, 3-dihydro-1, 4-phthalazinedione). Light emission generated in reactions catalyzed by Fe 3+ or Cu 2+ and oxidized by H 2 O 2 or NaClO was recorded using a Samsung Galaxy J5 and compared with measurements from a PASCO PASPORT High Sensitivity Light Sensor. The temporal evolution of light intensity could be narrowly described by a Gamma-type or a Lognormal function, representing a rapid rise followed by exponential decay. As expected, the addition of fluorescein in the reaction medium increased emission intensity and shifted the emission wavelength. Smartphone light sensors provide a low-cost platform for kinetic analysis of chemiluminescent reactions in instructional laboratories.

papers.title: Symmetry-Adapted Relaxation Theory (SART): variational embedding for convergent infinite-order induction without overpolarization
papers.abstract: The induction part of intermolecular interaction energy describes the effect of the mutual polarization of subsystems. Low-order induction effects can be reasonably described by symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT), but the capture of important higher-order polarization effects requires the use of an external correction from supermolecular Hartree-Fock (HF) theory, which is not free from artifacts. When one describes induction through a response to an embedding potential representing the other molecule(s) (which is the case in a number of existing approaches such as the electrostatic embedding, Hartree-Hartree-Fock, and explicit polarization (XPol) methods), it is easy to succumb to overpolarization unless the embedding potential fully accounts for the exchange effects, enforcing the Pauli exclusion principle and preventing a variational collapse to a Pauli-forbidden state. Here, we propose a new embedding framework that accounts for both electrostatic polarization and exchange effects in many-body systems. As a proof of principle, we apply the novel embedding potentials in a variational approach called symmetry-adapted relaxation theory (SART) that succeeds in recovering infinite-order induction energy from the HF method without a need to compute the HF wavefunction or energy of the entire complex. SART is expected to be the foundation for a new class of intermolecular perturbation theories, while the newly proposed potentials can also be applied to incorporate complete exchange into various embedding algorithms.

papers.title: Field-Assisted Substrate Ionization as a Plausible Initiating Step in Enzyme Catalysis
papers.abstract: Enzymes are widely understood to accelerate chemical reactions through transition-state stabilization and optimizing the orientation of reactants within their active sites. A growing body of work highlights the central role of strong electrostatic fields in these processes with magnitudes reaching ~108–1010 V/m in enzyme active sites. Here, we explore the hypothesis that such fields may, in some cases, facilitate catalysis by inducing field-assisted electron transfer or partial ionization of bound substrates. To assess the plausibility of this mechanism, semiclassical tunneling expressions in the quasistatic limit were applied to a curated dataset of enzymatic substrates with experimentally known or machine-learning-predicted ionization potentials. At field strengths of an order ≳ 1010 V/m, estimated ionization rates span the nanosecond-to-picosecond regime for a subset of substrates, suggesting that field-induced tunneling may render electron-transfer events statistically accessible within the residence time of enzyme–substrate complexes. These results are recast in probabilistic terms, showing that even modest tunneling rates can lead to non-negligible ionization probabilities over biologically relevant timescales. Electronic-structure calculations on the ketosteroid isomerase substrate (5-androstene-3,17-dione) indicate that one-electron oxidation leads to a redistribution of electron density consistent with enhancing electrophilic character at its reactive sites. While the tunneling expressions employed here are not intended to provide quantitatively predictive rates in condensed enzymatic environments, they offer a physically motivated metric for assessing the sensitivity of ionization barriers to strong electrostatic fields. Taken together, these results suggest that field-assisted substrate ionization or oxidation may represent a plausible, though not yet established, mechanistic component in certain enzyme-catalyzed reactions.

papers.title: The assembly of fused pyridazines via one-pot sequence IEDDA reaction, scope and limitations
papers.abstract: We suggested and optimized a convenient one-pot protocol for the preparation of a series of pyridazines fused to saturated oxa- and aza-heterocyclic moieties. The effectiveness of the approach allowed fusion with five-, six-, seven-, and eight-membered rings. Collidine was found to be the most beneficial base for the transformation. We tested the reaction time and temperature to optimize the conversion. The neutral solvents with reasonable boiling points were used in each case. We tested the reaction for multigame scale, and the high yields were determined for 5 and 6-membered cycles. The use of stable, readily available amine hydrochlorides without additional protection is an advantage of the suggested approach. The obtained series of compounds was used as building blocks for further modifications.

papers.title: Understanding Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering Experiments of Diazines via Quantum Dynamics Simulation†
papers.abstract: We present a combined theoretical and experimental study of the three diazine isomers pyrazine, pyrimidine, and pyridazine by means of resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) at the Nitrogen K-edge, employing fully time-dependent quantum dynamics simulations to understand the role of nuclear motion in core-excited states. The RIXS process is simulated by wavepacket propagation in both, the valence and core excited state manifold, carried out with the (multilayer) multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree [(ML-)MCTDH] method. We use linear vibronic coupling Hamiltonians with up to 22 electronic states and compare a full-dimensional (24-mode) and a reduced six-mode model. We find good agreement between experiment and theory for all three molecules. In particular, our study highlights the essential role of nuclear motions during the population of short-lived intermediate core-excited states. Specifically, we show that ultrafast non-adiabatic transitions induce symmetry distortion that lead to additional emission bands, while interstate vibrational dynamics lead to vibrational progressions in the inelastic scattering spectra. These results establish a dynamical picture of the RIXS process in diazines that emphasises the importance of including nuclear dynamics in the calculations of resonant Raman processes.

papers.title: Strongly Coordinated Al3+ Complex Formation Prevents Reversible Electrochemical Cycling in Haloaluminate-Free Ionic Liquids
papers.abstract: Advancements in aluminium-ion batteries require new non-corrosive electrolytes with high oxidation stability. Recently, haloaluminate-free electrolytes based on Al(OTF) 3 and Al(TFSI) 3 salts have attracted interest for aluminum electrochemistry; nevertheless, reversible Al 0/3+ cycling in these systems remains debated. This work reveals that Al 0 electrodeposition universally fails in Al(OTF) 3 and Al(TFSI) 3 based ionic liquid electrolytes because Al 3+ spontaneously extracts F - from anion and OH - from residual water, forming tightly bound tetrahedral complexes. Energy calculations show that deprotonation of coordinated water requires far less energy than Al 3+ desolvation, explaining why hydrogen evolution dominates. Even rigorous vacuum drying and LiAlH 4 addition cannot eliminate residual water from these hygroscopic salts. These findings provide a fresh perspective on aluminium electrolyte design, emphasizing ligand stability as a prerequisite for diversifying reaction towards Al 3+ desolvation and electroplating over parasitic processes.

papers.title: Which Metrics Best Capture Protein Structural Change in Molecular Dynamics Simulations? Evaluating Score Combinations and Force Field Effects
papers.abstract: The scores RMSD, TM-score, GDT, lDDT, SphereGrinder, CAD, QCS, FlexE, and MolProbity provide an automated, comprehensive assessment of conformational changes and structural quality of proteins and thus represent a promising tool for routine use in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, particularly in high-throughput settings. However, it remains unclear to what extent these scores provide redundant information and which scores are most informative for capturing conformational changes. Based on MD simulations of 268 diverse proteins, we demonstrate that the investigated scores are highly correlated and that one global score (or QCS), one local score, and FlexE capture almost 90% of the variance across all scores. Since MD randomness partially explains FlexE’s variability, we argue that a combination of one global and one local score is sufficient for most practical applications. We also investigate the influence of simulation setups and find that the choice of the force field can significantly affect scoring results. In particular, the setup using the Amber ff19sb force field yields systematically different scores than all CHARMM36m-based setups, emphasizing the importance of methodological choices when designing MD experiments and interpreting their results.

papers.title: Benchmarking Molecular Dynamics Simulations and Machine Learning Methods for Predicting Hydrocarbon Thermophysical Properties
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of the thermophysical properties of hydrocarbons is critical to the rational design of fuels, lubricants, and cooling fluids. We compare the performance of two widely used computational approaches for the prediction of the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of pure hydrocarbons, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML). To train the ML models, we construct a database containing more than 5,500 experimental data points for around 1,200 unique organic molecules between C10-C50, which is the expected range for lubricant base oils. We evaluate a range of ML architectures and molecular representations trained on this new database, which is the largest of its kind for these molecule sizes and property ranges. The XGBoost models trained on molecular descriptors consistently achieved the best predictive performance, significantly outperforming MD simulations across all properties for our selected target molecules. This study demonstrates that ML models trained on large experimental datasets can accurately predict the thermophysical properties of unseen hydrocarbons. The computational cost of the ML models is several orders of magnitude lower than the MD simulations, which makes them well-suited to high-throughput virtual screening workflows. Our methodology provides a valuable tool for the data-driven discovery of new candidate molecules for advanced lubricants and other formulated products.

papers.title: ROS-Programmed Intracellular Reaction Pathway Switching Enables Selective Nuclear Targeting of Nucleic Acids in Cancer Cells
papers.abstract: Selective chemical targeting of nucleic acids (NAs) in cancer cells remains constrained by the poor cytotoxic selectivity of classical NAs-reactive drugs for malignant over healthy proliferating tissues. Although elevated intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) provide a basis for conditional drug activation, directing ROS-responsive chemistry toward ROS-poor compartments such as the nucleus has remained a fundamental challenge. Here we report an ROS-programmed prodrug (5) that undergoes stimulus-dependent intracellular chemical transformation, enabling selective nucleic-acid targeting in cancer cells. In ROS-rich environments, prodrug 5 is converted into an active metabolite (6) that redistributes from lysosomal entry sites to nucleoli and mitochondria, where localized ROS amplification induces nucleic acid oxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and rapid shutdown of global protein synthesis, culminating in necrotic cell death. Under low-ROS conditions, including antioxidant-treated cancer cells and healthy fibroblasts, or in the presence of ROS-insensitive analogue of prodrug 5 (compound 12), an alternative intracellular pathway dominates, resulting in lysosomal sequestration and degradation without cytotoxic activation. Integrated imaging, biochemical analyses, and transcriptomics reveal that this chemistry-in-cells process initiates a coordinated nucleolar–mitochondrial stress cascade and integrated stress response rather than apoptosis. In vivo - evaluation in a syngeneic murine fibrosarcoma model demonstrates pronounced but heterogeneous antitumor activity consistent with variable tumor ROS levels, supporting a patient-stratified therapeutic strategy. These results establish intracellular reaction-pathway switching as a strategy to control organelle-specific drug activation and introduce ROS-directed chemical amplification as an approach for selective nuclear nucleic-acid targeting in cancer.

papers.title: Ensemble-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy: A Feature-Driven Framework for Microbial Classification and Spectral Interpretation
papers.abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of bacterial pathogens is essential in clinical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and food safety control. Here, we report an ensemble-enhanced Raman spectroscopy approach for the classification and spectral interpretation of nine bacterial species belonging to both Gram-positive and Gram-negative groups. Raman spectra were acquired from bacterial cells and preprocessed to isolate the fingerprint region, followed by a hybrid feature selection strategy integrating mutual information and random forest-based feature importance. The developed methodology demonstrated an overall classification accuracy of around 96% for the nine bacterial species by utilizing an optimized stacked ensemble of machine learning models. Our methodology outperformed other individual machine learning models, such as random forest, support vector machine, and standalone CNN models. Additionally, the developed methodology identified biochemically relevant Raman spectral features related to proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids, which provided valuable information on the molecular basis of bacterial differentiation. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of this ensemble Raman-machine learning platform as a rapid, label-free, and interpretable approach for culture-independent microbial classification.

papers.title: Standard reporting of the uncertainty in reaction yield applied to a CO2 transfer reaction
papers.abstract: In the organic literature, reaction yields are typically reported as single values with no estimate of uncertainty that would enable others to judge the reproducibility of reported procedures. Herein, we demonstrate a simple, standardised approach for reporting reaction yield as its mean value, accompanied by a confidence interval calculated from repeat experiments. We use CO 2 transfer carboxylation to show that variability plots and confidence intervals provide interpretable measures of yield reproducibility and are useful tools to identify outliers and prompt scrutiny of scale-up behaviour or sources of experimental variability. We make recommendations for best practice in reporting the variability of experimental outcomes and introduce a secure browser-based tool, the Physical Sciences Data Infrastructure (PSDI) Variability Plot Generator, to facilitate transparent reporting of process reproducibility.

papers.title: Active Delta-Learning for Surface Hopping: Efficient Fitting of Potential Energy Surfaces
papers.abstract: Active learning has become central to modern machine-learning workflows for trajectory surface hopping, enabling automatic construction of training sets for excited state potentials. However, currently used protocols can struggle with convergence, requiring large datasets and extensive human intervention. Here, we combine active learning with ∆-learning–where the ML model predicts the difference between a target quantum chemical method and a computationally efficient baseline–into an end-to-end protocol for active delta-learning (ADL) of surface hopping dynamics. The protocol is tested on a benchmark system, fulvene, where a twofold data efficiency is achieved with respect to fine-tuning from a pre-trained foundational model, OMNI-P2x. Next, we analyze the case of PSB4, a protonated Schiff base with multiple competing torsional deactivation channels. Here, pure ML active learning fails to converge despite extensive sampling of over 14000 points, while ADL converges within just two iterations and 900 sampled points, yielding good agreement with the reference, unreachable with pure ML.

papers.title: Two-Stage Chemical Degradation of PTFE with H- and HO-radicals: A DFT Study under PEMFC Operating Conditions
papers.abstract: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) plays a fundamental role in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFC) as it enhances the structural integrity of the gas diffusion layer and microporous layer, and more importantly, helps with water management. However, it is also vulnerable to different kinds of degradation under PEMFC operating conditions. One of these degradations is the chemical degradation under HO-radical attack. In this DFT study, we propose a two-stage degradation mechanism in which the process is initiated by H-radical attack on PTFE and subsequently propagated through reactions with HO-radical. For this, a comparative DFT study was conducted to investigate six chemical degradation pathways of PTFE via HO-radical at the ab initio PBE0/def2-TZVPP level. The Solvation Model based on Density (SMD) was employed as an implicit solvation model with water as the solvent to model PEMFC conditions. Reaction enthalpies, Gibbs free energies, and activation free energies were calculated for all elementary steps. Among the competing routes, pathways initiated at secondary carbon sites are both thermodynamically and kinetically favored, ultimately resulting in PTFE chain scission and CO2 plus water formation.

papers.title: Isolated Ti-sites in Silica-Supported Ruthenium Nanoparticles favor Ru Cluster formation and CO2 Methanation
papers.abstract: Efficient CO 2 methanation using renewable H 2 is an attractive route in the context of Power to X. Notably, Ru/TiO 2 display high activity, highlighting the potential role of Ru/TiO 2 interfaces. Here, using surface organometallic chemistry (SOMC), Ru nanoparticles supported on silica, with and without tailored Ti interfaces, are prepared and their catalytic performances compared. Namely, Ru nanoparticles supported on silica containing highly dispersed Ti sites (Ru/Ti@SiO 2 ) exhib-its notable CO 2 hydrogenation activity at 1 bar (H 2 /CO 2 /Ar = 4/1/5), achieving a methane formation rate reaching 39.7 mol CH4 ·mol Ru -1 ·h -1 with >99% CH 4 selectivity at 200 °C. This performance is markedly higher than the Ti-free benchmark catalyst, Ru/SiO 2 (14.9 mol CH4 ·mol Ru -1 ·h -1 , >99% CH 4 ). A pool of characterization techniques (HAADF-STEM, Ru K-edge XAS, XPS, CO-IR and CO chemisorption) shows that dispersed Ti sites induce an increase of Ru dispersion, i.e. formation of Ru clusters, and indicate that the enhanced methanation activity is mostly due to an increased dispersion and number of exposed Ru sites rather than a change in intrinsic site activity of Ru metal sites. This study demonstrates that the role of isolated Ti is primarily structural rather than electronic.

papers.title: Towards Scalable and Efficient Machine-Learning Force Fields: The MatPL package and Its Advancements on Neuroevolution Potentials
papers.abstract: The development of accurate and efficient machine-learning interatomic potentials is a transformative technology in computational materials science and molecular dynamics simulations. Here, we introduce the Materials Potential Library (MatPL) , a comprehensive software framework integrating multiple machine-learning potential architectures, with a particular emphasis on advancing the neuroevolution potential (NEP) framework. MatPL incorporates gradient-based optimizers to improve training stability and accuracy. A key innovation is its highly optimized, GPU-native interface for LAMMPS, seamlessly integrated with LAMMPS’s robust Message Passing Interface (MPI) infrastructure. This design transcends the limitations of single-node GPU execution, enabling efficient cross-node scalability without compromising the computational efficiency intrinsic to NEP. MatPL is a high-performance and versatile platform for next-generation atomistic modeling, balancing between high accuracy, training efficiency, and large-scale simulation capability.

papers.title: Molecular Structure Determines Phase Selectivity in Quasi-2D Halide Perovskites
papers.abstract: Controlling the phase distribution in quasi-two-dimensional (2D) halide perovskites (HPs) is a crucial bottleneck for bespoke manipulation of their optoelectronic functionalities. This mainly lies in the subtle interaction between molecular spacers and inorganic precursors during crystallization that steers phase synthesizability, which has been poorly explored. Here, we investigate the synthesis spaces of two distinct quasi-2D HPs incorporating phenylethylammonium (PEA) and octylammonium (OA)-possessing comparable molecular masses but different structures and chemical properties. Utilization of a high-throughput automated experimental workflow combined with a deep-learning analytic framework allows for fully uncovering the latent synthesis landscape and distinct crystallization behaviors across the two systems. Specifically, while PEA promotes rapid crystallization and the formation of multiple low-n phases, the OA system exhibits slower crystallization and a strong preference for single-phase growth. Such a selective and controlled behavior is found to originate from the structural instability of n=1 OA2PbI4 arising from alkyl chain-induced lattice distortion. These findings demonstrate how spacer molecular structure directs crystallization pathways and phase landscapes, which offer a guideline for the rational design of phase-controlled quasi-2D HPs from conventional nonequilibrium synthetic processes, thus benefiting future optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Synthesis of two methylolanthanin derivatives and the investigation of their lanthanide and iron binding capabilities
papers.abstract: Lanthanides (Lns) have recently been recognized as essential cofactors for certain bacterial enzymes, such as the methanol dehydrogenase (MDH), yet their poor bioavailability under physiological conditions has long suggested the existence of Ln-binding metallophores termed lanthanophores. In this context methylolanthanin (MLL), a chelator which is potentially involved in Ln-uptake of methylotrophic bacteria, was recently isolated and characterized. Herein we synthesized, two novel MLL derivatives, ortho- and meta- MLL, for comparative studies in order to gain a deeper insight into the unusual 4-hydroxy benzoate moiety of native para- MLL. For this we implemented UV-vis titrations, time-resolved laser-induced fluorescence spectroscopy (TRLFS) and ion mobility spectrometry-mass spectrometry (IMS-MS) complemented by density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate metal-binding behavior in both solution and gas phase to trivalent Lns. As our binding studies revealed that both artificial chelators tend to precipitate Lns similarly to the native para- MLL under biologically relevant conditions (pH 6.0), rather than solubilizing them, the solubility products of their Eu 3+ complexes were determined. Due to structural resemblance of the MLL derivatives to the siderophore rhodopetrobactin B (RPB B), we also investigated iron binding. In this regard ortho- MLL stood out in our analysis and showed a distinctly different binding behavior than the other two derivatives.

papers.title: Superimposed Coding of Count Fingerprints to Binary Fingerprints
PolycIMS: Polymers for Automated Cyclic Ion Mobility Spectrometry Calibration
papers.abstract: The development and commercialization of cyclic ion mobility spectrometry (cIMS) instruments has considerably expanded the level of structural details that can be accessed for gaseous ions. Commercial cIMS instruments rely on travelling wave ion mobility spectrometry (TWIMS), a technique that requires calibration of the measured arrival times to enable the determination of collisional cross sections (CCS). Most calibration strategies use peptide mixtures that span a CCS range of approximately 100 – 400 Å2, which can introduce significant inaccuracies when extrapolating to larger ion structures. In addition, TWIMS calibration remains a tedious data processing step that would greatly benefit from automation. Here, we introduce polycIMS, a command-line tool that automates cIMS calibration and generates charge-independent calibration curves covering a broad CCS range from 100 – 1500 Å², within just 3 minutes on a standard laptop. Calibrated CCS can be determined in He or N 2 ( TW CCS N2→He , TW CCS N2→N2 ) using inexpensive, commercially-available polymer standards and are validated against reported values for more than 50 reference ions. Furthermore, the derived calibration parameters are largely insensitive to collisional activation, making it possible to calibrate multistage cIMS workflows such as slice collision induced unfolding (CIU n ). We anticipate that the simplicity and accessibility of polycIMS will encourage its adoption as a new standard for cIMS calibration.

papers.title: Polyurethane Foams from a Triblock Copolymer Polyol with CO2-Derived, High-Tg Polycarbonate Segments
papers.abstract: We report the first polyurethane foams (PUFs) containing segments with a glass transition temperature (Tg) above 100 °C. The PUF properties are tuned by incorporating 0-15 wt% CO2- derived poly(cyclohexene carbonate) (PCHC) segments (Tg = 104 °C), and the PUF thermal resistance is markedly improved by incorporating PCHC segments. The network PUFs are synthesized using a triblock copolymer polyol with PCHC hard segments and a polycaprolactone (PCL) soft segment (PCHC-b-PCL-b-PCHC; 16 wt% CO2-derived). The room-temperature polyol is liquid, and its viscosity is adjusted by adding a low-viscosity PCL homopolymer polyol. Incorporating PCHC segments produces denser PUFs with smaller, more uniform cells. Increasing PCHC content from 0 to 15 wt% decreases PCL crystallinity from 29% to 5%. Compared to a PCHC-free PUF, at room temperature, a 15 wt% PCHC PUF exhibits ~40% reductions in compression modulus and compression strength (at 25% strain); however, it exhibits a fivefold increase in compression modulus and a 210% rise in compression strength at 70 °C, where crystallinity is absent. Thus, certain properties of PCHC-containing PUFs are much less temperature-dependent than those of PCHC-free PUFs: 15 wt% PCHC PUFs retain 54% of their room-temperature compression modulus at 70 °C, but PCHC-free PUFs retain only 7%.

papers.title: Design Rules for Tuning Thermal Lifetimes of Arylazopyrazole Photoswitches
papers.abstract: Predicting thermal relaxation rates in molecular photoswitches remains a major challenge, as competing reaction pathways and multiple electronic states govern their isomerization dynamics. Arylazopyrazoles exemplify this complexity while offering nearly quantitative bidirectional photoconversion and widely tunable thermal half-lives. Here, we map the isomerization landscapes of nearly 30,000 arylazopyrazole derivatives using a machine-learned interatomic potential trained on density functional theory data, enabling high-throughput simultaneous exploration of adiabatic and nonadiabatic pathways. The workflow identifies minima, transition states, and minimum-energy crossing points, allowing thermal relaxation rates to be computed at scale. Comparison with available experimental data demonstrates reliable prediction of absolute rate constants. Across chemical space, we uncover clear structure-mechanism-property relationships linking substituent position, pyrazole methylation, and electronic substitution patterns to mechanistic preference and overall relaxation kinetics. These results provide practical design rules for tuning the thermal stability of arylazopyrazole photoswitches and establish a general strategy for predicting relaxation kinetics in complex molecular switches.

papers.title: Chemically Interpretable Explanations for Molecular Property Prediction via Fragment-Level Shapley Values
papers.abstract: Machine learning has emerged as a powerful approach for molecular property prediction and drug discovery. However, the black-box nature of many machine learning models limits their interpretability, trustworthiness, and adoption in interdisciplinary research settings. This is especially the case in molecular machine learning, where explanations of model predictions are used for informed decision-making and downstream tasks. Shapley values, originating from cooperative game theory, provide a principled framework for attributing model predictions to individual input features. However, existing Shapley value-based explanations for molecular machine learning often rely on sampling-based approximations or operate at the level of abstract features, which can reduce attribution stability and limit chemical interpretability and actionability. Here, we introduce a fragment-level Shapley value framework that enables the exact computation of feature contributions at the level of chemically meaningful fragments for molecular property predictions without relying on sampling or feature imputation. By decomposing molecules into fragments, the proposed approach yields actionable explanations that can be directly related to established chemical concepts. We apply the method post hoc to random forest and graph convolutional network models using common molecular representations, including extended-connectivity fingerprints and molecular graphs. The approach is evaluated across three representative property prediction tasks: aqueous solubility, mutagenicity, and antiviral potency. Fragment-level Shapley values reproduce wellestablished chemical trends, identify known toxicophores, and enable guided molecular optimization. In addition, the method provides insights into model learning characteristics and helps delineate the applicability domain, particularly in settings with limited and structurally biased data. Overall, this work demonstrates that adapting Shapley values to chemically meaningful fragments enables interpretable explanations for molecular machine learning models, supporting molecular optimization and model validation.

papers.title: A coarse-grained molecular dynamics study of nanoscale phospholipid-cholesterol exosomes: curvature effects on cholesterol distribution and vesicle structure
papers.abstract: Nanoscale lipid bilayer vesicles are widely used as model systems for exosomes and synaptic vesicles, released by cells for intercellular communication, in which strong membrane curvature couples molecular packing to leaflet asymmetry. Here, we investigate DPPC, POPC or DLiPC phospholipid (PC)/cholesterol bilayer vesicles using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, systematically varying phospholipid chain unsaturation, cholesterol content (0–50 mol%), and vesicle diameter (10–30 nm for the DPPC system). Cholesterol undergoes rapid redistribution on submicrosecond timescales, and is preferentially enriched in the inner leaflet of all vesicles studied, with the degree of asymmetry depending on the vesicle curvature, cholesterol content and PC chain saturation. Increasing cholesterol content induces bilayer thickening, reduced area per lipid and enhanced chain ordering. Highly curved vesicles are thinner than planar bilayers. These effects depend strongly on PC unsaturation and vesicle size, highlighting the synergistic role of these variables in controlling membrane structure and cholesterol partitioning in exosome-like vesicles.

papers.title: Electron Alchemy with Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials: Case Studies of Local Charge in Bond Dissociation Curves
papers.abstract: The convergence of all-atom molecular dynamics (AAMD) simulations and machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promises density functional theory (DFT) level accuracy at near-classical force-field computational costs. However, while the average fidelity to reference energies and forces approaches perfection, several failure modes limit MLIP reliability in production simulations. These include spurious bond formation, inconsistent reproduction of long-range interactions, and inconsistent spin-state reference. Here, the origins of these behaviors are studied by benchmarking the UMA, ORB, MACE, and AIMNet2 models against reference DFT bond dissociation curves for an illustrative range of species. These benchmarks reveal that models without explicit atomic charge resolution predict spurious stable bonds between like-charged halide anions, effectively transmuting two Cl – ions into neutral Cl 2 . Models with atomic partial charge equilibration correctly predict repulsion in these systems. Conversely, several secondary limitations are exposed in these benchmarks, including inconsistent agreement with unrestricted versus restricted DFT energies and inconsistent core-region treatment. This comparative analysis suggests that, while artifacts related to core repulsion and asymptotic electrostatics are readily repairable through improved physical priors and better data curation, the issue of spurious bond formation is intrinsic to the inability of global charge specification to disambiguate similar local geometries at different charge and spin states.

papers.title: Pesticide Residue Profiling in Nigerian Cassava Tubers by GC-MS and Machine Learning-Based Toxicological Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: Pesticide residues in staple crops pose significant health risks requiring both accurate detection and toxicological evaluation. Traditional approaches separate analytical chemistry from toxicity assessment, limiting comprehensive risk characterization. We developed an integrated platform combining GC-MS residue analysis of cassava tubers from Nigerian farmland with machine learning toxicity prediction using Mordred molecular descriptors. Seven pesticides were detected and quantified across three composite samples, then subjected to Ames mutagenicity and carcinogenicity prediction using Random Forest and Gradient Boosting models trained on curated toxicological datasets. A web-based API enables real-time risk assessment combining concentration data with computational toxicology outputs. GC-MS analysis detected seven pesticides spanning three chemical classes — organochlorines (dieldrin, endrin, endosulfan II, methoxychlor), organophosphates (parathion, dimethoate), and a pyrethroid (deltamethrin) — all below Maximum Residue Limits (0.40–2.20% of MRL). ML models predicted all compounds as non-mutagenic and non-carcinogenic; however, Ames mutagenicity concordance with established literature classifications was 28.6%, indicating under-prediction of mutagenic activity for known organochlorine mutagens. Integrated risk assessment identified four compounds warranting MEDIUM priority monitoring despite regulatory compliance. This methodology bridges analytical chemistry and computational toxicology, providing a practical screening tool particularly relevant for developing country food safety programs, while transparently demonstrating current limitations of molecular descriptor-based toxicity prediction for persistent organochlorine compounds.

papers.title: High-fidelity methane plume modelling over coal mines: Integrating Large Eddy Simulations (LES) with remote sensing imagery
papers.abstract: Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from coal mine shafts represent 33% of the global CH 4 fossil fuel emissions into the atmosphere, and are subject to stricter regulations drafted in recent years (e.g. EU, China). Different measurement strategies have been deployed to quantify the amounts of CH 4 released, primarily onboard aircraft and satellites. For the first time, we simulate the CH 4 plume dynamics at high resolution using Large Eddy Simulations (LES) forced by meteorological data, obstacles (such as trees and buildings), 1-m terrain topologies, and exact source characterisation. We validated the plume characteristics against path-integrated measurements from a ground-based spectrometer horizontally scanning the coal mine plume from Pniówek V (Poland). We demonstrate that the exit velocity of the mine shaft’s gas, its concentration and the turbulence conditions are the key drivers to reproduce the CH 4 plume behaviour and magnitude.
