We estimated the uncertainties to be 9% (±2.5 m) for the altitude of maximum values and 17% for the peak CH 4 enhancement, resulting mainly from wind speed fluctuations. For coal mine shaft plumes, precise source characterisation is critical to simulation accuracy, whereas high-resolution terrain and building data are less essential. This is a direct result of the high-momentum, CH 4 -rich discharge from the diffusion tower, which dictates the plume trajectory more than local surface geometry.

papers.title: CysSelect: A Browser-Based Platform for Chemoproteomic Hit Calling, Enantiopair Analysis, Simulation, and Next-Library Design for Covalent Fragment Discovery
papers.abstract: Proteome-scale cysteine chemoproteomics has made it increasingly feasible to identify ligandable sites directly in native biological systems, but converting screening outputs into experimentally actionable decisions remains difficult. Practical bottlenecks include data quality control, transformation of peptide-intensity tables into interpretable competition metrics, comparison of enantiomer-resolved fragment behavior, prioritization of selective over broadly reactive interactions, and rational selection of improved compounds for subsequent screening rounds. Here, we present CysSelect, a browser-based research application designed to integrate these tasks into a single workflow. CysSelect enables upload and quality control of chemoproteomic screening tables, calculation of competition ratio, percent competition, enantiomer-specific response summaries, and ΔAUC, aggregation of pair-level promiscuity and stereoselectivity, sweet-spot prioritization, optional simulation-based benchmarking, and virtual-library scoring for next-round compound selection. Conceptually, the platform is grounded in recent advances in activity-based protein profiling, enantiopair-guided chemoproteomics, and data-driven covalent fragment design, and is intended to make these analytical principles easier to apply in routine research settings. By combining real-data analysis, synthetic benchmarking, and prospective library triage within an interactive browser interface, CysSelect provides a practical computational layer for covalent probe discovery, workflow standardization, and educational use. The platform is not intended to replace experimental validation, but rather to improve the transparency, reproducibility, and operational usefulness of chemoproteomic interpretation.

papers.title: Oncogenic resonance: a tensor approach to DNA stability
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a universal theoretical mapping covering the entire landscape of the 753 known oncogenes, defining a new paradigm in the understanding of genomic stability. Through a conceptual architecture that integrates the principles of Quantum Field Theory (QFT) with structural molecular biology, we have succeeded in describing the entire energetic configuration of the mutated double helix in terms of tensorial fields. The core of the research lies in the resolution of the Schrödinger equation applied to the singularities of hydrogen bonds, solved through an advanced computational protocol that systematically processed every oncogenic sequence. The results yield the complete spectrum of critical resonance frequencies (finterv), identifying the mechanical breaking points necessary to induce the selective collapse of tumor units only. This dataset constitutes the first operational encyclopedia of quantum biophysics applied to oncology, paving the way for therapies with zero biological impact.

papers.title: Emerging Trends in Biodegradable Polymers Derived from Vegetable Waste for Sustainable Agriculture: Challenges and Opportunities
papers.abstract: The widespread use of plastic in farming has greatly increased crop yields and made better use of resources. However, it has also had bad effects on the environment. Plastic waste from farming, such as mulch films, greenhouse coverings, and irrigation parts, breaks down and breaks apart, which leads to the buildup of microplastics in the soil. These microplastics stay in the soil for a long time, changing its physical and chemical properties, affecting microbial communities, messing up nutrient cycling, and possibly getting into the food chain. To solve these problems, we need to switch to more sustainable materials. Biodegradable plastics have come up as a promising answer. These are materials that can break down into natural substances like carbon dioxide, water, and biomass through the action of microbes. They are put into groups based on where they come from (bio-based or fossil-based) and how easy they are to break down. There is a big difference between bioplastics and regular plastics made from petroleum in terms of feedstock, how they break down, and how they affect the environment. Global market trends show that more people want biodegradable materials. This is because people are becoming more aware of the environment, technology is getting better, and policies are being put in place to reduce plastic pollution. Also, using green chemistry ideas in the creation of sustainable materials leads to synthesis processes that are good for the environment. In polymer science, green synthesis methods focus on using renewable materials, making products with less harmful chemicals, and using less energy. In this case, vegetable waste is a useful renewable resource for making biopolymers. This helps with degradation and strategies for a circular economy. To reduce plastic pollution in agriculture and make sure that soil health is managed in a way that lasts, it is important to combine biodegradable materials, green chemistry methods, and rules.

papers.title: DCM Alternatives for use in Steglich Esterifications, for Green and Sustainable Liquid Crystal Syntheses
papers.abstract: Dichloromethane (DCM) is a popular solvent for the synthesis of liquid crystalline materials owing to its solvating power, moderate polarity, and ease of removal. The environmental and toxicological issues surrounding DCM prompt us to explore alternatives. Here, we have screened an extensive selection of green and sustainable solvents to find the most efficacious DCM alternative for the synthesis of a conventional liquid crystal, CZP-5-N. Several factors are considered: yield, environmental impact, and health and safety concerns. The best performing solvent, dimethyl carbonate, was then used in the synthesis of common and novel liquid crystals, along with intermediates, giving excellent results, even for electron poor phenols. With esterifications prevalent in trending research areas like the ferroelectric nematic phase, this work allows a facile means for sustainability to be incorporated into synthetic pathways.

papers.title: QSAR as a Small-Deformation Theory of Effective Free-Energy Landscapes
papers.abstract: Quantitative structure-activity relationships (QSARs) remain widely used in medicinal chemistry, yet their physical interpretation is often limited and the meaning of their applicability domain (AD) is commonly treated in statistical or descriptor-space terms. Here we propose a conceptual framework in which QSAR is interpreted as a small-deformation theory of effective free-energy landscapes. Ligand binding or chemical substitution is represented as a perturbation of an effective free-energy landscape defined over reduced state variables, and the resulting free-energy response is expressed as a contracted observable over the equilibrium ensemble of the reference system via a Zwanzig-type perturbation formula. In the small-deformation regime, this response reduces to a low-order expansion in descriptor space, from which conventional linear QSAR emerges as the leading-order approximation. QSAR coefficients are thereby interpreted as ensemble-averaged effective sensitivities of the free-energy landscape to descriptor perturbations. The AD acquires a physical meaning as the region in which a local loworder expansion of the free-energy response remains valid. In the small-deformation regime, this same region further corresponds to ligand-induced landscape perturbations that remain local, smooth, and sufficiently weak over the reference ensemble. Conversely, QSAR breakdown, including activity cliffs, induced fit, state-dependent binding, and strong nonlinearity, is associated with qualitative reorganization of the effective landscape. At second order, the framework further suggests a non-positive correction to the leading-order free-energy response, arising from the variance of the landscape perturbation over the reference ensemble. This variance correction reflects a fluctuation-assisted effect in which configurational heterogeneity within the pre-existing ensemble allows Boltzmann reweighting to redistribute statistical weight toward microstates more strongly influenced by the perturbation. As a result, the free-energy response becomes systematically lower than the leading-order ensemble-average estimate, consistent with Jensen’s inequality.

papers.title: Promoting electrochemical reactions using like-charged co-ions
papers.abstract: Electrochemistry plays a central role in energy conversion, sustainable chemistry, and biomedicine. Electrochemical devices often hinge on chemical processes at charged electrode-electrolyte interfaces, where intermolecular forces cause electrolyte ions to be attracted or repelled from the interfacial environment 1 . Electrostatically, opposite-charged counterions are attracted and like-charged co-ions are repelled, leading to charge separation that screens surfaces 2 . Yet, this ion de-mixing also incurs substantial entropic penalties. Electric double layer formation hinges on how electrostatic and entropic forces balance to govern ion distributions and charge transfer at interfaces 1,3 . While classical models for double layer formation predict co-ions are excluded from charged surfaces 4 , we show that co-ions can play a defining role in electrocatalytic reactions under the high surface potentials inherent to many electrochemical systems, even under low ion concentrations where the bulk electrolyte behaves ideally. By studying the hydrogen evolution reaction as a model system, we reveal that co-ion identity can influence reactivity to an equal or greater degree than counterion identity. Further, we show that large surface potentials can drive co-ion accumulation at interfaces, contradicting predictions from classical theory. More broadly, we reveal that co-ions can be designed with specific chemical functionalities to promote reactivity, such as acting as a hydroxide sink, and generalize our findings to electrochemical CO 2 reduction to demonstrate the versatility of co-ions to promote electrocatalytic reactions critical to the energy sciences.

papers.title: Near Infrared Imaging of H2O2 in Plants with Nanosensors under Environmentally Changing Conditions
papers.abstract: Optical sensors are powerful tools to monitor biological systems. However, their practical deployment is often limited by environmental interferences such as autofluorescence, mechanical motion and fluctuating illumination. These challenges are particularly pronounced in plants because they require and use light, which has impaired the use of (fluorescent) sensors for plant stress signals such as H 2 O 2 . Here, we present a ratiometric sensing platform that overcomes these limitations by integrating three spectrally distinct components: 1) an H 2 O 2 sensor based on aptamer modified near infrared (NIR) fluorescent single walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs, ~1000 nm), 2) a stable NIR reference based on polyethyleneglycol modified Egyptian Blue nanosheets (EBNS, 900-955 nm) and 3) a visible (VIS) signal (~641 nm) to correct for the NIR autofluorescence tail of plants (>835 nm). This ratiometric approach enables robust signal correction under relevant perturbations, including leaf rotation and wind-induced motion. Furthermore, it allows continuous H 2 O 2 monitoring under dynamically varying illumination conditions (>300%), resulting in a 75% enhancement in signal contrast compared to single-channel detection. By spectrally resolving nanosensor signals and endogenous plant autofluorescence, this strategy enables in vivo monitoring of stress-induced H 2 O 2 under realistic environmental conditions. It establishes interference-resistant optical sensing and advances field-deployable nanosensor technologies for precision agriculture.

papers.title: Donor-Acceptor Molecular Radical Engineering Enables Efficient Solar-Thermal Conversion for Water-Electricity Cogeneration
papers.abstract: Organic photothermal materials are promising for solar-driven water purification and thermoelectric energy harvesting, yet their practical deployment is frequently limited by insufficient solar utilization, suboptimal photothermal conversion, and photobleaching under prolonged irradiation. Here we report TBT–ThT–O, an openshell donor–acceptor small molecule in which a strong D–π–A–π–D framework, 𝜋bridge extension, and radical character act cooperatively to enhance intramolecular charge transfer and suppress radiative decay, thereby favoring nonradiative heat dissipation under sunlight. TBT–ThT–O exhibits broadened solar absorption and excellent photothermal stability. When immobilized in porous polyurethane foam to construct an interfacial evaporator, TBT–ThT–O@PU achieves a high evaporation rate of 1.356 kg m-2 h-1 and a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 93.05% under 1 sun. As a photothermal coating coupled with a thermoelectric module, the system delivers a voltage of 245 mV and an output power density of 3.936 W m-2 under 1 sun. Furthermore, a lens-assisted hybrid platform is demonstrated to intensify outdoor solar flux for simultaneous freshwater production and electricity generation. This work demonstrates that open-shell D–A molecular engineering provides a viable route to stable, high-performance organic photothermal materials for integrated solar desalination and power generation.

papers.title: FlowKAN-Chem: A Unified Framework Integrating Invertible Flow Networks with KAN Hybrid Architectures for Molecular Property Prediction and Chemical Time Series Analysis
papers.abstract: Deep learning has transformed chemical research by enabling accurate molecular property prediction and process monitoring through time series analysis. However, existing methods treat multiple molecular properties independently and struggle with long-term dependency modeling in chemical process data, while lacking well-calibrated uncertainty quantification. We propose FlowKAN-Chem, a unified framework that integrates invertible flow networks with Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) hybrid architectures to simultaneously address these challenges. Our approach comprises a molecular graph encoder based on message-passing neural networks, an invertible flow network decoder for joint multi-property probabilistic inference, a KAN Mixer module for chemical time series forecasting, and a cross-modal alignment module that bridges molecular and temporal domains through contrastive learning. Experiments on MoleculeNet, QM9, USPTO, and ChemProcess benchmarks demonstrate that FlowKAN-Chem consistently outperforms state-of-theart methods, achieving an AUROC of 0.942 on BBBP, 0.867 on Tox21, and 0.678 on SIDER for molecular prediction, and an MAE of 0.231 with CRPS of 0.121 for chemical time series forecasting.

papers.title: A Versatile Reversed-Phase Liquid Chromatography Charged Aerosol Detection Method for Streamlined Monitoring of QS-21 Content and Stability in Liposomal Adjuvant Formulations
papers.abstract: Identifying and quantifying an active adjuvant along with its degradants in drug formulations is essential for ensuring the safety and efficacy of the drug product. QS-21 is a potent adjuvant that is being evaluated in several clinical trials and is currently formulated in licensed vaccines that protect against shingles, malaria, and RSV. In aqueous environments, QS-21 is subject to hydrolytic degradation that is influenced by pH and temperature, resulting in the formation of a degradant known as QS-21 Hydrolyzed Product, QS-21 HP, which can occur during manufacturing and/or prolonged storage. The intact QS-21 and QS-21 HP induce distinct immune response profiles, making it critical to monitor the degradation of QS-21 in vaccine adjuvant formulations. To date, there has been a paucity of reliable assays for QS-21, its isomers, and degradant QS-21 HP in liposomal adjuvant formulations available that can be transferred seamlessly in quality control (QC) environments. Herein, we introduce a simple and QC-friendly liquid chromatography coupled to a charged aerosol detector (LC-CAD) enabled by stationary phase screening combined with in silico method development optimization. The method exploits 2.7 µm fused-core phenyl hexyl particles, ensuring its versatility in standard and ultra-high pressure LC systems. This approach demonstrates a high correlation between predicted retention time (RT) and experimental outcomes with overall ∆RT <4%. In addition, this assay shows great linearity, precision, specificity, and accuracy to advance process development characterization of new vaccine formulations.

papers.title: Access to an Elusive Soft Deprotonation Manifold: Direct α-C(sp3) Silylation of Sulfonyl Compounds
papers.abstract: Soft deprotonation is a cornerstone of modern carbonyl chemistry, but an analogous process has remained unreported for superficially analogous sulfonyl compounds. Here, we report a general protocol for the C(sp3)–H functionalization of sulfone derivatives, including sulfones, sulfonamides, and sulfonates, to afford α-silylated derivatives that only calls for an amine base near ambient temperature for C–H deprotonation. The conditions reported herein exhibit exceptional functional group tolerance, proving to be compatible with a number of Lewis-basic heterocycles and applicable to complex pharmaceutical derivatives. This approach is scalable and transition metal-free, thus constituting a broadly applicable and practical route to access this versatile class of sulfonyl containing building blocks. Experimental mechanistic investigations and computational studies support a mechanism involving deprotonation facilitated by initial silylation of the sulfonyl compound to afford an unprecedented α-siloxy sulfoxonium ylide intermediate before rate determining C–Si bond formation to give the α-silyl sulfonyl derivative.

papers.title: Direct Spectroscopic Evidence of an Atom-Transfer Mechanism during Copper Electrodeposition on Gold
papers.abstract: Understanding how metals deposit at electrified solid–liquid interfaces is essential to electrochemistry, yet the molecular mechanism of electrodeposition has remained largely unresolved due to the intrinsic opacity of buried interfaces. Here, we combine operando, interface-sensitive soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy with first‑principles electronic‑structure simulations to directly track copper electrodeposition on gold with elemental and chemical specificity. A newly developed lock-in total electron yield detection scheme enables selective probing of the topmost nanometers of an operating electrochemical interface, overcoming long-standing limitations imposed by faradaic currents. Using this approach, we find unambiguous evidence that copper deposition does not proceed through classical outer‑ or inner-sphere electron-transfer pathways, but instead follows an atom-transfer mechanism mediated by a transient cuprous oxide (Cu 2 O) layer. This Cu(I) oxide forms at moderate cathodic potentials at pH ~4.5 and subsequently reduces to Cu 0 , establishing a stepwise sequence governed by interfacial chemistry rather than direct electron transfer. Our results redefine the mechanistic landscape of metal electrodeposition and establish a generalizable platform for resolving complex electrochemical transformations at buried interfaces.

papers.title: Enhancement of Circularly Polarized Luminescence upon Clay Adsorption: Distinct Photophysical Properties of Enantiopure and Racemic Ir(III) Complexes
papers.abstract: Controlling the spatial distribution of photoluminescent molecules within constrained microenvironments remains a fundamental challenge for enhancing their photophysical properties. Herein, we focus on the differential adsorption behaviors of enantiopure and racemic octahedral metal complexes on clay surfaces as a means to amplify these properties, including circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Two iridium(III) complexes exhibiting Δ and Λ chirality, [Ir(ppy) 2 (phen)](PF 6 ) ( Ir1-PF 6 ) and [Ir(piq) 2 (phen)](PF 6 ) ( Ir2-PF 6 ), were employed as chiral luminophores. Investigations into the adsorption behavior of these complexes on colloidal clay revealed that the Ir1 + cation, which possesses pseudo- C 3 symmetry, displays UV–vis, photoluminescence (PL), and circular dichroism (CD) spectra distinctly different from those of the free complex in solution. Conversely, no such spectral changes were observed for the bulkier and lower-symmetry Ir2 + complex in the clay colloidal suspensions. These spectral changes in Ir1 + are attributed to its conformational fixation on the clay surface and the restricted molecular motion, which effectively suppress nonradiative decay processes. Specifically, structural matching between the ligands of Ir1 + and the hexagonal cavities of the clay surface likely leads to rigid stabilization. In contrast, the bulkier ligands of I Ir2 + likely prevent such rigid fixation. Furthermore, Ir1-PF 6 and Ir2-PF 6 with the same absolute configuration (Δ or Λ) exhibited opposite CPL signs in solution. This inversion is attributed to the ligand-dependent changes in orbital topologies, which reverse the transition dipole moments. In colloidal suspensions, the CPL intensity of Ir1 + increased—an effect similarly attributed to conformational fixation—whereas that of Ir2 + decreased. Remarkably, this enhancement of CPL intensity of Ir1 + upon clay adsorption is highly reminiscent of cryogenic cooling. These results demonstrate that utilizing clay nanosheets as structural scaffolds is a powerful strategy for transforming molecules with weak inherent chiroptical properties into highly functional chiral luminescent materials.

papers.title: A Theoretical Investigation of Nonadiabatic Dynamics and Time-Resolved NEXAFS Spectra of Uracil
papers.abstract: Uracil, a fundamental RNA nucleobase, exhibits complex excited-state dynamics governed by nonadiabatic processes that prevent photodamage. Upon photoexcitation, population initially reaches the bright ππ∗ (S2) state and subsequently relaxes through the dark nπ∗ (S1) state via conical intersections, before returning to the ground state on sub-to few-picosecond timescales. In this work, we investigate these relaxation pathways using time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT)-based nonadiabatic surface hopping dynamics in combination with simulated time-resolved near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (TR-NEXAFS) spectroscopy of oxygen, nitrogen and carbon K-edges. This combined approach allows us to capture both electronic and nuclear motion during the ultrafast relaxation and to identify atom-specific contributions to the decay process. In particular, ππ∗ to nπ∗ transitions occurring within the first 150 fs leave traces in O 1s and C 1s NEXAFS signals, indicating C=O bond elongations and torsional motion along the C=C bond, respectively. Overall, our results provide a detailed picture of population transfer, electronic-state trapping, and structural evolution in photoexcited uracil.

papers.title: Photoinduced Disproportionation Enables Oxidative Addition of Aryl Iodides at a Gallium(I) Center
papers.abstract: Oxidative addition at transition metals underpins modern cross-coupling catalysis but remain largely unrealized at main-group centers for aryl halides. Here, we show that photoinduced disproportionation can serve as an enabling strategy for such transformations. Visible light promotes oxidative addition of aryl iodides to a Ga(I) metallylene, providing, to our knowledge, the first example of aryl C(sp²)–I activation at a monovalent group 13 center. Mechanistic studies suggest that this transformation is not consistent with direct excited-state reactivity with the Ga(I) complex. Instead, photoexcitation generates a triplet state of gallylene that undergoes intermolecular electron transfer with ground-state gallylene, triggering disproportionation to a reactive radical ion pair. This radical ion-pair manifold, which has not been widely considered in this context, enabled by ligand-centered redox ambivalence, provides aviable pathway to bond activation. These findingssuggestthat photoinduced disproportionation could represent a distinct activation mode for achieving transition-metal-like oxidative addition at main-group elements.

papers.title: Nanoscopic characterization of the thermal phase behavior of random poly(ethylene glycol – glycidyl methyl ether) copolymers (rPEGs)
papers.abstract: PEGylation – linking of poly (ethylene glycol) (PEG) to a nanocarrier or active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) to achieve stealth properties – is a key technology of nanomedicine. However, PEG has been shown to induce the formation of anti-PEG antibodies, motivating the search for alternative polymers for conjugation with nanocarriers. Recently the concept of randomized PEG (rPEG), random copolymers of ethylene oxide (EO) and glycidyl methyl ether (GME) was introduced. These polymers are structural isomers of PEG with potential for manifold biomedical applications. To investigate their phase behavior in aqueous solution, rPEGs with systematically varied monomer ratios were synthesized. Turbidimetric determination of the cloud point temperatures (Tcp) was applied to study macroscopic LCST behavior. Parallelling these measurements, local nanophase separation was investigated by electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy (EPR) using amphiphilic spin probes to address two key questions: (i) polymer hydration at nanoscopic level and (ii) to determine the temperature at which the onset of the collapse of the polymer chains occurs. The results reveal no phase separation below 96 °C for copolymers of a GME content of 35 mol% and less (26 and 0 mol% GME), while for GME content exceeding 40 mol%, cloud points of 70 °C – 96 °C were observed. Comparison of both methods shows good accordance between the cloud points determined by turbidimetry and EPR with the exception of poly (glycidyl methyl ether) (PGME), for which EPR showed a lower Tcp by 5 – 10 °C. Combining the results with literature data, a model could be established that gives a good approximation of the nanoscopic processes and macroscopic cloud point temperatures in dependence of GME content. Excellent aqueous solubility of all samples could be demonstrated in the physiological temperature range, satisfying the requirements for biomedical applications.

papers.title: Hydroxide-Permeable Hafnia–Organic Interlayers Protect Ionomer from Oxygen-Evolving Anodes in Pure-Water Alkaline-Membrane Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Pure-water-fed anion-exchange-membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) technology is in part limited by degradation at the oxygen-evolving anode-catalyst / ionomer interfaces. We use molecular layer deposition (MLD) to insert conformal hybrid hafnia–ethylene glycol films, Hf(EG), between Co-based anode catalyst layers and an ionomer topcoat. Compared with dense atomic layer deposition (ALD) hafnia coatings, Hf(EG)-coated anodes maintain low cell voltage while stabilizing the interface. Even thick Hf(EG) layers (~50 nm) impose only a small performance penalty (~70 mV at 1.0 A·cm -2 ), consistent with hydroxide-permeable transport through the hybrid film. Across a range of film thicknesses, Hf(EG) reduces cell-voltage degradation and delays the onset of degradation during constant-current operation. Ex situ XPS and TEM/EDX, together with online ICP-MS, indicate that Hf(EG) suppresses oxidative ionomer loss and reduces Co dissolution. These results show that hybrid hafnia–organic interlayers can provide hydroxide transport while physically isolating the ionomer from oxidative anode surfaces and thus offer a new tool in the drive toward commercially durable pure-water-fed AEMWE technology.

papers.title: Squaraine-Rotaxanes Enable Additive-Free Single-Molecule Fluorescence Microscopy with Ultrahigh Photon Output.
papers.abstract: Single-molecule fluorescence microscopy (SMFM) relies on fluorophores capable of sustained emission under high irradiation intensities. Rapid photobleaching and the requirement for oxygen scavengers and triplet-state quenchers limit performance and restrict applications in biologically relevant environments. Here, squaraine-rotaxanes (SeTaus) are systematically evaluated as a new class of fluorophores for SMFM and compared to widely used Alexa 647 and ATTO 647N. SeTaus exhibit superior bulk photophysical properties and deliver markedly enhanced single-molecule performance, including up to 50-fold higher photon output and survival times approaching 160 s under standard conditions. In the presence of ergothioneine, photon counts reach 6.8 million, among the highest reported values for small-molecule fluorophores in SMFM. Notably, SeTaus retain high brightness and long observation times in the absence of both oxygen scavengers and triplet-state quenchers outperforming conventional dyes even under optimized conditions. These properties position SeTaus for single-molecule experiments in environments where chemical additives are incompatible, including live-cell imaging and single-molecule protein–nucleic acid studies. This work establishes squaraine-rotaxanes as a powerful fluorophore platform for SMFM and provides a foundation for the development of next-generation probes that combine high photon outputs with minimal perturbation of biological systems.

papers.title: Local pH control for impure-water-fed bipolar-membrane electrolyzers
papers.abstract: Bipolar membrane (BPM) electrolyzers offer advantages in the electrolysis of impure waters by controlling ion flux, yet operation in salt-containing water feeds still couples interfacial polarization, anion crossover, and water transport in ways that degrade performance and durability. Here, we investigate the impact of NaCl electrolyte (nominally simulated seawater) on BPM electrolyzer operation and identify local pH gradients at electrode–membrane interfaces, arising from coupled ion transport and electrode reactions, as an origin of performance loss and degradation. NaCl in the catholyte induces pronounced pH gradients at the cathode | cation exchange-layer interface, leading to increased voltage, while partial Cl - crossover to the anode becomes detrimental under locally OH - -deficient conditions, promoting the chlorine evolution reaction and accelerating degradation. Direct physical integration of the cathode and anode catalysts onto the cation and anion exchange layers through spray coating and electrodeposition, respectively, mitigates these effects by minimizing the membrane–catalyst distance. The BPM electrolyzer built in this way achieves 0.50 A cm -2 at 2.8 V and shows a degradation rate of 5.5 mV h -1 over 120 h in 0.50 M NaCl electrolyte, compared to degradation of 71 mV h -1 in 0.50 M NaCl electrolyte with a typical porous transport layer device structure. This work thus establishes control of local pH gradients as a design principle for BPM electrolysis with impure water feeds.

papers.title: Viologen-Terminated Redox-Active [2]rotaxane Stabilised by Electrostatic Gating
papers.abstract: Mechanically interlocked molecules (MIMs), particularly rotaxanes, have evolved as robust building blocks for molecular machines and nanoscale devices. These are traditionally stabilised against de-threading by bulky, sterically demanding stopper groups. Here we demonstrate an alternative design principle in which electrostatic (Coulombic) repulsion, rather than steric bulk, provides the dominant barrier to mechanical disassembly. We report a redoxactive [2]rotaxane in which viologen units serve as terminal stoppers for a cyclobis(paraquat-p-phenylene) (CBPQT4+) macrocycle. In the fully oxidised state, Coulombic repulsion between the tetra-cationic macrocycle and the viologen termini stabilises the interlocked architecture. At the same time, upon reduction, complementary radical-ion pairing interactions preserve mechanical integrity even under thermal stimuli. The threaded structure is confirmed by extensive 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy, diffusion-ordered NMR, mass spectrometry, electrochemistry, and UV/Vis/NIR spectroscopy. Molecular dynamics simulations combined with meta-dynamics reveal a deep free-energy minimum centred on the recognition site, with electrostatic confinement dominating the de-threading pathway. These results establish chargebased gating as a viable alternative to steric-stopper design, providing an alternative conceptual

papers.title: Synthesis of enantioenriched aminonitriles catalysed by cyanohydrins and hydroxy acids: propagation of chirality in Strecker-type synthesis
papers.abstract: In Strecker-type synthesis, often regarded as an abiotic synthetic mechanism, aminonitriles and cyanohydrins serve as chiral intermediates leading to α-amino acids and α-hydroxy acids, respectively. Here, we demonstrate that cyanohydrins and hydroxy acids can act as chiral catalysts for the addition of HCN to imines, affording enantioenriched aminonitriles (up to 19% ee) under homogeneous conditions. In conjunction with amplification of ee by Viedma ripening, nearly enantiomerically pure aminonitriles (>99% ee) were obtained, possessing absolute configurations corresponding to those of the cyanohydrins and hydroxy acids. Since aminonitriles can be hydrolyzed to amino acids, a stereochemical correlation between two classes of abiotically relevant compounds is demonstrated for the first time through a plausible abiotic pathway. In contrast to the conventional transformation of cyanohydrins to aminonitriles via achiral intermediates, the present results extend the concept of generation of enantioenriched amino acids by emphasizing both the origin and propagation of chirality.

papers.title: Data-driven critical evaluation of the General Solubility Equation: When is it a valid solubility predictor for Drug-like Molecules?
papers.abstract: Solubility is a widely measured physicochemical property and a highly sought-after descriptor in the evaluation 16 of molecules for drug design and development, medicinal chemistry, and agrochemical sciences. Consequently, a 17 wide range of in-silico models based on deductive and inductive reasoning have been developed. However, the 18 General Solubility Equation (GSE) stands out as a simple, thermodynamically derived equation to predict intrinsic 19 solubility (log S0, in mol/L) of molecules from their melting point and n-octanol/water partition coefficient (logPN). 20 Despite its widespread use, the applicability of this equation has not been rigorously evaluated to establish when 21 it can or cannot produce accurate predictions. Therefore, a large-scale evaluation of the GSE was conducted using 22 an extensive database of fully experimental melting point and logPN data for 2740, mostly drug-like compounds. 23 A systematic analysis based on cheminformatics descriptors was conducted to identify the primary factors that 24 allow the GSE to achieve predictions within the experimental uncertainty range (±1 log S unit). This information 25 has been used to create GSESolver: a supervised machine learning classification model that, based on the selected 26 descriptors, can predict whether the GSE will perform accurately solely from its SMILES string. GSESolver tool 27 can be used by anyone in the scientific community to quickly assess molecules solubility which was developed 28 under the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) in a Google Colab notebook to 29 ensure ease of use. Finally, the utility of GSESolver tool was exploited in medicinal chemistry applications for the 30 in-silico prediction of the Maximum Absorbable Dose (MAD) of potential drugs, and in a rational agrochemical 31 design application where solubility is a key factor. 32

papers.title: Sodium expulsion from sodium closo-hydroborates under electron beam induced bias
papers.abstract: Electron microscopy (EM) invites the opportunity to locally characterize the properties of solid-state electrolytes important for choreographing ion motion within next-generation solid-state batteries. Through the combination of inert gas transfer, cryogenic, time-resolved low-dose analytical electron microscopy, we observe that mixed-anion sodium closo -hydroborate, Na 2 (B 10 H 10 ) 0.5 (B­­­ 12 H 12 ) 0.5 (NBH), solid electrolyte suffers from electrostatic charging damage under bias of both transmission electron microscopes (TEM) and scanning electron microscopes (SEM). During the process of beam damage, crystalline ordering of NBH is lost, while particle morphology remains unchanged. In regions exposed to electron beams at a dose rate of 1-8 e - Å -2 s -1 , spectroscopy confirms vastly reduced sodium signal or even absent from irradiated NBH at total doses less than 80 e - Å -2 . Simultaneously, we detect the growth of sodium metal crystals on the unirradiated faces of NBH particles. An SEM experimental study revealed the maximum damage rate occurs at 2 keV with increasing energy prolonging the time before sodium extrudes. This work also highlights that cryogenic conditions, while highly effective in mitigating certain types of inelastic beam damage, are not the panacea for eluding beam sensitivity. Rather, comprehensive awareness of the underlying physics in competing damage mechanisms is paramount in condition selection for battery interface characterization.

papers.title: The Syntax of Matter: Synthesis Planning as the Foundation of Generative Chemistry
papers.abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have improved benchmark performance for chemical property prediction, yet reliable transfer to new chemical domains remains limited. A contributing factor is that many models treat molecules primarily as static graphs, ignoring the causal logic of how they are constructed. This review surveys multistep synthesis planning (2020-2026) and argues that the field is undergoing a fundamental transition: from an Era of Navigability (2018-2023), focused on the computational feasibility of finding any route through combinatorial search space, to an Era of Validity (2024-Present), focused on the chemical correctness of those routes. We organize the literature around two dominant paradigms, search-based planning and direct sequence generation, and analyze how their design choices relate to different notions of validity. To resolve the ambiguity of current "solvability" metric, which frequently exceeds 99% by measuring only topological connectivity, we introduce a formalized Hierarchy of Chemical Validity (Solv-N). This framework distinguishes between syntactic (Solv-0) and topological (Solv-1) success, which are largely solved, and the higher-order constraints of selectivity (Solv-2) and executability (Solv-3), which remain open challenges. We critically examine how legacy benchmarks and inflated virtual inventories obscure this distinction, and we conclude with a roadmap for synthesis-aware foundation models evaluated under explicit Tier 2-3 constraints.

papers.title: MolMeDB RDF: transforming a relational database about biological membranes to the RDF format to increase interoperability
papers.abstract: Data on molecular behaviour within biological membrane models are pivotal for predictive pharmacology, particularly for modelling bioavailability and target engagement. MolMeDB provides a curated collection of such compound-membrane interaction data. To facilitate automated reasoning and data federation, we present a semantic transformation of MolMeDB into Resource Description Framework (RDF) format, exposed through a public SPARQL endpoint. The resulting schema incorporates community-standard ontologies-including those utilised by PubChem and ChEMBL-to maximise semantic interoperability and enable complex, crossdatabase federated queries. Scientific contribution: MolMeDB RDF provides data on interactions between molecules and membranes and molecules and transporters in machine readable graph format with links to other RDF databases. SPARQL endpoint servicing this dataset enables flexible federated querying, including structural queries utilizing SACHEM.

papers.title: The use of the Stefan-Maxwell Equations in Modelling Ion Transport in Concentrated Electrolytes
papers.abstract: This work has two primary objectives: (i) to give a clear mathematical explanation of how the Stefan-Maxwell equations can be used to derive a one-dimensional drift-diffusion model for ion transport in concentrated multi-species electrolytes; and (ii) to systematically derive a multi-dimensional mixed drift-diffusion-flow model of ion transport, in a concentrated electrolyte, from a generalisation of the Stefan-Maxwell equations. We begin by analysing a Stefan-Maxwell type model for a generic concentrated electrolyte in one-dimension (applicable, e.g., to molten salts or ionic liquids). It is shown that the Stefan-Maxwell equations admit a solution only under the condition of electroneutrality and require an additional constitutive relation for uniqueness. Following previous works, we employ an excluded volume constraint for this purpose. In higher dimensions (2D and 3D), the inclusion of a fluid momentum equation becomes necessary. A physically motivated drift-diffusion-flow model is first proposed on an ad-hoc basis and then derived systematically from generalised Stefan-Maxwell equations, which incorporate both inertia and viscous stresses. The analysis is specialised to moderately concentrated electrolytes, where salt concentrations remain small relative to that of the solvent, but ion-ion interactions are still significant, before specialising further to the dilute limit, in which the classical Nernst-Planck equations are recovered.

papers.title: Synthesis-aware screening of Co–Ir–Ni–Rh–Ru alloys for ammonia decomposition
Realistic Fuel Cell Catalyst Degradation via Automated Identical Location-SEM-PSD Analysis with GDE Half-Cell Setup
papers.abstract: A realistic evaluation of electrocatalyst stability requires experimental setups that accurately reproduce the coupled chemical and transport environments of membrane-electrode assemblies. Conventional GDE half-cells, however, are typically operated without a proton-exchange membrane, exposing the catalyst layer directly to liquid electrolyte and intensifying dissolution-migration-redeposition dynamics. Here we examine how the presence of a membrane alters degradation in PtCo/C catalyst layers and establish a quantitative workflow for tracking nanoparticle evolution under realistic conditions. Particle size distributions (PSDs) are extracted directly from low-kV identical-location SEM (IL-SEM) images of intact, micrometre-thick porous catalyst layers and validated against IL-TEM for surface accessible particles. Automated segmentation enables robust, high-throughput analysis across large datasets. Applying this framework to accelerated stress tests reveals that membrane-free GDEs undergo pronounced coarsening driven by severe Pt dissolution and redeposition under direct acid exposure, whereas membrane-protected electrodes constrain transport pathways and therefore exhibit more moderate, representative degradation behaviour. These findings underscore the indispensable role of the membrane for realistic half-cell durability studies and demonstrate that automated IL-SEM-based PSD analysis provides a powerful framework for linking morphological evolution to electrochemical performance in complex, three-dimensional porous electrocatalyst systems.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Molecular Dynamics of 4,4'-Bipyridine in a Break Junction: A Supramolecular Origin of the High Conductance
papers.abstract: In single-molecule electronics, 4,4'-bipyridine is a well-characterized molecule that serves both as a fundamental testbed for developing experimental methodologies and showcases the complex behaviors expected from molecular electronic components. In break junction experiments, it is generally understood to exhibit a high- and a low-conductance state that are attributed to a tilted and stretched single-molecule configuration. Despite this established view, we suggest a supramolecular origin for these conductance states that has not previously been considered. Our findings indicate that the high- and low-conductance states may arise from the presence of two molecules and one molecule, respectively, challenging the conventional interpretation. Using a state-of-the-art machine learning force field called the neuroevolution potential, we find that the conventional interpretation of a tilted and stretched configuration is inconsistent with our simulations. Instead, our results suggest that the presence of two molecules promotes junction geometries and gold rearrangements that stabilize a high-conductance state whose transmission exceeds twice that of the low-conductance state. Furthermore, we compare this interpretation to the existing literature of diverse experimental data on 4,4'-bipyridine in break junctions and find that it is consistent with the broader body of experimental evidence. Our results highlight the structural complexity of molecular behavior within break junctions, suggesting even more complex dynamics than originally anticipated. In this light, a broader examination of the dynamics of molecules in single-molecule break junctions with machine learning-assisted molecular dynamics is warranted.

papers.title: Benchmarking physics-inspired machine learning models for transition metal complexes with diverse charge and spin states
papers.abstract: Physics-inspired machine learning (ML) models can be categorized into two classes: those relying solely on three-dimensional structure and those incorporating electronic information. In this work, we benchmark both classes for predicting quantum-chemical properties of transition metal complexes with diverse charge and spin states, using three complementary datasets. The evaluated methods include molecular representations (SLATM, FCHL, SOAP, and SPA H M family) combined with kernel ridge regression, as well as geometric deep learning models (MACE and 3DMol). We examine how the inclusion of electronic information affects predictive accuracy across datasets and target properties. Models that incorporate electronic information consistently outperform purely structure-based models for properties whose distributions are strongly governed by electronic characters, such as spin-splitting energies and frontier orbital energies. In contrast, structure-only models perform well for predicting the HOMO–LUMO gap and dipole moment magnitude, whose distributions are relatively insensitive to electronic characteristics. Geometric deep learning models with charge and spin embeddings (MACE-QS and 3DMol-QS) show the highest overall accuracy, with 3DMol offering the best computational efficiency among the tested models. These results clarify when geometric information is sufficient and when incorporating electronic information becomes essential, providing practical guidance for selecting effective physics-based ML models for transition metal complexes.

papers.title: ARTEMIS: an Information-Theory Based Framework for Analysis of Communication in Biomolecular Systems
papers.abstract: Cellular processes rely on interactions of biomolecules, i.e. direct contact and subsequent configurational changes that provide a physical basis for information processing and transmission within the cell as well as for communication between its remote parts and with the environment. Molecular communication persists also at the level of a single biomolecule, whereby it is known as allostery - an internal mechanism to regulate biomolecular function. To investigate communication phenomena in different (bio)molecular systems, a universal information-theoretical approach utilizing mutual information (MI) was developed and implemented as a Python/C++ software package ARTEMIS. This tool gives the possibility to analyze intra- and intermolecular communication networks using all-to-all MI matrix for amino acids in proteins, nucleotides in nucleic acids, or any other molecular subgroups defined in the system. In the present study, configurational ensembles from microsecond all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are subjected into PARENT software to extract MI values from pairwise distributions of internal degrees of freedom and further processed in ARTEMIS to build the thus derived MD MI-matrices, remove noise, test convergence and analyze communication networks. Alternatively, for proteins and nucleic acids MI matrices can be generated from multiple sequence alignments (MSA) and further processed in the same way using ARTEMIS. Specifically, the framework allows: a) construction and visualization of MI matrices; b) analysis of pairwise communication and corresponding sequence biases (e.g. “specific contacts”); c) reconstruction of molecular communication networks and analysis of their modular organization using different clustering algorithms; d) search of allosterically coupled sites for a given target subset (e.g. active site); e) identification of critical residues for information transmission between communicating sites (e.g. active site / allosteric site). A potentially wide application of ARTEMIS is shown for different molecular systems, including lipid bilayers, peptides, disordered and globular proteins. Moreover, analysis of allosteric communication in proteins is shown to be in good agreement with the available experimental data. The MI-based approach realized in ARTEMIS provides a universal and efficient method for analysis of communication in any (bio)molecular system.

papers.title: DockM8: An All-in-One Open-Source Platform for Consensus Virtual Screening in Drug Design
papers.abstract: Virtual screening remains a critical step in structure-based drug design, yet variability in docking algorithms and scoring functions often limits its reliability. To address this challenge, we introduce DockM8, an open-source platform for consensus virtual screening that integrates pocket detection, ligand preparation, docking, rescoring, and consensus ranking within a single modular workflow. DockM8 supports 5 docking engines, 17 pose-selection methods, 17 scoring functions, and 5 consensus methods, all accessible through both a graphical user interface (GUI) and a Python application programming interface (API). Systematic evaluation on the DEKOIS 2.0, DUD-E, and Lit-PCBA datasets yielded median relative enrichments of 100%, 86.05%, and 8.675%, respectively, frequently outperforming state-of-the-art approaches and highlighting the robustness and adaptability of DockM8 across diverse targets. Our findings further reveal that no pose-selection or consensus strategy universally excels, emphasizing the need for tailored, target-specific workflows. DockM8 is freely available under the GNU General Public License at https://github.com/DrugBud-Suite/DockM8 . Scientific Contribution DockM8 is, to our knowledge, the first open-source platform to expose the complete consensus structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) pipeline within a single tool, yielding over 55 million configurable protocols, a breadth unmatched by previously published consensus docking software. Through systematic multi-benchmark evaluation, we demonstrate that no single pose-selection or consensus strategy generalizes across targets, motivating a target-specific workflow-selection paradigm in place of prevailing one-size-fits-all heuristics. By delivering this tunability through a graphical interface rather than scripts, DockM8 brings rigorous, reproducible consensus virtual screening within reach of non-specialist medicinal chemists.

papers.title: Transition Energy, Orientation Force and Work Done in Transitional Behavior Atoms: Formulating New Principles in Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: Researching basic parameters of heat and thermodynamics not only advances science but also explores new insights. In their transitional behaviors, atoms of both gaseous and solid elements explore remarkable advances. The advances and new insights are both in the chemical and physical sciences. An anomaly explicitly present with the first law of thermodynamics. By gaining transition energy, gaseous atoms undergo a transition state. A transition state is a mid-state in this study. The gaseous atoms self-perform their work. Symbolically, a plus sign is needed to attain the mid-state. A transition of the solid atom decreases the potential energy of its electrons. To attain the mid-state, a solid atom performs negative work. Suitable gaseous and solid atoms deal with electron-level forces. Force nature is different. In the atoms of suitable elements, a transitional energy at the electron level influences the potential energy. As a result, the atoms control the orientation of electrons. The changing equations of internal energy can resolve the anomaly linked with the fundamentals of thermodynamics. Gaseous and solid atoms introduce cooling and heat effects, respectively, when in the elastically driven electronic states. The driven electronic states in suitable atoms reach their mid-states. The mid-states of the electrons fall within the re-crystallization and liquid states. To generate cooling (or heating) energy, the electron of a gaseous (or solid) atom executes dynamics by remaining within its energy knot. Constantly driven electronic states of atoms cause disorder and irreversible cycling. This study provides a basic understanding of the first law of thermodynamics, cold and heat energy, entropy, and condensed matter science at the atomic and electronic levels.

papers.title: Spin and Charge Plasmons in Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons: Topology-Controlled Ring Currents and Coherent Wavepacket Dynamics with Real-Time Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
papers.abstract: Collective plasmonic excitations in polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) can be effectively tuned through molecular topology and ionization. Reduction gives rise to a complex manifold of molecular plasmonic resonances in the near-IR to visible spectrum that can support spin-polarized electronic dynamics. Using GPU-accelerated real-time time-dependent density functional theory (RT-TDDFT), we investigate the dynamics of plasmonic states in six PAHs from distinct topological classes comprising linear acenes (anthracene, tetracene, pentacene), a pericondensed benzenoid (pyrene), a circulene (coronene), and a phenacene (phenanthrene). Using linear response time-dependent density functional theory, we introduce a spin-resolved transition dipole moment (TDM) interference framework that enables the classification of open-shell plasmonic excitations as either molecular spin plasmons (MSPs) with antiparallel spin-channel TDMs, or molecular charge plasmons (MCPs) with parallel spin-channel TDMs. To complement this new framework we present a spin plasmonicity index that recovers the collective character of excitations whose conventional plasmonicity is suppressed by inter-channel cancellation. RT-TDDFT simulations confirm that MSP excitation generates counterpropagating spin-up and spin-down electron densities, creating spatially confined spin-density waves in the absence of both spin-orbit coupling and external magnetic fields. The PAH dynamics depend critically on topology and can be used to generate one-dimensional spin-density waves, ring currents from linearly polarized light, and coherent spin-charge beating in which a wavepacket periodically converts between charge and spin plasmon character. These results identify PAH radical anions as a topologically tunable platform for optically addressable, spin-polarized plasmonic dynamics relevant to all-organic molecular spintronics.

papers.title: Continuous-time quantum-walk centrality for protein residue interaction networks
papers.abstract: We present a quantum-dynamical framework for identifying structurally important residues in proteins based on continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on weighted residue–interaction networks constructed from experimentally resolved structures. By mapping the weighted adjacency matrix to a Hamiltonian, residue importance emerges from the long-time averaged occupation probability, confirmed analytically through its spectral decomposition. Across a dataset of 150 proteins spanning diverse structural and functional classes, CTQW centrality exhibits consistently strong agreement with classical eigenvector centrality in identifying central residues, while extending beyond it through incorporating signatures of quantum interference. Analyzing the time-averaged quantum transition matrix reveals consistently larger spectral gaps than the classical random-walk operator. Furthermore, biological relevance is confirmed through recovery of experimentally established functional residues in proteins kinase A and oxytocin. CTQW-derived centrality rankings are accessible on near-term intermediate-scale quantum hardware, as we demonstrate through a proof-of-principle implementation on IBM superconducting quantum hardware demonstrates. These results establish continuous-time quantum walks as a computationally tractable framework for protein network analysis, that connects network theoretical treatments of protein structural biology to continuous-time quantum walk dynamics.

papers.title: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning for Molecular Generation with Contribution-Aware Dynamic Modality Balancing
papers.abstract: We propose a Multimodal Iterative Reasoning Molecular Generation framework that integrates molecular graph topology, SMILES sequences, and physicochemical descriptors through a unified multimodal encoder. Our iterative reasoning decoder progressively refines molecular structures through geometric-semantic alternating denoising diffusion across multiple reasoning rounds. A contribution-aware dynamic modality balancing strategy adaptively adjusts the influence of different modalities during generation, ensuring critical structural features are preserved. Experiments on QM9, ZINC250K, and MOSES demonstrate that our method achieves 98.7% validity, 96.1% uniqueness, 94.8% novelty, and 79.5% property hit rate, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Tunable Chiral Phthalocyanines with Rationally Designed Aggregation for NIR Circularly Polarized Luminescence
papers.abstract: Chiral phthalocyanines hold significant promise for chiroptical and supramolecular materials; however, reported examples remain sporadic, and no general synthetic platform has been available to systematically control their structural and functional properties. Here, we report a practical and general synthesis of D 4 -symmetric chiral phthalocyanines from commercially available H8-BINOL. This modular route provides direct access to a broad palette of chiral architectures, enabling systematic investigation of how substituents govern supramolecular assembly. We found that aggregation behavior can be predictably tuned through simple structural modifications. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis guided the design of tailored non-covalent interactions that promote spontaneous and selective J -aggregation into well-defined chiral helices. The resulting supramolecular structures display narrowband near-infrared fluorescence (FWHM = 15 nm) and pronounced circularly polarized luminescence (CPL), with dissymmetry factors ( g lum ) of up to 0.01. Notably, the CPL signal of the aggregates remains detectable at nanomolar concentrations down to 500 nM, demonstrating the high chiroptical efficiency of these materials and their potential for low concentration applications.

papers.title: CAGE Ionic Liquids Meet Biomembranes: Unraveling Molecular Mechanisms and Partitioning Kinetics
papers.abstract: Choline-based ionic liquids (ILs) are extensively explored for drug delivery and antimicrobial applications, yet their interactions with lipid membranes remain poorly understood. Using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, free energy calculations, and recently developed kinetics models1 we investigate the partitioning of cholinegeranic acid/geranate (CAGE) formulations into zwitterionic, 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-snglycero-3-phosphocholine (POPC) and anionic 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoglycerol (DOPG) phospholipid membranes over a range of compositions and concentrations. The neutral component, geranic acid (GRA), forms micelles in aqueous IL formulations and dominates membrane partitioning due to a low free energy barrier. In contrast, the ionic components, geranate (GRI) and choline (COL), remain localized near the headgroup-water interface due to higher free energy barriers. Membrane structural responses were found to scale approximately linearly with CAGE concentration following a composition dependent trend (CAGE14 > CAGE12 > CAGE11). Equilibrium membrane partitioning isotherms reveal charge dependent uptake of GRI and COL, whereas GRA partitioning is governed primarily by CAGE composition. Partitioning kinetics, identifies two uptake mechanisms: a) membrane controlled first order kinetics for GRI and COL, and b) micelle size limited zeroth order membrane partitioning for GRA. Uptake kinetics were found to be slower in anionic DOPG membranes. Overall, our study provides a comprehensive simulation method to analyze both the dynamics and equilibrium partitioning of IL liquids into phospholipid membranes.

papers.title: Elucidating Solvent Effects on the Supramolecular Polymerization of NIR-Absorbing Triimide Dye: Insights from Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Solution-phase supramolecular self-assembly serves as a testbed for chemists to create shape-persistent, ordered nanostructures from smaller building blocks, with the goal to develop functional nanomaterials. In this process, solvent modulation plays a crucial role in influencing the thermodynamics and kinetics of supramolecular polymerization, however, the influence of binary solvent mixtures on this process remains understudied. This work employs molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how mixtures of a good solvent (chloroform) and a poor solvent (methylcyclohexane (MCH) or-isopropyl alcohol (IPA)) affect the solvation of the self-assembling, near-infrared absorbing triimide dye (2EH-G). Through extensive analysis the molecular and thermodynamic principles governing the solvation of both monomeric and polymeric 2EH-G are explored. Our results show that 2EH-G solvation is significantly influenced by the choice of poor solvent. In contrast to MCH, the IPA competes with chloroform molecules for interacting with 2EH-G resulting in less ordered 2EH-G self-assembly. Chloroform has more excess volume in the presence of MCH compared to IPA, leading to accumulation chloroform molecules around 2EH-G. IPA–chloroform mixture imposes greater restrictions on the motion of 2EH-G compared to the MCH-chloroform mixture leading to the solvent-dependent kinetics in the self-assembly behavior of 2EH-G molecules, potentially slowing down polymerization.

papers.title: Counterion-Specific Global Bridging Networks Inside a Polyelectrolyte Brush Layer: Investigations Using All-Atom Molecular Dynamics Simulations, Graph Theory, and Unsupervised Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Counterion-driven bridging in polyelectrolyte (PE) brush layer is a well-investigated localized event and refers to a given counterion strongly influencing (or bridging) closely located multiple monomers of a single or multiple PE chains. In this paper, we employ a combination of all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, graph theory, and unsupervised machine learning (ML) to propose a paradigm shift in our understanding of such localized counterion-driven bridging. We establish that such bridging demonstrates global characteristics via the formation of bridging networks. Specifically, we consider two systems: SO42--counterion screened PMETA+ [poly(2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl) trimethylammonium] brushes and SCN--counterion screened PMETA+ brushes. Using all-atom MD simulation results, for both these systems, we first construct a globally connective bridging network structure using graph theory, where both monomers and counterions are represented as nodes, and identify five node-level features characterizing this bridging network, ensuring a five-dimensional (5D) feature space for each node. Subsequently, we employ a two-step machine learning (ML) approach, where first this 5D feature space is mapped into a 2D space, followed by unsupervised clustering of this 2D data revealing that the bridging network is more heterogeneous (homogeneous) for the SO42--counterion (SCN--counterion) screened PMETA+ brushes. Further analysis of these five node-level features reveal that for the case of the kosmotropic SO42--counterion (chaotropic SCN--counterion) screened PMETA+ brushes, the bridging interactions are primarily governed by the specific electrostatic interactions (non-specific solvent-mediated interactions) between the counterions and the apolar {N(CH3)3}+ group of the PMETA+ brushes, and is therefore, less (more) susceptible to thermal fluctuations. The final result is that the global bridging network for the SO42--counterion (SCN--counterion) is longer (shorter) and is characterized by long-ranged and extended (short-ranged but localized) structures.

papers.title: Switching of Proton Conductivity via Electron-Transfer Phase-Transition in H3O+/NH3 Responsive Ni-Fe Chains
papers.abstract: Switchable proton conductivity remains a rare and underexplored property in coordination polymers, despite the broad functional potential of these materials. Here, we demonstrate that proton conductivity can be directly controlled by a thermally driven electron-transfer phase transition (ETPT) in the one-dimensional cyanido-bridged coordination polymer NH 4 [Ni(cyclam)][Fe(CN) 6 ]·5H 2 O ( 1 ). Owing to the room-temperature bistability of the system, reversible thermal switching of proton conductivity is achieved, with the low-temperature Ni III -Fe II state exhibiting over one order of magnitude higher conductivity than the high-temperature Ni II -Fe III state (50% relative humidity, 295 K). The switching arises from ETPT-induced changes in the hydrogen-bond network and charge distribution along the coordination chains. Furthermore, the exchange of NH 4 + for H 3 O + , occurring as a single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation, reversibly switches the ETPT ON and OFF, simultaneously changing the optical, magnetic, and electrical properties of the system, while subsequent NH 3 absorption fully restores them. Moreover, 1 exhibits sensitivity to acids, leading to H 3 O + -induced ETPT, reported here for the first time in a CN-bridged system in the solid state. The sensitivity of 1 to chemical stimuli was further exploited for spectrophotometric detection of HCl and NH 3 vapors using a polymer composite, demonstrating its potential for sensor applications.

papers.title: Visible Light-Induced Ipso-Chalcogenation of Aryl/Alkenyl Boronic Acids Assisted by a Chalcogen Radical Transfer (ChRT) Strategy
papers.abstract: We report a transition-metal free, visible light-induced method for the ipso-chalcogenation of aryl/alkenyl boronic acids. Our approach enables functionalization of a variety of electronically-diverse aromatic boronic acids under mild conditions by using cost-effective source of photons, eventually giving rise to a wide range of unsymmetrical sulfides, selenides as well as tellurides.

papers.title: Visible-Light-Driven Photocatalytic Utilization of Sulfur Hexafluoride (SF6) as an SF5 Radical Source
papers.abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF 6 ) is a potent greenhouse gas widely used in industry, but its chemical inertness has limited its use as a source of pentafluorosulfanyl (SF 5 ) groups. We report herein a visible-light-driven photocatalytic transformation that enables SF 6 to function as an SF 5 radical source for the synthesis of SF 5 enamides under ambient pressure. Using ynamides as radical acceptors, a range of β-SF 5 -substituted enamides were obtained under mild conditions in moderate to good yields. Mechanistic studies support the involvement of SF 5 radical intermediates and a hydrogen atom transfer process rather than a radical chain pathway. The resulting SF 5 enamides could be further transformed into diverse functionalized products, demonstrating their synthetic utility. This work highlights the potential of SF 6 as a practical SF 5 radical source for constructing valuable SF 5 -containing organic molecules under photocatalytic conditions. This work provides a new strategy for the direct utilization of SF 6 in synthetic organic chemistry.

papers.title: On the Universal Algebraic Structure of Kinetic Observables in Catalysis
papers.abstract: Apparent reaction orders, Tafel slopes, and apparent activation energies are the three experimentally accessible kinetic descriptors used to characterise heterogeneous catalytic mechanisms. Although they probe different experimental knobs, concentration, electrode potential, and temperature, we show that all three are instances of a single mathematical object: the logarithmic derivative of the net reaction rate with respect to an appropriately chosen dimensionless domain variable, which we term the generalised apparent reaction order. Within the unbound mean-field (UMF) adsorption framework, all three observables factor through a single universal kinetic matrix, which encodes the topology of the reaction network, and a domain-specific driving-force vector. In the square, single-path setting this factorisation collapses to a closed-form ratio of two determinants; for mechanisms with parallel reaction channels the same structure persists through the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse together with an explicit branching (occurrence-number) closure. The kinetic matrix is identical for all three domains; only the driving-force vector changes with the perturbation axis. This unification provides a compact, closed-form framework for the simultaneous analysis of kinetic data across experimental domains, and a freely available reference implementation and empirical benchmark suite are provided alongside the paper.

papers.title: When Are Simple Descriptors Enough in MOF Adsorption Machine Learning?
papers.abstract: Descriptor choice sits at the centre of MOF machine learning, yet the key scientific question is not simply whether richer representations win on average, but when compact, physically transparent pore descriptors already capture the governing adsorption physics. Here we benchmark four adsorption targets—CH4 uptake at 5.8 bar, CH4 uptake at 65 bar, CO2 uptake at 0.015 bar, and CO2 uptake at 0.15 bar—using one matched tabular workflow, four descriptor families, four accessible model classes, repeated random splits, and topology-aware group splits. The results show that descriptor adequacy is strongly regime dependent. For CH4 uptake at 65 bar, geometry-only HGB already reaches R2 = 0.975, and the best geometry-plus-topology model improves only marginally to 0.980. By contrast, for CO2 at 0.015 and 0.15 bar, adding topology to enriched geometry lifts R2 from 0.471 to 0.586 and from 0.688 to 0.771, respectively. The stricter group split reveals where interpolation optimism is severe: the best random-split score for CH4 at 5.8 bar drops from 0.774 to 0.234, whereas CH4 at 65 bar remains comparatively robust at 0.948. Cross-target feature-importance maps, computed by permutation importance on held-out test data and averaged across repeated splits, show a shift from density-dominated methane prediction to accessibility-and confinement-sensitive CO2 prediction. The resulting decision framework is target dependent: enriched geometry is sufficient for both methane tasks, simple geometry remains the most defensible choice for CO2 uptake at 0.015 bar under conservative evaluation, and topology augmentation is most justified for CO2 uptake at 0.15 bar.

papers.title: Quantifying Oxygen Vacancy Formation in Electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: Oxygen vacancies (VO) are widely invoked as key descriptors of the activity of transition metal oxide electrocatalysts. However, their thermodynamic stability under realistic electrochemical operating conditions remains poorly understood. In this work, we establish a thermodynamic framework for calculating VO formation energies as a function of pH and applied potential. Through a systematic evaluation of 19 representative oxygen reduction (ORR) and evolution (OER) catalysts, we demonstrate that while VO formation can be energetically favorable at standard states (0 V vs. RHE), the formation energies increase significantly under operando conditions, exceeding 0.50 eV for ORR and 2.00 eV for OER. These large thermodynamic barriers suggest that surface oxygen vacancies are unlikely to persist during electrocatalysis, particularly in the oxygen-rich environment of the OER. Our findings challenge the prevailing assumption of vacancy-mediated reaction mechanisms and highlight the necessity of accounting for potentialdependent surface stoichiometry when modeling the catalyst-electrolyte interface.

papers.title: Alternating Current–Driven Hydrogen Isotope Labeling of Aliphatic Amines Using 1,3-Propanedithiol as an Efficient Hydrogen Atom Transfer Reagent
papers.abstract: Hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) plays a pivotal role in the synthesis of isotopically labelled compounds, which are widely used in the pharmaceutical industry for drug pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies. While electrochemical HIE has emerged as a powerful strategy for site-selective labelling of C–H bonds, extending its application to alkyl aminecontaining drugs has been hindered by the instability of α-amino radicals and their susceptibility to overoxidation. Here, we report the first electrochemical HIE protocol that enables efficient deuterium (D) labelling of both cyclic and acyclic alkyl amine substrates. The key innovation lies in using 1,3-propanedithiol as the hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) catalyst, which could in situ generate a potent HAT agent—a mercaptothiyl radical—via alternating current electrolysis. This radical benefits from a significantly weakened effective S–H bond dissociation energy of 34 kcal/mol compared to conventional monothiol HAT catalysts (~80 kcal/mol), driven by exothermic disulfide ring formation. Mechanistic studies and computational analyses reveal a strong structure–activity relationship among dithiols, identifying 1,3-propanedithiol as the optimal catalyst, which is uniquely suited to balance fast HAT kinetics with efficient regeneration of the dithiol. The application of this method to over 30 pharmaceutically relevant compounds achieved up to 3.7 D per molecule. This work addresses a long-standing challenge in electrochemical HIE and introduces a new HAT platform with broad potential in synthetic and biological chemistry.

papers.title: Making infrared visible: Single-photon IR light upconversion using neutral and multianionic polymethines with a dioxaborine core
Chemically programmable nanopores in graphene membranes via localized fluorination for high-selectivity hydrogen separation
papers.abstract: Engineering nanopores in two-dimensional (2D) materials with angstrom-level precision and scalable control remains a central challenge for molecular separation. Here, we report a localized fluorination strategy that enables chemically programmable nanopores in graphene and graphene oxide (GO) using XeF2. Fluorination generates clustered C–F domains that locally convert sp2 carbon into mechanically weakened sp3 configurations, where control over cluster dimensions enables tunable pore diameter and density. In graphene, mild thermal activation removes strained regions to generate nanopores, and strain-driven C–C bond cleavage near epoxy groups enables room-temperature pore nucleation in GO, with angstromscale precision. Fluorination not only defines pore dimensions but also restructures the laminated GO framework, contracting interlayer spacing and establishing a dual-sieving network that integrates atomically precise through-plane pores with compacted galleries. The membranes achieve H2/CO2 selectivity up to 42.7 with H2 permeance of 1205 GPU, surpassing the conventional polymer membrane permeance–selectivity trade-off trend.

papers.title: Reaction-orthogonal solid-state reference enables potentiometric studies of vapor phase thermochemical catalysis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical mechanisms have been shown to be operative in the catalysis of numerous thermochemical redox reactions. These mechanisms have been elucidated by the measurement of the electrochemical potential of the catalyst during turnover (E cat ). A rich array of electrochemical tools allows for measurement of E cat during liquid-phase catalysis, but these are ill-suited to E cat measurements in higher temperature vapor-phase catalysis. Herein we report a solid electrolyte potentiometry (SEP) methodology that employs a Na β″-alumina solid electrolyte to measure E cat relative to the Na/Na + reference couple. As Na + is not typically a reactant or product in (electro)catalytic reactions, this reference is reaction-orthogonal, providing a common reference value for E cat measurement and analysis across diverse reaction classes and environments. Reaction-orthogonal SEP (RO-SEP) of Pt/C under H 2 enables measurement of the H 2 /H + equilibrium potential in the vapor phase across a wide temperature range from ambient to 325 °C. We find that promoting salts establish vapor phase proton activities comparable to their values in bulk aqueous medium, at ambient temperature. We apply RO-SEP to study the Au/C-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of 2-propanol to acetone and find that the catalyst is spontaneously and differentially polarized as a function of O 2 pressure under vapor phase reaction conditions. Simultaneous measurement of rate and E cat reveals a rate-potential scaling for vapor phase aerobic IPA oxidation that parallels that of liquid phase electrolytic IPA oxidation, suggesting a shared electrochemical mechanism between the two conditions. Lastly, H 2 /H + potentiometry reveals that alkali promoters in this reaction act principally via increasing the pH at the catalyst surface, which in turn enhances the kinetics of both the oxygen reduction and 2-propanol oxidation half-reaction. This reaction-orthogonal methodology for quantifying E cat enables broad-based investigations into the role of charge transfer in vapor phase heterogeneous catalysis.

papers.title: Machine Learning–Enabled Probabilistic Digital Twin for Halftone-Encoded Programmable Mechanical Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Programmable mechanical heterogeneity provides a powerful strategy for tailoring deformation behavior in architected materials; however, establishing predictive relationships between encoded material distributions and mechanical response remains challenging due to complex, nonlinear deformation.
