Here, we present a machine learning–enabled probabilistic digital twin for halftoneencoded architected materials fabricated via a binary, single-resin additive manufacturing approach. Specimens with systematically varied stiff domain fractions (0–50%) are subjected to uniaxial tensile loading, and deformation morphologies at large strain (60%) are used as input to a convolutional neural network, achieving a classification accuracy of 92%. Misclassifications occur primarily between adjacent stiffness states, reflecting the intrinsic continuity of the mechanical design space. To enable continuous prediction, classification outputs are reformulated through a probabilistic inference framework, where softmax probabilities are interpreted as distributions and converted into continuous estimates via probability-weighted averaging. Validation using unseen specimens with intermediate stiffness (25%) demonstrates accurate interpolation within the learned design space, with predictions confined within physically meaningful intervals near the ground truth. This approach establishes deformation morphology as a physically informative descriptor of encoded mechanical heterogeneity, enabling rapid, nondestructive prediction without constitutive modeling or finite element analysis. The framework provides a scalable pathway for integrating additive manufacturing, image-based mechanical testing, and data-driven modeling for the design and evaluation of architected materials.

papers.title: Carbohydrate-Directed Labeling Probes for UV-Independent Chemoproteomic Mapping of Carbohydrate–Protein Interactions
papers.abstract: Weak and transient carbohydrate–protein interactions hinder the detection of carbohydrate-binding proteins (CBPs) in native settings. Here, we introduce carbohydrate-directed labeling probes (CDLPs), modular ligand-directed covalent probes composed of a glycan ligand, an acyl-transfer electrophile, and a distal azide handle. Glycan binding positions the electrophile to enable proximity-based covalent capture of CBPs. This converts fleeting recognition events into stable, taggable adducts via traceless acyl transfer; the glycan ligand departs, leaving a minimal azide-bearing acyl tag on the protein. CDLPs capture carbohydrate–protein interactions with KD values extending into the millimolar range in a ligand-dependent manner. In Daudi B cells, a 6′-sialyllactose CDLP selectively engages CD22 (Siglec-2), demonstrating robust glycan-dependent labeling in live cells. Quantitative chemoproteomics using sialyllactose- and lactose-CDLPs yields complementary ligand-specific interaction maps (6′SL-CDLP: 95; Lac-CDLP: 113; 21 shared), including proteins lacking prior glycan-related annotations. CDLPs provide an accessible, UV-independent route to durable covalent readouts for targeted and proteome-wide discovery.

papers.title: Stirring-induced modulation of NIR emission in Tm3+-doped nanoparticles: evidence of apparent risetime sensitivity
papers.abstract: Recent studies on upconversion nanoparticles have shown that photoluminescence can indicate fluid motion, for example, through flow-dependent intensity ratios in the visible region. Building on this underexplored yet emerging direction, we here report the stirring-dependent near-infrared response in Tm 3+ -doped fluoride nanoparticles, providing the foundation for novel near-infrared flow sensors. More precisely, in colloidal dispersions of Tm 3+ -doped NaYbF 4 nanoparticles excited at 980 nm, stirring reproducibly and reversibly decreases the emission intensity at 1485 nm (Tm 3+ : 3 H 4 → 3 F 4 ) and simultaneously increases the emission around 1850 nm (Tm 3+ : 3 F 4 → 3 H 6 ). This effect is quantified by the luminescence intensity ratio (LIR = I 1485 / I 1850 ), which decreases with stirring speed. Importantly, time-resolved measurements show unchanged experimental luminescence lifetimes but altered apparent risetimes for both states under stirring, providing strong evidence for changes in population dynamics rather than decay kinetics as underlaying mechanism. Indeed, under direct, singlestep 808 nm excitation of 3 H 4 , no stirring-induced changes are observed, opposed to the proposed mechanism involving a multistep excitation pathway that populates 3 H 4 under 980 nm pumping. These results extend motion-sensitive luminescence into the near-infrared spectral region and open novel opportunities for noninvasive optical routes to monitor agitation or flow where deeper light penetration is advantageous.

papers.title: Overcoming the Energy Gap Law in NIR-II Fluorophores via S…S Interaction-Mediated Exciton-Vibrational Decoupling
papers.abstract: Although second near-infrared (NIR-II) theranostic fluorophores show great potential for noninvasive disease phototheranostics, the inherent antagonism between long-wavelength emission and high fluorescence brightness severely hinders their development. Herein, we propose a novel molecular design strategy based on through-space S···S interactions by introducing sulfur atoms in different molecular microenvironments into the conjugated backbone. The S···S interactions can simultaneously extend conjugation and rigidify molecular conformations, thus effectively suppressing non-radiative decay and breaking the bottleneck imposed by the energy gap law. Compared with its isomer NPTD without through-space S···S interactions, the designed fluorophore NTPD exhibits a redshifted emission peak and improved photoluminescence quantum yield in both molecular and aggregate states. These merits endow NTPD with great promise for high-resolution NIR-II imaging-guided photothermal therapy against cancer. This through-space S···S interaction strategy surmounts the traditional design limitations of long-wavelength fluorophores and provides a universal paradigm for creating high-performance NIR-II emitters.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Framework for Descriptor-Empowered Exploring High-Activity Co-Based Quaternary Molten Alloys Catalysts for Methane Pyrolysis
papers.abstract: Methane (CH 4 ) pyrolysis via molten media offers an attractive route to CO 2 ‑free hydrogen production with high‑value carbon as a co‑product. However, the rational design of multicomponent molten catalysts remains challenging due to the dynamic and disordered nature of active sites in the molten state. Here, we present a closed-loop framework that integrates potential catalyst exploration by descriptor data mining, CH 4 pyrolysis testing, and activity mechanism analysis to identify the high-activity catalysts for CH 4 pyrolysis. Using this approach, Bi 7 0Ni 18 Cu 6 Co 6 is identified as a promising catalyst for the first time, with experimental validation demonstrating it can achieve 40.3% CH 4 conversion at a moderate 1000 °C with a relative low activation energy (197.3 kJ·mol -1 ), outperforming the same experimental conditions Bi 73 Ni 27 (33.3%) and Bi 76 Ni 18 Cu 6 (37.4%) molten medias. The enhancement stems from a synergistic multi‑solute effect that the co‑dissolution of Ni, Cu, and Co in the low‑surface‑tension Bi solvent increases the density of exposed active sites and promotes direct interaction with CH 4 molecules. In particular, the introducing Co downshift the LUMO energy level of CH 4 molecular orbital (~1.3 eV), facilitating charge antibonding occupation, weakening C–H bonds, thereby accelerating the CH 4 dissociation. These findings provide deep insights of Co-based multi-elementary molten catalysts and chart a clear path toward the rational design of high-performance multicomponent molten catalysts for CH 4 pyrolysis.

papers.title: Single-Shot NMR Determination of Multiple Binding Constants in Diastereomer-Resolved Host–Guest Systems
papers.abstract: Quantitative analysis of host–guest systems with multiple equilibria is challenging because several species coexist and conventional methods often require reference systems or multiple measurements. Here, we report a 1 H NMR method that determines multiple binding constants from a single spectrum. Under slow-exchange conditions, resolved signals and mass-balance relationships enable direct analysis without enantiopure samples. Application to a Cu(I)-coordinated resorcinarene capsule demonstrates simultaneous determination of two binding constants and thermodynamic parameters.

papers.title: Boosting radioprotection by nitrogen-to-selenium substitution in melanin
papers.abstract: Growing risks from ionizing radiation have raised demand for efficient and biocompatible radioprotectors. Melanin shows radioprotective effects but suffers from limited efficacy. Here, a radioprotecting polymer featuring complete replacement of nitrogen in melanin by selenium (PDSe) was designed and synthesized via a heterocycle-engineering strategy. The key diselenide monomer, a structural mimic of dopamine, circumvents the poor stability of selenols and enables the formation of PDSe via a free-radical pathway. Experiments and density functional theory revealed the cascade reduction-oxidation-annulation-polymerization mechanism. PDSe retains key radioprotective motifs of melanin, including catechol group, benzofused heterocycles, persistent free radicals, and extended π-conjugation. Meanwhile, selenium substitution enhances radiation physical attenuation and antioxidant activity. PDSe showed significantly improved γ-ray protection, a survival rate increase from 0% to 100% in mice exposed to 6 Gy γ-ray total-body irradiation. This work promotes the development of safe radioprotectors and offers a multifunctional material for biomedical, optical, and device applications.

papers.title: Nitrogen plasma meets automated purification: Direct and reliable Fe isotopic analysis with MC-MICAP-MS
papers.abstract: Background: In conventional MC-ICP-MS, Fe isotopic analysis is hindered by spectral interferences arising from both the Ar plasma ( e.g. , 40 Ar 16 O + on 56 Fe + ) and the sample matrix ( e.g. , Cr, Ni, and matrix effects). To overcome these limitations, we evaluated the recently developed MC-MICAP-MS, which uses an N 2 -based plasma, for direct measurement of 56 Fe/ 54 Fe isotopic composition in biological samples, combined with a novel fully automated purification procedure. Results: The N 2 plasma eliminates Ar-based interferences, enabling direct measurement of 56 Fe/ 54 Fe under low resolution conditions with intermediate precisions of 0.07 ‰. CaN + and KN + interferences were negligible at Ca/Fe ≤ 0.01 and K/Fe < 0.1, while Na and Mg caused no significant matrix effects up to a matrix/Fe ratio of 1 : 1. Compared with other plasma-based techniques, MC-MICAP-MS provides a more robust approach for direct 56 Fe/ 54 Fe analysis. The automated purification method enabled unattended sample processing and yielded low, reproducible blanks (<5 ng), no carryover, high Fe recovery (98 % ± 8 %, 2 SD), and no significant on-column fractionation across bone, liver, hair, and river water matrices. Accuracy was confirmed using four biological and environmental reference materials. We propose δ 56 Fe/ 54 Fe IRMM014 values for NIST SRM 1400 of 0.06 ± 0.07 ‰, for GBW07601 of -0.14 ± 0.07 ‰, for GBW09101 of 0.06 ± 0.07 ‰, and for SLRS-6 of 0.44 ± 0.12 ‰. Significance: Automated purification combined with MC-MICAP-MS provides a robust, reliable, and high-throughput approach for precise Fe isotope analysis of biological samples, making it more accessible to a broader range of users.

papers.title: Biomimetic Asymmetric Heterogeneous Catalysis by Chiral Perovskites
papers.abstract: The rational design of intrinsically chiral solid catalysts remains a central challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Here we demonstrate that chiral 2D metal halide perovskites act as effective heterogeneous platforms for enantioselective transformations. Using (R-/S-MBA)2PbI4, we achieve asymmetric induction in a benchmark Diels–Alder cycloaddition, with enantioselectivity directly governed by the handedness of the perovskite lattice. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that stereocontrol arises from substrate confinement within a surface chiral pocket, where selective interactions stabilize the favored transition state. Unlike conventional strategies based on chiral modifiers, chirality is intrinsically encoded in the catalytic material, enabling direct control over reaction outcome. These findings establish chiral perovskites as a new class of solid-state catalysts bridging materials chemistry and asymmetric synthesis.

papers.title: Visible Light-Mediated Dearomative Cyclopropanation of Benzoheterocycles via 3-exo-trig radical cyclization
papers.abstract: Fused cyclopropanes are prominent motifs in bio-active molecules, yet their incorporation into densely functionalized frameworks remains a significant synthetic challenge. Herein, we report a light-mediated dearomative cyclopropanation of ben-zoheterocycles enabled by an energy-transfer (EnT) cascade. A precisely orchestrated radical sequence selectively generates a homoallylic radical that undergoes a rare 3-exo-trig cyclization, forging a highly strained cyclopropane ring. This transformation converts benzofuran,benzothiophene, and indole derivatives into complex polycyclic architectures bearing cyclopropane-fused units and multiple stereocenters, including contiguous quaternary carbons, with remarkable diastereoselectivity. Mechanistic studies, combining experimental investigations and DFT calculations, support an EnT activation pathway involving neutral diradical intermediates culminating in the unusual 3-exo-trig radical cyclization.

papers.title: Reversible Covalent Backbone Engineering in Disulfide-Bridged Diketopyrrolopyrrole-based Polymers
papers.abstract: Organic semiconducting polymers have become promising platforms to develop emerging electronic and sensing devices due to their tunable optoelectronic properties, mechanical flexibility, and solution processing compatibility. While dynamic non-covalent interactions have been widely explored to impart molecular stretchability and stimuli-responsiveness to these materials, the integration of dynamic covalent bonds within π-conjugated systems remains largely underdeveloped. This work focuses on the incorporation of dynamic disulfide bonds directly into the π-conjugated backbone of a diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based semiconducting polymer. The material was synthesized via a metal-free oxidative polymerization of in situ-generated thiolated precursors, providing a sustainable alternative to conventional Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling methods while yielding polymers with relatively high molecular weight and narrow dispersity. Compared to a fully conjugated analogue, the disulfide-linked polymer exhibited reduced πdelocalization but was shown to undergo redox-responsive functionality, enabling complete backbone cleavage and fluorescence recovery upon reduction. Comprehensive characterization, including optical spectroscopy, thermal analysis, atomic force microscopy, X-ray scattering, and computational modeling, revealed that incorporation of disulfide linkages disrupts long-range crystallinity while preserving semiconducting behavior, as confirmed by single-carrier diode measurements. The dynamic nature of the disulfide bonds, capable of reversible exchange under mild conditions, introduces a new mechanism for structural adaptability in conjugated polymers without requiring external stimuli.

papers.title: 4-Fluorophenyl Tagging as a Diagnostic Tool for Monitoring Sulfur Oxidation States via 19F NMR
papers.abstract: We report a simple and general strategy to monitor sulfur oxidation states using 19 F NMR by incorporating a 4-fluorophenyl tag on sulfur-containing molecules. A series of structurally related compounds spanning various sulfur oxidation states were compiled, and their 19 F NMR chemical shifts were recorded to establish a diagnostic fingerprint tool. This approach enables rapid characterization of products and byproducts in sulfur-based transformations, particularly those involving redox changes such as disproportionation. To demonstrate the utility of the method, we applied it to study reactions involving sulfur oxidation state changes, establishing a proof-of-concept for this diagnostic platform. This technique offers a valuable tool for mechanistic analysis and product profiling in diverse areas of sulfur chemistry.

papers.title: Tuning Mechanical Properties and Phase Behavior of Thermoplastic Polyurethane Elastomers with Unconventional Polycarbonate Hard Segments Derived from CO2
papers.abstract: Poly(cyclohexene carbonate) (PCHC) polyol is CO2-derived and has a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 104 °C. We incorporate PCHC into thermoplastic polyurethane elastomers (TPUs): a TPU with 35 wt% PCHC is 13 wt% CO2-derived. We investigate how TPU nanophase behavior and properties are affected when we maintain a constant level of conventional hard segment (HS), made by reacting 1,4-phenylene diisocyanate and 1,3-propanediol, while incorporating PCHC as a second HS. With 9 wt% conventional HS, the TPU tensile modulus is 9.3 MPa; upon incorporating 15-35 wt% PCHC, the modulus is reduced nearly a factor of 3. Relative to a TPU with 9 wt% conventional HS but no PCHC, strain-at-break values increase by factors of roughly 4, from 520% to 2000% and 2300%, in TPUs with 15 wt% and 35 wt% PCHC, the largest TPU strain-at-break values ever reported. Small-angle X-ray scattering reveals increasing inter-HS domain spacing with PCHC content, with HS domain number density decreasing and size increasing. The HS domains have a single Tg that decreases toward the neat PCHC Tg as PCHC content increases. There is also a broadening of the glass transition, with Tg breadth increasing from 25 °C at 0 wt% PCHC to 41-45 °C at 5-35 wt% PCHC. The broad HS- domain glass transition in TPUs with PCHC indicates that HS domains have intermixed conventional and PCHC HS, with heterogeneity among domains. These factors lead to extraordinary mechanical softening of the TPUs with increasing PCHC content. Nevertheless, the TPUs have robust physical cross-links up to 80-100 °C.

papers.title: A Fundamental Source of Misclassification in Single-Concentration Binding Screens
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: High-throughput screening of large libraries of compounds for binding to a target protein underpins drug discovery and chemical probe development. Primary screens typically test each compound at a single fixed concentration, classifying hits when a measured signal crosses a threshold. Only hits advance to secondary assays to determine equilibrium dissociation constants. Misclassification of compounds as hits or non-hits in primary screens is typically attributed to chemistry-specific nuisance behavior, readout artifacts, and screening design. Here, we identify a previously unrecognised fundamental vulnerability in single-concentration binding screens. Our first-principles analysis shows that when compound–target signals are non-additive, small errors in nominal concentrations can be amplified into large errors in the single-point readout. Non-additivity can arise through nonlinear signal formation during measurement and nonlinear post-acquisition transforms. End-to-end simulations reveal operating regimes where this amplification is most severe and demonstrate how it can drive irreversible false negatives because missed binders do not advance to secondary screening, including cases where true highaffinity binders are preferentially penalized and can fall below the threshold. We provide practical diagnostic criteria and design rules for robust single-concentration binding screening, including end-toend additivity checks, screening conditions that reduce sensitivity to depletion, and tight control of ligand and target concentrations.

papers.title: ParetoMol: A Free Web Application for Multi-Objective Pareto Analysis of Molecular Safety and Pharmacokinetics
papers.abstract: Molecular optimization requires balancing conflicting objectives—potency, selectivity, pharmacokinetics, and safety—yet freely available cheminformatics tools present these properties in isolation, forcing researchers to reconcile trade-o!s manually. Here, we present ParetoMol, an open-source web application that computes Pareto dominance across user-defined molecular objectives and provides 14 synchronized visualization tabs for interactive exploration of compound trade-o!s. ParetoMol accepts molecules via SMILES strings, CSV/SDF file upload, ChEMBL target identifiers, or PubChem name resolution; additional experimental data can be merged at any point via CSV/TSV upload. Visualization tabs include configurable Pareto scatter plots, BOILED-Egg partitioning, sca!old analysis, chemical space projection (UMAP/PCA/t-SNE), activity cli! detection, parallel coordinates, radar charts, and multi-parameter optimization scoring. Three demonstrations illustrate the platform’s analytical capabilities: (i) safety-augmented Pareto analysis of 1,949 FDA-approved drugs expands the Pareto front 3.6-fold, rescuing 131 compounds with favorable predicted safety profiles; (ii) sca!old-level analysis of 50 EGFR inhibitors reveals universal predicted AhR activation across the 4-anilinoquinazoline class (100% above threshold vs. 50% in matched controls; p = 5.61x10 -10 ); and (iii) cross-class comparison of 92 compounds across six drug classes reveals class-specific predicted risk profiles with orthogonal liability axes—including NSAIDs with minimal predicted cardiac and mutagenic risk but second-highest predicted DILI—that are invisible to single-endpoint screening. ParetoMol is freely available at https://paretomol.com under the MIT license.

papers.title: Manipulating reactive intermediate coverage and kinetically relevant steps via visible photon-mediated catalysis on Rh-doped perovskite oxides
papers.abstract: Catalyst behavior depends on surface adsorbate(s) energetics, which on metal catalysts are governed by scaling relationships. External stimuli ( e.g., photons), however, can disrupt these limitations and affect key intermediate coverages. Here, low energy photon flux is utilized to selectively control surface coverages of strongly-bound intermediates on well-defined isolated Rh active sites doped within a semiconductor perovskite oxide host (SrTiO 3 ). Red light (632 nm) facilitates the selective photolysis of Rh gem- dicarbonyl species that are ubiquitous site poisons, including for the probe reaction herein, CO oxidation to CO 2 . Thermochemical CO 2 rates (408 K) on Rh-doped SrTiO 3 are limited by adsorbed CO, exhibiting a negative apparent CO rate order (-0.6) and a positive O 2 rate order (+0.4). Arrhenius analyses, anaerobic CO oxidation measurements, and in situ spectroscopies assert that thermochemically, lattice oxygens from the doped perovskite contribute to CO 2 formation rates. Notably, under red light (0.76-2.02 W cm -2 ), the apparent CO rate order shifts to positive (+1), with photochemical rates depending directly on photon flux. This, combined with decreasing apparent activation energies and CO coverages (wavelength-agnostic) with increasing photon flux, indicates that photogenerated carriers facilitate selective Rh gem- dicarbonyl photolysis, thereby enhancing O 2 dissociation and increasing CO 2 rates. Finally, low energy red light enables the utilization of more stoichiometric feeds, leading to 650% higher CO 2 rates than those achieved thermally. Overall, this work on coupled photo/thermochemical transformations on photoactive Rh-doped SrTiO 3 elucidates how low energy light can be leveraged to selectively tune strongly-bound intermediate coverages and break scaling relationships to improve reaction rates.

papers.title: Rational Design of Tunable μ-Opioid Receptor–Preferring Scaffolds with Integrated Calcium Channel Interaction: An Analogue-Based Computational Study
papers.abstract: This study presents a computational, analogue-driven investigation aimed at identifying and refining a candidate scaffold with preferential μ-opioid receptor (MOR) interaction characteristics and potential secondary compatibility with voltage-gated calcium channelassociated binding regions. Rather than focusing on a single optimised compound, the work adopts an exploratory approach in which an initial scaffold, selected on the basis of predicted physicochemical suitability, was systematically modified and evaluated across an analogue series of approximately 30 structures. Docking was performed against both active-state (5C1M) and inactive-state (9MQ1) MOR conformations, in addition to κ-(4DJH) and δ-opioid (4N6H) receptors and the α2δ-1 calcium channel subunit (8IF3), allowing assessment of receptor-state preference and cross-target interaction behaviour. The parent scaffold demonstrated reproducible orthosteric MOR binding alongside consistent engagement of a defined polar interaction region within 8IF3. However, iterative analogue modification revealed that structural changes improving MOR active-state compatibility frequently disrupted the spatial arrangement required to maintain the calciumchannel-associated interaction motif. This behaviour was consistent across the series and defines a clear tradeoff between MORcompatible binding geometry and preservation of secondary interaction features, indicating the presence of a multi-objective optimisation constraint within this scaffold class. In parallel, reversible acetylation was explored as a strategy to modulate predicted CNS accessibility, acting at the level of delivery rather than core pharmacophore modification. Overall, the study identifies a tractable scaffold framework and characterises its interaction limits, positioning it as a candidate for further refinement. The findings are intended to support lead identification and prioritisation rather than establish functional activity, providing a structured basis for subsequent experimental evaluation.

papers.title: Mitigating Anaesthetic Emissions: CALF-20 for N2O Capture from exhaled anaesthetic streams
papers.abstract: Waste anaesthetic and analgesic nitrous oxide (N 2 O) accounts for ~2% of Western healthcare greenhouse emissions, yet capture technologies are scarce. Here, we highlight CALF-20 for high-efficiency N 2 O capture under clinically relevant conditions (2.17-2.78 mol kg -1 at 25-35 °C and 0.5 bar N 2 O), showcasing opportunities for sustainable anaesthetic gas capture technologies.

papers.title: Open Questions on Viral Frameshifting: Exploiting Structural Plasticity of the Frameshifting Element for Therapeutic Intervention
papers.abstract: Programmed Ribosomal Frameshifting (PRF) is a specialized controlled-slippage genetic mechanism that viruses like SARS-CoV-2 and HIV-1 use to shift the reading frame during translation. This process is used in compact viral genomes to enhance their protein repertoire, maintain a precise balance of viral proteins necessary for successful replication, and enhance survival within a host. Because this mechanism is vital to the viral life cycle and remains consistent across strains, frameshifting has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for new antiviral therapeutic strategies. However, the complexity of the frameshifting process has posed many challenges that need to be addressed so that the relationship between cellular mechanisms and viral replication can be exploited for novel therapeutics. In this mini review, we introduce frameshifting mechanisms, define open questions being explored by many modeling and experimental studies, and illustrate how coarse-grained graphs have been used in our lab to study frameshifting mechanisms. Specifically, we describe how conformational landscapes, mutation designs of frameshifting elements, all-atom molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling simulations have been combined with chemical mapping and functional experiments to advance studies on three viral systems employing −1 PRF: SARS-CoV-2, HIV-1, and Chikungunya.

papers.title: Auger Spectra of Thiouracils: Three Molecules and Four Edges
papers.abstract: This work presents a comprehensive investigation of the Auger spectra of three thionated uracils using a combination of theory and experiment. Non-resonant Auger spectra measured at the K-edges of carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen, as well as at the L 2, 3 e dge of sulfur are reported. Even though the final decay states (valence twohole states) are the same for all edges, the resulting Auger spectra are strikingly different, highlighting the local nature of the Auger decay. Theoretical modeling, which employed a series of approaches incorporating varying levels of correlation and different treatments of the metastable states, provides a clear interpretation of the experimental spectra. The analysis highlights the crucial role of electron correlation, evident in both the density of the decay states and the spectra constructed using channel-specific partial decay widths, as well as the importance of spin–orbit coupling in shaping the L-edge spectra of thiouracils.

papers.title: Revisiting heterotrophic denitrification modelling: a systematic parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification study
papers.abstract: This study revisits ASM3-based modelling of heterotrophic denitrification by assessing whether a concise non-competitive formulation can reproduce denitrification dynamics across literature datasets while preserving mechanistic interpretability and allowing extension to multiple nitrogen species. The model combines metabolically informed yield and maintenance relations, explicit feast and famine dynamics, intracellular polymer storage, and Bayesian calibration for parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification. The analysis shows that a concise one-step model based on nitrate equivalents reproduces short-term denitrification dynamics across seven datasets with narrow credible intervals, while revealing intrinsic variability associated with mixed cultures and measurement noise. A two-step extension was also developed to reproduce observed nitrite dynamics, interpreted as an imbalance between nitrite production and consumption, with acclimation reflected in shifts in nitrate and nitrite reduction rates. For acetate-based systems, four mechanistic parameters were sufficient across a wide range of conditions when minimum data quality requirements were met. By contrast, applications to complex wastewaters remained limited by uncertainty in substrate fractionation and by the scarcity of informative experimental data. Overall, the results support the use of concise mechanistic models with uncertainty quantification for interpretable analysis of heterotrophic denitrification.

papers.title: Attributing Ambient Hydrocarbon Concentrations to Local Oil and Gas Emission Sources
papers.abstract: Emissions from oil and gas sources located near populated regions can have impacts on air quality, resulting in potential acute and chronic exposures. This work couples a highresolution emission inventory with dispersion modeling to quantify the contribution of hydrocarbon emissions from oil and gas operations to populated areas in Midland, Texas, within the Permian Basin oil and gas production region. The analyses examine the impacts of oil and gas emission sources within three concentric zones extending 5, 10, and 15 km from the Midland city center. The spatially and temporally resolved inventory provides hourly emission estimates for oil and gas operations including pre-production activities, production, gathering, and flaring. Dispersion modeling was conducted at an hourly resolution for a representative one-week period in February 2022. Results predict that sources within the 15-km radius contribute average concentrations of 24 ppb, 25 ppb, and 0.28 ppb for ethane, propane, and benzene, respectively. These nearby sources account for an average of about 50% of the total predicted concentrations for ethane, propane, and benzene from oil and gas sources. The analyses also show that nearby sources, coupled with certain meteorological conditions, can lead to acute episodic concentrations exceeding 600 ppb for ethane and propane, and 7 ppb for benzene.

papers.title: A Systematic Survey and Benchmark of Deep Learning for Molecular Property Prediction in the Foundation Model Era
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction integrates quantum chemistry, cheminformatics, and deep learning to connect molecular structure with physicochemical and biological behavior. This survey traces four complementary paradigms, including Quantum, Descriptor Machine Learning, Geometric Deep Learning, and Foundation Models, and outlines a unified taxonomy linking molecular representations, model architectures, and interdisciplinary applications. Benchmark analyses integrate evidence from both widely used datasets and datasets reflecting industry perspectives, encompassing quantum, physicochemical, physiological, and biophysical domains. The survey examines current standards in data curation, splitting strategies, and evaluation protocols, highlighting challenges including inconsistent stereochemistry, heterogeneous assay sources, and reproducibility limitations under random or poorly defined splits. These observations motivate the modernization of benchmark design toward more transparent, time-and scaffold-aware methodologies. We further propose three forward-looking directions: (i) physics-aware learning embedding quantum consistency, (ii) uncertainty-calibrated foundation models for trustworthy inference, and (iii) realistic multimodal benchmark ecosystems integrating computational and experimental data. Repository: https://github.com/Zongru-Li/Survey-and-Benchmarks-of-DL-for-Molecular-Property-Prediction-in-the-Foundation-Model-Era.

papers.title: Characterization of Non-Radiative Recombination Mechanisms in Boron Gallium Nitride Edge Emitting Laser Diodes
papers.abstract: We simulate temperature dependent non-radiative recombination in deep-UV Boron GaN edge emitting laser diodes (EELDs) (270–600 K) and expose a distinguishing, self-compensating confinement mechanism unique to Boron GaN Multiple QWs. As temperature rises Shockley Read Hall SRH and Auger rates increase and hole leakage at the Electron Blocking Layer EBL becomes obvious, yet slope efficiency drops only ~8% (3.21→2.96 W/A) and high output is preserved (48.5 W at 270 K). Energy Band structure investigation shows that electron and hole confinement potentials rise with temperature, from approximately ϕe≈100 meV to ϕe≈216 meV and from ϕh≈ 80 meV to ϕh≈130 meV, respectively. Carrier distribution reveal temperature advanced electron injection and central Quantum Well QW localization, with stable QW hole density but strong EBL adjacent depletion. Recombination is centralized in the middle QW, with Auger progressions increasingly dominant above ~400 K. These findings explain the device’s thermal strength and guide targeted EBL or barrier engineering and thermal management to suppress non radiative losses.

papers.title: Interfacial Engineering of 2D/2D BiVO4/V2CTx Heterostructures for Enhanced Symmetric Supercapacitor Performance Across Various Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Engineering well-defined heterostructured composites is an effective strategy for improving the electrochemical performance of energy storage systems. In this study, a 2D/2D BiVO4/V2CTx heterostructure was synthesized via a simple hydrothermal method and, for the first time, systematically tested as a symmetric supercapacitor electrode in neutral (1 M Na2SO4), alkaline (1 M KOH), and acidic (1 M H2SO4) electrolytes. The composite showed better electrochemical performance compared to pristine V2CTx, with specific capacitances of 191.5 F g-1, 107 F g-1, and 239 F g-1 in Na2SO4, KOH, and H2SO4, respectively, at 0.016 A g-1. A high energy density of 83.3 Wh kg-1 at 147.5 W kg-1 was achieved in the neutral electrolyte, along with excellent rate capability and Coulombic efficiency. These improvements arise from the synergistic interaction between BiVO4 and V2CTx, which increases active site accessibility and promotes efficient ion and electron transport. Overall, the results show that the BiVO4/V2CTx heterostructure is a promising and versatile electrode material for high-performance supercapacitors.

papers.title: Photo-Activated Merging Cascades in Droplet Swarms upon Synergistic Solvation of Surfactants.
papers.abstract: Chemically active droplets at fluid interfaces provide versatile building blocks for dynamic matter, yet most systems are limited to behavior encoded within individual droplets or simple pairwise interactions. Here, we report a strategy to generate non-linear, cascading behavior in droplet swarms by combining photo-activation with synergistic solvation of a surfactant mesophase. At an air-water interface coated with a semi-crystalline decylamine (DA) layer, mesitylene-based droplets containing a photo-acid generator remain immotile until UV irradiation locally destabilizes the DA layer, which induces droplet motion via capillary effects. While both UV-responsive mesitylene droplets and tri(ethylene glycol) monododecyl ether (C 12 E 3 ) droplets are individually immobilized within the DA layer, their fusion produces hybrid droplets that dissolve the DA layer through synergistic solvation and exhibit enhanced motility that persists after UV irradiation is stopped. This non-linear activation enables cascades of chasing and merging events that propagate through large droplet fields well beyond the initial space-time window of photo-activation. By introducing repellent boundary structures, these cascades can be spatially confined, allowing control over collective swarm dynamics. Together, our results demonstrate how synergistic solvation allows to program emergent, multistep behavior in active droplet swarms, opening avenues toward droplet-based logics in chemically driven self-organization.

papers.title: Toward Resolving the RuO2/IrO2 Oxygen Evolution Activity Puzzle: Critical Roles of Spin Polarization and Exchange-Correlation Functional Accuracy
papers.abstract: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity ordering of RuO2 and IrO2 is well established experimentally, yet density functional theory calculations have persistently failed to reproduce this trend, undermining computational catalyst design. Here, we investigate this discrepancy by evaluating OER thermodynamic and kinetic activities of IrO2 and RuO2 using four exchange-correlation (XC) functionals (PBE, RPBE, r2SCAN, and MS2-rVV10) under spin-polarized and spin-unpolarized conditions. Spin polarization selectively stabilizes the O* intermediate on IrO2 while leaving RuO2 comparatively unaffected, and neglecting spin effects yields unphysically low kinetic barriers for IrO2. Among the four functionals, only MS2-rVV10 reproduces the experimentally observed thermodynamic activity ordering; however, all functionals fail to capture the correct kinetic barrier ordering. We trace these failures to a systematic correlation between adsorption-energy errors and deviations in the predicted activity trend. Notably, the OOH*-OH* scaling offset and theoretical limiting potential are themselves XC-functional dependent, cautioning against cross-functional comparison of overpotentials. Cross-code benchmarks rule out numerical implementation as the error source, while higher-rung functionals progressively overestimate Ru local magnetic moments in RuO2, introducing additional errors. This work provides a diagnostic framework for developing XC functionals that simultaneously capture surface reaction energetics and local magnetic properties for reliable OER catalyst screening.

papers.title: Spherulitic Crystal Growth in MAPbI₃₋ₓClₓ Thin Films Triggered by Ambient Moisture: Clarification of a 2017 Conference Report
Superalkali-Functionalized Cyclo[6]carbon Complexes, M3O@C6 (M = Li, Na, and K): Metal-Dependent Structure and Properties
papers.abstract: The geometric, electronic, and optical properties of hybrid materials M3O@C6 (M = Li, Na, and K), constructed by superalkali (M3O, M = Li, Na, and K) with excess electrons and the smallest electron-accepting carbon ring cyclo[6]carbon (C6), were systematically studied using (time-dependent) density functional theory [(TD-)DFT] combined with various wavefunction analysis methods. Natural population analysis (NPA) confirms charge transfer from M3O to C6 in complexes. Combined analyses of the independent gradient model based on Hirshfeld partition (IGMH) analysis, inter-fragment interaction energy (ΔEint), and Atoms in Molecules (AIM) indicate that the M3O interacts with C6 mainly through electrostatic interactions. The electronic properties, inter-fragment interaction strength, photoresponse behaviors, and electron absorption spectra of the M3O@C6 (M = Li, Na, and K) systems all vary monotonically with increasing alkali metal atomic number. Taking K3O@C6 with the largest isotropic (hyper)polarizability (αiso(-ω;ω) and βtot(-2ω;ω,ω)) in the series as an example, the anisotropic feature, spatial contribution, and structural origin of the (hyper)polarizability were revealed by analyzing the (hyper)polarizability tensor, investigating (hyper)polarizability density, and performing the (hyper)polarizability decomposition. Compared with the pristine C6, the M3O@C6 (M = Li, Na, and K) show a remarkably reduced intensity and an obvious red-shift in their electronic absorption spectra. Hole-electron analysis indicates that the excitations related to their maximum absorption are mainly localized on the carbon ring. This work not only clarifies the aforementioned properties of M3O@C6 (M = Li, Na, and K) hybrid complexes, but also reveals their regular metal-dependent variation, providing valuable insights into the design of novel optical materials with tunable photophysical performance.

papers.title: Studies of ion-exchange and migration of transition metals in bulk zeolite chabazite
papers.abstract: Transition metal zeolites, predominantly made via aqueous ion-exchange of a base zeolite with a metal salt solution, are crucial for a range of industrial applications from heterogeneous catalysis to gas separation. However the mechanism of ion-exchange (IE) under solvated conditions is poorly understood. Modelling this process at the atomistic level has proven to be challenging due to the non-trivial impact of the solvent on the migration path and the need for a large number of water molecules to be explicitly modelled. Here we tackle this hurdle by partially relaxing the metal and solvent along the migration pathway, followed by an optimisation of key points on the migration path in a scheme referred to as partial relaxation-geometry optimisation (PRGO). This approach dramatically reduced the computational cost of modelling the migration of CuII, CuII(OAc), CoII, FeII, and PdII and 7 distinct spin-states in bulk hydrated chabazite at the density functional theory (DFT) level. Intriguingly, via an exhaustive examination of spatial and spin phase space, we observed a spin degeneracy for the transition state of the CoII migration and a spin-flip from M = 5 to M = 3 for FeII when the metal entered the interconnecting 8-membered ring between the zeolite cages with this spin behaviour having a non-negligible effect on transport barriers. Nevertheless, comparisons to our direct, physical IE experiments indicate that surface rather than bulk diffusion processes limit the uptake of these commercially important catalytic metal cations.

papers.title: Multi-Fidelity Thermodynamically Consistent Neural Networks for Vapor Pressure Prediction of Petroleum Hydrocarbons
papers.abstract: Accurate vapor pressure data are the basis for many fields. Over the past decades, various vapor pressure regression and prediction models have been proposed, but a highly accurate, thermodynamically consistent, and generalizable method remains unavailable. To overcome the limitations, we propose the MFTCNN-VP—Multi-Fidelity Thermodynamically Consistent Neural Networks for Vapor Pressure prediction of petroleum hydrocarbons. It incorporates the Waring constraint and is trained on 459 hydrocarbon molecules. Only optimized molecular structure information and critical points are needed to calculate the prior predicted vapor pressure curves, and high-accuracy predictions are obtained for multi-fidelity calibration by combining with experimental data. We evaluate the MFTCNN-VP on a test set with 40 new substances and 1400 experimental points, achieving an impressive prediction accuracy of approximately 2.09% (AARD). By significantly outperforming current machine learning methods in both applicability and accuracy, the MFTCNN-VP demonstrates considerable potential for modeling a broader range of thermodynamic properties.

papers.title: Bioinspired adhesives from bio-sourced poly(amino acid)s coacervates: green, tough and smart
papers.abstract: Green adhesives are gradually replacing traditional synthetic adhesives due to their eco-friendly properties and sustainability. However, the industrial applications of green adhesives are limited by their lower strength and durability, longer curing time, higher cost compared to traditional synthetic adhesives. Here, inspired by the coacervation process of sandcastle worms and Dopa chemistry of mussels, we show green adhesives with combined high instant adhesive strength and low cost by enhancing the interaction of γ-polyglutamic acid (γ-PGA)/ε-poly-L-lysine (ε-PLL) coacervates through the introduction of tannic acid (TA). The preparation method is green, simple and fast, adhering to green chemistry principles. Specifically, taking advantage of variable non-covalent interactions between γ-PGA, ε-PLL and TA, the synergistical enhancement of cohesion and adhesion leads to the excellent adhesive strength of coacervates. As a result, the adhesive exhibits maximum adhesive strength of 18.21 MPa and instant adhesive strength of 1.54 MPa, surpassing most currently reported adhesives based on non-covalent bonds. Notably, the multiple non-covalent interactions endow the adhesive with reversible debonding-on-demand and recyclability, retaining its original adhesive strength even after 10 cycles. The feasibility to simultaneously overcome the major bottlenecks for green adhesives provides new insights for developing other sustainable green materials.

papers.title: Alkyl-Branched Acyl-Lysine Peptides as Potent Cell-Permeable Slow-Substrate Inhibitors of SIRT2
papers.abstract: Sirtuin 2 (SIRT2) is a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-dependent lysine deacylase implicated in cancer and neurodegeneration. Here, we report acyl-lysine peptide inhibitors bearing methyl-branched or cyclopropyl-modified acyl chains with low-nanomolar inhibitory potency. Their prolonged residence time and minimal catalytic turnover, confirmed by kinetic analysis, support a “slow-substrate” inhibition mechanism. Ternary crystal structures of SIRT2–peptide–NAD+ complexes are consistent with a rate-limiting initial nucleophilic attack of the amide oxygen on NAD+. The inhibitors stabilize a catalytically competent yet unproductive enzyme state, distinct from thiocarbonyl inhibitors that form stalled intermediates with NAD+. Comparative structural and biochemical analyses with SIRT1 and SIRT3 reveal isoform-specific acyl-chain trajectories underlying selectivity. Extension to potentially naturally occurring or drug-derived Nε-lysine modifications, i.e., phytanoyl- and ibuprofenyl-lysine, demonstrates that diverse branched acyl groups inhibit SIRT2. In cells, optimized inhibitors show low-nanomolar target engagement and induce robust α-tubulin hyperacetylation, establishing slow-substrate inhibition as a strategy for selective sirtuin targeting.

papers.title: Assessing the removal of microplastics, nanoplastics, and tire derived contaminants using chemically enhanced primary treatment
papers.abstract: Drinking water production facilities and wastewater treatment plants act as the final barrier to 16 prevent plastic contaminant release into the drinking water supply system and into natural waters, 17 respectively. In this study, the performance of chemically-enhanced primary treatment (CEPT) to 18 remove four types of micro- and nanoplastic contaminants (polyester microfibers, polyethylene 19 microspheres, tire crumb rubber, and polystyrene nanoplastics) from surface water and wastewater 20 influent was assessed under different treatment conditions and varying environmental factors. 21 Alternative coagulants, including ferric sulfate (FS) and aluminum chlorohydrate (ACH) improved 22 treatment under conditions that were challenging for alum (pH > 8). Namely, in wastewater at pH 23 7, FS and ACH effectively removed tire crumb rubber (83 ± 4% and 93 ± 3%, respectively) 24 compared to alum (27 ± 6%). Similarly, FS was an effective coagulant for treating surface water 25 at pH 8.5 with high removal across all micro-sized plastic contaminants: 90 ± 3% tire crumb 26 rubber, 89 ± 2% microfiber, and 87 ± 1% microplastic. No significant difference in polyester 27 microfiber or polyethylene microsphere removal was observed between coagulants at pH 8.5. Jar 28 tests also showed that environmental factors such as the presence of laundry detergent and UV-29 irradiation impacted the extent of plastic contaminant removal. Nanoplastic removal was observed 30 to be correlated with turbidity removal in both wastewater and surface water jar tests, with the 31 highest nanoplastic removal observed using alum to treat wastewater (51 ± 3%; pH 8.5) and ACH 32 to treat surface water (83 ± 1%; pH 7). Results from this work offer new insights into the impact 33 of treatment conditions, environmental factors, and plastic type and morphology on the 34

papers.title: Mechanical suppression of proton-coupled electron transfer in MXene nanoconfinement
papers.abstract: Ion adsorption and electron transfer govern electrochemical charge storage in porous electrodes 1,2 . When ions enter subnanometer pores, ionic desolvation and solvation can strongly shift this balance 2,3 . In two-dimensional (2D) materials like MXenes and graphene, insertion and removal of solvated ions induce significant interlayer expansions 4,5,6 . The transport mechanisms of protons and other ions behave differently under nanoconfinement. In extreme cases, electrolyte ions are sterically blocked by a trapped water monolayer, while water and protons remain mobile 7 . However, how externally applied pressure affects electrochemical processes under nanoconfinement is still unclear. Here, we show how various ions insert and react electrochemically within Ti₃C₂T ₓ MXene (T x : mixed terminations) layers under in situ mechanical constraint. We find that such nanoconfinement significantly suppresses redox reactions, including Ti–OH formation and water splitting. Using multiscale modeling — ab initio molecular dynamics, metadynamics, and a continuum kinetic model — we show that mechanical constraint disrupts the hydrogen-bond network of confined water, stabilizing surface-bound protons, and limiting their exchange with water. This coupling between mechanical and chemical effects enables micrometer-thin electrochemical pressure sensors that function under high loads and offers a route to suppress unwanted redox reactions, extending the safe voltage window for devices. These insights contribute to the advancement of pseudocapacitive energy storage, capacitive deionization, electrocatalysis, and electrochemical actuator technologies.

papers.title: Light-Driven Deaminative Nucleophilic Substitution via C(sp3)-N bond Cleavage: Nucleophilic Transamination of Alkyl Amines
papers.abstract: Herein, we report a photoredox-enabled catalytic transamination strategy that enables direct amine-to-amine interconversion without prefunctionalization. The reaction proceeds via a polarity inversion pathway, in which one amine is converted into an electrophilic iminium intermediate that couples with a second amine nucleophile. The method exhibits broad scope across benzylic, unactivated, and tertiary amines. Mechanistic studies support the intermediacy of α-amino radical and iminium species, and reveal that selectivity is governed by two key principles: reaction directionality is controlled by relative nucleophilicity, while site-selectivity in C(sp3)–N bond cleavage is dictated by electronic activation or steric accessibility. This work establishes a general platform for the direct functionalization of native amines, with potential applications in the late-stage modification of complex and bioactive molecules.

papers.title: Stereodivergent γ-Propargylation of α,β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
papers.abstract: Notwithstanding tremendous progress in stereodivergent cooperative catalysis during the past decade, the application of this strategy involving propargylic substitution reaction is scarce. We report herein the first stereodivergent γ-propargylation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes. With racemic propargylic acetates as the electrophile, this reaction is catalyzed cooperatively by a Cu(I)/Pybox complex and diphenylprolinol silyl ether to deliver γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes, bearing two adjacent stereocenters, with complete regio- (γ- over α-) and (E)-selectivity as well as outstanding diastereo- and enantioselectivity. This strategy leverages the nucleophilicity and enantiofacial selectivity, offered by the catalytically generated chiral dienamine, towards electrophilic Cu-allenylidene complex. Despite independent control of the stereochemistry at the respective reactive intermediate by each catalyst, their productive merger is essential for high diastereo- and enantioselectivity. Access to all four stereoisomers of (E)-γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes is possible through simple permutations of secondary amine catalyst and Pybox enantiomers.

papers.title: How Structural Subtleties Modulate Excited-State Lifetimes in Cyclometalated Cobalt(III) Complexes: Nonadiabatic Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Ultrafast excited-state dynamics of two Co(III) complexes, bearing different alkyl groups (Co1: Methyl, Co2: Ethyl) at the nitrogen of the imidazole ligand, are investigated using trajectory surface hopping based on a linear vibronic coupling model. Despite nearly identical MLCT absorption spectra, experimental singlet lifetimes differ markedly (1.45 vs 4.3 ps). Relaxation occurs via rapid internal conversion within a strongly vibronically coupled singlet manifold, accompanied by intersystem crossing to long-lived 3MC states. The prolonged lifetime of Co2 originates from enhanced vibronic coupling and larger structural distortions, which trap population in the singlet manifold rather than from spin–orbit effects. Minimum-energy crossing points reveal low barriers for nonradiative decay, rationalizing emission quenching. These results demonstrate how subtle structural differences, by modulating vibronic coupling, can substantially influence excited-state lifetimes in these complexes.

papers.title: Overcoming the Energy Gap Law in NIR-II Fluorophores via S…S Interaction-Mediated Exciton-Vibrational Decoupling
papers.abstract: Although second near-infrared (NIR-II) theranostic fluorophores show great potential for noninvasive disease phototheranostics, the inherent antagonism between long-wavelength emission and high fluorescence brightness severely hinders their development. Herein, we propose a novel molecular design strategy based on through-space S···S interactions by introducing sulfur atoms in different molecular microenvironments into the conjugated backbone. The S···S interactions can simultaneously extend conjugation and rigidify molecular conformations, thus effectively suppressing non-radiative decay and breaking the bottleneck imposed by the energy gap law. Compared with its isomer NPTD without through-space S···S interactions, the designed fluorophore NTPD exhibits a redshifted emission peak and improved photoluminescence quantum yield in both molecular and aggregate states. These merits endow NTPD with great promise for high-resolution NIR-II imaging-guided photothermal therapy against cancer. This through-space S···S interaction strategy surmounts the traditional design limitations of long-wavelength fluorophores and provides a universal paradigm for creating high-performance NIR-II emitters.

papers.title: Curated digital datasets of acid dissociation constants in dipolar aprotic solvents
papers.abstract: The acid dissociation constant is a key thermodynamic property, but large compilations of highly trustworthy data in non-aqueous solvents are scarce. This work presents a newly-digitized compilation, with corrections, of pK a data published originally by Kosuke Izutsu in 1990 as an official publication of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC). The data span the six solvents dimethylacetamide, hexamethylphosphoramide, 4-methylpentan-2-one (or methyl isobutyl ketone), N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone, nitromethane, and sulfolane. Because the original data were not critically evaluated, we also include proposed systematic corrections to the data, which resolve major inconsistencies in the original data compilation. We also present, analyze, and discuss a digital version of the new IUPAC 2025 dataset for neutral acids in the solvents dimethyl sulfoxide, acetonitrile, dimethyl formamide, pyridine, acetone, tetrahydrofuran, and propylene carbonate, compiled by Leito and collaborators. We discuss the creation and contents of these digital data compilations, and analyze not only the pK a values, but also the overall reliability, methodology, and other available metadata. The Izutsu dataset is available at: doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19626584 and the IUPAC 2025 dataset at doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.12608876.

papers.title: Decoupling intracellular delivery and controlled cytosolic release using radiation-gated phase-separated coacervates
papers.abstract: Efficient intracellular delivery of functional proteins remains limited by the lack of mechanisms for controlled cytosolic release following cellular internalization. Existing delivery strategies predominantly rely on endocytic uptake and stochastic endosomal escape, thereby coupling cellular entry with uncontrolled release and limiting spatiotemporal regulation of protein activity. Here we report a radiation-gated phase-separated system based on self-immolative polymer coacervates (SIP-coacervates) that decouples intracellular delivery and controlled cytosolic release. We found that organizing self-immolative polymers into phase-separated coacervates enhances the polymers’ sensitivity to radiation-triggered depolymerization, resulting in nearly 70% disassembly upon exposure to a single clinically relevant 2 Gy γ-ray dose. The coacervates efficiently recruit a wide range of proteins and enable their cytosolic entry in a sequestered state before activation by an external stimulus. Upon γ-ray irradiation, proteins are released on demand with high efficiency while preserving biological activity. Mechanistically, the phase-separated coacervates amplifies radiation-induced chemical reactions, enabling externally gated control over intracellular release processes. This work establishes a γ-ray-gated strategy for decoupling intracellular delivery and cytosolic protein release, providing a general framework for integrating external physical stimuli with intracellular chemical processes.

papers.title: The Roles of Surface Reconstruction and Framework Stability in Acetic Acid Leaching of Lithium-Ion Battery Cathodes
papers.abstract: Hydrometallurgical recycling is a promising route for recovering critical materials from lithium-ion batteries, but the mechanisms governing organic-acid leaching remain poorly resolved across cathode chemistries. Here, we establish a comparative mechanistic framework for acetic-acid leaching of three representative cathodes: LCO, NMC111, and LFP. A parametric study varying acetic acid concentration, hydrogen peroxide dosage, and solid loading was combined with inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and powder X-ray diffraction to connect extraction performance with surface and bulk solid-state evolution. Layered oxides exhibited a delithiation-initiated, reconstruction-limited pathway under peroxidefree conditions, in which preferential Li extraction was accompanied by transition-metalrich passivation and suppressed overall dissolution. By contrast, hydrogen peroxide enabled near-stoichiometric dissolution and nearly complete extraction by suppressing passivation and sustaining lattice breakdown. LFP followed a fundamentally different pathway: even in the presence of hydrogen peroxide, leaching remained strongly Li-selective, with minimal Fe dissolution, indicating that dissolution is constrained by the stability of the olivine Fe–O–P framework rather than by transition-metal redox accessibility alone. These results show that hydrogen peroxide plays chemistry-dependent roles, promoting congruent dissolution in layered oxides while intensifying selective delithiation in phosphate cathodes. More broadly, this work provides a surface-to-bulk mechanistic basis for designing safer, chemistry-aware hydrometallurgical recycling strategies using organic acids.

papers.title: Inert column chromatography: Purification of oxygen-sensitive polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons
Conceptual Bio-Templated Synthesis of Hierarchical Zeolites from Waste-to-Energy Ash: A Circular Economy Framework
papers.abstract: Despite having the potential to be used as raw materials for sophisticated functional materials, the silica and alumina-rich ash produced by Singapore's waste-to-energy (WtE) incineration facilities is usually landfilled. [1] This work presents a conceptual and literature supported framework for a bio-templated, sustainable synthesis method that uses microbial–mineral interface engineering to transform WtE ash into hierarchically organized zeolites. This approach draws on reported studies which shows that microbial cells and associated extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) [4], [15], [18], promotes zeolite nucleation and the formation of multi-scale porosity. They act as natural structure directing agents. The proposed synthetic pathways integrate ash pretreatment, aluminiumsilicate gel preparation, microbial or EPS incorporation, hydrothermal crystallization at moderate temperature (~120 °C) and subsequent calcination to eliminate organic matter [6], [25], [7]. As suggested by existing literature, that in comparison to ordinary zeolites, the bio-templated zeolites have been reported to demonstrate improved crystallinity, higher surface areas, and connected micro–meso– macro-porous networks [2], [14], [18], [4], [23]. Such hierarchical architectures have been reported to improve molecular diffusion, active site availability and overall performance in adsorption and catalytic application [2], [14], [20], [18]. It also helps in the removal of volatile organic compounds and dyes. In contrast to surfactant-templated synthesis, this process uses less energy, avoid hazardous chemicals [2], [16], and turns industrial waste into something useful in the context of a circular economy. This study is carried out by consolidating existing experimental findings into a coherent synthesis framework. This work highlights a viable pathway for future experimental validation and sustainable material development within Singapore's waste management strategy. The study presents a conceptual and literature supported framework and does not include new experimental data.

papers.title: Exploring Transition Metal Complexes with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Here we use a large language model for the exploration of chemical space of transition metal complexes (TMCs), fine-tuning the open-source Llama-3.2-1B model with a variation of the SMILES string representation tailored for coordination chemistry. We identify several key molecular properties that are critical to produce valid TMCs which we use for prompt engineering, creating TMC-Llama models that generate unique, novel, and structurally validated TMCs at high success rates, and exceeding the performance of both standard benchmarks as well as state-of-the-art generative methods in the literature. We use the pydentate workflow to show that the TMC-Llama model generates new TMC chemistries that are physically realistic, synthetically plausible, and geometrically consistent with large datasets of known experimental TMCs. Our study lays the groundwork for future TMC-Llama generative model applications to discover new TMCs for functional materials for catalysis, photochemistry, medicine, and sustainability technologies.

papers.title: Ball mill-assisted fractionation of lignocellulosic biomass and silica from rice husks
papers.abstract: Converting biomass into valuable components such as silica and lignocellulosic compounds offers significant economic and environmental benefits. This study utilized rice husks as a raw material to extract lignocellulosic fractions and silica, systematically investigating the effects of mechanical and mechanochemical activation on their recovery. Mechanical activation under varied milling parameters demonstrated that particle size reduction is predominantly influenced by the milling material and time, with tungsten carbide and extended milling promoting greater particle size reduction and disruption of the native fibrous morphology. Harsher milling conditions intensified amorphization, fragmentation, and morphological defects. Subsequent alkaline-assisted fractionation led to a successful isolation of hemicellulose, lignin, cellulose, and silica. Milling pretreatment using tungsten carbide resulted in a reduced particle size, thereby achieving the highest isolation efficiency. Mechanochemical treatments incorporating sulfuric acid or sodium hydroxide, with occasional methanol addition, was optimized using a Taguchi experimental design. The optimal conditions aiming for the highest lignin extraction were as follows: sulfuric acid 3.6%, methanol volume 12.6 mL, and sample mass 10 g. Statistical analyses identified acid concentration as the primary factor enhancing lignin dissolution under acidic conditions.

papers.title: Effect of composition on structural and optoelectronic properties of combinatorial BaZrS3 thin films
papers.abstract: The chalcogenide perovskite BaZrS 3 is composed of earth-abundant non-toxic elements and represents a chemically stable alternative to lead-halide perovskites for thin-film solar cell applications. While various synthesis routes for BaZrS 3 have been reported in literature, most studies focus on compositions close to the stoichiometric 1:1:3 ratio. In this work, we investigate offstoichiometric Ba-Zr-S-O thin films synthesized from oxide precursors deposited by pulsed laser deposition and subsequently sulfurized in 5% H 2 S in Ar. Thin film libraries with lateral compositional gradients in the ratio [Ba]/([Ba]+[Zr]) ranging from 0.42 to 0.58 were prepared, enabling highthroughput characterization of structural and optoelectronic properties. Using X-ray fluorescence (XRF), X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Raman spectroscopy, we derive a composition-resolved phase diagram. BaZrS 3 is identified as the dominant phase for compositions with BBZ < 0.5, whereas Ba-rich compositions lead to the formation of Ruddlesden-Popper phases Ba 4 Zr 3 S 10 and Ba 3 Zr 2 S 7 . On the Zrrich side, excess Zr results in the formation of ZrO 2 , while small amounts of ZrO 2 are also detected for stoichiometric and Ba-rich compositions. Spatially resolved optical absorption measurements yield band gap energies of approximately 2.0 eV for BBZ < 0.52 whereas a reduced band gap of about 1.8 eV is observed in Ba-rich regions where Ba 4 Zr 3 S 10 contributes substantially according to the phase analysis. Low-temperature photoluminescence spectroscopy reveals deep defect states across all compositions, with decreasing defect-related emission intensity for increasing Ba-content, indicating lower defect concentrations for stoichiometric or Ba-rich films compared to Zr-rich ones. Finally, optical-pump-terahertz probe spectroscopy shows initially higher charge carrier mobilities of up to 4 cm 2 V -1 s -1 for Zr-rich compositions, accompanied by faster trapping into deep defect states, consistent with luminescence results.

papers.title: Chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry with double helical inversion
papers.abstract: Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media and under non-equilibrium conditions remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules (MR) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers (SaS) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double helical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.

papers.title: Bipyridine Crowns for Active Template CuAAC and Crown Ether Amine Functionalisation Rotaxane and Catenane Synthesis
papers.abstract: Active template Cu-mediated alkyne-azide cycloaddition reactions and crown ether-mediated amine functionalisation approaches to rotaxanes and catenanes stand out for their efficiency, simplicity and substrate scope. Here we introduce the bipyridine crown ether macrocycles, readily available rings that efficiently achieve both powerful methodologies. Furthermore, the bipyridine crown platform is readily modified to allow controlled mechanical disassembly of the interlocked products, and the same modifications give rise to diastereostereoselective mechanical bond formation.

papers.title: Surfactant-free room temperature syntheses of stable colloidal silver nanoparticles in alkaline water-alcohols mixtures: pitfalls and opportunities
papers.abstract: Surfactant-free alcohol-mediated syntheses are emerging sustainable approaches to prepare metallic nanomaterials. A parametric study covering more than 270 experiments shows that using ethylene glycol in quantity as low as 5 v.% with only 0.5 mM NaOH rapidly leads at room temperature to silver nanoparticles in the size range 30-100 nm. The synthesis is best initiated in the dark to lead to colloidal dispersions stable for months at room temperature. The results pave the way to sustainable syntheses and studies of Ag nanomaterials relevant for catalysis and beyond.

papers.title: Computational Engineering of a Thermostable Enzyme for the Degradation of PET Through Manipulation of Disulfide Bonds
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution is a significant problem, accounting for approximately 12% of global solid waste [1], and plastic production and waste have more than doubled since 2000. Most plastics do not biodegrade and persist in the environment, slowly breaking down into toxic microplastics that harm ecosystems and create lasting adverse impacts. One of the most widely used plastics is polyethylene terephthalate (PET), accounting for 18% of global plastic production [2]. Currently, the most sustainable recycling method is biocatalysis, in which enzyme-catalyzed degradation of the polymer backbone generates low-molecular-weight fragments, enabling mild depolymerization. However, less than 1% of global plastic waste processing facilities use this process due to the limited thermostability of PETase enzymes, which limits the approach's general applicability and hinders its broad adoption [3]. One strategy by which nature enhances the thermal stability of enzymes is by the incorporation of disulfide bonds, a defining feature of thermophilic bacteria that thrive at elevated temperatures [4]. This study investigated whether increasing disulfide bond density could improve the thermostability of FAST-PETase by testing the hypothesis that additional disulfide bonds increase PETase thermostability. The FAST-PETase structure was mutated in PyMOL to introduce additional disulfide bonds, and the resulting mutants' thermal stability was evaluated. Engineered variants demonstrated enhanced thermal robustness compared to existing PETase benchmarks, indicating that rational disulfide bond engineering can stabilize PETase enzymes. These computational results demonstrate a novel enzyme-design approach that addresses a key bottleneck in biocatalytic plastic recycling and sets the stage for advancing enzymatic PET degradation toward global commercial viability.

papers.title: Stochastic Evaluation of Exciton–Exciton Annihilation Rate in 2D Molecular Aggregate
papers.abstract: Exciton-exciton annihilation (EEA) is a process by which two excitons combine to form a single high energy excitation. In molecular chromophore aggregates EEA is governed by microscopic two-exciton coherence that depends on long-range coupling and supramolecular geometry, motivating scalable quantum mechanical rate calculations beyond deterministic small-system diagonalization. Here, we develop a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-accelerated stochastic method for computing finite temperature EEA rates in large 2D excitonic molecular aggregates. We demonstrated agreement with conventional deterministic matrix diagonalization for small and intermediate systems, while achieving an improved scaling of O(N 2 logN) from O(N 6 ) cost. This approach enables large-scale parameter sweeps and structure–function screening in realistic 2D morphologies. We close by exploring the role of uncorrelated and correlated disorder, temperature and inter-exciton coupling in EEA.

papers.title: Decoupling electronic transport and mechanical compliance in conducting polymers through self-doping
papers.abstract: Achieving high electrical conductivity in polymeric materials typically requires dense, ordered π-conjugated networks, whereas mechanical compliance demands structural softness and disorder, resulting in a long-standing trade-off that limits the development of intrinsically stretchable conductors. Here, we show that self-doped conducting polymers resolve this conflict, preserving volumetric electronic density and mechanical deformability within a single-component system. Self-doped p-type and n-type conjugated polymers combine high conductivity (up to 1,904 S cm−1) with large stretchability (up to 210%) without insulating additives or post-treatment. In situ photoelectron spectroscopies and structural characterization under strain reveal that molecular interactions govern the evolution of electronic states and charge transport during deformation. Eliminating inactive components maximizes electroactive volume, yielding enhanced volumetric capacitance and device performance in fully stretchable electrochromic displays with improved contrast and stability. These results define a general strategy for designing soft electronic materials in which charge transport and mechanical compliance are no longer intrinsically antagonistic.

papers.title: Lipids and Lipid Nanoparticles Functionalized with Randomized Poly(Ethylene Glycol) (rPEG) for mRNA Delivery
papers.abstract: 2 Abstract PEG lipids are essential excipients in lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations and enable the transport of therapeutic ribonucleic acids, creating stealth properties for these nanocarriers. However, an increasing number of studies raise concerns related to the growing presence of anti-PEG antibodies (APA) in the population. The presence of APAs results in the recognition and accelerated blood clearance of PEGylated therapeutics, thus diminishing the desired stealth effect of PEGylation. In this study, we present the isomerization of PEG to randomized PEG (rPEG) as an efficient approach for inhibiting APA interaction while preserving the advantages of PEG. rPEGs were obtained via living anionic ring-opening (co)polymerization (AROP) of ethylene oxide (EO) with glycidyl methyl ether (GME). This yields rPEGs with narrow molar mass distributions (Mw/Mn = 1.04 – 1.07) for all EO:GME compositions synthesized. Chainend functionalization of rPEGs with lipid anchor groups was conducted to obtain rPEG lipids with C14-chains. APA interaction was investigated via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and X-ray reflectometry (XRR) at rPEG-DMG containing lipid monolayers, allowing for a general understanding of the relation between the chain architecture and APA interaction. LNPs containing rPEG lipids were formulated and compared to established PEG-based LNPs, showing similar particle sizes, encapsulation and transfection efficiencies, and cell viabilities in vitro for a variety of cell lines. It is demonstrated that rPEG lipids prevent APA binding but nevertheless exhibit similar performance in LNPs as comparable PEG lipids.

papers.title: Discovering Protein Excited-state Structures by Chemical-shift-guided Conformational Sampling with Generative Protein Structure Model
papers.abstract: Protein excited-state conformations are often low-populated and transient, yet can play critical roles in ligand binding, allostery, and catalysis. While NMR relaxation-dispersion and CEST experiments can provide chemical shifts for these otherwise invisible states, existing structure-determination strategies typically incorporate such data directly into restrained reconstruction workflows. Here we introduce CS-SelectFold, a training-free framework for discovering protein excited-state structures by chemical-shift-guided conformational sampling with SimpleFold. CS-SelectFold first generates a diverse ensemble of candidate conformations with SimpleFold, then predicts chemical shifts for each structure using UCBShift 2.0, and finally ranks conformations by agreement with experimentally determined excited-state chemical shifts. Using the L99A mutant of T4 lysozyme as a canonical benchmark, CS-SelectFold recovered excited-state-like conformations that reproduced the defining cavity-centered rearrangement of the known hidden state, including inward placement of Phe114 into the engineered cavity. Hotspot-region dRMSD analysis further showed that chemical-shift-guided post hoc selection enriched structures that escaped the dominant ground-state basin and converged toward the experimentally established excited-state structural basin. These results establish CS-SelectFold as a conceptually distinct sample-and-select strategy for excited-state structure discovery and suggest that experimentally determined chemical shifts can serve as an effective post hoc signal for identifying rare, functionally relevant conformations within generative protein structure ensembles.

papers.title: Improving QSAR model predictions using ensembled heterogenous features
papers.abstract: Quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models are widely used computational tools in drug discovery for predicting molecular activities and prioritizing compounds for experimental testing.
