papers.abstract: The ratio of Kekule structure count (*K*) to graph automorphism group order (|Aut(*G*)|), a classical graph-theoretic quantity arising from Cyvin's analysis of benzenoid symmetry, has not, to our knowledge, been tested as a quantitative predictor of carcinogenic potency. Here *K*/|Aut(*G*)| correlated with regulatory potency equivalency factors (PEFs) across 27 polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) with Spearman rho = +0.745 (95% CI +0.546 to +0.855; *p* = 8.38 x 10^-6), and remained predictive under leave-one-out cross-validation (rho = +0.708, *p* = 3.56 x 10^-5; RMSE = 1.25 log10 units). By contrast, the Kekule count *K* alone yielded a weaker correlation (Spearman rho = +0.420, raw *p* = 0.029) that did not pass the 17-predictor Bonferroni correction (adjusted *p* = 0.495; Benjamini-Hochberg q = 0.031). In binary classification at PEF >= 0.1, *K*/|Aut(*G*)| achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) = 0.95; the threshold *K*/|Aut(*G*)| >= 5.0 yielded 11 true positives, 12 true negatives, 2 false negatives, and 2 false positives. The two false negatives were 5-methylchrysene and benzo[*k*]fluoranthene; the two false positives were benzo[*ghi*]perylene and benzo[*e*]pyrene, the latter sitting at the classification boundary (*K*/|Aut| = 5.5) and lacking a bay region, illustrating how the descriptor and geometric criterion work in tandem. The largest regression error was DMBA, consistent with steric effects from methyl substitution not encoded in the pi-system graph. These results formalize and quantify the classical intuitions of Pullman (bond localization), Clar (sextet locking), and Cyvin (symmetry partitioning of Kekule structures) within a single transparent descriptor that connects molecular graph symmetry to CYP1-mediated metabolic activation. The result was robust to dataset composition: restricting the analysis to the 14 EPA Priority PAHs with Nisbet-LaGoy potency values yielded rho = +0.759 (*p* = 0.0016, AUC = 0.95), confirming that the correlation is not an artifact of the extended dataset. Coronene, which has the highest *K* in the dataset (*K* = 20) yet negligible potency, illustrates why *K* alone fails: D6h symmetry (|Aut| = 12) drives bond-order equalization, reducing *K*/|Aut(*G*)| to 1.67.

papers.title: Ultrafast Charge, Spin, and Lattice Coupling Facilitates Spin Transport as Magnon-Polarons in Yttrium Iron Garnet
papers.abstract: Low spin damping and long spin-polarization lifetimes are essential for spintronic and spinbased energy-conversion technologies, yet their microscopic origin in magnetic insulators remains poorly understood. Yttrium iron garnet (YIG), a prototypical magnetic insulator exhibiting exceptionally low damping and long magnon lifetimes, provides an ideal platform to investigate how charge, spin, and lattice interactions stabilize spin-polarized carriers. Here we directly probe these coupled dynamics using ultrafast linearly and circularly polarized extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) spectroscopy, which provides femtosecond time resolution together with element-and site-specific sensitivity to electronic structure and spin polarization. Our measurements reveal the ultrafast formation of magnon–polaron quasiparticles mediated by strong charge–spin–lattice coupling. XUV magnetic circular dichroism (XUV-MCD) directly resolves a transient spin reversal at the Fe tetrahedral (Td) site on the sub-picosecond timescale, relaxing Pauli exclusion, and enabling electron delocalization and efficient spin-polarized transport. Coherent charge–lattice dynamics and phonon coherence transfer further indicate the formation of delocalized quasiparticles extending over several to tens of unit cells. These results establish a direct microscopic link between magnon–polaron formation, the long-lived spin polarization and efficient spin transport in YIG, providing a framework for understanding how coupled spin–charge–lattice excitations govern spin transport in magnetic insulators.

papers.title: Mechanism-Based Drug-Excipient
papers.abstract: Drug-excipient incompatibility remains a leading cause of pharmaceutical formulation failure, yet computational prediction tools are limited to lookup tables of documented interactions that fail on novel drugs. I present a mechanism-based approach that detects reactive functional groups directly from SMILES strings (13 patterns via SMARTS matching), classifies excipients by reactive properties (4 classes: reducing sugars, peroxide-containing, alkaline, metal-containing), and predicts degradation mechanisms (11 pathways including three Maillard reaction variants, ester hydrolysis, and thiol oxidation). Applied to 100 drugs not in the system's knowledge base, the method generated 92 predictions; of 38 validated against published literature, 37 were supported and 0 were disconfirmed. An adversarial test set of 17 deliberately challenging cases (prodrugs, sterically shielded groups, electronically deactivated amides, soft electrophiles) produced 17/17 correct classifications. The approach is implemented in OpenMix, an open-source Python framework (pip install openmix) that evaluates formulations from multiple computational perspectives and classifies where they agree or disagree.

papers.title: Upcycling greenhouse refrigerants into sustainable chemical feedstocks
papers.abstract: Rising global temperatures are driving a surge in air conditioning demand worldwide. However, the leakage of conventional refrigerants with high global-warming potential (GWP) into the atmosphere accelerates warming, creating a problematic feedback loop. While converting these hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) into low-GWP alternatives via dehydrofluorination is a promising solution, catalysts are typically deactivated by by-product hydrogen fluoride (HF) , which also degrades target products. Here we show a continuous-flow process that overcomes these barriers by using alkali metal fluoride catalysts and silica as a sacrificial reagent to irreversibly capture HF. This system enables the direct upcycling of legacy refrigerants—such as HFC-134a and HFC-125— into sustainable chemical feedstocks, including low-GWP hydrofluoroolefins (HFOs) and key monomers for fluoropolymers. Furthermore, we demonstrate that waste glass from end-of-life solar panels can serve as the silica source, where the silica component is selectively recovered as silicon tetrafluoride (SiF 4 ). As SiF 4 can be readily converted back into silica and HF, our approach establishes a closed-loop recycling system for both fluorine and silicon. This integration of waste destruction with resource synthesis significantly mitigates the environmental impact of the cooling industry, providing a robust foundation for a circular refrigerant economy.

papers.title: Impact of α-Substitution on the Photodissociation Dynamics of Nitromethane: The CH3 and NO Release Channels
papers.abstract: Photolysis of 1-nitropropane, 2-methyl-2-nitropropane, and (nitromethyl)benzene at 213 and 225 nm reveals distinct mechanistic features in CH 3 and NO elimination channels. The CH 3 fragments exhibit anisotropic, non-statistical translational energy distributions, consistent with barrier-impulsive dissociation on the T 1 surface occurring on picosecond timescales with restrictive intramolecular vibrational redistribution (IVR). In contrast, NO fragments display bimodal translational energy distributions with large slow/fast branching ratios, indicating preferential dissociation on the S 0 surface following efficient IVR. Two-dimensional potential energy surface calculations along C–N and C–O coordinates show that NO 2 roaming constitutes the minimum energy pathway on the T1 surface, while semi-tight transition states dominate on the S 0 surface. Despite structural variation, α-substitution does not significantly alter the fundamental NO release mechanism; however, variations in triplet yield modulate the contribution of the fast component. Interestingly, the CH 3 and NO release follow contrasting behaviour in terms of IVR dynamics.

papers.title: Switching of the Door Way State from Triplet to Singlet Ground State for CO Release in Acetone
papers.abstract: The translational energy distribution of CO fragments following 266 nm excitation of several ketones are largely insensitive to alkyl substitution and consistent with dissociation occurring on the triplet surface. On the other hand, 230 nm excitation of acetone results in narrower translational energy distribution profile of CO, suggesting the emergence of an additional CO formation pathway at higher excitation energy, which is attributed to dynamics on the S 0 state. The most intriguing features of acetone UV photolysis is the transition in the CO release pathway—from a two-photon–driven T1 mechanism at lower energies to a one-photon–driven S 0 mechanism at higher energies.

papers.title: Photodissociation Dynamics of Hexafluoroacetylacetone at 266 nm
papers.abstract: Photodissociation dynamics of hexafluoroacetylacetone (HFAA) following 266 nm photolysis was investigated using velocity map imaging in combination with electronic structure calculations. The mass spectrum shows signals corresponding to CF 3 , CF, CO, and HCCO fragments, revealing the presence of multiple competing fragmentation pathways. The primary photochemical step involves terminal C–C bond cleavage, yielding CF 3 and CF 3 C(OH)CHCO radicals, and subsequent absorption of additional photons by these primary fragments lead to further dissociation. Analysis of translational energy distribution profiles demonstrates that CO and HCCO are mainly produced through single-photon absorption by CF 3 C(OH)CHCO, whereas CF formation requires multiple photon absorption by the CF 3 radical. Two-dimensional potential energy surface calculations support a concerted dissociation mechanism for CF 3 that forms CF and F 2 via absorption of two-photons of 266 nm.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because the content was an unintentional duplication of another ChemRxiv preprint (10.26434/chemrxiv.15002047/v1).

papers.title: An energy-corrected fast post-SCF local-hybrid scheme for highly accurate energy differences of large main-group systems
papers.abstract: Local-hybrid (LH) density functionals admix exact exchange locally in real space and thereby can be powerful tools to ameliorate the usual zero-sum game between reducing self-interaction errors and modeling static correlation. But the practical use of LHs for large systems is limited by the cost of evaluating exact-exchange quantities self-consistently. Here we introduce an energy-corrected local-hybrid framework, EC(LH)@GGA, in which a computationally expedient semi-local reference density is used for a single post-SCF evaluation with an advanced LH. Using the recent neural-network-based LH25nP LH as a prototype, we show that the EC route preserves the characteristic accuracy profile of the parent local hybrid and reaches state-of-the-art rung 4 performance on the GMTKN55 test suite (WTMAD-2 around 2.4–2.7 kcal/mol, depending on grid). The top performance of LH25nP for spin-restricted bond dissociation as a strong-correlation measure is retained in this framework. The dominant post-SCF overhead in timing is governed by the EC grid. For practical gridsizes 2–3, the total EC(LH)@GGA cost is only about ∼1.5–3× that of a GGA single point, less by a factor of 6-12 than a full LH SCF. Overall, EC(LH)@GGA provides a simple post-SCF route to state-of-the-art rung-4 energetics at a cost close to semi-local DFT, applicable to large systems as demonstrated for a protein.

papers.title: Biosynthesis and characterization of Copper Nanoparticles using Enicostemma littorale leaf extract
papers.abstract: In this study the copper nanoparticles (CuNPs) were synthesize using the leaf extract of plant Enicostemma Littorale, as green reducing agent. The parameters were optimized to maximize yield, regulate size and stability of the CuNPs. The characterization was done using X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) pattern, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), and dynamic light scattering (DLS). The majority of the CuNPs formed were in the size range of 20–30 nm. The XRD pattern showed distinctive peaks and confirmed the nanocrystalline nature of the synthesized CuNPs. SEM analysis revealed the agglomerated state of NPs. TEM analysis showed that the average size of synthesized CuNPs is around 25 nm.

papers.title: Characterization of Disulfide Bonds in Cyclic Peptides using Electron Transfer – Ultraviolet Photodissociation Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: Analysis of peptides with multiple disulfide bonds can be challenging because of the complexity of deciphering fragment ions originating from dual backbone and disulfide bond cleavages required to release fragment ions from the regions spanned by disulfide bonds. Two ion activation methods, electron transfer dissociation (ETD) and ultraviolet photodissociation (UVPD) have demonstrated the ability to cleave disulfide motifs, either via C-S or S-S bond cleavages, resulting in diagnostic fragment ions that can help localize disulfide bonds. Here these MS/MS methods are examined in comparison to a hybrid method, ET-UVPD, for characterization of peptides containing multiple disulfide bonds. Fragment ions arising from S-S and C-S bond cleavages, both with and without hydrogen atom transfer, and dual S-S and C-S cleavages, were searched based on a list of possible products generated from alternative cleavage pathways. Identification of these low abundance fragment ions can facilitate characterization of peptides constrained by multiple disulfide bonds.

papers.title: Design and Characterization of a Ligstroside-Derived Photoaffinity Probe
papers.abstract: Ligstroside (LIG) is a phenolic secoiridoid glycoside naturally occurring in olives and structurally related to the widely studied olive constituent oleuropein. Although LIG has been reported to exhibit diverse biological activities, it has received comparatively limited attention, and the molecular targets underlying its bioactivity remain largely unknown, thereby limiting exploration of its pharmacological potential. To facilitate target identification and mechanistic investigation, we designed and synthesized a LIG-derived photoaffinity probe (PAL-LIG) through minimal modification of the LIG scaffold. The probe incorporates a photoactivatable diazirine group that enables UVinduced covalent crosslinking with proximal proteins together with an alkyne handle that allows subsequent bioorthogonal conjugation via copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC). Following photo-crosslinking, probe-labeled proteins can be conjugated with azide-functionalized reporter tags, including biotin for streptavidinbased enrichment and pulldown or TAMRA for fluorescence detection and cellular imaging. Using this strategy, PAL-LIG enables enrichment of potential LIG-binding proteins as well as fluorescence-based visualization of probe labeling in cells. Importantly, PAL-LIG retains biological activity comparable to LIG, as demonstrated by its similar ability to promote ATP production in mouse C2C12 myoblasts, indicating that installation of the photoaffinity and alkyne handles minimally perturbs the intrinsic bioactivity of LIG. Collectively, PAL-LIG provides a chemical tool for investigating the direct protein targets and molecular mechanisms of LIG.

papers.title: Dual-Function Small-Molecules Capable of Controlling Ice Nucleation and Ice Recrystallization
papers.abstract: Uncontrolled ice formation and subsequent growth causes irreversible damage to cells during cryopreservation. Ice recrystallization inhibitors (IRIs) reduce ice crystal growth after nucleation and have proven beneficial for cryopreservation. Controlling ice nucleation can also minimize iceinduced injury and improve the reproducibility of freezing protocols. However, synergy between compounds that influence these processes remains largely unexplored. Herein, we evaluate seven biocompatible carbohydrate-based small-molecules and report that select compounds – 4bromophenyl-β-D-glucose (β-pBrPh-Glc, 1), 4-methoxyphenyl-β-D-glucose (β-PMP-Glc, 2), N-2fluorophenyl-D-gluconamide (2FA, 5), and N-4-chlorophenyl-D-gluconamide (4ClA, 6) – exhibit dual ice-modulating activity, defined as the ability to inhibit ice recrystallization and induce synchronous nucleation, representing a novel mode of ice nucleation control not previously reported. Our results confirm that nucleation control is dependent on carbohydrate structure, where glucose-based molecules are sensitive to AgI-mediated nucleation, producing small ice crystals, whereas galactose-based analogs are insensitive to AgI-mediated nucleation. Overall, our findings reveal that the synergy of ice nucleation and ice recrystallization inhibition is structure- and solvent-dependent.

papers.title: Realizing Near-Infrared Functional Conjugated Polymer Core-Shell Fibers via Electrospinning
papers.abstract: Donor-acceptor (DA) conjugated polymers are increasingly important in flexible electronics due to their intrinsic donor-acceptor interactions, which reduce band gaps and enhance charge mobility in undoped states. The processing of DA polymer into fibers and the corresponding structure-property relationship are not well understood. Here, we report the successful realization of core-shell DA polymer fibers via coaxial electrospinning, enabling modulation of optical response through improved microstructural order. The core-shell fiber comprises a flexible polymer core and a DPP-DTT polymer shell. Mechanical stretching was applied by varying the rotational speed of the fiber collector and post-processing the fibers, significantly influencing the DPP-DTT polymer morphology. The UV-Vis spectra captured a pronounced red shift in fibers, up to 140 nm relative to the thin film, indicating enhanced polymer chain ordering induced by mechanical stretching during fiber collection. Molecular dynamics simulations support the experimental findings, as the applied shear field aligns polymer chains in the shear direction, thereby improving microstructural order and increasing the degree of π-π stacking. The GIWAXS analysis reveals that at a higher collector rotational speed, the fibers exhibit a preferential orientation of DPP-DTT along the fiber radial direction. The approach employed here can be extended to large-scale fiber processing for optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Lipids and Lipid Nanoparticles Functionalized with Randomized Poly(Ethylene Glycol) (rPEG) for
papers.abstract: 2 Abstract PEG lipids are essential excipients in lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations and enable the transport of therapeutic ribonucleic acids, creating stealth properties for these nanocarriers. However, an increasing number of studies raise concerns related to the growing presence of anti-PEG antibodies (APA) in the population. The presence of APAs results in the recognition and accelerated blood clearance of PEGylated therapeutics, thus diminishing the desired stealth effect of PEGylation. In this study, we present the isomerization of PEG to randomized PEG (rPEG) as an efficient approach for inhibiting APA interaction while preserving the advantages of PEG. rPEGs were obtained via living anionic ring-opening (co)polymerization (AROP) of ethylene oxide (EO) with glycidyl methyl ether (GME). This yields rPEGs with narrow molar mass distributions (Mw/Mn = 1.04 – 1.07) for all EO:GME compositions synthesized. Chainend functionalization of rPEGs with lipid anchor groups was conducted to obtain rPEG lipids with C14-chains. APA interaction was investigated via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and X-ray reflectometry (XRR) at rPEG-DMG containing lipid monolayers, allowing for a general understanding of the relation between the chain architecture and APA interaction. LNPs containing rPEG lipids were formulated and compared to established PEG-based LNPs, showing similar particle sizes, encapsulation and transfection efficiencies, and cell viabilities in vitro for a variety of cell lines. It is demonstrated that rPEG lipids prevent APA binding but nevertheless exhibit similar performance in LNPs as comparable PEG lipids.

papers.title: A State-Averaged Formulation for Variational Multiconfigurational Pair-Density Functional Theory
papers.abstract: The accurate and efficient prediction of excited states in systems exhibiting both static and dynamic correlation remains a significant challenge in computational chemistry. To handle such challenges, we present a new state-averaged formulation for variational multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory. We assess the performance of this method on excitation energies for a diverse set of open-shell single radicals and closed-shell organic molecules. We compare the translated pure, global hybrid and rangeseparated PDFT functionals to regular spin-TD-DFT and high-level wavefunction methods. For small open-shell radicals, which are characterized by strong correlation, we find that MC–PDFT with pure and–more significantly–global hybrid GGA translated-functionals remarkably improve results of standard Kohn-Sham DFT (B3LYP, CAM-B3LYP) and EOM-CCSD. When range-separation is included, mean absolute errors against MRCISD+Q are as low as 0.06 eV. Regarding closed-shell medium size organic molecules, our analysis reveals a critical dependency on the electronic nature of the transition. While translated pure GGAs struggle with π → π∗ transitions—often severely underestimating energiesthe introduction of range-separation effectively corrects even large deviations. The range-separated srctBLYP functional provides a balanced description of both n → π∗ and π → π∗ states, and is shown to be competitive with high-level wavefunction methods such as CC3 and NEVPT4, offering a robust and computationally efficient strategy for modeling complex chemical systems.

papers.title: A general strategy for site-oriented protein anchoring on metal–organic frameworks: HER2-targeted delivery using an engineered antibody fragment
papers.abstract: Cancer therapies remain limited by poor selectivity and off-target toxicity, making biodistribution as critical as the drugs themselves. Antibodies have transformed cancer treatment by enabling the selective delivery of highly potent pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) to diseased tissues, thereby increasing efficacy while reducing systemic side effects. This targeted approach has revived the clinical use of cytotoxic agents, which were previously considered too toxic without precise biodistribution. Building on this principle, antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) combine these powerful drugs with antibodies to expand the therapeutic window and achieve controlled delivery to specific tumor sites. However, the low drug-to-antibody ratio and hydrophobic payloads often compromise ADC stability and limit the dosing. Nanoparticles offer an alternative route to achieve high-capacity drug delivery with controlled release, but few platforms combine efficient targeting with stable, site-specific conjugation. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are distinguished by their high porosity, modular chemistry, and high drug-loading capacity. However, their translation has been hindered by the challenge of conjugating proteins to their external surfaces in a stable and oriented manner. Herein, we report the first fragment antibody (Fab)- conjugated MOF nanoparticles, using a phosphate anchoring group on the zirconium-based MOF PCN-128. This site-specific conjugation ensures optimal Fab orientation for selective binding to HER2 receptors and efficient cellular internalization of the drug. We confirmed stable conjugation, specific HER2 recognition, and enhanced cytotoxicity when loaded with the potent payload MMAF. Together, these results establish Fab-functionalized MOFs as a versatile, high-capacity drug delivery platform and open a new path for next-generation targeted cancer therapy.

papers.title: Altered DNA Dynamics and Stability due to Protein Mutation in Cren7-DNA Complex driven by Non-covalent Interactions
papers.abstract: Non-covalent interaction plays key role in molecular recognition in biomolecular complex and thereby to control biomolecular functions. In this work, molecular dynamics simulations were employed to investigate the conformational dynamics and stability of DNA in the Cren7–DNA complex and to understand how protein mutation can alter DNA stability through non-covalent interactions. Both the wild-type (WT) protein and four aromatic mutants (W26A, F41A, F50A, and Y58A) were examined to assess the effect of protein mutation on DNA structural stability. Cren7 binding induced bending of DNA in both WT and mutant complexes, although the extent of bending varied. The mutants exhibited enhanced bending compared to WT, with the following trend: F41A > Y58A > W26A > F50A > WT. The radius of gyration (Rg) of DNA shows higher fluctuations in Rg for mutants in compared to WT, reflecting reduced compactness and stability of the DNA duplex upon mutation. Principal component analysis (PCA) further highlighted differences in collective DNA motions between WT and mutants, with mutants sampling a broader conformational space, consistent with enhanced flexibility and instability. In parallel, hydrogen bonding between base pairs was perturbed during the simulations, consistent with conformational rearrangements of the DNA helix. Alteration in base stacking interactions further highlighted changes in DNA stability. Analysis of intra-base pair and base-pair step parameters revealed notable deviations in the mutants relative to WT. These changes were accompanied by modifications in backbone dihedral angles as well as in groove width and depth, reflecting global perturbations in DNA architecture. The results provide qualitative and quantitative insights into structural and conformational control of DNA via protein mutation, which is solely governed by non-covalent interactions. This study also provides a comprehensive protocol for investigating the stability and conformational dynamics of protein-DNA complexes at a microscopic level.

papers.title: Selenoxanthylium Salts – Red-Light Absorbing Organic Photocatalysts
papers.abstract: Selenoxanthylium salts operate as red-light-absorbing organic photocatalysts under excitation at 650 nm. Incorporation of selenium into a xanthylium core shifts absorption toward the red region relative to lighter chalcogens (O and S). Photophysical studies define the excited-state topology, distinguishing locally excited and charge-transfer states. Under red-light irradiation, the photocatalysts engage in reductive quenching and operate on up to 5.0 mmol scale. Catalytic activity is demonstrated across multiple transformations, including [4+2] and [2+2] cycloadditions, C–H aminations, boronic acid oxidations, aza-Henry reactions, and trifluoromethylations.

papers.title: LiPHEX: A QSPR Framework for Predicting n-Hexadecane/Water logP Values
papers.abstract: The n-hexadecane/water partition, usually expressed as logP C16/w , describes a more apolar lipophilicity regime than the octanol/water system, which remains the most widely used reference. However, the availability of C16/w partition data in the literature is scarce and heterogeneous, which hinders the development of robust predictive models. In this work, we developed a QSPR model to predict logP C16/w from a curated set of 404 compounds and an independent external set of 16 compounds that we used for validation. From RDKit 2D descriptors and ECFP4 fingerprints, and after a filtering and feature engineering process, we evaluated several models, among which CatBoost reached R 2 = 0.87 and RMSE = 0.67 in the internal hold-out set, and R 2 = 0.94 and RMSE = 0.51 in the external set. The robustness of the model was evaluated through tests such as 5-fold cross-validation, bootstrapping, y-randomization, and an additional scaffold-aware evaluation based on Bemis-Murcko scaffolds. To interpret the patterns captured by the model, we included a TreeSHAP analysis, which showed a physicochemical pattern consistent with the system: signals associated with size, weighted topology, and nonpolar volume favored higher logP C16/w values, whereas variables related to polar surface and partial charge contributed negatively. Finally, we defined an applicability domain based on kNN distances and contextualized the chemical space coverage through PCA and UMAP. Overall, this study provides a predictive and interpretable model for the pre-screening in highly apolar hydrocarbon environments.

papers.title: Advancing Blue-light photoactivatable TAM Kinase Inhibitors for cancer treatment: Challenges in Using π‑Extended Coumarins as Photocleavable Protecting Groups
papers.abstract: This work presents the development of photocleavable tyrosine kinase inhibitors as a potential targeted cancer therapy. Focusing on the TAM family—Tyro3, Axl, and MERTK—overexpressed in several cancers (bladder, lung, and pancreas), we report the use of π-extended coumarins as photoremovable protecting groups to generate visible-light responsive photocleavable derivatives of the clinically relevant inhibitor UNC2025. This study highlights how the electronwithdrawing and donating groups in the π-extended coumarins affect both the photophysical properties of the photocaged UNC2025 and its biological activity in enzymatic and cellular assays, in terms of loss of inhibitory activity in absence of irradiation and recovery of UNC2025 activity following irradiation in the blue range. The most promising candidate was the N,O-dicaged compound bearing a π-extended coumarin with an electron-donating group.

papers.title: A Master Key for Accessible Solid Electrolyte Design
papers.abstract: The solid electrolyte design currently relies on heuristic approaches, lacking a unified framework to correlate atomistic lattice features with the accessible bulk ion transport properties. Nor could the rich literature be interpreted consistently to provide a definitive perspective on new solidelectrolyte engineering by design, with refined composition and lattice information. To address these needs and challenges, here we found a master key (Fig. S1), opening a door for accessible solid electrolyte design by encoding the composition-structure-property relationship validated by Li 10 GeP 2 S 12 (LGPS) and Li 4 GeS 4 (thio-LISICON) solid electrolytes with a new concept called “intrinsic lattice formation strain” (ILFS) (Fig. 1), which originates from the chemical bond formation and lattice relaxation from perfect symmetry of the unit cell. The master key uses Gibbs free energy terms expressed in ILFS to describe the ion transport properties of solid electrolytes that follow the Arrhenius law, correlating the experimental composition-structure-property trends across the open-literature sulfide solid electrolyte database with R 2 > 0.90 for LGPS and > 0.86 for thio-LISICON, respectively. The master key thus offers an intelligent pathway to guide new solid electrolyte design and discovery.

papers.title: Adaptive Photocatalytic Regimes Enabled by CO2 •− and ConPET Synergy: Cyclization-Carboxylation of Aryl Halides with CO2
papers.abstract: Selective activation of aryl halides across a broad reactivity spectrum remains a central challenge in photoredox catalysis, particularly due to the kinetic barriers associated with C−Cl bond reduction. Herein, we report a unified photocatalytic platform that enables substrate-dependent access to distinct reductive regimes through the synergistic integration of formate-derived CO2 •− and consecutive photoinduced electron transfer (ConPET). Under the developed conditions, aryl bromides and chlorides, despite exhibiting similarly demanding reduction potentials, display markedly different reactivity − governed by kinetic factors specific to the substrate and catalytic system. CO2 •− mediates rapid and thermodynamically matched reduction of aryl bromides, whereas more recalcitrant aryl chlorides are activated via a super-reducing excited photocatalyst radical anion generated through ConPET. Notably, formate serves a dual role as both the precursor to CO2 •− and the electron donor enabling ConPET, obviating the need for conventional super-stoichiometric sacrificial amines. This adaptive system enables efficient cyclization-carboxylation of (2-halophenoxy)allenes with CO2 under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies, including kinetic analysis, competition experiments, isotopic labelling, spectroscopic study, and DFT calculations, support a dual-regime mechanism governed by substrate-dependent activation barriers. This work establishes a framework for kinetically gated control of reductive strength in photoredox catalysis by harnessing CO2 •− as a reductant.

papers.title: Using 3D-printing to evaluate printed electrodes working in real-world settings
papers.abstract: Flexible electrochemical sensors have gained increasing attention due to their applicability in real-world analytical scenarios involving complex and non-planar surfaces. The influence of mechanical deformation on sensor performance has been previously reported; however, these effects are often evaluated under non-standardized conditions or after mechanical stress is applied, limiting a systematic and comparative understanding of sensor behavior under realistic operating conditions. In this context, 3D printing offers a versatile and accessible approach for fabricating customized platforms capable of applying controlled and reproducible mechanical deformation during electrochemical measurements. Herein, we present a strategy to evaluate the effect of mechanical stress on screen-printed electrochemical sensors (SPEs) fabricated on polyester, office paper, and Ecovio® biopolymeric substrates. While all sensors exhibited similar electrochemical behavior under flat conditions, significant differences emerged under bending, with substrate-dependent reductions in current and variations in signal stability. These effects were more pronounced for paper-based electrodes, whereas Ecovio-based devices showed greater robustness to deformation. The findings highlight the critical role of substrate mechanical properties in determining sensor performance under realistic operating conditions. The results show that controlled deformation reveals substrate-dependent performance differences not observable under flat conditions, enabling more consistent material evaluation. This versatile 3D-printed approach can be extended beyond electrochemical sensors, enabling reproducible testing and guided selection of flexible devices for optical and colorimetric applications.

papers.title: Stable Phenanthrene-Fused 1,2,4-Triazinyl Radicals with Ultra-narrow Electrochemical Gap Enabled by Attenuated Fusion-Ring Aromaticity
papers.abstract: The design of organic materials with narrow electrochemical gaps (Egap) is critical for modern electronics, yet achieving such narrow gaps while retaining robust stability and facile processability remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report a new strategy based on targeted attenuation of aromaticity in π-extended Blatter-type radicals that enables notable gap reduction to 0.75 eV—the lowest reported for this class. We prepare the robust Blatter radical derivatives 1 and 1-tBu, in which its triazinyl moiety is fused with the central ring of phenanthrene, creating an annulated ring system with reduced aromaticity, compared to classical Blatter radicals. Our studies indicate that reducing fusion-ring aromaticity lowers substantially the gas-phase ionization potential while moderating neutral-state solvation enhancement that typically accompanies π-extension, thereby preserving larger differential solvation stabilization and consequently a substantial Egap reduction. Experimental Egap is observed to exhibit high correlation with the DFT-computed total spin density on the triazinyl-fused ring for the studied Blatter derivatives. In addition, sublimable 1 forms well-ordered thin films of intact radicals on Au(111) surface, highlighting its practical processability. This work establishes aromaticity modulation as an effective strategy for stable, narrow-gap materials, based upon neutral radicals.

papers.title: Multi-task scheduling of self-driving laboratories under scientific constraints
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) integrate robotics, automation, and artificial intelligence to autonomously execute scientific experiments. As SDLs evolve toward multi-task parallel execution and support for heterogeneous experiments, experimental scheduling becomes a critical decision-making layer, determining the temporal order and execution timing of robot-performed operations under strict scientific constraints, including operation precedence, station allocation, batch processing, experimental parameters, and critically, time synchronization between consecutive operations. For example, in inorganic synthesis, temporal deviations during nucleation can fundamentally alter the material properties. While SDLs offer a promising route toward accelerated discovery, the absence of explicit scheduling for concurrent experiments leads to resource conflicts and uncontrolled interruptions. These deviations undermine the reproducibility and data quality essential for artificial intelligence modeling. Here, we present a multi-task scheduling algorithm that jointly accounts for scientific constraints. We integrated this algorithm into an SDL using a closed-loop communication architecture that enables tight coordination between scheduling and robotic experiment execution. The algorithm was validated through the concurrent multi-task synthesis of gold nanoparticles and metal-organic frameworks, distinct chemical reactions governed by nucleation and growth kinetics. By synchronizing robotic operations with experimental stations as well as chemical workflow, the algorithm preserves chemical fidelity and ensures consistent material quality across concurrent multi-task executions, unattainable with conventional scheduling algorithm that do not adequately account for scientific constraints. This paradigm establishes a practical scheduling framework for concurrent multitasking in SDLs, ensuring the experimental consistency required to generate the high-fidelity datasets foundational to autonomous, AI-driven scientific discovery.

papers.title: Discovering Protein Excited-state Structures by Chemical-shift-guided Conformational Sampling with Generative Protein Structure Modeling
papers.abstract: Protein excited-state conformations are often low-populated and transient, yet can play critical roles in ligand binding, allostery, and catalysis. While NMR relaxation-dispersion and CEST experiments can provide chemical shifts for these otherwise invisible states, existing structure-determination strategies typically incorporate such data directly into restrained reconstruction workflows. Here we introduce CS-SelectFold, a training-free framework for discovering protein excited-state structures by chemical-shift-guided conformational sampling with SimpleFold. CS-SelectFold first generates a diverse ensemble of candidate conformations with SimpleFold, then predicts chemical shifts for each structure using UCBShift 2.0, and finally ranks conformations by agreement with experimentally determined excited-state chemical shifts. Using the L99A mutant of T4 lysozyme as a canonical benchmark, CS-SelectFold recovered excited-state-like conformations that reproduced the defining cavity-centered rearrangement of the known hidden state, including inward placement of Phe114 into the engineered cavity. Hotspot-region dRMSD analysis further showed that chemical-shift-guided post hoc selection enriched structures that escaped the dominant ground-state basin and converged toward the experimentally established excited-state structural basin. These results establish CS-SelectFold as a conceptually distinct sample-and-select strategy for excited-state structure discovery and suggest that experimentally determined chemical shifts can serve as an effective post hoc signal for identifying rare, functionally relevant conformations within generative protein structure ensembles.

papers.title: Charge-neutral N–H···Br as a Hydrogen-bond Family for the Construction of Hydrogen-bonded Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: The design, synthesis, and application of porous molecular crystals constructed using intermolecular hydrogen bonds (hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks; HOFs) have attracted significant attention due to the potential flexibility and solution processability of HOFs, which arises from the nature of hydrogen bonds. HOFs are generally constructed via highly directional intermolecular N–H···N and O–H···O hydrogen bonds, while the study of HOFs constructed by low-directional hydrogen bonds has lagged somewhat. The present study reveals that charge-neutral N–H···Br hydrogen bonds are suitable for the construction of HOFs. Specifically, single crystals of a bis(benzimidazole)NiBr 2 complex (bis(benzimidazole) = phenylbis(benzimidazol-2-yl)methane) were found to be a HOF supported by intermolecular N–H···Br hydrogen bonds. This HOF exhibits interesting flexibility, i.e., the intermolecular N–H···Br hydrogen bonds are cleaved and reformed upon the adsorption/desorption of organic vapors. Moreover, it can adsorb organic vapors in a recyclable fashion (for at least 10 cycles when acetone is used). This study expands the classes of low-directional hydrogen bonds applicable to the construction of HOFs.

papers.title: Redox-Active Metal-Organic Cages for Multielectron Redox Processes
papers.abstract: Multielectron redox processes play crucial roles in energy storage, catalysis, and electrochemical energy conversion. The mechanisms of multielectron redox processes often involve stepwise redox events, multiple intermediate states, and electronic communication between redox sites. This complexity makes the understanding of these processes challenging. Metal-organic cages (MOCs) serve as an ideal platform to investigate multielectron redox processes because of their following features. MOCs are supramolecules composed of metal nodes and organic ligands, to which multiple redox-active sites can be introduced, and their designability and well-defined structures allow control over the number, spatial arrangement, and degree of electronic communication of the redox-active sites. This review highlights the critical role of the molecular-level behavior of MOCs near the electrode surface in understanding systems with multiple discrete redox-active sites. Redox-active MOCs (RMOCs) can be categorized into four groups based on which parts of the MOC structure possess redox-active components: metal nodes, organic ligands, metalloligands, or guests. The structure and unique electrochemical behavior of RMOCs are discussed by introducing how these MOCs behave in the electrical double layer (EDL), which unveils the characteristic features that distinguish RMOC from conventional redox-active small molecules. We also outline the future applications of RMOC in catalysis, energy storage, and sensing.

papers.title: Ligand field determines g-tensor anisotropy and biradical character of (L)RuV=O and (L)RuV=N catalytic intermediates
papers.abstract: Highly oxidized metal-based species exhibit complex electronic structures and a high chemical reactivity, particularly in multi-electron chemical transformations. However, such species are rarely stabilized for characterization with conventional methods and are more frequently observed in reactive mixtures or trapped by fast mixing and freezing approaches. We demonstrate how the biradical character of highly reactive (L)Ru V =X (X=O, N) complexes can be tracked via spectroscopic signatures and advanced electronic structure calculations. The Ru V complexes investigated here promote O-O bond formation in water oxidation and enable C(sp3)-H bond amination. We propose that electronic structure of the biradical is central to these multi-electron reactivities, however, experimental tools for probing the electronic nature of such species remain limited. Although hyperfine splitting (hfs) data are often scarce, g-tensor data are readily available for low spin (S=1/2) paramagnetic species. To assign (L)Ru V =X (X=O, N) EPR signatures reliably, we used complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) and N-electron valence perturbation theory (NEVPT2) combined with wave-function analysis. We found that the main contributors to the g-tensor anisotropy are the low-lying doublet states with partial biradical characters. We show that the magnitude of g-tensor anisotropy is determined by local selection rules for the spin-orbit interaction and the energy gap in the first excitation, which we elucidate using natural orbitals, spinless triplet natural transition orbitals, and wave-function descriptors.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven Optimization of ALD Coatings for Enhanced Interfacial Stability in Advanced Battery Materials
papers.abstract: Zinc metal anodes for aqueous batteries suffer from dendrite growth, corrosion, and hydrogen evolution, limiting cycle life. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) coatings have emerged as a promising protection strategy, yet systematic comparison across coating materials remains challenging due to heterogeneous testing protocols. Here, we present an exploratory machine learning analysis of ALD-coated zinc anodes, compiling symmetric cell lifespan data from 9 publications (2018–2025) encompassing 8 coating materials (Al2O3, TiO2, ZrO2, ZnO, SnO2, ZnF2, Alucone, Al-O-N) and 19 coated samples. Using 11 physics-based material descriptors—including bandgap, elastic modulus, and ionic conductivity—without one-hot encoding of material identity, Gaussian process regression (GPR) achieved modest but meaningful predictive performance (leave-one-out cross-validation R2 = 0.482, MAE = 0.198 log10(h), 95% CI [–0.008, 0.695]), outperforming random forest (R2 = 0.254) and linear models (negative R2). SHAP analysis suggests bandgap and elastic modulus are the most influential material descriptors for predicting lifespan, though these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small dataset. ZrO2 and ZnF2 exhibited the longest lifespans in the compiled dataset. This work represents a hypothesis-generating study that highlights both the potential and current limitations of data-driven approaches for ALD coating optimization, emphasizing the need for standardized testing protocols and larger datasets to enable robust predictive modeling.

papers.title: Intrinsic pH-driven actuation of DNA origami rectangles
papers.abstract: DNA origami is a versatile method for constructing molecular machinery, yet many designs rely on responsive motifs or added components to achieve dynamic behaviour. Here, we show that unmodified DNA origami rectangles – one of the most widely used DNA origami structures – exhibit an intrinsic, reversible transition between planar and tubular states upon pH modulation. This transformation occurs due to the cooperative mechanical coupling of crossover junctions: no DNA modification, special sequences, or extra motifs are needed. The curling/uncurling response extends to connected rectangles: dimers and nanoribbons curl reversibly below pH 7 to form nanotube architectures. This unexpected conformational flexibility of monolayer DNA with pH provides a simple framework for engineering responsive nanostructures that can be transformed using the intrinsic properties of DNA.

papers.title: A Simulated Translational Oncology DMPK Workflow Integrating ADME Profiling, Machine Learning, and PK/PD-Guided Candidate Prioritisation
papers.abstract: Drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics, DMPK, plays a decisive role in oncology drug discovery because biochemical potency alone rarely translates into a clinically useful candidate without adequate exposure, tissue distribution, safety margin, and dose feasibility. Here, we present a proof-of-concept translational oncology workflow based on a simulated compound portfolio designed to emulate discovery-stage decision-making from lead optimisation to human translation. A dataset of 320 synthetic compounds was generated to span key physicochemical, ADME, safety, and pharmacology variables, including solubility, Caco-2 permeability, plasma free fraction, intrinsic clearance, oral bioavailability, tumor:plasma ratio, projected human clearance, projected halflife, and potency-linked coverage. The workflow integrated descriptive profiling, correlation analysis, principal component analysis, k-means clustering, supervised classification, regression modelling, permutation importance, composite candidate ranking, and a simplified PK/PD scenario analysis. The simulated portfolio reproduced biologically plausible translational trade-offs. Higher intrinsic clearance was associated with lower oral bioavailability, increasing lipophilicity was associated with declining solubility, and tumor distribution alone did not ensure high potency-normalized coverage. Unsupervised analysis resolved four distinct translational clusters, including a high-clearance low-coverage subgroup and a more optimal low-clearance high-coverage subgroup. For prediction of high-tier developability, the random forest classifier outperformed logistic regression, achieving an AUROC of 0.954, AUPRC of 0.920, accuracy of 0.888, and F1 score of 0.830. Regression models predicted oral bioavailability more accurately than projected human clearance, with ridge regression reaching an R2 of 0.864 for oral bioavailability, whereas gradient boosting produced the best projected clearance model with an R2 of 0.385. Feature-importance analysis identified solubility, microsomal intrinsic clearance, hepatocyte intrinsic clearance, hERG liability, cLogP, and cellular potency as major contributors to high-tier classification. Composite translational ranking identified CRH_301 as the top candidate, with oral bioavailability of 95.0%, coverage ratio of 6.556, projected human clearance of 6.075 mL/min/kg, projected half-life of 54.758 h, and predicted effective dose of 74.949 mg. However, simplified PK/PD analysis indicated that predicted free tumor concentration remained below the cellular EC50 threshold, highlighting a residual translational gap despite otherwise favorable portfolio-level properties. Together, these findings show that oncology candidate quality emerges from balanced systems-level performance rather than potency alone, and they illustrate how DMPK, quantitative modelling, and machine learning can be integrated into a transparent workflow for candidate prioritisation and translational decision support.

papers.title: Replication of chiral α-hydroxy acid via induction and amplification through an enantioenriched cyanohydrin conglomerate
papers.abstract: A spontaneous absolute asymmetric synthesis of cyanohydrins has been developed without any external chiral source through the combination of conglomerate formation and solution-phase racemization. This method integrates HCN addition reaction to an aldehyde with subsequent Viedma ripening; consequently, spontaneous deracemization and enantioselective reactive crystallization of cyanohydrins are achieved for the first time. Importantly, the hydrolysis products of the cyanohydrin—namely, the corresponding α-hydroxy acid and hydroxyamide—serve as chiral inducer that direct the handedness of solid-state asymmetric amplification, leading to highly enantioenriched cyanohydrins with matching chirality. This feedback between product formation and asymmetric amplification establishes a reaction network in which chirality is propagated and reinforced across molecular transformations. In combination with cyanohydrin hydrolysis, this system constitutes a chemically coupled process that approaches the replication of chiral α-hydroxy acid and hydroxyamide, key products in abiotic Streckertype synthesis, and is therefore relevant to the origin of biological homochirality.

papers.title: Closed-loop, Human-AI–driven optimization of geological hydrogen production
papers.abstract: Geological hydrogen produced from iron-rich rocks via serpentinization is an emerging low-carbon energy pathway. However, reaction rates remain slow and difficult to control due to the coupling of multiple parameters and the complexity of rock-fluid interactions. Here we report a closed-loop, high-throughput experimental platform that integrates domain knowledge, Bayesian optimization and human-in-the-loop decision making to navigate and control the high-dimensional reaction landscape governing geological hydrogen production. By systematically exploring a nine-dimensional parameter space, the platform converges to high-production conditions in fewer than 90 experiments, achieving hydrogen concentrations up to two orders of magnitude higher than baseline rock–water reactions. Experiments using both model brucite and natural rocks identify moderate temperatures, bicarbonate-rich fluids, and elevated catalyst and surfactant loadings as key drivers of enhanced hydrogen yield. Mechanistic characterization links these optimized conditions to accelerated redox Fe2+ to Fe3+ kinetics and the early formation of oxidized iron oxide phase. Together, these results establish an AI-driven strategy for understanding and controlling complex rock-fluid reaction systems, enabling accelerated and scalable geological hydrogen production and advancing pathways for clean energy generation, using Earth as a chemical factory.

papers.title: CALCULATIONS AND SIMULATIONS OF HEAVY METALS AND RARE EARTH ELEMENTS IN VENEZUELAN EXTRA-HEAVY CRUDE OIL TREATED WITH BIOCOMPATIBLE PHARMACEUTICAL FORMULATIONS
papers.abstract: In this study, the partitioning behavior of heavy metals (HM) and rare earth elements (REEs) among fractions of Venezuelan extra-heavy crude oil treated with biocompatible pharmaceutical formulations (BPFs) based on Polysorbate 80 (P80) and various alcohols was evaluated using standardized calculation procedures. The results reveal a clear separation between the hydrophilic liquid fraction (F1), containing dissolved ionic species and mineral elements, and the solid residual fraction (F3), composed primarily of asphaltenes, resins, and other organic residues capable of forming organometallic complexes (OMC-X). The upgraded and recovered crude corresponds to Fraction 2 (F2). Short-chain alcohols preferentially promote partitioning toward F1, whereas long-chain alcohols enhance migration toward F3. Two hypotheses are proposed. First, extra-heavy crude oil becomes enriched with heavy metals and rare earth elements during prolonged geological residence in the subsurface, where these elements are incorporated into organometallic complexes associated with asphaltenes and resins, thus acting as a geochemical sink. Second, BPF systems based on P80 and alcohols are capable of extracting these species into F1 and F3, thereby reducing their concentration in F2 and effectively upgrading the crude. The formation of OMC-X (X = Ce, La, or Y) was investigated through molecular simulations and sio Index determination, using a dimeric cyclooctadiene rhodium chloride complex as a model compound. Simulation results suggest that chloride ions stabilize OMC–REE species, which may explain the migration of ionic species from the liquid phase (F1) toward the solid phase (F3) in systems containing alcohols with six or more carbon atoms.

papers.title: On-Surface Synthesis of a Low Bandgap Cyclopenta[c,d]azulene-Based Polymer
papers.abstract: Non-benzenoid topologies offer a compelling strategy to tailor the electronic properties of low-dimensional carbon materials. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis of a non-alternant polymer incorporating a [7–5–5] cyclopenta[c,d]azulene motif on Au(111) via thermally-induced Ullmann coupling. Bond-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy confirms the robustness of the [7–5–5] framework. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy, together with dI/dV mapping supported by density functional theory calculations, reveals a remarkable narrow bandgap of 1.5 eV. The electronic structure is governed by intramolecular charge transfer from the heptagonal ring to the adjacent fused pentagonal rings, resulting in a pronounced dipole moment despite being composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen. Aromaticity analyses indicate the coexistence of locally aromatic and antiaromatic regions, highlighting the intrinsic electronic frustration associated with the non-alternant topology. The reduced bandgap is directly linked to this interplay. These findings demonstrate how the controlled incorporation of [7–5–5] motifs enable the rational bandgap engineering in carbon-based polymers and expands the scope of non-benzenoid design in on-surface synthesis.

papers.title: Charting the evolving chemical synthesis repertoire at Roche
papers.abstract: Predictive chemistry models are constrained by the success bias of the public literature, which obscures the failures and operational constraints of real-world laboratory execution. To address this limitation, we present the Database of Unified Chemical Knowledge (DUCK), which includes public and corporate reaction data and implements an internal enterprise data architecture that transforms unstructured electronic lab notebook records into machine-readable format. We analyze nearly 700,000 chemical transformations performed at Roche between 2010 and 2024 to establish an overview of industrial synthesis. The industrial reaction repertoire turns out to be concentrated, with four reaction superclasses accounting for more than two thirds of all recorded single-batch instances. Temporal mapping reveals a decade-long increase in molecular complexity that plateaued after 2020. Furthermore, we identify a departmental division of labor, contrasting the transformations of discovery chemistry with the route-optimized focus of downstream development. An examination of core C–C and C–N bond formations highlights strong reagent-level standardization, but also reveals a baseline of documented synthetic failures. This study bridges the disparity between academic literature and industrial practice by taking advantage of the full breadth of data. The result is a refined high-integrity baseline for predictive machine learning models in chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Aza[7]Helicene Diimide: Backbone-Controlled Excited-State Charge Transfer and Electronic Coupling
papers.abstract: A carbazole-embedded aza[7]helicene diimide (aza[7]HDI) was synthesized as a backbone-engineered [7]HDI. Unlike outer-rim donor-substituted push–pull [7]HDIs, aza[7]HDI combines pronounced excited-state charge transfer character with strengthened inter-imide electronic communication. It exhibits strong solvatochromic fluorescence and circularly polarized luminescence, a large excited-state dipole-moment change, and enhanced fluorescence quantum yields. Electrochemical and quantum-chemical analyses consistently support enhanced through-space coupling. Backbone donor incorporation thus emerges as an effective strategy for tuning excited-state polarization and electronic coupling in chiral donor–acceptor helicenes.

papers.title: Pinning and depinning of imbibition fronts by evaporation-induced salt precipitation and cracking in porous media
papers.abstract: Spontaneous imbibition - the capillarity-driven uptake of liquids into porous media - is a fundamental process underlying phenomena from plant transpiration and soil infiltration to oil recovery and drug delivery. Classical theory predicts that evaporation arrests imbibition through an equilibrium between capillary inflow and diffusive outflow, that salt crystallization blocks pore connectivity, and that displacement of a low-viscosity fluid by a viscous one maintains a stable two-phase interface. Contrary to these expectations, we show that when concentrated salt solutions imbibe into porous media, evaporation-induced salt precipitation sustains and even accelerates the process. The resulting subflorescence disrupts the dynamic equilibrium, depins the imbibition front, and fractures the matrix - transforming the imbibition front from flat and stable to convex and ultimately into intricate fingering patterns. In-situ X-ray scattering and advanced electron microscopy reveal these transitions from single-nanopore up to the porous-medium scale. Complementary continuum modeling and molecular dynamics simulations identify a coupled interplay between imbibition, evaporation, precipitation, and cracking that governs this anomalous behavior. Our findings challenge conventional understanding and suggest new mechanisms for fluid manipulation in porous media, with potential applications in energy, environment, materials, and medicine.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into the Dispersion Mechanism of CNT in Ionic Liquids : The Role of Cation
papers.abstract: The comparative dispersion performance of three ionic liquids namely 1-butyl-3methylimidazolium (BMIM+), N-butyl-pyridinium (BPy+), and N,N-butyl methylpyrrolidinium (C4MPy+), paired with the tetrafluoroborate anion (BF4 –) as a common counterion is tested in the present work. Dispersion of carbon allotropes remains challenging due to strong van der Waals interactions that keep nanotubes bundled, limiting their large-scale application. The interplay of the cation aromaticity, hydrophobic interactions and non-covalent interaction strength with the CNT surface synergistically affects the overall the dispersion mechanism. Our simulations show that all ILs form a highly ordered interfacial layer around CNTs, dominated by strong cation tail-CNT interactions observed from RDF data. Also, COM-RDF of CNT as a reference and cations show higher peak intensity for BMIM cations in comparison with BPY and C4MPY and lower for anions. Tilt Angle Distribution at the Carbon Nanotube Surface indiactes parallel orientation of BMIM ring that maximizes π-π stacking along with near-parallel and antiparallel alignments of N–C tail vector to the CNT axis. These results along with PMF data supports BMIM-BF4exhibits the strongest stabilizing effect and the lowest CNT separation free energy, while other shows relatively similar performance. Residence time correlation shows faster correlation decay for the cations displaying shorter binding events and more frequent exchange with the bulk. Results were further supported by QM based analyses indicating comparatively stronger BMIM adsorption while pyrrolidinium and N-butylpyridinium IL binds moderately. Furthermore, adsorption of ILs over CNT surface preserves its electronic structure. The selection of cation play a significant role in the stability of the ILs adsorbed CNT complexes and also this will affect the interfacial interaction between ion-pair and surfaces. These insights provide a molecular-level rationale for the superior dispersing ability of ILs and support their use as effective, non-destructive media for carbon nanomaterials.

papers.title: Aromatic fluorination enhances hydrophobicity and antimicrobial activity of magainin 2
papers.abstract: Inspired by the structure of the natural antimicrobial peptide magainin 2 (MG), we developed a series of fluorinated magainin 2 analogues (FMGs) incorporating pentafluorophenylalanine residue and systematically studied their physicochemical properties and antimicrobial activities. Analytical reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography and circular dichroism spectroscopy demonstrated that incorporation of pentafluorophenylalanines effectively modulates hydrophobicity and secondary structure of peptides. Membranedisruption assays using model lipid bilayers, together with evaluations of antibacterial activity assays against Escherichia coli and hemolytic toxicity assays toward red blood cells, revealed that FMGs exhibit enhanced antimicrobial activity, with minimum inhibitory concentration values reduced by up to an order of magnitude relative to MG, without a substantial increase in toxicity. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that the preferential membrane-disruptive activity arises from selective binding to negatively charged bacterial membranes. These findings provide detailed structure-activity relationships for fluorinated antimicrobial peptides and highlight the introduction of fluorinated aromatic units as a powerful strategy to enhance hydrophobicity and antimicrobial activity.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review on Green Nanoengineered Smart Plasmonic Nanoparticles for Sensing and Plant Growth Applications
papers.abstract: Phytosynthesized plasmonic nanoparticles (PNP) of Au, Ag, Pt, and Pd, prepared from plant extracts (leaves, stems, flowers, and seeds), provide an eco-friendly, biocompatible, and cost-effective alternative to conventional chemical synthesis methods. These particles exhibit unique optical properties arising from their surface plasmon resonance (SPR), demonstrating applications in sensing, plant growth, and photobiology. This review critically examines recent advances in plant-source-mediated PNP, focusing on their synthesis, applications, and challenges. The mechanistic understanding of green extracts and their role in PNP formation was discussed, followed by characterisation techniques which provide crucial insights into nanoparticle-mediated applications, particularly in environmental and analytical sensing using colourimetric/optical, SERS, and electrochemical/hybrid sensors. Next, phytogenic PNP applications for plant growth via photo-biological processes, including growth enhancement, photosynthetic efficiency, biomass accumulation, abiotic stress tolerance, and ROS management, were addressed. Indeed, with the advancement of technology, PNP synthesised from plant sources has improved in application, though with certain limitations due to various gaps, including lot variability, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and limited long-term stability. Addressing these gaps will enable the safe, sustainable, and impactful integration of phytosynthesized PNP into precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and light-driven biological systems, advancing the goals of green nanotechnology and plant nanobiology.

papers.title: A modular and affordable self-driving laboratory enables vision-guided optimization of metal electrodeposition
papers.abstract: Metal electrodeposition is a widely used materials synthesis technique; however, industrial applications often require optimization of complex precursor formulations and electrodeposition parameters, which is typically performed in a slow, inefficient, and empirical manner. Self-driving labs (SDLs) that combine automated electrodeposition with machine-learning-guided decision-making could accelerate discovery in these complex, high-dimensional parameter spaces, but they face practical challenges. Notably, automated electrodeposition platforms need a continuous supply of pristine electrode surfaces, preservation and logging of electrodeposited samples, and the ability to easily incorporate non-electrochemical, downstream characterization. To overcome these challenges, we developed a modular, affordable, and accessible automated electrochemistry platform that uses a roll-to-roll design to enable continuous electrodeposition experiments. The roll-to-roll architecture enables easy integration with downstream characterization techniques in a conveyor-belt fashion, and electrodeposited samples are stored by rolling up the spent electrode material. We performed 300 identical Cu electrodeposition experiments over 35 hours, demonstrating high repeatability and continuous 24/7 experimentation. We demonstrate the use of our platform for an autonomous campaign, employing a vision-guided Bayesian optimization (BO) workflow to tune electrodeposition parameters and additive concentrations to achieve a visible-light-absorbing Cu deposit. An interpretable machine-learning approach was used to identify benzotriazole as a key additive for controlling the brightness of deposited Cu films. The roll-to-roll design enabled preservation of samples and offline analysis with scanning electron microscopy, providing insight into the impact of benzotriazole on the morphology of the deposited films.

papers.title: A Generalized Theory for the Structural and Spatial Mapping of Energy, Entropy, and Free Energy
pH-Inverted Histidine-Rich Nanochelants for Trapping Furin-Processed Polycationic Nanotoxins: A Quantum-Classical Platform for Dual Heavy-Metal Detoxification and Broad-Spectrum Countermeasures
papers.abstract: Furin cleaves polybasic sites in endosomes and the secretory pathway, releasing linear (>3 net positive charges) and concentric (metal-coordinating) nanotoxins that drive metabolic disease, cytokine storms, neurodegeneration, autoimmunity, cancer immune evasion, and infection. We introduce 5H-EAF, an erythritol-capped linear penta-histidine nanochelant (MW ≈ 868 Da) that activates to +4–5 net charge at endosomal pH 5.5–6.5, trapping these species via electrostatic clamping and coordination, then deprotonates and releases harmlessly at neutral pH. DFT (B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVP, explicit solvation) yields Pb²⁺ ΔG = –11 to –16 kcal/mol (low pH) → –3 to –6 kcal/mol (neutral); SARS-CoV-2 PRRAR⁺ motif clamping ΔG ≈ –8 to –13 kcal/mol; and anthrax PA63 pore blockade analogous to validated cationic blockers (Kd nM–µM, planar-bilayer literature) supported by all-atom MD simulations (MM-PBSA ΔG = −28.7 kcal/mol at pH 5.5). The platform speaks furin’s native pH/Ca²⁺/charge language without global inhibition. It unifies GLP-1 optimization, cytokine control, α-syn/amyloid management, Pb neuroprotection, and biodefense against furin-dependent pathogens (anthrax, Ebola, H5N1, SARS-CoV-2, Dengue).

papers.title: Realization of Self-Terminating Underpotential Electropolymerization by Strong Supramolecular Monomer-Electrode Interaction
papers.abstract: In this report, we show that electropolymerization of 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene (EDOT) can take place at 0.4 V, a voltage far lower than the conventionally employed voltage of 1.0 V, in a self-terminating manner, when gold is employed as a working electrode. DFT calculations revealed that the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) of EDOT is elevated by approximately 1 eV when it directly interacts with the gold surface compared to that without such direct interaction. In other words, monomers become highly reactive for oxidative polymerization when they are directly adsorbed onto gold. Once the polymer forms and covers the electrode surface, the monomer can no longer interact with the electrode surface, thus the polymerization is terminated. Such selfterminating polymerization behavior was supported by in situ electrochemical surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (EC-SERS) and the current profile during the voltage scan. This is in sharp contrast to electropolymerization under ordinary high-voltage conditions, where the polymer film continuously grows. This study may provide solutions to control the polymerization on the solid surface, which is considered to be very important for adhesive, coatings, and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation. It is also expected to lead to new synthetic methods via electropolymerization for monolayer polymers, which have recently attracted attention for their potential to exhibit various functions.

papers.title: More accurate and reproducible glass transition temperature calculation with unsupervised machine learning and neural network charges
papers.abstract: Accurate computational modeling of the glass transition is a longstanding challenge in polymer chemistry. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations offer a powerful approach to observe the changes in viscoelasticity, density and chain mobility associated with the glass transition, yet they often overestimate the glass transition temperature (T g ) and have limited sensitivity to number average molecular weight and dispersity. These deficiencies are largely attributed to high levels of noise in simulation data masking the T g , inaccurate polymer representations, and limited force field transferability. In this study, we build a robust and automated workflow to calculate T g using unsupervised machine learning, and apply it to a range of polymer models and dispersities. We show that our workflow provides improved T g estimates when compared to other established, 'bulk' measurements (e.g., monitoring changes in RMSD or density). We also benchmark different neural network charge models, which streamline polymer force field parameterization, and assess their influence on the T g .

papers.title: Nanoplastics can build themselves
papers.abstract: To understand nanoplastics through modeling, e.g., to assess their toxicity and environmental impact, reliable starting structures are required. In this study, we present a new approach to generate nanoplastic particles from classical molecular dynamics simulations. Starting with the initial aggregation of monomer units and allowing for their subsequent growth into polymer strands yields stable aggregates with polymers of diverse length, avoiding the need to define the number of polymer units with a set length a priori. The generated particles are compared to existing model nanoplastics and show agreement in terms of structural characteristics and energetics. The novel approach is computationally efficient and allows for a greater diversity of structures than approaches with predefined chain lengths.

papers.title: The Elusive Nature of Aromatic Carbocation Intermediates in Confined Catalytic Environments
Phenoxy-Benzothiadiazole Donor-Acceptor Compounds Exhibit Solvatochromic Fluorescence and Are Precursors to Open-Shell Phenoxyl Radicals
papers.abstract: In this work, we present the synthesis of two highly fluorescent phenoxy-benzothiadiazole donor-acceptor (DA) compounds, which exhibit quantum yields of up to 84% in solution under an atmosphere of air. These compounds display solvatochromic fluorescence within the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum, characteristic of DA exciplex behavior, and exhibit reversible reactivity under acidic conditions as monitored by UV-Vis spectroscopy. We demonstrate the reversible oxidation of compound to the open-shell phenoxy radical 5·. In contrast, compound 6 undergoes irreversible oxidation to bis(quinone) 7, despite the loss of aromaticity. We also observe the comproportionation of 6 and 7 to compound 6· upon UV light irradiation in solution, as evidenced by EPR spectroscopy. The structures of compounds 5, 6, and 7 were confirmed through X-ray crystallography.

papers.title: Quaternary ammonium–modified cellulose fibers can enhance wastewater treatment performance under challenging conditions
papers.abstract: Wastewater treatment is challenged by refractory contaminants and rising water demand, while conventional coagulation-flocculation suffers from low throughput and is sensitive to the influent water conditions. Cellulose fibers can act as super-bridging agents offering enhanced turbidity removal when used in conjunction with traditional coagulants and flocculants. However, the chemical modification of cellulose fibers and their performance under challenging influent conditions remain largely unexplored. In this study, recycled cellulose fibers are modified with cationic quaternary ammonium groups, imparting a positive charge that can improve treatment performance for a wider range of water matrices including varying influent pH, ionic strength, and turbidity. Modified fibers achieve turbidity below 5 NTU across all influent pHs (7.0–8.9) and turbidities (62–285 NTU) tested, while pristine fibers show that the target turbidity of 25 NTU is not reached when the influent pH or turbidity exceed 8.2 or 130 NTU, respectively. Additionally, modified fibers achieve the target turbidity of 25 NTU even in the presence of an additional 20 mM NaCl, while pristine fibers cannot reach this target at an additional 10 mM NaCl. Furthermore, the modified fibers enhance the removal of metals such as Zn, Cr, Fe, and Pb through the incorporation of metal hydroxide precipitates within fiber-based flocs. Overall, pristine and modified fiber-enhanced treatments remove 52% and 65% of metals, respectively, compared to 39% with the conventional method. Therefore, modified cellulose fibers represent a promising strategy for enhancing coagulation-flocculation treatment performance.

papers.title: Multi-State Photoswitching in Thienoquinoid-Based Fluorescent Trithiophenes
papers.abstract: Achieving multi-site photoisomerization within a single π-conjugated scaffold while retaining luminescent functionality remains a formidable challenge, as electronic coupling between isomerizable units typically promotes intramolecular energy transfer that suppresses sequential switching, and the additional nonradiative pathways inherent to multiple isomerizable bonds further impede emissive behavior. Herein, we report a methine-bridged trithiophene bearing 2,6-dichlorophenyl substituents, in which two C=C double bonds embedded in a thienoquinoid framework undergo photoisomerization, affording three interconvertible geometrical isomers ( ZZ , EZ , and EE ). The steric constraint imposed by the ortho-chloro groups suppresses nonradiative torsional relaxation, yielding a fluorescence quantum yield of 0.402 for the ZZ -isomer in cyclohexane, which decreases upon photoisomerization to the EZ - and EE -isomers—a significant enhancement over the corresponding derivative lacking ortho-substituents on the aryl groups—accompanied by a markedly reduced Stokes shift. The photostationary state composition varies systematically with the irradiation wavelength, reflecting the wavelength-dependent differences in molar absorption coefficients among the three isomers, thereby enabling wavelength-selective multi-state control over isomer 2 distributions that are inaccessible under thermodynamic equilibrium. Fluorescence lifetime measurements reveal isomer-dependent excited-state lifetimes, confirming that molecular geometry governs the photophysical properties within this conjugated framework. This work establishes a molecular design strategy for luminescent multi-state photoswitches applicable to multi-level optical information processing.

papers.title: Synthesis of Secondary N-Trifluoromethyl- and N-(Per)fluoroalkylamides
papers.abstract: Stable secondary N-trifluoromethylamides have been prepared and isolated by two complementary methods: from N-trifluoromethyl-1,2,3-triazoles via thermally generated ketenimines, and by thioacid ligation with azidotrifluoromethane. These transformations overcome the long-standing instability of N-trifluoromethyl amine precursor and provide direct, scalable routes to bench-stable secondary N-trifluoromethyl- and N-fluoroalkylamides, tolerating diverse functional groups and structural motifs. Detailed experimental and computational studies reveal their high thermal stability, good hydrolytic stability, significantly higher acidity, and enhanced lipophilicity and hydrogen bond donor strength compared to conventional secondary amides. The new class of compounds expands the chemical space of fluorinated amides and introduces N-(per)fluoroalkyl secondary amides as easy to handle molecules with potential applications in medicinal and material chemistry.
