papers.abstract: Double network hydrogels (DNHs) achieve exceptional toughness through sacrificial fracture of a brittle first network embedded in a ductile second network. Despite extensive theoretical and macroscopic studies, direct experimental correlations between molecular bond scission and applied deformation remain scarce, and damage is commonly assumed to follow the macroscopic deformation field. Here, we directly visualize and quantify bond scission in DNHs during deformation by combining in situ confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) with anthracene-based optical force probe (OFP) crosslinkers and a customized uniaxial stretching device. This approach enables spatially resolved mapping of molecular bond rupture in real time while simultaneously probing mechanical response. Surprisingly, we find that bond scission is strongly heterogeneous even under nominally homogeneous macroscopic deformation. Quantitative comparison with a mechanochemical damage model shows that this discrepancy arises from intrinsic network heterogeneity that is not captured by conventional homogeneous-material descriptions. Our results demonstrate that molecular damage in polymer networks cannot be inferred solely from macroscopic deformation fields and highlight the necessity of spatially resolved measurements for understanding the mechanics and fracture of DNHs.

papers.title: datalab: Federated data management infrastructure for materials chemistry and beyond
papers.abstract: datalab is an open source laboratory data management platform for chemical and material sciences, consisting of a Python web server, user-friendly Vue.js web app, and an associated ecosystem of plugins and tools. It is designed to be deployed at the level of a research group or consortium, providing functionality to track samples and their connections through the entire research lifecycle. In doing so, datalab seeks to enable FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reproducible) data workflows while simultaneously saving researchers time and effort in managing and analyzing experiments.

papers.title: Amorphous Carbon-Rich Carbon Nitride-based Photocatalyst for Selective C-C Bond Cleavage in Lignin β–O–4 Linkages
papers.abstract: In this study, an amorphous carbon-rich carbon nitride photocatalyst was prepared by nitric acid treatment of pyrolyzed melamine followed by nitrogen annealing. The resulting semiconductor material exhibited an up-shifted valence band that enhances the oxidizing power of photogenerated holes, enabling selective Cα–Cβ bond cleavage of 2-phenoxy-1-phenylethanol (2-POE). Using 1.5 g.L -1 of the optimized photocatalyst in acetonitrile, 2-POE underwent first order conversion with a reaction rate of 2.55 h -1 under a 9 W blue LED light source. Product analysis showed formation of benzaldehyde as the major product, confirming C-C bond scission with 93.1% selectivity. In addition, ring-opening reactions were observed, producing fumaric and maleic acids as the by-products. Photocatalytic depolymerization of organosolv lignin further demonstrated ring-opening of the β–O–4 linking motifs, forming dicarboxylic acids analogous to those generated from 2-POE. These findings highlight a novel metal-free photocatalytic platform capable of promoting selective lignin depolymerization and producing valuable industrial products and precursors.

papers.title: Reversible Hydrogen Atom Exchange Between Phenoxyl Radical and Phenol at Cobalt(II): Role of Coordination-induced Bond Activation
papers.abstract: Tyrosine residues serve as a hydrogen atom (H • = H + +e – ) responsive functionality within the vicinity of many metalloenzyme active sites, therefore, understanding the roles of transition metal ions on net H-atom exchange routes are fundamentally important. This study reports isolation and comprehensive characterization (X-ray diffraction, UV-vis, FTIR, and magnetic susceptibility) of phenol complexes ( N 2 SArOH )M II Br 2 ( 1-M ; where, M = Co/Ni), supported by an unsymmetrical tripodal ligand N 2 SArOH . Application of Bordwell relationship, which combines the pKa values of the phenolic moieties in 1-M (determined from UV-vis spectrophotometric titrations) and the redox potentials of the corresponding phenolate complexes ( N 2 SArO )M II Br ( 2-M ), affords the O–H bond dissociation free energy (BDFEOH) values as 73.55 for 1-Co and 82.87 kcal mol –1 for 1-Ni . These results underscore the critical role of the metal site in governing the thermochemistry of the coordinated phenol. H-atom exchange reaction between phenol in 1-Co and isolated 2,4,6-tri-tert-butylphenoxyl ( t Bu 3 ArO • ) results in the isolation of a cobalt(II)–phenoxyl radical complex 4-Co with S =1 electronic ground state. Furthermore, reactivity of the phenoxyl functionality in 4-Co with H • (/H + +e – ) donors (such as phenol/thiol) smoothly yields the phenol complex 1-Co , thereby illustrating reversible H-atom exchange. Detailed kinetic studies on the H-atom exchange reactions of 4-Co with various substituted phenols provide the kinetic isotope effect (KIE) and activation parameters (ΔH ‡ , ΔS ‡ , E a ), thereby enabling an experimental distinction between H-atom transfer (HAT) and proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathways. Together, this complete set of isolated phenol, phenolate, and phenoxyl radical complexes delineates the relay of protons and H-atoms within the coordination sphere of the metal site, thereby showcasing the strong potential of the phenol-tethered coordination motifs in PCET/HAT based catalysis. These findings also shed light on the functional role of the hemilabile tyrosine residue in the active sites of metalloenzymes like lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs).

papers.title: Integration of Mechanical Persistence and Recoverability in Entangled Poly(ionic liquid) Ion Gels
papers.abstract: Designing physically crosslinked ion gels that combine dynamic recoverability with long-lived mechanical integrity remains challenging because fast self-healing generally requires short-lived interactions, whereas resistance to stress relaxation and repeated deformation demands persistent network constraints. Here, we address this trade-off by constructing a poly(ionic liquid) ion gel (PIL-IG) in which high-molecular-weight chain entanglements and solvent-mediated transient ionic associations act cooperatively. The gel is prepared by polymerizing N-[2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl]-N,N-dimethylbutan-1-aminium trifluoromethanesulfonylimide ([N1142MA][TFSI]) in the anion-matched ionic liquid 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide ([C2mim][TFSI]), which enables the formation of entangled P[N1142MA][TFSI] networks without chemical crosslinkers. The resulting PIL-IG exhibits extraordinarily slow stress relaxation, negligible residual strain under repeated large deformations, and stretchability exceeding 1000%, while still achieving complete self-healing within 30 min at room temperature. Comparison with neutral polymer ion gels indicates that entanglements alone cannot account for this unusual combination of properties. Instead, the results support a dual-network mechanism in which long-lived entanglements provide mechanical persistence, whereas transient ionic associations allow local network reconstruction. These findings establish an effective molecular design strategy for mitigating the trade-off between recoverability and durability in soft ionic materials.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Synthesis of Glycosyl Bromides in Flow
papers.abstract: A new photocatalytic method for the preparation of glycosyl bromides has been developed, exhibiting broad applicability to commonly used substrates. Upon irradiation with purple LEDs, bromine reacts with benzotrifluoride (PhCF3) to generate hydrogen bromide (HBr) in situ, which subsequently transforms the substrate into the glycosyl bromide in excellent yield. Unlike classical methods, the new strategy generates minimal acidic waste and features a simple work-up. Notably, its scalability was demonstrated under photo-flow conditions, enabling rapid, multigram-scale synthesis of glycosyl bromides. Furthermore, we show that the product bromides can be used directly as glycosyl donors in one-pot glycosylations.

papers.title: Rational Design of Ce-Based Mixed Oxides via Dopant Synergy for Enhanced Oxygen Release and Combustion
papers.abstract: Ce-based mixed oxides with enhanced oxygen release properties were rationally designed by substituting Ce sites in the fluorite lattice with group 3 and 4 metal cations. Structural characterizations confirmed the formation of homogeneous solid solutions with tunable lattice strain and local coordination environments. By combining H 2 -TPR and in operando XANES-TPR, dopants were classified into three categories based on their roles: intrinsically reducible cations, lattice-stabilizing cations with small ionic radii, and trivalent cations that promote oxygen vacancy formation. These dopants enhance oxygen release through distinct mechanisms, including direct redox participation, improved Ce reducibility, and facilitated oxygen diffusion. A clear synergistic effect was observed when co-doping elements from different categories, leading to significantly reduced oxygen release temperatures. Guided by this principle, a quaternary oxide (CePrZrSmO ₓ ) exhibited the best oxygen releasing performance. This enhanced oxygen release behavior directly translated into superior soot combustion activity, demonstrating strong correlations between oxygen release properties and soot combustion. This work provides a rational strategy for designing high-performance ceria-based materials for enhanced oxygen releasing and catalytic combustion applications.

papers.title: The preparatory (anti)bonding character of molecular orbitals
papers.abstract: The strengths of chemical bonds define our world by influencing chemical reactivity and molecular structure. Yet, trends in bonding strengths upon oxidation or reduction of molecules are insufficiently predicted by molecular orbital theory, the central theory for chemical bonding. This work presents such unpredicted changes in bonding energies of isolated molecular aluminum organometallics. Their chemical bonding situation was investigated computationally by energy decomposition analysis, generalized and the concept of preparatory (anti)bonding molecular orbitals is introduced. Its validity is demonstrated on standard molecules like methane, benzene or water, for which the relative stability of homolysis products changes upon redox reactions. The preparatory character of orbitals allows qualitative predictions of trends in bonding energies, being a valuable addition to molecular orbital theory across all fields of chemistry.

papers.title: Improving QSAR model predictions using ensembled heterogenous features
papers.abstract: Quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models are widely used computational tools in drug discovery for predicting molecular activities and prioritizing compounds for experimental testing. However, many existing QSAR methods still suffer from limited applicability domains, overfitting, and instability across different datasets. To address these challenges, we present GT-QSAR, an automated machine learning workflow for structure-centric QSAR modeling that integrates heterogeneous molecular representations through ensemble learning. GT-QSAR supports both receptor- and ligand-based modeling strategies and combines diverse feature groups, including molecular descriptors, pharmacophore fingerprints, graph-based embeddings, grid-based shape and electrostatic representations, and protein–ligand interaction features. Systematic benchmarking using the Papyrus dataset demonstrates that GT-QSAR provides improved predictive accuracy, model stability, and generalizability compared with control tools. In addition, virtual screening experiments using the LIT-PCBA benchmark show that GT-QSAR substantially improves enrichment compared with conventional similarity-based and docking-based screening methods and previously reported target-specific machine learning models. These results demonstrate that GT-QSAR provides a robust and generalizable framework for QSAR modeling, enabling improved prioritization of active compounds in realistic drug discovery campaigns. The data used for QSAR modeling as part of this work is made publicly available. GT-QSAR is available online at https://gtqsar.standigm.com.

papers.title: In Situ Observation of Li-Ion Insertion-Induced Solvation Structure Change at Water-in-Salt/Lithium-titanate Interface by Electrochemical Atomic Force Microscopy
papers.abstract: Water-in-salt (WiS) electrolytes are promising candidates for safe aqueous lithiumion batteries (ALIBs) due to their expanded electrochemical stability window compared to diluted aqueous solutions. However, the interfacial phenomena between WiS electrolytes and electrode materials during electrochemical reactions remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the interfacial solvation structures of two WiS electrolytes, a monosalt system based on lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) and a bisalt system containing both LiTFSI and lithium bis(pentafluoroethanesulfonyl)imide (LiBETI), on a Li4Ti5O12(111) (LTO) electrode using electrochemical frequency-modulation atomic force microscopy (EC-AFM) with a qPlus sensor. In situ EC-AFM observations revealed that the distinct layered solvation structures observed at the open-circuit potential were significantly altered by Li-ion insertion. In the WiMS system, Li-ion insertion induced a transition from the thick (∼1.3 nm) layered structure characteristic of WiS to a layered structure with a thickness of approximately 0.3 nm, similar to that of dilute aqueous solutions. In contrast, the WiBS system maintained its original layered structure after Li-ion insertion. These results suggest that the higher salt concentration and significantly suppressed free water activity in the WiBS system play a crucial role in maintaining the interfacial solvation structure against local cation depletion during the electrode reaction.

papers.title: Stabilization of Cu Species in UiO-66 Metal-Organic Framework for CO2-to-Methanol: Insights from Operando X-ray and Electron Microscopy Studies
papers.abstract: UiO-66, a Zr-based metal-organic framework (MOF), provides an ordered porous environment capable of adsorbing/retaining CO2 and oxygenated intermediates relevant for methanol synthesis. Although UiO-66-based composites containing Cu and Cu-Zn species show promising performance for CO2-to-methanol conversion, the role of the MOF framework in stabilizing the active metallic species under working conditions remains insufficiently understood. Here, the stabilization of copper species by UiO-66 and the influence of Zn promotion on Cu speciation and catalytic performance during CO2 hydrogenation are investigated. Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Cu, Zn, and Zr K-edges is combined with electron microscopy and density functional theory calculations to follow the evolution of metal species and the framework during reduction, reaction, and transient switching experiments. Zn promotes the formation and stability of highly dispersed Cu under reaction conditions, while the Zr6 nodes of UiO-66 respond dynamically through reversible hydroxylation and dehydroxylation. By correlating metal speciation, framework response, and methanol productivity under continuous-flow conditions, this work provides molecular-level insight into metal stabilization in Zr-based MOFs and informs the design of MOFbased catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation.

papers.title: Organocatalyzed Asymmetric Allylic Alkylation: A key step in the synthesis of spirolactone cycloheptannulated heteroarenes
papers.abstract: A concise three-step strategy provides enantioenriched, densely functionalized cycloheptannulated heteroarenes bearing a spirolactone motif adjacent to a tertiary stereocenter. The sequence begins with racemic α-heteroaromatic γ-butyrolactones, which undergo a microwave-assisted Aromatic Cope rearrangement to afford key α-(allyl)heteroaryl lactone intermediates. A subsequent organocatalytic Allylic Alkylation, leveraging a readily accessible Lewis base, enables the efficient synthesis of chiral lactones with excellent stereoselectivity (dr up to > 99 :1, er up to 99 :1) and good to very good yields (up to 94%). The final Ring-Closing Metathesis step seamlessly constructs the target polycyclic frameworks, demonstrating broad structural versatility.

papers.title: GEOMETRY OF AROMATIC INTERACTIONS IN CRYSTAL STRUCTURES, PART I
papers.abstract: Aromatic interactions are a commonly encountered geometrical feature in crystal structures indicative of a strong adhesion between components. Aromatics Analyser 2 is a program that highlights many types of ring pairs in a crystal structure that have relative positioning consistent with a strong aromatic interaction. The program functions through the CCDC crystal structure visualiser, Mercury, for interactive analysis, and the CSD Python API for large data analysis.

papers.title: Handedness-Switchable Assembly Chirality of Non-Chiral Soft Materials Twisted by Programmable Displaced Quadrupolar Electric and Magnetic Fields: Generation and Modulation of Circularly Polarized Light
papers.abstract: Chiral materials can produce or interact with circularly polarized light, therefore have promising applications in optical communications and displays. Herein, displaced chiral quadrupole electric and magnetic fields possessing mirror asymmetry were generated from eight electrodes or electromagnetic coils arranged in two contrary four-unit groups positioned with reversed spatial displacements. These deviated quadrupolar fields were reversibly switchable between two oppositely twisted mirrored configurations exhibiting chirality of different handedness, where the degrees of chiral twisting could be continuously adjusted by varying the strengths of applied voltages or electrical currents. Orientationally directed assembly of non-chiral responsive soft translucent materials (e.g., nematic liquid crystalline molecules or colloidal superparamagnetic magnetite nanoparticles) in chiral fields resulted in asymmetrically twisted superstructures, which showed macroscopic collective chirality and were swiftly reconfigurable with programmed electrical signals, thus enabling the selective generation and modulation of left- and right-handed circularly polarized light.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review on Green Nanoengineered Smart Plasmonic Nanoparticles for Sensing and Plant Growth Applications
papers.abstract: Phytosynthesized plasmonic nanoparticles (PNP) of Au, Ag, Pt, and Pd, prepared from plant extracts (leaves, stems, flowers, and seeds), provide an eco-friendly, biocompatible, and cost-effective alternative to conventional chemical synthesis methods. These particles exhibit unique optical properties arising from their surface plasmon resonance (SPR), demonstrating applications in sensing, plant growth, and photobiology. This review critically examines recent advances in plant-source-mediated PNP, focusing on their synthesis, applications, and challenges. The mechanistic understanding of green extracts and their role in PNP formation was discussed, followed by characterisation techniques which provide crucial insights into nanoparticle-mediated applications, particularly in environmental and analytical sensing using colourimetric/optical, SERS, and electrochemical/hybrid sensors. Next, phytogenic PNP applications for plant growth via photo-biological processes, including growth enhancement, photosynthetic efficiency, biomass accumulation, abiotic stress tolerance, and ROS management, were addressed. Indeed, with the advancement of technology, PNP synthesised from plant sources has improved in application, though with certain limitations due to various gaps, including lot variability, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and limited long-term stability. Addressing these gaps will enable the safe, sustainable, and impactful integration of phytosynthesized PNP into precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and light-driven biological systems, advancing the goals of green nanotechnology and plant nanobiology.

papers.title: Electrode-Electrolyte Co-Design for Enhanced Alkaline Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: We modified Ni electrodes via rapid galvanic displacement with Pt and Rh and paired each with its reaction-specific optimized electrolyte for alkaline water electrolysis. This approach improves the performance of individual hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions, establishing electrode-electrolyte co-design as a viable strategy to enhance alkaline electrolyzer performance.

papers.title: Resonant Doping in Binary Sb(V)-oxide Sb2O5 for High-Mobility Transparent Conductors
papers.abstract: The development of earth-abundant transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) requires materials that combine high carrier concentrations with minimal degradation of electron mobility. Sb(V)-based oxides have recently emerged as promising candidates owing to their highly dispersive Sb 5 s -derived conduction bands and deep valence-band positions. While degenerate conductivity in Sb 2 O 5 has previously been predicted through anion-site F substitution, the viability of resonant donor engineering on the cation sublattice remains unexplored. Here, using hybrid density functional theory and rigorous defect thermodynamics, we show that W acts as an effective resonant donor dopant when substituted on Sb sites in Sb 2 O 5 , whereas Mo exhibits only weak donor behavior. Both W Sb and Mo Sb exhibit low formation energies under n-type conditions, with W-doped Sb 2 O 5 yielding an electron concentration exceeding 1×10 19 cm -3 while Mo-doping results in a moderate value of around 1 × 10 18 cm -3 . Unfolded band structure analysis reveals that the W 5 d and Mo 4 d donor states reside well above the conduction band minimum and exhibit negligible hybridization with the Sb 5s states that govern transport. This preservation of the dispersive conduction band enables degenerate doping without significant perturbation of band curvature. These results establish resonant cation-site doping as a transferable design strategy in Sb(V)-based oxides and broaden the chemical space for high-mobility, earth-abundant TCOs.

papers.title: 1 A Geometry-Derived Structural Map of Graphite Intercalation Compounds across Chemically Diverse Intercalants
papers.abstract: The diversity of intercalants in graphite intercalation compounds (GICs) has prevented a unified understanding of their structure–composition relationships, leading predominantly to case-by-case interpretations. Here we present a geometry-derived structural map of GICs based solely on constraints of the graphitic host. We derive the local gallery volume Vlocal as defined by gallery height di, staging s, and carbon-tointercalant-ratio x. Analysis of 97 representative compounds—including metal cations, metal–Lewis base complexes, alkylammonium and heterocyclic cations, and a wide range of perfluoroanions—reveals three regimes. In Region I, the expanded di (7.4-14.5 Å) is just above a host-imposed residual separation. The vertical increase of Vlocal is controlled by lateral dilution. In Region II, increasing di up to 28 Å linearly grows the volume. This reflects gallery opening at a constant effective in-plane area Aeff depending on intercalant family. In Region III, intercalants enlarge di further (35 Å) but the volume decreases, ascribed to intercalant conformational flexibility and tight lateral packing. A critical gallery height di* is proposed dividing Region II and III. This host-controlled structural map unifies disparate GIC families without invoking electronic structure calculations or intercalant-specific bonding models. Our work provides a rational basis for comparing existing donor- and acceptor-type GICs and for navigating unexplored intercalation regimes.

papers.title: ReadMOF: Structure-Free Semantic Embeddings from Systematic MOF Nomenclature for Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Systematic chemical names, such as IUPAC-style nomenclature for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), contain rich structural and compositional information in a standardized textual format. Here we introduce ReadMOF, which is, to our knowledge, the first nomenclature-free machine learning framework that leverages these names to model structure-property relationships without requiring atomic coordinates or connectivity graphs. By employing pretrained language models, ReadMOF converts systematic MOF names from the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD) into vector embeddings that closely represent traditional structure-based descriptors. These embeddings enable applications in materials informatics, including property prediction, similarity retrieval, and clustering, with performance comparable to geometry-dependent methods. When combined with large language models, ReadMOF also establishes chemically meaningful reasoning ability with textual input only. Our results show that structured chemical language, interpreted through modern natural language processing techniques, can provide a scalable, interpretable, and geometry-independent alternative to conventional molecular representations. This approach opens new opportunities for language-driven discovery in materials science.

papers.title: Tunable Morphologies of Dried Colloidal Deposits in Graphene Oxide-laden Aqueous Sessile Droplets Mediated by Mesophase Characteristics
papers.abstract: We experimentally report wide-ranging tunability in the sessile droplet desiccation-assisted colloidal deposit morphologies of Graphene Oxide (GO), governed by characteristic mesophases in aqueous medium. Our observations unraveled mesophase-directed distinct regimes of GO-deposit patterns spanning from ring-like to uniform deposits; and within the uniform deposit regime, the morphologies vary from prominent striped to mosaic-like configurations. Experiments revealed that polydispersed GO suspensions with larger average lateral sheet-size (∼ 2.2 µm) but weaker oxidation (C/O=14.4) form orientationally ordered nematic domains, resulting in schlieren-type birefringent textures under crossed polarizers. This characteristic self-assembly subsequently transforms into radially striped morphologies at the end of the droplet lifetime. Alternatively, smaller in average lateral sheet-size (∼ 0.5 µm) but strongly oxidized (C/O=10.4), polydispersed GO colloids selfassemble in lamellar smectic domains as continuous elastic sheets in the aqueous media conforming with the linear smectic elastic framework. Subsequently, it results in uniform deposits with mosaic-like fine-structural morphologies. We also investigated the respective cases of concentration-dependent disordered (isotropic) and ordered phase-driven regimes of ring-like and uniform deposit patterns formed by both aforementioned GO-suspensions. Thus, the GO-structural configurations and suspension concentration independently control the mesophase order of GO in aqueous media and the associated tunability in the dried deposit patterns. The measurements corroborate with theoretical frameworks involving orientational order parameter and smectic elastic response. Lastly, the gained information on the GO-mesophasic characteristics were supported by analyzing their structural response to externally applied shear via rheological characterizations. The nematic phase-forming GO-suspensions exhibit lower apparent viscosity with gentler shear-thinning under steady shear, and show viscous-dominated response to an oscillatory shear. In contrast, the GOaqueous suspensions with smectic-like lamellar stack domains exhibit higher viscosity and steeper shear thinning, with elastic-dominated response to oscillatory shear. This work elucidates the general rules governing the structure-mesophase correlation-driven combined modulation in dried colloidal deposit patterns and flow characteristics of GO, addressing the variability in the deposit patterns and flow characteristics realized across available GO samples of varied structural features. The gained insights are therefore potentially effective in unified understanding of the efficiency of inkjet printing, spray coating processes.

papers.title: Probing the spin state and a putative Ru-Ru bond in a dinuclear Ru(II) complex with X-ray quantum crystallography
papers.abstract: Determining the spin state of the metal complexes is central to understanding the electronic structure and the magnetic properties of materials. Inferring spin states from conventional crystallography is often ambiguous because it is largely limited to detecting geometric variations associated with different spin states. In this study, X-ray quantum crystallography (QCr) is employed to determine the spin state of a dinuclear ruthenium (II) complex by comparatively analyzing restricted and unrestricted wavefunctions fitted to high-resolution X-ray diffraction data. QCr models obtained from Hirshfeld Atom Refinement (HAR) and Xray constrained wavefunction (XCW) fitting at different spin multiplicities indicate that the ruthenium centers adopt a low-spin state consistent with the electronic configuration of Ru(II), which is further corroborated by NMR spectroscopy. Additionally, electron density and bond-order analyses of the putative Ru–Ru bond based on the X-ray-derived wavefunction reveal the absence of bonding features between the Ru centers, in contrast to the single bond expected from conventional electron-counting methods.

papers.title: Macrocyclic Parallel Rubrene Dimers for Room-Temperature Optically Addressable Quintet Spin Qudits
papers.abstract: Electron spins in molecules offer chemically tunable qubits that can be optically initialized and readout at room temperature, while high-spin states enable multilevel quantum operations and enhanced coupling to external quantities. Quintet spins generated through singlet fission are therefore attractive as optically addressable multilevel qubits, qudits, yet their realization under ambient conditions has remained elusive due to the lack of modular molecular designs for prolonged spin coherence and optical readout. Here we demonstrate a synthetically modular rubrene-based macrocyclic parallel dimer that integrates these requirements. Structural constraints suppress angular fluctuations of specific molecular axes, affording sublevel-selective and angle-robust quintet spin coherence times up to 315 ns at room temperature. In addition, optically detected magnetic resonance measurements reveal optical readout of quintet spins at room temperature. These results establish synthetically modular macrocyclic parallel molecular architectures as a versatile platform for roomtemperature, optically addressable spin qudits.

papers.title: Assessing the Potential for Galvanic Corrosion of TRISO Fuel
papers.abstract: TRi-structural ISOtropic (TRISO) particle fuel is an attractive advanced fuel type due to its improved fissionproduct retention and mechanical and thermal stability. Several investigations have confirmed the high performance of TRISO fuel under reactor operation and safety-testing conditions; however, the fuel’s degradation mechanisms and pathways under disposal repository conditions are poorly understood. Particularly underexplored is the possibility of galvanic corrosion of the uranium ceramic fuel kernel coupled to the significant amounts of graphite within the fuel layers and matrices. Herein, we report the first approach to evaluating galvanic corrosion of TRISO fuel by studying the macroscale electrochemical behaviour of UO2 and nuclear-grade graphite. The macroscale electrochemistry of nuclear-grade graphite was found to be somewhat complex, complicating electrochemical analysis; however, we show that glassy carbon is a reasonable proxy. Of the relevant radiolysis oxidants explored—O2, H2O2, NaClO, NaNO3, and NaNO2—only O2, H2O2, and NaClO may drive galvanic corrosion.

papers.title: S-Adenosyl-L-homocysteine Hydrolase Side Reactivity Enables Biocatalytic Access to 4′,5′-Dehydro Nucleosides as Nucleoside Drug Precursors
papers.abstract: S-Adenosyl-L-homocysteine hydrolase (SAHH) reversibly cleaves S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH) into adenosine and L-homocysteine, regulating the cellular potential to perform S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM)-dependent methylation of DNA, RNA, proteins, and small molecules. Another route of SAH metabolism involves the deamination to S-inosyl-L-homocysteine (SIH) followed by degradation to L-homocysteine and inosine catalyzed by Sinosyl-L-homocysteine hydrolase (SIHH). SAHHs have long been studied as regulators of cellular methylation potential, making them attractive targets for antimicrobial, antiviral, and anticancer drug development. In this study, we elucidate the often-reported co-detection of the nucleobases adenine and hypoxanthine in acidquenched in vitro experiments testing SAHHs and SIHHs. This finding highlights a reaction mechanism previously established for adenosine and demonstrates that it can also be applied to inosine, an aspect that has been rarely recognized. Intermediates formed during a dehydratase-like reaction catalyzed by SAHHs and SIHHs were detected by LC-MS/MS. Isolation of these intermediates enabled structural analysis by NMR spectroscopy and their identification as 4′,5′-dehydro nucleosides, as well as systematic assessment of their stability toward pH‑dependent depurination. The dehydratase-like reactivity of SAHHs and SIHHs can be repurposed and utilized in scaled-up reactions to efficiently produce 4′,5′-dehydro adenosine and 4′,5′-dehydro inosine. In addition, nonnatural nucleoside substrates were converted to the respective 4′,5′-dehydro nucleoside analogues. We propose that the SAHH- and SIHH-catalyzed dehydration reaction offers a straightforward strategy for the enzymatic synthesis of diverse 4′,5′-dehydro nucleosides as valuable precursors for chemical functionalization yielding 4′- or 5′-substituted nucleoside drug candidates.

papers.title: 1,2,3-Triazole Bridged Binuclear Iridium Pincer Complexes: Comparing Reactivities with Monometallic Analogues
papers.abstract: Binuclear iridium-pincer complexes bearing metal centres with different coordination spheres could provide a promising platform for new reactivities and enable cooperative catalytic properties. Herein, we report the synthesis of the Ir(III)−Ir(III) pincer complexes [( t Bu POCN 3 N 2 CO t Bu P)Ir 2 (H) 2 (acac) 2 ] ( 3b ) and [CF 3 −( t Bu POCN 3 N 2 CO t Bu P)Ir 2 (H) 2 (µ-OAc)(µ-Cl)] ( 4b ). For each complex, a bridging 1,2,3-triazole scaffold in the ligand framework allows for two distinctive Ir-POCN pincer moieties, one having an Ir−N 3 bond and the other fragment with a hemi-labile Ir−N 2 coordination. Comparative studies on the structures, reactivity and catalytic transfer dehydrogenation activity of these complexes with the reactivity of their monomeric analogues − the previously reported [( t Bu POCN 3 Triaz )Ir(H)(acac)] ( 1b ) and independently synthesised [( t Bu POCN 2 Triaz )Ir(H)(acac)] ( 2b ) − are further described. While subsequent reactivity of the mononuclear complexes with CO affords the Ir(I) monocarbonyl complexes, the binuclear complexes instead result in mixed valent Ir(I)−Ir(III) tricarbonyl species. The described binuclear complexes and their reactivity products are the original examples of systems containing non-identical iridium pincers within the same framework.

papers.title: pH-Inverted Histidine-Rich Nanochelant 5H-EAF for Electrostatic Dust Mitigation and Cation Detoxification in Lunar Regolith: Enabling Lightweight In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) for Artemis Missions
Navigating the Concept of Digital Twin in Electrochemical Energy Devices
papers.abstract: Currently, there is considerable excitement surrounding the potential of Digital Twins (DTs) for electrochemical energy devices; however, there is also significant ambiguity regarding the DT term itself. Often, it is confused with a standard mathematical model, which is simply a digital representation of a physical system. In this Perspective article, we aim to provide a unified definition of a DT. We clarify that a true DT requires real-time, automated, and bidirectional interaction between the physical system and its digital counterpart. We then explore how this concept has evolved in various fields, focusing specifically on the battery field, including battery management systems, self-driving laboratories for battery material synthesis, and battery manufacturing. Finally, we discuss how advances in artificial intelligence can help revolutionize DT development for the accelerated design and optimization of electrochemical energy devices.

papers.title: From Waste to High-Value: Red Mud/Hydroxypropyl Cellulose Composites as Cost-Effective Platinum-Alternative Electrocatalyst for Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
papers.abstract: This study explores the high-value utilization of industrial waste red mud (RM) by combining it with biomass-derived hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) to fabricate RM/HPC composites for use as electrocatalyst in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSCs). The composites were prepared via high-temperature treatment under a nitrogen atmosphere. Extensive characterization—including SEM, TEM, XRD, Raman, XPS, EPR, hysteresis loop, synchrotron radiation, and photoelectrochemical measurements—reveal that the optimal material, RM/HPC(1/1)-800 (1:1 mass ratio treated at 800 °C), possesses a hierarchical structure and magnetic properties. Notably, the Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ ratio increased to 1.87. Electrochemical results demonstrate that the RM/HPC(1/1)-800 electrode exhibits exchange current density and charge-transfer resistance comparable to those of noble Pt electrode, along with excellent electrocatalytic activity and reversibility toward the I⁻/I₃⁻ redox couple. In the device testing, the DSCs of the electrodes using RM/HPC(1/1)-800 achieved a high power conversion efficiency, which was comparable to that of the DSCs based on Pt electrodes. This work demonstrates a promising strategy for transforming industrial waste into efficient, low-cost electrode materials for high-performance DSCs.

papers.title: Designing Charge Carrier and Exciton Dynamics for Efficient Organic Long-Persistent Luminescence
papers.abstract: Organic long-persistent luminescence (OLPL) relies on the generation and storage of charges that later recombine to produce delayed emission. Efficient OLPL, therefore, requires simultaneous control of charge separation, long-lived charge retention, and emissive charge recombination, which makes rational material design difficult. Here, we analyze the individual steps of the OLPL mechanism to understand how each process contributes to persistent emission and how they can be combined to achieve a highly performing OLPL. We show that tuning the molecular orbitals of constituent molecules controls charge generation, charge retention, and the energy of the intermolecular charge-transfer (CT) excited states, whereas the alignment of intermolecular CT and locally excited (LE) states determines whether recombination produces weak CT or bright LE emission. Based on this understanding, we combined CT-mediated charge generation with trapassisted charge retention and achieved bright LPL through LE–CT hybridization. Here, we provide a practical route for identifying and optimizing materials suitable for efficient, air-stable, and color-tunable OLPL.

papers.title: Data-driven critical evaluation of the General Solubility Equation: When is it a valid solubility predictor for Drug-like Molecules?
papers.abstract: Solubility is a widely measured physicochemical property and a highly sought-after descriptor in the evaluation 16 of molecules for drug design and development, medicinal chemistry, and agrochemical sciences. Consequently, a 17 wide range of in-silico models based on deductive and inductive reasoning have been developed. However, the 18 General Solubility Equation (GSE) stands out as a simple, thermodynamically derived equation to predict intrinsic 19 solubility (log S0, in mol/L) of molecules from their melting point and n-octanol/water partition coefficient (logPN). 20 Despite its widespread use, the applicability of this equation has not been rigorously evaluated to establish when 21 it can or cannot produce accurate predictions. Therefore, a large-scale evaluation of the GSE was conducted using 22 an extensive database of fully experimental melting point and logPN data for 2740, mostly drug-like compounds. 23 A systematic analysis based on cheminformatics descriptors was conducted to identify the primary factors that 24 allow the GSE to achieve predictions within the experimental uncertainty range (±1 log S unit). This information 25 has been used to create GSESolver: a supervised machine learning classification model that, based on the selected 26 descriptors, can predict whether the GSE will perform accurately solely from its SMILES string. GSESolver tool 27 can be used by anyone in the scientific community to quickly assess molecules solubility which was developed 28 under the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) in a Google Colab notebook to 29 ensure ease of use. Finally, the utility of GSESolver tool was exploited in medicinal chemistry applications for the 30 in-silico prediction of the Maximum Absorbable Dose (MAD) of potential drugs, and in a rational agrochemical 31 design application where solubility is a key factor. 32

papers.title: Unlocking coordination chemistry and photocatalytic activity of Mn(IV) complexes with 1,4,6,10-tetraazaadamantane-based tris-hydroxylamine ligand TAAD
papers.abstract: Manganese(IV) species play an essential role in natural photoredox processes, making the development of artificial biomimetic catalysts a promising goal, which is, however, complicated by the lack of stable and soluble Mn(IV) complexes. Cyclic tris(hydroxylamine) ligands were recently shown to stabilize atypical +4 oxidation states for a variety of 3d metals due to a strong σ-donating ability of three deprotonated N–OH moieties. Here, we report a comprehensive study of manganese coordination chemistry with the 1,4,6,10-tetraazaadamantane-based tris(hydroxylamine) ligand (TAAD). A series of mono- and dinuclear Mn(IV)–TAAD complexes were obtained and studied by SC-XRD analysis, HRMS, NMR (Evans method), UV–Vis spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, and DFT calculations. The TAAD ligand was found to stabilize [Mn2(μ-OR)3]-dimeric motifs uncommon in Mn(IV) chemistry. These dinuclear motifs were shown to disassemble into mononuclear species upon treatment with chelating N-ligands. Mononuclear Mn(IV)–TAAD complexes exhibited photocatalytic activity in the oxidative azidation/ring-opening of 1-phenylcyclohexene with TMSN3 and molecular oxygen.

papers.title: A widely used C-Reactive Protein aptamer does not bind C-Reactive Protein in solution, suggesting potential streptavidin-driven artifacts in biosensors
papers.abstract: Aptamer sequences are often reused in diagnostics without independent confirmation of binding activity, although rigorous validation requires quantitative solution-phase testing by orthogonal methods. Here, we re-examined a DNA sequence reported in 2010 to bind C-reactive protein (CRP) with a Kd of 3.5 nM by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) that has since been adopted in many CRP aptasensors. We tested this sequence by two orthogonal solution-phase methods, each in direct and competitive formats, with a validated CRP-binding SOMAmer tracer in the competitive assays. In all four assay configurations, we found no detectable binding of the reported aptamer to native CRP, consistent with a Kd well above the micromolar range. Reproducing the original SPR format showed that CRP binds strongly to streptavidin/dextran surfaces even without immobilized DNA, whereas immobilization of the reported sequence did not measurably change the response. Thus, the originally reported affinity is best explained by a surface-driven artifact rather than true aptamer-CRP recognition. More broadly, because streptavidin is widely used to immobilize biotinylated DNA and may adsorb abundant serum proteins nonspecifically, many streptavidin-based aptasensors may be vulnerable to surface-driven artifacts in complex clinical matrices. This case underscores the need for orthogonal solution-phase validation before aptamers are reused in analytical or diagnostic applications.

papers.title: Energy transfer pathways in plant Photosystem I from first-principles modeling
papers.abstract: The photosynthetic supercomplex Photosystem I–light harvesting complex I (PSI-LHCI) of plants is a molecular machine involved in energy conversion. Concentration of energy in the PSI reaction center is strikingly efficient, despite the unusual presence of low-energy, trapping states (red forms) spatially far from the reaction center. The main energy transfer processes occurring in PSI-LHCI are still unclear, as the size and complexity of the system prevent immediate interpretation of spectroscopic signals and challenges traditional modeling approaches. Here we present a multiscale quantum chemical model able to characterize the exciton structure of the full Chlorophyll aggregate in plant PSI-LHCI, including the red forms. The calculation of transfer rates between all pigments allows us to simulate population decay upon different initial conditions, and to ultimately identify the most relevant pathways at molecular resolution. The timescales associated to such pathways closely match the ones extracted from experiments, demonstrating the effectiveness of a quantum mechanical description. This analysis allows us to quantify the role of red forms in the energy transfer, and to reveal the design strategies for efficient light harvesting in plants.

papers.title: Do humans and large language models agree on the quality of synthesis plans?
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have seen a widespread adoption in all spheres of science including chemistry and cheminformatics. Nevertheless, our knowledge of how they operate is limited, giving rise to exploration of their capabilities in different areas of science and different operation modes. Here, we investigated whether LLMs could mimic human experts on the challenging task of assessing retrosynthetic path feasibility in routes generated by a popular computer-aided synthesis planning tool (AiZynthFinder). We evaluated the agreement between LLMs and expert chemists on holistic evaluations of the proposed routes as well as the individual chemical reactions in them. We used four frontier LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4.1, GPT-o3, and Gemini 2.5 Pro) and employed 17 expert chemists to grade 50 retrosynthetic paths. We found out that when instructed with clear possible categories for the evaluation of a given reaction in a retrosynthetic tree, human experts tend to converge in their opinions. Another important finding was that Gemini 2.5 Pro performs remarkably well out of all the LLMs explored, GPT-o3 tends to be more pessimistic, and Claude and GPT-4.1 tend to be overly optimistic when compared to the majority vote of human experts.

papers.title: Universal Scaling and Many-Body Resurrection of Polaritonic Double-Quantum Coherences
Stochastic Difference-Dedicated Configuration Interaction for Magnetic Exchange in Large Active Spaces
papers.abstract: The simulation of magnetic properties in strongly correlated systems remains a central challenge in electronic structure theory. The Difference-Dedicated Configuration Interaction (DDCI) method is widely regarded as a gold standard for computing magnetic exchange couplings, but its applicability is limited to small magnetic systems due to the steep growth of the configuration-interaction space with the number of correlated electrons. Here we introduce a stochastic formulation of DDCI based on full configuration interaction quantum Monte Carlo and the generalized active space framework, which largely alleviates the computational bottleneck of conventional DDCI. The implementation is validated by comparison with conventional DDCI for the spin ladder of a trinuclear [Mn(IV) 3 O 4 ] 3+ cluster (S local = 3/2). Using a small CAS(9,9) reference, DDCI fails to reproduce the spin-state energy differences defined by a two-parameter (J=−76, J’=−11cm −1 ) Heisenberg–Dirac–van Vleck Hamiltonian extracted from experimental measurements. In contrast, Stochastic-DDCI enables calculations with a much larger CAS(33,21) reference and reproduces the experimental spin ladder with remarkable accuracy, yielding deviations smaller than 33cm −1 with respect to the spin ladder extracted from the experimental measurements. This development extends DDCI methodologies to substantially larger active spaces and opens the door to the study of more complex magnetic systems.

papers.title: A Single Active-Site Water Molecule Encodes Two Distinct Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer Pathways in Fatty Acid Photodecarboxylase
papers.abstract: Active-site water molecules are increasingly recognized as functionally involved species in enzymatic proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), yet whether a single water molecule can support distinct catalytic roles within the same active site remains poorly understood. Here, using a multiscale computational approach we show that a previously unidentified water molecule (denoted here Wat3) in fatty acid photodecarboxylase (FAP), a natural photenzyme that converts fatty acids into alkanes, mediates radical quenching via two mechanistically distinct PCET pathways. In the lower-barrier pathway (∆A ‡ ≈ 23 kJ·mol -1 ), Wat3 acts as a hydrogen-bond donor, stabilizing the transition state of a direct proton transfer from cysteine C432 to the alkyl radical (water-assisted PCET). In an alternative, higher-barrier pathway (∆A ‡ ≈ 42 kJ·mol -1 ), the same water molecule acts as a proton shuttle, relaying the proton from C432 to the radical in a quasi-concerted two-proton transfer (water-relay PCET). In both scenarios, the flavin semiquinone provides the electron. The water-assisted route dominates the kinetics under ambient conditions and is consistent with the experimentally measured ∼100 ns timescale. The water-relay pathway, though less accessible in FAP, represents a mechanistic alternative that may become operative in engineered variants or in other enzymes. Additionally, we characterize the fate of the CO 2 coproduct, showing that it reacts with the nascent cysteine thiolate to form a transient thiocarbonate adduct, providing a structural interpretation of previously unassigned electron density in crystallographic data. These findings highlight the ability of a single active-site water molecule to modulate radical PCET through distinct functional roles, with implications for understanding and engineering light-driven biocatalysts.

papers.title: Computational Prediction of Moiré Superlattice Engineering in Magic-Angle Twisted Bilayer Graphene: A Literature-Validated Framework for Molecular Filtration and Electrochemical Applications
papers.abstract: We present a literature-validated computational framework for magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) heterostructures at θ = 1.05° ± 0.05° investigating two potential room-temperature applications through synergistic moiré engineering. The framework employs density functional theory (DFT-D3 with VASP 6.3.0, 600 eV cutoff, 18×18×1 k-mesh for ~15,500-atom supercell), molecular dynamics (LAMMPS with AIREBO/TIP4P/2005, 50 ns production), and grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations validated against 18 peer-reviewed experimental studies. For molecular filtration, we predict water flux 180-450 L/m²/h at 2-10 bar with >99.5% NaCl rejection through precision nanopores (3.0 ± 0.1 Å diameter, 10¹²-10¹³ pores/cm²) positioned at AA stacking sites with 13.4 nm moiré periodicity-representing 2.7-6.8× flux enhancement versus single-layer graphene literature baseline (66 L/m²/h per bar). For electrochemical energy storage, calculated 153× density of states enhancement (147 ± 15 states/(eV•cell) versus 0.96 for pristine graphene) produces quantum capacitance CQ ≈ 535 µF/cm², enabling predicted specific capacitance >300 F/g-representing conservative 1.2-1.5× enhancement over activated carbon supercapacitors (150-250 F/g) with simultaneous high energy density (50-90 Wh/kg) and power density (10-15 kW/kg). Complete experimental protocols disclosed for independent verification: CVD synthesis (1030°C, CH₄/H₂), angular alignment (±0.03° precision via crossed polarizers or ±0.05° via machine vision), electron beam nanopore drilling (STEM, 80-120 keV, controlled dwell), and performance characterization (ASTM E2550-17, IEC 62391-1). This computational methodology establishes a conservative framework for translating magic-angle TBG physics from cryogenic quantum phenomena into functional roomtemperature applications, with all predictions anchored to experimental literature benchmarks.

papers.title: Catalyst-free hydrophosphination of alkenes enabled by protic solvents
papers.abstract: Under catalyst-free conditions, activated olefins are subject to hydrophosphination in Click-like efficiency unexpectedly in polar protic (alcohol) solvent. Hydrophosphination of more challenging styrene substrates can be achieved in polar protic solvents as well under irradiation. While the former reaction is apparent conjugate addition, the latter is still under consideration.

papers.title: Sculpting the Pores of a Metal–Organic Framework to Enhance Mixture Separation: An Illustrative Study based on Xe/Kr Separation
papers.abstract: Postsynthetic modification (PSM) of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is an attractive approach for enhancing functionality and boosting performance of these nanoporous materials. Often PSM relies on elaboration of either metal nodes or organic linkers of candidate MOFs. Herein, we introduce an alternative approach, sculpting the pores of a zirconium-based MOF, NU-903, with a size-matching Keggin polyoxometalate (POM) and apply the approach to separation of Xe/Kr mixtures as a test application. The computationally optimized structure of POM@NU-903 showed that the original 3-dimensional pore network was sculpted to a 2-dimensional pore. Although the pore volume decreased by 20%, Xe and Kr uptake capacities were nearly doubled at 298 K and 1 bar, with significantly boosted selectivity and heat of adsorption. Given the agreement between computational and experimental results and the great variety of MOFs and POMs, we envision a sizable library of pore-sculpted MOFs for demonstration and optimization of desired chemical separations.

papers.title: One-pot synthesis of functionalised coumarin fluorophores enables rapid access to live cell bioorthogonal labelling and microenvironmental sensing agents
papers.abstract: Coumarins are robust and versatile organic scaffolds, with broad applications in fluorescence imaging. Herein, we report a one-pot methodology to functionalised coumarins from commercially available and readily accessible intermediates. Using this streamlined approach, we synthesised a library of 7-aminocoumarins with diverse substituents and varied photophysical properties in good yields and on gram scale. To demonstrate the versatility of this methodology, we developed two functional imaging agents: CouPyC6, a mitochondrially targeted viscosity sensor for fluorescence intensity and lifetime imaging, and CouTz, the first zero-distance tetrazinyl-coumarin which can participate in fluorogenic IEDDA reactions with a range of dienophiles. The latter enables wash free, real-time bioorthogonal imaging of labelled proteins and glycan targets on the surface of live cells, offering simple access to functional coumarins for advanced imaging applications.

papers.title: Visible-Light-Mediated Aryl Ketone Coupling with Vinyl Thianthrenium Salts Enables Formal Paternò-Büchi Reactions
papers.abstract: Oxetanes are valuable motifs in drug discovery, yet their synthesis from native functional groups remains challenging. The Paternò-Büchi reaction offers a direct approach by oxetane construction from alkenes and carbonyls. However, under visible- light condi-tions this platform remains limited by the high triplet energies of common carbonyls. We report a ketone-alkene coupling strategy that achieves formal Paternò-Büchi reactivity relying on the design principle of alkene radical anion formation from vinyl thi-anthrenium salts. Selective olefin reduction decouples reactivity from carbonyl redox properties, enabling the construction of 2-aryl, 2’-alkyl oxetanes that would otherwise be inaccessible by visible-light-mediated [2+2]-cycloadditions. Initial formation of β-hydroxy thianthrenium intermediates is followed by a subsequent cyclization to give 2,2’-disubstituted oxetanes under mild, visible light-enabled conditions. This approach enables a general blueprint for visible-light-mediated oxetane synthesis beyond the limitations of traditional Paternò-Büchi photochemistry.

papers.title: AlarmLM: A decoder-only transformer for industrial alarm sequence modeling — from Markov transition matrices to learned attention
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a framework that treats industrial alarm sequences as a formal language and applies a decoder-only transformer architecture (AlarmLM) to learn their temporal grammar. Each alarm event is encoded as a token, with time intervals discretized into temporal gap tokens, enabling the model to learn both the causal structure and the characteristic timing of alarm cascades. The approach is validated on two datasets: the ALPI industrial packaging alarm logs (444,834 events, 154 alarm types, 20 machines) and the Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP) benchmark, where alarm events are generated from process variable thresholds. On ALPI, AlarmLM achieves 54.2% next-alarm prediction accuracy versus 16.9% for bigram baselines — a 3.2x improvement. On TEP, a novelty detection approach is introduced: the model is trained exclusively on normal operation sequences and fault detection is performed by measuring sequence perplexity. This strategy detects 10 out of 18 fault types (56%) with perplexity ratios up to 6.62x relative to normal baseline, without any fault-specific supervision. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the transformer's self-attention weights can be extracted and aggregated into a learned alarm transition matrix structurally equivalent to the HAZOP-derived Markov matrix proposed by Larraz (2007), but computed automatically from operational data and capturing higher-order dependencies. The complete framework requires only 350,000 parameters and trains in minutes on a single GPU.

papers.title: Alternative mechanisms for fullerene growth: the spiral of “stick”, “handle”, and “horn” intermediates
papers.abstract: Traditionally, fullerene growth is considered to proceed via C2 insertion. Based on theoretical calculations, this study proposes a novel mechanism for fullerene growth that involves the classical “stick” and “handle” intermediates as well as the “horn” intermediate introduced herein. A comparison with the reaction energy barrier of the traditional C2 direct insertion mechanism indicates that the growth mechanism proposed in this work is a competitive pathway to the traditional C2 insertion mechanism, and this new mechanism is further extended to fullerene derivatization. Furthermore, this work also investigates the C4 insertion mechanism and proposes a possible formation pathway for C3v(1911)-C64.

papers.title: 2-Alkyl Furans Undergo Radiolytic Crosslinking
papers.abstract: Induced covalent bond formation, or crosslinking, is a powerful strategy for interrogating and modulating biological systems. Current strategies rely largely on photochemical processes, which generally restrict their use to cellular or other optically accessible settings. Broadening the chemistry underlying the crosslinking-initiating event could extend these approaches to more complex biological systems. Ionizing radiation - a cornerstone of cancer therapy – is an attractive but unexplored trigger for covalent chemistry. Here, we detail the systematic comparison of a series of rationally designed radiolytic crosslinking candidates. These studies reveal that 2-alkyl furans efficiently label a representative protein in a radiation dose-dependent manner. Mechanistic analyses suggest that radiolysis induces hydroxyl radical–mediated oxidation of the furan, generating an electrophilic dicarbonyl intermediate that reacts with lysine residues. We apply this strategy to enforce the covalent capture of an otherwise reversible small-molecule–protein interactions in cells. Together, these findings establish ionizing radiation as an effective trigger for covalent chemistry, expanding the scope of radiolytic chemistry to include bond formation. This work provides a foundation for future applications leveraging spatially targeted radiation for target identification or the development of next-generation therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: VortexNet: Emergent Topological Phase Singularities from Learned Unitary Wave Dynamics on Molecular Representations
papers.abstract: We introduce VortexNet, a complex-valued neural architecture that encodes molecular features into a Hilbert space and evolves them under a learned unitary Hamil-tonian augmented with Gross–Pitaevskii nonlinearity. We demonstrate that this process spontaneously generates topological phase singularities—vortices with integer-valued winding numbers—constituting a new class of emergent molecular descriptors. These topological invariants are discrete, noise-robust, and arise naturally from the learned dynamics rather than from manual feature engineering. Through three architectural generations (V1–V3), we show that transitioning from a closed to an open quantum system formulation enables the emergent physics features to carry independent predictive signal (1.2–1.8% ablation gap), and that a dual-head prediction architecture prevents the raw wave state from overwhelming the topological features. We validate the framework on three MoleculeNet regression benchmarks under a rigorous scaffold-split, multi-restart protocol, achieving competitive performance with only ∼66K parameters—two orders of magnitude smaller than pretrained approaches—while providing physically interpretable, topologically protected descriptors fundamentally unavailable in graph neural networks.

papers.title: Thickness-Dependent Transport Control in Polymer Conformal Coatings for Electrochemical Corrosion Suppression
papers.abstract: Thickness-dependent corrosion suppression in polymer conformal coatings is governed by transport limited reaction rather than geometric barrier effects alone. This study establishes a processing-structure-property correlation for a UV-cured solvent-free acrylate–urethane and a moisturecured solvent-borne modified acrylate applied on Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold plated copper (ENIG–Cu) under biased chloride exposure. Integrated electrochemical, dissolution, and microstructural analyses reveal a strong linear increase in polarization resistance with critical thickness and R2 > 0.9, indicating diffusion-length-controlled enhancement of transport resistance. The densely crosslinked UV-cured network achieves effective suppression at lower thickness, whereas the solvent-borne system requires greater thickness due to higher microstructural heterogeneity. Interfacial elemental mapping confirms that corrosion initiation in thin films originates from chloride-assisted activation at the buried interface, while thicker coatings suppress ion accumulation and exhibit stable dielectric behaviour. These results provide quantitative guidance for thickness optimization in polymerbased corrosion protection systems.

papers.title: Is a bit over okay?–Overcomplete sets of localized molecular orbitals
papers.abstract: Quantum chemical bases are mostly linearly independent, whether orthonormal or not. However, in certain applications, using an overcomplete set of functions, not forming a basis in the strict sense offers distinct advantages. Localized molecular orbitals (LMO) projected from atomic orbitals (PAO) are a primary example. Use of redundant LMOs is facilitated by the mathematical theory of frames. Along with a systematic presentation of the necessary background, it is shown that the trace of one-electron operators can be obtained by a formula analogous to the orthonormal case. For instance, the electronic dipole moment can be expressed as a sum of frame LMO centroids multiplied by their fractional populations as weights. An advantage of frame LMOs is demonstrated when following reaction coordinates. When a system passes through a high-symmetry point between lower-symmetry arrangements, orthogonal LMOs often exhibit abrupt changes. This occurs when a specific set of localized orbitals does not represent the molecular point group of the highsymmetry structure, resulting in equivalent sets of orthogonal LMOs that may induce discontinuities in LMO based quantities. It is shown that PAO related frame LMOs transition smoothly in these scenarios, without any extra algorithmic effort.

papers.title: Viscosity-insensitive and Membrane Potential Independent Mitochondria Specific Bright Near Infrared Fluorescent Probe
papers.abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent probes are extremely beneficial for visualizing organelle structure and dynamics, due to the minimal autofluorescence, cell damage, low phototoxicity, and excellent photostability. There are dozens of probes available to image mitochondria, one of the most important organelles in mammalian cells. However, most of the available probes are either dependent on mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) or are often affected by the local viscosity due to mitochondrial dysfunction. Herein, we report a cyanine-based NIR fluorescent probe (Cy-D) bearing a long hydrophobic C 10 alkyl chain, both for MMP and viscosity-independent efficient mitochondrial staining. The probe exhibits good quantum yield, low toxicity, and excellent photostability inside the cellular environment. Our findings demonstrate that Cy-D is a robust probe to stain mitochondria with very high specificity both in plants and mammalian cells, even under highly stressed conditions.

papers.title: A Room Full of Experts, None of Them Human: Multi-Agent AI as Virtual Research Teams
papers.abstract: Scientific progress has historically depended on collaboration. For the first time, some collaborators may be non-human. Multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) systems operate as teams of specialised digital scientists addressing shared challenges. Instead of relying on a single model, these systems integrate multiple AI agents, each assigned distinct roles, perspectives, or reasoning strategies. Agents generate proposals, critique one another’s suggestions, and iteratively refine solutions through both collaboration and competition. Advancement arises from the interaction of diverse viewpoints and the exchange of ideas, rather than from a single insight.

papers.title: Trigonal planar crystal field to approach the limit of Ytterbium(III) magnetic anisotropy
papers.abstract: We report the archetypal representatives of single-molecule magnets (SMMs) based on the “most prolate” lanthanide ion: Yb(BHT)3 (1) and Yb(DBP)3 (2) (BHT = 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenolate, DBP = 2,6-di-tert-butylphenolate). The coordination sphere of the metal center was designed to accommodate only three aryloxide ligands yielding highly symmetric nearly trigonal planar geometry which maximizes the magnetic anisotropy associated with the prolate character of the mJ = |7/2| of YbIII. Detailed magnetic and optical studies combined with cantilever torque magnetometry measurements and ab initio calculations, unambiguously unravel the giant magnetic easy axis anisotropy, with the easy magnetization axis perpendicular to the trigonal coordination plane. Our results highlight an exceptional magnetic splitting of the 2F7/2 state (> 1500 cm-1), close to the maximum theoretical value, as well as extremely pure composition of the wavefunction describing each Kramers doublets (KD). This best possible electrostatic environment for the stabilization of the prolate f-electron density does not favour Orbach relaxation, but rather a Raman relaxation process. Nevertheless, the low temperature emission spectra demonstrate that the very strong YbIII anisotropy indeed induces an extremely rare and strong splitting of the 2F7/2 KD in both compounds, as the near infra-red (IR) emissions arising from radiative deexcitation toward the 2F7/2 ground state span over 1695 (1) and 1573 cm−1 (2) at 4 K. Based on this observation, a direct link between the YbIII position with respect to the trigonal coordination environment created by the oxygen atoms and the IR emission can be drawn in solid-state, but also in solution. This allows for going well beyond the crystal structure determination and provides hints about the geometry of such systems in solution.

papers.title: Discovery and Investigation of Novel Perand Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Degrading Enzymes through Metagenomic Mining
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are highly persistent fluorinated chemicals linked to widespread environmental contamination and elevated cancer risk. Its ongoing contamination of Indian water sources(such as the ganga river) raises a national issue. Their exceptional stability arises from strong C–F bonds, making biodegradation challenging. Fluoroacetate dehalogenases (FAcD) can cleave monofluorinated substrates through an SN2 mechanism, but steric and electronic barriers limit activity against larger PFAS, and the lack of known homologs constrains their potential. This study aimed to identify novel FAcD homologs with enhanced catalytic versatility by mining metagenomic datasets. Fifty-one environmental samples were assembled into MAGs (Metagenome Assembled Genomes) using standard protocols, annotated using Bakta, and converted into 1024-dimensional ProtTrans embeddings. An XGBoost classifier trained on known dehalogenases screened candidate proteins. Of 583 proteins scoring above 0.9, conserved-motif filtering via BlastP and catalytic site analysis using fPocket narrowed the set to 20 novel proteins, three annotated as Epoxide Hydrolases. Site-specific docking using AutoDock4 against 20 representative PFAS ligands showed that novel receptors exhibited a mean binding affinity of –7.23 kcal/mol versus –6.38 kcal/mol for reference proteins. About 25.5% of the novel proteins demonstrated strong binding (≤ –8 kcal/mol), nearly double the proportion in 249 reference sequences (13.8%). A correlation between pocket volume and binding affinity indicated increased binding strength for pockets between 400–800 Å3. This study identifies 20 novel proteins with catalytic potential toward PFAS degradation, with findings suggesting a previously unrecognized role of Epoxide Hydrolases in PFAS chemistry.

papers.title: High-Fidelity Transfer of Chiral Sulfoximine Radicals
papers.abstract: Radicals with intrinsic stereogenic and radical centers offer a promising yet largely unexplored platform for synthetic chemistry. We reported a family of chiral sulfonimidoyl radicals that enable stereoretentive radical transfer by using our bench-stable reagents. This approach unlocked switchable, modular access to enantioenriched sulfoximines or sulfinamides, avoiding the use of strong oxidants and organometallic nucleophiles. Additionally, mechanistic studies and computational investigations provide insightful and plausible explanations for the observed high-fidelity of these underexplored chiral sulfonimidoyl radical species.

papers.title: Understanding CO2/N2 adsorption and selectivity in Aluminum Formate MOF through a multiscale modeling approach.
papers.abstract: The efficient separation of CO2 from N2 in post-combustion flue gas streams remains a critical challenge for carbon-capture technologies. Adsorption-based separation using porous materials offers a promising alternative to conventional solvent-based processes, particularly when adsorbents exhibit high CO2 selectivity and thermal stability. In this study, we present a comprehensive multiscale computational investigation of CO2 and N2 adsorption in aluminum formate, Al(HCOO)3 (ALF), an earth-abundant metal–organic framework characterized by ultramicroporous channels. Grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations were employed to predict the adsorption isotherms and CO2/N2 selectivity, whereas classical density functional theory (cDFT) calculations provided independent statistical mechanical validation. Periodic quantum mechanical calculations were used to identify the preferred adsorption sites, complemented by electron localization function (ELF) analysis to elucidate the electronic origin of the host–guest interactions. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations probed the thermal stability and dynamic behavior of adsorbed gas molecules. Across all length and time scales, ALF demonstrates a pronounced preference for CO2 over N2, arising from ultramicropore confinement, electrostatic interactions, and favorable charge redistribution. The consistent agreement among all methods establishes a robust picture of CO2/N2 separation in ALF and highlights the effectiveness of simple formate-based MOFs for energy-efficient carbon-capture.

papers.title: Comparison of the Relative Homodimer Binding Energies of the Canonical Nucleobases, Nucleosides, and Nucleotides Determined via Tandem Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: Noncovalent intermolecular interactions, particularly hydrogen bonding, play an important role in the stability and reactivity of biochemically relevant molecules. In nucleic acids, hydrogen bonding governs both molecular recognition and higher-order structure. Previously, we showed that nucleobase hydrogen-bonding patterns correlate well with observed microdroplet-driven RNA oligomer formation trends. However, a quantitative comparison of interaction strengths between nucleic-acid building blocks with increased chemical moieties, from nucleobases to nucleosides and nucleotides, is required before conclusions can be made on the impact of hydrogen bonding on droplet-mediated oligonucleotide formation. Here, tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) via collision-induced dissociation (CID) was used to probe noncovalent bond strengths of homodimers of the four canonical nucleobases, as well as their corresponding nucleosides and nucleotides. Breakdown curves were produced from the protonated homodimers of each species, and sigmoidal fits of those data provided two useful comparative metrics: the mean fragmentation energy (E1/2) and the full-width, half-maximum values (FWHM) in fragmentation energy as determined from the derivative of the breakdown curves. Across the three molecular classes, ΔE1/2 values decreased with the inclusion of more chemical moieties (e.g., from nucleobase to nucleoside to nucleotide) due to more degrees of freedom (e.g., vibrational modes) for the complex molecules. Hydrogen bonding and other noncovalent intermolecular interactions are known to be largely preserved from the solution phase to the gas phase, which enables the application of these data to aqueous solution and the microhydrated air-water interface. Importantly, nucleobase E1/2 values correlated with previously observed trends in microdroplet-driven RNA oligomerization, which suggests that hydrogen-bonding character at the nucleobase level may influence phosphodiester bond formation in interfacial environments. In contrast, nucleotide E1/2 values align with oligomerization trends in bulk aqueous systems, consistent with stronger intermolecular forces between nucleotides enhancing oligomerization, particularly in the presence of mineral catalysts. Together, these results provide a relative quantitative framework to connect noncovalent intermolecular interactions to environmentally dependent RNA-formation pathways.

papers.title: Harnessing Flexibility from Inflexible Systems: A Case Study in Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical devices can play a critical role in providing demand-side flexibility to the power grid, enabling greater integration of renewable power and enhancing system resilience. However, highly dynamic operation that tracks fluctuating market signals can accelerate degradation. This work proposes a new operational paradigm that aggregates parallel units operating under structured dynamic protocols with the goal of mitigating device degradation. Using a grid-connected hydrogen electrolysis system as a case study, we develop an optimization framework that determines optimal mixing of predefined structured protocols that minimizes total electricity costs. Our results show that cost of the protocol-based parallel setting closely approximates that of fully flexible operation. This trend is consistently observed across different sets of protocols and under diverse market conditions, demonstrating the wide applicability of the proposed concept. The proposed approach can also enhance predictability and practical implementation.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Image Analysis of Complex Chemical Mixtures: Synthetic Urine Droplets as a Test System
papers.abstract: Dried droplet deposits encode compositional information through evaporation-driven self-organization, offering a potential low-cost sensing modality for chemical analysis. Here, we evaluate the feasibility of inferring solute concentrations and pH from photographic images of dried synthetic urine stains using automated experimentation and machine learning. A robotic droplet imager (RODI) combined with Latin hypercube sampling was employed to efficiently explore compositional space and generate standardized datasets comprising 70,000 images across two experimental systems: a two-component urea-NaCl model and seven-component synthetic urine mixtures spanning physiologically relevant ranges for urea, NaCl, KCl, creatinine, glucose, a combined salt group, and pH. Each image was reduced to 47 descriptors capturing spatial morphology and texture. Random Forest classifiers trained on these descriptors achieved overall accuracies near 89% for both systems, reliably distinguishing compositional classes. Random Forest regression yielded useful predictive performance for NaCl in the two-component system and identified pH as the most robustly inferred parameter in the complex mixture. However, continuous prediction of individual solute concentrations in the seven-component system remained limited possibly due to the sparsity of training points across the high-dimensional compositional space. These findings delineate both the current capabilities and information-theoretic constraints of image-based compositional inference for complex chemical mixtures.

papers.title: A modular and affordable self-driving laboratory enables vision-guided optimization of metal electrodeposition
papers.abstract: Metal electrodeposition is a widely used materials synthesis technique; however, industrial applications often require optimization of complex precursor formulations and electrodeposition parameters, which is typically performed in a slow, inefficient, and empirical manner.
