These precursors were efficiently converted into linear Cu(I)–NHC complexes via a weak-base protocol and into Ru(II)–arene carbonato and dichloro NHC complexes using an analogous methodology, highlighting operationally simple, scalable approaches suitable for sensitive or multifunctional ligands. Structural characterization confirmed the formation of well-defined metal–carbene species. Biological evaluation revealed that Cu(I)–NHC complexes exhibit potent antiproliferative activity against ovarian (A2780, A2780cis) and breast (MCF-7) cancer cells, including cisplatin-resistant models, and induce apoptosis with moderate selectivity over non-tumorigenic keratinocytes. In contrast, Ru(II)–NHC complexes displayed moderate cytotoxicity but are consistent with profiles favouring anti-metastatic and mechanistically distinct actions. These results underscore the potential of backbonefunctionalized NHC ligands to fine-tune metallodrug activity and highlight Cu(I)–NHC complexes as promising candidates for further development against resistant cancers.

papers.title: Variational Quantum Circuits for Pesticide Environmental Fate Prediction: A Comparative Study with Classical Machine Learning on the EU SPIN Database
papers.abstract: Predicting pesticide environmental fate properties—specifically soil degradation halflife (DegT50) and organic carbon sorption coefficient (Koc)—is essential for regulatory risk assessment under EC 1107/2009. Classical QSAR models achieve moderate predictive power for Koc but struggle with DegT50 due to its dependence on complex soil microbial processes. This work investigates whether variational quantum circuits (VQCs) can capture non-linear molecular descriptor relationships that elude classical regressors. We encode 21 physicochemical descriptors for 110 EU-registered pesticides into per-target quantum circuits: an 8-qubit circuit for DegT50 (17 core features) and a 12-qubit circuit for Koc (all 21 features), each with IQP-style encoding and data re-uploading. Leave-one-out crossvalidation benchmarks reveal that Random Forest (RF) achieves R2 = 0.287 for DegT50 and 0.712 for Koc, while Gradient Boosting (GB) reaches 0.283 and 0.750, respectively (fair 20-feature set, excluding circular bioaccessibility). An MLP neural network achieves only 0.075 and 0.497. The VQC alone underperforms all classical baselines (R2 = −0.028 for DegT50, 5-fold CV). A hybrid stacking framework with nested LOO-CV for leakage free α optimization yields α = 0.20±0.02, but the resulting hybrid R2 (0.288 for DegT50) improves over standalone RF by only +0.001—a negligible and statistically insignificant margin. These results demonstrate that near-term VQCs on small regulatory datasets (N ≈ 110) cannot outperform properly feature-engineered classical models, and caution against premature claims of quantum advantage in chemistry applications with limited training data.

papers.title: MACE-MDP: A General Dipole and Polarizability Model for Organic Molecules and Materials
Strategies to predict and design spin defects for quantum technologies
papers.abstract: The design of materials with functionalities optimally suited for quantum information applications is a critical need in the field of quantum science and engineering. This Perspective focuses on a specific class of systems, spin defects in semiconductors and insulators, and on the manipulation of their electron spins, which can provide controllable qubits with long relaxation and coherence times, and can be coupled to nuclear spins for long-lived quantum memories. We summarize our recent contributions to the development of integrated theoretical frameworks and high-performance codes to predict and design spin defects and present examples of validated predictions and interpretations of experimental results. Starting from a brief description of the structural and charge stability at zero temperature using density functional theory, we present simulations to understand the mechanism of spin defect formation with first-principles molecular dynamics and machine learned potentials. We then discuss two classes of properties that are essential for the prediction of spin defects' functionalities: electronic and coherence properties. The discussion of computational frameworks is followed by that of results for specific systems illustrating successes, open problems, and future applications, with examples for heterogeneous solids, inclusive of surfaces and mesoscopic defects, and with a focus on quantum sensing and communication applications.

papers.title: Natural Orbital Correlation Analysis of Cluster Bonding: From Aromatic Clusters to Metallic Superatoms with Quantum Topology Probes
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of electron correlation across molecular and cluster systems using the number of effectively unpaired electrons ND = P i ni(2 − ni), the Takatsuka–Head-Gordon index, computed from coupled-cluster natural orbital occupations over the complete correlated orbital space. Computed at the CCSD/def2-SVP level, all systems studied exhibit substantial total electron correlation when the full natural orbital space is retained: aromatic Al4 2 – (ND = 3.84), antiaromatic Al4 4 – (4.03), planar and icosahedral B12 clusters (4.42 and 4.99), heteroatomic B6N6 (5.11), and cesium–aluminum superatoms Cs3Al8 – and Cs3Al12 – (5.58 and 7.10, respectively). We show that ND is an extensive quantity dominated by the dynamic correlation tail over many weakly occupied virtual orbitals, and introduce the per-electron correlation density fe = ND/Ncorr as a complementary intensive measure. This intensive measure reveals a clear separation: small clusters (Al4, B12, B6N6) exhibit fe ≈ 0.08–0.14, while metallic superatoms show fe ≈ 0.04, reflecting the diluted nature of correlation in large delocalized systems. We demonstrate that truncation of the natural orbital space to a small active window dramatically underestimates ND, and that complete occupation data are essential for physically meaningful correlation diagnostics. In a separate study, we explore whether molecular bonding topology generates characteristic entanglement signatures on a neutral-atom quantum processor (Pasqal). Mapping atomic coordinates of nine molecular systems onto Rydberg atom registers, we find that different chemical topology classes—aromatic, antiaromatic, cage, and metallic—produce systematically distinct entanglement patterns, suggesting that molecular graphs encode topological information accessible to analog quantum hardware.

papers.title: NovoExpert-2: State-of-the-Art ADMET Prediction via Gradient-Boosted Trees on MapLight Fingerprints and GIN Embeddings
papers.abstract: We present NovoExpert-2, a dual-method approach to molecular property prediction that achieves state-of-the-art performance on five endpoints of the Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC) ADMET benchmark. Our primary model combines MapLight-style fingerprint fea- tures (2,573 dimensions: Morgan ECFP, Avalon, ErG, and RDKit 2D descriptors) with 300- dimensional GIN supervised masking embeddings from the DGL-LifeSci pretrained model zoo, passed to a 5-seed CatBoost classifier/regressor ensemble. We additionally evaluate a Chemprop v2 directed message-passing neural network (D-MPNN) as a secondary method, and for each endpoint report the stronger of the two. Evaluated on all 22 endpoints of the TDC ADMET benchmark using official splits and per-endpoint metrics, NovoExpert-2 exceeds published state- of-the-art on CYP2D6 Veith (AUPRC 0.778 vs. 0.750, +0.028), CYP3A4 Veith (AUPRC 0.916 vs. 0.900, +0.016), CYP3A4 Substrate Carbonmangels (AUROC 0.660 vs. 0.656, +0.0040), Clearance Hepatocyte AZ (Spearman 0.511 vs. 0.487, +0.024), and DILI (AUROC 0.922 vs. 0.916, +0.006). The first four wins use CatBoost+MapLight+GIN; DILI uses Chemprop v2, which exploits end-to-end learned representations that better capture the multi-mechanism drug- induced liver injury phenotype. We additionally present a metric correction for our previously reported NovoExpert-1 CYP2D6 result: prior work measured AUROC (0.864) while the TDC leaderboard uses AUPRC; under the correct metric, NovoExpert-1 would score approximately 0.64 AUPRC on CYP2D6 and would not have beaten SOTA. NovoExpert-2, evaluated with the correct per-endpoint metric throughout, provides a more rigorous basis for leaderboard comparison. All code, trained models, and prediction files are publicly available.

papers.title: Synthesis and optical quantum memory characterization of α-Eu(IO3)3, β-Eu(IO3)3, and NaEu(IO3)4
papers.abstract: Three phases of stoichiometric europium (III) iodate compounds are probed as candidates for optical quantum memory to determine the impact of reaction conditions on phase formation and relate crystal structure to their ability to host persistent excited states relevant to quantum memory. Hydrothermal synthesis procedures for growing macroscopic single crystals of rectangular-block α -Eu(IO 3 ) 3 ( P 2 1 / c ), yellow hexagonal plate β -Eu(IO 3 ) 3 ( P 2 1 /n), and transparent plate NaEu(IO 3 ) 4 are presented. The ability to burn narrow and long-lived spectral holes on the 7 F 0 → 5 D 0 optical transitions is a necessary condition for implementing optical quantum memory. α - Eu(IO 3 ) 3 was determined to be incapable of hole-burning due to the presence of insufficient site asymmetry of the europium site, which forbids the required optical transition. β -Eu(IO 3 ) 3 was determined to be incapable of storing information due to a lack of observed spectral hole burning, likely caused by decoherence due to the closely-packed edge-sharing Eu(III) polyhedra. Analysis of each phase’s crystal structure suggests that the Eu-Eu nearest neighbor distance and distortion of europium site symmetry are critical material design parameters for quantum memory applications.

papers.title: Supercapacitor-Based CO2 Capture Enhanced by Electrolyte pH Control
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 capture by supercapacitors is emerging as an energy-efficient alternative to traditional thermally-driven technologies. Despite recent advances, the underlying mechanism of capture remains unresolved, with two competing hypotheses currently debated: a molecular mechanism, involving the uptake of CO2 molecules, and an ionic mechanism, driven by the uptake of bicarbonate (HCO3‾), which is in equilibrium with the gaseous CO2. In this study, combined electrochemical CO2 sorption measurements and solid-state NMR spectroscopy experiments reveal that CO2 capture occurs in both highly basic and highly acidic electrolytes, where the formation of aqueous CO2 or bicarbonate is suppressed, respectively. In basic electrolytes where bicarbonate is the dominant species, we observe 30% higher CO2 adsorption capacities and capture rates compared to neutral electrolytes, supporting the dominance of the ionic mechanism. In contrast, in an acidic electrolyte, where CO2 is the only species present, we observe a 60% decrease in CO2 adsorption capacities, despite having higher electrochemical capacitances. This indicates that bicarbonate is the primary species responsible for high electrochemical CO2 capture rates in supercapacitors that utilize aqueous electrolytes and porous carbon electrodes. Overall, this work provides mechanistic insight into the mechanism of electrochemical CO2 capture using aqueous supercapacitors and highlights the importance of CO2 speciation and electrolyte pH in optimizing performance.

papers.title: Toward Low-Energy Direct-Air Capture by Reversible Proton-Intercalation Mediated Alkalization
papers.abstract: Mitigation strategies to avoid climate change impacts rely on direct air capture (DAC) of CO 2 . We demonstrate capture of CO 2 at 400 ppm, and its release, by using solid proton-intercalation electrodes to swing the pH of an alkaline electrolyte. 1.76±0.16 GJ tonne -1 of electrical energy is used when enriching CO 2 two-fold, extrapolating to 25.3±0.16 GJ tonne -1 to include water condensation and compression energy. Twenty-fold enrichment requires 5.81±2.42 GJ tonne -1 of electrical energy, extrapolating to 7.81±2.42 GJ tonne -1 . Here, symmetric potassium-stabilized alpha-phase manganese dioxide electrodes are used to (de)intercalate protons from two separate electrolyte streams, thereby swinging dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) solubility in an asynchronous cycle wherein electrochemical steps occur in sequence with CO 2 transfer steps. Mixing among aqueous streams is shown by theory to reduce CO 2 transfer, where the retention of DIC concentration during alkalizing/dealkalizing steps is affected by mixing more so than alkali-ion concentration swing. Energy use further reduces by pre-mixing post-capture and post-release electrolytes. Theory predicts that alkali-ion concentration swing increases with increasing electrode specific capacity and decreasing mixing volume, motivating the co-design of active materials and their electrode microstructures to enhance efficiency, productivity, and enrichment. The present DAC cycle may also be implemented using other electrochemical architectures.

papers.title: Overriding Nitrogen Radical Reactivity Enables Enantiospecific Sulfur-Centered Radical Chemistry
papers.abstract: The enantiospecific synthesis of sulfoximines under mild and modular conditions remains a longstanding challenge, reflecting a broader limitation in accessing stereocontrolled sulfur-centered radical reactivity. Here, we show that sulfinamides, previously restricted to nitrogen-centered radical pathways, can instead engage in productive sulfur-centered radical chemistry. This enables a general, enantiospecific photoredox strategy to access vinyl sulfoximines. The configurational stability of the sulfinamidyl radical allows precise transfer of stereochemical information, revealing a kinetically controlled S-centered pathway that overrides thermodynamically favored nitrogen reactivity. These findings redefine the reactivity landscape of sulfinamidyl radicals and establish a general blueprint for stereocontrolled heteroatom-centered radical chemistry.

papers.title: Exhaustive Molecular String Enumeration for Data Augmentation and Structure Exploration
papers.abstract: Molecular strings such as SMILES and SELFIES are linear representations of molecular graphs. Due to the inherent nonlinear structure of molecular graphs, a priori, there is no unique string representation for a given molecular graph but rather many alternative strings correspond to the same graph. This allows for the randomization of molecular strings to be used both as a means of data augmentation for training sequence-based deep learning models and, when applied to SELFIES strings, for the systematic exploration of chemical space through random string mutations and interpolations. However, established algorithms for the randomization of molecular strings only account for the randomization of the starting atom and the main and sub branches. They do not randomize the spanning trees of the molecular graphs. This results in a substantial number of overlooked molecular strings for structures with at least one ring. Herein, we present TYCHE, an algorithm for the exhaustive enumeration of all spanning trees of molecular graphs and, thus, for the generation of many more randomized molecular strings. TYCHE shows a systematic and robust performance increase when used for data augmentation, string mutation, and string interpolation. Several case studies showcase the large potential of TYCHE for impact in cheminformatics and molecular machine learning.

papers.title: Predicting the Thermodynamic Limits of Metal–Organic Framework Metastability
papers.abstract: The vast combinatorial space of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) has led to their widespread consideration across diverse application areas. That said, much remains unknown about what factors govern their thermodynamic stability. Herein, we use density functional theory to compute the formation energy and construct convex hull phase diagrams for 20,000+ MOFs and coordination polymers. Using the energy above hull as a measure of stability with respect to decomposition and phase transitions, we validate and expand upon previous hypotheses that all MOFs are thermodynamically metastable and that there is an inherent energetic penalty associated with permanent porosity. We also describe how MOF composition and metal/linker identity influence the degree of metastability, in addition to demonstrating how the energy above hull can be used as a synthesizability metric for newly proposed MOFs. To democratize the knowledge gained from our study, we have released the QMOF-Thermo Database, which is the first database of energy above hull values for MOFs and coordination polymers. We conclude by using the QMOF-Thermo Database to benchmark the ability of pre-trained machine learning interatomic potentials to predict the energy above hull of MOFs, and we identify opportunities to correct their performance.

papers.title: Amyloid-Catalyzed Terephthalate Degradation
papers.abstract: Terephthalates, particularly BHET and MHET, are partial hydrolysis products of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET), the most ubiquitous plastic waste, and considered major pollutants and health hazards. We demonstrate, for the first time, that amyloid fibrils, both de-novo designed fibrils comprising alternating phenylalanine-lysine motif, and physiological functional bacterial amyloids, efficiently catalyze BHET and MHET hydrolysis. Peptide variant screening, physicochemical experiments, and structural analyses shed light in the catalytic mechanism, facilitated by surface docking via pi-pi interactions between the terephthalates and phenylalanines, and hydrogen bonding with lysine sidechains. Hydrolysis subsequently 2 proceeds via nucleophilic attack by the lysines’ butylammonium sidechains. Catalytic, recyclable terephthalate degradation was also accomplished by coupling the amyloid fibrils to silica beads and placing in a conventional recyclable column setup, and by bacterially secreted PSMα amyloid fibrils, pointing to potential applicability in natural bacterial biofilms.

papers.title: Enhancing the Stability of Pt/Carbon with Ti3C2Tx MXene for the Oxygen Reduction Reaction in Acidic Media
papers.abstract: Platinum on carbon remains the proton exchange membrane fuel cell cathode state of the art catalyst, however durability losses tied to support corrosion and Pt coarsening hinders this catalyst. This study investigates into utilizing different variations of Vulcan XC-72 and Ti3C2 MXene to improve oxygen-reduction ORR activity and stability. The materials characterization results provide in depth knowledge of the Pt, carbon and MXene composites. The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy of the synthesized samples shows that the Ti3C2Tx has oxidized, and the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy further reveals that the Pt (111) fringes are present with local anatase TiO2 on the Ti3C2 MXene, which is also confirmed by Xray microscopy. Rotating disk electrode shows Pt kinetics (~60 mV/dec) and ranks activity as similar Pt/75%C+25%Ti3C2 and Pt/C, followed by Pt/50%C+50%Ti3C2 and then the Ti3C2-rich samples. GDE testing confirms the hierarchy at 1 A/cm2 (75%C+25%Ti3C2 > Pt/C Pt/50%C+50%Ti3C2). Furthermore, galvanostatic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy indicates the lowest charge-transfer/transport losses for Pt/75%C+25%Ti3C2. After a DoE derived accelerated stress test, the Pt/75%C+25%Ti3C2 our performs the Pt/C. TEM size histograms and Raman D/G shifts reveals that a Ti3C2 fraction strengthens metal-support interactions and mitigates Pt growth while preserving percolation and gas pathways. The Pt/75%C+25%Ti3C2 composite defines a practical composition window and a reproducible half-cell protocol for Pt/C+MXene screening. This study is the first coupled cathode half-cell performance and potential-cycling durability testing for MXene derived composites benchmarked against Pt/C and provides vital information on materials discovery for the ORR.

papers.title: Discrete Self-Assembled Porphyrin Structures Across the Exterior of Supramolecular Nanocages Delocalize Their Excited-States
papers.abstract: Natural photosynthesis utilizes light-harvesting systems that operate at near perfect efficiency under light-limited conditions. Excited-state energy transport is enhanced beyond the Förster rate due to the contribution of delocalized quantum states known as vibronic excitons, which arise as a result of the relative arrangement of chromophores. In order to emulate photosynthesis and control excited-state energy transport, artificial systems need to achieve similarly precise arrangements of chromophores. The self-assembly strategy of metal-organic nanocages produces discrete assemblies of chromophores in specific topological configurations. In this manuscript we report a series of PdnL2n porphyrin-appended nanocages, arranging 4 (Pd2L4) or 24 (Pd12L24 and Pd12Lx24) porphyrin chromophores around a metal-organic nanocage scaffold. The average inter-porphyrin separation and orientation are controlled by the nanocage structure. The nanocage-porphyrin assemblies were characterized structurally with 1H-NMR, DOSY, HR-TOF-MS, and optically with both steady-state and time-resolved absorption and fluorescence spectroscopies. These studies indicate magnetic and dipolar interactions between the assembled porphyrins, which vary as function of porphyrin packing density and orientation. Fluorescence anisotropy decay measurements indicate incoherent Förster-type hopping on the nanosecond timescale. However, power-dependent transient absorption reveals ultrafast annihilation events for some nanocage-porphyrin assemblies, indicating that the porphyrin excited states are highly mobile. Such enhanced excited state hopping rates align with the presence of vibronic excitons. Since excited state delocalization is a defining property of photosynthetic light-harvesting systems, the metal-mediated self-assembly approach developed here can act as a stepping stone towards artificial photosynthesis.

papers.title: Accessing Solid-State 13C NMR Prediction in Polymers with Machine-Learned Chemical Shifts
papers.abstract: Solid-state 13C nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is among the most powerful probes of polymer structure, yet predicting solid-state 13C NMR spectra from molecular simulations has remained infeasible due to intractable computational costs. Here we introduce PNGWNN, a framework coupling molecular dynamics and machinelearned chemical shifts to efficiently generate solid-state 13C NMR spectra from molecular simulation. Trained on three polymer chemistries, PNGWNN achieves ∼1 ppm chemical shift prediction accuracy against density functional theory and transfers quantitatively to six chemically distinct test polymers across amorphous, crystalline, surface, multiphase, and copolymer morphologies. Moreover, predicted spectral features can be decomposed into atomically detailed contributions associated with specific conformations, hydrogen-bond motifs, and phase compositions, revealing structure–spectrum relationships without prior structural hypotheses. PNGWNN makes solid-state 13C NMR a computationally accessible observable, opening routes to simulation-driven structural inference and experimental design in polymers.

papers.title: Engineering of LNA‑Modified DNA-AuNP Nanomachines for Intracellular miRNA Imaging
papers.abstract: DNA nanomachines based on gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) are promising platforms for intracellular sensing of microRNAs (miRNAs), which are biomarkers involved in a wide range of diseases. However, achieving robust performance under intracellular conditions remains a challenge. In this study, we investigated the effect of locked nucleic acid (LNA) modification on an entropy-driven DNA-AuNP nanomachine designed for miRNA detection. By incorporating LNA into probe sequences, we evaluated signal generation, sensitivity, and selectivity under cytosol-mimicking conditions. As a result, appropriately designed LNA modifications were shown to substantially restore nanomachine functionality under intracellularly relevant conditions. In contrast, excessive or unfavorably positioned LNA incorporation led to increased nonspecific background signals. Under optimized conditions, the LNA-modified nanomachine achieved a detection limit of approximately 10 pM for miRNA-21 with high sequence specificity. Furthermore, when delivered into cancer cells, MCF-7, using a transfection reagent, the LNA-modified DNA-AuNP nanomachine showed a higher fraction of fluorescence-positive cells compared with the unmodified system. This study clarifies the critical role of probe modification in the design of DNAAuNP nanomachines operating within living cells and presents an effective strategy for realizing livecell miRNA imaging based on molecular robotics concepts.

papers.title: Redox-Neutral C(sp3)–H Alkenylation via Photocatalyzed Tandem HAT and Oxidative RPC
papers.abstract: Herein, we present a photocatalytic route that exploits a redox-neutral tandem hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and oxidative radical polar crossover (RPC) manifold. This method enables the efficient synthesis of valuable allylic amides and ethers through the valorization of three classes of ubiquitous feedstock chemicals: carboxylic acids as precursors to hydrogen atom abstractors, amides or ethers as C(sp 3 )–H donors, and olefins as radical acceptors. The protocol operates under mild conditions, exhibits broad functional group tolerance, and is readily scalable. The redox-neutral nature of this transformation mechanistically distinguishes it from traditional net-oxidative approaches associated with exogenous stoichiometric oxidants. Crucially, it allows the engagement of HAT substrates with ‘hydridic’ C−H bonds (e.g. α- to heteroatom: X−CHR 1 R 2 ) to be engaged in Giese-type addition reactions and subsequent oxidative RPC/nucleophilic trapping, where traditional netoxidative approaches inevitably result in Shono-type further oxidation of the HAT-derived radical (e.g. α- to heteroatom: X+=CR 1 R 2 ) and nucleophilic interception prior to intermolecular radical addition.

papers.title: Unprotected C‑ Aryl Glycosides from Native Sugars via Sulfonyl Hydrazides：A Thermal Cap‑and‑Glycosylation Strategy
Synergistic Stabilization and CO Activation in a Be4(NCl)2 Cluster: From EDA-NOCV Energetics to Electron Localization Topology
papers.abstract: The electronic structure, bonding nature, and small-molecule activation potential of the Be4(NCl)2 cluster were investigated using M06-2X/def2-TZVP density functional theory. Structural analysis identifies a D2h -symmetric framework featuring a robust Be4 core with inter-fragment Be–Be distances of 2.05 Å. Energy Decomposition Analysis (EDA-NOCV) reveals that the cluster is stabilized by an intense covalent-like interaction (ΔEorb = -369.92 kcal/mol), which is several times larger than the electrostatic contribution. Natural Orbital for Chemical Valence (NOCV) and topological analyses, including Electron Localization Function (ELF) and Localized Orbital Locator (LOL) maps, confirm a multi-centre delocalized bonding regime within the beryllium core. Broken-symmetry DFT calculations rule out diradicaloid character, confirming a stable closed-shell singlet ground state with a high HOMO-LUMO gap of 5.30 eV. While the cluster exhibits a slightly repulsive interaction with H2 (+0.38 kcal/mol), global docking and geometry refinement demonstrate an exceptional affinity for Carbon Monoxide (CO). CO chemisorption is characterized by a high binding energy of -83.09 kcal/mol, a C–O bond elongation to 1.312 Å, and a dramatic vibrational red-shift to 1440.47 cm-1, signalling potent activation through π-back-donation. These findings highlight Be4(NCl)2 as a robust main-group cluster capable of significant small-molecule activation.

papers.title: Vibrational and Electronic Spectroscopies of Dibenzoterrylene Conformers: Computational Insights
papers.abstract: Dibenzoterrylene (DBT) is a coherent molecular single-photon emitter that exhibits an interesting energetic landscape with multiple lowenergy, accessible conformations. In this work, using first principle approaches, we systematically investigate the conformational landscape of DBT in the gas phase, identifying five unique conformers, four of which are expected to be thermally accessible in a solid state host. We further analyze vibrational and electronic spectroscopies to identify conformer-specific spectral signatures. We find that each conformer exhibits distinct spectral fingerprints in both IR and Raman spectra across conformers, highlighting the sensitivity of the C-H bending modes to subtle geometric changes. The electronic absorption and emission spectra also reveal multiple conformer-specific features. Finally, we explore the Franck-Condon-Herzberg-Teller vibrationally resolved electronic excitation spectrum which showcases even more rich conformation-specific landmarks. Collectively, our results provide a comprehensive framework for understanding how DBT’s conformerspecific electronic structure could play a role in observed optical behaviors.

papers.title: Right into the Saddle: Stereochemistry-Aware Generation of Molecular Transition States
papers.abstract: Determination of transition state structures is fundamental to the mechanistic understanding of chemical reactivity and selectivity, yet conventional approaches require extensive expert intervention for geometry preparation and saddle-point optimization, severely limiting the throughput of computational reaction analysis. We present RitS, a generative model trained on a curated dataset of approximately 2 million transition states computed at the GFN2-xTB level of theory. RitS generates three-dimensional transition-state geometries directly from reactant–product bond connectivity without requiring pre-optimized molecular structures as input. The model accommodates H, B, C, N, O, F, Si, P, S, Cl, Br, I elements, systems containing up to 51 total atoms, and both neutral and charged species, substantially extending the chemical scope of prior generative approaches. Benchmarking on the Transition1x dataset demonstrates that RitS achieves the lowest median root-mean-square deviation among current methods. Cross-dataset evaluation yields intrinsic reaction coordinate validation rates exceeding 90% from a single generated structure, rising to approximately 99% with three independent samples. A key capability of RitS is stereochemistry-aware generation: encoding product chirality in the input graph enables selective generation of competing diastereomeric transition states, as demonstrated for endo versus exo Diels–Alder cycloadditions and E versus Z elimination pathways. The model further generalizes to the multistep Hajos–Parrish–Eder–Sauer–Wiechert organocatalytic cycle, capturing each elementary step including the enantiodetermining intramolecular aldol transition state. These results establish RitS as a tool for automated, high-throughput transition-state generation applicable to mechanistic studies, selectivity analysis, and large-scale reaction network exploration.

papers.title: Upconversion of Infrared Light Via Plasmon-Induced Hot Thermal Carrier Transfer
papers.abstract: The robust upconversion of infrared light would bypass its low photon energy, enabling efficient utilization. Here we employ hot thermal carriers produced through excitation of localized surface plasmon resonances in semiconductor nanocrystals to efficiently upconvert infrared photons. Transient absorption spectroscopy shows hot-electron transfer from plasmonic tin-doped indium oxide (ITO) nanocrystals to semiconductor thin films, overcoming a 1.1 eV barrier via infrared photoexcitation at 0.52 eV. The rate of hot-electron transfer is consistent with kinetic and power dependencies for hot thermal carriers and well described by Marcus Theory. Analysis reveals the low, tailorable carrier concentration in ITO compared to metals enables this upconversion process. This mechanism facilitates upconversion throughout the infrared without constraints imposed by absorption cross sections, phonon energies, or energetic barriers.

papers.title: Visible-Light-Driven Divergent Carboxylation of Alkenes with CO2 via Single Photocatalyst
papers.abstract: Photoredox carboxylation of alkenes with CO2 has been largely confined to reductive carboxylation, whereas keeping C=C double bond remains elusive. Herein we report the first visible-light-driven formal C(sp2)–H carboxylation of alkenes under atmospheric CO2 condition. The key to success is a single binaphthol photocatalyst not only serves as a strong reductant to form alkenes radical anion, a nucleophile to activate CO2, but also forms an O-centred radical that couples with the generated C-centred radical in situ. This radicalradical coupling/E2-elimination sequence (RCEs) furnishes the E-cinnamate with exclusive stereoselectivity. Further introduction of B2pin2 switches the manifold to 1,2-dicarboxylation, accomplishing succinates with good to excellent yields. This divergent platform establishes a reliable route for π-conserving CO2 fixation, providing modular access to two distinct carboxylic acid architectures from a single photocatalytic system..

papers.title: A TALE OF TWO HETEROCYCLES: HOW OXYGEN AND SULFUR SHAPE DIVERGENT KEMP REACTIVITY
papers.abstract: The Kemp elimination is a well-studied reaction that proceeds through the deprotonation of the carbon-3 of benzisoxazoles, followed by irreversible ring opening by cleavage of the labile O-N bond. The base-catalyzed reaction is concerted, with no detectable intermediate. Due to the similarity in composition and structure, benzisothiazoles are also candidates for Kemp elimination reactions; however, little information was previously available on such compounds. We found that benzisothiazoles also undergo Kemp elimination, and we have fully characterized the Kemp product. As previously observed with benzisoxazoles, reactions of benzisothiazoles are significantly accelerated by polar, aprotic solvents and by the presence of electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) on the six-membered ring. In mixed water/DMSO systems, we found a strong inverse linear relationship between the logarithm of the second-order rate constant and the molar fraction of water for both benzisoxazoles and benzisothiazoles. Extrapolations from the observed data to neat solvent suggest that the hydroxide ion is 14 orders of magnitude more efficient as a catalyst in DMSO than in pure water for benzisoxazoles and 7 orders of magnitude more efficient for benzisothiazoles. Electrostatic potential (ESP) analyses of the products, used as proxies for late-transition states, support a picture in which oxygen-based systems develop more localized negative charge that benefits disproportionately from strong solvent dipoles and electron-withdrawing substituents, whereas sulfur allows broader charge delocalization and thus a muted response. These findings rationalize the different solvent and substituent sensitivities of the two scaffolds and provide guidance for selecting Kemp substrates when benchmarking general-base catalysis and de novo enzyme designs

papers.title: Ligand-Controlled Pd(II)-Catalyzed α,β-Unsaturation and β-Arylation of Long-Chain Acids
papers.abstract: Direct synthesis of β-aryl α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acids from simple aliphatic acids remains challenging, as it requires β-C(sp³)–H activation, β-hydride elimination, and C–C bond formation to occur within a single catalytic system. Herein, we report a ligand-enabled Pd-catalyzed strategy for the conversion of free aliphatic carboxylic acids into trans -cinnamic acid derivatives. A CF₃-substituted pyrazole–pyridone ligand facilitates β-methylene C–H activation while promoting β-hydride elimination and suppressing premature oxidative addition. This sequence generates α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acids in situ , which subsequently undergo a Heck-type β-arylation. The reaction exhibits broad functional group tolerance, accommodating heteroaryl and sterically hindered aryl iodides, as well as complex substrates, thereby enabling late-stage diversification. Mechanistic studies support a sequential unsaturation–arylation pathway rather than an initial β-arylation process, underscoring the critical role of ligand design in controlling reaction order and selectivity. Overall, this strategy provides a general and efficient approach to cinnamic acid derivatives from native carboxylic acid feedstocks.

papers.title: Conductivity- and configuration-dependent discharge regimes at plasma–liquid interfaces in a liquid–gas–liquid system
papers.abstract: Plasma discharges at gas–liquid interfaces are widely investigated for water treatment, medical applications, and materials processing because they generate reactive species directly in liquids. However, most previous studies have employed configurations in which solid electrodes were partially exposed to the gas phase, making it difficult to isolate the intrinsic role of the liquid in determining discharge behaviour. In this study, both metallic electrodes were fully immersed in the liquid, and plasma was generated in the gas region between the two opposing liquid surfaces, thereby eliminating solid–gas interfaces. By varying the conductivity and arrangement of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and ultrapure water (UPW), two distinct discharge regimes were identified under identical driving conditions. PBS–PBS produced a spark-to-DC-glow transition with pronounced interfacial heating and enhanced chemical production, whereas UPW-containing systems exhibited dielectric barrier dischargelike behaviour characterized by transient streamers, minimal gas heating, and reduced chemical yields. These findings demonstrate that the liquid phase acts as an active structural component, governing the discharge regime and plasma-induced chemistry while shaping the spatial distribution of optical emission. This work advances the fundamental understanding of liquid–gas–liquid plasma systems and provides a basis for selective control of discharge regimes through liquid-property design.

papers.title: bRiteWeight: Randomized iterative reweighting for biased trajectory data
papers.abstract: Determining the stationary distribution from a set of stochastic-process trajectory data, e.g., molecular dynamics, has long been a challenging if under-appreciated problem. We recently proposed a randomized iterative reweighting algorithm, “RiteWeight,” which provided a solution given unbiased trajectory data, i.e., trajectories generated directly from the dynamics of interest (potential surface, temperature, etc.). However, numerous sampling methodologies use biased dynamics, typically generated from a smoothed energy surface. Here, we introduce the bRiteWeight algorithm, which modifies RiteWeight for biased dynamics based on Girsanov (importance sampling) weights for trajectory snippets. We show theoretically and with simple examples that the new algorithm can correct biased dynamics to yield the stationary distribution of the unbiased system. As with RiteWeight, the algorithm is suitable both for equilibrium and nonequilibrium steady states.

papers.title: Why We Must Break the World
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is entering materials science and manufacturing at a moment when retrieval is often mistaken for discovery. We argue that models trained to optimize plausibility within a closed theoretical system are structurally biased toward interpolation and away from the anomalies from which scientific revolutions arise. In materials and manufacturing, this limitation becomes acute because the design space is combinatorial, multiscale, and physically constrained. What is needed is not another assistant for summarizing what is already known, but systems that can assemble compositional world models, invert the forward problem, falsify their own principles, and test those principles against simulation and fabrication. Drawing on recent work in graph-native reasoning, inverse protein design, multi-agent scientific discovery, and AI-integrated manufacturing, we outline an architecture for discovery built on three capabilities: world-model construction, adversarial falsification, and physical grounding. The central claim is that materials innovation will accelerate when AI moves beyond retrieval and surrogate prediction toward systems that can generate, challenge, and physically realize new hypotheses. In that sense, discovery requires breaking the current world model in order to build the next one.

papers.title: Deep Learning Architectures for the Inverse Design of Covalent Organic Frameworks with Tailored Thermal Transport: A High-Throughput Materials Informatics Study
papers.abstract: The precise control of thermal conductivity (κ) in porous crystalline materials is a fundamental challenge for the next generation of thermoelectric and microelectronic cooling technologies. Covalent Organic Frameworks (COFs) offer a unique structural platform due to their modularity, yet the sheer dimensionality of their chemical space precludes exhaustive experimental or ab initio characterization. In this work, we present a robust Materials Informatics framework that integrates Neural Network Potentials (NNPs) with High-Throughput Screening (HTS) to explore the thermal landscape of 2,500+ COF topologies. Our model utilizes Behler-Parrinello symmetry functions to encode local atomic environments, achieving near-DFT accuracy (RMSE < 1.5 meV/atom) at a speedup factor of 10 5 . We identify a novel class of ”thermal-insulating” COFs with κ < 0.05 W/mK, driven by synchronized phonon rattling in large-pore imine-linked networks. Conversely, we discover high-thermal conductivity candidates facilitated by stiffened azobenzene linkages. This study elucidates the scaling relations between pore geometry, linker anharmonicity, and lattice heat transport, providing a comprehensive library of thermal properties for the COF Materials Genome.

papers.title: Rethinking Ytterbium(III)-based Single-Molecule Magnets -Why Trigonal Planar Doesn't Work!
papers.abstract: Yb(III)-based single-molecule magnets (SMMs) have remained conspicuously absent under zero-field conditions, appearing only with applied dc fields or under diamagnetic dilution. Utilising both CASSCF and CASPT2 methodologies, we systematically investigate the crystal field splitting of Yb(III) in a series of symmetry-constrained model complexes to elucidate the electronic origins of this limitation. By analysing equatorial ligand field environments that promote maximal axial anisotropy and benchmarking against the behaviour of Er(III), we identify fundamental differences in their electronic structures that disfavour slow magnetic relaxation in Yb(III). Quantitative estimates of the quantum tunnelling of magnetisation (QTM) rates reveal substantial transverse g-tensor components are intrinsic to Yb(III) in most high-symmetry coordination environments, leading to rapid zero-field relaxation. Notably, even ideal D 3h , D 4h , and D 6h symmetries fail to sufficiently suppress transverse anisotropy. Only D 5h and D 4d symmetries lead to the plausible prediction of SMM behaviour owing to the formal quenching of wavefunction mixing and thus QTM. Comparatively, Er(III) complexes systematically show higher g -tensor axiality, rationalising their superior zero-field performance. Using ideal crystal field parameterisation within a model Hamiltonian framework, we establish stringent symmetry criteria specifically for Yb(III) thereby guiding future synthetic efforts.

papers.title: Pan-Mitochondrial Privileged Scaffolds: Adenine, Pyridine, and a 7H-Purine Bioisostere as Multi-Target Fragments in the MitoCoreX Drug Discovery Campaign
papers.abstract: Background: Fragment-based drug discovery relies on identifying privileged scaffolds that exhibit broad activity across multiple biological targets. For mitochondrial therapeutics, no systematic characterization of pan-mitochondrial privileged scaffolds has been reported from a curated compound library. Identifying such scaffolds enables efficient generative design by providing validated starting points with demonstrated multi-target reach. Methods: Fragment-based analysis was performed on a 201-compound mitochondrial therapeutic library. Each compound was decomposed into constituent heterocyclic frameworks and evaluated for cross-target activity span, ligand efficiency (LE), and occurrence frequency. Scaffolds active across four or more structurally and functionally distinct mitochondrial targets were classified as privileged. Results: Three heterocyclic frameworks met the privileged scaffold criteria. Adenine (MW 135 Da, HA 10) achieved a maximum ligand efficiency of 0.96 kcal/mol/heavy atom across four targets spanning oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS, MT-CYB), voltage-dependent anion channel isoform 1 (VDAC1), mtDNA replication (TK2), and helicase activity (TWNK). Pyridine (MW 79 Da, HA 6) spanned DRP1 (fission machinery) and three additional targets. A 7H-purine variant (MW 120 Da) bridged Complex I (MT-ND1), TK2, VDAC1, and a purine kinase node. Each scaffold occurred in 4-8 library compounds. The cross-target reach of these three frameworks suggests a mitochondria-specific privileged scaffold space distinct from canonical kinase or protease pharmacophores. Conclusions: These findings represent, to the authors' knowledge, the first systematic characterization of pan-mitochondrial privileged scaffolds from a curated mitochondrial compound library. Fragment elaboration of PF_003 and PF_090 targeting the MTND1/VDAC1/TK2 axis is recommended as the first generative design objective for the MitoCoreX campaign.

papers.title: In Silico Pharmacological Profiling of MitoCorex Candidate Molecules: ADMET, Target Engagement, Selectivity, and Stability Analysis
papers.abstract: Background: In silico pharmacological profiling is the critical computational validation step between molecule design and experimental synthesis prioritization. Standard ADMET prediction platforms (pkCSM, SwissADME, ADMETlab 2.0) characterize compounds by generalized physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties but lack mitochondria-specific endpoints, creating a blind spot for the growing class of mitochondria-targeted therapeutics. Methods: Here we report the complete pharmacological profiling of 11 primary candidate molecules from the MitoCorex de novo design pipeline, applying a four-filter validation cascade: (i) Lipinski Rule of Five and PAINS screening, (ii) rescue mechanism compatibility assessment, (iii) selectivity threshold via a 72-rule SMARTS-based structural alert library derived from eight toxicology frameworks, and (iv) molecular dynamics stability proxy assessment. The 72-rule library spans 8 toxicological categories: PAINS interference (15 rules), Brenk unwanted substructures (13), reactive metabolite alerts (8), Ames mutagenicity alerts (10), mitochondrial toxicity alerts (8), hERG pharmacophore alerts (5), hepatotoxicity structural alerts (6), and phospholipidosis inducers (4). Additionally, three mitochondria-specific ADMET endpoints were evaluated: mitochondrial membrane permeability, mitochondrial accumulation potential, and inner membrane uncoupling risk. Results: All 11 candidates passed all four filter tiers with zero eliminations. Predicted GI absorption was HIGH for 9 of 11 candidates; BBB penetration was predicted for KND-002 (TPSA 49.3 Å², MW 271 Da). CYP3A4 risk was LOW for 8 and MODERATE for 3. hERG risk was LOW for all 11. Five synthesis priorities were identified: KND-002, PKA-002, DSA-001, SDA-002, and NDS-002. The 0% filter failure rate reflects front-loaded physicochemical property enforcement in molecule design rather than cascade leniency, corroborated by comparison to the 20–40% Lipinski failure rate expected in random drug-like libraries. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the feasibility of mitochondria-specific in silico profiling and provides a reusable 72-rule SMARTS library for mitochondrial drug discovery programs. Patent pending: US Provisional Application 64/018,624, filed March 27, 2026.

papers.title: Molecular Pinball: A Deterministic Chemistry Environment for Benchmarking Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: The paradigm shift from empirical reward modeling to rule-based verification has redefined modern reinforcement learning research. Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a cornerstone methodology for developing sophisticated reasoning capabilities in autonomous agents, circumventing the limitations of human-annotated preference data. By leveraging deterministic reward signals—such as the execution correctness of code or the logical validity of a mathematical proof—RLVR enables agents to learn through unconstrained exploration, implicitly incentivizing coherent, step-by-step reasoning. However, the application of RLVR has historically been restricted to purely textual, mathematical, or programmatic domains. The physical sciences, where reasoning requires navigating continuous spatial dynamics gated by discrete logical rules, present a largely untapped frontier.

papers.title: Enantioselective Preparation of α-Amino Ketones via Ni-Catalyzed Thermoredox Coupling of Enamines and Aldehydes
papers.abstract: This work describes a Ni-catalyzed, SiH/DTBP-mediated asymmetric thermoredox coupling of Bz-protected enamines with aldehydes, delivering chiral α-aminoketones in good coupling yields and high enantioselectivities. Enantioinduction arises from L n Ni II H migratory insertion into enamines, forming an N-α-C(sp 3 )–L n Ni II species. In parallel, the aldehyde carbonyl C–H bonds undergo HAT to tBuO· radical, generated via SET reduction of DTBP with L n Ni(I)X, to furnish an acyl radical. Radical capture then forms the key dicarbon–Ni III intermediate. Mechanistically, this pathway is distinct from existing Ni-catalyzed approaches to α-aminoketones and provides complementary substrate scope, accommodating readily accessible enamines and a wide range of alkyl/aryl aldehydes bearing functional groups, including those incompatible with photoredox conditions. By incorporation of an alkene-migration ligand enabled extension to linear amines bearing remote terminal alkenes, affording migratory hydroacylation products in high enantioselectivities and further broadening the scope of the method.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn at the author’s request due to presence of confidential research data.

papers.title: Effective Detergent-Free Removal of Blood Contamination from Surgical Instruments Using Hydrogen Nanobubble-Enhanced Electrolysed Alkaline Water and Sonication
papers.abstract: Background: Effective decontamination of reusable surgical instruments is essential for preventing healthcare-associated infections. Current standard protocols rely on specialised alkaline detergent solutions, which present logistical, environmental, and cost challenges. Aim: To evaluate a novel, detergent-free cleaning protocol combining hydrogen nanobubble-enhanced electrolysed alkaline water (EAW; pH 12.6) and sonication (40 kHz) against mock blood contamination on three types of difficult-to-clean surgical instruments. Methods: Haemostats, ENT suction catheters, and dental injection needle assemblies (n = 3 per group) were mock-contaminated with anticoagulated sheep blood and assigned to one of three protocols: negative control (RO water rinse only), conventional manual alkaline detergent cleaning (EBOS Pro Type, 1:1500 dilution), or the experimental nanobubble–EAW protocol (2 min electrolysis followed by 1 8 min sonication at 40 kHz). Residual protein was quantified using the Chemdye® PRO1 MICRO system (lower limit of quantification 1.0 µg). Pass/fail outcomes (<1.0 µg = pass) were compared using two-proportion z-tests (Python statsmodels 0.14.6). Findings: The experimental protocol achieved a 100% pass rate (9/9) compared with 67% for the conventional protocol (6/9) and 0% for the negative control (0/9). The experimental protocol significantly outperformed both the negative control (p < 0.0001) and the conventional protocol (p = 0.058). Conclusion: A detergent-free nanobubble–EAW protocol with sonication achieved superior surgical instrument decontamination compared with conventional alkaline detergent cleaning, offering a practical, cost-effective, and environmentally sustainable alternative for both centralised and decentralised healthcare settings.

papers.title: Towards Scalable and Efficient Machine-Learning Force Fields: The MatPL package and Its Advancements on Neuroevolution Potentials
papers.abstract: The development of accurate and efficient machine-learning interatomic potentials is a transformative technology in computational materials science and molecular dynamics simulations. Here, we introduce the Materials Potential Library (MatPL) , a comprehensive software framework integrating multiple machine-learning potential architectures, with a particular emphasis on advancing the neuroevolution potential (NEP) framework. MatPL incorporates gradient-based optimizers to improve training stability and accuracy. A key innovation is its highly optimized, GPU-native interface for LAMMPS, seamlessly integrated with LAMMPS’s robust Message Passing Interface (MPI) infrastructure. This design transcends the limitations of single-node GPU execution, enabling efficient cross-node scalability without compromising the computational efficiency intrinsic to NEP. MatPL is a high-performance and versatile platform for next-generation atomistic modeling, balancing between high accuracy, training efficiency, and large-scale simulation capability.

papers.title: Physics-Simulated Molecular Interactions Predict Olfactory Perception Without Pretrained Models
papers.abstract: Predicting olfactory similarity between molecular mixtures remains a fundamental challenge due to the absence of a universal structure-to-percept mapping. Existing approaches rely on pretrained representations or graph neural networks requiring large datasets. Here we introduce PhysSim, a physics simulation engine that predicts mixture similarity by evolving molecular embeddings under four fundamental forces -- gravity with general relativistic corrections, Coulombic interactions, van der Waals potentials, and spin-orbit coupling -- with learnable physical constants. These forces operate as structured inductive biases in a learned 128-dimensional latent space, constraining the model to only 162,315 parameters and seven learnable constants. Without pretrained models, PhysSim achieves Spearman rho = 0.613 on molecule-level cross-validation (Snitz 2013 dataset, 10 seeds x 5 folds, n = 50), significantly outperforming an attention-based mixture model inspired by POMMix (rho = 0.602, p = 0.050), Morgan fingerprint MLPs (rho = 0.584, p = 0.0002), message-passing neural networks (rho = 0.560, p < 1e-7), and descriptor-based MLPs using the same input features (rho = 0.508, p < 1e-14). In zero-shot transfer without fine-tuning, PhysSim achieves rho = 0.408 on a separate similarity dataset (Ravia 2020, 2.0x the RDKit cosine baseline) and rho = -0.492 on cross-task discriminability prediction (Bushdid 2014, 264 pairs). Ablation experiments confirm that Coulombic interactions provide the largest unique contribution (p = 0.022), and the learned physical constants converge to interpretable values that offer mechanistic insights into molecular interaction types governing olfactory perception.

papers.title: Synthesis-aware design rules for ammonia decomposition on Co-Ir-Ni-Rh-Ru alloys via segregation and surface-entropy retention
Guest-Induced Chirality Transfer in Trimers of Invertible Cylinder-Shaped Macrocycles
papers.abstract: Transfer of chiral information is abundant in biological processes. To mimic them in artificial systems, chiral macrocyclic molecules are particularly promising components for their simplicity and easy-to-predict intermolecular interactions. Herein, we report a chirality transfer system which shows turn-on chirality alignment of cylinder-shaped macrocycles with invertible chirality. The system is based on trimeric pillar[5]arene macrocycles linked covalently with alkyl chains. From a “native” state, the chirality changes to “off” and “on” states upon adding particular types of guest molecules for the macrocycle host components. Due to the weak inter-macrocycle interactions, the system can additionally switch the chirality from “on” state to “off” state, different from previous systems in which strong electrostatic interactions autonomously led to thermodynamically stable states.

papers.title: Atomic-Level Valence-State Engineering Redirects CO2 Electroreduction on Cu Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: Atomically precise thiolate-protected Cu nanoclusters (NCs) typically suffer from an intrinsic bias toward the two-electron formate pathway in CO2 electroreduction, limiting access to more deeply reduced products. Breaking this selectivity within a structurally well-defined system remains a significant challenge due to the difficulty of precisely tuning the Cu valence states. Here, we address this limitation through atomic-level valence-state engineering by introducing a sulfide-templated [S@Cu50S12(StBu)20(CF3COO)12] (S@Cu50) NC, featuring a controlled Cu(I)/Cu(II) ratio within an conserved structural framework. Single-crystal analysis reveals a core–shell S@Cu14S12@Cu36 architecture, while XPS confirms an increased Cu(II) population compared to the reference [Cu50S12(StBu)20(CF3COO)12] (Cu50) analogue. Despite similar overall catalytic activity, S@Cu50 exhibits a striking shift in product selectivity during CO2 electroreduction, suppressing formate formation (Faradaic efficiency of <11% vs. 38% in Cu50) and enabling CH3OH production with a Faradaic efficiency of ~19% at −1.0 V vs. RHE—absent in Cu50 system. DFT calculations attribute this mechanistic switching to valence-induced electronic modulation, which stabilizes CO-derived intermediates and promotes sequential hydrogenation toward CH3OH, in contrast to HCOO stabilization in the reference NC. This work establishes that subtle modulation of the Cu(I)/Cu(II) balance can fundamentally redirect reaction pathways, providing a molecular-level strategy to overcome intrinsic selectivity limitations in Cu NC catalysis.

papers.title: Intrinsically stretchable complementary circuits based on direct photo-patternable polymer semiconductors
papers.abstract: Intrinsically stretchable electronics have demonstrated potential in applications ranging from wearable health monitors to soft robotics. However, despite recent developments in material design, processing techniques and bio-integration, the fabrication of complementary circuits using scalable methods remains challenging. Here, we report intrinsically stretchable organic complementary circuits that are solution processed and based on direct photo-patternable polymer semiconductors with excellent processing stability. By covalently embedding a high-performance n-type polymer semiconductor inside an elastomer matrix, we fabricated fully stretchable transistors with electron mobilities of 0.28 cm 2 /V·s under 100% strain. Furthermore, with a covalent functionalization strategy on the p-type polymer semiconductor layer, we demonstrated successive, direct photo-patterning of n-type polymer semiconductors without electrical degradation on the existing p-type. We use this approach to fabricate intrinsically stretchable logic gates and ring oscillators with stable performance up to 100% strain at a low operating voltage of 2 V.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Large Language Models and Agentic AI Systems for Chemistry and Materials Science
papers.abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has catalyzed a paradigm shift in computational chemistry and materials science, evolving from passive prediction tools to active autonomous agents capable of orchestrating complex scientific workflows. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of LLM based systems in chemistry and materials science from 2020 onwards, establishing a taxonomy that progresses from domain specific language models through tool augmented systems to fully autonomous closed loop discovery platforms. We systematically examine chemical foundation models including ChemBERTa, MoLFormer, and MolT5, alongside materials-focused architecture such as MatSciBERT and MatterGPT. We evaluate their capabilities across molecular property prediction, reaction planning, materials design, and experimental optimization. The review critically analyzes agentic systems such as ChemCrow, Coscientist, and multi agent frameworks that integrate retrieval, simulation tools, and robotic laboratory interfaces to enable autonomous experimentation. Detailed benchmark mappings, evaluation metrics, and reproducibility standards are presented while addressing critical challenges in verification, safety, and trustworthiness for lab facing AI agents. Special emphasis is placed on grounding strategies to mitigate hallucinations, formal constraint validation, and human in the loop safeguards. Our analysis reveals that while current systems demonstrate impressive capabilities in constrained tasks, fundamental challenges remain in true chemical reasoning, uncertainty quantification, and long horizon planning. We conclude by outlining a research agenda for multimodal scientific foundation models, standardized community benchmarks, and governance frameworks necessary for the responsible deployment of autonomous discovery systems in chemistry and materials laboratories.

papers.title: Temperature Dependence of the Hydrated Electron’s g-Factor and Persistence of a Cavity-Localized Electron at Elevated Temperature
papers.abstract: The structure of the aqueous electron, e − (aq), has been the focus of intense scrutiny from both theory and experiment. The temperature dependence of its g -factor, measured via electron paramagnetic resonance and significantly shifted from the free-electron value, has been suggested to be inconsistent with the conventional picture of an electron localized in a cavity. Here, we use ab initio molecular dynamics simulations and quantum chemistry calculations to compute the ensemble-averaged, isotropic g -factor for e − (aq) over the entire liquid-phase temperature range. A temperature-dependent shift is obtained, in reasonable agreement with experiment, without any qualitative change in either the localized structure of e − (aq) or its average coordination number. Far from being inconsistent with the measurements, persistence of the cavity structure actually supports the rather mild temperature dependence of the g -factor because the amount of spin density hosted in oxygen orbitals, which is quantified by our calculations, is found to change very little with temperature. These results support a cavity structure for e − (aq) over the entire liquid range, T = 273–373 K at P = 1 atm. The simulations are broadly consistent with the fact that no abrupt changes in the absorption spectrum of e − (aq) are observed as a function of temperature or pressure, even into the supercooled and supercritical water regimes. This analysis further entrenches the cavity-centric picture of e − (aq).

papers.title: Bio-functionalized polymer semiconductors towards soft and stretchable transistor-based biosensors
papers.abstract: Organic materials with tunable chemical and mechanical properties are ideal for interfacing with skin and tissue in biomedical applications. While polymer semiconductors (PSCs) have advanced toward skin-like mechanical performance, the limited capacity for biofunctionalization has restricted their biosensing applications. In this study, we introduce a direct biofunctionalization strategy for PSCs based on thiol-ene chemistry. We selectively grafted thiolated biomolecules (e.g., aptamers) onto elastomeric domains within an interconnected semiconductor/elastomer network. This approach enables high-resolution patterning down to 10 µm while preserving the electronic performance of PSCs. Leveraging this platform, we designed and fabricated skin-like electrolyte-gated organic field-effect transistors (EG-OFETs) with biofunctionalized channels. These soft and stretchable devices exhibit stable operation in physiological buffers for over 50 days and maintain performance under up to 50% strain. When functionalized with cortisol-binding aptamers, the sensors achieved sensitive detection across physiologically relevant concentrations, down to the picomolar range. This work establishes a foundation for integrating stretchable and biofunctional PSCs into skin-like wearable devices.

papers.title: Physics-informed design of drug-excipient nanoparticles via free energy calculation and yoked deep learning
papers.abstract: The discovery of self-assembling molecular systems is often constrained by the high computational cost of physics-based simulations and the limited generalizability of data-driven models trained on experimental datasets. This limits our ability to efficiently navigate massive design spaces. Here, we introduce a physics-informed discovery framework that integrates free-energy calculations with sequential-pool active learning and adaptive yoked deep learning to effectively navigate vast chemical coassembly spaces. Using pairwise free energy as a physically grounded descriptor of co-assembly propensity and excipient net charge as a proxy for interfacial stabilization, our approach predicts nanoparticle-forming drug–excipient combinations without relying on experimental data for model training. Our sequential-pool yoked deep learning strategy utilizes adaptive machine learning to reduce the number of expensive simulations required while maintaining predictive accuracy, enabling screening of 18 million molecular pairs. Prospective validations identified 24 drug nanoparticles using eight previously unknown stabilizing molecules. The new nanoparticles exhibit ultra-high drug loading, effectively improve the aqueous solubility of drugs, and maintain in vitro drug efficacy. Together, this work establishes a generalizable framework coupling molecular simulations and yoked deep learning to accelerate discovery in self-assembling molecular systems.

papers.title: Acetylene Functionalization of Multiple-resonant Emitter Enabling Strong Two-Photon Absorption and Delayed Luminescence with Highly Efficient Exciplex-Sensitized Electroluminescence
papers.abstract: Two-photon absorbing luminophores with narrowband emission are rare despite growing demand for color-pure optoelectronic materials. Multiple-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters offer intrinsically narrow emission, but their nonlinear optical response remains largely unexplored. Here, we report an acetylene, core-induced charge transfer (CT) strategy that enables significant two-photon absorption (2PA), two-photon delayed luminescence and highly efficient exciplex-sensitized electroluminescence in a dipolar MR-TADF emitter, DtCzBCCH. Installation of a terminal acetylene moiety extends π-conjugation and delocalizes the LUMO, introducing some degree of intramolecular CT (ICT) character to the second singlet excited state (S2), which is responsible for 2PA. This enhances the two-photon absorption cross-section from 36 GM for parent molecule, DtCzB to 156 GM for DtCzBCCH, while preserving unity photoluminescence quantum yield and narrowband emission. Exciplex-host sensitized solution-processed and vacuum-deposited OLEDs deliver color-pure green electroluminescence with a peak external quantum efficiency of 25.2 %, retaining 94.2 % efficiency at 1000 cd m-2 and operational stability up to LT50 = 30 h. This acetylene-mediated multiresonance CT design provides a general route to integrate strong 2PA with color-pure, efficient, and stable electroluminescence for integrated optoelectronic-photonic applications.

papers.title: Autonomous Computational Catalysis Research via Agentic Systems
papers.abstract: Fully automating the scientific process is a transformative ambition in materials science, yet current artificial intelligence masters isolated workflow fragments. In computational catalysis, a system autonomously navigating the entire research lifecycle from conception to a scientifically meaningful manuscript remains an open challenge. Here we present CatMaster, a catalysis-native multi-agent framework that couples project-level reasoning with the direct execution of atomistic simulations, machine-learning modelling, literature analysis, and manuscript production within a unified autonomous architecture. Across progressively demanding evaluations, CatMaster achieves perfect scores on four end-to-end short-form catalysis scenarios, reaches near-leaderboard performance on five of six MatBench tasks, performs self-discovery of reaction mechanisms grounded in literature or from scratch, and executes a fully closed-loop single-atom catalyst design problem. Together, these results show that end-to-end autonomous computational catalysis is now practical for research programmes, while highlighting that bridging the gap to genuine scientific closure requires tighter integration with reliable physical engines and domain-rigorous methodologies.

papers.title: Chiroptical Properties, Electronic Structure, and Multicenter Bonding in a Dissymmetric Binuclear Beryllium Alkyl Complex: Be2(C(CH3)2)2
papers.abstract: The electronic structure, bonding, and chiroptical signatures of the binuclear beryllium complex Be2(C(CH3)2)2 were characterized using density functional theory (DFT) and topological analysis. The results reveal a remarkably short Be–Be distance of 1.9219 Å with a Mayer bond order (MBO) of 0.705. Topological analysis via the Electron Localization Function (ELF) and Atoms in Molecules (AIM) identifies a framework stabilized by multicentre Be–C–Be interactions rather than a direct metal–metal covalent bond. The simulated UV–Vis and Electronic Circular Dichroism (ECD) spectra exhibit a prominent feature at 362.3 nm, identified through Natural Transition Orbital (NTO) analysis as a metal-cantered σ to σ* excitation with significant charge-transfer character.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Guided Bayesian Optimization of Ag+ Doping in CdSe Nanoplatelets Enables Deterministic Optical Prediction across the Gamut
papers.abstract: Heterovalent doping is a versatile strategy for modulating the otherwise discrete optical properties of cadmium selenide nanoplatelets. However, identifying the correlation between ideal synthetic parameters and desired optical outcome is challenging due to the large experimental space. We present a machine learning–driven application for rapidly optimizing post-synthetic Ag+ doping in CdSe nanoplatelets. Using Bayesian Optimization with In-Context Learning (BO-ICL) on large language models, our approach directly integrates continuous and categorical synthesis and cationexchange experimental variables to predict and improve photophysical properties. Specifically, we jointly optimize the total quantum yield and dopant peak area to capture the trade-off between emissive efficiency and spectral tunability. Compared to a Gaussian Process baseline, the LLM-based optimizer recommends high-performing experimental protocols with fewer trials. Moreover, we illustrate interpretability via SHAP values, revealing that doping percentage, dopant mass, reaction volumes, and NPL dimensions are the most influential factors in controlling the photoluminescence response. In addition, we demonstrate the use of accurate multidimensional color predictions from BO-ICL, without excessive fine-tuning, to obtain experimentally accurate optical responses on a CIE chromaticity plot. This one-step method underscores the promise of large-language models to accelerate materials innovation and holds the potential to guide the rational design of doped nanocrystal systems.

papers.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of P(V)-Stereogenic Phosphacycles by NHC-Catalyzed Desymmetric Annulation
papers.abstract: P(V)-stereogenic compounds show diverse biological properties and remain as a focal point in medicinal chemistry and agrochemicals. Traditional approaches to access enantioenriched P(V)-stereogenic molecules largely depend on chromatographic resolution, chiral auxiliaries, and/or the use of optically active starting materials. In contrast, catalytic strategies have recently advanced, with desymmetric substitution emerging as a powerful method for generating P(V) stereocenters. However, current strategies are predominantly restricted to acyclic systems, where control is exerted solely over the P(V) stereogenic center. Herein, we report the first N- heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-catalyzed desymmetric annulation for the enantio- and diastereoselective synthesis of phosphacycles bearing P(V) and C-stereogenic center at 1,4-positions. The control over remote chirality and multiple stereogenic center are the key challenges of the present strategy, which was successfully achieved by choosing the suitable NHC precursor and substrate. DFT studies shed light on the importance of the annulation step, rather than the initial NHC addition to the aldehyde, as the crucial step for the enantio- and diastereoselectivity control of the reaction. The derivatization of the synthesized seven membered phosphacycles emphasizes the practical utility of the present methodology.

papers.title: Topological and Energetic Landscapes of a Binuclear Beryllium Complex: Identifying Non-Nuclear Attractors and Correlation-Driven Stability
papers.abstract: The nature of metal-metal bonding in main-group elements remains a significant challenge for electronic structure theory. In this work, we present a comprehensive computational study of a binuclear beryllium complex, Be2C12N2H14, utilizing Density Functional Theory (DFT) and high-level DLPNO-CCSD(T) calculations. The complex features a remarkably short Be–Be bond of 1.884 Å. Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) and Energy Decomposition Analysis (EDA-NOCV) confirm a strong covalent σ-bond stabilized by significant electron correlation and electrostatic interactions. Topological analysis via the Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) reveals the presence of non-nuclear attractors, characterizing a unique electron-trapping bonding environment. Time-Dependent DFT (TD-DFT) predicts an intense absorption peak at 399.8 nm, suggesting potential applications in optoelectronic materials.

papers.title: From Fluorine to Chlorine: How Atomic Vibrations Enable Efficient Triplet Harvesting in Crystalline TADF Scintillators
papers.abstract: Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) offers a powerful route for harvesting triplet excitons in organic scintillators, yet achieving simultaneously small singlet–triplet gaps and efficient spin–orbit coupling (SOC) in rigid molecular crystals remains a fundamental challenge. Here we demonstrate that targeted halogen substitution can activate vibrationally assisted spin-flip channels that dramatically enhance triplet harvesting in crystalline donor-acceptor emitters, tailoring them for scintillators with higher light yield and faster response times. Using DMAC-TRZ derivatives bearing fluorine or chlorine substituents, we combine single-crystal structural analysis, temperature-resolved photoluminescence, radioluminescence spectroscopy, and quantum-chemical calculations to reveal how subtle changes in halogen chemistry control excited-state dynamics. While fluorination reduces sharply the singlet-triplet energy gap, chlorine additionally introduces dynamic SOC enhancement mediated by the vibrations of Cl atoms within the crystal lattice. As a result, the chlorinated crystal exhibits an exceptionally small activation energy (Ea = 3.9 meV), (sub)microsecond-scale delayed fluorescence, and a scintillation yield of 26 000 photons MeV-1. These results reveal a powerful, atom-economical approach to achieving near S1-T1 degeneracy combined with vibrationally activated heavy-atom effects, enabling high-performance TADF scintillators in organic crystals.

papers.title: Computational Methods in Physical Virology: A Critical Perspective Across Lengths and Timescales
papers.abstract: Physical virology investigates viral particles by focusing on their assembly, stability, mechanics, and interactions with host cells, neutralizing antibodies, and surfaces. Within this field, computational virology is becoming an indispensable pillar, serving as a “computational microscope” that bridges the spatio-temporal scales of viral processes, from individual protein dynamics to capsid assembly and cellular entry. This perspective article offers a critical overview of the current state, challenges, and future directions of computational approaches in physical virology. Our vision is anchored in the research presented at the 2025 EMBO/FEBS Lecture Course on Physical Virology held in Sant Feliu de Guixols, Spain, and complemented by a targeted survey among attendees. We survey the principal methodological frameworks in use, from all-atom to multiscale molecular simulations, mesoscale simulations, and growing integration of artificial intelligence tools. We also critically examine the central obstacles impeding the field's progress, including the computational–experimental interface gap, limited accessibility to simulation data, reproducibility concerns, and systemic gender and geographic inequities. Finally, we outline future perspectives, proposing that integrating physics-aware AI with multiscale simulation frameworks, combined with community-driven data-sharing initiatives, will transform the computational microscope from a descriptive tool into a predictive engine for antiviral therapies, rational vaccine design, and biotechnological innovation.

papers.title: Crosslinking of Linear Polyimines into Aminal-Linked Porous Organic Polymers for Efficient Hydrocarbon Separation
papers.abstract: Hypercrosslinked polymers, a class of porous organic polymers (POPs), are constructed by crosslinking linear polymers or knitting small aromatic molecules with a molecular crosslinker, typically via Friedel–Crafts alkylation. In this study, we report a new approach for the synthesis of POPs via the crosslinking of linear polyimines with m‑phenylenediamine through nucleophilic addition of amines to imines, forming aminal linkages. The resulting aminallinked POPs, with an estimated low cost of 16 USD/kg, exhibited high surface areas up to 650 m2/g and abundant microporosity, in contrast to the ~100 m2/g observed for the linear polyimine. This method demonstrated good generality: four linear polyimines with different structures were successfully crosslinked into POPs with high porosity. Both experimental results and theoretical calculations indicate that the use of diamines at the meta-position is critical for efficient crosslinking, whereas para-diamines did not initiate crosslinking. With their high surface area and rich microporosity, these POPs displayed high adsorption capacities for C2 hydrocarbons and CO2, but significantly lower capacity for CH4. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirmed excellent separation performance for C2 hydrocarbons/CH4 mixtures, highlighting their potential for hydrocarbon separation. This study provides a new strategy for the synthesis of cost-effective POPs and demonstrates their promising applications in gas separation.
