An equation-oriented approach is used for techno-economic optimization for minimizing the levelized cost of adhesive (LCOA). It is found that the plant consisting of a plug flow reactor for the BCD reaction of kraft lignin along with a hybrid heat integration approach via vapor compression and supplementary low pressure steam results in the best economic performance. The minimum LCOA is found to be $634.21/mt, which is very competitive considering the current approximate market price of $1000 – 4000/mt for commercial adhesives, including bio-based adhesives.

papers.title: Towards Tailored Metastability: Exploring Oxanorbornene Chemical Space for Structure-Stability Relationships with Atypical Furan Diels-Alder Adducts
papers.abstract: The furan Diels-Alder (DA) cycloaddition is a highly versatile synthetic tool in the design of smart and biobased molecular and macromolecular applications. As a prototypical example of reversible reactions, it is ideally suited for exploring intrinsic chemical metastability, i.e. how to introduce a degree of non-persistence, tailored to an envisaged application, into the molecular architecture. While the (furan) DA field has seen tremendous progress since its emergence nearly a century ago, its scope remains largely limited to combinations of activated addends. Here, we explore previously inaccessible areas of the oxanorbornene chemical space by investigating the properties of atypical furan DA (formal) adducts and demonstrate that stability against cycloreversion, i.e. their metastability, can be altered over six orders of magnitude. The emerging structure-stability relationships provide new insights into the delicate kinetics/thermodynamics interplay of furan [4+2] cycloadditions, paving the way for the rational design of applications that exploit either direction of the DA equilibrium. Such tailored non-persistence can be exploited as a strategy for a sustainable materials transition.

papers.title: Ensemble Siamese Neural Networks for Prodrug Activation Prediction
papers.abstract: Prodrug design enhances critical drug properties by harnessing metabolic activation to release the active pharmaceutical ingredient. However, predicting prodrug activation remains challenging, causing design failures and limiting systematic exploration of prodrug design spaces. Here, we developed an ensemble Siamese neural network model to predict prodrug activation. We demonstrate that our model accurately captures prodrug activations from molecular structure, including in a prospective, in-house prodrug development effort. The model reliably identifies competing metabolic pathways and distinguishes true activations from metabolic counterfactuals. Attribution analysis reveals that predictions are driven by chemically meaningful substructures associated with site-specific reactivity. Taken together, this work establishes a generalizable framework for prodrug activation prediction and suggests that key determinants of metabolic reactivity can be learned directly from molecular structure, which could enable more rational prodrug design to accelerate the development of safer and more effective medicines.

papers.title: Armstrong's Range Exponent Electron Configuration Model (AREECM)
papers.abstract: Traditional electron-configuration notation (e.g. 1s22s22p6) compresses multi-electron quantum information into integer occupancies that convey allowed maxima and most-probable arrangements but obscure the underlying probabilistic distribution and the spread of possible measurement outcomes. We present a representation that replaces integer superscripts with explicit occupancy measures derived from quantum mechanical one-electron observables: (i) spatial probability mass within physically defined volumes (Parr & Yang, 1989), and (ii) orbital occupation numbers obtained from the one-electron reduced density matrix (1-RDM) and its natural orbitals (Löwdin, 1955). We define notation, a canonical algorithm to compute occupancy ranges [PMin, PMax​] for each labeled orbital or spatial zone, and discuss practical choices (partitioning scheme, quality of electronic structure method). This representation is purely notational, it does not change quantum mechanics, but it makes probabilistic information explicit and quantifies the uncertainty and spread that the integer notation hides.

papers.title: Should I Stay or Should I Go? - Leveraging an Overlooked Feature of Click-to-Release Chemistry for Affinity Labeling
papers.abstract: Click-to-release (C2R) chemistry is widely used for controlled payload liberation, yet the chemical reactivity of its transient intermediates has remained largely unexplored. Here we show that an intermediate formed during the reaction of trans -cyclooctene (TCO)-appended protein-targeting ligands with release tetrazines (rTzs), previously regarded as a byproduct rapidly quenched by water, can be viewed from a different perspective and exploited as an electrophile for ligand-directed covalent protein labeling. The bioorthogonally generated dihydropyridazine methide (DHP-methide) enables affinity-directed protein labeling that predominantly results in capture at surface-exposed histidine residues proximal to the site of electrophile generation, revealing a histidine-biased covalent modification pathway. Incorporation of functional handles into the rTz platform enables modular reporter installation via orthogonal bioorthogonal reactions. A fluorogenic leaving group design further allows direct optical reporting of the electrophile-generating elimination event, enabling real-time monitoring of DHP-methide formation during the labeling process. Selective labeling is retained in complex protein mixtures and in spiked lysate experiments and can be translated to a cellular context, as demonstrated by confocal imaging of surface-expressed targets following post-labeling fluorophore installation. These findings reframe a mechanistic intermediate of click-to-release chemistry as a functional electrophile for ligand-directed protein modification and establish a previously unrecognized bioorthogonally gated strategy for affinity labeling.

papers.title: Mapping the Conformational Landscape of the Cold-Regulated Intrinsically Disordered Protein COR15A
papers.abstract: Cold regulated protein 15A (COR15A) is a late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) protein from Arabidopsis thaliana that is expressed in response to low temperatures and dehydration. Here, we use a combination of ion mobility-mass spectrometry (IM-MS) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations at elevated temperatures for enhanced sampling to explore the conformational landscape of COR15A. The IM-MS data display charge states from +5 to +12, and collision cross section (CCS) distributions indicative of two dominant coexisting conformational families centered on approximately 1200 and 1800 Å 2 , with subconformers evident. The structures sampled with MD are histogrammed, which provides a pseudo -CCS distribution ( p CCS) highly similar to experimental IM-MS data, allowing us to compare with SAXS-derived structures of COR15A in functional conditions. This approach gives compelling evidence that the experimental gas-phase data correspond to natively accessible states. In contrast to commonly used biophysical approaches, IM-MS permits simultaneous observation of disordered forms as well as conformers populated upon dehydration, allowing insights into dehydration-responsive LEA proteins.

papers.title: Synthesis of Azidosugar and Thioglycoside Building Blocks Using EtOAc, EtOH and Cyclopentyl Methyl Ether (CPME) as Greener Solvents
papers.abstract: There is a need to decrease the use of hazardous substances in chemical synthesis. Lewis acid promoted reactions to prepare thioglycosides or azidosugars are often performed in dichloromethane (DCM). The US environmental protection agency has recently prohibited most industrial and commercial uses of DCM, due to its hazardous nature, requiring alternative solvents to be identified. The azide group is widely used in click chemistry or as a precursor to amines or in other reactions, indicating azidosugars have wide applications. Thioglycosides are widely used in glycoside synthesis or investigated as glycomimetics. Here, we replace DCM as a solvent for preparing glycosyl azides and thioglycosides with more desirable EtOAc or cyclopentyl methyl ether (CPME). In addition, we used EtOH-EtOAc mixtures for global deacetylation reactions, as an alternative to MeOH, as MeOH is significantly more toxic than EtOH (ethanol). We also describe oxidation of diacetone-d-glucose to its ketone derivative using Dess-Martin periodinane (DMP) in EtOAc as solvent, rather than in DCM. A deterrent to using green solvents may be that they are more costly than traditional solvents, with CPME, for example, being currently >3-fold more expensive than DCM. However, researchers can minimise the quantity of CPME used and add EtOAc to facilitate reaction work-up.

papers.title: Widespread Omission of Aptamer-Target Binding Verification in Aptasensor Development: Consequences for Sensor Performance and the Need for a Kd Gate
papers.abstract: Aptamer-based biosensors (aptasensors) are widely explored for diagnostics because aptamers combine molecular recognition with scalable chemical synthesis. Yet aptasensors have achieved limited translational impact, motivating scrutiny of development practices. Critical reviews emphasize verifying target binding of the aptamer construct by determining its equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd, a standard measure of binding strength) prior to aptasensor development to avoid interface-contingent artifacts. We refer to this pre-development requirement as the Kd gate: an auditable, construct-matched determination of Kd in homogeneous, non-denaturing solution under sensing-relevant conditions. Here we assess compliance with the Kd gate by analyzing 208 aptasensor publications spanning six targets. Only 19 of 208 papers reported any solution-phase verification assay, and none passed the Kd gate; the few Kd values reported in solution were weakly constrained or format-contingent and therefore not auditable. As a result, reported sensor-performance claims often cannot be interpreted, transferred, or optimized on a fully rational basis. Because well-established solution-phase Kd-determination methods are available, this persistent omission is unlikely to be explained solely by technical infeasibility. We conclude that voluntary recommendations have not, in practice, functioned as an effective gate and that passing the Kd gate should become a mandatory requirement, supported by a checklist that enables editors and reviewers to audit compliance.

papers.title: Neural Network-Accelerated Bayesian Inference for Rapid and Interpretable SAXS Analysis

Integrated Simulation of Grid and Solar PV-Powered Alkaline Water Electrolysis for Green Hydrogen Production from Seawater: An Electrical and Chemical Process Study Using MATLAB/Simulink and Aspen Plus
papers.abstract: This study presents an integrated simulation framework for green hydrogen production combining MATLAB/Simulink electrical modelling with Aspen Plus chemical process simulation. A dual-source power system comprising a three-phase grid supply and a solar photovoltaic array with lithium-ion battery storage drives an alkaline electrolyzer consuming 229 kW. The electrical model employs a six-pulse diode rectifier, a tap-changing transformer, and a DC-DC buck converter for power conditioning. The Aspen Plus model encompasses seawater pretreatment, two-stage reverse osmosis desalination, electrodeionization, alkaline electrolysis with KOH electrolyte at 80°C, hydrogen drying, multistage compression to 200 bar, cooling, and pressure swing adsorption purification. Simulation results demonstrate a hydrogen production rate of 4.99 kg/hr, specific energy consumption of 53.5 kWh/kg, voltage efficiency of 65.88%, and final hydrogen purity of 99% at 200 bar. The ELECNRTL thermodynamic property method ensures rigorous electrolyte solution modelling. This integrated approach provides a foundation for techno-economic optimization of utility-scale green hydrogen plants.

papers.title: BRIDGING SMALL MOLECULES AND POLYMERS: A COARSE-GRAINED GRAPH PRETRAINING FRAMEWORK FOR POLYMER PROPERTY PREDICTION
papers.abstract: Polymer property prediction is limited by scarce labeled data and the poor transferability of atom-level molecular representations to macromolecules and experimentally relevant polymer systems. Here we introduce CGMNet, a fragmentation-aware coarse-grained graph pretraining framework that uses chemically meaningful fragments as a shared structural vocabulary across small molecules and polymers. Pretrained on unlabeled small molecules by fragment identity prediction on coarsegrained graphs, CGMNet learns transferable chemical semantics while remaining competitive with leading atom-level models on standard small-molecule benchmarks. When transferred to polymers, CGMNet performs strongly across nine datasets spanning DFT-derived, MD-derived and experimental properties, achieving the best performance on seven of the nine properties with the most suitable fragmentation scheme in each case. Beyond idealized linear homopolymer benchmarks, CGMNet also extends to more complex polymer systems specified as heterogeneous formulations, where fragment-based encoders outperform molecule-level mixing across thermoset datasets. Together, these results show that CGMNet can support polymer representation learning not only for idealized benchmarks, but also for structurally heterogeneous systems closer to practical applications.

papers.title: Photochemically Triggered Para-Hydrogen-Induced Polarization in a Diplatinum Trihydride Complex
papers.abstract: Transition metal complexes containing platinum(II) are of substantial interest for their rich photophysics, biomedical applications, and catalytic function. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra of the spin-1/2 isotope, 195 Pt, offer detailed insights into the molecular structures of closed-shell Pt(II) complexes, including solvent effects. However, the sensitivity of 195 Pt NMR is mediocre, and its NMR spectra are typically complex. As a result, 1 H NMR spectra are used as the primary characterization tool for Pt(II)-based molecules, relying on J -coupling to the 195 Pt nucleus to provide structural information from the resulting satellite peaks. In efforts to significantly improve the information content from 1 H NMR spectroscopy in a Pt(II)-containing molecule, we utilize [Pt 2 H 2 (μ-H)(μ-dppm) 2 ]PF 6 , where dppm is bis(diphenylphosphino)methane, and leverage its established photoactivity with UV light and H 2 for para-hydrogen-induced polarization (PHIP) to enhance the resultant NMR signals, revealing numerous 195 Pt J-couplings. Moreover, we investigate direct solvent hyperpolarization effects, as well as the indirect effects of solvent on the various observed J -coupling constants in the Pt species, demonstrating correlations with both Lewis basicity and dielectric constant.

papers.title: Atomistic Simulations of Biomolecular Condensates
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates formed through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) play essential roles in various cellular processes. Understanding the molecular interactions, conformational dynamics, and solvent effects within these condensates is important for elucidating their functionality. However, studying these properties remains challenging. Atomistic condensedphase simulations provide a powerful computational approach to complement experimental studies by offering high-resolution insights into these complex systems. In this chapter, we present a workflow for generating atomistic structures of biomolecular condensates from coarse-grained (CG) simulations. By performing coexistence CG simulations, we obtain equilibrated condensedphase structures, which are then backmapped to all-atom (AA) models. We outline the technical considerations and common challenges in obtaining stable AA configurations and provide strategies for generating robust condensed-phase structures for molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. This approach enables the characterization of intermolecular interactions, solvent and ion partitioning, and conformational properties. We anticipate this chapter will serve as a valuable resource for researchers studying atomistic condensed phase simulations, providing a framework for investigating the molecular mechanisms underlying phase separation and further advancing our understanding of biomolecular organization and function.

papers.title: Time-Resolved Single-Particle Kinetics of Light-Directed Electrophoretic Deposition
papers.abstract: Electrophoretic deposition (EPD) is widely used in research and industry to create thin, uniform films from colloidal suspensions on conductive surfaces. The operational simplicity of EPD has facilitated steady methodological and theoretical advances over the past century. However, our current mechanistic understanding of deposition remains indirect, rooted in theory and ex-situ bulk measurements. Here, we introduce an interferometric scattering (iSCAT) microscopy methodology that enables direct, real-time spatiotemporal monitoring of the electrode during EPD. Using this approach, we detect and localize polystyrene nanoparticles as small as 15 nm. Real-time video captures the evolving deposition landscape, offering a highly sensitive and versatile platform that reveals electrochemical double-layer formation and deposition kinetics under varying photoelectrochemical conditions.

papers.title: Concise Synthesis of Stephadiamine via Vinylogous Wenker Cyclization
papers.abstract: A short and diastereoselective synthesis of stephadiamine is presented. The carbocyclic framework of the alkaloid was built in the opening step through a homoconjugate addition–Wittig olefination cascade with a modified Schweizer–Fuchs cyclopropyl phosphonium salt. The challenging aza[4.3.3]propellane was subsequently installed through a vinylogous substitution of an allylic hydroxyl group with a primary amine that was developed for the purposes of the synthesis. After a series of oxidations, a second α-tertiary amine was introduced through a diastereoselective Strecker reaction, thus establishing the syn-diamine motif. Finally, an undesired retro-Strecker pathway was circumvented by using an azide functionality to mask the primary amine during a late-stage lactonization, thus enabling the completion of the synthesis in twelve steps.

papers.title: Anion transport and selectivity in ordered nanoporous polymers with 1 nm scale charged pores
papers.abstract: Solvated ions of the same valency and charge exhibit minor differences in bulk transport but may display strong ion-specific effects in nanoscale environments. Investigating such effects is challenged by the heterogeneous nature of conventional nanostructured membranes, which can smear out underlying structure-property correlations. We use a combination of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy, NMR relaxometry, and molecular dynamics simulations to systematically investigate anion transport in nanoporous polymers with uniform charged 1 nm scale pores. The pores are water-containing channels formed by lyotropic self-assembly of positively charged amphiphilic monomers that are then crosslinked to produce a highly ordered nanoporous polymer. Across a series of monovalent anions, we observe strong correlations of activation energy and conductivity with hydration enthalpy – more strongly hydrated species have higher conductivity and lower activation energies. These effects originate from differences in pore-wall interactions and solvation shell behavior, with more weakly hydrated species showing larger departures from their bulk behavior in their water coordination and activation energy in the membrane. Our results indicate that pore confinement amplifies the impact of water contributions to ion motion. Specifically, the ability to maintain hydration shell waters and concomitantly, to avoid interactions with hydrophobic pore wall patches, leads to significant differences in transport, and to ion-specific trends that are unexpected in nanoporous materials. These results provide new insight into ion transport in highly confined and hydration-limited geometries and suggest a mechanism by which ion selectivity can be explicitly manipulated.

papers.title: Computational Characterization of Three Novel Molecules: The Asymmetric Proton-Bridged Cation [ArHKr]+, the Noble-Gas Metal Hydride XeAuH, and the Bismuth Tetrahydride Anion [BiH4]
papers.abstract: We report the computational characterization of three novel molecules using density functional theory, contributing to the fields of theoretical inorganic chemistry, relativistic bonding, and computational astrochemistry. The asymmetric proton-bridged cation [ArHKr]+ is characterized at the PBE0/aug-cc-pVTZ level. The optimized geometry places the proton closer to krypton (H–Kr = 1.588 Å) than to argon (Ar–H = 1.526 Å), fully consistent with krypton's higher proton affinity (PA(Kr) = 424.3 kJ/mol vs. PA(Ar) = 369.2 kJ/mol) and confirmed by the Mayer bond order asymmetry (H–Kr = 0.601 vs. Ar–H = 0.440). The CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ dipole moment of 1.666 Debye enables potential radioastronomical detection at 3.637 GHz. The dissociation energy to KrH+ + Ar is 56.4 kJ/mol. The linear noble-gas metal hydride XeAuH is characterized at B3LYP/def2-TZVP with a confirmed Xe–Au covalent bond at 2.905 Å (Mayer bond order 0.196), dipole moment 3.364 Debye, Au–H stretching frequency 2186.74 cm−1, and dissociation energy to AuH + Xe of 22.6 kJ/mol. The bismuth tetrahydride anion [BiH4]− is characterized at B3LYP/def2-TZVP as the first Group 15 [MH4]− species, adopting a see-saw C2v geometry with Bi–H bond lengths of 1.803 Å (axial) and 2.148 Å (equatorial), dipole moment 2.620 Debye, and dissociation energy to BiH3 + H− of 148.8 kJ/mol. Geometry optimizations at the ωB97X-D3 level confirm all key structural conclusions. All three species exhibit exclusively positive harmonic vibrational frequencies confirming true potential energy minima.

papers.title: Fluid Dynamics and Cavitation Revisited
papers.abstract: A Fluid Dynamics methodology for predicting three-dimensional flows with extensive cavitation is revisited. The model is based on the multiphase flow equations, with mass transfer due to cavitation appearing as source and sink terms in the liquid and vapour continuity equations. The mass transfer rate is derived from a simplified Rayleigh-Plesset model, which remains the foundation of contemporary cavitation modeling approaches. The methodology is implemented within a control volume finite element framework featuring implicit coupling of continuity and momentum equations. The model is validated on a range of applications including flow over a hydrofoil, an inducer, and transient cavitation in a venturi. Recent advancements in turbulence modeling for cavitating flows, including compressibility-enhanced formulations and scaleresolving simulations, are discussed within the context of modern computational capabilities. Key words: Caviation, Rayleigh-Plesset, Hydrofoil, Inducer, Venturi-cavitation

papers.title: Albumin-Anchored Triggered Release (AATR): A Universal Modular Platform for Targeted Drug Delivery
papers.abstract: Contemporary pharmacology treats albumin binding as a liability: it compresses the free drug fraction, necessitates loading doses, and produces systemic toxicity before therapeutic concentrations reach target tissue. Six decades of dosing architecture built around compensating for this binding constitute, in aggregate, the empirical demonstration that Human Serum Albumin is the dominant force in drug distribution. The field has been managing a system it has not chosen to engineer. Albumin-Anchored Triggered Release (AATR) converts this involuntary function into a controlled delivery platform. The architecture is a three-module conjugate: a high-affinity Albumin Key recruits the conjugate onto albumin and maintains sub-clinical free fractions throughout systemic transit; a microenvironment-sensitive Cleavable Linker holds the assembly intact under physiological conditions and cleaves upon detecting a pathological signal; and the unmodified Drug is released as a progressive local concentration at the target site. Transport and pharmacological action are structurally decoupled. The drug cargo requires no metabolic activation upon release. At sites of disease where vascular integrity is compromised, albumin extravasates through damaged endothelium and accumulates in the diseased interstitium via impaired lymphatic clearance. This passive pre-enrichment concentrates the conjugate at target tissue before the trigger fires, functioning as a pharmacokinetic amplifier on top of the active release mechanism. AATR does not depend on this phenomenon for release selectivity; the active trigger operates independently of vascular architecture. We analyse the medicinal chemistry feasibility, pharmacokinetic implications, engineering constraints, and boundary conditions governing generalisation of this architecture across drug classes and pathological targets.

papers.title: Diastereoselective Access to Densely-Functionalized Azaspirobicyclic Scaffolds from Bicyclobutanes
papers.abstract: Azaspiro[3.3]heptanes are known as conformationally stable bioisosteres of piperidines in drug discovery. However, the limited number of synthetic routes to access diverse derivatives of these scaffolds poses a major challenge to their use in medicinal chemistry. We report a one-step addition/spirocyclization process between N-alkyl imines and bicyclobutanes that forms 2-azaspiro[3.3]hept-5-en-1-ones. These densely-functionalized scaffolds serve as access points to several azaspirocyclic structures. In addition to N-functionalization through reduction, deprotection, and acylation, we demonstrate skeletal rearrangements to spirocyclic [2.3] and [3.4] systems from the parent molecule.

papers.title: Hydrazine Production via Chemical Looping of Electrochemically Synthesized Concentrated Bleach
papers.abstract: Distributed production of hydrazine, an energy-dense fuel and valuable commodity chemical, can enable energy resilience and flexibility in resource-constrained areas. In this work, we electrify the Bayer Ketazine process and demonstrate a bench-top device for modular, distributed hydrazine production. By implementing an anode assembly with gas permeable membrane, we electrochemically produce bleach with transient chlorine gas in the system, achieving a 75% Faradaic efficiency and concentrations of up to 1.67 ± 0.02 M, an order of magnitude more concentrated than conventional onepot electrochemical bleach production systems. When combined in a tandem reactor setup, we used this electrochemically generated hypochlorite to synthesize hydrazine, achieving 25% electron-to-azine efficiency while looping the hypochlorite via recycling of the sodium chloride salt. This system demonstrates that electrochemical processes can enable modular production of fuels and commodity chemicals, enabling access to these important chemicals and fuels in logistically isolated locations with limited feedstocks.

papers.title: Synthesis and Conversion of InAsxP1-x Alloy Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: III–V semiconductor alloys offer a powerful platform for bandgap engineering, yet achieving precise compositional control in colloidal nanocrystals remains a challenge. Here, we report a nanocluster-mediated strategy for the synthesis of compositionally tunable InAsxP1-x alloy nanocrystals. InAsxP1-x nanoclusters with varied As:P anion ratios were synthesized using a bottom-up method and isolated to establish alloy composition before growth to small nanocrystals via thermolysis. These nanoclusters were then used as single-source precursors in a second extended growth step to further tune the size and resulting bandgap of the alloy nanocrystals. This two-step approach provides continuous bandgap modulation from 3.1 to 2 eV through both initial nanocluster composition and quantum confinement of the resulting nanocrystals. To enhance the optical properties, InAsxP1-x cores were shelled with ZnSe, leading to an increase in photoluminescence intensity through effective surface passivation. This work demonstrates that nanocluster precursors serve as a platform for precise alloy control in colloidal III–V semiconductors and provides a generalizable route to compositionally and size-tunable alloy nanocrystals.

papers.title: Molecular Structure Predictor: A Lightweight Web-Based Platform for 2D and 3D Molecular Visualization Using RDKit
papers.abstract: Molecular visualization plays a crucial role in chemical education and research by enabling the interpretation of structural, geometric, and spatial properties of molecules. However, many existing tools require installation, computational resources, and technical expertise, limiting accessibility for beginners. This work presents a lightweight, web-based molecular visualization platform that converts chemical names and SMILES strings into 2D and 3D molecular structures. The system is implemented using RDKit for cheminformatics processing and Streamlit for web-based deployment. The computational workflow includes SMILES parsing, hydrogen addition, threedimensional coordinate generation using the Experimental-Torsion Knowledge Distance Geometry (ETKDG) algorithm, and geometry optimization using the Universal Force Field (UFF). The platform is publicly accessible and supports reproducibility through open-source deployment:  Hugging Face Application: https://huggingface.co/spaces/ShiddharthTiwari11/molecularstructure-predictor  Source Code Repository: https://github.com/siddharth70286-design/Molecular-predictor-

papers.title: STING, guided active learning for Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials examined on Lithium Thiophosphate solid state electrolytes
papers.abstract: All solid state batteries, based on lithium thiophosphate (LiPS) solid state electrolytes, offer a promising route to safer, higher energy density storage. Computational characterisation of these materials, and their interfaces with electrode materials, demands accurate and efficient machine learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Foundation MLIPs provide attractive performance out of the box, however reliability across novel materials is poorly characterised. In this work, we systematically benchmark seven foundation MLIPs across six LiPS compositions: two established electrolytes, Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 along with four novel materials from the Li2S-Li3P tie line, Li11P3S, Li5PS, Li7PS2, Li8P2S. We evaluate performance across geometry optimisation, phonon calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations. Foundation MLIPs show impressive stability and qualitative accuracy, but exhibit inconsistent performance across materials and their predicted properties. Phonon second-order force constants predictions are the most discriminating test with MACE-OMAT being the only model that predicts realistic phonons on novel materials. This demonstrates a lack of quantitative accuracy while using foundation MLIPs, necessitating custom MLIPs with system specific data. To develop reliable custom MLIPs, we introduce Strategic Training via Iterative Network Guidance (STING), a light-weight active learning framework that uses committee based uncertainty estimation to iteratively build system specific training datasets. STING incorporates stable foundation MLIP performance to minimise the required volume of DFT calculations. We also introduce the coefficient of standard deviation in the force components as a metric for structure selection, allowing for scaled comparison across temperature ranges. STING trained MLIPs consistently outperform foundation MLIPs across all benchmarks, showing sub 0.1 meV/atom energy RMSEs, and a reduction in force RMSEs by factors of 2-10 meV/Å. We also observe stable second-order force constants for all materials and a reduction in second-order force constants RMSEs by factors of 2-10. We further demonstrate that the STING coefficient of the standard deviation uncertainty metric produces well balanced training data across all training temperatures. These results establish a practical two stage strategy for development in solid state electrolyte research, and lay the groundwork for future interfacial simulations of LiPS electrolytes against Sulphur cathode material.

papers.title: Acyl-Transfer Selectivity Encoded in the Structure of Phosphate Intermediates
papers.abstract: Acyl phosphates are central intermediates in biological acyl-transfer chemistry, where their reactivity is governed by molecular recognition and confinement within structured environments. Achieving comparable control in abiotic systems remains challenging, as reactive intermediates typically lack recognition elements to direct specific outcomes. Here, we show that aminoacyl phosphates can be structurally diversified in-situ to program acyl-transfer reactivity. Copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition installs recognition elements directly into activated phosphate intermediates, generating species whose phase behavior creates confined environments that regulate nucleophile accessibility, sequester DNA, phospholipids, and ions, and control reaction outcomes. In mixtures, subtle differences in intrinsic reactivity are amplified through charge redistribution and self-assembly, enabling selective outcomes from simple amino acid derivatives. These findings suggest that the enduring question of why nature selected acyl phosphates may lie in their ability to couple reactivity with confinement, enabling selection in chemical reaction networks and expanding their roles beyond biology.

papers.title: A review on modern intensified extraction technologies of bioactive polyphenols
papers.abstract: Plant derived polyphenols are natural secondary metabolites having strong therapeutic effects. The rising need for natural ingredients in food, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals has made the extraction of polyphenols from plant sources more essential. Hence, efficient extraction of polyphenols has attracted a lot of interests lately among researchers. Thus, this review emphasizes modern extraction processes and influence of critical parameters that provide intensified polyphenol yield while maintaining their functionality and stability. Recent development, case studies and mechanism of intensified methods that uses ultrasound, microwave, electric field, enzymes, pressurized liquid, supercritical fluids etc. are discussed here. Further, latest forms of various kinetic modellings are discussed that are essential for comprehending the mechanics of mass transfer, tuning the process variables for higher extraction yields, refining the extraction and forecasting the performance results. Moreover, statistical sensitivity analysis of the modellings are also discussed. Therefore, this review serves as a valuable resource for researchers and industry professionals by consolidating current knowledge on theoretical aspects, mechanism and recent sustainable development works with critical analysis on advanced extraction strategies and applications.

papers.title: In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy to study redox dynamics in Ni and Cu co-catalysts on porous TiO2 photocatalyst films during H2 evolution
papers.abstract: Bimetallic NiCu co-catalysts are consistently reported to be more active than monometallic Ni and Cu counterparts for photocatalytic H2 evolution. There is consensus in the literature that this effect is due to the NiCu electronic structure, which provides an optimal adsorption/desorption energy landscape for faster H2 evolution kinetics compared to monometallic co-catalysts. Less is known, however, about the oxidation state of Ni and Cu co-catalysts under photocatalytic conditions, both in the case of mono- and bi-metallic systems. Red-ox dynamics for Ni and Cu are particularly complex in liquid aqueous media where, in addition to changes in oxidation state induced by photogenerated charge carriers, Ni and Cu can undergo dissolution, redeposition and surface reconstruction. Several diverging hypotheses on Ni and Cu oxidation states have been formed in recent years, most of which were based primarily on results of ex situ characterization techniques. Herein, we use in situ X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy to investigate red-ox dynamics in Ni-, Cu-, and NiCu-TiO2 photocatalysts in plain water and water/methanol solutions under hydrogen evolution conditions. This enables us to monitor changes in Ni and Cu oxidation state over time and identify the active phase of Ni and Cu co-catalysts “at work”. It is proposed that the observed synergy in NiCu/TiO2 arises from a division of roles, where Cu serves as an efficient electron sink for hydrogen evolution, while Ni acts as a dynamic hole buffer through reversible oxidation, thereby enhancing charge separation and suppressing self-deactivation pathways.

papers.title: Discovery of Potent and Non-Cytotoxic HDAC3- Selective Degraders Featuring a Propyl Hydrazide
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) is an important therapeutic target in cancer, yet selective HDAC3 degraders remain limited. In this study, we report the development of novel class I HDAC degraders derived from the HDAC3-preferential inhibitor FL-007 . Two linker exit vectors were investigated, leading to the identification of a series of potent compounds ( 2a-d ) exhibiting low micromolar inhibition of HDAC2 and submicromolar inhibition of HDAC1 and HDAC3, together with selective HDAC3 degradation. Degradation activity was confirmed in MM.1S, HCT116, A2780-HDAC3-HiBiT, and Cal27CisR cells using immunoblotting and HiBiT/LgBiT assays, achieving Dmax values of up to 92%. Notably, these compounds showed no cytotoxicity up to 100 µM in both cancerous and non-cancerous cell lines. Selective HDAC3 degradation resulted in moderate chemosensitization of cisplatin-resistant Cal27CisR cells, in contrast to the stronger effects observed with cytotoxic HDAC inhibitors. For compound 2b , the chemosensitizing effect was associated with increased histone H3 acetylation and increased p21 expression.

papers.title: Vat photopolymerization of semicrystalline thermoplastics via photoinitiated ring opening metathesis polymerization
papers.abstract: Vat photopolymerization (VP) is one of the most powerful tools today for the fabrication of complex materials. However, despite the variety of materials compatible with VP today, the fabrication of thermoplastics still remains a challenge. In this work, inspired by recent developments in photoinitiated ring-opening metathesis polymerization (photoROMP), we develop a photoROMP-compatible resin for the printing of semicrystalline poly(cyclooctene), and systematically explore their thermomechanical behavior. We show that crystallinity, and thus mechanical properties, evolve predictably as a function of thermal history, aging time, and light intensity during printing, enabling predictable tuning of stiffness and strength. Leveraging the contrast between amorphous and semicrystalline states, we further demonstrate thermally responsive architectures in which localized melting can be used to spatially modulate material stiffness on-demand, enabling programmable deformation. In addition, we highlight the robust shape memory behavior and excellent chemical stability of these printed pCOE materials. More broadly, this work demonstrates the ability of photoROMP to expand the material landscape of VP and underscores the potential utility of semicrystalline thermoplastics for the fabrication of adaptive 3D-printed structures.

papers.title: A small molecule dual inhibitor of agr quorum sensing and ATP synthase blocks acute and chronic virulence phenotypes in Staphylococcus aureus
papers.abstract: The accessory gene regulator (agr) quorum sensing system in Staphylococcus aureus plays a prominent role in acute infections caused by this common pathogen. In contrast, ATP synthase affects the ability of S. aureus to establish chronic infections and persist as small colony variants. In this study, we report that a synthetic small molecule, CP-20, is capable of dually inhibiting agr and ATP synthase. We demonstrate CP-20’s ability to counteract key virulence phenotypes associated with both pathways, including hemolysis, biofilm formation, and antibiotic resistance. We also show that CP-20 facilitates more efficient clearance of S. aureus by murine macrophages than genetic inactivation of either agr or ATP synthase alone, suggesting that dual inhibition may have an additive effect on ablating intracellular survival. This work demonstrates the utility of a single chemical modulator to attenuate S. aureus pathogenesis via two non-essential pathways and suggests a pathway toward non-bactericidal virulence control.

papers.title: In-Silico Investigations of Inhibition Capabilities of Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators Against Estrogen Receptor-α (ER-α) in Breast Cancer
papers.abstract: This comprehensive study presents a comparative evaluation of three prominent selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs), including two benzothiophene-derived compounds, Raloxifene and Arzoxifene, and one tetrahydronaphthalene-based molecule, Lasofoxifene, using an integrated computational approach. Utilizing advanced computational techniques, the molecular docking invetigations identified Lasofoxifene possess the highest binding affinity towards ER-α among the studied SERMs, which were subsequently investigated through extensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the stability and interaction behavior of the ER-α-SERM complexes over nanosecond timescales. In perticular, the ER-α complexes with Lasofoxifene and Arzoxifene exhibit more compactness and structural stability of the receptor, based on their radius of gyration and hydrogen bond analysis data. However, principle component analysis (PCA) reveals the nature of conformational fluctuations in the ER-α-Lasofoxifene complex, indicating a reduced conformational state compared to the other complexes. Further, the binding free energy analysis using the MM-PBSA approach displayed the most favourable energetic profile corresponds to the ER-α-Lasofoxifene complex, govern predominantly by the hydrophobic interactions within the binding pocket. A combined evaluation of docking scores, stability parameters, and energetic profiles consistently identifies Lasofoxifene as forming the most stable complex with ER-α among the investigated ligands. So, the investigations provide a molecular-level understanding of ER-α inhibition and highlight Lasofoxifene as a promising condidate with strong inhibitory potential.

papers.title: Visible-light cobalt(II)-catalysed synthesis of aroyl amides from arylazo sulfones.
papers.abstract: A strategy combining the unique properties of arylazo sulfones as dyedauxiliary group-bearing substrates for arylation reactions and Co2(CO)8 as a catalyst in carbonylation processes was used to prepare aromatic amides. This versatile method was utilized to create a library of aroyl amides with good to excellent yields.

papers.title: Effects of 6PPD-Q and Its Hydroxylated Metabolites on function in the Rainbow Trout Cell Line RTgill-W1
papers.abstract: The tire rubber-derived contaminant 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) exhibits high acute toxicity to salmonid species, yet the toxicological profiles of its hydroxylated metabolites and the underlying mitochondrial mechanisms remain poorly characterized. This study investigated the cytotoxicity and mitochondrial function in rainbow trout gill cells (RTgill-W1) exposed to 6PPD-Q and three mono-hydroxylated metabolites (p-hydroxy 6PPD-Q, 6PPD-Q-1-OH, and 6PPD-Q-4-OH). Using OECD Test Guideline 249 in combination with complementary physiological assays, we demonstrate a clear structure–toxicity relationship (STR). Among the tested compounds, p-hydroxy 6PPD-Q exhibited the greatest toxicity, exceeding that of 6PPD-Q, whereas the alkyl-hydroxylated metabolite showed little to no detectable toxicity. Mechanistic analysis revealed that the toxic variants induced a concentration-dependent collapse of mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and severe ATP depletion, concurrent with a significant disruption of intracellular calcium homeostasis. Although no statistically significant differences in total oxygen consumption were observed, likely due to uncoupling-like effects or compensatory cellular dynamics, these results demonstrate that 6PPD-Q and its active transformation products compromise rainbow trout cell viability primarily by targeting the mitochondrial bioenergetic axis.

papers.title: SMSD Pro: Coverage-Driven, Tautomer-Aware Maximum Common Substructure Search
papers.abstract: Maximum common substructure (MCS) search is foundational to scaffold hopping, matched molecular pair analysis, and reaction mapping. However, the problem's inherent NP-hardness often necessitates time-constrained heuristics, which can introduce variance into computational pipelines. We introduce a label-frequency upper bound (LFUB) that provides a time-independent certificate of MCS optimality, reducing the need for arbitrary timeouts. We further define tautomeric equivalence classes with pKa-informed relevance weights that recover pharmacophoric overlap across tautomeric shifts, bypassing the combinatorial overhead of O(2κ) pre-generation (where κ is the number of tautomeric sites). Supported by fast paths that reduce polymer degeneracy from factorial to O(N ·M) and efficiently resolve branched acyclic structures, the framework achieves a 22x geometric-mean speedup over industry-standard baselines ( e.g., RDKit; range 4.4–8,617x), while recovering up to 11 additional matched atoms in tautomer-sensitive systems. Source code is available at https://github.com/asad/SMSD .

papers.title: Thermodynamic Geometry of the Cosmological Background: dS ∧ dE, Gibbs Closure, and a Zero-Parameter Hubble Law Decisively Preferred over ΛCDM
papers.abstract: Classical thermodynamic identities—the Gibbs relation, partition-function statistics, and critical-point universality—are applied to the cosmological sector through the entropy–energy wedge product dS∧dE. Six axioms, rooted in standard physical chemistry (Gibbs free energy, Bose–Fermi counting, one-bit equilibrium entropy), together with the spacetime dimension D = 4, determine the complete late-time cosmological background with zero free parameters: the matter fraction Ωm = 9 ln 2/20 ≈ 0.3119, the ruler invariant K = H0 rd ≈ 10 070 km s−1, and the Hubble constant H0 = 68.5 ± 1.6 km s−1Mpc−1. Tested against 1 623 data points (Pantheon+ supernovae, cosmic chronometers, DESI 2024 BAO), the zero-parameter model achieves χ2 = 1416.4—identical to flat ΛCDM (4 free parameters)—and is decisively preferred by the Bayesian Information Criterion: ∆BIC = −29.6. The closure amplitude |ξ∗| ≈ 0.032 is independently confirmed by two internal consistency routes that agree to 0.5%.

papers.title: High-Throughput Screening of Piezoelectric Hybrid Organic–Inorganic Perovskites via Density-Functional Theory and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites (HOIPs) are promising candidates for piezoelectric devices owing to their structural tunability, low density, and intrinsic mechanical compliance. However, rational design principles linking molecular composition to orientation-independent piezoelectric performance remain underdeveloped, and the vast ABX3 compositional space precludes exhaustive first-principles exploration. Here, we establish a “distribution-aware” density functional theory–machine learning (DFT–ML) workflow for scalable discovery of high-performance and flexible piezoelectric HOIPs. “Distribution-aware” refers to an explicit strategy to mitigate compositional distribution shift between the DFT training set and the much larger virtual screening library, by augmenting training with representative structures sampled from the candidate space. We first construct a uniform DFT dataset of 1,346 structures spanning 192 ABX 3 compositions and compute elastic tensors, piezoelectric tensors, band gaps, densities, and formation energies. To enable symmetry-independent screening, we introduce a rotation-invariant spectral descriptor, 𝜎max, defined as the largest singular value of the Kelvin-scaled piezoelectric strain tensor. Feedforward neural networks trained on periodic structural descriptors achieve near-unity accuracy for thermodynamic and electronic properties, and moderate but meaningful predictive performance for mechanical moduli and 𝜎 max . To mitigate compositional distribution shift between the DFT dataset and the much larger hypothetical design space, representative structures from the candidate library were incorporated to enhance training diversity, and an external validation subset was reserved to explicitly evaluate model generalization in unseen compositional regions. The resulting ML models demonstrate robust transferability beyond the original DFT dataset. Leveraging the retrained models, we screened 2.7 million enumerated ABX 3 formulations, yielding 5,573 stable and geometrically optimized candidates. Multi-objective optimization identified two distinct material families: mechanically robust HXA-based mixedhalide frameworks for high-performance piezoelectric applications, and compliant EDA/MS-based systems for flexible device concepts. The workflow delivers experimentally testable targets and practical guidance for lead-free hybrid piezoelectrics. In addition, this workflow also facilitates the experimental exploration of the broader material systems and illuminates the structure–property relationships that govern piezoelectricity of HOIPs.

papers.title: Enhanced Growth in Sb2Te3/SnSe2 Multilayered Atomic Layer Deposition: Nucleation and Nanostructure Modification
papers.abstract: Multilayer thin film structuring offers a versatile strategy to tailor nanostructures through interface engineering. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) provides precise control of composition and structure via supercycle approaches that enable the multiple metal species introduction. However, the resulting growth behavior is often interpreted without fully accounting for interfacial effects that govern precursor nucleation and nanostructure evolution. In this work, we demonstrate that introducing SnSe2 layers into Sb2Te3/SnSe2 multilayer films using ALD supercycle significantly enhances Sb2Te3 nucleation and accelerates out-of-plane growth, leading to an increase in growth per cycle (GPC) from 0.18 to 0.69 Å/cycle. First principles atomistic simulations of precursor deposition chemistry and extremely surface-sensitive low-energy ion scattering (LEIS) analysis confirm promotion of growth of Sb2Te3 in Sb2Te3/SnSe2 multilayer structures, which is also accompanied by elemental exchange reactions between Te and Se atoms. The resulting Sb2Te3/SnSe2 multilayer thin films exhibit increased charge carrier and phonon scattering, leading to a significant reduction in lattice thermal conductivity from 1.09 to 0.25 W/mK at room temperature due to the modulated nanostructure. This study establishes a robust analytical framework for understanding and engineering interfacial reactions and nucleation phenomena in ALD-based multilayer systems.

papers.title: Mapping the Carbon Footprint of Chemicals in Commerce
papers.abstract: The chemical industry is a major contributor to global CO 2 emissions, accounting for ~10% of total greenhouse gases, underscoring the need for a sustainability transition. However, reliable public carbon footprint data exists for only hundreds of the over 100,000 chemicals in commerce, limiting effective action. To address this, we collect high-quality primary chemical carbon footprint data and refine a machine learning model to estimate the carbon footprint of 94,697 chemicals in commerce across 26 national and regional chemical inventories. Our analysis reveals clear molecular structure–carbon footprint relationships that may guide future molecular design: carbon footprints are strongly linked to molecular frameworks, the number of ring structures, and types of heteroatoms. Newly commercialized chemicals tend to have higher carbon footprints than older chemicals, emphasizing the urgent need to embed “sustainable-by-design” principles into chemical innovation from the outset. This study provides a reliable database of chemical carbon footprints and actionable insights for sustainable design and use of chemicals, supporting environmental decision-making of chemical producers, consumers, and policymakers.

papers.title: GRACE-OFF: A machine-learned interatomic potential for organic liquids using the GRACE architecture
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have become an increasingly important tool for molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, enabling near quantum-mechanical accuracy at significantly reduced computational cost. In this work, we assess the Graph Atomic Cluster Expansion (GRACE) neural network architecture for the prediction of potential energy surfaces. GRACE models of varying depth and size are trained on the SPICE v2.0 dataset—which comprises a large and chemically diverse set of organic molecules—and are integrated into the MD program ASE. We validate the resulting models using a variety of benchmarks. These include single-point energy and force predictions, torsional energy profiles, condensed phase properties of organic liquids and water (thermodynamic properties, self-diffusion coefficients, radial distribution functions, and temperature-dependent water density), as well as the stability of biomolecular MD simulations for gas-phase Ala 15 and solvated crambin. For the single molecule benchmarks (single point energies and forces, torsional energy profiles) the one-layer models showed only mediocre performance, whereas the two-layer models outperformed the MACE-OFF models to which we compare to, including the latest MACE-OFF24(M). For the condensed phase properties, in particular the medium and large two-layer models gave significantly better results than the MACE-OFF family of MLIPs. For water and hexane, the GRACE-OFF models also beat the much more expensive UMA(S) model. In particular, the two-layer GRACE-OFF models accurately reproduce experimental water radial distribution functions and predict water densities in close agreement with experimental data over a wide temperature range, substantially reducing the systematic overestimation observed for MACE-OFF. Finally, GPU throughput benchmarks demonstrate that GRACE-OFF achieves substantially higher MD performance than comparable MACE models in both single and double precision. This establishes GRACE-OFF as an accurate and computationally efficient foundation potential for routine simulations of organic liquids and biomolecular systems.

papers.title: Collective Reaction–Surface Dynamics during Ligand Exchange in Atomically Precise Metal Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: Ligand exchange reactions (LERs) govern the stability, reactivity, and functional evolution of monolayer-protected metal nanoclusters (NCs), yet their molecular mechanisms are poorly understood due to the complexity of surface–ligand dynamics during the reactions. Here, we employ machine-learning interatomic potentials-based enhanced sampling simulations to resolve the free-energy landscapes of ligand exchange in Au25(SR)18 NC, with near first-principles accuracy and extended time scales. We identify two chemically distinct, site-specific exchange pathways-‘apex ’ and ‘side’ routes from solution–with the side pathway exhibiting a relatively lower free energy barrier, consistent with facile ligand exchange. On the other hand, intercluster ligand exchange proceeds via ‘stepwise substitution’ mechanism involving a metastable intermediate and a higher free energy barrier. Notably, our analyses reveal that ligand exchange involves collective rearrangements of surface atoms in the first coordination shell. These findings provide a unified atomistic and thermodynamic description of ligand exchange and establish a generalizable computational framework for investigating coupled surface–ligand dynamics in metal nanoclusters.

papers.title: Molecular-Level Insights into Alkali-Metal Cation–CO2 Interactions at Electrified Copper Interfaces by Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: The electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR) has garnered considerable attention as a promising strategy for converting anthropogenic CO2 into value-added organic compounds. The structure of the electric double layer, where interfacial electron transfer occurs, strongly governs CO2RR activity. In this interfacial region, partially dehydrated alkali-metal ions (AM+ ions) stabilise CO2 molecules and CO2RR intermediates in promoting the CO2RR. However, whether such interaction-enabled molecular configurations can form within the electric double layer under electrochemical conditions and how their formation probability depends on the applied potential remain unclear. In this study, we used classical molecular dynamics simulations to systematically evaluate how the hydration environment of AM+ ions and their spatial relationship with CO2 molecules evolve as functions of the applied potential and AM+ ion identities. The simulations revealed that when larger AM+ ions such as Cs+ and K+ are used and a potential more negative than −0.92 V vs. point of zero charge is applied, partially dehydrated AM+ ions, having lost two to three coordinating water molecules, emerge in the immediate vicinity of the Cu surface. In addition, analysis of the local environment surrounding CO2 molecules near the Cu surface revealed that the likelihood of partially dehydrated AM+ ions residing within the first coordination shell of CO2 molecules increases with the use of larger AM+ ions. These results deepen the molecular-level understanding of CO2–AM+ ion interactions within the electric double layer and provide important mechanistic insights for advancing the CO2RR.

papers.title: Metal-organic polyhedra as intracellular nitric oxide delivery systems towards biomedical applications
papers.abstract: Nitric Oxide (NO) is a molecule with wide-ranging therapeutic potential but is challenging to administer due to its reactive nature. Drug delivery systems (DDS) that can deliver NO reliably and efficiently allow for its exogenous administration with spatiotemporal control of the release. This study introduces two water-soluble metal-organic polyhedra (MOPs) based on dirhodium or diruthenium paddlewheels assembled in a cuboctahedral geometry, decorated with sulfonate groups on their surface. NO molecules coordinate with the open-metal sites (OMS) at the axial site of the paddlewheel moieties. We studied NO capture and release in the solid state and in physiological media in response to two stimuli: light and water. The release amount and its kinetics were varied by changing the light intensity and duration. We further investigated the spatiotemporal control of the NO release in a single cell, establishing the potential of these molecules for biomedical applications.

papers.title: Accelerated materials discovery through in situ X-ray diffraction: Solvothermal formation of PdxMy (M = Si, Ge, Sn, Pb) intermetallic nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Machine learning and artificial intelligence approaches are expected to accelerate the development of new materials, e.g., through automated synthesis. Here, we investigate another approach to accelerate materials discovery, namely in situ synchrotron Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), which enables efficient exploration of a large range of synthesis parameters to identify optimal synthesis conditions. We study the solvothermal formation of PdxMy (M = Si, Ge, Sn, Pb) nanoparticles with varying temperature, solvent, and metal precursor. Intermetallic phases are obtained for all systems except for PdxSiy, and specific conditions are identified for preparing Pd25Ge9, Pd2Ge, SnPd2, Sn13Pd20, SnPd, Pb3Pd5, Pb9Pd13, PbPd, and Pb2Pd intermetallic phases. A general formation mechanism is suggested, where Pd nanoparticles are formed initially, followed by absorption and diffusion of the secondary metal to form intermetallic phases. Based on the learnings from the in situ experiments, SnPd2, Sn13Pd20, and SnPd nanoparticles are synthesized ex situ in a simple solvothermal process. Scanning transmission electron microscopy - energydispersive X-ray spectroscopy (STEM-EDS) establishes a gradient of Sn across the nanoparticles with a Pd-rich core and increasing Sn content towards the edges, reflecting the diffusion of Sn into the initial Pd nanoparticles and thereby corroborating the formation mechanism observed from the in situ data.

papers.title: Aspen Plus V14.0 Process Simulation of Seawater Alkaline Electrolysis for Green Hydrogen Production: A Complete Unit Operation Study from Desalination to Compressed Purified Hydrogen
papers.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive steady-state process simulation of a seawater-fed alkaline electrolysis plant for green hydrogen production, developed in Aspen Plus V14.0 using the Electrolyte Non-Random Two-Liquid (ELECNRTL) thermodynamic property method. The simulation encompasses eleven interconnected unit operations: coagulation-flocculation pretreatment, ultrafiltration, seawater reverse osmosis at 60 bar, brackish water reverse osmosis at 12 bar, electrodeionization, potassium hydroxide electrolyte preparation, alkaline electrolysis at 80°C and 1 bar with 99% water conversion, gas-liquid separation, flash drying, isentropic compression to 200 bar, countercurrent heat exchange, and pressure swing adsorption purification. Starting from a seawater feed of 149.46 kg/hr, the simulation delivers a final hydrogen product of 4.94 kg/hr at 200 bar and 40°C with 99% purity and zero CO2-equivalent emissions. The total compression power requirement is 31.1 kW and the overall seawater-to-ultrapure-water recovery is 28.8%. The ELECNRTL property method accurately captures the thermodynamics of the KOH-H2O electrolyte system across all operating conditions. This simulation framework provides a rigorous, reproducible foundation for techno-economic optimisation and scale-up of coastal green hydrogen production facilities.

papers.title: Stabilization of Low-Valent Beryllium–Beryllium Units through Charge-Shift amido-bridges and Core Aromaticity
papers.abstract: We report the theoretical characterization of a unique amido-bridged beryllium cluster, Be4(N-Ar)2. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the TPSS/def2-TZVP level reveal a stable, planar six-membered Be2-N-Be2-N ring core. The structure features distinct covalent Be-Be single bonds (2.049 Å) within the dumbbells. Multi-method analyses including Natural Bond Orbital (NBO), Localized Orbital Locator (LOL), and Electron Localization Function (ELF) demonstrate that the core is stabilized by significant Nitrogen lone-pair donation into the electron-deficient Beryllium centers (nN Be). Magnetic criteria (NICS(0) = -5.22 ppm) confirm the aromatic character of the framework. Furthermore, topological signatures from LOL and Laplacian mapping identify the Be-N bridges as possessing substantial charge-shift character.

papers.title: Host–Guest Engineered Pure Organic Phosphorescent Proteins for Long-Persistent Bioimaging and Photocatalytic Controlled Radical Polymerization
papers.abstract: Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) in proteins is exceptionally rare due to efficient quenching of triplet excitons in aqueous and biological environments. Here, we report a general supramolecular strategy to engineer phosphorescent proteins by embedding organic phosphors within protein scaffolds via host–guest interactions, where the confined microenvironment suppresses nonradiative decay and stabilizes triplet states, enabling bright and long-lived phosphorescence in both the solid state and aqueous media. The stabilized triplet excitons further endow these phosphorescent proteins with photocatalytic activity, allowing them to serve as efficient photosensitizers for photoinduced electron transfer-mediated reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer polymerization in water, exhibiting excellent temporal control, predictable molecular weights, and narrow dispersities, with mechanistic studies supporting an electron-transfer pathway. Moreover, these systems enable polymerization-induced self-assembly to generate vesicular structures that encapsulate the photoactive proteins while retaining persistent afterglow emission, thereby integrating cellular-like compartmentalization with intrinsic optical traceability. This work establishes a versatile supramolecular route to RTP proteins and expands protein–phosphor assemblies toward artificial phosphorescent cells and light-driven biochemical systems.

papers.title: Trifluoroacetic acid removal from aqueous solution using as-synthesized UiO-66 wet gel
papers.abstract: Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), an ultrashort-chain PFAS, is a ubiquitous molecule found in the environment, but conventional adsorption methods struggle to remove it because of its very low hydrophobicity. Here. we demonstrate that the zirconium-carboxylate metal-organic framework UiO-66, used in its as-synthesized wet gel form, captures TFA from aqueous solutions without further drying or thermal activation. Removal efficiencies (HEs) measured by 19F liquid-state NMR ranged from 30.1% to 70.5% and varied with adsorbent dosage (0.8-3.2 g wet gel per 40 mL). STEM-EDS elemental mapping of TFA-loaded gel revealed F co-localized with Zr throughout the aggregates. Deploying UiO-66 as a wet gel eliminates energy intensive activation and simplifies handling, highlighting a practical, low-energy route to mitigate ultrashort-chain PFAS in water. Further work will optimize regeneration media and validate performance in representative water matrices.

papers.title: Carbonylative Aminative Suzuki–Miyaura Coupling: Pd-Catalyzed Synthesis of Amides from Vinyl/Aryl Halides and Boronic Acids
papers.abstract: Amide synthesis is critical for the development of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. Here, we report a four-component variant of the Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura coupling that repurposes partners conventionally used for C–C bond formation to instead yield amides. The sequential insertion of CO, from Mo(CO)6 as a convenient surrogate, and NH, from O-(diphenylphosphinyl)hydroxylamine (DPPH), allows access to a broad scope of amides, enamides, α,β-unsaturated amides, and α,β-unsaturated enamides. Drug-like analogs can be rapidly assembled, and we show that “reverse amide” counterparts can be generated from the same starting materials.

papers.title: A Modular Inhibitor Approach to Mapping the Catalytic Trajectory of an Iterative Siderophore Synthetase, DesD
papers.abstract: Under iron limiting conditions, bacteria biosynthesize and secrete small molecule iron chelators, siderophores, to scavenge this essential metal. Siderophores are biosynthesized by non-ribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPS) or NRPS independent siderophore (NIS) synthetases, the latter of which are significantly less studied. Streptomyces spp. utilize an iterative NIS synthetase, DesD, to produce desferrioxamine type siderophores through dimerization, trimerization, and (in some cases) macrocyclization of monomers such as N 1 -hydroxy- N 1 -succinyl cadaverine (HSC) and N 1 -hydroxy- N 1 -acetyl cadaverine (HAC). Prior work has utilized an acyl-sulfamoyl adenosine (AMS) inhibitor of monomeric HSC (HSC-AMS) to interrogate the initial adenylation reaction of HSC. However, much is still unknown about how the enzyme active site accommodates substrates of varying sizes during further oligomerization reactions. To answer this question, AMS analogs of the monomer (HSC-AMS), dimer (HSC-HSC-AMS), and trimer (HSC-HSC-HSC-AMS) were chemically synthesized. Biochemical results from in vitro DesD reactions, IC 50 assays, and isothermal titration calorimetry along with structural studies conducted via co-crystallization inform an updated mechanistic model for the iterative DesD catalytic cycle. The acyl adenylate motif in the growing substrate chain drives tight binding in the enzyme active site while the N-terminal HSC units dynamically sample conformations en route to terminating macrocyclization of the HSC-HSC-HSC trimer.

papers.title: Diborylfluoromethane as C1F1 Synthon for the Synthesis of α-Fluoroketones
papers.abstract: The selective α-monofluorination of ketones is a significant synthetic challenge. In this study, we introduce a base-promoted coupling reaction that utilizes carboxylic acid esters and diborylfluoromethane, which serves as a C1 fluorine (C1F1) synthon. This reaction provides an efficient and convergent synthetic strategy for making α-fluoroketones. It generates a boron-enolate equivalent that can be subsequently trapped with water and other electrophiles, including alkyl halides and fluorinating agents.

papers.title: Ring expansion of benzocyclobutenols toward benzo[b]furans
papers.abstract: An efficient 4-to-5 ring expansion through aryne intermediates is disclosed. A wide variety of iodo-substituted benzo[ b ]furans are prepared from benzocyclobutenols via unusual oxyiodonation of aryne intermediates. The great transformability of the resulting aryl iodides enables the access to diverse highly functionalized benzo[ b ]furans.

papers.title: Coupling Nanoscale Viscoelastic Measurements and Infrared Heating of Polymers with AFM-IR
papers.abstract: In heterogeneous polymer systems, the viscoelastic response of polymers around interfaces or with nanostructured morphology may deviate from bulk values. However, current measurement techniques tend to mask these local variations, which are crucial for understanding and developing these materials. Coupling the high spatial resolution of atomic force microscopy (AFM) with dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) offers an avenue to circumvent this limitation. We previously demonstrated the advantages of using a focused infrared (IR) laser on an AFM-IR system to locally heat a sample during nanomechanical measurements, with heating modulated by varying the IR repetition rate. [1] Herein, we present a brief demonstration of coupling nDMA with our previously demonstrated chemistry-selective IR heating. We first measured the storage and loss modulus of poly(propylene glycol) (PPG)-4,4′-methylenebis(phenyl urea) (MPU) at varying IR repetition rates, demonstrating a viscoelastic modulus response with typical heating characteristics upon crossing the glass transition temperature. We further demonstrated stress relaxation of an enaminelinked vitrimer possessing significant bond dynamicity at elevated temperatures. Overall, this method is in the preliminary stages of development, and this working paper aims to serve as a basis for feedback and discussion.

papers.title: A Crystalline Silaspiropentane and its Rearrangement to a Silacyclobutane
Uncertainty in MD-Derived Diffusion Coefficients Depends on Analysis Protocol, Not Just Simulation Data
papers.abstract: Bonkowski and De Souza [Sol. Stat. Ionics 429, 116967 (2025)] provide a guide for performing molecular dynamics simulations of ion transport, including methods for estimating diffusion coefficients and their uncertainties from mean-squared displacement (MSD) data. The discussion of uncertainty in estimated diffusion coefficients presents the statistical properties of specific analysis protocols—ordinary least squares regression with particular data processing choices and other, statistically equivalent, approaches—without explicitly stating the scope of applicability for these results. Without explicit scope statements, the guide presents these results as universal characteristics of diffusion coefficient estimation; i.e., uncertainty in D* is determined only by the input simulation data. Here, we clarify that for diffusion coefficients estimated by linear regression of MSD data, the uncertainty depends not only on the input simulation data, but also on the choice of statistical estimator (OLS, WLS, GLS) and data processing decisions (fitting window extent, time-averaging). By clarifying this dependence on analysis protocol, we hope to help researchers avoid incorrect uncertainty estimates and encourage the adoption of statistically efficient methods for analyzing molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Tuning Connectivity in Hybrid Organic-Inorganic Antimony Halides through Reactant Concentration Effects
papers.abstract: In this study, we report the synthesis and characterization of two hybrid organic inorganic (HOI) antimony halides using DABCO (DABCO = 1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane) as the organic cation. Varying the concentration of the starting materials leads to different oxidation states, resulting in different inorganic substructures ranging from isolated units to layers and a new interconnected metal halide framework. The structure of (DABCOH2)SbVCl7 (1) contains isolated [SbVCl6]– units separated by the organic cation. Mixed-valent (DABCOH2)12(SbIII)14(SbV)2Cl79(H3O)3(H2O)12 (2) features an interconnected framework of [SbIIICl6]3– units as well as [SbVCl6]– and an octahedral chloride hydrate cluster. Compound 2, including its chloride hydrate cluster, was characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopic methods, and computational methods. Compound 2 was compared to the literature-known mixed-metal HOI (DABCOH2)4SbIII2CuII2Cl18(H2O)4, which was obtained under the highest reactant concentrations. This compound also contains a chloride hydrate cluster, which was identified and characterized by solid state NMR in this work. Compound 2 is the first HOI antimony chloride with an interconnected framework structure, featuring a yet unknown network topology; it also contains the first structurally characterized chloride hydrate cluster, in which the chloride is located in the center of the water shell. These compounds show that by selecting appropriate organic cations and conditions, thechemical space of antimony halides can be systematically expanded by careful reaction control.

papers.title: CBRdb: A Cheminformatic Database for Biochemical Reaction Analysis
papers.abstract: We present CBR-db, a database with detailed chemical properties data for biochemical compounds and reactions. We provide the first chemically consistent analyses and detailed chemical properties data for a biologically relevant set of 148,673 reactions and 18,716 small molecules derived from the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) and the ATLAS of Biochemistry. CBR-db provides detailed atom tracking, reaction similarity classification, compound properties, chiral centers, molecular assembly indices, and thermodynamic properties. CBR-db is designed to be continuously updated, open source, and reproducible. This report highlights the cheminformatic data, explains the curation and dataset, and highlights the data’s utility for researchers working at the intersection of chemical properties and biology. We anticipate a broad range of potential applications for these data, given their position at the intersection of cheminformatics and bioinformatics, including for researchers interested in molecular properties and reaction mechanisms found in metabolism, the chemical underpinnings of synthetic biochemical design and engineering, and how the origins and evolution of biochemistry have selected among properties of molecules and reactions within chemical space.

papers.title: N-N Coupling of Nitrosyl Ligands in a Dinitrosyl Iron Complex Mediated by Exogenous Acids
papers.abstract: We disclose the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity profiles of a dinitrosyl iron complex (DNIC) toward exogenous Brønsted and Lewis acids. Treatment of the {Fe(NO) 2 } 10 complex butyl NNFe(NO) 2 ( 1 ) ( butyl NN = 2-(1-butyl-5( tert -butyl)-1 H -pyrazol-3-yl)-6-methylpyridine) with a variety of Brønsted and Lewis acids generates an oxidized {Fe(NO) 2 } 9 species [ butyl NNFe(NO) 2 ][PF 6 ] ( 2-PF 6 ) and, in the presence of a radical reagent, N 2 O. The pathway for N 2 O formation is governed by acid additives, and mechanistic studies indicate the acid promotes electron transfer from the iron center in 1 and facilitates NO lability, providing a pathway for N 2 O formation.

papers.title: Regioselective Hydroarylation of Internal and Terminal Alkenes with Pyrazoles Enabled by a Lanthanum Catalyst
papers.abstract: Catalytic C–H alkylation of pyrazoles with internal alkenes represents an ideal strategy for constructing functionalized pyrazoles—privileged heterocyclic scaffolds prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and biologically active molecules. However, such a transformation has remained underexplored to date, likely due to the inherently low reactivity of internal alkenes and the lack of suitable catalysts. Herein, we describe a lanthanum-catalyzed highly regioselective C–H alkylation of N-arylpyrazoles with internal alkenes. The key to success of this unprecedented transformation is the use of an imidazolin-2-iminato lanthanum catalyst, whose large ionic radius provides an open coordination environment that facilitates the coordination of sterically demanding internal alkenes to the metal center and subsequent alkene migratory insertion. Beside internal alkenes, 1,1-disubstituted styrenes and terminal alkenes were amenable to the reaction. This protocol offers a straightforward and atom-efficient route for the synthesis of a new family of N-(ortho-alkylaryl)pyrazole derivatives (91 examples, up to 99% yield, >19:1 rr). The scale-up synthesis and further transformation to hedgehog enzyme inhibitor analog highlights the potential application of this method. On the basis of experimental and computational studies, the influence of metal ion size on the turn-over limiting migratory insertion step and the possible reaction mechanism were elucidated.

papers.title: ADMET Profiling of a Mitochondria-Focused Compound Library: Physicochemical Baselines, Membrane Permeability Classification, and Tier-Based Filtering for AI-Driven Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Background Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties determine whether a compound with high in vitro target potency can become a drug. For mitochondria-directed therapeutics, conventional ADMET frameworks based on Lipinski rule-of-five criteria systematically misclassify compounds that use organelle-specific targeting mechanisms including triphenylphosphonium (TPP+) conjugates, Szeto-Schiller peptides, and lipophilic ubiquinone analogs — as druglike liabilities, when their physicochemical profiles are optimized for inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) accumulation rather than classical oral absorption. Objectives This study describes the ADMET profiling methodology and results for the 201-compound MitoCoreX seed library, establishing physicochemical baselines and a tier-based classification system calibrated for mitochondrial therapeutic contexts. A key objective is to demonstrate where standard computational ADMET tools (SwissADME, pkCSM, ADMETlab 2.0) would misclassify TPP+-class compounds relative to the mitochondria-specific framework.
