Oxidation of FeII(MPH) by GOX proceeds with a half-life of 4.1 minutes and produces a 7-fold increase in relaxivity. Changes in relaxivity are reversed by addition of ascorbate. This data highlights the di erences between a probe containing a coordination site for binding peroxide and one that lacks a binding site. FeII(MPB) is one of the first reported examples of a Fe(II) macrocyclic MRI probe that is unreactive to O2 but reacts rapidly with micromolar concentrations of peroxide to increase signal for increased selectivity in monitoring inflammation.

papers.title: SCOPE: A Chemically-Aware Workflow Automation Software for Molecules and Molecular Crystals
papers.abstract: Large-scale computational chemistry studies increasingly rely on automated and reproducible workflows to explore chemical space. In practice, these workflows typically involve multiple tools for chemical representation, quantum chemistry jobs execution, and data analysis. However, these components are often disconnected, making it difficult to construct end-to-end computational pipelines that remain both cohesive and reproducible. Here we introduce SCOPE, an open-source Python framework for automating computational chemistry workflows involving molecules and molecular crystals. SCOPE integrates chemically aware representations of molecular systems, with workflow construction, HPC execution, and structured data management within a unified architecture. Chemical objects encode hierarchical relationships between atoms, ligands, molecules, and molecular crystals, enabling workflows and analyses that follow chemical intuition. Computational tasks are organized through a structured workflow model, while results are captured in dedicated state objects that enable automated analyses such as spectra and thermodynamic properties. The capabilities of SCOPE are illustrated through workflows involving a spin-crossover transition-metal complex and an azo-based molecular photoswitch. By combining chemical awareness with workflow automation, SCOPE enables reproducible computational pipelines and facilitates the generation of datasets for high-throughput and data-driven studies.

papers.title: Cu underpotential deposition on Au(111) in methyl sulfonic acid: Analysis of Frumkin interactions on nucleation and growth.
papers.abstract: Methylsulfonic acid (MSA) is widely utilized in commercial electroplating. However, fundamental investigations into its influence on metal deposition remain scarce. Most studies of MSA adsorption on metal single crystals have focused on bare electrode surfaces. This work investigates the influence of MSA on the Cu underpotential deposition (UPD) on Au(111), one of the most thoroughly characterized model systems in electrochemistry. In MSA, the Cu UPD process exhibits a distinct potential-dependent behavior. The onset of Cu UPD is identical to that in perchloric acid, a classic non-specifically adsorbing electrolyte. Kinetic analysis suggests Cu island formation driven by an attractive interaction between copper adatoms. In this potential regime, shell-isolated nanoparticle enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SHINERS) reveals no evidence of specific methylsulfonate adsorption. At lower potentials, however, the interfacial behavior changes significantly. Sharp voltammetric features and the SHINER spectra demonstrate a transition to specific methylsulfonate adsorption on the Cu-covered Au(111) surface. Furthermore, Cu bulk deposition is kinetically hindered, similar to the Cu UPD process on Au(111) in the presence of acetic acid. This inhibition is attributed to the hydrophobic moiety shared by both acetate and methyl sulfonate.

papers.title: TorchDisorder: A Differentiable Framework for Generating Physically Realistic Disorder Structures from Experimental Diffraction Data
papers.abstract: Determining the atomic structure of amorphous materials remains a fundamental challenge in condensed-matter physics and materials science. Unlike crystalline solids, disordered systems lack long-range periodicity, which makes conventional diffraction analysis insufficient for resolving the three-dimensional atomic arrangements. Existing reverse Monte Carlo (RMC) approaches rely on stochastic sampling, limiting both computational efficiency and the ability to enforce chemically realistic local environment. Here we present TorchDisorder, a PyTorch-based framework that replaces stochastic moves with gradient-based optimization via automatic differentiation, built on three tightly integrated components: GPU-accelerated neighbor list construction via torch-sim, augmented Lagrangian constrained optimization via the Cooper library, and a differentiable structure factor engine that propagates gradients through the full Faber-Ziman weighted Fourier transform. Coordination constraints for tetrahedral, octahedral, and other geometries are specified via JSON configuration files generated automatically from crystalline precursors, and requires no manual parameter tuning. We apply TorchDisorder to three glass systems relevant to energy technology, namely silica (SiO2), germania (GeO2), and lithium thiophosphate (Li2S-P2S5) solid electrolytes, and obtain structural models in quantitative agreement with experimental scattering data ($R^2 \geq 0.955$) within 5000 gradient steps, outperforming stochastic RMC in both convergence speed, and constraint satisfaction

papers.title: Using Data Science and Experimental Tools to Determine Molecular Design Principles for Commercial Quinone Posolytes
papers.abstract: Quinones are promising electrolyte candidates for aqueous redox flow batteries (ARFBs) and are widely commercially available, but their application is limited by challenges balancing redox potential, chemical stability, and solubility. While redox potential is relatively straightforward to measure or compute, chemical stability, particularly resistance to degradation, remains complex and experimentally demanding. In this study, we sought to quantify quinone degradation across diverse substitution patterns and to identify molecular features that contribute to improved performance using machine learning regression algorithms. Experimental results confirmed that redox potential and stability are not linearly correlated, complicating simultaneous optimization. We therefore sought to optimize each metric independently and construct a Pareto front based on predicted experimental metrics. This work demonstrates the power of descriptor-driven virtual screening, supported by experimental validation, for the rational design of next-generation quinones for ARFBs and assesses the current landscape of commercially available quinones for their application.

papers.title: GA-Optimized Bin Difference Partial Least Squares Regression for Spectroscopic Calibration
papers.abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy is a cornerstone of non-destructive analysis, yet its complexity necessitates sophisticated multivariate modeling. While partial least squares regression (PLSR) is the standard approach, its efficacy depends heavily on independent, sequential steps of preprocessing and variable selection. A significant research gap exists in current workflows: most selection methods focus on absolute intensities at specific wavelengths, failing to exploit the relational information and contrast between spectral regions which are often more resistant to baseline shifts. Furthermore, treating preprocessing and variable selection as isolated tasks ignores their functional interdependencies. This study introduces Genetic Algorithm-Optimized Bin Difference PLSR (GA-OBD PLSR), a framework that unifies feature construction and variable selection. By representing spectra as the difference between integrated intensities of two optimized spectral bins, the method captures relational absorbance patterns directly in the native spectral domain. A genetic algorithm jointly optimizes bin locations, widths, and feature sparsity within a nested cross-validation framework to ensure unbiased performance estimates. Evaluated across diverse pharmaceutical and agricultural datasets, GA-OBD PLSR consistently reduced model dimensionality by 60 to 80 percent while maintaining or enhancing predictive accuracy. The most substantial gains occurred on raw spectra, where the bin-difference representation functioned as an inherent, targeted noise-reduction step. Analysis of selected features confirmed that the algorithm identifies chemically meaningful regions, while DModX diagnostics showed superior orthogonality to non-predictive variation. Beyond improved generalization, the reduction in predictor variables yielded a 7.36x speedup in prediction time, with the reduced model. These results demonstrate that GA-OBD PLSR provides a robust, interpretable, and computationally tractable alternative to full-spectrum modeling.

papers.title: Recyclable Pt-catalyzed biphase hydrosilylation on water: from functionalized monomers to polymer materials
papers.abstract: This study proposes ways to resolve the main challenges of the important industrial hydrosilylation process using biphase “on water” catalytic systems. The Pt/H2O-catalytic system consists of a commercially available Pt-precatalyst, K2PtCl4, and the most naturally abundant and environmentally benign solvent, H2O. It is easily prepared by mixing them without the use of ligands or an inert atmosphere, at r.t. for 2 min. The use of affordable KBr as an additive significantly increases the efficiency of the method for a range of substrates. Mechanistic studies revealed that during hydrosilylation, single-atom complexes (mainly in Pt/H2O) and cluster (mainly, in Pt/KBr/H2O) Pt0-complexes are generated, which are responsible for the high catalytic activity of these systems. Pt/H2O- and Pt/KBr/H2O-catalytic systems are highly efficient in the hydrosilylation of a wide range of hydrosilanes, including oligomeric and polymeric ones, as well as aliphatic and aromatic alkenes and alkynes containing N-, O-, S-, Si-, and Hal-containing functional groups. The method allows for the synthesis of products in high yields with anti-Markovnikov selectivity, in air at r.t. Using the Pt/KBr/H₂O-catalytic system, cured silicone materials were obtained both as monoliths and thin films, from PDMS derivatives with Si–H-groups with linear and cyclic vinylsiloxanes, various dienes, and, more importantly, by gaseous acetylene and butadiene. Pt-free (monomer, polymer, and cured) products can be isolated from the biphasic catalytic system by simple decantation. The possibility of multiple catalyst recycling (demonstrated over 15 cycles), combined with low Pt-loadings (0.01–0.1 mol%) and high product yields (up to 99%), allows for achieving low E-factor (≤0.07) and high TON (>104). We also constructed a tube-in-tube flow reactor, which enables reaction scale-up with greater efficiency than in batch and the automatic separation of products and the catalytic system.

papers.title: Lewis Acidity of Trigonal-bipyramidal Formal Cu(III) Halide Complexes Enables General Deoxyhalogenation of Alcohols
papers.abstract: We report the reactivity of formal Cu(III) centers as potent Lewis acids to activate the C(sp3)–OH bond in alcohols and convert them into the corresponding fluorides, chlorides, and bromides. A series of formal Cu(III) halide complexes (X = F, Cl, Br) supported by the tris(2‑pyridylthio)methanide (TPTM, L) ligand were synthesized and fully characterized. These trigonal‑bipyramidal [LCuIII–X]+ complexes feature an anionic carbon donor trans to the halide, resulting in weakened Cu–X bonds. Treatment of [LCuIII–X]+ with alkyl alcohols affords the corresponding alkyl fluorides, chlorides, and bromides. The efficiency of the deoxyhalogenation reaction correlates with the Lewis acidity of the Cu(III) center. Mechanistic studies using substrates containing cyclopropyl motifs indicate that the reaction proceeds through a carbocation intermediate. This unprecedented C(sp3)–OH bond activation at a Cu center has implications for the C–H halogenation reactivity observed in copper-dependent halogenases. While enzymatic C(sp3)–H halogenation is commonly proposed to proceed via direct formation of C(sp3)–halogen bonds, our results suggest an alternative stepwise pathway in which a C(sp3)–H bond is first converted to C(sp3)–OH bond, followed by a copper-mediated deoxyhalogenation that converts C(sp3)–OH to C(sp3)–X bond.

papers.title: Democratizing LYTACs—A Modular Click Chemistry Platform for the Rapid Assembly of Lysosome-Targeting Chimeras
papers.abstract: Lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) are emerging therapeutics that mediate extracellular targeted protein degradation. Through simultaneous engagement of a target protein of interest and a lysosomal trafficking receptor, these bifunctional molecules can facilitate the degradation of both secreted and cell-surface proteins. The original LYTACs were designed to engage the cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor (CI-M6PR) via complex glycopolymer or glycopolypeptide ligands conjugated to target-specific antibodies. However, the complexity of these ligands has limited the broader adoption of LYTACs as research tools. Here we describe a simple, rapid, and modular click chemistry platform for the generation of CI-M6PR-binding LYTACs. The approach utilizes only commercially available reagents and standard laboratory equipment and allows for the conversion of virtually any antibody into a LYTAC. This method for “democratizing” LYTAC generation should facilitate the widespread adoption of these tools for biological discovery.

papers.title: Elucidating key reducing species beyond ions in hydrogen plasma smelting reduction of iron ore
papers.abstract: Hydrogen plasma smelting reduction (HPSR) of iron ore has attracted significant attention over the past decade due to its high-temperature operation, rapid plasma mediated reduction kinetics, and ease of separating the molten iron product. All of these attributes are critical when utilizing low-grade ores for downstream use in electric-arc furnaces. While positive ions exist within the plasma arc, this work demonstrates that near the anodic ore surface, hydrogen radicals and vibrationally excited hydrogen species dominate and their densities correlate directly with observed reduction rates. Species concentrations in the transferred plasma arc and at the plasma–ore interface are quantified using coupled thermal plasma and near-wall non-equilibrium plasma models. The thermal plasma model is validated against experimental voltage data and spectroscopic measurements of plasma temperature and density for varying current inputs. Modeling of the near surface thermochemical non-equilibrium and anode sheath layer of ∼ 5 µm thickness reveals, in addition to the expected H+, significant concentrations of ArH+ and H+3 ions, typically not observed in thermal plasmas under thermodynamic equilibrium. Our results show that the inverted sheath structure at the anodic ore surface strongly suppresses reactive positive ion fluxes, while non-equilibrium electron-impact processes generate abundant hydrogen radicals and vibrationally excited species. These findings highlight the critical role of non-equilibrium effects in hydrogen arc–driven iron ore reduction and advance understanding beyond prevailing hypotheses centered on hydrogen ion–driven mechanisms.

papers.title: Harnessing Collective Electrophilic Reactivity of Affinity Labeling Probes for Versatile Target Identification
papers.abstract: Affinity labeling has been employed as a powerful tool for target protein identification, yet outcomes are often unpredictable due to the inherent protein-dependent reactivity of electrophilic labels. This problem is especially pronounced for carbohydrate ligands with weak binding affinity. We report a data-driven approach to designing affinity labeling probes that addresses the inherent limitations of traditional single-electrophile probes. Using the lactose-lectin pairs as model systems, we developed a multiwell plate reaction analysis method to quantitatively evaluate a library of gold nanoparticle-based electrophile probes. By treating the electrophile library as a multisensor array, we characterized target proteins based on their unique reactivity profiles. Application of linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to the reactivity data set revealed that proteins can be distinguished by their reactivity fingerprints. Optimization using LDA identified a minimal subset of five electrophiles spanning distinct reaction mechanisms, which is capable of efficient protein discrimination. Guided by these multivariate analyses, we developed the heteromultivalent gold-nanoparticle probe that simultaneously displays the optimized electrophile ensemble. Our five-electrophile probe achieved higher labeling efficiency for a target protein in complex lysate compared to an equivalent mixture of five single-electrophile probes. Our findings provide a systematic platform for the design of versatile affinity labels, offering an effective new strategy for capturing elusive target proteins.

papers.title: Metallaphosphinidene Coupling with a Phosphorus Ylide to Form Phosphavinyl [P=CH2]–
Engineering Tunable Elastin-Like Polypeptide/Poly(ethylene glycol) Diacrylate Composite Hydrogels for Injectable Soft Tissue Fillers
papers.abstract: Soft tissue augmentation is widely used for cosmetic and reconstructive indications, requiring void filler materials that can be delivered minimally invasively while maintaining structural stability and tissue-like mechanics. Here, we engineered a biocompatible, injectable composite hydrogel based on elastin-like polypeptides (ELPs) and poly (ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) with tunable viscoelasticity, favorable mechanical properties, and high structural integrity for soft tissue reconstruction. Hydrogels were formed by photoinitiated crosslinking involving thiol–ene coupling between cysteine thiols on ELP and acrylate groups of PEGDA, yielding rapid in situ gelation. The ELP component provided elastin-like extensibility, while PEGDA contributed resilient elastic recovery with low energy dissipation under cyclic loading. By modulating the PEGDA/ELP ratio, the composite viscoelastic response could be tuned, enabling mechanical performance that exceeded either polymer network alone and producing soft tissue–like elastic moduli. Notably, the ELP/PEGDA (50/50) formulation achieved >300% elongation, minimal permanent deformation (~3.5%), and low energy loss (~15%), comparable to native elastin, supporting its potential as an injectable void filler for soft tissue reconstruction.

papers.title: Probing Vibrational Excitation Patterns of Benzene Dimer using Machine Learning Tools
papers.abstract: In this letter, another important application of machine learning (ML) techniques is demonstrated in understanding and analyzing vibrational excitation patterns of benzene dimer complex. A total of 15000 trajectories is integrated via chemical dynamics simulations to generate the required data for the present ML applications. This work shows that, when training with the survival probability information of the complex, a Multi Layer Perceptron model can predict the same when all modes are randomly excited. A Gradient Boosting model is used to find out the contribution from modes of different frequency groups to the overall dissociation pattern. Most importantly, a Decision Tree Regression model shows its power in predicting the result obtained from a different excitation energy without using any data from that energy.

papers.title: A Hybrid Kinetic Monte Carlo Algorithm for ATRP: Coupling Deterministic Mean-Field Kinetics with Stochastic Chain Growth
papers.abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations of Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization (ATRP) suffer from severe computational stiffness due to the fast activation-deactivation equilibrium, which consumes the vast majority of computational resources and limits applicability to large-scale or complex architectures. In this work, we propose a Hybrid Mean-Field/kMC Algorithm designed to significantly enhance computational efficiency while maintaining microscopic accuracy. The core strategy involves decoupling the macroscopic concentration evolution from the microscopic chain growth. First, a stiff Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) solver is employed to pre-compute the macroscopic trajectories of radical and deactivator concentrations. Subsequently, within the Monte Carlo kernel, we introduce the concept of "Effective Activation Cycles." By sampling the number of monomer additions per activation event directly from a geometric distribution, the algorithm bypasses millions of null activation/deactivation loops. Furthermore, a monomer-consumption-based time stepping mechanism and a Poisson-process-driven termination strategy are implemented to ensure the physical fidelity of chain growth. Benchmarking results demonstrate that the hybrid algorithm yields perfect agreement with the exact Stochastic Simulation Algorithm (SSA), achieving a computational speedup of approximately 20 folds. To demonstrate its versatility, the framework is extended to computationally challenging regimes, including continuous catalyst regeneration and diffusion-controlled kinetics. Most notably, by integrating a dynamic disjoint-set topological algorithm, the method successfully bypasses the mathematical singularities of continuum models at the gel point. It accurately resolves extreme kinetic timescales—from the ultrafast transient microgelation in conventional free radical polymerization (FRP) to the delayed network percolation in ATRP—providing a high-fidelity digital twin of macroscopic sol-gel transitions and microscopic topological defects.

papers.title: Aryne-Mediated Direct Assembly of O-Bridged Seven-Membered Cyclic Diaryliodoniums: Access to Oxaheteropines and Cannabinols via Skeletal Modification
papers.abstract: Cyclic diaryliodonium salts are versatile intermediates for the synthesis of functionalized aromatic compounds and polycyclic systems. Their preparation, however, typically relies on oxidative cyclization of preorganized iodoaryl–aryl frameworks, and medium-sized cyclic diaryliodoniums remain largely underexplored within this synthetic paradigm. Here we report an aryne-mediated direct assembly of O-bridged seven-membered cyclic diaryliodoniums from (pseudo)cyclic diaryliodanes bearing an O-nucleophilic benzyl alcohol-derived ligand and a dummy 2,4,6-trimethoxyphenyl ligand. The transformation involves aryne engagement of the oxygen and intramolecular ambiphilic capture by the iodine(III) center, followed by protonation of the dummy ligand to furnish the cyclic diaryliodonium products. These cyclic diaryliodoniums serve as versatile platforms for skeletal modification, enabling access to oxaheteropine frameworks through iodine replacement and a concise synthesis of cannabinol via iodine deletion.

papers.title: Convergent Synthesis of Natural-Mimetic Glycerophospholipids: New Tools for Biological Studies and Cancer Cells Labelling
papers.abstract: Glycerophosphlipids (GPLs) constitute the most important subclass of phospholipids. These biomolecules play multiple roles at the cellular level and are involved as major constituents in membrane bilayers, cellular compartmentalization and as intramolecular signaling molecules. We have recently demonstrated that, to preserve the native biological behavior of phosphatidic acids (PA, a GPL) probes, no modifications should be made to their fatty acid chains nor phosphate head, whereas only the addition of a clickable moiety on the glycerol backbone is acceptable. Since PA represent only a tiny fraction of GPLs, we have extended our synthetic methodology to more challenging families of GPLs such as phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylcholine or phosphatidylserine by using an innovative and convergent approach. Moreover, the clickable moiety was used to allowed flexible grafting in cellulo of different molecules to GPLs analogues for various biological applications. This innovation thus provides powerful tools for selectively labeling cancer cells by exploiting the difference of composition of the membrane leaflets between normal and cancer cells.

papers.title: On the Informational Consequences of Categorical State Partitioning on Quantum Electron Transfer Mechanics:
papers.abstract: We demonstrate zero-backaction measurement of electron dynamics in proteins using categorical quantum mechanics. Tracking Cu(I) → Cu(II) transfer in azurin from Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PDB: 4AZU), we extract categorical coordinates (n, ℓ,m, s) from five spectroscopic modalities (optical absorption, Raman scattering, EPR, circular dichroism, and timeof-flight mass spectrometry). These coordinates commute with physical observables, enabling trajectory tracking without wavefunction collapse. Through ternary trisection with weak internal perturbations (∆E ≪ kT ), we achieve mean per-iteration backaction of (1.68± 0.32)× 10−4, representing a 6,000-fold improvement over classical measurement. Over 17 measurement iterations spanning 160 femtoseconds, ternary localization extracts 16.5 bits of information with Shannon entropy 0.613 trits per measurement, demonstrating effective three-way spatial partitioning. The electron trajectory exhibits systematic displacement at velocity 12.4 ± 0.8 km/s, matching literature values for the His46–Cys112 pathway. Categorical coordinates evolve through discrete quantum state transitions [(n=1, ℓ=0) → (n=1, ℓ=2) → (n=2, ℓ=2)] with S-entropy conservation (Sk + St + Se = 1.00± 0.01), confirming measurement preserves quantum coherence. Five visualization panels present the 3D electron trajectory, statistical backaction verification, categorical coordinate evolution, probability density dynamics, and S-entropy space trajectory. This work establishes categorical measurement as a rigorous method for visualizing quantum dynamics in complex biological systems.

papers.title: Fluctuation-driven chemistry at aqueous interfaces and beyond
papers.abstract: Interfacial electric fields at gas–water, oil–water, and solid–water boundaries are frequently invoked to explain radical formation under ambient conditions. Field strengths of 10 7 –10 9 V m -1 are often cited as sufficient for this purpose. Yet the electrostatic work accessible from such fields over molecular distances is orders of magnitude smaller than the energies required for homolytic bond dissociation or one-electron ionization. This discrepancy raises the question of whether interfacial electric fields directly drive chemistry or modulate an intrinsic mechanism of liquid water. We argue that equilibrium interfacial electric fields bias molecular orientation and reaction kinetics but do not constitute a primary energetic input for bond-breaking chemistry. Instead, we propose a fluctuation-driven model in which transient, partially charge-separated configurations (H 2 O +δ ···H 2 O -δ ) arise from cooperative hydrogenbond fluctuations. In this picture, interfaces, ions, and weak perturbations reshape the free-energy landscape and alter fluctuation statistics.

papers.title: One-Dimensional Fully sp2 Carbon-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Powerful Photoreduction of CO2
papers.abstract: Precisely arranging organic π-conjugated macrocyclic units to long range-ordered arrays might not only diversify the geometric and topological structures, but also bring out exceptional semiconducting properties. Herein, upon Knoevenagel condensation of angular ditopic phenanthroline and tetratopic biphenyl or bipyridinyl derivatives, we synthesized new types of one-dimensional (1D) fully sp2 carbon-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Powder X-ray diffraction patterns and nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherms revealed the repeated vinylene-linked macrocycles interconnected by carbon-carbon single bonds, which further assembled to long-range ordered alignments along the in-plane and vertical directions. Such unique 1D COF motifs are the congeners of the crystalline assemblies of linear conjugated polymacrocycles, favorable for dispersion and active site exposure. The πdelocalization of these COFs can be efficiently modulated by the macrocycle moieties with the cross- or linear-conjugation mode, then affecting their electron coupling and exciton dynamics. With the phenanthroline nitrogen atoms in the macrocyclic backbones serving as catalytic active sites, they exhibited photocatalytic reduction of CO2 to CO in a generation rate of 3535.9 umol.g-1.h-1, and up to 19678.3 umol.g-1.h-1 upon loading cobalt (II) cation. Both values are among the highest values of the organic or organic-inorganic hybrid photocatalysts to date.

papers.title: Unique fluoroalkyl substituents: the case of fluoroisopropyl (-CFMe2) group
papers.abstract: The CFMe2-substituent is a close analogue of the CF3-group. The CF3 for CFMe2 replacement in model compounds mostly does not affect key physicochemical properties: water solubility, lipophilicity, and metabolic stability. Analogous replacement in the anticancer drug Enasidenib, however, provides a biologically active analogue with improved solubility and reduced lipophilicity.

papers.title: Balancing composition and phase stability in High-Entropy Metal Phosphates for proton conduction
papers.abstract: The transition to sustainable energy technologies involves, among others, the development of proton-conducting electrolytes that minimise the use of critical raw materials. Transition metal phosphate octahydrates offer a robust structural model platform for proton transport; however, their performance appears to be dominated by the specific identity of the host cation, with scarce and expensive cobalt serving as the baseline. Here, we demonstrate a high-entropy design strategy that effectively decouples proton conductivity from cobalt reliance. By synthesising complex, single-phase solid solutions containing up to seven distinct metal cations via a scalable aqueous precipitation method, we reveal that increased configurational entropy produces a synergistic enhancement in proton mobility. Statistical modelling of the multi-dimensional compositional space using Random Forest and ridge regression confirms that at 80°C, configurational entropy surpasses absolute cobalt content as the primary driver of transport performance. This entropy-driven effect allows for the reduction of cobalt to below 40 mol% while achieving conductivities that match or exceed the pure cobalt baseline. Our findings establish that high-entropy structural disorder can effectively compensate for the dilution of critical elements, providing a versatile platform for designing next-generation, sustainable functional materials.

papers.title: Intrachain Interactions Accelerate Access to a Modifiable Fluoro-Polyester Library With End-of Life Fluoride Recyclability
papers.abstract: Fluorinated polymers offer outstanding material properties but lack viable end-of-life options. Here we report a general ring-opening copolymerisation strategy that delivers a broad library of fluorinated polyesters with tunable thermal properties, straightforward post-polymerisation modification and quantitative fluorine recovery as sodium fluoride upon degradation. In mapping the scope of this methodology across diverse anhydride partners, we found that fluorination accelerates catalysis mostly when both monomers are aromatic and one is fluorinated. Density functional theory and mechanistic experiments reveal that the rate enhancement does not originate at the catalyst but within the growing polymer chain itself, through intrachain π–π stacking interactions that stabilise the transition state. The polymer chain constructs a structured non-covalent environment around the active centre with every turnover making chain microstructure an unexpected determinant of catalytic rate. These findings reframe how we think about chain-derived effects in polymerisation catalysis, and are accompanied by a modifiable fluoropolyester library spanning glass transition temperatures from below -14 °C to 144 °C, from which fluorine can be recovered upon degradation.

papers.title: Translating π-adsorptive sites across reticular chemistries for water-tolerant CO2 capture
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are among the most versatile platforms for CO2 capture, yet their performance under realistic, humid conditions remains a major limitation. Strategies that enhance CO2 affinity often rely on highly polar adsorption sites, which simultaneously promote water uptake and compromise selectivity and stability. Overcoming this trade-off between adsorption strength and operational robustness remains a central challenge in the field. Here we show that this limitation can be addressed by translating a π-based CO2 recognition motif from a carboxylate MOF into a denser pyrazolate framework. In the resulting material, MUV-92, structural confinement reconfigures the adsorption energy landscape, redistributing CO2 binding over several energetically similar sites rather than concentrating it in a single dominant environment. This redistribution leads to homogeneous adsorption energetics and enhanced uptake without introducing additional polar functionalities. Framework densification also creates a more confined pore environment dominated by weakly interacting polyaromatic surfaces, which limits water access to the adsorption cavities. As a result, MUV-92 maintains efficient CO2 capture under humid conditions. Dynamic breakthrough and competitive adsorption experiments demonstrate sustained performance even under saturated humidity, a regime in which benchmark materials typically suffer severe performance losses.

papers.title: Achieving Consistency in Redox Flow Battery Power Characterization: Methodologic Insights
Assessing surface hopping methods for long-time internal conversion dynamics: The case of lutein
papers.abstract: Surface hopping methods, such as fewest switches surface hopping (FSSH), are widely used to simulate ultrafast nonadiabatic phenomena. However, their accuracy in capturing long-time nonadiabatic dynamics remains largely untested. Here, we assess and compare several surface hopping approaches for describing long-timescale nonadiabatic dynamics, using the S 1 → S 0 internal conversion of the carotenoid lutein in vacuum and in solution as a test case. Our simulations show that the commonly used FSSH with energy-based decoherence-correction (FSSH-EDC) and our recently proposed semi-focused mapping approach to surface hopping (SMASH) fail to accurately describe the slow internal conversion of lutein. In contrast, two surface hopping variants introduced in this work, namely an adapted FSSH-EDC scheme (A-EDC) and a decoherence-corrected SMASH method (SMASH-DEC), effectively improve the treatment of decoherence effects, compared to their parent methods, and predict S 1 → S 0 decay times in significantly better agreement with experimental spectroscopic data and more consistent with ab initio multiple spawning (AIMS) simulations.

papers.title: First-Principles Analysis of Protonation-Induced Electronic Effects in Tetrakis(p-aminophenyl)porphyrin (TAPP)
papers.abstract: The optical response of pH-sensitive porphyrins depends critically on where protonation occurs, not merely on the total charge accumulated. Using first-principle linear response theory, we systematically map all symmetry-distinct protonation states of tetrakis(p-aminophenyl)porphyrin (TAPP) from neutral to fully protonated (+6), revealing that peripheral and core protonation produce qualitatively different photophysical outcomes. Peripheral protonation preserves the Soret band character with minor shifts, while core protonation drives conformer convergence, symmetry-breaking Soret splitting, and selective Q-band collapse. Q-band oscillator strength evolves non-monotonically ─ increasing initially through orbital mixing before weakening as charge-transfer character emerges. At intermediate protonation (+4/+5), remaining unprotonated aminophenyl groups act as donors in aminophenyl to macrocycle charge-transfer (CT) excitations, identified through charge-density difference (CDD) analysis. Core protonation additionally widens the singlet-triplet gap relative to peripheral protonation, with implications for intersystem crossing and triplet-state engineering. Together, these results establish protonation topology as a molecular design parameter for controlling absorption, charge transfer, and excited-state properties in pH-responsive porphyrin systems.

papers.title: Iron Catalyzed Friedel–Crafts Reactions of Unactivated 3-Aryl-oxetanols Exploiting HFIP Stabilization of Carbocations
papers.abstract: Robust methods to access 3,3-disubstituted oxetanes are desired due to the attractive physicochemical properties offered by the polar 4-membered rings and their potential use as replacement groups for carbonyl or gem-dimethyl functionality in medicinal chemistry. The generation of benzylic oxetane carbocations from oxetanols offers considerable potential, particularly in the generation of diaryloxetanes, a structural type that is seldom reported. To date however, Friedel-Crafts reactions have been limited to oxetanols bearing an electron-rich aromatic group due to the carbocation destabilizing nature of the oxetane. Here, an alternative Fe-catalyzed Friedel–Crafts reaction is described, employing HFIP as a solvent, enabling oxetanyl carbocation formation directly from oxetanols bearing phenyl and other electron-poor arenes. HFIP with its strong hydrogen bond donor (HBD) ability and enhanced Brønsted acidity cooperatively promotes the generation of the carbocations in the presence of the Lewis acid. The oxetane-HFIP adduct was detected, likely formed reversibly as a stabilizing off-cycle intermediate. The developed methodology enabled the concise synthesis of oxetane-analogues of Fenofibrate and Tesmilifene, replacing diarylmethane and benzophenone motifs respectively. Additional mechanistic studies into the fate of these carbocation intermediates provides insights into the reaction mechanism.

papers.title: Accelerating Protonation by Amphiphilic Proton Donor for Enhancing Li-mediated Nitrogen Reduction
papers.abstract: Lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li-NRR) enables electrochemical ammonia synthesis under mild conditions but is limited by a fundamental trade-off: more acidic proton donors can accelerate productive protonation while also promoting parasitic hydrogen evolution at electroplated Li. Here, we demonstrate that 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol (TFE), an amphiphilic alcohol, overcomes this trade-off by decoupling thermodynamic acidity from kinetic reactivity. Despite its high acidity, TFE suppresses parasitic reactions via the formation of a protective, fluoride-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Blending TFE with ethanol further optimizes proton activity and hydrogen bonding, promoting the growth of a thin, uniform SEI with highly crystalline LiF. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte achieved an ammonia Faradaic efficiency of 59.0% and stable performance for 10 hours under a potential cycling protocol in a continuous-flow reactor. This study highlights proton donor engineering as a key strategy to modulate SEI nanostructure for enhanced Li-NRR.

papers.title: Local Symmetry Breaking and Two-Stage Phase Transition in RuP Uncovered by a Fine-Tuned Atomistic Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Resolving short-range structural distortions that persist within high-symmetry crystal structures remains a central challenge in materials chemistry. These distortions are dynamic, with correlations extending over nanometer length scales and picosecond timescales, making their atomistic modeling computationally demanding. Here, we address this challenge by modeling the parent compound of ruthenium-pnictide superconductors, RuP, in which such distortions and correlations are prominent. We fine-tune an atomistic foundation model (AFM) on ab initio molecular dynamics datasets and use the resulting interatomic potential to perform machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations of RuP. Analysis of the temperature dependence of lattice parameters and structure factors reveals a two-step phase transition, including an isosymmetric monoclinic-to-monoclinic transition near 180 K, followed by a monoclinic-to-orthorhombic transition near 330 K. Local order metrics and correlation functions further show that short-range monoclinic distortions persist above 330 K within the average high-symmetry phase, providing direct evidence of local symmetry breaking. Electronic-structure calculations reproduce the experimentally observed evolution from an insulating low-temperature state to an intermediate pseudogap-like regime and finally to a metallic high-temperature state, connecting the two-stage electronic transition to the underlying structural transformation. Phonon dispersion analysis reveals the emergence of imaginary phonon modes above the second transition, consistent with the dynamical instability of the average orthorhombic structure and the persistence of local lattice distortions. These findings provide an atomistic picture of local symmetry breaking in RuP and demonstrate that fine-tuned AFMs provide a practical approach for quantifying short-range distortions and correlated fluctuations in crystals with complex phase behavior.

papers.title: BONAFIDE: A Python Framework for the Calculation of Local Features for Atoms and Bonds in Molecules
papers.abstract: Data-driven chemistry relies on robust, efficient, and reproducible pipelines for generating digital molecular representations. While comprehensive software for global molecular descriptors is widely available, the calculation of local atom and bond features remains fragmented across disparate tools with inconsistent interfaces. Here, we introduce the BOnd aNd Atom FeaturIzer and Descriptor Extractor (BONAFIDE), a Python package designed to standardize the generation of local descriptors. BONAFIDE provides a unified application programming interface that integrates 11 external computational chemistry and cheminformatics packages, including RDKit, MORFEUS, and Multiwfn as well as quantum chemical engines like xtb and Psi4 for single-point energy computations. The software currently supports the calculation of 590 distinct atom and bond features derived from either 2D or 3D molecular representations and electronic structure data. Key functionalities include flexible input format processing as well as output customization, seamless atom and bond feature calculation across all implemented descriptors, transparent hyperparameter tracking, comprehensive logging, and the possibility to implement custom featurizers within the BONAFIDE ecosystem. We also include runtime statistics for featurization and a case study that demonstrates how the tool is used for the featurization of amines through a multistep featurization pipeline. Current limitations and future development directions are discussed. BONAFIDE is available free of charge as open-source software under the Apache 2.0 license and can be obtained from GitHub (https://github.com/MolecularAI/atom-bond-featurizer).

papers.title: Green-to-red photopolymerization via Dual-Role Dyes for Transparency-Tunable 3D-Printed Hydrogels
papers.abstract: Speed and resolution of light-based 3D printing typically relies on multicomponent photopolymer formulations. Here, we present a unique single-dye system that not only controls printing speed and resolution but also tunes the final optical properties of the printed constructs. Photobleaching behavior and photorheology of five dyes in the green-to-red light region were investigated. To gain deeper insight into the printing mechanism and resulting optical properties, one dye (methylene blue) was selected and studied across a series of concentrations to evaluate curing depth, curing resolution, and environmental photobleaching under different light and pH conditions. Together, these results establish a simple route to traceless visible-light DLP hydrogels with tunable optical properties and high print fidelity for biomedical applications.

papers.title: Strong Proper C-H Hydrogen Bonds: Experimental Evidence across Spectral Ranges
papers.abstract: C-H bonds are known as weak hydrogen bond (H-bond) donors, and the H-bonds they typically form are improper: C-H bond shortens, frequency of its vibrational transition blueshifts and intensity decreases. All these characteristics are opposite to familiar-proper-H-bonds. Here we demonstrate that an sp-hybridized terminal alkyne (≡C-H) is a potent proper hydrogen bond donor. Tuning across >50 solvation environments we demonstrate the propensity of this moiety to form H-bonds with heteroatoms in polar solvents, aromatic -systems and, most surprisingly, even with single -bonds in non-polar molecules. We directly observe the H-bond formation and comprehensively characterize it using the combination of infrared (IR) absorption, 1 H and 13 C NMR and broadband time-domain terahertz spectroscopies. Experimental results are interpreted using ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Both electric field effects and non-electrostatic short-range interactions determine the frequency of the hydrogen-bonded ≡C-H stretch. Based on purely experimental observables, we propose a method to disentangle and quantify these contributions. We also show that a non-hydrogen bonded ≡C-H is a powerful sensor of dispersion interactions read out from its IR shift even in the presence of much stronger competing interactions. Overall, the alkynyl ≡C-H mimics an O-H group rather than resembling a typical aliphatic C-H. Its distinct local character and spectral isolation from other C-H stretches, high electric field sensitivity, strong propensity toward H-bond interactions, compactness and ease of incorporation into molecular scaffolds make this overlooked vibrational marker a strong contender for sensing.

papers.title: Reshaping Ru Polypyridyl Photochemistry with Choline-Geranate (CAGE) Ionic Liquids
papers.abstract: Choline-geranate (CAGE) ionic liquids are emerging as powerful topical delivery media, yet their impact on the photochemistry of metal-based phototherapeutics remains unexplored. Here we show that CAGE ILs can substantially reshape the excited-state landscape of Ru polypyridyl complexes, promoting ligand photorelease in a prototypical PDT scaffold while preserving the expected behaviour of photo-labile and photo-inert analogues. These findings highlight CAGE ILs as both an enabling delivery platform and an active medium that can tune Ru photoreactivity, with implications for designing PDT and photoactivated chemotherapy strategies.

papers.title: Electrochemical Characterization of Photo-driven Hole-Scavenging by Cadmium Sulfide Quantum Dot-Nitrogenase Biohybrid Complexes
papers.abstract: Light-driven biohybrid systems that couple semiconductor nanocrystals with enzymes offer a promising strategy for solar-to-chemical energy-conserving reduction reactions, yet are often limited by inefficient electron-hole scavenging. Hole scavenging is critical for maintaining charge separation in the light-absorbing electron donor molecule and thus for sustaining catalytic turnover, making quantification essential for improving system efficiency. Here, we introduce a photoelectrochemical approach for real-time monitoring of hole scavenging in cadmium sulfide (CdS) quantum dot (QD)-nitrogenase MoFe protein biohybrids that catalyze H+ and N2 reduction. Using hydroquinone (HQ) as the sacrificial electron donor (SED), oxidation to benzoquinone (BQ) by photogenerated valence-band electron holes is coupled to electrochemical reduction of the BQ at an electrode, enabling quantification of the hole-scavenging reaction via chronoamperometry. This approach provides a continuous, real-time readout of charge-transfer dynamics under illumination. Systematic variation of light intensity and donor concentration reveals that hole-scavenging scales with photon flux and exhibits a non-linear dependence on SED concentration, with an optimum at intermediate HQ concentrations. These results establish chronoamperometry as a powerful tool for probing photoinduced charge transfer, advancing the quantitative understanding of hole-scavenging in biohybrid systems, and offering a generalizable framework for optimizing solar-driven biocatalysis.

papers.title: Disentangling the impact of cation identity on transport and kinetics in nitrate electroreduction to ammonia
papers.abstract: The electroreduction of the nitrate anion is surprisingly catalyzed on surfaces that are perceived as negatively charged, conditions where cations from the electrolyte are—on average—closer to the surface in the electrical double layer (EDL). As such, the charge density of alkali metal cations and the extent of their interactions with nitrate could notably impact both transport of nitrate to the surface and the rates of its reduction. We separate these effects quantitatively for the electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) on cobalt in alkaline media, which has high selectivity to ammonia (~90%). A K + -containing electrolyte has higher NO3RR kinetic currents than a Li + -containing one, though the magnitude of this difference depends on catalyst pretreatment. Surprisingly, an ~2x difference in the apparent NO3RR diffusion limited current is observed between Li + and K + electrolytes, inconsistent with the reduction of uncharged reactants. This difference arises in part from the availability of active sites, also involved in (oxy)hydroxide formation due to the highly oxidizing nature of the nitrate reactant and nitrite intermediate. The dynamic role of such species during NO3RR is uniquely influenced by the nature of the cation, pointing to a complex coexistence of (hydr)oxides and cations in stabilizing the anionic reactant under the reducing conditions of NO3RR.

papers.title: Transition Metal-Free Formal 2,3-Hetaryne Insertion into C–C Bonds of Benzocyclobutenones
papers.abstract: The formal insertion of 2,3-hetarynes into the C–C bonds of strained cyclic ketones has been achieved. This process proceeds under mild conditions and does not require the use of a transition metal catalyst. A variety of annulated indoles, 7-azaindoles, and other annulated heteroaromatics relevant to bioactive scaffolds were efficiently accessed through this methodology. Mechanistic studies reveal a unique role of base in facilitating C–C bond cleavage to generate a reactive intermediate that is proposed to ultimately engage in a dearomative cycloaddition process with indoles enabled by halogen substitution.

papers.title: Early- and late-stage chemoenzymatic functionalisation of steroid-inspired compounds
papers.abstract: Selective C-H functionalisation of small molecule leads is a powerful approach for efficient chemical space exploration and medicinal chemistry optimisation. Here, we report a screening platform for early- and late-stage chemoenzymatic oxidation of steroid-inspired compounds using a panel of P450 BM3 variants. Late-stage oxidation of sterol transport protein inhibitors and their intermediates revealed enzyme- and substrate-dependent regioselectivity, yielding hydroxylated analogues that provided rapid structure-activity relationship insights into the spirooxepinoindole as a privileged scaffold and its potential metabolic products. Early-stage functionalisation of steroidal building blocks, including the Wieland-Miescher ketone and acetyl- cis -decalone, furnished hydroxylated derivatives with high diastereoselectivity. Notably, both enantiomers of both diastereoisomers of the C6-hydroxylated Wieland-Miescher ketone were obtained in preparative quantities, enabling access to valuable early-stage building blocks. This work highlights the potential of chemoenzymatic approaches to deliver regio- and stereoselective oxidations of challenging steroid-like scaffolds, complementing classical synthetic methods and expanding opportunities in medicinal chemistry and natural product synthesis.

papers.title: Coacervates of Single Amino acid Derivative act as Micro-reactors en route their Supramolecular Assembly into Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Peptides and proteins often assemble into one-dimensional supramolecular architectures responsible for cellular activities (e.g., actin and tubulin filaments) as well as pathological processes such as amyloid fibrillation. In many systems, such aggregation proceeds through liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), where the metastable coacervates act as dynamic microreactors for nucleation and growth of one-dimensional supramolecular polymers. However, how reaction conditions regulate the mechanism and kinetics of such assemblies remains unclear. Herein, we report a minimalist single-component system in which a pyreneappended arginine derivative, L-ArgPy, combine zwitterionic character with aggregationinduced emission (AIE), enabling fluorescence monitoring of its assembly. Under chargeneutral conditions, L-ArgPy self-assembles to form coacervate droplets that mediate supramolecular polymerization into tubular structures, whereas slight deviations from physiological conditions bypass the coacervate state and lead directly to one-dimensional growth. Mechanistic studies and controlled experiments reveal that cation–π interactions are responsible for the coacervate stabilization, anion–water interactions promote droplet coalescence, and π–π interactions drive polymerization via a liquid-to-solid transition. The coalescence of the membraneless coacervates is a critical step for the nucleation and growth of supramolecular polymers, as surface passivation of the coacervates inhibit the liquid to solid transition. Notably, L-ArgPy coacervates exhibit biosensing capability and antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting their potential as programmable supramolecular biomaterials.

papers.title: First-Principles Computational Discovery of Succinyl-CoA Synthetase Inhibitor Candidates Using the Ashebo Local Potency Density Field Method
papers.abstract: We report the application of the Ashebo Local Potency Density (LPD) field method — a firstprinciples, training-data-free computational framework based on Atomic Volume Theory (AVT) — to the druggability assessment and de novo inhibitor design targeting human ADPforming Succinyl-CoA Synthetase (SCS, PDB: 6G4Q, SUCLG1‒SUCLA2 complex). The method ranked 6G4Q at the 97th druggability percentile among a curated benchmark panel of 38 proteins spanning druggable, difficult, and undruggable targets, placing it above BCL-2 (target of venetoclax). The Inverse MPS (Molecular Potency Surface) algorithm independently derived the molecular formula C17H25ClF2N6O4 (MW 450.5 Da) as the optimal composition for Pocket 9 of the binding site, without access to any known SCS ligand data. Subsequent SMILES enumeration using RDKit and AutoDock Vina docking against the 6G4Q crystal structure produced five drug-like candidates with predicted binding affinities of −7.2 to −7.5 kcal/mol (estimated Kd ~3‒5 μM). These affinities represent early-stage computational hits; approved drugs typically achieve nanomolar affinity, and medicinal chemistry optimisation would be required to advance these candidates. Critically, the structural enumeration independently converged on a xanthine (purine-2,6-dione) scaffold — the same bicyclic nitrogen-rich system present in ADP/ATP, the native substrate of SCS. This convergence was not anticipated and was not encoded in the algorithm. Cross-Preprint Notice: This manuscript has not undergone peer review. Results are computational predictions and have not been experimentally validated. The methods described use proprietary parameters; sufficient detail is provided for scientific evaluation of the results but not for independent replication of the algorithm. validation against two related targets — glutaminase (PDB: 6LOX) and GTP-forming SCS (PDB: 8Z02) — confirmed that the method correctly identifies known allosteric pockets and generates chemically consistent nitrogen-rich, sulfur-containing candidates across the SCS isoforms. These results suggest that the AVT/LPD field framework captures real binding site geometry and generates chemically rational starting points for drug discovery without training data or prior ligand knowledge.

papers.title: Observation of ”negative” persistent photoconductivity effect at T > 200 oC in N-polar GaN/AlGaN/GaN heterostructures
papers.abstract: It is rarely reported that semiconductor materials can exhibit the ”negative” persistent photoconductivity (PC) effect. In this work the ”negative” persistent PC effect was observed in the Nitrogen (N)-polar oriented GaN/AlGaN/GaN heterostructure under the sub-bandgap illumination (2.0-2.8 eV) in the temperatures range of 200-250 oC. This is the first observation of the negative persistent PC effect in semiconductor materials at such high temperatures. The phenomenon was explained based on the model, which assumes the interaction between the absorbed oxygen species on the N-polar GaN surface, the DX centers in the GaN channel layer and two-dimensional electron gas at GaN/AlGaN interface. The discovery of high temperature ”negative” persistent PC in N-polar III-nitrides heterostructures may lead to novel applications such as temperature stable optical memories.

papers.title: Rho2Wave: TD-DFT Sonification and Chirality Encoding
papers.abstract: Rho2Wave is a software tool that converts time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) output into stereo audio and synchronized visualizations to support instruction on chirality, electronic excitations, and electronic circular dichroism (ECD). The program parses quantumchemistry output files from Gaussian (.log) and ORCA (.out) and maps excitation energies, oscillator strengths and rotatory strengths to pitch, amplitude and a tunable binaural chirality cue. The resulting sonifications are paired with 2D/3D spectrogram outputs that explicitly separate left and right channels to enable comparison of enantiomeric spectra as an auditory analogue of differential absorption for left- and right-circularly polarized light. The mapping strategy and graphical user interface are described and the approach is demonstrated across five molecular systems: benzene as an achiral baseline, as well as four enantiomeric pairs spanning point chirality (camphor, bromochlorofluoroethane), axial chirality (Kenner’s biphenyl) and helical chirality ([6]helicene). The maximum rotatory strength increases by two orders of magnitude across this series, producing a corresponding progression from moderate to extreme stereo lateralization. Ready-to-use materials, a systematic parameter sensitivity analysis, the extended chirality dataset and the complete mathematical framework are provided.

papers.title: Stepwise Proximity Labeling with a Switchable Organophotocatalyst
papers.abstract: Photoinducible proximity labeling (PL) using photocatalysts offers high spatiotemporal resolution for profiling protein–protein interactions (PPIs). Conventional approaches require genetic installation of a tag to tether the photocatalyst to a protein of interest (POI), which may perturb native protein function and cause artificial labeling. Ligand-directed delivery of photocatalysts to native POIs has emerged as a tag-free alternative; however, this strategy suffers from nonspecific labeling by unbound catalysts and an inherent washing dilemma, where insufficient washing leads to background labeling while excessive washing disrupts ligand binding. These limitations have severely restricted tagfree, ligand-directed PPI profiling. Herein, we report a switchable photoinducible PL strategy based on a nitrobenzoxadiazole (NBD) unit that becomes catalytically active only after covalent conjugation to a POI. This approach consists of a two-step process: introduction of an N -NBD moiety into the POI using a catalytically inactive O -NBD unit, followed by light-induced PL catalyzed by N -NBD. Model experiments identified N -methyl luminol as a selective labeling reagent activated by N -NBD. Using a biotin-conjugated O -NBD unit as a catalytically inactive precursor, biotinconjugated protein A was selectively labeled as a PPI partner of streptavidin. This switchable PL method circumvents the washing dilemma, suppresses nonspecific labeling, and enables high-resolution, tag-free proteomic analyses.

papers.title: HyDRA-II: Spectroscopic results and BEsT guesses for the mono-and dihydrate blind challenge
papers.abstract: HyDRA blind challenges aim at unbiased forecasts of water vibrations in vacuumisolated hydrate complexes of organic molecules by different computational protocols. In this work, directly after the completion of the HyDRA II challenge and ignorant of its computational results, the experimental findings for the 9 new solvates with a total of 12 hydrogen-bonded water OH stretching wavenumbers are disclosed and discussed. We further summarise and analyse the 70 entries of the training database, which were made available at the start of the challenge. Monohydrates of 4 other previously uncharacterised solvates are added to support the assignment of the blind test entries and to widen the future training database. The compounds for which gas phase monohydrate OH stretching fundamentals are reported for the first time comprise a difluorobenzonitrile, a difluorobenzoic acid, eucalyptol, an iodo-methylpyrazole, a methoxy pyridine, Hünig’s base, a pyrrolidine ethanol, TEMPONE, diethylhydroxylamine, pyrazine, pyrimidine, a triazine and a chiral chloropropionic acid. An experimental bridging approach (BEsT guess) using inexpensive harmonic DFT predictions from the training database for educated guesses of unknown vibrational wavenumbers is proposed to assist the future evaluation of the blind challenge. Proposals on how to compare computational predictions to experiment depending on the employed level of anharmonic perturbation are made. It will be interesting to see how different computational protocols perform in the wide range between outstanding predictions (root-mean-square deviation <10 cm−1) and placebo-quality deviations (>100 cm−1) for the 12 disclosed wavenumbers. Quantum-chemical methods are very useful and versatile tools for experimental spectroscopists.

papers.title: The Syntax of Matter: Synthesis Planning as the Foundation of Generative Chemistry
papers.abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have improved benchmark performance for chemical property prediction, yet reliable transfer to new chemical domains remains limited. A contributing factor is that many models treat molecules primarily as static graphs, ignoring the causal logic of how they are constructed. This review surveys multistep synthesis planning (2020-2026) and argues that the field is undergoing a fundamental transition: from an Era of Navigability (2018-2023), focused on the computational feasibility of finding any route through combinatorial search space, to an Era of Validity (2024-Present), focused on the chemical correctness of those routes. We organize the literature around two dominant paradigms, search-based planning and direct sequence generation, and analyze how their design choices relate to different notions of validity. To resolve the ambiguity of current "solvability" metric, which frequently exceeds 99% by measuring only topological connectivity, we introduce a formalized Hierarchy of Chemical Validity (Solv-N). This framework distinguishes between syntactic (Solv-0) and topological (Solv-1) success, which are largely solved, and the higher-order constraints of selectivity (Solv-2) and executability (Solv-3), which remain open challenges. We critically examine how legacy benchmarks and inflated virtual inventories obscure this distinction, and we conclude with a roadmap for synthesis-aware foundation models evaluated under explicit Tier 2-3 constraints.

papers.title: Adhesion of soft materials depends on interfacial strength
papers.abstract: In the conventional description, peeling of an adhesive from a solid substrate is characterized in terms of adhesion energies at adhesive-substrate interfaces. However, this energy based identification faced considerable difficulties in explaining why the adhesion energy, also known as peel strength /gamma p , is many orders of magnitude greater than Dupré's thermodynamic work of adhesion, sigma0. In this study we present experimental evidence to demonstrate that polymer adhesion is governed by interfacial strength formed between the adhesive and substrate whose surface energy /gamma s plays no explicit role in controlling the adhesion strength /sigma adh . On different substrates with widely varying surface energies, by carrying out both tensile-adhesion tests to demonstrate the dependence of /sigma adh on applied rate and temperature and conventional peeling tests to show the effects of peeling speed v p and temperature on /gamma p , we propose that /gamma p explicitly depends on /sigma adh through a characteristic length scale P instead of /gamma s and /gamma 0 . Here P is the distance of the adhesive layer away from the peeling front, beyond which the adhesive undergoes little deformation. Since P is a much larger length scale than a molecular scale and /sigma adh directly depends on polymer-substrate interfacial interactions rather than substrate surface energy, peel strength /gamma p has no relationship with /gamma 0 and its dependence on temperature and peeling speed stems from the time and temperature dependencies of interfacial strength /sigma adh . As activated processes, interfacial debonding on shorter time scales and lower temperature required higher interfacial stress. Consequently, /sigma adh is rate and temperature dependent.

papers.title: Accelerating Quantum Chemistry Automation: Early Detection and Recovery of SCF Convergence Failure via Time Series Feature Extraction
papers.abstract: Self-consistent field (SCF) convergence failures bottleneck high-throughput quantum chemistry, particularly in open-shell systems. To address this, we introduce an autonomous pipeline treating the electronic structure descriptors from initial spin-unrestricted SCF iterations as a time series. Using statistical descriptors extracted from just the first ten iterations, a lightweight gradient-boosted classifier accurately predicts convergence failures. The model achieves 94.8% accuracy on 55,000 test molecules after training on only 10,000 examples. Coupling this early-warning predictor with a 𝛽-level-shift restart (𝛽-RST) heuristic, derived from Bayesian Optimization of the shift parameters, enables automated recovery. Across six diverse calculation settings, our pipeline successfully rescued 57.5% of inherently difficult-to-converge molecules while maintaining a 94.1% convergence rate for easy cases, resulting in a 460,000-iteration reduction across the 1200 calculations. Ultimately, this framework provides a highly transferable, data-efficient, and autonomous solution for largescale electronic structure calculations.

papers.title: N-Heterocyclic Imines and Olefins as Stabilising Donors for Geminal Carbodications
papers.abstract: Geminal carbodications ( g CD) violate the electronic octet rule. We present a systematic quantum chemical analysis of diverse doubly cationic (hetero)cumulenes in a push towards identifying ideal frameworks for localizing and stabilizing the charges. Readily available N-heterocyclic imine (NHI) donors have recently successfully been used for the isolation of bis(iminyl) g CDs ((NHI) 2 C 2+ ). We herein analyze and compare their behavior to N-heterocyclic olefin (NHO) donors as promising stabilizing ligands to form bis(vinyl) carbodications ((NHO) 2 C 2+ ). Their geometry structures and bonding characteristics are analyzed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the r 2 scan-3c level, including geometry metrics, ion affinities, bond order analyses, topology approaches (QTAIM, ELF), together with IBO and NBO analysis. While both families exhibit pronounced Lewis superacidic character, they differ markedly in reactivity, charge distribution and delocalization. Our findings suggest that N -heterocyclic olefins are robust ligands to stabilize dicoordinate C 2+ centers through crucially allowing unpolar σ-bonds that avoid additional charge accumulation. The presented results support the design of further isolable g CDs which will help develop this class of compounds towards applicability.

papers.title: Assessing the Potential of Zero Charge in Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Accurate determination of the potential of zero free charge (PZFC) of an electrode from ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations remains a longstanding challenge, largely due to ambiguities in computational setups and potential referencing at electrochemical interfaces. Here, we critically assess two widely used referencing strategies, the work function (WF) and computational standard hydrogen electrode (cSHE) approaches, by combining a comprehensive analysis of literature data with new AIMD results. We demonstrate that both methods suffer from intrinsic limitations, arising from statistical uncertainty at the water/vacuum interface (WF) and from a strong dependence on setup-specific inner reference energies (cSHE). To overcome these shortcomings, we introduce a revised work-function approach (revWF) that unifies the strengths of both schemes while avoiding their principal weaknesses. The revWF method enables a more transferable and computationally efficient determination of the PZFC. Beyond these methodological considerations, we also reexamine and summarize the physical interpretation of the PZFC within the framework of an analysis originally suggested by Trasatti. Overall, this work provides practical guidelines for evaluating computational PZFCs and establishes revWF as a robust reference scheme for AIMD simulations of electrochemical interfaces.

papers.title: Structure guided optimization of novel inhibitors of Plasmodium lysyl-tRNA synthetase with multistage activity against malaria parasites
papers.abstract: A fused dihydropyrrolidino-pyrimidine hit with low lipophilicity and excellent ligand efficiency (LE=0.4, LLE 4.9) was identified in a biochemical screen of the Global Health Chemical Diversity Library (GHCDL) against Plasmodium lysyl-tRNA synthetase (KRS). A structurally enabled lead optimization campaign led to the identification of analogues with potent parasite growth inhibition, excellent biochemical and cellular selectivity (>1000 fold) and efficacy in the malaria NOD-scid IL2Rγ null (SCID) mouse model after oral dosing. Structural information and computational methods were deployed to identify a potent and selective basic KRS inhibitor ( 30 ) with an extended half-life to reduce the dose regimen to a single-dose cure. This basic lead displayed long half-life across preclinical species, a favourable safety profile, and activity across Plasmodium species as well as against drug-resistant and sensitive P. falciparum strains and field isolates. Unfortunately, 30 lacked oral bioavailability that could not be mitigated with a prodrug approach. Nevertheless, learnings from this series will assist future programmes on new KRS inhibitors to deliver a clinical candidate with this novel mode of action.

papers.title: Modeling Limits of Detection in Headspace GC/MS
papers.abstract: The limits of detection (LOD) for headspace Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) of a diverse series of compounds were accurately predicted using a simple linear regression model incorporating Henry’s law constants and a polarity descriptor. LODs were predicted with an R 2 of 0.9154 and a standard error of the estimate (SEE) of 1184 nmol/L (approximately 17 μg/L) over a range of LODs from 2 μg/L to 585 μg/L using Henry’s law constants and dipole moment. This study has important practical applications, as experimental LOD studies are often time-consuming. The ability to estimate LOD values from existing data provides a rapid means of approximating the method sensitivity. A simple rule of thumb derived from this study is that for compounds with comparable molecular weights, nonpolar hydrocarbons have the lowest limit of detection, polar aprotic solvents have intermediate LODs, and polar protic solvents have the highest LODs. These generalizations are directly related to the ability of the species of interest to interact with water molecules. Henry’s constants capture the bulk of the variations in sensitivity for this data set, while the dipole moment captures the non-ideal interaction effects that are not resolved by Henry’s law constants alone.

papers.title: Progress in the Synthesis and Biological Activities of the Calothrixin and Topopyrone Natural Products
papers.abstract: Natural products represent a rich source of structurally diverse and biologically potent compounds. Among these are the calothrixins (cyanobacterial indolo[3,2-j]phenanthridine alkaloids) and the topyrones (fungal anthraquinone-type polyketides). While originating from different kingdoms of life and possessing distinct overall architectures, both scaffold families share a crucial quinone pharmacophore that is intrinsically linked to their potent cytotoxic activities, often involving DNA interaction and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the progress in the total synthesis and biological characterization of these two intriguing natural product classes. We discuss the various synthetic strategies developed to access their complex cores.

papers.title: A Straightforward Fabrication Technique to Minimize Evaporation and Surface Fouling in Microscale PDMS Devices for Nucleic Acid Amplification by dLAMP
Interfacial Energetics of C2–C18 Aliphatic Moieties on Hydrogenated Si(111) and Si(110) surfaces: a DFT Study
papers.abstract: We present a computational study based on density functional theory to systematically investigate how aliphatic moiety functionalization affects the interfacial electronic structure of H-terminated Si(111) and Si(110) surfaces. We explore the energetics, dipole formation, and charge transfer mechanisms for alkyl, alkenyl, and 1-alkynyl chains containing from 2 to 18 carbon atoms chemisorbed on both crystallographic orientations. Our analysis reveals that alkenyl moieties exhibit pronounced chain-length dependence of surface dipoles and tunneling barriers, whereas alkyl and 1-alkynyl chains show saturation effects for longer chains. We found that H–Si(111) exhibits surface dipoles up to 33% larger than H–Si(110), due to differences in atomic packing density and Si-H bond orientation. The resulting charge injection barriers for both thermionic and tunneling transport are quantified and discussed. The tilted geometry adopted by alkenyl moieties on Si(110) is rationalized through analysis of molecular orbital hybridization with surface states. These results provide quantitative guidelines for engineering interface energetics in silicon-based molecular electronic devices through rational choice of molecular termination and substrate orientation.

papers.title: Defining Chemical Bonds and Molecules via FCC Radii
papers.abstract: Despite extensive study, the definitions of chemical bonds and molecules remain ambiguous, and no universally rigorous criterion exists to determine whether two atoms are bonded. To address this issue from first principles, we introduce the FCC radii, an atomic radius defined as half the equilibrium nearest-neighbor distance obtained by relaxing identical atoms within an ideal face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice. By maximizing local symmetry and eliminating directional environmental effects, FCC radii provides a non-empirical, environment-independent measure of atomic size. Using this framework, two atoms are considered bonded if their center-to-center separation does not exceed the sum of their FCC radii, and the largest connected set of such atoms defines a molecule. This approach applies consistently to both molecules and crystals, captures the geometric basis of bonding, and reproduces conventional bonding patterns, including covalent, ionic, and hydrogen bonds. The FCC radii thus provides a rigorous, parameter-free, and physically grounded foundation for defining atomic size, chemical bonds, and molecular connectivity across diverse chemical systems.

papers.title: Porous Membrane Adsorption for Capturing Small Extracellular Vesicles Enables Accessible Single-Particle Analysis
papers.abstract: Quantitative analysis of small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) at single-particle resolution remains challenging due to their nanoscale dimensions and compositional heterogeneity. Existing methods rely on specialized and costly instrumentation and expert operation, limiting accessibility for many researchers and retarding sEV science. Here, we present a simple single-particle analysis method using a standard wide field fluorescence microscopy, which employs porous anodized aluminum oxide (AAO) membranes as nanoscale compartments to spatially isolate individual vesicles. AAO pores accommodate vesicles to sufficiently separate them beyond the optical resolution limit, ensuring reliable attribution of fluorescent spots to individual vesicles. PMACS achieves reliable quantification of culture cell-derived sEVs across a broad dynamic range (10 3 – 10 6 particles / μL). This performance is comparable to or exceeds conventional single-particle analysis although PMACS eliminates the need for either advanced instrumentation or expert operation. We demonstrate that PMACS allows colocalization analysis of sEV cargo by assessing tetraspanin (CD9, CD63, CD81) population.

papers.title: Structure-Based De Novo Design of Novel Allosteric smHDAC8 Modulators: A Fragment-Based Strategy to Combat Schistosomiasis
Reprogramming RiPP Scaffolds through Skeletal Editing Unlocks Chemical Space
papers.abstract: In this study, we report (1) a scalable, systematic, and general synthetic approach for the supply of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) bearing Tyr–Trp cross-linkages, and (2) the comprehensive expansion of novel chemical space through their skeletal diversification. In recent years, numerous biaryl-containing peptides have been discovered, and some of these RiPPs exhibit potent biological activities. However, despite the high metabolic stability and strong target protein binding generally attributed to biaryl RiPPs, their significant strain and rigidity have limited the availability of general synthetic methods. Here, we demonstrate the high versatility of modular synthetic strategies for the construction of RiPPs and achieve the synthesis of a variety of RiPPs containing Tyr–Trp cross-linkages. Furthermore, skeletal diversification via scaffold hopping enables access to artificial RiPP scaffolds incorporating quinazoline and quinoline motifs, whose preparation has previously been challenging.

papers.title: Src kinase app: valid inhibitor generation and prediction with explanation using predictive model and selfies
papers.abstract: Generative models trained on small datasets often underperform, limiting their ability to explore chemical space effectively.
