Owing to the selective adsorption of PLA end blocks at the oil–water interface and the solvation of the PEO midblock in the aqueous phase, this polymer is expected to form reversible droplet-bridging networks. During the process, the polymer concentration, molecular weight of the mid and end blocks, and the dispersed phase volume fraction were adjusted, and the factors governing network formation were elucidated using oscillatory rheology and stress-relaxation measurements. The results show that anchoring of the PLA end blocks and PEO-mediated bridging predominantly control the strength and dynamic reversibility of the network. Step-strain experiments further reveal that the droplet-bridging interactions can be disrupted under large deformation and partially recover when small-strain conditions are restored, confirming the presence of reversible physical associations. These findings establish a molecular design strategy for biodegradable telechelic copolymers as effective and reprocessable structuring agents in emulsion gels. The shear-responsive, tunable, and reversible nature of the droplet-bridging network makes this material platform particularly suitable for injectable emulsion gels for advanced soft matter and biomedical engineering applications.

papers.title: Synthesis of 4-Quinolone N-Oxides via Controlled Partial Hydrogenation of 2-Nitrobenzoyl Enamines
papers.abstract: An operationally simple procedure for the synthesis of 2-alkyl-4-quinolone N-oxides, relying on controlled platinum-catalyzed partial hydrogenation of 2-nitrobenzoyl enamines, has been demonstrated. The P. aeruginosa metabolite 2-heptyl-4-quinolone-N-oxide (HQNO) and four analogous products have been prepared in good yield and high purity by this method.

papers.title: Breaking the strength-activity tradeoff in high-temperature CO2 electrolysis with a hybrid solid oxide cell
papers.abstract: Electrochemical conversion of CO2 into chemicals and fuels offers a promising route towards a circular carbon economy. High-temperature CO2 electroreduction in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) delivers high selectivity and energy efficiency, but suffers from a tradeoff between mechanical robustness and electrochemical activity. Here we resolve this constraint using a hybrid ionic-conductor architecture that decouples electrocatalysis, ionic transport and mechanical support into function-specific layers. The resulting cell achieves one of the highest reported mechanical strengths (fracture load >7 N), while delivering 1.5-3.0fold higher CO2-to-CO activity than state-of-the-art SOECs over operating temperatures of 600-800 °C. Stable operation is maintained for over 1,000 hours at a current density of 1.0 A cm-2. Furthermore, we demonstrate scalability with a single-cell area of 100 cm 2 , achieving total currents up to 120 A and powers up to 200 W. This work establishes a general strategy for developing mechanically resilient, efficient, and scalable energy conversion devices.

papers.title: When Do Models Win? A Learning Curve Benchmark for Molecular Property Prediction in Low-Data Regimes
papers.abstract: In many molecular property prediction tasks, such as drug discovery and OLED material design, labeled data are often limited to only tens to thousands of samples due to high experimental costs. Despite the rapid development of machine learning models, it remains unclear which model classes are most effective under such low-data regimes and how their performance evolves with increasing data. In this work, we present a comprehensive learning curve benchmark across traditional machine learning methods, graph neural networks (GNNs), transformer-based molecular language models, and hybrid architectures. We systematically vary the training data size from 50 to 3,000 samples and evaluate performance on QM9, ESOL, Lipophilicity, and BACE datasets using scaffold splits with repeated trials for statistical robustness. We further propose two hybrid models combining GCN and ChemBERTa with different fusion strategies-concatenation (GTCA-Cat) and cross-attention (GTCA-CA)-and analyze their data efficiency through ablation studies. Our results reveal that (1) hybrid models substantially improve over single-modality GCN in low-data regimes for physicochemical property targets (e.g., 32% RMSE reduction on ESOL at N=50), (2) simple concatenation fusion generally outperforms or matches cross-attention due to reduced overfitting and improved stability, and (3) clear crossover points exist where traditional kernel-based methods outperform deep learning models depending on the task type. Importantly, we identify regimedependent model optimality: deep learning models dominate continuous physicochemical property prediction, while kernel-based methods can be more effective for bioactivity prediction across most data scales. Our findings provide actionable guidelines for model selection under data scarcity and highlight the importance of learning curve analysis as a principled tool for understanding model behavior.

papers.title: Selective Post-Synthetic Reduction of Pyridinium Hydrazone Cages
papers.abstract: Post-synthetic modification of a series of hexacationic organic cages containing pyridinium and hydrazone groups gave a new family of neutral organic cages through a high-yielding single step reduction reaction. The reduction selectively reduces all six pyridinium rings to 1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridines but leaves the hydrazone C=N bond untouched. The neutral cages display strong and cooperative sulfate binding to give cage•(SO4 2-)2 complexes in DMSO.

papers.title: Surface-Neutralized HgCdSe Quantum Dots for High-Detectivity Infrared Photodetectors
When Three-Body Interactions Become Redundant: Scaling Graph Neural Network Potentials
papers.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNN) are currently the vehicle for large scale molecular dynamics at quantum accuracy, but their practical scalability remains limited by the rapidly increasing size of graph representations required for large atomistic systems. In particular, the construction of higherorder interactions such as triplets leads to substantial memory and computational overhead during both training and inference. In this work, we investigate strategies to improve the scalability of GNNbased potentials while preserving predictive accuracy. We show that pruning triplet interactions during training and inference has minimal impact on regression accuracy for formation energies, band gaps, and elastic moduli. For molecular dynamics simulations, we find that pruning triplets during inference preserves structural fidelity while significantly reducing computational cost. This allows for upscaling of GNNs to large structures (beyond 30k atoms). To further extend scalability, we introduce a spatial chunking scheme that decomposes large atomistic systems into padded subgraphs, enabling efficient evaluation of forces for systems containing hundreds of thousands of atoms. Using this approach, we perform molecular dynamics simulations of a 400,000-atom LGPS supercell on a single GPU using the M3GNet and DIEP models. Our results demonstrate that fully trained manybody GNN potentials contain significant redundancy that can be exploited to improve scalability, providing a practical pathway toward large-scale atomistic simulations with universal machinelearning potentials.

papers.title: Mapping the Applicability Domain of Lipophilicity Models Through Chemical Space Topology
papers.abstract: The applicability domain (AD) of a QSAR model defines the boundary of chemical space within which its predictions are statistically valid. For large-scale lipophilicity (logP) modeling, conventional AD formulations produce a binary in-domain/out-of-domain classification that conceals the internal topology of prediction uncertainty. This paper presents a PCAbased spatial error analysis over a 426,850-molecule bioactive dataset assembled from three independent chemical databases. The seven-dimensional descriptor space reduces to a 2D manifold capturing 76.83% of total variance (PC1: 52.85%; PC2: 23.98%), revealing a bimodal topology: Lipinski-compliant drug-like molecules form a dense central core, while pharmacologically extreme molecules scatter at the periphery. Overlaying ElasticNet prediction residuals (computed exclusively on held-out test molecules) demonstrates that mean absolute error (MAE) is 2.73× higher at the periphery than at the central manifold (1.567 vs. 0.574 logP units), with non-overlapping bootstrap 95% confidence intervals confirming significance at α=0.01. A Lipinski-stratified dual-model strategy motivated by this topology achieves RMSE=0.838 for the Drug-Like population and R²=0.767 for the Extreme population, the latter surpassing the global XGBoost baseline (R²=0.765). The contribution is primarily methodological: PCA-based error topology provides an interpretable, quantitative diagnostic for AD characterization that directly informs production deployment decisions. The approach is general and not specific to logP.

papers.title: Identification of Roasting Reaction Products of Catechin Exhibiting Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitory Activity
papers.abstract: Food processing and cooking methods that involve high-temperature heating (such as roasting) alter the composition of raw food materials. Even polyphenols, which are generally considered thermally stable, undergo changes in their chemical structure during roasting. This study investigated the roasting reaction of catechin, a functional polyphenol, at a temperature of approximately 200 ℃ and found that it enhanced xanthine oxidase inhibitory activity. Purification and separation of the products derived from the catechin roasting reaction revealed two types of moderately active compounds: dimeric products with a linkage between the C and A rings, and an aurone-like benzofuran product. Additionally, several fractions containing oligomeric products were identified as highly active fractions. These results suggest that catechin enhances xanthine oxidase inhibitory activity by transforming into dimeric, aurone-type, and probably oligomeric products.

papers.title: MgCl2-Mediated Mechanisms of Oxygen Solubility in Molten Salt Reactor Fuels
papers.abstract: In molten salt reactors, oxygen impurities accelerate structural material corrosion. Moreover, the ingress of oxide species may promote the formation of insoluble actinide oxychlorides or oxides, potentially raising safety concerns. To limit the undesired precipitation of such phases, MgCl 2 has been proposed as a complementary fuel component to sequester oxygen by enhancing the solubility of actinide oxide species. In this study, we provide direct, molecularlevel evidence of an MgCl 2 -mediated oxygen solubility mechanism. This was achieved through high-temperature 17 O nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy on NaCl-MgCl 2 -LaCl 3 melts with various amounts of dissolved 17 O-enriched LaOCl, corroborated by classical molecular dynamics with the polarizable ion model and first-principles NMR calculations. Experiment and simulation both show that adding MgCl 2 drives Mg 2+ to compete with La 3+ for O 2- coordination, disrupting La-O clustering that facilitates oxide precipitation. Altogether, these results establish a mechanistic framework for tuning oxygen speciation and solubility through compositional design in high-temperature molten salt systems.

papers.title: A new equation for the calculation of activity coefficients in non-ideal solutions
papers.abstract: Based on the thermodynamic expression of excess volume, a new equation is derived to calculate the activity coefficients of components in a non-ideal solution. For an ideal binary solution, it is proved that this equation is valid. For non-ideal binary solutions, the damped Newton method is applied to find the roots of this equation iteratively. The iterative process is not dependent on the initial guesses of activity coefficients. The convergence of iterative process is always reached. For two negative and three positive deviation solutions, the activity coefficients of components are calculated iteratively. They are in good agreement with the activity coefficients reported in literature. The total activity coefficient is also calculated to show the deviation of the entire solution from the hypothetic ideal solution. Based on the activity coefficients calculated in this work, the total activity coefficients γ of five non-ideal solutions are in very good agreement with the total active coefficients calculated with activity coefficients reported in literatures. The magnitude of γ can be understood from intermolecular interaction. This interaction is estimated qualitatively with the interaction of the molecular dipole moments calculated with the density functional theory.

papers.title: Lithium plating and stripping facilitated by thin sputtered silver and carbon interlayers in anode-free all-solid-state batteries
Unlocking a shortcut: Active machine learning in non-aqueous battery electrolyte development for sodium-based batteries
papers.abstract: Sodium-based batteries are promising candidates for sustainable large-scale energy storage, yet systematic electrolyte design remains challenging due to the high dimensionality and physical constraints of formulation space. Here, we present a data-driven workflow that combines high-throughput experimentation with batch-wise active learning to efficiently map and model non-aqueous sodium-based electrolyte formulations. Rather than targeting a single optimal composition, the approach constructs predictive surrogate models over the full space of physically admissible formulations, which in the present case corresponds to a three-dimensional, compositionally constrained feature space defined by salt content and solvent mixing ratios. Training identical models on sodium-and lithium-based data sets enables a direct, composition-wide comparison of both cations within the same solvent framework, revealing largely similar conductivity landscapes with modest but systematic differences that can be rationalized by differences in ionic size and solvation characteristics. The formulation space can be reliably described using only 72 electrolyte compositions acquired in two active learning iterations, corresponding to a reduction in required experiments by a factor of 4-7 compared to random sampling. Conductivity-guided electrolyte selection leads to improved rate capability and low-temperature performance in sodium-ion full cells, while also highlighting the limitations of ionic conductivity as a sole performance descriptor. Overall, this work establishes a transferable, physics-informed framework for data-efficient electrolyte exploration.

papers.title: Dispersion from polarizabilities of atoms in molecule: DPAIM
papers.abstract: A new atom-atom pairwise dispersion function DPAIM (dispersion from polarizabilities of atoms in molecules) has been developed. The dynamic polarizabilities, both dipole-dipole and quadrupole-quadrupole, of a set of reference molecules obtained from the time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) are first spherically averaged and then split into AIM atomic contributions using the generalized effective atomic sizes based on Hirshfeld's partitioning of DFT molecular density. The polarizability

papers.title: When Do Simple Models Win? Machine Learning Architectures for UV Absorption Prediction and Insights for General Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: What determines which machine learning architecture wins for molecular property prediction? We address this question through a controlled comparison of five models spanning four architecture families: fingerprint-based ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost), a directed message-passing graph neural network (GNN), a bidirectional gated recurrent network (BiGRU), and a pretrained Transformer, using UV absorption wavelength (λ max) prediction as a testbed across 18,755 solute-solvent pairs with stratified 5-fold cross-validation and two external datasets totaling over 40,000 molecules. The answer depends on the task. For screening within known chemical space, RF with Morgan fingerprints is optimal: it matches the GNN (RMSE = 31.34 ± 1.82 vs. 31.69 ± 3.18 nm, p = 0.77), trains in 15 minutes on a CPU with no hyperparameter tuning, and outperforms all sequence-based models. For exploring novel scaffolds, deep learning is superior: experimental validation on 16 novel UV-absorbing 1 compounds shows that the GNN (MAE = 26.2 nm), Transformer (26.3 nm), and Bi-GRU (28.6 nm) all outperform RF (38.5 nm), as learned representations generalize where fixed fingerprints cannot. In either case, encoding solvent identity improves all models: a simple SMILES/fingerprint concatenation strategy yields 6-8% RMSE reductions across fingerprint, graph, and recurrent architectures (p < 0.02), without domain-specific descriptor engineering. Interpretability analysis confirms that both RF feature importance and BiGRU gradient saliency independently highlight the same chromophore motifs, and that architectures with local inductive bias systematically outperform global-attention Transformers on this locally determined property. These findings provide general guidance for molecular property prediction: the largest or most complex model is not always the best choice. Instead, optimal model selection depends on the locality of the target property and the relationship between target compounds and available training data. When the target property is governed by local molecular features and the prediction task is interpolation within known chemical space, simple fingerprint-based models offer an efficient and accurate alternative to deep learning.

papers.title: Open-Source Computational Workflows for Drug Repurposing: A Methodological Strategy Against Arterial Hypertension
papers.abstract: Arterial hypertension remains a leading global risk factor for cardiovascular mortality. The traditional de novo drug discovery pipeline is hindered by exorbitant costs and prolonged developmental timelines. Drug repurposing-identifying new therapeutic indications for existing approved drugs-presents a highly efficient alternative. This methodological essay critically evaluates the implementation of completely open-source computational workflows for in silico drug repurposing against key hypertensive targets, such as the Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) and the Angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor (AT1R). We systematically dissect a generalized Computer-Aided Drug Design (CADD) pipeline utilizing freely available software: RDKit for cheminformatics library preparation, AutoDock Vina for high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS), and GROMACS for molecular dynamics (MD) trajectory analysis. Consolidating literature data, we demonstrate how open-source automation frameworks (like KNIME and Python/Jupyter) democratize pharmacological research, enabling academic laboratories to execute complex polypharmacological screenings. Our analysis highlights that open-source pipelines can achieve hit-identification accuracies comparable to proprietary software, reducing computational screening costs by 100% while compressing the preclinical target validation timeline by over 60%.

papers.title: Cationic Imidazolium Macrocycles Enable Array-based, Site-Selective Optical Detection of Peptide Phosphorylation
papers.abstract: Simple polycationic imidazolium macrocycles, formed in one step from commercial precursors, show strong affinity for peptide strands with anionic and hydrophobic character, and can be paired with styrylpyridinium dyes in an arrayed format to enable site-and state-selective optical detection of phosphorylation at serine residues. Even though they show affinity for anions in aqueous solution, the cationic macrocyclic hosts do not bind the modified serine phosphate residues themselves, rather they exploit π-stacking interactions with the native peptide backbone and different sidechains, allowing interaction with both modified and unmodified peptides. When combined with cationic indicators that can also bind the peptide targets, a complex equilibrium is established consisting of peptide:host, peptide:dye and dye:host assemblies, as well as peptide:dye:host ternary complexes. These multiple equilibria enable differentiation of miniscule changes in peptide target, differentiating phosphate residues at different sites on otherwise identical peptide strands.

papers.title: Transparent Reporting for Agentic Catalysis Enabled by Artificial Intelligence (TRACE-AI): Community Guidelines and A Publication Checklist
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into catalysis science, enabling agentic workflows in which AI systems perceive inputs, reason under constraints, plan, and autonomously execute in silico or physical experiments with minimal human intervention. While these closed-loop capabilities hold promise to accelerate knowledge generation and technological innovation, they inevitably introduce new sources of variability in data lineage, model specification, and agent policies that can undermine FAIRness, rigor, and reproducibility. These risks are particularly pronounced in heterogeneous catalysis, where subtleties in catalyst synthesis and pretreatment, dynamic restructuring under operating conditions, and transport-mediated local environments can largely determine catalytic outcomes. To address these challenges, we introduce TRACE-AI (Transparent Reporting for Agentic Catalysis Enabled by Artificial Intelligence) as a set of community guidelines paired with a publication checklist. TRACE-AI emphasizes end-to-end traceability across the full lifecycle of an agentic catalysis campaign, linking research objectives to data and models, agent reasoning and action, and the knowledge acquired. By promoting standardized and accountable reporting, TRACE-AI aims to cultivate a shared foundation for accelerating scientific discovery while reinforcing safety and trust as autonomous catalysis laboratories continue to emerge.

papers.title: Application of machine learning to identify key physicochemical predictors for mimicking UHT cow milk
papers.abstract: Plant-based milk alternatives (PBMAs) differ from cow milk in their physicochemical properties, creating a significant challenge in their ability to replicate dairy-like functionality. In this study, machine learning was applied to identify the key physicochemical predictors associated with dairy-like properties in PBMAs. Two models, Random Forest Regression (RFR) and Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR), were trained using physicochemical, chemical composition and ingredients data from cow (10), soy (10), oat (10), almond (10), coconut (10), rice (3), and plant-hybrid (1) milk types. Model performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R²), root mean square error (RMSE), learning curves, and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Both models demonstrated strong predictive performance on testing data, RFR (R² = 0.80 ± 0.05; RMSE = 1.29 ± 0.19), and GBR (R² = 0.76 ± 0.05; RMSE = 1.46 ± 0.27), with no statistical difference in predictive accuracy. Permutation feature importance identified fat, carbohydrate, and xanthan gum content as the key predictors of physicochemical similarity to cow milk, reflecting their roles in determining volatile compounds, viscosity, particle size, whiteness, and physical stability. Volatile compounds, including δ-octalactone, also contributed to predictive accuracy. The performance of the models was limited by the small dataset size, the absence of sensory data, and commercial formulations. This study demonstrated the value of machine learning in predicting key physicochemical predictors in PBMAs mimicry of dairy. Future work should focus on formulation prediction, increasing dataset size, and the integration of sensory data to improve model robustness.

papers.title: A theoretical analysis of propargyl oxidation by the hydroperoxyl radical
papers.abstract: The kinetics of the C 3 H 3 + HO 2 reaction system were investigated theoretically using high-level quantum chemical methods combined with statistical rate theory. The potential energy surface (PES) was explored to identify intermediates and transition states using reactive molecular dynamics with ChemTraYzer-TAD. The resulting thermochemical data and energy barriers for products P0 to P13 were used in RRKM/master equation calculations to determine the temperature-and pressure-dependent rate constants suitable for incorporation into chemical kinetic models. Implications for chemical kinetic model predictions and future model development were assessed by representative jet-stirred reactor simulations of stoichiometric propyne/air mixtures at 10 atm and 800-1200 K. These simulations show that the widely employed allyl + HO 2 analogy overestimates propargyl consumption. In the jet-stirred reactor case considered here, replacing the analogy-based treatment with the theory-based update reduces the contribution of C 3 H 3 + HO 2 reactions to the overall consumption of C 3 H 3 from up to 26 % to no more than 15 %. The corresponding changes in benzene predictions are visible, but remain within the experimental uncertainty. Based on these findings, a compact reduced three-reaction submodel is proposed for future chemical kinetic model development. Novelty and significance statement We present the first comprehensive ab initio and master equation-based kinetic investigation of the C 3 H 3 + HO 2 reaction system. Barrierless and new low-barrier channels were identified using potential energy surface exploration with ChemTraYzer-TAD, and the resulting temperature-and pressuredependent rate coefficients provide a substantially more reliable description of this chemistry than the allyl + HO 2 analogy commonly used in chemical kinetic models. Jet-stirred reactor simulations show that replacing the analogy-based treatment reduces predicted C 3 H 3 consumption via reactions with HO 2 and leads to visible changes in benzene predictions that remain within the experimental uncertainty. Brute force sensitivity analysis further shows that only the OH-forming channel, C 3 H 3 + HO 2 = P-C 3 H 3 O + OH, noticeably affects the predicted C 3 H 3 and benzene mole fractions. Based on these findings, a compact reduced three-reaction submodel is proposed for future chemical kinetic model development. Because C 3 H 3 is a key C0-C4 core species, the refined kinetics are relevant beyond aromatic chemistry.

papers.title: Gas6-Enriched NIR-II Nanodecoys for Chemo-Photothermal Therapy and Preemptive Inhibition of Lung Metastasis in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, and preventing its metastasis remains a major clinical challenge. In this work, we developed biomimetic nanodecoys (NDs) capable of precise diagnosis and effective treatment of NPC while concurrently preventing lung metastasis. The NDs were synthesized via precipitation polymerization to form a pH-and thermal-responsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-acrylic acid) nanogels (PA NGs), followed by encapsulation a newly developed aggregation-induced emission luminogen (AIEgen), NDA-N, for strong near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence imaging (FLI) and remarkable photothermal therapy (PTT) performance. In combination with the 2 chemotherapeutic drug doxorubicin (Dox), these NDs achieved effective chemo-photothermal combinatorial therapy. Triggered by the acidic tumor microenvironment, the NDs released Dox, and this release was further accelerated under NIR irradiation due to the generated heat. Moreover, we demonstrate that growth arrest-specific 6 (Gas6)-camouflaged NDs (PND@Gas6(+)) could function as a prophylactic agent to bind Axl receptor in lung metastatic niches, thereby preemptively blocking the Gas6/Axl axis and preventing metastatic colonization. This study presents an innovative strategy that integrates real-time NIR-II monitoring and synergistic chemo-PTT therapy for NPC, while also providing a rational design for metastasis inhibition, offering substantial promise for improving NPC treatment.

papers.title: Diclofenac Aptasensor Based on Graphene Field-Effect Transistor
papers.abstract: Biosensors are analytical tools whose performance is highly influenced by the transducing method and the construction protocol. Graphene field-effect transistors (GFETs) are recognized as sensitive sensors owing to their strong response to changes in surface charge, but their use is limited by complex fabrication and integration processes. In this work, we employ a straightforward method to modify commercially available GFET surfaces via diazonium salt reduction, yielding reproducible and robust interfaces. Using a protective-deprotective strategy to form controlled nanostructured monolayers, a GFET aptamer-based sensor was developed for the detection of diclofenac (DCF). For that purpose, an azide-modified aptamer sensitive to DCF was immobilized on the surface of the functionalized graphene by click chemistry, an orthogonal and biocompatible covalent immobilization strategy. The sensor had a linearity range from 5 to 100 nM, reaching a satisfactory limit of detection of 3.1 nM, comparable to the concentrations of the analyte found in the environment. Moreover, the sensor has good selectivity, stability, repeatability, and performance in river water. This strategy marks the first attempt to develop an aptamer-based GFET sensor for DCF detection.

papers.title: Biaryl Tetrazines as Chemoselective Double-Click Reagents
papers.abstract: Biaryl 1,2,4,5-tetrazines are established as a new class of bench-stable bifunctional click reagents for chemoselective double Diels-Alder reaction sequences. A unified approach to both symmetric and unsymmetric biaryl tetrazines via Pd-catalyzed coupling of bromotetrazines is described, providing derivatives amenable to further functionalization, including via mutually orthogonal Cu-catalyzed azide-alkyne Huisgen click reactions. Diels-Alder studies reveal that biaryl tetrazines undergo chemoselective mono-cycloaddition reactions with strained alkynes as dienophiles, which can be followed by a second Diels-Alder reaction with a dienophile at either the alkyne or alkene oxidation level. Computational analysis reveals that a subtle interplay between electronic interactions and substrate distortion energies governs cycloaddition chemoselectivity. Leveraging this reactivity, we demonstrate a model bioconjugative double Diels-Alder sequence that exhibits advantageous proximity-enabled fluorescence quenching properties.

papers.title: Long-Term Release Behavior and Cytotoxicity Assessment of Therapeutic Agents from Nanostructured Laser-Modified Titanium Niobium Zirconium Tin Implants
papers.abstract: The development of advanced biomaterials for implantable devices has increasingly focused on improving both therapeutic functionality and biocompatibility. In this study, nanostructured surfaces were engineered on titanium-niobium-zirconium-tin (Ti-Nb-Zr-Sn) alloys using laser modification techniques to enable controlled drug delivery and enhanced cellular response. The laser processing generated hierarchical surface features that significantly increased surface area and facilitated the incorporation of therapeutic agents within the nanostructures. The long-term release behavior of the loaded agents was systematically evaluated under physiological conditions, revealing a sustained and predictable release profile over extended periods without significant burst effects. Cytotoxicity assessment was conducted using relevant in vitro cell models to evaluate the biological safety of the modified implants. The results demonstrated high cell viability, minimal inflammatory response, and improved cell adhesion and proliferation compared to untreated surfaces. The synergy between the nanostructured topology and controlled drug release contributed to a favorable microenvironment for tissue integration. Furthermore, the Ti-Nb-Zr-Sn alloy exhibited excellent corrosion resistance and mechanical stability, supporting its suitability for long-term biomedical applications. Overall, the findings highlight the potential of laser-modified nanostructured Ti-Nb-Zr-Sn implants as multifunctional platforms for localized therapy and improved osseointegration. This approach offers a promising pathway for next-generation implantable devices with enhanced therapeutic efficiency and reduced adverse effects.

papers.title: Co-Al LDH nanoclusters for enhanced visible-light-driven photocatalytic H2 production
papers.abstract: The efficient conversion of solar energy into chemical energy represents one of the most significant challenges in contemporary society. Photocatalytic systems combining a catalyst, a photosensitizer (PS), and a sacrificial electron donor (ED) are widely explored for this purpose. Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) have shown great potential as catalysts. In this study, we demonstrate efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution using Co-Al LDH nanoclusters synthesized by the epoxide method in the presence of fluorescein as the photosensitizer and triethanolamine as the electron donor. Colloidal nanosized LDH display a remarkable hydrogen production of 28863 µmol H 2 g –1 after 3.5 h, while redispersed solid reached 12567 µmol H 2 g –1 . Increasing PS concentration to 1 mM further enhances the activity to 54105 µmol H 2 g –1 . By contrast, micrometric LDHs synthesized by the urea hydrolysis method produce only 2065 µmol H 2 g –1 . PL studies suggest that the acac layer on the nanosized LDH surface confers a hydrophobic environment, mitigating aggregation-induced quenching. Electrochemical experiments confirm a lower charge-transfer resistance in nanometric LDHs, explaining their superior charge transport and catalytic efficiency.

papers.title: Chemical vapour deposition of high-purity, heavily boron-doped diamond in a low-cost, custom-built microwave plasma reactor
papers.abstract: Boron-doped diamond, an outstanding electrode material, is commonly synthesised via chemical vapour deposition (CVD) using expensive and toxic boron-containing gases. Alternative boron sources are therefore attractive; however, their use in the growth of phase-pure diamond films is so far limited. This study presents how trimethyl borate (TMBT; B(OCH 3) 3) can be used as a liquid precursor of boron for the growth of high-quality, heavily boron-doped diamond films in a custom-made, microwave plasmaassisted CVD system. These polycrystalline films were deposited on Si plates at a very high boron-tocarbon molar ratio (105,000 ppm) with homogeneous distribution throughout the film. The films exhibit an atypical surface morphology, composed of {110} and {100} crystallographic facets. Typical growth rates of about 1.5 μm/h were achieved for the process carried out without enhancements. The average concentration of boron in the films was determined to be 6.48×10 21 cm-3. Moreover, the films are characterised by negative electron affinity. The availability of these diamond films from a highly reproducible and very accessible procedure is opening new possibilities for electrochemistry, sensing and photo-electrocatalytic applications.

papers.title: Substitution-Driven Control of Excited-State Dynamics in Mono-Annulated Indigos
papers.abstract: A series of mono-annulated indigo (MAI) derivatives was synthesized and systematically investigated to elucidate the role of structural asymmetry on excited-state dynamics. The synthesized MAIs exhibit pronounced solvatochromism, large Stokes shifts, and base-induced NIR absorption. Transient absorption measurements showed ns-lived singlet states and ms-lived triplet states, demonstrating substitution-controlled ISC and relaxation pathways.

papers.title: Face saturation at ρ * = 4 ln 2: a universal threshold separating cooperative from individual relaxation in hydrogen-bonded liquids
papers.abstract: The non-Arrhenius crossover in the dielectric relaxation of liquid water near 35-45 • C has been documented for four decades. No existing model predicts the crossover temperature without a fitted parameter. We show that the crossover occurs at a topological threshold ρ * = 4 ln 2, derived from the 4-simplex (K5) and not adjusted. A periodic table of K5 hydrides (CH4, NH3, H2O, HF and their third-row analogues) reveals that water is the only simple hydride combining a permanent dipole with an effective hydrogen-bond density ρ above the threshold. The crossover at ∼ 40 • C is a direct consequence of this unique position. We test the universality of ρ * on a database of 11 hydrogen-bonding liquids with published temperature-dependent dielectric relaxation data. Using the measured number of hydrogen bonds per molecule nHB as the effective density ρ, the threshold classifies 10 of 11 liquids correctly: B19 • Regime II (ρ * < ρ < 2ρ *): cooperative. Water, formamide: 2/2. • Regime I (ρ < ρ *): individual. DMF, DMA, MeOH, EtOH, PrOH, DMSO, CH3CN: 7/7. • Regime III (ρ > 2ρ *): vitrification. Glycerol: 1/1. The single exception is N-methylformamide (NMF, nHB = 2.0 < ρ * , cooperative). Neutron diffraction shows NMF forms linear chains, not triangular clusters: its cooperativity arises from sequential bond breakage, a mechanism distinct from K5 face saturation. The gap between the lowest cooperative ρ (formamide, 3.08) and the highest individual ρ (ethanol, 1.5) straddles ρ * = 2.773 with no overlap. All nHB values are sourced from neutron diffraction or molecular dynamics; all τ (T) classifications are from the original authors. No existing model (Tanaka, Stanley, Poole) extends beyond water. D2O (nHB = 3.76) and ethylene glycol (nHB = 3.0-3.7) are predicted to show cooperative relaxation. Both are testable immediately. The threshold also predicts a critical concentration in water-alcohol mixtures: the non-Arrhenius crossover in τ (T) should disappear at x * MeOH ≈ 0.35 (25 • C) in water-methanol, and x * EtOH ≈ 0.39 in water-ethanol. B20 In the (T, nHB) plane, the cooperative-individual boundary is a horizontal line at nHB = ρ * , regardless of how nHB is varied (temperature, concentration, or pressure). Four K5 constants, together with one measured input (f coord), predict the relaxation time τ of 6 hydrides with τ free derived from geometry, and of 5 further molecules across three decades (3-1500 ps). All 11 predictions fall within a factor 3. B17 Companion script: 123 tests, 20 blocks, all PASS.

papers.title: A Columnar Liquid Crystalline Self-Assembly of a Donor-Acceptor TADF Emitter Design for Solution-Processed OLEDs
papers.abstract: The self-assembly of π-conjugated molecules into supramolecular columnar structures has become as an effective strategy for the creation of soft, durable, and adaptable materials with immense potential for application in organic optoelectronic devices. In this regard, the columnar organization of discotic liquid crystals (DLCs) is well-studied in terms of a quasi-1D charge transport medium, which can be exploited across a range of organic electronic device applications. There are relatively few examples of room temperature columnar DLCs emitting thermally activated delayed fluorescent (TADF). Herein, we demonstrate a molecular design strategy to deliver a material that simultaneously shows bright and efficient TADF and self-organizes into columnar DLCs at room temperature. The compound TCzTRZ-DLC contains three dendrimeric carbazole-based donors with mesogenic units decorating a central 1,3,5-triphenyltriazine acceptor. Notably, the system exhibited a desired homeotropic alignment resulting in preferential aromatic p-stacking among disc-like molecules, which is beneficial to boost the light out-coupling efficiency in solution-processed organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). The resulting green-emitting SP-OLEDs emitted at lEL of 488 nm and showed a maximum external quantum efficiency, EQEmax of 15.5%. This represents a significant improvement in OLED efficiency compared to other solution-processed devices using TADF emitters bearing mesogenic groups.
